(1) Inspired by the pyramid convolution structure, we devise a pyramid multi-head attention mechanism, which serves as an important calculation foundation for the feature learning in FDBG; (2) To improve the quality of each modality, we suggest a pyramid prior enhancement method that combines the current sample with several similar historical samples; (3) We put forward a fusion decomposition method to effectively complete the missing modalities, which first fuses the three modalities with the pyramid self-attention, and then decomposes the fusion feature into three modalities and completes the missing modalities with the self-attention interaction mechanism; and (4) To eliminate the interference, we introduce a backbone gathering method to translate and fuse the three modalities into a single modality. Based on three public benchmark datasets (IEMOCAP, MELD and CMU-MOSI), we conduct extensive experiments and prove that FDBG outperforms the 12 baseline models. The source codes of this work are available at https://github.com/SHX-AI/FDBGMSA.

title: Game-theoretic approach on strategizing cooperation model in community group-buying
abstract: Sound operational strategies and strong partnerships derive the development of community group-buying platform. Although the existing literature has concerned this unique platform, it largely neglects the design of its cooperation model. To fill this gap, this study proposes a cooperation framework based on a Stackelberg game approach in the context of community group-buying. Our model results demonstrate that collaborating with the local dealer through resale model enhances the platform’s profitability. Meanwhile, adopting a proportional commission model with the community leader can create a win-win-win situation involving the platform, the local dealer, and the community leader. Furthermore, a proportional commission structure exhibits superior incentive effects compared to a fixed commission structure in motivating community leader’s service efforts, especially when the local dealer operates in the resale model. Notably, our findings reveal that certain key parameters significantly influence the behavior of the platform’s partners, encouraging the local dealer and the community leader to adopt higher prices and exert greater effort in community group-buying service, while simultaneously providing opportunity for free-riding behavior. Experimental results confirm that the game-theoretic approach enables the platform to identify the optimal cooperation model, thereby achieving profit maximization.

title: Bridging the gap in cross-domain graph anomaly detection: Enhanced source utilization and label accuracy
abstract: Cross-domain graph anomaly detection is crucial for maintaining data security and system stability, as it can identify and respond to anomalous behaviors spanning various data domains. However, current methods are limited by their inability to fully leverage the complex source domain information and accurately assign labels due to the ambiguity and variability of anomalies across domains. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative approach, namely Bridging the Gap in Cross-Domain Anomaly Detection (BGAD). Our method employs high-frequency information-enriched node initialization and anomaly-aware denoised auto-encoders to deeply mine insights from the source domain and align them with the target domain. Additionally, a feedback-driven label shifting correction mechanism dynamically enhances label prediction precision. Our method has been rigorously tested on four different datasets. Compared with the most advanced CD-GAD method CDFS, BGAD has increased the AUC-ROC by 15.7%, significantly reducing false positives and false negatives, demonstrating outstanding effectiveness and practicality.

title: Dynamic loss balancing for long-tailed multi-label problem in document-level relation extraction
abstract: Documents contain multiple entity pairs, with specific pairs associated with multiple relations. The long-tailed distribution of relations further exacerbates the complexity of the document-level relation extraction (DocRE) task. In this study, we introduce a novel DocRE framework called HeterDLB. The HeterDLB constructs mention-level heterogeneous graphs by employing two types of meta-paths to capture the rich structural and contextual information within the document. To address the long-tailed distribution in multi-label DocRE, we propose an adaptive confidence threshold strategy that effectively distinguishes between positive and negative classes. To mitigate the imbalance between positive and negative classes during the training process, we first define the gradient update process of HeterDLB as a multi-objective optimization problem that involves adjusting the penalty strength among various loss functions through dynamic weights. We evaluate the HeterDLB on four benchmark datasets: DocRED, Re-DocRED, and two biomedical datasets, CDR and GDA. HeterDLB achieves F1 scores of 65.96% and 82.20% on DocRED and Re-DocRED, and 70.95% and 85.18% on CDR and GDA, respectively. Compared to the recent models, HeterDLB achieves average F1 score improvements of 5.43%, 15.48%, 4.07%, and 7.85% on the respective datasets when using the BERTbase model. Extensive experiments from multiple perspectives further validate the effectiveness of our framework.

title: BiT ConViT MultiKernelFormer with token mixing for robust multi-dataset histopathological image classification
abstract: Digital pathology is rapidly producing large-scale image repositories that must be efficiently triaged, indexed, and retrieved for clinical decision support. However, automated histopathological image classification remains fragile under domain shift caused by stain and scanner variability, organ-specific morphology, and magnification changes. We propose BiT-ConViT MultiKernelFormer with Token Mixing (BiT-ConViT-MKT), a compact hybrid that couples a BiT-ResNetV2 backbone with multi-kernel convolutional pathways, Global Context Enhancer (GCE) blocks with bounded gating, and a lightweight token-mixing transformer for global context. The model formalizes multi-kernel fusion as a convex, differentiable operator with Lipschitz stability, enabling bounded feature variation and interpretable fusion weights under distribution shift. Extensive evaluation on four public benchmarks: BreakHis (8 subtypes; 40×/100×/200×/400×), LC25000–Lung (3 classes), LC25000–Colon (2 classes), and OCT (4 classes). BiT-ConViT-MKT achieved 99.80% (Colon), 99.87% (Lung), 99.48% (OCT), and 96.23% (BreakHis merged) accuracy, with AUC values≥0.99 across all datasets. Magnification-specific results on BreakHis were consistently above 95.50%, with a +0.7 percentage-point gain over the strongest pretrained baseline at 400× . With 42.7 M parameters, BiT-ConViT-MKT provides a practical accuracy–efficiency trade-off suitable for routine deployment.

title: A self-modified hypergraph neural network for multimodal relation extraction
abstract: Multimodal Relation Extraction (MRE) aims to identify semantic relationships between entities in text-image pairs, playing a crucial role in multimodal understanding. Current graph-based MRE methods have achieved considerable success in modeling fine-grained multimodal interaction. However, there are limited by binary edges that require multi-hop reasoning and are prone to noise propagation. Moreover, these methods often overlook the exploitation of edge features, restricting structural optimization. To overcome these issues, we propose a Self-Modified Hypergraph Neural Network (SMHGNN). We construct a multimodal hypergraph where a hyperedge connects multiple nodes, enabling direct modeling of high-order semantic interactions. A key innovation is our mutually enhancing optimization mechanism between node features and hypergraph structure: hyperedges serve as feature carriers with attentional weighting, and the model iteratively self-modifies its connections through stacked HGNN layers to reduce noise and refine representations. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks show that SMHGNN achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a significant +1.84% F1 gain over the strongest baseline and a +3.13% improvement compared to the best graph-based method. The model also demonstrates strong robustness in low-resource scenarios.

title: A disentangled multimodal neural topic model
abstract: This study focuses on multimodal topic modeling and attempts to separate public topics (shared across modalities) from private topics (unique to each modality) hidden in text and image data. To address this issue, we propose a novel Disentangled Multimodal Neural Topic Model (DMNTM). Specifically, we design the modality-specific encoder with an independence constraint to capture private topics, and the public encoder with a product-of-experts module to extract cross-modal shared topics. We conduct extensive experiments on six public datasets, including multimodal online reviews from Amazon, posts from Flickr, tweets from Twitter, and webpages from Wikipedia. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, we find that DMNTM significantly improves topic modeling performance in terms of perplexity, coherence, diversity, and topic quality over the best baseline. In two downstream tasks, including recommendation and sentiment classification, DMNTM further improves the performance. These results show that disentangling public and private topics effectively enhances both the quality and utility of multimodal representations.

title: Arbiter: Towards joint and fine-grained index and partition tuning in analytical databases
abstract: Existing index and partition tuning methods optimize these components in isolation, leading to sub-optimal workload latency in analytical databases. We propose Arbiter, a joint optimization system that simultaneously tunes indexing and partitioning strategies through three key innovations: (i) partition-aware fine-grained indexing that creates dedicated index sets for each data partition based on local characteristics, (ii) a unified search framework that captures complex index-partition interdependencies, and (iii) query-driven search space pruning using workload-specific filtering and database-aware guidance models. We evaluate Arbiter on TPC-H, TPC-DS, and Wikimedia (ranging from 8.3GB to 100GB) across multiple workloads on Greenplum and DuckDB. Results demonstrate that Arbiter achieves up to 69.6% performance improvements over six competitive baseline methods while exhibiting the highest tuning efficiency through intelligent search space pruning. Our joint optimization approach consistently outperforms isolated tuning methods across all tested scenarios, validating the effectiveness of capturing index-partition interdependencies in analytical database optimization.

title: Clinical Data-Driven preliminary screening for Alzheimer’s disease via integrated imputation and evolutionary feature selection
abstract: As Alzheimer’s disease (AD) becomes increasingly prevalent, clinical data offers a cost-effective alternative to expensive neuroimaging for preliminary screening. This study develops a preliminary AD screening system utilizing clinical data with missing values, addressing the urgent need for accessible AD screening. In this system, we construct a framework that simultaneously performs missing value imputation and feature selection, overcoming limitations of traditional methods that sequentially perform imputation and feature selection, which neglect the complex interdependencies between imputation quality and feature relevance. Due to complex interactive relationships and the NP-hard nature of feature selection in medical data, we propose an improved genetic algorithm (IGA-G) that enhances standard genetic algorithms through two mechanisms: grey wolf optimizer-based exploration and dataset weight-based local search. The integrated framework couples multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) with evolutionary feature selection, enabling robust analysis of incomplete medical records while maintaining computational efficiency. We analyzed 120 subjects from the OASIS-3 dataset across 222 clinical features. Experiments with four classifiers show that IGA-G outperforms seven algorithms across multiple metrics, achieving up to 78% accuracy with random forest and yielding an improvement of 2.3% over the best baseline. Ablation analysis further confirms the contribution of each component, and the integrated framework achieves a 3% improvement over traditional sequential approaches, providing a practical solution for community-based AD screening.

title: InsQABench: Benchmarking Chinese insurance domain question answering with large language models
abstract: We present InsQABench-the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs’ capabilities in Chinese insurance QA. InsQABench comprises 95K carefully curated QA pairs derived from real-world insurance documents, covering 3 distinct tasks, 44 question types, and 55 specialized insurance topics. Our experiments evaluated and reported the performance of mainstream LLMs under both fine-tuned and zero-shot settings, demonstrating that fine-tuning on InsQABench can significantly improve model performance. We also introduced two frameworks that further enhanced task-specific performance, achieving 4.91% and 5.11% enhancement in accuracy over the next best-performing model.

title: SMIR: Span-based multi-grained information refinement for joint multimodal entity-relation extraction
abstract: Multimodal named entity recognition and multimodal relation extraction are two pivotal subtasks within multimodal knowledge graph construction. Traditional pipeline frameworks tackle the two tasks separately, neglecting the mutual support between them. Recently, word-pair relation tagging frameworks are proposed for joint multimodal entity-relation extraction (JMERE). However, these methods overlook the reciprocal comprehension among words within entities. To this end, we advocate focusing on spans rather than words to tackle this issue in JMERE. However, focusing on spans in JMERE is not trivial, which will encounter the challenges of information crudity and information redundancy. Consequently, in this paper, we propose a novel Span-based Multi-grained Information Refinement (SMIR) framework to address these challenges. Specifically, we first construct span representation matrices as a replacement for word-pair relation tagging. Then, we propose a multi-grained information refinement module to address the challenge of information crudity, encompassing global sample refinement, local vision refinement, and local span refinement, to provide more precise and comprehensive information for spans. Finally, to address the challenge of information redundancy, we design a span-guided cross-modality fusion method to integrate heterogeneous multimodal information related to spans. Experimental results on the JMERE dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our SMIR framework, which achieves 2.09% absolute improvement on the F1 score compared to state-of-the-art JMERE methods.

title: RoleSimLLM: Towards large-scale and comprehensive social propagation simulation via role-based LLM-driven agents
abstract: Large-scale social propagation simulation is essential for understanding complex interactions and predicting societal trends in social networks. Traditional rule-based agent-based models (ABMs) define user personality and interactions through manually crafted rules, leading to limited generalization. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer opportunities for realistic agent decision-making, simulating each user with an independent LLM is computationally prohibitive. Given that users of the same propagation role in social networks often exhibit similar behavioral traits, we propose a Role-driven Multi-agent Social Propagation Simulation Framework based on Large Language Models (RoleSimLLM), where each agent makes propagation decision based on shared role traits and its dynamic social context. Specifically, we utilize an LLM-driven role simulator to generate behavior distributions for each role rather than specific behaviors for each user, thereby reducing simulation overhead while preserving intra-role heterogeneity. A graph-based agent interaction module integrates these distributions with users’ dynamic neighborhoods to capture complex social interactions. This way, RoleSimLLM balances fine-grained user simulation with computational efficiency, enabling large-scale social propagation simulations. Experiments on million-scale Weibo and Twitter datasets demonstrate the model’s superiority. It achieves a 5.50% higher AUC for microscopic user behavior prediction and reduces MLSE for macroscopic propagation scale prediction by 3.66%, using only 1% of the computation time compared to other LLM-based methods. Furthermore, the model successfully replicates key social phenomena, including group polarization and echo chamber, through social simulation.

title: Unified semantic-aware reasoning for fake news video detection
abstract: The rapid spread of fake news videos on social media poses significant chal lenges for content verification and credibility assessment. Existing methods often rely on isolated feature extraction or simple classification, and are un able to capture the complex semantic correlations among multimodal false cues. To address these limitations, we propose a Unified Semantic-Aware Reasoning (USAR) framework. Specifically, we design a Collaborative Aware Correlation Reasoning (CACR) that mines potential fake clues in videos from object-level, frame-level to segment-level through bottom-up cross-grained adaptive aggregation and analyzes their semantic consistency with textual descriptions. Secondly, we propose a unified Veracity Semantic Collabora tion Transformer (VSCT), which uses an adaptive gating mechanism to fuse semantically rich static and audio features into a unified video representa tion to enhance the detection of news video veracity. Experiments on FMNV and FakeTT show USAR improves accuracy by 2.0% and 5.1% over state-of the-art baselines, achieving 80.59% F1-score on FakeTT. Qualitative analysis demonstrates its ability to localize manipulated objects while providing in terpretable evidence for fake content.

title: Information bottleneck based graph structural learning for OOD generalization
abstract: Graph out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization aims to learn generalizable knowledge from source domains that can transfer to unseen target domains. Existing methods typically assume a single-source setting and rely heavily on supervised labels, which renders them inadequate for modeling complex distribution shifts across multi-source domains with heterogeneous feature spaces and limited labeled data. To this end, we propose the information bottleneck based graph structural learning method tailored for multi-source settings. The core insight is to mitigate the discrepancy of feature spaces across domains and extract domain-invariant signals through structural learning. Specifically, we first derive hierarchical raw features from the graph topology to construct a domain-agnostic representation space among diverse sources. Then, we introduce an unsupervised structural contrastive learning module optimized with a refined information bottleneck to capture invariant subgraph patterns shared in multi-source domains while suppressing spurious and domain-specific correlations. Extensive experiments on seven datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model, which achieves an average improvement of 9.9% in node classification and 7.5% in graph classification.

title: MNSPM: Merging-based nonoverlapping gap-constrained sequential pattern mining
abstract: Gap-constrained sequential pattern mining (Gap-SPM) discovers meaningful patterns by imposing gap constraints between consecutive pattern items. Among three widely-used support calculation conditions, the nonoverlapping condition has attracted significant research attention because it satisfies the Apriori property for efficient candidate pruning. However, existing nonoverlapping Gap-SPM methods primarily adopt the pattern join strategy for candidate generation and construct patterns through item-by-item extension. This approach results in extensive repetitive pattern construction during the mining process, leading to computational inefficiency. To address this challenge, this paper proposes MNSPM, a Merging-based Nonoverlapping Gap-Constrained Sequential Pattern Mining algorithm that ensures both pattern completeness and high efficiency. Utilizing 2-patterns as building blocks, we design a novel pattern construction mechanism that generates longer patterns by iteratively merging 2-subpatterns. We then propose HB-TableSet, an indexed structure that compactly stores pattern occurrences and enables rapid support calculation. Additionally, a common-position-based pruning strategy (CPS) is developed to identify infrequent candidates early, particularly for long-sequence datasets. Extensive experiments on eight real-world datasets demonstrate that MNSPM significantly outperforms NOSEP in mining efficiency, achieving speedups predominantly ranging from 2.3 ×  to 6.4 × .

title: API-DONet: A knowledge-guided deep neural operator network for flood forecasting
abstract: Deep operator networks (DeepONets), capable of learning mappings between input and output function spaces via the operator approximation principle, have become a widely used method in Earth sciences applications. However, when applied to flood time series forecasting, DeepONets struggle to model the complex dynamic evolution of spatiotemporal features and lack explicit incorporation of physical principles, limiting physical consistency and predictive accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose an adaptive physics-informed DeepONet (API-DONet), a knowledge-guided neural operator network for accurate and adaptive flood forecasting. Specifically, we introduce a newly designed U-CBAM module as the branch net to encode the spatiotemporal relationships between different channels. Additionally, a decoder guided by the enhanced Fourier neural operator is used to extract global features, facilitating rapid and effective flood prediction under nonlinear dynamic conditions. Importantly, we design the loss function of the proposed model based on flood physics theory, ensuring that the predicted results are more consistent with the principles of flood physics. Moreover, we extend an adaptive gradient descent-based adversarial training strategy that dynamically balances the trade-off between prediction accuracy and physical consistency. Experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that API-DONet outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy and consistency. Compared to benchmark models, RMSE and MAPE were reduced by 45.071% and 5.523%, respectively, while NSE and KGE increased by 5.182% and 22.058%, respectively. Code is available at https://github.com/KingslyZ/APIDNO.

title: Human-in-the-loop learning to align cross-domain geographic knowledge graphs
abstract: Aligning geographic knowledge graphs is crucial for integrating multi-source geographic data and building high-quality knowledge graphs. Current research faces challenges such as limited datasets, reliance on labeled data, and poor model interpretability. To address these issues, we proposed a human-in-the-loop (HITL), learning-enhanced, cross-domain geographic knowledge graph alignment framework. First, it employs a graph attention mechanism to aggregate multi-hop neighborhood information and utilizes clustering to generate candidate entity pairs, thereby enhancing the quality of alignment sample generation through human–machine collaboration. Second, by integrating active learning techniques, it designs an uncertainty measurement approach based on ranking and distance information, enabling the model to achieve efficient and accurate knowledge graph alignment even with a limited amount of manually labeled data. Experiments conducted on our self-constructed geographic dataset, GeoEA2024, demonstrate that the proposed sample generation method can construct a high-quality alignment dataset while reducing annotation costs by approximately 98 %. Compared with mainstream alignment models, our approach effectively corrects misaligned samples produced by other models and achieves superior performance across multiple evaluation metrics, with the Hits@1 score improving by >4 %. Furthermore, the framework requires only a small amount of manual labeling to achieve performance comparable to fully supervised models after several iterations, significantly reducing human annotation costs and validating the efficiency and scalability of the proposed method.

title: Robust drug recommendation based on patient status awareness and unbiased prediction
abstract: The AI-based drug recommendation system can recommend a suitable series of drugs for patients, which is a significant application in current healthcare field. However, current drug recommendation methods overlook personalized differences among patients, leading to the spread of personalized information among the generic patient populations, thereby resulting in information bias. Additionally, patients’ historical visits are not always strongly correlated, indicating that the patient may not always suffer from same or similar diseases in different visits. Therefore, we propose Robust Drug Recommendation Based on Patient Status Awareness and Unbiased Prediction (PAUP). First, we introduce a concept of the ”Standardized Doctor” module, which constrains the input and output of the model to capture patient-agnostic generic treatment strategies, thereby avoiding information bias caused by personalized patient differences. Then, we design a personalized patient information mining module that explicitly captures patient-specific information by mapping biases between generic and real drug representations. Through the two aforementioned modules, we formulates personalized treatment strategies for patients. Finally, we employ attention mechanisms to attenuate the influence of weakly correlated historical visits on current visit, which is utilized as auxiliary information to guide the final recommendation results. Additionally, we model both 2D and 3D molecular structures of drugs to preprocess drug representation. Experimental results on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets demonstrate that PAUP outperforms the state-of-the-art in drug recommendation. In addition, compared to the suboptimal baseline, PAUP saves 59% of training time and 38% of inference time, with a faster convergence rate. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/PAUP-master.

title: A novel multi-criteria evaluation method for rumor-refutation effectiveness of rumor-refutation accounts on social media platforms integrating social network analysis
abstract: Rumor-refutation accounts on social media platforms serve as a critical means to address the issue of online rumors. But previous studies have neglected to evaluate the rumor-refutation effectiveness (RRE) of rumor-refutation accounts themselves. This paper proposes a novel multi-criteria evaluation method to evaluate rumor-refutation accounts’ RRE, namely the Optimal Clustering (OC)-TOPSIS-Sort-C method. The innovation of this method lies in its construction of RRE evaluation indicator system based on Social Network Analysis (SNA) principles and information credibility, trust propagation, and diffusion theory, and comprehensive determination of indicator weights by combining subjective and objective weights via game theory and Extended Fourier Amplitude Sensitivity Test (EFAST) method. Then, the TOPSIS-Sort-C method is optimized by determining the characteristic profiles between classifications using the OC algorithm of machine learning to solve subjective bias issue in the classification results, enhancing the automation and objectivity of the evaluation process. And the method is applied to evaluate 17,427 rumor-refutation articles and 141,259 comments posted by 42 rumor-refutation accounts on the Weibo platform in 2024. The results show that only 9.52% of the accounts exhibit fair RRE, while as high as 16.67% and 73.81% respectively demonstrate good and satisfactory, with the results aligning with reality. This method provides a new scientific tool for rumor-refutation accounts’ RRE evaluation and management, which has important theoretical and practical significance for the formulation of social media rumor-refutation measures. Overall, this study enriches the relevant literature on rumor-refutation accounts’ RRE evaluation and provides practical insights for other social media platforms.

title: A trusted industrial data space for automotive supply chain (TIDS-ASC): enabling secure and traceable data sharing
abstract: As a representative scenario of multi-stakeholder collaborative manufacturing, the automotive supply chain (ASC) requires frequent cross-organizational data sharing while ensuring secure access control and accountable usage. However, existing Industrial Data Space (IDS) solutions primarily focus on architectural interoperability and governance, lacking executable mechanisms that jointly enforce fine-grained usage control and post-incident responsibility attribution. To bridge this gap, this study proposes a Trusted Industrial Data Space Architecture for the Automotive Supply Chain (TIDS-ASC), and designs a traceable ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption scheme (TRA-CP-ABE) as its cryptographic enforcement mechanism. The proposed approach is validated through a real-world case study at a leading ASC enterprise, using 1000 access and tracking records generated by 60 users across multiple roles. Experimental results show that TRA-CP-ABE achieves 100% traceability under fingerprint perturbations of 3%, reduces key storage overhead by up to 40%, and maintains efficient encryption and decryption with attribute sets of up to 80. Results demonstrate that TIDS-ASC provides a practical and scalable solution for secure and traceable data sharing in ASC environments.

title: Multimodal fusion with LLM content via hierarchical progressive transformer for explainable fake news detection
abstract: Detecting fake news on social media has become a significant challenge due to the rapid dissemination of misleading information. Current works often focus on combining limited modalities, lacking deep and progressive integration of diverse features. Apart from textual and image features, there remains a challenge in incorporating other features while also ensuring the explainability of the detection results. To address these problems, we propose a novel Explainable Fake News Detection method that integrates Multimodal Fusion with Large Language Model-generated content (LLM-MFEFND). This model utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate background knowledge and comments to integrate the LLM’s interpretation of news. To extract deep and cross-modal knowledge, we propose Hierarchical Progressive Transformer (HPT) to integrate images, texts, aligned multimodal features, background information, and user comments deeply and progressively. Furthermore, we design Multimodal Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (MLIME) method to provide explanations for the detection results. Through extensive experiments on datasets such as WeiBo21 (6,010 news items) and FineFake (15,140 news items), we demonstrate that the LLM-MFEFND model using DeepSeek outperforms existing methods. Specifically, our method achieves an accuracy of 94.5% on WeiBo21 and 81.1% on FineFake, representing improvements of at least 1.7% and 2.2% respectively over existing approaches. By combining LLM-driven context enrichment with robust multimodal fusion and explainability, our framework advances the fight against misinformation. The code is available at https://github.com/li1608335419/LLM-MFEFND.

title: AI-driven skill keyword suggestion for multi-round interviews: A graph-based topic approach
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruitment has rapidly advanced in areas such as resume evaluation, person-job matching, and recommendation. However, AI’s role in assisting interview questioning for skill assessment remains limited. This study proposes the Topic-Oriented Suggestion Model (TOSM), a deep learning framework designed to suggest skill assessment keywords tailored to multi-round interviews. The framework comprises two modules: a Graph-based Topic Learning Module, which captures latent relationships between skills and their contextual dependencies through graph representation learning, and a Topic-specific Keyword Suggestion Module, which dynamically adapts attention to the thematic topic focus of each interview round. Using a real-world dataset of multi-round interview cases from a leading technology company, TOSM achieves superior performance compared with baseline methods in keyword suggestion tasks. Visualization analyses further demonstrate that the model components effectively bridge vocabulary mismatches across different recruitment texts and adjusts its focus according to each interview round. This study contributes by proposing a novel framework that integrates graph-based topic model with multi-label learning. It extends AI-assisted recruitment research to the domain of interviewer questioning. It also provides practical implications for developing intelligent interview systems that support interviewer-side question design and improve the structure and efficiency of skill assessment in multi-round interviews.

title: Medical multi-recall embedding: Adaptive retrieval for diverse evidence in medical RAG systems
abstract: Large language models have demonstrated promising capabilities in medical question answering but frequently generate unreliable or hallucinated content. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this issue by incorporating external knowledge, yet its effectiveness critically depends on retrieval quality. Existing medical retrievers are typically trained under a restrictive one-to-one paradigm, where each query is paired with a single document, failing to reflect the complexity of real-world clinical scenarios that often require synthesizing information from multiple complementary sources. To address this limitation, we introduce a specialized multi-document medical retrieval dataset comprising 6273 queries paired with approximately 20,810 annotated passages spanning five clinical domains: general practice, cardiology, dermatology, breast tumor, and ophthalmology. Each query is associated with multiple clinically relevant documents that provide diverse yet complementary perspectives. Leveraging this dataset, we propose the Medical Multi-Recall Embedding (MMRE) model, which employs a one-to-many retrieval strategy enhanced by a novel Adaptive Multi-Recall Loss (AMR Loss). AMR Loss introduces three components–Adaptive Positive Margin, Difficulty-Aware Weighting, and Loss Normalization–and ablation studies on each component demonstrate that all three contribute effectively and work synergistically. Extensive retrieval experiments demonstrate that MMRE substantially outperforms competitive baselines across all evaluation metrics and domains. On average across five domains, MMRE achieves more than 10 percentage point gains in Recall@10 and significant improvements in Hit Rate, MRR@10, and NDCG@10. Furthermore, when integrated into a RAG pipeline with a frozen language model, MMRE considerably improves downstream clinical question answering accuracy by at least 4 percentage points across all specialties, underscoring its effectiveness in enhancing the factual reliability and clinical relevance of LLM-generated medical answers. The constructed dataset and source code are publicly available https://github.com/WVKerl/Medical-one-to-many-data.

title: Ubuntu-IntAct : A dialogue-act annotated multi-party conversation dataset and graph-based intention modeling
abstract: Multi-party dialogues involve multiple speakers, dynamic roles, and complex discourse structures, which pose significant challenges for dialogue modeling. Graph-based methods are a natural choice to capture such interactions, but current approaches often ignore speaker intentions and simply connect utterances as nodes, leading to oversimplified graph construction and low interpretability. To bridge this gap, we construct Ubuntu-IntAct, a large-scale dataset of 25,000 multi-party conversations, in which every utterance is annotated with one of eight dialogue acts (e.g., Query, Response, Suggestion). Building on this resource, we propose GraphInt, a graph-based model that explicitly incorporates dialogue acts as edge types to encode speaker intentions. Experiments show that GraphInt achieves substantial improvements over BART, including +17.7% BLEU-1 and +27.1% METEOR, demonstrating the effectiveness of intention-aware graph modeling for multi-party response generation. The dataset is released in https://github.com/ahxchzt/Ubuntu-IntAct.

title: HeterMV: Multi-view reasoning over source-aware heterogeneous evidence graph for multi-source fact verification
abstract: Multi-source fact verification aims to assess claim veracity using heterogeneous textual evidence. Existing methods lack explicit relation modeling for multi-source evidence. This makes verification redundant and noisy. To address this problem, we propose HeterMV, a Heterogeneous Multi-View evidence reasoning framework for fact verification. The framework unifies multi-source evidence into a Source-Aware Heterogeneous Evidence Graph. In this graph, core evidence, context, and reference documents are modeled as distinct node types. We then use directed multi-relational propagation to hierarchically aggregate auxiliary signals into the core evidence representation. Furthermore, building on this graph formulation, we construct four views to capture distinct evidence perspectives, including the multi-source fusion view, the core-corroboration view, the context-infusion view, and the knowledge-citation view. To tightly couple view-specific reasoning with claim verification, we introduce View-Conditioned Prompt Tuning to enable perspective-aware claim–evidence alignment. We further propose Cross-View Consistency Contrastive Learning. It uses the core-corroboration view as the anchor to align supportive auxiliary signals and suppress noise. Experiments on the Check-COVID (1,504 claims) and FEVEROUS-S (29,890 claims) datasets demonstrate that HeterMV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. On Check-COVID, it improves Micro-F1 by +3.06% in the gold setting and +3.27% under BM25 retrieval. On FEVEROUS-S, the gains are +1.72% and +1.41% in the corresponding settings.

title: Progressive feature refinement network for blind gaussian image denoising
abstract: Robustly restoring visual information from images corrupted by blind Gaussian noise with unknown statistics remains a critical challenge in information processing. To address the limitations of static receptive fields in existing networks, we propose the Progressive Feature Refinement Network (PFRNet). Specifically, PFRNet incorporates the Parallel Expanded Receptive Field (PERF) module, which aggregates multi-scale contextual information via parallel dilated convolutions to enhance global structure perception. Complementing this, the Tri-Kernel Split-and-Fuse (TriSF) module leverages depthwise separable convolutions with heterogeneous kernel sizes and a unique split-and-fuse mechanism for adaptive and efficient feature extraction. Extensive experiments on five synthetic datasets and two real-world benchmarks demonstrate that PFRNet achieves superior performance while maintaining computational efficiency. For instance, with a compact model size of 7.86M parameters, PFRNet achieves PSNR of 26.55 dB on the BSD68 dataset and 29.96 dB on the McMaster dataset at the severe noise level of σ=50.

title: From answering to discussing: Advancing human-AI cognitive collaboration in dialogue agents
abstract: Current proactive dialogue agents primarily focus on gathering user information within predefined task schemas, but often lack deep collaboration mechanisms. While expected results have been achieved in well-defined scenarios, their shallow interaction patterns coupled with hasty task execution tend to prove inadequate when confronted with exploratory and continuously evolving personalized demands, confined to generic and non-targeted responses. To tackle this challenge, we define, for the first time, a novel Cognitive Collaboration Dialogue (CCD) task and propose its dedicated dialogue agent framework, CoCo-Agent. In such tasks, the AI agent collaborates with humans on exploratory, highly specialized, and personalized problems (e.g., personal career development), leveraging their respective cognitive capabilities to work together. Through trajectory planning, interaction coordination, timely monitoring and regulation, they gradually establish a shared understanding of the problem, thereby collaboratively developing personalized solutions. Building on this, we contribute CoCoDial, the first automatically generated multi-turn CCD dataset. It comprises 1460 complex dialogues across eight personalized domains with 120 distinct user profiles, featuring exceptional lexical diversity, fine-grained procedural annotations, and fully customized solutions. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CoCo-Agent achieves state-of-the-art performance in collaboration quality and personalized problem-solving, surpassing existing baselines by an average of 58.4% and 3.8%, respectively. These results further validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, providing valuable insights for advancing human-AI collaboration in complex personalized tasks.The code and dataset can be accessed at: https://github.com/arenceLi/CoCoDial.

title: Understanding peer effects in intelligent manufacturing transformation: The roles of competitive and informational motives
abstract: Peer effects are well documented among consumers facing uncertainty, yet they remain insufficiently understood at the inter-firm level. Intelligent transformation in manufacturing is more uncertain and complex than traditional digital transformation, leading firms to rely more on peer behaviors in strategic decisions. Motivated by this gap, our study examines whether, how, and under what conditions peer effects shape intelligent transformation among manufacturing firms. Using natural language processing on annual reports from 2893 A-share listed manufacturing firms (2012–2022), we construct a semantic index of intelligent transformation and find significant peer effects: a one-unit increase in peers’ intelligent transformation levels leads to a 12.42 % increase in a focal firm’s own level. Drawing on a dual-motivation framework of competitive and informational motives, this study finds that competitive pressure and informational learning jointly mediate peers’ transformation signals and reinforce diffusion. The strength of these effects is shaped by structural conditions: higher market entry barriers and greater network density weaken peer effects, while higher network centrality amplify them. This study provides an organizational perspective on peer effects and a novel framework for understanding strategic behavior in intelligent manufacturing transformation ecosystems.

title: Waved zero streaming: A time series compression framework with adaptive segmentation optimization
abstract: The proliferation of time-series data from Internet of Things devices has made efficient compression mechanisms critical for large-scale data management. However, existing state-of-the-art algorithms often flounder when facing dynamic data fluctuations due to their reliance on rigid encoding strategies, while general-purpose compressors incur prohibitive latency. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces Wave Zero Streaming (WZS), a novel lossless compression framework specifically architected for non-stationary data streams. WZS synergizes three pivotal innovations: adaptive segmentation to isolate local fluctuation intensity, a heuristic genetic algorithm-based optimizer to fine-tune compression parameters dynamically, and a stream processing module enabling real-time adaptive algorithm selection. Extensive empirical evaluations across 43 diverse datasets reveal that WZS outperforms leading algorithms–including Camel, Chimp, and ACTF–achieving an average compression ratio improvement of 36.41% (peak: 53.08%), with a notable 13.28% enhancement specifically over the state-of-the-art Camel algorithm. Moreover, WZS surpasses general compression methods by 15.07% in compression ratio while reducing computational latency by two orders of magnitude, and exhibits a 16.45% speed advantage over comparable floating-point streaming baselines. These findings validate WZS as a scalable, high-performance solution that effectively balances efficiency and speed for resource-constrained IoT and edge computing environments.

title: S2CR: A self-supervised self-consistency reasoning framework coupled to retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Existing approaches to the self-consistency exploration in Large Language Models (LLMs) primarily rely on post-hoc selection, overlooking the inherent logical structures essential for reasoning. To address this gap, we pioneer a new perspective by introducing S2CR, a self-supervised reasoning framework that presents the LLM consistency from internal modeling while coupling retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for knowledge integration and process supervision. This framework operates in four stages: Information Retrieval patches the parametric knowledge of LLMs and provides factual grounding for evaluation; Response Generation generates multiple candidate responses for input to explore diverse reasoning paths; Consistency Evaluation quantifies logical consistency by aligning extracted triples from both the generated responses and retrieval information; and Duality Synergy Optimization (DSOP) further bolsters the consistency performance through two complementary modules, Introspection-Driven Self-correction Guidance (IDSG) and Fine-Grained Consensus Alignment (FGCA). Experiments conducted on three public datasets POPQA, Biography, and ALCE-ASQA demonstrate that S2CR achieves objective quantification of internal self-consistency and significantly improves performance ranging from 3.19% to 23.49% over Baseline⋄ across diverse foundational LLMs, e.g., GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, and open-source models LLaMA3-8B and LLaMA3-70B.

title: How to teach and forget: Towards cross-modal semantic consistency for entity alignment
abstract: Multimodal Entity Alignment (MEA) aims to match identical entities across Multimodal Knowledge Graphs (MMKGs) by integrating complementary information from different modalities, such as visual and structure. In practice, MEA is complicated by two issues. Within a single MMKG, different modalities describing the same entity may not align well semantically. Across different MMKGs, the same entity may be associated with inconsistent or incomplete modality information, even within the same modality type. To address these challenges, we propose TeFo, a novel framework designed to enhance cross-modal semantic consistency by Teaching and Forgetting. Specifically, we introduce the Adaptive Modality Distillation module to teach. It aggregates semantic signals from multiple modalities to construct a modality-aware teacher representation. This teacher helps align each single-modality student toward a unified semantic space, which in turn alleviates inter-graph heterogeneity. Furthermore, we design the Gated Adversarial Alignment module to forget. It combines a gated feature selector and a modality discriminator trained with gradient reversal to reduce modality-specific variation. This encourages TeFo to rely less on modality-specific cues, and implicitly improves its robustness to modality asymmetry. Extensive experiments on nine public datasets show that TeFo significantly surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods, yielding absolute gains of 1.9%-2.3% in Hits@1 and 1.4%-2.4% in MRR. Our code is available at https://github.com/wonderCS1213/TeFo.

title: Dynamic alignment of visual and language semantics for referring video object segmentation
abstract: Referring Video Object Segmentation (RVOS) aims to segment objects in videos based on language expressions. In this task, existing methods often face challenges due to semantic misalignment between language and visual modalities. To address this, this paper categorizes semantic misalignment into word-level, sentence-level, and cognitive-level issues. For these issues, we propose the Dynamic Alignment of Visual and Language Semantics (DAVLS) framework. In DAVLS, to address word-level semantic misalignment, we design the Word-level Semantic Dynamic Alignment (WSDA) to maximize the alignment of word-level semantics with appropriate visual features by embedding them into frame-level visual features and enabling cross-modal fusion visually. Based on accurate sentence-level object semantics generated by the textual adapter (TA), we propose the Sentence-level Semantic Dynamic Alignment (SSDA) to address sentence-level misalignment by aligning these semantics with the visual object state of the video clip. Due to the intrinsic linkage between WSDA and SSDA, they are integrated into a unified module, named SDA. Moreover, to mitigate the cognitive-level misalignment between humans and the segmentation model in understanding the semantics of referring objects, we introduce Semantic Augmentation (SA) to enhance the model’s comprehension of object semantics by expanding linguistic expressions. Simulation results on Ref-YouTube-VOS (3,978 videos), Ref-DAVIS17 (90 videos), A2D-Sentences (3,782 videos), and JHMDB-Sentences (928 videos) demonstrate the competitive performance of DAVLS, achieving a 0.9% improvement in J&F on Ref-YouTube-VOS and a 1.0% increase in Overall IoU on A2D-Sentences. Moreover, a statistically significant result (p=.03125), validated by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, confirms the reliability of the performance gains.

title: Toward better pragmatic tagging of peer review: Enhancing benchmark datasets via human-in-the-loop multi-agent collaboration
abstract: Pragmatic tagging datasets for peer review, i.e., sentence-level functional annotations, are essential for assessing review quality and developing intelligent review systems. However, existing benchmark datasets often suffer from annotation inconsistencies and limited coverage. To address these issues, we propose a Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework (HMCF) for verifying, correcting, and expanding pragmatic annotation datasets. HMCF first leverages a large language model (LLM), prompted by annotation guidelines, serving as a large agent that validates human annotations and suggests corrections. Annotations where the human and large agent agree constitute the gold data, which is then used to fine-tune a smaller pretrained language model (PLM) as a small agent. The small agent helps resolve disagreements between human and large agent annotations, while unresolved cases are adjudicated by additional experts. Experiments show that HMCF reduces human effort, improves annotation consistency, and reveals the categories most susceptible to annotation errors. Moreover, the small agent enables large-scale annotation of unlabeled peer reviews, yielding richer, high-quality resources. Collectively, HMCF demonstrates both theoretical significance and practical value in advancing pragmatic tagging of peer review. The corrected and expanded dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/andy8/HMCF. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/ECNU-Text-Computing/HMCF.

title: MSSFN: Multi-stimulus stereo spatiotemporal fusion network with pattern disentanglement for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis
abstract: Eye movements have been established as biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Current methods use diverse cognitive stimuli to elicit diagnostic responses, but face two challenges: the lack of 3D spatiotemporal modeling for comprehensive fusion and the entanglement of cognitive patterns within and across stimuli. To overcome these challenges, we propose the multi-stimulus stereo spatiotemporal fusion network (MSSFN) for AD diagnosis. The MSSFN contains two core modules: (1) stereo spatiotemporal embedding fuses binocular spatial fixation distributions, temporal scanpath dynamics, and stereo priors to establish unified 3D spatiotemporal eye movement modeling; (2) local-sensitive contrastive disentanglement implicitly extracts and decouples intrinsic cognitive patterns via a local-sensitive attention and a cognitive contrastive constraint to separate diagnostic cognitive patterns across stimulus paradigms. In addition, demographic-guided cognitive aggregation incorporates participant information as auxiliary covariates in the final decision. On a demographically matched, clinic-recruited cohort of 100 clinically diagnosed AD patients and 100 healthy controls (age: 72.12  ±  6.18 years), participants completed three stimulus paradigms: saccade, visual search, and visual attention. Under subject-wise 5-fold cross-validation, MSSFN demonstrates superior performance, achieving 0.87 accuracy, 0.87 AUC, 0.88 sensitivity, and 0.86 specificity, surpassing the strongest baseline MCGRL (0.81 accuracy) by 7.4%. Ablation studies further verify the contributions of the proposed modules. These results suggest that MSSFN enables efficient eye movement based AD screening as a complement to existing AD biomarkers, supporting future large-scale deployment.

title: Unsupervised feature selection via graph-based proximity and structured autoencoder-like NMF
abstract: Most unsupervised feature selection (UFS) methods select discriminative features by using graph learning or matrix factorization techniques to generate pseudo-labels. However, existing methods suffer from two major limitations. First, graph learning-based approaches usually capture only first-order similarities and therefore fail to model higher-order relationships among data samples. Second, matrix factorization-based methods mainly focus on decoding, that is, reconstructing the data from latent factors, but they do not provide explicit encoding mechanisms for learning meaningful representations directly from the original features. To address these challenges, we propose UFS-GAN, a novel UFS method based on Graph-based proximity and structured Autoencoder-like Nonnegative matrix factorization. UFS-GAN leverages non-negative spectral clustering for interpretable cluster discovery and adopts an encoder–decoder design: the encoder projects features into embeddings, and the decoder reconstructs features from them. This joint process integrates representation learning and interpretability within a unified model. UFS-GAN further incorporates a structured proximity matrix to adaptively integrate both first- and higher-order graph proximities, thereby capturing the intrinsic data structure more effectively. Simultaneously, it employs a complementary NMF-based encoder-decoder model that combines the encoding capacity of autoencoders with the interpretability and structured latent space of NMF, yielding more meaningful and interpretable feature representations. Finally, UFS-GAN unifies these two nonnegative embedding- and representation-based encoder-decoder models within a structured framework for feature selection. Experiments on ten benchmark datasets show that UFS-GAN reliably identifies discriminative features without class labels, outperforming several state-of-the-art UFS methods. Overall, UFS-GAN delivers consistent improvements, achieving on average nearly 6% higher accuracy than the strongest competing methods, with gains of up to about 9% on some datasets.

title: Legacy Learning Strategy Based on Few-Shot Font Generation Models for Automatic Text Design
abstract: Text design plays a vital role in enhancing user experience and maintaining visual coherence across digital platforms. However, for languages containing thousands of glyphs, creating new fonts remains costly and labor-intensive. Few-shot font generation (FFG) has emerged as a promising approach that synthesizes unseen glyphs from a small number of reference samples. Nevertheless, over 5–10% of glyphs must still be manually produced, limiting scalability. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a plug-and-play legacy learning strategy that enhances both stylistic diversity and structural stability. The model-agnostic method performs iterative cross-font fine-tuning, progressively aligning the pretrained models' style representation toward a legacy-centric embedding space while introducing a content preservation loss to constrain geometric deformation and maintain glyph integrity. The proposed strategy was applied to five state-of-the-art FFG models and evaluated on large-scale Korean, Chinese and Thai font sets. Experimental results based on Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) similarity show that the generated glyphs gradually diverged from the original font distribution while converging toward the legacy font distribution, achieving stylistic variety with structural coherence. In addition, quantitative assessments of structural preservation and readability (Dice similarity, Chamfer distance, and OCR) confirm geometric stability without structural collapse. Cross-language and multilingual generalization was further verified, and a user study with 70 participants (experts and nonexperts) achieved average usability scores above 4.5/5. These results highlight legacy learning as an efficient and scalable strategy for automated, high-quality font generation in multilingual digital content environments.

title: Dualmark: A novel dual watermarking approach for large language models
abstract: Watermarking, which embeds imperceptible yet machine-detectable patterns into generated text, has emerged as a leading solution for detecting machine-generated content. While green-red watermarking methods embed detectable signals by biasing a “green” token subset, they remain vulnerable to paraphrasing attacks and context shifts: green tokens can be replaced, and edits to preceding tokens can disrupt the green-red partition. To address these limitations, we introduce DualMark, a novel ensemble-based dual-watermarking framework that employs an ensemble-inspired approach to embed two independent green-red watermarks using separate context windows and partitioning strategies. During generation, DualMark applies a tiered bias strategy, strongest to tokens in the intersection of both green lists while also biasing tokens unique to each list. Detection succeeds if either watermark yields a statistically significant signal. DualMark integrates seamlessly with existing watermarking schemes and incurs minimal overhead. Extensive experiments across various adversarial scenarios demonstrate that DualMark maintains text quality while substantially outperforming single-watermark baselines: it improves detection AUROC by over 11% under severe word-deletion attacks and doubles the true positive rate (TP@1%) against adaptive baselines under heavy paraphrasing, all while incurring only a 5% increase in generation latency.

title: Evolution of cooperation in public goods games on temporal higher‑order networks driven by utility and degree vectors
abstract: While higher-order networks offer a powerful framework to characterize population structure, a catalyst for cooperation, the existing Higher-Order Activity-Driven (HOAD) model, despite accounting for the temporal nature of interactions, overlooks individual adaptability and learning behaviors. To address this limitation, this paper integrates historical payoffs and interaction frequency into the generative mechanism of temporal higher-order networks and investigates the evolutionary dynamics of cooperation in Public Goods Games (PGG). Specifically, three novel network construction models and their algorithms are presented. These models, represented as temporal hypergraphs, are the Higher-Order Utility-Driven (HOUD) model driven by historical game utility vectors, the Higher-Order Degree-Driven (HODD) model driven by historical degree vectors, and the Higher-Order Utility-Degree-Driven (HO(U–D)D) model, which integrates both HOUD and HODD with a coordination factor. Then, Monte Carlo (MC) simulations explore the topological properties of the generated networks and the corresponding dynamics of cooperation in the PGG. Results show that, compared with the HOAD model, these three proposed models significantly enhance cooperation, increasing the final cooperation frequency from 0 to 0.12–0.84. They also dramatically lower the critical thresholds for both the enhancement factor and the maximum hyperedge size. Notably, the HODD model performs best, primarily due to its moderate levels of heterogeneity, sparsity, and clustering. Finally, according to the microscopic Markov chain approach (MMCA), the dynamical equations for the expected cooperation frequency are derived theoretically. Numerical simulations have verified that the MMCA theory results are in good agreement with the MC results.

title: Explicit geometric relationships under limited spatial reference points guide 3D visual grounding
abstract: Three-Dimensional Visual Grounding (3DVG) aims to locate objects in 3D scenes based on natural language queries. Existing methods typically rely on absolute position encoding of global objects to model spatial relationships for target localization. However, this often results in inadequate spatial understanding and redundant or invalid encoding. To address these limitations, we propose the Relative K-object Fusion Perception 3D Visual Grounding (3DRelKG) framework. By dynamically sampling a limited number of scene reference points, our approach enhances the modeling of spatial relationships for localization targets by learning only the positional and relative spherical geometric features of these reference points with respect to scene objects. Additionally, we introduce a heterogeneous feature fusion module, whose core is an information interaction mechanism based on the similarity matrix of heterogeneous features. This approach naturally avoids the problem of unreliable attention interaction weights that arise from directly calculating the similarity between heterogeneous features. Experiments on ScanRefer, SR3D, and NR3D demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art models, improving accuracy by 2.3%, 4.3%, and 2.1%, respectively, and increasing inference speed by 43.8%.

title: Empowering open-domain LLMs for legal document correction via legal knowledge integration and decoding constraints
abstract: Legal document correction is essential for ensuring the accuracy and validity of legal texts. While open-domain large language models (LLMs) perform well on general text correction, they often make substantive errors in legal contexts due to limited domain knowledge. Fine-tuning can inject legal knowledge but is computationally costly and may introduce over-correction and mechanical errors. To address these challenges, we propose Legal Document Correction (LDC), a lightweight two-stage framework that enables open-domain LLMs to correct legal documents with high accuracy using only 1,000 training samples. LDC first constructs a legal knowledge base from formal legal expressions and statutory articles. In Stage 1, it applies retrieval-augmented fine-tuning to mitigate substantive legal errors. In Stage 2, it detects over-correction and applies constrained decoding to preserve legal elements while fixing mechanical issues. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and data efficiency of LDC. On CAIL, LDC improves F0.5 from 13.89 to 52.12 and reduces false-positive edits from 800 to 49; on Tailing, it improves F0.5 from 40.92 to 74.77 and reduces false-positive edits from 1119 to 167. With only 100 training examples, LDC achieves up to 763% and 269% improvements in F0.5 on CAIL and Tailing, respectively.

title: CTJANet: A class-task joint-aware network for enhanced few-shot image classification
abstract: Few-shot image classification remains challenging due to the difficulty of recognizing novel categories from limited labeled samples. While recent methods employ information-aware strategies, they often depend on a single type of perceptual cue, missing the benefits of integrating multiple perspectives. To overcome this limitation, we propose a CTJANet (Class-Task Joint-Aware Network), which jointly leverages class-aware and task-aware cues for enhanced feature representation. Furthermore, we introduce a Task Adaptive-Aware Module (TAAM) that dynamically extracts task-specific embeddings through task-aware functions, improving adaptability to diverse tasks. Extensive experiments show that CTJANet outperforms the baseline FewTURE by significant margins: +5.29% (1-shot) and +3.74% (5-shot) on mini-ImageNet, +4.98% (1-shot) and +4.12% (5-shot) on tiered-ImageNet, +3.00% (1-shot) and +1.54% (5-shot) on CIFAR-FS, and +3.90% (1-shot) and +3.58% (5-shot) on FC100. Ablation studies also confirm the superiority of CTJANet, maintaining high classification accuracy and strong generalization. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/xiaozhugongqang/ZitWMY.

title: Fuzzy neighborhood rough set-based attribute reduction over temporal information systems with application to clinical efficacy evaluation
abstract: Efficacy evaluation is an important topic in medical management. In unlabeled, multi-time point clinical follow-up data characterized by high dimensionality, temporal imbalance, attribute heterogeneity, and missing values, performing effective attribute reduction remains a key challenge. Assessing individual state changes between adjacent time points is also challenging. To address these issues, this study proposes a framework for unsupervised attribute reduction and dynamic trend discrimination in temporal information systems. First, a temporal information system is constructed to handle data with imbalanced, incomplete, and heterogeneous attributes. Second, based on Gaussian-kernel fuzzy relations and a multi-β neighborhood coverage approximation, a set of unsupervised quality metrics and a joint optimization objective Q is developed. The objective Q serves as a unified criterion driving both attribute reduction and learning. It enables flexible trade-offs among coverage, consistency, stability, and robustness to obtain more discriminative and interpretable attributes. Next, we employ a state-space model to smooth latent health state estimates. Further, we introduce false discovery rate (FDR) control to adaptively determine classification thresholds. We also incorporate an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) evidence-accumulation mechanism to capture gradual trends. This approach robustly achieves three-category trend discrimination (improvement, under observation, deterioration). The validation based on 21,917 time stamped medical records from 50 patients with chronic nephritis at the Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine during 2019–2022 indicates that OURS attains Qmean=0.4403 with quartiles (Q25=0.3770,Q50=0.4254,Q75=0.4995); by metric, accmean=0.3992, bwmean=0.4462 and conmean=0.7229. The proposed method outperforms nine comparative methods, further demonstrating its scientific validity and feasibility. Additionally, sensitivity analyses and ablation experiments confirm its robustness and generalizability. This study proposes an innovative integration of rough sets and machine learning for clinical efficacy evaluation, thereby advancing data-driven decision-making in medical management.

title: Refine and reflect: Explainable stock predictions with large language models
abstract: Accurately predicting stock movements from investor-generated text is challenging due to noisy discourse and the need for interpretable reasoning. We propose a novel explainable prediction framework that integrates sentiment modeling, event extraction, a dual-stage reflection mechanism, and reinforcement learning optimization. Using 194,304 investor comments from East Money forums (covering A-share firms, 2022–2024), the framework constructs sentiment indices and structured events to guide a large language model in generating both forecasts and causal explanations. A reflection module enables the model to identify and correct reasoning errors, and fine-tuning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) balances accuracy with interpretability. Experiments on an independent test set of 70,000 comments show that our method improves prediction accuracy to 54.5% (a 3.7% gain over the base model) and enhances explanation quality by over 20%. These results demonstrate a scalable path toward transparent and trustworthy financial AI.

title: Causal continual unlearning with disentangled anomaly representations for private industrial vision
abstract: Continual Learning and Private Unlearning (CLPU) in industrial anomaly detection (IAD) demands lifelong adaptation to new product-defect pairs while enabling GDPR-compliant erasure of proprietary client data. Existing methods fail to reconcile three critical limitations: (i) disentanglement gap, inability to share universal anomaly primitives while isolating IP-sensitive semantics; (ii) causal leakage, unmodeled transitive privacy violations in multi-stage inspection pipelines; and (iii) memory inefficiency, prohibitive storage costs for high-resolution vision. We redefine unlearning not as parameter deletion, but as structured information control: a theoretically grounded process that selectively removes sensitive knowledge while preserving transferable representations. We introduce Causal Disentangled Industrial Unlearning (CaDIU), which establishes (1) privacy-preserving disentanglement via causally factorized latent spaces, (2) system-level causal indistinguishability through Defect Propagation Graphs with ancestral restoration, and (3) information-theoretic memory bounds enabling exact unlearning with O(polylog(d)) storage. Evaluated on four industrial benchmarks, VisA, MVTec-AD, Real-IAD, and BTAD, CaDIU achieves state-of-the-art performance: Anomaly Primitive Fidelity  ≥  0.96, IP Reconstruction Error  ≤  0.12, Causal Leakage Score  ≤  0.03, and Memory Efficiency Ratio = 0.08. Our framework is the first to enable efficient, private, and certifiable lifelong industrial vision, providing a foundation for GDPR-compliant, edge-deployable AI in multi-client manufacturing environments.

title: Hierarchical dynamic pattern analysis and adaptive fusion of multimodal physiological signals for emotion recognition
abstract: The inherent dynamic characteristics that exist in the temporal and spatial domains of different physiological signals, as well as in cross-modal collaborative relationships among them, are highly related to emotional states. However, these properties are overlooked in the previously proposed multimodal emotion recognition models. To address this limitation, a new fusion model that effectively combines the above emotion-related neuroscience prior knowledge is proposed. First, a temporal progressive pattern extraction strategy is introduced by segmenting signals into multiple phases, extracting differential entropy features from each phase, and adopting the modified depthwise separable convolution to capture the temporal progressive pattern across phases. Second, a spatial asymmetric coupling pattern extraction method based on the multi-layer graph attention network is designed to capture multi-scale spatial asymmetric coupling features. Finally, an adaptive fusion strategy based on the cross-modal Transformer is developed to adaptively fuse emotion-related components in modality-consistent information and those in modality-specific information. Experimental results on DEAP, DREAMER, and PhyMER indicate that our model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an accuracy improvement of 0.99%-14.46% (0.82%-6.77%) and F1 score improvement of 0.48%-16.23% (0.17%-7.41%) under subject-dependent (subject-independent) scenarios, in binary and four-class classification tasks with equivalent or even smaller computational complexity. Moreover, all the key modules in the above-designed methods contribute to the performance enhancement. Our findings indicate that extracting the dynamic patterns existing in the temporal and spatial domains of each physiological signal, and those reflected in the cross-modal collaborative relationships, enhances the emotion representation ability and interpretability of the proposed model.

title: Robust social bot detection via multi-relational and noise-aware representation modeling
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of social platforms, bot-driven manipulation has become increasingly pervasive, underscoring the urgent need for robust social bot detection. Although recent work advances multi-relational and heterophily-aware modeling, many frameworks still fuse heterogeneous relations in a relation-agnostic way, amplifying structural noise and causing over-smoothing under heterophily or adversarial conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose BotMGTD, the first social bot detection framework to integrate target-conditioned multi-relational graph encoding with diffusion-based denoising. Specifically, BotMGTD constructs relation-specific subgraph embeddings and designates one dominant relation as the target to anchor message passing, while adaptively incorporating auxiliary relations via attention-based fusion. A latent diffusion denoiser, conditioned on the target representation, iteratively suppresses structural and feature perturbations in the latent space, improving stability on heterogeneous multi-relation graphs. Compared with the baselines, BotMGTD is consistently the most noise-robust, achieving the best performance under latent-space noise injection, edge perturbation, adversarial node infiltration, and cross-dataset transfer, with markedly smaller accuracy degradation than competing methods. The code is available at: https://github.com/FengLiuii/BotMGTD.

title: Multi-view co-clustering with dynamic feature-level clustering candidates
abstract: Multi-view co-clustering aims to simultaneously cluster instances and features by exploiting complementary information from multiple data perspectives. Existing approaches typically adopt a single, fixed clustering configuration along the feature dimension for each view, which may restrict the quality of learned consensus representations. To address this limitation, we propose a novel information-theoretic framework termed Dispersion in Clustering (DiC), which explicitly incorporates dynamic feature-level clustering candidates into multi-view co-clustering. The DiC framework consists of two core modules: Internal-view Candidates Exploitation (ICE) and Inter-view Consensus Clustering (ICC). In the ICE module, multiple feature-level clustering candidates are generated for each view, and their contributions are adaptively weighted through entropy minimization to reduce redundancy. In the ICC module, these candidates are integrated across views using learnable view weights regulated by entropy maximization, enabling balanced and robust consensus instance-level clustering. By jointly optimizing candidate-level and view-level weights, DiC effectively explores diverse feature-level structures without requiring prior specification of a single clustering configuration. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first multi-view co-clustering approach that involves dynamic clustering along the feature dimension. Experimental results on seven benchmark datasets, including Dermatology, ORL, ALOI, Caltech20, NUS-WIDE, HW Digits, and CIFAR-10, with sample sizes ranging from 366 to 60,000 instances and from 2 to 7 views, show that DiC outperforms state-of-the-art co-clustering algorithms, achieving an average improvement of 3.68% in ACC, 2.53% in NMI, and 3.73% in Purity, thereby highlighting the effectiveness of dynamic feature-level clustering candidates in enhancing multi-view co-clustering performance.

title: ALC-DRKG: an active learning-based framework for dynamic knowledge graph construction for drug repositioning
abstract: Knowledge Graph (KG) technology plays a key role in drug repurposing. Current KGs for drug repurposing are predominantly constructed from limited static databases, commonly exhibiting data sparsity issues. Dynamic KG construction techniques can reduce this issue by extracting triples from biomedical literature. However, its incremental strategy of direct integration may result in redundancy of information, leading to a decrease in downstream task model prediction accuracy. Considering this, this paper defines the dynamic KG construction process as an active selection problem involving information-rich triples and introduces active learning (AL) to address it. It proposes the Active Learning Collection for Drug Repositioning Knowledge Graph (ALC-DRKG) framework. We propose two AL algorithms: entity clustering combined with uncertainty (EC-U) and power law distribution combined with uncertainty (PL-U). EC-U enhances data balance by clustering entities to capture latent relationships between them. PL-U captures global critical association information based on the scale-free properties of biomedical networks. We use two drug repositioning knowledge graph (DRKG) datasets, HetioNet (2250,197 triples) and Multiscale Interactome Network (MSI) (478,728 triples), to validate ALC-DRKG. Experiments show that proposed algorithms significantly outperform traditional algorithms, with an average improvement of 28.4%. Especially on the MSI dataset, ours achieves over 80% of full-dataset performance using 25% of the data, while surpassing full-dataset performance in the Hits@1 metric. Meanwhile, we conduct an interpretable analysis of the proposed algorithms' performance advantages based on network theory. The study provides an efficient way to optimize the construction of dynamic DRKGs. The code and data are available at https://github.com/hiL-hiL/ALC-DRKG.

title: ChainCare: Clinical prediction via bidirectional monitoring event chains and multi-event time series modeling
abstract: Clinical prediction based on electronic health records is a key research direction in healthcare, with disease prediction and medication recommendation as its core tasks. Although prior studies have acknowledged the importance of monitoring-level events, such as lab tests and medication administrations, their independent modeling has led most approaches to overlook the event execution logic between these events and to neglect the identification of clinically salient event groups. In this work, we introduce ChainCare, a novel learning framework that, to our knowledge, is the first to jointly model two types of monitoring-level events under a unified representation and explicitly capture their execution logic through bidirectional event chains.
