Equally importantly, to enable more effective centralized modeling of heterogeneous monitoring events, we propose a hierarchical mechanism that adaptively assigns weights to the unified event set at each time step, allowing the model to identify key event groups and further extract critical visit-level representations from patients’ longitudinal records. These designs jointly enhance the performance of disease prediction and medication recommendation. Extensive experiments on the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our method over state-of-the-art approaches, confirming the effectiveness of modeling event execution logic between monitoring-level events and identifying key event groups. Specifically, ChainCare achieves Jaccard score improvements of 0.8% for disease prediction and 3.3% for medication recommendation on the MIMIC-III dataset, and 0.8% and 7.8% on the MIMIC-IV dataset, respectively. Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/guangyunms/ChainCare.

title: Privacy-preserving heterogeneous graph representation learning for recommendation
abstract: Heterogeneous information networks (HINs), rich in structural and semantic information, have emerged as an effective paradigm for mitigating data sparsity in recommender systems. However, most existing HIN-based recommender systems rely on centralized data storage, which inevitably poses significant privacy risks. The inherently distributed and structurally complex nature of HINs renders existing privacy-preserving solutions inadequate for such recommendation tasks. To this end, we propose PP-HGRL, a privacy-preserving framework for HIN-based recommendation with formal edge-level differential privacy (DP) guarantees. Specifically, our framework employs a heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) to incorporate heterogeneous relational semantics into user-item interaction modeling, thereby effectively mitigating data sparsity. To protect sensitive interactions in the HIN, we propose a dual-stage DP method that eliminates reliance on trusted third parties and provides privacy protection spanning from data sharing to model deployment. Furthermore, PP-HGRL is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated with various HGNN architectures. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that PP-HGRL outperforms existing state-of-the-art privacy-preserving methods, achieving improvements of up to 12.89 % in Recall and 10.12 % in NDCG under a reasonable privacy budget.

title: Fine-grained dynamic graph learning for irregular multivariate time series
abstract: Irregular Multivariate Time Series (IMTS) are prevalent in many real-world applications but pose significant challenges for representation learning because of missing values, unequal sequence lengths, and asynchronous sampling. Recent methods attempt to alleviate these challenges through techniques such as interpolation, continuous-time modeling, attention mechanisms, and graph learning. However, these methods frequently fail to capture the evolving temporal dependencies and dynamic interactions among variables, leading to suboptimal performance in high sparsity and irregularity. To address these challenges, we propose FgDGL, a novel Fine-grained Dynamic Graph Learning framework. FgDGL proposes a multi-lag partial correlation initialization mechanism to initialize graph structures, thereby providing a causally grounded, lag-aware graph prior. This mechanism captures decaying autocorrelation dependencies and cross-variable conditional interactions with irregular observation intervals. Moreover, FgDGL further develops a fine-grained incremental adjacency matrix update scheme guided by a semantic memory, thereby acting as a temporal regularizer for dynamic graph evolution. This scheme aligns the evolving adjacency matrix with temporally consistent structures and reduces spurious correlations caused by missing values, without requiring global updates. Finally, the latent representations at the last observed time step are fused with optional static covariates, enabling robust classification under unequal sequence lengths. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that FgDGL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in IMTS classification, achieving improvements of up to 1.4% AUROC and 2.6% AUPRC improvements over the best baselines.

title: Reasoning-guided structured planning and search in large language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often fail on time-sensitive queries without external search. We present R-Search, a single-LLM framework that produces a structured trace: <think> reasoning, a natural-language directed acyclic graph (NL-DAG) <search>, executed results <result>, and a final <answer>. The model is trained with reinforcement fine-tuning (ReFT) using a composite reward for answer accuracy, DAG validity, and format compliance. We construct a training set of 1000 multi-hop Q&A pairs from recent news and academic abstracts. On FinSearchBench-24, R-Search attains 78.13% with 1535 tokens/answer and 8.58 s latency, outperforming multi-agent and single-LLM baselines and cutting tokens and latency by approximately 70% and 50% versus FinSearch. On SearchExpertBench-25, it reaches 73.0% with comparable efficiency. Across seven QA datasets, it averages 41.87% EM. These results indicate that explicit NL-DAG planning within a single LLM narrows the plan-execution gap and improves both effectiveness and efficiency for search-augmented generation.

title: DRUM: Distributionally robust optimization for LLM-based user model in interactive recommendation
abstract: Interactive Recommender Systems (IRSs) learn the dynamic changes in user interests through multi-step interactions. Considering training costs, most Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based IRSs are developed offline. These systems leverage user log data to train a user model, which provides feedback for training the RL agent. However, existing approaches primarily use neural networks to construct user models, which struggle to achieve high-quality modeling in the face of data sparsity. To address this issue, we utilize Large Language Models (LLMs) with rich world knowledge as the user model in IRSs. Meanwhile, recognizing that LLMs may introduce distribution shifts between generated and real user feedback due to biases in their pretraining corpora, we introduce Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) and propose a method called Distributionally Robust Optimization for LLM-based User Model (DRUM) in Interactive Recommendation. Specifically, we first align LLMs with recommendation tasks through instruction fine-tuning to serve as the user model in IRSs. Then, we construct an exposure simulator using a mixture of multiple recommendation models to generate an exposure distribution that can be used as the nominal distribution for DRO. Finally, we incorporate the obtained exposure distribution and add penalty prompts to the original prompt template to further fine-tune the LLM-based user model, mitigating the impact of biases in the pretraining corpora. Experimental results demonstrate that DRUM improves recommendation performance and enhances model robustness in data-sparse scenarios, with cumulative reward improvements of 24.06%, 38.27%, and 4.33% and interaction length improvements of 1.11%, 1.08%, and 1.54% on three datasets, respectively.

title: A framework for developing a text simplification index: Design, validation, visualization
abstract: In the rapidly developing field of text simplification, there is a significant gap between the paradigms of machine and manual simplification. Social and regulatory pressure creates a need for rapid and widespread improvement in text comprehensibility, while plain language guidelines (e.g., ISO 24495-1:2023) discourage the use of machine tools and readability metrics. In this paper, we attempt to bridge this gap. We propose the Text Simplification Index (TSI), a new framework for evaluating the degree of text simplification. TSI assesses the similarity of a given text to the key linguistic features of naturally simple and widely read texts. We identified these features by comparing a positive benchmark corpus (3917 online media texts) with a negative one (2160 official texts requiring simplification). To verify the performance of TSI, we conducted a study with 24 experienced plain language experts who were asked to evaluate 21 texts. The correlation between the experts’ judgment and the TSI diagnosis was 0.67—higher than the correlations of other readability formulas. We also verified the possibility of modifying TSI variables during the text simplification process. For this purpose, we conducted a quasi-experiment where 306 domain experts, after a brief plain language course, simplified 14 texts. The results showed that all TSI components can be modified by domain experts, although the degree of improvement for a given feature depends on its type, the expert’s skills, and the text topic. Our framework culminates in the design of a practical infographic that precisely shows authors, editors, and researchers the progress in text simplification across each feature.

title: MLAFormer: Multi-scale transformer with local convolutional auto-correlation and pre-training for time series forecasting
abstract: Transformer-based models have achieved strong performance in long-term time series forecasting, yet they often struggle to jointly model short-term local patterns and long-range dependencies under a unified representation, especially when temporal dynamics vary across different resolutions. To address this challenge, we propose MLAFormer, a multi-scale encoder-decoder framework for long-sequence forecasting. MLAFormer learns temporal representations across multiple resolutions through a cross multi-scale architecture, enabling information exchange between fine-grained and coarse-grained temporal features. In addition, we propose a Local Convolutional Auto-correlation mechanism to enhance local contextual modeling while capturing periodic dependencies efficiently. To further improve representation quality, we incorporate self-supervised pre-training within the encoder-decoder framework and investigate different masking strategies for time series reconstruction. Extensive experiments on nine benchmark datasets demonstrate that MLAFormer consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods in long-term forecasting. On average, MLAFormer reduces MAE by 7.4% compared with the recent advanced model, with an additional 3.0% improvement through pre-training.

title: Quantifying within-category spillovers in retail promotions — Causal evidence from double machine learning
abstract: Promotional activities play a key role in retail marketing, yet their influence often extends beyond the promoted items. Quantifying these indirect effects within a product category is essential for effective pricing, shelf allocation, and inventory management, but remains challenging due to the complex interdependence of consumer responses. This study proposes a two-stage methodology for the causal estimation of within-category spillover effects generated by price promotions in retail environments. The first stage develops an advanced data processing framework to uncover many-to-one relationships between promoted and non-promoted products and to construct a feature-rich representation of observational retail data. This enables the second stage to causally estimate spillover effects through a DML approach, complemented by empirical diagnostic checks. The methodology is examined under three alternative DML specifications and evaluated using 42 months of daily data from the Carbonated Soft Drinks category of a large Italian grocery retailer. Results indicate that fully linear models fail to capture the complexity of promotional interactions, whereas flexible nonparametric approaches yield statistically significant effects generating average sales variations ranging from −36.96% to +25.65%. The findings reveal predominantly negative spillovers, reflecting cannibalization and inter-brand competition in line with established marketing research, alongside limited evidence of complementarity under context-dependent conditions, as highlighted through model explainability analysis. Placebo permutation tests provide additional support against spurious findings in the observational setting. Overall, the study combines causal inference with explainable analytics, offering actionable insights for promotion management and category planning.

title: Understanding citation intents by generative intent model based on heterogeneous graph neural network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel synthetic intent-based model for the citation intent classification, called SynIntent. Unlike prior works that treat citation contexts as plain text and rely on deep neural networks (including language models (LMs)) for representation learning, we investigate an unexplored information for this task: latent intent. To exploit these signals, we represent each citation context as a bipartite heterogeneous graph which composed of two node types: sentence nodes and latent intent nodes. Initial node representations are produced by a graph initialization module and subsequently refined through a graph attention network to capture sentence-intent dependencies, yielding a richer and more informative contextual representation. By leveraging latent intent information and sentence–intent relationships, SynIntent provides a novel, deeper and more holistic understanding of the semantic structure underlying citation contexts. The experiments on public datasets demonstrate that SynIntent outperforms the state-of-the-art models in both multiclass and multilabel classification scenarios. Specifically, we achieve a remarkable increase of 4.3% macro-F1 and 4.4% in accuracy on the ACL-ARC dataset. For the multilabel classification, we also observe improvements of 1% for strict metrics and 2% for weak metrics on the MultiCite dataset.

title: Emotion-based song recommendation for mothers with postpartum depression
abstract: Postpartum depression is a mental health disorder that can occur in first-time mothers. Music therapy is one of the treatments to help reduce Postpartum Depression (PPD) symptoms and provide sootheness for postpartum mothers. This study aimed to develop an emotion and genre-based music recommendation system designed to meet the emotional needs of mothers with PPD. A music classification model was developed using cochleogram and chromagram-based audio representations to obtain music emotion and genre features through a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) architecture. An evaluation was conducted to assess the effect of using both audio representations on music classification performance. The results show that the use of cochleogram and chromagram-based audio representations, which aims to integrate music spectral and key modulation information, can provide better accuracy compared to other music classifications that only utilizes spectral information. The feature extraction results in the classification process are used to make music recommendations based on similarity between the music emotion and genre information. The result of this study is to provide music recommendations that match the emotional state and preferences of mothers with PPD, as well as contribute to the literature related to audio processing for music classification and recommendation. The user evaluation testing was conducted to 35 new mothers and the satisfaction score result is 65%. Furthermore, subjects claimed that by listening to the recommended music from the app for 5 minutes make them feel more relaxed than before.

title: Local hyperplane-constrained self-representation for manifold clustering
abstract: To address the challenge of rejecting cross-manifold interference in non-linear data clustering, this paper proposes a novel method termed Local Hyperplane-Constrained Self-Representation for Manifold Clustering. By incorporating a local hyperplane constraint within each sample’s neighbors from other manifolds, the framework explicitly models local geometric separability to ensure that each sample is reconstructed primarily from points on the same manifold while suppressing neighbors from other manifolds. Theoretical analysis establishes error bounds for the model and provides a sufficient condition for manifold preservation, enhancing the method’s interpretability. Extensive evaluation on 12 synthetic and 10 real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms eleven state-of-the-art algorithms. Specifically, the method yields an average accuracy improvement of approximately 8%-15% over representative baseline methods, with gains exceeding 20% on certain datasets. Furthermore, the model achieves 100% clustering accuracy on the PIE dataset and demonstrates high computational efficiency by converging within just five iterations. The source code is available at https://github.com/HNU-MingjieCai/LHCMC.

title: Uncovering the formation dynamics of technology convergence: A multi-dimensional BTERGM approach integrating static and temporal mechanisms
abstract: Technology convergence is a core engine of innovation. However, most empirical studies rely on static proximity indicators. These static models often overlook topology structure, heterogeneous knowledge attributes, external factors, and temporal path dependence. This study develops a mechanism-oriented dynamic network framework using a Bootstrapped Temporal Exponential Random Graph Model (BTERGM). Based on 16 million USPTO invention patents (2011–2020), we construct annual CPC-4 co-occurrence networks and jointly model four mechanism families: (i) structural properties (sparsity, triadic closure, degree and eigenvector centrality), (ii) semantic proximity captured by CPC hierarchy and text embeddings, (iii) macro-level policy and industry context, and (iv) temporal memory capturing tie persistence, stability, loss, and innovation. Results indicate that structural properties and external drivers operate as independent yet complementary forces shaping convergence. The network is globally sparse but locally cohesive, with strong triadic closure and centrality effects, while semantic proximity remains among the most powerful predictors of tie formation. Funding and industry alignment further tilt convergence toward domains where resources and market demand co-align. Incorporating temporal memory reveals pronounced dyadic inertia—once technologies converge, they are far more likely to remain connected—and improves out-of-sample performance (AUC-PR  ≈ 0.94). Robustness check shows that strong, high-weight ties are especially anchored in structural centrality, external support, and persistence. By integrating multi-dimensional mechanisms within a unified generative framework, this study advances patent-based convergence research and provides a scalable tool for mechanism inference, forecasting, and actionable technology roadmapping.

title: Network infrastructure construction and digital innovation resilience: Evidence from Broadband China policy
abstract: We use data from 271 prefecture-level cities in China from 2011 to 2023 and treat the Broadband China policy as a quasi-natural experiment to examine how network infrastructure construction influences digital innovation resilience. The results indicate that network infrastructure construction raises digital innovation resilience. This conclusion remains valid after instrumental variable estimation and a series of robustness tests. This effect is particularly pronounced in cities characterized by high traditional infrastructure construction, low intellectual property protection, and strong government support for science and education. Mechanism analysis suggests that resilience is enhanced mainly through narrowing the digital divide and fostering innovation collaboration, while the mediating role of digital finance is not supported. This study adds to the literature on digital innovation resilience and offers policy insights for promoting network infrastructure construction in a sustainable way.

title: Integrating managerial and investor textual data for financial distress prediction: A framework combining multi-source financial information fusion network with LLM
abstract: While prior financial distress prediction (FDP) studies have increasingly incorporated multi-source data, existing approaches rarely integrate financial indicators with fine-grained narrative signals in a unified framework. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel FDP framework that integrates simultaneously financial ratios, Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), and investor comments from social media. We first propose an LLM-BERT based triplet extraction approach to capture aspect-level semantic and sentiment information from MD&A texts. Second, we utilize FinBERT to extract sentiment features from investor comments. These textual features are then combined with financial ratios and integrated into a Multi-source Financial Information Fusion Network (MFIFN), trained with focal loss to mitigate class imbalance. Based on the dataset of 24,429 firm-year samples from Chinese listed companies between 2014 and 2023 (including both distressed and non-distressed firms), experimental results demonstrate that incorporating social media and MD&A features provides incremental predictive values on top of financial ratios. In particular, the proposed MFIFN model achieves an AUC of 0.9541. Furthermore, the LLM-BERT based triplet extraction method improves feature quality, delivering consistent performance gains across compared with traditional textual feature extraction methods. These findings suggest that integrating financial indicators with fine-grained narrative signals can enhance early warning systems, providing stakeholders with more timely and comprehensive risk assessment tools.

title: Dual-stream multimodal shared prompt model for fake news detection
abstract: Current mainstream fake news detection methods primarily rely on pretrained models for encoding and feature extraction of both images and text, and then design interactive network modules based on the extracted features to achieve multimodal feature interaction. However, these interactions are often shallow and may not explore the complex relationships between image and text information, nor fully harness the potential of the advanced architecture of pretrained models. In response to these challenges, we propose a dual-stream multimodal shared prompt (DMSP) method based on pretrained models, which exploits the complementarity between image and text by introducing a learnable multimodal shared prompt into the image-text encoder. This enables the model to generate dual-stream deep image-text feature interaction vectors, maximizing the deep correlations and complementarity between image and text during the multimodal information interaction process. Furthermore, we design a pseudo-siamese attention network that learns multimodal interaction feature from two perspectives, local features and global features. This network effectively captures important interaction features, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to identify fake news. Finally, a classifier is used to perform binary classification on the dual-perspective deep image-text mixed features. Experimental results show that DMSP outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models with only five training epochs, achieving a 3.7% and 1% improvement in detection accuracy in the public PolitiFact and GossipCop datasets, respectively.

title: Uncertainty-aware memory-enhanced cross-window dependency learning for robust multivariate time series anomaly detection
abstract: Existing time series anomaly detection methods typically rely on fixed-length sliding windows for feature extraction, which constrains their ability to capture long-range dependencies and global temporal dynamics. Moreover, real-world data are often contaminated with anomalies, and the assumption of clean training data may lead to overfitting.While memory-based approaches aim to model normal patterns under such contamination, their fixed-dimensional representations struggle to capture the complexity and variability of normal dynamics and often ignore the intrinsic uncertainty in the normal pattern distribution, ultimately undermining detection accuracy and robustness. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-aware Memory-Enhanced Cross-Window Dependency Learning for robust multivariate time series anomaly detection (UMECD). A global-window dual positional encoding mechanism is proposed, where positional memory vectors store cross-window context and supervised regression of positional labels enables explicit learning of long-term dependencies and local dynamics. By jointly reconstructing features with integrated global and local positional information, the model enhances temporal representation and generalization. Furthermore, a Bayesian memory module probabilistically models normal patterns through Gaussian distributions and reparameterized sampling, effectively suppressing noise and improving adaptability to input variations. The method is evaluated against 23 state-of-the-art multivariate time series anomaly detection approaches on five real-world datasets using three evaluation metrics.It achieves the best overall average performance, with five best and two second-best results. Compared to the top-performing baseline, the average performance across all datasets and metrics improves by over 4.97%. Moreover, it obtains the lowest average rank across all metrics, confirming its superior effectiveness and robustness.

title: Fair client selection for multi-task federated learning in mobile edge networks
abstract: Multi-task federated learning (FL) in mobile edge networks faces significant challenges due to the coexistence of heterogeneous tasks, dynamic client states, and limited computational resources. Most existing client selection methods often assume a single-task scenario with prior knowledge of client conditions, making them unsuitable for real-world multi-task training. Moreover, a critical issue is fairness: if resource-abundant devices are consistently favored, weaker clients may be excluded, leading to biased global models and lower training performance. To bridge this gap, we propose multi-task client selection MTC, a novel online algorithm that reformulates the selection process as a multi-agent multi-armed bandit (MAMAB) problem with proportional fairness constraints. MTC operates in rounds, each comprising four stages-exploration, mapping, exploitation, and rounding-enabling it to learn client performance while ensuring efficient and fair resource allocation. Theoretically, MTC can achieve both sub-linear regret and computational efficiency. Empirically, extensive experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that MTC not only improves accuracy by up to 2% to 26% over state-of-the-art baselines (EffI-FL, EMAFL, Fair-CFL, and FedProx), but also significantly enhances fairness-ensuring that even resource-constrained devices contribute to training. These results highlight the practical value of fair client selection for robust FL in real-world mobile edge networks.

title: Extracting policy attention from Chinese texts: An LLM-enhanced dynamic topic modeling approach for the “Dual Carbon” agenda
abstract: Extracting dynamic policy attention from large-scale Chinese policy texts remains challenging due to limitations in semantic representation and temporal modeling. This study proposes a Chinese-Prompt Dynamic Topic Model (CPDTM) that integrates Chinese pretrained language models with large language model–based prompt engineering to systematically link governmental attention allocation to governance outcomes. Taking 3056 “dual carbon” policy documents issued between October 2020 and June 2024 as an example, CPDTM achieves the best performance in topic quality. Our experiments identify the evolving policy attention in four key domains: ecological and meteorological development, green and low-carbon governance, industrial energy conservation and emission reduction, and technological innovation and development, showing a significant shift toward green and low-carbon governance. Furthermore, an autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) indicates that a 1% increase in long-run policy attention is associated with carbon emissions reductions of 0.5%, 0.3%, 0.2%, and 1.4% across these domains, while short-run effects vary substantially. Additionally, policy attention reduces carbon emissions through three primary channels: environmental governance constraints, green technology innovation, and industrial structure adjustment. This study contributes by (1) advancing dynamic topic modeling through LLM-enhanced prompting for large-scale Chinese policy texts, (2) uncovering the temporal evolution of “dual carbon” policy attention, and (3) providing empirical evidence on how information embedded in policy texts translates into emission outcomes, offering insights for policy optimization and sustainable governance.

title: DCFRec: Sequential recommendation via diffusion denoising and context-aware frequency-domain analysis
abstract: Sequential recommendation aims to accurately capture users’ dynamic preferences. However, existing models still face critical challenges in decoupling users’ true preferences from interaction noise and effectively modeling the complex multi-scale periodic patterns in user behavior. To address these challenges, we propose Diffusion Denoising and Context-aware Frequency-domain analysis for Sequential Recommendation (DCFRec). This model adopts a “denoising-analysis” architecture, integrating diffusion denoising with time-domain and frequency-domain analysis through end-to-end joint optimization. Specifically, we devise a reverse denoising network that combines bidirectional Mamba to capture long-range ordered dependencies and a bidirectional self-attention mechanism to capture global contextual correlations. This network aims to generate a more robust representation of user behavior sequences through signal reconstruction. The denoised sequence representation is then fed into a parallel dual-analysis structure: a Fourier analysis module that adaptively decouples and aggregates multi-scale periodic patterns using a learnable frequency band attention mechanism, and a time-domain Transformer encoder that simultaneously models sequential dependencies. The outputs from both modules are ultimately fused to generate the final user preference representation. DCFRec is optimized through joint training to enhance both its robustness and recommendation accuracy. Experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that DCFRec significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various recommendation metrics, with an average improvement of 6.8% on HR@20 and 7.4% on NDCG@20, validating its effectiveness in capturing diverse user preferences and achieving robust learning. The code of our method is available at https://github.com/yyt-1219/DCFRec.

title: A novel K-shell-based feature for detecting influential nodes in directed complex networks: Addressing resolution and core-like groups problems
abstract: The identification of influential nodes plays a crucial role in understanding the dynamics of complex networks. However, most existing methods, particularly when applied to directed networks, still suffer from limited resolution and accuracy. To address these issues, we propose three variants of the k-shell method specifically designed for directed networks and introduce a hybrid approach that integrates k-shell with degree centrality. This combination resolves the challenges of low resolution and the core-like group problem in both directed and undirected networks. To support this, we provide a mathematical formulation. Furthermore, to validate the effectiveness of our method, we conduct extensive experiments using the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) model on 27 real-world networks, including 19 undirected and 8 directed networks, and compare the results against 27 benchmark methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves accuracy by 57.8% over Balanced Iterative Influence (BII) and 53.5% over Return Random Walk Gravity (RRWG), while maintaining linear time complexity and higher precision. These findings indicate that the proposed method is both scalable and robust, offering a more reliable framework for analyzing influence in complex directed networks.

title: SCGRN: Spatiotemporal causal graph reasoning network for regional economic development modeling
abstract: High-quality economic development calls for data-driven, interpretable modeling to support regional policy decisions. However, existing forecasting methods struggle with causal reasoning and spatiotemporal integration. Traditional econometric models capture structural relationships but often miss complex nonlinear patterns, while recent machine learning models (e.g., deep neural networks) achieve accuracy at the cost of interpretability. In particular, current spatiotemporal graph neural networks (ST-GNNs) assume fixed or learned correlations but lack explicit causal modeling and struggle to jointly capture spatial spillovers and temporal dynamics. To address these gaps, we propose a Spatiotemporal Causal Graph Reasoning Network (SCGRN) that integrates causal discovery, spatial graph learning, temporal sequence modeling, and counterfactual policy simulation. SCGRN first uncovers a directed acyclic causal graph of key economic factors, then embeds regions in a spatial graph neural network, and finally models temporal dynamics with recurrent units-all guided by the causal graph. Experiments on a 21-year panel dataset covering 31 Chinese provincial-level regions (651 province-year observations) demonstrate a 12.3% reduction in RMSE over state-of-the-art baselines, and SCGRN recovers economically plausible directed relations consistent with prior evidence. Moreover, SCGRN supports policy scenario analysis: by simulating interventions, it generates interpretable counterfactual outcomes for decision-makers. This work provides a novel interpretable AI approach for regional economic development modeling, with practical potential for evidence-based policy and resource allocation.

title: Dynamic emergency resource allocation via graph attention networks and hierarchical reinforcement learning
abstract: The efficient, equitable, and timely allocation of limited emergency resources is critical for enhancing response speed and minimizing losses when confronting diverse, fast-evolving emergencies. This paper investigates a dynamic emergency resource allocation problem (DERAP) that considers fairness, coordination, adaptability, timeliness, and resource insufficiency, and proposes a graph attention network-based hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm (GAT_HRL). Firstly, this paper establishes a mathematical model for the dynamic emergency resource allocation problem, with objectives of fairness, coordination, adaptability, and timeliness. Secondly, the complex multi-dimensional emergency resource allocation information is structured as a heterogeneous graph, and the intricate relationships between resources and demands are mined through Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to capture the state features of resource allocation. Subsequently, the method completes resource and demand allocation decisions separately through the top-level agent and the low-level agent. Finally, experimental validation was conducted across 800 instances across 4 distinct scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior solution performance across all scenarios. Compared with heuristic algorithms and other state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms, the average Gap is improved by a minimum of 2.49% and a maximum of 159.32%. Furthermore, the method exhibits strong scalability—models trained on small-scale datasets generalize effectively to large-scale problems—highlighting its robust generalization capability.

title: Opinion maximization on social trust networks considering local and global information
abstract: Opinion maximization extends traditional influence maximization by aiming to maximize the spread of desired opinions rather than merely the number of influenced nodes. In this paper, we propose a continuous opinion dynamics model for Social Trust Networks (STNs), incorporating both global public information and local consensus information into opinion updates. We prove that the formulated optimization problem is NP-hard, and its objective function is non-monotone and non-submodular. To address this challenge, we develop a two-stage seed selection algorithm (TSSA) that first filters potential seeds using a heuristic rule and then applies a Greedy strategy to determine the final seed set. Experiments conducted on four real-world social network datasets illustrate that TSSA consistently outperforms several baseline algorithms, and maintains stable performance across different network structures. Comparison with a greedy algorithm further confirms that TSSA provides substantial computational advantages while retaining a high level of solution quality. Specifically, TSSA achieves a reduction in computation time by approximately one to three orders of magnitude, while its opinion maximization results remain very close to those of Greedy, with only a 0.13 % to 3.98 % decline in the final objective value. Additional simulation studies reveal that both global public information and the opinion interaction threshold play a significant role in enhancing the performance of opinion maximization.

title: Dual-view fusion of structure and behavior: A robust learning item recommendation framework against interest drift and cold-start
abstract: Accurately modeling learners’ evolving interests and knowledge structures remains a key challenge in online learning-item recommendation, especially in cold-start and interest-drift scenarios. This paper proposes a dual-view preference recommendation framework, called DVPRec, which jointly captures learners’ long-term knowledge preferences and short-term behavioral dynamics. Specifically, a graph-based structural view models latent knowledge dependencies and group-level learning patterns through subgraph partitioning, structural denoising, and layer-attentive graph convolution. Meanwhile, a sequential behavioral view uses Transformer-based modeling to track short-term, goal-driven interest shifts. An adaptive gating mechanism dynamically combines the two views to balance long-term stability and short-term responsiveness in recommendation decisions. Extensive experiments are conducted on two large-scale real-world educational datasets: EdNet-KT1 and Assistments2017 (filtered), which contain tens of thousands of learners, thousands of items, and millions of interactions, respectively. Compared with state-of-the-art graph-based and sequential baseline models, DVPRec consistently achieves better performance. On EdNet-KT1, DVPRec improves Recall@10, NDCG@10, and MRR by 3.6 %, 3.7 %, and 3.4 %, respectively. On the sparser Assistments2017 dataset, the improvements are more notable, with Recall@10 and MRR increasing by 6.8 % and 6.2 %. Ablation studies further show that both structural denoising and dynamic interest fusion are critical to these improvements. These findings confirm that jointly modeling structural regularities from interaction graphs and short-term behavioral dynamics provides a robust recommendation approach. This approach effectively balances long-term pattern consistency with short-term adaptability in the context of sparse and evolving interaction data.

title: A framework for hallucination mitigation in domain-specialized large language models with application to aviation maintenance decision support
abstract: Hallucination in large language models (LLMs) poses significant risks when applied to safety-critical domains such as aviation maintenance. To address this challenge, this study proposes HALC (Hallucination-Aware LLM for Critical Scenarios), a reliability-centered reasoning framework designed to ensure factual consistency through evidence-grounded, stepwise verification and uncertainty-aware control in domain-specialized LLMs. HALC establishes a closed-loop reliability architecture integrating two complementary mechanisms: a semantic-entropy-based hallucination detection mechanism that quantifies step-level uncertainty to identify potential inconsistencies, and a multi-source retrieval-augmented verification chain that cross-validates generated reasoning steps against maintenance records and technical manuals with traceable citations. Experiments conducted on 2443 real-world maintenance records, evaluated across 30 benchmark retrieval cases and a validated 199-sample test subset, demonstrate that HALC effectively mitigates hallucinations, achieving a substantial (>85 %) reduction in unsafe acceptance risk, operationalized as false positive acceptance under fixed high-safety (low-FPR) constraints, and a ∼20 % improvement in factual reliability compared to domain-tuned baselines. The proposed framework contributes to advancing trustworthy and explainable LLM reasoning, providing a scalable pathway for reliable deployment of LLMs in safety-critical industrial applications such as intelligent maintenance and fault diagnosis.

title: AI-driven remanufacturing supply chains: Greening and intelligence diffusion
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) based training recycled data was applied in remanufacturing to minimize the screening and inspection misses. We focus on the diffusion of green practices and intelligent technology when AI is applied to remanufacturing supply chains and how to control. A remanufacturing supply chain network is constructed based on epidemic models with a three-stage game, where an AI provider activates, then firms produce, and consumers purchase. This model captures the firms’ learning and consumers’ imitation, and reveals a seesaw effect between the self-driven power from AI and the out-driven power from the AI provider. We show that appropriately leveraging influential “big customers” with high hyperdegree and configuring network connectivity can promote greening and intelligence diffusion. Interestingly, contrary to traditional wisdom, higher data efficiency and accuracy of AI do not always accelerate diffusion, highlighting the potential mismatch between technological performance and adoption. Based on 16 parameter experiments, each involving over 2000 data instances with 100 replicates, simulations indicate that incomplete diffusion is general. However, adjusting these factors increase the greening and intelligence diffusion level to up to 94.73% and 81.50%, while inspection misses are reduced by 38.11% compared to the baseline. These results imply that more firms are induced to remanufacture and adopt AI-enabled inspection, so as to improve operational efficiency and reduce waste. Furthermore, neither the remanufacturer nor the third-party technical vendor is universally dominant as an AI provider, as their motivations to activate AI adoption vary across industry contexts. Overall, we indicate that promoting green practices and smart technologies depends on the integration of network structure, product design, and technical attributes, rather than relying solely on technical performance or provider identity.

title: Handling unseen entities with dual-level interaction dynamics in temporal knowledge graphs
abstract: Inductive reasoning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) aims to predict missing links with unseen entities, a practical yet under-explored task. Existing approaches relying on trained entity representations struggle to generalize to new entities. To address this challenge, we propose DIST (Dual-level Interaction in both Structural and Temporal dimensions), a relation-driven framework that captures rich relational patterns. Instead of relying on explicit entity information, it identifies multiple types of relational patterns from topological and chronological perspectives. The framework models dual-level interactions: (1) a relation-level Relational Pattern Encoder that encodes semantic representations for relations from diverse relational patterns, and (2) an entity-level Query-specific Temporal Reasoner that integrates these relation representations with fine-grained, query-specific context in TKGs. DIST shows competitive performance in transductive settings while consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods in inductive scenarios. On ICEWS18-ind (inductive), DIST achieves average gains of 8.07% in MRR and 10.76% in Hits@1 over state-of-the-art inductive methods, demonstrating strong generalization capabilities. Moreover, DIST offers interpretability, providing insights for practical applications.

title: From graphs to tokens: Substructure-aware molecular representation for large language models
abstract: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to process graph-structured data holds significant potential for advancing molecular research, especially in tasks related to molecular structure analysis and understanding. However, a key challenge remains in effectively tokenizing molecular graphs to align with the capabilities of LLMs. To bridge the gap, this paper proposes SubStructure-aware Tokenization (S2Token) that fragments molecules into chemically meaningful, reusable substructures. The key idea is to generate semantically enriched substructure token embeddings and represent the complex relationships between tokens in the LLM embedding space, allowing LLMs to learn and generalize chemical patterns effectively. To achieve this, S2Token begins by decomposing molecular graphs based on frequency and functionality to build a vocabulary. Then, we establish a dual-view token embedding method that jointly encodes fine-grained structural and functional attributes of molecular substructures. Furthermore, we propose an efficient token alignment strategy to associate the dependencies between non-sequential substructures with the LLM token embedding space. In this way, our method activates the LLMs’ generalization ability to unseen molecular graphs. To evaluate this, we curate four task-specific molecular datasets designed to investigate generalization. Extensive experiments on three standard benchmarks and four curated datasets demonstrate that S2Token consistently yields substantial performance improvements. On the molecular caption benchmark, S2Token achieves a 12.6% average performance gain across six metrics, outperforming the best LLM-based method. For forward reaction and retrosynthesis tasks, it enhances fingerprint similarity for synthesized molecules by 6.6% and 8.6%, respectively. Moreover, S2Token shows advantages on four generalist evaluation tasks, including 9.7% and 3.0% reductions in MAE on the molecular property prediction task, compared to graph- and node-centric tokenization methods. Code is available at https://github.com/GraphMoLab/S2Token.

title: Uncertainty-aware significance and interaction-enhanced feature selection: A fuzzy multi-granularity information perspective
abstract: Most existing information theoretic-based feature selection methods cannot effectively handle the uncertainty prevalent in data and often fall into the dilemma of feature correlation coupling. Motivated by these issues, this paper proposes an uncertainty-aware significance and interaction-enhanced feature selection (SIFS) approach. Specifically, a fuzzy multi-granularity space (FMGS) consisting of adaptive fuzzy neighborhood grains is first constructed, which is defined by a distributionally adaptive constraint set. Then, an uncertainty-aware fuzzy multi-granularity information uncertainty measures (FMIUMs) framework is established based on the adaptive fuzzy neighborhood grains in the FMGS. And the FMIUMs framework is used to characterize and capture feature correlations in the feature space, respectively. Moreover, significance and interaction are enhanced to design global weighting factors for features. Furthermore, a significance and interaction-enhanced feature selection (SIFS) approach with maximum relevance minimum class-constrained redundancy is proposed to excavate the most discriminative information in the feature space. The experimental comparison results with nine representative feature selection algorithms on fifteen datasets show that the proposed SIFS approach achieves the best classification performance and reduction effect, while statistical significance tests also demonstrate its significant advantages. Additionally, ablation experiment also validates the effectiveness of considering fuzzy multi-granularity information.

title: Beyond the prompt: Log-based threat detection and attribution for multi-Agent LLMs
abstract: Multi-agent large language models (LLMs) expand capability by delegating subtasks and invoking tools, but they also enlarge the attack surface with instruction-sensitive threats (e.g., prompt hijacking, retrieval poisoning, tool-use redirection) that unfold across agent-to-agent interactions and may look benign in text alone. We present ALTEDA, a log-based Threat Detection and Attribution framework for multi-agent LLMs that does not use user prompts or responses, reducing privacy risk while capturing cross-agent attack signals. ALTEDA red-teams a target workflow to collect synchronized application, network, and system logs, converts each run into an attributed directed multi-graph, and trains a graph-level detector which also supports early compromise detection from partial traces. In addition, our framework attributes detections back to responsible agents and interactions via SHAP with aggregator-aware redistribution. On a red-teamed multi-agent LLM system, we generate 800 traces with a 31.4% attack success rate and show that ALTEDA achieves strong end-to-end detection performance. Our result also shows ALTEDA can surface high-trust early alerts by around 40% trace progress and largely converges toward full performance by mid-trace, enabling intervention before attacks complete. Despite avoiding user content entirely, ALTEDA remains competitive with text-based detectors and incurs low computational overhead, making it suitable for real-time monitoring.

title: Multimodal fake news video explanation: Dataset, model and evaluation
abstract: While social media platforms facilitate information access, fake news videos pose serious societal risks. Most detection methods treat fake news as a binary classification problem, ignoring the unique deceptive patterns of each fake item. To address this, we introduce the Fake News Video Explanation (FNVE) task, which generates natural language explanations for fake news videos. To support this, we develop FakeVE, a new dataset comprising 2672 fake news video posts, which provides explicit explanations for four real-world deceptive aspects of fake news videos. Furthermore, we propose a Multimodal Relation Graph Transformer (MRGT) model that explicitly models intra- and inter-modal inconsistencies via graph reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MRGT achieves state-of-the-art performance on FakeVE, outperforming strong baselines including recent Multimodal Large Language Models by up to +1.36 in BLEU-4 and +8.80 in ROUGE-L. Our work provides the first systematic benchmark for generating explanations for false news video, and highlights the importance of specialized architectures for this task. We release our code and dataset at https://github.com/Lieberk/FakeVE.

title: Multi-domain generalization few-shot intent recognition with dual representation learning
abstract: Intent recognition stands as one of the key challenges in achieving high-quality human-computer interaction, with few-shot intent recognition specifically addressing data scarcity. Existing approaches assume either identical data domains or single-domain generalization, overlooking the inherent diversity of intent domains in real-world scenarios. Intent expressions across domains often exhibit significant differences, severely impairing a model’s recognition capability in new domains. However, existing methods focus solely on in-domain adaptation or cross-domain transfer, resulting in an isolation between in-domain and cross-domain representation learning. To address this, in this paper, we propose a novel Dual Representation Learning (DuRL) method that simultaneously enhances in-domain and cross-domain representation learning. DuRL improves accuracy for multi-domain generalization few-shot intent recognition by increasing the discriminative power of in-domain samples and reducing cross-domain representation differences. In the in-domain, DuRL utilizes the generalized knowledge from support instances to enhance the representations of query instances. Simultaneously, to reduce confusion between different class representations, we introduce class discrimination regularization to drive representations of distinct classes apart in feature space. In the cross-domain, DuRL employs representations from various domains to perform adversarial learning, thereby obtaining domain-invariant representations. During the adversarial process, the representations from different domains are pulled closer together to confuse the discriminator. In few-shot recognition, DuRL predicts the target class by computing the matching similarity between support and query instances. Theoretical proofs demonstrate the feasibility of enhancing in-domain generalization, while extensive experiments confirm that DuRL achieves state-of-the-art performance. Results show DuRL outperforms the SOTA by 4.39% and 2.15% on average in Clinic150 → Hwu64 of 10-way 1-shot and 3-shot scenarios, respectively.

title: PhiMark: watermarking relational data robustly with zero distortion
abstract: Relational data is vulnerable to copyright infringement during data transactions. Robust database watermarking is an effective approach to protect data copyright. However, existing schemes embed watermarks by altering the original data, which inevitably compromises data utility and restricts their applicability in high-accuracy applications (i.e., governmental applications, medical applications, etc.). To address these issues, a zero-distortion robust database watermarking scheme (PhiMark) is proposed by employing a novel partition-and-mask approach. Specifically, a hash function is used to partition the original data, and a mask is generated for each partition based on extracted features. A genetic algorithm is introduced to automatically optimize the watermark parameters to reduce the manual efforts involved in parameter tuning. Subsequently, the verification evidence is derived by calculating the mask and watermark (i.e., copyright information) and stored for watermark extraction. PhiMark is a promising approach to both support digital asset protection and maintain the protected database unchanged. Additionally, it is compatible with both textual and numerical data, while existing schemes are tailored for either one. These features significantly enhance its potential for practical deployment. Experimental evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate the superior robustness of PhiMark over state-of-the-art schemes. Specifically, on a dataset with tens of millions of tuples, watermark embedding requires only 84 seconds, and the average accuracy of watermark extraction remains at 94.3% under common malicious attacks (such as deletion, alteration, etc.) with a 95% attack ratio, which is 12.6% higher than the existing optimal scheme.

title: A self-guided few-shot semantic segmentation model based on query foreground-background similarity
abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) commonly relies on generic support query matching. However, existing methods generally overlook two key cues: (i) Humans discriminate new categories by focusing on distinct image regions (e.g., salient foreground vs. background), but current methods lack such selective attention modeling. (ii) Pixels within a single object show much stronger feature consistency than pixels across different instances of the same class, even with intra-object variation. Based on this observation, we proposed SGTNet, which instead uses a Self-Guided Transformer (SGT) to refine the query itself. Specifically, SGT utilizes intra-query feature similarity to partition query images into distinguishable and ambiguous regions, dynamically guiding interactions between them to enhance discriminative capabilities. Extensive experiments on mainstream FSS benchmarks and cross-domain evaluation settings demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods. Additional analyses validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed token partitioning and interaction strategy. The implementation code has been made publicly accessible at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SGTNet-BF5E

title: A dual-source knowledge distillation framework for hate speech detection based on cognitive distortion awareness
abstract: Traditional hate speech detection methods primarily focus on surface-level semantic cues and emotional intensity, resulting in suboptimal performance when identifying implicit and complex hate speech. To address this challenge, this study introduces cognitive distortion as an actionable reasoning cue and proposes a Cognitive Distortion-Aware Dual-Source Knowledge Distillation (CDA-DKD) framework. The framework employs a two-stage strategy. First, an Expert-Guided Cognitive Amplification (EGCA) mechanism is designed to enrich sparse signals and resolve ambiguous boundaries associated with cognitive distortions in training data. Second, a Dual-Teacher Single-Student Dual-Source Knowledge Distillation (DSKD) architecture is constructed. This architecture efficiently distills knowledge from two specialized expert teachers—one focusing on semantics and the other on cognitive distortions—into a lightweight student model. Evaluated on three public datasets (IHC, SBIC, and DYNA), the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art Macro F1-scores of 79.73%, 91.34%, and 84.25%, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that CDA-DKD significantly improves detection robustness, particularly in identifying implicit hate speech devoid of explicit offensive vocabulary.

title: TemFRC: Enterprise financial risk prediction with temporal folding and risk contrast
abstract: Enterprise financial risk prediction constitutes a critical component of contemporary corporate governance, profoundly impacting an organization’s capacity for risk mitigation and data-driven decision-making. However, existing methods that treat financial data as a time series mostly focus on capturing trend variations, while ignoring the fact that enterprise development often exhibits periodic patterns and inter-enterprise similarities, resulting in limited model capacity to learn financial characteristics. To address this issue, we propose TemFRC, a novel method for enterprise financial risk prediction that enhances model performance by capturing various periodic patterns in financial data and leveraging risk similarity among enterprises. Specifically, TemFRC consists of two core modules: the temporal folding module and the risk contrast module. The temporal folding module transforms one-dimensional time series into two-dimensional temporal feature maps, enabling more comprehensive capture of trend variations and periodic patterns in financial data. The risk contrast module optimizes enterprise feature representations within the embedding space via contrastive learning, thereby facilitating the modeling of inter-enterprise risk similarities. Finally, the feature representations learned through the two modules are leveraged to determine whether a company is at risk of financial distress. Experiments are conducted on a real-world financial statement dataset comprising 3622 listed companies. The results demonstrate that TemFRC achieves state-of-the-art prediction performance, reaching a Macro-F1 score of 0.8753, which represents a 2.87% improvement over the best-performing baseline model.

title: Multi-view learning with hierarchical cross-attention for next POI recommendation
abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict a user’s next destination from historical check-in behavior. Many existing methods handle sequential, spatial, and semantic information in separate modules and combine them at later stages, making it challenging to capture how sequential patterns influence spatial choices, how geographic context shapes semantic preferences, and how category transitions guide temporal decisions. We propose MvHCA-POI, a multi-view framework with hierarchical cross-attention that enables cross-view feature integration during encoding. MvHCA-POI builds three graph-based views: a category sequence graph, a POI sequence graph, and a geographic graph that captures both local proximity and global structural relationships. Unlike traditional methods that integrate view embeddings at a late fusion stage, our hierarchical cross-attention operates in two stages. The category sequence first guides token-level enhancements within each view, emphasizing relevant recent check-ins and nearby POIs, and then serves as a semantic bridge to align view-level representations across different views. Experiments on four real-world LBSN datasets demonstrate that MvHCA-POI achieves 6.5% to 11.2% improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in standard ranking metrics. Ablation studies further confirm the contribution of each component in the hierarchical cross-attention framework.

title: A cooperative game-based compensation allocation mechanism for consensus in group decision-making
abstract: In group decision-making processes, achieving consensus often requires decision-makers to adjust their initial preferences, which incurs adjustment costs and may be constrained by individual budget limitations. Existing consensus models mainly focus on optimizing preference adjustments, while insufficient attention has been paid to budget feasibility and compensation allocation. To bridge this gap, this study proposes a consensus compensation analysis framework that explicitly incorporates individual budget constraints and external compensation. We first develop a budget feasibility diagnostic model to evaluate whether a target consensus level can be achieved under given budget conditions and to determine the minimum required compensation. Building on this, a minimum cost consensus model incorporating individual budgets and compensation is constructed, and its feasibility conditions are derived. To address situations of budget shortfalls, two compensation allocation mechanisms are designed based on Nash bargaining and the Shapley value, respectively. An illustrative example inspired by the Taihu Lake Basin, involving eight decision-makers and four governance alternatives, demonstrates the implementation process. Sensitivity analysis and comparative experiments demonstrate the feasibility, fairness, and robustness of the proposed framework under limited budgets.

title: A distributed quantization mechanism for lightweight federated learning model in heterogeneous on-device AI networks
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy, yet its practical deployment remains constrained by communication bottlenecks, hardware heterogeneity, and limited bandwidth. This study introduces Quantization-aware Federated Learning (QFL), a dual-sided quantization framework designed to enhance communication efficiency and scalability in resource-constrained environments. QFL integrates 4-bit and 8-bit QSGD to compress model updates symmetrically at both client and server sides, forming a bidirectional compression pipeline that optimizes uplink and downlink communication without compromising convergence stability. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, real-world Diabetes and Mortality Prediction datasets validate QFL’s robustness across diverse data distributions and hardware configurations. The framework achieves up to 87.5% model compression with less than 2% accuracy degradation, while reducing ATT by 29% and RTT by 43% compared to full-precision baselines. Theoretical analysis further establishes QFL’s unbiased gradient estimation and bounded quantization variance, confirming convergence equivalence.QFL demonstrates strong applicability for real-time, privacy-preserving FL in heterogeneous edge environments, particularly in healthcare, IoT, and intelligent industrial systems, offering a scalable, energy-efficient foundation for next-generation distributed intelligence.

title: Who am I? And who should I be? The use and trust effects of identity strategies in AI-generated science communication
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen-AI) is now integral to science communication, but its identity strategies and their impact on audience trust are not well understood. To address these issues, this paper conducts two studies. Study 1 employs an algorithmic auditing method to analyse the identity strategies frequently used by Gen-AI in producing science communication content, revealing that Gen-AI more frequently adopts an expert identity rather than a layperson identity when generating science communication content. Different large models use these strategies differently, indicating that identities used by Gen-AI in science communication may be culturally informed. To further explore the trust effects of these identity strategies, the results of Study 2, an experimental study (n = 1304), indicate that audiences trust AI-generated science communication content more when it is framed using expert rather than layperson strategies. This effect is positively mediated by perceived process-based and institution-based trust but negatively mediated by characteristics-based trust. This mechanism shares some similarities with the human science communication scenario. Communicative context (Gen-AI vs. human) only negatively moderates the effect of identity strategies on perceived institution-based trust, indicating that expert strategies enhance institutional trust to a lesser extent in Gen-AI contexts than in human contexts. These results clarify the ‘anthropomorphic characteristics’ of Gen-AI in science communication and further suggest that using expert identity strategies in Gen-AI may be the better way to earn audience trust.

title: DiaCOLQ: A benchmark for Chinese offensive language quadruple prediction in multi-turn dialogues
abstract: Warning: This paper contains offensive language that may cause discomfort for readers. Structured analysis of offensive language in multi-speaker dialogues remains underexplored in Chinese, where expressions are often implicit, context-dependent, and spread across multiple turns. Prior research has primarily focused on sentence-based classification, lacking the ability to model the dynamic, interactive nature of real-world offensive discourse. In this paper, we propose the task of Chinese Offensive Language Quadruple Prediction in multi-turn dialogues, which aims to extract structured quadruples identifying the target, argument, category and speaker within dialogue contexts. To support this task, we construct DiaCOLQ, the first Chinese dialogue-based dataset for offensive language understanding, comprising 6401 utterances and 3854 annotated offensive quadruples. The dataset preserves reply-thread structures and incorporates coreference resolution to unify cross-turn references, enhancing its capacity for fine-grained semantic representation. We evaluate several vanilla and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) on DiaCOLQ. Results show that while vanilla LLMs can detect explicit offenses, fine-tuned LLMs significantly improve quadruple consistency and semantic alignment, with Hard-F1 and Soft-F1 increasing by 6.15% and 5.23%, respectively.

title: Dynamic knowledge landscape construction for AI-driven emergency decision-making: An STM-LLM framework with triple-LLM synergistic labeling
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance emergency decision-making, but systematic reviews of its knowledge evolution remain lacking. Based on 525 papers on AI-driven emergency decision-making (AI-EDM) from Web of Science (2020–2025), this study proposes an STM-LLM framework integrating Structural Topic Modeling (STM) and Large Language Models (LLMs), and develops a Triple-LLM Synergistic Labeling (TLS) mechanism for automated and bias-resistant topic labeling generation. To validate the efficacy of the framework, systematic comparative and ablation experiments were designed. The application of the framework in the field of AI-EDM facilitates the identification of research topics, followed by analysis of their spatiotemporal distribution and evolution. A Logistic-Normal Generalized Linear Model (GLM) quantified the effects of five covariates on topic prevalence, and a three-dimensional strategic map identified research frontiers and gaps. The experimental results show that the STM-LLM framework significantly outperforms mainstream baseline methods in both topic label quality and generation efficiency, and the TLS mechanism effectively improves labeling stability. The study identified nine stable topics in the AI-EDM domain that show a “growth-consolidation-decline” pattern. Research funding showed a positive correlation with the development of human–AI collaborative platforms (β=0.054,p<0.05), and differences in research focus were observed between Chinese and international scholars. None of the topics demonstrated significant preferences in terms of collaboration type. Both human intervention and type of decision objective demonstrated distinct patterns of association with different topics. Furthermore, Topics are categorized into four types—Leading, Emerging, Receding, and Persistent. Based on these findings, we further propose a “problem–technology–benefit” framework to systematically support domain advancement. The STM-LLM framework automates dynamic knowledge landscape construction, overcoming manual topic labeling limitations and offering data-driven methodological and practical support for AI-EDM research.

title: Mitigating cross-modal interference in multimodal fake news detection via adaptive feature optimization
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Feature Matching Optimization (AFMO) for multimodal fake news detection. AFMO integrates modality-specific feature extraction with dual outlier filtering and a simulated-annealing feature-selection module to optimize the fusion of heterogeneous signals. Its main contribution is an adaptive selection mechanism that suppresses cross-modal interference, thereby improving discrimination between authentic and fake content. Experiments on Weibo, GossipCop, and PolitiFact show that AFMO consistently outperforms recent competitive baselines. On Weibo, AFMO achieves 92.23% accuracy, supporting the claim that mitigating cross-modal interference can materially improve veracity prediction.

title: PsychoDial: A framework for building a suicide risk dialogue dataset in human-AI conversations
abstract: Suicide has a serious impact on families and society. As more people start to share their feelings with AI, human-AI dialogues present new opportunities for suicide risk detection. However, this field faces two major hurdles: (1) it lacks dedicated datasets, and (2) existing detection models, which are trained on social media, perform poorly in the unique context of human-AI interaction. This study’s goal is to fill these gaps by (1) constructing the first high-quality, scenario-specific dataset and (2) developing effective cross-scenario detection models. For the dataset, we develop the PsychoDial Framework, a novel method grounded in real user data and psychological theory. Using this framework, we generate 4040 multi-turn dialogues, including 2000 risk dialogues and 2040 non-risk dialogues. This dataset is rigorously validated, achieving high quality scores from human experts (9.28/10) and LLMs (9.32/10). For detection, our proposed LLM-based cross-scenario methods learn common expressive patterns across social media and new Human-AI dialogue situation. Our methods surpass all single-scenario baselines, achieving accuracy scores of 0.92 and 0.84 in the respective scenarios. By constructing the first high-quality dataset and proposing the cross-scenario baseline models, this work greatly promotes future research for the critical task of suicide risk detection in human-AI interactions. The dataset can be accessed at link: https://zenodo.org/records/18684594

title: Distributed semantic trajectory similarity join
abstract: Similarity join is a fundamental operation for managing semantic trajectory data. In massive data scenarios, distributed paradigms can be utilized to process similarity joins for huge amounts of semantic trajectory data, but they face the challenge of locally aware partitioning of the data. To address this problem, we propose a distributed similarity join framework based on trajectory segments. The semantic trajectory data are partitioned by segments, and semantically similar trajectories are stored in the same partition to improve the local similarity of the partitions. We design global and local indexes to efficiently manage partitioned data. We develop a filtering validation framework to enhance similarity query performance by pruning irrelevant trajectories based on the temporal, spatial, and semantic distances of trajectory segments. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior scalability and query efficiency, compared to other methods.

title: Robust image steganography without modification based on co-occurrence labels
abstract: Most existing image steganography without modification (SWM) methods leverage stable features for covert transmission that resist common channel attacks. However, their limited feature space restricts hiding capacity. To this end, we propose a robust SWM method based on co-occurrence labels (CooL-SWM). It exploits both the semantic stability and co-occurrence patterns of object category labels. Specifically, CooL-SWM extracts co-occurrence features from natural images and constructs co-occurrence matrices through label permutations, expanding the feature space. By using unique spatial positions, CooL-SWM establishes a bijective mapping between secret messages and co-occurrence features. This improves feature space utilization and hiding capacity. We also introduce a structured text prompt template and a label-to-image semantic consistency strategy. These ensure the generated stego images strictly match the co-occurrence label sequences, improving hiding success rate and extraction accuracy. Different from existing object-based SWM methods, CooL-SWM requires no auxiliary information such as the number of stego objects per transmission, obviating additional transmission risks. Experimental results based on VOC2012 and COCO2014 demonstrate that, while ensuring complete hiding of secret messages, the proposed CooL-SWM achieves 1.75 times and 2.33 times higher hiding capacity compared with existing object-based SWM methods, with average extraction accuracy improvements of 23.48% and 30.59%, respectively, showcasing its application prospects in real-world lossy network channels.

title: Opinion importance analysis with single-review representation for enhanced restaurant selection decision-making
abstract: Online restaurant reviews often express multiple viewpoints within a single review, yet existing studies predominantly focus on aggregated representations at the restaurant level and rarely model the relative importance of opinions at the single-review level. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel opinion importance analysis model that jointly considers content semantics and sentiment characteristics to estimate the relative importance of viewpoints expressed within a single review. Building on this, we develop a single-review level opinion representation framework, together with an opinion completion strategy that infers missing viewpoints based on neighboring reviews, and an importance-aware aggregation mechanism for integrating information across reviews. Experiments on a real-world Yelp dataset comprising 31,412 reviews from 10 restaurants extract six key themes using a combined topic model. Empirical analysis shows that multi-theme opinion expression within individual reviews is prevalent, with approximately 56%–86% of reviews containing viewpoints across multiple themes, while a substantial portion of theme-level opinions remains unobserved within individual reviews. The proposed opinion completion strategy effectively recovers these missing viewpoints, enabling more comprehensive review representations. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that explicitly modeling opinion importance and completing missing viewpoints yield more informative review representations than existing alternatives. Sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the proposed framework with respect to key parameters. This work provides a novel paradigm for review analysis, shifting from coarse-grained aggregation at the restaurant level to fine-grained, single-review opinion modeling that captures both opinion importance and missing viewpoints, with important implications for advanced opinion mining and personalized recommendation systems.

title: From Perception to Comprehension: A cognitive hierarchy for multimodal relation extraction
abstract: Human comprehension of multimodal information follows a hierarchical cognitive process that evolves from perception to integrated understanding. Inspired by this mechanism, we reinterpret multi-modal relation extraction (MRE) as a cognitive progression rather than a flat feature fusion task as in the existing methods. We propose a Cognitive Hierarchy Framework (CHF) that models multimodal reasoning through sequential stages: perception, association, reasoning, self-regulation and comprehension. Each stage incrementally aligns and refines cross-modal representations, leading to interpretable and efficient relational understanding without incorporating external structured knowledge or explicit relational supervision. Experiments on two datasets show that CHF achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving F1 by 2.37% on MNRE and 1.25% on MORE, while reducing fusion parameters by 62%. Ablation and visualization analyses further demonstrate how cross-modal consistency is gradually established across stages. These results suggest that incorporating hierarchical cognitive principles provides a promising direction for human-like multimodal reasoning.

title: PTQNet: Periodic-temporal query network for long-term multivariate time series forecasting
abstract: Long-term multivariate time series forecasting remains challenging due to the entanglement of periodic structures and irregular dynamics, especially under high-dimensional settings. This paper proposes Periodic-Temporal Query Network(PTQNet), a lightweight architecture that explicitly decomposes multi-scale seasonal patterns from residual variations.
