Two core contributions of PTQNet involve: a hierarchical cycle module that learns data-driven periodic embeddings to capture structured seasonality over a generic bank of candidate cycle lengths and a phase-aware residual attention mechanism that dynamically modulates query representations based on seasonal phase, enabling context-sensitive modeling of non-repeating fluctuations. By jointly optimizing periodic and residual pathways, PTQNet achieves accurate and interpretable forecasts with low computational overhead. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets show that PTQNet outperforms eleven state-of-the-art models, with an average MSE reduction of 15.68% and an average MAE reduction of 14.88% compared to the mean of the 11 baselines. These results demonstrate that PTQNet offers a scalable and practical solution for long-horizon forecasting in resource-constrained environments.

title: R&D partner recommendation and network prediction using patent data: A deep learning approach
abstract: R&D partner selection is often guided by expert judgment, and prior patent-based studies rarely integrate bibliometric, semantic, and network evidence in a unified predictive framework. This study develops a deep learning approach that fuses patent bibliometric indicators, SBERT-based textual embeddings, and network link prediction features to recommend R&D partners and anticipate future collaboration networks. Using USPTO patent applications in the self-driving vehicle domain (2018 to 2023), we construct a dataset of 23,796 patents, including 5237 collaborative patents. The fused model achieves 83.33% precision, 66.67% F1, and 57.55% PR-AUC, improving F1 and PR-AUC by 3.18 and 5.18 percentage points over the strongest single-feature baseline. It also outperforms classical machine-learning baselines, raising PR-AUC by 20.58 percentage points relative to XGBoost. SHAP-based analysis indicates complementary contributions from bibliometric, semantic-textual, and network signals, supporting shortlists for both exploitation-oriented and exploration-oriented collaboration strategies. Beyond partner recommendations, the model offers forward-looking insights into network evolution, indicating a continued tendency toward denser and more interconnected collaboration clusters in this sector.

title: LLM-guided multi-view representation learning for legal case retrieval via structured event chains and role-aware aggregation
abstract: Legal case retrieval (LCR) requires ranking precedents according to their legal relevance, which is often poorly captured by surface-level semantic similarities alone. We propose a multiview retrieval framework that augments strong text encoders with structured factual representations extracted from case descriptions. Specifically, an instruction-tuned Llama3-8B model is prompted to produce an ordered event chain and participant roles under a constrained schema. We encode both the raw text and extracted structure and combine four complementary similarity signals—text similarity, event-chain similarity, event-type overlap, and role-aware alignment—via a learnable non-negative score aggregator. To support deployment at the corpus scale, candidate-side extraction and embeddings are computed offline and cached, and online inference is used to perform a single query-side extraction followed by artificial-neural-network retrieval and re-ranking over a small top-K shortlist. Experiments on two Chinese LCR benchmarks (LeCaRD and CAIL2022-LCR) demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines, yielding a 3%–5% improvement in NDCG@K and better top-K retrieval quality. Qualitative analyses demonstrate that aligning matched events and participant roles provides interpretable evidence for retrieved results, which is valuable in legal applications.

title: Adaptive model selection and ensemble via spatiotemporal graph-guided expert routing
abstract: Ensemble learning has shown strong potential for spatiotemporal inference by integrating multiple base models to improve accuracy and robustness. However, existing methods often rely on fixed sets of base models and localized ensemble strategies, limiting their adaptability to dynamic data patterns and global spatiotemporal correlations. To address this, we propose an adaptive ensemble framework that dynamically selects and fuses multiple models under varied spatiotemporal conditions. First, a graph-based module is presented to encode the spatial relationships among sensor nodes and the temporal dynamics of their time series into unified context embeddings. Second, an adaptive routing mechanism is designed to compute context-dependent response scores to guide model selection. Finally, a context-specific ensemble strategy aggregates model outputs using weights derived from these scores. Experiments on traffic flow, traffic speed, and air quality datasets show that the proposed framework achieves consistently competitive and often better performance than both mainstream ensemble methods and recent dynamic graph models, reducing inference errors by up to 2.1%-4.7% while using 11%-60% fewer parameters and maintaining comparable inference efficiency. Further interpretability analysis confirms that the framework effectively captures spatiotemporal correlations and performance heterogeneity, thereby enabling adaptive model selection and fusion in response to local contextual variations.

title: Disentangled graph recommendation via dynamic long and short-term intent modeling
abstract: User decision-making behavior is driven by multiple latent intents. These intents not only reflect user preferences but are also jointly influenced by long-term interests and short-term demands. However, in real-world scenarios, user intents evolve with changes in both time and environment. Existing disentanglement recommendation methods neglect the dynamic characteristic, making it difficult to effectively model the time-varying nature of user intent. Thus, we propose a disentanglement graph recommendation model based on long and short-term intent modeling(DGRLS), aiming to cope with the challenge of dynamic intent modeling. Specifically, DGRLS models user preferences across two dimensions: i) For short-term modeling, dynamic intent routing mechanism is introduced to capture the hierarchical relationships among multi-intent features and to optimize immediate intent through a decay time factor mechanism. ii) For long-term modeling, DGRLS analyzes users’ historical behavioral data employing a large language model, and integrated with a transformer architecture to accurately represent long-term interests. It is worth mentioning that, unlike existing approaches that employ hypergraphs or transformer to model long-term user behavioral preferences, DGRLS models the distribution of users’ dynamic intentions based on modal information in the semantic space. Extensive experiments on three public datasets show that the method is effective, which provides a new perspective for actively understanding modal information for user intent representation.

title: KG-LTSR: Knowledge graph-augmented contrastive learning for sequential recommendation of long-tail users
abstract: Long-tail users pose persistent challenges for sequential recommendation due to their extremely short interaction sequences. While existing sequential recommendation approaches that leverage knowledge graph (KG) or data augmentation attempt to address this problem, they often introduce semantic noise or fail to meaningfully enrich the inherently limited interaction sequences. To this end, we propose KG-LTSR, a KG-augmented contrastive learning approach that strategically enhances sequential recommendation for long-tail users. KG-LTSR first performs a semantic-aware similar item selection process on a collaborative KG to filter out irrelevant relations and identify semantically similar candidate items. Leveraging these candidates, we then design two KG-driven sequence augmentation operators (i.e., KG-Replace and KG-Insert) that preserve sequence integrity while enriching short sequences with similar items. These operators are integrated into a contrastive learning paradigm to generate robust self-supervised views. Through multi-task training, KG-LTSR jointly optimizes the primary recommendation task, contrastive self-supervision learning, and KG embedding through parameters sharing. This ensures that KG-LTSR learns high-quality representations for long-tail users’ sequences. Extensive experiments conducted on four real-world datasets demonstrate that KG-LTSR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in sequential recommendation for long-tail users, achieving average improvements of 5.87% in HR and 6.69% in NDCG. The code is available at: https://github.com/ZZP-RS/KG-LTSR.

title: LLM-assisted fake news detection with adaptive boosting framework incorporating contrastive learning
abstract: With the rapid development of digital technologies, the widespread spread of fake news on social media platforms may threaten social stability. Existing methods often use small models as feature extractors for news content, relying on the inherent pattern differences between true and false news as the basis for fake news detection. However, smaller models cannot perceive latent background information in news content. Additionally, fake news is much less prevalent than true news on real social platforms, which may lead to issues with data collection imbalance of true and false labels. These challenges may limit the effectiveness of existing detection methods. Therefore, we propose a Large Language Model-assisted Fake News Detection method with Adaptive Boosting, denoted as LFND-AB. Specifically, we first employ the large language model to generate analyses of the truthfulness and falseness of news text, which contains background information about the news. We then design an explainable base learner for fake news detection that utilizes contrastive learning to align the similarity between the news text and the corresponding generated analyses to obtain higher-quality fused representations. Furthermore, we design an adaptive ensemble boosting framework based on the base learner. This framework adjusts the weights of misclassified samples to improve the detection performance in the next base learner, thereby optimizing the model’s ability to handle label imbalance. The comprehensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that both the proposed base learner and LFND-AB outperform State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) methods. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/FEND.

title: L-SIMCL: label-guided semantic interaction with multi-dimensional contrastive learning for hierarchical text classification
abstract: Hierarchical text classification (HTC) remains challenging under complex label hierarchies and long-tailed distributions. Current HTC models typically rely on static label dependency modeling and implicit regularization to integrate hierarchical information, which leads to the inability to dynamically capture fine-grained semantic information based on labels and difficulty in constructing discriminative boundaries for long-tailed labels in the embedding space. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Label-guided Semantic Interaction with Multi-dimensional Contrastive Learning model (L-SIMCL). First, a new label-guided semantic interaction module is proposed, which employs multi-head attention mechanisms to generate a unique, context-aware embedding for each label. Second, a new hierarchical hard negative construction method is proposed, which leverages parent-child and sibling relationships in the label hierarchy to construct hard negative samples at the sample-level. Third, a new hierarchical distance-aware optimization method is proposed, which leverages the label hierarchy to adaptively modulate the embedding distance between labels at the label-level. The efficacy of L-SIMCL was evaluated using four real-world HTC datasets: WOS, RCV1-V2, NYT and BGC. On the more hierarchically complex NYT dataset, L-SIMCL outperforms the strongest contrastive learning-based baseline, achieving absolute gains of 0.15% in Micro-F1 and 0.28% in Macro-F1, while demonstrating competitive performance on the RCV1-V2 dataset. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of L-SIMCL, particularly in addressing the challenges of complex label hierarchies and long-tailed distributions.

title: AMART: A multi-agent reflective framework for detecting and correcting faithfulness errors in translation
abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in machine translation. However, their practical deployment in high-stakes applications is critically hindered by the generation of “hallucinations”—content detached from the source text, which severely compromises translational faithfulness. Furthermore, relying on unconditional self-correction often proves counterproductive, as models may blindly alter originally faithful translations or overlook subtle errors without explicit multi-dimensional guidance. To address this fundamental limitation, we propose AMART, a Multi-Agent Reflective framework designed to instill a structured, two-stage deliberative process into the translation workflow of LLMs. In AMART, we first employ a multi-agent detection system where specialized agents, operating at complementary granularities (sentence, chunk, and word), collaboratively scrutinize an initial translation for potential faithfulness deviations. If an error is flagged, AMART initiates a conditional reflective process, which first prompts the LLM to analyze and articulate the nature of the identified error, and only then guides it to regenerate a corrected translation based on its own reflection. This mechanism compels the model to form a metacognitive understanding of its failure modes, moving beyond simple error correction. Extensive experiments on challenging hallucination benchmarks show that AMART improves hallucination detection accuracy by up to 1.3-fold and substantially reduces faithfulness errors. On the WMT24++ and FLORES-200 test sets, the framework consistently improves overall translation quality and achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming strong baselines by up to 2.2 BLEU and 2.4 COMET points. Ablation and efficiency analyses further indicate that the conditionally triggered architecture allows diagnostic signals to guide targeted corrections, improving semantic faithfulness while keeping inference cost manageable.

title: DiPaNet: Discriminative Pattern-aware Network for Multivariate Time Series Classification
abstract: The core objective of multivariate time series classification is to identify temporal-wise and variable-wise discriminative patterns. Previous methods either focus solely on temporal features within individual variables or have limited capacity to model interactions among variables, particularly when capturing short-term patterns (locality) and delayed responses among variables (asynchrony). To address these limitations, we propose a novel method, Discriminative Pattern-aware Network for Multivariate Time Series Classification (DiPaNet), which jointly models discriminative patterns along both the temporal and variable dimensions. Along the temporal dimension, the multivariate time series is divided into local segments, and a temporal convolutional structure is employed to extract temporal-wise discriminative patterns. Along the variable dimension, a Variable Interaction Pattern Detection Module is introduced to capture variable-wise discriminative patterns. In this module, the graph construction step represents each variable within a segment as a node in a graph. The Pattern-based Graph Neural Network incorporates the pattern-based adjacency matrices into the message-passing process and employs pattern fusion to combine node features derived from different patterns, thereby enhancing the model’s sensitivity to critical interaction structures. Experiments on 22 UEA datasets demonstrate that DiPaNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 1.8%.

title: Catching fraudulent “invisible hands”: An approach to finding associative dense blocks in bipartite graphs
abstract: Frauds always trail with humans as shadows through a variety of channels, leading to severe social and economic damage. In cyberspace, fraudsters often act in coordinated groups, while higher-level actors operate as low-intensity “invisible hands” spanning multiple groups. In this paper, we formalize a novel group-fraud structure on bipartite graphs, termed Associative Dense Blocks (ADB), consisting of several dense subgraphs linked by associative (bridging) nodes. To quantify such anomalous structures, we introduce the Association Score (AS) as the optimization objective, and propose a greedy algorithm, SMEA, to maximize the objective for ADB detection. We also propose SMEAr, a similarity-based variant that reduces redundant re-evaluations during node merging. This variant substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Meanwhile, through theoretical analysis of a generated random graph, we derive a lower bound on the approximation quality of the proposed algorithms for recovering ADB structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic bipartite graphs demonstrate the effectiveness and adaptivity of the proposed methods, achieving improvements of up to 39.3% on Jaccard similarity over the state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, group fraud detection analysis on a large real-world telecom network with 124,680 calling records presents its practical utility in identifying fraudulent “invisible hands”.

title: An All-in-One Quality Assessment Agent for 4D digital human: Bridging talking heads and animated human
abstract: As advancements in 4D digital human (4DDH) technology continue to progress rapidly, ensuring and evaluating its quality has become a significant concern. To support the ongoing development of 4DDH and enhance user experience, we conduct a comprehensive quality assessment of 4DDH content. Specifically, we introduce H4DQA, the large-scale 4DDH quality assessment dataset, comprising 3220 4DDH samples categorized into two groups: Talking Head and Animated Human. Furthermore, the dataset incorporates model-based, motion-based, and quality of experience (QoE) distortions to enhance diversity and robustness in quality assessment. Building upon the H4DQA dataset, we develop an All-in-One Quality Assessment Agent (A3gent) for 4DDHs, leveraging a multimodal large language model (MLLM). This framework provides an effective, reliable, and efficient objective quality assessment method for 4DDHs. The proposed A3gent integrates visual, phonetic, and posture features, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on the H4DQA dataset. Our approach offers valuable insights for advancing digital human technology and establishing standardized quality assessment protocols.

title: Mind perception of artificial intelligence: A systematic review
abstract: Mind perception shapes human-AI interaction, yet there is a lack of comprehensive review for understanding the antecedents and outcomes of the mind perception of AI. This review analyzes 153 empirical studies from the past 20 years and synthesizes the key antecedents and outcomes of the mind perception of AI. We first identify human-related antecedents (e.g., demographics, personality traits, psychological conditions), AI-related factors (e.g., humanlike appearance, transparency, social identity cues, functions), and interaction-related factors (e.g., how humans interact with AI, how AI responds, interaction outcomes) that shape perceptions of AI’s agency and experience. These perceptions of AI’s agency and experience lead to cognitive, emotional, attitudinal, and behavioral consequences that are different from human-human interactions. By comparing findings across the dimensions of agency and experience, we offer nuanced insights into how people perceive AI’s mind and how these perceptions affect human-AI interactions. Finally, we suggest promising avenues for future research.

title: VTFAformer: A visual–tactile fusion network for object attribute recognition
abstract: A precise and comprehensive understanding of object characteristics is essential for object attribute recognition tasks. However, in complex and unstructured real-world scenarios, vision-only recognition approaches struggle to form a holistic understanding of object attributes (e.g., hardness). To effectively integrate visual and tactile data, we propose VTFAformer, a novel framework that introduces a task-oriented, pre-fusion alignment stage. This stage compels the model to disentangle and extract modality-invariant core concepts (i.e., attributes), which significantly enhances synergistic reasoning between the visual and tactile modalities. Extensive experiments were conducted on five public datasets (encompassing a total of 275K samples): TacQuad, ObjectFolder Real, ObjectFolder 2.0, ObjectFolder 1.0, and Touch and Go. Compared to existing state-of-the-art visual–tactile fusion algorithms, our method achieves an average improvement of 1.78% in mA and 2.41% in Acc. These findings demonstrate VTFAformer’s multimodal advantage in environmental perception, highlighting its potential in processing heterogeneous sensor data.

title: Unified Generative Intent Discovery: Bridging in-domain classification and open-world intent generation
abstract: Open-world intent discovery is critical for task-oriented dialogue systems, where static intent taxonomies fail to capture emerging user intentions and existing methods show limited generalization beyond predefined label spaces. To address this issue, we propose Unified Generative Intent Discovery (UGID), a unified framework that reformulates intent understanding as a conditional text generation task, enabling both in-domain (IND) intent classification and out-of-domain (OOD) intent discovery within a single architecture. UGID adopts a two-stage training strategy. First, instruction-tuned supervised fine-tuning strengthens semantic discrimination among known intents. Second, a self-play reinforcement learning mechanism simulates iterative user–system interactions to explore, refine, and validate novel intent labels. In addition, a reward design combining semantic fidelity and domain relevance guides the generation process toward coherent and meaningful intent discovery. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that UGID consistently achieves strong performance, reaching ACC scores of 79.63%, 82.70% and 87.50% on BANKING, StackOverflow and CLINC, respectively. Compared with the strongest generative baseline, IntentGPT-4, UGID further improves ACC by 14.87 and 4.21 percentage points on BANKING and CLINC, respectively. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the proposed design. Overall, UGID provides an effective and scalable framework for intent understanding in dynamic open-world dialogue scenarios.

title: AmanNet: Adaptive multi-window and adversarial noise network for volatile time series prediction
abstract: Volatile time series is characterized by significant uncertainty and fluctuations, posing significant challenges for accurate prediction. Existing approaches often face two major limitations: (1) the difficulty of modeling both long-term and short-term patterns using their fixed-length input strategies, and (2) the susceptibility to overfitting and poor generalization due to the data scarcity and high noise. To address these issues, we propose Adatpvie multi-window and adversarial noise Network (AmanNet), a novel framework with two key innovations: (1) adaptive multi-window networks that process input via variable and learnable look-back window lengths, enabling dynamic capture of multi-scale temporal patterns, and (2) adaptive adversarial noise that injects adversarial noise with varying intensities across multi-window networks, thereby enhancing model robustness. Evaluated on seven real-world datasets of cryptocurrencies and stock price sequences, AmanNet achieves accuracy improvements of 4.3–8.1% and MCC gains of 19.3–55.2% over state-of-the-art models, under both 1-day and 3-day predictions. These results demonstrate AmanNet’s effectiveness in modeling volatile, noisy time series with superior generalization and robustness. Code is available in https://anonymous.4open.science/r/AmanNet_IPM26-1.

title: Forecasting secondary risks in emergencies: A transferable early warning framework using event logic graphs from social media
abstract: Social media has become a critical arena for public opinion during emergencies, where the rapid evolution of events can generate unforeseen secondary risks. This study develops and validates a transferable early warning framework that applies Event Logic Graphs (ELGs) to move beyond retrospective analysis, toward proactive risk forecasting. First, this study proposes a novel hybrid Rule-Large Language Model framework to extract events and multiple types of logical relations from noisy social media data. Second, a comparative analysis is conducted by constructing separate ELGs for each event: a natural disaster and public health crisis. Finally, regarding the historical ELG as the knowledge base, the framework incorporates the event chain similarity calculations with context-aware filtering and sentiment enhanced re-ranking mechanism. Specifically, this mechanism ensures prediction validity by filtering context mismatched risks and capturing verified public sentiment to prioritize potential threats. The results present that the hybrid framework significantly outperforms the pure rule-based model in logic triples extraction. The analysis reveals that emergencies evolve into two different structural prototypes: natural disaster is manifested as “linear cascade” models, and public health crisis shows “cyclic feedback loop” characteristics, which provides a new computational perspective for agenda setting theory. In addition, the cross-event secondary risk prediction framework achieves satisfactory predictive performance across Top-3, 5, and 10 cutoffs , demonstrating that integrating context constraints and, more critically, credibility weighted sentiment analysis, achieves the most substantial improvement in identifying high-priority risks. This research contributes to the literature by proposing a robust method for building ELG with multiple logical relationships, helping emergency management shift from passive monitoring to active risk prevention and control.

title: Semi-COPRA: An overlapping community-aware model for multi-dimensional opinion dynamics and consensus analysis
abstract: The evolution of group opinions in social networks is fundamentally shaped by community structure, particularly in networks with overlapping communities and multi-dimensional opinions. In this study, we propose Semi-COPRA, an overlapping community detection algorithm that combines a semi-asynchronous label update mechanism with a dynamic threshold strategy to mitigate sensitivity to random initialization. Experiments on four real-world networks demonstrate that Semi-COPRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding average improvements of 81% in EQ, 15% in F1 score, and 27% in ONMI over the original COPRA. Building on the detected overlapping communities, we further develop a multi-dimensional opinion dynamics model incorporating a community-aware trust function and a topic interdependence matrix. Simulation results show that increasing community overlap enhances inter-group consensus while weakening intra-group cohesion. In addition, moderate topic interdependence accelerates convergence across opinion dimensions, facilitating the formation of global consensus. These findings establish a structurally integrated modeling framework that links overlapping community detection with multi-dimensional opinion evolution, providing new insights into information diffusion and opinion regulation in complex social systems.

title: A dual-level indicative representation learning method for multimodal sarcasm detection
abstract: Multimodal sarcasm detection is essential for enhancing interpersonal understanding and communication, particularly in social media analysis and human–computer interaction. However, while existing methods effectively integrate deep features from multimodal information, they often neglect the semantic contrast between literal expression and underlying intent. This contrast arises from the implicit meanings of specific elements within a single modality, as well as the descriptive contradictions that emerge between elements across different modalities. To address this challenge, we formalize contrast characterization as a problem of indicative representation learning and propose a Dual-level Indicative Representation Learning Method (DIRLM), which is designed to explicitly capture these sarcastic elements. Specifically, to explore intra-modality contrast, DIRLM incorporates a supervised module that employs counterfactual reasoning to identify key indicative features across diverse contextual scenarios. To further leverage inter-modality contrast, the method introduces an unsupervised projection module based on orthogonal mapping, which enhances cross-modal coherence by suppressing non-indicative features while amplifying indicative ones. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed method, we conducted comprehensive experiments on two widely-used real-world datasets, MMSD and MMSD2.0. Our method achieved an accuracy of 88.98% on the MMSD2.0 dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin of at least 2.16%.

title: Which LLM performs best in crisis knowledge generation? Automatic evaluation across multiple events and knowledge categories
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer the possibility of automatically generating crisis knowledge. However, the content they generate must meet the strict requirements of high accuracy and actionability. Existing general evaluation methods and benchmarks struggle to assess these aspects effectively. To address this, this study constructs CKEval, an automated evaluation benchmark for crisis knowledge generation. This dataset covers four types of public emergencies and four categories of knowledge: conceptual, factual, rule-based, and model-based. It contains over 500,000 entries. Based on the multidimensional knowledge quality theory, we design an indicator system with five dimensions: intrinsic quality, contextual quality, representational quality, actionable quality, and effectiveness quality. We also innovatively propose a dual-path automatic scoring framework. This framework combines rule-based objective computation with LLM-based intelligent evaluation. Eight mainstream models are systematically evaluated using this benchmark. The results show that models like Claude and GPT lead in overall performance. All models excel in basic dimensions such as security and neutrality. However, they show significant weaknesses in completeness, interpretability, and user adaptability, which directly impact practical usability. The benchmark and framework developed in this study provide a scientific basis and practical tool for evaluating, comparing, and optimizing LLMs in the field of crisis management.

title: An LLM-based NLP pipeline to assist government agencies in digesting massive public comments and mitigating spam
abstract: Public comments are a crucial resource for regulatory agencies in policy-making. However, large-scale comment analysis is labor-intensive and heavily distorted by spam. While large language models (LLMs) present a promising solution, real-world deployments face critical challenges, including spam-biased topic distribution and argument-extraction errors. Moreover, several agencies we interviewed treat data privacy as one of their top priorities, hence restricting the use of cloud-based LLMs. Meanwhile, the effectiveness of privacy-preserving local models remains underexplored in rule-making. This study aims to develop a unified LLM-based summarization pipeline that jointly quantifies spam volume, detects spam templates, and enables argument-aware summarization, while remaining deployable under real-world privacy constraints. We conduct experiments on three public comment datasets drawn from the Federal Communications Commission, the Forest Service, and the Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division in collaboration with communication experts and government staff. The results reveal that the proposed pipeline achieves promising performance on quantifying spam volume, with an F1 score of 0.987, 0.993, and 0.995. The pipeline further addresses spam template detection, consistently achieving a high BERTScore when compared with expert-defined ground-truth templates. We also evaluate the pipeline’s performance on argument-aware summarization, finding that few-shot prompting notably outperforms its zero-shot counterparts. When implemented locally in Llama, a much smaller version of the LLM, the pipeline performed comparably to GPT-4, the state-of-the-art cloud-based LLM. This work enables regulatory agencies to efficiently distill public opinions from large-scale comment datasets, providing structured, argument-aware summaries that inform evidence-based policy rule-making.

title: Veritas: Structuring and verifying LLM knowledge for logically consistent behavior tree generation in LLM-based agents
abstract: Behavior trees (BTs) have been widely adopted in autonomous task planning because of their modularity and reactivity. Recently, automatic BT generation based on Large Language Models (LLMs) has attracted growing research attention. However, synthesizing BTs for long-horizon tasks without relying on predefined expert rules remains an open problem, and it poses two key challenges: ensuring the logical consistency of the generated BTs, and maintaining their factual alignment with the ground truth of the environment. To address these challenges, this paper presents Veritas, a novel verification-driven framework for automatically generating logically consistent BTs. Veritas integrates STRIPS-like symbolic operators with a multi-layered verification mechanism, thereby transforming the planning process into a coherent chain of logical derivations. We further introduce Veritas+, which augments this framework with a memory module that accumulates both successful and failed execution experiences, enabling dynamic self-correction and improving factual consistency. We evaluate the framework on 67 long-horizon tasks in Minecraft and 116 real-world tasks in AndroidWorld. Experimental results show that Veritas and Veritas+ are highly effective and significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines.

title: FFC: Clustering via identification of edge objects based on feature-force
abstract: Traditional clustering methods often suffer from a critical issue that cluster performance heavily relies on centroids or core-region samples. Inappropriate core-point assignment can lead to catastrophic consequences in cluster partitioning. To address this issue, we propose a novel Feature Force-based Clustering (FFC) method, introducing an edge-prioritized paradigm to reduce dependency on core regions. FFC introduces the Feature Force (FF) metric to identify edge-region samples, a Subcluster Formation and Merger Strategy (SFMS) for boundary clustering, and a set-distance metric for core-region assignment. Empirical experiments on 11 synthetic/real-world datasets (e.g., Circle, Moon, Olivetti Faces) demonstrate FFC achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, with perfect clustering (ARI=1.000) on non-convex Moon/Circle datasets and 20.4% higher ARI than Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) on overlapping Aggregation data. Its edge-first mechanism effectively mitigates core-region dependency, while enabling accurate identification of arbitrary cluster shapes and edge structures. FFC also offers a transformative paradigm for clustering task by breaking traditional centroid/core reliance through the novel FF-based edge-first assignment strategy, and opens new research frontiers at the intersection of clustering and edge detection methodologies with nature-inspired concept (FF). The code of FFC will be available at https://github.com/Hankbet/FFC.

title: Adaptive online bagging with hybrid sampling for non-stationary imbalanced data streams: A case study on credit card fraud detection
abstract: Detecting credit card fraud in streaming data demands simultaneous adaptation to class imbalance and concept drift—two challenges that degrade model performance. A unified Adaptive Online Bagging with Hybrid Sampling (AOBHS) framework is designed to address both challenges in streaming fraud detection. AOBHS employs a drift-sensitive sketch estimator to guide hybrid sampling of underrepresented fraudulent cases, generating temporally relevant minority samples to preserve class balance amid concept drifts. Furthermore, by combining active drift detection with passive performance-based replacement of underperforming classifiers, AOBHS adopts a dual-mode drift adaptation strategy that addresses both abrupt and gradual drifts, enhancing fraud identification accuracy over time. Comprehensive empirical evaluations across 108 synthetic datasets with 9 drift types, 5 real-world datasets across multiple domains, and a credit card transactions case study, demonstrate that AOBHS maintains robust and competitive performance compared to established benchmarks, with particular strengths in Recall, G-mean, and operational cost. These results confirm that AOBHS is particularly suited for scenarios where high recall and low operational cost are critical, and reveal its practical value for strengthening financial risk management and operational resilience in digital payment systems.

title: Mapping scholarly knowledge: A systematic review of Knowledge Graphs for academic papers
abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are vital for organizing the vast scholarly literature. However, existing research has predominantly focused on KGs that model relationships across documents, a paradigm we refer to as “inter-paper” KGs, often overlooking the rich internal semantic structure of individual papers. This gap limits the ability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems to reason across different levels of abstraction, a capability that is essential for deep knowledge comprehension. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, this paper provides a systematic review and comparative analysis of KG approaches derived from academic literature, introducing a conceptual distinction between inter-paper (breadth-oriented) and the less-explored intra-paper (depth-oriented) KGs. We analyze 102 studies to map their methodologies, tools, datasets, applications, challenges, and future directions, and we incorporate a structured appraisal of methodological rigor and reproducibility. Our findings show that inter-paper approaches (81.4%) leverage scalable Natural Language Processing (NLP) and network analysis on large bibliographic databases for tasks such as recommendation and trend analysis. Conversely, intra-paper approaches (12.7%) prioritize precise extraction and detailed semantic modeling to support fine-grained reasoning within single documents. Large Language Models (LLMs) are an emerging trend for both categories. The study concludes that the key distinction lies in this breadth-versus-depth trade-off. Recognizing their complementary strengths, we argue that integrated, multi-granular KG systems are pivotal for advancing scholarly communication. Such systems can enhance the explainability of AI-driven insights by tracing findings to their evidential roots, provide robust grounding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and facilitate machine-assisted scientific discovery, ultimately contributing to more interpretable, trustworthy, and intelligent systems for synthesizing scientific knowledge.

title: Predicting tourism product advertising effectiveness: Fusing multimodal large language models with visually-rich document understanding
abstract: With the advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI), which has drastically reduced the cost of content generation, the design of visual and textual advertising for online tourism products has gained new significance. However, how to design effective multimodal advertising remains underexplored. Prior research has shown that such advertising influences consumer decisions, yet few studies have extracted hierarchical visual cues in an interpretable manner and have quantified their predictive value for promotional outcomes. We propose a multimodal prediction framework based on a multimodal large language model (MLLM) for tourism advertising effectiveness. The framework extracts visual structural cues with LayoutXLM and abstract visual content cues with an MLLM, then fuses them via a dual-gated module to predict advertising effectiveness, providing quantitative support for evaluation and deployment. We conducted experiments on 8640 products collected from Ctrip over a period of five months. The results indicated that fusing visual structural features and content features enabled the model to achieve the best performance. Compared with the baseline, the MSE decreased by 0.2396. The RMSE decreased by 0.1280. The R² increased by 0.1541. This study provides merchants with practical guidance on advertising design and offers online travel platforms data-driven strategies for advertising placement.

title: Toward accurate and cost-effective LLM agents via information flow optimization: Insights from a phishing detection case study
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong performance on complex decision-making tasks that require reasoning over heterogeneous inputs. However, these gains often come at a substantial operational cost, as incorporating additional modalities and tool calls leads to rapidly increasing API usage in real-world deployments. We argue that this tension is not solely a modeling issue, but a consequence of how information is shared with agents, and we systematically investigate how information-flow design shapes the performance–cost trade-off in LLM-based agentic systems. Using phishing website detection as a representative case study, we evaluate a spectrum of LLM-based agent designs spanning single-input baselines, parallel-input agents, and progressively more cost-aware sequential strategies. While providing all information in parallel improves detection performance, it incurs prohibitive costs due to large input sizes. To address this, we examine sequential escalation strategies that defer expensive inputs until earlier evidence proves insufficient. A multi-agent pipeline following a fixed, cost-aware sequence reduces cost substantially while maintaining competitive accuracy. Building on this, a single-agent sequential design that preserves reasoning context across steps further improves performance (F1-score = 0.964) with only a moderate cost increase. Finally, a dynamic sequential agent that autonomously selects which information to request next achieves the highest performance (F1-score = 0.974), though at higher operational cost. These results demonstrate that structured information flow, not merely model choice, plays an important role in determining the accuracy–cost trade-offs of agentic AI systems. While our findings are based on phishing detection as a representative case study, extending these insights across domains remains an important direction for future work.

title: Generative AI and cloud deployment for intelligent systems: a retrieval-augmented generation framework using amazon bedrock
abstract: The growing demand for scalable, semantically grounded intelligent systems has revealed limitations in many current generative AI deployments, including weak contextual grounding, static rule-based adaptation, and inconsistent latency under cloud-based orchestration. This study presents UL-RagCloud, a cloud-native Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to operationalize the infrastructural and semantic foundations of ubiquitous learning environments. Ubiquitous learning (UL) systems can be conceptualized as comprising multiple interdependent layers, including infrastructural scalability, adaptive interaction mechanisms, and learner-level outcome evaluation. The present study focuses on the infrastructural and adaptive layers required to ensure reliable and safe integration of generative AI within UL environments. The architecture integrates Amazon Titan Text Embeddings, OpenSearch Serverless, and Claude v3 Sonnet via Amazon Bedrock within a stateless, serverless pipeline that supports domain-sensitive semantic context-awareness at the query level and evidence-grounded response generation. UL-RagCloud enables real-time question answering by dynamically retrieving semantically indexed content and generating contextually grounded responses through a stateless, serverless pipeline. The framework is empirically evaluated using the SQuAD v2.0 dataset, comprising 10,570 question–answer pairs across 1,204 documents. Retrieval performance is assessed using Grounded Contextual Retrieval Evaluation (GCRE), achieving high Context Precision (87.75%), Recall (90.12%), and F1 Score (88.92%). Semantic answer quality is evaluated via RAGAS metrics, demonstrating strong Faithfulness (86.9%), low Hallucination (13.1%), and high Answer Relevancy (79.9%). Cloud diagnostics confirm low-latency execution (5.5 seconds) and lightweight resource utilization (82 MB). These results demonstrate UL-RagCloud’s robustness and efficiency as a cloud-native, query-level semantic adaptation framework supporting evidence-grounded interaction in ubiquitous learning infrastructures. While the primary use case targets ubiquitous learning, the architecture is designed to support semantic context-aware retrieval and evidence-grounded response generation within heterogeneous knowledge bases, providing an infrastructural foundation that could be adapted to other knowledge-intensive domains.

title: Multi-dimensional association scoring and confidence awareness for multimodal cancer survival prediction
abstract: Integrating pathology whole-slide images (WSIs) with genomic data for cancer survival prediction holds promise but faces three key challenges: (1) the semantic gap hindering feature alignment; (2) the lack of confidence estimation for individual modality predictions; (3) fusion strategies that neglect reliability differences across modalities. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-dimensional Association Scoring and Confidence Awareness (MASCA) framework. First, we design a multi-dimensional WSI–genomic association scoring mechanism that jointly incorporates semantic similarity, structural matching, and functional attribution to achieve fine-grained alignment between WSI and genomic instance representations. Second, we impose a normal inverse gamma (NIG) prior on the predicted risk scores of all instances to capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty of each modality. The NIG distribution is then marginalized to yield a t-distribution, facilitating convenient confidence quantification and cross-modality fusion. Third, we develop a confidence-aware fusion strategy based on the t-distribution that adaptively adjusts fusion weights according to modality-specific confidence levels, thereby improving the reliability of the fused results. Moreover, we devise a confidence ranking regularization term that further enhances the robustness of the fusion process. We evaluated MASCA on five cancer datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), including 2831 survival cases of cancer patients. The results demonstrate that MASCA outperforms state-of-the-art methods, enhancing the C-index by 1.6% and the time-dependent AUC (tAUC) by 2.7%. Therefore, our method can provide more accurate survival predictions for cancer patients, while also assisting clinicians in making effective clinical decisions.

title: Discriminative approximate low-rank projection with adaptive distance penalty for feature extraction
abstract: With the increasing prevalence of high-dimensional images, it has become a popular research topic to find effective ways to extract their essential features. Latent low-rank representation (LatLRR) has emerged as a powerful unsupervised method for extracting salient features. However, LatLRR suffers from several limitations, including its unsupervised nature, inability to reduce feature dimensionality, and disregard for local manifold structures. To address these challenges, we propose a discriminative approximate low-rank projection with adaptive distance penalty (DALP-ADP), in which LatLRR is extended to the supervised scenarios by combining feature extraction with linear discriminant regression and a label relaxation matrix is introduced to enhance inter-class separability. Additionally, the low-rank projection is approximated by two different matrices to learn the features of any dimension. Furthermore, an adaptive distance penalty is incorporated to construct a weighted affinity graph, preserving both global and local structural relationships among samples. Extensive experiments on diverse image datasets demonstrate that DALP-ADP outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods, achieving good classification accuracy and robustness.

title: Label distribution-driven semantic discrimination enhanced hashing for cross-modal retrieval
abstract: Supervised hashing leverages labels as semantic supervision to mitigate cross-modal heterogeneity, however, traditional methods that rely solely on logical labels capture only binary relationships, failing to explore deeper sample-label correlations Moreover, a major challenge in cross-modal retrieval is how to embed semantic supervision to eliminate inter-modal heterogeneity while preserving sufficient multi-modal features. To tackle the above issues, this paper introduces a two-stage cross-modal hashing (CMH) method, dubbed Label Distribution-Driven Semantic Discrimination Enhanced Hashing (L3DEH) for cross-modal retrieval. In the label reconstruction stage, semantic classification centers and the nuclear norm are incorporated to integrate modal structural information into the reconstructed labels. Constraints are also introduced to ensure the labels reflect classification importance while preserving the original classification information. Secondly, to account for the characteristics of real-value labels, a novel label semantic similarity metric is designed to hierarchically process relationships among samples. Additionally, an asymmetric optimization strategy is adopted to eliminate heterogeneity across modalities. These approaches effectively embed semantic features into hash codes, enhancing discriminative power. Comprehensive experiments on MIRFlickr-25K, IAPR-TC12, and NUS-WIDE datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, with L3DEH achieving average mAP improvements of 0.8%, 0.2%, and 1.1%, respectively. Furthermore, despite its more complex two-stage design, L3DEH incurs no significant increase in training time, as verified by both complexity analysis and empirical runtime comparisons.

title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation
abstract: Explainable scholar recommendation aims to identify potential scholars of interest and provide reasonable explanations for the recommendations. However, existing frameworks struggle with optimization-induced noise and ”hub node bias”, yielding trivial explanations that lack hierarchical depth and personalization. To this end, we propose a novel explainable scholar recommendation model, Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning (named PAGSL). PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31% in F1-score, 6.29% in Accuracy and 5.95% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. PAGSL achieves strong performance in both recommendation accuracy and explainability.

title: MFND-DCL: Multimodal fake news detection based on dual contrastive learning
abstract: The rapid proliferation of multimodal fake news on social media necessitates robust detection methods, yet existing approaches often struggle to capture fine-grained cross-modal inconsistencies and discriminate semantically similar samples. To address these issues, this study proposes MFND-DCL, a Multimodal Fake News Detection framework based on Dual Contrastive Learning. At the cross-modal level, we align text and image features in a shared semantic space via contrastive loss, thereby capturing cross-modal consistency. At the inter-sample level, supervised contrastive learning is employed to optimize the feature space layout, enhancing the distinction between samples that are semantically similar but differ in veracity. Experiments conducted on the Weibo (N = 9,527 posts) and PHEME (N = 5,802 tweets) datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing baseline models in both accuracy and F1 score, achieving accuracies of 95.5% and 90.1%, respectively. Moreover, the method maintains stable performance across different language scenarios, validating the effectiveness and robustness of dual contrastive learning. This study offers new perspectives for the early identification of fake news. We release the code and data at https://github.com/chenyujia-max/MFND-DCL.

title: GLINT: Global–local fusion with attention intervention for MLLM hallucination mitigation caused by insufficient visual resolution
abstract: Existing hallucination mitigation methods for MLLMs, such as contrastive decoding and visual attention enhancement, often struggle with small objects. To address this issue, we propose GLINT, a training-free framework inspired by the global-to-local strategy of human vision to mitigate hallucinations. GLINT introduces a semantic-driven global–local encoding component to automatically crop informative regions, an attention-guided masking strategy, and an attention intervention mechanism to encourage balanced utilization of global image, local image, and language. Additionally, it integrates contrastive decoding with an auxiliary text-only model to suppress hallucinations induced by language priors. Extensive experiments on nine widely used datasets show that GLINT outperforms the SOTA method by an average of 1.1 F1-score points.

title: Dynamic weighted knowledge distillation for skin lesion diagnosis
abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers an effective strategy for skin cancer diagnosis, enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained clinical environments while maintaining high diagnostic accuracy. Although existing methods for mitigating logit collapse have shown promise, they often fail to capture the intrinsic relationships among non-target classes, thereby limiting effective knowledge transfer, especially in skin cancer diagnosis where similar lesions require capturing inter-class relationships. To address the problem, we propose Dynamic Weighted Knowledge Distillation (DWKD), a novel framework that constructs a sample-wise weighting mechanism based on the normalized prediction entropy of the teacher model. This mechanism dynamically balances two key knowledge: logit knowledge and inter-non-target-class relational knowledge extracted from skin lesion feature representations. By adaptively regulating the distillation process, DWKD effectively alleviates the limitations of non-target class knowledge transfer caused by logit collapse in conventional methods. We conducted extensive experiments on two large-scale, publicly available skin lesion datasets, where DWKD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art knowledge distillation methods, achieving 88.5% accuracy on ISIC 2019 and 91.0% on ISIC 2018.

title: Multiple minds are better than one: Enhancing temporal knowledge graph forecasting with mixture of diverse graph experts
abstract: Temporal knowledge graph forecasting (TKGF) focuses on inferring future events by effectively modeling and utilizing past factual information. Although recent structure-aware methods excel at modeling dynamic event correlations, they often lack semantic-aware capabilities. Meanwhile, semantic-aware methods suffer from two main limitations: (1) insufficient modeling of evolving properties, and (2) gap between graph and LLMs. To tackle these challenges, we propose FMOGE, a novel Flexible Mixture Of diverse Graph Experts framework that performs fast thinking for global contextual facts and slow thinking for local logic rules, thereby enabling structural–semantic joint learning. Specifically, FMOGE consists of three complementary components: (1) The evolution-aware expert models the dynamic structural evolution of entities and relations across different facts. (2) The context-aware expert captures global contextual semantic knowledge from query-dependent contextual graphs via context-aware graph encoders, serving as a global shallow reasoner. (3) The logic-aware expert iteratively mines temporal logic rules through a rule-induced graph attention mechanism, enabling deep local reasoning. Furthermore, we design a hierarchical dynamic merging strategy that enhances each expert’s representation with relation-guided signals and adaptively integrates their knowledge for joint decision-making. Experiments on six benchmarks – ICEWS18, ICEWS14, ICEWS15, GDELT, WIKI and YAGO – demonstrate that FMOGE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving relative improvements of 6.09%, 11.20%, and 12.44% in Hit@K (K = 1, 3, 10) on ICEWS14, confirming its effectiveness in precise event forecasting.

title: MFC4POI: Multi-factor collaboration for next point-of-interest recommendation using large language models
abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict the next location a user will visit based on historical behavioral data. Given their strong natural language understanding and reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly introduced into next POI recommendation, as conventional methods are limited by their numerical representations, which often obscure the inherent semantic information embedded in contextual features However, LLM-based approaches struggle to effectively comprehend multiple factors holistically and express them in natural language. To address this issue, we propose Multi-Factor Collaboration for Next POI Recommendation (MFC4POI), a pretraining and fine-tuning framework that reformulates the next POI recommendation task as a question-answering problem. It leverages the strong comprehension and reasoning capabilities of LLMs to analyze user’s current behavior based on historical trajectories, and real time on-site situation, including the dynamic preferences and nearby geographic information in natural language. Due to the inherent limitations of LLMs in accurately modeling temporal and geographical information, MFC4POI introduces an intent identification agent to capture users’ dynamic preferences based on Spatio-temporal Intent-based Knowledge Graph (STIKG). It alleviates the weak spatial reasoning capability of LLMs while providing clear reasoning paths that make the recommendations more intuitive and coherent. To further improve understanding of users’s real-time on-site situation, MFC4POI integrates geographic information with dynamic preferences by providing nearby POIs that align with these dynamic preferences, thereby further enhancing LLMs’ performance. Experiments on three real-world datasets, containing up to 4000 users and 405000 check-ins, show that MFC4POI consistently outperforms strong baselines. Specifically, it achieves better performance than most baselines on Acc@1 and surpasses all baselines on Acc@5 and Acc@10 across all datasets.

title: LSFL: A Lightweight and Secure Federated Learning scheme for Internet of Vehicles
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) presents a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative training in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments. Its IoV deployment introduces security vulnerabilities requiring systematic mitigation, with a pivotal challenge being adversarial crafting of malicious model updates that compromise global model integrity and functional performance, while adversaries may also exploit gradient leakage to reconstruct sensitive private data, exacerbating IoV privacy concerns. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Lightweight and Secure Federated Learning (LSFL) scheme for IoV, where LSFL specifically incorporates a robust cosine similarity based aggregation mechanism to identify and filter malicious updates for countering poisoning attacks, further integrates lightweight homomorphic encryption to safeguard gradient confidentiality and mitigate private data reconstruction risks, and takes minimizing overhead as a core objective to ensure compatibility with resource-constrained IoV edge devices. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets and models show that LSFL significantly enhances model robustness against poisoning attacks, effectively prevents privacy reconstruction from gradients, and reduces encryption overhead compared to baseline methods. This provides a practical and secure solution for privacy-preserving federated learning in Internet of Vehicles.

title: Leveraging GraphSAGE and large language models with cross-attention for transaction fraud detection: Evidence from credit card and PaySim datasets
abstract: Online purchasing fraud has grown with e-commerce, causing economic losses and undermining consumer trust. Due to its diversity and dynamism, few studies have examined e-commerce fraud detection. Traditional machine learning algorithms, such as random forest and support vector machines, have achieved poor performance because they do not always capture the rich contextual metadata or the underlying relational structure between transactions. In response to these shortcomings, we introduce a new hybrid fraud detection method that utilizes a lightweight large language model (specifically, DistilBERT) and Graph Neural Networks (GraphSAGE). Using a cross-attention mechanism, our model learns both structural information encoded in the transaction network and semantic information (e.g., transaction type and metadata). By including rich metadata embeddings and transaction graph structures into its architecture, the model learns to effectively detect frauds, even when signals are weak or unclear. With this connection, fraud detection becomes more efficient and resilient. Two benchmark datasets were used for the experiments: the PaySim financial transaction simulator and the European Credit Card Dataset (ECCD). The suggested model obtained 89.1% accuracy, 85.0% F1-score, and 85.5% AUC on ECCD and 90.0% accuracy, 87.0% F1-score, and 85.0% AUC on PaySim using a chronological 70/10/20 train–validation–test split. These findings show that, in comparison to single-modality models, merging structural transaction graphs with semantic metadata greatly enhances fraud detection performance.

title: Attention Is All We Need: Collaborative Filtering Transformer
abstract: Graph encoding and the attention mechanism enable Graph Transformers (GTs) to extract features of graph structures. However, employing graph encoding and Transformer-based attention mechanism may lead to two defects: high computing complexity and sensitivity to graph structures. Therefore, this paper designs a graph feature extractor with a pure or lightweight attention mechanism that does not rely on graph encoding or feature projection matrices, called Collaborative Filtering Transformer (CFT). CFT uses the pure attention mechanism as the main structure of the encoder and introduces non-interaction information by constructing preference sentences. The core of CFT is that its encoder does not contain any collaborative information, but only plays a role in generating associations between different nodes, so that a node on the graph can notice its non-neighboring nodes. The utilization of collaborative information is only achieved through optimizing the loss function. In addition, through theoretical analysis and experimental verification, we prove that adding path-based graph encoding in CFT has a negative effect on the feature extraction process of the attention mechanism. Furthermore, experiments show that during the optimization process, the proposed pure attention mechanism can always assign higher attention scores to nodes with interactions, while making the attention scores between nodes without interactions approach zero. Finally, our model achieves the best performance when compared with the latest methods on five real-world datasets, and compared to the second-best baseline, the recommendation performance is improved by up to 20.60%. Moreover, CFT achieves considerably high training efficiency across all five datasets, with training time comparable to that of simple matrix factorization-based baselines.

title: A hierarchical RL model for Chinese medical NER with radical semantics and dynamic decision
abstract: To address key challenges in Chinese medical Named Entity Recognition (NER)-such as ambiguous entity boundaries, poor generalization of low-frequency entities, and the difficulty of integrating external knowledge-we propose a novel model that integrates radical semantics with hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL). First, we design an adaptive gating mechanism that fuses radical features (e.g., “疒” for diseases) with MacBERT embeddings to enhance semantic representation. Second, a decoupled HRL framework decomposes NER into boundary detection (Actor-Boundary) and type classification (Actor-Type), optimizing nested entity recognition via dynamic rewards. Third, a lightweight BiGRU-Transformer architecture with dynamic CRF decoding reduces computational costs. Evaluated on the CCKS2019 dataset (1,379 annotated samples), our model achieves a 92.51% F1-score-outperforming BERT-BiLSTM-CRF-based baselines. Robustness is validated on CMeEE, IMCS, and DiaKG datasets, providing a transferable solution for electronic medical record structuring.

title: Benchmarking and enhancing the ability of large language models on event generalization
abstract: Event generalization represents the mapping from specific events to abstract events, which is vital for information extraction tasks. Despite the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) on various information extraction tasks, their capability in event generalization is still under-explored due to the lack of open-source benchmark datasets. In this work, we construct the first open-source dataset ElizBench for event generalization, with 5757 data samples and 85 abstract event classes. We not only systematically benchmark mainstream LLMs on ElizBench, but also propose the Stepwise Self-Rethinking Event Generalization (SSR-EG) framework to further enhance LLMs’ performance. This framework stimulates LLMs to leverage their internal knowledge to rethink their responses step-by-step without introducing any external information. Experimental results show that ElizBench identifies deficiencies in existing LLMs when dealing with event generalization. Meanwhile, our proposed SSR-EG framework consistently enhances the performance of LLMs with various scales, improving their weighted F1 scores by 2.03% on average over direct prompting.

title: Wavelet transform-based versatile watermarking for facial manipulation source tracing and detection
abstract: Malicious facial manipulation poses a critical challenge to digital forensics, as existing passive and proactive methods struggle to achieve reliable source tracing and facial manipulation detection. We propose a novel wavelet transform-based versatile watermarking method, WavMark, to address the above challenges. First, WavMark combines the semi-fragile image watermark with the robust bit watermark, integrating watermark embedding and extraction into an end-to-end framework. Second, we propose a WGFB with an ADSF strategy, which enhances the detection capability of the semi-fragile image watermark by decomposing and fusing the low-frequency and high-frequency components of the original and watermarked images. In addition, we introduce the Bit Encoder for embedding bit information and enhancing the robustness of the bit watermark against facial manipulation attacks. Finally, we propose a PGAL strategy within the random noise manipulation pool, which enables automatic sample label assignment without requiring pre-labeled data. Comprehensive experiments on CelebA-HQ demonstrate that WavMark significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art forensics approaches, achieving 91.11% BCR and 100% AUC in the cross-manipulation source tracing and facial manipulation detection scenario at the resolution of 256 × 256. The results verify that WavMark effectively unifies robust source tracing and reliable facial manipulation detection, providing a scalable and imperceptible proactive forensic solution for real-world applications.

title: Latent diffusion-augmented cross-modal representation learning for radiology report generation
abstract: Radiology report generation aims to produce comprehensive textual descriptions from medical images, enhancing diagnostic efficiency and alleviating the workload of radiologists. However, it often suffers from weak semantic expression of subtle lesions and inherent heterogeneity between visual and textual modalities. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Latent Diffusion-augmented Cross-modal Representation learning (LDCR), which enhances pathological representations and promotes deep cross-modal alignment. Specifically, LDCR introduces a Latent Diffusion Enhancement Module (LDEM) that simulates progressive degradation and semantic reconstruction in latent space through a diffusion mechanism, improving sensitivity to subtle pathological lesions. Building on latent diffusion-enhanced visual representation, a Heterogeneous Information Fusion Module (HIFM) is devised to bridge the modality gap by aligning visual and textual features in a shared semantic space Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks, IU X-ray and MIMIC-CXR, demonstrate that LDCR outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving improvements of up to 1.5%, 0.8% and 3.5% in BLEU-4, METEOR and ROUGE-L on IU X-ray, and 3.7%, 1.9% and 1.7% on MIMIC-CXR, respectively. The code is available at https://github.com/Eleanorhxd/LDCR.git.

title: Hypergraph Kolmogorov–Arnold networks contrastive hashing for unsupervised cross-modal retrieval
abstract: Cross-modal hashing has become a prominent research focus due to its ability to achieve efficient information retrieval, high-speed query performance, and minimal storage overhead, making it indispensable for processing complex multimedia datasets in academic and industrial applications. However, existing methods suffer from three intertwined challenges: limited nonlinear fitting capacity due to fixed-architecture networks (e.g., MLPs), which struggle to model complex cross-modal semantics; inability to capture beyond-pairwise correlations as they often rely on simple graphs, thus failing to preserve fine-grained structural information; and sensitivity to false-negative pairs in unsupervised contrastive learning, which severely degrades retrieval accuracy. To systematically tackle these challenges, we propose Hyper-KAN Contrastive Hashing (HKCH), an unsupervised framework that introduces three key architectural innovations: first, we redesign the feature mapping module by replacing traditional MLPs with Fast-Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (F-KANs) employing learnable spline-RBF activation functions, enabling dynamic and expressive nonlinear semantic representation; second, we incorporate hypergraph neural networks to model higher-order associations within and across modalities, effectively capturing multi-way structural correlations while filtering semantic redundancy; third, we develop a novel contrastive hashing module with adaptive weights and an improved ternary loss to robustly mitigate false-negative interference and enhance semantic alignment. These components are not merely combined but are structurally integrated into a coherent architecture that advances beyond existing approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that HKCH achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with average accuracy gains of 1.38% on MIRFlickr, 1.72% on NUS-WIDE, and 1.37% on MSCOCO significant margins that validate its architectural effectiveness.

title: MedCTM: A CNN-Transformer-Mamba Hybrid Network for Medical Image Classification
abstract: Medical image classification requires models that jointly capture local textures and long-range dependencies, while remaining efficient enough for practical use. To meet these requirements, we propose MedCTM, a CNN-Transformer-Mamba hybrid network. It decomposes feature learning into three complementary branches: local feature extraction, long-range dependency modeling, and cross-branch interaction. The core of MedCTM is the Bidirectional Channel Interaction Attention (BCIA) module. This module enables dynamic information exchange between CNN and Mamba features by allowing each to condition the other. A three-stage cascade is then used to progressively refine multi-scale representations. We evaluate MedCTM on eight medical image datasets that span seven modalities and over 100,000 samples. The model achieves strong performance with only 1.42-2.63 GFLOPs. On the average F1 score across the eight datasets, MedCTM outperforms the state-of-the-art MedViTv2 by 0.5%–1.7%, while using 12.9%–24.4% fewer parameters.

title: Domain-spanning migration dilemma of serial entrepreneurs in reward-based crowdfunding: Information-based breakthrough strategies
abstract: Knowledge about whether serial entrepreneurs in reward-based crowdfunding face the domain-spanning migration dilemma and corresponding information-based breakthrough strategies is still limited. Based on signaling theory, this study aims to mitigate this gap by using 28,438 serial entrepreneurs and their 74,978 projects on Kickstarter. We employ text mining methods to identify domain-spanning migration and classify information-based breakthrough strategies into two types: reward value and risk prospect (risk disclosure and prospect hint). The findings indicate that domain-spanning migration reduces the success odds of serial entrepreneurs by 57.5%. Compared with cognitive value-based rewards, functional value-based rewards and symbolic value-based rewards can weaken the migration penalty by 28.7% and 24%, respectively. Risk disclosure and prospect hint can enhance the migration penalty by 11.8% and 22.6%, respectively. This highlights that serial entrepreneurs who engage in domain-spanning migration should rationally design their information disclosure strategies, seeking a balance in information to maintain crowdfunding transparency while effectively mitigating the migration penalty. The post-hoc analysis indicates that the propensity of serial entrepreneurs to migrate is affected by the first-time entrepreneurial results. This study provides both theoretical basis and practical insights for serial entrepreneurs and platform managers to break the migration dilemma through information strategies.

title: Synergistic denoising: Dual-correction of semantic control and distribution optimization for sequential recommendation
abstract: Sequential recommendation aims to predict a user’s next interaction based on their historical behavior. While diffusion models have advanced sequential recommendation by capturing user uncertainty, they suffer from a fundamental challenge: distribution misalignment. This issue arises when models compress a user’s multi-dimensional interests into a single representation for conditional guidance, causing the generated distribution to deviate from true user preferences. We propose DSCDO, a framework that resolves this challenge through a Dual-correction of Semantic Control and Distribution Optimization. It synergistically integrates two components: (1) an orthogonal semantic decomposition module that projects the user’s interaction history into non-interfering semantic subspaces, thereby preventing the collapse of multifaceted user preferences into a single, over-generalized representation, and (2) an gradient enhance denoising network that employs a score-matching objective to explicitly model the gradient of the true preference distribution, thereby applying a precise, single-step adjustment to the initial prediction to directly fix the distribution misalignment. Experiments on four real-world datasets show DSCDO achieves 2.3%–16.75% improvements in HR@20 and 1.9%–9.14% gains in NDCG@20 over state-of-the-art baselines.11https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DSCDO.

title: BFDM: Continual relation extraction via bidirectional feedback and dynamic multi-teacher knowledge distillation
abstract: Continual Relation Extraction (CRE) aims to continuously learn new relations while preventing the forgetting of previously learned relations. However, existing methods still face significant challenges in effectively retaining and utilizing prior knowledge, and their performance is strongly influenced by the degree of task fusion. To address these challenges, we propose a CRE model based on Bidirectional Feedback and Dynamic Multi-teacher knowledge distillation (BFDM). The model significantly enhances the fusion of current and historical tasks through the bidirectional feedback module, enabling new-task learning and memory-replay learning to relearn from each other via feedback. Additionally, the dynamic multi-teacher knowledge distillation module saves the optimal parameters for each new task into separate teacher models, which are then sequentially distilled into the student model during the memory replay learning phase. This ensures accurate and consistent retention of prior knowledge. With an average accuracy of 92.45% and 88.61% on the two benchmark datasets, BFDM demonstrates promising performance, highlighting its potential as a competitive state-of-the-art model. Ablation studies further validated the effectiveness of the BFDM model. Removing any module resulted in varying degrees of decline in average accuracy across both datasets.
