The maximum drop when removing a single module reached 1.18% and 1.37%, respectively. Our source code is available at https://github.com/lids316/BFDM.

title: Disentangling generative chaos: A multi-scale hypergraph diffusion framework for interpretable recommendation
abstract: Generative recommendation often suffers from “generative chaos”—a disordered and entangled latent state that degrades ranking accuracy and interpretability. To address this challenge, we propose Dis-Rec, a framework that pioneers a “structure-guided generation” paradigm. Dis-Rec operates through three synergistic components: (1) utilizing a latent diffusion model to construct a high-fidelity user preference manifold, providing a robust informational foundation; (2) introducing a multi-scale hypergraph strategy to concurrently encode short-term sequential contexts and long-term interest patterns into a unified structural prior; and (3) devising a disentangled gating decoder that exploits these topological priors to steer the automatic decomposition of chaotic latent vectors into semantically orthogonal intent channels, enabling context-aware adaptive fusion via a dynamic gating mechanism. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate significant performance gains. Notably, compared with the strongest baseline, Dis-Rec achieves a 7.67% relative improvement in NDCG@10 on ML-1 M and a 4.24% Recall gain on the sparse Toys dataset, effectively overcoming the data scarcity bottleneck typical of generative models. These results verify the critical role of structured disentanglement in enhancing the robustness of generative recommendation.

title: Multimodal large language model-driven entity alignment via hierarchical interaction
abstract: Multi-modal entity alignment aims to identify equivalent entities across different multi-modal knowledge graphs. However, existing methods represent a bottleneck due to two primary limitations: insufficient fine-grained cross-modal semantic associations caused by decoupled encoding, and incoherent semantic-structural interactions resulting from modality heterogeneity. To address these issues, we design a unified framework that integrates a multi-modal large language model-driven semantic perception module with a hierarchical semantic-structural interaction strategy. First, to resolve the insufficient associations, the framework builds a semantic perception module that jointly encodes textual and visual attributes through adaptive token fusion and contrastive learning, which not only enhances cross-modal modeling but also enables robust representation learning under limited labeled data. Second, to mitigate incoherent interactions, we propose a hierarchical interaction strategy that integrates feature-level alignment for structural-semantic consistency as the foundation, with semantic-level alignment for task-oriented output coherence as the refinement. Extensive experiments on five widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art baselines, achieving improvements such as an average increase of 2.4% in Hits@1 on FBDB15K and 3.5% on FBYG15K. Furthermore, our analyses under low-supervision settings reveal that the framework remains highly effective, highlighting its robustness and generalization capability.

title: Focus on latent: Toward a meaningful and interpretable latent representation for diffusion models
abstract: Diffusion models achieve high-fidelity data generation but remain limited by poor interpretability, restricting their use in applications requiring semantically grounded representations. Existing methods to enhancing the interpretability either rely on post-hoc analysis that passively reveal latent semantics or extract unconstrained latent representations, often failing to produce latent representations with clear semantic meaning and discriminative capacity. To address this, we propose a diffusion model Focus on Latent, FcLDiff, which aims to explicitly learn semantically meaningful and interpretable latent representations without introducing post-hoc analysis components that require additional training. Our method employs a dual strategy: a constraint-driven optimization strategy compels the latent representation to capture the core semantics of the data by leveraging semantic encoders along with a mutual information constraint; simultaneously, a mechanism-guided modulation strategy further directs the model’s focus toward the latent representation through a feature weighting mechanism, which adaptively modulates the hierarchical importance of skip and backbone features within the UNet architecture. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of FcLDiff across classification, generation, and disentanglement tasks. On four benchmark datasets, FcLDiff achieves a maximum gain of 0.224 in classification accuracy and a 0.202 improvement in the TAD disentanglement metric. On a materials microstructure dataset, it achieves a classification accuracy of 0.983 and generates smooth, semantically coherent interpolations, highlighting its strong potential for interpretable generative modeling and scientific analysis.

title: Stochastic dynamics of competitive information dissemination in cyber–physical integrated networks
abstract: The integration of physical and cyber networks can be a double-edged dynamic. While it accelerates the dissemination of positive information, it also intensifies the diffusion of negative information. A clear understanding of the stochastic dynamics of competitive information dissemination is essential. It enables effective control strategies to curb the spread of negative information and maintain social stability. However, designing and controlling the dissemination of competitive information in cyber–physical integrated networks (CPINs) is challenging due to competition and stochasticity. Moreover, the heterogeneity of CPINs further aggravates this problem. To address this, we propose a competitive information dissemination method to capture and control the stochastic dynamics in CPINs. Specifically, we build a CPIN model to characterize the heterogeneity between physical and cyber networks. Furthermore, we develop a temporal point process-based competitive information dissemination model (TPP-CIDM) that captures the stochastic evolution of both positive and negative information. This dissemination model quantifies the stochastic dynamics by computing the probability distribution of the sizes of competitive information, reducing biases inherent in deterministic solutions. Finally, we design an event-driven optimal control (EOC) strategy to dynamically modulate the intervention intensity. The intervention optimization problem is formulated to maximize utility under cost constraints, and a heuristic solution is provided. Numerical simulations on both synthetic and real-world networks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Exploring contextual and pairwise semantic-enhanced embedding with adaptive fusion for knowledge graph completion
abstract: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims to predict missing facts by embedding entities and relations, emerging as the predominant method for intelligent reasoning. However, existing KGC approaches tend to ignore the potential noise and uncertainty, as the contribution of each connected relation to entities varies across distinct link scenarios. Moreover, the simple aggregation process during embedding learning struggles to capture both global and local information simultaneously. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes the Adaptive Contextual-Pairwise Network (AdaCPN) model. Specifically, hybrid-granularity semantic augmentation derives a contextual representation of triplets by attending to the surrounding feature information, and suppressing redundant semantic information. Furthermore, it boosts predictive semantics with pairwise frequency weights of triplets, achieving dynamic contribution allocation and alleviating semantic distribution disparity. Additionally, AdaCPN utilizes adaptive convolution kernels of distinct sizes to broaden the receptive field, which fuses global and detailed features during the aggregation process. AdaCPN is validated on nine benchmark datasets, containing millions of triplets. Experimental results confirm that in MRR on FB15k-237 and WN18RR, AdaCPN not only outperforms neural network-based SOTA methods with improvements of 5.8% and 3.4% (0.430 vs. 0.372, 0.551 vs. 0.517), but also improves by 3.8% and 0.2% (0.430 vs. 0.392, 0.551 vs. 0.549) compared to LLM-based SOTA approaches.

title: Deciphering oracle bone characters: Pictographic captioning and reasoning for morphological recognition
abstract: Oracle Bone Characters (OBCs) represent the earliest mature writing system in China, yet their intricate structures and diverse variants pose significant challenges for automated decipherment. This paper proposes the Pictographic Captioning and Reasoning (PCR) framework, reformulating OBC decipherment from a traditional image recognition problem into a visual-language semantic reasoning task. Emulating the logic of human paleographers, PCR adopts a two-stage pipeline. First, a Large Multimodal Model (LMM), fine-tuned with domain knowledge, generates fine-grained pictographic descriptions to explicitly characterize structural compositions and visual attributes. Subsequently, by integrating these captions with the Oracle Bone Studies Knowledge Base (OBS-KB), a Large Language Model (LLM) performs semantic inference to determine glyph categories. We evaluate the framework on a dataset of 600 OBC categories, each associated with an Ideographic Description Sequence (IDS) and 30 generated captions. Results demonstrate that PCR significantly outperforms existing character-level and radical-level methods. Notably, in open-set scenarios for unseen glyphs, PCR achieves a flexible accuracy exceeding 49%. This research demonstrates the efficacy of coupling visual perception with linguistic reasoning and provides a novel modeling perspective for OBC decipherment.

title: From latent structures to explicit reasoning: Synergizing clustering and LLM for explainable and robust rumor detection
abstract: Misinformation disseminated on social media poses a systemic risk to the global information environment. Existing detection models encounter a transparency robustness bottleneck, while Large Language Models (LLMs) suffer from ungrounded hallucinations. To address these deficiencies, we propose Topic-Aware Chain-of-Reasoning (TA-CoR), a dual process framework synergizing unsupervised structure distillation with symbolic inference. To instantiate native explainability, the Hierarchical Topic Residual Refinement (HTRR) mechanism distills latent discourse into multi granular thematic priors, acting as semantic guardrails that guide grounded LLM reasoning. Systemic robustness is reinforced through a Semantic Adversarial Training (L-SAT) regimen, which utilizes meaning preserving reformulations to cultivate adversarial cognitive alignment, forcing the model to discern the invariant mendacious core of misinformation. Evaluations on Twitter15, Twitter16, and PHEME demonstrate that TA-CoR achieves state-of-the-art accuracies (80.89%, 82.97%, and 77.34%). Notably, the framework exhibits superior resilience within less than a 15% drop in performance under attacks and human evaluation confirms high rationale fidelity (>4.6/5.0). This work transitions rumor detection from opaque pattern matching to a transparent and reasoning method grounded on evidence.

title: Cross-platform evaluation of reasoning capabilities in foundation models
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive cross-platform evaluation of reasoning capabilities in contemporary foundation models, establishing an infrastructure-agnostic benchmark across three computational paradigms: HPC supercomputing (MareNostrum 5), cloud platforms (Nebius AI Studio), and university clusters (a node with eight H200 GPUs). We evaluate 15 foundation models across 79 problems spanning eight academic domains (Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology, Statistics, Calculus, and Optimization) through three experimental phases: (1) Baseline establishment: Six models (Mixtral-8x7B, Phi-3, LLaMA 3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9b, Mistral-7B, OLMo-7B) evaluated on 19 problems using MareNostrum 5, establishing methodology and reference performance; (2) Infrastructure validation: The 19-problem benchmark repeated on university cluster (seven models including Falcon-Mamba state-space architecture) and Nebius AI Studio (nine state-of-the-art models: Hermes-4 70B/405B, LLaMA 3.1-405B/3.3-70B, Qwen3 30B/235B, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-OSS 20B/120B) to confirm infrastructure-agnostic reproducibility; (3) Extended evaluation: Full 79-problem assessment on both university cluster and Nebius platforms, probing generalization at scale across architectural diversity. Results challenge prevailing scaling assumptions through a parameter efficiency paradox: Hermes-4-70B (70B parameters) achieves the highest score among extended models (0.598), outperforming both its 405B counterpart (0.573) and Meta’s LLaMA 3.1-405B (0.560). Domain-specific analysis reveals LLaMA 3.1-405B achieves record Calculus performance (0.717), while DeepSeek-R1 sets unprecedented standards for reasoning transparency (0.716 step-accuracy). Qwen3 models demonstrate exceptional consistency, with mean per-evaluation standard deviation of 0.013, the lowest among Nebius models. The findings challenge conventional scaling assumptions, establish training data quality as more critical than model size, and provide actionable guidelines for model selection across educational, production, and research contexts. The tri-infrastructure methodology and 79-problem benchmark enable longitudinal tracking of reasoning capabilities as foundation models evolve.

title: Graph-driven knowledge stream method for knowledge management in vertical domain large language models: Case study on pit engineering application
abstract: Embedding professional knowledge is crucial during developing vertical domain large language models (LLMs). While rapid progress of LLM coexists with barriers to professional knowledge access. Such coexistence highlights the need for effective knowledge management during vertical domain LLM development, yet existing research seldom focuses on this. To solve this gap, we conduct three works: (1) Based on insights of knowledge structural representation, we propose a graph-driven knowledge stream method that models knowledge enabling activities as measurable flows; (2) a knowledge graph (KG)-anchored evaluation protocol is proposed to quantify graph coverage, constraint consistency, hallucination rate, and retention for evaluating knowledge enablement; (3) we integrate graph-anchored evaluation, LLM-graph interaction pipeline, federated learning (FL), and blockchain as graph-driven vertical domain LLM development framework (GVLDF). GVLDF enables knowledge aggregation and reuse, efficacy auditing, and continual optimization. In a foundation pit engineering case study (58,451 tokens fine-tuned vertical domain LLM), GVLDF improved graph coverage from 0.712 to 0.889, raised constraint consistency from 94.3% to 98.1%, and reduced hallucination rate from 0.220 to 0.063, while maintaining retention above 0.87. These findings show that structural anchoring systematically enhances reliability, compliance, and sustainability in vertical LLM development. Our research provides a reliable theory and solution for sustainable enablement and robust deployment of vertical domain LLM.

title: When input perturbation outperforms gradient perturbation: Achieving high-accuracy deep learning under local differential privacy
abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success but remains vulnerable to privacy threats such as membership inference attacks (MIA), where adversaries infer the presence of specific user data in the training set. While differential privacy offers a theoretical framework naturally suited to defend against MIAs, existing implementations face significant challenges. Gradient perturbation methods typically rely on a trusted central server, posing risks of privacy leakage; conversely, input perturbation eliminates this trust assumption but often suffers from severe utility degradation due to excessive noise. To address these problems, we propose DL-LDP, a novel framework that alleviates the utility loss inherent in input perturbation through two key strategies. First, we employ a piecewise mechanism that applies bounded perturbation to normalized data, thereby maximizing the probability that perturbed values fall within high-utility intervals. Second, we integrate a strategic dropout mechanism during training to counteract model bias induced by the added noise. Theoretically, we show that DL-LDP generates perturbed data that maintains a linear correlation with original features, enabling the model to effectively learn latent representations, while the dropout technique reduces the misclassification of non-feature regions. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that DL-LDP not only significantly outperforms traditional input perturbation methods but also surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) gradient perturbation techniques. Notably, on the CIFAR-10 dataset with a privacy budget of ϵ=5, DL-LDP achieves an accuracy increase of approximately 13% compared to SOTA gradient methods, while reducing the model loss from 1.397 to 0.520. DL-LDP enables individuals to contribute data for improving intelligent services without compromising their personal privacy to service providers.

title: MSTDF-AD: Modeling spatiotemporal dependency fusion for non-stationary time series anomaly detection
abstract: Existing time series anomaly detection methods often rely on stationarity assumptions, struggling with real-world non-stationary factors, such as trend shifts and seasonal fluctuations, which result in high false alarms, missed detections, and inadequate spatiotemporal modeling. This paper proposes a novel modeling spatiotemporal dependency fusion for non-stationary time series anomaly detection (MSTDF-AD), featuring three key innovations: (1) Spatiotemporal fusion decomposition: Jointly models complex dependencies while extracting stable components; (2) Multiscale feature fusion: Integrates cross-scale information to enhance local–global anomaly perception; (3) Dynamic KL divergence weight: Using simulated annealing to adaptively optimize VAE training, mitigating posterior collapse. Evaluated on five real-world datasets, industrial control (SWaT), cloud services (PSM), hardware maintenance (SMD), and aerospace monitoring (MSL/SMAP), MSTDF-AD achieves a 96.47% average F1-score, outperforming 19 baseline methods (e.g., +2.58% over GDCMAD, +0.21% over MtsCID), with exceptional performance in hardware fault detection (SMD: 93.94%) and spacecraft telemetry (SMAP: 97.85%), validating its effectiveness in anomaly detection tasks. The code is available at https://github.com/Conviss/MSTDF-AD.

title: NMFL: Coupling probabilistic diffusion dynamics with fitness landscape analysis for influence maximization problem in social networks
abstract: Existing meta-heuristics for the NP-hard Influence Maximization (IM) problem are often constrained by inefficient fitness evaluation and a lack of structural awareness. To address these challenges, this study proposes NMFL, a fitness landscape-aware discrete Nelder–Mead algorithm. Specifically, a Probabilistic Recursion Estimation (PRE) fitness function, modeled on the Bernoulli distribution, which utilizes engineering linearization and Taylor series approximations, is developed to balance evaluation accuracy with computational efficiency. Furthermore, the discrete solution space is mapped onto a fitness landscape, where a novel discrete centroid indicator is introduced to guide evolutionary trajectories and rectify search deviations. Experimental results on six real-world networks, ranging from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of nodes, demonstrate that NMFL outperforms mainstream meta-heuristics by an average of 8.1% in influence spread. Crucially, it achieves solution quality comparable to greedy benchmarks while reducing computational time by several orders of magnitude, offering a scalable blueprint for decoding IM dynamics.

title: How does digital hoarding affect user resistance to social media switching behavior: The role of nostalgia, inertia and mindfulness
abstract: Social media has afforded users unprecedented affordances for accumulating digital content and fragments and emerged as a fundamental space for digital hoarding and emotional connection, increasing the likelihood that consumers will remain on existing platforms due to resource lock-in, path dependency, or social connections. This study identifies a mechanism linking digital hoarding on social media to user switching resistance, grounded in conservation of resources theory. We conducted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, involving quantitative analysis of a three-wave time-lagged survey of 316 social media users from an initial pool of 725 using SmartPLS 4.0 and 20 follow-up interviews for qualitative interpretation. Findings reveal that digital hoarding on social media directly predicts user resistance to switching, while also driving nostalgia and inertia, which subsequently influence user resistance to switching. Mindfulness moderates the effect of inertia and digital hoarding on user resistance to switching. Further multigroup analysis demonstrates that there are generational differences in the pathways of our model. Augmenting these findings, the interview data offer a more nuanced explanation regarding how the above five constructs materialize and how digital hoarding contexts function and interact with nostalgia and inertia as users engage in resistance to switching. Importantly, the qualitative evidence also captures several novel insights that extend beyond the scope of the quantitative results. Our research brings valuable insights into the dynamic processes underlying user resistance to switching in the social media context from a novel perspective and challenges mainstream calls to eliminate digital hoarding by highlighting its role in fostering user stickiness and informing platform design strategies for digital consumption experiences.

title: LiteKV: A KV cache compression method for efficient inference on resource-constrained devices
abstract: Transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on Key-Value (KV) cache to accelerate autoregressive decoding, but memory and compute requirements still grow with context length, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices. Existing training-free KV cache compression methods mainly rely on attention-driven retention heuristics, which may under preserve structurally informative tokens under tight cache budgets, especially when such tokens are not strongly highlighted by local or cumulative attention signals. As a result, long-range evidence and semantic continuity can be weakened in long-context inference. We propose LiteKV, a training-free KV cache management strategy that addresses this limitation with a three-ring cache structure and a Semantic Shift Awareness (SSA) mechanism. LiteKV maintains a recent window, a heavy-hitter region, and an overview zone, while SSA introduces a semantic-momentum signal to complement attention-based retention and improve the preservation of transition-relevant tokens. We evaluate LiteKV on Qwen 3, Llama 3.1, and Mistral 7B models against Full KV, StreamingLLM, H2O, and SnapKV on several tasks. On LongPPL over 20k tokens from WikiText-103, LiteKV reduces perplexity from 12.74 for H2O to 10.68, corresponding to a 16.2% reduction. In the Needle-in-a-Haystack task, LiteKV’s retrieval accuracy matches the Full KV baseline in several segments and remains substantially stronger than H2O and StreamingLLM in entity-specific retrieval. LiteKV also remains robust on L-Eval benchmark under aggressive compression. For example, on Qwen3-30B with a 3.125% cache budget, LiteKV retains 83.5% of the Full KV score on meeting summarization task and 99.1% on review summarization task. These results suggest a favorable memory–quality trade-off for long-context inference across multiple model families.

title: SocLitGen: An LLM-assisted framework for automated literature review in social sciences
abstract: Existing automated literature review technologies primarily target computer science contexts and face significant adaptability challenges in social science disciplines. Addressing this gap, this study proposes SocLitGen, a seven-module framework specifically designed for social science literature review generation. SocLitGen was evaluated using review tasks from management and economics topics on a corpus of 1,559,141 papers, comparing against Naive RAG, AutoSurvey, and graduate student writing. Baseline comparisons show that in citation quality (recall and precision), SocLitGen outperforms Naive RAG by at least 39.9%; in content quality (academic professionalism, structural rationality, and language fluency), SocLitGen outperforms AutoSurvey by at least 13.1% and graduate student writing by at least 9.5%. Cross-context evaluations reveal differentiated performance patterns: cross-disciplinary analysis confirms consistent performance across management and economics; cross-model experiments show Qwen2.5 performs optimally in academic and structural dimensions while GLM-4 excels in language fluency; cross-literature scale analysis demonstrates that large-scale sets enhance professionalism and structure but reduce fluency.

title: CIM: Interpretable model with consistency representation and prompt learning
abstract: Supervised learning that rely exclusively on class labels often suffer from insufficient guidance for training deep neural networks (DNNs), resulting in inherent model biases and limited interpretability. To address these challenges, this study introduces the Consistent Interpretable Model (CIM) for interpretable image classification. The proposed CIM is constructed based on three core components. First, causal inference analysis is employed to model the learning process of DNNs, establishing a theoretical foundation for identifying spurious feature-task correlations. Second, the unbiasedness of task features is ensured by aligning original image embeddings with task-relevant prior knowledge. Finally, rich semantic knowledge from contrastively pre-trained text encoders is exploited to strengthen the alignment between the model’s task feature distribution and real-world scenarios. Extensive experiments show that CIM substantially improves DNN performance, particularly in fine-grained and out-of-distribution classification (achieving over 8% improvement in Top-1 accuracy) tasks. Moreover, CIM outperforms existing methods in terms of causality (with over a 10% gain in Grad-CAM’s Overall metric) and consistency (with over a 4% gain in Grad-CAM’s CH metric) of model explanations. Additionally, the alignment of prompt text representations with task object representations in CIM enables textual explanations for DNN decisions. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/DLAIResearch/CIM.

title: S2RAF: A Semantic and Structure aware ReAsoning Framework for question answering over textual graphs
abstract: Textual graph question answering (Graph QA) aims to answer natural language queries by reasoning over graphs with textual attributes. Existing methods typically introduce secondary or noisy information when retrieving question-relevant subgraphs. Moreover, the information gap between graph structure and semantics often results in information loss, negatively impacting model performance. In this paper, we propose a Semantic and Structure aware ReAsoning Framework (S2RAF), which integrates structural and semantic information for precise retrieval of relevant facts and high-quality injection of reasoning knowledge. Specifically, we first develop a question-guided retrieval mechanism to dynamically adjust node weights for the adaptive extraction of targeted subgraphs. Then, a dual-level optimization strategy is introduced, combining an LLM-based reasoning scorer with a similarity-based semantic scorer to jointly optimize the subgraphs, effectively denoising and focusing on critical facts. Finally, we propose G-Adapter, which dynamically injects graph information into LLMs, achieving graph-text fusion and enhancing reasoning ability over graphs. Extensive experiments on four Graph QA datasets demonstrate that S2RAF successfully achieves competitive performance. Particularly, S2RAF outperforms existing methods by 5.63%, 5.36%, and 23.83% on ExplaGraphs, SceneGraphs, and CWQ datasets, respectively, confirming the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed model.

title: A comprehensive review of Artificial Intelligence in Qur’anic research: Trends, methods, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a transformative tool in the Holy Qur’an domain, supporting diverse tasks including recitation accuracy assessment (e.g., Tajweed rule detection), semantic exegesis (e.g., contextual retrieval of Tafsir), verse classification (e.g., identifying rulings or themes), and memorization support (e.g., providing feedback on recitation accuracy). However, applying AI in the domain of the Holy Qur’an requires prioritizing religious principles and ensuring a high level of accuracy in accordance with those principles. This study provides a comprehensive review of the role of AI in Qur’anic research, based on an analysis of 151 core studies. These studies have been systematically analyzed and evaluated using a well-defined set of evaluation criteria. It is structured around six thematic axes: trends, tasks, techniques, resources, challenges, and ethical concerns, each formulated as a distinct research question. This article also develops several taxonomies and classifications, providing a structured framework for researchers and practitioners to navigate the complexities of applying AI in Qur’anic research. The first taxonomy, a generic taxonomy, highlights key tasks, approaches, modalities, resources, subjects, and languages, offering a comprehensive overview of the field. Another classification focuses on the AI techniques applied in this domain, including machine/deep learning, NLP, speech recognition, computer vision, and ontology-, rule-, and semantic-based approaches. A further taxonomy is developed to address the challenges in this field, categorizing them into Qur’anic-related, computational processing, Arabic NLP-related, limitations of resources, and ethical and religious considerations. It also provides a critical analysis of current approaches in the field, identifies key limitations, and recommends future research directions to enhance progress and address existing challenges. Ultimately, this research serves as a thorough guide, deepening the understanding of the AI landscape in the field and offering valuable insights for developing reliable, advanced, and sensitive AI techniques.

title: ALD2: Adaptive layer-wise denoising decoding for hallucinations mitigation in large vision-language models
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong reasoning capabilities by leveraging Large language models (LLMs). However, hallucination remains a challenge for many LVLMs. Through our experiments, we identify that existing noise in shallow layers often leads to unstable token predictions during reasoning. We find that visual token pruning technologies along with multiplicative decoding effectively mitigate this interference. Building on this insight, we propose Adaptive Layer-wise Denoising Decoding (ALD2), a novel framework that mitigates hallucinations within LVLMs by dynamically selecting an optimal shallow layer for visual-token pruning and multiplicatively fusing the denoised distributions with that of the final layer. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks (CHAIR with 500 images; POPE with 500 images; MME with 2374 cases) demonstrate that ALD2 consistently improves the accuracy across multiple LVLMs. For example, we achieve an average accuracy improvement of 5.61% on POPE metrics using the InstructBlip-Vicuna-7B model and an increase of 88.56 MME score points in the MME evaluation benchmark with the LLaVA-Next-8B model. Code available at: https://github.com/Yangmrl-nlp/Adaptive-Layer-wise-Denoising-Decoding.

title: Mining temporally aware patterns with fuzzy utility measures under dynamically moving window environments
abstract: Mining high temporal fuzzy utility patterns from data streams is important for interpretable real-time information processing. However, prior incremental methods that handle the entire data suffer from inefficiency with the continuous stream arrival, which is problematic in real-time information processing environments. Moreover, handling concept drift is critical, as the data distribution changes over time and information from older data becomes less representative in current conditions. To handle the limitation, a novel approach is introduced for extracting high temporal fuzzy utility patterns from data streams, adopting dynamically moving windows via a sliding window strategy to handle concept drift. Rather than processing the entire accumulated streams, the proposed approach efficiently manages the most recent fixed-size batches. Furthermore, pruning strategies optimized for the moving window are adopted to minimize the search space. Comprehensive evaluations on six real-world datasets with four membership functions indicate that the proposed approach demonstrates enhanced runtime performance with competitive memory usage, achieving up to 40% improvement in runtime. Scalability evaluation demonstrates its scalability across five increasing transaction sizes, showing at least 1.34 times smaller runtime growth than comparison methods under on-par memory usage. Statistical performance on 30 sampled thresholds and sensitivity analyses show its stable efficiency to parameter variations, while accuracy analysis on a total of 240 samples indicates that it obtains results without any pattern loss. Moreover, the analysis of result pattern characteristics reveals that the proposed approach effectively captures recent data trends, and the case study under the concept drift shows its applicability in various stream environments.

title: Community detection in multiplex networks via multiview layer-specific graphformers-based embedding with heuristic weighting and refinement strategies
abstract: Community detection in multiplex networks is a challenging task due to heterogeneous layer structures, weak inter-layer consistency, and noisy relations. The main objective of this study is to design an effective community detection framework that can adaptively exploit layer-specific information while preserving meaningful global structures across layers. To address this problem, we propose a new method named MLGFA, which integrates multiview layer-specific GraphFormers-based embeddings with heuristic layer weighting and label refinement strategies. The method first obtains expressive node embeddings for each layer, capturing both local and semi-local structural patterns. Then, an adaptive layer weighting mechanism is applied to quantify the relative contribution of each layer during node similarity computation. Finally, a deep learning-based boundary node reassignment process is employed to refine ambiguous community labels. The proposed framework by combining heuristic initialization, transformer-based representation, adaptive layer weighting, and deep filtering of the detected communities provides an efficient approach for identifying community structures in multiplex networks. The proposed framework is evaluated on several real-world and synthetic multiplex networks generated using the LFR benchmark. Experimental results are compared against several state-of-the-art methods, including GenLouvain, Infomap, MDLPA, LCDMN, MVGL, MPBTV, DGFM3, and LART. The results show that MLGFA consistently achieves higher or competitive performance in terms of NMI and ARI, especially under high mixing parameters. For example, obtained results on multiple real-world and synthetic multiplex datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over the best competing baseline methods, with relative NMI gains ranging from 0.26% to 122.81% across real networks and from 9.23% to 22.04% on LFR benchmarks. This indicates the high capability of MLGFA in extracting the structure of real communities in multiplex networks. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/phdutm2009/Multiplex-Community-Detection.

title: Towards distribution-aware active learning for data-efficient neural architecture predictor
abstract: Neural Predictors (NPs) are pivotal for efficient Neural Architecture Search (NAS) but suffer from limited accuracy due to the high cost of acquiring labeled training data. While active learning (AL) can mitigate this by prioritizing informative samples, existing methods suffer from selection bias under imbalanced data distributions, often sacrificing representativeness for diversity. To address this, we redefine the sample selection mechanism in AL and propose a Distribution-aware Active Learning framework for Neural Predictor (called DARE). The goal is to select samples that not only ensure diversity but also exhibit a high degree of generalizability, making them more representative of the underlying data distribution. Our approach first extracts architecture representations via a graph-based encoder enhanced with a consistency-driven objective. Then, a two-stage selection strategy identifies both globally diverse and locally reliable samples through progressive representation learning and refinement. For non-uniform data distributions, we further introduce an adaptive mechanism that anchors sampling to key regions with high similarity density, avoiding performance degradation caused by outliers. Extensive experiments on NAS-Bench-101, NAS-Bench-201, NAS-Bench-301, and DARTS demonstrate that DARE achieves state-of-the-art prediction performance with extremely scarce labeled data. For instance, on NAS-Bench-101, it outperforms the second-best baseline by 4.29% in Kendall’s Tau with only 424 samples. Furthermore, DARE efficiently identifies optimal architectures using as few as 100 queries on DARTS.

title: Noise-robust item modeling and dynamic multiview contrastive learning for multimodal recommendation
abstract: Multimodal recommender systems enhance recommendation accuracy by leveraging multimodal item information together with users’ interaction histories. Existing methods mainly use item–item semantic graphs and user–item interaction graphs to model item and user preferences. However, in item modeling, existing methods often overlook collaborative relationships between items, which makes it difficult to capture comprehensive item features. On the interaction side, they treat all interactions as equally reliable, overlooking differences across behavior types and their varying importance to users. To address these issues, we propose Noise-Robust Item Modeling and Dynamic Multiview Contrastive Learning (NRDMC), a novel method for multimodal recommendation. First, we extract latent collaborative signals between items from user–item interactions to enhance comprehensive modeling of item features. Second, we design intra-modal and cross-modal attention mechanisms. The intra-modal attention suppresses noise within each modality, while the cross-modal attention exploits complementary information across modalities. Finally, NRDMC adopts dynamic multi-view contrastive learning to capture latent behavior prototypes and their importance in user–item interactions. This enables the model to construct higher-quality contrastive views and improve recommendation performance. To ensure fair comparison, we evaluate NRDMC on three public Amazon Reviews benchmark datasets (Baby, Sports, and Clothing) under standard settings. Experimental results show that NRDMC consistently outperforms strong baselines, achieving average performance gains of 3.49%, 7.54%, and 1.64% on Baby, Sports, and Clothing, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/50hehe/NRDMC.

title: SADET: Efficient active suspension control for intensive care ambulances via self-attention and deterministic experience tracking
abstract: High-dimensional vibration control in intensive care ambulances demands algorithms that are simultaneously high-performance and lightweight for real-world deployment. This study proposes the SADET algorithm, which integrates a Self-Attention (SA) mechanism with Deterministic Experience Tracking (DET) within an asymmetric strong Critic and weak Actor architecture. Built upon a 7-DOF ambulance dynamics model and a domain-randomization training protocol over ISO 8608 random road profiles, the SA-enhanced Critic enables an extremely lightweight Actor, with the derived SADET-n requiring only 124 parameters, representing a 99.9 % reduction from the DET baseline. Experimental results demonstrate that the top-performing SADET-x variant achieves vertical vibration suppression improvements of 62.9 %, 56.4 %, and 11.0 % over DDPG, TD3, and DET respectively, while reducing the root mean square values of roll and pitch accelerations by 75.4 % and 56.5 %. Generalization studies on 400 unseen road profiles spanning Classes A through D, vehicle speeds from 10 to 50 m/s, and sprung mass variations of ±500 kg confirm robust cross-scenario adaptability, and dedicated fault-injection tests further verify that performance is sustained under sensor noise and intermittent data loss representative of production automotive sensor networks. Comparative power analysis additionally shows that SADET delivers state-of-the-art comfort improvement at an actuator power consumption no higher than that of substantially less effective baselines. The present work establishes a deployable lightweight framework for the application of deep reinforcement learning to complex real-world control systems and provides a meaningful advance in the safety and comfort of medical transportation.

title: LoTTA: Low-rank test-time adaptation for unsupervised tabular anomaly detection
abstract: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection aims to identify anomalous samples in tabular data without labeled examples, relying on the core assumption that the training set contains only normal samples. Consequently, existing methods typically force the model to overfit the training data, leveraging metrics such as the reconstruction error to separate anomalies during inference. However, due to the inherent limitation of the training data, it cannot encompass all possible normal patterns, which often causes existing methods to misclassify unseen normal samples as anomalies and lead to a high false positive rate. To address this issue, we propose LoTTA, a novel method that enhances the robustness of unsupervised tabular anomaly detection through Low-rank Test-Time Adaptation. Specifically, LoTTA operates in two stages. First, a pseudo-label generator is constructed by jointly training two self-supervised tasks with a shared encoder. Second, the low-rank test-time adaptation is performed, leveraging pseudo-labels to dynamically adjust the model to the normal distribution of test data while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Anomalies are finally identified based on the reconstruction error from the fine-tuned encoder–decoder model. Extensive experiments on 20 widely used benchmarks demonstrate that LoTTA achieves state-of-the-art performance, with an average AUC-PR across all datasets approximately 9.98% higher than that of previous leading models.

title: Unveiling heterogeneity in tourist-generated content quality: A large language model approach with multi-dimensional analysis
abstract: The rapid growth of tourist-generated content demands scalable and reliable quality assessment methods. This study introduces an LLM-driven framework that combines parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompt engineering to evaluate content quality accurately and interpretably. Applied to 484,930 reviews from MaFengWo, TripAdvisor, and Ctrip, the approach achieves superior performance (RMSE=0.3040, NDCG@100=0.500, BERTScore=77.95%) with 9 × higher efficiency. Spatial-temporal-semantic analyses reveal platform-specific quality patterns: MaFengWo exhibits prominent spatial centrality and stable temporal cointegration; TripAdvisor demonstrates simplified core-periphery structures with high volatility; Ctrip presents dynamic multicentricity particularly in Shanghai. Two domestic platforms, MaFengWo and Ctrip, expose systematic deficiency on the theme ‘Decision-making Plan’ (92.9∼96.4% lacking operational suggestions), while international TripAdvisor emphasizes ‘Practical Information’ and ‘Consumption Activity’ but 40.76% neglects original viewpoints. Heterogeneous network analysis identifies the behavioral signatures of high-reliability user—preference attachment, quality stability, and profile homogeneity. This work bridges theoretical rigor with operational scalability, demonstrating the potential of LLMs in content governance for digital tourism.

title: Structure-aware multi-teacher distillation for noise node classification
abstract: Knowledge distillation methods are very popular for solving the issue of noise node classification (NNC). However, these methods often fail to consider the structural information in graph data or output uncorrected prediction labels in the teacher models due to the influence of noise labels, resulting in degraded generalization performance for constructing a teacher–student training framework in the Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). To effectively address this challenge, we propose a new method named Structure-Aware Multi-Teacher Distillation (SAMTD) for noise node classification. Specifically, we first train multiple teacher models to ensure diversity. We then propose an embedding structure consistency distillation method to make the student model capture the rich structural information encoded in the teachers’ embeddings, as well as a prediction consistency weighting strategy to guide the student model to focus more on the reliable classification knowledge provided by the teacher models. Finally, we introduce a label enhancement module to continuously improve the overall label quality in the dataset. Experimental results on five real-world datasets under five different noise settings demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in classification accuracy, achieving an average improvement of 1.2%. The source code is at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SAMTD.

title: Bridging cross-modalities: Deep learning approaches for sketch-based 3D shape retrieval
abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized 3D content processing, elevating it to new levels and generating opportunities for intuitive interaction in virtual reality and industrial design. This article surveys the current landscape of Deep Learning-based Sketch-Based 3D Shape Retrieval (SBSR), focusing on its methodological evolution, effectiveness, and transformative impact. Based on a comprehensive review of over 130 studies published since the shift from handcrafted features, we discover that the potential of deep learning is particularly notable in a proposed four-level analytical framework: (1) Data Augmentation, examining sketch-domain techniques covering both non-learnable and learnable methods, as well as 3D shape-domain strategies based on point clouds and multi-view renderings, to mitigate data scarcity and enhance cross-modal consistency; (2) Feature Extraction, examining both static and dynamic (sequential) sketch representations, as well as the optimization of multi-view 3D representations; (3) Feature Alignment, categorizing strategies into unidirectional and bidirectional collaborations to bridge the semantic gap; and (4) Feature Matching, discussing metric learning advancements. Furthermore, by analyzing performance trends on key benchmarks (e.g., SHREC’13, SHREC’14), we highlight how the emergence of dynamic sketch modeling and the adoption of advanced multi-view 3D fusion strategies have significantly advanced the state-of-the-art. We conclude by emphasizing emerging frontiers—such as fine-grained, zero-shot, and scene-level retrieval. Finally, we introduces derivative tasks related to SBSR, discusses the key challenges faced by the research community, and proposes directions for future work.

title: Large Language Model Guided Graph Capsule Network with Local-Enhanced Alignment for Fake News Detection
abstract: Fake news on social media increasingly employs advanced deceptive strategies such as partial tampering and semantic misleading, which create a camouflaged consistency as it exhibits superficial coherence while harboring deeper inconsistencies. Existing detection methods treat cross-modal consistency as a monolithic concept and apply uniform strategies across all samples, rendering them insensitive to these nuanced deception patterns. To address the above issues, we propose the Large Language Model Guided Graph Capsule Network with Local-Enhanced Alignment (LGCNLA) model, a framework that systematically targets three critical dimensions of deception. First, at the semantic layer, we leverage Large Language Models to generate multi-perspective image-enhanced descriptions and supplement external entities, making implicit misleading cues explicit and providing richer contextual evidence. Second, at the structural layer, we construct a dual-channel heterogeneous graph capsule network whose dynamic routing mechanism preserves and amplifies local anomalous patterns that traditional graph based methods would smooth away. Third, at the distributional layer, we reformulate fake news detection as a hierarchical domain alignment task and introduce Local-Enhanced Maximum Mean Discrepancy, which separately aligns cross-modal distributions for real and fake news by minimizing divergence for authentic content while maximizing it for deceptive content, with locality-aware sensitivity to fine-grained inconsistencies. These three components function synergistically such that semantic enrichment provides the evidence, structural preservation highlights the anomalies, and distributional calibration defines the decision objective, thereby creating a holistic detection system that penetrates the camouflage of advanced deceptive strategies. Extensive experiments on Weibo, PolitiFact, and GossipCop datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, with accuracy improvements of at least 0.021, 0.029, and 0.036 respectively. The main code is available at https://github.com/sgysgywaityou/LGCNLA.

title: Data ethics in training large language models: A systematic review of machine-learning strategies and AI governance frameworks
abstract: We conduct a systematic review of ethical, technical, and governance challenges in the development and deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) and map these challenges to machine-learning (ML) strategies and governance practices reported in recent research. Using a PRISMA-guided process, we identified 1300 records, removed 220 duplicates (1080 unique), screened titles/abstracts, assessed 480 full texts, and included 101 studies (2021–2025) spanning healthcare, education, law, and public policy. From this corpus, we synthesize a taxonomy covering data curation, consent and privacy, bias representation, provenance, and auditability, and align each area with actionable ML controls (e.g., documentation and tracing, bias detection and mitigation, privacy-preserving learning, quality checks, and auditing). Building on this synthesis, we present an integrative governance framework that links dataset processes and ML controls to oversight checkpoints across the LLM lifecycle, supporting accountable development and deployment. Overall, the review provides an evidence-based map from ethical risks to implementable ML techniques and governance touchpoints to reduce harm and strengthen transparency and accountability in real-world LLM pipelines.

title: Memory-KGC: Memory-augmented structural learning for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), Knowledge Graphs (KGs) have become crucial for enhancing factual reasoning in Natural Language Processing (NLP). However, the inherent incompleteness of KGs limits their effectiveness, motivating the Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) task, which aims to infer missing relations from known facts. Existing KGC approaches often rely on local subgraphs, which restrict global structural utilization and may introduce noise. To address these limitations, we propose Memory-KGC, a memory-augmented structural learning framework for KGC. Our model introduces a trainable memory module that explicitly captures and stores the global structural knowledge of KGs, while integrating local subgraph information to refine entity matching and reduce noise. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including large-scale graphs with over 4.5 million entities, show that Memory-KGC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of both the memory module and subgraph integration.

title: EvoFlow: A closed-loop first-order optimizer for stable and robust deep learning
abstract: Robust and efficient optimization remains a central challenge in deep learning as widely used first-order methods are often sensitive to learning-rate selection and noisy or non-stationary gradients. This paper proposes EvoFlow, an O(d) first-order optimizer that introduces closed-loop update regulation through cosine-adaptive momentum with a momentum floor, alignment-based step amplification, and trust-aware suppression driven by inter-iteration gradient change. These mechanisms are designed to improve stability and reduce tuning sensitivity without costly second-order approximations or perturbation-based updates. Under bounded-preconditioner and momentum-tracking assumptions, the analysis establishes non-convex convergence at the standard first-order rate O(T−1/2) and derives stability bounds for the adaptive momentum and suppression terms. Experiments across vision, language understanding, generative modeling, and language modeling tasks show that EvoFlow is competitive with strong baselines under a unified tuning budget. Across CIFAR, GLUE, ImageNet-1K, and robustness benchmarks, EvoFlow demonstrates statistically supported improvements in selected settings and competitive performance in others, with effect sizes interpreted in relation to cross-seed variability where repeated trials are available. In GAN training, EvoFlow provides balanced generator–discriminator optimization and stable FID/KID trajectories. Under the tested WikiText-2 language-modeling protocol, EvoFlow obtains the lowest evaluation loss and perplexity on GPT-2, Pythia-1B, and GPT-Neo, while incurring higher resource costs than some throughput-optimized baselines. The results suggest that EvoFlow offers a theoretically grounded and practically implementable framework for feedback-regulated first-order optimization in stable deep learning.

title: Mask-enhanced and multi-view aligned heterogeneous graph for text classification
abstract: Text classification serves as a fundamental task in natural language processing, with widespread applications across multiple domains. Nevertheless, The existing sequence based methods have the problem of semantic isolation, and the graph neural network based methods have the problems of noise sensitivity and rough multi-source information fusion mechanism. To address these shortcomings, we introduce a Mask-Enhanced and Multi-View Aligned Heterogeneous Graph (MEMVAHG) method for text classification. First, three heterogeneous graphs: word–document graph, document–label graph and word–document–label graph, are systematically constructed to comprehensively model semantic relationships. Subsequently, graph augmentation strategy is incorporated into a graph encoder–decoder framework to enhance model robustness. Finally, a multi-view feature alignment mechanism is designed, where the distribution of document representations obtained from different graph decoders is constrained through the minimization of Maximum Mean Discrepancy loss, thereby achieving deep semantic collaboration. Multiple comparative experiments on 5 benchmark datasets demonstrate that, compared to the best baseline results on each dataset, MEMVAHG achieves improvements of at least 0.0167, 0.0151, 0.0138 and 0.0204 in Accuracy, Precision, micro-F1 and macro-F1 respectively across all datasets, demonstrating its consistent superiority and robust performance. The main code is available at https://github.com/sgysgywaityou/MEMVAHG.

title: Graph-prompted explainable fake news detection with multimodal large language models
abstract: As online news increasingly evolves into multimodal content, the rapid development of social media has intensified the spread of fake news, making multimodal fake news detection an important research problem. However, existing methods often fail to effectively leverage structural and textual information in propagation graphs, and they also suffer from limited knowledge coverage and weak information integration, which leads to poor interpretability and generalization. To address these issues, we propose a Graph Prompt-Augmented Multimodal (GPAM) framework for fake news detection. GPAM integrates textual content, visual evidence, and propagation structures by combining pretrained large vision-language models with graph neural networks. Specifically, we encode rumor propagation structures as soft prompts and transform structured user comments into hard prompts, enabling the model to jointly reason over multimodal and structural signals. Extensive experiments on the Pheme and Weibo benchmark datasets demonstrate strong performance, improving over current state-of-the-art multimodal methods by approximately 1.2% and 3.6%, respectively. Moreover, our model exhibits superior generalization, reducing performance degradation by over 20 percentage points in cross-dataset transfer settings, and delivers more faithful and informative explanations, achieving 17%–24% higher quality scores than existing LVLM-based approaches.

title: DADSA: Dual-Side Adaptive Deep Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
abstract: Most existing safety alignment methods for large language models (LLMs) constrain only the initial tokens of generation. However, safety signals decay with generation depth and these methods lack adaptivity in capturing deep-level unsafe signals. To tackle these issues, we propose Dual-Side Adaptive Deep Safety Alignment (DADSA), a deep safety alignment framework that adaptively models both generation depth and constraint strength. First, we extend existing safety benchmarks by constructing SafetyPre and HarmSafetyPre, comprising 510 instructions and 510 instruction–response pairs across 17 harmful categories, respectively, to support adaptive deep alignment. Furthermore, we develop a dual-track data regime that balances safety and utility. Second, we propose Adaptive Curriculum Safety Augmentation (ACSA), which combines adaptive risk-aware depth sampling based on token level refusal probabilities with a curriculum depth scheduler, gradually guiding the model from shallow refusal patterns to robust defenses over long contexts and harmful semantic regions. Third, we present Adaptive-γ Soft-Constrained Fine-Tuning (Aγ-SFT), which adaptively adjusts token-level constraint strength as a function of generation position and safety deviation, yielding an optimization paradigm that is stable while preserving shallow safety and enforcing strong deep level refusal. Extensive experiments on mainstream LLMs show that ACSA lowers attack success rate by 21.86% under GCG attacks, and Aγ-SFT lowers attack success rate by 51.27% under fine-tuning attacks.

title: A benchmark framework for detecting cyberbullying: Conceptual and operational definitions, dataset development, and methods evaluation
abstract: Cyberbullying detection is vital for maintaining public order online. Yet the lack of standardized benchmark frameworks makes it difficult for datasets and models to reflect cyberbullying’s essential attributes. In particular, many studies focus only on classifying content as aggressive or non-aggressive while overlooking other dimensions, a problem that has long received insufficient attention. To fill this gap, this study introduces a new benchmark framework for cyberbullying detection, covering conceptual and operational definitions, dataset development, and methods evaluation. Specifically, this study: (1) proposes conceptual and operational definitions that reflect the four core characteristics of cyberbullying: targeting, aggression, repetition, and harmfulness; (2) publicly releases a relatively large-scale Chinese Multimodal Cyberbullying dataset (texts with emojis) that strictly follows the definition of cyberbullying and can reflect its core characteristics, containing 20,211 annotated instances; and (3) provides results for eight baseline methods covering classical machine learning, encoder-based and decoder-based Large Language models (LLMs). The results show that BERT trained on the developed dataset achieves the best overall performance. In terms of PRAUC, BERT surpasses the second-best LR method by 13.88%, and outperforms the 10-shot instruction-optimized Qwen2.5-7B and DeepSeek-V3.2 by 23.61% and 20.6%, respectively. Attention and SHAP analyses further indicate that BERT effectively captures cyberbullying characteristics and offers interpretability. The framework standardizes definitions, characteristics, data collection and splitting, and evaluation metrics and protocols, while allowing flexible design for harmfulness specification and event selection. All data and code are publicly available.

title: TPTSI: Ternary paradigm-driven and dual-framework semantic interaction techniques for metaphor recognition
abstract: Metaphor recognition is a challenging task in natural language processing (NLP) due to the subtle semantic nuances and dynamic contextual features of metaphors, which existing methods fail to fully capture. To address this issue, we propose a Ternary Paradigm-Driven and Dual-Framework Semantic Interaction model (TPTSI) for metaphor recognition. Specifically, we design a ternary paradigm construction module that combines positive examples, anchor sentences and negative examples to excavate the metaphorical features of sentences in depth. We also develop a Dual-Framework Semantic Interaction Module integrating Selectional Preference Violation (SPV) and Metaphor Identification Procedure (MIP) to assess the semantic fit and deviation of target words in sentence contexts, enhancing the model’s understanding of metaphorical semantic structures. Extensive experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets with distinct scales and characteristics: MOH-X (1849 target words, 1702 sentences), TroFi (4387 target words, 4269 sentences) and VUA-20 (189,008 target words, 16,506 sentences). TPTSI significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines, yielding 1.4%, 2.4% and 4.5% F1-score improvements on the MOH-X, TroFi and VUA-20 datasets respectively. Ablation experiments further validate the indispensability of each core component, with the ternary paradigm construction module leading to up to 25.9%, 3.6% and 12.8% F1-score gains on the MOH-X, TroFi and VUA-20 datasets respectively.

title: Asynchrony as information: Predicting technology transfer opportunities through science–technology knowledge lag
abstract: Predicting technology transfer opportunities bridges the gap between science and technology (S&T) knowledge discoveries and industrial applications. Constrained by the perspective of single technology transfers, prior studies cannot capture the temporal evolution of technology transfer opportunities at the industry level. Furthermore, they overlook S&T asynchrony, which signifies more than a temporal delay and embodies forward-looking commercial potential of technology. To address this, this paper proposes a prediction framework that operationalizes S&T knowledge lag to represent this asynchrony. First, to resolve terminological discrepancies between S&T knowledge, we construct a sub-technology list and fine-tune an LLM to map knowledge texts to unified sub-technologies, achieving semantic alignment. Subsequently, we construct temporal co-occurrence networks for S&T knowledge and employ time-lag cross-correlation to quantify the temporal knowledge lag between sub-technologies as an implicit network attribute. Finally, we design a graph-based dual-stream attention mechanism with a gated fusion strategy to integrate this implicit lag attribute with the explicit transfer structure. This mechanism adaptively balances the structural and attribute streams, enabling accurate and interpretable prediction. Experiments on an AI dataset demonstrate that the model exhibits superior performance in 1-step, 3-step, and 5-step ahead predictions, achieving F1-score improvements of 1.6%, 2.3%, and 6.88%, respectively, over the best benchmark model. Crucially, the value of S&T knowledge lag becomes increasingly pronounced as the prediction step extends. This model empowers the industry to proactively anticipate technological evolution and identify commercially viable opportunities.

title: Dynamic cross-instance context mining for multimodal sentiment analysis
abstract: Contextual modeling is pivotal in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA). Existing methods primarily rely on an instance-centric paradigm, which focuses on intra-modal dependencies (refining single-modality features) and inter-modal interactions (fusing cross-modality cues) within a single utterance. This isolated approach fails to exploit cross-instance semantic correlations, making models susceptible to local modality noise and incomplete expressions. To bridge this gap, we propose DC2M, a framework that shifts the focus from static single-sample fusion to dynamic cross-instance context mining. Our technical highlights are twofold: (i) the Adaptive Context Mining Module (ACMM), which captures cross-instance emotional evolution by retrieving the top-K relevant samples as semantic anchors, effectively increasing the contextual information gain; and (ii) the Heterogeneous Feature Fusion Module (HFFM), which optimizes intra-sample complementarity. Unlike traditional models that treat each utterance independently, DC2M performs utterance-level sentiment prediction enhanced by cross-instance contextual information from semantically related utterances. Experiments on the CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI benchmarks show that DC2M achieves competitive performance, reaching 89.33% and 87.62% Acc-2, respectively. Notably, DC2M outperforms fine-tuned Qwen-1.8B by 3.31% and ChatGLM3-6B by 0.77% in Acc-7, despite a substantially more lightweight architecture. Ablation studies confirm that ACMM and HFFM synergistically enhance contextual representation learning.

title: ECO-SFL: Efficient collaborative Split Federated Learning for mitigating stragglers via resource heterogeneity in IoT devices
abstract: Split Federated Learning (SFL) enables resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices to participate in training large-scale deep neural networks by leveraging the server’s computational capabilities. However, the inclusion of these devices introduces severe latency bottlenecks caused by slower participants (known as stragglers), which forces an unsustainable reliance on the server for workload offloading. This, in turn, leads to excessive server-side resource consumption and processing congestion, even interrupting the overall training process. To address these challenges, we introduce ECO-SFL, an efficient collaborative SFL framework that uniquely transforms resource heterogeneity from a performance barrier into a driving force for reducing latency and increasing the system’s tolerance to stragglers. Specifically, we design a Layer-wise Collaborative Strategy (LCS) that dynamically forms teams by pairing high-performance “helper” clients with resource-constrained “recipient” clients, utilizing helpers’ idle time while waiting for server updates to process recipients’ residual workloads, thereby significantly reducing latency. To enable optimal team formation and workload allocation, we design a lightweight Roofline-based time estimation method that allows the server to predict each client’s layer-wise processing latency locally without imposing extra computation or model loading on clients. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed ECO-SFL effectively mitigates the straggler problem while maintaining accuracy and convergence performance. Especially under the hardware disparity configuration, ECO-SFL demonstrates significant advantages on ResNet-152, reducing system latency by more than 90% compared to baseline methods.

title: A synergistic causal-driven two-stage hierarchical adaptive integration paradigm with breakpoint segmentation for carbon price prediction
abstract: Accurate carbon price prediction is crucial for the global low‑carbon transition, yet non-stationarity and structural changes pose challenges. Validated on two Chinese carbon markets and the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), this study proposes a framework to address limitations of existing models in handling data breaks, causal insight and adaptability. It first employs a segmentation-guided multi-scale feature extraction (SG-MSFE) technique, which can detect breakpoints and capture multi-frequency components per segment. DoWhy causal inference technique then filters key external drivers for these components. From a diverse pool, optimal base models are selected per component using a noise-injected scoring mechanism balancing accuracy and stability. A hierarchical ensemble strategy is applied: Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) integrates component predictions locally for each segment, forming independent ensemble models. Then Q-learning dynamically assigns weights globally to these models for the final prediction, adapting to real-time market dynamics. This design enhances interpretability through segmentation context, explainable causal drivers, transparent model selection, and dynamic weights revealing market regime relevance. In the Hubei market, the framework achieved mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.0624, 0.1293, 0.5381%. Outperforming other advanced models, it shows superior forecasting and potential for broader applicability.

title: Labels matter: Incorporating label knowledge into dual branch knowledge distillation framework for long-tailed ICD code assignment
abstract: Deep learning-based automated International Classification of Diseases (ICD) code assignment is essential and valuable task for modern healthcare systems. However, due to the long-tailed distribution of ICD codes, the data-driven deep learning-based approaches perform poorly on rare diseases. To address this challenge, we propose a novel dual-branch knowledge distillation (DBKD) framework that explicitly incorporates label knowledge for long-tailed ICD code assignment. The proposed framework introduces two key innovations: (1) the joint integration of label semantics, label hierarchy and label co-occurrence to enhanced feature learning and classifier learning, and (2) a dual-branch knowledge distillation strategy that balances discriminative feature learning with less-biased classifier learning. We evaluate DBKD on publicly available datasets MIMIC-III and a private Chinese electronic medical record dataset, used solely as an external validation to assess generalization. Experimental results demonstrate that DBKD achieves competitive performance and superior generalization capability in long-tailed learning scenario. Further interpretability analysis highlights credibility and clinical utility of our proposed method. The source code and related dataset are available at https://github.com/Cai-Linkun/DBKD.

title: Fine-grained sequential recommendation with prototype-level individualized opinion adjustment
abstract: Current review-based sequential recommendations typically leverage item attribute content to infer user interest for next-item prediction. However, due to the semantic complexity of review texts, existing approaches often struggle to accurately capture fine-grained individualized opinion biases in user behaviors. To address this limitation, we propose POARec, a fine-grained sequential recommendation framework based on prototype-level individualized opinion adjustment. POARec leverages an LLM-based agent to extract fine-grained attribute-opinion pairs from raw reviews, enabling the construction of comprehensive and interpretable user and item opinion profiles. Building on these profiles, the framework introduces a prototype-guided opinion adjustment mechanism to learn group-level attribute prototypes. These prototypes are used to calibrate semantic noise and alleviate sparsity in individual opinion representations to model fine-grained attribute-aware sequence embeddings for next-item prediction. We evaluated POARec on four real-world datasets, Amazon Sports, Amazon Beauty, Amazon Clothing, and Yelp. Experimental results show that POARec improves Hit@10 and NDCG@10 by 3.03% and 14.95% on the Sports dataset, 4.86% and 6.93% on the Beauty dataset, 7.72% and 11.42% on the Clothing dataset, and 9.03% and 4.84% on the Yelp dataset, respectively. Furthermore, visualization results confirm that the fine-grained opinion adjustment mechanism enhances model interpretability.

title: A secure federated feature selection framework for horizontally distributed medical data
abstract: Feature selection is important for reducing dimensionality of medical data that is distributed across institutional silos. Existing federated feature selection (FFS) techniques, including evolutionary or population based methods, still suffer from local optima, slow convergence, and limited privacy protection. We propose a secure and robust framework for feature selection over horizontally partitioned medical data. Specifically, we introduce Binary Heterogeneous Comprehensive Learning Symbiotic Organism Search (BHCLSOS) and its federated extension (FBHCLSOS). In FBHCLSOS, each client runs BHCLSOS locally, and a central server computes mutual information (MI) from ɛ-differentially private contingency tables uploaded by the clients. These statistics form informative feature groups that guide and refine the clients’ search in future rounds, which improves the quality of feature subsets without exposing raw data or statistics. BHCLSOS is further improved with reverse-bit and forward-bit mutation to preserve population diversity and reduce feature selection bias. Experiments on 15 public medical datasets with a KNN classifier show that FBHCLSOS outperforms several state-of-the-art FFS methods in terms of accuracy and F1-score under strict privacy constraints. The Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on 135 pairwise comparisons indicate that FBHCLSOS is significantly better in 110 cases (81.5%), with the remaining comparisons being statistical ties and no losses (p<0.05). This consistent dominance indicates that FBHCLSOS reliably extracts more relevant features than its peer competitors. A scalability study conducted as part of the experiments shows only minor accuracy degradation when the federation size grows, which indicates that FBHCLSOS can scale well to larger multi-institutional deployments.

title: Robust Copyright Verification for Remote Sensing Datasets via Latent Space Embedding
abstract: Existing copyright protection for remote sensing datasets is severely limited by the fragility of pixel-domain watermarks against inevitable lossy compression. To address this, we propose LSBI, a compression-resilient latent space backdoor injection framework. This framework constructs triggers via a dual orthogonal projection mechanism and utilizes feature consistency to constrain the embedding position, anchoring the trigger features into compression-robust subspaces to ensure both imperceptibility and robustness. Experimental results on the EuroSAT, PatternNet, and NWPU-RESISC45 datasets demonstrate that LSBI effectively balances imperceptibility, utility, and robustness. Regarding imperceptibility, the method achieves high quantitative visual fidelity with a PSNR exceeding 31 dB and an SSIM above 0.97. In terms of utility, the classifier maintains high clean accuracy with fluctuations generally within approximately 5% as the watermark injection rate increases, indicating efficient decoupling between watermark and original texture features. Regarding robustness, even in black-box scenarios with unknown compression strengths, the method maintains consistent performance across mainstream architectures such as ResNet and VGG. Specifically, under strong compression with a quality factor as low as Q=50, the verification success rate consistently remains above 92%. Moreover, the framework exhibits strong robustness against model fine-tuning and pruning, maintaining success rates exceeding 97% and 92% respectively, providing a robust mechanism for the copyright verification of remote sensing datasets in open environments.

title: Scientific hypothesis prediction based on large language models and causal graphs
abstract: Scientific hypotheses connect known facts with unknown possibilities. This study proposes a novel approach for scientific hypothesis prediction by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with causal graphs. Using a corpus of over 60,000 academic publications, we extracted 115,484 structured causal variable pairs through a comparative analysis of 18 groups of LLMs. We then constructed a Causal Claim Network (CCN) to capture implicit causal relationships in the literature. Building on this network, we introduce LLMCCN, a hypothesis-inference algorithm. Unlike existing hypothesis-prediction approaches, LLMCCN jointly identifies independent and dependent variables, traces effect pathways, and pinpoints mediating and moderating mechanisms. It therefore yields interpretable causal propositions rather than mere link predictions. Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations show that LLMCCN surpasses existing baselines. The evaluations also show that it outperforms AI-only baselines in novelty and helpfulness, and that its effectiveness is further enhanced with the assistance of domain experts. To validate the generated hypotheses, we conducted a large-scale empirical case study by analyzing 47,181 annual reports and > 710,000 publicly disclosed invention patents. Rigorous econometric analyses confirmed the statistical significance of most findings at the 1% level. These results validate the theoretical novelty and practical relevance of our inferred hypotheses. This study offers an efficient and scalable framework for automated and interpretable hypothesis discovery.

title: From bibliometrics to AI safety: Measuring internal persona disruption in LLMs with the DI-Persona metric
