abstract: Persona shifts in Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly regarded as a latent safety risk, as they can disrupt internal reasoning pathways in ways that output-based evaluations often fail to detect. In this study, a new metric (DI-Persona) is introduced to quantify internal persona disruption by adapting the bibliometric Disruption Index (DI) to the dense internal representations of Transformer models. DI-Persona is assessed across four distinct model architectures (GPT-2, Qwen2.5–7B, Llama-3.1–8B and Gemma-2–9B) spanning 117M to 9B parameters, using a controlled evaluation suite of 2400 prompts forming 1200 contrastive scenarios across three safety-critical traits: evil, sycophancy, and hallucination. Results show consistent trait-specific disruption patterns across the tested model families. A distinct “hallucination vulnerability” was observed consistently across all four architectures (scores ranging from 0.0019 to 0.0046), suggesting that non-factual generation triggers a consistent restructuring of the model’s latent representations. Conversely, sycophancy exhibited a more model-dependent pattern: scores remained near zero in GPT-2 and Qwen2.5–7B, but were higher in Llama-3.1–8B and Gemma-2–9B. Because model scale, instruction tuning, and model-family differences vary together in the present comparison, this pattern should not be attributed to any one of these factors in isolation. These findings suggest that DI-Persona can be computed consistently across the tested Transformer architectures and may serve as a complementary internal diagnostic signal for persona stability. DI-Persona is presented as a complement to output-based safety evaluations, not as a standalone pre-deployment decision tool. A pilot behavior-linked validation is also reported, relating DI-Persona to harmful compliance, sycophantic agreement, and factual error rates.

title: A multi-scale spatio-temporal dynamic graph neural network for airborne network intrusion detection
abstract: Intrusion detection systems are a core component of airborne network security. Traditional machine learning approaches usually rely on fixed time-domain sliding windows for feature extraction, which results in limited receptive fields. To address the robustness limitations of convolutional neural networks that depend on such windowing mechanisms, this paper proposes a multi-scale perspective convolution module. In this module, perspective parameters and learnable parameters are configured across multiple scales to comprehensively capture airborne network communication patterns. To further capture the complex and dynamic spatial features of network traffic, a collaborative spatio-temporal learning framework is proposed, integrating a time-domain causal convolutional network with a spatial-domain dynamic graph neural network. Experimental results on the MIL-STD-1553 and CICIDS2017 airborne network datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 99% detection accuracy with low false alarm rates. Compared with the state-of-the-art baseline methods, the proposed method shows superior detection performance and strong potential for practical deployment.

title: MASSANet: Multiscale adaptive spectral–spatial dual-path attention network for motor imagery decoding from EEG
abstract: The decoding capability of electroencephalogram (EEG) motor imagery (MI) signals directly affects the performance of EEG-based brain–computer interface (BCI) systems. Effective MI-EEG decoding requires the joint extraction of spectral, spatial, and temporal features. However, conventional convolutional neural networks often struggle to capture broadband spectral characteristics and complementary multi-frequency features under noisy and non-stationary EEG conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a multiscale adaptive spectral–spatial dual-path attention network (MASSANet), which employs a spectral branch for multi-scale frequency pattern extraction, a spatial branch for discriminative electrode-related representation learning, and an attention-based fusion strategy to adaptively integrate complementary information. This design reduces the dependence on manual frequency-band selection and improves the robustness of MI-EEG decoding across different recording conditions. The proposed method is evaluated on three public benchmark datasets, including BCI Competition IV 2a, BCI Competition IV 2b, and OpenBMI. Experimental results show that MASSANet achieves classification accuracies of 74.46%/84.07%, 88.38%/88.85%, and 65.50%/87.09% under cross-session and within-session conditions, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness across different MI-EEG decoding scenarios. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Taowelll/MASSANet.

title: Explicit token modeling and hierarchical feature reasoning for multimodal fake news detection
abstract: Fake news dissemination poses serious challenges to information credibility, making multimodal fake news detection an important research problem. However, many existing methods rely heavily on implicit global alignment and encoders’ final-layer global representations, which can blur fine-grained token-patch correspondences and overlook semantic cues that emerge across intermediate layers, ultimately limiting detection performance. In this paper, we propose EMHR, a unified framework that couples explicit cross-modal consistency modeling with hierarchical semantic reasoning. Specifically, Explicit Token Modeling embeds token-patch consistency directly into cross-modal fusion, enabling the detector to capture subtle semantic mismatches that may be missed by implicit alignment. Moreover, Hierarchical Feature Reasoning progressively exploits intermediate textual representations to track semantic evolution across layers, providing fine-grained reasoning complementary to final-layer features. At the decision level, Confidence-Adaptive Feature Fusion aggregates multi-branch predictions via confidence-aware weighting, yielding more stable and discriminative outputs. Extensive experiments on Weibo17, Politifact, and GossipCop demonstrate the effectiveness of EMHR, delivering a 2.6% accuracy improvement on GossipCop over the strongest competing method and highlighting its superior ability to capture fine-grained cross-modal semantic discrepancies.

title: BJZM: A scalable framework for developing and benchmarking LLMs with an open leaderboard in Chinese literature
abstract: Despite advances in generative AI, large language models (LLMs) still struggle with Chinese literature. This literature is rich in artistry, history, culture, and emotion. Data scarcity and linguistic complexity limit LLMs’ domain-specific effectiveness. To address this, we propose BJZM, an open-source framework for Chinese literary LLMs. It integrates data, modeling, and evaluation into a unified ecosystem. BJZM has three key components. ChnLid is a diverse literary instruction dataset covering 6 tasks and 11 datasets, totaling 686K samples. BaiJia is a fine-tuned LLM available in 7B and 20B versions. ZhengMing is a benchmark with unseen datasets for robust evaluation. Experiments show that existing LLMs vary in performance. BaiJia generalizes well and excels in knowledge understanding and sentiment parsing. It rivals ChatGPT on several tasks. ZhengMing supported an evaluation workshop with 89 teams, many of which surpassed ChatGPT, demonstrating BJZM’s potential to advance literary AI. By providing data resources and an open leaderboard, BJZM facilitates research and promotes global appreciation of Chinese literary heritage. Code and data are available at https://github.com/isShayulajiao/BJZM.

title: Turning hallucinations into knowledge: Towards identifying clickbait using LLM-generated fallacies
abstract: Knowledge hallucination, commonly known as LLM-generated responses that contain ”false or misleading information” presented as fact, has become one of the spotlight issues in current LLM-related studies, which could be ruinous for discriminative tasks, including clickbait detection. Unlike cutting-edge research that aspires to eliminate the occurrence of ”Hallucinations”, this study attempts to turn LLM hallucinations into known ”false knowledge” instead of treating them as errors. To achieve this goal, we develop a novel supervised LLM reflection-based inference generation method, which allows LLMs to produce both correct (ground-truth) and incorrect (hallucinated) inferences for given news. We then deploy a three-BERT-Encoders-embraced clickbait detection model that conducts contrastive learning for the inferences, as well as the semantic consistency learning between news and inferences. We additionally design a student model via knowledge distillation to avoid the influence of supervised inference production, thereby enabling the model testing to be inference-free. Our experiment results verified on three clickbait datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms four kinds of baselines, including LLM prompting, SLM fine-tuning, and task-specific models across various metrics.

title: Causal deconfounding via multiplex spatial–temporal confounder disentanglement for next POI recommendation
abstract: Existing next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation methods often struggle to capture the true behavioral mechanisms underlying continuous spatial–temporal transitions, because complex cross-dimensional dependencies and latent confounding effects are insufficiently modeled. To address this issue, we propose DiMuST, a causal deconfounding framework for next POI recommendation. DiMuST characterizes user mobility transitions through a structured causal perspective that distinguishes dimension-specific confounders from joint-dependency confounders. Specifically, a variational multiplex graph autoencoder (VMGAE) is employed to learn proxy representations of different confounders from multiplex spatial–temporal transition graphs, a causal-invariant probabilistic fusion module is designed to recover shared collaborative transition structure, and independence as well as contrastive causal constraints are introduced to purify transition evidence by suppressing spurious correlations. We validated DiMuST on three real-world public datasets NYC, TKY, and CA, which contain between 105,267 and 239,401 check-in records. Compared with advanced models, DiMuST achieved average improvements of about 23.7% and 19.78% in Acc@K and MRR respectively. The experimental results demonstrate that DiMuST can effectively balance independent learning and collaborative verification and generate and interpretable representations.

title: What drives the popularity of user-generated derivative videos on video-sharing platforms? Exploring the influence of sentiments in video titles
abstract: This study investigates how content creators’ sentiments relate to the popularity of derivative videos on online video-sharing platforms. Using a large-scale dataset from Bilibili, China’s leading video-sharing platform, we apply a universal information extraction method to identify sentiments embedded in derivative video titles and analyze their association with video viewership. The results show that derivative videos with critical or negative sentiments are generally associated with higher viewership. Furthermore, this association is moderated by the creator’s social status and institutional endorsements. These findings provide important insights for content creators, platforms, and audiences, highlighting the role of emotional expression in shaping the online popularity of user-generated content.

title: FMCNS: Flow Matching with Causal-aware Negative Sampling for Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal recommendation integrates multimodal semantic information of items to model user preferences, where high-quality negative samples are critical for learning discriminative representations. Conventional heuristic methods select negatives based on interaction statistics rather than content semantics, failing to capture fine-grained cross-modal distinctions. Recent diffusion-based approaches generate modality-aware hard negatives but suffer from training instability and overlook exposure bias, where models conflate item visibility with genuine user interest. We propose FMCNS, a framework combining deterministic flow matching with causal intervention for negative sampling. FMCNS constructs straight-line flow trajectories from fused multimodal representations to hard negatives grounded in optimal transport theory, achieving semantically coherent and computationally efficient generation while avoiding noise accumulation inherent in diffusion models. To eliminate spurious correlations from exposure bias, we design a frequency-based causal intervention mechanism that decouples item exposure frequency from user selection probability, adaptively balancing flow-enhanced representations with collaborative embeddings to learn invariant preferences. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets against a wide range of representative baselines demonstrate that FMCNS achieves up to 4.69% and 4.47% improvements in Recall@10 and NDCG@10 over the state-of-the-art methods, while also exhibiting substantial advantages in training efficiency and negative sampling. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaxinji/FMCNS.

title: A transferable attack framework for face impersonation with surrogate ensemble and semantic guidance
abstract: Face recognition systems (FRS) have achieved remarkable progress in real-world applications but they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples. Such attacks manipulate benign face images to mislead deployed FRS, posing risks to identity authentication, financial assets, and personal security. However, existing face attack methods often transfer poorly across models and insufficiently exploit target-identity semantics, especially in impersonation attack tasks. To address these limitations, we propose S2FA, a transferable multimodal framework for face impersonation attacks that integrates semantic guidance with a scaled model ensemble strategy. S2FA employs a diffusion-based generator conditioned on textual prompts and visual features to produce semantically guided adversarial face candidates. A Grad-CAM-based semantic projector further localizes identity-relevant regions and constrains perturbation injection, while a scaled surrogate ensemble strategy improves cross-model transferability. These components are jointly optimized through a multi-objective loss that combines adversarial embedding similarity, CLIP-based semantic alignment, and perceptual regularization, thereby improving attack success while preserving visual fidelity. Experiments on benchmark datasets and multiple FRS show that S2FA outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 20% improvement in attack success rate in the best case. Ablation studies and additional analyses further confirm the contribution of each component.

title: M2SC2-AD: Multiscale Missing-aware Anomaly Detection framework with scale consistency constraints for sparse multi-sensor
abstract: Multi-sensor time series anomaly detection is critical for ensuring reliability in industrial production and IoT security systems. However, most existing methods are designed for complete data and cannot address missing data caused by communication interruptions and nonuniform sampling. To this end, we propose a Multiscale Missing-aware Anomaly Detection framework with Scale Consistency Constraints for sparse multi-sensor data (M2SC2-AD). Our approach leverages downsampling to generate multiscale series and corresponding missing masks from incomplete Multivariate Time Series (MTS), which are then processed through a novel Multiscale Missing-aware Embedding (MME) module to effectively model missing information. We introduce an Interaction-enhanced Component Decomposition Mixing (ICDM) module to decompose and fuse trend and seasonal components, capturing both long-term trends and cyclical information at each scale. To mitigate the information masking caused by missing values, we propose Scale-consistent Contrastive Learning (SCL), which guides the model to learn scale-invariant representations across different temporal resolutions. The framework is jointly optimized through an Observed Reconstruction Task (ORT) and a Masked Imputation Task (MIT), enabling end-to-end anomaly detection under sparse observation conditions. Extensive experiments on five real-world benchmarks and three additional datasets from distinct application domains demonstrate the superiority of our method. Specifically, M2SC2-AD achieves an average improvement in the F1 score of 2.19% across all benchmarks, and is further validated on the three cross-domain datasets.

title: Learning general-purpose and robust representations of microservice system states from multi-modal data
abstract: Microservice systems generate fragmented and misaligned multi-modal data, including metrics, logs, and traces, posing a major challenge for AIOps, which requires coherent system-state representations for downstream analytics. Existing approaches typically model spatio-temporal relations at a coarse granularity or are tailored to specific tasks, limiting their generalizability across different O&M scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose M3RL, a unified pre-training and fine-tuning framework for learning robust and transferable system-state representations. At its core, the spatio-temporal network (STNet) performs fine-grained semantic fusion of multi-modal data along both temporal and spatial dimensions and models evolving communication-driven dependencies among services. We further pre-train STNet with three complementary objectives: denoising reconstruction for robustness, future prediction for temporal evolution modeling, and causal contrastive learning for node-level discriminability. Extensive experiments on two public benchmark datasets demonstrate that M3RL consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art baselines across key downstream tasks, reducing state prediction MAE by 1.9%, increasing anomaly detection F1 by 4.7%, and improving root cause localization HR@1 by 4.8% on average. These results show that M3RL provides a robust and transferable representation backbone for multiple AIOps tasks.

title: Dynamic valuation of data assets via multi-agent reinforcement learning and Shapley value
abstract: Accurately valuing data assets is critical for unlocking their economic potential, yet traditional static methods fail to capture their dynamic, context-dependent value. To address this, we propose DSV-MARL, a novel framework that integrates Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with a differentiable dynamic Shapley value mechanism. Each data asset is modeled as an autonomous agent learning to contribute within simulated business environments, while the Shapley approximation enables real-time, interpretable quantification of marginal contributions. Experiments on 3782 real-world data asset records show that DSV-MARL achieves a Spearman correlation of 0.87 with market prices—an improvement of 8.8% over the best baseline—and reduces MSE by 37.3%. The model also demonstrates superior fairness and faster convergence. These results provide a robust, dynamic valuation tool that supports data investment, pricing, and equitable profit-sharing in collaborative data ecosystems.

title: Hierarchical process-level generative reward modeling with adaptive long-horizon reasoning for robust LLM alignment
abstract: We introduce HPR-GenRM, a hierarchical process-level generative reward model for robust large language model (LLM) alignment in offline reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) settings, unifying long-horizon reasoning with explicit step-by-step verification through a three-tier architecture. Training on 25K hierarchically-annotated instances from HelpSteer2, MATH, and CodeContests, our Llama-3-8B-based model achieves 82.3% accuracy on RM-Bench (7.2% improvement over state-of-the-art), 89.1% step accuracy on MATH-500 with error localization F1 of 0.83, and 61% relative reduction in undetected adversarial attacks. Integration into RLHF yields 58.3% win rate on AlpacaEval2 (11.1% gain) while reducing policy-level reward hacking from 15% to 5%. This work presents hierarchical process-level reasoning as an effective approach for interpretable reward modeling within offline reward labeling and quality-sensitive alignment settings.

title: IMGSL: Citation-based Innovation Motif Graph Structure Learning for scholar profiling
abstract: Scientific research is inherently cumulative, as new achievements are often inspired by prior contributions, built upon them, and recombined with existing knowledge. Identifying structural patterns underlying such cumulative knowledge development is a key challenge in scholar profiling and expert finding. In this paper, we define a set of citation-based Innovation Motifs, including the Giant Motif, to characterize higher-order patterns of citation evolution in scientific citation networks and to model how prior knowledge is repeatedly inherited and extended in scholars’ research trajectories. Based on large-scale real-world citation data spanning seven computer science subfields and 3500 scholar profiles, we empirically show that these motif structures exhibit systematic differences between awardees and non-awardees. Leveraging this observation, we construct Giant Motif-enhanced citation subgraphs and propose an Innovation Motif Graph Structure Learning (IMGSL) framework to learn scholar representations. We evaluate IMGSL on multiple real-world datasets through downstream tasks such as scholar award prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art graph neural network baselines, achieving up to a 3.61% performance improvement in the NLP field. Comprehensive analyses further demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and interpretability of IMGSL, showing that motif-enhanced structural representations provide useful evidence for characterizing scholars’ long-term research trajectories.

title: Collective-level propagation analysis via LLM-enhanced hypergraph transformer for fake news detection
abstract: Fake news detection is crucial for safeguarding information security and maintaining social stability. Existing studies use graph neural networks to capture news propagation features to boost fake news detection. However, constrained by the pairwise nature of conventional graphs, they decompose propagation into a set of individual-level behaviors. In practice, news diffusion is a collective propagation process rather than a simple aggregation of individual behaviors. Real and fake news exhibit distinct collective propagation behavior patterns, which can provide valuable cues for fake news detection. To exploit such collective-level characteristics, we propose LeHT, an LLM-enhanced hypergraph transformer framework for fake news detection via collective-level propagation analysis. LeHT leverages a large language model as a context provider to generate context-enhanced semantic representations, alleviating semantic sparsity in short news posts and enabling better understanding of semantics that may trigger collective reactions. Meanwhile, we construct propagation hypergraphs to explicitly model collective propagation behaviors, where each news item is represented as a hyperedge connecting all participating users. Based on the propagation hypergraph and the context-enhanced semantic representations, we design a hypergraph transformer network with a three-level attention mechanism to capture complex higher-order correlations in collective propagation behaviors and learn discriminative collective propagation behavior pattern representations for fake news detection. Experiments on three public datasets — Twitter (1152 news items), PHEME (1705 news items), and DRWeibo (6037 news items) — demonstrate that LeHT achieves ACC/F1 scores of 0.923/0.921, 0.926/0.924, and 0.916/0.913, respectively.

title: Towards higher quality and fewer hallucinations: A multi-agent collaboration framework for LLMs
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in natural language tasks, single-agent architectures face an inherent optimization conflict between maximizing generative response quality and mitigating factual hallucinations. To address this, we propose the Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework (MA-CF), a structured prompt-driven pipeline that decomposes generation into distinct phases of drafting, parallelized evaluation, and final synthesis. By architecturally decoupling factuality verification from linguistic assessment into separate agent roles, MA-CF empirically mitigates the suboptimal trade-offs and consensus biases observed in both monolithic single-agent systems and traditional multi-agent debate frameworks. We evaluated MA-CF using small-scale backbones (Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B) against single-agent baselines, iterative debate architectures, and large-scale models across three datasets: PreciseWiki (N=2000), LongWiki (N=250), and HaluEval 2.0 (N=800). Experimental results demonstrate substantial quantitative improvements. On the LongWiki dataset, MA-CF increased Llama3.1-8B’s Recall@32 from 15.38% to 35.22% and F1@32 from 22.63% to 44.22%. On the cross-domain HaluEval 2.0 benchmark, the framework improved the Average Factual Rate from 65.24% to 73.28%. Furthermore, on the PreciseWiki dataset, MA-CF significantly improved the model’s ability to reject unanswerable queries, effectively reducing the probability of model error. Significantly, our findings confirm that a strategic ensemble of 8B-parameter models can match or surpass the hallucination mitigation capabilities of 671B-parameter models (e.g., DeepSeek-V3), offering a computationally efficient architecture for deploying reliable LLM systems in resource-constrained information environments.

title: Attribution-driven background modeling network with context-aware anomaly suppression for hyperspectral anomaly detection
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to identify pixels whose spectral signatures deviate from the surrounding background without requiring prior knowledge. Although autoencoder-based methods achieve promising performance, they often suffer from insufficient separation between background and anomalous samples and inadequate modeling of heterogeneous background patterns. Moreover, the strong representation capability of neural networks may cause certain anomalies to be reconstructed, resulting in missed detections. To address these limitations, we propose an attribution-driven background modeling network with context-aware anomaly suppression, termed ADANet. The proposed framework adaptively mines sample attributions, explicitly models diverse background patterns, and suppresses anomaly reconstruction. Specifically, we develop a feature-guided sample attribution mining (FGSAM) strategy that leverages representative background prototypes to infer sample attributions, enabling effective separation of multiple background categories and reliable identification of anomalies. Building on this, a spectral-feature consistent discriminative (SFCD) loss is designed to enforce intra-class compactness and inter-class separability among background features, while maintaining structural consistency between the spectral and feature domains. In addition, we propose a context-aware anomaly suppression (CAAS) module that leverages background features from the spatial neighborhoods of anomalous pixels to constrain anomaly reconstruction, driving reconstructed anomalies toward the background distribution and thereby reducing missed detections. Quantitative comparisons with state-of-the-art methods show that our approach achieves consistently high AUC(PD,PF) values across six hyperspectral image datasets, with the highest value reaching 99.95%, and outperforms the second-best method by up to 0.70%. Qualitative comparisons further support the superiority of the proposed method.

title: DCEA: A dynamic cognition-emotion aggregation model for interpretable satisfaction prediction with AI conversational services
abstract: Enterprises are increasingly deploying AI services, but AI agents may fail to satisfy some users, particularly for those with complicated service requests. It becomes imperative for enterprises to identify these unsatisfied AI services and provide subsequent follow-up by human servers. Current user satisfaction estimation methods predominantly rely on single-dimensional user experience, resulting in suboptimal satisfaction prediction outcomes. This study proposes a theory-driven framework that comprehensively models dynamic multidimensional user experience, enabling interpretable and robust satisfaction prediction with AI services. Specifically, we model user experience from both cognitive and emotional dimensions, and introduce a novel strategy to dynamically reallocate the contributions of user experiences from implicit multi-topic requests toward final satisfaction. An auxiliary task is also designed to identify the reasons for user dissatisfaction, enhancing the interpretability and robustness of user satisfaction prediction. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model, we conduct extensive experiments on three user–AI dialogue datasets derived from real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in predictive performance, especially achieving an average accuracy improvement of 23.91% compared to LLMs. These findings offer valuable theoretical and practical insights for user experience and satisfaction with AI services research.

title: Hint-oriented self-suggestive learning for commonsense information processing
abstract: Multi-Choice Commonsense Question Answering (MC-CQA) is an important component of cognitive information science, particularly for advancing the reasoning functions of information systems. However, effective information processing for reasoning remains difficult. Distractors are often plausible when models lack relevant knowledge or explicit guidance. This article presents Hint-Oriented Representation Learning (HORL), an effective and integrated framework designed to synergize internal and external hints for enhanced reasoning. Within this framework, internal hints are formalized as structured intent descriptors, while external hints consist of expert-like advice simulating human knowledge acquisition to delineate correct and incorrect inferential paths. Specifically, HORL implements a dual-task learning paradigm: a keyword prediction task for intent internalization, and a contrastive learning task that optimizes information representations by aligning them with expert-guided pattern. Through this approach, the framework simulates a self-suggestion mechanism during training, effectively internalizing the reasoning patterns derived from both internal hints and external expertise into the model’s latent space. To evaluate the system’s decision-support robustness, we employ RoBERTa, ELECTRA, Flan-T5, and LLaMA as backbone models and evaluate HORL on the CODAH and Discosense benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that HORL consistently outperforms baseline methods. By leveraging external advice from GPT-5, HORL achieves accuracy improvements of 5.58% and 3.52% on CODAH and Discosense, respectively. Furthermore, HORL surpasses state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) in both Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and zero/few-shot settings. This framework provides an effective way to integrate internal and external hints into reasoning models. Our findings offer practical insights for developing knowledge-enhanced intelligent systems.

title: Boosting multimodal CoT reasoning through DPO with Error-prone Sample Synthesis
abstract: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (MCoT) reasoning extends CoT by incorporating visual evidence into structured textual rationales, enabling more accurate and coherent step-by-step reasoning in multimodal scenarios. However, MCoT methods still face two major challenges: (1) error propagation, where a single flawed intermediate step can derail the final answer, and (2) over-reasoning, where unnecessarily long chains on simple or mismatched problems induce hallucinations. To address these challenges, we propose Critic-MCoT, a unified adversarial framework for step-wise multimodal CoT alignment. Specifically, (1) to prevent error propagation, we introduce a step-wise adversarial process that synthesizes plausible error-prone samples and yields (win, lose) pairs for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and (2) to mitigate over-reasoning, we train stage-specific LoRA modules via DPO, forming an integrated reasoning module that adaptively handles diverse problem complexities. Experiments on both science and math benchmarks are conducted using 2.5 K science and 2.5 K math training instances to synthesize error-prone samples. Evaluation is performed on 4.2 K science test instances and 9.5 K math test instances in total. On ScienceQA, Critic-MCoT improves over the strongest MCoT baselines by 2.65% (3B) and 4.72% (7B) in average accuracy; on multimodal math benchmarks, it further improves the weighted average accuracy by 4.59% (3B) and 6.02% (7B). Moreover, after training, the average normalized error rate across six error types is reduced by approximately 10.7% in relative terms.

title: Similarity-aware feature calibration stabilizes low-contrast and missing-modality brain segmentation
abstract: Reliable fusion of heterogeneous MRI sources for brain tumor segmentation remains difficult under misalignment, incomplete protocols, and weak local contrast. We study a recurrent instability in U shaped encoder decoder networks where skip features are fused without verifying semantic consistency, which can inject semantic noise and trigger prediction collapse in low contrast regions. We propose a similarity aware calibration framework that replaces passive skip fusion with reliability conditioned feature propagation. A non local adaptive prior provides anatomy-consistent prior features via variational reconstruction, and a similarity weighted gating module uses local normalized cross correlation to suppress inconsistent skip information in a scale invariant manner. A contrast enhanced region attention module amplifies faint boundary evidence to mitigate gradient starvation in fuzzy transitions. On BraTS 2019, 2021, and 2023 validation benchmarks, NAP SCAF achieves average Dice scores of 94.14%, 96.05%, and 96.74%, respectively. On BraTS 2023, it improves average Dice by 6.73 points and reduces average HD95 by 4.19 mm relative to HFF Net. The framework mitigates collapse failures by reducing extreme Hausdorff outliers above 150 mm to values around 10 mm, and it remains robust under missing modality settings, achieving 93.79% average Dice across 14 modality subsets and 92.16% with a single modality on BraTS 2021. Code is available at https://github.com/mh-zhou/NAP-SCAF.

title: CA-DE: Heterogeneous component-aware and antagonistic dependency-enhanced dual paths for long-term time series forecasting
abstract: Time series forecasting is widely applied in real-world scenarios. However, existing methods typically employ a unified architecture within a shared feature space, resulting in coupled representations that limit forecasting performance. To address this issue, we propose the CA-DE (Component-Aware and Dependency-Enhanced), a dual-path framework that decouples feature modeling along the temporal and variable dimensions. Along the temporal path, CA-DE employs time component awareness to hierarchically abstract low-frequency trends and reconstruct multi-period high-frequency seasons, thereby capturing long-term dependencies and cyclical phase patterns, facilitating targeted modeling of heterogeneous time components. Along the variable path, CA-DE employs a dependency enhancement mechanism that reverses variable sequences to construct antagonistic dependency channels, enabling explicit modeling of negative correlations between variables. It then independently integrates the bidirectional dependency features between variables outside the time feature space, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to express complex inter-variable dependencies. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that CA-DE achieves strong performance across multiple domain-specific forecasting tasks. Notably, on the Exchange dataset, CA-DE reduces MSE and MAE by 26.9% and 13.6%, respectively, highlighting its effectiveness and generalization ability for long-term time series forecasting.

title: TECP: Insight into hybrid propagation factors from prompt-based LLMs for comprehensive cascade prediction
abstract: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future scale of post propagation on social networks. Existing models primarily rely on cascade sequences observed after a specific propagation period, overlooking the intrinsic influence of the text and metadata of source posts on the propagation scale, thereby limiting their ability to provide early-stage predictions and reducing interpretability. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) can extract propagation-related factors by analyzing source post text and metadata, experiments show that they often fail to adaptively select useful insights from these factors. To address these limitations, we propose a Textual Enhanced Cascade Prediction Model based on Large Language Model (TECP). Specifically, TECP utilizes LLMs to analyze the text and metadata of source posts and extract key factors influencing post spread from three aspects rooted in communication theories: topic, content, and audience. To selectively extract meaningful insights from these factors, a Text-Factor Collaboration module is proposed for propagation-aware textual representation. By leveraging multi-task learning, TECP can predict the future cascade level using only textual representations, which can also be seamlessly integrated into existing sequence-based cascade models to predict cascade scale. Experiments on Weibo and Twitter datasets demonstrate the model’s superiority. It achieves a 15.6% higher Macro-F1 for cascade level prediction without relying on cascade sequences. Moreover, as a plug-and-play module, it reduces the average MSLE by 5.24% for sequence-based models in cascade scale prediction. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TECP-DFB9/.

title: A mechanistic interpretability perspective on personality in large language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly reported to exhibit stable personality-like behaviors under standardized psychometric evaluations such as the Big Five, yet how such behaviors arise from internal computation remains unclear. In this work, we take a mechanistic perspective and aim to characterize how Transformer computation paths give rise to personality-consistent behavior. To enable this analysis, we introduce TraitTrace, to our knowledge the first dataset specifically designed for mechanistic studies of personality in LLMs, comprising 1800 human-curated situational prompts for circuit discovery and validation. Our analysis shows that personality-consistent behaviors are supported by compact circuits that involve only a small fraction of model components, rather than being diffusely distributed across the network. Across Llama2-7B-Chat and Phi-2, the extracted personality circuits achieve near-full-model Hit@10 performance, with an average score of 0.99, while retaining, on average, only about 8% of nodes and fewer than 0.05% of edges for each trait and level. Structural analyses reveal that high and low levels of the same trait are implemented by circuits that share similar nodes but differ in routing. Additionally, we find that Neuroticism exhibits comparatively lower cross-trait overlap, consistent with prior psychometric observations that it is less correlated with other Big Five traits. Furthermore, causal intervention experiments reveal that a small number of early-layer nodes act as bottlenecks that disproportionately govern personality expression. Together, these results provide a circuit-level account of personality in LLMs, bridging behavioral assessment and mechanistic interpretability, and suggesting new directions for more interpretable and targeted personality control and alignment.

title: A multi-expert adaptive framework for test-time personalization in federated learning
abstract: The heterogeneity of client data (i.e., non-IID distributions) in federated learning (FL) limits the generalization ability of global models across diverse test datasets. To address this challenge, we propose FedMEA (Multi-expert federated adaptive learning), which clusters clients into groups to distill expert models and dynamically integrates their predictions through self-supervised ensemble strategies. This design improves robustness to previously unseen data distributions with a controllable overhead confined to the Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) phase, while preserving standard inference efficiency after adaptation. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed FedMEA, we conducted extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets. FedMEA consistently outperformed state-of-the-art federated learning methods. Specifically, compared with FedAvg and FedProx, FedMEA improved average global accuracy by 26.3% and 26.5%, respectively, while maintaining competitive personalized performance on local datasets, demonstrating its robustness and scalability in handling client data heterogeneity. Further analyses confirm its superior performance from multiple perspectives.

title: Disentangling relational semantics in graph data to summarize entity descriptions
abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs), despite their widespread applications, suffer from severe information overload. Entity Summarization (ES) has emerged as a crucial technique to mitigate this issue. However, existing methods typically formulate ES as an item-wise ranking problem, where each description is evaluated largely in isolation. Such formulations are limited in capturing set-level complementarity, especially when a summary is expected to cover multiple semantic aspects. In this paper, we model summary complementarity as relations induced by latent semantic preference factors among descriptions. From this perspective, a high-quality summary is not merely a collection of individually salient descriptions, but a coherent set whose members reflect distinct yet mutually supportive semantic aspects. To this end, we propose the Disentangled Relational Summarizer (DRS), a novel approach that frames ES as an explicit link prediction task. DRS is built upon a graph-based neural architecture that learns disentangled representations to explicitly model the multifaceted semantic preferences between descriptions. Furthermore, a composite loss mechanism is introduced to maintain the diversity of description representations, counteracting representational collapse during message passing. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that DRS achieves strong overall performance, improving average F1 scores over the strongest baselines by 7.2% and 12.2%, and achieving the best Property Coverage result in five of six settings with a 5.0% average PC improvement over the strongest baseline.

title: An explainable ensemble learning approach for financial fraud detection: Integrating SHAP and LIME on the PaySim dataset
abstract: Credit card fraud detection requires highly accurate and interpretable models to minimize financial losses and build trust in automated systems. Although machine learning models achieve high predictive accuracy, their deployment is often hindered by class imbalance, computational efficiency, and interpretability challenges. Many existing studies overlook precision–recall performance under extreme imbalance, computational burden, and explanation reliability. This study addresses these challenges using the PaySim dataset, which simulates mobile money transactions with extreme class imbalance. The research investigates four core dimensions: SMOTE for imbalance mitigation, explainable AI (XAI) methods using SHAP and LIME for interpretability, learning-curve analysis for data sufficiency insights, and computational cost assessment reflecting real-time system constraints. Multiple advanced ensemble models were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, including AdaBoostClassifier with RandomForestClassifier and a StackingClassifier combining ExtraTrees, AdaBoost variants, and XGBoost. A dual-strategy framework is proposed: StackingClassifier as the primary model when computational resources are available, and AdaBoostClassifier with RandomForest as an efficient alternative for resource-constrained environments. Both models were evaluated under two operational scenarios: post-transaction and real-time fraud detection. In post-transaction scenarios, the StackingClassifier achieved 99.99% accuracy, 0.9999 F1 score, 0.9999 precision, 1.0 recall, and 0.9999 AUC, while AdaBoostClassifier achieved 99.99% accuracy, 0.9999 F1 score, 0.9998 precision, 1.0 recall, and 1.0 AUC. In real-time scenarios (excluding balance-related features unavailable during live processing), both maintained superior performance despite feature reduction. Comprehensive analysis on AdaBoostClassifier with RandomForest demonstrated consistent, interpretable explanations and computational efficiency. The study offers a resource-aware framework balancing accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability across different operational contexts.

title: Every bird has its nest: Boosting graph convolutional network via hierarchical learning
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various graph analyzing tasks. They follow the message-passing paradigm, learning node representations by iterative aggregation of neighborhood information. The existing studies have explored various interesting techniques to boost the performance of GNNs, including initial residual, identity mapping, feature fusion, weighted aggregation, etc. However, most of them leverage the uniform message-passing radius for information aggregation, which results in a limited receptive field and impairs the ability of the model to capture dependencies at varying distances. To address this limitation, a novel HieRarchical Graph Convolutional Network (HieRaGCN) is proposed, which distributes each node into an optimal message-passing radius for hierarchical-aware graph representation learning. Specifically, it employs eigenvector centrality to quantify node importance, which is the foundation for hierarchical learning. Then, it designs two optional partitioning schemes (i.e., adaptive partitioning and hardcoded partitioning) to map various nodes into the ideal receptive field. Furthermore, it devises an innovative vertical loss to enrich the distinctiveness of features across various receptive fields. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that HieRaGCN achieves consistent improvements, outperforming baseline methods by 2.07%∼4.10% in node classification and 0.56%∼2.55% in link prediction. The source codes of this work are publicly available at https://github.com/ZZY-GraphMiningLab/HieRaGCN.

title: Enhancing decision boundaries in continual learning through a decoupled Gaussian framework
abstract: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to acquire new knowledge while retaining previously learned information. CNN-based and prompt-based CL methods have achieved remarkable progress in recent years. However, most prior work has primarily focused on reducing forgetting from the perspective of the model itself. In this paper, we investigate CL from the perspective of decision boundaries, analyzing the impact of instance-level feature overlap. To address this issue, we propose a generic Decoupled Gaussian Softmax Classifier that enhances class discriminability during CL process. Specifically, we decouple the features extracted by the backbone into multiple Gaussian distributions, which are directly fused into the feature space through weighted integration. A regularization term is introduced to penalize the overlap of similar features, while an adaptive decision boundary is assigned to each class to encourage inter-class separation and intra-class compactness. Experiments on 4 widely used continual learning datasets and 12 CL scenarios show that our method has good plug-and-play capability. It improves the average accuracy by 1%–2.63% over the baseline models, while effectively reducing both the forgetting rate and the Expected Calibration Error. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DGSC-main-310D.

title: Synergistic evolution and trade-off mechanisms of ecosystem services in coal-grain composite areas a 23-year spatiotemporal analysis of mining subsidence impacts and reclamation strategies
abstract: In eastern China, where grain production and coal mining coexist, mining-induced subsidence is reshaping ecosystem services (ES) in the coal–grain composite areas (CGCA). Understanding the dynamic trade-offs and synergies among ES is crucial for sustainable land management. This study developed a 23-year (2001–2023) assessment framework for five ES—food production (FP), water conservation (WC), soil conservation (SC), oxygen release (OR), and climate regulation (CR)—using multi-source datasets. Subsidence-induced waterlogged areas (SIWAs) were delineated using the LandTrendr algorithm, ES were quantified with biophysical models, and their interactions were assessed via time-series analysis and structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results show that while all five ES increased overall, SIWAs expanded 2.54 times, with over 70 % of these areas showing FP declines. Targeted reclamation, such as Yellow River sediment filling, drove localized FP surges (up to 465.40 %) but also triggered severe trade-offs, with sharp declines in SC (−950.11 %), WC (−22.75 %), and CR (−41.86 %). PLS-SEM revealed strong, region-specific linkages, from pronounced FP–CR synergies (β = 0.971) to significant FP–WC trade-offs (β = −0.461). A novel dynamic equivalence factor adjustment framework (DEFAF), which integrates spatiotemporal changes, improved ES valuation accuracy. This mechanism-informed framework provides a scientific basis for balancing ecosystem services in mining landscapes and offers actionable guidance for adaptive reclamation policies.

title: Can OECD countries lead the green transition? Leveraging green innovation, trade openness, information globalization and financial depth for environmental sustainability
abstract: In an era marked by mounting climate challenges and rising global environmental consciousness, the urgency for sustainable economic transitions has never been greater. This study explores the heterogeneous impacts of green innovation (GRIO), trade openness (TROP), information globalization (INGN), and financial depth (FNDH) on environmental outcomes in OECD countries from 1994 to 2023. To capture environmental sustainability (ES), this study employs carbon dioxide emissions (COXE) as a widely recognized proxy, since reductions in CO2 emissions represent a fundamental pathway toward sustainability goals. Recognizing the limitations of existing literature that often focuses on country-specific or linear models, we employ Panel Quantile Regression (PQR) to uncover nuanced relationships across different levels of emissions. Both first-generation and advanced second-generation econometric approaches are applied to ensure robustness. The findings reveal that GRIO significantly reduces COXE across almost all quantiles (10th to 90th), confirming its central role in supporting sustainability transitions. TROP also exerts a strong mitigating influence on COXE across quantiles, though with varying intensity. Interestingly, the effect of INGN is asymmetric, reducing COXE significantly at lower and middle quantiles (10th to 50th) but becoming weaker at higher emission levels, suggesting diminishing marginal gains in advanced economies. FNDH shows limited influence, with a predominantly negative effect only at the lower quantile—20th quantile. Moreover, economic growth (GRPC) significantly increases COXE in the middle and higher quantiles (50th to 90th), while foreign direct investment (FINT) reduces emissions in the lower and middle quantiles (20th to 50th). By capturing distributional effects and nonlinearities, this study provides novel insights into how different structural drivers influence COXE, thereby contributing to the broader discourse on climate mitigation and sustainable economic transitions in advanced economies.

title: Toward climate-resilient supply chains: Analyzing the impact and mechanisms of physical climate risks on supply chain network in China’s listed companies
abstract: Existing studies have predominantly concentrated on supply chain disruptions caused by individual climate risks and its subsequent propagation, with limited in-depth analysis of the specific impacts on supply chain network traffic. Our study innovatively examines these impacts by considering multiple physical climate risks simultaneously, including floods, earthquakes, extreme temperatures, and storms. Utilizing a dataset of Chinese A-share listed companies spanning over two decades (2001–2022), we employ a novel combination of directed minimum spanning tree and fixed-effects regression methods for empirical analysis. The results show that spatially, supply chain core hubs are alarmingly concentrated in high-risk areas; urban clusters with multi-core complex supply chain structures exhibit stronger resilience. Temporally, an increase in natural disaster frequency coincides with a decline in supply chain net flow. Regression analysis confirms that physical climate risks significantly and negatively impact supply chain net flow (β=−22.4465, p<0.01). This primarily disrupts supply chains by weakening transportation capacities, increasing short-term financial pressure on enterprises, and restricting their comprehensive financing capabilities. Finally, we recommend that governments enhance infrastructure development in disaster-prone areas and subsidize corporate technological transformation to improve supply chain resilience. Meanwhile, enterprises can effectively counter physical climate risks by optimizing network layouts and establishing contingency financing mechanisms.

title: Synergistic effects of spatial urban form on PM2.5 concentration and urban heat islands: A multi-scale explanatory machine learning
abstract: Urban form significantly influences environmental challenges, such as fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration and the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. However, few studies have explored the synergistic effects of urban form's spatial configuration on PM2.5 concentration and UHI prediction, with most overlooking spatial autocorrelation in their analyses. This study calculates four built-up landscape pattern metrics, alongside built-up volume, built-up surface, and 2D and 3D greenery, to investigate their effects at various scales on PM2.5 concentration and UHI intensity in Vilnius, Lithuania. Using an explanatory machine learning method, we identified non-linear relationships between contributing factors and their impact on PM2.5 concentration and UHI, while accounting for spatial autocorrelation. Our findings reveal the consistent prominence of the largest patch index (LPI), percentage of landscape (PLAND), and built-up volume in prediction models, although their relative importance varies across scales. LPI is strongly associated with UHI, while built-up volume and PLAND are more influential in predicting PM2.5 at finer resolutions. Two-way interactions among leading variables indicate that high values of LPI or PLAND, combined with high built-up volume, are associated with increased PM2.5 concentration and UHI levels. Furthermore, areas with high tree cover height (TCH) and high built-up volume in urban canyons restrict airflow, exacerbating pollutant accumulation and increasing PM2.5 concentration.

title: Evaluating technical soil derived from lithium mica residue: Integrating soil quality and life cycle assessment for functional performance and environmental sustainability
abstract: The large-scale accumulation of Lithium Mica Residue (LMR) poses environmental challenges, requiring sustainable utilization beyond conventional disposal or limited reuse. Constructing technical soil from LMR shows promise but lacks comprehensive design, quality assessment, and environmental evaluation frameworks. This study developed LMR-based technical soil by blending industrial and agricultural wastes to explore the performance mechanisms and identify key indicators through analyses of physicochemical properties, maize seedling growth, and microbial communities. A statistical Soil Quality Index (SQI) analysis indicated that optimal formulations could be obtained. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) demonstrated notable environmental advantages under the optimal formulations-particularly in reducing carbon emissions and land use-against landfilling and cement use. Overall, transforming LMR into technical soil represents a promising and comparatively sustainable utilization strategy, with the integrated design-SQI-LCA framework providing a rigorous methodology to evaluate, optimize, and advance waste-derived soil substitutes for broader environmental applications.

title: On-demand thermal regulation and water harvesting via liquid metal-infused bio-inspired microchannel architectures
abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting in humid regions demands textiles that balance efficient moisture capture with desirable thermal gradients, a challenge complicated by liquid metal (LM) integration. The incorporation of LMs like EGaIn into textiles presents distinct challenges: controlling the conductive fluid's stability, ensuring reliable encapsulation within flexible fiber matrices, and sustaining functionality under both mechanical stress and thermal cycling, particularly in moisture-rich environments. To address the challenges of extreme weather and water scarcity, we introduce a novel biofabric featuring a liquid metal-integrated, multichannel nanofiber structure. Fabricated via multi-fluid electrospinning, this design securely encapsulates EGaIn particles within hollow PLA nanofibers, creating a stable, lychee-inspired rough surface that achieves rapid photothermal response (53.6 % efficiency) without leakage. Co-integration of phase change materials (PCMs) and biomimetic hollow channels enables exceptional energy storage (89.7 J/g) and minimizes radiative heat loss. The fabric further demonstrates efficient atmospheric water harvesting (6.00 g/g), adaptable PCM tuning via physical blending, and robust durability (85.3 J/g after cycling). This multifunctional textile overcomes key barriers of LM-integration to pioneer effective thermal management and rapid water sorption-desorption, standing at the forefront of smart fabric innovation for extreme environments.

title: An integrated DPSIR-TOPSIS modeling approach for assessing and predicting coastal wetland ecological security: A case study of Haikou, China
abstract: Coastal wetlands (CWs) provide critical ecosystem services but are increasingly threatened by rapid urban expansion and industrial restructuring. These pressures highlight the need for an improved assessment of the ecological security (ES) of CWs, yet the existing approaches lack the integrated frameworks for a comprehensive evaluation. This study addresses that gap by developing an integrated assessment framework that combines the driving-pressure-state-impact-response (DPSIR) model with the technique for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution (TOPSIS) analysis to evaluate the ES of Haikou's CWs. The framework integrates multi-source data and ecological process indicators (ecosystem services, landscape ecology, socioeconomics, and climate factors) to analyze spatiotemporal changes from 1990 to 2023 and employs a grey model (GM (1,1)) to project the trends through 2030. The results indicate substantial wetland loss (34.67 km2) and fragmentation due to urban expansion, corresponding to an initial decline in ES. The ecological security index (ESI) of the driving and state layers increased by 0.0277 and 0.4621, respectively, while the indicators of pressure, impact, and response layers showed a general downward trend. Among them, the pressure dimension decreased by 79.46 %. The ESI followed a decline-stagnation-recovery trajectory with a notable rebound by 2023 (reaching 0.4586), which indicated a delayed ecological response to management interventions. Spatially, the low ES areas extend from the urban periphery to the core wetland areas driven by urban encroachment and intensified agriculture. If current protection policies stand, the ESI are projected to rebound to approximately 0.5183 by 2030. Overall, the DPSIR-TOPSIS framework effectively captures the complex socio-ecological dynamics in ES. This integrated framework offers a practical reference for sustainable urban planning and wetland conservation in rapidly urbanizing coastal regions.

title: Deep insights into the effects of polystyrene nanoplastics on methanogenic microbial communities in food waste anaerobic digestion under meso-thermophilic temperatures
abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NP) from improper plastic disposal can enter the anaerobic digestion (AD) process with food waste (FW), potentially impacting AD performance. This study investigates the effect of PS-NP on FW AD at meso-thermophilic temperature (45 °C). Exposure to 0.1 and 1 g L−1 PS-NP had no significant impact on the AD process, but 2 g L−1 caused a significant decrease in methane production, organic matter accumulation, and system acidification. However, the inhibitory effect was alleviated after day 12. Microbial composition analysis revealed a shift in the core microbial community, with Methanosarcina, Defluviitoga, Proteiniphilum, and Tepidimicrobium as dominant taxa. Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses indicated that PS-NP exposure did not disrupt methane metabolism pathways, but inhibited AD by reducing the transcription of functional genes. Notably, acetoclastic methanogenesis (AM) was impaired, as transcription of ackA and pta increased while cdh decreased. Conversely, genes involved in the reverse Wood-Ljungdahl (WL), glycine cleavage system (GCS), and methylotrophic methanogenesis (MM) pathways were significantly upregulated. These findings suggest that PS-NP exposure shifts methane production from AM to syntrophic acetate oxidation (SAO) and hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis (HM), coupled with MM. This study provides new insights into the impacts of PS-NP on AD performance under meso-thermophilic conditions.

title: Structure–solubility relationships of CO2-soluble surfactants for in-situ foaming in enhanced oil recovery and CO2 sequestration
abstract: In-situ foaming using green hydrocarbon-based CO2-soluble surfactants offers a promising approach for enhancing oil recovery and geological CO2 sequestration. Compared to water-based foams, this strategy enables deep transport of surfactants via supercritical CO2, facilitating in-situ foam formation and increasing CO2 storage through formation water consumption. However, low surfactant solubility in supercritical CO2 remains a key challenge. This study introduces a static equilibrium sampling method to directly measure surfactant solubility under various temperature–pressure conditions, overcoming the limitations of traditional cloud point methods. The novelty of this method lies in its coupling of static sampling with a sensitive, IFT-based quantification technique, which is particularly suited for non-chromophoric surfactants. Validation against vapor–liquid equilibrium data confirms a deviation within 5 %. The solubility of 11 surfactants—including nine DFQ variants and two commercial references—is systematically assessed from 10 to 26 MPa and 35–65 °C. The primary contribution of this work is the establishment of the first systematic structure-solubility relationship for this class of surfactants. Structure–solubility analysis reveals that solubility decreases with increasing PO/EO group numbers and alkyl chain lengths but increases with branching and higher PO/EO ratios. DFQ-4 exhibits the highest solubility among all synthesized surfactants, reaching 0.382 wt% at 50 °C and 26 MPa, significantly surpassing commercial NP-15. Its foam performance is tested in brine (60,000 mg L−1) at 0.4 wt% under 10–50 MPa and 35–65 °C. The foam volume reaches a maximum of 88 mL at 35 °C and 30 MPa, and declines with increasing temperature. Foam stability, assessed through drainage half-life measurements, exceeds 110 min under 35 °C and 50 MPa. These findings confirm DFQ-4's strong compatibility with CO2 and suitability for in-situ foam generation. This work provides design principles for next-generation CO2-soluble surfactants and establishes a robust methodology for structure–performance evaluation under reservoir conditions.

title: Enhancing nutrients recovery from source-separated urine through a novel bioelectrically assisted forward osmosis coupled with gas permeation membrane system: reaction kinetics and mechanisms
abstract: Effective nutrient recovery from source-separated urine is essential for sustainable resource management and water pollution control. In this study, we developed an innovative bioelectrically assisted forward osmosis coupled with a gas-permeation membrane system (BFGS) to simultaneously recover nitrogen and phosphorus from urine. The BFGS substantially improved nutrient recovery efficiency, achieving 80.44 % nitrogen and 99.92 % phosphorus recovery. Relative to a control system without an electric field, the electric field accelerated the kinetics of nitrogen and phosphorus recovery by factors of 1.25 and 1.22, respectively. Electronic equilibrium analysis revealed that the BFGS achieved optimal electronic balance, facilitating efficient oxygen reduction reaction and minimizing electronic losses. Partial least squares path modeling further identified electric field–assisted forward osmosis as the primary driver of nutrient recovery. Mechanism exploration disclosed that the BFGS enabled simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus recovery by inducing ion migration by the electric field while exploiting the reverse salt flux of the FO membrane. This work offers novel insights into nutrient recovery using the BFGS and highlights its remarkable efficiency and feasibility for sustainable management of source-separated urine.

title: Harnessing policy synergies to decarbonize China's light-duty passenger vehicle fleet
abstract: Many studies have evaluated single-policy measures for decarbonizing China's light-duty passenger vehicle fleet, but few have systematically addressed policy interactions. Using a dynamic fleet-based life cycle greenhouse gas emission model, we assess six major policies under 1152 scenarios. We find that accounting for synergies increases mitigation potential by up to 19.3 Gt CO2 eq, raising the number of scenarios consistent with the 2 °C pathway from 3 to 449. The strongest synergies arise from the joint acceleration of vehicle electrification, lightweighting, and power sector decarbonization, while rigid demand-side restrictions tend to reduce overall effectiveness. These results underscore the importance of coordinated policy portfolios. We recommend prioritizing technology-driven strategies and complementing them with flexible demand-side measures to maximize mitigation outcomes.

title: Advanced multi-functional biomass aerogel for enhanced acoustic absorption and flame retardant
abstract: With the increasing demands for safety and environmental protection in the construction field, there is an urgent need for multifunctional green materials that are mechanically robust, noise-reducing, and fire-resistant. Aerogels made from natural biomasses such as cellulose are eco-friendly. However, they are limited by the antagonistic effects between various performance parameters, making it difficult to improve mechanical, acoustic, and flame-retardant properties simultaneously. To address this issue, a kapok fiber-gelatin-based composite aerogel (KGMP) is prepared. The aerogel is made from delignified kapok fiber, magnesium hydroxide, and phytic acid-modified magnesium hydroxide, crosslinked with gelatin. The effects of gelatin concentration, phytic acid-modified magnesium hydroxide concentration, and cavity depth on the acoustic is investigated. The aerogel not only exhibits good sound absorption, but also has compressive strength and flame resistance. These features make the aerogel meet safety requirements and provide new insights for the development of green multifunctional materials.

title: An innovative deep learning surrogate for watershed pollutant-carbon synergistic optimization
abstract: Current watershed management lacks a synergistic consideration of the three objectives of water quality, economic costs, and carbon emissions, while developing a computationally efficient surrogate model for water environments that also captures spatial structure is absent in optimization studies. This study addresses this gap by developing a Graph Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (GC-LSTM) network surrogate model for water environments. The model is based on inputs and outputs from mechanistic watershed models. We integrated this model into a multi-objective optimization framework to analyze the synergistic effects of watershed environment regulation measures on pollution control and carbon mitigation. The proposed framework was applied to the Dianchi watershed, a typical plateau lake watershed in Southwest China. Results show that the GC-LSTM model achieved R2and NSE values above 0.9, demonstrating strong generalizability and reliability as a surrogate for mechanistic models. The model reduced simulation runtime from 504 seconds to just 1.6 seconds per instance, a 315-fold improvement in computational efficiency. Within the three-dimensional (water quality-carbon emissions-economic costs) optimization framework, pollutant concentration entering the lake was reduced by 33.5 %, and carbon emissions by 12.5 % relative to current conditions. A comparative analysis with conventional two-dimensional optimization (water quality-economic costs) revealed that the two-dimensional approach favors solutions with reduced implementation scales for watershed constructive regulation measures. This leads to increased reliance on inter-basin water transfers and external wastewater discharges, suggesting that neglecting carbon emissions incentivizes solutions prioritizing external measures over in-situ watershed improvements. The developed GC-LSTM-based co-optimization methodology can spatially configure regulation measures—optimizing their type, scale, and geographic placement—to simultaneously enhance watershed water quality and mitigate carbon emissions, thereby advancing “dual carbon” goals.

title: Enhanced flotation upgrading of high-ash fine waste coal with a novel compound collector: High-value and clean utilization of waste
abstract: The enhance flotation upgrading of high-ash fine waste coal (HFWC) is urgent, as the low economic value and environmental risks from direct disposal necessitate a clean and efficient separation technique. In this work, HFWC was upgraded to a high-value coking coal product via flotation using a novel compound collector, H708, thereby achieving goals in both waste utilization and clean production. The H708 collector significantly improved the flotation performance of the HFWC, producing a clean coal concentrate with an ash content of 12.25 %, a 52.79 % yield, and 71.40 % combustible recovery at a dosage of 1000 g/t. FTIR and GC/MS analyses confirmed the main components of H708 to be hydrocarbons, esters, and hydroxyl-containing species. The flotation mechanism was investigated through measurements of Zeta potential, wrapping angle, and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) force analysis. These measurements confirmed that H708 selectively enhances low-density coal flotation by promoting stronger interactions with coal's oxygen-containing groups and increasing hydrophobicity. Meanwhile, it boosts the electrostatic repulsion between coal and kaolinite, effectively suppressing clay coating and hetero-coagulation to achieve high combustible recovery and low ash content. A simplified economic analysis indicates the potential for a substantial annual net profit, estimated at $41.52 million. This work demonstrates that the application of H708 in HFWC flotation is efficient, economical, and offers promising industrial application prospects.

title: Electrochemical detection and electro-Fenton degradation of fipronil via Fe/Ni-BTC/MS-derived NiFe2O4@C core-shell catalyst
abstract: The core-shell material NiFe2O4@C, prepared from a maize straw-derived metal-organic framework (MOF) precursor of Fe/Ni-BTC/MS, was developed for the simultaneous detection and degradation of trace fipronil in water bodies. This material exhibited ultra-sensitive detection performance with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.901 fmol L−1 and a linear range from 10−12 to 10−4 mol L−1 for fipronil, where the detection mechanism was attributed to the specific capture of fipronil molecules by Ni3+/Fe2+ bimetallic sites; it simultaneously demonstrated efficient degradation capability, achieving complete mineralization of 10 mg L−1 fipronil within 60 min with a rate constant of 0.0702 min−1, which was dominated by •OH radicals, as verified by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), whose generation relied on the continuous activation of H2O2 through Fe2+/Fe3+and Ni2+/Ni3+ valence cycling. Meanwhile, combining experimental methods and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the electron migration pathways and structural properties of NiFe2O4@C were explored systematically. This strategy was confirmed to provide an integrated detection-degradation solution for pesticide pollution control.

title: Non-conventional thermal treatment of organic hazardous waste: Conversion to high-energy materials via molten sucrose system
abstract: Based on the rapid detonation reaction between sucrose and potassium chlorate, we propose a method for modifying distillation residues from chemical pesticides using molten sucrose as a reaction matrix, thereby enhancing their detonation performance. Within the molten sucrose medium, sugar radical-driven dehydration condensation reactions, coupled with azetidine ring-opening and rearrangement, generate functional groups such as C ≡ N, N-C=O, and N-H. Concurrently, this process promotes substitution or cleavage of halogenated CF3/C–Cl groups. Two primary products are formed: C25H25F3N2O and C34H22Cl2N2O2. Structural and electronic characterisation reveals both exhibits layered hollow crystal structures. C25H25F3N2O forms a regular layered cavity lattice featuring strong charge polarisation, intra-layer C–H···O/N hydrogen bonds, and interconnected π channels, facilitating ordered charge and energy transport. C34H22Cl2N2O2, however, is governed by halogen-mediated interactions and local positive potentials, rendering C–Cl bonds susceptible to cleavage. This generates Cl· radicals that accelerate KClO3 decomposition; C–F/CF3 charge rearrangement or bond cleavage induces azetidine ring-opening and strain energy release; Thermal cracking of C ≡ N and N-C=O generates nitrogen-containing free radicals and promotes electron transfer, while N–H groups form hydrogen bonds at the interface between the modified product and KClO3, enhancing electron-proton coupling. The resulting rapid radical generation, interfacial charge complementarity, and layered crystal topology significantly reduce the detonation initiation energy barrier, substantially enhancing detonation velocity and energy output. The molten sugar bath effectively improves the energy density, material composition, and structure of various low-calorific-value organic hazardous wastes, laying a solid foundation for pioneering new pathways in the synergistic treatment and resource recovery of organic hazardous wastes using energetic materials.

title: Toward industry 5.0: Quantum-biological synergistic mechanisms for lithium battery recycling through multiscale optimization
abstract: The transition to sustainable industrial systems requires innovative approaches that combine advanced technologies with circular economy principles. This study proposes a novel smart circularity framework for Industry 5.0 that enables cross-industry collaboration, creating an integrated network for lithium battery recycling. Our approach combines the structured production methods from the steel industry, circular material flow patterns from the paper industry, and specific lithium recycling requirements to develop a bio-inspired architecture enhanced by quantum principles. Through advanced modeling and control systems, we demonstrate how quantum-inspired mechanisms can optimize material flow interactions and improve recycling efficiency through biological self-regulation principles. Key contributions include: 1) Cross-industry synergy: Quantum-based coherence measures enhance material recovery in different production systems; 2) Integrated governance: A three-level framework combining quantum-assisted carbon tracking, biological processing, and adaptive control improves system stability; 3) Industry 5.0 integration: Combining digital twins with biological-quantum feedback makes recycling an inherent system function. Case studies confirm that our approach significantly improves collection, recovery, and reuse performance, providing scalable solutions for regenerative economies that extend beyond battery recycling. Based on the robustness analysis and simulation-reality gap assessment, this study further proposes a systematic optimization pathway to bridge the gap between theoretical simulations and practical applications in lithium recovery.

title: AI-driven energy and environmental control for sustainable space farming under altered gravity
abstract: Space controlled environment agriculture (SpaCEA) offers promising solutions for sustainable life support in closed environments but require careful balancing of energy use and resource efficiency. In this study, we use computational modeling and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate key performance metrics–oxygen production, carbon dioxide scrubbing, water recycling, food production, and energy consumption–of SpaCEA under two decision-making strategies: a resource-focused strategy and an energy-focused strategy. Specifically, we develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based environmental regulation system to effectively manage supplemental CO2, lighting, and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) in SpaCEA. The DRL system streamlines resource production and consumption in SpaCEA using only basic environmental information like bulk CO2/O2 concentration, air temperature and humidity, without requiring detailed knowledge of the biological plant's photosynthetic, respiration and transpiration rates as well as leaf surface/canopy conditions.
