This study provides a scientific basis for integrated social-ecological governance in the YZRB and an adaptive research framework for sustainable development in similar regions worldwide, helping to advance SES research from theoretical exploration to practical application.

title: Effect of silane and alkali/silane surface treatments on incinerated sewage sludge ash-reinforced polylactic acid composites: Mechanical properties and interfacial compatibility
abstract: To mitigate the environmental burden of incinerated sewage sludge ash (ISSA, a polluting municipal waste often landfilled) and reduce reliance on petroleum-based plastics, this study valorizes ISSA as a reinforcing filler for biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA). A key challenge for PLA/ISSA composites is poor interfacial compatibility, which compromises their mechanical performance. To resolve this problem, two surface modification strategies were developed: silane treatment (yielding M-ISSA) and alkali pretreatment coupled with silane treatment (yielding M-OH-ISSA). PLA composites with 15 wt% modified/unmodified ISSA were fabricated. Mechanical tests revealed that unmodified PLA/ISSA underperformed neat PLA, whereas both modified composites showed enhancements, with the alkali/silane strategy achieving optimal results: PLA/M-OH-ISSA reached a tensile strength of 55.20 MPa, flexural strength of 67.08 MPa, and elongation at break of 2.88 %. Microstructural analyses confirmed reduced ISSA agglomeration and stronger interfacial adhesion with PLA, facilitating efficient stress transfer within the matrix. In addition to performance gains, 15 wt% ISSA reduces virgin PLA consumption and costs, and the filler itself has a near-zero embodied carbon (unlike energy-intensive synthetic fillers). This simple, scalable strategy enables high-performance PLA composites, aligning with cleaner production and circular economy principles, to advance waste valorization and bioplastics.

title: Establishing a resource allocation compensation framework based on Green Water Credit concept to coordinate up-downstream development
abstract: Green Water Credit(GWC) integrates Green Water Management(GWM) with credit arrangements. This concept allocates resources to areas with higher efficiency and minimal environmental impact. It promotes coordinated socio-economic development between up-downstream regions in water-scarce basins. However, in large basins, the interests of weaker parties are often overlooked. Credit arrangements between up-downstream governments are difficult to sustain. A robust credit system is only applied in small basins, limiting the further development of GWC. This study addresses these issues by integrating GWC into the optimal allocation of soil and water resources in large basins. We improve the GWC model and propose a new framework. This framework comprises hydrological simulations, scenario evaluations, and horizontal and vertical compensation scheme. Using the Huangshui basin in the upper reaches of the Yellow River as a case study, the feasibility and applicability of the framework were evaluated. The results show that: ①Implementing GWM upstream significantly boosts economic and ecological benefits, with the average annual benefit across five GWM scenarios reaching 707.4 million CNY. ②Supervision and participation by central departments (the GWC Foundation) can mediate conflicts of interest between upstream and downstream regions. This helps establish a long-term stable management and compensation mechanism, ensuring the sustainability of GWC. ③The new framework is expected to promote high-quality, coordinated development in the basin. The proposed compensation scheme is shown to reduce the socio-economic development gap (measured by static imbalance difference) by up to 47.3 % for key management measures. The framework offers promising soil and water conservation prospects, pollution reduction, and enhanced water resource availability.

title: Metabolic mechanism of ethanol pre-fermentation to enhance anaerobic digestion of acidified food waste
abstract: Acidified food waste is often characterized by low anaerobic digestion (AD) efficiency during the treatment process, significantly hindering its effective recycling and utilization. Ethanol pre-fermentation can significantly improve the AD stability of food waste by biologically regulating the acidogenic pathway. In this study, the introduction of distillers’ grains eliminated the negative effects of acidification on food waste during ethanol pre-fermentation. The pre-fermentation stage involved ethanol-type and butyric acid-type fermentation, and the activity of the electron transport system was significantly enhanced. After pre-fermentation, 443.23 ± 11.39 mL/g VSS of methane was produced, representing a 24.45% increase. Pre-fermentation improved the utilization of organic matter during AD. The removal rates of volatile suspended solids and total chemical oxygen demand were increased by 49.98% and 28.45%, respectively. Metagenomic analysis showed that pre-fermentation facilitated carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism, promoting the hydrolysis of macromolecular organic matter and providing a more available substrate for acidogenesis. Additionally, pre-fermentation facilitated the expression of genes related to acetic acid production. It also enhanced the methanogenesis pathways involving acetate, methanol, and methyl compounds. This study revealed the mechanism by which the pre-fermentation affects the AD metabolic process, thereby paving a novel pathway for the resource utilization of acidified food waste.

title: Power load analysis and configuration optimization of a hybrid microgrid integrating food waste-to-biogas and photovoltaics
abstract: The growing challenges of urban food waste accumulation and the urgent demand for low-carbon energy transition highlight the need for integrated solutions that couple waste management with renewable energy utilization. However, most existing studies have not fully achieved an effective integration of high-efficiency energy utilization and resource circularity, leading to limited energy recovery and weak system synergy. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel microgrid system that couples PV power generation with food waste treatment to achieve efficient energy utilization and resource valorization. The system incorporates anaerobic digestion for biogas production, biogas power generation, waste heat recovery, and the use of residual heat for insect protein production. A comprehensive system framework is created, with subsequent optimization of parameters and refinement of the energy dispatch strategy to improve performance. The proposed system achieves multi-stage energy cascade utilization, maximizing waste-derived energy recovery and reducing energy losses compared with conventional microgrids. The optimized LCOE for the grid-connected mode is 0.075 $/kWh, representing a 17.58 % reduction compared to the isolated mode. Optimization results reveal that the grid-connected mode achieves LOLP of 5.91 %, CO2 emissions of 163 t/year and insect protein production of 7.17 t/year, whereas the isolated mode yields an LOLP of 0.42 %, CO2 emissions of 45 t/year, and insect protein production of 10.56 t/year. Compared with recent studies on PV–biogas-based microgrids, the proposed system achieves a significantly lower LCOE, demonstrating strong techno-economic advantages and providing a scalable pathway for the development of high-efficiency microgrids aligned with circular economy principles.

title: Sustainable Hydroponic Farming: Towards sustainable management of production and distribution
abstract: Up to 40 % of all food is wasted, posing a critical environmental sustainability challenge for food supply chains. One promising alternative to reduce waste is local Farmer-to-Consumer (F2C) hydroponic farming; however, many farms adopting this approach struggle financially. This study explores economic and environmental sustainability in vertical hydroponic food production for multi-channel F2C distribution. This paper defines the sustainable growing problem in vertical hydroponic farming developed in dialogue with a midwestern hydroponic farming company. The proposed solution, grounded in green inventory management principles, formulates the hydroponics growing problem as a modified dual-objective multi-channel newsvendor model. The numerical analysis is based on actual production, emission and demand data from a hydroponic farm. It reveals that by applying this model the farm can both improve financial results and increase environmental sustainability by reducing food waste and emissions. However, it also reveals that the last incremental financial gains come at disproportionately high environmental costs (and vice versa). E.g., in the farm considered an increase of emissions of 0.54 % from its minimum value resulted in an increase in expected profit of 7.22 % while a similar additional increase of emissions only raised the expected profit by an additional 0.28 %. Considering the absence of existing research in the field and the dual challenges of emissions from food waste and the financial viability of vertical hydroponic farms, these findings contribute to both the practice and theory of operations and supply chain management. Specifically, this research advances understanding in agriculture, food waste mitigation, and green inventory management.

title: Reducing the healthcare carbon footprint through fully self-service artificial intelligence-powered screening: A comparative simulation study utilizing data from Shanghai City and Lixin Town, China
abstract: Healthcare mode transformation changes carbon emissions, but assessments that evaluate both carbon emissions and clinical effectiveness are limited. This study integrates environmental perspective into primary eye care by comparing five eye disease detection scenarios. Combining life cycle assessment, decision tree and Markov model, we assessed carbon footprint and detection effectiveness of diabetic retinopathy, a predominant blinding disorder. The primary outcome was the novel Incremental Carbon Emissions-Effectiveness Ratio (ICeER), a composite metric capturing changes in health value per unit carbon emission across strategy transitions. The results revealed that screening significantly reduced emissions compared to clinical follow-up. Reduction rates increased with advancements in digitalization, from 63.00 % (p < 0.01, in-person screening), 63.47 % (p < 0.01, manual telemedicine screening), 65.63 % (p < 0.01, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered telemedicine screening) to 70.72 % (p < 0.01, fully self-service AI-powered screening). However, poor referral compliance diminished this benefit, limiting emission reductions to 31.93 % (p < 0.01) to 51.90 % (p < 0.01). Due to the poorer compliance in rural, the expected reduction would be 2 %–10 % less than that in urban. Furthermore, under limited ophthalmologist resources, both in-person and manual telemedicine screening showed minimal carbon reduction (representing <10 % reduction). Human resource constraints prevented comprehensive coverage of residents, leading those not screened to rely on carbon-intensive clinical follow-ups. Consequently, the most digitized fully self-service AI-powered screening with consistently the lowest ICeER values emerged dominant, delivering the greatest carbon reduction while enabling the most timely patients detection. This research underscores that integrating AI is crucial for sustainable healthcare transformation, showcasing how intelligent technologies can tackle climate challenges while addressing health needs.

title: Zoning-grading optimization of watershed ecological security network integrating function and structure: A case study in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area
abstract: Scientifically optimizing the ecological security network and formulating differentiated ecological restoration strategies are the spatial realization path of regional ecological civilization construction and provide ecological foundation guarantee for regional sustainable development. This study establishes a systematic framework for the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (TGRA) that integrates the assessment of ecological security functions, the construction of ecological security network, the analysis of their dynamic coupling coordination, and spatial zoning and grading for optimized management. By integrating landscape ecology with complex network theory, this study identifies key ecological restoration areas, prioritizes restoration levels, and proposes zone-specific optimization strategies based on the coupling coordination relationship between watershed ecological security function and network structure. The results showed that ecological security network exhibits small-world properties with strong local connectivity in the TGRA. High function-structure coupling coordination zones predominantly aligned with ecological sources and major corridors, while low-coordination areas overlapped with human construction zone, revealing dynamic evolution characteristics of ecological security network under conservation-development conflicts. We identified the Zhongliang and Tongluo Mountain areas as priority restoration zones due to severe function-structure discordance. A key finding is that structural enhancement of the watershed ecological security network must precede the improvement of its ecological security function. These insights advance the integration of landscape ecology with network science and provide a actionable framework for spatial ecological restoration.

title: Evaluation of deconvolution methods and loading parameters in nanoindentation characterization of sodium aluminosilicate hydrate gel in fly ash based geopolymers
abstract: In this study, the two critical aspects of nanoindentation techniques—deconvolution methods and loading parameters—for characterizing sodium aluminosilicate hydrate (N-A-S-H) in fly ash based geopolymers were experimentally investigated. Three prevailing deconvolution methods, i.e., Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), Probability Density Functions (PDF), and Cumulative Distribution Functions (CDF), are employed to separate the gel phase and capture its micromechanical properties and proportions. Meanwhile, novel indicators were introduced to assess the effectiveness of deconvolution models. The optimal number of phases (K) was determined using information-theoretic and clustering quality metrics, including the Bayesian Information Criterion, silhouette coefficient, and Calinski–Harabasz index. Furthermore, the Bin Size Index was utilized to optimize the bin size for PDF models, ensuring robust histogram representation. Results indicate that the GMM demonstrates superior fitting quality when the optimal K is 6. The PDF model demonstrated optimal performance under K = 4, with bin sizes of 2.0 GPa and 0.15 GPa for elastic modulus and hardness, respectively. The CDF model achieved an optimal balance between model complexity and fitting accuracy at K = 4. Furthermore, comparative analysis reveals that GMM is superior in clustering capability among the other two deconvolution methods. By utilizing this method, the influences of loading parameters on test results were further studied. It was found that the increase in the holding load leads to a decrease in elastic modulus and hardness with a more concentrated distribution and an increased gel phase proportion, but overlooks local microstructural characteristics. Extended holding times induce creep deformation, creating larger indentation areas that underestimate hardness and affect unloading analyses. A power function relationship exists between mechanical properties and indentation depth, with holding load exerting significantly greater influence than holding time on penetration depth. Based on a comprehensive evaluation of indentation depth, model accuracy, and microstructural preservation, a loading regime of 5 mN for 10 s was identified as optimal for N-A-S-H gel characterization.

title: Five-birds-with-one-stone: Employing novel sucrose derived carbon dots to modify cementitious materials
abstract: Conventional nanomaterials used in cement-based materials generally suffer from poor dispersibility and high production costs, tend to cause excessive hydration heat and low fluidity, and deliver insufficient improvements in mechanical properties and durability. These drawbacks consequently limit their large-scale applicability. To address these challenges, this study proposes a “five-birds-with-one-stone” strategy by developing novel sucrose-derived carbon dots (SCDs), simultaneously achieving five key improvements in cementitious materials: high dispersibility, low cost, reduced hydration heat, enhanced fluidity, and effectively improved mechanical strength and durability. Specifically, SCDs exhibit good dispersion stability in saturated Ca(OH)2 solution. And SCDs are low-cost (0.05 $/g); more importantly, the incorporation of 0.1 wt% SCDs not only reduces mortar cost and CO2 emissions by 16.41 % and 17.87 %, respectively, but also decreases the peak hydration heat by 9.6 % (with a 3 h delay) and enhances mortar fluidity by 14.7 %. Meanwhile, after 28 days of curing, compressive strength and chloride binding capacity are increased by 22 % and 86 %, respectively. Microscale characterization and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that SCDs delay hydration through surface adsorption and Ca2+ complexation, improve workability via by facilitating particle lubrication and regulating interfacial water, and enhance strength and durability by promoting C–S–H formation and increasing chloride physical adsorption. This work presents a multifunctional carbon-based nanomaterial designed to enhance cementitious materials. It effectively overcomes five key limitations including poor dispersibility, high cost, excessive hydration heat, low fluidity, and insufficient mechanical strength and durability, offering a sustainable pathway toward next-generation high-performance construction materials.

title: A lotus-leaf-inspired bionic structured gel membrane made from straw, solvent-free preparation, and surface modification for oil-in-water emulsion separation
abstract: Addressing the persistent bottlenecks of low efficiency, high costs, and complex fabrication in large-scale oil-in-water emulsion separation, especially for submicron emulsions where environmental compatibility and performance further degrade, this work introduces a cost-effective, biomass-derived separation layer, a straw-based gel membrane (SBGM), that emphasizes green design and functional integration. Fabricated via simple straw pretreatment and surface modification under solvent-free conditions, the SBGM is produced through an entirely green and straightforward route: one-step regeneration of straw cellulose to form gel spheres and a supporting matrix, followed by surface coating with a blended PVA/TiO2 functional layer. Featuring a lotus-leaf-inspired bionic structure and abundant hydrophilic groups, the membrane exhibits superhydrophilicity (WCA = 0°) and underwater superoleophobicity (UOCA = 162°), together with exceptional durability and stability against acids, alkalis, and extracellular polymers in wastewater. Critically, it delivers over 99 % separation efficiency across diverse submicron oil-in-water emulsions and maintains stable performance over repeated cycles, with a flux recovery rate of approximately 90 % and a fouling deposition ratio of approximately 30 %. Moreover, the photosensitive properties of TiO2 confer superior hydrophilicity and self-cleaning capability, enabling the SBGM to sustain over 99 % separation efficiency even when treating real kitchen wastewater. Collectively, these advances markedly enhance the SBGM's practical potential for submicron oil-in-water emulsion separation.

title: Bio-based polyelectrolyte complexes for customized soil stabilization: Linking polymer adsorption to soil mechanical performance
abstract: Various chemical processes are used for soil stabilization, which aims to improve soil performance and durability. However, the variability in soil mineralogy, morphology, and composition introduces significant challenges for soil stabilization. This study evaluates two bio-based polyelectrolytes (PEs), cationic chitosan (CHI) and anionic sodium lignosulfonate (LS), and their complexes (PECs), as potential customizable, sustainable stabilizers for two soils – silty sand (SM) and lean clay (CL) containing smectites (e.g., montmorillonite (MMT)). To determine the engineering properties of PE- and PEC-stabilized soils of different types, the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) and direct shear strength under dry and wet conditions were evaluated. These tests provide complementary performance metrics, which are directly applicable to subgrade design and offer insights into soil behavior. Individually tested LS, CHI, and CHI/LS PECs at molar ratios of 0.3 and 3.5 (in moles of polymer units), abbreviated as PEC-0.3 and PEC-3.5, showed different improvement levels in dry UCS, which were tailorable to specific soil types by a selection of specific PEs and PEC compositions. When tested in wet conditions, CHI- and PEC-stabilized soils retained their structural integrity and demonstrated superior moisture resistance (up to 68 % higher UCS retention) compared to the untreated samples. In direct shear tests, PECs outperformed individual PEs in shear strength improvement. The improvement in shear strength of the silty sand was due to an increase in cohesion, while it was due to increasing both cohesion and friction angle for the clay-rich soil. In addition, to establish correlations between PE-induced soil stabilization and binding of PEs with mineral particles, this work quantitatively assessed the adsorption of CHI, LS, and their PECs onto surfaces of the soil components (MMT and quartz, QZ) and established the molecular basis for the high effectiveness of CHI in soil stabilization. This work highlights the promise of using bio-based polyelectrolytes for soil stabilization as an eco-friendly alternative to traditional chemical stabilizers.

title: The green performance of major economies within global green value chains: A 20-year review
abstract: Global value chains (GVCs) are central to both economic integration and the redistribution of environmental burdens. However, existing studies have largely focused on single-dimensional metrics, either economic value added or environmental footprints, failing to provide an integrated assessment of green performance. This gap limits our understanding of genuine trade benefits in an environmentally constrained world. To bridge this gap, this study develops a novel framework for decomposing global green value chains (GGVCs) based on environmentally extended multi-regional input–output (EMRIO) model, to assess the evolution of green value added (GVA) across 19 major economies from 2000 to 2020. The analysis reveals that the gap in the green production and exports level between developed and developing economies has largely narrowed in the past 20 years with their disproportionate strides in enhancing environmental sustainability, while developed economies continue to capture a higner share of GVA by externalizing environmental burdens through trade. GVCs trade production dominates the GVA that is generated by the production of trade products. Substantial heterogeneity emerges across economies, with resource- and technology-intensive economies capturing the higher levels of real green trade gains. For most economies, changes in the economic scale are the main driving factors of changes in GVA, and the effects of green technology and input‒output technology are also important factors that cannot be ignored. The study contributes empirical novelty by quantifying green gains along value chains over two decades, and it underscores the urgent need for policies that align trade benefits with environmental responsibilities. Our results inform international just transition and suggest that green upgrading of GVCs is pivotal for achieving equitable and sustainable low-carbon transitions.

title: Mild extraction of PdAg precious metal components and efficient recovery of Al2O3 supports from spent acetylene hydrogenation catalyst
abstract: Addressing the challenges of simultaneously extracting Pd and Ag components from spent acetylene hydrogenation catalysts, severe structural damage to the Al2O3 supports, and high wastewater discharge, here, we propose a “hydrochloric acid–ammonium chloride–ammonia” (HCl–NH4Cl–NH3) complexation system that enables efficient extraction of PdAg leaching alongside recovery of the Al2O3 supports. The leaching rates of Pd and Ag exhibit an increasing trend with rising concentrations of HCl, NH4Cl, and NH3, the increase of reaction temperature, and the extension of reaction time. Nevertheless, excessively high HCl concentration, overly elevated reaction temperature, and unduly prolonged reaction time caused some damage to the structure of the alumina support and reduce its mechanical strength. Under optimized conditions (0.2 M HCl, 1.0 M NH4Cl, 120 °C, 6 h, 5 wt% ammonia), the PdAg components were efficiently leached while effectively preserving the crystal phase and pore structure of the Al2O3 beads. The leaching rates of Pd and Ag reached 95.6 % and 94.4 %, respectively; and the recovered Al2O3 beads have a pore diameter of 30.8 nm, a specific pore volume of 0.244 mL g−1, a specific surface area of 29.2 m2/g, and a crushing strength of 53.2 N, corresponding to retention rates of 95.2 %, 96.0 %, 100.2 %, and 98.6 %, respectively. The HCl–NH4Cl–NH3 complexation system, combined with cyclic washing, shows advantages of low cost, mild extraction conditions, and reduced wastewater discharge, which keeps to the principles of green development.

title: Risk identification and prediction of corporate low-carbon transition via multi-agent reinforcement learning: Using OpenEI and CDP database
abstract: This work identifies and predicts the multi-dimensional risks faced by enterprises during the low-carbon transition process, thus improving the scientific nature of risk management and the targeted nature of policy interventions. Based on this, the work implements an integrated model combining multi-agent reinforcement learning with causal inference. The data used includes the multi-source heterogeneous data from the Open Energy Information platform and the Carbon Disclosure Project database. The potential transformation failure issues may arise in the enterprises under the influence of factors such as insufficient carbon disclosure, delayed policy response, and weak governance structures. To address these issues, the work designs behavior mechanisms for three types of agents: enterprises, governments, and investors. It establishes a risk evolution simulation system and uses causal graphs and the Causal Forest algorithm to identify key causal paths. This work focuses on solving the following problems: (1) How to model the dynamic game behavior between enterprises and the policy environment for risk prediction; (2) How to identify deep mechanism variables for risk formation through causal inference; (3) How to achieve integrated modeling of risk identification, mechanism explanation, and intervention evaluation. Experimental comparisons with models such as Deep Causal Forest and Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning are made. The results demonstrate that the optimized model outperforms others in prediction accuracy, stability, and interpretability. With a sample size of 3,000, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 0.882, an Area Under Curve value of 0.957, and a precision of 0.854, significantly outperforming existing models. Furthermore, causal tracing results show that carbon disclosure quality, corporate governance capability, and policy intensity are the three core causal risk variables. Among them, the average causal effect of carbon disclosure scores is −0.164, indicating high intervention potential. Therefore, this work provides theoretical innovation and technical pathways for risk identification and prediction in corporate low-carbon transition, and offers significant reference value and practical implications for green governance and corporate strategic decision-making.

title: Transport, logistics, and emergent technology within the circular economy
abstract: The paper reviews various important topics at the nexus of the themes of the special issue Transport, Logistics, and Emergent Technology within the Circular Economy. An overview of the articles and directions for research are also presented.

title: Outstanding self-healing ability of weathered asphalts endowed with deeply degraded tire rubber
abstract: The decline in the self-healing capability of aged asphalt leads to the deterioration of pavement. Incorporating tire rubber into asphalt both enhances the self-healing ability of aged asphalt and provides a sustainable solution to the growing accumulation of waste tires. In this study, deeply degraded tire rubber (DR) containing a high content of liquid rubber was used as a modifier to evaluate the self-healing ability of aged asphalt. The effects of DR on the physical, chemical, and rheological properties of the modified asphalt during weathering were investigated. Dynamic mechanical analyzer, dynamic shear rheometer, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, fluorescence microscope, gel permeation chromatography and toluene solubility analysis were used to explore the self-healing ability and aging mechanism. The self-healing mechanisms were analyzed through wetting and molecular diffusion. The results revealed that DR increased the surface energy and enhanced the molecular segment mobility, thus significantly enhancing the self-healing efficiency (from 72.9 % to 100.9 % at 25 °C) of modified asphalt, concurrently reducing the initial self-healing temperature (from 30 to −10 °C). Fluorescence microscopy indicated that the DR modified asphalt retained its network structure. Rheological properties (lower complex modulus) and toluene solubility tests of aged samples demonstrated that DR delayed asphalt aging through a degradation-recombination process during weathering. Moreover, the degradation of rubber and hardening of asphalt synergistically modulated the viscoelastic behavior of the composite modified asphalt. Understanding the self-healing behavior of tire rubber in the modified asphalt during weathering is of great significance for improving pavement service life.

title: Silica-structured lignin biochar engineered via pyrolysis for multifunctional remediation of Cd-contaminated soils
abstract: Soil cadmium (Cd) pollution poses a serious threat to food security and ecosystem health. Silicon (Si)-modified biochar shows great promise for remediation; however, the critical influence of the timing of Si introduction (whether during hydrothermal or pyrolysis synthesis) on Si speciation, stability, and interactions within soil-plant systems has been largely overlooked. This study systematically compares two preparation methods: introducing silicon during hydrothermal (HPC-Si@HT) or pyrolysis (HPC-Si@PY) stages. Comprehensive characterization revealed that HPC-Si@PY formed a stable amorphous silica structure, yielding a significantly higher Cd2+ adsorption capacity (315.53 mg/g) than HPC-Si@HT, primarily via ion exchange and C-Si complexation. In contrast, HPC-Si@HT, with lower stability, relied on complexation and precipitation. Pot experiments confirmed the remarkable remediation efficacy of HPC-Si@PY: it reduced exchangeable Cd by 26.1 % while increasing residual Cd by 143.3 % through silicon-driven precipitation and pH modulation. Furthermore, HPC-Si@PY enhances soil multifunctionality by improving nutrient cycling and enriching Cd-resistant microbes. For Pakchoi, HPC-Si@PY increases biomass by 81.67 % and reduces Cd accumulation by 68.96 % through integrated mechanisms of rhizosphere immobilization, antioxidant activation, and silicon-mediated deposition. The limited performance of HPC-Si@HT underscores the fundamental importance of incorporating silicon during the pyrolysis stage to create stable, reactive amorphous silica structures. These findings establish crucial design principles for engineering effective silicon-biochar that enable superior cross-scale remediation of Cd-contaminated environments.

title: Seasonal response greenhouse gas accounting model supporting regionalized carbon reduction in wastewater treatment plants
abstract: Greenhouse gas mitigation in wastewater treatment plants is imperative under global climate change. However, existing greenhouse gas estimation models lack seasonal adaptability and high-resolution data integration, obscuring spatiotemporal emission heterogeneity and hindering climate-specific strategies. To address these limitations, a seasonal-responsive greenhouse gas accounting framework was developed, incorporating temperature-sensitive emission factors and multi-temporal datasets to holistically quantify process-wide emissions. To validate the model's seasonal responsiveness, greenhouse gas emission accounting was conducted specifically for wastewater treatment plants in cold regions. The findings revealed marked seasonal disparities in emissions, with winter greenhouse gas intensity surging by 26.24 %. Compared to traditional carbon accounting models, the proposed model applied to high-temporal-resolution datasets exhibits significantly enhanced sensitivity to seasonal fluctuations. Leveraging the regional emission patterns derived from the seasonal-responsive model, a region-tailored near-zero-carbon framework was developed to achieve substantial carbon offset potential without compromising treatment efficacy. By bridging seasonal emission dynamics with greenhouse gas reduction imperatives, this work provides scalable strategies for transforming wastewater treatment plants into energy-efficient systems, advancing global climate governance objectives.

title: Integrated processing of ionic liquid recovery with clean hydrogen production via electrodialysis in biorefinery
abstract: Ionic liquids have caught wide attention in biorefinery due to a few unique characteristics. The efficient and fast recycling of ionic liquids is necessary before their scale-up application in practical biorefinery. The feasibility of integrated ionic liquid recovery with clean hydrogen production has rarely been studied. Electrodialysis has been verified valid in the recovery of different ionic liquids after biomass processing, which could also be used for clean hydrogen production. Thus the integrated recovery of ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate (EmimAc) with clean hydrogen production after biomass pretreatment was studied based on an electrodialysis unit, which could selectively transfer Emim+ with Ac− from diluted compartment to concentrated compartment and realize the hydrogen evolution reaction of H+ on the cathode. The recovery ratio of EmimAc, transfer rate of Emim+ and specific energy consumption for EmimAc recovery reached 98.7 %, 598.2 mmol/(m2·min) and 7.385 mol/kw·h. The production rate of H2 and Faraday efficiency approached 670.76 mmol/(m2·min) and 97.1 %. The operational stability of electrodialysis and recycling performance of regenerated EmimAc were both testified for 5 cycles without showing obvious reduction. The calculated recovery cost for EmimAc was less than 0.5 % of its purchasing price. Results of this research provided a new insight for the system design of cleaner processing of ionic liquid recovery with H2 production in biorefinery.

title: The evolving structure of emissions in the transition to renewable electricity systems
abstract: Deep decarbonization of national energy systems requires high percentages of renewable electricity supply and significant electrification of transport and heat. As the proportion of renewable electricity supply increases, operational emissions will gradually decrease, making embodied emissions a more important component of the total emissions of these future electricity systems. Embodied emissions from electricity systems remain largely overlooked in existing energy and climate policy frameworks that prioritise operational emissions. Life cycle assessment (LCA) provides a systematic approach to evaluating both the operational and embodied emissions from these electricity systems. However, systematic LCA studies of future highly renewable electricity systems are scarce, and previous studies have omitted emissions associated with distribution and transmission infrastructure. To address these gaps, this study applies scenario-based LCA modelling to six future decarbonization scenarios for the New Zealand national electricity system, including a scenario that achieves 100 % renewable supply by 2045. Comparative analysis of two periods (2020–2035 vs. 2036–2050) shows operational and maintenance emissions drop from 85 % to 60 % of total life cycle emissions, while the share of embodied emissions more than doubles. Mitigation priorities should therefore shift from reducing fossil fuel use to improving and decarbonizing renewable energy technologies as their share grows. Including embodied emissions results in all five scenarios exceeding the electricity sector's allocated carbon budget by around 2037. The framework and findings in this study are applicable to other countries pursuing deep decarbonization of their energy system.

title: Recent heat wave across the Yunnan-Guizhou plateau and its impact on alpine lakes
abstract: Lakes are integral components of the global terrestrial ecosystem, with lake water temperature serving as a key parameter influencing the physical and biogeochemical processes within lake systems. In recent years, however, the intensification of global warming has significantly impacted lake water temperatures, resulting in a range of environmental consequences, including the increased frequency and intensity of algal blooms (ABs). This study focused on the Yunnan-Guizhou (YG) Plateau, a region sensitive to climate change, as the research area. The warming trends of the whole area were analyzed since the establishment of 234 meteorological stations. The trends in land surface water temperature (LSWT) and the ABs risk in 14 plateau lakes over the past 25 years were assessed using MODIS land surface temperature dataset, water quality monitoring data, and key climatic parameters, an evaluation framework was developed using machine learning algorithms (random forest, RF) and logistic regression (LR) models. The main findings of this study are as follows: 1. The YG Plateau has undergone significant warming since 1960 (0.20 °C/10a), with the most rapid temperature increase occurring after 2000 (0.37 °C/10a) and 2023 recorded as the warmest year on record; 2. All 14 lakes in the region have exhibited significant warming, although the rate of increase in LSWT is lower than that of the surrounding air temperature (0.26 °C/10a lower); 3. The ABs risk range is influenced by the lakes' water quality characteristics, all lakes have shown a significant increase in higher risk levels of ABs over the past 25 years. This study aims to provide a scientific basis for the development of climate change adaptation strategies and holds practical significance for the management of local aquatic environments.

title: Construction and optimization of wetland ecological networks integrating subjective–objective integrated weighting and scale effects: A case study of the Wuhan metropolitan area
abstract: Wetlands are essential components of ecosystems, providing key ecological services such as water regulation, habitat support, and climate moderation. They also serve as critical ecological infrastructure for regional sustainable development. However, rapid urbanization has led to significant wetland loss and reduced connectivity, disrupting species migration routes, shrinking habitats, degrading biodiversity, and intensifying environmental pollution. Traditional single-scale ecological network construction methods are insufficient to address the complexity of these challenges. This study proposes a multi-scale wetland ecological network framework by identifying ecological sources at three spatial levels, constructing a resistance system through subject-object integrated weighting, and incorporating the cross-scale effects of corridors. Ecological corridors were then generated using Circuitscape and spatial overlay analysis. Results reveal that: (1) landscape patterns reveal a shrinkage of core patches and a loss of connectivity-relevant areas, with core patch coverage decreasing from 81.34 % in municipal districts to 30.57 % in main urban areas. Ecological sources are primarily concentrated along major rivers and lakes in the central metropolitan area; (2) resistance factors vary by scale, but land use and distance from higher-level corridors consistently hinder connectivity; (3) the integrated network forms dense corridors in southern Wuhan, eastern Xiantao, and southeastern Huangshi, while the northern region remains fragmented; and (4) the multi-scale wetland ecological network significantly enhances the network structure compared to the single scale model, while highly matching the distribution of target species and ecological policies. Innovations lie in integrating subjective-objective weighting for resistance factors, incorporating cross-scale interactions, and applying these advances to the construction of a multi-scale wetland ecological network. This framework provides practical guidance for cross-jurisdictional wetland planning, spatial optimization, and the transition from passive restoration to resilience-based conservation.

title: Sustainable and mechanically robust fully bio-based aerogels with leaf-inspired structure for multifunctional air filtration
abstract: Air pollution from intensive livestock farms threatens human health, animal welfare, and ecosystem sustainability. Most existing air filters are unable to achieve efficient purification of particulate matter (PM), ammonia (NH3), and bacteria simultaneously. Inspired by the dust-proof property of natural leaves, this study proposes a biomimetic design strategy based on a cross-scale mechanism to fabricate high-performance air filters. Using silk fibroin (SF) as the matrix and loofah sponge (LS) as the three-dimensional scaffold, the hydrogen bond network and pore structure of the aerogel were regulated by carboxymethyl chitosan (CMC) and gelatin (GT). The SF/CMC/GT/LS (SCGL) composite aerogel with biomimetic leaf structure was successfully synthesized. The biomimetic structure endows the SCGL aerogel to exhibit the characteristics of low density, mechanical robustness, and low pressure drop. Component synergy enables aerogel multifunctional filtration performance, including efficient PM interception (>99.43 %), NH3 adsorption capacity (239.60 cm3/g) and antibacterial efficacy (>84.26 %). Simultaneously, the SCGL aerogel demonstrates biodegradability and negligible environmental impact. This work provides a simple, efficient, and eco-friendly biomimetic strategy for air purification, advancing agricultural efficiency and environmental sustainability.

title: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of a biobased solvent-driven lignocellulosic biomass refinery
abstract: Conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to fuels is one of promising pathways to tackle the emerging fossil fuels depletion and environmental pollution issues. Within the biorefining supply chain, pretreatment is a critical step in fractionating cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin for downstream utilization. While biobased green solvents pretreatment shows great promise for efficient biomass fractionation under mild conditions, its industrial feasibility remains uncertain due to the lack of comprehensive analysis at the system level. This study evaluates the industrial feasibility of employing dimethyl isosorbide (DMI) as a representative biobased green solvent within a scalable, closed-loop biorefinery process for the efficient fractionation of lignocellulosic biomass. Here, strategies to enhance lignin recovery and DMI recycling were developed and optimized guided by techno-economic assessment and life cycle assessment assisted with process simulation. The MSP of ethanol produced by designed conceptional biorefinery is estimated to $1169.7/t with a GWP of −0.431 kg CO2 eq./kg when solid loading of pretreatment reaches 20 % and biomass used for heat and electricity. In addition, two alternative value-added products, 2,3-BDO and high purity DMI, are simulated with MSPs of $1567.4/t and $1731.5/t with GWPs of −0.257 kg CO2 eq./kg and 1.06 kg CO2 eq./kg, respectively, lower than reported values. This work provides an example for evaluation-guided experimental optimization, accelerating the transition to carbon-neutral biorefining systems.

title: Research on the urban carbon reduction effect and impact mechanism of regional collaborative innovation: An quasi-natural experiment based on the G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor in the Yangtze River Delta
abstract: Regional collaborative innovation plays a significant role in the low-carbon transformation of cities and the shaping of new industrial patterns. Based on the analytical framework of the STIRPAT model, this study takes the construction of the G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor in the Yangtze River Delta as a quasi-natural experiment. It employs the difference-in-differences (DID) method to empirically examine the effect of regional collaborative innovation on urban carbon emission reduction, and incorporates a mediation effect model to further clarify the pathways and transmission mechanisms through which regional collaborative innovation influences urban carbon emissions. The results reveal a significant spatiotemporal dynamic correlation between the implementation of the collaborative innovation strategy and the reduction in urban carbon emission intensity, with the effect being particularly pronounced in interprovincial adjacent areas. Empirical analysis demonstrates that regional collaborative innovation significantly contributes to urban carbon emission reduction. This conclusion remains robust after controlling for parallel trends and conducting a series of robustness tests, including PSM-DID and placebo tests. Comparatively, the carbon reduction effects of interregional collaborative innovation are more prominent in interprovincial neighboring cities, higher-tier cities, cities with low carbon emission intensity, and resource-based cities, as opposed to average cities. Moreover, the policy dividends of regional collaborative innovation exhibit a certain degree of lag and transformation period, and the effects display a significantly increasing marginal trend over time. Mechanism analysis indicates that regional collaborative innovation primarily promotes urban carbon emission reduction through four key pathways: infrastructure improvement and upgrading, industrial structure transformation, market integration, and the innovation and diffusion of green technologies.

title: Degradation of organic refractory contaminants by phosphate buffer activated peroxymonosulfate: The overlooked roles of oxygen reactive species
abstract: Phosphate was generally applied as a buffer and its effect as a common water constituent has been extensively investigated in peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-contained advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), although its role remains controversial. In this study, it was surprisingly found that phosphate buffer solution (PBS) was readily to activate PMS at initial pH (pH0) of 7.0 and 8.0 with different activation pathways, and satisfactory removal efficiencies (≥95 %) were achieved for all nine target organic refractory compounds (ORCs) especially at pH0 8.0, thus the catalytic contribution of PBS might be underestimated. Typical quenching methods, electron spin resonance (ESR) spectrum and density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrated that HPO42− and H2PO4− could effectively break the O-O bond of PMS, leading to the formation of different active radicals (i.e., sulfate radical, singlet oxygen, etc.) in the PBS/PMS system. The probable degradation pathway was elucidated. The toxicity of the intermediates was predicted and the biotoxicity of the treated solution was monitored. In addition, the PBS/PMS system could be well reused and maintained strong resistance and tolerance to most common inorganic ions (Cl−, NO3−, PO43− and SO42−) and natural organic matter (NOM). Overall, this work provides a promising metal-free PMS technique, highlights the overlooked roles of oxygen reactive species, and thereby deepens our understanding of PBS/PMS process in water purification.

title: Mechanisms of AMF-mediated correlation between nutrient uptake and soil micropatterns in sugar beet plants under rotational and continuous cropping soil environments
abstract: Continuous cropping limits the sustainability of sugar beet cultivation, and as an important soil-plant symbiotic microorganism, the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi can significantly mitigate crop growth stress. This study utilises sugar beet as the subject of investigation, employing physiological and biochemical indices alongside amplicon sequencing technology to analyse the regulatory mechanisms of AMF inoculation on the growth, soil physicochemical properties, and rhizosphere microbial communities of sugar beet in continuous cropping. The findings indicate that AMF enhanced plant nutrient uptake through the mycelial network and significantly increased biomass. Inoculation of AMF improves soil structure; pH is increased by 0.3–0.5; the mycelial network further activates phosphorus, promotes nitrogen transport, and improves soil nutrient use efficiency. AMF also enhances soil extracellular enzyme activity, with phosphatase activity elevated by 35.2 %–42.7 % across all treatment groups. Amplicon sequencing data indicate that AMF treatment enhances the diversity of rhizosphere microorganisms, diminishes the prevalence of harmful bacteria, elevates the fraction of beneficial bacteria such as Proteobacteria and Actinobacteria, and stabilizes the microbial ecological network. PLS-PM analysis shows that AMF improves the adaptability of sugar beet to the soil environment and promotes nitrogen partitioning capability by elevating soil enzyme activity and nutrient efficiency. The experiment proves that AMF can effectively mitigate the continuous cropping disorder in sugar beet, which provides a theoretical basis for the utilisation of AMF in sugar beet farming. Subsequent research should investigate the impacts of various bacterial strains and their interactions with the soil, refine application methods, and advance the environmentally sustainable farming of sugar beet.

title: Sustainable MXene-mediated in-situ ZnO/cellulose composites via green fabrication with enhanced mechanical durability, antimicrobial activity, and EMI shielding performance
abstract: The development of multifunctional composite films integrating robust mechanical strength, potent antibacterial activity, and efficient electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding is critical for advancing next-generation smart materials. Herein, the rational engineering of CEL@ZnO/MXene composite films was achieved by the in-situ growth of ZnO nanoparticles on cellulose substrates and by synergistically harnessing the unique physicochemical attributes of ZnO and two-dimensional MXene nanosheets. This interfacially engineered and network-reinforced structure endowed the CEL@ZnO/MXene 5:5 composite film with superior mechanical properties, including a tensile strength of 32.5 MPa, a Young's modulus of 2.35 GPa, and an elongation at break of 1.87% achieving a balanced integration of strength, stiffness, and flexibility. In addition, the CEL@ZnO/MXene 5:5 composite film exhibited potent bioactive functionality by achieving antibacterial efficiencies of 86.2% against Escherichia coli, 89.4% against Staphylococcus aureus, and antioxidant activity exceeding 80%, which in turn mitigates bacterial proliferation and oxidative stress. Furthermore, the obtained CEL@ZnO/MXene 5:5 composite film exhibits an EMI shielding property of 38.67 dB across the X-band (8.2–12.4 GHz) with reflection coefficients consistently above 0.8, indicating stable properties dominated by surface reflection complemented by controlled absorption. This study highlights the extensive application potential of the composite films in antibacterial protection, environmental safety, and electronic equipment shielding due to combined advantages in mechanical robustness, effective antibacterial activity, and electromagnetic interference shielding.

title: Designing resilient remanufacturing strategies: A probabilistic framework for uncertainty-aware decision making
abstract: Remanufacturing is a vital strategy for advancing sustainability and resource efficiency across diverse industries. However, developing effective remanufacturing plans remains challenging due to inherent uncertainties, such as varying conditions of returned products and fluctuating market demands. Previous studies have a limitation in reflecting these uncertainties, as they rely on deterministic inputs in optimization models. This study proposes a new framework—referred to as Probabilistic Green Profit Design (PrGPD) model—that explicitly incorporates uncertainties into remanufacturing optimization. The model assigns probability density functions to key parameters based on expert knowledge and empirical data, enabling stochastic analysis through synthetic data generation. Furthermore, the framework identifies critical factors affecting remanufacturing outcomes by analyzing constraint activities under varying conditions. The proposed approach was validated through a case study involving a recreational boat engine. The results showed that improvements in the quality of disassembled parts directly enhance both profitability and carbon reduction, justifying the targeted investments in Design for Remanufacturing (DfR), early-return programs, and quality inspection systems. Additionally, the analysis revealed that profit margins remain stable across different market conditions, indicating that green profit opportunities are robust even under demand fluctuations. Overall, this research develops a practical and adaptable decision-support tool for remanufacturing businesses, providing more resilient strategies than traditional deterministic approaches.

title: Does ecological product protection compensation have a green effect? Empirical evidence based on the value accounting of ecological products in key ecological functional areas of the Yellow River Basin
abstract: The construction of ecological civilization is a core national strategy for sustainable development in China, and realizing ecological product value is a critical foundation. Using 2010–2023 panel data for the Yellow River Basin and 30m grid-level land-use data, this study measures ecological product value via an integrated framework combining market valuation and equivalence factor methods, and constructs a multidimensional ecological compensation model to assess regional compensation capacity across ecological, economic, and social dimensions. A two-stage system generalized method of moments (SYS-GMM) model is then employed to examine how compensation capacity affects ecological product value realization. Results show that stronger compensation capacity significantly promotes value realization and remains robust across multiple tests; the effects are heterogeneous across hydrological zones, development stages, and urban–rural integration levels. Mechanism analysis identifies new-quality productivity as the main transmission channel, while the digital economy and green finance strengthen the compensation effect; additional evidence from super-efficiency epsilon-based measure (Super-EBM) estimations and multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) analyses indicates improved spatiotemporal efficiency and positive impacts of pilot policies. These findings provide empirical support for optimizing ecological product compensation frameworks and advancing sustainable value transformation in ecologically sensitive regions.

title: Dynamic modeling of consumer behavior in sustainable food markets
abstract: Organic food markets face a persistent problem of delivering reliable availability and acceptable profitability while meeting strict limits on waste and greenhouse emissions. This research develops a continuous time behavior to operations framework that links consumer choice, shaped by health concerns, label credibility, price salience, and product visibility, to service level inventory control for perishable goods while jointly determining pricing, replenishment, and marketing policies. The methodology employs risk aware optimization to guard against adverse demand and supply conditions, establishes rigorous performance guarantees, and assesses policy effectiveness through simulations calibrated to settings representative of California and India. The results indicate that maintaining target service levels and on-shelf availability strengthens reputation, reduces price sensitivity, speeds switching to organic products, and enables coordinated pricing, marketing, and replenishment to raise profit while meeting waste and emission limits; the profit-environment trade-off is well behaved, yielding practical rules for prices and steady stock levels. The framework abstracts from individual-level heterogeneity and uses stylized costs, so it requires local calibration and would benefit from multi-product extensions and field studies; in practice, it offers clear levers-service targets, focused marketing, and disciplined pricing-to grow organic adoption with safeguards. The contribution is a unified, easy-to-apply behavior-to-operations framework with mathematical guarantees that links consumer psychology to operational control under sustainability guardrails, providing actionable guidance for managers and policymakers.

title: Unraveling greenhouse gas accumulation and emission characteristics of partial and full nitrification-denitrification in anaerobic/aerobic/anoxic municipal wastewater treatment systems
abstract: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from biological nutrient removal in municipal wastewater treatment arise from multiple operational phases, yet the spatiotemporal patterns across gas-liquid phases remain poorly resolved. This study quantified gaseous and dissolved N2O, CH4 and CO2 in two parallel sequencing batch reactors (SBRs) inoculated with partial and full nitrification-denitrification (PND and FND) sludge, treating identical municipal wastewater under an anaerobic/aerobic/anoxic operation mode. Results showed that the anaerobic phase was dominated by CH4 release, with transient dissolved N2O (dN2O) generated after mixing being nearly completely reduced and both systems exhibiting strong N2O reduction capacity. The aerobic phase was characterized by CO2 release, while CH4 was mainly stripped at aeration onset. The average N2O emission rate in PND-SBR was 1.3 times that of FND-SBR. In the anoxic phase, N2O dominated GHG emissions, with PND-SBR releasing 3.5-fold more N2O than FND-SBR. dN2O in PND-SBR increased from 0.17 ± 0.07 mg-N/L to 0.23 ± 0.08 mg-N/L, whereas FND-SBR exhibited notable N2O reduction capacity, with effluent dN2O decreasing to 0.01 mg-N/L. Overall, the carbon-equivalent emissions of PND-SBR were 1.7 times those of FND-SBR. Metagenomic analysis revealed that Dechloromonas, enriched in FND-SBR, harbored nosZ genes typically associated with high N2O affinity, suggesting a potential role in enhanced N2O reduction. Moreover, higher abundance of CH4 oxidation genes in FND-SBR contributed to its slightly lower CH4 emissions. These findings advance understanding of phase-specific GHG dynamics in PND/FND systems under the AOA mode and provide actionable insights for targeted GHG monitoring and process optimization toward sustainable wastewater treatment.

title: Simultaneously reducing carbon emissions and endogenous pollutants release: a novel CaO2 composite-induced in-situ microbial community reconfiguration
abstract: In response to the mutual promotion of water eutrophication and greenhouse effect, a composite CaO2 (CCM) which slowly releases O2 and induces CH4 oxidation was developed in this study. Unlike exogenous microbial addition, CCM reshaped the native microbial community, enriching indigenous methane oxidizers for a more stable and cost-effective solution. The results indicated the domain-limiting effect of CCM ensured a long-lasting O2 release, prolonging the release duration by 2.6-fold versus powdered CaO2. Optimal effect was achieved at the CCM dosage of 150 g m−2, which reduced the NH4+-N, PO43−-P, and COD in the overlying water by 88.74 %, 89.01 %, and 81.45 %, and decreased the global warming potential by 83.99 %. The oxidation property and dissolution products of CCM inhibited methanogenic archaea proliferation, while increased methanotrophic bacteria abundance, CH4 monooxygenase activity, Proteobacterial pmoA in surface sediments and M. nitroreducens mcrA in middle sediments. By reducing greenhouse gas production and promoting CH4 oxidation, the CCM established a three-dimensional metabolic network of “surface aerobic oxidation, middle anaerobic oxidation, and deep heterotrophic metabolism”, which could provide new ideas for carbon reduction and ecological restoration in slow-flow water.

title: Petrophysical responses to different CO2 injection methods in shale: Insights from flow and geological sequestration
abstract: CO2 injection into shale integrates resource exploration with carbon sequestration. Prior investigations have relied predominantly on crushed samples or CO2-brine mixtures to study long-term geochemical interactions during soaking. Consequently, the essential mechanisms governing the evolution of flow capacity and microstructure across different injection methods remain poorly understood under realistic formation conditions. This study employs nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and multiple characterization techniques to investigate the microscopic mechanisms of flow evolution and sequestration efficacy across different CO2 injection methods under actual formation conditions. Quantitative criteria are established to evaluate the contributions of distinct processes, and the influences of key factors and their interactions are systematically analyzed. Furthermore, a prediction model with multifactor coupling is constructed based on correlation analysis. The results show that CO2 soaking under thermodynamic equilibrium transitions from physical to chemical control as pressure increases. At low pressure, limited particle migration rises blockage risks in micropores in zones above 0.06 mD. Elevated pressure enhances elastic energy, improving flow capacity by 100–200 % in zones below 0.06 mD despite increased macropore blockage risks. Conversely, CO2 flooding remains physically controlled by pressure gradients. Low pressure causes sharp flow decline due to particle blockage in narrow pore-throats, while increased pressure promotes high-speed CO2 flow, reducing flow capacity by 7.79 %–50.48 % but increasing CO2 gas column height by 1.67 %–18.32 %. For engineering practice, CO2 flooding should be avoided in high-permeability, low-porosity formations under low pressure. Instead, during the middle-to-late stages, massive flooding in ankerite-rich zones is recommended to couple capillary and mineralization trapping.

title: An advanced fuzzy based multi-layered decision-making system for sustainable carbon emission reduction strategy selection in steel industry
abstract: The steel industry generates close to 8% of global carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, releasing about 1.85 tons of CO2 for every ton of steel produced. Tackling this challenge requires decision-support tools that can handle uncertainty and balance competing criteria. This work introduces a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) model that combines Interval-Valued Bipolar Fuzzy Soft Sets (IVBFSS), the Logarithmic Percentage Change-Driven Objective Weighting method (LOPCOW), and an enhanced COBRA ranking procedure. Assessments from three decision-makers were combined using the IVBFSS Weighted Aggregation Operator and Score function, enabling both linguistic vagueness and differing expert perspectives to be represented. The ranking derived from the model is: Legal and liability framework for storage (1) > Revenue from CO2 utilization (0.593) >CO2 concentration in flue gas (0.584) > Transport infrastructure availability (0.404) > Maintenance requirements (0.153) > Net CO2 emissions reduction (0.097) > Energy consumption per ton of captured CO2 (0). This outcome points to the central role of legal frameworks, utilization revenues, and flue gas concentration, while high energy demand emerges as the least attractive option. To test robustness, the rankings were compared with nine established MCDM approaches using Spearman and Kendall correlation coefficients, along with significance testing. Sensitivity checks were also applied using bootstrap resampling to obtain confidence intervals, Monte Carlo simulations to test stability under weight variations, and comparisons across different objective weighting schemes. Together, these evaluations demonstrated our framework yields consistent and dependable results under a range of conditions.

title: Operationalizing urban greenery for carbon mitigation futures: From potential to practice
abstract: Urban carbon emissions are a major driver of climate change, which makes sustainable decarbonization strategies essential. Urban greenery is a promising nature-based solution, but its long-term potential for carbon sequestration is often underestimated because research tends to focus on short-term benefits such as aesthetics, cooling effects, and energy savings. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic literature review of 175 publications (with no restriction on publication year) to examine urban greenery's role in decarbonization across three dimensions, i.e., mechanisms (carbon fixation and storage processes), technologies (methods for quantifying carbon fluxes), and implementation (multi-scale interventions). The quantitative evidence shows substantial but variable impacts. Some green spaces can sequester thousands of tons of CO2 annually, and in a few cases, offset up to about 7% of municipal emissions, while green roofs sequester on average about 0.3–0.4 kg CO2 m−2. Progress is nevertheless limited by a lack of dynamic lifecycle assessments, fragmented data, and a gap between design optimizations and real-world implementation. We propose that future efforts should develop integrated frameworks that combine dynamic life-cycle inventories, multi-source data fusion, and AI-enhanced cross-scale modeling. Based on policy-public collaborative governance pathway, implementing scalable guidelines and toolkits that span building, neighborhood, and urban scales will help translate these strategies into context-specific actions that advance climate resilience and equitable urban futures.

title: Multi-load Undersea single-wire inductive power transfer system for sustainable ocean observation
abstract: Ocean observation constitutes a fundamental aspect of researching the sustainable development of marine environments. Mooring buoys, equipped with an array of underwater sensors, facilitate fixed-point ocean observation, serving as a crucial method for data collection. Nevertheless, the reliance on battery-powered underwater sensors necessitates annual retrieval and maintenance, incurring significant costs and hindering sustainable practices. In this paper, an Underwater Single-Wire Inductive Power Transfer (USWIPT) system is proposed. Through the transmission medium composed of mooring cable and seawater, the solar energy collected on the water surface is transmitted to the underwater sensor, thereby improving the sustainability of the system. The circuit model of the system was meticulously constructed, and the factors influencing system efficiency were thoroughly investigated. The quality factor of the system is dictated by the number of loads, which subsequently impacts efficiency. The accuracy of the circuit model is validated through experiments performed on a USWIPT system prototype equipped with a 50-m-long mooring cable. The multi-load USWIPT system can open up a new cleaner power transmission technology for sustainable ocean observation.

title: Layer-by-layer assembly pesticide carrier with the balance between adhesion and controlled release for pest control
abstract: The adhesion and controlled release of pesticide carriers are difficult to balance, which is the main reason for the inefficient use of pesticides and ecological hazards. In this work, a novel pesticide carrier with the balance between adhesion and controlled release is constructed by layer-by-layer assembly technique. This carrier has a unique layered structure, which not only increases the drug loading (18.88 %), but also realizes the coordinated control of rapid passive release and stimulus-responsive release of pesticide. The release rate of avermectin rapidly increased to 5.83 %/h within 2 h with phosphate stimulation, whereas the release rate rapidly decreased to 1.71 %/h in the next 2 h when phosphate stimulation is stopped. The release results confirm that the pesticide release rate can be modulated in response to changing pest dynamics throughout the entire crop growth cycle, and significantly increased the insecticidal rate (>90 %) and targeted utilization rate of pesticide. More importantly, the anti-scouring ability on crop surface of this carrier is increased by 8.7 times compared with commercial avermectin, which avoids the non-target loss and environmental hazard of pesticides caused by poor adhesion. This study presents a novel design concept for pesticide carriers that achieves the balance between adhesion and controlled release, facilitating the development of high-efficiency, low-dosage pesticide formulations.

title: Constraints of electron exchange capacity on biostimulation and bioaugmentation for arsenic detoxification in aquifers
abstract: The complex structural heterogeneity of aquifers generates diverse redox-active components that create spatial variability in electron exchange capacity (EEC). However, the mechanistic constraints governing EEC's role in arsenic bioremediation within contaminated aquifers remain poorly characterized. This study integrated biostimulation and bioaugmentation approaches to quantitatively investigate changes in EEC during the bioremediation of As(III) and explored the factors influencing EEC variability. The results indicated that during the sustained oxidation of As(III), EEC continuously decreased from 33.0 μmol e−/kg to 23.9 μmol e−/kg in the biostimulation system, whereas in the bioaugmentation system, EEC initially increased after primarily decreasing. The relationship between EDC change and As(III) oxidation showed a significant positive correlation in the biostimulation group, and a biphasic trend (initial increase followed by decrease) in the bioaugmentation group. Component studies indicated that organic matter was a decisive factor influencing EEC variations. Long-term remediation experiments confirmed the synergistic effect between microbial-derived organic matter and As(III) in regulating EEC. Microbial analysis evaluated the synergistic effect of exogenous remediation agents with As(III) oxidizing functional microorganisms. These findings enhance our understanding of EEC dynamics during arsenic bioremediation through both biostimulation and bioaugmentation approaches, while providing practical guidance for field-scale remediation applications.

title: Toward sustainable pavement materials: Electromechanical self-monitoring and self-repair in carbon fiber-reinforced asphalt mixtures
abstract: The long-term sustainability of road infrastructure depends not only on high-performance materials but also on their capacity for autonomous recovery and extended service life. Asphalt mixtures capable of self-monitoring and self-repair offer a pathway to reduce maintenance frequency, resource consumption, and life-cycle environmental impacts. This study investigates the self-repair and self-monitoring behaviors of a carbon fiber and iron tailing aggregate (CF-ITA) reinforced conductive asphalt mixtures through an integrated two-phase electromechanical approach. Cyclic tensile and compressive loading tests were performed to characterize the amplitude-dependent multiscale evolution and recovery of internal damage by simultaneously monitoring fractional change in electrical resistance (FCR), strain, and internal damage parameter (D). The results show that tensile loading disrupts the conductive network and induces irreversible deformation, while cyclic compression facilitates mechanical and electrical restoration via matrix densification, particle realignment, and CF bridging. The results quantitatively establish three distinct amplitude regimes. Cross-correlation analysis confirms that electrical restoration (FCR decrease) systematically precedes mechanical recovery by 1–3 cycles, validating FCR as a leading indicator for predictive maintenance. The mechanistic coupling between FCR, D, and strain reveals a progressive and amplitude-dependent self-repair process. These findings provide a fundamental basis for developing sustainable, self-adaptive pavement materials that enhance infrastructure resilience and reduce environmental and maintenance burdens throughout the service life.

title: Energy poverty and the high-carbon trap in high-mountain rural areas
abstract: In the context of compounded energy shortages and growing climate vulnerability, mountainous regions are grappling with formidable dilemmas and urgent challenges in pursuing a clean and low-carbon energy transition. A limited systematic understanding of household energy consumption patterns and related carbon emissions has become a key bottleneck hindering the development of targeted transition policies. Taking the Tibetan Plateau as a representative region, this study draws on a survey of 1808 rural households across an altitudinal gradient of 1500–4500 m to systematically examine the current status of rural household energy use, transition pathways, and the impacts on carbon emissions. The results indicate that: (1) space heating is the primary household energy-consuming activity, still almost entirely dependent on solid fuels, with solid fuels accounting for as much as 65.7 % of cooking activities, highlighting the severity of energy poverty; (2) the altitudinal gradient exacerbates household energy poverty, revealing a vertical zonation pattern in which total energy consumption decreases with elevation while fuel types become increasingly primitive; and (3) in low-altitude areas, the shift in heating fuels from biomass to coal represents a high-carbon pathway, leading to a rebound in total household carbon emissions and forming a structural trap where the emission reduction benefits of clean cooking are offset by high-carbon heating. This study provides a scientific basis for formulating differentiated energy transition policies across elevation zones on the Tibetan Plateau and offers important insights for promoting sustainable development in mountainous regions that are inhabited by over 500 million people worldwide.

title: Differential ozone responses to temperature change in inland and coastal cities: comparison between Beijing and Shanghai, China
abstract: Different meteorological conditions, particularly wind patterns, between inland and coastal urban environments significantly influence surface ozone (O3) pollution responses to temperature changes, yet comparative studies on ozone-temperature relationships under these distinct meteorological regimes remain limited. This study investigates how these meteorological differences affect ozone-temperature relationships by comparing decade-long monitoring data (2014–2023) from representative inland (Beijing) and coastal (Shanghai) cities using integrated spatiotemporal and three-dimensional wind field analysis. Both inland and coastal cities exhibit positive ozone-temperature correlations during daytime (10:00–17:00) periods (Beijing: R2 = 0.966, slope = 0.066; Shanghai: R2 = 0.701, slope = 0.051). However, their nighttime (22:00–05:00) responses differ fundamentally: Beijing maintains positive correlations (R2 = 0.896, slope = 0.055), while Shanghai exhibits negative correlations (R2 = 0.557, slope = −0.060). Three-dimensional wind field analysis reveals distinct physical mechanisms underlying these contrasting nighttime responses. In Beijing, rising temperatures induce atmospheric subsidence that suppresses vertical dispersion and enhances surface O3 accumulation, while in Shanghai, higher temperatures strengthen onshore sea breezes that advect marine air masses with lower O3 concentrations inland. These findings demonstrate that uniform ozone control policies may be ineffective across different urban types, necessitating geographically-tailored strategies. Under climate warming scenarios, Beijing may experience exacerbated nighttime ozone accumulation, while Shanghai could benefit from enhanced marine air dilution effects, highlighting the critical importance of incorporating local meteorological dynamics into regional air quality management and climate adaptation policies.

title: Techno-economic analysis of 3D printed modular housing: Productivity, cost, and environmental assessment
abstract: The construction sector faces persistent productivity deficits and widening housing shortfalls, particularly in countries such as Australia where build times are lengthening and policy targets for new dwellings are not being met. Modular construction and 3D concrete printing (3DCP) have each been promoted as routes to faster, lower-cost and lower-carbon delivery, yet integrated assessments of their combined application remain scarce. This study presents a techno-economic analysis (TEA) of modular 3D-printed construction (M3DP) for Australian detached housing. Using a 120 m2 Class 1a dwelling as the functional unit, we compare a conventional modular baseline with an M3DP variant in which load-bearing walls are produced by 3DCP and designed to meet National Construction Code structural performance requirements under AS 1170 load combinations. The TEA couples capital and life-cycle costs, construction time, labor hours, material waste and embodied carbon, drawing on Australian price indices, industry cost guides, case-study evidence and peer-reviewed life cycle assessment data. For a representative 2025 cost and carbon setting, M3DP reduces upfront construction cost by around 20–30 % relative to conventional modular construction, shortens construction time by approximately 50–70 %, and cuts material use and embodied emissions by up to ∼40 % and ∼55 %, respectively, while achieving comparable thermal performance when appropriate insulation detailing is adopted. On-site labor demand falls by roughly 80–95 %, implying substantial productivity and safety gains in a constrained labor market.
