Sensitivity analysis shows that economic viability is most strongly influenced by scale of deployment and material prices; underutilisation of equipment can erode, and in some cases eliminate, the cost advantage. The findings indicate that, where sufficient project pipelines and regulatory pathways can be secured, modular 3D-printed construction offers a high-impact pathway to accelerate housing delivery, enhance affordability and support embodied-carbon reduction in the built environment.

title: Stepwise pyrolysis of biodiesel-derived oil sludge: Product distribution, sulfur/nitrogen release, and resource recovery
abstract: Biodiesel-derived oily sludge (BOS) poses significant challenges due to its complex composition, including degraded triglycerides, free fatty acids, polymers, and food residues, which complicate behavior prediction and pollutant release. This study investigates the thermal behavior, pollutant release, and resource recovery potential of BOS under stepwise pyrolysis. Stepwise pyrolysis regulated the release of nitrogen- and sulfur-containing pollutants, with most emissions occurring below 400 °C. Compared to pyrolysis, the stepwise heating strategy enhanced product selectivity, enriching low-temperature liquid fractions with fatty acids and alkanes/alkenes while reducing aromatic compound formation. Gas products evolved progressively with increasing temperature, yielding large amounts of CH4, C2H6, and C3H8. XRF and XPS analyses confirmed that inorganic residues, such as CaSO4, remained stable in solid residues. Elemental distribution analyses indicated effective carbon conversion into fuel-grade liquid and gaseous products, with pollutants retained in the solid phase. A techno-economic evaluation demonstrated the profitability and economic feasibility of stepwise pyrolysis for the sustainable valorization of BOS.

title: Interpretation and validation of a machine-learning-assisted database for aqueous biodegradation behaviors of biodegradable plastics
abstract: Understanding and predicting the biodegradation behavior of biodegradable plastics (BPs) in aqueous environments remains challenging due to complex interactions among material properties, environmental factors and diverse degradation mechanisms. This study addresses these complexities by employing machine learning (ML) to predict BP biodegradation behaviors using multivariate attributes and regressed biodegradation parameters of biodegradation rate (k), lag time (T), and degradability (A), with a comprehensive and unified databases on BP biodegradation. The systematic review and data processing of 193 qualified articles yielded 1196 datasets, covering 31 different features across polymer structure, material properties, specimen parameters, biodegradation condition parameters, and biodegradation parameters. Its extent and completeness identify material property gaps and support robust model training. Among six ML algorithms evaluated, the Random Forest model performed best (R2 of k = 0.71, T = 0.56, and A = 0.35, respectively). SHAP analysis identified surface area, crystallinity, and molecular weight dominate of biodegradation kinetics. To assess model generalizability and support material design, three types of novel commercial BP (BioPBS™ FD92, FX85, and Cellophane™ PT25) were experimentally tested. Results demonstrated the model's ability to capture degradation trends and revealed structure-dependent differences in biodegradation behavior. The integrated framework demonstrates a data-driven approach for forecasting BP biodegradation and provides practical guidance for designing environmentally degradable materials.

title: Coordinating sulfamethoxazole removal and fouling control through species–ratio configurations in membrane microalgal–bacterial coupling systems
abstract: Microalgal–sludge interactions strongly influence both contaminant removal and membrane fouling in membrane microalgal–bacterial coupling (MMBC) systems, yet prior work has typically varied species or biomass ratio in isolation. Here, we systematically evaluated two microalgae-to-sludge (A/S) configurations (1:5, 2:1) using Chlorella sp. and Spirulina maxima under sulfamethoxazole (SMX) stress to disentangle combined species–ratio effects. A sludge-dominant configuration (1:5) consistently improved SMX attenuation at high load (10 mg/L), with Spirulina maxima-1:5 achieving 35.41 % removal versus 21.19 % for 2:1 (p < 0.05). Metagenomic profiling revealed that sludge dominance selectively enriched known degraders (Azospirillum in Chlorella sp., 25.6 % vs. 0.1 %; Rhodanobacter in Spirulina maxima, 10.6 % vs. 0.1 %), concurrent with shifts in functional gene abundance. Fouling outcomes diverged by species: Chlorella sp.–2:1 produced protein-rich extracellular polymeric substances (EPS)/soluble microbial products (SMP) signatures and pronounced transmembrane pressure (TMP) rise, whereas Spirulina maxima–2:1 showed reduced filamentous growth and lower SMP accumulation. UPLC-QTOF/MS and QSAR-based assessments indicated MMBC-specific SMX transformation pathways (S–N/C–N cleavage; oxazole modifications) that yielded intermediates with lower predicted toxicity than those from conventional sludge reactors. Collectively, species–ratio configurations coordinate pollutant degradation, toxicity attenuation and fouling behavior; tailoring A/S ratios to influent characteristics thus offers a practical route for sustainable treatment of antibiotic-laden wastewaters.

title: Hybrid PVT-PVSFs powered desalination system with phase change material thermal energy storage: Dynamic simulation in an actual weather condition for sustainable off-grid freshwater production
abstract: The growing demand for freshwater in rural and off-grid communities highlights the need for sustainable desalination systems that operate independently of fossil fuels and unstable grid electricity. This study investigates a hybrid solar-powered desalination unit that integrates a photovoltaic–thermal collector with perforated V-shaped fins, a water-based phase change material (PCM) thermal storage tank, and a two-stage reverse osmosis (RO) system. A coupled simulation framework combining computational fluid dynamics, dynamic thermal modeling, and RO process software was developed to evaluate thermal, electrical, and water production performance under realistic weather conditions in Tangshan, China. Results show that the hybrid collector reduced average photovoltaic cell temperature by 14.8 %, lowering the peak temperature by 12.7 °C and enhancing electrical efficiency by 7 %. The PCM tank with 50 kg of storage material increased stored energy by 27.7 % and stabilized outlet temperature. Thermal preheating reduced RO feed pressure by 0.7–1.0 % and decreased the specific energy consumption from 5.086 to 4.831 kWh/m3, a 5.0 % saving. Unlike previous solar RO systems that focus primarily on either PV cooling or thermal storage in isolation, the present work uniquely combines PVT-PVSFs active thermal management, PCM-based energy buffering, and two-stage membrane desalination in a single integrated platform evaluated through multi-physics simulation using ANSYS Fluent, Python, and Toray RO software. The results demonstrate a viable and economically competitive approach for decentralized, emission-free desalination, achieving a water cost of approximately 3 USD/m3 and a payback period of 5.3–7.4 years in solar-rich regions.

title: Mechanistic insights into microbial and metabolomic responses in PAHs-contaminated soil derived from a coal gasification site
abstract: Microbial remediation offers a promising in situ solution for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs)-contaminated soils at coal gasification sites, where these persistent pollutants cause long-term ecological risks. However, the mechanistic links between microbial metabolic processes, community dynamics, and degradation efficiency under realistic remediation conditions remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a large-scale soil column experiment evaluated an integrated bioremediation approach combining bacterial consortium inoculation, nutrient supplementation, and intermittent bio-ventilation (BA treatment). The BA treatment significantly accelerated the degradation of PAHs in soil, particularly high-concentration PAHs such as naphthalene (NAP), phenanthrene (PHE), pyrene (PYR) and benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), and resulted in pronounced changes in differential metabolites (DEMs), with notable enrichment of key transformation intermediates such as pyrene-1,6-dione and phenanthrene-1,2-oxide. KEGG pathway analysis indicated significant enrichment in xenobiotic biodegradation, amino acid metabolism, and lipid metabolism pathways, reflecting microbial functional expression associated with pollutant breakdown and cellular metabolic activity. Simultaneously, BA treatment enhanced dehydrogenase and fluorescein diacetate hydrolase activities while also increasing available phosphorus, which were strongly correlated with PAHs removal and metabolite profiles. Mantel tests and co-occurrence network analyses revealed strong linkages among microbial genera, PAHs, DEMs and soil biochemical properties, highlighting synergistic interactions underlying degradation. Specific bacterial genera exhibited close associations with PAH-related metabolites, suggesting functional contributions to pollutant transformation. Overall, the enhanced microbial treatment not only promoted PAHs removal but also altered soil metabolic profiles and biochemical activity, providing evidence of synergistic microbe–metabolite interactions that contribute to efficient bioremediation.

title: Inhibition effect of coating cement on the sticking behavior of pellets in hydrogen-based shaft furnace direct reduction
abstract: The sticking behavior of reduced pellets directly influences gas distribution, burden descent smoothness, and continuous operational stability in the shaft furnace. Coating a small amount of inhibitor on the pellet surface is currently a simple, low-cost, and effective method under the given raw material and process conditions. Therefore, based on the atmospheric conditions of a hydrogen-based shaft furnace in China, this study investigates the sticking behavior of pellets and its inhibition mechanism using various types of coating agents and different coating dosages. The results show that the reduction sticking behavior of pellets is aggravated with the increase of reduction temperature and reduction time, among which reduction temperature plays a decisive role. Combined with SEM-EDS detection and analysis, it is determined that the formation of low-melting-point eutectic phases initially induces high-temperature sticking, while the subsequent emergence of highly lamellar reactive metallic iron in the later reduction stage constitutes the primary cause of pellet sticking in hydrogen-based shaft furnaces. To mitigate these issues, small amounts of different cementitious materials are coated on the pellet surface before reduction. It is found that P.O 32.5 slag Portland cement and P.O 42.5 ordinary Portland cement have significant inhibitory effects on the reduction sticking phenomenon, while silica fume has a poor effect, which is directly related to the composition of coating agents. Compared with Fe2+ ions, Ca2+ ions in CaO-based coatings are more likely to migrate to iron vacancies during wüstite reduction, thereby altering the formation structure of nascent iron, reducing the activity of freshly formed metallic iron, and further significantly lowering the reduction sticking strength and sticking index (SI) of pellets. SiO2-based coating can also inhibit sticking, but the low-melting-point fayalite phase formed by the reaction of SiO2 with FeO reduces the inhibitory effect. The SI decreases with increasing coating dosage. When the reduction temperature does not exceed 1000 °C, a coating amount of 3 kg per ton of pellets can meet the inhibition requirements. In the future, either selecting coating agents with high CaO and MgO content or adding small amounts of CaO and MgO to cement can enhance the inhibition effectiveness of the coating.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and resilience optimization of urban ecological networks: A case study of the Xiong'an New Area
abstract: Ecological networks (ENs) are critical for enhancing urban ecological resilience and mitigating the impacts of natural hazards by sustaining biodiversity and ecosystem services. However, previous studies often rely on proxy indicators or composite indices to assess resilience, with limited attention to the dynamic resilience of ENs under future land use scenarios. This study proposes an integrated framework to trace the spatiotemporal evolution of ENs and assess their resilience dynamics. Taking the Xiong'an New Area (XNA) as a case study, land use patterns in 2035 were simulated under natural development scenario (NDS) and planning conservation scenario (PCS) using the patch-generating land use simulation (PLUS) model. Circuit theory was then applied to construct ENs and evaluate their resilience from 2005 to 2035 via complex network analysis. Results showed that the establishment of the XNA reversed the declining trends in both ecological land area and EN resilience. Under the PCS, ecological land was 120.24 % greater than under NDS. EN resilience values ranged from 0.85 to 1.20 between 2005 and 2035, with PCS (1.15) surpassing NDS (0.99) in 2035. The Baiyangdian wetland, a key ecological hub with the highest node importance, plays a vital role in the XNA but its overreliance increases network vulnerability. Accordingly, integrated strategies for protection and restoration were provided to strengthen urban ecological resilience, leading to an 18.97 % improvement in network resilience. The proposed framework provides a reproducible pathway to identify network resilience variations and design resilience-oriented spatial strategies, offering valuable insights for urban green infrastructure and sustainable land use planning.

title: Assessing microbial internal drivers of nitrogen–cycle functional potential in lakeside wetlands: insights from random forest modelling and co-occurrence network analyses
abstract: Environmental factors are widely assumed to influence nitrogen (N) cycle processes in lakeside wetlands. However, recent studies suggested that shifts in environmental conditions do not consistently correspond to proportional changes in N–functional potential. To elucidate the contributions of different drivers, multiple influences, including environmental factors, microbial diversity, functional microbial genera, and gene abundance, were examined by integrating a random forest model (RFM), variation partitioning analysis (VPA), network co-occurrence analysis, and structural equation modeling (SEM). Almost 66 % of functional genes in RFM analysis exhibited a preferable R2 fit over 0.6. VPA analysis revealed that functional microbial genes (55.1 %) and genera (35.1 %) accounted for over 90 % of the explanatory contribution rate, surpassing environmental influences (4.3 %) and diversity indices (5.4 %). Network co-occurrence demonstrated that denitrification genes (norB/C/D/E; napA) formed central connective nodes in the network linked to nitrogen-cycle functional potential, and functional genera–gene linkages were closely aligned with variations in N-functional potential. SEM results further revealed that environmental factors did not exhibit a significant direct association with functional genes; instead, their effects were mediated indirectly through the restructuring of microbial community composition. Under long-term hydrological and nutrient fluctuations, microbial communities exhibited internal co-occurrence networks that were associated with N–cycle functional potential. Recognizing these internally structured microbial associations provides new insight into microbial contributions to N–cycle functional potential and may guide the design strategies of sustainable lakeside wetland restoration.

title: Optimized crystallization and thermal treatment for high-purity calcium fluoride recovery from fluoride-containing wastewater
abstract: Industrial semiconductor wastewater contains extremely high fluoride concentrations, yet conventional treatments often produce low-purity calcium fluoride (CaF2) sludge. This study establishes an optimized crystallization process combined with thermal treatment to recover high-purity CaF2 directly from real wastewater. Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) suspension was used as the calcium source, and the [Ca2+]/[F−] ratio was systematically adjusted to determine optimal conditions. At the optimal ratio of 0.39 under alkaline conditions (pH 10), fluoride removal reached 98 %, yielding products with 99 wt% CaF2 purity. X-ray diffraction (XRD) characterization revealed that drying at 105 °C retained chemically bound water, leading to amorphous CaF2 formation (2.17 wt%). Meanwhile, thermal treatment at 400 °C effectively addressed these limitations through dehydration and recrystallization, reducing amorphous content to 1.10 wt%. The recovered CaF2 exceeded acid-grade CaF2 concentrate requirements (>97 wt%), demonstrating that hazardous wastewater can be upcycled into a stable, high-value mineral resource. These results highlight the importance of thermal treatment in producing CaF2 with crystallographic quality suitable for industrial reuse.

title: Hydrothermal carbon-based sulfate-reducing bioagent for enhanced sulfate reduction and acidification mitigation in oligotrophic environments
abstract: Sulfate reduction via sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) is a key strategy for mitigating acidification in acid mine drainage (AMD). However, SRB are limited by low acid tolerance and reliance on external carbon sources, leading to inefficient sulfate reduction under strongly acidic and nutrient-deficient conditions. To address these challenges, we developed a hydrothermal carbon (HC)-based SRB bioagent and investigated its dual role as a microbial carrier and an intrinsic carbon source. Among the HC materials synthesized under different conditions, the sample prepared at 220 °C for 3 h exhibited the highest performance and was selected for further study. In nutrient-deficient environments, the HC-SRB bioagent significantly enhanced sulfate reduction, lowering sulfate concentrations from 1100 to 730 mg L−1, while free SRB showed negligible activity. The bioagent also increased system pH from 5.3 to 6.5, compared with 5.6 for free SRB. This improvement is attributed to the dual function of HC, which provides a protective microenvironment and continuously releases bioavailable carbon to support SRB growth. Importantly, the HC-SRB bioagent maintained stable sulfate reduction after five consecutive reuse cycles, achieving sulfate reduction efficiencies of up to 99 %. Overall, our results demonstrate that HC-SRB bioagents effectively overcome the main limitations of conventional SRB under acidic and carbon-limited conditions, offering a sustainable and green approach for AMD treatment.

title: How do national wetland parks promote corporate green innovation? Evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
abstract: Climate change driven by carbon emissions poses a grave threat to the sustainable development of human societies and economies. Most existing studies focus on traditional environmental regulation tools such as pollution fees and carbon taxes, while giving little attention to whether national wetland parks serve as an important driver of corporate green innovation. Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2002 to 2024, this paper empirically investigates how China's national wetland parks affects corporate green innovation. The results show that China's national wetland parks strengthen corporate green innovation, and this effect proves to be persistent over time. Mechanism analysis shows that China's national wetland parks foster corporate green innovation by improving corporate ESG performance and expanding their environmental investments. Heterogeneity analysis shows that China's national wetland parks have a stronger effect on corporate green innovation among non-state-owned and non-high-pollution firms than among state-owned and high-pollution firms. Our findings provide actionable guidance for the Chinese government on how to design and implement wetland-park policies that more effectively stimulate corporate green innovation.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of an efficient green methanol production system based on biomass gasification and carbon capture
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing demand for renewable energy and escalating environmental pressures from fossil resources, developing efficient, low-emission biomass conversion technologies has become a crucial direction for optimizing the energy structure. This study developed an innovative integrated poly-generation system for the co-production of energy and chemicals from biomass resources. This system synergistically couples biomass gasification, high-efficiency steam-organic Rankine dual-cycle power generation, cryogenic distillation, carbon dioxide capture, and methanol synthesis, achieving coordinated utilization of biomass energy and carbon resources. Key operating parameters were optimized through comprehensive process simulations, thermodynamic assessments, and sensitivity analyses. Under optimized configuration, the system achieved an overall energy efficiency of 71.83 %. The economic evaluation reveals a dynamic payback period of 4.44 years and a net present value of US$118.14 million, underscoring the strong investment feasibility of this project. Life cycle assessment based on multiple intermediate point categories and damage endpoints indicates that feedstocks dominate resource consumption and ecotoxicity indicators. At the same time, the methanol production stage contributes the most to human health, ecological quality, climate change, and resource consumption, accounting for 41–87 % of the total. This study provides a systematic solution for the efficient and clean utilization of biomass, offering important technical references for the future regionalized production of low-carbon fuels and chemicals.

title: Energy efficiency and carbon emission reduction of fly ash vacuum insulation boards: A coupled thermal modeling and lifecycle assessment
abstract: This study develops a fly ash-based composite insulation (FAHM-MF) to balance building performance and carbon reduction. It quantifies the impact of fiber volume fraction (Vfibre) and vacuum conditions on pore structure parameters. Increasing Vfibre reduces porosity (φ), fractal dimension (D), and regularizes pore structure, but lowers connectivity (Cconn), affecting thermal conductivity (λ). Vacuum conditions enhance λ through low φ. The pore structure complexity coefficient (k2) is the most sensitive parameter to λ (sensitivity 79.28 %), with ±2SE fluctuations resulting in a ±8.2 % change. Sensitivities of the vacuum correction coefficient (k3) and fiber reinforcement factor (β) are lower at ±3 % and ±1.5 %, respectively. Lifecycle assessment shows FAHM-MF buildings reduce carbon emissions by 10.2 % (464.85 tons CO2) compared to EPS. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that grid emission factors (sensitivity 0.96) cause ΔCO2 fluctuations of ±28.75 % with ±30 % variation, and reduce the emission-reduction potential in coal-powered regions by more than 20 %. Extending building lifespan to 60 years improves ΔCO2 by 17.7 %. This framework optimizes the use of building materials and supports sustainable development.

title: Effects of absorbent physical properties on microscale hydrodynamics in structured packing for CO2 capture and new correlations for interfacial area and liquid holdup
abstract: Chemical absorption using structured packing columns is an economical and efficient technology for mitigating CO2 emissions. The fluid dynamics and gas-liquid mass transfer behaviors within such packings are remarkably affected by solvent properties and geometric features (such as perforations on the corrugated sheets). However, the explicit representation of perforations in three-dimensional simulations and their impact on the microscale hydrodynamics of different solvents remain insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed a computational domain comprising 2 × 4 Representative Elementary Units of 250.Y structured packing, with full geometrical resolution of the perforations. Gas-liquid two-phase flow simulations were conducted using the Volume of Fluid method. The investigation systematically examined the effects of solvent properties (characterized by Kapitza number), surface wettability, and flow rate on flow patterns, interfacial area, and liquid holdup. The results demonstrate that perforations promote rivulet separation, droplet formation, and periodic renewal of gas-liquid interface. A lower Kapitza number stabilizes rivulet flow and enhances wettability. Notably, for perforated sheets, the wetted area is smaller than the interfacial area, which contrasts with the behavior observed in non-perforated sheets. The dependence of interfacial area on contact angle (γ) exhibited two distinct regimes: in Region I (γ > 30°), the area shows weak sensitivity to γ, while in Region II (γ ≤ 30°), it increases markedly as γ decreases. Finally, modified correlations were developed to enable more accurate prediction of liquid holdup and interfacial area in perforated packings. These correlations can facilitate improved column design and operational optimization, thereby contributing to cleaner industrial production and carbon emission reduction.

title: Engineered microbial consortium enhances tomato salt tolerance through rhizosphere modulation for sustainable crop production
abstract: Salinity stress in agricultural soils severely inhibits crop growth and jeopardizes global food security. This study involved the construction of an ACC deaminase-engineered bacterium, BL-EF, which was combined with multifunctional Enterobacter cloacae Rs-2 and injected into potted tomato plants experiencing salt stress. Eight parallel treatments were established to investigate the optimal compounding ratio by altering the proportions of the two bacterial complexes. The morphological indicators of plants inoculated with the optimal ratio of the bacterial consortium were monitored, revealing that the compounded bacteria enhanced the seedling metrics of plant length (69.45 %), fresh weight (81.26 %), dry weight (176.41 %), and stem diameter (16.61 %). Moreover, the bacterial consortium enhanced the levels of photosynthetic pigments, peroxidase activity, and osmoregulatory chemicals in the plants. Furthermore, soil nutrient availability and enzyme activity in the rhizosphere were significantly enhanced. Additionally, the bacterial consortium altered the composition of the rhizosphere microbial community. The potential synergistic mechanism of these two bacteria may be attributed to their salt tolerance and enhancement capabilities, the optimization of the rhizosphere microenvironment, and the establishment of novel ecological niches within the rhizosphere. This study underscores the potential of BL-EF as a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium and the prospective applications of this bacterial consortium.

title: Unlocking the potential of pyrite by mechanochemistry ball mill for efficient heterogeneous Fenton degradation of florfenicol
abstract: Ball milling of pyrite significantly improves the degradation of florfenicol (FLO) by activated H2O2, extending the effective pH range. After 5 h of ball milling, FeS2bm can degrade more than 95 % of FLO in the pH range of 3–9 at 0.1 g/L dosing with 2 mM H2O2, and the performance is approximately 70 times higher (as kobs) than that of raw pyrite. The ball milling process renews the pyrite surface, reducing the percentage of oxidized iron sulfide species by 44.18 % and 12.05 %, respectively, while decreasing particle size and creating a rough, porous surface. The total dissolved Fe ions of FeS2bm increased by 16.6 times and H+ production by 7.1 times, concurrently, the Fe2+/Fe3+ cycling was enhanced. The ·OH produced by the activation of H2O2 by dissolved Fe2+ is the primary contributor to FLO degradation. LC/MS analysis confirmed the complete degradation of FLO. FeS2bm/H2O2 system demonstrated excellent durability and the capacity to degrade various antibiotics, using air as the ball milling atmosphere or switching to natural pyrite as the raw material had no significant effect on the properties of the ball-milled material. Overall, these findings offer valuable insights into the engineering of ball-milled pyrite for enhanced H2O2 degradation of antibiotics.

title: Carbon-digital interplay in industry risk spillovers: Analyzing spatiotemporal dynamics and network topology for adaptive governance
abstract: Advancing low-carbon and digital transformation represents two major global challenges of the era. Carbon regulation and digital transformation jointly pressure and empower industries, yet prior studies mostly examine their effects separately and neglect how their interaction reshapes multi-regional and multi-sectoral risk spillovers, being an issue of both theoretical and practical importance that remains underexplored. To address this gap, this study employs China, an economy undergoing this dual transformation, as the empirical context. This study utilizes panel data covering 30 Chinese provinces and 17 industries from 2006 to 2022, applies time-varying parameter vector autoregressive model to delineate dynamic risk spillover pathways, and incorporates regression models to systematically examine the impact mechanisms of carbon emissions, digitalization, and their interaction on industry risk spillovers. The main findings are: (1) industry characteristics: China's industry risk spillovers generally declined temporally and characterized by “higher in the north and lower in the south” spatially, with manufacturing being the primary source of risk spillovers; (2) carbon-digital nexus: carbon emissions and digitalization significantly aggravate risk spillovers separately but with substitution interaction effects; (3) adaptive governance: proposing tailored suggestions to the cyclical differences in carbon-digital adaptation across regions and sectors. Theoretically, the paper extends the Substitution Theory of Resource Constraints into industry risk spillovers, revealing the substitution effects in carbon-digital interactions. Practically, it proposes a multi-tiered synergistic governance framework and offers differentiated, actionable policy and enterprise strategies for managing risks during concurrent carbon and digital transitions. It also contributes as a referential theoretical framework and practical paradigm for global emerging economies pursuing low-carbon digital governance.

title: Sensitivity analysis of design variables in semi-batch reverse osmosis for energy-efficient water treatment
abstract: Stricter water quality regulations have increased the demand for advanced water treatment technologies. Reverse osmosis (RO) is widely applied to remove emerging contaminants but remains limited by water recovery constraints. To address this limitation, semi-batch reverse osmosis (SBRO) has been developed to enhance recovery. Despite growing interest in SBRO, optimal design variables for large-scale water treatment applications have not been sufficiently studied. This study determined optimal SBRO design variables through sensitivity analysis for a large-scale system (100,000 m3/d) to optimize specific energy consumption (SEC). The analysis focused on the number of RO elements per pressure vessel (PV), feed ratio, plug-flow (PF) recovery, and closed-circuit (CC) recycled concentrate flow rate. Cost efficiency was evaluated by determining the optimal number of RO elements per PV, indicating that four elements per PV minimized total costs by balancing PV capital cost and the increase in SEC. Adjusting the feed ratio from 100 % to 200 % reduced the SEC by 6.2 % due to lower operating pressure during the CC phase. PF recovery from 0 % to 50 % improved water production, reducing SEC by 4.0 %. Further analysis of the CC recycled concentrate flow rate, from 54,000 m3/d to 162,000 m3/d, resulted in a 19.3 % increase in SEC. The CC recycled concentrate flow rate was identified as the most influential factor through Shapley additive explanations, and optimized design variables were proposed based on varying feed conditions and overall recovery. This sensitivity analysis provides an analytical basis for optimizing large-scale SBRO design to achieve energy-efficient water treatment, thereby resulting in cleaner water production.

title: One-step treatment of hydrometallurgical wastewater of photovoltaic laminates with ferrite process under weak alkali conditions: Regulation, precipitation characteristics, and mechanism
abstract: The metal ions contained in the hydrometallurgical wastewater from decommissioned photovoltaic laminates are harmful to the environment. A high-efficiency ferrite one-step strategy is proposed to regulate and treat these metal ions under weak alkaline conditions. The optimal experimental conditions (pH = 8, n(Fe3+):n(Fe2+) = 1, n(Fe2+):n(Me) = 7.5, t = 10 min, T = 55 °C) resulted in a 99.04 % removal of metals from wastewater. The residual concentration of metals complies with the emission standards of China. Through XRD, XPS, SEM and TEM characterization of the precipitate, it was determined that the main components were ferrites. Cu2+ is introduced into the spinel lattice to form CuFe2O4, which is the key to achieving one-step stability, whereas other metal ions are stably encapsulated and removed in a composite form. The TEM and vibrating sample magnetometry characterization showed that the precipitate had a large specific surface area and high saturation magnetization. Under a 1500 Gs magnetic field, the sedimentation rate was increased by 80 % compared to natural sedimentation, achieving rapid solid-liquid separation. The removal of multiple metals from the waste liquid undergoes two stages: the formation and doping of ferrite, and the stable encapsulation of metal compounds by ferrite. The resulting composite precipitates exhibit high stability and have potential applications in adsorption, wave absorption, catalysis, and various other fields after drying. This provides a green, circular and efficient approach for the treatment, disposal, and resource utilization of photovoltaic modules during the decommissioning stage.

title: Novel mechanisms of cadmium detoxification mediated by selenium nanoparticles in selenium hyperaccumulator plants: Discovery of HSP90-1 as a pivotal potential regulatory hub
abstract: Selenium(Se) is an essential trace element for the human body. However, in areas with high Se content, the soil usually also has excessive levels of cadmium (Cd), which poses a challenge for the Se - rich industry. This study investigates the physiological and molecular mechanisms by which nano - selenium (SeNPs) alleviates Cd stress in the Se hyperaccumulator plant Cardamine violifolia. This study comprehensively elucidated the co-regulation mechanism of selenium and Cd in plants based on physiological and biochemical indicators, combined with transcriptomics analysis and molecular docking technology. The results indicated that treatment with SeNPs resulted in a significant reduction (73.9 %) in cadmium accumulation in the plants, along with a 16.3 % increase in biomass and a 27.0 % improvement in net photosynthetic rate. Physiological experiments reveal that SeNPs reconstruct the redox balance network by activating antioxidant enzyme systems, particularly peroxidase (POD). Furthermore, SeNPs conferred comprehensive protection on the photosynthetic apparatus by regulating stomatal closure, maintaining pigment levels, and moreover, enhancing the activity of key photosynthetic enzymes. Transcriptomic analysis identifies, for the first time, the heat shock protein HSP90 - 1 as a key common target of Se and Cd. Molecular docking confirms that SeNPs competitively displace Cd from the active site of HSP90 - 1 via Se - S bond formation, restoring its ATPase activity and chaperone function.This study proposes a ternary regulatory model of "essential trace element (Se) - toxic heavy metal (Cd) - Co-regulated target (HSP90 - 1)," offering novel molecular targets and nutritional intervention strategies for controlling Cd pollution in Se - enriched crops. These findings hold significant implications for the sustainable development of functional agriculture.

title: Privacy preserving reserved pricing & energy allocation mechanism for smartgrid peer-to-peer energy trading
abstract: Determining a fair and secure energy trading price is an important concern in smart grid energy trading networks, where participants interact with each other and the grid using bi-directional communication links. Moreover, the information shared on these communication links is prone to possible vulnerabilities, such as man-in-the-middle attacks, where an intruder sniffs the information, alters it, and gains undue benefit by falsely reporting the participants’ data. To overcome this issue, the proposed model offers a promising approach to address these challenges by introducing a homomorphic encryption-based privacy-preserving model that ensures the privacy of the participants’ data. Furthermore, without exposing the financial conditions of the participants and by utilizing the concept of reserved pricing, a sequential quadratic optimization-based model is proposed to determine the final energy trading price. This is done in such a way that the final price always adheres to the participants’ reserved prices while keeping the real-time supply-to-demand ratio in account. Moreover, the stochastic generation of renewable sources also poses challenges to ensuring fairness in the energy market, where several participants are treated as non-trader entities. For this purpose, the proposed model offers a Euclidean distance-based energy allocation policy to establish fairness in the energy allocation process. The simulation results of the proposed model reveal that it can reduce the energy bills of buyers by 6.53% to 22.11% and boost the revenues of sellers by 6.23% to 32.80% compared to other state-of-the-art models.

title: Can artificial intelligence promote urbanization processes in harmony with carbon emissions abatement?
abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology provides new opportunities for achieving greener and more sustainable urbanization. The relationship between urbanization and carbon emissions has long been a focus of both academic research and policy discussions. Traditional views generally maintain that urbanization inevitably leads to higher carbon emissions, creating a significant challenge for sustainable urban growth. However, AI technology's rapid development opens up new possibilities for reconfiguring this relationship. This study examines whether, and under what conditions, AI can help harmonize urbanization with carbon emissions reduction. Using a balanced panel dataset covering 68 countries from 2005 to 2019, this study revisits the relationship between urbanization and carbon emissions and explores how AI technology may change this relationship. The findings reveal three key points: (1) Baseline regression reconfirms the established positive relationship between urbanization and carbon emissions. (2) AI has the potential to mitigate this positive correlation. (3) Additionally, the study identifies a non-linear relationship between urbanization and carbon emissions across varying stages of AI development. Specifically, as AI advances, the influence of urbanization on carbon emissions follows an “inverted U” pattern. In the initial phase of AI development, urbanization continues to increase carbon emissions. However, beyond a certain threshold of AI progress, the impact of urbanization on carbon emissions begins to decline, eventually leading to a synergistic in carbon emissions reduction alongside urbanization growth in regions with high AI development. These results offer new insights into the potential of AI to align urbanization with environmental goals. They provide a valuable empirical foundation for developing strategies in smart city planning and environmental policy.

title: Pre-optimization-based deep reinforcement learning for autonomous economic and exergy management of stochastic H2/CO ratio syngas switching downstream processes
abstract: Driven by global warming and escalating energy demand, sustainable syngas production continues to advance as an essential cleaner energy carrier. The switching of the syngas H2/CO ratio can supply tailored feedstock for synthesizing diverse downstream chemicals. However, unsteady state, stochastic behavior, and plant-model mismatch characteristics of the downstream process complicate existing control strategies and operational management. This study addresses the critical challenge of intelligent operational management in stochastic syngas switching downstream (SSSD) processes characterized by strong stochasticity and dynamic losses. To this end, a pre-optimization-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) control framework is proposed for autonomous economic and exergy (2E) management of SSSD process. First, a high-fidelity dynamic model of SSSD process is developed to simulate the stochastic behavior and dynamic losses of the system. Then, the optimization constraint algorithm is innovatively embedded into the DRL framework to obtain an optimized initial set of actions for each random reset. Finally, the agent is trained to interact with the dynamic model in pursuit of efficient exploration and reward, which produces an optimal control strategy. The proposed method reduces exergy destruction by 3.8 % and 2.1 % compared to proportional-integral-derivative (PID) and conventional DRL frameworks, while obtaining the minimum operating cost of $8542 and the most stable product control. The well-trained agent is also able to self-adapt to process uncertainties with higher exploration efficiency and stability, achieving intelligent and sustainable production for complex and dynamic processes.

title: Identification of carbon emission aggregation effects and transition patterns in Chinese provinces under the progressive emission reduction pathway
abstract: Global warming caused by carbon emissions has become a critical concern for countries worldwide. Defining carbon emission transition patterns for Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement is crucial for achieving carbon neutrality targets. As a key signatory, China's evolving emission reduction trends and transition patterns at the provincial level remain unclear, which complicates the development of policies that balance regional emissions with sustainable development. To address this issue, the study adopts the progressive emission reduction pathway and employs the Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM) to simulate and predict the spatiotemporal evolution of carbon emissions across 31 provinces in China from 2025 to 2060. This study quantifies the contribution rates of influencing factors to carbon emission across provinces by combining the Translog Production Function Model and Ridge Regression, subsequently categorizing the provincial carbon emission reduction patterns. The results indicate: (1) China's carbon emissions follow a phased pattern, initially increasing and then decreasing, with significant spatial aggregation. High carbon emissions are concentrated in eastern coastal regions, while low emissions are mainly found in the western inland regions. The significance of this pattern decreases over time. (2) The average contribution rates of power generation, energy structure, energy intensity, economic development, and technological progress to carbon emission reductions are 9.2 %, 8.4 %, 54.1 %, 4.2 %, and 24.0 %. Among these factors, energy intensity and technological progress are the primary factors of carbon emission reductions. (3) Provincial regions can be classified into four carbon emission transition patterns: “high contribution, high cleanliness,” “low contribution, high cleanliness,” “low contribution, low cleanliness,” and “high contribution, low cleanliness.” Similar transition patterns exhibit spatial clustering. Consequently, distinct regional emission reduction strategies should be developed based on the development patterns and variations in carbon emission transition patterns. The research provides valuable insights for decision-making in advancing the low-carbon transformation of China's energy system and offer guidance for other nations aiming to achieve carbon neutrality.

title: From inhibition to enhancement: Time-staged complementary roles of sugarcane bagasse ash and red mud in sustainable cementitious composites
abstract: Functionalizing industrial and agricultural wastes, such as sugarcane bagasse ash (SCBA) and red mud (RM), is imperative for developing sustainable cementitious materials. While binary OPC systems with high dosages of either this waste underperformed, due to the low reactivity of SCBA or the inhibitory effect of RM, ternary OPC-SCBA-RM blends demonstrated a promising synergistic enhancement. To offer optimization strategies and mechanistic insights, this study investigated ternary OPC-SCBA-RM systems using response surface methodology, isothermal calorimetry and multi-scale characterizations. The results indicate that SCBA and RM functioned via distinct yet complementary mechanisms. SCBA primarily reduced total porosity and elongated the silicate chain length in C-S-H gels. Differentially, RM preferentially refined harmful macropores and the polycondensation degree of reaction products, evidenced by the increased partial correlation coefficient, the presence of Al-coordinated Q2(2Al) and Q3(3Al) units alongside the significantly higher MCL value than plain mixture (7.52 vs. 4.54). The interactive synergy in ternary cement-based mixtures mitigated the RM-induced retardation upon phase boundary reaction and diffusion kinetics. This synergy represented not an additive but a competitive interaction, shifting the hydration pathway toward more favourable late-stage kinetics. A promising formulation for the ternary composite of 76.3 % OPC, 20.7 % RM, and 3 % SCBA was identified to exhibit equivalent mechanical performance to the pure OPC control. Moreover, a 28 % cement replacement can be achieved with ≤5 % strength loss. This meaningfully presents a viable route for high-volume waste utilization in low-carbon cementitious composites.

title: Energy absorption performance of pomelo-inspired thin-walled tubes for sustainable lightweight design
abstract: Driven by carbon peaking and carbon neutrality targets and cleaner production principles, crashworthy structures for transportation vehicles need to balance high energy absorption, lightweight design and recyclability. Simple structures can provide basic energy-absorbing capacity but offer limited performance, whereas complex multi-material or thin-walled configurations can significantly enhance crashworthiness at the expense of higher manufacturing energy consumption and poorer recyclability. To address this issue, this study proposes a pomelo-inspired multi-petal thin-walled energy-absorbing tube (PITEAT). The petal cross-section is parameterized using Fourier functions, and the effects of outer diameter-to-height ratio, end curvature, Fourier coefficients C1/C2 and petal number on energy absorption are investigated. A constitutive model is calibrated through material tensile tests, and a finite element model is established and validated against axial compression experiments. The results show that appropriate adjustment of geometric parameters can markedly improve specific energy absorption and crushing force efficiency; when C1 = 0.10, C2 = −0.10 and the petal number is eight, the PITEAT maintains a controllable peak force while increasing the specific energy absorption by 60 % and achieving a crushing force efficiency of 80 % compared with a circular tube under the same geometric envelope. Life cycle assessment (LCA) indicates that, for a functional unit of absorbing 11.24 kJ of energy, the PITEAT reduces CO2 emissions by 35–60 % relative to conventional circular and foam-filled tubes, while the metal recyclability exceeds 90 %. The PITEAT can be manufactured from conventional structural steel using standard forming processes, achieving high energy absorption, controlled peak force and reduced environmental burden, and providing an optimized design approach for lightweight crash protection in transportation vehicles.

title: Multi-cluster assessment of microplastics discharge from textile effluent treatment plants of India: Removal efficiency, characterization and associated environmental risk
abstract: Microplastics discharged from textile industries represent a significant yet under documented source of pollution in developing industrial regions. This study provides the first multi-cluster assessment of microplastic (MP) levels in influent and effluent from textile industries across major manufacturing hubs in India. MPs were quantified and characterized using wet peroxide oxidation, stereomicroscopy and μ-FTIR imaging. Influent samples showed high MPs abundance (24,500 ± 12,500 MP/L), which decreased to 10,900 ± 4000 MP/L after treatment. Size distributions shifted towards smaller particles (25–50 μm) in effluents, indicating fragmentation and limited fine-particle retention. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyamide (PA), polypropylene (PP), and polyethene (PE) dominated the polymer profile, while high-hazard polymers, such as polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) and acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS), although less abundant, significantly increased hazard levels. Polymer Hazard Index (PHI) values ranged from 19.35 to 1133.38, placing several industries within the high-risk and danger categories due to the presence of polymers with elevated hazard scores. Correlation and redundancy analyses revealed strong associations between MP characteristics and effluent chemistry, pointing to combined chemical-mechanical pathways of microfiber generation. Findings highlight textile industries as persistent point sources of MP and underscore the need for polymer-targeted mitigation, improved tertiary treatment, and strengthened regulatory oversight in textile-intensive industrial clusters.

title: CO-enhanced mechanism for the oxidation of aluminum nitride in secondary aluminum dross via carbon addition under low-oxygen atmosphere
abstract: The oxidation of AlN in secondary aluminum dross (SAD) at elevated temperatures is significantly inhibited under O2-deficient conditions, often resulting in prolonged treatment duration. In this study, a pyrometallurgical approach was developed to enhance AlN oxidation in SAD under low O2 atmospheres by introducing carbon. Between 700 °C and 1000 °C, the AlN removal rates in both 10 % and 5 % oxygen atmospheres were markedly higher when carbon was added than under carbon-free conditions. Kinetic analyses confirmed that adding 10 % activated carbon to SAD lowered the apparent activation energy of AlN oxidation in low-oxygen atmospheres relative to air. The results suggest that AlN was converted into Al2O3 through reaction with CO, which was generated from the reaction between carbon and oxygen under low-O2 conditions. This mechanism was consistent with AlN oxidation in the case of roasting SAD in a CO atmosphere. Gibbs free energy calculations revealed that the adsorption energy of CO on AlN at 900 °C was −0.871 eV, which was more negative than that of O2 (−0.552 eV). This indicated a stronger affinity of CO for AlN. XRD analyses showed no formation of aluminum–carbon compounds, while XPS results confirmed the presence of Al–O–C and C–O–Al bonds, supporting the hypothesis that AlN was fully converted to Al2O3. This method was subsequently applied to the enhanced treatment of SAD containing carbon-rich dust, demonstrating its practical effectiveness in oxygen-limited conditions.

title: Assessing the coupled exposure risks of heatwaves and particulate matter: Based on the empirical analysis of 347 cities in China
abstract: Global climate change and rapid urbanization have led to significant increases in temperature and air pollution. Extreme heatwaves can exacerbate fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution, posing a serious threat to the health of urban residents, especially when the two effects are coupled. However, the heatwaves - PM2.5 coupled exposure (HPE) assessment remains limited, particularly regarding its distribution and evaluation method. Therefore, this study developed a population-weighted exposure model to assess HPE. First, spatial distribution characteristics and influencing factors were analyzed using kriging interpolation. Then, the impacts of economic development and industrial structure level on HPE were evaluated. Finally, mitigation strategies were proposed to reduce HPE impacts. The results indicate that heatwaves exposure (HWEP) in 347 Chinese cities shows a geographic variation, with higher HWEP in the southeast coastal region and Xinjiang's Turpan Basin (approximately twice the national average) and lower in the central and northern regions. Meanwhile, the spatial distribution of PM2.5 exposure (PMEP) in Chinese cities is characterized by high in the central part, medium in the southeast and low in the west. Moreover, there is obvious spatial heterogeneity in the HPE of Chinese cities, with Shanxi and Henan having the highest HPE values of 8.35–12.72, which are the core areas of coupled pollution in the country. In addition, the relationship between the level of economic development and HPE is characterized by the environmental Kuznets curve. This study proposes improvement measures for HPE contamination from 2 different perspectives (NDVI and level of healthcare services). This study provides valuable guidance for urban planning and design to improve environmental quality.

title: Institutional perceptions, subjective well-being, and public pro-environmental behaviour: Moderating effects of perceived environmental conditions – evidence from China
abstract: Pro-environmental behavior (PEB) is a crucial approach to promoting environmental sustainability and a key indicator of modern ecological civilization. Based on the institutional-life analysis perspective, this study employs 2512 valid responses from the 2021 Chinese General Social Survey (CGSS, 2021) to examine the relationships between institutional perception and subjective well-being (SWB) and both public and private pro-environmental behaviors, while testing the moderating effect of perceived environmental conditions (PEC). Empirical findings indicate that institutional perception and SWB have significant positive impacts on PEBs in both domains. Furthermore, PEC positively moderates these relationships. The study examines the empirical relationship between institutional perception, SWB, and PEB. Practically, it provides policy implications for promoting environmental sustainability by emphasizing institutional design and public education, enhancing the fairness and accessibility of public service provision, and establishing differentiated incentive mechanisms to jointly foster both public and private pro-environmental actions.

title: Impacts of land-sharing practices in tea plantations on the sustainable development goals: A case study from a flagship national park in China
abstract: Tea cultivation is a cornerstone of the livelihoods of millions of rural households worldwide. To mitigate the threat posed by tea plantation expansion to global biodiversity, land-sharing practices have been proposed as a promising approach to balancing tea production with biodiversity conservation. While many studies have evaluated the effects of land sharing on agricultural production and ecosystems, few have explored its broader impacts on sustainable development goals (SDGs), particularly in the context of tea plantations. In this study, we examined the effects of land-sharing practices implemented by tea plantations in Wuyishan National Park, China, on four sustainable development goals and their interrelationships: SDG 1 (income), SDG 3 (well-being), SDG 15 (willingness for wildlife conservation), and SDG 16 (support for the national park). Our findings show that conventional tea plantations contributed to SDG 1 and SDG 3 but had a significant negative impact on SDG 15. In contrast, the adoption of land-sharing practices in tea plantations enhanced SDG 1, but adversely affected SDG 16, and contributed little to SDG 3 and SDG 15. These results suggest that eco-friendly land-sharing practices in tea plantations enhanced economic benefits, but they unintentionally weakened community support for the national park, generating complex impacts on the interrelationships among the sustainability goals. The approach and findings from this study provide valuable tools and insights for designing targeted strategies that can effectively leverage land-sharing for sustainable tea productions in China and beyond.

title: Revealing the material flows and embodied GHG emissions of carbon fibers industry in China from 2000 to 2060
abstract: Carbon fibers (CF) are critical materials that play an indispensable role in the low-carbon energy transition, yet research on the CF flows, stocks and associated greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the life cycle remains limited. This study integrates material flow analysis (MFA) with GHG accounting models to quantify GHG emissions from China's CF industry between 2000 and 2060, and to assess mitigation potential under 21 distinct scenarios. The results indicated that the apparent consumption of CF products increased from 1.91 kt in 2000 to 44.35 kt in 2023. The cumulative GHG emissions of CF industry was 13.12 Mt CO2 eq. from 2000 to 2023, with 3.64 Mt emitted in 2023 alone. The production stage accounted for the highest GHG emissions (96.14 %), with energy consumption as the primary emission sources (77.14 %). Based on scenario simulations, GHG emissions from China's CF industry are expected to decrease to 1.28 Mt CO2 eq. under the lowest emissions scenario by 2060, and could increase to 19.67 Mt CO2 eq. under the highest emissions scenario. Among all individual mitigation measures, increasing the recycling rate demonstrates the greatest mitigation potential, contributing 27.02 % to the total technical reduction potential. This underscores the critical role of establishing the CF recycling system in decarbonizing the CF industry.

title: Renewable energy vs. direct air capture and utilization at the macroeconomic level: A Computable General Equilibruim analysis in Japan
abstract: Mitigating global warming relies on a combination of carbon pricing and the development of renewable energy (RE) and negative emission technologies. RE is a completely clean energy source to replace traditional fossil fuels, and direct air capture (DAC) can effectively reduce carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere. With technological advancement, membrane-based DAC with utilization of gas conversion (DAC-U) shows potential for carbon abatement; however, research into the large-scale deployment of DAC remains insufficient at the macroeconomic level. Furthermore, carbon pricing's potential negative impact on the large-scale deployment of DAC-U and its effects on RE development remain underexplored. Therefore, this study conducts a macroeconomic analysis to evaluate the environmental and economic impacts of carbon pricing on the large-scale deployment of DAC-U and RE development, simultaneously exploring the relationship between these two technologies. This research adopts the computable general equilibrium model, which is an effective tool to analyze the economic impact of environmental policies at the macro-level. Our results reveal a competitive relationship between RE and DAC-U under carbon taxes, where an explicit carbon tax enhances the competitiveness of DAC-U more than electricity, including RE. Furthermore, DAC-U is conducive to sustaining energy-intensive industries as the carbon tax stimulates intermediate demand for DAC-U and upstream industries. Nevertheless, the tradeoff between carbon abatement and economic growth persists, even under a carbon tax.

title: Effects of torrefaction pretreatment on the composting of tetracycline mycelial residues: Antibiotic resistance
abstract: The persistence of tetracycline (TC) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in tetracycline mycelial residue (TMR) has emerged as a concern. Torrefaction has been demonstrated as an effective treatment for reducing both contaminants. However, the effect of torrefaction as a pretreatment on controlling antibiotic resistance during composting remains unclear. Thus, the dynamics of residual TC, ARGs, and the microbial community succession were compared during composting of raw and torrefied TMR. The results indicate that torrefaction at 200.0 °C for 60.0 min is an effective pretreatment for improving the safety of TMR composting without negatively affecting its performance. No TC was detected in the compost derived from TMR torrefied under these conditions, while ARG relative abundance (RA) remained consistently low throughout the process. Compared with the control group, torrefaction at 200.0 °C for 60.0 min reduced ARG RA in the fertilizer by 10.4 %. Furthermore, the RA of ARGs associated with potential human pathogenic microorganisms (HPMs) decreased by 58.9 % in the final product. The limited mobility of residual ARGs (rsmA, mexK, and vanRO) in compost products and the non-pathogenic phenotype of their hosts collectively indicate limited environmental risks. The persistence of these ARGs was attributed to the high-temperature, oxidative composting environment and dynamics secondary metabolites. These findings demonstrate that torrefaction combined with composting is a promising strategy for mitigating antibiotic resistance risks and facilitating the resource reutilization of TMR.

title: Turning NH3 liability into humus asset: In-situ microbial engineering as a priority approach to compost gas management
abstract: Ammonia volatilization during composting is both a major environmental pollutant and a driver of nitrogen loss, reducing the nutrient value of final products. The mechanisms by which nitrogen loss reshapes humification pathways through microbial regulation of organic matter mineralization remain unclear. We compared two composting systems with contrasting emissions: high emission (HL) and low emission (LL). In HL, humic acids formed mainly by aggregation of aliphatic and phenolic compounds, yielding hydrophobic structures. In LL, phenolic oxidation products condensed with fatty acids, pyridines, and lignin derivatives, generating aromatic–nitrogen covalent networks that stabilized structure and retained nitrogen. Distinct microbial communities drove this divergence, with Saccharomonospora and Pseudomonas mediating stage-specific metabolic branching. Functional gene profiling showed that LL communities integrated “nutrient cycling-energy flow” with “information transmission-bacterial chemotaxis,” synchronizing carbon release and energy acquisition while enhancing niche adaptability. Guided by these insights, we propose a model-driven two-stage integrated reinforcement learning optimization framework (RVS-Stack RL) to dynamically regulate compost microbiomes for enhanced nitrogen retention and efficiency. These findings highlight the importance of prioritizing in situ microbial engineering to channel nitrogen into humification, rather than relying on end-of-pipe ammonia control, thereby sustaining the resource value of composting.

title: Seawater-derived struvite fertilizers: Agronomic potential and environmental benefits in aquatic plant cultivation
abstract: Aquatic crop production must curb phosphorus (P) enrichment in sensitive aquatic environments while reducing reliance on finite phosphate rock. Struvite, a recognized slow-release fertilizer in terrestrial agriculture, represents a promising but untested solution for aquatic cultivation under flooded soil conditions; importantly, the agronomic performance of emerging seawater-derived struvite (STR) remains largely unevaluated. Here, we characterized STR and systematically evaluated its agronomic performance against single superphosphate (SUP) in lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) cultivation. Our results demonstrate that STR matched or exceeded the performance of SUP in several key aspects. STR contained higher P and markedly higher Mg than SUP and exhibited lower heavy-metal contents. Dissolution assays showed that STR released little P in water over the incubation period, but dissolved rapidly in citric acid, consistent with organic-acid–promoted, rhizosphere-relevant P mobilization. STR matched or outperformed SUP in agronomic performance by increasing soil-extractable P and Mg, raising soil pH and mitigating acidification, and reducing plant uptake of heavy metals. Illumina sequencing of soil DNA indicated that STR caused minimal changes in α diversity but induced treatment-dependent community shifts, including increased relative abundance of Proteobacteria compared with SUP at matched P inputs, suggesting shifts in nutrient-cycling–related taxa. Overall, these results help address key application and mechanistic gaps by demonstrating that seawater-derived struvite can serve as an effective P source in aquatic crop cultivation and may support more sustainable phosphorus management.

title: Natural background levels of nitrate and ammonia nitrogen in groundwater from intensively farmed areas: A new exploratory data analysis method
abstract: Groundwater nitrogen pollution in intensive agricultural regions poses a significant threat to drinking water safety and the ecological health of local residents. Accurately determining the natural background levels of nitrate and ammonia in groundwater within these regions is crucial for preventing and controlling nitrogen pollution, as well as assessing the impact of human activities. However, due to the intricate nature of human activities in agricultural areas, conventional pre-selection methods often suffer from high subjectivity, leading to potential inaccuracies in estimating the natural background levels of nitrate in groundwater. We developed a novel method for estimating the natural background levels of nitrogen by leveraging its chemical properties. This approach integrates the [Cl−-NO3-/Cl−] graph with the Grubbs test and was compared and validated against several other established methods for calculating natural background levels, including the water chemistry-parameter method, machine learning-water chemistry method, isotope method, and pre-selection screening. Through reasonableness analysis, we identified the optimal method and verified its effectiveness. The results indicate that the [Cl−-NO3-/Cl−] graph -Grubbs method, which incorporates both the intrinsic transformation laws of nitrogen and the statistical characteristics of the data, identifies the largest number of outliers, exhibits the fewest inflection points in the remaining dataset, and demonstrates lower data dispersion compared to the other four methods, thereby achieving the best outlier identification performance. The validation analysis results indicated that the δ15N-NO3- values of the anomaly points predominantly corresponded to pollution sources such as sewage and manure. The abnormal groundwater nitrogen concentrations were likely attributable to human activities, particularly cattle and sheep farming in rural areas. Approximately 91.7 % of the anomalies could be validated using a combination of indicators, including the percentage index of the pollution index, land use type, total nitrogen content in the soil surface layer, and nitrogen isotope abundance. This demonstrates the rationality and reliability of the [Cl−-NO3-/Cl−] graph -Grubbs method for calculating the environmental background level of nitrogen. The natural background level of groundwater nitrogen is shaped by the Quaternary depositional environment, aquifer redox conditions, regional and local water flow systems, and hydrogeological conditions, and exhibits significant spatial and temporal variability. The findings of this study can serve as an informative reference for accurately identifying groundwater nitrogen pollution in agricultural regions, optimizing farmland management strategies, and enhancing groundwater resource management.

title: Pineapple-crown papers with partial NaOH substitution: Performance, costs, and life-cycle footprints
abstract: Non-wood agro-residues can reduce the environmental and cost burdens of papermaking, yet process alkalinity often drives impacts. Pineapple crowns were valorized as fiber feedstock and evaluated partial substitution of NaOH with NaHCO3 during processing, using NaOH–NaHCO3 ratios of 1:0, 3:1, and 1:1 (P100:0, P75:25, P50:50). Physical (grammage, thickness, porosity, burst, pH, water uptake) and instrumental characterizations, including Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric and derivative thermogravimetric analysis (TGA/DTGA), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), were coupled with cradle-to-gate life-cycle (CF: carbon footprint; WF: water footprint) and unit-cost analyses. P75:25 achieved the highest grammage (71.86 ± 0.49 g/m2) and balanced network consolidation, while P100:0 maximized burst (19.53 ± 0.91 psi); P50:50 increased porosity and moisture uptake. TGA/DTGA indicated effective polysaccharide/lignin breakdown for P100:0 and P75:25, with elevated high-temperature residue in P50:50, aligning with SEM-resolved fiber compaction. Environmental results decreased monotonically with sodium-bicarbonate substitution: total CF = 0.25, 0.22 (−12 %), and 0.19 kg CO2-eq for P100:0, P75:25, and P50:50. WF per sheet was 6.56, 3.72, and 3.28 L for P100:0, P75:25, and P50:50, respectively. Despite lab-scale costs (≈4.0 USD/sheet), sensitivity indicates reagent price and electricity as main levers. Overall, P75:25 offers the best performance-to-impact trade-off preserving mechanical integrity while lowering CF and WF vs P100:0 supporting pineapple-crown papers as credible candidates for lightweight packaging and printing.

title: Optimizing China's regional power generation structure for cost-effective emission reduction: A multi-scenario analysis integrating CCUS and policy pathways
abstract: As China navigates the dual imperatives of decarbonization and economic growth, strategic optimization of regional power generation portfolios emerges as a critical policy challenge. This study develops a novel multi-regional optimization framework integrating marginal abatement cost (MAC) curve analysis with a power generation optimization model to evaluate seven transition scenarios. And strategies for optimizing the regional power generation structure are proposed. Results show that between 2012 and 2020, the MAC in the power sector declined across most provinces, and the current average MAC significantly exceeds the actual carbon price. The scenario with the lowest comprehensive abatement costs is the Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) development combined with the Announced pledges scenario (CCUS&APS). There are differences in the scope for thermal generation across provinces under each scenario. Under the optimal scenario CCUS&APS, fifteen provinces have space to increase thermal power generation, while the other half need to reduce thermal power generation. The grouped provinces were not highly correlated in the geographical dimension, but their historical carbon emissions and economic development levels were relatively consistent. Policy strategies under the CCUS&APS scenario represent the optimal choice, effectively incentivizing emissions reductions at the lowest comprehensive abatement cost while promoting an orderly transition in provincial power generation structures.

title: Carbon emissions trading policy, social trust and green innovation: A path study based on an informal institution
abstract: To clarify the driving effect and pathway of carbon trading policies on green innovation in enterprises, this paper focuses on data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2007 to 2021, introducing the double-difference model to explore the changes in innovation level under the effect of Carbon Emission Trading Policy on enterprise green transformation. The research findings demonstrate that the adoption of the policy can efficiently encourage green innovation behavior, with green utility model innovation exhibiting a higher incentive effect than green invention innovation. For innovation quantity, the promoting effect is more significant in state-owned enterprises, companies with low technology levels, and enterprises in non-manufacturing industry. Moreover, from both quantitative and qualitative perspectives, the incentive effect of policy is reduced due to funding constraints, whereas government research and development subsidies have strengthened it. Finally, mechanism analysis indicates that the behavior of green innovation in enterprises can be enhanced. The empirical results provide empirical evidence for improving carbon trading policies and formulating differentiated green innovation incentive strategies for enterprises with different characteristics, which has important reference value for promoting sustainable development of enterprises and assisting in the achievement of the "dual carbon" goals.

title: Dual Z-scheme-driven sonophotocatalytic degradation of norfloxacin via PMS activation using BiVO4@LaCoO3@g-C3N5: Mechanisms, pathways, and environmental applications
abstract: The contamination of aquatic environments by persistent pharmaceutical pollutants poses significant challenges, necessitating the development of advanced catalytic systems for their effective removal. This study presents a novel BiVO4-LaCoO3@g-C3N5 (BVLCO@gCN) composite, designed for sonophotocatalytic degradation of norfloxacin (NOR) via peroxymonosulfate activation under ultrasonic-visible conditions. The 25BVLCO@75gCN composite exhibited outstanding catalytic performance, achieving 97.9% NOR degradation after 30 min of adsorption followed by 15 min of degradation, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.1995 min−1. Comprehensive material characterization using Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and X-ray diffraction analysis revealed an enhanced surface area, efficient charge transfer properties, and strong interfacial interactions between BiVO4@LaCoO3 (BVLCO) and g-C3N5. Mechanistic investigations through electron spin resonance spectroscopy and radical scavenger experiments confirmed that singlet oxygen (1O2) and hydroxyl radicals (•OH) were the primary reactive species driving NOR degradation. Additionally, the BVLCO@gCN composite demonstrated excellent stability and reusability, retaining over 95% efficiency after five regeneration cycles. These findings highlight the potential of BVLCO@gCN as a multifunctional catalyst for the effective removal of pharmaceutical contaminants, contributing to sustainable water management solutions.

title: The recycling of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries: A review on current progresses and technologies from an industrial utilization perspective
abstract: Since the lithium-ion battery (LIB) was successfully developed, it has been widely applied in many emerging fields. Among different types of LIBs, lithium iron phosphate batteries (LFP) hold a large market share due to their relative safety, low-cost raw materials, and long service life. With the prolonged service life and deterioration in battery capacity, the scrapping of LFPs is inevitable. Given environmental protection and resource recycling, the proper handling of spent LFPs has attracted the attention of scholars. Therefore, an overview of the existing recycling processes and associated problems is crucial. This paper presents the current status of the recovery processes, existing challenges, and outlook of industrial applications. This research is expected to guide the development of industrial production and provide insights for technological progress.

title: Investigation into release and transformation mechanisms of chlorine during representative industrial organic solid waste incineration
abstract: Co-incineration of municipal solid waste (MSW) with industrial organic solid waste (IOSW) offers a viable pathway for clean disposal and resource recovery of IOSW. However, the distinct thermochemical behavior of chlorine in IOSW compared to that in MSW presents significant challenges for emission control. Therefore, this study investigated the release and transformation mechanisms of chlorine during IOSW incineration. The results demonstrated that organic chlorine accounted for over 93% of total chlorine in typical IOSW, such as plastic, leather, and fabric. Chlorine release mainly occurred in the range of 350 °C–500 °C, primarily as organic chlorine and hydrogen chloride (HCl). Specifically, high-chlorine IOSW like poly(acrylonitrile-co-vinyl chloride) fibers released organic chlorine and aromatic compounds within this temperature window, while HCl was released within the 300–400 °C range. Furthermore, a quantitative analytical method developed in this study was employed to elucidate the distribution and transformation mechanisms of chlorine in IOSW incineration products. It was found that 40%–88% of chlorine in leather/fabric migrated to the gaseous phase as organic chlorine at 400–900 °C, whereas 70%–90% of chlorine in plastic converted into inorganic chlorine. Moreover, mechanistic analysis revealed that HCl was primarily generated via direct aliphatic chain dechlorination during plastic incineration, alongside organic chlorine formation through cyclization and secondary reactions. In contrast, for leather and fabric, chlorine underwent multi-stage pyrolysis to form organic chlorine, which subsequently decomposed into HCl. In this process, the generation and consumption of volatile organic chlorine occurred simultaneously and competitively. These findings provide critical insights for chlorine emission control during clean incineration of IOSW.

title: Energy, exergy, and economic analyses of a novel carbon dioxide-pumped thermal energy storage system with cooling, heating, and power cogeneration
abstract: Carbon dioxide-pumped thermal energy storage (CPTES) is an emerging energy storage technology that combines compressed carbon dioxide energy storage with heat pump technology. In the CPTES system, CO2 circulates within a closed loop, eliminating the need for separate CO2 storage. However, conventional CPTES systems suffer from reduced efficiency because electricity is consumed to generate cooling during discharging. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel CPTES system for combined cooling, heating, and power generation. The proposed system enhances power output by utilizing solar heat energy and recovers waste heat through an absorption refrigeration cycle and an organic Rankine cycle. The evaluation of the novel system performance is performed in terms of thermodynamics and economics.
