Under design conditions, the novel system can supply 11,335.6 kW of power, 4976.9 kW of heating, and 3252.4 kW of cooling. Compared to conventional systems, the novel system shows significant performance gains: round-trip efficiency increases by 27.82 %, energy efficiency by 14.98 %, and exergy efficiency by 8.44 %. In terms of economics, the novel system achieves a reduction of 5.61 years in the dynamic payback period and a reduction of $0.0725/kWh in the levelized cost of energy.

title: Optimization of reverse logistics network for electric vehicle batteries considering decommissioning forecast and carbon emission
abstract: Under China's “dual-carbon” goals, managing end-of-life electric vehicle batteries presents a critical challenge alongside the industry's rapid growth. This study develops an optimization model for the reverse logistics network of electric vehicle batteries, integrating a grey forecasting model for sales and a Stanford model for scrappage predictions. By simultaneously optimizing recycling node placement and transportation routes under carbon tax and carbon trading scenarios, the results demonstrates that a carbon tax, while reducing emissions by 3.18 %, increases total costs by 7.15 %. In contrast, a carbon trading market not only achieves emission reductions but also decreases costs by over 6 % compared to the tax scenario. This demonstrates that market-based mechanisms are superior to pure taxation in fostering a sustainable and economically viable electric vehicle battery recycling ecosystem.

title: Evaluating environmental–economic synergies of hydrogen production pathways: Insights from a life cycle perspective
abstract: Positioned at the forefront of global decarbonization strategies, hydrogen's environmental–economic synergies are highly contingent on production pathways and power sources. This study assesses the carbon mitigation potential and environmental co-benefits of steam methane reforming (SMR), alkaline electrolysis (ALK), and proton exchange membrane electrolysis (PEM) in China using an integrated EcoHealth–LCC model. Results show that, under the current grid mix, the carbon footprint of electrolytic hydrogen (35–37 tonnes CO2 eq/tonne H2) exceeds that of SMR (11 tonnes CO2 eq/tonne H2). When powered by renewable electricity, both ALK and PEM achieve reductions of approximately 10 tonnes CO2 eq per tonne hydrogen relative to grid-powered SMR. PEM–wind scenarios yield the highest environmental co-benefits, valued at 176.3 USD/tonne H2, reflecting avoided ecological and health costs relative to the baseline pathway. The results show substantial spatial heterogeneity. Water electrolysis in renewable-abundant provinces (Sichuan, Yunnan, Tibet, Qinghai) exhibits decarbonization advantages, while coal-dependent regions experience higher overall environmental impacts. Incorporating environmental co-benefits shortens payback periods by about two years, especially in high-quality wind regions. Overall, the findings demonstrate that the environmental and economic performance of hydrogen depends on renewable integration and region-specific deployment. The proposed framework offers a decision-support tool to align policy incentives with carbon mitigation and broader societal benefits, providing guidance for scaling sustainable hydrogen in emerging economies.

title: Multi-dimensional sustainability assessment of 2-ethylhexanoic acid production pathways: Integrating techno-economic analysis with planetary boundaries framework for butyraldehyde and isooctanol processes
abstract: 2-Ethylhexanoic acid (2-EHA) represents a critical fine chemical with extensive industrial applications in plasticizer, lubricant, and coating formulations. Currently, two principal manufacturing pathways dominate global production: the butyraldehyde condensation process, which constitutes the prevailing international standard, and the alkaline-mediated isooctanol oxidation approach, predominantly employed in Chinese industrial practice. Despite their industrial adoption, a systematic comparison of these routes—considering technical, economic, and environmental factors, particularly within the Planetary Boundaries framework is lacking. This study presents a systematic techno-economic and environmental assessment of both production routes using rigorous process simulations in Aspen Plus. The analysis encompasses detailed mass and energy balances, capital and operating cost structures, and carbon emission profiles. The results demonstrate that the butyraldehyde condensation process exhibits significant advantages, with a production cost of 1143 USD per ton of 2-EHA, representing a 11 % reduction compared to the 1291 USD per ton required for the isooctanol oxidation route at the same scale. Furthermore, the condensation process generates only 0.20 kg of CO2 per kg of 2-EHA produced, substantially lower than the 0.68 kg CO2 per kg associated with the oxidation method. Sensitivity analysis reveals that the butyraldehyde process is most affected by fuel gas price variations, with a 10 % price fluctuation leading to a 3.46 % change in total annual cost. In contrast, the isooctanol oxidation process shows greater sensitivity to electricity and steam costs, where a similar 10 % variation results in a 1.93 % and 1.90 % cost adjustment. The trade-off is clear: China's oxidation method offers simplicity, but the global-standard condensation route demonstrates superior economic and environmental performance within the gate-to-gate system boundary, excelling in energy efficiency and associated CO2 emissions. This study provides a systematic quantitative multi-criteria comparison of these production routes, offering valuable insights for process selection and sustainable optimization in the 2-EHA industry.

title: Enhanced membrane antifouling performance via interfacial hydroxide ions mediated pore contraction for efficient oil-water separation
abstract: Membrane fouling remains a critical challenge that severely limits the practical application of superwetting oil–water separation membranes. Here, an electrically enhanced separation strategy is presented, which effectively removes fouling through electro-driven pH-responsive membrane interface characteristics. The incorporation of polyacrylic acid (PAA) imparts pH-responsiveness to the PVDF membrane, whereas copper metallization confers superior electrical conductivity. As a cathode, the membrane electrolyzes water to generate OH−, directly triggering contraction of the pores, which lowers the flux from 11938 to 1755 L m−2·h−1·bar−1 under electrolysis. This contraction is accompanied by enhanced hydration, and the heterogeneous diffusion of interfacial OH− promotes the upward squeezing of oil droplets, reducing the adhesion area. During this process, both surface-pinned and pore-blocking oil droplets can be detached. Meanwhile, the membrane exhibits superhydrophilicity and underwater superoleophobicity (WCA = 0°, UWOCA = 162°), achieving over 98.4% rejection for various oil–water emulsions. After long-term cycling, the membrane maintains a flux recovery rate exceeding 96.2% for both oil and protein-based fouling under electrically controlled cleaning. The separation efficiency is significantly enhanced without high charge densities or additional agents, presenting promising potential for wastewater treatment applications.

title: A novel mainstream application of aerobic granular sludge for nitrite supply to Anammox: insights from granule size and microbial stratification
abstract: Aerobic granular sludge (AGS) offers compact footprint and process stability but is often limited in mainstream wastewater treatment. Here, we proposed a new application paradigm: operating AGS to simultaneously achieve pollutants removal and stably supply NO2−-N as substrates for downstream anaerobic ammonium oxidation (Anammox). The system was operated for 110 days, with average NH4+-N and COD removal efficiency reaching 98.09 % and 89.18 % respectively. The average accumulated concentration of NO2−-N reached 17.75 mg/L, and the nitrite accumulation ratio (NAR) was 73.49 %. Intracellular polyhydroxyalkanoates storage supported endogenous partial denitrification during the anoxic phase. Microbial analysis revealed a distinct enrichment of AOB (1.03 %), GAO (7.96 %), and partial denitrification functional bacteria (20.74 %). Batch tests demonstrated that the medium-sized granules (800–1250 μm) achieved the highest NAR (81.14 %) due to optimal stratification, substrate diffusion, and higher nitrate reductase gene abundance over nitrite reductase. FISH confirmed spatial separation of AOB, NOB, and denitrifying bacteria within granules. Two strategies were proposed for integrating AGS with Anammox, enhancing nitrogen removal and reducing carbon footprint. These results provide significant insights into sustainable wastewater treatment and mainstream AGS promotion under low-strength and low C/N conditions.

title: Decrypting water–energy–food nexus resilience in the Yellow River Basin: Spatiotemporal evolution, internal obstacles, and external drivers
abstract: Understanding and strengthening water–energy–food nexus resilience (WEFNR) is essential for promoting regional sustainability amid increasing environmental and socioeconomic pressures. Drawing on evolutionary resilience theory, this study develops a WEFNR assessment framework built on three core capacities: robustness, restorability, and adaptability. Using China's Yellow River Basin (YRB) as a case study, we construct a region-adapted city-level indicator system and evaluate the spatiotemporal evolution of WEFNR from 2011 to 2022. The obstacle degree model and geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) are applied to identify internal obstacles and external drivers. The results indicate that WEFNR in the YRB has shown a moderate overall increase, but disparities among cities have widened. Spatially, this manifests as a pattern of “lower reaches > middle reaches > upper reaches,” exhibiting distinct spatial clustering characteristics. Internally, significant obstacles include energy production and storage capacity, per capita arable land, and water availability per unit area. Externally, average annual precipitation, temperature, economic development, industrial structure rationalization, population density, fiscal investment in science, technology, and education, as well as digital inclusive finance, all exert significant yet heterogeneous impacts across space and time. These findings advance the conceptual and empirical understanding of WEFNR and provide policy-relevant insights for enhancing resilience in the YRB and other comparable regions.

title: Biomimetic dual-layer fertilizer: Hydrophilic-hydrophobic synergistic system for enhanced water retention and controlled nutrient release
abstract: In response to issues such as soil degradation caused by traditional urea (U) applications, low fertilizer utilization rate, and insufficient coordinated supply of water and nutrients, we propose a biomimetic fertilizer system that integrates water retention and controlled nutrient release. The bionic concept of the amphiphilic bilayer structure of cell membranes as a dynamic barrier for molecular permeation was introduced into the design of controlled-release fertilizers (CRFs). A bilayer-coated controlled-release fertilizer composed of polyaspartic acid-carboxymethyl cellulose double-network hydrogel (P-C), and stearic acid (S) was constructed, breaking through the limitations of traditional single-coating materials in terms of mechanical strength, fertilizer release kinetics, and water responsiveness, and achieving dynamic regulation of water-triggered and rate-limited release. The P-C outer layer has mechanical reinforcement function and absorbs water through swelling to achieve water retention, while the S inner layer acts as a hydrophobic barrier to prevent rapid release of urea. This cell membrane-like bilayer structure effectively regulates water-nutrient balance. P-C/S/U increased soil water holding capacity from 34.28 ± 1.21 % to 48.53 ± 2.58 % and extended water retention duration from 10 to 20 d. The P-C/S/U achieves a synergistic effect of water retention and nutrient controlled release, extending the nitrogen release period from 5 to 30 d and revealing a two-stage “lag-sustained release” mechanism. This release mechanism mirrors the growth dynamics of rapeseed plants, which exhibit favorable growth performance. This study provides a biomimetic structure design paradigm for intelligent fertilizer development.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on sustainable productivity changes in OECD Countries: A NO-SBM-DEA assessment
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sustainable productivity and eco-efficiency across 38 OECD countries from 2018 to 2023. Using a Non-Oriented Slack-Based Measure (NO-SBM) model integrated with the Malmquist Productivity Index (MPI), the analysis jointly accounts for desirable (GDP) and undesirable (CO2 emissions) outputs to measure total-factor productivity changes before, during, and after the pandemic. Results show that average sustainable productivity declined by 6.4 % during 2020–2021 but rebounded by 4.7 % in 2022–2023, resulting in an overall average annual change of −0.9 % across the full period. The decomposition indicates that recovery was driven primarily by technological change (TC)—reflecting innovation and digital transformation—while efficiency change (EC) played a secondary role. Regression analysis reveals that early vaccination rollout and moderate containment policies were positively associated with productivity recovery, whereas prolonged high stringency in 2022 slowed efficiency gains. Robustness checks across alternative DEA specifications (IO-SBM, IO-CCR, IO-BCC) and variable-exclusion tests confirm the consistency of these findings. The results highlight that adaptive governance, institutional agility, and sustained investment in clean technology and digital infrastructure are key to achieving resilient, innovation-driven, and environmentally sustainable productivity growth in the post-COVID era.

title: Unraveling the spatiotemporal dynamics of intergenerational carbon inequality in the context of China's aging population
abstract: Assessing the spatiotemporal dynamics of household carbon footprints (HCFs) and associated inequalities is crucial for achieving climate equity in aging societies. Previous studies have primarily focused on income-based inequality, while intergenerational carbon inequality and its link to aging remain unclear. By integrating an environmentally extended multiregional input-output (EE-MRIO) model with detailed household survey data, we quantified the urban–rural differences in HCFs across age groups in China and evaluated the evolution of intergenerational carbon inequality. The results revealed that between 2012 and 2017, HCFs exhibited rapid growth in a few regions and specific consumption categories but a general decline in others. Although the absolute change in per capita HCFs was marginal, the HCFs from the elderly accounted for as much as 39.4 % of certain expenditures, such as “Health”. With respect to intergenerational carbon inequality, rural areas exhibited higher inequality indices than urban areas, with the elderly contributing the most to overall inequality. Notably, they contributed as much as 33.2 % to inequality convergence in urban areas. We further identified a nonlinear relationship between intergenerational carbon inequality and aging, manifesting as an “inverted U-shaped” trajectory in urban areas and a “U-shaped” trajectory in rural areas. In response, differentiated strategies should be developed for specific regions and age groups. Concurrently, efforts should be made to refine the supporting mechanisms for delayed retirement and the policy measures supporting childbearing, thereby advancing the low-carbon transition and climate equity within an aging society.

title: Exploring three industrial waste-derived alkali activators in high-phosphogypsum supersulfated cement: Properties and hydration kinetics
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG), a major by-product of phosphoric acid production, is generated in vast quantities, posing serious environmental challenges. Conventional supersulfated cement (SSC) relies on carbon-intensive Portland cement clinker to activate relatively low PG dosages (<20 %), limiting both carbon reduction and waste utilization. Replacing clinker with alkaline industrial wastes in high-PG systems offers an ultra-low-carbon alternative, yet their comparative activation efficiency and substitution limits remain unclear. This study investigates the substitution of Portland cement clinker with three alkaline industrial wastes, namely steel slag (SS), red mud (RM), and calcium carbide residue (CCR), as activators in high-PG (60 %) SSC. Activation efficiency, optimal dosage ranges, and underlying mechanisms were evaluated through hydration kinetics, microstructural characterization, and mechanical performance analysis. The results reveal distinct activation behaviors among the three wastes. SS exhibits optimal performance at 25–50 % replacement by synergistically promoting C-(A)-S-H gel formation and reducing Ca/Si ratios, whereas higher replacement levels lead to a sharp strength decline. RM shows a similar dosage-dependent trend, enhancing gel polymerization at moderate contents but failing to sustain strength development when fully replacing clinker. In contrast, CCR effectively regulates AFt formation and mitigates late-age deterioration, achieving 28-day compressive strength comparable to clinker-based references without apparent dosage limitations. Environmental and economic assessments indicate substantial benefits. At optimal dosages, SS and RM reduce carbon emissions by 28.4 % and 34.1 % and costs by 26.8 % and 31.5 %, respectively, while CCR enables complete clinker substitution with 23.2 % carbon emission reduction and 11.4 % cost savings. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of waste-derived alkaline activators for developing sustainable, high-performance SSC with high PG utilization.

title: Integrating multi-criteria decision analysis and risk mapping for European Union clean energy technology roadmaps
abstract: The European Union's clean energy transition requires not only scaling up low-emission technologies, but also managing strategic vulnerabilities such as import dependence and exposure to critical raw materials. This study develops a transparent, data-driven framework to help European decision-makers to prioritize clean energy technologies under competing policy objectives. It combines Analytic Hierarchy Process with multi-criteria decision methods to evaluate 20 key technologies across seven indicators capturing techno-economic performance, environmental impacts and strategic dependence. Two alternative strategic perspectives are explored: (i) a “strategic autonomy” perspective that gives higher weight to supply chain resilience, and (ii) an “environmental–and-maturity” perspective that prioritizes lifecycle emissions and technological readiness. Technologies are ranked using Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution, and results are stress-tested through VIKOR, Preference Ranking Organization Method for Enrichment Evaluations, clustering analysis and Monte Carlo simulations of weight uncertainty. The analysis shows that heat pumps and onshore wind remain robust front-runners across perspectives, while advanced PV and battery technologies exhibit “high-performance–high-risk” profiles due to their strong dependence on critical raw materials and non-EU manufacturing. By contrast, some medium-performance technologies offer lower strategic dependence and can play a stabilising role in diversified portfolios. The paper derives a stepwise policy roadmap linking each indicator to EU instruments such as the Critical Raw Materials Act, REPowerEU and the Net Zero Industry Act. The proposed framework is intended as a screening tool for EU and national policymakers to align technology support portfolios with both decarbonization and resilience objectives.

title: Study on mix ratio optimization, microstructure evolution, and economic benefits of iron tailings-fly ash-limestone powder ternary geopolymer
abstract: Iron ore tailings (IOT) can be synergistically combined with other solid wastes under alkaline conditions to form eco-friendly cementitious materials. This study synthesized a ternary geopolymer using sodium silicate (Na2SiO3) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) as a composite alkali activator, along with IOT, fly ash (FA), and limestone powder (LSP) as precursors. We systematically examined the effects of activator modulus (M), alkali-to-precursor ratio (A/P), water-to-binder ratio (W/B), and FA replacement ratio (ω) on mechanical performance through orthogonal design and single-factor testing. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis were employed to characterize the microstructure, pore features, and alkali-activation mechanism. A cost comparison between the developed geopolymer and ordinary Portland cement (OPC) was also performed. Orthogonal test results revealed the following order of factor significance on strength: M > ω > A/P > W/B, with optimal levels of M = 1.2, A/P = 0.38, W/B = 0.26, and ω = 30 %. In single-factor tests, strength increased nonlinearly with extended curing time and reduced alkali modulus. A low-modulus activator (M = 1.0) created a highly alkaline environment that accelerated the dissolution of reactive Si-Al components from FA/IOT and calcium from LSP. Interactions among these dissolved species promoted C-(A)-S-H gel formation, leading to a denser matrix. Compared with OPC, the geopolymer offered clear economic advantages in non-structural applications such as road subbase layers.

title: Valorization of raw hide trimmings as alternative protein source for poultry feed: A step towards sustainable waste management and circular bioeconomy
abstract: The rising cost of traditional protein sources such as soybean meal and maize has prompted a search for sustainable alternatives in poultry feed. This study investigates the use of tannery raw hide trimming waste, a collagen-rich byproduct generated before chrome tanning, as a partial replacement for conventional protein. The extracted protein content was 96 % on a dry weight basis, determined using the Kjeldahl method. This study presents a novel approach by applying protein derived from pre-tanning tannery raw hide trimming waste in poultry feed formulation-an area that remains largely underexplored in current literature. Feeding trials with layer chickens showed that a formulation containing 21 % protein and 3200 kcal/kg energy led to a 9.3 % increase in weight gain and a 3 % improvement in egg production efficiency. A 15 % reduction in feed production cost was also achieved. The prepared feed was characterized using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy to identify functional protein groups, X-ray Diffraction to assess crystallinity and structural integrity, Scanning Electron Microscopy to observe morphology, and Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy to quantify trace metals. Chromium was apparent at 0.002 ppm, a negligible level substantially below the 10-ppm limit prescribed by European and Indian feed safety standards for poultry feed. These findings highlight the potential of tannery raw hide trimming waste as a sustainable feed ingredient, supporting circular economy goals by converting tannery waste into a value-added resource for poultry production.

title: Spatial distribution of bird diversity sensitivity to air pollutants
abstract: Air pollutants, as a global environmental issue, demand in-depth investigation into the mechanisms and spatial patterns by which they affect avian diversity. Existing studies often rely on coarse-resolution data or limited indicators of ecological pollutants, which constrain the applicability of management recommendations. This study uses the Yangtze River Delta urban agglomeration in China as a representative region, integrating multi-source environmental data with bird observations and employing a CNN-GCN weighted fusion deep learning model to infer a 1 km resolution map of bird diversity. Coupled with SHAP interpretability, we analyze the nonlinear effects of nine air pollutants. Our results show that ozone precursors NMVOC and CO exhibit the highest sensitivity, with high-value effects in opposite directions; NOx and NH3 display clear ecological thresholds or interval effects; PM2.5 generally exerts a weak negative effect across most areas, while particulates such as NMVOC and CO tend to have negative effects. By applying K-means clustering to GridSHAP rasters, we partitioned the grid into 4 sensitivity zones, revealing shared pollution-driven influences and enabling zone-specific governance strategies. Across regions, we identify the most effective priority management actions; for example, in Cluster 3, the priority should be reducing CO emissions. This study implements spatially explicit governance of pollutant effects on bird diversity, providing precise, region-specific, and differentiated guidance for ecological protection and environmental management.

title: Biodegradation of bioplastics under a simulated full-scale composting temperature profiles during biowaste composting as a clean and sustainable organic recycling method
abstract: Bioplastics labelled as compostable biodegrade in ISO standard conditions (with mature compost (C)). However, in real conditions, bioplastics will not be composted with C but with biowaste (B), i.e. biodegradable organic matter, which can affect the efficiency of bioplastic degradation. This study investigated the 90-day aerobic biodegradability of bioplastics containing polylactic acid (PLA), starch (FS), poly (butylene succinate) (PBS), and cellulose (Cel) under a simulated full-scale composting temperature profile (CTP, 1-week ↑ to 60 °C, 3-week at 60 °C, 4-week ↓ to ambient temperature, 5-week at ambient temperature) with B. To intensify bioplastic degradation, laccases were applied (B + L). Degradation with C was the control. Three biodegradability indicators were investigated: i) the time during which the mechanical properties could be determined, ii) the duration that pieces were visible, and iii) the time needed for complete bioplastic biodegradation. With L, the bioplastics lost mechanical properties and remained visible during a shorter time than with B only. Moreover, laccase significantly enhanced B degradation, as shown by nearly twofold higher total OM removal in B + L compared with B alone, resulting in final OM contents of 52.34 % and 60.65 %, respectively. Although the first two biodegradability indicators are important for scientific understanding of the mechanisms of decomposition, for technological application, the complete biodegradation of the bioplastics is most important. Taking this into consideration, the order of bioplastic biodegradability with B under CTP can be ranked as follows: FS > Cel > PBS > PLA. The findings represent a step forward in advancing the understanding of the clean biodegradation of bioplastics through composting and may support the establishment of guidelines for sustainable bioplastic management.

title: Engineering optimization of food waste treatment via anaerobic digestion: Building causal machine learning networks for comprehensive analysis
abstract: The efficiency of anaerobic digestion (AD) of food waste is currently facing the challenge of converting laboratory-optimized bioprocesses into stable industrial-scale operations. Here, an integrated causal machine learning framework was developed that combines interpretable feature analysis, causal inference, and counterfactual prediction. This study built a two-stage predictive modeling framework (R2 = 0.95) and conducted SHAP analysis to identify correlations among variables. Subsequently, the study applied a causal inference model to disentangle the effects of covariates and confounding variables, elucidating the dual role of volatile fatty acids (VFA) as both a substrate and a toxin, with an average treatment effect (ATE) = 0.41, and the concentration-dependent effect of total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) (ATE = 1.97). The causal analysis model constructed a quantitative network of causal relationships among the variables (a 1 m3 increase in daily feed volume results in a 13.2 % increase in VFA concentration), with significant relationships identified (p-values <0.05). Counterfactual simulations further identified feasible operating thresholds for key parameters. This framework and findings provide both theoretical insights and optimization strategies for improving the process efficiency and stability of anaerobic digestion systems.

title: Biomimetic rehabilitation of damaged contaminant-containment and load-bearing structure by a near-zero disturbance method: Pilot-scale test in an operating plant
abstract: As widely used ancillary facilities for preventing soil and groundwater pollution during industrial production, the contaminant-containment and load-bearing structures (CLS) are susceptible to damage in service. However, low-disturbance rehabilitation methods for damaged CLS are currently critically lacking in operating plants. In this study, a novel near-zero disturbance polyurethane grouting rehabilitation method for damaged CLS is proposed and validated via comprehensive field mechanical and environmental performance tests. The results demonstrated that the solidified polyurethane filled in the CLS slab cracks, and the cavities between the CLS slab and the underlying substratum markedly enhanced the structural integrity of the damaged CLS and improved its smoothness by 71.4 %. A maximum two-order-of-magnitude reduction in the permeability coefficient and 0.43 times of improvement in axial compressive strength were observed for the rehabilitated CLS (RCLS) slab cores. Furthermore, the long-term contaminant-containment performance of RCLS was enhanced by a 21.3 % increase in penetration resistance and a 17.3 % rise in dry density of the substratum soil. The effective and readily acceptable method for rehabilitating damaged CLS in operating plants holds great promise for application in the prevention and control of soil pollution sources.

title: Toward clean production of power batteries: An electrode burr detection method fusing line laser scanning and enhanced PointNet++
abstract: With the global advancement of transportation electrification policies, demand for power batteries continues to rise, and the requirements for safety and reliability during cell manufacturing have become increasingly stringent. As the core component of a battery, the electrode is prone to producing tiny burrs attached to the electrode surface during the slitting process. These micro-scale protrusions can readily puncture the separator, induce internal short circuits, and trigger severe thermal runaway incidents. Owing to the micro-scale dimensions and diverse morphologies of burr defects, conventional detection methods struggle to have effective detection. This study proposes a three-dimensional intelligent surface burr detection method that integrates line-laser scanning with deep learning, and benchmarks it against a widely deployed charge-coupled device (CCD) visual detection scheme in terms of detection performance, environmental impact, and techno-economic outcomes. According to the real production environment, the proposed method achieved a recall of 96.08% with a false positive rate of 6.54%, markedly outperforming the control group. From the environmental perspective, the line-laser camera scheme can daily reduce emissions by up to 93.14 kg CO2 per production line relative to the CCD detection scheme. In addition, the proposed approach offers clear economic advantages, with an estimated investment payback period of 160 days compared with the control group.

title: Spectral and molecular insights into dissolved organic matter-mediated hydroxyl radical formation during oxygenation of Fe-bearing clay mineral
abstract: Molecular diversity of dissolved organic matter (DOM) drives the differential of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) formation during Fe-bearing clay minerals (Fe-CM) oxygenation. However, the specific effects of multiple types of DOM on •OH formation, particularly focusing on investigating the transformation of reactive Fe species and DOM molecular perspective, remain inadequately understood. Here, we explored the effects of six types of DOM on •OH formation during reduced montmorillonite (rSWy-3) oxygenation. Adding DOM accelerated the •OH formation rates during rSWy-3 oxygenation. Humic acid or natural organic matter promoted 2.1 %–203.0 % •OH yield, but exhibited different concentration dependencies. Fulvic acid promoted •OH formation at high concentration (250 mg/L, increase by 174.4 %–180.5 %). DOM accelerated the conversion of surface-bound Fe(Ⅱ) to dissolved Fe2+, and enhanced the oxygenation of trans-coordinated octahedral Fe(Ⅱ) in reactive structural Fe(Ⅱ) by direct electron transfer or indirect structural rearrangement. These synergistic processes mediated by DOM promoted •OH formation during rSWy-3 oxygenation. High-resolution mass spectrometry revealed that highly unsaturated molecules with 0.17 < (DBE-O)/C < 0.28, including lignin and aromatic structure compounds with 0.27 ≤ O/C ≤ 0.56, enhanced •OH formation at low DOM concentration (50 mg/L). These molecules exhibited the inhibition phenomenon for •OH formation at high DOM concentration. The findings offer molecular-level perspectives on the mechanism of DOM-mediated •OH formation during Fe-CM oxygenation.

title: Unraveling urban resilience dynamics through social network analysis: Evidence from the Yangtze River Delta
abstract: Urbanization and climate change have intensified the frequency and impact of natural disasters, posing tremendous challenges to urban resilience and sustainability. Understanding how urban resilience evolves and what drives its transformation has become critical for adaptive urban governance. This study investigates the dynamic structure of urban resilience in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) region by developing an Environment–Institution–Infrastructure–Agent (EIFA) analytical framework comprising 43 indicators. Using Social Network Analysis (SNA), two decades of change in resilience linkages at multiple levels are examined, including the overall system, subsystem interactions, and key influencing nodes. Results reveal that: (1) overall connectivity among resilience factors has progressively weakened, indicating declining systemic integration; however, institutional resilience remains central, reflecting governance continuity amid increasing fragmentation; (2) after 2012, the synergy among resilience subsystems markedly declined, accompanied by rising network modularity, suggesting a transition toward isolated subsystem development; and (3) the environmental dimension exhibits high temporal volatility and weak coupling with other dimensions, highlighting its marginalization in coordinated resilience strategies. Notably, indicators related to smart city development and digital infrastructure have gained influence, enhancing information flow and governance efficiency. Overall, the YRD's resilience system is characterized by declining systemic integration, institutional–infrastructural dominance, weak environmental coupling, and emerging yet path-dependent digital resilience, rather than a transformative restructuring. By adopting a longitudinal and relational perspective, this study advances understanding of urban resilience as a dynamic networked process and provides policy-relevant insights for integrated and sustainable resilience planning in rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: Efficient extraction of valuable metals and preparation of FePO4·2H2O from lateritic nickel ore via clean magnetizing roasting-selective leaching process
abstract: With the rapid development of the new energy industry under the dual–carbon policy, lateritic nickel ore, rich in Ni, Co, Mn, and Fe, has become the primary source of nickel for industrial applications. However, current metallurgical processes still face challenges, including complex separation steps, low extraction efficiency, and poor product quality. This study proposes a process to enhance the formation of spinel ferrites (MFe2O4, where M = Ni, Co, and Mn) during roasting of transitional laterite ore prior to phosphoric acid leaching, thereby facilitating the enrichment and separation of nickel and cobalt from iron. The effects of calcination temperature, additive dosage, and seed–crystal addition on spinel formation, particle growth, and magnetic separation were investigated. The addition of 8 % Na2CO3 and 15 % seed crystals at 1000 °C promoted molecular aggregation and ordered arrangement, accelerating spinel crystal formation and growth with the increase of saturation magnetization to 11.6 emu/g, resulting in a nickel content of 8.05 % (recovery: 91.25 %), a cobalt content of 0.17 % (recovery: 89.87 %), and a manganese content of 2.41 % (recovery: 91.58 %) after magnetic separation. The selective phosphoric acid leaching of the magnetic concentrated yielded efficiencies of 97.6 %, 95.7 %, and 94.5 % for Ni, Co, and Mn, respectively, while the Fe leaching efficiency was only 3.8 %. This process produced a leaching liquor containing Ni2+, Co2+ and Mn2+ ions, along with an FePO4·2H2O residue, which can serve as precursors for lithium-ion battery cathode materials.

title: Ultrafast and selective recovery of lithium from spent cathodes via flash Joule heating-driven chlorination
abstract: The rapid growth of the electric vehicle market has made the disposal of used lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) a pressing global concern. Conventional recycling methods, such as hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy, are often hindered by high energy costs, chemical consumption, and secondary pollution. This study therefore proposes an ultrafast, selective chlorination strategy based on flash Joule heating (FJH) for the recycling of spent LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathode materials. Applying a 36 V pulse for just 3 s rapidly heated a mixture of spent NCM811, sodium chloride (NaCl) and carbon black to over 1500 °C. Under these conditions, a carbothermal reduction and chlorination process was triggered, which selectively converted lithium into the water-soluble compound lithium chloride (LiCl). This allowed a high Li leaching efficiency of 92.4 % to be achieved using only water as the lixiviant. Meanwhile, the transition metals (nickel, cobalt and manganese) were reduced to lower valence states or metallic forms and remained in the solid residue. Mechanistic analysis confirmed that the process involves the outward migration of Li+ and O2−, followed by a reaction between lithium oxide (Li2O) and NaCl facilitated by carbon. The method demonstrated excellent versatility, achieving lithium recovery rates of 90.3 %, 87.0 % and 89.6 % for spent LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 (NCM622), LiCoO2 (LCO) and LiMn2O4 (LMO) cathodes, respectively. This work provides a promising, energy-efficient, and rapid approach to the selective recovery of lithium from various spent LIBs cathodes, showing great potential for industrial application.

title: Synergistic evolution and mechanism analysis of pollution and carbon reduction: A cross-basin perspective from China
abstract: As the environmental governance system in China continues to mature, it has become essential to understand cross-basin coordination mechanisms for pollution reduction and CO2 mitigation (PRCM) in order to achieve synergistic emission reduction targets. This study proposes a novel multidimensional analytical framework to systematically evaluate the spatiotemporal evolution regularities and cross-basin interaction mechanisms of PRCM across the ten major river basins in China from 2000 to 2022 through integrated the coupling coordination degree (CCD) model, a spatial gravity model incorporating natural, economic, and social attributes, as well as a gravity-augmented graph attention network. The results indicate that pollutant discharge levels and CO2 emission intensity have shown downward trends, with spatial heterogeneity patterns of “south-high, north-low” and “north-high, south-low”. The CCD trends indicate a clear progression of PRCM coordination level from weak (CCD <0.47) to strong (CCD >0.78). Spatial gravity analysis reveals the emergence of a core zone for PRCM gravitational diffusion centered on the Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Hai River Basins (accounting for 87 % of the total gravitational intensity), while peripheral basins such as the Southwest and Northwest Rivers act as critical “bridging” nodes. Meanwhile, pollutant discharges and CO2 emissions across basins have gradually decoupled from economic growth. In addition, spatial analysis demonstrates that socio-economic drivers (e.g., GDP) and natural conditions (e.g., vegetation coverage) jointly drive the spatial spillover effects of cross-basin PRCM. This study provides insights into the synergy mechanisms of PRCM and offers strategic reference for enhancing cross-basin environmental governance under the dual-carbon targets in China.

title: Tuning muscovite into geopolymer product through thermal–mechanochemical activation
abstract: Enhancing the reactivity of highly crystalline T–O–T clays such as muscovite remains a bottleneck for alkali-activated binders. This work compares thermal treatment (T), mechanochemical activation (MCA), and their sequences—calcination followed by MCA (T–MCA) and MCA followed by calcination (MCA–T)—to establish how activation order governs structure–reactivity–performance. Integrated multi-scale characterization, supported by molecular dynamics, shows that T induces dehydroxylation with limited framework disruption, whereas MCA generates defects and particle refinement without removing long-range order. In contrast, T–MCA produces extensive loss of periodicity and a higher density of accessible reactive sites, accelerates early dissolution–polycondensation, and yields mixed N-A-S-H/K-A-S-H gels with superior early strength. MCA–T promotes the persistence of defects via layer collapse and local reorganization, thereby slowing reaction kinetics and yielding Na-dominated gels with limited strength. These findings position T–MCA as a practical route to convert muscovite into high-performance alkali-activated binders and geopolymers—particularly where conventional ashes or slags are scarce but muscovite resources are abundant—and provide design guidance linking layered-silicate destabilization to reaction kinetics, gel assemblage, and mechanical performance.

title: Tracking food-nutrition-carbon footprint evolutions and driving forces of China's megacity: insights from dietary transitions in Chengdu
abstract: With large-scale population aggregation, rising affluence, and changing food environments, megacities have become focal points of food consumption and associated climate impacts. This study examined the dietary transition process in Chengdu, a major megacity of China, and evaluated associated carbon footprint impacts. In addition, the driving forces during different dietary transition phases were analyzed using Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) model. Results show that Chengdu's dietary transition was characterized by the phased, diversified and persistent substitutions of foods rich in carbohydrate with those rich in fat and protein. Consequently, the per capita diet-linked carbon footprints increased by 35.73%, and total carbon footprints of Chengdu increased by 2.84 times. The calorie supply intensity, industrial structure and carbon intensity conjointly reduced the footprints by 48.68 Mt CO2e, while the per capita GDP, dietary structure and population drove the footprints up by 62.13 Mt CO2e, substantially offsetting the gains made by the mitigating factors. Driving factors contributed differently across distinct dietary transition phases. Per capita GDP was the dominant driver of increasing carbon footprints, but its effects weakened in the last phase. Calorie supply intensity played a key role in reducing carbon footprints during the first three phases, while industrial structure became the leading contributor to reductions since 2013. Notably, carbon intensity had limited effects to decline the footprints, underscoring the necessity of tackling non-energy-related emission sources. Chengdu's dietary transition serves as a forward-looking case for other developing cities in China.

title: Spatio-temporal photovolatic power forecasting via Bayesian-optimized dynamic graph convolutional networks with temporal convolutional networks
abstract: Accurate and reliable Photovoltaic power forecasting is essential for optimizing grid management and ensuring efficient renewable energy integration. However, the inherent intermittency and variability of solar generation pose significant challenges for existing forecasting methods, which often struggle to fully exploit spatio-temporal dependencies in Photovolatic (PV) data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Bayesian-optimized (BO) hybrid deep learning prediction framework that integrates Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) with Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) for enhanced spatio-temporal PV power forecasting. First, the GCN component can capture intricate spatial dependencies among geographically distributed stations, enabling the model to account for localized variations and interactions. Meanwhile, the TCN component can excel in extracting long-term temporal patterns from time-series data, which is essential for accurate and reliable predictions. Then, the introduction of BO can ensure optimal hyperparameter configuration of GCN-TCN, which is critical for maximizing model performance. By integrating spatial and temporal features, the proposed model can effectively address the challenges of modeling complex nonlinear relationships and high-dimensional data, thereby demonstrating superior adaptability to dynamic environmental changes. Compared with the existing prediction models, such as CNN-Gated Recurrent Unit, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory and Transformer, simulation tests conducted under different PV stations, seasons and weather conditions demonstrate that the proposed prediction model exhibits excellent performance in terms of mean absolute error (2.92 KW), root mean square error (4.51 KW), mean absolute percentge error (2.04 %), and coefficient of determination (0.995) metrics.

title: When does ESG drive efficiency? The roles of individualism and business strategy in the telecom sector
abstract: Existing studies have identified several drivers of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) engagement, including external pressure, managerial traits, and firm strategies. However, these factors are often examined separately, and the findings are inconsistent across institutional settings. That is, prior research does not clarify how broader national conditions and firm-level strategic choices jointly shape the relationship between ESG and firm efficiency (FE). This omission is important because ESG outcomes depend not only on internal capabilities but also on the cultural and strategic environments in which firms operate. To address this gap, the present study investigates how business strategy (BS) and national culture function together as higher-order moderators of the ESG–FE link. Using a three-stage range directional measure (RDM) within data envelopment analysis (DEA), we evaluate FE for 69 leading global telecom firms across 34 countries from 2018 to 2022. We then apply a hierarchical regression grounded in resource-based and institutional theories. The results show that aggressive strategies strengthen the positive effect of social ESG initiatives on innovation and sustainability efficiency, whereas individualistic cultures weaken this influence. Robustness tests using lagged variables confirm these findings. This study demonstrates that social ESG practices yield stronger efficiency gains when aligned with strategic orientation and embedded within supportive cultural environments.

title: Determinant factors of government change capability towards smart cities: A dynamic capability perspective
abstract: This study investigates critical factors shaping government capability for organizational change within smart city initiatives. Despite Indonesia's significant investment in smart city programs, uneven implementation and inconsistent results highlight gaps in understanding how digital and organizational capabilities impact performance. This research addresses these gaps by examining how Information Technology Capability (ITC), Organizational Change Capability (OCC), 21st-century digital skills (DS), and innovativeness (INN) collectively influence organizational performance (OP). The study employs a multilevel quantitative survey design with multisource data collection, involving 1384 middle and lower-level managers from the Surabaya City government in Indonesia. Data was analyzed using multilevel modelling in MPlus 8.3, examining relationships at both individual and organizational levels. ITC has a positive effect on OP but not on OCC. OCC also enhances OP, yet it does not mediate the ITC–OP link. DS strengthens the ITC–OCC path, and INN strengthens the OCC–OP path. This study addresses digital transformation in smart city programs by using an organizational change capabilities perspective, focusing more on the middle manager role rather than IT infrastructure or other technical capabilities.

title: Anaerobic granular sludge as a multifunctional carrier for enhanced partial nitrification: Effective nitrite-oxidizing bacteria suppression and in-situ nitrate removal
abstract: Partial nitrification (PN), a crucial step in the anammox-driven nitrogen removal process, is often compromised by NO3--N accumulation due to difficulties in effectively suppressing nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB). This study aimed to develop a carrier-based granulation strategy that not only enhances NOB suppression structurally but also addresses the residual NO3--N issue. Three sequencing-batch reactors were operated for 130 days: a control reactor (R-CON), one with granular activated carbon (R-GAC), and one inoculated with heterotrophic anaerobic granular sludge (R-AnGS) as a microbial carrier. The reactors were subjected to increasing nitrogen loading rates to evaluate the formation of PN granules and their nitrogen transformation performance. The results demonstrated that both carriers accelerated sludge granulation and improved NO2--N accumulation. However, R-AnGS outperformed others, achieving the highest NO2--N accumulation ratio (89.3 ± 5.2 %) and the lowest effluent NO3--N, alongside superior stability under high nitrogen load. This enhanced performance is attributed to the denser granular structure (>200 μm fraction: 62.4 %), elevated extracellular polymeric substance production, and the development of pronounced anoxic cores in R-AnGS. AnGS facilitated the co-enrichment of ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (e.g., Nitrosomonas) and denitrifiers (e.g., Thauera), enabling simultaneous NO2--N accumulation and internal NO3--N removal. This study reveals that AnGS serves a dual function: as a structural nucleus for rapid aerobic granulation and as a microbial reservoir that introduces intrinsic denitrification capacity. The findings offer an efficient strategy for optimizing PN processes, with implications for improving the robustness of subsequent anammox treatment.

title: Intelligent control of food waste composting based on PID and LSTM: analysis and comparison of strategies
abstract: To address high energy consumption and inefficiencies in food waste composting under manual or empirical control, this study developed an intelligent control strategy using a Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM) for real-time prediction and regulation of pile temperature and oxygen concentration. A PID-based control strategy (PID-BCS) was used as the benchmark. The LSTM-based strategy (LSTNet-BCS) achieved superior prediction accuracy for temperature and oxygen, with RMSE of 0.0114 and 0.0032, respectively, and R2 > 0.93. Critically, LSTNet-BCS reduced composting duration by 42.86 %: compost attained a Seed Germination Index (GI) of 96.2 % with organic matter content (OMC) of 48.07 % by day 16 (384 h), whereas PID-BCS required 24 days (576 h) to reach GI = 96.23 % (OMC = 50.58 %). Microbial community analysis showed that LSTNet-BCS advanced the establishment of a thermophilic, lignocellulose-degrading consortium compared with PID-BCS, with Thermomyces peaking at 80.78 % relative abundance and Bacillus and Saccharopolyspora together exceeding 40 % by day 12–16, while comparable community restructuring under PID-BCS occurred only after day 20. At the pilot scale, techno-economic evaluation indicated that the shorter, less labour and energy intensive LSTNet-BCS cycles reduced unit capital and operating costs and yielded a positive net margin of 277.16 ¥·t−1 FW, whereas PID-BCS generated 89.57 ¥·t−1 FW. These findings confirm that the LSTM model can simultaneously stabilize composting kinetics, accelerate organic matter decomposition and improve economic performance, thereby elevating compost quality and overall process value. This work establishes a framework for intelligent organic waste valorization and provides foundations for composting technology upgrades.

title: Revealing fine-scale carbon disparities using daily CO2 emissions estimated from plant-level NOx monitoring data
abstract: Real-time estimation of regional CO2 emissions remains a major challenge, limiting the development of effective local low-carbon policies. This study developed a novel method to estimate daily CO2 emissions from large industrial plants by integrating satellite observations with plant-level nitrogen oxide (NOx) monitoring data, using China's largest carbon-emitting province as a case study. The fine-scale carbon distribution was then mapped, and the key emission drivers were identified using machine learning. Results indicated that plant-level records constrained by satellite observations effectively captured daily industrial emission dynamics, which closely matched the COVID-19 lockdown timeline. The significant upward emission trend was disrupted in 2020, with the steel and cement sectors declining by more than 40 %, while the power sector declined by only 9.2 %. Although analyses based on the Gini coefficient suggested moderate inequality in CO2 emissions between rural and urban areas and across cities, group-based comparisons revealed remarkable disparities. Rural areas generally bore a higher carbon burden, with average daily industrial CO2 emissions exceeding those in urban areas by 7.498 (7.197–7.500) kt. Economically developed regions exhibited lower carbon intensity: the top three cities contributed 36.0 % of industrial GDP but only 21.1 % of CO2 emissions, whereas the bottom three cities contributed 9.3 % of GDP but accounted for 18.8 % of emissions. Reducing energy intensity and enforcing stringent policies remain critical for substantial emission reductions. Overall, this study proposed a framework to derive finer temporal-resolution carbon emission estimates from plant-level monitoring data and calls for incorporating carbon disparities into climate policy.

title: Sustainable utilization of citrus biowaste through pharmacoinformatic and green extraction approaches to develop polymethoxyflavones-rich extract targeting xanthine oxidase in gouty arthritis
abstract: Citrus biowaste, a major by-product of juice and food processing, is produced in large quantities but remains underutilized. This underuse contributes to environmental issues and overlooks its potential as a rich source of bioactive compounds, notably polymethoxyflavones (PMFs), with therapeutic value. This study presents a comprehensive pipeline for the sustainable valorization of PMFs from citrus waste, targeting gouty arthritis. Pharmacoinformatic analyses identified xanthine oxidase inhibition and inflammation modulation as key mechanisms, with structure-activity relationships highlighting tangeretin, sinensetin, and nobiletin as lead PMFs. Molecular docking and dynamics confirmed strong and stable binding to xanthine oxidase, especially for sinensetin (binding free energy = −79.9 kcal/mol). Citrus reticulata (Kinnow) was identified as the most PMF-rich cultivar. Using natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES; betaine-glycerol) and ultrasound-assisted extraction, PMFs yields increased threefold over ethanol extraction, as verified by High performance liquid chromatography. These NADES extracts demonstrated enhanced antioxidant (half-maximal inhibitory concentration = 10.17 mg/mL) and anti-inflammatory activities. Kinetic modeling and scanning electron microscopy confirmed improved mass transfer and cell disruption. Enzyme kinetics showed potent xanthine oxidase inhibition by both sinensetin and NADES-extracts, surpassing allopurinol. Overall, this integrative, bio-guided approach promotes eco-friendly PMF recovery and supports their development as natural therapeutics for metabolic and inflammatory diseases.

title: Frost-aware performance analysis and optimization of annular thermoelectric generators for liquefied natural gas vaporizers
abstract: Thermoelectric recovery of liquefied natural gas (LNG) cold energy is limited by wall frosting and low conversion efficiency. We establish a coupled mathematical model that links internal LNG phase-change heat transfer, external frosting heat transfer, and thermoelectric energy conservation for an ambient-air vaporizer integrated with an annular thermoelectric generator array (VATEG). Using this framework, we analyze VATEG performance and mechanisms under frosting across tube length and inlet flow rate, and we evaluate a graded-width annular thermoelectric generator as a structural optimization. When frosting is explicitly included, the optimal length shifts from 8.9 to 11.7 m and the peak power and efficiency decrease from 155 W to 1.7 % to 114.3 W and 1.05 %, indicating overestimation by 35.6 % and 62 % if frosting is neglected; integrating annular thermoelectric modules elevates the two-phase wall temperature and reduces local frost thickness from 15.2 to 9.5 mm (−37.5 %); under frosting, the unit-length power density decreases in the gas region, exhibits a step-rise to a near-constant plateau across the two-phase region whose height peaks at medium flow, and then decreases in the liquid region; a graded-width design with Δw = 6 mm increases peak power by 69.4 % at 20 % rated flow, while the optimal length increases linearly with Δw within the examined range. These results provide practical guidance for frost-aware co-optimization of length, flow, and module geometry in LNG vaporizer thermoelectric systems.

title: A self-healing asphalt mixture with palm oil capsules: A cost-effective approach toward net-zero pavement maintenance
abstract: Given the high carbon footprint of conventional asphalt maintenance methods, this study develops a novel self-healing asphalt mixture with bio-rejuvenating capsules containing refined palm oil. Unlike surface-applied petroleum rejuvenators or energy-intensive microwave heating, these capsules autonomously release a low-carbon bio-oil at crack locations during service. To find the optimum palm oil capsules for asphalt mixtures, three types of calcium alginate capsules with different oil-to-water ratios (5 %, 10 %, and 15 % O/W) were developed and underwent various tests, including compressive strength, size measurement, thermal sensitivity, thermogravimetric analysis, and scanning electron microscopy. The impact of optimum capsules on the mechanical and self-healing properties of the asphalt concrete (at micro and macro scale) was then assessed using the indirect tensile stiffness modulus, semi-circular bending, indirect tensile fatigue, and Fourier Transform infrared spectroscopy tests. The carbon emissions, energy use, and costs of asphalt pavements incorporating these capsules were also evaluated and ranked using two multi-criteria decision-making approaches that combined mechanical performance and environmental indicators. Results showed that although palm oil capsules slightly (p-value > 0.05) degraded mechanical properties of asphalt mixtures, adding 0.7 wt% capsules significantly enhanced the macro- and micro-damage healing properties, resulting in improvements in fracture strength, fracture energy, stiffness modulus, and fatigue life of 52 %, 50 %, 25 %, and 22 %, respectively. Also, the mixture with 0.35 % capsules reduced life-cycle cost, carbon emissions, and energy use by 26 %, 17 %, and 29 %, respectively, and achieved the best overall performance, indicating that capsule-based self-healing asphalt can modernize pavement maintenance and support progress toward Net Zero pavements.

title: The upcycling of biomass-based single-use products via co-digestion with organic waste: organic acids production and dewaterability performance
abstract: Biobased single-use products, primarily encompassing biopolymers like polylactic acid (PLA) and biofiber materials such as various paper products, are common in municipal solid waste streams. However, they are mainly treated by landfilling or incineration, neglecting their bioconversion potential. This study investigated the feasibility of utilizing PLA and waste paper for organic acid (volatile fatty acids and lactic acid) production through co-digestion with food waste or sewage sludge. Results indicated that the organic acid yield from PLA co-digestion with food waste reached 419 mg/g-volatile solids (VS), compared to 372 mg/g-VS in the control reactor. Moreover, lactic acid was the predominant organic acid in the PLA co-digestion reactor, representing 79.5 % of the total yield, which was significantly higher than the 45.7 % contribution in the control reactor. Furthermore, the improvement in organic acid production from paper waste was only significant during thermophilic co-digestion with sewage sludge. The organic acid yields from different paper substrates were 107 mg/g-VS and 99.1 mg/g-VS, respectively, compared to 80.2 mg/g-VS in the control reactor. Interestingly, co-digestion with the two types of waste paper significantly altered the dewatering performance of the fermented liquid. Specifically, the capillary suction time of the fermented liquid decreased by 19.6 % and 23.4 % when co-digested with food waste, with each percentage corresponding to a different paper type. This was attributed to the redistribution of extracellular polymeric substances. This study provides valuable insights into the bioconversion of single-use biobased products for organic acid production, considering both acid yield and fermented liquid dewatering characteristics.

title: Research on preventing soil-borne diseases by crop residue burning: equipment design, combustion performance, and thermophysical contact killing effect
abstract: The abuse of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, continuous cropping patterns, improper crop residue returning, and other factors have triggered frequent soil-borne diseases in crops, significantly reducing crop yield and quality while threatening food security and agricultural sustainable development. Based on the experimental platform of the developed self-propelled soil disinfector, the combustion performance of crop residue and the thermal contact effect of high-temperature flue gas on the killing rate of soil-borne diseases are investigated. The combustion performance results show that the combustion efficiency is 84.21 %, the outlet flue gas enthalpy of 731 kJ/kg can be achieved when the fuel feeding rate is 195 kg/h and the air excess ratio is 1.6. The killing rate and energy utilization ratio (EUR) of the thermal contact killing unit are optimized by conducting three factors and three levels Box-Behnken response surface experiments. Taking the flue gas temperature (X1), soil moisture content (X2), and soil feeding rate (X3) as the factors, and the bacteria killing rate (Rb), fungi killing rate (Rf), and EUR as the indicators, the three quadratic polynomial regression models are established. Through model optimization, the round optimal working parameters are obtained as X1 = 379 °C, X2 = 16 %, and X3 = 243 kg/h, with corresponding predicted values of Rb = 95.03 %, Rf = 95.93 %, and EUR = 76.57 %. The relative error between the experimental results and the model optimization results is less than 5 %, indicating that the model demonstrates high prediction accuracy. Finally, the optimal soil moisture content ranges for soil-borne disease control in practical applications are determined. The research results can provide reference value for the optimization of operating parameters for thermophysical prevention and control of soil-borne diseases.

title: Multi-step battery temperature prediction for electric vehicles: Vehicle identification-driven long short-term memory neural networks based on real-world charging pile data
abstract: Accurate prediction of battery temperature is critical for ensuring the safety of electric vehicles (EVs), which are pivotal for achieving cleaner transportation and reduced carbon emissions. Current research on battery temperature prediction relies primarily on laboratory or onboard battery management systems (BMS) data. However, these data sources have limitations in reflecting the complexity of real-world charging scenarios. In addition, the lack of vehicle identification information in charging pile data challenges accurate temperature prediction. To address this issue, this paper proposes a new approach that combines vehicle identification and grouping with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to predict battery temperature using real-world charging pile data. This study first proposes a multi-parameter disparity-based vehicle identification grouping (MPDVIG) strategy to group the charging data by vehicle identification. Then, the LSTM model is used to predict the temperature based on the overall and grouped data. By comparing the results of the two approaches, it is found that the accuracy of the method of identification followed by prediction is higher. For instance, the mean relative error for the highest temperature predictions decreased from 1.45 % to 1.06 %. This is the first time the LSTM model has been applied to the battery temperature prediction based on the real-world charging pile data, providing a reference for the subsequent safety warning.

title: Impacts of coal rank on the CO2 adsorption capacity of nitrogen/sulfur-doped coal-based adsorbents
abstract: To achieve efficient and low-cost CO2 capture, doped coal-based solid sorbents offer a highly promising pathway. In this study, N-doped and N, S co-doped coal-based adsorbents were prepared via a one-step treatment using urea and thiourea as nitrogen and nitrogen/sulfur sources, respectively. Experimental results combined with numerical analysis show that, after doping, the maximum relative increases in nitrogen- and sulfur-containing functional groups reach 54.08 % and 309.8 %, respectively, with thiourea treatment leading to a particularly pronounced increase in nitrogen functionalities. A key finding is that, as the maximum vitrinite reflectance (R0, max) increases from 0.560 to 3.533, the CO2 uptake of the doped coals exhibits a volcano-type trend, first increasing and then decreasing with R0, max, revealing a strong dependence of adsorption performance on coal rank. The density functional theory calculations further indicate that the incorporation of N and S atoms narrows the energy gap, lowers the barrier for electronic excitation, enhances the chemical reactivity of the coal matrix, and facilitates charge transfer with CO2. These insights provide important guidance for the structural design and optimization of coal-based adsorbents and are highly relevant for the development of large-scale CO2 capture technologies.

title: Integrating environmental footprint analysis and analytic hierarchy process for sustainable decision-making for in situ groundwater remediation
abstract: Green and sustainable remediation (GSR) is critical for balancing the needs of environmental preservation and technical efficacy when managing contaminated sites; however, the lack of an effective quantitative tool compromises the assessment and selection of GSR technologies. This study is aimed at introducing a framework by integrating Spreadsheets for Environmental Footprint Analysis (SEFA) with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to facilitate decision-making of site remediation. The SEFA quantifies lifecycle environmental footprints by encompassing material use, water consumption, energy consumption, and air emissions, whereas AHP prioritizes technologies through expert-weighted criteria. This new framework was employed to evaluate four presumptive in situ remediation technologies for the cleanup of a 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) contaminated site in Binzhou City, Shandong Province, China: groundwater risk control (GRC), in situ chemical oxidation (ISCO), in situ activated carbon adsorption (ISAC), and a permeable reactive barrier (PRB). Our results demonstrated a clear sustainability hierarchy according to the composite index (CI) that reflects the environmental footprints and their indicator weighting: ISAC (0.16) ≈ ISCO (0.18) < PRB (0.47) < GRC (2.31). ISAC and ISCO emerged as the optimal GSR strategies (i.e., smallest CI), with the lowest material use (71–106 t), energy consumption (1.85–1.94 × 106 MJ), and greenhouse gas emissions (81–83 t CO2-eq). Their water consumption was less than one-third of that required by GRC, while PRB operated without process water. By integrating quantitative metrics and expert-weighted priorities, this framework provides policymakers with a robust and transparent tool for GSR-oriented decision-making with promise of incorporating socioeconomic factors and stakeholder engagement to further enhance the applicability of the SEFA–AHP methodology.

title: Decoding mineral separation mechanisms via interpretable machine learning
abstract: The efficiency of mineral processing is currently constrained by a reliance on empirical optimization, largely due to the opacity of particle-scale separation physics. To address this challenge, we present an interpretable machine learning framework that integrates separation experiments, automated mineralogy, and explainable AI to decode these underlying mechanisms. The framework reveals that operational parameters function as dynamic feature selectors, modulating the extent to which geometrical features and particle locking states constrain the composition-dominated process. This critical insight enables rational process design. By enabling digital particle tracking, this approach facilitates a mechanism-guided optimization strategy that reduces repetitive physical experimentation with knowledge-based control. This shift significantly advances cleaner production by minimizing the resource and energy consumption associated with traditional trial-and-error testing. Using rhodochrosite magnetic separation as a proof-of-concept, the framework successfully translated mechanistic insights into a two-stage strategy with experimentally validated performance improvements. The methodology is transferable across particle-based separation technologies, enabling a paradigm shift from empirical experience to mechanism-driven control in sustainable mineral processing.

title: How does territorial spatial transition improve basin resource-environment coupling? A socio-environmental development gradient perspective
abstract: Understanding how territorial spatial transitions reshape resource-environment interactions is essential for sustainable basin development. Existing studies predominantly focus on linear relationships between land use change and isolated resource or environment factors, overlooking the nonlinear effects of multidimensional land use function combinations on resource-environment coupling across basin development gradients. This study introduced an analytical framework based on production-living-ecological functions to diagnose territorial spatial transitions along socio-environmental development gradients in the Dianchi Lake Basin. It further evaluated how these transitions influenced resource-environment coupling. The results revealed distinct transition trajectories across the gradients between 2000 and 2024. The core ecologically sensitive zone experienced ecological degradation followed by restoration, while the ecological-urban transition zone underwent sustained losses in ecological space. Both the optimized development zone and the peripheral control zone shifted from single-dominant to composite-dominant functions. The peripheral control zone exhibited the highest resource-environment coupling level, which improved consistently over time. Other zones displayed U-shaped coupling trajectories. Transitions towards composite dominant functions generally enhanced resource-environment coupling, particularly evident in the peripheral control zone. Conversely, reversion to single dominant functions significantly weakened coupling in most zones. These findings contribute to research on human-environment interactions by integrating a functional combination perspective into the analysis of complex spatial transitions. They also offer practical insights for differentiated territorial spatial governance in basin regions.

title: Carbon implied volatility and return volatility of EU emissions: Evidence from machine learning methods
abstract: In contrast to recent research that has primarily focused on predicting carbon price return volatility, the present study investigates whether the information content of a newly introduced carbon implied volatility (CVIX) index improves the forecasting accuracy of realized volatility in EU carbon returns. To this end, it uses data from September 7, 2013 to December 31, 2022, and employs Machine learning (ML) based shrinkage techniques, including the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), elastic net (ENET), and ridge regression (RR). In the process, Mean Absolute Percentage Error and Diebold-Mariano (DM) statistics are used to evaluate the forecasting performance of LM techniques relative to traditional linear models, such as autoregressive (AR) processes. The main results indicate that the CVIX index significantly improves volatility forecasts for EU market returns. All shrinkage methods outperform both baseline and extended AR models, and these findings remain robust when forecasting both good and bad volatilities. Therefore, the information content of carbon market implied volatility should not be ignored when forecasting return volatility of EU emissions. The results have important implications for investors and risk managers aiming to construct low-carbon portfolios with EU carbon assets and improve their forecasting models.

title: Systematic assessment and improvement for the intelligent municipal solid waste sorter
abstract: Efficient municipal solid waste (MSW) sorting helps MSW reuse but faces challenges in accurate detection and stable robotic gripping. Based on the previous study and the nine innovative sorting subindices proposed, this study enhanced the Intelligent MSW Sorting System (IMSWS) by innovatively integrating the state-of-the-art YOLO-based model, tracking algorithm, filter mechanisms, and a Suction end-effector equipped with a Vacuum Generator and a Sponge Lip (SVGSL). The results show that YOLOv11 outperformed the previous detection algorithms on dataset images and real-world sorting tests. The best detection algorithm, namely YOLOv11 combined with the ByteTrack tracker and the Identification (ID) Filter (YBTIF), could efficiently reduce ID switches of moving MSW in the actual sorting tests. Consequently, YBTIF obviously improved detection accuracy (DA) and gripping success (GS), with YBTIF achieving the highest sorting accuracy. The GS increased not only because of the use of SVGSL but also because of the improvement of DA. The MSW-ID filter performed better than the MSW-type filter. Overall, the IMSWS with YBTIF and SVGSL could achieve a high DA of 98.89 %, GS of 90.27 %, and SA of 92.22 %. In addition, the subindices could be further used to systematically identify the dominant factors and potential improvement directions for the enhanced IMSWS. However, some gripping failures remained due to the limitations of the SVGSL gripper and object shape factors like complex surfaces. Improving the gripper was identified as a key direction for further study.

title: Band structure-dependent performance of TiO2 and g-C3N4 in photocatalytic chlorine activation: A comparative efficiency–cost–risk assessment
abstract: Antibiotics contamination in aquatic systems necessitates development of cost-effective and scalable removal strategies. Photocatalytic chlorine activation (PCaCl), which synergistically couples photocatalysts with hypochlorous acid (HClO), has emerged as a promising alternative due to its robust performance, low cost compared to other oxidants (e.g., O3, H2O2, peroxymonosulfate), and inherent disinfection potential. However, the suitable catalysts for PCaCl process are poorly understand due to limited studies on the PCaCl process. Here, we systematically evaluated two solar amenable photocatalysts with contrasting band structure, “reductive” g-C3N4 (conductive band: −1.3 eV) and “oxidative” TiO2 (valence band: +2.7 eV), using trimethoprim as a target contaminant. TiO2 exhibited higher pseudo-first-order rate constant (0.889 min−1 vs. 0.658 min−1 for g-C3N4), attributed to its higher capability to generate •OH and ClO• radicals. It also generally showed better resilience in different pH, natural organic matter and ion concentrations. Interestingly, Cu2+ at ambient levels (0.01 mg/L) increased the degradation rate constant of the TiO2 system by 5.9 times. The electrical energy per order (EE/O) calculation revealed the cost advantage of TiO2 (0.275–0.749 vs. 0.323–1.13 kW h·m−3·order−1 for g-C3N4) in 11 different setups. Furthermore, the TiO2 system generated higher DBP concentrations, while the g-C3N4 system presented higher integrated cytotoxicity and genotoxicity. Despite the overall superior performance of TiO2, g-C3N4 demonstrated distinct advantages under visible light due to its narrower bandgap and stronger absorption within the solar spectrum. These features, combined with its robust ClO• generation tendency, made g-C3N4 a promising candidate for decentralized systems utilizing natural sunlight for treating electron-rich antibiotics. In the future, further performance comparison under real or simulated solar light could be a valuable focus.

title: Enhanced the recovery of micro-fine molybdenite via an alkyl xanthogenic based collector: synthesis, performance, and mechanism
abstract: To address the technical bottleneck of declining hydrophobicity in finely ground minerals that leads to low recovery of traditional hydrocarbon oil collectors, this study utilized computational simulations to design and synthesize a novel collector.
