(2) Both the traditional and the digital promotion strategies can significantly improve catastrophe avoidance behavior when they are utilized concurrently, with digital strategies exhibiting a stronger marginal effect. (3) The two extension methods have a substitution effect on farmers' disaster preparedness behavior, indicating that farmers' reliance on one type of promotion method will weaken the behavioral promoting effect of the other type. Therefore, to further strengthen the effectiveness of disaster prevention and management, this paper proposes to optimize traditional disaster prevention publicity strategies, advocate farmers to adopt digital learning approaches, and build an interactive online and offline disaster prevention knowledge dissemination system.

title: Quantifying transboundary ecosystem services flows to inform ecological compensation in the China-Indochina Peninsula Economic Corridor
abstract: Transboundary sustainability challenges increasingly require integrated evaluations of ecosystem service (ES) interdependencies to support equitable and efficient resource governance. Yet, current frameworks remain constrained by static, local-scale accounting, overlooking the tele-coupled dynamics of cross-border flows in rapidly integrating economic zones. Bridging this gap, we propose a novel methodology that couples the spatial quantification of biophysical flows with socio-economic valuation. We analyze the tele-coupled flows of four critical ES—food, freshwater, carbon sequestration and recreation—across the China-Indochina Peninsula Economic Corridor (CIPEC). Our approach transcends conventional mapping by monetizing these flows, thereby establishing a rigorous foundation for transnational ecological compensation (EC). We reveal significant spatial mismatches between ES supply and demand among participating nations. The results show that Myanmar, endowed with abundant natural resources, acts as the primary ES supplier in the CIPEC, with a total surplus valued at USD$20.31 billion, whereas Thailand is a main beneficiary, facing deficits in freshwater and carbon sequestration services valued at USD$1.20 billion and USD$20.00 billion, respectively. The strongest tele-coupling effects were observed for recreational and food services between Singapore and Malaysia (79.68% and 48.76%, respectively), and for freshwater and carbon sequestration between Yunnan Province, China and Myanmar (18.14%), and Myanmar and Thailand (33.17%). These findings provide a strategic tool for shifting from siloed national management to cooperative regional governance, offering precise quantitative evidence to design equitable cross-border payment schemes. Ultimately, this study contributes to cleaner production strategies by elucidating how optimizing transboundary resource allocation can align environmental liabilities with entitlements, thereby enhancing regional resilience and socio-ecological sustainability.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution of trade-off/synergy relationships and bundles in ecosystem services in Fujian, China: An integrated PLUS-InVEST-SOM framework
abstract: Coastal regions in developing economies increasingly face trade-offs between ecosystem services (ESs) provision and urban expansion, while scenario-based projections of ESs remain limited. This study integrated the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS), Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST), and machine-learning approaches to quantify five ESs—water yield (WY), soil retention (SEC), carbon storage (CS), habitat quality (HQ), and phosphorus emission (PE)—under natural development (ND), economic development (ED), and ecological protection (EP) scenarios in Fujian, China, during 2030–2060. Key findings are as follows: (1) Model validation demonstrated high predictive accuracy (Kappa = 0.86; Figure of Merit = 0.40). ND and ED scenarios resulted in approximately 7.5% forest loss, whereas the EP scenario preserved 99.17% of existing forest cover. (2) Temporal analysis revealed divergent ESs dynamics: CS and HQ decreased by 2.4% and 4.4%, respectively, while WY, SEC, and PE increased concurrently with urban expansion. Conversely, the EP scenario exhibited marginal increases in WY (0.03%), SEC (0.01%), and CS (0.71%), while PE and HQ remained stable. Spatial correlation analysis identified seven synergistic relationships among WY, SEC, HQ, and CS, and three trade-off relationships involving PE. (3) Ecosystem service bundles (ESBs) were classified into four distinct types. ND and ED scenarios substantially restructured ESBs, whereas the EP scenario maintained structural stability and high service diversity. (4) ESBs under the ND and ED scenarios exhibited alternating dominance of climatic, topographic, and socio-economic drivers, whereas the EP scenario fostered stable ESBs configurations through topography–climate synergies. Overall, this study provides robust scientific support for cross-scale governance aimed at achieving regional ecological–economic equilibrium.

title: Research on the spatio-temporal evolution and influencing factors of the coupling coordination among climate risk, new energy resilience and economic growth
abstract: Driven by China's dual objectives of green economic transformation and carbon neutrality, investigating the synergistic relationship among climate risk, new energy resilience, and economic growth holds significant strategic importance. Taking 30 Chinese provinces as the research subjects, this study constructs a three-dimensional system evaluation index framework for "climate risk – new energy resilience – economic growth". By comprehensively applying the coupling coordination degree model, spatial autocorrelation model, and Beta regression model, it reveals the spatio-temporal evolution patterns and influencing factors of the three-dimensional system's coupling coordination degree from 2011 to 2023. Findings indicate: (1) The coupling coordination degree of the three-dimensional system across the 30 provinces first declined before fluctuating upwards during the study period; (2) The spatial pattern exhibited a "higher in the east, lower in the west" distribution. Over time, regions with high coupling coordination gradually expanded from eastern provinces like Guangdong and Jiangsu towards central and western provinces such as Xinjiang and Qinghai, with the three-dimensional system demonstrating significant positive spatial correlation; (3) Beta regression model results indicate that climate policy uncertainty exerts a significant negative impact on the development of three-dimensional system coupling coordination, while the level of new energy infrastructure development exerts a significant positive impact. Policy recommendations are proposed based on these findings to accelerate the sound coordinated development of the three-dimensional system.

title: Aluminum-doped carbon anodes derived from denim waste for high-performance microbial fuel cells: Electrochemical enhancement and life-cycle sustainability
abstract: This study proposes a cleaner production pathway for simultaneous wastewater treatment and energy recovery by converting denim textile waste into high-performance anodes for microbial fuel cells (MFCs). Waste cloth was coated with carboxymethyl cellulose, cross-linked with aluminum sulfate, and subsequently carbonized to produce a three-dimensional aluminum-doped carbon anode. In this approach, aluminum ions serve as both a carbonization catalyst and a biocompatible dopant, enhancing the development of graphitic structure, surface area, and electrical conductivity without adversely affecting electroactive microorganisms. The optimized anode carbonized at 800 °C exhibited a high specific surface area of 539 m2 g−1 and promoted effective biofilm formation and extracellular electron transfer. When deployed in single-chamber MFCs treating sugarcane wastewater, this anode achieved an open-circuit voltage of 760 ± 8.6 mV and a maximum power density of 1174 ± 9.8 mW m−2, corresponding to a 5.4-fold increase relative to commercial carbon felt. Improved electrochemical performance was coupled with enhanced wastewater treatment efficiency, achieving 65% chemical oxygen demand and 74% biochemical oxygen demand removal. Life cycle assessment, conducted using a functional unit of 1 Wh of electricity generated, revealed substantially lower environmental impacts across climate change, human toxicity, ecotoxicity, and resource depletion categories compared with conventional carbon felt anodes. By integrating textile waste valorization, energy-efficient electrode fabrication, and bio-electrochemical wastewater treatment, this work demonstrates a scalable, easy-to-design, and environmentally favorable route toward cleaner energy and circular resource management.

title: Dynamic distribution of heavy metal fractions in European soils during 2009–2018: spatiotemporal modeling
abstract: Soils in the European Union (EU) are widely contaminated with heavy metals (HMs) due to intensified industrial and agricultural activities. Although the EU has released maps of total concentrations for 11 soil HMs, comprehensive knowledge of HM fractions is essential for accurate risk assessment. In this study, we compiled global database encompassing 27,756 data points from 199 studies on HMs. After systematic data processing and model hyperparameter tuning, the established optimized extra tree model achieved an R2 of 0.81 on the test dataset. The spatiotemporal distribution of the exchangeable fraction of the six prevalent HMs across the EU in 2009, 2015, and 2018 (0.05° resolution) was mapped using this extra tree model. Chromium (Cr) exhibited the highest percentage of the exchangeable fraction among the six HMs, averaging 27.57% in the three investigated years. From 2009 to 2018, the exchangeable fraction of Cr fluctuated, with an initial decrease and a subsequent increase, which was primarily due to changes in soil properties. To quantify the effects of HMs on crops, a normalized HM risk indicator was defined using HM content, the percentage of the exchangeable fraction, and crop yield. Using this indicator, the potential influence of Cr on wheat was assessed as a case study, revealing a persistently high risk around central Europe. Our model effectively elucidated the dynamic trends of HM fractions and quantified the associated risks to crops. These results provide critical insights into risk assessment, thus supporting targeted governance strategies and informing rational crop distribution planning.

title: Multifunctional interfacial material for integrated energy-carbon-cost optimization in unconventional petroleum development: A techno-economic-environmental analysis
abstract: Unconventional petroleum development faces a critical challenge in balancing energy output, carbon emissions, and economic viability. This study introduces a novel multifunctional interfacial material that integrates the roles of multiple chemical agents (demulsification, viscosity reduction, corrosion inhibition, and displacement enhancement) into a single molecular architecture. We develop a dynamic techno-economic-environmental model that simulates the full upstream supply chain from extraction to refinery intake, using oil sands bitumen as a case study. The model translates material performance into process variables, enabling a system-level assessment of energy use, carbon emissions, and operational costs. Compared to conventional water and chemical flooding, the multifunctional material reduces energy consumption by 65.7% and 50.7%, carbon emissions by 56.9% and 38.1%, and costs by 19.2% and 10.2%, while increasing oil production by 31% and 12%, respectively. These results demonstrate that molecularly integrated materials can effectively reconcile the energy-carbon-economics trilemma, offering a scalable pathway toward low-carbon and cost-effective unconventional resource development.

title: A novel biopolyurethane foam synthesized from Pterocarya stenoptera seed oil and polyethylene glycol and its efficient application for oil-water separation
abstract: Polyurethane foam (PUF) is widely used across industrial sectors due to its lightweight structure and tunable mechanical properties; however, its conventional synthesis depends heavily on petroleum-based polyols. Developing renewable and sustainable polyols is therefore essential for advancing green polyurethane technology. Herein, we report a novel biopolyurethane foam (POPUF) synthesized from Pterocarya stenoptera seed oil via a thiol-ene photo-click reaction. The P. stenoptera seed oil polyol (POP) exhibited a hydroxyl value of 119 mg KOH·g−1 under optimized conditions (12 h reaction time, 4:1 M ratio of mercaptoethanol to C=C). Substitution of polyethylene glycol 400 (PEG-400) with POP yielded foams with adjustable pore morphology and improved physicochemical performance. At 15 wt% POP addition, POPUF displayed a reduced pore size (172 ± 30 μm), increased density (138.6 kg m−3), and higher water uptake (4.20 g g−1). Thermal analyses confirmed enhanced crosslinking, greater ester content, and increased soft-segment flexibility, contributing to superior thermal stability. TiO2 nanoparticles and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) were sequentially deposited onto POPUF to impart selective wettability for separation applications. The modified foam demonstrated rapid adsorption kinetics (<30 s), solvent uptakes up to 21.45 g g−1, excellent recyclability (>94% retention after 20 cycles), and outstanding oil-water separation efficiency (>98.3% under static and gravity-driven conditions). This study demonstrates an efficient and sustainable approach for converting underutilized seed oil into a high-performance bio-based polyurethane foam, offering a promising pathway toward renewable polymeric materials for environmental and separation applications.

title: Developing an ‘evolution’ understanding of the multi-level alignment in regional sustainability transition: insight from Baotou, China
abstract: Existing studies have acknowledged that alignment among multilevel (landscape, regime, and niche) elements is crucial for regional sustainability transitions. Through examining the PV (photovoltaic)-led transition in Baotou, China, this research demonstrates that multilevel alignment is operated through the evolution of a regime underpinned by agency-structure interplay. Herein, the regime of a region functions as a selective mechanism that enters a path-creation status to develop new functions, through promoting agencies for developing and diffusing niches, thereby adapting to emerging landscape dynamics. Following this line, this research further reveals that the local state plays a key role in shaping the agency-selective mechanism by performing place-based leadership to orchestrate and align different stakeholders into collective agencies. These findings provide a new explanation, based on agency-structure interplay, of the dynamism regime in transition studies beyond previous structure- and actor-oriented perspectives, as well as enlarge existing knowledge of the hybrid actor played by the local state in shaping transition pathways.

title: Varying weight aggregation framework for assessing the perceived digital-supported resilience in EV-LIB Supply Chain Concerning Dual Reference Points
abstract: In the booming age of electric vehicles (EV), a stable and robust lithium-ion battery (LIB) supply chain is vital for electric vehicle manufacturers (EVM) to maintain consistent production. To enhance the resilience of the EV-LIB supply chains, many EVMs are implementing digital transformation, which can help them to realize digital operation functions, such as supplier’s dynamic evaluation, real-time production monitoring and adjustment, automatic inventory optimization, and precise sales prediction. To accurately evaluate the digital-supported resilience (DSR) of the EV-LIB supply chain, dual reference points are considered in EVM’s perceived DSR as benchmarks, such as the main competitor’s and industrial service resilience levels. This study provides a novel aggregation method concerning dual reference points with varying dominance to assess EVM’s perceived DSR. In particular, the definition of DSR and the set of potential appraisal indicators are introduced. The standardization process for calculating DSR is proposed according to different quality characteristics. Additionally, the psychological perceptions induced by external reference points are calculated according to prospect theory, in which EVM’s optimistic preferences on reference points are explored. Furthermore, varying weighting methods related to the changing optimistic preferences are designed to describe EVM’s dynamic attitudes on external reference points. Finally, the case of a digital supply chain is conducted to demonstrate its feasibility and effectiveness, in which the dominance of external reference points is dynamically varying. Research conclusions of the study can assist the EVM in selecting resilience KPIs, choosing suitable innovation modes, determining proper benchmarks, and confirming the dynamical dominance of external references.

title: Transformation of organic matter in swine wastewater treatment via an artificially enhanced stratification system
abstract: In this study, a full-scale artificially enhanced stratification system (AESS), composed of horizontal and vertical units constructed from inexpensive, readily available industrial materials, was applied for swine wastewater treatment at an intensive pig farm (∼5000 finishers) in Guang'an, Sichuan, China. Operating at HRT 163 days and OLR 0.2 kg COD/m3·day, the AESS achieved average removal efficiencies of 98.8 ± 1.3% for COD, 99.5 ± 0.8% for SS, 98.3 ± 1.7% for TN, 98.6 ± 1.7% for NH3–N, and 98.4 ± 1.7% for TP over nine months. Despite 97.3% DOC removal, high influent COD (7256–88,081 mg/L) left substantial residual DOM. To investigate the potential transformation mechanism, we employed Excitation-Emission Matrix Parallel Factor (EEM-PARAFAC) to monitor the compositional and fluorescent characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) across key process stages (CK, T2, T4) and at various vertical depths (surface, middle, bottom) in Treatment Pool-2. The results demonstrated that the treatment process preferentially removed protein-like components, while microbial activity led to the accumulation of humic-like substances and a significant increase in humification. Vertical profiling revealed that the bottom layer served as a sink for stable humus, in contrast to the surface layer. Seasonal observations further indicated that summer conditions promoted the production of fresh organic matter, whereas winter conditions enhanced humus stability. Collectively, this multi-angle analysis confirms that the AESS achieves efficient removal and transformation by immobilizing DOM within its layered artificial structure. These findings provide a foundation for the technology and present a scalable, carbon-neutral framework for the treatment of intensive livestock wastewater.

title: Fabricating polyphosphonic acid-based ion exchanger with spatially symmetric structure for efficient removal of uranium
abstract: Effective elimination of uranium (VI) from wastewater is critical to environmental remediation. Herein, a novel polyphosphonic acid-based ion exchanger PDVA/SiO2 with spatially symmetric structure was designed and fabricated, and its adsorption behavior towards uranium in pH 4 solution was investigated at both mg/L and μg/L concentration levels using batch and column experiments respectively. The adsorbent could rapidly recognize and complex with uranium and reach adsorption equilibrium within 5 min, with the adsorption efficiencies of uranium in pure water, tap water, lake water and seawater were about 99.9%, 98.7%, 96.5% and 71.5% respectively. Uranium could be consistently and efficiently removed using a column separation device, with the concentrations in the purified solution less than 30 μg/L. The adsorption mechanism was dominated by ion exchange between UO22+ and H+ (in P–OH). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrated that the complex formed by the phosphate group with bi-deprotonated binding to UO22+ possessed higher stability, and the binding process was accompanied by charge transfer and energy reduction.

title: Differentiated carbon emission patterns and multi-scenario low carbon transition pathways of classified Chinese cities
abstract: Cities are facing highly heterogeneous low-carbon transformation pressures. However, existing studies often classify cities using territorial emissions or traditional socio-economic indicators, ignoring the role of cities in intercity supply chains and providing limited support for differentiated pathways. This study establishes a city classification that jointly reflects the carbon responsibility externality and internal mitigation capacity by combining cities' positions in the carbon transfer network with their economic structures. We use the self-organizing map and K-means clustering for classification and then apply a unified analysis framework, including emission phases identification, Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index decomposition based on production and consumption, and multi-scenario pathway projections. The results show that 55% of Low-Carbon Leading Hub Cities are still in the growing carbon emissions phase. Traditional Carbon-Supporting Cities and High-Carbon-Resource Output Cities have higher carbon intensity and energy intensity and only 14.58% of the latter show a decreasing emission trend. 49% of emissions of the wealthiest cities are generated from outsourced production, generating 21%-25% of value-added for less affluent cities. In Low-Carbon Leading Hub Cities, industrial structure and energy efficiency effectively offset the emission growth from consumption. The carbon reduction potential of High-Carbon-Resource Output Cities can offset 30% of Low-Carbon Leading Hub Cities’ consumption-related emissions. Traditional Carbon-Supporting Cities face stronger emission growth pressure, with carbon peaking delayed to after 2035 in the high-carbon scenario. This study provides theoretical and practical insights for low-carbon urban development and differentiated carbon peaking strategies.

title: Synthesis and application of a novel selective detoxification agent to enhance cellulosic ethanol production
abstract: Environmental pollution and energy crises have accelerated the development of rice straw-based cellulosic ethanol. However, ferulic acid (FA) which predominantly acts as a fermentation inhibitor produced by alkaline pretreatment processes of rice straw feedstock may substantially compromise bioethanol production efficiency. In this study, a novel molecularly imprinted adsorbent (AEPA250@MIPs) was synthesized using enzymatic hydrolysis residue as a matrix to selectively separate FA. Density Functional Theory (DFT) identified 2-MEA as the optimal functional monomer. AEPA250@MIPs exhibited excellent selective adsorption performance, with a distribution coefficient (Kd) exceeding 2.67 in competitive adsorption experiments, representing a significant improvement compared to conventional adsorbents. In simulated fermentation systems, AEPA250@MIPs achieves a 16.6% enhancement in ethanol production yield. Microporous diffusion, hydrogen bonding, and π-π interactions were identified as key mechanisms for selective adsorption. Compared to previous studies, AEPA250@MIPs achieved higher selectivity and reduced glucose loss. This work provides a promising solution to enhance alkaline hydrolysate detoxification and improves the efficiency of bioethanol production.

title: Magnetic biochar-immobilized enzymatic systems for bioremediation of penicillin G sodium in antibiotic-laden fermentation residues: Removal efficiency, degradation mechanism, and ecological safety
abstract: Developing an efficient method to remove the high concentration of residual penicillin G sodium (PGNa) from penicillin fermentation residue (PFR) is of great significance for safeguarding human and animal health. In this study, the scaled-up production of PGNa-degrading enzymes was achieved for the first time using a 5 L stirred-tank reactor, reaching an enzyme activity of 1288.09 U/mL. Comparison of different treatments including strain SQW1, biochar SAMB, free enzymes, and immobilized enzymes SAMB-E showed that SAMB-E exhibited the best PGNa removal performance, achieving a 98.72% removal rate within 120 min using only 0.1 g of immobilized enzymes. The biological effects of PGNa degradation intermediates were evaluated using the disk diffusion method and ECOSAR software, and the results indicated that these intermediates exhibited no significant antibacterial activity and generally low ecological toxicity. Metagenomic analysis further revealed that SAMB-E treatment increased microbial α-diversity while reducing the abundance of most high-risk antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs). In addition, LC–MS analysis demonstrated that PGNa was primarily degraded by immobilized enzymes through enzymatic hydrolysis followed by subsequent biotransformation reactions, ultimately yielding low-toxicity products. This study is the first to apply immobilized enzymes for the removal of PGNa from PFR, providing a novel, cost-effective, and highly efficient approach for mitigating PGNa contamination. The treated fermentation residue also shows great potential for high-value utilization of hazardous waste.

title: Effects of recycled rubber crumbs on the maintenance behavior of a new composite ballast bed
abstract: The huge number of waste rubber tires in existence can cause serious environmental pollution, and the recycling of discarded tires in ballast beds is of paramount importance. This is the first detailed investigation of tamping maintenance for a composite rubber-ballast bed, with the aim of mitigating tamping-induced damage and enhancing maintenance effects. A numerical model of a composite rubber–ballast bed model was established, and tamping maintenance was simulated. The effects of recycled rubber crumbs on the maintenance behaviors of composite rubber–ballast beds were studied with this model. The results indicated that adding rubber crumbs could substantially mitigate the mechanical response and improve the mechanical state of a composite rubber–ballast bed. Balancing the damage and maintenance effects caused by tamping, rubber crumb contents of 15% and 20% and a diameter of 20 mm were recommended. This research could greatly facilitate the application of recycled rubber tires in ballasted tracks.

title: Photocatalytic and antimicrobial efficacy of CO2 capture photocatalytic material for environmental applications
abstract: Urban air pollution and the high carbon footprint of construction materials pose significant environmental challenges. To address these issues, this study evaluates a novel TiO2-SiO2-based photocatalytic material that integrates CO2 capture via carbonation curing with advanced environmental purification. Distinct from conventional cementitious carriers where natural carbonation often induces pore blockage and activity loss, TSC utilizes controlled carbonation curing to permanently sequester CO2. This process constructively generates a stable, porous carbonate-silica matrix that ensures sustained reactant accessibility and efficient photocatalysis. Its NOx degradation performance was systematically optimized under varying gas flow rates, light intensities, and humidity levels. Model-based simulations for Hong Kong indicated a theoretical kinetic potential for NOx removal reaching 100% under peak UV conditions. While demonstrating robust climate adaptability, these results reflect a kinetic overcapacity relative to pollutant flux rather than absolute environmental clearance. Furthermore, TSC exhibited superior antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Chlorella, attributed to enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. By integrating carbon sequestration, air purification, and biofouling resistance, TSC emerges as a holistic, sustainable solution for resilient urban infrastructure.

title: Machine learning for imbalanced WWTP energy consumption data in China: A spatially informed resampling framework with region-specific driver analysis
abstract: Growing concerns over energy consumption in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) have highlighted the need for more accurate and reliable predictive tools. While machine learning offers promising solutions, its effectiveness is often limited by spatial imbalance in real-world WWTP operational data. To address this, we developed a spatially informed resampling framework using a Relative Local Deviation Weight (RLDW) function to guide sample selection, combined with Cross-Resampling Generalization Testing (CRGT) to evaluate model robustness across different resampling strategies. We applied this framework to operational data from 2256 WWTPs in China, testing multiple machine learning models under various resampling scenarios. Independent test-set evaluation demonstrated robust predictive performance (R2 = 0.9403; MSE = 0.0058), while five-fold cross-validation indicated high internal consistency of the optimal model (average R2 = 0.9974; MSE = 0.0039). CRGT further confirmed the robustness and generalization of this model across heterogeneous and imbalanced data. To explore regional heterogeneity, SHAP analysis was applied to WWTPs grouped by geographic region. Results indicate that the key drivers of energy consumption vary spatially: treatment capacity dominates in southern provinces, whereas influent BOD5 and TN exert greater influence in northern regions. By integrating spatial imbalance handling with region-specific interpretability, this study advances machine learning applications for energy-efficient wastewater management and provides actionable insights to inform regionally targeted environmental policies.

title: Stock liquidity and signaling sustainability in emerging markets: Voluntary ESG disclosure, firm valuation, and institutional investor participation
abstract: Sustainability disclosure is increasingly salient in emerging markets; however, it remains unclear how voluntary, firm-initiated ESG disclosure translates into stock market participation when reporting is not mandated, and material ESG risks are not fully reflected in market activity. We examine the association between firm-timed ESG disclosure and stock liquidity, conceptualized as turnover-based trading, in an advanced emerging market with concentrated ownership, minimal state presence, and a substantial institutional investor base. We combine fixed-effects panel models and robustness tests with a liquidity co-movement network approach that captures market-wide synchronization patterns. We find that disclosure is positively associated with liquidity, with ESG pillar-specific effects, stronger for E and G than for S, and more pronounced among lower price-to-book firms, consistent with higher informational frictions and the greater diagnostic value of verifiable content. Institutional ownership is positively associated with liquidity but does not robustly moderate the ESG disclosure–liquidity relationship, consistent with substitution through private information channels among sophisticated investors. Network evidence indicates tighter and more persistent liquidity co-movement among ESG disclosers, consistent with attention and comparability channels, while remaining compatible with alternative explanations, including common shocks, sectoral clustering, and index-related trading strategies. Our findings are best interpreted as market responses to disclosure activity in a voluntary regime, rather than as evidence of informational efficiency in sustainability fundamentals, underscoring the importance of credibility, verifiability, and comparability infrastructures for translating ESG communication into stock market participation. The study highlights critical boundary conditions for regulators, investors, and firms on the ESG disclosure-stock liquidity link.

title: Novel perspective on membrane fouling mitigation in pre-oxidation–ultrafiltration processes for surface water treatment: Unexpected role of isolated catalyst particles
abstract: Heterogeneous catalytic oxidation has been extensively adopted as a pre-treatment process for ultrafiltration (UF) in surface water treatment. However, whether spent catalysts require removal prior to UF following pre-oxidation remains a subject requiring meticulous consideration. This study systematically investigated membrane fouling behaviors and underlying mechanisms associated with natural organic matter (NOM) with varying compositions, both in the presence and absence of catalyst particles. Results showed that NOM complexes caused more severe fouling compared to single-component NOM. In the absence of catalyst particles, the accumulation of NOM on the membrane surface was primarily governed by permeation drag forces and adhesion forces. Conversely, when catalyst particles were present, particle-induced scouring forces and hydraulic shear forces became dominant, effectively impeding the approach of NOM towards the membrane surface. Consequently, the presence of catalyst particles significantly alleviated flux decay during UF of NOM complexes, reduced overall membrane fouling severity, and shifted the fouling mechanism from cake filtration to intermediate or standard blocking fouling. Furthermore, the extent of fouling mitigation was found to be positively correlated with the humic acid content within the NOM complexes, which is attributed to an increased repulsive energy barrier and reduced adhesive interaction between the NOM complexes and the membrane surface under higher humic acid concentrations. This study underscores the non-essential nature of removing catalyst particles prior to UF, providing guidance for design and optimization of UF-based water treatment processes.

title: Pre-curing time effect on carbon capacity and microscopic properties of paste backfill produced by alumina production solid wastes and its practical application
abstract: To address the urgent need for CO2 sequestration amid global warming, this study proposes a novel strategy for storing CO2 in goaf areas using tailings-cemented paste backfill (TCPB) derived from alumina production wastes. The influence of pre-curing time (1d, 1.5d, 2d, 3d and 4d) on the CO2 storage capacity and microscopic properties of TCPB was systematically investigated across three curing stages: initial pre-curing (Stage I), CO2 curing for 1d (Stage II), and subsequent conventional curing up to 28d (Stage III). Results indicated that CO2 uptake first increased and then decreased with prolonged pre-curing time, reaching a maximum of 3.14% at 2d. Specimens pre-cured for 2d achieved a compressive strength of 5.18 MPa after Stage III, meeting engineering backfilling requirements. TG-DTG analysis revealed that the total CaCO3 content in these specimens reached 10.68% and 12.65% after Stages II and III, respectively. XRD and FTIR analyses further demonstrated enhanced crystallinity of CaCO3 and a higher degree of silicate polymerization in samples pre-cured for 1∼2d. Microstructural observations confirmed the formation of acicular aragonite and well-crystallized calcite, along with a moderately developed pore structure that facilitated CO2 participation in strength development. This study presents an integrated “backfilling-mining-CO2 storage” strategy, demonstrating that pre-curing TCPB in goaf for 2d enables the sequestration of approximately 708.49 kg of CO2 in a single 6 × 60 × 3 m3 goaf. The work provides a scientifically grounded and scalable dual solution for industrial solid-waste valorization and CO2 mineralization, offering a synergistic pathway towards systemic cleaner production that combines waste recycling, carbon management and safe mining practices.

title: Dynamic variation law and model construction of adsorption-induced deformation under low pressure: Implications for methane emission reduction from abandoned mines
abstract: Abandoned coal mines harbor considerable coalbed methane resources. Efficient utilization of these resources promotes energy recovery and mitigates methane emissions, supporting carbon peaking and carbon neutrality objectives. However, low extraction efficiency remains a major constraint on their utilization. Adsorption-induced coal deformation alters coal seam permeability, a critical factor for enhancing extraction efficiency in abandoned mines and reducing associated emissions. Moreover, these deformations are strongly affected by fluctuations in gas pressure within abandoned mine environments. Therefore, this study utilizes a custom-designed testing system to examine coal deformation and effective stress variations, aiming to investigate dynamic strain behavior during adsorption under varying gas pressures. In addition, numerical simulations were performed to establish a dynamic coal deformation model and to analyze its influence on permeability, with the results validated against engineering data. Results indicate that coal initially undergoes brief mechanical compression during adsorption, followed by rapid gas penetration and adsorption-induced swelling deformation. As gas pressure increases, both the magnitude and rate of expansion strain across different bedding planes first increase and then decrease. A critical pressure condition exists where strain magnitude and rate reach their maximum, leading to a rapid permeability increase. Coal deformation contributes to stabilizing daily gas extraction volume. At the gas pressure inducing maximum coal strain, permeability increases rapidly, thereby enhancing daily gas production. This provides new insights for improving gas extraction efficiency in abandoned mines and reducing methane emissions.

title: A data quality driven framework for developing a high resolution provincial LCA database of China's coal industry
abstract: Accurate and regionally representative life cycle assessment (LCA) data are crucial for reliable carbon accounting in energy-intensive sectors. However, developing regionalized LCA databases faces challenges due to heterogeneous data sources, inconsistent standards, and varying data quality, especially when reconciling bottom-up measurements with top-down statistics. This study develops a high-resolution, provincial-level LCA database for the Chinese coal industry and proposes a data quality–driven integration framework to address these issues. A Data Quality Rating–Weighted Fuzzy Logic Model (DQR–WFLM) framework is introduced to support transparent data source prioritization and conditional integration under heterogeneous conditions. The framework incorporates data quality evaluation, allowing explicit decision rules for screening, prioritizing, and integrating multiple data sources. Methane emission factors (MEFs), characterized by spatial heterogeneity and discrepancies between data types, are used as a case study. Application across 23 coal-producing provinces reveals different data handling strategies, such as single-source prioritization and data fusion based on predefined quality criteria. Conditional data fusion ensures internally consistent and traceable MEFs. Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis shows that fused data exhibit lower variance than bottom-up or top-down data alone, confirming the framework's effectiveness. The resulting provincial coal LCA database, comprising 1473 datasets, preserves regional heterogeneity while ensuring transparency in uncertainty propagation. Application to thermal power generation demonstrates that using provincialized data improves the robustness and interpretability of carbon footprint results. The proposed framework offers a transferable methodology for developing regionalized LCA databases in sectors with significant spatial variability.

title: Droughts, floods, and grain yield: Exploring the association between well-facilitated farmland and disaster-resistant capacity in China
abstract: This study investigates whether and how well-facilitated farmland (WFF) construction enhances the disaster-resistant capacity of grain production (DRCG) in China. In the context of intensifying global drought and flood impacts, understanding how agricultural infrastructure contributes to disaster-resistant capacity is essential for global food security. This study adopts the super-efficiency SBM model to evaluate the climate adaptability of grain systems in various provinces of China from 2011 to 2023, identifies the marginal effects of WFF construction by double machine learning method, and tests its regional evolution trend by β absolute convergence model, thus systematically explaining the internal logic of the continuous growth of China's grain output. It is found that the DRCG has shown a significant overall improvement, the average level reached 0.484 in 2023, representing an increase of 30% from 2011. The WFF construction is positively associated with the improvement of DRCG, and shows a stronger marginal effect in non-main producing areas, which indicates that the construction strategy oriented by “targeted infrastructure enhancement” has played a key role in enhancing the climate adaptability of grain systems in vulnerable areas. However, it is worth noting that the contribution of WFF construction diminishes over time, so it is important to pay attention to the necessary maintenance and upkeep of the facilities after construction. Meanwhile, the analysis of 31 provinces in China reveals a β absolute convergence trend in disaster-resistant capacity, indicating that regions with initially lower capacity are gradually narrowing the gap with those having higher capacity, thereby forming a pattern of coordinated development. This study provides other regions vulnerable to drought and flood impacts with China's practical experience, offering insights on enhancing disaster-resistant capacity through infrastructure development.

title: Enhancement mechanisms of bio-promoter on denitrification system against flow fluctuations: metabolic regulation, antioxidant defense and microbial community reconstruction
abstract: The fluctuating characteristics of rural water volume pose challenges for rural sewage systems, making the denitrification process vulnerable to be inhibited by hydraulic retention time (HRT) fluctuations. This study applied a bio-promoter coupled with multiple components (L-cysteine, biotin, and cytokinin) to the denitrification system, improving its resilience to HRT fluctuations ranging from 50% to 500% of the control value. Compared with natural recovery, the bio-promoter accelerated performance recovery by 53.84% and 22.56% under shortened (50% HRT) and prolonged (500% HRT) conditions. Bio-promoter enhanced the carbon metabolism by stimulating the tricarboxylic acid cycle (ACS, SDH, MDH, etc.), providing sufficient electrons for the electron transfer chain. With the increased contents of electron carriers (NADH, FMN, FAD, and Cyt c), the electron transfer system activity increased by 15.16%∼23.53%. Ultimately, the denitrifying enzyme gained sufficient electrons to reduce NO3−-N under the HRT fluctuations. Bio-promoter activated the antioxidant stress system, reducing oxidative stress by 14.13%∼35.39%, repairing cell damage caused by HRT fluctuations. Furthermore, the bio-promoter directionally enriched electroactive species (Fusibacter and Erysipelothrix) and antioxidant stress species (Hydrogenophaga), enhancing the robustness of the denitrification system. Through the synergistic effects of metabolic regulation, antioxidant defense and microbial community reconstruction, the resilience of the denitrification system to HRT fluctuations was enhanced. This research provided an efficient solution for wastewater treatment facilities facing flow fluctuations.

title: Uncovering the impact of trade-related lithium supply risks on China's power system decarbonization
abstract: Growing dependence on critical minerals sourced through international trade has introduced new vulnerabilities to power system decarbonization. For countries with limited domestic resources, trade-related supply disruptions and price volatility can directly affect the deployment of clean energy technologies. China, as the world’s largest renewable energy market and a major importer of lithium, is increasingly exposed to such risks. However, existing studies rarely quantify how trade-related mineral supply risks shape power system transitions under dynamic market and price responses. This study develops an integrated framework that couples a System Dynamics model of the lithium market with a power system optimization model, enabling year-by-year feedback between mineral supply conditions, price adjustments, and clean technology deployment. Focusing on lithium as a critical input for energy storage, the framework is applied to China’s power system transition under rapid demand growth and import disruption scenarios. Results show that lithium demand from the power system could increase by 4.3-57.8 times between 2020 and 2060, placing substantial pressure on supply. Under supply-demand imbalances, lithium prices rise persistently from 2025, reaching up to five times the unconstrained level by 2050, leading to a 10.6% reduction in cumulative battery deployment and a 0.43% increase in total transition costs. Temporary import disruptions further amplify these effects, raising lithium prices by 5.8-29% and constraining storage deployment during critical expansion periods. These findings underscore the importance of explicitly incorporating trade-related mineral supply risks into long-term power system planning and demonstrate the framework’s applicability for analyzing energy transitions under international trade uncertainty.

title: Autothermal hydrogen production from wood biomass based on low-temperature alkaline glycerol pretreatment synergized with efficient heat storage media
abstract: Thermochemical conversion processes have pioneered a pathway for transforming waste biomass into hydrogen. However, its scalability was challenged by a reliance on external heat sources and the inherent limitations of the raw materials. In this paper, a novel method was proposed to improve the reaction characteristics of wood biomass by utilizing alkali and glycerol pretreatment systems. And a porous media reactor integrated with stainless steel theta rings and inert particles was designed to realize efficient heat recirculation and gas production. The results indicate that the addition of theta rings enhanced the combustion temperature and the hydrogen production was increased to 12.9%. With the solution of sodium hydroxide (3 w/w%) and glycerol (50 v/v%), the maximum hydrogen of 18.1% was obtained after 60 min water-bath treatment at 90 °C. The appropriate wood drying time optimized the reaction path for hydrogen generation, and the highest hydrogen selectivity (47.42%) was achieved when drying for 2 h. Moreover, the discrete structure of wood significantly affected the hydrogen production and combustion time. And the hydrogen mole fraction of the spherical structure was 223.21% higher than that of the filamentous structure. The corresponding results verified the feasibility of biomass hydrogen production technology, which provided a novel direction for the industrial application of biomass resources.

title: Co-treatment and resource utilization of stainless-steel pickling sludge and Zn-bearing dust via direct reduction by petroleum coke
abstract: Both Zn-bearing dust and stainless-steel pickling sludge, which are metallurgical solid wastes produced by ironmaking and steelmaking processes, contain valuable metals such as Zn, Fe, Ni, and Cr. The efficient recycling and utilization of these materials has always been a hot topic in the metallurgical industry. In this study, petroleum coke was introduced, as a new reducing agent, to substitute the traditional coal-based reductant used for co-treating and extracting valuable metals from stainless-steel pickling sludge and Zn-bearing dust via a carbothermic reduction. The optimal conditions and mechanisms of carbon-thermal reduction were investigated via thermodynamic analysis, carbon-thermal reduction via roasting experiments, and non-isothermal kinetics analysis. The results indicated that iron and chromium oxides were reduced at 680 and 730 °C, respectively, and they eventually melted or vaporized during the carbothermal reduction process. The optimal calcination temperature range was 1050–1200 °C. The experiments confirmed that co-processing significantly improved efficiency, with metallic Fe generated at 800 °C and metallization rate reaching 98.86 % when the ratio of stainless-steel pickling sludge to Zn-bearing dust was 3:7 at 1100 °C. Non-isothermal kinetic analysis indicated that the reaction occurred in four stages, and increasing the proportion of stainless-steel pickling sludge reduced the overall activation energy by 36–58 %. Further, changing the ratio altered the reduction mechanism, and the second stage conformed to the interface model when the ratio was 3:7.

title: Optimized scheduling of multiple integrated energy systems considering hydrogen energy transportation
abstract: Inland river corridors often exhibit abundant wind-solar resources, yet their utilization remains constrained by renewable uncertainty and fragmented hydrogen supply chain (HSC) planning across spatially distributed integrated energy system groups (IESGs). This study proposes a corridor-scale scheduling framework that explicitly couples the HSC, inland waterway traffic flow (IWTF), and IESGs by modeling hydrogen-fueled ships (HFS) as mobile hydrogen storage and transfer carriers. To capture realistic logistics-operation coupling, a wind-wave-aware ship energy consumption model (SECM) is developed to quantify route- and environment-dependent navigation energy demand, thereby linking route planning and hydrogen deliverability to system-level scheduling decisions. Building on this foundation, a renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H)-driven inter-IESG interaction model and an emission-constrained IWTF model are formulated to co-optimize hydrogen production, transport, and sharing across multiple IESGs. Wind conditions along shipping routes are characterized via a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)-based probabilistic prediction module, and the resulting large-scale problem is solved using an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based distributed algorithm that enhances scalability while preserving data privacy. Case studies under representative summer and winter conditions demonstrate improved renewable energy source (RES) utilization and operational performance. Moreover, an added economic assessment shows that the interconnected hydrogen-sharing mode reduces the aggregate cost of three IESGs by 3.95% compared with standalone operation on a typical winter day, primarily by reducing net electricity purchases and mitigating renewable curtailment losses. These results indicate that HFS-enabled hydrogen sharing can serve as a practical coordination mechanism for cleaner production and low-carbon, cross-regional renewable collaboration along inland river basins.

title: Multi-scenario urban territorial spatial development suitability evaluation and integrated zoning under different decision risks
abstract: Industrialization and urbanization have intensified pressures on resources and the ecological environment, making the evaluation of Territorial Spatial Development Suitability (TSDS) and research on integrated zoning imperative. Traditional TSDS evaluation adopts a singular methodology, neglecting decision-making risks and oversimplifying aggregation logic; existing Resource and Environmental Carrying Capacity (RECC) methods struggle to define relative carrying capacity advantages. Taking Changchun City as a case study, this research develops a TSDS evaluation method incorporating decision-making risks and establishes an Integrated Zoning of Territorial Spatial Development (IZTSD) method based on the comparative advantages of TSDS and RECC. The results indicate that the TSDS distribution varies significantly under seven decision scenarios. As the decision risk coefficient α increases from 0.0001 to 10000, the TSDS across Changchun shifts from the highest to the lowest, with enhanced ecological constraints. Under the scenario of balancing economic development and ecological protection, the areas classified as highly suitable, suitable, moderately suitable, slightly suitable, and unsuitable for development are 3211.32 km2 (13.01%), 2992.09 km2 (12.12%), 1648.39 km2 (6.68%), 349.7 km2 (1.42%), and 16485.68 km2 (66.78%), respectively. By synthesizing the TSDS and CARECC results under 3 distinct decision-making risk scenarios, 8 types of IZTSD were identified. Among these, Z1 exhibits the largest area across all three scenarios, exceeding 16000 km2. This method achieves the quantitative expression of decision-making risks and diverse aggregation logics of indicators, pioneering a novel pathway for the dynamic and precise evaluation of TSDS. This study provides critical insights into informing the spatial restructuring, sustainable growth, and territorial arrangement of urban areas.

title: Biodiversity disclosure and capital market pricing efficiency: Evidence from stock price synchronicity
abstract: The degradation of the natural environment and the loss of biodiversity are increasingly threatening the sustainability of human life. As key participants in economic activities, firms are facing growing expectations to contribute to biodiversity conservation. However, the capital market value of biodiversity-related disclosure has yet to receive adequate scholarly attention. In particular, whether biodiversity disclosure(BD) can effectively reduce stock price synchronicity(SYN) and improve pricing efficiency remains an open question. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2023, this study finds that BD significantly decreases SYN, suggesting enhanced pricing efficiency. These findings are robust to endogeneity and robustness checks, and additional analyses indicate that BD improves the information environment, by increasing analyst coverage and media attention and reducing information asymmetry, thereby enhancing market pricing efficiency. Heterogeneity tests show that the effect is more pronounced among firms located in national park areas, non-heavily polluting industries, and large-sized enterprises. This study highlights the potential role of voluntary environmental disclosure in enhancing capital market efficiency.

title: Increasing refractory dissolved organic carbon neutralizes the benefits of environmental investment for COD improvement in a plateau lake under ecological restoration processes
abstract: Chemical oxygen demand (COD) is a commonly used indicator for assessing water organic pollution. Despite effective control of external loads, COD concentrations persistently increase in many lakes, revealing a gap between the measured values and actual organic pollution. However, the mechanisms driving COD dynamics remain poorly understood. This study integrated trend tests, boosted regression tree modeling, pathway analysis, and dissolved organic matter (DOM) characterization to identify the dominant drivers of permanganate index (CODMn) and dichromate method (CODCr) in Lake Erhai, China. Based on trends in COD and key restoration efforts, the 23-year study period was divided into three stages (2001-2008, 2009-2014, and 2015-2023). CODMn exhibited a decrease-increase-increase trend, while CODCr followed an increase-decrease-increase pattern, ultimately leading to a net increase of 30.6% and 18.3% in lake-wide concentrations over the entire study period. Key drivers transformed from external pollution sources to internal processes, particularly the accumulation of algal-derived, autochthonous refractory dissolved organic carbon (RDOC). The internal process was amplified by prolonged water residence time (WRT) and elevated water temperature (WT), which explained up to 21.4% and 19.4%, respectively. Our bulk water chemical analysis showed that RDOC alone accounted for over 57% of the variance in CODMn and 46% in CODCr, confirming its central role. Additionally, the divergence between CODMn and CODCr was attributed to oxidative efficiencies, resulting in distinct sensitivities to DOM sources from allochthonous to autochthonous. Overall, our study demonstrates that COD in restored eutrophic lakes overestimates the actual organic pollution, limiting its utility as a management target. This study highlights the importance of the proposed stage-specific assessment framework, which focuses on the regulation of in-lake ecological processes that drive RDOC production, rather than solely on total COD reduction.

title: Resolving the industrial transfer sustainability paradox: The constraint-innovation dualism framework from China
abstract: The sustainability paradox of industrial transfer describes a complex scenario where regional restructuring may increase environmental pressure while simultaneously stimulating green innovation. This paradox reflects the tension between the pollution haven effect and the Porter hypothesis. Drawing on provincial panel data for China from 2005 to 2022, this study uses a two-way fixed effects model to evaluate the impacts of industrial transfer on carbon emission intensity and green innovation. Furthermore, the analysis incorporates evidence from South-South cooperation cases to enhance the external validity of the results. The empirical findings reveal a U-shaped relationship between industrial transfer and carbon emission intensity, and an inverted U-shaped relationship between industrial transfer and green innovation. These results indicate that pollution risks and innovation responses may coexist and evolve with the scale of industrial transfer. Based on these findings, the study proposes a “constraint and innovation” governance framework that integrates environmental threshold management with innovation incentives. The framework includes dynamic negative lists, a coordinated policy mix covering fiscal, financial, and talent measures, and cross-border accountability mechanisms. The study provides evidence-based guidance for promoting industrial–environmental coordination in China and offers transferable policy insights for emerging economies pursuing green transition.

title: Global sustainable fisheries: Linking scientific knowledge with policy and governance
abstract: Sustainable fisheries are fundamental to achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14 (SDG 14), yet the alignment between scientific research and fisheries governance remains fragmented. To elucidate the academic evolution and policy orientation within sustainable fisheries, this study follows the PRISMA guidelines to analyze 1700 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection published between 2001 and 2025. By integrating quantitative bibliometrics with qualitative text mining, we systematically review the field's research trajectories and intellectual hotspots. The findings reveal a steady but uneven expansion of the research field, with scientific outputs dominated by the natural sciences, such as marine biology, ecology, and environmental science, while social science perspectives on policy design, economic mechanisms, and institutional governance remain underrepresented. The United States, China, and Canada lead in publications, but international collaboration networks are extensive yet characterized by weak ties. Keywords analyses identify six major thematic clusters: fisheries management and governance, small-scale fisheries, climate adaptation, marine ecological management, species-level studies, and the use of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. Despite progress toward sustainability-oriented research, empirical and interdisciplinary frameworks connecting science with policy application remain limited. This study calls for more targeted financial support, stronger cross-disciplinary collaboration, more open data sharing, greater engagement from developing economies, and stronger link between scientific research and policy in the sustainable fisheries. By elucidating the global knowledge structure and governance gaps, this work provides an evidence-based foundation for integrating scientific insights into effective and equitable fisheries management.

title: Time–frequency collaborative multi-scale neural network for PEMFC performance degradation prediction and interval estimation under dynamic operating conditions
abstract: Data-driven methods have been proven effective for predicting PEMFC degradation, but most existing studies use only a single time-domain voltage signal and ignore the roles of multiple operating variables and frequency-domain information. Under dynamic load conditions, water management imbalance and membrane electrode aging jointly change the high-frequency ohmic characteristics and the mid–low-frequency mass transfer characteristics, causing the output voltage to exhibit a combination of low-frequency aging and high-frequency fluctuations. Therefore, a modeling approach that fuses multivariable and frequency-domain features is more consistent with the physical degradation mechanism of PEMFCs. This paper proposes a frequency-domain aware multi-scale network (FAMSNet) for performance degradation prediction under dynamic load cycling conditions. The model integrates fast fourier transform (FFT) and discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to perform multi-scale frequency decomposition of key time-domain signals, thereby extracting critical features across different frequency scales. These features are efficiently fused through two-dimensional convolution and an adaptive aggregation mechanism. To further enhance predictive capability and uncertainty modeling, a time–frequency hybrid loss function (TFHL) is designed, combining time-domain quantile loss with frequency-domain fourier loss to impose dual constraints on the model. Experimental results show that FAMSNet reduces the point prediction RMSE by 31.49%–48.86% on dynamic load cycling datasets while providing accurate prediction interval estimation. The proposed TFHL framework also achieves consistent improvements in prediction accuracy across multiple benchmark models. In addition, it demonstrates superior and stable performance in both benchmark comparisons and multi-step prediction tasks, maintaining an average RMSE between 0.0067 and 0.0073, outperforming existing mainstream approaches.

title: Quadripartite evolutionary game analysis of low carbon production strategy of offshore outsourcing under transnational cooperative supervision mechanism
abstract: To solve the delineation of responsibilities for low-carbon production under offshoring, an increasing number of supply chain members and supervisions have carried inter-governmental cooperation. This study proposes the low-carbon production mechanism of offshoring based on “cooperation between the two countries” and outsourcing “incentives”. A quadripartite evolutionary game model of contract manufacturer (CM), original equipment manufacturer (OEM), the government of the CM (GCM) and the government of the OEM (GOEM) is constructed. The stability of multi agent strategy and simulation experiments are analyzed. The result shows that only when the cost of rent-seeking, outsourcing fines, regulatory penalties and carbon taxes are greater than the limit threshold, can the optimal combination of low-carbon production of the outsourcing enterprises and strict supervision by the two governments be promoted. The evolution system of offshore outsourcing is more affected by the willingness of both parties to participate, and carbon tariff is a necessary policy, but the implementation effect is limited to unilateral low-carbon production, and the carbon tax has a better effect on the promotion of the four parties to achieve the ideal state. The incentive contract promotes the OEM to produce low-carbon products under a non-ideal state, and controls the inflow of products composed of ordinary components into the market to a certain extent. Regulatory penalties in inter-governmental contracts are more binding on the GCM than regulatory incentives.

title: A flexible methanol production process scheduled by carbon price fluctuation: Techno-economic and risk analysis
abstract: Carbon price fluctuations significantly affect the economics of methanol production. Conventional renewable and fossil fuel-based processes exhibit varied economic performance under different carbon prices and face economic risks when carbon prices fluctuate. This study proposes a carbon price-driven flexible process for methanol production. The system integrates green hydrogen production, carbon capture, methanol synthesis, and methane reforming, and dynamically switches between two operational modes: under higher carbon prices, it runs on renewable energy. However, under lower carbon prices, it operates based on fossil fuels. Monte Carlo simulations are conducted under three fluctuation amplitudes (10–20 $/t) and standard deviation levels (10 %–20 % of the mean). The results show the flexible process performs better in all scenarios. Compared to the purely renewable route, it achieves revenue advantages of 10.65 M$ and 11.21 M$ at carbon price fluctuations of 15 $/t and 20 $/t, respectively. Across different standard deviation levels, the advantage expands to 23.41–36.39 M$. The proposed process effectively improves both economic returns and risk resistance in methanol production.

title: How does mandatory climate change disclosure affect corporate social responsibility? Evidence from US-listed firms
abstract: With the issuance of Commission Guidance Regarding Disclosure Related to Climate Change as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a difference-in-differences model to examine the causal effect of mandatory climate change disclosure on corporate social responsibility performance. The results show that mandatory climate change disclosure significantly improves corporate social responsibility performance. In addition, we observe that the relationship between mandatory climate change disclosure and corporate social responsibility performance is stronger when firms are headquartered in Democratic states or with high institutional shareholders ownership. Finally, enhancing executive climate change attention is the channel through which mandatory climate change disclosure improves corporate social responsibility performance. This paper provides insights into the effectiveness of mandatory climate change disclosure in influencing corporate social responsibility and provides a theoretical basis for governments to promote corporate social responsibility governance through mandatory disclosure policy tools.

title: System-level modeling and parametric analysis of dibenzyl-toluene hydrogenation for liquid organic hydrogen carrier
abstract: Hydrogen energy is experiencing rapid commercialization and technological development, particularly in the advancement of hydrogen storage solutions. Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers (LOHCs) are pivotal in enabling scalable and efficient hydrogen trade. This study develops an advanced reactor model based on the Langmuir–Hinshelwood–Hougen–Watson (LHHW) kinetic framework to optimize the hydrogenation process of dibenzyltoluene (DBT), a representative LOHC. Unlike many system-level DBT hydrogenation models that rely on lumped kinetics, fixed conversions, or steady-state assumptions, the proposed model explicitly captures the hydrogenation pathway of key intermediates (H6-DBT and H12-DBT) and computes the reaction heat evolution in a time‐resolved manner. Building on these intermediate-resolved kinetics, we perform a system-level net specific energy consumption (SEC) analysis for both stand-alone and heat-integrated hydrogenation configurations, enabling consistent accounting of time-resolved reactor heat release and balance-of-plant electricity demands. The key novelty is the consistent coupling of (i) an intermediate-resolved LHHW reactor model with time-resolved heat release, (ii) a practical time-to-conversion criterion, and (iii) subsystem-level net SEC accounting in a unified Aspen Plus® framework. Parametric studies varying temperature, pressure, and hydrogen feed rate identify operating windows that minimize net SEC under the time-to-conversion constraint. Results show that thermal integration reduces the net system SEC by 1.01 kWh·kg−1·H2 relative to the non-integrated configuration at the feasible optimal condition. This research provides in-depth insights into in-reactor phenomena during DBT hydrogenation and compares system-level performance across different configurations. It offers operating-condition performance maps to support scale-up assessment and future translation to continuous reactor systems. These advancements contribute to the development of scalable, flexible LOHC-based hydrogen systems, thereby supporting the establishment of sustainable hydrogen supply chains.

title: Valorization of high-iron bauxite residue using low-temperature alkali beneficiation
abstract: Bauxite residue (BR) is a major environmental liability due to its high alkalinity and large-scale stockpiling. This patented study offers a low-temperature (60–160 °C) alkali beneficiation route for sustainable valorization of high-iron BR. Under optimized conditions (5 min milling, 120 min baking at 140 °C with a 0.75 g/g NaOH/BR ratio), the process achieves 81% alumina and 42% soda recovery while producing an iron-oxide-rich residue containing 63.5% Fe2O3. Phase evolution analysis shows that alumina recovery is governed by temperature-induced sodium aluminate formation, whereas soda recovery is controlled by extended leaching (60 min) to dissolve slow-reacting aluminosilicate phases. Selective alkali baking leaves sodium aluminosilicate as the sole Al-bearing phase in the leach residue, which is enriched in hematite, goethite, and Ti-bearing phases and exhibits a reduced soda content (3.5% to 2.7%). The optimized NaOH dosage and high true leaching efficiency of soda (96.7%) allow low reagent consumption and the use of leach residue as a 7–34% blending material in conventional ironmaking sinters. A preliminary techno-economic assessment indicates a positive operating margin of €14.1/t, with potential improvement to €117.6/t through reduced water consumption. Overall, the proposed low-emission process substantially lowers energy and reagent demand compared with conventional high-temperature routes and offers a scalable, circular pathway for converting hazardous BR into marketable alumina, soda ash, and iron-rich feedstocks.

title: Sustainable production-oriented systematic-dynamic assessment framework for integrated risks in China's energy internet
abstract: Amid global low-carbon transition and China's dual-carbon strategy advancement, the Energy Internet (EI), as a core platform for energy transformation, faces complex systemic risks due to cyber-physical integration, multi-energy coupling, and socio-environmental interactions, threatening its safe operation and sustainable production. Existing studies mostly focus on static assessment of single subsystems, lacking integrated analysis of multi-dimensional risk dynamic coupling. To address this gap, this study constructs a multi-dimensional risk assessment framework covering social-environmental, Cyber-Physical System (CPS), and Integrated Energy System (IES) dimensions, and establishes a dynamic coupling risk quantification model by combining System Dynamics (SD) with entropy weighting method. Validation based on Inner Mongolia's EI demonstration base shows that CPS risks and IES reliability are dominant, presenting an inverse bathtub curve trend, rising initially due to technical bottlenecks, then declining with technological progress and preventive maintenance, while social-environmental risks remain low and gradually decrease. This study uncovers the dynamic evolution mechanisms of coupled risks in EI, the findings provide actionable strategies with practical implications. The multi-dimensional dynamic assessment logic offers a China-oriented policy framework reference for global energy transition, especially for developing countries, bridging the gap between systemic risk theory and sustainable production practice.

title: New insights into divalent metal ions removal by sludge-derived porous carbon: Thermal evolution and synergistic adsorption at multi-active sites
abstract: Converting industrial solid wastes into efficient adsorbents for heavy metal ions via thermal processing represents a promising yet challenged strategy, often limited by low efficiency, complex mechanisms, and undefined inter-site interactions. Herein, a Ca/Al/Si-rich paper mill sludge (PS) was transformed into a multiple active sites-coordinated porous carbon (PSC850) via controlled high-temperature activation. Despite micropore collapse above 750 °C, high-temperature treatment promoted CaCO3 decomposition into reactive Ca(OH)2, CaS and exposed α-Al2O3/α-SiO2 phases, establishing a hierarchical adsorption mechanism dominated by chemical precipitation, ion exchange, and surface complexation. PSC850 achieved maximum adsorption capacities of 1063.0, 252.6, and 247.6 mg g−1 for Pb2+, Cu2+, and Cd2+ in single-ion systems, respectively, with near-complete removal across pH 3-6. In competitive multi-component systems, Pb2+ and Cu2+ retain high capacities (290.1 and 214.0 mg g−1), overcoming persistent limitations of site masking and pH limitations of conventional solid waste-derived adsorbents.

title: A green bio-cementation strategy based on microbially induced carbonate precipitation for preventing leachate leakage during the in-situ leaching of ionic rare earth ores
abstract: Lack of bedrock at the bottom of stopes can lead to leachate leakage during the in-situ leaching of ionic rare earth ores, resulting in the loss of rare earth resources and environmental pollution. To address these issues, this study utilized microorganisms to induce green bio-cement for solidifying the soil at the bottom of such stopes. We investigated the effects of the cementation solution (CS) concentration (0.5, 1.0, 1.5 mol/L) and the bacterial solution (BS) to CS injection frequency ratio (1:1, 1:2, 1:3) on the properties of bio-cemented samples. The analyzed properties included calcium carbonate (CaCO3) content, permeability coefficient, disintegration coefficient, hardened layer thickness, and microstructure. The results showed that microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) technology significantly enhanced the impermeability and structural stability of the rare earth ore samples. The permeability coefficient of the samples decreased continuously with increasing CS concentration and injection frequency. In contrast, the disintegration coefficient exhibited a trend of first decreasing and then increasing; while the CaCO3 content and hardened layer thickness showed a trend of first increasing and then decreasing. The optimal performance was achieved with a CS concentration of 1.0 mol/L and a BS:CS injection ratio of 1:2. Under these conditions, the CaCO3 content reached 18.28%, the permeability coefficient decreased by 99.32%, the hardened layer thickness was 39.59 mm, and the disintegration coefficient was only 5.1%. Analyses using scanning electron microscope-energy dispersive spectrometer (SEM-EDS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) revealed that the precipitated CaCO3 crystals effectively bridged adjacent rare earth particles and filled soil pores, with crystal sizes up to approximately 60 μm. This study confirms the feasibility of bio-cementation for sealing the base of ionic rare earth ore stopes, providing a novel strategy to prevent leachate leakage and mitigate environmental pollution. These findings offer valuable insights for promoting the green mining of ionic rare earths.

title: A “Quantification-zoning-driving factors” analysis framework for mitigating ecosystem service supply-demand mismatches in urbanized areas
abstract: Mitigating the mismatch between the ecosystem service (ES) supply and demand is crucial for urban sustainable development. However, existing mismatch quantification has rarely considered the spatial relationship between ES supply and demand, which is determined by diverse ES flows. In this study, we quantified ES supply-demand mismatches by incorporating ES flows, delineated management zones, and analyze mismatch driving factors. These three analytical components are interlinked and form an integrated framework for informing ES supply-demand mismatch mitigation. We took the Eastern New Area of Chengdu, China, as a case study, and focused on four typical ESs (soil retention, crop pollination, flood regulation, and natural recreation). We found that: (1) The four ES supply-demand mismatches demonstrated heterogeneous distributions, and the integration of ES flows enhanced the accuracy of mismatch quantification; (2) Four distinct ES supply-demand management zones were delineated. The flood regulation-natural recreation mismatch zone accounted for the largest proportion of area (32.68%), while the ES match zone accounted for the smallest (5.93%); (3) The direction and magnitude of socio-ecological factors’ influence on ES supply-demand mismatches varied across zones. Overall, the green space proportion alleviated most ES supply-demand mismatches, whereas the population density, construction land proportion, and road density exacerbated them. This study advances the quantification of ES supply-demand mismatches, and more importantly, offers a practical analysis framework for mitigating mismatches in urbanized areas.

title: Integrate green into manufacturing? The impact of green factory certification on corporate green technology convergence in China
abstract: China's Green Manufacturing plays a key role in advancing the green transformation of the manufacturing sector. This study investigates whether green manufacturing facilitates corporate green technology convergence (CGTC). Building on the calculation of CGTC levels and leveraging the green factory certification (GFC) as a quasi-natural experiment, we analyze the impact of the GFC on CGTC using a staggered difference-in-differences approach. The results reveal a significant positive relationship between the GFC and CGTC. Moreover, the attention of stakeholders such as media, investors, and downstream customers is a prominent impact path. Moderating effect test indicates that mandatory environmental regulation positively moderates the GFC’ impact in regions with low certification rates. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the GFC’ effect is more pronounced among firms with weaker reputations, lower financing constraints, higher cash rewards, and those exposure to dynamic certification adjustment. Finally, we reveal that firms may adopt strategic CGTC behaviors to address the periodic review. Furthermore, the GFC improves firms' ESG performance, particularly in environmental and governance dimensions.
