Overall, the optimal mix provides the best balance among printability, thermal insulation, and mechanical properties. These findings provide reference guidelines for developing low-carbon, energy-efficient 3DPC materials.

title: Mapping the global development likelihood of wastewater treatment plants using a novel positive-unlabeled deep neural network
abstract: Sustainable management of water and sanitation requires the constructions of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) to remove pollutants from wastewater. Information on potential areas where future WWTPs will be developed is useful to optimize implementations of WWTPs while minimizing the negative effects on environment and climate. The suitability analysis for WWTP siting can be framed as a binary classification task in machine learning, yet current inventory datasets only document confirmed locations of WWTPs (positive samples) and lack information on unsuitable locations for WWTPs (negative samples). To address the problem of binary classification without labeled negative samples, here we propose a novel positive-unlabeled deep neural network to model the global development likelihood of WWTPs using fourteen socioeconomic and geographic factors. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, recall, precision, and F1-score of the model are 0.9876, 0.8611, 0.7178, and 0.7822, respectively. The predicted potential area suitable for WWTPs is about 8,287,091 km2 globally, 51% of which is distributed in the United States, China, India, Russia, and Germany. Cropland, built-up area, tree, and rangeland account for 96% of the potential area. The derived global probability map of WWTPs can provide input for decision-makers to implement multi-objective optimization considering various sustainable development goals.

title: Quantifying methane emissions and assessing uncertainties in China's natural gas compressor stations
abstract: Methane is the world's second-largest greenhouse gas, and controlling its emissions can significantly mitigate climate warming. Natural gas compressor stations are among the most important methane emission sources along transmission pipelines. However, facility-level estimates for compressor stations can still be highly uncertain if some emission sources are missed or if intermittent, operation-related releases are not measured often enough to represent a full year. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework to quantify methane emissions from natural gas compressor stations, using China as a case study. A total of 7511 venting records and 12398 component-level leak test results were compiled from historical operating records and LDAR surveys using a FID, covering venting, fugitive leakage, and combustion-related emissions. Based on these data, methane emission factors and probability distribution models were developed for the three emission categories. Uncertainty in total methane emissions was quantified using Monte Carlo simulation. Sobol sensitivity analysis was applied to identify the key parameters driving emission variability and uncertainty. Results show that the average methane emission from Chinese compressor stations is 143.65 Mg/yr per station, with a 95 % CI of (79.84,263.33) Mg/yr, and venting accounts for 98 % of total emissions. The estimated facility-scale methane emissions differ from those reported in previous studies by 3.24 %–69.26 %. The findings provide evidence for developing a more accurate methane emission model for natural gas compressor stations in China.

title: Intelligent design routes for carbon-sequestration materials: A stacking machine learning-based predictive framework for compressive strength modeling of biochar-modified cementitious composites
abstract: The transition toward low-carbon and environmentally responsible construction materials has amplified the importance of biochar-modified cementitious composites (BMCC), which provide long-term carbon sequestration due to the stable retention of biogenic carbon. However, predicting the compressive strength (CS) of BMCC is challenging because mixture components—especially biochar-related properties—interact in nonlinear and non-monotonic ways. Such complex behavior limits the applicability of traditional empirical correlations and illustrates the importance of advanced artificial intelligence (AI)-based modeling. This paper develops an explainable AI-guided framework using four base learners and ten stacking machine-learning (ML) models to estimate the CS of BMCC based on a curated dataset of 482 instances compiled from 26 independent studies. Among the evaluated model configurations, the SM-8 stacking model, integrating Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Random Forest (RF), and Extra Trees Regressor (ETR) base learners, achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding superior test-phase performance with R = 0.972, R2 = 0.945, RMSE = 3.90, MAE = 2.68, and MAPE = 7.84%. Explainability analyses using SHAP and ICE identified age, w/c, cement, SP, and biochar characteristics as the dominant factors influencing CS, while also highlighting nonlinear relationships and optimum-performance regions for critical parameters. In addition, cradle-to-gate life-cycle carbon footprint and production cost indicators were quantified to support sustainability-oriented mixture assessment. To enhance practical accessibility, a user-friendly tool was developed, enabling real-time predictions, guided parameter ranges, model selection, and simultaneous reporting of environmental and economic indicators. Overall, the proposed explainable AI framework enables accurate BMCC mix optimization, supporting sustainable construction and practical engineering decision-making.

title: The carbon footprint of Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) production and consumption based on primary data
abstract: According to the European Green Deal proposed by the European Union, biofuels are seen as one of the potential solutions to reduce the carbon dioxide equivalent emissions of the transport sector. Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) is a biofuel with chemical properties similar to those of fossil diesel and can be used in existing diesel internal combustion engine vehicles, with commercially available examples such as HVOlution®. Primary data-based LCA studies of large-scale HVO refineries are rare. Based on the primary data provided by Enilive, the current paper analyzes the carbon footprint of the HVO production in two Italian biorefineries, Venice and Gela, and its use in European territory. The analysis is conducted using the process-based Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology. Used cooking oil (UCO), palm oil mill effluent (POME), animal fat, and castor oil are the 4 different feedstocks for HVO production. The study considers the processing and transport of the feedstocks. The carbon footprint of HVO produced in Venice and Gela refineries is in the range of 10.6–17.9 and 15.2–22.2 g CO2 eq./MJ, respectively, with the lower and upper range for the POME and castor oil pathways. For an average scenario, the carbon footprint of the life cycle of HVO distributed in France, Italy, and the Netherlands is in the range of 20.2 to 21.9 g CO2 eq./MJ (34.4 to 37.3 g CO2 eq./km). This represents a 75% reduction compared to commercial diesel, highlighting the significant potential of HVO to contribute to the decarbonization of the transportation sector. With future developments and the use of low-carbon hydrogen, even higher carbon footprint mitigation can be obtained.

title: Knowledge-embedded deep reinforcement learning for real-time dispatch of wind-solar-hydro hybrid generation systems
abstract: Amidst the global energy transition, high penetration of wind and solar power presents significant challenges to power system security and stability. While wind-solar-hydro hybrid generation systems (WSHHGS) offer integration benefits, their complex coupling characteristics and uncertainties limit traditional optimization methods' computational efficiency and safety. This study proposes a novel unit-level real-time dispatch method for WSHHGS based on knowledge-embedded deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The real-time dispatch problem is first mathematically formulated and modeled as a Markov decision process. Subsequently, a knowledge-embedded proximal policy optimization (KE-PPO) algorithm is proposed to determine optimal active power dispatch strategies for hydro units. The method incorporates expert dispatch prior knowledge via a supervised expert loss, leveraging behavior cloning to accelerate agent training. Meanwhile, safety constraint prior knowledge is embedded through safety rule discrimination, action correction, and a regularization loss to guide the agent away from unsafe operations, such as those within vibration zones. Case studies in the Beipan River, China, demonstrate KE-PPO's robust adaptability across varying operational scenarios. Results indicate significant improvements in DRL training efficiency, convergence speed, and action safety. Compared to PPO, deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), and genetic algorithm (GA), KE-PPO significantly reduces hydro unit water consumption (by 2.19%, 2.53%, and 1.13%, respectively). Furthermore, it effectively mitigates operation traversing vibration zones and reduces start-up/shut-down frequency.

title: Dynamic correction of E/C/γ parameters and construction of human health quantification system for air pollution damage assessment based on virtual governance cost method
abstract: Although the virtual governance cost method based on GB/T 39793.1-2020 is widely applied for air pollution damage assessment, it ignores human health economic losses, resulting in incomplete damage quantification. This study developed a comprehensive damage assessment system integrating optimized virtual governance costs (Dopt) and human health economic losses (Vhealth). For Dopt, key parameters were optimized: the pollutant quantity (E) was dynamically corrected via a turbulence diffusion-sedimentation model, showing deviation rates of 11.3% (SO2), 11.6% (NOx), and 13.2% (PM2.5) from static calculations; the unit governance cost (C) was optimized using a thermodynamics-based life cycle model, yielding 601 yuan/kg (PM2.5), 562 yuan/kg (SO2), and 677 yuan/kg (NOx), lower than traditional industry averages; the adjustment coefficient (γ) was revised to 0.756 by integrating multi-pollutant synergistic toxicity (weighted sum = 0.861) and dynamic degradation of soil cation exchange capacity (β = 0.879). Vhealth was quantified via a “pollutant exposure-health effect-economic transformation” chain, with a case study value of 13,180 yuan and a reasonable range of 65,000–130,000 yuan. Case verification showed the new system reduced the assessment deviation of the traditional method by 11.3-13.2%; the optimized virtual governance cost was 22,700 yuan, 40.4% lower than the traditional result (38,100 yuan). Additionally, the case's composite pollution index (CPI) reached 137.1%, 4.34 times the industry average, and the cumulative exceedance index (CEI) was 0.92, exceeding the level-III warning threshold. Vhealth accounted for 60-70% the total damage. This research fills the gap of single-dimensional assessment in traditional methods and provides a scientific basis for environmental policy optimization and corporate pollution control decisions.

title: Multiscale thermal response and hazardous hydrocarbon gas evolution during low-temperature coal oxidation in sealed fire zones
abstract: Low-temperature coal oxidation in sealed fire zones promotes heat accumulation, hydrocarbon gas emissions, and coal loss, posing challenges to resource efficiency, cleaner production, and sustainable coal mining. To clarify coal oxidation behavior and the stage-dependent evolution of hazardous hydrocarbon gases, low-temperature oxidation experiments under different oxygen concentrations were integrated with infrared spectroscopy, model compound analysis, and quantum chemical calculations. The results demonstrate that hydrocarbon gas generation exhibits distinct stage-dependent characteristics governed by the progressive activation of reactive functional groups and the evolution of the free-radical reaction system. CH4 is preferentially generated under all oxygen conditions, followed by C2H6 and C3H8, whereas C2H4 is mainly produced at elevated temperatures. Oxygen concentration significantly regulates the onset temperature and generation intensity of hydrocarbon gases by controlling functional group activation and radical reaction intensity. Mesoscopic and molecular analyses demonstrate that aliphatic side chains play a dominant role in heat release and hazardous hydrocarbon generation. In particular, long or branched side chains preferentially decompose into methyl and ethyl radicals, thereby amplifying early-stage gas emissions. Among all pathways, CH4 formation via hydrogen abstraction exhibits the lowest kinetic energy barrier, explaining its preferential and early release. Furthermore, methyl radicals are identified as the key intermediates governing hydrocarbon gas formation pathways, while radical coupling and disproportionation reactions drive the evolution toward higher-carbon unsaturated hydrocarbons at elevated temperatures. Overall, this study provides mechanistic insights that contribute to reducing coal loss, mitigating hazardous gas emissions, and supporting the implementation of cleaner and more sustainable coal mining practices.

title: Revealing wet-weather overflow pollution mechanisms of storm drains based on categorical boosting and Shapley additive explanations
abstract: Wet-weather overflow pollution deteriorates the water quality of receiving waters, and understanding its complicated mechanism is the prerequisite for proactive strategies for overflow pollution abatement. To address this, we developed an interpretable machine learning framework to predict pollutant concentrations in urban drainage systems. Using categorical boosting (CatBoost) and multi-source data from four stormwater systems in Shanghai, the model achieved MAE/RMSE values of 63.12/109.81 mg/L for chemical oxygen demand (COD) and 1.46/1.59 mg/L for ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N). Compared with gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), random forest (RF), and adaptive boosting (AdaBoost), CatBoost improved prediction accuracy by up to 60.4%. The Shapley additive explanations demonstrated that human-driven factors, notably illegal sewage discharge and elevated overflow peaks, were dominant in determining pollution levels. COD concentration was primarily driven by flow-related parameters and illegal inflows, while NH3-N levels were more sensitive to rainfall factors. These findings underscore the importance of targeted pollution control strategies, such as eliminating illegal connections and intelligently regulating stormwater pumps. Adopting smart stormwater systems with optimized control logic could significantly reduce wet-weather pollution and enhance resilience by effectively managing both organic and nitrogenous pollutants. The proposed comprehensive framework provides actionable insights for urban overflow management under changing climate and infrastructure conditions.

title: MoS2@Fe3O4 nanozyme redirects carbon to strengthen symbiotic nitrogen fixation in soybean for fertilizer-minimizing cleaner production
abstract: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF) can reduce synthetic nitrogen fertilizer use in legume-based systems, but its efficiency is constrained by source-sink imbalances and suboptimal carbon allocation. Here, we evaluate a foliar-applied MoS2@Fe3O4 heterostructured nanozyme, constructed by in situ coupling of MoS2@Fe3O4 nanoparticles to integrate Mo-centered cofactor support for nitrogen fixation with Fe-associated peroxidase-like redox catalysis, as a systems regulator of soybean C-N budgeting under low-N supply. The heterostructured nanozyme, exhibiting peroxidase-like activity, preferentially accumulates in leaves, thereby enhancing photosynthetic capacity (higher Vcmax and Jmax) and up-regulating key genes involved in photosynthesis and sucrose transport. Without increasing the total mineral N input, MoS2@Fe3O4 treatment reallocates sucrose from leaves to roots and nodules, strengthens nodule sink strength, and increases nitrogenase activity by 75.98% and grain yield by 60.32% relative to the water control. Metabolomics and gene expression show a coordinated metabolic reprogramming in nodules in which carbon-intensive flavonoid/jasmonic acid defence pathways are down-regulated, while purine-ureide metabolism, Mo-Moco-XDH signalling and antioxidant buffering are enhanced, supporting higher SNF and ureide export. These results demonstrate a nanozyme-enabled route to activate endogenous SNF rather than relying solely on external N inputs. From a cleaner-production perspective, strengthening biological N supply in soybean offers a promising lever to lower synthetic fertilizer demand and associated emissions, provided that future field trials and life-cycle assessments confirm agronomic, environmental and economic benefits.

title: Smarter brains, greener cities? Unveiling the spatial effects of computational power on sustainable development
abstract: As AI-driven data analytics and edge computing networks underpin urban sustainability transitions, understanding how computational power – the foundational prerequisite for the diffusion and operationalization of emerging technologies – affects sustainable development becomes crucial for informed urban policy. Building on a panel dataset of 235 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2023, this study develops a multi-dimensional computational power index and employs spatial econometric models to assess its direct and spatial spillover effects on sustainable development. Research findings indicate that computational power significantly enhances sustainable development. The positive effect exhibits spatial spillovers that extend beyond administrative boundaries and remain robust across alternative spatial matrices. Second, green total factor productivity moderates the relationship between computational power and sustainable development in a U-shaped manner. Third, the quantile analysis reveals that the catalytic effect of computational power on sustainability intensifies after threshold crossings. This study contributes to the literature by unveiling the distinct role of computational power in shaping urban sustainable development through its direct, spatial, and heterogeneous effects. Policy insights are generated for countries seeking digital-led sustainability transitions.

title: Prediction and optimization of light transmission to enhance microalgae growth in built-in light sources photobioreactor for efficient CO2 fixation
abstract: Artificial supplementary lighting can resolve the instability of CO2 fixation efficiency by microalgae. The influence of light source arrangement on light distribution and microalgae growth remains unclear. This study specifically targets built-in light sources photobioreactors (PBRs), where photosynthetic efficiency heavily depends on light distribution. In this study, a spatial light attenuation model was constructed based on light spatial divergence characteristics to predict light distribution. Expanding the light-emitting area from 0.02 m2 to 0.65 m2 enhanced light distribution uniformity by 93.42%. It achieved a maximum CO2 fixation rate of 1.44 g-CO2/L/day. This rate was 1.58-fold higher than the initial rate (0.912 g-CO2/L/day). Discretizing a single large light-emitting area into 16 smaller light sources expanded lighting coverage by 1.86-fold and increased the microalgal maximum specific growth rate by 28.10%. Increasing the dispersion degree of light sources was more effective for promoting microalgae growth than increasing light intensity. Under the same light-emitting area, doubling the number of light sources achieved a 55.1% increase in biomass productivity. The light energy utilization efficiency was increased to 18.66%, and the total investment cost was reduced to 8.72 $/kg. This model provides a quantitative basis for designing energy-efficient industrial-scale PBRs and may contribute to improving the economic feasibility of low-value microalgal products.

title: Multiphysics simulation of microwave drying process of excavated soil for resource recycling: Optimization toward enhanced drying efficiency and reduced energy consumption
abstract: Excavated soil (ES), a major by-product of urban construction, poses significant disposal challenges but also offers potential as a recyclable raw material. Employing the dispersive dry-sieving method to extract sand from ES for subsequent use in construction projects represents a promising and sustainable approach, in which drying represents the rate-limiting step. Previous studies have already proved that microwave drying is more efficient and less energy-intensive compared with conventional hot-air method. Thus, it is worthwhile to further conduct research on the microwave drying characteristics of ES to obtain the optimal drying parameters, thereby further enhancing the drying efficiency, and reducing the drying energy consumption. In this study, a multi-physics field model integrating electromagnetic field, heat transfer, moisture transport, and fluid flow was established in COMSOL Multiphysics to simulate the process of microwave drying ES. The model was validated against experimental data and was capable of accurately capturing the spatiotemporal evolution of temperature and moisture. Simulations revealed that water and vapor migration played a critical role in mitigating nonuniform temperature distribution, and that no rewetting phenomenon occurred in ES throughout the microwave drying process. Increasing microwave power significantly shortened specific drying time while only marginally increasing specific energy consumption. Parametric analysis showed that a microwave power of 12 kW and an upper surface area of 15.9 × 10−2 m2 achieved the best trade-off between drying efficiency and energy consumption, with a sample thickness below 109 mm corresponding to an initial mass below 25 kg. Finally, a concise regression equation for specific drying time was derived, offering a practical and robust tool for optimization in batch drying of ES.

title: A self-sustained spray-assisted bioelectro-Fenton biotrickling filter with sulfur-modified Fe–Co cathodes for energy-efficient removal of hydrophobic volatile organic compounds
abstract: Hydrophobic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are difficult to remove in conventional biological systems because of limited gas–liquid mass transfer and low bioavailability. In this study, a self-sustained spray-assisted biotrickling filter integrated with a bioelectro-Fenton process (BTF–BEF) was developed for efficient hydrophobic VOC removal with low energy and water demand. A sulfur-modified Fe–Co cathode enabled in situ H2O2 generation and dual-radical production (•OH and SO4•-) without external power input, chemical oxidant addition, or pH adjustment. The spray-assisted configuration enhanced gas–liquid contact and improved reaction efficiency. The system achieved 98% removal of 600 ppm styrene and maintained stable performance over 45 days. Sulfur modification improved electron transfer, promoted Fe2+/Fe3+ redox cycling, and reduced metal leaching, thereby enhancing catalytic durability. The system also showed good tolerance under neutral and mildly alkaline conditions. These results demonstrate a promising and scalable strategy for hydrophobic VOC treatment and provide useful insights into sustainable air pollution control and cleaner industrial off-gas treatment.

title: Anthropogenic carbon sequestration redefines the terrestrial carbon cycle: Insights from concrete buildings
abstract: Conventional carbon sequestration policies are narrowly focused on natural ecosystems, thereby overlooking the substantial role of anthropogenic sequestration. This omission distorts global carbon budgets and undermines equitable climate governance. This gap is especially acute in rapidly urbanizing regions, where infrastructure-derived carbon sequestration remains underemphasized in accounting frameworks. Here, we propose an expanded carbon accounting framework that explicitly integrates anthropogenic processes, using cement carbonation as a representative pathway. Applied to China (2000–2020), our analysis shows that carbon sinks in terrestrial anthropogenic ecosystems (TAEs) rose from 2% to 27% of the total terrestrial ecosystems (TEs). In highly urbanized provinces with extensive cement stocks, carbonation uptake can be substantial within the adopted accounting framework and may exceed forest carbon sequestration at the provincial scale. Specifically, concrete buildings exhibited a twentyfold increase in annual carbon sinks and a two-hundredfold increase in carbon pools, surpassing forest sinks in highly urbanized provinces such as Jiangsu by 9–14 times between 2010 and 2020. This carbonation represents the partial re-absorption of previously emitted cement-related CO2 rather than an independent net atmospheric carbon sink comparable to forest sequestration. Fine-scale analysis further reveals nonlinear effects: under intense urbanization, concrete structures demonstrate a sequestration capacity that not only rivals but can surpass natural carbon sinks, forming a coupled human–natural metabolism system. Under a gross uptake–focused accounting boundary rather than a net carbon sink, these findings highlight the urgency of redefining carbon sink boundaries. Excluding anthropogenic sinks distorts responsibility allocation and places urbanized regions at a disadvantage. We argue for their formal integration into international carbon accounting standards, climate negotiations, and urban decarbonization strategies. Such a shift enhances systemic climate resilience, promotes fairness, and incentivizes carbon-positive infrastructure. Our framework provides a transferable model for rethinking carbon governance in the Anthropocene.

title: Carbon supported iron-single atoms/ultrafine atom clusters mediated electron-proton coupling transfer for enhanced anaerobic digestion
abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) represents a high-efficiency approach for resource recovery from organic wastewater. The metabolic imbalance and sluggish electron transfer between syntrophic anaerobic microorganisms is the key limiting factor for methanogenesis in AD process. To better address this issue, a carbonized Fe-based metal-organic framework (CMIL-800) was strategically developed in this study. The CMIL-800 was characterized by the integration of uniformly dispersed Fe single atoms and their ultrafine clusters with the carbon substrate, which fundamentally minimized the interfacial charge-transfer resistance and established localized potential differences on the interface to actively drive interspecies electron transfer in AD process. Furthermore, the exceptional charge capacity and proton-conduction capability of CMIL-800 can provide multiple-mediatory pathways for maintaining microbial metabolic equilibrium and accelerating methane conversion. Experimental results showed that the AD efficiency was effectively improved via the addition of CMIL-800. Kinetic isotope effect (KIE) tests and extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) structural evolution results provided powerful evidence for a simultaneous enhancement in electron and proton transfer rates within the AD system. Moreover, a significant increase in the abundance of genes associated with methanogenesis, proton transfer, and electron transport was also observed, further confirming the multi-dimensional regulatory effects of CMIL-800 on metabolic imbalances among syntrophic anaerobes. In summary, this work provided a novel and efficient strategy for optimizing AD performance.

title: Bi-level multi-objective optimization for the vehicle routing problem from a waste-to-energy reverse logistics network
abstract: Given the considerable economic and environmental challenges posed by kitchen waste, this paper proposes a reverse logistics network equipped with four potential transportation and treatment technologies to achieve efficient waste reduction and energy recovery. A bi-level multi-objective optimization model is developed to address the vehicle routing problem derived from the network. The upper-level local authority aims to minimize fiscal expenditure and carbon emissions by determining subsidy amounts and carbon emission quotas. The lower-level kitchen waste operator seeks to maximize total profits by determining vehicle routes and waste loading amounts. The proposed model incorporates technology parameters, enabling decision makers to assess waste-to-energy efficiency across different technology combinations. The model is applied to a real-life case study in China, and the calculation results and sensitivity analyses provide key insights: (1) The combination of diesel trucks and black soldier fly technology currently yields the highest economic profits, with the operator independently generating 41% of its profits; (2) Under the optimal technology combination, raising the resource utilization rate can further enhance waste-to-energy performance and boost the operator’s economic profits; (3) Expanding truck capacity can increase the operator’s economic profits without adding to the fiscal burden on the local authority.

title: Mitigating environmental impacts and reducing nitrogen footprint by novel tripartite pig husbandry with maximized waste recycling
abstract: Pig husbandry requires high resource input and is a known heavy greenhouse gas (GHG) emitter. This study proposed a novel tripartite pig husbandry system (high-yielding rice-dry AD-MP production) with maximized waste recycling technologies. It assessed the system's nitrogen footprint (NF), and environmental impacts categorized into global warming, acidification, eutrophication, and biological toxicity, using life cycle assessment (LCA). Conventional pig husbandry with pig manure treated by wastewater treatment and solid waste composting serves as the base scenario. Substituting corn in pig's feed with locally grown, high-yielding rice can reduce the impacts of global warming, acidification, eutrophication, and biological toxicity by 29.1 %, 56.4%, 40.3%, and 63.9%, respectively, and NF by 54.7%. On the other hand, the MP incorporates the carbon of biogas and nitrogen of digestate into biomass, which is a significant carbon and nitrogen sink for the novel tripartite system. MP production could markedly mitigate the evaluated categorized environmental impacts of pig husbandry by up to 80∼90%, owing to the increased output of overall proteins. Also, the biogas upgrade products can be versatile, using carbon and nitrogen from dry AD as feed. The tripartite pig husbandry system is carbon-lean, which could lessen the burdens associated with conventional pig husbandry by maximizing waste recycling and closing the loops as a circular bioeconomy model, presenting a promising configuration for next-generation pig-raising industries.

title: Quantifying ecological spillover contributions to mitigate supply–demand spatial mismatch: An integrated ecosystem service flow framework
abstract: Rapid urbanization has intensified the spatial mismatch between ecosystem service (ES) supply and demand, posing critical challenges for sustainable regional development. Existing assessments, largely based on static supply–demand patterns, often fail to capture the redistributive role of ecosystem service flows (ESFs) in regulating spatial ecological imbalances. To address this limitation, we propose an integrated ecosystem service flow framework that explicitly simulates ESF pathways, magnitudes, and spillover contributions, thereby linking static mismatch assessment with dynamic flow processes. Using multi-source geospatial datasets and process-based models, we quantified the spillover effects of water yield (WY), food production (FP), and carbon sequestration (CS) across the Urban Agglomeration in the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River (UA-MRYR). Results show that ESFs substantially alleviated ecological deficits, with compensation rates of 79.68% (FP), 74.79% (WY), and 61.94% (CS). The three ESFs demonstrated distinct flow mechanisms—unidirectional hydrological routing for WY, market-regulated multi-source networks for FP, and diffusion-driven processes for CS. Integrating flow intensity, total volume, and conflict patterns, we developed a multi-dimensional zoning scheme that delineates Key Functional Zones, Scale Advantage Zones, Potential Cultivation Zones, and Efficiency Focal Zones. By translating ESF spillovers into actionable spatial governance tools, this study offers a scalable pathway for correcting ecological imbalances and guiding adaptive ecological planning in rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: Biofilm microbiome responses to multi-source rewetting in dry rivers: Flume experimental insights and implications for sustainable wastewater reuse
abstract: Rewetting is essential for the recovery of dry river ecosystems, yet the ecological risks associated with widespread wastewater overflow necessitate the development of sustainable strategies. This study evaluates a multi-source rewetting approach, using riverine biofilms as integrated indicators of ecosystem diversity and function. We systematically compared the impacts of three water sources (reservoir water, treated wastewater effluent, and wastewater) on the recovery of biofilm microbial communities and metabolic pathways following drought. Treated wastewater effluent restored 86.35% of pre-drought biofilm biomass and increased microbial α-diversity (Shannon index from 4.64 to 5.03), along with reactivating key metabolic pathways such as carbon fixation and nitrification. However, it failed to completely reestablish autotrophic capacity with the autotrophic index (AI) increasing by 8.83%. In contrast, reservoir water uniquely restored chlorophyll-a content by 97.12% and reduced AI to the initial level, indicating recovery of autotrophic function. Untreated wastewater upregulated key biogeochemical pathways (e.g., cysH in sulfur cycling, 1.94-fold upregulation) but elevated pathogen gene abundance by 2.26-fold, posing significant ecological risks. The rapid response and functional redundancy of biofilm microbiota confirm their effectiveness as a robust bioindicator for rewetting events. Collectively, these findings support a staged water replenishment strategy, implemented through a sequence of treated wastewater for initial functional priming, reservoir water for autotrophic recovery, and limited wastewater for enhancing specific metabolic functions. This strategy can promote the transformation of river management from a conventional water-supply approach to a function-oriented cleaner production model, thereby providing a scientific basis for sustainable watershed management and water resource recycling.

title: Smart production of bioenergy from food waste: A multi-objective approach considering inflation and subsidies
abstract: The smart production system is integrated into the food waste-to-bioenergy supply chain to enhance system adaptability, reduce operational inefficiencies, and lower dependency on fossil fuels through sustainable energy production. The model employs a triple bottom line framework, striking a balance among economic, environmental, and social objectives, while incorporating inflation-adjusted costs and government subsidies to evaluate long-term financial feasibility. Food waste is collected through incentive-based return programs supported by community awareness initiatives. When the return rate is low, partial outsourcing from external suppliers ensures continuity in feedstock supply. The system leverages smart technologies, including variable production rates, energy savings, and a district heating network, which enhances energy efficiency and operational resilience. A multi-objective mixed integer linear programming problem is optimized using the multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. Results indicate that a high return rate of food waste minimizes the total cost and environmental impact. In contrast, a low return rate necessitates partial outsourcing, which raises costs by 5.12% and significantly increases environmental impact by 6.91%, while also improving social benefits through job creation. The variable production system improved load balancing, reduced internal energy waste by 70%, and achieved a 90% net energy recovery rate. Sensitivity analysis reveals that a 50% increase in inflation results in a 5.06% increase in total cost, underscoring the importance of resilient financial planning. The study highlights the trade-offs among environmental, economic, and social objectives. It demonstrates that integrating smart technologies, effective return policies, and supportive governance can significantly enhance the sustainability and resilience of bioenergy systems.

title: Data dependency in deep learning-based multi-scale fracture system characterization using hydrogeophysical data
abstract: Characterizing the spatial distribution of fractures, an inherently heterogeneous and multi-scale system, is essential yet challenging in subsurface energy and environmental applications such as enhanced geothermal system and high-level waste disposal. Success relies heavily on the quality, variety, and scale of hydrogeological and geophysical data. This study investigates how fracture scale influences data dependency and model performance in deep learning (DL)-based fracture characterization. Two DL models are evaluated: DAOCRN for spatial distribution mapping and ResNet50 for parameter identification. Using three representative fracture systems (from single fractures to complex networks) and four hydrogeophysical data types (pressure, concentration, temperature, self-potential), we analyze model and data behaviors across scales. Results show that both models require increased data size as fracture complexity grows, highlighting strong scale-dependent data needs. DAOCRN exhibits lower sensitivity to data size in small-scale systems but higher dependency in large-scale systems, achieving up to 90.4% loss reduction when trained with more data. ResNet50 is more data-efficient under limited conditions, but its improvement saturates at ∼12%. Surrogate modeling is used to compare cross-model performance within a unified framework. Data ablation studies reveal that while not all additional data types improve results, multi-source fusion generally enhances performance by reducing reconstruction error and improving model robustness. This work provides new insights into scale-sensitive data dependency in DL-based fracture characterization and highlights the value of tailored data acquisition and fusion strategies for subsurface applications.

title: A hybrid game-based trading strategy for electricity-hydrogen-frequency regulation market of integrated hydrogen production and refueling stations considering privacy protection
abstract: Integrated hydrogen production and refueling stations (IHPRSs) exhibit considerable operational flexibility due to electricity-hydrogen coupling and fast-response electrochemical equipment, enabling participation in electricity, hydrogen, and frequency regulation ancillary service (FRAS) markets. However, profit-oriented decision-making across multiple markets may lead to profit offset effects and undermine coordinated operation, while distributed hydrogen trading raises concerns regarding the leakage of sensitive operational information. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a coordinated trading strategy for electricity-hydrogen-FRAS markets that jointly considers economic performance and privacy protection. A hybrid game-theoretic framework is developed by integrating a Stackelberg game between the power system operator and multiple IHPRSs with a Nash bargaining-based cooperative game among IHPRSs, enabling coordinated decision-making across heterogeneous market layers. To support privacy-preserving distributed hydrogen trading, a differential privacy-enhanced consensus ADMM (DP-C-ADMM) algorithm is designed, which mitigates information leakage risks while maintaining convergence and computational tractability without relying on a trusted third party. Case studies based on the IEEE 300-bus system indicate that the proposed solution method exhibits satisfactory convergence performance. The proposed strategy enables IHPRSs to obtain additional revenues from FRAS participation without materially reducing hydrogen market profits, which achieves an effective balance between market coordination and data privacy.

title: Nitrogen losses, controlling factors, and mitigation potential of global maize and wheat production
abstract: Nitrogen fertilizer application to staple crops such as maize and wheat farmland has surged dramatically, leading to substantial losses of soil nitrogen in various forms. However, the nitrogen losses, controlling factors, and mitigation potential of global maize and wheat production have been far from clear. Here, we develop machine learning models to account for more key factors than before to investigate the spatial distribution, key controlling factors, and mitigation potential of soil reactive nitrogen losses in maize and wheat fields worldwide at a 5-arcmin resolution. We estimate the annual global soil nitrogen losses from synthetic nitrogen fertilizer use in 2020, including emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O), ammonia (NH3), nitrogen oxides (NO), nitrogen leaching, and runoff. These losses amounted to 0.21, 2.36, 0.13, 2.50, and 1.21 million tons of nitrogen, respectively, for maize; and 0.19, 1.21, 0.10, 2.74, and 1.09 million tons of nitrogen, respectively, for wheat. The hydrological pathway contributed over 55% of total losses and is more susceptible to extreme precipitation events, while gaseous losses are more influenced by climate and soil texture. Mitigation primarily relies on improving nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and replacing fertilizer types. The most effective approach involves raising NUE to 60% while fully adopting efficient nitrogen fertilizers, achieving emission reductions of 80.6% for wheat and approximately 23.9% for maize. These findings not only hold scientific value for precise modeling of agricultural nitrogen cycling but also provide critical scientific basis for developing regionally differentiated, crop-specific nitrogen fertilizer management and emission mitigation strategies.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of tightened emission standards in reducing real-world vehicle emissions: Evidence from on-road testing and inventory analysis
abstract: Vehicle emissions pose a significant threat to public health and air quality worldwide. Although increasingly stringent emission standards are being implemented globally to address this challenge, the continuous growth in vehicle fleet size has introduced considerable complexity to emission control efforts. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of emission standard upgrades by analyzing changes in both per-vehicle emissions and total urban emission trends. Using a portable emission measurement system (PEMS), localized emission factors (EFs) and chemical composition profiles of particulate matter (PM) from typical light-duty and heavy-duty vehicles complying with China 3 to China 6 standards were obtained in Qingdao, a representative Chinese city. Based on real-world measurements, a high-resolution urban vehicle emission inventory for 2020 was developed. The results show that per-vehicle EFs for CO, NOx, THC, and PM consistently decreased with increasingly stringent emission standards. For heavy-duty trucks, upgrading from China 3 to China 4 reduced NOx, CO, THC, and PM emissions by 22.9%, 52.8%, 73.3%, and 36.6%, respectively. Carbonaceous components dominated the PM mass, accounting for 62.2%–72.6%, with Fe, Ti, Al, and Zn identified as key elemental markers. Despite a growing vehicle population, total urban emissions of CO, THC, NOx, PM, and SO2 in 2020 showed significant declines compared to 2007–2014, with particularly notable reductions in PM, CO, and SO2. The key innovation of this study is the establishment of measurement-based localized EFs and PM composition spectra, which enhance the accuracy of emission inventories. It provides the first full-chain validation—from per-vehicle emissions to urban totals—demonstrating that stringent emission standards could effectively decouple emission growth from fleet expansion. The findings provide scientific basis for regional air pollution control, including updating inventory parameters, evaluating policy effects, and implementing accelerated elimination and precise control for high-emission vehicle models.

title: Selective adsorption mechanism of an eco-friendly depressant on hemimorphite and calcite surfaces and its response to flotation separation
abstract: Hemimorphite is a typical oxide zinc mineral, whereas calcite is the dominant calcium-bearing gangue mineral. The selection of appropriate depressants is crucially important for the efficient flotation separation of hemimorphite from calcite. In this study, konjac glucomannan (KGM) was selected as an eco-friendly and highly effective depressant, and its separation mechanism was systematically investigated through flotation tests combined with multiple characterization methods. Flotation tests showed that KGM could effectively depress calcite flotation while exerting negligible influence on hemimorphite. Specifically, single-stage flotation of artificially mixed hemimorphite–calcite samples yielded a high-quality concentrate with a grade of 41.94% Zn and an associated zinc recovery of 86.89%. Comprehensive characterization results showed that KGM adsorbed more strongly on calcite than on hemimorphite surfaces, which induced differentiated regulation of subsequent sodium oleate (NaOL). Particularly, KGM occupied the active sites on calcite surfaces, thereby depressing NaOL adsorption and the subsequent hydrophobic modification of calcite. Conversely, NaOL adsorption on hemimorphite surfaces remained unaffected. Correspondingly, hemimorphite retained high hydrophobicity, while calcite exhibited a sharp decline in hydrophobicity in the KGM-NaOL binary system. These findings illustrate that hemimorphite can be selectively separated from calcite using KGM as an eco-friendly depressant, highlighting its considerable potential for industrial application.

title: Synergistic Fe3+ coordination optimization and electron transfer: boosting photo-Fenton performance of carbon dots for advanced water treatment
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs), due to their good light absorption and water solubility, are considered potential catalysts for photocatalytic Fenton reactions. However, their catalytic efficiency is limited by the rapid recombination of photogenerated charge carriers and the slow Fe3+/Fe2+ cycle. This study compares the catalytic mechanisms of S-CDs, P-CDs, and Cl-CDs in photo-Fenton systems. It was found that S-CDs exhibited the best photo-Fenton performance, with rhodamine B degradation rates 40.6 and 15.2 times higher than those of P-CDs and Cl-CDs, respectively. The results reveal that surface functional groups, particularly sulfonic acid and thiol groups on S-CDs, effectively promote photoinduced electron transfer and optimize Fe2+ coordination, thereby accelerating Fe3+ reduction. In contrast, P-CDs strongly chelate Fe3+, which hinders electron transfer, while Cl-CDs suffer from weak Fe3+ coordination and low carrier density, both leading to suppressed catalytic activity. Overall, this work demonstrates how surface functional groups, through synergistic modulation of electron donation and metal coordination, influence catalytic performance, highlighting the crucial role of the surface chemical environment. These findings provide new insights for the design of efficient carbon-based photocatalytic Fenton catalysts.

title: Performance-based evaluation framework for life cycle assessment: A case study on silicon monoxide anodes for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Battery technology based on carbon-coated silicon monoxide (SiO/C) as an anode material has gained considerable attention owing to their high capacity and enhanced cyclic durability. However, the environmental impact of SiO/C has not been comprehensively discussed. This work evaluated the environmental impact associated with SiO/C using life cycle assessment. The global warming potential based on the active material mass of the synthesized SiO/C (GWPmass) was 39–54 kg-CO2eq/kg-SiO/C, with the electricity used for the SiO synthesis identified as a hotspot for GWP. The surplus ore depletion from synthesizing SiO/C (SOPmass) was 0.14–0.27 kg-Cueq/kg-SiO/C. The SOPmass of SiO/C varied depending on the Si grade used. For metallurgical-grade Si, SiO production was identified as the hotspot for SOP. In contrast, for solar-grade Si, high-purity Si production was recognized as hotspots due to their intensive energy and resource requirements. Furthermore, the concept of environmental impact per active material delivered lifetime capacity (DLC) was proposed to integrate both battery performance and environmental impact into a single parameter. The values for GWP and SOP per active material DLC (GWPDLC and SOPDLC) were 2.5 × 10−1–3.5 × 10−1 kg-CO2eq/kA hDLC and 9.0 × 10−4–1.7 × 10−3 kg-Cueq/kA hDLC, respectively, which were higher than those of the conventional graphite (Gr) active material. By contrast, to reduce these values for the SiO/C active material to those for the Gr active material, the SiO/C active material should maintain 94% capacity for 1.3 × 103 cycles. The proposed new framework for battery development and performance-oriented functional unit as well as the evaluated environmental impacts of SiO/C active materials could contribute to the advancement of next-generation batteries with both high performance and low environmental impacts.

title: Integrating phosphorus sustainability and environmental burden mitigation through systemwide-optimized strategy in China's Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Resolving the global phosphorus (P) paradox—ensuring food production for growing population while preventing geological resource depletion and aquatic degradation—demands innovative strategies that move beyond simply reducing environmental discharges. Current solutions often overlook the synergistic benefits of source control and circular economy enhancement, leading to fragmented sustainability assessments. Here we investigate China's Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), a global socioeconomic nucleus exhibiting archetypal P imbalances. By integrating seven decades (1950-2020) of substance flow analysis with a novel systemwide evaluation module, we systematically quantified the sustainability potential of 15 interventions across production, processing, consumption, and waste disposal stages. Our finding revealed peak-plateau P flow dynamics characterized by a critical transition from organic nutrient recycling to inorganic P rock dependency (11.5 Mt/yr). This shift has accelerated geological reserve depletion to less than 30 years while driving annual environmental discharges exceeding 2.65 Mt, particularly in socioeconomic hubs intersecting major hydrological networks. Forward-looking scenarios for 2050 indicate that comprehensive waste valorization (S4) could more than double regional P reserve longevity (+119.8%), while synergistic agricultural reform (S2) might halve peak environmental losses. This systemic mineral provisioning-water security framework provides a transferable policy design paradigm for P-vulnerable basins worldwide that face similar sustainability paradoxes.

title: A mechanistic machine learning framework to decode reverse osmosis membrane retention mechanism for neutral low-molecular-weight organics
abstract: Neutral low-molecular-weight (LMW) organics (e.g., urea, N-nitrosodimethylamine) with molecular weights <250 Da can permeate reverse osmosis (RO) membranes, compromising reclaimed water quality and posing health and industrial risks. However, the permeation characteristics of LMW organics and the mechanisms governing their retention are unclear. This study innovatively integrated data-driven machine learning (ML) with physicochemical mechanisms to decode RO retention characteristics and mechanisms of neutral LMW organics. A comprehensive database of 1254 retention data points for 190 organics was built, and six ML algorithms were evaluated. The XGBoost model, optimized via physicochemical mechanism-guided feature engineering (capturing steric, van der Waals, electrostatic, and hydrophobic interactions), achieved an adjusted R2 of 0.91 and MAE of 3.53%, outperforming traditional models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed steric and van der Waals effects as core retention mechanisms, with cross-mechanism synergies between steric and van der Waals interactions dominating retention. This framework mitigated data leakage (MAE reduced from 15.78% to 2.76% via compound-based splitting) and guided membrane design strategies: tuning pore size <0.4 nm for steric exclusion, enhancing polarizability for van der Waals adsorption, and optimizing pH-responsive charge layers. The study provided a transformative engineering roadmap for next-generation RO membranes, bridging data-driven predictions with mechanistic material design for sustainable water management.

title: Synergistic optimization of filter bag arrangement and shape for vortex suppression flow equalization and resistance reduction in a straight-through baghouse dust collector
abstract: Straight-through baghouse dust collectors are used for fine particulate control in industrial processes. However, flow instability inside the housing can trigger separation vortices that intensify local energy dissipation, accelerate premature filter bag wear, and degrade energy efficiency. To achieve flow equalization while retaining the low-resistance advantage of straight-through configurations, this study proposes a synergistic optimization of filter bag arrangement and shape guided by vortex-structure-based flow reconstruction. Two-dimensional simulations show that a stepped filter bag arrangement reduces vortex intensity by 70%, and replacing circular bags with elliptical bags further reduces vortex intensity by 74%. Three-dimensional simulations confirm that combining the stepped arrangement with elliptical filter bags substantially improves airflow distribution uniformity, decreasing the non-uniformity coefficient from 13% to 2%. Performance at four representative operating stages is evaluated in terms of airflow uniformity, dust distribution uniformity, pressure drop, and energy efficiency. The optimized configuration maintains airflow non-uniformity below 5% and dust distribution non-uniformity below 6.5% while reducing the pressure drop by 15% and improving energy efficiency by more than 10%. These results demonstrate that the proposed synergistic optimization strategy provides an effective and practical route for performance enhancement and structural refinement of straight-through baghouse dust collectors.

title: Targeted thorium removal in ultra-acidic effluents using novel electrode system
abstract: Thorium, as a promising alternative nuclear fuel, poses significant ecological risks due to its dual chemical and radiotoxicity. The conventional methods often suffer from poor selectivity and low efficiency in strongly acidic solutions. Herein, a novel targeted thorium removal electrode system was developed with the assistance of an active metal anode. The system achieved 92.4% thorium removal efficiency at pH 1.0, tripling the performance of traditional inert anode configurations. Furthermore, the system exhibited exceptional selectivity for thorium in the presence of five competing cations (K+, Mg2+, La3+, Pr3+, and Nd3+), with separation factors exceeding 488.9 and reaching a maximum of 1363.2. The system maintained robust performance across a broad pH range (1.0-6.0) and thorium concentrations (25-200 mg/L), retaining over 90% and 80% removal efficiency, respectively. The addition of supporting electrolyte could further enhance the thorium removal performance at pH 1.0 of the system, and up to 96.1% of thorium could be effectively removed within 120 min under optimized conditions with 0.3 M NaCl as the supporting electrolyte. Mechanistic studies revealed a synergistic multi-mechanism process: (1) electric field-driven adsorption/electrosorption of Th4+ on the cathode; (2) Zn2+-derived hydroxide/oxide precipitates providing additional adsorption sites; and (3) Zn2+-mediated synergistic precipitation with Th4+. This work opens new avenues for designing advanced electrode systems and enhancing electrosorption technologies for selective thorium removal from highly acidic solutions.

title: Research on feature selection and interaction analysis of coal mine accident causation: Applying PGI-SDMI and machine learning methods
abstract: Coal mine accident reports serve as a crucial pathway for analyzing the significance of influencing factors and deriving lessons learned, which aids in reducing accident occurrence rates. However, most research on coal mine accident influencing factors has focused on the likelihood of accidents, with less attention paid to the impact of causes on accident severity. Therefore, this study proposes a two-stage PGI-SDMI method to screen the causal features of coal mine accidents, develops a severity prediction model, and employs SHAP for interpretability analysis. The total of 298 historical coal mine accidents were used as a case study to validate the proposed methodological framework. The results indicate that the SVM_SMOTE_ENN method effectively addressed the class imbalance issue, while stability and predictability were combined to quantify the effectiveness of the feature selection method. The prediction accuracy was highest when the number of selected features was 26. These features were then input into the LightGBM model for prediction. Based on SHAP interaction values, it was found that variables such as “inadequate implementation of systems and measures” and “insufficient technical management” are key interactive causal features leading to different accident severity levels, and they are also the primary causes requiring focused prevention and control to mitigate accident losses. Furthermore, from a counterfactual perspective, the effects of single-factor and multi-factor risk control measures were analyzed. This research contributes to enhancing coal mine accident risk prevention and control both theoretically and practically, promoting a shift in coal mine safety governance towards a more proactive and precise model.

title: The removal behavior of Bi and Pb during the purifying arsenic by the vacuum sublimation graded condensation
abstract: High-purity arsenic (As) is an essential material for GaAs and InAs semiconductors. However, bismuth (Bi) and lead (Pb) are difficult to effectively remove during the conventional chlorination process for high purifying arsenic. Therefore, efficient pre-purification of crude arsenic is highly necessary. In this study, a vacuum sublimation graded condensation method combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is used to elucidate and control the migration behavior of Bi and Pb during crude As pre-purification. Although thermodynamic calculations indicate that Bi and Pb do not volatilize in the experiment, the MD results show that there is a strong binding force between Bi and Pb and As, and they enter the gas phase in the form of stable As-Bi and As-Pb clusters; and the diffusion coefficients of most impurity-containing clusters are lower than that of the dominant As4 cluster. Based on this mechanism, a vacuum sublimation graded condensation experiment was carried out. Through optimizing the structure of the condenser and process parameters, efficient separation of Bi and Pb was achieved. Experimental results showed the removal rates of Bi and Pb were 99%, the direct recovery rate of As was 89% at a temperature of 748 K, with a holding time of 60 min and a pressure of 10 Pa. The efficient separation of bismuth, lead, and arsenic is attributed to the hierarchical condensation of gas-phase clusters during vacuum condensation mass transfer, achieved through differing diffusion rates. This reagent-free physical approach provides an efficient and environmentally friendly route for stabilizing high-purity As manufacturing.

title: A process-based and data-driven framework for carbon emission evaluation in integrated shipbuilding and repair in a typical small-to-medium sized shipyard
abstract: To promote the development of low-carbon shipyards and reduce carbon emissions during the shipbuilding and repair processes, it is urgent to establish a scientific and practical carbon footprint accounting system. Taking a typical small-to-medium sized (SME) shipyard in China as a case study, seven categories of representative shipbuilding and repair processes are systematically classified, and multi-source data acquisition and statistical verification methods are integrated to analyze the activity data. Based on the IPCC carbon footprint accounting principles, an integrated carbon footprint accounting model for shipbuilding and repair was constructed by coupling activity data with emission factors. The carbon emission intensities of key processes were derived and updated, and the applicability and rationality of the model were validated through actual shipbuilding and repair projects. The results indicate that hull processing and assembly, as well as derusting and painting, are the two most carbon-intensive processes. Electricity consumption is the primary emission source, followed by diesel, CO2, O2, natural gas, and industrial water. The proposed model can accurately identify the carbon emission characteristics of different ship types during the shipbuilding and repair processes in similar shipyards, providing a valuable reference for establishing standardized carbon management systems in SME shipyards. Meanwhile, it addresses the challenge of accurately classifying activity data in single-ship carbon footprint accounting, offering practical value for identifying key emission reduction priorities, optimizing production processes, and accelerating the industry's low-carbon transformation.

title: pH-tuned hydrothermal synthesis of sludge-derived biochar for enhanced activation of peroxymonosulfate in tetracycline degradation
abstract: The persistent contamination of aquatic environments by tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) and the escalating challenge of sewage sludge disposal necessitate sustainable and scalable remediation strategies. This study developed an energy-efficient pH-modulated hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) strategy to convert sewage sludge into high-performance sludge-derived biochar (SSB) for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Alkaline modification (pH = 11.0) significantly increased the specific surface area, optimized the pore structure, and enhanced the formation of oxygen-containing functional groups and structural defects on SSB, thereby synergistically enhancing PMS adsorption and activation. The optimized SS-Na3PO4 catalyst achieved over 99% TC removal within 60 min under mild conditions, representing a 1.8-fold improvement in degradation kinetics compared to the neutral-synthesized SS (SS-pH = 7). Mechanistic investigations unveiled a multi-pathway oxidation process dominated by 1O2, with supplementary contributions from •O2−, •SO4−, and •OH. Additionally, the SS-Na3PO4/PMS system exhibited enhanced performance in natural water matrices, owing to the presence of coexisting inorganic ions, which facilitated the degradation process by acting as electron shuttles to promote PMS activation. The catalyst retained over 85% of its initial activity after five consecutive catalytic cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further corroborated the critical role of oxygen-containing functional groups in mediating electron transfer and PMS activation. This work establishes a scalable “treating-waste-with-waste” strategy, offering a sustainable pathway for simultaneous sludge valorization and water purification.

title: How does business diversification shape ESG? Unpacking U-shaped patterns in performance and disclosure
abstract: Corporate diversification is a common growth strategy, yet its sustainability implications remain underexplored. Using panel data from Chinese A-share firms (2018–2024), this study examines how diversification affects ESG performance and disclosure transparency. We document a U-shaped relationship in which diversification initially deteriorates ESG outcomes before generating improvements at higher levels. At lower levels of diversification, weakened managerial focus and control lead to poorer ESG performance and less transparent disclosure. Only when diversification surpasses a certain threshold do firms begin to realize potential benefits—such as resource synergies, cross-unit learning, and reputational incentives—thereby improving both ESG performance and disclosure quality. Notably, the majority of firms in our sample remain on the left side of the curve, suggesting that diversification continues to exert negative sustainability impacts for most companies, which have yet to capture its potential benefits. We further show that this nonlinear relationship is conditional on organizational and external governance factors, with managerial myopia and media attention significantly moderating the shape and strength of the U-shaped effect. Additional analyses reveal that the U-shaped pattern is primarily driven by unrelated diversification, underscoring the importance of business relatedness in shaping the sustainability consequences of diversification. Overall, the study highlights how strategic complexity generates nonlinear ESG dynamics, offering insights for firms seeking to balance growth with credible sustainability management.

title: One-step retrieval of ground-level ozone concentrations from OMI hyperspectral observations using machine learning
abstract: Ground-level ozone (O3) pollution poses significant risks to ecosystems and public health, particularly in China. Current satellite-based retrieval approaches largely rely on total-column ozone and precursor products derived from radiative transfer models, which can introduce uncertainties due to assumptions regarding surface and atmospheric conditions. To address these limitations, we developed a one-step retrieval framework to directly estimates ground-level O3 concentrations from Ozone Monitoring Instrument (OMI) hyperspectral imagery using an Extremely Randomized Trees (ERT) model. The ERT was trained by integrating OMI spectral observations with ground-based O3 observations, enabling automatic identification of informative wavelength features through a hybrid data-driven and physics-informed strategy. Independent validation demonstrates its strong predictive performance, with a high sample-based ten-fold cross-validation correlation coefficient (CV-R) of 0.92 and a low root mean square error (RMSE) of 13.55 μg/m3. It also exhibits robust spatial extrapolation capability (space-based CV-R = 0.91) and moderate temporal transferability (time-based CV-R = 0.76) for regions and periods without training samples, although performance slightly declines in densely vegetated areas and under elevated boundary layer conditions. Our analysis demonstrates the critical importance of OMI observations, with model accuracy decreasing by up to 15% when OMI data are excluded. Leveraging these advantages, the model effectively captures characteristic spatiotemporal O3 patterns across China and successfully identifies severe summer pollution hotspots in the North China Plain (NCP) and Yangtze River Delta (YRD) regions, which are driven by distinct factors. This is a first demonstration of direct ground-level O3 retrieval from OMI hyperspectral imagery without dependence on its secondary products, potentially establishing a new paradigm for satellite-based air quality monitoring.

title: Organic metabolism through NAD+ accumulation promotes extracellular electron transfer-dependent anammox for enhanced nitrogen removal potential in domestic wastewater
abstract: The traditional anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) process offers a low-carbon approach to wastewater treatment; however, its performance is often limited by nitrite (NO2−) availability. To overcome this limitation, Fe2O3@EPS was employed as an extracellular electron acceptor, enabling an extracellular electron transfer-dependent anammox system for domestic wastewater treatment. The system operated stably for 128 days, even as influent NH4+-N increased from 40 to 80 mg/L in the absence of NO2−. Metagenomic analysis revealed that electroactive anammox bacteria activated an organotrophic acetyl-CoA synthesis pathway, leading carbon into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. This process converted organic matter in domestic wastewater into pyrimidine and purine for bacterial growth, while oxaloacetic acid served as a precursor for NAD+ synthesis, thereby regulating NAD+ production. Consequently, intracellular NAD+ levels increased by 1.69-fold, enhancing electron transfer across membranes and boosting ATP production by 1.24-fold. Extracellular electron transport to Fe2O3@EPS was enhanced by 1.43-fold. The combined substrate and energy supply enriched electroactive anammox bacteria, leading to a 1.3-fold increase in their abundance. Furthermore, anammox bacteria restructured the EPS matrix, increasing tightly bound EPS (TB-EPS) enriched in cytochrome c to 68%, thereby reducing interfacial resistance and enhancing electron transfer efficiency. Ultimately, 95.12% total nitrogen removal was achieved without external carbon or aeration, with effluent nitrogen below 4 mg/L. This study demonstrates the feasibility of an extracellular electron transfer-dependent anammox system, offering insight and guidance for efficient nitrogen removal technologies.

title: Multi-scale integrated learning with mechanism-data fusion for multi-objective optimization of sintering process: Production-energy consumption trade-off
abstract: Achieving high-efficiency and low-carbon iron ore sintering has become increasingly critical under tightening energy and emission constraints in the iron and steel industry. This study develops a mechanism-informed, multi-scale prediction and optimization framework that simultaneously forecasts specific fuel consumption and an overall sinter quality score, while providing process-feasible optimization strategies. First, a hybrid subjective-objective evaluation model is established to integrate key quality-related indicators, including FeO content, basicity, drum index, and yield, into a unified comprehensive quality score, enabling holistic characterization of sinter quality. A multi-scale ensemble learning architecture is then constructed. At the parameter scale, a multi-objective evolutionary ensemble model combines evolutionary feature selection with nonlinear modeling, achieving high predictive accuracy for fuel consumption (R2 = 0.9293) and the quality score (R2 = 0.9165). At the process-category scale, a mechanism-guided CatBoost model incorporates physicochemical knowledge through grouped features, producing interpretable and thermochemically consistent predictions. Performance-weighted fusion of the two scales further improves robustness, yielding final R2 values of 0.9501 for fuel consumption and 0.9273 for the quality score. Building on the predictive layer, a mechanism-constrained multi-objective optimization strategy is developed using high-quality historical operating conditions. The resulting Pareto solutions demonstrate that fuel consumption can be reduced to approximately 44.2 kg/t while increasing the quality score to about 87.5. For a sinter plant with an annual output of 3.7 million tons, this improvement corresponds to approximately 23,500 tons of fuel savings and 70,600 tons of CO2 reduction per year. Overall, the proposed framework integrates multi-scale data, mechanism knowledge, and optimization principles into a coherent and interpretable system, offering substantial potential for energy conservation and decarbonization in industrial sintering operations.

title: Recycling of salt-lake magnesium slag as the magnesium material for magnesium oxy-sulfate cement: Strength performance, hydration mechanism, and application
abstract: Salt-lake magnesium slag (SMS) contains abundant Mg(OH)2. Magnesium oxy-sulfate (MOS) cement contains ∼60 wt% α-MgO. The consolidation of iron ore tailings (IOT) lacks cheap cement. This work recycled SMS to provide α-MgO for MOS cement preparation, and then the MOS cement with the highest compressive strength was applied to consolidate IOT, using as the backfilling materials in mines. 1) The phases composition, α-MgO content, and specific surface area of calcined SMS was studied. 2) The compressive strength, hydration phases' composition and their content, hydration heat evolution, and morphology of prepared MOS cements were determined. 3) The slump and compressive strength of the MOS cement on IOT were studied, as well as the consolidation mechanism. Results showed that SMS obtained the highest α-MgO content and specific surface area at 650 °C, with 55.69 wt% and 297.1 m2/kg, competently providing the α-MgO for MOS cement preparation. The MOS cement prepared with 60.00 wt% addition obtained the highest compressive strength (10.80 MPa at 3 days, 27.96 MPa at 28 days), meeting 32.5-grade cement standard. And when the IOT concentration was 56 wt%∼58 wt% and the M60 to IOT ratio was 1:6∼1:8, the mortar samples met the requirement of the slump and compressive strength, for the backfilling materials in mines. Results indicated that the main hydration phases of MOS cement were the stable 5·1·7 phase (block shaped) and metastable 3·1·8 phase (rod-shaped). The 5·1·7 phase content development was consistent with the compressive strength and the cumulative hydration heat obtained at stabilization stage. Results also showed that IOT particles were well encapsulated by the gel phases (3·1·8 phase and 5·1·7 phase) hydrated from this cement, forming a whole. This work contributes to the recycling of SMS and materials’ supplement for MOS industry and provide an application path for MOS cement by applying to consolidate IOT.

title: Water resources security assessment and trend prediction: An integrated approach using entropy-mutation theory and explainable machine learning
abstract: Water resources are vital to human survival, and ensuring their security plays a key role in ecological protection and planning. To enhance regional water security, it is urgent to quantitatively assess water security status and diagnose its obstacles to implement appropriate protection measures. This study takes the water supply-demand balance of Hubei Province as a case and constructs an evaluation index system covering four dimensions: water resources, society, economy, and ecology. The Improved Entropy-Mutation Order Method, which integrates information entropy to eliminate subjective bias in hierarchical ranking, is used to assess the water resource carrying capacity of Hubei Province from 2007 to 2024, and the Shapley-weighted method (SHAP) combined with explainable algorithms is applied to predict water resource trends. Random Forest and Bayesian Optimization models are employed for future trend prediction, and data imputation methods are analyzed. The results indicate that from 2007 to 2024, water resource security in Hubei Province has continuously improved, with subsystem coordination mechanisms playing a key role. Since 2013, pressure system indicators have become the main influencing factors. This study verifies the reliability of the Entropy-Mutation Order Method, and the combination of Random Forest and Bayesian Optimization (RF-BO) models demonstrates superior predictive accuracy, achieving a minimal Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0011 and a high coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.942. The model can predict various water resource indicators and handle missing data, providing valuable references for water resource management in other regions.

title: CFD-assisted microscopic mechanism analysis and molecular design of pesticide synergists for agricultural precision deposition
abstract: Developing efficient pesticide synergists is crucial for minimizing pesticide usage and reducing environmental pollution. Currently, synergist development relies heavily on empirical repetitive testing, which is time-consuming and costly. To overcome this limitation, we propose an integrated computational-experimental framework that couples computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with interfacial characterization—a novel methodology for synergist design. The CFD model demonstrates high accuracy in predicting droplet impact dynamics on hydrophobic surfaces, supported by goodness-of-fit R2 ≥ 0.88. Moreover, this CFD model can quantitatively analyze the spatiotemporal distribution and evolution of microscopic energy during the droplet impact process, including kinetic energy, surface energy, and dissipation energy. Our findings reveal that the optimal synergist TX-102 enhances droplet deposition primarily by increasing the viscous dissipation coefficient (VD∗). Self-assembly and diffusion ordered spectroscopy studies further uncover that the strong adsorption capacity of TX-102 molecules at the solid–liquid interface is the underlying mechanism for the enhanced VD∗. The practical effectiveness of TX-102 in improving spray deposition was confirmed across a range of plant leaves. Overall, this study introduces a CFD-guided, mechanism-driven strategy that transitions pesticide synergist development from empirical screening to rational, data-driven formulation engineering, offering a transformative and cost-effective pathway toward precision plant protection.

title: Sustainability assessment of electrified naphtha cracking pathways for carbon-neutral ethylene production
abstract: Ethylene production via naphtha steam cracking is one of the most energy- and carbon-intensive processes in the petrochemical industry. As global efforts toward carbon neutrality accelerate, electrification has emerged as a promising pathway for reducing reliance on fossil fuel combustion. This study evaluates the sustainability of electrified naphtha cracking, considering both electrified steam cracking and plasma arc cracking, using six electricity sources and multiple methane utilization pathways. Industrial-scale process models, supported by pilot-scale data for plasma cracking, were developed to obtain detailed material and energy balances. Comprehensive techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), and carbon avoidance cost (CAC) evaluation were performed. The results show that plasma cracking achieves higher ethylene selectivity but requires a substantially higher energy input than electrified steam cracking.
