Economically, electrified steam cracking with methane-to-blue-hydrogen conversion powered by wind achieved the lowest levelized cost of ethylene (LCOE) ($1.66/kg ethylene) and a negative CAC (–$89.30/tonne CO2-eq), indicating simultaneous cost savings and emission reduction. Environmentally, the lowest emissions occurred in a case study with plasma cracking with methane-to-blue-hydrogen conversion powered by hydropower, achieving an 80.32% reduction relative to that of conventional naphtha steam cracking. Monte Carlo simulation confirmed the robustness of this finding, with the most cost-effective configuration showing an 86.5% probability of CAC below the current carbon price. Overall, this study identified renewable-powered electrified steam cracking combined with carbon-capture-enabled methane utilization as the most cost-effective near-term pathway for carbon-neutral ethylene production, while highlighting the efficiency improvements needed for future plasma cracking technologies.

title: Port carbon emission reduction strategies under government incentive-based regulation: An evolutionary game analysis
abstract: Promoting low-carbon port development, this paper employs evolutionary game theory to construct a tripartite model involving the government, port enterprises, and shipping enterprises. This model comprehensively incorporates multi-dimensional incentive-based regulations, including fiscal subsidies, technical support, tax incentives, personnel motivation, and collaborative benefits. It investigates the nonlinear influence mechanisms of regulatory parameters on the emission reduction behaviors of both ports and shipping enterprises. The results reveal three key findings. First, fiscal subsidies and technical support significantly promote proactive emission reduction, but exhibit pronounced diminishing marginal effects. Exceeding optimal subsidy thresholds prolong government evolution, while technical support effectiveness is dominated by its diminishing coefficient, rendering intensity increases ineffective without controlling diminishing returns. Second, tax incentives demonstrate asymmetric effectiveness, with shipping enterprises 2.5 times more responsive than ports due to higher capital intensity, while balanced collaborative benefit allocation (γ≈0.5) accelerates system convergence by approximately 30% compared to imbalanced distributions. Third, instrument interaction analysis reveals super-additive synergy between fiscal subsidies and tax incentives and between technical support and personnel motivation, enabling combined deployment to achieve 40% faster convergence than single-instrument approaches. By demonstrating that linear policy parameterization obscures empirically observed nonlinear dynamics, introducing partial derivative analysis to quantify directional incentive effects, and revealing complex instrument interactions that necessitate policy mix analysis, this study makes three interrelated theoretical contributions. On a practical level, the findings support phased implementation strategies including whistleblowing mechanisms in early stages, coordinated incentive packages during transition, and performance-linked instruments in mature systems. These insights provide a theoretical basis for designing dynamic and calibrated incentive-based carbon regulations while offering actionable guidance for ports and shipping enterprises pursuing a low-carbon transition.

title: Low-energy ionic liquid biphasic solvents for CO2 capture: New insights on anion regulated solvated shell and delayed phase change
abstract: This study employs high CO2-reactive Diethylenetriamine (DETA+) as the primary absorbent, constructing an ionic liquid system by regulating different anions to achieve efficient and energy-saving CO2 capture from flue gas. After preliminary screening of H2O, ethylene glycol butyl ether (EGBE), and [Diethylenetriamine+1,2,4-Triazole-] ([DETA+MTZ−]) at various mass ratios, an optimal biphasic solvent was obtained with a mass ratio of 2:5:3 (2H5E3DMZ). Experimental results indicate that compared to OTZ− (1,2,3-Triazole-) and BTA− (Benzotraizole−)-regulated ILs, 2H5E3DMZ exhibits a delayed phase separation critical point of 518 s, an enhanced pre-phase separation loading of 1.89 mol kg−1 (29.61% of the enriched phase volume), and achieves an overall CO2 loading of 3.782 mol kg−1. Importantly, NMR and theoretical calculations indicate the significant enhancement in loading capacity is attributed to the reduced self-aggregation of predominantly aggregated products in the rich phase due to the solvation shell effect. This significantly lowers the molecular polarity index (MPI) of highly polar molecules (e.g., the MPI of CO32− decreases from 248.41 kcal mol−1 to 133.19 kcal mol−1 (CO32--EGBE dimer) and 203.32 kcal mol−1 (CO32--H2O dimer)), achieving slow-phase separation and preserving a longer time window for the high mass transfer phase. In addition, 2H5E3DMZ exhibits outstanding antioxidant properties, thermal degradation resistance, and low corrosion potential, with a corrosion rate of only 8.25% that of MEA and regeneration energy consumption as low as 1.72 GJ t−1 CO2. This research provides new insights for developing energy-efficient phase change absorbents and fills a research gap in the in-depth correlation between liquid-liquid phase separation delay mechanisms and absorption capacity.

title: Lignin as a renewable asphalt modifier: a meta-analysis review
abstract: The efficient usage of renewable resources, especially waste management, poses a significant challenge to contemporary economic and social development. One use is the incorporation of lignin into asphalt mixtures for pavement building. Although numerous investigations have assessed the incorporation of lignin in different forms into asphalt mixtures, synthesizing a complete and quantitative understanding is hindered by the heterogeneity across studies in lignin type, mixing protocols, dosage selection, and performance evaluation methodologies. To address these inconsistencies, this systematic review aims to evaluate the meta-analysis of lignin as a renewable asphalt modifier for asphalt performance improvement. Five research databases were searched using a meta-analysis methodology: Web of Science, Science Direct, PubMed, EBSCO, and Google Scholar. In order to assess the sustainability impact of lignin on asphalt, meta-analyses of 54 pertinent variables were conducted on 39 published articles. Based on the random forest model analysis, lignin emerged as an influential factor affmecting the mechanical properties, stability, durability, thermal characteristics, and chemical performance of asphalt mixtures and binders. The analysis further indicated that lignin could reduce the fatigue damage rate, permeability, and ductility of the asphalt. Subgroup analyses identified outcome-specific moderator effects, particularly for mixing-related conditions, whereas meta-regression showed that lignin type, mixing method, dosage, and study location contributed significantly to between-study heterogeneity. These results highlight lignin's potential as a viable renewable modifier for performance enhancement and sustainability goals, while also indicating that performance gains depend on source-specific chemistry and processing conditions. Future studies should prioritize standardized protocols and field-scale validation.

title: Comparing approaches to identify social risks in upstream supply chains: a case study on critical raw materials incorporated in solid oxide electrolysis cells
abstract: The volume and relevance of social impacts assessments have been rising in the last few years, in line with the needs of a sustainable development. However, these assessments remain occasional, and methodologies lack maturity. This study explores two methodological approaches to social risks and opportunities identification: a quantitative analysis, inspired by the Social Life Cycle Assessment (SLCA) methodology and a semi-quantitative analysis based on documentary research involving a panel of online sources. These approaches are applied to the Critical Raw Materials (CRM) necessary to the manufacturing of a Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cell (SOEC). For every material, the mining and refining steps are studied, considering the main producing countries. Results present social risks levels for the affected stakeholders (local communities, workers, society, value chain actors, consumers and children). Social hotspots are compared, highlighting strengths and limitations of the methods and ultimately indicating that both could reveal to be insufficient on their own. Countries with medium to high social risks are often identified as such by both approaches whereas stakeholders affected can differ. The SLCA-inspired analysis covers a wide range of social indicators, and data are easily accessible, but its low data granularity is a setback for interpretating results. On the other hand, the documentary analysis shows a crucial lack of data availability for some materials, but provides contextual and recent reporting of events. The application of both approaches in this study enabled exclusively social risks identification, showing the need for an approach that can better integrate social opportunities.

title: Can carbon emissions trading increase corporate carbon risk premium?
abstract: Whether the carbon emissions trading (CET) can increase corporate carbon risk premiums (CRP) is crucial for carbon emission reduction and corporate development in China. This paper theoretically analyses the intrinsic mechanism of CET affecting corporate CRP from two levels of default risk and stock price information efficiency. Then, based on the data of 837 heavily polluting listed corporations from 2010 to 2022, the effect of CET on corporate CRP is empirically analyzed using a Double Machine Learning(DML) model. The findings show that carbon emission rights trading enhances corporate CRP in general. The validity of this conclusion is supported by extensive robustness. The mechanism analysis concludes that CET can affect corporate carbon risk premium through the default risk mechanism and the stock liquidity mechanism, and the positive effect of the default risk mechanism is greater than the negative effect of the stock price information efficiency mechanism. The discussion and analysis conclude that although CET can increase default risk by raising abatement costs and financing costs,it can also improve the information efficiency of stock price by reducing information asymmetry and increasing investor concerns. Therefore, after participating in CET, corporations should pay more attention to default risk and stock price information to better manage CRP.

title: National-level evaluation of the socio-economic benefits of biomass supply through the aeroponic technology in cultivating Short Rotation Coppice willows
abstract: Fossil fuels release large quantities of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, with bioenergy offering a more sustainable alternative to fossil fuels. However, the shortage of biomass feedstocks limits the ability to produce bioenergy on a large scale. Short Rotation Coppice willow (SRCw) is recognised as a potential biomass feedstock, with the potential to accelerate their cultivation utilising aeroponic technology. In this study, a Dynamic Biomass-embedded Computable General equilibrium (DBGE) model is proposed to simulate the long-term potential impacts arising from the enhanced biomass supply achieved through aeroponic technology in the UK socio-economic system. Various scenarios related to technology, market, biomass application and policy are also discussed. The results show that the use of aeroponic technology to cultivate SRCw can bring significant socio-economic benefits, such as GDP, renewable energy sector output, employment, and resident welfare. Among the three cultivation environments, i.e., polytunnel, greenhouse, and field multiplication bed, polytunnel cultivation technology brings greater benefits. Based on conservative estimates (narrower technology application scope, lower SRCw planting density, and lower expected biomass yield), by 2050, aeroponic technology under polytunnel can bring a cumulative 10.7% positive impact on GDP. Our study suggests that the wide application of aeroponic technology in cultivating SRCw could contribute to the mitigation of biomass feedstock shortage and promote development of the bioenergy sector and socio-economic benefits in the UK.

title: Turning constraints into gains: Climate-smart agriculture adoption improves maize yield and yield stability under production constraints
abstract: Climate change threats global crop yield, particularly in vulnerable regions like Henan Province in China, where maize yield remains low and highly variable. To address these challenges, Climate-smart Agriculture (CSA) offers a promising solution. Using cross-sectional data from 432 maize farmers, this study constructs a CSA adoption index and applies a Multinomial Endogenous Switching Regression (MESR) and Random Forest (RF) to assess and validate the impact of CSA adoption on maize yield. Results show higher CSA adoption level weakens key production constraints including poor soil fertility and extreme weather conditions, and shifts yield determinants from external resource dependence toward internal capabilities like education. MESR estimates further show that if transitioning to high adoption, low adopters would increase yield by 599.3 kg/ha (10.50%) and medium adopters would increase yield by 288.4 kg/ha (7.55%). Additionally, higher adoption improves yield stability. Under the counterfactual high-adoption scenario, the coefficient of variation (CV) declines from 0.136 to 0.096 for low adopters and from 0.108 to 0.086 for medium adopters, and the interquartile range (IQR) falls from 1140.5 kg/ha to 854.8 kg/ha for low adopters and from 802.1 kg/ha to 631.5 kg/ha for medium adopters, indicating more stable yields at higher adoption. These improvements in maize yield and stability provide evidence for the effectiveness of higher CSA adoption under production constraints, supporting more resource-efficient and resilient maize production under growing climate uncertainty and resource constraints.

title: Understanding Zebrafish predation on microplastics: The impact of multimodal sensory cues
abstract: The widespread contamination of aquatic ecosystems by microplastics (MPs) has raised urgent concerns about their ecotoxicological impacts on fish species. While previous studies have focused on direct MPs toxicity, the critical role of sensory cues in mediating fish-MPs interactions remains poorly understood. This investigation systematically examines how six potential infochemicals (three visual cues: rhodamine B, methylene blue, methyl green; three olfactory signals: dimethyl-beta-propiothetin, albumen powder, oxytetracycline) and their multimodal interactions influence polyethylene MPs (PE-MPs) predation behavior in zebrafish (Danio rerio). Olfactory infochemicals demonstrated significantly greater influence than visual cues in modulating zebrafish predation propensity toward PE-MPs. Zebrafish exhibited adaptive recognition capabilities, developing conditioned avoidance toward PE-MPs loaded with inedible infochemical signatures. However, multimodal sensory integration (tactile-visual-olfactory combinations) disrupted this discrimination capacity, increasing PE-MPs consumption through sensory conflict mechanisms. The surface of PE-MPs becomes rougher after passing through the zebrafish digestive tract, with the formation of 1–10 μm flaky or spherical MPs on the surface of PE-MPs. The findings emphasize the need to incorporate multisensory environmental parameters in aquatic risk assessments and inform the development of bioinspired MPs mitigation strategies.

title: Towards cleaner industrial steam generation: Dynamic performance optimization and control of an auto-cascade heat pump for waste heat recovery
abstract: Recovering industrial waste heat for steam generation via high-temperature heat pump (HTHP) technology is a pivotal pathway toward industrial decarbonization. While recent literature has demonstrated the thermodynamic advantages of various zeotropic mixture heat pumps under steady-state conditions, their dynamic operational stability and controllability under unavoidable industrial waste heat fluctuations remain a critical unexplored gap. To address this, this study proposes a parallel compression auto-cascade HTHP using the environmentally benign low global warming potential (GWP) mixture R1234ze(E)/R1336mzz(Z) to replace high-carbon emitters. To accurately predict transient behaviors, a finite volume dynamic model was constructed, integrating experimentally validated heat transfer correlations specific to this zeotropic mixture. Sensitivity analysis identified critical operational barriers: heat source fluctuations caused superheat surges (up to 9.2 K) or liquid slugging risks, destabilizing the system. To overcome these, a control strategy was implemented, which successfully locked superheat at 5 K, reduced response time by 60 %, and improved the coefficient of performance (COP) by 3.5 %-directly translating to reduced electricity consumption. Furthermore, the study characterizes a passive “self-adaptive” composition shift mechanism: under partial loads, the phase separator spontaneously re-equilibrates the circulating composition, acting as a thermodynamic buffer to maintain performance. Finally, evaporator geometry optimization via a Python-Dymola framework yielded an additional 2.3 % efficiency gain. These results demonstrate that integrating dynamic control with zeotropic fluid properties provides a robust, low-carbon solution for unstable industrial waste heat recovery.

title: Governing green: Unpacking inclusive leadership for sustainability transitions in agriculture
abstract: This study investigates the role of green inclusive leadership in accelerating sustainability transitions within the agricultural sector of Ngawi, East Java, Indonesia. Drawing upon resource orchestration theory, the research conceptualises green inclusive leadership through four key dimensions: vision and sustainability messaging, upskilling and support, budget allocation, and inclusive leadership practices. Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, qualitative data were collected from 47 diverse stakeholders, including government officials, extension workers, and community leaders. These insights were informed by a quantitative survey administered to 657 farmers across 19 sub-districts. Structural equation modelling revealed that green inclusive leadership significantly enhances farmers’ adoption of sustainable agricultural practices by strengthening social norms, building trust, and increasing perceptions of government support. The impact of leadership was moderated by gender, highlighting the need for inclusive and gender-responsive policy frameworks that address diverse farmer needs and promote equitable participation. The study contributes to leadership theory by contextualising green inclusive leadership within the agricultural sustainability challenges of a developing country and advances methodological rigour through robust mixed-method validation. It provides actionable guidance for policymakers, agricultural leaders, and development practitioners seeking to implement culturally aligned, participatory leadership strategies that effectively promote environmental stewardship and rural resilience. This research bridges leadership theory with cleaner production scholarship by linking leadership mechanisms to the adoption of green practices, offering critical insights that support broader sustainability goals in emerging economies.

title: Zero-waste removal and sustainable reuse of rubber lining by air-jet with ultra-low-temperature ice particles: A novel green cleaning strategy
abstract: The periodic removal of aged rubber linings from industrial pipelines generates significant waste and poses environmental challenges when using conventional removal methods. This study proposes an air-jet with ultra-low-temperature ice particles (AJUIP) technology for an efficient and eco-friendly rubber removal. Through experimental measurements, numerical simulations, and theoretical modeling, the temperature variation, material removal mechanisms, and parameter effects were systematically investigated. The results demonstrated that the cleaning process involves dynamic thermal competition between the impact-induced heating and the ice-layer cooling, with a surface temperature stabilizing near −3.9 °C. The rubber fragmentation followed a mixed ductile-brittle fracture mode, characterized by crack networks and rock-like morphologies. The key parameters, such as gas pressure and target distance, were optimized to maximize the cleaning efficiency. From an engineering perspective, the AJUIP process achieves near-zero waste generation by directly converting the waste lining into high-quality, reusable rubber particles, offering a practical pathway that aligns with circular economy principles and advances sustainable industrial maintenance.

title: Bioremediation of arsenic in calcareous soil by microbial-induced calcium carbonate precipitation and attapulgite in arid northwest China
abstract: Microbially induced calcite precipitation (MICP) provides a promising approach for the in situ stabilization of cationic heavy metals in soil; however, substantial challenges remain regarding arsenic (As) remediation and the long-term stability of treatment effectiveness. In this study, urease-producing bacteria isolated from As-contaminated calcareous soil, together with six natural attapulgite types, were applied for 150 days in both laboratory and field experiments. The results demonstrated that calcium and nitrogen sources significantly influenced As remediation efficiency, with a maximum removal efficiency of 61% achieved at 60 mM calcium chloride and 6% urea. Compared with single treatments, attapulgite addition enhanced the transformation of labile As species into more stable fractions, primarily due to its water-soluble calcium content and the presence of chlorite and palygorskite. Combined bacterial and attapulgite treatment significantly increased urease activity and calcium carbonate accumulation while decreasing soil pH, indicating sustained microbial activity and ongoing biomineralization. Calcium- and iron-rich domains within attapulgite supplied calcium for microbial mineralization and facilitated As fixation through coprecipitation and embedding into aluminosilicate clay matrices, forming a calcium carbonate–based microbial metal pump. Arsenic concentrations in remediated maize grains and associated dietary exposure risks remained within safe limits. Overall, integrating locally abundant attapulgite with MICP represents a promising and scalable strategy for remediating As -contaminated calcareous soils.

title: Predicting chemical dosages and settled water quality in water treatment via an interpretable dual-level feature attention transformer
abstract: Ensuring a safe and sustainable drinking water supply is challenging due to raw water quality fluctuations, complex treatment processes, and stringent regulatory requirements. Accurately predicting chemical dosages and treatment outcomes is essential for optimizing treatment efficiencies. Although deep learning models have demonstrated strong predictive performance, their application in water treatment remains limited by insufficient feature-level interpretability for operational decision-making. This study introduces a novel transformer-based framework incorporating a dual-level feature attention mechanism (i.e., single-feature attention for temporal patterns per feature and cross-feature attention) to enhance interpretability while achieving high predictive accuracy. The proposed model was applied to predict chemical dosages (coagulant [mg L−1], pre- and mid-chlorine [mg L−1]) and settled water quality (turbidity [NTU] and residual chlorine [mg L−1]) in a water treatment plant. Compared with baseline models (MLP, GRU, CNN-GRU, and Autoformer), the proposed model consistently improved prediction accuracy (R2) by 2−232% and reduced error metrics (MAE, MAPE, MSE, and nRMSE) by 3−98% across all target variables. Feature importance scores derived from the proposed model revealed that raw water turbidity was the dominant predictor of coagulant dosages and settled water turbidity, while raw water TOC strongly influenced chemical dosages and residual chlorine. By providing accurate predictions together with transparent feature-level interpretability, the proposed framework supports data-driven chemical dosing strategies, contributing to chemical savings and ultimately to cleaner water treatment operations.

title: Deep carbon option: A transfer learning method for carbon derivatives valuation based on option pricing theory
abstract: Carbon options are significantly influenced by policy interventions and external economic fluctuations, which pose substantial challenges to conventional financial option pricing models. Moreover, the limited availability and imbalanced distribution of carbon option data often hinder the performance of deep learning approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposes a transfer learning framework-Deep Carbon Option-which is grounded in financial option pricing theory for carbon option pricing. The framework first utilizes structural financial models, selected to reflect the jump dynamics and regime switching characteristics inherent in carbon option markets, to generate simulated pricing data. Those data are then employed to embed essential theoretical knowledge into a convolutional neural network (CNN) through pre-training. Subsequently, a time series analysis module, MordernTCN, is incorporated into the CNN architecture and fine-tuned on real carbon option data, enhancing pricing efficiency in carbon market. Additionally, attention mechanisms are integrated to enhance cross-channel information fusion, further improving the model’s adaptability and predictive power in practical scenarios. For empirical validation, we employed a dataset of European Carbon Emission Allowance options from the European Energy Exchange for training and evaluation. Ablation studies, comparative experiments, and the Diebold–Mariano test demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing approaches, particularly in scenarios with limited sample data near the option’s maturity date.

title: Kinetic modeling, parameter estimation, and techno-economic optimization for producing kraft lignin-isolated soy protein bio-adhesive
abstract: This work develops an integrated framework combining reaction kinetic modeling, plant-wide process simulation, and techno-economic optimization for the production of a formaldehyde-free, sustainable bio-adhesive. The manufacturing pathway involves the crosslinking of soy protein isolate with a degraded lignin/oligomer solution derived from base-catalyzed depolymerization (BCD) of kraft lignin under high pressure and moderate temperature conditions (140 – 200 °C) by using a mild alkaline catalyst. A lumped kinetic model for the BCD of kraft lignin is developed and its kinetic parameters (e.g., activation energy, pre-exponential factor, base concentration exponent) are optimally estimated by using the experimental data. A representative stoichiometric model for the reaction scheme is also developed. Several plant configurations are proposed for producing 45,408 mt/year bio-adhesive by using a batch reactor, typically used at the laboratory scale, as well as a proposed continuous scale reactor. Plant-wide process models also include heat and mass integration. An economic model is developed. An equation-oriented approach is used for techno-economic optimization for minimizing the levelized cost of adhesive (LCOA). It is found that the plant consisting of a plug flow reactor for the BCD reaction of kraft lignin along with a hybrid heat integration approach via vapor compression and supplementary low pressure steam results in the best economic performance. The minimum LCOA is found to be $634.21/mt, which is very competitive considering the current approximate market price of $1000 – 4000/mt for commercial adhesives, including bio-based adhesives.

title: Plasma-assisted sorption-enhanced H2 production from biomass/plastic co-pyrolysis over multifunctional catalyst: Design, optimization, and mechanistic insights
abstract: The sustainable and efficient conversion of heterogeneous carbonaceous wastes into hydrogen-rich gas is vital for advancing clean energy technologies and addressing the dual challenges of environmental pollution and resource recovery. This study establishes a pioneering plasma-assisted and sorption-enhanced strategy for efficient green H2 production from biomass/plastics mixtures over a structured multifunctional catalyst. The core novelty lies in the synergistic integration of plasma with a structured multifunctional catalyst, enabling simultaneous volatile cracking, catalytic reforming, and in-situ CO2 capture. The Ni-Mg-Ca/γ-Al2O3 catalyst is rationally engineered to integrate reforming activity, Mg/Ca-induced basicity and CO2 capture functionality within a discharge-optimizing monolithic structure. Under non-thermal dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma conditions, the synergistic coupling of plasma and catalyst significantly enhances the decomposition of heavy volatiles, tar cracking and CO2 removal, leading to improved H2 yield and selectivity. The improved in-situ CO2 sorption by CaO and plasma promotes thermodynamically favorable water-gas shift and dry reforming reactions, while the structured design ensures uniform plasma discharge and mitigates catalyst deactivation. Overall, this integrated system demonstrates a promising route for low-temperature, modular H2 production from mixed carbonaceous wastes, offering both catalytic efficiency and operational flexibility. The proposed strategy highlights the potential of combining plasma catalysis with in-situ CO2 sorption for next-generation waste-to-hydrogen energy technologies.

title: Too fast to balance? past trends and multi-scenario of land use intensity and landscape ecological risk in China
abstract: Over the past three decades, intensified human activities have increased land use intensity (LUI), thereby affecting landscape ecological risk (LER), yet the long-term national-scale coupling between the LUI and LER and its future trajectories under different scenarios remain poorly understood. To address this gap, this study, taking China as a case study, analyzed the spatiotemporal dynamics of the LUI and LER from 1992 to 2022 across four major regions (Northeast, East, West, and Central China) and also identified key driving factors and evaluated their coupling coordination degree (CCD). Furthermore, this study simulated spatial distributions under multiple 2030 scenarios by using the PLUS model. The results showed that the LUI increased steadily nationwide, with the largest growth in East China, and the smallest with most fluctuating growth in West China. However, regional variations existed: it decreased in Northeast China but increased in West and Central China. In addition, the digital elevation model (DEM) played the dominant role in the LER in most regions, whereas East China was more affected by gross domestic product (GDP), construction land proportion (CLP), population density (PD), and other factors. The CCD remained low and gradually declined, indicating a growing imbalance between land use expansion and ecological protection. Scenario simulations exhibited that both LUI and LER grow most under the natural development scenario (NDS). Ecological coordination, however, was maximized under the ecological protection scenario (EPS). The most pronounced regional differences occurred in Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Hunan, and Sichuan. These findings highlight the persistent imbalance between development and ecological protection, providing a scientific basis for region-specific strategies to achieve sustainable land management and mitigate ecological risk in China.

title: Coupling input-output analysis with deep learning to quantify the carrying capacity of water resource for sustainable development in arid region
abstract: Precisely quantifying carrying capacity of water resource (CCWR) can address the imbalance between water supply and water demand thus, and promote socio-economic and environmentally sustainable development of water-scarce regions. Through coupling input-output analysis with deep learning methods, an input-output CNN-LSTM-Attention (abbreviated as IOCLA) model is developed. IOCLA has advantages in identifying the key drivers of virtual water, predicting future water supply and water demand, and shrinking water shortage under socioeconomic and climate scenarios (SSPs-RCPs). Methodologically, IOCLA also excels at tracing economy-wide virtual-water transfers along supply chains and capturing nonlinear spatiotemporal dynamics. IOCLA is then applied to the Inner-Shaan-Ning region (a typical arid region located in the upper reaches of the Yellow River Basin), which economic development is constrained by the shortage of water resources. The main findings are summarized as follows: (i) in the Inner-Shaan-Ning region, the main driving factors of virtual water are water intensity, investment, exports, and imports; (ii) water shortages are lowest under SSP126 and highest under SSP585 (e.g., by 2050, water shortages rank as SSP126 < SSP245 < SSP370 < SSP585); (iii) compared with SSP245, SSP370, and SSP585, the CCWR under SSP126 increases by 6.7%, 23.1%, and 45.4%, respectively, indicating that SSP126 scenario is more suitable for this region. The findings are conductive to adjusting industrial structure, reducing the imbalance between water supply and demand, and facilitating socio-economic and environmentally sustainable development.

title: Integrated thermal dechlorination and catalytic pyrolysis of PVC for aromatic-rich oil with low organic chlorine content
abstract: The production of aromatic-rich oil with low organic chlorine content represents a pivotal challenge in PVC pyrolysis. To address this, an integrated process combining thermal dechlorination and catalytic pyrolysis of PVC was investigated in a two-stage fixed bed reactor. The results indicated that a high temperature significantly enhanced the dechlorination efficiency and promoted the aromatization of de-HCl PVC. 340 °C was chosen as an optimal temperature for the preliminary thermal dechlorination step, achieving a dechlorination efficiency of 89.94%. As pyrolysis temperature increased, tar cracking was strengthened, and the conversion of organic chlorine to inorganic one was facilitated. On the other hand, CO2 accelerated the retention of organic chlorine compounds in the liquid phase product, and its organic chlorine content was about 1.4 times higher than that in N2. Finally, the addition of coconut shell derived biochar or HZSM-5 zeolite enhanced secondary tar cracking, leading to the increased HCl yield and reduced organic chlorine content. HZSM-5 zeolite exhibited the superior catalytic performance. Moreover, compared to the direct catalytic pyrolysis, the stepwise mode not only decreased organic chlorine content, but also mitigated chlorine deposition on the catalysts and lowered its poisoning risk. Thus, a two-stage integrated process was proposed: an initial thermal dechlorination of PVC at 340 °C, followed by a catalytic pyrolysis of de-HCl PVC over HZSM-5 zeolite at 600 °C in N2. The process produced a liquid phase product with an organic chlorine content of 73.61 mg/g and an aromatic yield of 11.7%. This study establishes a practical and efficient strategy for PVC waste valorization, providing a scientific basis for its industrial-scale pyrolysis application.

title: Phycosphere microbial assembly reinforces microalgae-driven soil organic carbon sequestration and methane mitigation in black soil paddies
abstract: Global climate change threatens food security, with paddy fields being major greenhouse gas sources. Microalgae, as novel inoculants, show contested emission effects and unclear synergy with phycosphere bacteria. Integrating meta-analysis and incubation experiments, we systematically investigated microalgae-bacteria interactions in black soil paddy fields. Microalgae significantly increased the response ratio of soil organic carbon (+1.0644, 95% CI: +0.7625 to +1.3663) and reduced the response ratio of methane emissions (−1.1713, 95% CI: −1.7316 to −0.611). Live-microalgae drove methane mitigation via a dual-pathway, suppressing mcrA and enhancing pmoA gene abundance, enriching type I methanotrophs (e.g., Methylobacter) while inhibiting key methanogens. Microalgae specifically recruited abundant, diverse phycosphere bacteria, forming functional microniches. The microalgae-bacteria consortium (MA + B) exhibited optimal synergy, reducing CH4 emissions by 47.78%, and increasing SOC by 5.71%, linked to elevated dissolved oxygen, extracellular polymeric substances, and bacterial-derived carbon. This study reveals microalgae enhance carbon sequestration by reshaping microbial networks, offering a new paradigm for sustainable agriculture.

title: Multi-scenario simulation of mountain land gradient use and carbon emission assessment: A case study of the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration, China
abstract: Owing to the complex and varied topography of mountainous regions, land use displays pronounced vertical zonation characteristics. Guided by the carbon neutrality agenda, accurately projecting future trajectories of land gradient use and associated carbon emissions has become a fundamental prerequisite for advancing regional low-carbon transitions. Based on the case of the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration, this research first evaluates the current carbon emissions related to land gradient use, then constructs a coupled model to conduct multi-scenario simulations for optimizing land gradient use and forecasting future carbon trajectories. Results indicate that the proposed simulation model effectively overcomes the limitations of conventional two-dimensional approaches, enabling refined projections of future land-use dynamics and associated carbon trajectories in mountainous regions. Across five projected scenarios, both the structural composition and spatial configuration of land gradient use exhibit significant vertical differentiation. Specifically, cropland, water bodies, urban land, rural settlements, and industrial-mining land decline with increasing gradient, while woodland and grassland display an inverted U-shaped distribution, and unused land expands markedly in higher-gradient zones. By 2035, total carbon emissions across all scenarios are projected to be lower than in 2020, with the SSP1-2.6 scenario yielding the most substantial reduction, and the historical development scenario yielding the highest emissions. Aligning the future development trajectory of the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration with the SSP1-2.6 pathway offers the greatest potential for supporting the carbon neutrality strategy. This study provides a scientific foundation and methodological reference for enhancing territorial spatial optimization and promoting green, low-carbon development in mountainous regions.

title: Explainable AI-driven energy prediction and optimization for cleaner intelligent weaving: A hybrid large language model and weaving graph method
abstract: In the field of intelligent weaving, energy consumption of looms is influenced by multiple factors such as process parameters, operating conditions, and production stability, which are highly interrelated. Traditional energy consumption modeling methods struggle to achieve high accuracy in prediction and energy-saving decisions under complex and variable working conditions. To address this, this study proposes a hybrid intelligent framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with a weaving knowledge graph (WKG) to enable a closed-loop application for energy prediction, interpretable reasoning, and optimization recommendation generation. The framework achieves energy consumption modeling based on variable-rank adaptive fine-tuning, which allows the model to automatically adjust its rank value under different operating conditions to balance prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Additionally, the constructed weaving knowledge graph endows the model with multi-layer causal reasoning abilities, enabling the explanation of the mechanisms behind factors such as yarn tension, weaving speed, and machine stoppage behavior in influencing energy consumption changes, thereby enhancing the model's interpretability (Explainable AI). Validation based on actual workshop data shows that the model has an average absolute error (MAE) of 103.92 kWh and an average absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.73%, outperforming traditional methods in prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and adaptability to multiple working conditions. Further field deployment results indicate that the system can monitor equipment status in real-time and generate energy-saving optimization recommendations, effectively supporting clean production and sustainable operation of the weaving process, and providing a new paradigm for the fusion of AI and manufacturing knowledge. System demonstrations and application examples can be accessed at: http://106.12.219.66:81/agent/#/.

title: Biomimetic strategy enhanced microalgal CO2 fixation via dual synergies in photosynthetic electron flow
abstract: The escalating atmospheric CO2 concentration underscores the urgent need for clean and sustainable carbon mitigation strategies. Photosynthetic microalgae play a vital role in global carbon fixation and hold great promise for sustainable CO2 sequestration and bioenergy production. However, their practical application is often constrained by inefficient photosynthetic electron transport, which limits overall carbon conversion efficiency. While traditional methods, such as conductive nanomaterials, are hindered by low bioavailability and oxidative toxicity, we propose a class of biomimetic iron-ligand complexes that overcome these limitations through coordination structures mimicking natural electron carriers. Here, we propose a class of biomimetic iron-ligand complexes to enhance electron diffusion in Calvin cycle and avoid the nanotoxicity of oxidative stress. Among three candidates evaluated, iron(II)-2-(2′-thiazolylazo)-p-cresol (Fe-TAC) exhibited the most pronounced enhancement, boosting carbon fixation by 2.71-fold and improving photosynthetic energy efficiency by 3.38-fold. Mechanistic investigations attributed this enhancement to a dual-synergy mechanism. First, enhanced extracellular electron shuttling is mediated by electroactive EPS into photosystem II (PS-II). Furthermore, internalized electrons accelerated intracellular linear electron flow (LEF) through activated photosystems I and II, as evidenced by improved photosynthetic parameters (Fv/Fm, ETR, qP). A series of results proved that the biomimetic iron-ligand complexes optimized the entire photosynthetic electron transport chain. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for employing biomimetic electron carriers to boost microalgal photosynthesis. This biomimetic strategy uses natural components to safely boost carbon fixation, avoiding the bioavailability, toxicity, efficiency, and cost issues of synthetic alternatives. It thus offers a scalable, ecologically compatible pathway for integrating microalgal carbon capture and utilization (CCU) into circular bioeconomy systems.

title: The carbon–cooling paradox: Delayed rebound of urban heat risk following green industrial transition
abstract: Decarbonization is widely assumed to deliver co-benefits for urban cooling, yet its thermal consequences over time remain poorly understood. Using panel data from 284 Chinese cities (2001–2020), this study reveals a previously overlooked Carbon–Cooling Paradox, whereby green industrial transition initially suppresses urban heat risk but subsequently induces a delayed rebound. We develop a dynamic early-warning framework based on time-lagged cross-correlation analysis to quantify the hysteresis between industrial restructuring and heat risk. Results show a robust two-phase heat-risk response following industrial restructuring: an inhibition period (mean lag 2.86 years) followed by a rebound period (mean lag 4.61 years), creating a critical mid-term risk window often missed by static policy assessments. The rebound intensity is highly uneven, with stronger penalties in lower-tier cities and in Southern Subtropical and Temperate regions, while high-GDP cities exhibit more durable inhibition. These findings challenge the assumption of synchronous mitigation–adaptation benefits and highlight the need for time-sensitive, differentiated urban resilience strategies during low-carbon transitions.

title: Integrated coal-water mining strategy: evaluating the ecological support potential of mining-induced water in Western China
abstract: In the ecologically fragile coal mining regions of western China, high-intensity mining leads to massive groundwater drainage and wastage, exacerbating regional water scarcity. Transforming the mining-induced water resources into a supply for ecological restoration is a critical cleaner production strategy for balancing energy extraction and environmental protection. Taking the Chahasu coal mine as a case study, this research investigates the dynamic evolution and resource utilization potential of mining-induced water resources. A lifecycle stage model was established based on water flow patterns and the self-healing characteristics of mining-induced fractures. To ensure precise water volume calculation and prediction, an improved equivalent large-diameter well method was proposed for the mining stage, while a long-term prediction model integrating Bi-LSTM-Attention with an adaptive multi-population genetic algorithm was developed for the post-mining recovery stage. Additionally, a volume potential evaluation system using AHP-Entropy-TOPSIS was constructed to calibrate the prediction results. Results indicate that water volume follows a non-linear growth pattern, reaching a corrected final annual volume of 187.73 × 104 m3 with a prediction error below 5%. Crucially, the supply-demand balance analysis shows that the annual mining-induced water resources available for ecological restoration during the mining stage is 75.09 × 104 m3, which is higher than the ecological vegetation water demand of 66.82 × 104 m3. Furthermore, predictions confirm that the water volume can continue to sustainably meet this demand even after mine closure. This study provides a theoretical basis and technical support for integrated coal-water mining, promoting a circular economy and sustainable development in mining areas.

title: Energy-efficient drying via an advanced conveyor-based tumbling cold plasma system: Enhancing process efficiency and industrial sustainability
abstract: The industrial application of cold plasma (CP) in food drying is impeded by the absence of conveyor-compatible apparatus and empirical data about energy, environmental, and economic efficacy. This study developed an advanced conveyor-based tumbling CP device utilizing gliding-arc discharge, with a chain-belt drive system that concurrently flips and transports samples to provide continuous and uniform exposure of blueberries. The findings indicated that treating 1 kg of blueberries required merely 0.96% of the device's power for the tumbling action, while the overall CP module accounted for approximately 1% of the total electricity consumed for CP treatment and drying. Nonetheless, CP pretreatment reduced total drying time by 27.59–65.52% (up to 570 min), enhanced energy efficiency from 2.91% to 8.41% (+189%), and decreased specific energy consumption from 80.72 to 27.88 MJ/kg (−65.46%) along with CO2 emissions by up to 65.45% per kg of water evaporated. CP-treated dried blueberries exhibited a 32.09–94.25% increase in total phenolic content and a 31.15–68.54% enhancement in antioxidant capacity compared to the control, without negative alterations in color. Techno-economic analysis revealed that CP treatment reduced the payback period from 7.84 years to a range of 1.22 to 4.68 years. The alterations in microstructure and moisture distribution indicated that CP-induced cuticle etching, membrane breakdown, and water state redistribution were fundamental to the accelerated moisture removal. This study presents quantitative evidence that CP pretreatment can be integrated into commercial drying systems to facilitate low-carbon, high-quality food processing.

title: Green synthesis of glycerol carbonate from glycerol and CO2 using a polymeric ionic liquid catalyst: An experimental and theoretical study
abstract: The catalytic conversion of waste glycerol (GLY) and emitted CO2 to produce glycerol carbonate (GC) is a promising approach for adding value to waste products and reducing CO2 emissions. However, the selectivity and yield of the traditional catalytic method remain low. In this study, propylene oxide (PO) was introduced to replace conventional dehydration agents, and quaternary ammonium ionic liquids having different halide counterions (I−, Cl−, and Br−) were used as catalysts. The addition of PO resulted in a two-step GLY/CO2 reaction involving cycloaddition and transesterification. The addition of the quaternary ammonium ionic liquid catalyst resulted in the reaction becoming thermodynamically favorable. Among the studied catalysts, the iodide-containing quaternary ammonium ionic liquid, denoted PDBA-I, showed the best catalytic yield of 69.4% of glycerol carbonate after self-polymerization. In addition, solvent effects were investigated, and the combination of PDBA-I with methanol achieved a GC yield of 77.2% under mild conditions (100 °C and 15 bar of CO2). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed the experimentally observed reduction in the activation energy barrier and the roles of GLY and PO. These findings highlight the unique advantage of employing a halide-containing quaternary ammonium ionic liquid catalyst, offering new insights and an effective strategy for achieving highly active GLY carboxylation.

title: Model-driven AI analysis and optimization of a dynamic continuous stirring tank reactor system for biofuel production by lignin bio-oil upgrading
abstract: This study develops an integrated mechanistic-data-driven AI framework to model a biofuel production process by the conversion of lignin-derived bio-oil with the hydrodeoxygenation of isoeugenol (I-HDO). A transient continuous stirring tank reactor (CSTR) model is developed utilizing experimentally supported kinetics and is then employed to generate an extensive database. Multiple artificial neural networks are evaluated to recognize the reactor behavior, among which the double-layer cascade feedforward scheme trained with the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno algorithm (DLCFF-trainbfg) delivers the highest accuracy (an average absolute relative deviation of 1.04%) without violating physical constraints. Statistical error analyses further confirm the reliability of this model, which is subsequently utilized to conduct a sensitivity analysis of the process. Sensitivity analysis reveals the dominant influence of feed temperature, flow rate, and concentration, as well as catalyst load on steady-state establishment, reaction mechanism and product distribution, product yields, biofuel quality, and hydrogen requirement. Then, the DLCFF-trainbfg model is integrated with a genetic algorithm to determine optimal operating conditions that yield the highest production rates of propylcyclohexene and propylcyclohexane and heating value in tandem with the lowest hydrogen consumption. The optimized condition resulted in a rapid development to a steady-state regime (3.58 h) and a high-energy-density (48.66 MJkg) biofuel stream rich in propylcyclohexene and propylcyclohexane (hydrocarbon yield of 66.23 wt%), while minimizing oxygenates yield (1.63 wt%) and hydrogen consumption (1.272 m3hr). The results confirm that the hybrid AI-assisted approach accurately describes I-HDO behavior, provides computationally efficient optimization, and offers a scalable pathway for the design and intensification of lignin-derived biofuel production.

title: Multifunctional additive-driven efficient critical metal recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries via all-solid-state subcritical process
abstract: The sustainable recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is crucial for ensuring resource security and minimizing environmental impact. To address this challenge, we developed an innovative all-solid-state (ASS) subcritical process using FeCl2·4H2O as a multifunctional reaction mediator. This method achieves near-quantitative recovery of valuable metals (99.9%) from LiNixCoyMnzO2 (NCM) cathode materials. In our process, spent NCM are directly mixed with solid FeCl2·4H2O and heated under controlled subcritical conditions. This initiates a rapid structural breakdown of the cathode material, facilitated by a synergistic redox reaction involving Fe2+ and in-situ generated HCl. As a result, the valuable metals are efficiently leached out in just 10 min, using an ultra-low amount of water (low liquid-solid ratio). Mechanistic investigations reveal a dual activation pathway: thermal hydrolysis of Fe2+ generating proton flux for lattice protonation, and chloride-assisted electron transfer inducing transition metal reduction. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations quantitatively demonstrate the synergistic effect of different components of FeCl2⋅4H2O in destabilizing the NCM lattice framework. This closed-loop process exhibits exceptional sustainability metrics, including zero acid consumption, significant energy reduction, and substantially reduced aqueous emissions. The methodology establishes a techno-economically viable paradigm for next-generation green battery recycling infrastructures.

title: Synergistic electrocatalytic-biological degradation of Ni-EDTA in a baffled three-dimensional reactor: Performance optimization and mechanism analysis
abstract: Ni-ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (Ni-EDTA) complexes pose significant challenges for sustainable wastewater treatment due to their stability and resistance to conventional removal methods. This study develops an integrated baffled three-dimensional electro-biological coupling reactor (BTD-EBR) as a sustainable solution for Ni-EDTA wastewater treatment, aligning with cleaner production principles by synergizing energy-efficient electrocatalysis with biological processes. The system synergized electrocatalysis (0.35 mA/cm2) with spatially segregated aerobic (•OH-mediated decomplexation) and anaerobic (Trichococcus-dominated biodegradation) zones, achieving removal efficiencies of 69.71% (Ni-EDTA), 93.76% (chemical oxygen demand, COD), and 94.43% (ammonium nitrogen, NH4+-N), outperforming controls (current density, CD = 0) by 56.25%, 13.50%, and 19.11%, respectively. Mechanistic analysis revealed aerobic zones contributed 34–46% efficiency via •OH/active chlorine oxidation, while anaerobic zones achieved 47–58% COD removal through hydrolysis. Compared to conventional Fenton processes, the BTD-EBR demonstrated 45% lower global warming potential (GWP), 70% sludge reduction, and operational cost savings of ¥1.5 perton. Microbial analysis revealed enrichment of Trichococcus, Nitrospira, and Hydrogenophaga, with metabolic pathways (e.g., citrate cycle, environmental metabolism) critical for Ni-EDTA breakdown. Electrochemical processes destabilized Ni-EDTA, while biofilms enhanced biosorption and biodegradation. This work provides a scalable, energy-efficient solution for refractory metal-organic wastewater treatment, aligning with circular economy principles.

title: Modified bentonite-catalyzed oxidation of typical odorous substances in wastewater: comparison of H2O2 and ClO2 systems and mechanism study
abstract: In recent years, industrial emissions and waste treatment have increasingly contributed to organic odour pollution, necessitating efficient degradation technologies for typical odorous substances like dimethyl disulfide, trichloroethylene, and p-xylene. This study innovatively employs acid- and iron-modified bentonite (Fe-H-Bent) as a catalyst to enhance the oxidation performance of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and chlorine dioxide (ClO2) systems, addressing the limitations of low oxidant utilization in conventional methods. By comparing degradation efficiencies, the Fe-H-Bent + ClO2 system demonstrated superior removal rates (99% for DMDS, 91% for TCE, and 87% for p-xylene under optimal conditions: catalyst-to-oxidant ratio of 1:2, 40 °C, pH = 3), attributed to its enhanced redox potential and catalytic active sites. Mechanistic investigations, combined with electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and Fukui function calculations, revealed a dual oxidation pathway: hydroxyl radical (·OH)-mediated attack on methyl-adjacent sites of p-xylene and ClO2-driven electron transfer reactions on para-methyl positions, forming intermediates like 2,5-dimethylphenol and alkyl radicals. This work highlights the synergy between modified bentonite and ClO2, offering a novel, efficient strategy for odorous substance removal in wastewater treatment, with theoretical insights into radical- and electron-transfer co-oxidation mechanisms.

title: Recycled copper and V2G accelerate carbon neutrality in China: Decoupling power and passenger vehicle sectors from copper constraints
abstract: The power and passenger vehicle sectors are critical to the energy transition. Under carbon neutrality targets, the energy transition in these two sectors is heavily dependent on stable supply of copper. However, the existing copper supply may serve as a critical constraint. This study integrates Dynamic Material Flow Analysis and linear programming model to quantify the impacts of copper constraints on carbon mitigation in power and passenger vehicle sectors during 2023-2060, and further assess the carbon mitigation potentials of enhancing recycling and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) adoption. The results show that: 1) China's energy transition in the power and passenger vehicle sectors will generate a cumulative copper supply shortage of 21.9 Mt; 2) Copper constraints significantly curb renewable energy and new energy vehicle (NEV) deployment, resulting in carbon emissions of 2.99 Gt in 2060, exceeding carbon neutrality targets by 16.2%; 3) improved and aggressive recycling will achieve reductions of 11.7% and 13.3% in 2060 compared to the current recycling level; 4) V2G deployment drives progressive emission reductions, approximately achieving an emissions mitigation of 1.5%∼6.2% in 2060; 5) The carbon neutrality targets for these two sectors can be achieved through the synergy between enhanced recycling and V2G: greatly improving copper recycling efficiency combined with a V2G penetration rate exceeding 65% alleviates copper scarcity and closes the resulting carbon emissions gap relative to the Carbon Neutrality Scenario.

title: Corporate responses to the carbon border adjustment mechanism: Impacts, policy interactions, and strategic pathways
abstract: This study examines how the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) affects export-oriented manufacturing firms in Taiwan and shapes their strategic responses toward decarbonization and cleaner production. As CBAM is scheduled to impose carbon charges on selected imports from 2026, carbon-intensive industries—particularly steel, aluminum, cement, and fertilizers—are expected to face rising compliance costs and increasing pressure to adjust production and investment decisions. Using a mixed-methods approach, this study integrates focus group discussions with a structured questionnaire survey and applies the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to analyze firm-level decision-making under multiple criteria. A total of 32 valid responses were collected from Taiwanese firms with actual exports to the European Union. The results indicate that firms place the greatest emphasis on carbon reduction effectiveness, followed by policy support, while cost considerations rank third. This pattern suggests that firms are increasingly willing to pursue structural decarbonization and cleaner production strategies when supported by clear and credible policy incentives. In terms of strategic preferences, firms prioritize direct payment of CBAM charges as a short-term compliance strategy, while mitigation-oriented options—such as participation in domestic decarbonization projects combined with preferential carbon pricing—emerge as viable medium-term alternatives. Overall, these findings provide practical insights into how carbon border measures influence firm-level production strategies and highlight the importance of aligning domestic carbon pricing and policy support mechanisms to facilitate industrial transition toward cleaner production.

title: Predicting and interpreting the effects of steel slag amendment on soil acidification across diverse agricultural conditions
abstract: Soil acidification poses a significant challenge to global agricultural sustainability, while steel slag (SS), as an alkaline industrial by-product, is regarded as a potentially efficient soil amendment. However, existing studies on the application of SS for mitigating soil acidification remain largely confined to regional field trials, lacking quantitative tools capable of efficiently predicting amendment effectiveness and systematically elucidating the underlying mechanisms. This study compiled 211 field experimental records on soil amendment using SS, covering broad gradients in SS properties, soil characteristics, and agronomic scenarios. A machine learning model was constructed to predict the effect of SS amendment on soil acidification, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.929. The results indicate that the application of SS amendment increased soil pH by an average of 1.671. Application rate, initial soil pH, and soil particle size were identified as the primary numerical features influencing improvement effect, with a cumulative importance of 53.813%. A threshold effect was observed at pH = 5.0, below which soils exhibited more pronounced improvements. The results also highlight the trade-off between improvement effect and economic input, as well as the importance of supplementary application to maintain regulatory effects. Overall, this study provides an interpretable and readily accessible decision-support tool for soil management, while offering a methodological and empirical basis for the resourceful utilization of industrial by-products.

title: Revisiting emergy algebra: The cross-looping problem in emergy accounting on systems networks
abstract: Emergy accounting relies on tracing available energy contributions through systems networks using a special set of rules to handle features such as splits, co-products and feedbacks, collectively known as emergy algebra. This algebra has been subject to diverse interpretations and is not always applied consistently in the literature, with important consequences for reported emergy values. This study provides a fundamental examination of two accounting approaches in systems with splits and cycling: the standard emergy algebra and an alternative procedure also referred to as the network method. We describe a phenomenon that seems to have gone unnoticed thus far. This phenomenon, which we term the cross-looping effect, arises from different choices in system partitioning and feedback allocation and significantly affects standard emergy algebra computations. It leads to undesirable and arbitrary variations in computed emergy flows, even though these variations correspond to no real differences in resource use or system performance. In contrast, the alternative emergy algebra is inherently robust to this effect. Through analytical examples and generalisation to an arbitrary number of subsystems, we demonstrate that the results of standard emergy algebra approach those of the alternative method only in a certain limiting case. Overall, our findings expose a limitation of the standard interpretation of the emergy accounting rules when applied to systems featuring recycling, feedbacks or complex network structures and support the use of the alternative emergy algebra in such cases, thereby contributing to more reliable emergy-based sustainability assessments and to a clearer theoretical understanding of emergy computations on networks.

title: Release and reprecipitation of phosphorus during peroxymonosulfate-based sludge disintegration
abstract: Phosphorus recovery from waste activated sludge is essential for sustainable resource management. Peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based oxidation is a promising technique for sludge disintegration and phosphorus release, yet the transformation pathways during disintegration remain poorly understood. This study achieves high phosphorus release efficiency and reveals phosphorus release–reprecipitation process during the treatment. At a PMS dosage of 0.6 mmol/g total suspended solids, concentrations of PO43− and total dissolved phosphorus in sludge supernatant reached a maximum of 99.82 and 107.75 mg/L, enhanced by 99.84% and 112.36% after sludge disintegration. However, a decrease of phosphorus concentration in the sludge supernatant after reaching the peak was observed due to reprecipitation. By combining Visual MINTEQ software simulations with the Standards, Measurements and Testing sequential extraction of solid-phase phosphorus, we confirmed the framework of release-reprecipitation and revealed the dominance shift of reprecipitation between Al3+ and Fe3+. The results revealed that phosphorus reprecipitated with metal ions released by sludge disintegration in supernatant, forming non-apatite inorganic phosphorus dominated by variscite and strengite. When the PMS dosage was within 0.4 mmol/g TSS, Al3+ dominated the reprecipitation process, thereby limiting the release of phosphorus. As the PMS dosage increased to 0.6 mmol/g TSS, Al3+ exhibited a decrease in its reprecipitation effect and Fe3+ replaced Al3+ as the dominant metal ion of reprecipitation, leading to further phosphorus release. The results demonstrate that balancing the release and precipitation of phosphorus can promote efficient phosphorus recovery, providing a critical theoretical foundation for phosphorus resource recovery from sludge.

title: The awareness-action gap in sustainable development: faculty perceptions and practices in Palestinian higher education
abstract: Higher education institutions worldwide are increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable development through teaching, research, and community engagement. Universities play an important role in preparing graduates capable of addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. However, existing research on sustainability in higher education has focused largely on institutions in politically stable and economically advantaged countries. This geographical concentration leaves limited understanding of how sustainability is taught and implemented in contexts affected by prolonged conflict and resource scarcity. Addressing this gap, the present study investigates professors’ perceptions, practices, and challenges related to integrating sustainable development and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals into academic work in Palestinian higher education. The study aims to examine whether faculty awareness of sustainability concepts is reflected in teaching and research practices and to identify institutional conditions that influence implementation. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed. A validated online questionnaire was distributed to full-time faculty members at public universities in the West Bank, producing a final sample of 388 respondents representing a range of academic disciplines. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, and one-way analysis of variance. The findings reveal an awareness–action gap. Although approximately 75% of respondents reported high awareness of the importance of sustainable development, extensive integration was reported by only 28% in teaching and 25% in research. Significant differences were observed by gender, discipline, and professional experience. The results indicate that sustainability approaches developed in stable higher education systems may require adaptation in conflict-affected contexts. The study highlights the importance of faculty development initiatives, institutional incentives, and curricular support to strengthen sustainability education in Palestinian universities.

title: Coordinating carbon and pollution reduction with human settlements in Chinese cities: A key step toward achieving sustainable development goals
abstract: China's rapid urbanization has raised living standards but also intensified environmental pollution, traffic congestion, and housing shortages that threaten human settlements (HS). Coordinating carbon and pollution reduction (CPR) with HS improvement is therefore critical to high-quality green urban development. However, existing studies largely examine CPR and HS separately, with limited attention to whether coordinated emission reduction improves human settlements at the city scale. Most city-level research also focuses mainly on spatial heterogeneity, while giving little attention to intercity networks and directional information flows. To address these gaps, this study uses data from 280 prefecture-level cities to build an integrated framework that combines coupling coordination and spatial association. Separate indicator systems are constructed to quantify CPR and HS, a modified coupling coordination degree model is used to gauge their interdependence, and social network analysis is applied to map spatial linkages within and between the two systems. Results show that (1) both CPR coordinated-development level and HS quality improved over time, with CPR exhibiting a south-high, north-low pattern and HS showing a coastal-high, inland-low pattern; (2) the CPR-HS coupling coordination relationship displayed pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and both coupling degree and coupling coordination degree increased overall with fluctuations, shifting from maladjustment toward coordination, although the overall coordination level remained moderate; and (3) CPR and HS networks showed clear modularity and tightly connected regional structures, while the HS network became slightly denser over time. Cross-system information flows, however, remained weak, with CPR→HS spillovers slightly stronger than HS→CPR. This study integrates urban system coupling with spatial diffusion theory and provides evidence to guide place-specific and cross-regional green governance strategies, thereby promoting sustainable development.

title: Nanoplastic-driven microbial communication breakdown weakens biogeochemical resilience in constructed wetland ecosystems
abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) are increasingly detected in constructed wetlands (CWs), yet we still lack a mechanistic understanding of how nanoscale contaminants disrupt microbial communication and thereby destabilize coupled C-N-P-S cycling. Here, we address this gap by integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, metabolic network reconstruction, and multi-model causal inference to elucidate how NPs perturb cross-habitat microbial cooperation. We demonstrate that NPs do not merely alter community structure; they fundamentally rewire microbial regulatory architecture by (i) inducing sustained oxidative stress that diverts ATP and reducing equivalents toward cellular defense, and (ii) degrading or adsorbing quorum-sensing molecules (AI-2, AHLs), which suppresses key signal synthases (luxS, cqsA) and breaking down interspecies coordination. This coupled oxidative and signaling disruption collapses metabolic complementarity between rhizosphere and non-rhizosphere communities, leading to spatial decoupling of nitrogen redox transformations, enhanced phosphorus immobilization, and divergence in carbon fluxes. Through integrated PLSR-RF-SEM modeling, we identify dsrA/dsrB, nosZ, phoA/pstC, and luxS as previously unrecognized regulatory “control points'’ that mechanistically link nanoscale perturbation to ecosystem-scale functional decline. Our findings reveal an emergent mechanism-NP-induced oxidative-informational collapse-through which anthropogenic nanoparticles erode the self-organizing capacity of wetland microbiomes, providing a predictive basis for assessing plastic-driven biogeochemical vulnerability.

title: Mechanisms driving the effects of tetramethylammonium hydroxide on the operation of anaerobic baffled-Anammox reactor: Nitrogen removal, sludge characteristics, and microbial community
abstract: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH) is a common toxic pollutant in microelectronics wastewater and creates challenges for environmental governance. This study evaluated the effects of different TMAH concentrations on the nitrogen removal performance and microbial ecology of an anaerobic baffled reactor-Anammox (ABR-Anammox) coupled system. The results showed that at a low TMAH concentration (≤25 mg/L), the system maintained NH4+-N and NO2−-N removal rates above 80%. At a high TMAH concentration (50 mg/L), nitrogen removal performance dropped to below 60%. Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) and Three-dimensional fluorescence spectroscopy (3D-EEM) analyses revealed that TMAH stress altered the composition and structure of extracellular polymers (EPS) in sludge. Within the EPS, the proportion of α-helix in the protein secondary structure decreased from 25% to 13%, and the proportion of β-sheet increased from 34% to 40%. A microbial community analysis indicated that the abundance of the core ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Candidatus Brocadia decreased from 28.34% to 10.30%. Metagenomic analysis further revealed that TMAH inhibited the expression of the electron transport chain (i.e., atpA decreased by 38.4%), the tricarboxylic acid cycle (i.e., key genes decreased by 31-49%), and denitrifying-related genes (i.e., narG decreased by 54.8%). This weakened the energy metabolism and denitrification pathways at the molecular level. This study reveals the concentration-dependent inhibition mechanism of TMAH on the ABR-Anammox system, providing a theoretical basis for the biological treatment process of industrial wastewater containing TMAH.

title: Kinetic modelling of continuous biomass liquefaction for biopolyols and bio-based polyurethane synthesis
abstract: Overconsumption of fossil fuels has led to detrimental effects on the environment, underscoring the need to shift industrial processes towards the adoption of renewable sources. Biomass is valorised in thermochemical conversion for sustainable fuels and chemicals production. This work aims to construct robust kinetic models to predict process performance in the liquefaction of different biomasses to obtain biopolyols, green compounds used in bio-based polyurethane synthesis. The models were developed in Aspen Plus adopting power-law kinetics, achieving good agreement with experimental data, with errors below 15%. The model validation for batch liquefaction of municipal solid waste resulted in bio-oil yields of 33.7, 46.3 and 58.8 wt%, at 300, 325 and 350 °C respectively, with errors of 11.1% at 325 °C and only 0.17% at 350 °C. About microalgae liquefaction, theoretical bio-oil yields of 16.7, 21.1, 26.4 wt% were found at 180, 200, and 225 °C, respectively, with errors of 1.2, 0.5 and 2.7%. Model validation of sewage sludge batch liquefaction achieved less than 10% errors on products flow rates and excellent agreement with experimental biopolyols yields: 65.0 wt% from solvent glycerol (0.04% error), 49.1 wt% from sewage sludge (0.1% error). The present work provides the first simulations of continuous solvothermal liquefaction for waste biomass conversion into biopolyols, optimising the pilot plant design for the company Ecorbio Ltd. Through sensitivity analysis, this novel study identifies optimal reactor temperatures and dimensions to reduce energy demand and enhance biopolyols yield for bio-based polyurethane production.

title: Energy yield and water resource utilization in Chlorella pyrenoidosa under saline-alkali stress: An integrated physiological, ionomic, and transcriptomic approach
abstract: Saline-alkali water is increasingly recognized as a promising alternative resource for microalgal cultivation. However, it remains unclear which ion-homeostasis constraints most directly limit growth and are linked to metabolic reprogramming under combined saline-alkali (SA) stress. Here, Chlorella pyrenoidosa was exposed to a gradient of saline-alkali stress established by NaCl and a Na2CO3/NaHCO3 mixture, and its physiological, biochemical, ionomic, and transcriptomic responses were analyzed to identify the key physiological constraints underlying saline-alkali adaptation. Notably, intracellular Mg2+ levels were strongly associated with biomass and cell density, and 2 × Mg2+ enrichment under high irradiance during saline-alkali stress increased biomass by 20.6% and gross energy output by 61.8%, indicating that Mg2+ bioavailability is a practical lever for improving cultivation performance under saline–alkali conditions. Saline–alkali stress markedly suppressed growth yet promoted carbon reallocation toward carbohydrates and lipids, thereby strengthening the strain's potential contribution to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with the highest contributions observed for SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy, 56.2%) and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger, 19.1%). Ionomic profiling revealed marked Na+ accumulation accompanied by substantial K+ depletion and elevated intracellular Ca2+, suggesting disruption of Na+/K+ homeostasis and potential activation of Ca2+-mediated stress signaling. Transcriptomic analyses further identified candidate genes associated with membrane/transport functions, energy metabolism, and redox regulation, supporting a “survival-over-growth” strategy that redirects carbon flux to starch/sucrose and lipid synthesis while repressing proliferation-related processes (e.g., DNA replication). These findings provide a practical basis for optimizing microalgal cultivation strategies to enhance biomass and energy production in saline-alkali water.

title: Short term economic outcomes associated with ecological sustainability practices among small and medium scale agricultural producers in Chile
abstract: Ecological sustainability practices have become central to debates on agricultural systems and climate resilience, yet evidence on their short-term economic implications for small- and medium-scale producers remains fragmented. This question is consequential because household livelihood security hinges on income cycles that rarely align with the temporal horizons of ecological processes.
