Moreover, the heavy metals were highly homologous (correlation coefficients>0.4). Taking major cities as an example, COD and NH3-N concentrations can be predicted by key factors like annual rainfall (AR), SI, and FC: a 5% increase in FC raises COD and NH3-N concentrations by 4.90% and 4.88%, respectively. The study recommended integrating the TMDL (Total Maximum Daily Load) system with economic incentives (e.g., a $77.50 monthly fee per 1000 m2 of impervious surface) and implementing area-specific control strategies. This research provides a scientific basis for identifying runoff pollution drivers and optimizing urban stormwater management.

title: Embodied carbon transfer in global steel trade: shared responsibility for carbon reduction
abstract: Steel industry, the material foundation of global industrialization, annually contributes 7∼9% to worldwide CO2 emission, facing unprecedented decarbonization imperatives. The decarbonization of steel industry is a worldwide issue, not only because its high carbon-intensity but also the carbon leakage within global trading. Although several climate actions have been issued to prevent the carbon leakage, the uncovered embodied carbon transfer within the global industry chain hindered the fairness of those actions. To address that problem, refined embodied carbon transfer across regions in global steel trading from 2000 to 2020 are analysed in this study, based on environmentally extended Multi-regional Input-output model and Structural Path Analysis. The embodied carbon transfer is featured by multi-interactions among different countries or regions. By conducting a mathematically multi-tier carbon transfer analysis across steel initial producer, intermediate processor and terminal consumer in the global chain, carbon allocation pattern based on shared responsibility from the co-benefit perspective is established, with sharing factor identification in each carbon transfer tier. The shared pattern provides basis for distributed value-chain accountability of carbon-intensive sectors, which could help to develop a more reasonable and refined carbon allocation method compared with previous production- and consumption-based principle.

title: Restructuring metabolic networks and hydrogen-mediated electron transfer to enhance methanogenesis process through microelectrolysis
abstract: Although anaerobic digestion (AD) has been widely used to treat waste activated sludge (WAS), there remains a critical need to develop cleaner production strategies for enhancing methane yield and purity, thereby advancing waste-to-energy conversion and circular economy goals. This study proposed to use microelectrolysis to enhance sludge AD performance through restructuring metabolic networks and hydrogen-mediated electron transfer. Results showed that the microelectrolysis reactor enabled an increase in methane yield by 29.4% from 155.7 to 201.6 mL/g and biogas methane content by 15.6% to a final value of 80.3%, along with a 31.2% improvement in volatile solids (VS) removal compared to the control system. Mechanistic analysis revealed that microelectrolysis selectively promoted macromolecular organic degradation via enzymatic hydrolysis, with protease and α-glucosidase activities increasing by 55.8% and 113% relative to the control, respectively, without affecting acidogenesis. Furthermore, microelectrolysis activated both methanogenic pathways, elevating acetoclastic and hydrogenotrophic methane production by 26.8% and 47.5% via enhanced F420 activity and an increased abundance of key genes. Microbial community analysis suggested that microelectrolysis enriched hydrolytic bacteria, electroactive, and syntrophic archaea facilitating a shift in electron transfer from interspecies hydrogen transfer to direct interspecies electron transfer. Metagenomic analyses further suggested abundance increase of genes related to methanogenesis (cdhCDE, fwdBCDEF), electron transport components (hydrogenases, cytochrome oxidase), and quorum sensing regulators (lasR, rpfC), supporting enhanced metabolic network activity. This study demonstrates that microelectrolysis effectively enhances sludge AD performance and elucidates the multi-level underlying mechanisms, providing a sustainable technological pathway for efficient sludge treatment and bioenergy recovery within the framework of cleaner production.

title: How LARG is a supply chain? Application of adaptive neuro fuzzy inference system in agriculture sector
abstract: The increasing complexity of the agricultural supply chain necessitates integrating the principles of Leanness, Agility, Resilience, and Greenness (LARG) to enhance efficiency, adaptability, and sustainability. This study assesses the adoption of LARG in the agricultural sector using an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) and provides a data-driven assessment of key supply chain (SC) indicators. The results reveal that resilience (0.55) is the strongest dimension, indicating a well-developed capacity to withstand disruptions, primarily driven by technological advancements. Leanness (0.50) demonstrates moderate efficiency, with room for improvement in lead time and cost optimization. However, agility (0.48) and greenness (0.47) are weaker, highlighting the need for enhanced delivery efficiency, employee satisfaction, and sustainable practices. The study suggests that integrating real-time tracking, AI-driven forecasting, and circular economy principles can significantly improve SC responsiveness and environmental sustainability. Future research should explore sector-specific LARG applications, cross-country comparative analyses, and dynamic ANFIS models for real-time decision-making. By strengthening LARG dimensions, the agricultural sector can develop a more competitive, adaptive, and sustainable SC, ensuring long-term efficiency and environmental responsibility.

title: A framework for parametric evaluation of urban growth strategies under climate change
abstract: Rapid population growth in metropolitan areas increases building energy consumption and exacerbates environmental problems, while climate change further intensifies these impacts. In this context, the study proposes a multi-criteria and quantitative evaluation framework to support sustainable urban growth strategies under current and future climate conditions, using Istanbul, a metropolitan city with a temperate-humid climate, as a case study. Within this framework, a total of 216 highly representative parametric urban form alternatives were generated based on urban density (FAR1, FAR2, FAR3), window-to-wall ratio (WWR: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%), road width (10 m, 15 m, 20 m), and two main building typologies (High-rise and Scatter). These alternatives were comparatively evaluated using performance criteria including energy consumption (heating, cooling, total), outdoor thermal comfort (UTCI), and urban heat island effect (UHI). Simulation-based calculations were conducted using Ladybug, Honeybee, Dragonfly, and UWG plugins within the Rhinoceros/Grasshopper environment. Regression analyses were performed on the obtained outputs to reveal the statistical effects of design variables on performance criteria. The findings indicate that increasing outdoor temperatures in the future will make cooling-oriented design strategies inevitable. Urban density (FAR ratio) was identified as the most influential variable across all performance criteria. In addition, the best (H_F3R10W20) and worst (S_F1R20W80) performing scenarios were identified using the weighted sum method. The study provides a practical and multi-dimensional evaluation approach to support decision-makers in climate-compatible urban building and urban design.

title: Towards circular photovoltaic value chains: alkali-based recycling of waste solar cells with life cycle and techno-economic assessment
abstract: With the rapid global expansion of photovoltaic cell deployment, the end-of-life crystalline silicon (c-Si) modules are projected to reach ∼78 million tons by 2050, creating both environmental risks and vast opportunity for resource circularity. This study develops and evaluates an integrated laboratory-scale recycling framework for end-of-life c-Si solar cells, putting silica upcycling within circular PV supply chain. The research addresses three core questions: how selective wet-chemical recycling can support material circularity, which environmental hotspots are most sensitive to the process chemistry, and whether value-added silica recovery can increase techno-economic feasibility. High-purity mesoporous silica was recovered as the primary product, alongside silver, alumina and hydrogen as co-products, while secondary waste streams were cautiously managed through gas capture and ammonium-salt treatment. Gate-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) for a functional unit of 1 kg recovered solar cells indicate relatively low climate impacts, with reagent consumption, thermal energy demand and ammonium-salt treatment identified as key environmental drivers. Avoided production of primary silica and alumina generated environmental credits across several major impact categories. Overall, the findings exhibit how process-integrated environmental management and value-added silica recovery can provide a futuristic entry-point for emerging PV recycling infrastructures.

title: Land use prediction for SSPs climate scenarios with carbon emission gradients: A FiLM-modulated conditional GAN framework
abstract: The impact of climate change on land use is particularly complex in fragmented land use regions, and accurate simulation of land use spatial patterns in such regions is crucial for national spatial planning. This study, using Kunming as the research area, addresses the insufficient adaptability of traditional models by constructing a conditional GAN land use prediction model, SFiLM-GAN, based on FiLM feature modulation. This model uses U-Net as the encoding and decoding backbone, embeds FiLM to implement scenario constraints, and combines a multi-scale PatchGAN discriminator to enhance the rationality of spatial patterns. The model's results are validated, and predictions are made using the CMIP6 multi-carbon emission-driven climate scenario. Results show that the SFiLM-GAN model achieves OA, Kappa, and mIoU of 94.25%, 91.58%, and 88.32%, respectively, with an AD of only 4.56%. It demonstrates accurate land use identification and strong ability to distinguish land uses with overlapping landscape features. From 2000 to 2020, forest land in Kunming remained stable, urban land expanded by a cumulative 3.37%, cultivated land and grassland decreased by 1.32% and 1.58%, respectively, water areas increased slightly, and unused land remained stable. Under different carbon emission scenarios in 2030, urban land expansion intensity is the core differentiator in land use patterns. Scenario SSP585 shows an expansion of 2.85%, while scenario SSP119 shows the mildest expansion of 1.73%. Cultivated land and grassland are preserved more intact, while other land types show no significant differences across scenarios. The landscape pattern in the study area continues to fragment, with PD increasing from 0.33 to 0.38, reaching 0.41 for SSP585 in 2030. LSI is rising, while AI and CONNECT are declining. Low-carbon development scenarios can mitigate this deterioration. The model constructed in this study can provide scientific support and decision-making basis for accurate land use simulation in complex geomorphological areas, as well as regional spatial planning and sustainable development.

title: Drought-induced disaster Chains: A global perspective of propagation probabilities and mitigation priorities
abstract: Drought, one of the most frequent natural hazards worldwide, often triggers cascading secondary disasters, forming drought disaster chains that pose severe threats to human society. Understanding these chains is critical for effective risk management. However, fewer studies relied on systematic regional analyses and assessments of drought disaster chain propagation probabilities and pathways from global perspective. By integrating the EM-DAT and Munich Re's NatCatSERVICE databases, this study aims to qualitatively and quantitatively clarify drought disaster chains—including heatwaves, wildfires, epidemics, and insect infestations—at national scales. Using the triggering rate index (Y) to quantify propagation dynamics among nodes and links of disaster chains and monthly Palmer Drought Severity Index as well as Locust Treat Areas for disaster case verification. The results show that: (1) Coastal countries are particularly vulnerable to drought disaster chains, with wildfire- and heatwave-prone nations concentrated in Europe, while regions susceptible to drought-induced epidemics and insect infestations are primarily clustered in Africa. (2) Extreme heat and drought present synergistic interactions, amplifying their integrated disaster impacts. Among all disaster chains, wildfires demonstrate the highest propagation probability, with mean triggering rates of 3.2% for both "extreme heat → wildfire" and "drought → wildfire" chains. (3) China and the United States experience the most severe impacts from drought disaster chains, with mean triggering rates of 4.4% and 3.8% respectively - significantly higher than the global average (0.3%). These countries also reveal the most complex propagation pathways, encompassing four distinct disaster chains. For effective drought mitigation, China is suggested to prioritize preventing insect infestations and epidemics, while the United States needs to enhance epidemic and wildfire control. Following extreme heat events, China's key concerns shift to drought and epidemic management, whereas the U.S. should concentrate on drought and wildfire mitigation measures. The methodology and findings established a global perspective for formulating regional policy strategies to prevent and mitigate the impacts of disaster chains, put forward suggestions for the global integrated management of drought risk.

title: Oxygen-mediated electrochemical CO2 mineralization for power generation
abstract: CO2 mineralization batteries can recover the chemical energy released during CO2 mineralization through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) reactions, rather than losing it as heat in traditional mineralization processes. However, previous ex-situ electrochemical mineralization batteries using PCET redox couples (e.g., H+/H2, Q/QH2) face challenges in safety risks, product separation, and stability. Here, we propose an in-situ CO2 mineralization power generation strategy using a safe O2/OH- redox couple. By integrating a gas diffusion electrode (GDE) with an oxygen cathode, the system couples electrochemical alkali (OH−) production, in-situ CO2 mineralization, and electricity output without requiring separation of CO2 from the redox couple. Our system achieves a peak power density of 3.31 W m−2 and produces 98.88% pure NaHCO3. Theoretical analysis shows that 1 ton of CO2 can generate 42.73 kWh of electricity and 1.91 tons of NaHCO3, providing a new way for CO2 mitigation, electricity generation, and NaHCO3 production.

title: Urban air pollution and walking mode switches: A study to explore commuters’ responses to emission charges and flextime
abstract: Rising air pollution levels may be driving a shift from green transportation modes, such as walking, to motorized alternatives. Focusing on walking, we introduce the Dynamics of Walking Mode Switches, explaining how commuters respond to air pollution and policy interventions in three states: walking adoption (switching to walking), walking shift (switching away from walking), and walking retention (continue walking). Through a cross-sectional survey, 734 valid questionnaires were collected in a populous city in Iran, capturing respondents' revealed and stated work tour choices. The results show a significant negative association between air quality index (AQI) and the probability of walking adoption, while walking retention is less sensitive to AQI changes. We found that higher emission charges are associated with an 75% increase in walking adoption probability. This increase is greater at moderate air pollution which suggests that financial disincentives to car use may promote sustainable transportation. Additionally, flextime is associated with lower walking shift probability in commuters' work tours, particularly at higher AQI levels, suggesting that it may serve as a compensatory measure against shifts to motorized modes during pollution episodes. These findings can assist decision-makers in designing strategies to promote sustainable transportation by combining policy measures tailored to different air pollution scenarios.

title: Decarbonization of the cement industry: Pathways and life cycle impact assessment
abstract: The Indian cement industry alone contributes for 7% of total CO2 emissions. Majority of these emissions originate from clinker production, which is the primary intermediate product in cement manufacturing. Clinker consumes about 3.07-3.3 GJ/t of thermal energy were predominately supplied by fossil fuels, while limestone calcination further results in emissions of 0.9-1 t CO2eq./t. Hence, to decarbonize clinker production, fossil fuels must be replaced with alternative fuels and implementing carbon capture technologies to capture the CO2 emitted from the calcination process. In this regard, this study evaluates the potential of rice husk (RH) and torrefied rice husk (TRH) as alternative fuels to decarbonize clinker production, along with the integration of carbon capture and storage (CCS). Six scenarios were developed and compared with business-as-usual (BAU) through a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment to identify the environmental sustainability of the process. Among these, scenarios 5 and 6 demonstrated the highest emission reductions, with emissions reduced from 926.5 kg CO2eq./t of clinker in BAU to 709.7 kg CO2eq./t in scenario 5 and 708.7 kg CO2eq./t in scenario 6. The emission reduction was mainly attributed to the substitution of fossil fuels (25%) with RH and TRH, along with CCS. Hence, the use of alternative fuels along with CCS can facilitate to reduce the carbon intensity of clinker production and aid India in achieving its decarbonization target (560 kg CO2eq./t of cement) for the cement sector by 2030.

title: Towards A nearly zero-energy building: A sensitivity- informed multi-objective optimization of cost, carbon, and flexibility in hybrid energy systems
abstract: In response to the escalating challenges of global warming and environmental pollution, hybrid energy systems have emerged as a crucial approach to reducing carbon emissions and alleviating grid stress. Nearly zero-energy buildings (NZEBs) are characterized by low energy loads and high renewable penetration, which introduce significant operational volatility. Identifying key variables and achieving multi-objective optimization during the early design phase remains a significant challenge. This study proposes and validates a sensitivity-informed multi-objective optimization framework to address these challenges. By coupling TRNSYS simulations with two global sensitivity analysis (GSA) methods (Morris and EFAST) and the NSGA-II algorithm, we systematically identified key design variables and derived optimal configurations for an NZEB in a severe cold region. Global sensitivity analysis revealed that the number of EVs was the most influential parameter, with a first-order sensitivity index (Si) of 0.8402 for life-cycle cost (LCC) and 0.7784 for grid integration level (GIL). Following optimization, the globally optimal solution achieved a LCC of 167711.83 CNY and a GIL of 0.1583. Compared to the baseline configuration, this optimal solution reduced grid-imported electricity by 74.36% and improved the on-site energy fraction by 40.59%. Notably, the interaction between EV charging parameter and storage capacity dictates system performance. The optimization reveals a critical trade-off: while maximizing flexibility requires oversizing storage capacity, the global optimum achieves balanced gains across all three objectives by strategically reducing EV numbers and prioritizing renewable self-consumption. The framework's primary contribution lies in establishing EV quantity as the critical leverage point for NZEB optimization, providing designers with a clear prioritization strategy: optimize EV penetration and its bidirectional control before fine-tuning generation and storage capacities. This approach offers a replicable methodology for decarbonizing building energy systems in cold climates while maintaining economic viability and grid flexibility.

title: Role of PM2.5 sources and environmental drivers in the triangular relationship of nitrate-sulfate-ozone system
abstract: Nitrate (NO3−), sulfate (SO42−), and ozone (O3) are key atmospheric pollutants, yet the underlying mechanisms of their interactions are highly complex and remain insufficiently characterized from a quantitative perspective. This study conducted a comprehensive field observation in Tianjin, a typical megacity in the North China Plain, from 2022 to 2023, focusing on the dynamic evolution of the NO3−-SO42--O3 system. The NO3−/SO42− ratio effectively delineates distinct regimes of pollutant interactions: at low ratios, strong photochemistry drives O3 production while suppressing secondary inorganic aerosol formation; as the ratio increases, accumulated nitrate and sulfate progressively enhance heterogeneous reaction pathways under elevated humidity, consuming gas-phase oxidants and intensifying aerosol radiative extinction, thereby suppressing O3 while promoting further nitrate accumulation. The Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) receptor model was applied to quantify the contributions of six emission sources to PM2.5, and a Random Forest model combined with SHAP analysis was employed to quantitatively assess the contributions of environmental factors and source contributions to NO3−, SO42− and O3 concentrations. Machine learning quantitatively confirms that temperature, source contribution, and aerosol liquid water content are dominant regulators, while sulfate and nitrate exhibit competition at the source level. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for the coordinated control of PM2.5 and O3 in regional air quality management.

title: Resistance characteristics of irregular exhaust hoods and inverse design based on airflow distribution in rolling mills
abstract: Oil mist pollution generated in metal processing and rolling facilities poses significant risks to occupational health, equipment reliability, and workshop cleanliness. Rolling mills are typical high-emission environments, where oil mist is released in three distinct zones: the uncoiling, rolling, and recoiling areas. Efficient control of these emissions relies on precise airflow distribution among the three zones; however, this is difficult to achieve during system design because the resistance characteristics of the irregular annular and sealed exhaust hoods are not available. This study quantitatively determines the resistance characteristics of these hoods and reveals their sensitivity to geometrical parameters. Single-factor analyses show that the resistance coefficient of the annular exhaust hood decreases exponentially with the inlet-outlet area ratio, whereas that of the sealed hood increases as a cubic function of the inlet-to-outlet area ratio within the investigated range. Based on these findings, a Box-Behnken response surface model is developed to construct a continuous resistance surface for the annular hood, and a coupled quadratic model is further proposed to directly relate hood geometry to airflow distribution among the three zones. Model predictions agree with simulation results within a deviation of ≤5%, enabling an inverse design method for exhaust systems in rolling mills. Once the desired distribution ratios are specified, the required geometric dimensions of the hoods can be directly determined, avoiding iterative field balancing and improving design-stage accuracy.

title: Assessment of inter-plant circularity using an integrated life cycle emergy analysis framework
abstract: Circular Economy (CE) approaches are gaining traction for driving resource efficiency and sustainable business models. Yet, conventional environmental assessment tools often fail to capture CE's complexity, especially in industrial contexts. Attempts to integrate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), Emergy Analysis (EmA) and other ecological footprints remain limited, as these mono-dimensional metrics struggle to link process performance with ecosystem service use and environmental sustainability. This paper presents an integrated methodological framework for assessing inter-plant circularity through the combined LCA and EmA principles. The framework, known as Circular-Life Cycle Emergy Analysis (C-LCEmA), is demonstrated through case studies in disposable diaper manufacturing, incorporating both emergy-based and LCA-based circularity indicators to provide a comprehensive evaluation of circular economy implementation. Two distinct scenarios are examined: the utilization of recycled superabsorbent polymers (SAP) in concrete production and the use of recycled polypropylene (PP)/polyethylene (PE) mix in wood plastic composites (WPCs). Circularity is defined as the ability of production systems to recover materials, minimize waste, and reduce reliance on new raw inputs. Positive circularity values show efficient resource use and material recovery, while negative values signify that recycling processes consume more emergy than virgin production pathways, indicating resource inefficiency. The analysis reveals that resource efficiency in secondary applications is the dominant factor determining overall circularity, with secondary sector emergy consumption exerting primary influence on both system circularity (CS) and life cycle circularity (CLCEmA). Sensitivity analysis (±15% parameter variations) confirms this dominance across all scenarios. This integrated C-LCEmA framework effectively quantifies circularity across industrial sectors and reveals crucial differences in recycling pathways. PP/PE recycling for WPC production demonstrates better circularity (7.38 × 1023 seJ) compared to SAP recycling for concrete (−2.24 × 1023 seJ), driven by higher waste stream proportion (41.2%) and greater virgin material displacement (29% of WPC composition). The integrated C-LCEmA framework enables quantitative comparison of alternative circular pathways across industrial sectors, providing critical insights for optimizing circular economy strategies in manufacturing.

title: Multi-scenario land use optimization towards carbon neutrality: An integrated predict-optimize-evaluate decision support framework
abstract: Rapid urbanization creates complex trade-offs among economic development, ecological conservation, and food security within limited land resources. Traditional planning methods struggle to simultaneously optimize multiple objectives while providing spatially explicit solutions. This study develops an integrated predict-optimize-evaluate framework for carbon neutrality-oriented land use planning in Southern Jiangsu, China. The framework operates through three interconnected stages: (1) multi-objective prediction quantifies six objectives (net carbon sink, economic development, food production, suitability, compatibility, transition probability) for 2030/2060 using machine learning models and dynamic climate-informed assessments; (2) multi-scenario optimization employs a Multi-Objective Spatial Genetic Algorithm (MOSGA) to generate spatially optimal configurations across four pathways—low-carbon development (LCS), economic-oriented growth (EDS), food security priority (FPS), and balanced development (BDS); (3) multi-dimensional evaluation assesses scenario performance to support decision-making. Results demonstrate that strategic land use optimization can facilitate the synergistic enhancement of competing objectives. Historical analysis (2000–2020) shows that construction land expanded by 3492 km2 while cropland decreased by 3765.87 km2. Multi-objective optimization results reveal that the LCS scenario achieved optimal carbon performance, improving net carbon balance by 64.9% by 2060, substantially narrowing though not eliminating the carbon deficit. The FPS scenario realized progressive cropland restoration, with net gains of 116.37 km2 by 2030 and 132.93 km2 by 2060 compared to the 2020 baseline, despite continued urbanization; this was facilitated through rural settlement consolidation, which reduced the rural settlement area by 10.15%–14.66% relative to the 2020 baseline. Regional average carbon emission intensity declined from 2.47 t CO2/10,000 CNY (2000) to 0.04 t CO2/10,000 CNY (2060) across all optimization scenarios, demonstrating that the decoupling of economic growth from carbon emissions is robust across all policy orientations. The framework improved land use suitability by 5.56%, spatial compatibility by 8.33%, and land use transition probability by 3.70%, enhancing both spatial rationality and implementation feasibility of optimization outcomes. This methodology provides planning practitioners with quantitative tools for evaluating development scenarios under changing climate conditions, offering broader applicability for sustainable urban planning in rapidly urbanizing regions worldwide.

title: Triple-goal governance of urban agglomerations under SDG 11: A causal inference and deep reinforcement learning framework
abstract: Conflicts among the objectives of economic development, pollution control, and health protection in urban systems have become a key constraint on advancing the urban Sustainable Development Goal (SDG 11). To address limitations in existing studies regarding conflict-structure identification, mechanism characterization, and coordinated policy design, this paper proposes a triple-goal collaborative governance analytical framework for the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region. Based on city-level data from 13 cities over 2000–2023, we integrate hot–cold spot analysis, interpretable surrogate modeling, causal graph construction, and deep reinforcement learning optimization TabNet–SHAP, LiNGAM–DoWhy, and DQN–NSGA-III optimization across seven policy scenarios. The framework links spatial diagnosis, causal pathway identification, and adaptive multi-objective optimization. The results show that: (1) GDP hotspots remain concentrated in the Beijing–Tianjin core, whereas pollution and health risks persist in southern Hebei; (2) the TabNet–SHAP model identifies nonlinear and heterogeneous effects of variables such as industrial structure, environmental investment, and fiscal expenditure to GDP, PM2.5, and HVI; (3) results from LiNGAM and DoWhy suggest significant direct and mediated causal pathways among variables; and (4) DQN–NSGA-III optimization, yields representative non-dominated solutions across scenarios, with the balanced scenario showing the most consistent co-improvement in pollution reduction and health protection while maintaining economic feasibility. This study develops a multi-stage integrated analytical pipelinefor triple-goal governance under SDG 11, offering a reference approach for addressing implementation challenges of SDG 11 at the urban-agglomeration scale.

title: Virtual to reality: How user engagement in green digital platforms promotes users’ low-carbon behavior? –A case study of Ant forest in China
abstract: Green digital platforms are interactive systems that encourage environmentally friendly behaviors by leveraging digital technologies to engage users and promote sustainability. Although previous studies have examined user motivation and platform engagement, less is known about how specific forms of goal design influence users' behavioral expectations and low-carbon behaviors. Based on goal-setting theory, this study examines how goal level and goal orientation in green digital platforms influences users' behavioral expectations and behavioral outcomes. Using Ant Forest in China as the research context, two experiments were conducted to test the effects of different forms of goal design. The results show that (1) lower goal levels increase users’ behavioral expectations by making goals seem more achievable; (2) goals oriented toward platform engagement behaviors generate higher behavioral expectations than goals oriented toward real-world environmental behaviors; (3) goals oriented toward real-world environmental behaviors are more effective in promoting low-carbon behavior outside the platform; and (4) behavioral expectation fully mediates the relationship between goal level and platform engagement behavior. These findings expand the theoretical understanding of green digital platforms and provide actionable insights for developers, governments, and organizations seeking to design platforms that encourage sustainable behaviors and contribute to environmental goals.

title: Spatiotemporal prediction and differentiated governance of coal mining subsidence in the desert-loess transition region
abstract: In Yulin, a typical desert-loess transition region and energy base in China, the conflict between intensive coal mining and ecological fragility is increasingly acute, with mining-induced subsidence causing land degradation and ecological damage that constrain regional sustainability. In this study, subsidence prediction, damage assessment, impact quantification, and zonal governance were used to clarify the distribution patterns and restoration pathways of mining subsidence. Results shown that 1) Yulin's mining subsidence is a spatial pattern of “severe north, mild south; dense east, sparse west” and a temporal trend of steady growth in 2021∼2025 and accelerated expansion in 2026∼2035, driven by the combined effects of shallow coal depth, thin bedrock, and high-intensity mining, with distinct subsidence and damage types between aeolian grasslands and loess hills; 2) A three-dimensional land damage assessment system based on surface fissures, slope gradient, and water accumulation identifies dominant mechanisms, subsidence and waterlogging in grasslands, horizontal deformation and ground fissures in loess zones, with forest and grassland showing higher deformation tolerance than farmland; 3) Coal mining exerts cascading ecological impacts, including water quantity and quality loss, farmland degradation, and ecosystem decline, exacerbated by the compound stress of wind-water erosion and mining disturbance; 4) A differentiated governance system of six zones and nine key projects, integrating geomorphology, damage, and industry, achieves synergistic ecological restoration, industrial development, and livelihood improvement, providing a replicable model and supporting the Yellow River Basin ecological security and energy base sustainability.

title: A novel and intelligent system for ciprofloxacin sensing by molecularly imprinted polymers loaded graphitic carbon nitride-based municipal wastewater sludge
abstract: To achieve sensitive, visual, and intelligent identification of ciprofloxacin (CIP), a novel colorimetric sensing platform was developed by integrating municipal wastewater sludge (MWS)-based graphitic carbon nitride (CN) with molecularly imprinted polymers (MIP) for CIP detection to form MIP@MWSCN. This system employs Rhodamine B (RhB) as a colorimetric indicator within a light-driven photocatalytic sensing framework. CIP detection is based on the inhibition of RhB photocatalytic decolorization in the presence of CIP under light illumination within a short reaction time of 10 min. The resulting composite leverages a low detection limit of 3.56 μg.L−1 with remarkable selectivity over a concentration range of 4 to 100 μg.L−1. The mechanism was primarily governed by the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), such as predominant hydroxyl (•OH) and superoxide (O2●‒) radicals, contributing to the RhB decolorization as well as high sensitivity of the colorimetric response. It demonstrated excellent analytical performances in various actual water matrices, achieving recovery ranging from 96.12 to 100.91% and relative standard deviations (RSD, n = 5) below 3.83% when measured using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer, whereas the recovery was obtained from 95.87 to 101.97% using a portable device. These results highlight the platform's capability to deliver highly sensitive, precise, and reproducible readouts in complex environmental samples. Overall, this study introduces an innovative, light-driven sensing strategy that combines dye chemistry and photocatalysis for visual pollutant detection, offering a low-cost, environmentally friendly, and practical approach for environmental water quality assessment.

title: Impacts of nitrogen deposition on N2O emissions from agricultural ecosystems in China based on a biogeochemical model
abstract: Agricultural ecosystems are one of the most significant anthropogenic sources of nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions. Substantial evidence indicates that atmospheric nitrogen deposition (N deposition) exerts profound influences on soil nitrogen dynamics and associated biogeochemical processes, potentially promoting N2O efflux from agricultural systems. Nevertheless, the quantitative linkage between N deposition and agricultural N2O emissions remains insufficiently characterized. This study establishes a novel modeling framework integrating biogeochemical and chemical transport models to systematically evaluate the effects of current and projected N deposition patterns on agricultural N2O emissions. Our simulations incorporated state-of-the-art meteorological datasets and emission inventories for both baseline (2020) and future scenarios. The simulated N deposition well reproduced the observed horizontal distribution characteristics of ammoniums and nitrates. The analysis revealed that N deposition contributed approximately 0.1 Tg N2O emissions in 2020 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 91.4–123.1 Gg), accounting for approximately one quarter of the total annual agricultural emissions. The results further indicated that, by 2050, N deposition would be reduced by 19% and 37% in two future scenarios, correspondingly reducing agricultural N2O emissions by 5% (95%CI: −4.7%–23.5%) and 11% (95%CI: −0.8%–27.9%), respectively. These findings underscore the critical role of N deposition management in climate change mitigation strategies. The demonstrated sensitivity of agricultural N2O emissions to N deposition patterns highlights the necessity of incorporating nitrogen cycle feedback into policy frameworks addressing greenhouse gas reduction.

title: Toxicity difference analysis of typical plastic leachate components using Phaeodactylum tricornutum
abstract: Plastics persist long-term in marine environments, and continuously release additive, which threaten marine ecosystem health. However, research on the toxicity mechanisms of specific plastic additives and the differences in toxicity among additives remains limited for marine primary producers. Accordingly, we investigated the differential toxicity of the two most toxic compounds N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and 4-methylbenzylidene camphor (4-MBC) identified from ten plastic exudate components using marine diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum (P. tricornutum) as a model organism. The EC50 values of 6PPD and 4-MBC were approximately 0.32 and 0.77 mg/L, respectively. Both 6PPD and 4-MBC induced photosynthetic damage and oxidative stress in microalgae, disrupting intracellular homeostasis and leading to reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the 4-MBC treatment group were mainly enriched in pathways related to the proteasome, protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum and folate biosynthesis, whereas, DEGs in the 6PPD treatment group were associated with ribosome biogenesis in eukaryotes, carbon metabolism and carbon fixation. Compared to 4-MBC, 6PPD obviously affected the expression of PsbM and PetC genes, indicating its greater impact on the microalgal photosynthetic performance. Both pollutants impaired DNA replication and repair functions, thereby inhibiting algal reproduction. This study provides molecular-level evidence for distinguishing additive-specific toxicity on marine microalgae.

title: Recovery of manganese from mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) wastewater via carbonate precipitation for electrolytic manganese metal production
abstract: The rapid growth of high-pressure acid leaching (HPAL) technology for laterite nickel processing has resulted in a large amount of manganese-rich wastewater, which is generated after nickel and cobalt precipitation, posing both environmental and resource utilization issues. In this study, manganese was recovered from mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) wastewater via carbonate precipitation using CaO as the alkaline reagent and CO2 as the carbonate source. The effects of key operational parameters, including pH, CO2 flow time, temperature, Ca(OH)2 flow rate, and Ca(OH)2 concentration, on manganese precipitation behavior were thoroughly analyzed. Under optimized conditions, a manganese recovery efficiency of 92.76% was achieved. The recovered manganese carbonate was subsequently leached and purified to produce a manganese sulfate solution suitable for electrolytic manganese metal (EMM) production, with a manganese leaching efficiency of 94.16% and Fe, Al, and heavy metal concentrations below 0.1 mg/L. This integrated process enables simultaneous wastewater remediation, CO2 utilization, and manganese resource recovery, providing a sustainable and cost-effective pathway for economically utilized HPAL-derived mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) wastewater and supporting circular resource utilization in nickel and manganese processing industries.

title: Unraveling multiscale spatial networks of marine aquaculture carbon sink efficiency: An EBM-ERGM integrated framework for China's coastal regions
abstract: Strengthening the carbon sink capacity of marine aquaculture is crucial for mitigating global warming and enhancing carbon neutrality. Compared with static measurements of the scale and efficiency of carbon sinks, systematic explanations regarding the formation of a stable interregional correlation network for the marine aquaculture carbon sink (MACS) efficiency, its multiscale structural characteristics, and the underlying driving factors remain lacking. Therefore, in this study, focusing on nine coastal provinces in China from 2007 to 2023, we measured MACS efficiency using the super-efficiency Epsilon-Based Measure (EBM) model and characterized its spatial correlation structure at the overall, sectoral, and local levels by integrating social network and motif analyses. Additionally, an Exponential Random Graph Model (ERGM) was constructed to identify the formation mechanisms underlying the spatial correlation network. (1) During the sample period, MACS efficiency in China's coastal regions exhibited an overall upward trend, with the average value increasing from 0.59 to 0.71. Fujian, Guangxi, and Shandong were the top three provinces regarding average efficiency. (2) Although the sectoral composition of the spatial correlation network remained generally stable, the functions of these sectors notably evolved, with different provinces dynamically transitioning between roles such as net spillover, net benefit, brokerage, and primary benefit. (3) The network connections exhibited pronounced triangular transmission characteristics, with reciprocal, cyclic, and clustered motifs gradually strengthening, indicating enhanced synergistic interregional correlations. (4) ERGM revealed that endogenous structural effects, including reciprocity, cyclicity, and connectivity within the network, along with exogenous relational attributes, such as regional trade linkages, notably influenced the spatial correlation network of MACS efficiency. Concurrently, actor attributes substantially affected the sending, receiving, inhibition, and reciprocal formation of correlations. This study advances the understanding of MACS efficiency from the relational networks perspective, providing empirical evidence for the development of cross-regional synergistic mechanisms to enhance carbon sinks and optimize coastal aquaculture policies.

title: Multi-scenario simulation of urban land use and carbon stock in Bangkok
abstract: Bangkok, a rapidly growing tropical megacity, has undergone significant transformations in land use and land cover (LULC) in recent decades, with a substantial impact on carbon sequestration within the city. The ecosystem degradation and loss of carbon stock have become a key concern in both global as well as regional context. This research, offering a spatially explicit understanding of carbon dynamics in tropical urban regions, remains limited. Addressing this gap, the present study investigates the long-term impacts of LULC changes on total carbon stock in Bangkok from 1995 to 2045. The study integrates the Cellular Automata–Markov Chain (CA–MC) model with the InVEST carbon sequestration model, forming a hybrid framework to analyze historical LULC transitions, simulate future scenarios, and quantify associated carbon storage changes. The result highlights that built-up areas have significantly increased from 22.44% in 1995 to a projected 52.44% by 2045, largely replacing agricultural and vegetated land. This transformation has resulted in a significant loss of carbon stock, exceeding 7 million Mg, over the 50-year period. Between 1995 and 2025, an estimated 5.95 million Mg of carbon were lost, and a further 959243.24 Mg is expected to be lost between 2025 and 2035. Although carbon loss is expected to stabilise after 2025, the ecological and economic repercussions remain significant, with the net present value (NPV) of total carbon loss estimated at over USD 380 million. Spatial analysis further reveals the fragmentation of carbon-rich zones and the expansion of carbon-poor areas in the urban core. This study proposes a carbon–land collaborative management framework tailored for rapidly urbanizing areas in Southeast Asia, serving as a policy-relevant tool to integrate ecological valuation into urban planning through strategies such as land-use zoning reforms, green infrastructure planning, afforestation incentives, and carbon offset programmes.

title: Achieving superior tribological performance and extended cutting life of multilayer coated cutters during high-speed dry cutting of Ti-6Al-4V
abstract: Constructing coatings with excellent tribological performance, fatigue resistance and thermal stability is crucial for suppressing degradation and sustaining cutting performance of coated cutters for high-speed dry cutting use, while B-containing multilayer coatings are promising candidates. In this work, various multilayer AlCrBN/AlCrN coatings (AlCrBN sublayers alternately deposited with AlCrN sublayers with bilayer numbers of 1, 5, 10, and 20, denoted as T1, T5, T10, and T20, respectively) were fabricated by cathodic arc ion plating to investigate the relationship between their microstructures and high-speed dry cutting performance of titanium alloys. Results showed that the multilayer architecture significantly improved coating adhesion (Lc2 up to 71 N) and impact fatigue resistance compared with the monolayer coating. The T10 coating exhibited the lowest wear rate (1.21 ± 0.11 × 10−16 m3 N−1m−1) and a reduced friction coefficient (0.38 ± 0.02) at room temperature, whereas T20 retained superior hardness after post-annealing. High-speed dry cutting (HSDC) tests (without cutting fluid) showed that the T10 multilayer coating presented the best comprehensive cutting performance, TEM analysis of the worn rake face of the T10 coated insert further confirmed the superior structural stability of the coating. This was attributed to its optimal adhesive strength of 71 N (Lc2), excellent impact fatigue resistance, strong interfacial enhancement effect and the ability to maintain the structural integrity under thermo-mechanical loading.

title: Evaluation and optimization of water-land intermodal transportation routes of engineering spoil
abstract: The off-site transportation of engineering spoil faces multi challenges, i.e., high transportation cost, tight schedule, traffic safety hazards, and environmental pressures. The water-land intermodal transportation is an effective way to tackle with these challenges, especially in areas with well-developed waterway network. However, there is limited scientific standards and methods to comprehensively evaluate the existing water-land intermodal routes and optimize the inferior routes. Existing research had limited focus on the related aspects, including the evaluation indicator system, optimization model, and optimization algorithm. Therefore, this study proposed an AHP based evaluation model consisting of eight evaluation indicators to assess the performance of the intermodal routes of engineering spoil. In the proposed indicator system, a dynamic indicator, i.e., road congestion level, was novelly proposed to be estimated by random forest algorithm. Then, a multi-objective optimization model considering cost, comprehensive transportation performance and carbon emission, was established based on NSGA-II, aiming to optimize the inferior route(s). Through a case study in Guangzhou, the effectiveness of the proposed evaluation and optimization model was verified. Nine water-land intermodal routes were evaluated. Then, the worst-performing route was optimized through the proposed multi-objective optimization model. A Pareto front containing 24 solutions was obtained by NSGA-II. Compared with the original route, the optimization solutions have achieved significant improvements in cost (45.96% less), comprehensive transportation performance (33.92% better), and carbon emission (59.60% less). Theoretically, the proposed evaluation and optimization model provided methodological contribution to the related research field by integrating the strengths of AHP and NSGA-II. In practical, this study addressed the challenges of current urban C&D waste transportation in cost, efficiency, safety, and environmental impact.

title: Research on remote sensing ecological index prediction based on deep learning—Taking the application of long short-term memory neural network in Yili prefecture as an example
abstract: Ecological monitoring is often limited by the lag in post-event assessment, while predicting future ecological conditions is crucial for proactive environmental management. Therefore, we developed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to predict the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) for the study area in 2025 and employed the Shapley Additive Interpretation (SHAP) method to explain the relative contributions of natural and anthropogenic factors. Studies show that drastic land-use change reduces prediction accuracy; therefore, we introduced a regional correction mechanism based on Bayesian conjugate priors to integrate land-use information into the deep learning prediction. This method was applied to the Ili region of Xinjiang, China, and performed well compared to measured data from 2020. Furthermore, its predicted regional average index for 2025 is consistent with the persistence indicated by the Hurst index. The study shows that ecological foundation and precipitation are the main positive drivers of future ecological quality, while high temperatures, soil drought, and intensive urbanization and grazing activities will reduce ecological quality. The results of the global bivariate Moran's index indicate a spatial correlation between land use change intensity and model residuals; areas with greater change are more likely to be adjacent to areas with larger prediction biases. Furthermore, we introduced a confidence parameter to measure the relative confidence between prior and predicted values and determined the optimal setting for balancing goodness of fit and robustness. Our research not only improves the model's predictive accuracy in areas of rapid land use transition, but also integrates spatial planning with ecological prediction. The findings support policymakers in anticipating multiple possible ecological outcomes when developing different regional planning pathways.

title: On the dynamics of the municipal separate waste collection: The case of Italy
abstract: The transition toward circular economy targets requires effective monitoring of waste-management performance at the level where services are actually organized and financed. This paper analyzes the dynamics of separate source collection of municipal waste across Italian municipalities over the period 2012–2021. Using a novel panel dataset covering nearly 7000 municipalities, we estimate β-convergence models to assess whether municipalities with lower initial levels of separate collection tend to improve more rapidly over time. The empirical analysis combines panel regressions with fixed effects and a set of structural controls capturing socio-economic characteristics, financial resources devoted to waste management, and technical efficiency in service provision. The results indicate the presence of conditional convergence in separate source collection. While unconditional convergence and conditional convergence with no fixed effects are estimated to be relatively slow, the speed of adjustment increases substantially once municipality-specific characteristics are taken into account. This finding suggests that municipalities adjust relatively quickly toward municipality specific steady states, reflecting persistent structural differences in local waste-management conditions. Additional results show that higher technical efficiency and greater per-capita expenditure on waste management are associated with faster improvements in collection performance. From a policy perspective the results of our analysis, faster speed of convergence than previously documented and the importance of unobserved characteristics at the municipal level, provide evidence of more persistent dynamics that may call for place based intervention.

title: From barriers to better work: Strategic insights on barriers to job quality for web-based gig workers
abstract: The web-based gig work (WGW) provides flexible employment opportunities and access to the global markets. However, several barriers obstruct gig workers' job quality. Existing literature inadequately examines the interconnected nature of WGW and offers limited understanding of platform strategies and regulatory environment. This study addresses these gaps by developing a hierarchical model of job quality barriers to demonstrate their interrelationships and interdependencies in WGW. A mixed-method approach is implemented in three phases, integrating expert insights through focus group discussions, fuzzy Delphi method, and FISM–MICMAC analysis. This investigation led to the selection of the twenty-one barriers, structured into an eight-level hierarchical model. The regulatory gaps, platform capitalism, and algorithmic domination were found to be the fundamental barriers that drive and reinforce the dependent barriers, including work-life imbalance, technostress, insecurity and emotional challenges. Findings offer insights for advancing research and theory in WGW. These insights can help regulators, platforms and clients understand barriers to ensuring job quality and strategically address these barriers for developing sustainable platform strategies and effective regulatory environment.

title: Nano-biochar enhances energy taxis of Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 and the bio-utilization of minerals and Cr(VI)
abstract: Nano-biochar (NBC) is recognized as an effective mediator for microbial extracellular electron transfer (EET). However, its specific role in regulating microbial energy taxis toward insoluble minerals and toxic soluble electron acceptors remains unexplored. In this study, it was demonstrated through swim plate and capillary assays that NBC effectively mediated the tactic response of Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 toward ferrihydrite (Fh) and hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)). Among the tested variants, NBC pyrolyzed at 600 °C (NBC600) exhibited the optimal mediating efficacy. Its abundant redox-active quinone groups facilitated the bacterial energy taxis, expanding the migration area diameter (at 50 mg/L) by 1.3 to 1.6 times compared to other variants. Furthermore, for the soluble Cr(VI), energy taxis represented a dynamic metabolic trade-off. While 1.0 mg/L Cr(VI) suppressed migration by 75.3% compared to 0.1 mg/L due to cytotoxicity, NBC addition alleviated this stress primarily through physical sequestration. This intervention improved the energetic cost-benefit balance, restoring migration by 226.3% and boosting cellular ATP production by 25.7%. NBC therefore dynamically facilitates microbial energy taxis, offering a mechanism to support the survival of electroactive bacteria in contaminated environments.

title: Enhancing sustainability in zinc electrowinning: Pre-oxidation modification of Pb-Ag electrodes for improved performance and reduced energy consumption
abstract: Conventional Pb-Ag anodes for zinc electrowinning suffer from high oxygen evolution overpotentials and severe galvanic corrosion. To address this, an innovative pre-oxidation strategy was developed that electrochemically modifies Pb-1wt.%Ag alloys in a Pb(II)-NaOH solution (0.1 mol/L Pb(II), 3 mol/L NaOH, 35 °C), constructing a multi-component PbO/α-PbO2/Ag interfacial layer. This seed layer directs in-situ formation of a hybrid β/α-PbO2 coating during operation, with XRD/SEM-EDS confirming Ag doping expands β-PbO2 (110) interplanar spacing by 0.02 Å – an unignorable enhancer of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. Electrochemical evaluations, including cyclic voltammetry (CV), linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and Tafel analyses demonstrate that the modified PbOn@Pb-Ag electrodes exhibit enhanced catalytic activity (335 mV reduction in OER overpotential) and corrosion resistance (96.3% lower corrosion rate (3.35 vs. 89.77 mm/a)). During zinc electrodeposition, the modified electrode demonstrated a 100 mV reduction in tank voltage compared to the conventional Pb-Ag anode. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a hybrid β-PbO2 and α-PbO2 layer, which offers superior catalytic and corrosion-resistant properties. These findings suggest that this surface modification technique not only improves electrode performance but also contributes to energy efficiency and sustainability in zinc electrowinning operations, aligning with the principles of cleaner production.

title: Advancing industrial-scale biogas production through cassava processing integration: From process water recovery to optimized multi-substrate digestion
abstract: Cassava processing industries generate substantial organic waste contributing to underutilized biomass streams that compromise energy efficiency in agricultural production systems. Cassava (Manihot esculenta) wastewater typically contains 8000–20,000 mg/L COD, whereas solid residues, such as peels and onggok, contain 15–50% total solids and a C/N ratio of 25–35, making them as highly suitable substrates for biogas production. This study introduces an integrated biogas production strategy that transforms cassava waste into a valuable energy resource through advanced multi-substrate anaerobic digestion (AD) and optimized parameters control. The system was implemented in three identical digesters (30 m diameter × 16 m height each) with total production rate of 72,000 Nm3/day. A closed-loop water management system was also implemented by recycling starch-rich process water to the digesters, simultaneously reducing freshwater consumption and increasing organic loading rate for enhanced biogas production. Stable anaerobic process conditions were observed at total alkalinity capacity (TAC) when ranged from 1850 to 3535 mg CaCO3/L, volatile organic acids (FOS)-to-TAC ratio up to 0.24, and pH between 6.83 and 7.57, which corresponded to controlled VFA accumulation and consistent methane production. By integrating diverse cassava fractions including starch, meal, fiber, and solid waste, methane content was significantly enhanced from 53.98 to 61.74%, compared to single-substrate digestion. Outlier removal using Z-score approach retained 62.4% of industrial-scale data, ensuring that subsequent analysis for optimization modeling was based on representative and reliable observations. Employing Response Surface Methodology (RSM), the multi-substrate approach optimized methane production, achieving a peak methane content of 62.39% under precisely controlled conditions (FOS 365 mg HAc/L, TAC 2771 mg CaCO3/L). Model validation through ANOVA confirmed RSM regression terms were statistically significant (F-value: 105.14, p-value <0.0001, R2 = 0.9563) with an overall desirability score of 0.801, indicating strong predictive reliability. The improved resource management system coupled with optimized multi-substrate AD and its significant methane quality improvements signal a promising pathway towards sustainable and decarbonized industrial energy systems.

title: Climate dynamics and air quality interactions: Machine learning analysis of diurnal temperature range drivers in three major Bangladesh cities
abstract: Satellite-derived land surface temperature diurnal range (LST-DTR), computed as the difference between MODIS daytime and nighttime LST, acts as a meaningful proxy for surface radiative dynamics in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study employed three machine learning algorithms (Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Decision Tree) integrated with SHAP importance analysis to quantify the impacts of black carbon (BC), PM2.5, aerosol, and albedo on LST-DTR across three major Bangladesh cities: Dhaka, Chattogram, and Rajshahi. Satellite-derived MODIS and MERRA-2 data (2001-2023) were analyzed using 5-fold cross-validation, yielding moderate yet stable model performance (R2 = 0.35-0.43; RMSE = 2.04-2.51). SHAP analysis showed BC as the dominant predictor in all three cities (SHAP importance: 0.94-1.59), highlighting its key role in urban land surface thermal dynamics through radiative absorption and surface albedo modification. Albedo emerged as a key secondary factor (0.30–1.27), ranking highest in Rajshahi, where it nearly matched BC, while Aerosols ranked second in Dhaka and Chattogram (0.27–0.94), and PM2.5 had the weakest influence (0.08-0.35). The dominance of BC over PM2.5 in LST-DTR modulation suggests that current air quality policies, which primarily focus on particulate matter, may overlook the most critical driver of urban land-surface thermal variability. The study provides evidence for targeted actions: encouraging diesel particulate filters, updating kiln technology, urban greening with high-albedo vegetation in fast-growing zones, and cool roofing with reflective materials. These findings inform evidence-based environmental policies for sustainable urban development in rapidly expanding South Asian cities.

title: Optimizing water-nitrogen management mitigates GHG emissions: microbial mediation across soil oxic and hypoxic interfaces
abstract: Over half of soil organic carbon and nitrogen are stored in subsoils deeper than 20 cm, and water-nitrogen management would stimulate the conversion of these buried nutrients into greenhouse gases (GHGs). Microorganisms are pivotal drivers underlying GHG conversion process, however, the specific microbial mechanism in soil profile remains unclear. Here, we conducted a field investigation and field experiment to investigate microbiome-driven effects on GHGs across soil oxic and hypoxic layers under the optimized water-nitrogen management, including irrigation regime (water-saving irrigation vs. flooding irrigation), irrigation water (aquaculture water vs. fresh water), and fertilizer dosage (reduced vs. traditional). Results showed that optimizing water-nitrogen management reduced nitrogen input and irrigation water volume by 3.7% and 17.6%, and effectively mitigated soil methane, carbon dioxide, and nitrous oxide by 52.1 ± 11.3%, 16.2 ± 6.2%, and 17.4 ± 5.4%, respectively. The optimized management improved soil oxidation-reduction potential and carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, and further downregulated microbial factors promoting GHGs. Specifically, optimizing water-nitrogen management preserved soil bacterial diversity, but the relative abundance of taxa associated with GHG-related functions was reduced by 1.5% in oxic layer and 56.7% in hypoxic layer. Moreover, optimizing water-nitrogen management resulted in reduced complexity and interspecies competition within bacterial networks in oxic layer and keystone networks in hypoxic layer. For microbial functions, genes associated with GHG production significantly decreased by 11.1%∼35.1% in hypoxic layer, and the related enzyme activities decreased by 11.4%∼27.6% in oxic layer and 16.2%∼40.1% in hypoxic layer. Noticeably, the specific microbial driving mechanisms on GHGs varied with soil layers. In the oxic layer, bacterial diversity, co-occurrence patterns, and enzyme activities promoted GHG emissions, whereas in the hypoxic layer, keystone taxa and microbial functional genes related to GHGs played a dominant role. Overall, our findings emphasized the importance of optimizing water-nitrogen management in regulating soil microbial traits and mitigating GHG emissions.

title: A green approach to photocatalysis: Silk-sericin-exfoliated MoS2 modified silk fabric for degradation of doxorubicin and textile wastewater
abstract: The treatment of pharmaceutical pollutants and textile wastewater has become increasingly important because these contaminants persist in the environment and pose risks to ecosystems and human health. Recently, photocatalysis has surfaced as a compelling strategy to address this critical issue. However, most photocatalytic systems rely on suspended powder catalysts that are difficult to recover and are often evaluated in simplified model solutions, thereby limiting their practical application. Furthermore, sustainable methods for incorporating photocatalysts into reusable, biodegradable substrates are underinvestigated. This study presents a novel biopolymer-based nanocomposite, silk fabric modified with molybdenum disulfide (silk-sericin/MoS2-coated fabric) as a scalable and environmentally sustainable alternative. This composite demonstrates potential as a photocatalytic agent for degrading both textile effluents and pharmaceutical substances, exemplified by the antineoplastic drug doxorubicin hydrochloride (DOX.HCl). Under optimal conditions, the silk-sericin/MoS2-coated fabric composite efficiently degrades DOX.HCl (94.32%) in just 30 min and degraded textile effluent (99.4%) within 90 min using advanced oxidation process (AOPs). The impacts of catalyst dosage, pollutant concentration, and oxidant level were investigated, and the system exhibited pseudo-first-order kinetics. To assess its practical application, the photocatalyst was evaluated in the presence of wastewater components, including dissolved salts, competing inorganic ions, and organic surfactants. These conditions slowed the reaction rate, but the catalyst maintained a clear and consistent degradation trend, suggesting high tolerance to matrix interference and suitability for real-world effluent conditions. We further examined the impact of scavengers on the degradation rate and determined that superoxide radicals (O2•-) primarily govern the degradation capacity, while hydroxyl radicals(•OH) serve as the principal pathway-controlling reactive oxygen species (ROS). This study shows that the silk-sericin/MoS2-coated fabric is a robust photocatalytic platform capable of addressing pharmaceutical contaminants and complex textile wastewater.

title: Mechanism of deep and selective sulfate removal from high-concentration CaCl2 solutions via porous interfacial deposition on calcium-modified carbon
abstract: Sulfate accumulation in industrial effluents severely impairs the production of high-quality calcium chloride (CaCl2), a high-value product with strong market adaptability whose economic benefits can well offset sulfate removal costs. Developing sulfate-selective adsorbents for high-concentration chloride systems remains a technical bottleneck, and herein, a calcium-modified porous biomass composite (ACCA) was synthesized via mechanochemical planetary ball-milling to address CaO agglomeration and poor stability. FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, TGA, and XPS confirmed ACCA has a well-developed porous structure with abundant Ca–O, C=O, and O–H groups. Calcium ions, as the intrinsic component of CaCl2 brine, were used as the core to enhance the positive interfacial charge of ACCA without introducing exogenous impurities, ensuring the purity of treated brine for high-quality CaCl2 preparation. ACCA achieved 84.874% sulfate removal in real 38∼40% CaCl2 brine, with highly dispersed Ca2+ capturing SO42− via electrostatic and complexation interactions against high-concentration Cl− interference. Kinetic, isotherm, TGA, and point-of-zero-charge (PZC ∼12.33) analyses confirmed that sulfate removal was dominated by chemical adsorption on a heterogeneous surface, which overcomes the high ionic-strength inhibition of traditional ion exchange and is suitable for continuous industrial processes. Post-adsorption studies confirmed the key role of Ca-O groups in sulfate binding, and the low solubility of CaSO4 in high-concentration CaCl2 brine synergized with adsorption to reduce sulfate levels. Raman spectroscopy and XPS clarified sulfate speciation (free ions/ion pairs) in the high-chloride system, shedding light on the removal mechanism. This work develops a high-performance ACCA for deep desulfurization of industrial CaCl2 brines and proposes a novel porous interfacial deposition strategy integrating solubility-controlled precipitation and targeted chemical adsorption, providing a feasible technical solution for deep sulfate removal and high-quality CaCl2 recovery from high-concentration chloride brines.

title: Mechanistic controls of soil organic matter content, water content and bulk density on soil screening levels: A VOC-focused evidence from contaminated sites in Jiangxi Province, China
abstract: China's new national soil screening levels (CSSLs) provide unified benchmarks, but the risks posed by local volatile organic compounds (VOCs) may require regional adaptation. Analyzing 4043 soil samples from Jiangxi Province in China, we evaluated 16 pollutants with concentrations exceeding the CSSLs. The application of region-specific soil parameters revealed substantial intra-provincial variation in the derived screening levels for VOCs. These discrepancies reached up to 533%, suggesting that even greater diversity likely exists at the national level. Mechanistic evaluations identified soil organic matter (fom), water content (Pws), and bulk density (ρb) as the dominant controls on VOC vapor intrusion. Crucially, we reveal that relying on the composite parameter of water-saturated porosity (θws) obscures the non-linear interactions between its independent driving factors, Pws and ρb. While Pws consistently suppresses exposure by restricting both gas-phase partitioning and effective diffusion, higher ρb exerts a dual role-initially promoting partitioning but ultimately physically impeding diffusion. Their effects are highly interdependent; increased ρb amplifies the suppressive impact of Pws on exposure levels. Furthermore, a clear mechanistic hierarchy emerges where strong sorption in high-fom soils effectively masks the physical impacts of Pws and ρb fluctuations, and high-Pws environments overshadow the effects of ρb. These findings provide a scientific basis for establishing a tiered national policy framework to optimize soil quality governance. We recommend combining conservative national baselines with region-specific soil screening levels, wherein fom serves as a mandatory baseline indicator, while the separate measurement of Pws and ρb should be prioritized in high-risk, low-fom areas. This approach provides a resource-efficient, scientific foundation for advancing environmental standardization in China and other geographically diverse nations.

title: Reverse solar interfacial evaporation for high salinity wastewater zero liquid discharge
abstract: The treatment of high salinity wastewater remains a major environmental challenge. Zero liquid discharge (ZLD) technology represents a promising solution; however, its large-scale application is hindered by high energy consumption and secondary environmental pollution during evaporation crystallization. This research proposes a novel strategy for ZLD based on advanced reverse solar interfacial evaporation. The proposed method separated the crystallization interface from the photothermal interface, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of salt crystallization on solar absorption, and the salt crystallization antiscalant was introduced to disrupt uniform nucleation of crystallization precursors and delay their precipitation. Experimental results demonstrated that salt crystals formed at the crystallization interface exert negligible influence on photothermal performance. The formation of micro-meniscuses liquid film between hydrophilic cotton fibers enhances Marangoni effect, improving evaporation efficiency and promoting NaCl crystallization at fiber tips. The composite antiscalant MDC220 could delay crystal nucleation, modify NaCl crystal morphology, boost crystallization efficiency during the initial stages of ZLD process. However, during continuous evaporation, pre-nucleated crystals may become encapsulated and overgrown by newly formed NaCl crystals, leading to salt layer clogging and reduced efficiency in later stages. These findings highlight the substantial potential of proposed reverse solar interfacial evaporation design and crystallization control strategy as a low-cost, energy-efficient, and sustainable solution for achieving ZLD in high salinity wastewater treatment.

title: Mapping biomass availability in China: Bridging theoretical potential to practical utilization through sustainability and cost analysis
abstract: Biomass holds significant promise for advancing China's goals in carbon neutrality and energy security. However, its sustainable use is constrained by logistical feasibility, economic barriers, and competition from alternative uses. Here, a systematic, spatially explicit assessment of agricultural residues, forestry residues, and livestock manure in China from 2000 to 2020 is presented, with biomass categorized into theoretical, collectible, and sustainable potentials at 1 km spatial resolution. Integrating statistical, spatial, and cost analyses, the assessment indicates that although China's annual theoretical biomass availability reaches 32.8 EJ yr−1, only about 25% (8.2 EJ yr−1) can be sustainably exploited for energy production due to collection constraints and competing uses. Sustainable biomass is concentrated in Northeast China, the North China Plain, and the Sichuan Basin, indicating strategic areas for bioenergy deployment. From 2000 to 2020, increases in theoretical biomass were jointly driven by intensity change (44.0%) and land-use change (56.0%), whereas the increase in sustainable biomass was influenced most strongly by rising availability (45.6%). Supply cost modelling reveals a steep marginal cost effect, with only 9.6% of sustainable biomass economically available below 30 $/t, but 72.9% becoming available at 40 $/t Our study presents a high-resolution, cost-informed framework for biomass use planning, highlighting key regions for strategic bioenergy deployment. These findings support the implementation of targeted policies and infrastructure investments to enhance the role of biomass in China's low-carbon transition.

title: Application research on indirect evaporative cooling systems with groundwater pre-cooling for multi-climate zone data centers
abstract: The ongoing surge in digital services has pushed data center (DC) energy demand to new heights, with cooling systems accounting for a dominant share and making sustainable cooling a pressing priority. Indirect evaporative cooling (IEC) is recognized as a promising sustainable solution. Although return air pre-cooling concepts have been previously explored, the specific integration of stable, low-temperature groundwater as a pre-cooling medium for IEC systems, and a systematic assessment of its cross-climatic applicability, remains insufficiently investigated. This paper investigates a system configuration that integrates groundwater pre-cooling with an IEC system, referred to as a Server Room Return Air Pre-cooling Type Indirect Evaporative Cooling (SERAP-IEC) system. Here, using a thermodynamic and energy consumption model established for a DC configuration based on an actual project, we evaluated system performance across five representative Chinese climate zones. The Simcenter Amesim platform simulated the pre-cooling finned-tube heat exchanger, and hourly annual energy analyses were conducted using Python. We found that the SERAP-IEC system can elevate climate switching thresholds by 3 °C–6 °C versus conventional IEC, potentially reducing annual high-energy hybrid mode operation by up to 22% in Xi'an and eliminating such operation in Kunming under simulated conditions. Total annual cooling energy consumption decreased by up to 15.05% in Xi'an, with a corresponding estimated Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) reduction of 0.01–0.03. These results further indicate that the system may contribute to significant annual CO2 emission reductions (estimated 1358.64 tons/year in Xi'an) and could decrease Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) by up to 71.57% in mild climates.

title: Impacts of artificial intelligence on urban carbon emission efficiency in China: A comparative analysis of geographic and network spillovers
abstract: As the digital economy reshapes production and governance, understanding whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to urban green transformation is critical for achieving carbon-neutrality goals. Existing studies mainly emphasize spillovers driven by geographic proximity, while paying limited attention to cross-regional transmission through innovation networks. Using panel data for 281 Chinese cities from 2000 to 2023, we construct a green innovation network-based spatial weight matrix from inter-city co-applied green patents and estimate the direct and spillover effects of AI on carbon emission efficiency (CEE) within a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM). We further apply Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) to characterize spatio-temporal heterogeneity. (1) We find that both AI-related intelligentization and CEE increase steadily over time, exhibiting a persistent “high in the southeast and low in the northwest” spatial pattern; meanwhile, China's green innovation network evolves from a single-core diffusion structure toward a more polycentric configuration. (2) The robot-based proxy for AI-related intelligentization is positively associated with local CEE and generates significant spillovers.
