Fundamental differences existed in nitrogen transformation pathways: during HTC, proteins were hydrolyzed into amino acids, which were converted to pyrrolic nitrogen and immobilized in the char skeleton; whereas pyrolysis induced in situ cyclization of nitrogen-containing intermediates, gradually forming pyridinic and quaternary nitrogen incorporated into the aromatic carbon structure. Although both organic extracts exhibited high HHVs (37.71–39.61 MJ/kg), their high nitrogen content (4.56–10.11 wt%) may pose a risk of nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions when used as fuel, necessitating subsequent upgrading treatment.

title: Satellite reconstruction of offshore wind turbine development processes in mainland China: Spatiotemporal patterns, installed capacity, and carbon reduction implications
abstract: Offshore wind power (OWP) has become an important pathway for mainland China to promote low-carbon energy transition and decarbonize its power system under the “dual-carbon” targets. To better understand the development process of OWP in mainland China and assess its contribution to global climate change mitigation, this study develops a Two-stage Offshore wind turbine (OWT) Identification Framework (TOIF) based on remote sensing. By integrating Random Forest (RF) pre-classification and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) refinement, the TOIF reconstructed a 15-year (2010–2024) OWT distribution dataset with an OWT identification accuracy of 0.9775. Based on scattering features derived from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, the hub heights of all identified OWTs were estimated and subsequently translated into the installed capacity of offshore wind farms (OWFs) using an empirical hub height–rated power relationship. Combined with grid emission factors and life-cycle emission factors, the resulting electricity generation was used to quantify the net carbon mitigation of the OWP sector. Results showed that by 2024, a total of 7236 OWTs had been installed along the coast of mainland China, with 71.6% of the installed capacity concentrated in the 3–6 MW range. Over the past 15 years, cumulative installed capacity reached approximately 37855 MW (empirical variation range: 33810-41900 MW), with Jiangsu and Guangdong provinces accounting for 30.7% and 27.3%, respectively. Spatially, OWT construction has evolved from early nearshore sites (typically <10 m deep and <15 km offshore before 2015) to a deployment across <40 m water depths and <30 km offshore distances, with provinces such as Jiangsu and Guangdong extending into the 30–60 km range. The year 2021 marked a major expansion in OWP development, with 2659 turbines installed and more than 13397 MW of new capacity added. Based on the total installed capacity, mainland China's OWP sector is estimated to achieve an annual carbon reduction of approximately 50–67 Mt in 2024. This study may serve as a reference for monitoring OWP deployment and evaluating carbon mitigation potential in coastal regions worldwide.

title: Valorization of phosphogypsum and municipal sludge into functional ceramic filter for closing the loop in the phosphorus chemical industry: A sustainable "waste-treats-waste" strategy
abstract: Targeting the "resource misallocation" of phosphogypsum (PG) pollution, this study proposes a sustainable "waste-treats-waste" strategy. By synergistically valorizing PG and municipal sludge, the phosphogypsum ceramic filter (PGC) was developed for the adsorptive treatment of phosphogypsum leachate (PGL). Specifically, PGC was fabricated via a two-stage thermal process (400 °C pre-calcination and 1000 °C co-sintering) using an optimal mass ratio of PG, sludge, and bentonite (4:4:2), wherein the sludge synergistically acted as a pore-forming agent. The optimized PGC exhibited robust mechanical strength (1.51 MPa) and satisfactory adsorption capacities (4.06 mg/g for phosphate, 1.61 mg/g for fluoride), validating its stability in dynamic filtration. To decouple the "black-box" mechanisms, a cross-scale verification framework was constructed. At the hydrodynamic level, the Wakao-Funazkri model revealed that hydraulic shear physically thinned the stagnant liquid film, effectively eliminating external mass transfer barriers. At the meso-scale, an interpretable Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR) model (R2 > 0.97) was developed to quantitatively optimize process parameters of flow rate, filtration time and filter bed height. Microscopically, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidated an intrinsic "adsorption-induced crystallization" mechanism, where surface Ca sites chemically anchor pollutants via strong orbital hybridization, inducing the growth of thermodynamically stable Ca3(PO4)2 and CaF2 phases to ensure secure immobilization. Life cycle cost assessment confirmed an ultra-low production cost of ∼$0.16 USD/kg. These reconfigure the PG valorization pathway, achieving the "Zero-waste" goal and transitioning toward a green closed-loop circular system for the phosphorus chemical industry.

title: A case study of R-corporation Eco-design internal system development
abstract: Recently, the quality gap in environmentally friendly products between large South Korean enterprises and advanced foreign companies has been notably narrowing. However, the quality of Green Products from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in South Korea remains comparatively low. This study specifically examines R-corporation, a medium-sized enterprise, which currently produces Green Products of lower quality than those of advanced competitors. To address this, an environmental assessment of R-corporation's current situation was conducted. Based on benchmarking advanced enterprises, a comprehensive Eco-strategy, detailed Guidelines, an Eco Tool, and an optimized Eco Process were developed and implemented. This approach, integrating principles of Eco-design, is expected to bring about significant positive effects within the Green Product industries. Furthermore, this initiative is anticipated to serve as a valuable case study, demonstrating how South Korean SMEs can enhance the global competitiveness of their environmentally friendly products.

title: Clean and efficient utilization of high-iron bauxite by reductive digestion based on structural modification
abstract: As the conventional Bayer process is the predominant method for alumina production from high-iron bauxite, its inherent inefficiency in iron recovery leads to substantial resource wastage and significant red mud discharge. To realize the comprehensive utilization of high-iron bauxite a novel structural modification-induced reductive digestion strategy was proposed to simultaneously enhance the alumina extraction and magnetize the iron minerals by generating reducing organics for following magnetic separation. The effects of key activation and digestion parameters on reductive digestion performance were investigated, and the associated kinetics and reaction mechanisms were elucidated. Elevated reductive digestion temperature and appropriate triethanolamine addition significantly promote both alumina digestion and iron recovery, whereas excessive activation temperature or duration leads to over-decomposition of polyethylene glycol. Under the optimized conditions, the alumina digestion efficiency reaches 96.96%, the TFe content in the iron concentrate attains 61.22% and the iron recovery efficiency reaches 91.99%. This work provides an effective and integrated strategy for the co-recovery of valuable metals from high-iron bauxite while minimizing red mud generation, offering a practical route toward more sustainable alumina production.

title: Food waste homogenizes anaerobic digestion performance across heterogeneous waste activated sludge through multi-scale metabolic convergence
abstract: Waste activated sludge (WAS) heterogeneity poses critical challenges for anaerobic digestion (AD), with organic matter variations causing substantial performance instability. This study demonstrates that food waste (FW) co-digestion acts as a “performance equalizer”, reducing methane yield variability from 22.6 to 8.8% across three heterogeneous WAS sources through multi-scale homogenization mechanisms. FW supplementation increased methane yields by 44.2–62.7% while narrowing VFA composition disparities from 16.8 to 4.6%. Mechanistic investigations revealed a hierarchical convergence cascade: (1) substrate-level compensation: FW-derived carbohydrates enhanced soluble substrates by 1.07-1.89-fold, with greatest augmentation in originally substrate-deficient systems; (2) microbial functional convergence: selective enrichment of identical functional guilds (Prevotella_7: 80.4-260.6%; Bathyarchaeia: 2.1-95.6%) established uniform hydrolytic-methanogenic capacities; (3) network reorganization: positive correlations increased from 60.8-63.2% to 69.7-80.2%, with convergent keystone species (Limosilactobacillus) coordinating syntrophic cooperation; and (4) metabolic pathway standardization: coordinated upregulation of acetate biosynthesis (ackA: 8.8-33.6%), methanogenesis (cdhC: 1.2-5.5-fold), and electron transfer genes (ribE: 22.4-67.6%) homogenized biochemical activity. This work provides mechanistic insights into achieving stable bioenergy recovery from heterogeneous WAS streams and practical guidance for implementing robust FW-WAS co-digestion systems in full-scale WWTPs.

title: Study on the interaction mechanisms of urban flood risk driving factors based on explainable machine learning: A human-centered assessment framework
abstract: Flood risk is shaped by the complex coupling of natural and human factors, and its scientific assessment is essential for reducing economic losses and enhancing urban resilience. However, incorporating nonlinear relationships, spatial heterogeneity, and dynamic population responses into flood-risk assessment remains challenging. In this study, an integrated people-centered assessment framework was developed by combining multi-source big data, RF–GeoShapley, and spatial statistical analysis. Hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and adaptability were systematically integrated to characterize flood risk from the perspective of spatiotemporal patterns, factor interactions, and population mobility responses. By introducing GeoShapley, this study identified the dominant factors affecting mobility responses under heavy rainfall and quantified their global contributions, nonlinear effects, and spatial interactions, thereby improving the interpretability of flood-risk assessment and reducing the subjectivity of weight allocation. The driving mechanisms of mobility responses were further examined at the functional-zone scale to support differentiated risk management. Using Jingdezhen City as a case study, the results show that flood risk exhibits significant spatial clustering and corridor-like extension. High-risk areas are concentrated in the central urban area, built-up areas along the Changjiang River, and the northern study area. Spatial location, housing price, rainfall intensity, and service accessibility make substantial contributions to explaining population mobility responses, with evident nonlinear, threshold, and spatially conditional effects. Residential areas, public administration and service areas, and industrial areas show more prominent risk structures, while dominant risk factors differ across functional zones. This study provides an interpretable approach for people-centered urban flood-risk assessment and targeted governance.

title: Innovation quality trade-offs in transport decarbonization: Evidence from EU environmental regulation and national resilience
abstract: This study examines how European Union (EU) transport-environment regulation shapes innovation quality across 14 major economies over 1998–2021. While prior studies have focused primarily on patent quantity, three gaps remain: quality–quantity trade-offs are empirically underspecified, mechanisms of differential national resilience are unclear, and instrument-specific long-run quality effects are poorly understood. Analyzing 43 policies and 147,832 patents classified under the Y02T10 Cooperative Patent Classification code for greenhouse gas-reducing road transportation technologies, we measure innovation quality using the Regulatory Quality-Adjusted Innovation Index (RQAI), which integrates forward citation impact, SciBERT-based semantic novelty, and Bayesian-weighted economic value. Results from exposure-weighted difference-in-differences and distributed lag models show that stricter regulatory exposure significantly increases patent quantities while degrading average innovation quality, which we term the regulatory "Quality Trap." The effect varies systematically by instrument type, with command-and-control regulation producing the largest and most persistent quality declines, while informational instruments generate positive long-run effects. Cross-national heterogeneity is substantial; the United Kingdom demonstrates greater resilience than its Group of Seven (G7) peers, consistent with stronger knowledge network centrality and dynamic capabilities. These findings refine the Porter Hypothesis by demonstrating that quantity-based patent metrics can obscure divergent quality trajectories and provide instrument-specific implications for sustaining transformative green innovation during decarbonization.

title: Integrated biodiversity, ecosystem services, and ecological connectivity for conservation effectiveness: Evidence from the Yuanjiang-Lixianjiang River basin, China
abstract: Global biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation have emerged as core challenges to sustainable human development, with establishing a well-connected, comprehensive global protected area system being an international consensus. River basins, as key biodiversity hotspots and hubs of ecosystem service provision, are critical for advancing global conservation goals. However, existing protected area planning lacks consideration of ecological connectivity and thus fails to meet the demands of preserving river basin ecosystem integrity. To address this gap, we proposed an optimized approach for river basin protected areas integrating biodiversity, ecosystem services, and ecological connectivity, using the Yuanjiang-Lixianjiang River Basin (YLRB) as a case study. We first assessed suitable habitats for 12 flora and fauna species, 4 ecosystem services, and their correlations; then identified key ecological pinch points between existing protected areas; next delineated priority conservation areas (PCA) via systematic conservation planning, overlaying these with pinch points to map integrated PCA and conservation gaps; finally, potential protected areas were determined based on gap priority and spatial clustering. Results showed: (1) a weak positive correlation between biodiversity and ecosystem services; (2) 10312.98 km2 (16.92%) of first priority and 11877.21 km2 (19.49%) of second priority conservation gaps; (3) 10963.53 km2 (17.99%) of highly aggregated potential protected areas. The optimized protected area expanded from 5953.65 km2 (9.77%) to 16917.18 km2 (27.76%), markedly improving conservation effectiveness. We further proposed hierarchical management and OECM-based supplementary protection for the YLRB. This approach addresses traditional planning limitations and provides a pathway for functional, connected river basin protected area networks.

title: Valorization of waste tire pyrolysis residues in sustainable asphalt pavements: Anti-UV mechanisms and eco-efficiency assessment
abstract: The valorization of waste materials in road engineering is pivotal for achieving carbon neutrality. This study investigates the potential of pyrolytic carbon black (PCB) derived from waste tires for developing anti-UV aging asphalt and elucidates the chemo-morphological evolution and eco-efficiency of the modified binder during long-term aging. PCB-modified asphalt (PCBMA) with a dosage of 10 wt% was prepared and subjected to accelerated indoor UV aging for up to 20 days. The performance evolution was evaluated via a comprehensive framework integrating microscopic characterization, macroscopic rheology, and environmental assessment, with base asphalt (BA) serving as the benchmark. Results indicate that the carbonaceous skeleton and inorganic ash (ZnO/ZnS) within PCB not only construct a physical shielding layer but also drive the migration of light components to the surface via a diffusion gradient. This process leads to the formation of an iridescent oil film, which functions as a dynamic oxygen barrier while maintaining surface hydrophobicity. The failure temperature increment of PCBMA was only one-third of that for BA, and its LAS fatigue life was extended by an order of magnitude. Furthermore, the asphalt matrix achieved a heavy metal immobilization efficiency exceeding 99.9%. Even under acid rain conditions, the leaching concentrations of toxic elements remained far below the Class II limit values for surface water. The annualized carbon footprint and production costs of PCBMA were significantly lower than those of BA. This research elucidates the synergistic anti-UV aging mechanism of PCBMA at the binder level, highlighting its potential as a sustainable modifier and laying a preliminary foundation for its future application in long-term durable asphalt infrastructure.

title: Environmental burdens eclipse economic gains: China's negative net benefit in global solar trade
abstract: Global photovoltaic (PV) supply chains, while accelerating energy transition, are reshaping climate governance through environmental cost transfers. This study integrates life-cycle data from 139 countries covering polysilicon, wafers, and modules, constructing a multi-regional model based on 2021 trade flows to reveal a critical paradox: despite commanding 80% of global PV market share, China bears $25.27 billion in net exported environmental costs, constructing a multi-regional model based on 2021 trade flows to reveal a critical disconnect: despite commanding 80% of global PV market share, China bears $25.27 billion in net exported environmental costs, which, when internalized, result in overall net benefits of −$2.15 billion. This finding challenges conventional trade advantage paradigms by revealing a systematic transfer of environmental burdens from high-regulation regions (e.g., EU/US) to low-regulation areas, resulting in a net outflow of environmental costs for manufacturing hubs like China. Four policy scenario simulations demonstrate the limitations of unilateral measures: developing countries' carbon tariff retaliation slashes China's module net benefits by 325.9% while increasing global emissions, whereas green hydrogen technological breakthroughs show transformative potential—converting China's wafer and module trade deficits to positive net benefits of $1.45 billion and $9.65 billion respectively. The study proposes a tiered carbon pricing system coupled with technology transfer compensation mechanisms, providing scientific basis to reconcile global supply chain security with climate justice. These findings carry significant policy implications for multilateral governance under the Paris Agreement framework.

title: Climate-smart straw return amplifies CO2 fertilization effects while decoupling N2O emissions: Evidence from soil metagenomics and metabolomics
abstract: Straw return is a key agricultural practice for soil carbon sequestration, but its effect on nitrogen cycling and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, especially under future elevated atmospheric CO2 conditions (eCO2), remains poorly understood. Critically, while the individual effects of eCO2 and straw return on N2O emissions have been studied separately, a significant research gap exists regarding their combined and interactive effects, particularly in leguminous systems like soybean. Furthermore, most studies have failed to integrate functional genes, metabolites, and microbial diversity into a unified mechanistic framework, leaving the underlying mechanisms between genetic potential and actual N2O emissions largely unexplored. To address these gaps, a controlled experiment was conducted with soybean to investigate the individual and combined effects of straw return and eCO2 on plant growth, soil properties, enzyme activities, N2O emissions, and the underlying microbial and metabolic mechanisms. The combined application of eCO2 and straw return synergistically increased soybean aboveground biomass by 82.25% and significantly enhanced total nitrogen by 26.37%. However, this treatment also induced a pronounced shift in the soil nitrogen cycle towards higher N2O production potential. Notably, straw return significantly increased the abundance of denitrification genes (narG, nirK) and the (nirK + nirS)/nosZ ratio, elevating genetic potential for N2O production, yet N2O emissions under combined treatment showed a non-significant decreasing trend. This decoupling was attributed to sharp reductions in nitrate reductase activity (−74.47%) and soil NO3−-N content (−58.37%), imposing substrate limitation on denitrifiers. These genetic changes were linked to increased abundances of key bacterial phyla (e.g., Nitrospirae, Candidatus_Rokubacteria) and correlated with a spike in N2O emissions at the flowering stage. Metabolomic profiling revealed that L-alloisoleucine, a branched-chain amino acid derivative, exhibited strong positive association with Nitrospirae (r > 0.8, p < 0.05) under straw return, though this association was attenuated under eCO2, suggesting CO2-mediated modulation of plant-microbe metabolite signaling. Our findings demonstrate that integrating straw return with eCO2 enhances crop productivity and labile carbon pools while decoupling N2O genetic potential from realized emissions. This study provides mechanistic insights and practical guidance for optimizing straw residue utilization to achieve cleaner agricultural production under future atmospheric CO2 scenarios.

title: The adsorption study of an azo dye using graphene oxide derived from sugarcane bagasse as a green precursor: A waste-to-resource supply chain
abstract: The valorization of agricultural waste into functional carbon materials offers a promising approach for sustainable wastewater remediation. Herein, graphene oxide (GO) is synthesized from sugarcane bagasse (SB), a low-cost and renewable precursor, thereby managing both water contamination and waste disposal. The physicochemical characterization revealed that the SB-derived GO (SBGO) possessed abundant oxygen-containing functional groups and a porous morphology (surface area = 192.65 m2/g). The adsorption performance of SBGO for removing Basic Blue 41 (BB41) dye was examined in a batch system under various operating parameters, revealing that initial pH, adsorbent dosage, and dye concentration significantly influenced the process. The adsorption isotherm followed the Langmuir and Temkin models, and the pseudo-second order model provided a good explanation of the kinetics. The negative values of ΔH° (−13.90 kJ/mol) and ΔG° in the thermodynamic examination exhibited that the adsorption was exothermic and spontaneous. Optimization applying response surface methodology (RSM) based on central composite design (CCD) identified optimal values of initial pH (10), SBGO dosage (0.4 g/L), and BB41 concentration (227 mg/L), resulting in a removal efficiency of 89.74% and an adsorption capacity of 510.48 mg/g. Furthermore, the mechanism investigation indicated physical adsorption was more dominant than chemisorption, as evidenced by the ΔG° and ΔH° values. SBGO demonstrated acceptable regeneration performance over four cycles, highlighting its stability and reusability. Overall, SBGO, as a green and high-performance adsorbent, not only shows promising potential to address environmental challenges posed by dye-contaminated water but also contributes to the circular economy by providing a waste-to-resource supply chain approach.

title: Sustainable recycling of waste crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules based on heavy liquid separation and metal chloride etching
abstract: This study proposes an environmentally friendly treatment process based on heavy liquid separation and metal chloride etching for the recovery of valuable resources from crystalline silicon photovoltaic (c-Si PV) modules. It addresses key limitations of conventional recycling methods, such as low component separation efficiency and heavy reliance on strong acids and alkalis in hydrometallurgical steps. In the separation stage, the zinc bromide (ZnBr2) heavy liquid method is used to achieve highly efficient (>98%) separation among glass particles, solar cells, and solder strips. In the purification stage, a metal chloride etching approach is employed. Under hydrothermal conditions, a synergistic etchant composed of aluminum chloride hexahydrate (AlCl3·6H2O) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) completely removes silver (Ag), aluminum (Al), and silicon nitride (Si3N4) from the solar cell surface. Then copper chloride dihydrate (CuCl2·2H2O) solution is utilized to effectively remove lead (Pb) and tin (Sn) from the solder strips. Ultimately, valuable materials such as silicon wafers, silver chloride (AgCl), and copper (Cu) are successfully recovered. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) confirm that the proposed process is a sustainable recycling solution for c-Si PV modules, offering both environmental benefits and industrial scalability. Building on these results, this study proposes a novel green and low-toxic recycling strategy for end-of-life c-Si PV modules, providing a viable technical pathway toward sustainable development of the photovoltaic industry.

title: Modeling food security risk propagation: A hybrid static-dynamic analytical framework
abstract: Multiple concurrent crises including conflict, climate change, and economic volatility are intensifying global food security risks (FSRs). Ignoring FSR propagation dynamics can lead to critical bottlenecks and suboptimal policies. To bridge this gap, this study introduces a hybrid static-dynamic analytical framework within the Chinese context. 53 key FSR factors across the four dimensions of availability, access, utilization, and stability are identified, and their interactions are quantified through expert elicitation. These interactions are then modeled using a directed weighted network for static topological analysis and a modified susceptible-infectious-recovered model for dynamic propagation simulation. The analysis reveals that the FSR system exhibits a sparse (density = 0.055), modular (modularity = 0.314), core-periphery network structure with a small-world propensity of 0.785, suggesting a possible explanation for how localized perturbations could escalate into systemic crises. Within this structure, food price volatility, high production costs, and agroecosystem degradation act as highly connected hubs; low cultivation willingness and land-use change serve as critical bridges; and insufficient agricultural infrastructure alongside the prevalence of smallholder agriculture function as primary risk sources. Simulation results indicate that perturbations from production base, natural environment, international shocks, or management system can trigger the most severe FSR propagation yet offer the greatest mitigation potential. This suggests that fundamental food security threats may stem not only from external shocks but also from deep-seated domestic vulnerabilities. By mapping these micro-level structural and dynamic features, this study provides a preliminary foundation for developing targeted, systemically informed FSR management strategies.

title: A Ca-MOF@COF composite and its in situ grown gel membrane for highly efficient capture of Cd2+
abstract: Rapid and efficient adsorption of Cd2+ is crucial for water resource remediation and environmental protection. MOF@COF composites have emerged as breakthrough adsorbent materials that integrate the abundant active sites of MOFs with the robust stability of COFs. However, conventional MOF@COF hybrids suffer from the risk of toxic metal ion leaching, posing a secondary pollution risk. Addressing this critical challenge, this work pioneers a novel environmental safety Ca-MOF@COF hybrid composite using biocompatible and low-cost Ca2+ as the metal nodes, followed by fabricating a uniform Ca-MOF@COF gel membrane via controlled in situ growth on a polyacrylamide substrate. Integrated experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate the synergistic integration of Ca-MOF and COF not only creates a stable framework with enhanced interfacial contact but also provides dual binding sites, leading to superior adsorption performance surpassing both their parent components. The Ca-MOF@COF composite reached an adsorption capacity as high as 212.0 mg g−1 for Cd2+ within 15 min. Furthermore, the composite and gel membrane maintains consistent high adsorption efficiency for Cd2+ in six natural water samples collected from lakes/rivers across six provinces with distinct geographic zones. This study not only develops a promising environmental safety adsorbent for Cd2+ remediation but also provides a new strategy for designing safe and efficient MOF@COF hybrids for environmental applications.

title: Transformation and iodination mechanisms of tyrosine to disinfection byproducts in mixed-halide waters
abstract: Tyrosine (Tyr) is a crucial precursor for iodinated disinfection byproducts (I-DBPs) in mixed-halide waters. However, its transformation mechanism in such complex systems remains poorly understood. Herein, we employed a novel approach by integrating kinetic experiments, spectroscopic analysis, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to systematically understand the mechanisms of bromide (Br−)-modulated Tyr transformation and iodination. Kinetic results demonstrated that Br− significantly accelerated Tyr degradation (kapp = 3.23 × 102 M−1s−1) by forming the reactive HOBr. Br− facilitated the conversion of iodide (I−) to stable iodate. Spectral analysis indicated that the presence of Br− shifted the reaction pathway from carboxyl oxidation to electrophilic substitution on the aromatic ring. On the basis of the 104 transformation products identified by HRMS, three degradation pathways for Tyr were proposed. Calculated additive toxicity analysis of four typical aliphatic DBPs revealed that I-DBPs were the major contributors to cytotoxicity. DFT calculations showed that H2OI+ was thermodynamically and kinetically favored under water-assisted conditions. Furthermore, within the studied pH range (6.5–8.5), the total I-DBP yield increased and was associated with the enhanced contribution of deprotonated Tyr (Tyr–), despite the reduced availability of reactive iodinating electrophiles. These results provide molecular-level insights into the complex reactions in mixed-halide systems and highlight important implications for the cytotoxicity risk of disinfection byproducts while disinfecting such waters.

title: Parametric module library for automated design of precast concrete components integrating DFMA and BIM
abstract: This paper presents an automated design methodology that integrates design for manufacturing and assembly (DFMA) with parametric building information modelling (BIM) for precast concrete (PC) construction. A DFMA-oriented module library is developed by defining modular design rules, embedding manufacturing and assembly knowledge, and implementing combinatorial algorithms through secondary BIM development. This approach enables the flexible generation of vertical, horizontal, and irregular modules, which can be rapidly combined into standardised components. A large-scale residential case study demonstrates that parametric modules can be modelled within minutes, achieving an average improvement of 73.9% in design efficiency and a 67% reduction in costs. In addition to accelerating modelling processes, the framework establishes a cloud-based environment that supports seamless data transfer across design, manufacturing, and assembly, thereby ensuring enhanced constructability and reliability. The proposed methodology offers a scalable pathway for industrialised construction, providing both theoretical insights and practical solutions for automation-driven prefabricated building design.

title: Ecological footprint, renewable energy, and growth in Europe: Exploring the roles of innovation-driven agriculture, governance effectiveness, and regulatory synergy
abstract:
This study examines the EU-27's transition toward ecological sustainability, focusing on the interlinkages between renewable energy consumption, ecological footprint, and real economic growth within the European Green Deal framework. Using FMOLS, DOLS, Westerlund cointegration, and MMQR over 2002–2021, it assesses both long- and short-run dynamics, incorporating innovation, agricultural value addition, and institutional quality in relation to SDGs 7, 8, and 13.
Results
show that renewable energy and innovation-driven agriculture improve ecological outcomes, while economic growth and institutional quality yield mixed effects, indicating trade-offs in the growth–environment nexus. Causality tests reveal bidirectional links in agriculture and key unidirectional effects from renewable energy, innovation, and regulation toward ecological outcomes, with additional feedback from growth to renewable energy and governance. Overall, the findings highlight that achieving carbon neutrality depends on coherent policy design that strengthens innovation, governance, and regulatory quality. Strong multilevel coordination, consistent with SDG 17, is essential to align economic growth with long-term ecological sustainability in the EU-27.

title: The ecological environment and production efficiency of cities: An empirical study based on ecological restoration and urban repair policy in China
abstract: The advancement of social economy development has propelled urban development, while within cities, there exists a conflict between the ecological environment and social economy growth. Improving the urban ecological environment has become a key pathway to promoting sustainable urban socio-economic development. To explore the feasibility of this approach, we use China's Ecological Restoration and Urban Repair Policy as a natural experiment, employing an unbalanced panel dataset from 285 cities between 2005 and 2021. A difference-in-differences model is adopted to evaluate the impact of urban ecological environments on urban productivity. The results indicate that improving the urban ecological environment significantly enhances urban production efficiency, and this result remains valid after various robustness tests. Further analysis shows that improving the ecological environment indirectly impacts urban productivity by promoting infrastructure construction, digitization and resource allocation efficiency. In addition, this conclusion is affected by urban agglomeration and regional differences between north and south, resulting in significant heterogeneity. These findings confirm the importance of the urban ecological environment for urban social economy growth, extend the theoretical boundaries of the Environmental Kuznets Curve, and provide research references and policy recommendations for harmonized urban development.

title: A novel approach for advanced removal of iron impurities from vein quartz: Mechanism and process of stepwise chlorination roasting
abstract: Iron (Fe) impurities represent a significant challenge in producing high-purity quartz sand from vein quartz. Conventional purification methods are characterized by low Fe removal efficiencies and high operational costs. This study systematically investigates the thermodynamic behavior of Fe impurities as they react with various chlorinating agents, depending on their occurrence states. Based on these insights, a novel stepwise chlorination roasting process has been developed. In the first stage, surface and exposed Fe impurities are removed through low-temperature roasting (673-973 K) using NH4Cl. In the second stage, internal Fe impurities are eliminated at elevated temperatures (1073-1373 K) using Cl2. Following staged chlorination roasting, the Fe content in quartz decreased from 2081.22 μg/g to 20.20 μg/g, achieving an Fe removal efficiency of 99.03%, which significantly surpasses that of conventional roasting-acid leaching methods. The stepwise chlorination treatment not only enhances quartz porosity, promoting the exposure and removal of internal Fe impurities but also induces surface defects and structural rearrangements that facilitate the migration and elimination of lattice-bound Fe. This process utilizes the advantages of chlorination roasting to achieve highly efficient and thorough iron removal during the pyrometallurgical roasting stage. This approach eliminates the need for an acid leaching stage, offering a novel method for the efficient, low-cost purification of low-grade quartz ore.

title: Impact of coal mines on aquifer vulnerability and groundwater quality: A DRASTIC-based modified approach in the Raniganj Coalfield (Lower Gondwana) in eastern India
abstract: The Raniganj Coalfield in eastern India is the oldest coalfield in the country. Due to the prolonged exposure to the coal mining industry, the areas in and around this coalfield have witnessed rapid land degradation and deteriorating quality of groundwater. Although studies on hydrogeochemical characteristics of groundwater in this Lower Gondwana Coalfield are common, analyses of aquifer vulnerability to pollution are relatively lacking. In this study, the DRASTIC model has been applied to assess the groundwater vulnerability and also the validity has been checked with respect to groundwater quality parameters which were obtained from point locations given by the Central Groundwater Board. The groundwater geochemistry was assessed with the help of the Piper Trilinear Plot and its suitability for domestic and irrigation purposes was determined by the popular water quality indices (WQI). The Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve was then applied to validate the WQI and DRASTIC- based aquifer vulnerability and the Area Under Curve (AUC) was obtained as 0.22. Considering the relatively low validation scores, the existing DRASTIC Model was modified by taking into consideration five other factors viz., distance from mines, industries and water treatment plant as well as slope and topographic wetness index with a combined AUC of 0.87. Finally, the administrative units were classified based on the ROC category and a sample unit was considered from each category for perception survey. It is concluded that coal mines play a detrimental role to groundwater quality and any model on aquifer vulnerability should be customized with respect to coal mines for better reliability.

title: Measuring carbon footprints of renewable energy driven seawater desalination retrofitting in China's coastal areas
abstract: China's seawater desalination capacity has expanded rapidly to address water scarcity, yet its reliance on the carbon-intensive power grid poses a significant challenge to the national carbon neutrality target. In line with the low-carbon retrofitting of seawater desalination projects nationwide, this study establishes the life-cycle carbon footprint accounting framework for 150 reprehensive seawater desalination projects in China, quantifies their carbon emissions and mitigation potential during low-carbon transition from 2026 to 2045, and proposes a phased large-scale retrofitting scheme based on national action plans, which provides a critical pathway analysis towards the 2060 carbon neutrality goal. The results indicated that the total carbon emissions of wind-powered seawater desalination projects decreased by about 20.54% compared to pre-retrofitting levels, while solar-driven projects achieved a reduction of about 11.13%. The annual carbon emissions of seawater desalination projects in China can be reduced by about 5.23 E+05∼7.63 E+05 tCO2e after the renewable energy retrofitting, representing a 17.72% reduction compared to pre-retrofitting levels. The operational carbon emission reductions accumulated from retrofitted seawater desalination projects can offset the embodied carbon emissions of the retrofitting investment within 2.23 years. The proposed carbon accounting methodology and transition strategies provide valuable references for establishing low-carbon water supply systems in coastal nations and water-scarce regions, while offering essential guidance for in-depth optimization of energy structures and low-carbon transition pathways in the global desalination industry.

title: Reinforcing sustainable growth: The co-evolution of digitalization, green innovation, and ecological transition
abstract: The environmental implications of the digital economy remain debated, as most empirical studies focus primarily on carbon emissions while overlooking broader ecological pressures and the structural conditions shaping environmental outcomes. This study investigates how the digital economy (DE) and green innovation (GI) influence the ecological footprint (EF), while accounting for the conditional roles of renewable energy transition (RET) and industrial structure (IS) across 37 OECD countries from 2008 to 2023. To operationalize these relationships, DE is measured using a composite index reflecting digital infrastructure and technology diffusion; GI is proxied by environment-related patent activity; EF is derived from the Global Footprint Network accounting framework; RET represents the share of renewable energy in final energy consumption; and IS captures structural upgrading toward advanced, less resource-intensive sectors. The analysis employs second-generation panel techniques and Dynamic Common Correlated Effects estimators to address cross-sectional dependence, heterogeneity, and unobserved common factors. The empirical results indicate that DE significantly reduces EF, implying that expansion of the digital economy is associated with improved ecological efficiency. Similarly, GI contributes to lower EF by supporting environmentally oriented technological progress. Additionally, the environmental benefits of DE are amplified when supported by a high share of renewable energy, particularly through the integration of digital platforms, smart grids, and intelligent management systems. Moreover, economies with less resource-intensive industrial structures can better leverage digitalization for ecological gains through automation, precision manufacturing, and value-added services. The findings suggest that DE promotes renewable energy transition and industrial restructuring, whereas GI more directly shapes ecological outcomes.

title: Research on low-altitude technology adoption in the green transformation of forest supply chains: A socio-technical co-construction perspective
abstract: The application of low-altitude technology in the forest supply chain is not a matter of whether the technology is feasible. This article examines these adoption mechanisms in combination with online discourse analysis and survey modeling. First of all, we use LDA topic modeling and BERT for emotional analysis, analyze 6727 social media comments on low-altitude technology, and identify four cognitive dimensions: risk cognition, innovation cognition, value cognition and functional cognition. Then, we used the structural equation model to test these four dimensions with the survey data of 413 practitioners. Value cognition and risk cognition have the strongest impact on the adoption of intentions, followed by innovative cognition; it is worth noting that functional cognition is not significant (β = 0.164, p = 0.063). The results show that the application of drones is not only evaluated as an operating tool. In the forest supply chain, the technical performance of the foundation may have become a threshold condition, and adoption behavior is more affected by perceived ecological values, confidence in risk management, and expectations for technological innovation. Linking online discourse with behavioral intentions, this study offers a more down-to-earth explanation for how low-altitude technology supports clean production in forestry. Future studies can also use longitudinal or cross-regional evidence to test these relationships.

title: A two-dimensional cloud model for agrivoltaic project risk assessment in rural China
abstract: Agrivoltaics (AV) offers an effective solution to reconcile the conflict between China's limited land resources and its massive demand for clean energy; however, the complexity of rural socio-technical systems and the dynamic nature of project life cycles present overlapping multi-risk challenges for AV projects. This study constructs a two-dimensional cloud model for project risk analysis to achieve the quantification and visualization of dual risk dimensions, thereby filling the gap in existing research regarding uncertainty management and the characterization of two-dimensional risk features. The findings indicate that the risk factors of rural AV projects are complex and exhibit close nonlinear interdependencies. Overall, rural AV projects in China are situated within a high-risk interval, characterized by a core profile of “high occurrence frequency–medium severity.” Technical and organizational risks occupy critical positions in the risk assessment, with technical adaptability being the most sensitive factor. Through multi-scenario empirical research on four typical cases, significant differences were found in the risk levels and dominant factors across different regions, with the northwest exhibiting significantly higher risks than the southwest and north China regions. Theoretically, this research identifies risk derivative mechanisms under collective land ownership. Methodologically, it pioneers a two-dimensional cloud model framework, forming an “identification–association–two-dimensional quantification” chain to manage randomness and fuzziness. Practically, it offers differentiated governance strategies, providing methodological guidance for investment and scientific support for the sustainable development of rural AV projects.

title: Decoding spatiotemporal signatures of membrane drying in PEM fuel cell via distributed sensing and attentive deep learning
abstract: Accurate and timely diagnosis of membrane drying in proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells remains challenging, primarily due to the limited spatial resolution of conventional, externally measured lumped sensor data. To address this gap, this paper proposes an attentive deep learning framework that leverages distributed sensing to directly capture and decode spatiotemporal patterns and internal current density heterogeneity associated with membrane drying. This paper pioneers the use of internal current density distribution for diagnosis, directly linking its spatiotemporal evolution to gradient membrane drying conditions. The developed CNN-LSTM-SEAM framework effectively integrates convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory network (LSTM), and squeeze-and-excitation attention mechanism (SEAM) to jointly model spatial distributions and temporal dynamic. The attention-weighted reverse decoding mechanism innovatively provides interpretable insights into characteristic contributions. An attention-weighted reverse decoding mechanism is designed to provide interpretable insights by quantifying the contribution of spatiotemporal features to the diagnosis. Extensive validation confirms diagnostic accuracy above 99.30% and identifies the inlet/outlet as critical zones. This work presents a novel, interpretable approach that enhances both the precision and mechanistic understanding of membrane drying fault diagnosis in PEM fuel cells.

title: Low-carbon and robust optimal scheduling strategy for park-level integrated energy system considering supply-side participation in carbon tariff mitigation
abstract: Exporting firms face significant impacts from carbon tariffs. However, since these firms bear the burden of carbon tariffs while the energy supply side does not bear it directly, there is currently a lack of proactive participation by the supply side in addressing carbon tariffs. Therefore, this study constructs a bi-level model comprising a park-level integrated energy system (PIES) and exporting firms, utilizing energy flows embedded with economic and environmental attributes to achieve supply–demand coordination in response to carbon tariffs. Furthermore, the carbon tariff accounting framework proposed in this paper excludes the free carbon allowances of the carbon market in the country of origin when calculating the effective carbon price, which aligns with existing policies. The research findings reveal the following: first, active participation by PIES in carbon tariff mitigation can reduce carbon tariff costs by up to 32.07% and total system costs by 8.44%, confirming the necessity of incorporating carbon tariff costs into supply-side decision-making to foster its proactive participation. Second, compared to existing studies, the carbon tariff accounting framework proposed in this work improves the accuracy of carbon tariff calculations by 12.14%. Finally, the study finds that carbon capture and storage (CCS) plays a crucial role in mitigating the impact of carbon tariffs owing to its flexibility in capturing carbon based on system conditions, and its ability to compensate for low-carbon energy shortages and stabilize energy and carbon emission costs under the renewable energy uncertainty.

title: High-performance, fully bio-based cellulose hazy film via competitive dissolution induced in-situ scatterer construction and impregnation hydrophobic surface modification
abstract: Hydrophobic glycerol-containing regenerated cellulose composite films (GL-MCFs) are successfully prepared through a competitive dissolution and impregnation hydrophobic surface modification (IHSM) process. The addition of glycerol (GL) induces competition between hydrogen bonding sites, leading to the formation of micron-scale fibers that function as in-situ light scatterers, subsequently, IHSM is performed using soybean oil anhydride. The resulting fully bio-based films exhibit outstanding transparency exceeding 93% at 550 nm and a widely tunable haze range from 2.81 ± 0.37% to 93.45 ± 0.88%, while surface modification significantly enhances hydrophobicity, achieving a water contact angle of 103.9 ± 0.9o. Specially, 3D Raman mapping confirms uniformity and effectiveness of esterification throughout the film thickness. When applied as light-managing layers in solar cells, the film increases the photoelectric conversion efficiency by 10.04%. This work establishes an environmentally friendly preparation pathway for high-performance cellulose optical materials, positioning them within the family of fully bio-based plastics and offers a sustainable alternative for optoelectronic applications distinct from traditional petroleum-based substrates.

title: Producing purple bacteria in a membrane bioreactor for fish feed: Enhancing growth, immunity, and survival of GIFT tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: The dependence of aquafeeds on environmentally detrimental protein sources such as fishmeal and soybean meal necessitates the creation of sustainable alternatives. Purple phototrophic bacteria (PPB) are a promising, protein-rich alternative to fishmeal with beneficial antioxidants, although it remains unclear whether PPB-exclusive diets can concurrently optimize growth performance and enhance disease resistance in fish. This study assessed PPB, a single-cell protein derived from organic wastewater, as an innovative feed component for GIFT tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). Utilizing a phototrophic membrane bioreactor (MBR) tailored for varying light and sludge retention time conditions, PPB enrichment was elevated to 79.9%, resulting in >70% COD removal and ∼100% ammonium removal, while transforming organic contaminants into useful biomass rich in protein and pigments. In a 5-week feeding trial, tilapia fed on a 50% PPB diet achieved a superior weight gain rate of 399.3% and a better feed conversion ratio of 2.77 compared to those on the commercial diet (234.3% and 3.21, respectively). Besides, the 100% PPB diet conferred a substantially enhanced resistance to Vibrio parahaemolyticus, reducing cumulative mortality by 70% compared to the commercial diet control (100%). Based on economic analysis including capital expenses and operational expenses, the production cost of PPB in the MBR was $0.56 kg−1, demonstrating its strong economic competitiveness. It proposes the viability of the PPB-MBR system as a sustainable platform for organic wastewater treatment and aquafeed production, hence promoting a circular bioeconomy in aquaculture.

title: Towards a cleaner food supply chain: power asymmetry, cooperation, and food waste—a hybrid evolutionary-game and agent-based analysis
abstract: Food waste remains a major global challenge driven not only by technical inefficiencies but also by a lack of coordination among supply chain actors. This paper develops a theoretical framework to examine how cooperation between farmers and retailers can emerge under different forms of power asymmetry, proxied by the allocation of revenue and burden of food waste. Using a hybrid approach that combines evolutionary game theory with an agent-based model (ABM), we simulate how cooperation evolves when players adapt through social learning, bounded rationality, and repeated interaction. Results show that the distribution of benefits and burdens strongly shapes cooperative behavior: higher retailer revenue shares shift cooperation downstream while lower shares shift it upstream to farmers. Across several scenarios, the ABM predicts that cooperative clusters may persist even when deterministic models forecast defection. These findings suggest that real supply chains—characterized by heterogeneity, uncertainty, and localized learning—may sustain more cooperation than standard analytical models imply. The framework offers policy-relevant insights into how adjusting revenue- and burden-sharing mechanisms, together with fostering communication and repeated interaction, can strengthen collaborative efforts to reduce food waste in agri-food systems.

title: Sustainable valorization of olive pomace into functional edible films: Application in Kashar cheese packaging
abstract: Growing interest in sustainable packaging has encouraged the application of agricultural by-product–based industrial products as value-added functional components. In this study, olive pomace (OP), the main residue of olive oil processing, was utilized as a natural bioactive ingredient in gelatin-based edible films and evaluated for its implementation in Kashar cheese packaging. Films containing 5%, 10%, and 15% OP extract were prepared and then assessed for their physical, mechanical, optical, and antioxidant properties. Addition of OP significantly increased total phenolics (TP) and enhanced antioxidant activity (AA), confirming the effective transfer of bioactive compounds into the film matrix. Film thickness remained stable (≈0.16 mm) across all formulations, indicating that OP addition did not affect film formation conditions. The addition of OP resulted in higher tensile strength and lower elongation at break, implying a more compact and strongly interacting polymer structure. Water solubility and water vapor permeability (WVP) exhibited concentration-dependent changes, with WVP values decreasing at lower OP levels (5%) and slightly increasing at higher concentrations, indicating structural modifications within the film matrix. Sensory evaluation of Kashar cheese coated with OP-containing films revealed that formulations with 5–10% OP maintained acceptable color, flavour, and overall acceptability, whereas 15% OP resulted in noticeably lower sensory scores. These findings demonstrate that OP can be effectively valorized into functional edible films exhibiting enhanced antioxidant and mechanical properties. Importantly, optimal OP concentrations (5–10%) enable the development of sustainable packaging systems without compromising sensory quality, highlighting the potential of this approach as a cleaner production strategy for value-added utilization of olive oil processing residues.

title: Pollutants in urban shield tunneling muck: detection methods, occurrence characteristics, and ecological toxicity assessment
abstract: Residual additives used in shield tunneling remain in shield muck, posing potential ecological risks and hindering its utilization, yet this issue has received limited attention. This study presents the first systematic investigation of pollutants in shield muck in China. A comprehensive field survey was conducted across 14 shield muck projects in the Pearl River Delta. High-resolution mass spectrometry was employed to characterize the major pollutant components, and analytical methods were developed for three key pollutant classes, with special emphasis on establishing a low-toxicity-solvent, in situ-compatible pretreatment and detection method for anionic surfactants. Representative pollutant concentrations in shield muck were then systematically analyzed, followed by ecological toxicity assessment. The results revealed the presence of multiple high-risk pollutants in shield muck, including anionic surfactants, petroleum hydrocarbons, and heavy metals. The analysis method for alkyl ether sulfates (AES) significantly improved detection accuracy and efficiency, with excellent precision (RSD<1.22%) and recoveries (99.8–103.3%). AES concentrations ranged from 28.32 to 288.68 mg/kg in shield muck and 0.64 to 4.81 mg/L in leachate, with all leachate concentrations exceeding the regulatory threshold of 0.5 mg/L. Bioassay results using Vibrio fischeri showed strong inhibition of bioluminescence in leachate samples, with inhibition rates reaching up to 99.66%, and a mean inhibition of 30.46%. ECOSAR modeling further predicted relatively low toxicity for AES-type surfactants (ChV: 20.10–70.30 ppm). This study clarifies the nature and extent of shield muck pollution and provides a scientific basis for its sustainable management and utilization.

title: Contrasting but complementary: divergent impacts of no-till and deep tillage on soil health in black soil regions globally
abstract: Black soils have undergone structural degradation and functional decline due to prolonged intensive cultivation. Although no-tillage (NT) and deep tillage (DT) are widely adopted regenerative practices to increase soil health and sustainability, systematic assessments and generalization of the soil health responses to these practices in black soil regions remain limited. We collected 2535 paired observations from 221 peer-reviewed articles and combined meta-analysis with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to evaluate the effects of NT and DT on soil health across four dimensions: crop productivity, soil physico-chemical properties, microbial diversity, and enzyme activities. Compared with conventional tillage, NT increased bulk density and reduced porosity, thereby constraining early crop growth leading to limited yield gains (+1.1%). However, NT tended to support long-term increase in soil nutrient content (total nitrogen +10%, and soil organic matter +7%), enzyme activities (from 5% to 38%), and microbial diversity. In contrast, DT improved soil physical structure (SP +5%, SBD -1%), increased yield (+7%) and plant biomass accumulation (+19%), but had limited effects on biological indicators. 45% of paired observations under NT achieved a “win–win” outcome for soil health and crop yield, while DT produced a higher win-win proportion (55%). Agronomic management practices substantially modulated these outcomes: long-term NT combined with straw mulching and crop rotation alleviated soil structural constraints and increased microbial diversity and enzyme activities in soil, whereas DT primarily raised short-term yield recovery. The integrated soil health index was slightly higher under NT (+7%) than under DT (+6%) as compared to conventional tillage. This study highlights the complementary roles of NT and DT, and provides a scientific basis for the development of tailored tillage strategies to foster sustainable agriculture in black soil regions globally.

title: Novel insights into industrial waste oil pyrolysis from the perspective of component interaction: Pyrolysis behavior, kinetic triplet, and coking indication
abstract: As a typical hazardous solid waste, the high-value utilization of industrial waste oil (IWO) is critical for petroleum resource recycling and ecological protection. To address the gap in understanding how component interactions regulate pyrolysis behavior, kinetics and coking, this study integrated component fractionation, thermal analysis, iso-conversional kinetic methods, and master plot methodology for comprehensive elucidation. All samples exhibited two pyrolysis stages with strong compositional dependence: increasing heavy components weakened distillation (3.96-0.36 wt %) but enhanced thermal cracking (92.33-94.59 wt %) and coking (3.71-5.05 wt %) from aromatic-rich to aromatic-poor fractions. Then activation energy increased with conversion, presenting stage-specific and average values rising from the aromatic-rich fraction (142.45 kJ/mol) to IWO (163.13 kJ/mol) and aromatic-poor fraction (257.96 kJ/mol). Moreover, stage-dependent mechanisms were identified via master plot method, validating the necessity of stage-specific kinetic analysis. Third, comparative analysis of experimental and linearly additive theoretical data revealed strong synergistic interactions between the two fractions, manifested as non-additive deviations in curve peak, activation energy, and coking yield (3.95 vs. 4.82 wt %, 22.05 % deviation), with these interactions mediated by six key physicochemical processes. From this study, it could offer quantitative parameters and mechanistic guidance for optimizing IWO's thermal conversion, facilitating its safe and high-value utilization.

title: Carbon-aware production scheduling for industrial decarbonization: An artificial intelligence framework integrating environmental and public health co-benefits
abstract: Industrial manufacturing accounts for 21% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet conventional production scheduling systems fail to incorporate real-time carbon awareness into operational decision-making. Epidemiological studies have identified high rates of asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and premature deaths in the communities in areas where industries release such emissions over a long period. Though the policies focused on decarbonization in industries are growing, the current production scheduling strategies are imperfect in terms of incorporating the environmental and public health concerns into the decision-making process. This paper suggests that incorporating the concept of carbon-conscious optimization into manufacturing, by constructing the SmartOps-Green artificial intelligence framework, can result in co-creation in carbon emissions and air pollutants emissions. The framework integrates graph neural networks to learn the topology of a production system and deep reinforcement learning to learn to modify scheduling policies during the course of changing operational and environmental conditions. Progressive incentives on the amount of emissions to be reduced with production viability: a ladder-like carbon trading mechanism in line with market-based policies on climate would give the incentives. The suggested method was tested on the basis of the Steel Industry Energy Consumption Dataset and Appliances Energy Prediction Dataset with the consideration of the real-life grid carbon emission factors. Findings indicate that SmartOps-Green yields 23.7% lessening in carbon emission on operations than the conventional approaches of scheduling operational activities, yet the throughput of production in relation to optimal standards is at 2.3%. According to the common emission factors of electricity production using fossil fuel, it would result in the estimated improvement of 18–22% in NO x emission and 15–20% in SO x emission. Using exposure-response relationships on a screening level, it is estimated that the emission decrease will prevent about 6-14 cases of asthma exacerbation, 2-5 respiratory illness hospitalization, and 0.3-0.6 premature mortality per facility. The carbon emission prediction component was very accurate (R2=0.948±0.012), thus making accurate short term of prediction. Collective data using statistical analysis made significant results on energy efficiency (18.4% ± 1.2%, p<0.001) and savings in operational costs (12.6% ± 0.8%, p<0.001). These results indicate that smart carbon conscious scheduling can provide quantifiable environmental and population health gains without reducing productivity justifying the shift towards sustainable low-carbon manufacturing systems and helping to better the environment and the health of the population in industrial areas.

title: Cross-sectoral impact of emerging technologies on U.S. manufacturing resilience and competitiveness
abstract: Introducing new technologies in one energy-intensive industry can affect how other industries operate and stay resilient, yet these cross-sector interactions are often underappreciated in conventional technology roadmaps. In practice, industrial systems do not evolve in isolation. They are linked through shared upstream and downstream dependencies, such as electricity and fuel supply, critical materials, transportation networks, and enabling infrastructure. As a result, large-scale technology deployment in one sector can reshape resource availability, infrastructure demand, and operational risk in others. These interdependencies mean that technology deployment decisions in one sector can create unintended bottlenecks or cascading benefits in others. This article argues that a cross-sector, system-of-systems perspective is essential for evaluating and scaling emerging technologies in energy-intensive industries. By framing industrial transformation as an interconnected systems challenge rather than a set of isolated sectoral decisions, the study highlights how interdependence shapes technology feasibility, adoption pathways, and resilience outcomes. The article illustrates how cross-sector linkages can amplify both risks and benefits, and it emphasizes the importance of integrated planning approaches that account for shared dependencies, cascading impacts, and co-optimization opportunities. Adopting this broader perspective can support more robust technology roadmaps, improve strategic coordination across industries, and strengthen the long-term resilience of the industrial sector as a whole.

title: Measuring adaptive circularity: A composite index for national circular economy transitions
abstract: This study develops the Index of Adaptive Circularity (IAC), a composite indicator that assesses national circular economy (CE) transition performance by integrating material efficiency outcomes with structural enablers of systemic change. The index combines four material pressure indicators (CO2 emissions per capita, material footprint, domestic material consumption intensity and manufacturing value added) with four adaptive capacity enablers (GDP per capita, R&D expenditure, renewable energy share and digital connectivity). It is applied to an unbalanced panel of fifteen countries observed annually from 2000 to 2024. All indicators are normalised using a transparent min–max procedure and aggregated through equal weighting, with robustness assessed using alternative aggregation and weighting schemes. The results reveal substantial cross-country heterogeneity in adaptive circularity performance: advanced European economies consistently achieve higher IAC scores, reflecting strong innovation systems, renewable energy deployment and digital readiness, whereas resource-intensive and emerging economies display lower scores and slower transition dynamics despite recent investments in adaptive enablers. The longitudinal analysis identifies distinct transition pathways, including early movers, converging economies and structurally constrained trajectories. By operationalising adaptive circularity within a longitudinal framework, the IAC contributes to CE measurement by linking material performance to underlying structural capacities. The index offers policymakers a transparent and replicable diagnostic tool to identify transition bottlenecks, monitor progress and inform targeted policy interventions to support sustainable circular-economy transitions.

title: Highly efficient visible-light-responsive Ag/BOHI photocatalyst for comprehensive antibiotic remediation in complex wastewater
abstract: The widespread occurrence of antibiotics in aquatic environments poses increasing ecological and public health risks. In this work, a multifunctional Ag/BOHI (ABI) visible-light photocatalyst was rationally constructed via a two-step co-precipitation strategy. By integrating a Z-scheme heterojunction with Ag nanoparticles, the catalyst exhibited strong surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effects, significantly enhancing visible-light harvesting and charge separation. The optimized 3 wt% ABI catalyst achieved nearly complete degradation of sulfadiazine within 15 min under visible-light irradiation. In addition, the catalyst showed effective removal of other organic pollutants, including bisphenol A and 2,4-dichlorophenol. The photocatalyst maintained stable performance under various pH conditions and in the presence of coexisting anions or humic acid, demonstrating strong environmental adaptability. When applied to real livestock wastewater, the system achieved 61% COD and 48% TOC removal, confirming its practical applicability in complex water matrices. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited strong antibacterial activity, achieving complete inactivation of E. coli within 40 min and 97.1% inactivation of S. aureus within 2.5 h. Morphological observations revealed severe membrane disruption, indicating synergistic oxidative and structural damage to bacterial cells. Mechanistic studies identified singlet oxygen (1O2), superoxide radicals (·O2−), and photogenerated holes (h+) as the dominant reactive species responsible for pollutant degradation and bacterial inactivation. This SPR-enhanced Z-scheme Ag/BOHI photocatalytic system provides a promising strategy for simultaneous antibiotic degradation and antibiotic-resistant bacteria control in complex aquatic environments.

title: Integrated anti-chlorine-corrosion and self-cleaning Al2O3@Ni-based dendritic electrode matrix for efficient seawater electrolysis
abstract: To address anodic corrosion and cathodic blockage in seawater electrolysis, an integrated electrodeposition strategy is proposed to fabricate Al2O3@nickel-based dendritic electrode matrix (Al2O3@NDEM) with combined chloride resistance and self-cleaning capability. Al2O3 particles are uniformly embedded on the dendritic surface, imparting dual functionality. At the anode, in situ generated [Al(OH)n]- species repel Cl− and facilitate OH− transport, suppressing corrosion and enhancing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. At the cathode, inter-dendritic channels enable continuous bubble transport for self-cleaning, while Al2O3 buffers local pH fluctuations to suppress Ca2+/Mg2+ deposition. A subsequent Fe3+ treatment induces the formation of a FeOOH/α-Ni(OH)2 active layer, further enhancing catalytic activity. The optimized Fe–Al2O3@NDEM exhibits a low overpotential of 274.16 mV at 100 mA cm−2 for the OER and 116.49 mV at 10 mA cm−2 for the HER, along with excellent durability (>3000 h at 500 mA cm−2). Through integrated structural and compositional design, this system simultaneously addresses anodic Cl− corrosion and cathodic deposition, providing a viable pathway toward practical seawater electrolysis.

title: Enhanced hydrogen-rich syngas production from steam gasification of woody biomass using fly-ash supported Ni bifunctional catalysts
abstract: Steam gasification of woody biomass waste offers a promising pathway to produce hydrogen-rich syngas, contributing to the solutions of energy crisis and climate warming. However, its application is hindered by low H2 yield and substantial tar formation. This study developed a low-cost and high-performance bifunctional catalyst (Ni/WCF) for woody biomass gasification by upcycling fly-ash via washing, calcination, and Ni impregnation. Unlike conventional CaO-based counterparts, Ni/WCF features a porous support with naturally doped Fe as a promoter. The catalyst significantly enhanced gasification performance, increasing cold gas efficiency and H2 yield by factors of 1.5 and 3.7, respectively, while reducing tar formation by 31.3% and lowering aromatic content by 50.8% compared to non-catalytic process. The catalyst also exhibited good stability over three consecutive reaction cycles without intermediate regeneration. Furthermore, systematical characterizations were performed to experimentally verified the synergy of two mechanisms: the formation of Ni-Fe alloy through interaction with Fe in the support created highly active Ni sites that promoted tar reforming; the porous Ca-rich structure with abundant oxygen-vacancies of the WCF support facilitates CO2 adsorption and H2O activation, accelerating the WGS reaction. This work provides an efficient and sustainable strategy for high-quality syngas production, enabling the integrated utilization of biomass and industrial solid waste.

title: Coupled heat and moisture effects on recycled cotton insulation: An experimental–numerical study
abstract: The construction sector is one of the most important fields through which energy consumption can be reduced and emissions limited. Moreover, recycling used products decreases manufacturing costs and supports the concept of sustainable development. The present study assesses the effectiveness of recycled cotton in its loose form as an environmentally friendly thermal insulation material by evaluating its thermal properties and the effect of humidity on its performance. To achieve this, the study combines an experimental approach under local environmental conditions with a numerical simulation based on the finite element method (FEM), the reliability of which was verified. The main findings indicate that adding an insulating layer reduces the average heat flux by approximately 11%. Furthermore, an increase in relative humidity from φ = 0.2 to φ = 0.8 results in energy consumption rising by up to 26%. The research also focused on determining the optimal insulation thickness, ranging from 1 cm to 12 cm, depending on user requirements and preferences. In addition, a vapor barrier within the insulated Wall was introduced, and the optimal location was identified, resulting in a 33% reduction in moisture levels within the insulation, thereby enhancing thermal performance and ensuring the longevity of the building envelope. These results support the feasibility and effectiveness of recycling cotton in its loose form for use as thermal insulation in buildings, thus contributing to energy security and reinforcing sustainable development policies.

title: A macro–micro nested coupling framework for assessing water resources carrying capacity in the Gansu section of the Yellow River Basin
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensive human disturbances, the Gansu section of the Yellow River Basin is facing increasing water scarcity and low water-use efficiency. To reveal the characteristics and underlying mechanisms of regional water resources carrying capacity, this study developed a macro–micro nested water resources coupling framework and integrated structural equation modeling (SEM), an improved TOPSIS model, and an ARIMA–linear regression coupled forecasting approach to systematically analyze the level of water resources carrying capacity, key influence pathways, and the coupling–coordination mechanisms among subsystems in the Gansu section of the Yellow River Basin. The results indicate that (1) From 2010 to 2017, water resources carrying capacity in some river sections was in an overloaded or severely overloaded state. Since 2018, the carrying capacity of the entire basin has improved markedly, with most regions reaching or exceeding the critical carrying level, mainly owing to improvements in industrial water-use efficiency, increases in wastewater treatment and reuse, and enhanced farmland irrigation efficiency. By 2022, the Lanzhou–Hekou section remained at the critical carrying level, whereas the sections above Longyangxia, Longyangxia–Lanzhou, and Longmen–Sanmenxia had improved to a bearable state. The forecasts indicate that water resources carrying capacity will further improve across all subregions by 2030, suggesting an overall positive development trend.(2) The carrying capacity of the social subsystem exhibited a general downward trend over time across most river sections, except for the Longyangxia–Lanzhou section. In contrast, the carrying capacity of living space showed a declining trend over time in the sections above Longyangxia and in the Longmen–Sanmenxia section, indicating that strengthened management and regulation of key indicators related to the social subsystem and living space are required.(3) The section above Longyangxia was primarily constrained by interactions among the social, economic, and ecological subsystems; the Longyangxia–Lanzhou section was characterized by a pronounced structural imbalance that prioritized economic development over ecological protection; the Lanzhou–Hekou section was mainly constrained by the social subsystem; and the Hekou–Sanmenxia section was chiefly subjected to negative pressures from economic activities. Across all sections, factors such as water yield modulus, runoff, and urbanization rate played key driving roles.(4) Most river sections exhibited a pattern of “high coupling and low coordination” in most years. In 2022, the coupling coordination degree (D) indicated that the sections above Longyangxia and the Lanzhou–Hekou section were in a barely coordinated state, whereas the Longyangxia–Lanzhou and Longmen–Sanmenxia sections were approaching imbalance. The results contribute to the coordinated development of water resources carrying capacity in the basin and provide a theoretical basis for the sustainable development of basin water resources.

title: Fluorite tailings derived NaA@MoS2 core-shell composites for efficient visible-light photodegradation of rhodamine B: performance and mechanism insights
abstract: A novel MoS2 disulfide-loaded NaA zeolite composite (NaA@MoS2) with a core-shell structure was synthesized via a hydrothermal route using fluorite tailings as the silica source. Structural characterizations show that abundant ultrathin MoS2 nanosheets were uniformly anchored on cubic NaA zeolite, forming a dense pore-accessible interface. Under visible light, NaA@MoS2 achieved synergistic adsorption and photocatalytic removal of rhodamine B (RhB). At 100 mg L−1 RhB (50 mL) and a catalyst dosage of 1.0 g L−1, more than 98% RhB was removed within 180 min after 30 min dark adsorption.
