The composite dosage of 1.0 g L−1 and an initial RhB concentration of 100 mg L−1 at pH ≈ 7 offer a good balance between reaction rate and catalyst utilization. After five cycles, the removal efficiency decreased from ∼92% to ∼70%, while post-reaction characterization and leaching tests showed that the crystalline framework and porous architecture were largely retained. RhB+ was preconcentrated at the NaA@MoS2 interface by the porous and negatively charged NaA framework, while visible-light excited MoS2 generated e−/h+ pairs that formed •O2−/•OH reactive radicals. Optical, electrochemical, and DFT results supported a coupled “adsorption-enrichment-photooxidation” pathway for fast and deep RhB removal. This work provides a promising strategy for tailings valorization and visible-light treatment of organic wastewater.

title: A pore-structure-informed multiphysics carbonation model enabling evaluation of durability and CO2 sequestration potential of sustainable cementitious materials
abstract: Carbonation in cementitious materials governs both concrete durability and its capacity for CO2 sequestration potential. However, many sustainable cementitious materials are more prone to carbonation than Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) because of their distinct hydration products and pore structures. This increased susceptibility complicates durability design and the assessment of their CO2 sequestration potential. To address these issues, this study develops a pore-structure-informed multi-physics carbonation model that not only couples CO2 and moisture transport, heat transfer, and carbonation reactions, but also explicitly links transport parameters to pore-scale descriptors and carbonate formation. By incorporating thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP), and carbonation depth data into parameter identification, the model can be applied to sustainable cementitious materials while simultaneously reducing reliance on empirical assumptions. Sensitivity analysis shows that the CO2 diffusion coefficient (Dg0), the moisture correction factor (F(H)), the carbonation consumption coefficient (α1), and the carbonation rate (vc0) are the dominant parameters controlling carbonation kinetics, whereas the water generation coefficient (α2) has a negligible influence on carbonation depth. The model calibrated with supersulfated cement (SSC) exhibits good agreement with both accelerated and natural carbonation data. Its application to calcium sulfoaluminate (CSA) and alkali-activated slag (AAS) systems further confirms its ability to capture carbonation behavior across different sustainable cementitious materials by employing pore-structure-related and rate parameters from the literature. The proposed framework provides a unified, microstructure-based tool for evaluating carbonation resistance and CO2 uptake capacity of sustainable cementitious materials, thereby serving as a quantitative foundation for durability design and future life-cycle CO2 sequestration assessment.

title: Sustainable lithium extraction from low-grade aqueous resources via reverse Li/Mg separation enabled by hydrated cation-π interaction
abstract: Lithium extraction from abundant low-grade resources, particularly seawater and high-Mg/Li ratio salt lake brines, is vital to meeting the surging global demand. Existing nanofiltration membranes, which rely on the Donnan effect and steric hindrance to block Mg2+ while allowing Li + to pass, typically require high pressures (>5 bar) and show limited selectivity (<20) in complex brines. Here, we report a membrane strategy enabled by hydrated cation-π interactions that fundamentally reverses the conventional Li/Mg selectivity. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the interaction between hydrated Mg2+ and graphene oxide (GO) sheets is about three times stronger than that of hydrated Li+. This exceptionally strong affinity thermodynamically compensates for the dehydration energy penalty, allowing Mg2+ to preferentially permeate the Li + -controlled GO interlayers while Li+ is strongly excluded. The optimized membrane achieves a remarkable separation factor of 37.1 at an extreme Mg/Li mass ratio of 100 under 1 bar, with near-zero Mg2+ rejection and over 95% Li+ retention. The separation performance remains robust across diverse low-grade feedstocks, maintaining separation factors above 20 and stable permeances exceeding 4 L/(m2⋅h⋅bar). Furthermore, a simulated 6-stage filtration process successfully reduces the Mg/Li ratio from 100 to 1.68 and enriches the Li+ concentration from 350 to 1900 mg/L, indicating substantial potential for downstream industrial processing. Importantly, this ultra-low-pressure operation directly processes highly concentrated brines, effectively minimizing energy consumption and the massive dilution steps typically necessitated by conventional nanofiltration methods. This high-selectivity approach demonstrates excellent adaptability to challenging feedstocks, providing a highly promising proof-of-concept for energy-efficient and freshwater-saving sustainable lithium extraction.

title: High-value recycling of waste PET/TPEE blends via supercritical CO2 foaming: Enhanced toughness and thermal insulation for lightweight applications
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and thermoplastic polyester elastomer (TPEE) are two of the most widely used polymer materials due to their excellent mechanical properties, processability, and durability. However, the massive generation of PET and TPEE wastes has posed significant environmental impacts and hindered the global “dual carbon” goals. The recycling of these two polymer wastes remains a formidable challenge: PET waste undergoes severe chain scission and thermal degradation during mechanical recycling, leading to drastically reduced toughness and processability; TPEE waste, particularly from discarded athletic shoe midsoles and industrial components, is limited by high cost and low tensile modulus despite its excellent flexibility. To address these issues and realize the synergistic valorization of both waste polymers, we propose a novel strategy combining blend modification and supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO2) foaming technology. R-PET/TPEE blends with varying r-TPEE contents (0–30 wt%) were prepared, and their crystallization behavior, rheological properties, dynamic mechanical properties, and mechanical performance were systematically investigated. Subsequently, the blends were foamed via scCO2 foaming technology, and the cellular structure, thermal insulation, and compression properties of the resultant foams were characterized. The results demonstrate that r-TPEE significantly enhanced the toughness and viscoelasticity of r-PET/TPEE blends, facilitating foaming. Moreover, increasing r-TPEE content leads to a more uniform cells, a significant increase in expansion ratio, and a reduction in thermal conductivity. This work provides a feasible technical route for the high-value recycling of r-PET and r-TPEE wastes, offering potential applications in automotive, packaging, and aerospace fields as lightweight and thermally insulating materials.

title: Backbone resilience of national-sectoral production networks for urban provisioning: Persistence, rewiring, and rebound
abstract: Cities depend on geographically extensive production systems for essential provisioning functions, including food supply, energy, construction, refined petroleum products, chemicals, and trade-related services. Yet research on sustainable cities has paid limited attention to the external production structures that materially sustain urban life under systemic disruption. This study examines the resilience of national-sectoral production backbones for urban provisioning using OECD Inter-Country Input–Output (ICIO) data from 2018 to 2022. Adopting a macro-structural perspective, this study constructs annual directed, weighted country–sector networks and analyzes their persistence, rewiring, and rebound across the 2020 disruption and its aftermath. The results reveal a pattern of persistent–adaptive resilience rather than systemic collapse. Cross-border backbone integration contracted in 2020 but subsequently re-expanded, while a large share of backbone relations remained continuously present across the full observation period, indicating a durable structural core. Rewiring intensified most strongly in the post-shock adjustment phase, but transition evidence shows that adjustment occurred mainly through edge-status reallocation between the backbone and the periphery rather than through wholesale creation or disappearance of production relations. Rebound was highly uneven across economies and sectors and was concentrated in sectors central to urban provisioning, including construction, wholesale and retail trade, food products, electricity and gas, petroleum products, and chemicals. These findings reposition urban resilience as a multi-scalar property shaped by local capacities, external production backbones, and the layered interaction between structural continuity and adaptive flexibility. The study advances the Persistent–Adaptive Urban Supply Backbone (PAUSB) framework and supports a multi-scalar understanding of resilience in sustainable urban development.

title: Exploring the multidimensional synergistic evolution mechanism of green watershed policies in China: A network analysis approach
abstract: Building green watersheds is crucial for achieving integrated ecological and socio-economic development in China. Policy synergy plays a key role in ensuring the effective implementation of environmental strategies. However, research on policy synergy in green watersheds remains limited. This study investigates the temporal dynamics of policy synergy using 464 national-level policy documents (1997–2024) and focuses on key themes such as pollution reduction, carbon reduction, greening expansion, and economic growth. A multidimensional analytical framework is developed to examine the synergistic evolution of green watershed policies across three dimensions: policy tools, policy objectives, and their linkages. Policy synergy is quantitatively assessed across three dimensions using text mining and network analysis. The findings revealed that synergy among policy tools, policy objectives, and their linkages strengthened from 1997 to 2017 and then gradually declined after 2018. Tool synergy evolved from bottom-line control to high-quality empowerment through three stages: government-led tools, mechanical combinations, and organic synergy. Policy objective synergy indicated a transition from a singular focus on pollution reduction to a more integrated, multi-objective framework. Tool–objective synergy highlighted the differentiated applicability of specific tools to distinct policy objectives. This study introduces a novel analytical framework for policy synergy analysis and provides methodological and empirical guidance for designing green watershed policies in China and other developing countries.

title: Environmental performance of jeans manufacturing: LCA-based scenario analysis and TODIM ranking
abstract: Tunisia occupies a prominent position in the global jeans industry due to its recognized expertise in jeans manufacturing. Yet, this sector keeps contributing significantly to environmental damage, largely due to the manufacturing step which is often neglected regardless of its considerable environmental impact. This study examined potential improvement scenarios for jeans manufacturing via the development of 24 alternatives varying according to energy sources (fossil fuel-based and renewable solar energy), zipper materials (brass and steel), and washing processes (enzymatic, stone, and mixed wash). Climate change (CC), terrestrial acidification (TA), freshwater eutrophication (FE), terrestrial ecotoxicity (TET), freshwater ecotoxicity (FET), and water consumption (WC) were examined. Evaluating eco-design alternatives entails multiple environmental criteria, making decision-making complicated and requiring a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approach. Therefore, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was combined with TODIM (an acronym in Portuguese for Interactive and Multi-criteria Decision Making) method. LCA findings highlighted garment manufacturing and industrial washing as the main environmental hotspots within most impact categories. According to TODIM's ranking results, scenario 11 which integrates solar photovoltaic electricity, a steel zipper, and a mixed washing process delivered the best environmental performance. Conversely, scenario 12 ranked below the reference scenario despite integrating solar thermal energy, demonstrating trade-offs between different environmental indicators.

title: Reuse of oxidatively remediated petroleum-contaminated soil as flowable fill: Solidification mechanisms and performance evaluation
abstract: This study developed a flowable fill using oxidatively remediated petroleum-contaminated soil stabilized with cement and bentonite. The fluidity, strength, permeability, durability, leaching behavior, and microstructural characteristics of the material were systematically evaluated. Results showed that a cement-to-bentonite ratio of 5:4 and a binder dosage of 10-15% yielded suitable fluidity (140-200 mm). After 14 days of curing, the solidified specimens met the key engineering criteria for subgrade backfill, with an unconfined compressive strength exceeding 0.80 MPa and a hydraulic conductivity below 1 × 10−7 cm/s. Mineralogical and microstructural analyses revealed that hydration products (C-S-H/C-A-S-H) effectively improved the soil fabric, whereas residual oxidants and hydrocarbons in the remediated soil led to a slightly more porous structure and marginally lower mechanical performance than that of the solidified virgin soil. Supplementary tests using natural soil confirmed that the optimized cement-bentonite formulation remained applicable under more realistic soil conditions. TCLP results further showed low leaching concentrations of extractable petroleum hydrocarbons (C10-C40) and dissolved Fe, while hydrogen peroxide was not detected in the leachates of remediated-soil-based specimens. In addition, the solidified material showed good durability under wetting-drying cycles, maintaining structural integrity and acceptable performance. This study provides a practical waste-to-resource pathway that can reduce the disposal burden of remediated soil while decreasing the demand for virgin construction materials.

title: Microgrid energy optimal scheduling in ports incorporating the bidirectional event trigger mechanism
abstract: Coordinated scheduling of port logistics and energy systems is essential for improving the economic and environmental performance of electrified ports. However, existing studies often optimize logistics operations and energy management separately, without adequately accounting for their strong coupling or the mismatch in operating time scales between logistics activities and energy resources. To address this issue, this paper proposes a day-ahead and real-time multi-time-scale coordinated scheduling framework for port microgrids with a bidirectional event trigger mechanism (BETM). In the day-ahead stage, an hourly mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is developed to jointly optimize berth and quay crane assignments, renewable energy utilization, grid electricity procurement, and energy storage dispatch, thereby generating a feasible baseline schedule. In the real-time stage, system operation proceeds at 15-min intervals, with system states and short-term forecasts continuously updated to account for operational uncertainties. BETM simultaneously monitors logistics-side and energy-side deviations from the day-ahead baseline and activates re-optimization only when the triggering conditions are met. Once triggered, the real-time MILP is re-solved over a 1-h prediction horizon and implemented in a rolling-horizon manner, thereby enhancing disturbance adaptability while avoiding unnecessary schedule revisions. Adaptive time-varying thresholds are designed according to system operating conditions. Case studies based on Tianjin Dongjiang Port show that, compared with model predictive control (MPC) and a logistics event trigger mechanism (LETM), the proposed method reduces total operating cost by 18.64% and 22.44%, respectively, while decreasing total online solution time by 88.90% and 77.76%, respectively. Moreover, it achieves near-zero renewable energy curtailment and favorable environmental performance in terms of peak-load reduction, carbon intensity, and renewable energy utilization. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to enhance the cleaner production performance of electrified ports through improved economic efficiency and low-carbon energy utilization.

title: Safeguarding biodiversity from renewable energy development in China
abstract: The perception of photovoltaic (PV) energy as an environmentally benign technology can obscure its unintended ecological consequences. Here this study provides the national-scale, multi-taxa assessment of biodiversity risks associated with PV development in China, using a hybrid species distribution model integrated with a spatial risk-assessment framework. We find that 364 km2 or approximately 10% of PV installation area overlaps with Key Biodiversity Areas, with the most pronounced encroachment occurring in Northwest China. At the same time, regions with low biodiversity intactness, particularly East and Central–South China, exhibit the highest exposure of threatened species to PV installations, highlighting a spatial mismatch between renewable-energy expansion and conservation priorities. Cumulative risk distribution curves show that aggregate biodiversity risk at existing solar farms consistently exceeds national benchmarks across the 50th, 75th, and 90th percentiles, underscoring the biodiversity oversight in current PV siting practices. More than one-tenth of solar farms are located in areas of extremely high biodiversity risk—exceeding the risk levels of 90% of the nation’s terrestrial land—with avian species facing the greatest threats. Moreover, the average biodiversity risk within solar expansion areas increased by 44% between 2010 and 2022, indicating rising biodiversity pressures per unit area of PV development. These findings reveal critical biodiversity pitfalls of land-based climate mitigation and provide a scalable assessment framework for biodiversity-inclusive renewable energy planning.

title: Steering non-radical peroxymonosulfate activation via Au-S interfacial electronic engineering on defect-rich MIL-101(Fe)-NH2: From radical suppression to singlet oxygen domination
abstract: Achieving selective generation of non-radical reactive oxygen species (ROS) from peroxymonosulfate (PMS) remains a significant challenge for advanced oxidation processes due to the chaotic coexistence of radicals. Herein, we report a precise interfacial engineering strategy to construct a defect-rich, Au-S coordinated composite catalyst, MN-SO4-Au-SH, for highly selective PMS activation. Initially, sulfuric acid etching was employed to tailor the topology of MIL-101(Fe)-NH2 from octahedrons to sea-urchin-like clusters, introducing abundant oxygen vacancies (Ov) to enhance surface affinity. Subsequently, Au nanoparticles were anchored to construct a high-speed electron transfer channel. Crucially, thiol (-SH) functionalization regulated the interfacial electronic structure through Au-S coordination, which not only stabilized the metal nodes but also modulated the d-band center of Au sites. This modulation steered the reaction pathway from non-selective radical generation to a dominant singlet oxygen (1O2) mechanism by optimizing the adsorption energy of PMS and reducing the energy barrier for O-O bond scission. Consequently, the catalyst exhibited a 7.3-fold increase in reaction rate compared to the pristine MOF and achieved near 100% removal of sulfadiazine in complex matrices with negligible metal leaching. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidated that the Au-S interface promotes directional electron injection into the σ∗ orbital of PMS, validating the non-radical-dominated mechanism. This work offers a new paradigm for designing durability-enhanced and pathway-controllable catalysts for precision water remediation.

title: Upcycling Cotton–PET textiles into hydrogel adsorbent sheets for water pollutant removal
abstract: Blended textiles represent a rapidly growing waste stream that remains difficult to recycle due to the reliance on separation-based approaches. Here, we report an integrative upcycling strategy that directly converts cotton–PET blended textiles into hydrogel-immobilized textile adsorbents without fiber separation. The PET fraction is selectively transformed via aminolysis (190 °C, 30 min) into amine-rich oligomers, while the cotton component is preserved as a fibrous scaffold, enabling complete utilization of the textile components without generating secondary waste. Subsequent cross-linking of the oligomers and immobilization of the hydrogel within the cotton matrix yields mechanically stable composite sheets with a tensile strength of ca. 20 MPa. The hydrogel network confined within the textile matrix exhibits a moderate swelling ratio of 5 g g−1. Protonation of amine groups enables pH-responsive and charge-selective adsorption of various anionic dyes, with an equilibrium adsorption capacity of Orange II dye of ca. 387 mg g−1, maintaining >99% removal efficiency over 10 adsorption–desorption cycles. Pseudo-second-order adsorption kinetics indicates interaction between dye molecules and amines, and equilibrium behavior described by the Temkin model suggests heterogeneous adsorption energies. The adsorbent also exhibits effective uptake of Cu2+ ions (Qe = 140.0 mg g−1) and the ketoprofen pharmaceutical (Qe = 18.9 mg g−1), highlighting its potential for removal of diverse contaminants. By integrating both cotton and PET components into a single functional material, a separation-free upcycling route offers a practical pathway for circular utilization of blended textile waste in water treatment applications.

title: Do microplastics hinder biochar remediation of Cd-contaminated soil growing rice?
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread in Cd-contaminated soils and may interact with biochar, a widely-used amendment for soil remediation, potentially compromising biochar remediation efficiency. However, whether MPs interfere with the remediation effect of biochar in Cd-contaminated soils remains a knowledge gap. Here, we aimed to explore whether MPs hinder the remediation effects of biochar on Cd-contaminated soil using a range of endpoints, including soil physicochemical properties, rice growth and physiological response, Cd accumulation, and microbial communities. Three types of MPs were compared, i.e., polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyester (PES), and polylactic acid (PLA). Regardless of the presence of MPs, biochar provided multifaceted benefits to the soil-rice system, including improved soil properties (pH and available P), enhanced plant growth (root biomass +77%), decreased oxidative damage (higher soluble protein and lower malondialdehyde contents in shoots), reduced Cd accumulation, and increased soil bacterial diversity (Shannon index) and richness (Chao1 index). Overall, MPs caused no significant negative effects on soil properties, plant performance, and microbial communities, particularly when biochar was added. In most cases, MPs had no significant interactions with biochar on the measured endpoints. Only PLA MPs and biochar combination specifically modified soil bacterial composition. To conclude, biochar exerted multiple benefits for soil quality, rice growth and Cd mitigation, and soil microbial community, whereas the presence of microplastics did not weaken these benefits. Biochar shows the promising potential for the remediation of Cd-MPs co-contaminated soil for safe production of rice.

title: Temporal and spatial distribution of ship wastewater generated in the Yangtze River
abstract: With the ongoing expansion of shipping along the Yangtze River, ship-generated wastewater has attracted increasing attention due to its environmental impact. Untreated or inadequately treated shipborne wastewater poses significant threats to aquatic ecosystems through nutrient loading, pathogen introduction, and chemical contamination, yet comprehensive quantification remains lacking to guide pollution control efforts. To support effective monitoring and control strategies, this study presents the first high-resolution quantification of shipborne wastewater—including both greywater and blackwater—across the trunk and branch lines of the Yangtze River. Using Automatic Identification System (AIS) data and a robust wastewater estimation model, the analysis provides a detailed spatial and temporal assessment of wastewater generation patterns. Results indicate that the total amount of wastewater generated by ships operating in the Yangtze River basin in 2022 is 2.01 × 107 m3, in which 1.55 × 107 m3 of wastewater (1.28 × 107 m3 greywater, 2.7 × 106 m3 blackwater) generated in trunk line, and 4.6 × 106 m3 (3.8 × 106 m3 greywater, 8 × 105 m3 blackwater) in the branch lines. Passenger ships account for 31.5% of the total wastewater, while cargo ships account for 19%. Among all vessel types, passenger ships are the largest contributors to wastewater generation across both main and secondary routes. A sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the total wastewater estimate could range from 1.21 × 107 m3 to 3.13 × 107 m3, yet the relative contributions of ship types and spatial hotspots remain robust across all scenarios. Spatiotemporal analysis reveals that the lower reaches of the Yangtze River have the highest wastewater production, underscoring the need for prioritised environmental monitoring in this region. By identifying high-risk zones and quantifying ship specific contributions, these findings provide critical data to inform and optimize the strategic placement of wastewater collection facilities in port areas, supporting more effective pollution management along the Yangtze River.

title: Long-term trajectories of vegetation structure and function in China: greening does not always indicate enhanced productivity
abstract: Climate change and intensified human activities are fundamentally altering terrestrial ecosystems, inducing complex and nonlinear shifts in the coupling between vegetation structure and function. Despite observed global greening, the extent to which these structural gains translate into enhanced ecosystem function remains unclear. This study proposes an integrated framework that combines temporal trajectory analysis (trends and shapes) of vegetation structure and function. Based on the joint temporal dynamics of Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) and Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), we identified the coupling and spatial heterogeneity of vegetation structural–functional trajectories across China from 2000 to 2020. Our analysis revealed a nationwide increase in both trend of vegetation structure (FVC, 57.8% of pixels) and function (GPP, 91.5% of pixels). Notably, over half of China's territory (54.91%) exhibited a coupled enhancement, predominantly in humid regions of the northeast and south. In contrast, functional-leading trajectories with increasing GPP were prevalent in arid and high-altitude regions (33.69%), suggesting that productivity gains may occur under relatively constrained structural trajectories. Conversely, trajectories of coupled decline and structure-leading change were rare (3%), largely confined to decertifying or rapidly urbanizing areas. These spatial patterns were found to be moderated by hydroclimatic conditions and ecological baselines, while climate-human interactions were linked to greater regional disparities. Specifically, coupled enhancement reflects strong climate–vegetation synergy, whereas coupled decline points toward localized disturbances rather than macro-scale drivers. Meanwhile, structure-leading trajectories are tied to baseline vegetation status, and functional-leading patterns signify hydro-thermal compensatory productivity. Our results demonstrated that vegetation greening is not synonymous with functional improvement, highlighting the critical need to integrate functional metrics into ecosystem assessments. The proposed framework offered a tractable approach for long-term ecosystem monitoring, quality evaluation, and targeted restoration management.

title: Integrated valorization of bottom ash derived unburnt carbon and municipal solid waste into high-performance briquettes for industrial boiler co-firing
abstract: Coal consumption in Indonesia's industrial sector generates substantial amounts of fly and bottom ash (FABA), with bottom ash accounting for nearly 80% of the total volume. Despite containing recoverable unburnt carbon (UC), this bottom ash is often discarded as hazardous waste because of its low volatile matter content. This study develops an integrated approach to convert UC-rich bottom ash and municipal solid waste (MSW) derived biomass into Biomass Coal Fuel (BCF) briquettes for application in industrial boiler co-firing. A 60:40 UC-to-biomass ratio was formulated and evaluated through physical, thermal, and environmental characterizations, including shatter index, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP). Adding MSW biomass compensated for the low volatility of the bottom ash, resulting in a briquette with sufficient structural durability and improved thermal reactivity. Continuous co-firing trials in a commercial textile fluidized-bed boiler using 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% BCF substitution ratios showed stable operational performance. Replacing coal at an optimal 10-15% ratio reduced fossil fuel consumption by 16-25% and accelerated the rise in steam pressure by 31-33%. TGA results indicated a reduction in ignition temperature, while emission testing confirmed that particulate matter, SO2, and NO2 concentrations complied with national regulatory standards due to the low sulfur and nitrogen content in the biomass fraction. The findings demonstrate that integrating UC and MSW biomass into BCF briquettes offers a practical approach to industrial waste recovery and reducing reliance on fossil coal.

title: Decarbonization of blast furnace gas for H2/CO syngas production with coke oven gas reducing via dual chemical-looping
abstract: Blast furnace gas (BFG) is a major source of carbon emissions in the steel industry. To address this, a novel dual chemical-looping process is proposed for producing H2/CO syngas from BFG while achieving decarbonization. The process integrates an oxygen carrier cycle and a carbon carrier cycle, coupling chemical-looping technology with integrated CO2 capture and utilization (ICCU), and utilizes coke oven gas (COG) as the reducing agent to convert all carbon in BFG into CO. Oxygen carriers and carbon carriers are screened from various candidate metal oxides. Among them, NiO, Fe2O3 and CuO as oxygen carriers exhibit high melting points, high oxygen transport capacities, high equilibrium constants, and strong spontaneity in reactions with CO, while CaO as the carbon carrier shows high CO2 desorption and adsorption capacity under required reaction conditions. With these selected carriers, the carbon fixation and release processes are systematically investigated through thermodynamic analysis, focusing on the effects of temperature, pressure, and feed ratio. Under the combined action of each oxygen carrier and CaO, both carbon fixation rates and CO yields nearly reach 100%, indicating that the proposed process achieves highly efficient decarbonization of BFG. Building on these findings, energy, environmental, and economic analyses are conducted. Compared to conventional processes such as pressure swing adsorption separation and dry reforming of methane, the proposed process exhibits lower energy consumption. Furthermore, it is environmentally advantageous, achieving net-negative carbon emissions in most scenarios across the three oxygen carriers, and economically viable, with a positive net present value (NPV).

title: Reactor-scale modeling of dye transport and adsorption in polyester dyeing with supercritical carbon dioxide
abstract: Understanding the coupled mass transfer and adsorption behavior of dyes on polyester fibers in supercritical carbon dioxide dyeing is essential for improving dyeing efficiency and advancing sustainable, water-free textile technologies. In this study, a coupled computational fluid dynamics model integrating the Langmuir adsorption isotherm and the Linear Driving Force kinetic equation was established to simulate dye transport, adsorption kinetics, and flow behavior under supercritical conditions. Temperature- and pressure-dependent thermophysical properties of CO2 were incorporated through User-Defined Functions. This approach enables the simultaneous solution of momentum, energy, and species transport equations within the dyeing vessel. The simulation results demonstrate that dye uptake in the fabric region follows a characteristic two-stage evolution, consisting of an initial rapid adsorption stage driven by a high concentration gradient and adsorption potential, followed by a diffusion-controlled stage dominated by porous resistance and intra-fiber mass transfer limitations. Significant flow-field attenuation and non-uniformity occur as the dye-laden supercritical fluid penetrates the porous textile layer. This attenuation leads to heterogeneous spatial distributions of velocity, dye concentration, and local adsorption capacity, particularly near the outlet region. Parametric analysis reveals that operating pressure plays a dominant role in enhancing dye solubility, fluid density, polymer swelling, and equilibrium dye uptake, thereby accelerating dyeing kinetics and shortening equilibration time. In contrast, temperature exhibits a non-monotonic influence due to the competing effects of reduced solvent density and enhanced molecular diffusion and polymer plasticization. Overall, the findings highlight the strong interdependence among flow distribution, mass transfer, and adsorption kinetics, and provide a physically consistent and quantitative framework for optimizing operating parameters and reactor design in scCO2 dyeing systems.

title: Turning green under the spotlight? Environmental information disclosure, legitimacy manipulation, and green total factor productivity
abstract: As a novel environmental regulatory instrument, mandatory environmental information disclosure (EID) and its effects on firms' environmental performance remain insufficiently understood in emerging economies. Using China's heavily polluting firms under government monitoring as the empirical context, this study examines the effects of EID on firms' green total factor productivity (TFP) through the lens of legitimacy pressure. The findings show that mandatory EID significantly improves firms' green TFP; however, this positive effect is weakened by firms' legitimacy manipulation in response to local government environmental regulation. The beneficial effects of EID occur primarily through intensified government regulation and reputational penalties. The impact of green competition is observed only in consumer product industries, but not in industrial product industries. Additional analyses indicate that the positive effect of EID on green TFP is more pronounced among private firms, in high-tech industries, and in regions with well-functioning business environments. Furthermore, the improvement in green TFP is mainly attributable to technological innovation rather than managerial innovation. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of the firm-level effects of EID in emerging markets and provides important implications for improving environmental policy.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions and carbon mitigation in an adaptive activated sludge system under dissolved oxygen gradients
abstract: In the context of China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality targets, wastewater treatment plants have become significant sources of anthropogenic carbon emissions, highlighting the urgent need for low-carbon treatment technologies. In this study, a modified anaerobic–anoxic–oxic (AAO) process, referred to as the adaptive activated sludge (AAS) system, was developed to simultaneously enhance pollutant removal and reduce process-level carbon emissions. The system incorporates a dynamic regulation zone and controlled dissolved oxygen (DO) gradients (≤1.0–3.0 mg/L), enabling coordinated regulation of mainstream pollutant removal and greenhouse gas emissions. This integrated evaluation framework identified an optimal low-DO operational window that minimizes carbon emissions while maintaining stable removal of the monitored pollutants (COD, NH4+–N, and TN). The AAS system achieved average removal efficiencies of approximately 90% for COD, 99% for NH4+–N, and 54% for TN. Compared with the conventional AAO process under the same accounting framework, the AAS configuration exhibited substantially lower model-calculated carbon emissions. The lowest total carbon emissions (24.856 kg CO2-eq/a) were observed under low-DO conditions (≤1.0 mg/L), underscoring the critical role of DO optimization in mitigating greenhouse gas emissions. Overall, this study provides novel insights into the integration of carbon accounting with process optimization and offers practical guidance for developing low-carbon operational strategies in wastewater treatment systems.

title: Energy transition, industrial structure optimization, and policy trade-offs in a resource-constrained advanced economy: Evidence from Japan
abstract: Resource-constrained developed economies face increasing challenges in aligning energy transition with industrial restructuring. This study uses panel data from 47 prefectures in Japan from 2005 to 2022 to examine the impact of energy transition, measured by renewable energy penetration, on industrial structural change. A fixed-effects model is employed to distinguish between two dimensions: industrial upgrading and industrial rationalization. The results show that energy transition is significantly associated with industrial upgrading, reflected in an increased share of the tertiary sector, but has no significant effect on industrial rationalization. This suggests that energy transition primarily induces directional shifts in industrial composition rather than improvements in allocation efficiency. The effect is more pronounced in regions with favorable structural conditions, indicating the presence of regional heterogeneity. Further analysis using the 2011 Fukushima nuclear accident as a structural breakpoint shows that the effect of energy transition becomes significant only in the post-Fukushima period, highlighting the importance of systemic changes in the energy sector. In addition, environmental regulation is found to moderate this relationship, with the estimated effect reflecting changes in regulatory stringency over time within a unified national framework. Overall, the findings indicate that the industrial effects of energy transition are conditional on institutional settings, energy system transformation, and regional characteristics. Effective policy design requires a balanced approach that aligns energy, industrial, and regulatory policies with region-specific development conditions.

title: A heterogeneous energy collaborative forecasting scheduling method considering source-load low carbon complementarity and matching
abstract: To mitigate source-load bilateral uncertainty and fully tap into low-carbon dispatchable resources on both the source and load sides, a heterogeneous energy collaborative forecasting scheduling method considering source-load low-carbon complementarity and matching is proposed. First, a forecasting model for wind power, photovoltaic power, and power load is developed based on Laguerre polynomials, pseudo-inverse learning, and ensemble learning. This model balances forecast accuracy with stability to reduce uncertainties on both the source and load sides. Second, low-carbon dispatchable resources on the source and load sides are tapped into, and the complementary advantages of low-carbon characteristics between the two sides are analyzed. A low-carbon complementary operation mechanism is proposed. On the source side, an integrated flexible operation mode of a carbon capture power plant is introduced. Wind power, photovoltaic power, and concentrated solar power plants are adopted for coordinated power supply to provide zero-carbon power output. On the load side, logistic active demand response is considered to optimize the power load distribution. A ladder-type carbon trading mechanism is incorporated to control power system carbon emissions. Finally, a source-load matching coefficient is introduced to account for the matching degree between power output and power load. A multi-objective dispatch model is established with the objectives of maximizing the source-load matching degree and minimizing the comprehensive economic cost. Validations on 10-unit and 20-unit power systems demonstrate the favorable robustness and engineering applicability of the proposed method, aiming to provide an effective solution for the low-carbon, economic, and secure dispatch of power systems.

title: Can existing land-use intensification mitigate urban heat and reduce carbon emissions in megacities? evidence from Shanghai
abstract: Amid global warming and rapid urbanization, megacities confront dual pressures from greenhouse gas emissions and urban heat islands. For resource-constrained cities, achieving carbon neutrality and thermal mitigation through intensive land management remains an unresolved challenge. Using Shanghai as a case study, this research employs a transition-based perspective and geographically weighted regression (GWR) to examine the spatiotemporal relationships among land-use mixture, urban heat island intensity (UHII), and land-use carbon emissions (LCE) from 2010 to 2020. The analysis uses high-resolution data to trace how specific mixed-use types and transitions relate to environmental outcomes. Results indicate a citywide intensification of land-use mixture, corresponding with an average UHII increase of 0.23 ± 0.46 °C and a total LCE rise of 1499.43 kilo-ton C. Environmental responses varied by configuration: mixed industrial or transportation areas exhibited lower heat intensity and emissions relative to their single-use counterparts, whereas mixed residential areas displayed reduced heat alongside increased emissions. Between 2010 and 2020, 37.38% of mixed land underwent functional transitions. While most transitions yielded carbon reductions, they frequently coincided with UHII intensification. In particular, conversions from ecological to mixed construction land emerged as pathways involving simultaneous increases in warming and emissions. Furthermore, GWR analysis reveals that transition outcomes exhibit spatial heterogeneity. Localized synergistic increases in heat and emissions driven by industrial conversions were concentrated in specific southern zones, whereas agricultural transitions governed environmental shifts in the urban fringe. These observations highlight the need for future planning to emphasize carbon–heat synergy to support climate-resilient megacity development.

title: The hidden waterlines of urban energy: Tracing production and consumption based pressures on water quantity and quality
abstract: The Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region faces severe water scarcity and quality degradation, yet existing studies overlook the dual water pressures embodied in interregional energy trade from a consumption-based city-level perspective. To fill this gap, this study integrates a city-level multi-regional input-output model with structural decomposition analysis to examine dual pressures of water quantity and quality within Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei energy sectors from 2012 to 2017. By measuring blue and grey water footprints, the results reveal a significant divergence between production and consumption perspectives. From a production perspective, the blue water footprint (BWF) decreased by 26.4% from 647.5 to 476.5 million cubic meters (mcm), while the grey water footprint (GWF) dropped significantly by 90.5% from 1763.9 to 167.8 mcm. From a consumption perspective, BWF surged to 2689.4 mcm in 2017 which is 460% higher than its production-based counterpart. Although the consumption-based GWF footprint declined across all cities during the study period, its absolute value remained 494% higher than the production-based GWF by 2017. These trends were underpinned by a 240% increase in virtual water imports from external regions. Structural decomposition analysis indicates that while technological efficiency and economic restructuring were the primary factors mitigating BWF, rapid economic expansion offset 76.3% of the gains from efficiency improvements. On the demand side, evolving consumption patterns emerged as the dominant driver, contributing 62.1% to the growth of the consumption-based BWF. For GWF, the significant reduction in intensity served as the most substantial mitigating factor, though its positive effects were partially offset by the expansionary scale of per capita consumption. The study underscores the necessity of an inter-regional beneficiary-pays ecological compensation mechanism and integrated demand-side management to achieve sustainable water-energy governance and support Sustainable Development Goals 6 and 7.

title: Assessing the policy effectiveness of green hydrogen in transportation via system dynamics
abstract: Green hydrogen transport represents a critical pathway for decarbonizing the transportation sector, and its progress will directly shape China's energy transition. To support the development of this industry in line with dual-carbon targets, this study develops a system dynamics (SD) model to forecast industrial trajectories under three policy scenarios: promote technology research, increase budget expenditure, and reduce renewable energy electricity prices. Results show that the sector is currently constrained by hydrogen production and storage costs, but is expected to enter a rapid growth phase around 2029 as technological advances and scale effects accumulate. In the baseline scenario for 2035, green hydrogen output reaches 16.29 million tons, the unit cost declines to 21.47 CNY/kg, the stock of fuel cell vehicles reaches 1.38 million, and the total number of hydrogen refueling stations is 5709. Policy simulations indicate that (1) advancing both clean hydrogen production and storage/delivery technologies simultaneously yields the strongest effect on cost reduction and output growth; (2) expanding transport and green budget expenditures effectively accelerates the deployment of vehicles and refueling infrastructure, with green budgeting exerting greater influence; and (3) renewable electricity pricing critically affects hydrogen supply and cost, excessive price reductions risk overcapacity and system-level imbalance arising from supply-demand misalignment. These findings provide policy insights for accelerating the transition toward a green hydrogen transport system.

title: Coupling polymer traits and environmental drivers to predict microplastic aging and DOC release in aquatic systems
abstract: Microplastic (MP) photoaging in aquatic environments reflects coupled controls from polymer traits and environmental forcing, yet transferable prediction across polymers remains limited. Here, we combine 32-day xenon-lamp photoaging experiments with a trait-environment kinetic framework for polystyrene (PS), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene (PE), using baseline-corrected carbonyl development (ΔCI) and polymer-mass-normalized DOC yields to quantify oxidation and dissolved-product export. Under the reference condition (100 μm, 0 psu, 0 rpm), PS showed the strongest oxidation development (ΔCI = 0.3163 at day 32), whereas PE and PET exhibited weaker ΔCI growth (0.0848 and 0.0415), and PVC remained near-zero/negative, consistent with non-carbonyl pathways. DOC increased monotonically for all polymers but diverged by day 32 (PS 1.2141, PVC 0.8765, PE 0.7041, PET 0.4626 mg g−1). Trajectory-based decoupling index metrics further showed that oxidation- and DOC-leading phases differed among polymer–treatment series. Across all scenarios, PS reached the highest DOC yield (2.1874 mg g−1 at 3 μm) while PET peaked under intensified mixing (0.9215 mg g−1 at 800 rpm), indicating that surface-area scaling and hydrodynamic forcing jointly regulate cumulative dissolved-product export with polymer-dependent sensitivity. Methodologically, we introduce a Monte Carlo-based trait-environment parameterization that maps fitted kinetic descriptors (ΔCImax, kCI, DOCmax, kDOC) to explicit predictive equations driven by polymer physicochemical traits and environmental conditions. This framework jointly predicts ΔCI and DOC from trait–environment coupling without using polymer identity as a categorical fitting term, achieving strong predictive performance across polymers and treatments (R2 = 0.8499–0.9983). Fluorescence characterization resolved three reproducible components that changed systematically with irradiation, indicating progressive changes in the optical signatures of dissolved products beyond bulk DOC.

title: Within-industry heterogeneity of emission productivity: Evidence from Portuguese manufacturing firms
abstract: Industrial decarbonisation policies are predominantly organised around sectors, targeting energy- and carbon-intensive industries as the main units of regulation. In contrast, a large body of economic literature documents substantial heterogeneity among firms operating within narrowly defined industries. To examine if similar heterogeneities can be observed regarding carbon emission performance, this article employs a novel data set of constructed energy-related scope 1 and scope 2 emissions for Portuguese manufacturing firms. The data set is build from administrative financial information with detailed energy use data, providing unusually broad coverage of firms within narrowly defined industries. The article analyses how much energy-related emission productivities vary across firms, and how much of this variation can be attributed to firm-level versus sector-level factors. Using within-industry dispersion measures, the results show that energy-related emission productivity varies widely across firms operating in the same sector, with substantially larger dispersion than observed for labour, capital, or material productivity. To investigate the sources of this heterogeneity, a variance decomposition analysis shows that while sector-level factors matter more for energy-related emission productivity than for other productivity measures, firm-level effects remain the dominant source of variation. These findings highlight the importance to further research within industry heterogeneities of emission performances to clarify if the results found for energy-related emissions productivity can be generalised to emission productivities more generally.

title: Terrain-constrained functional zoning and driver attribution for resource-efficient sustainability governance in a mountain urban agglomeration
abstract: Mountain urban agglomerations face increasing challenges in coordinating urban development, ecological protection, and resource-efficient sustainability governance under strong terrain constraints. Existing spatial Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) assessments often rely on administrative units or regular grids, limiting their ability to capture terrain-conditioned heterogeneity, cross-period comparability, and terrain-dependent driver attribution. Taking the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration, China, as a case study, this study proposes a terrain-constrained and temporally consistent framework for ecosystem-service-supported SDG functional zoning and model-based driver attribution. SDG composite indices for 2000, 2010, and 2020 were constructed using ecosystem service indicators, pooled min–max normalization, and equal-weight aggregation. These indices were integrated with temporal trajectories, spatial coordinates, geomorphological hierarchy, and topographic unit (TopoUnit) classes to delineate spatially coherent and temporally comparable functional zones. eXtreme Gradient Boosting–Shapley Additive Explanations (XGBoost-SHAP) was used to quantify the explanatory contributions of climatic and human-related predictors, while the Hierarchical Dominance Index (HDI) and Climate–Human Competition Index (CHI) were introduced to characterize terrain-dependent attribution differentiation. The proposed zoning model outperformed baseline methods, with Cluster Compactness Index (CCI), Moran's I, Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), and overlap ratio values of 0.224, 0.763, 0.812, and 0.846, respectively. Functional zones showed strong temporal stability, with stable areas accounting for 84.39%, 84.65%, and 87.92% in the three temporal comparisons. The mean SDG composite index increased from 0.6099 in 2000 to 0.6297 in 2020, while the high-value class expanded from 25.84% to 38.53%. XGBoost models achieved stable validation performance, with R2 values of 0.791–0.826. In 2020, human-related predictors contributed 57.5% of the total SHAP-based explanatory contribution, exceeding climatic predictors at 42.5%. HDI and CHI varied significantly across geomorphological hierarchy levels, confirming terrain-dependent attribution patterns. This framework provides a spatially explicit basis for differentiated sustainability governance in mountain urban agglomerations.

title: Continuous plastic film mulching reduces global warming potential (GWP) in greenhouse soil biosolarization by regulating microbial carbon and nitrogen metabolism
abstract: Soil biosolarization, which combines organic matter incorporation with solarization, is effective for soil improvement but may generate substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Plastic film mulching is a key operational factor in soil biosolarization. However, it remains poorly understood how different mulching strategies regulate soil temperature, moisture, and redox conditions and thereby reshape microbial carbon and nitrogen transformation pathways and GHG emissions. This study compared continuous film mulching (ContFM), no film mulching (NoFM), and intermittent film mulching (IntFM) during soil biosolarization. ContFM produced the highest soil temperature and moisture and likely favored the most persistent O2-limited microenvironment with prolonged anaerobic conditions, while IntFM showed intermediate and phase-dependent characteristics between ContFM and NoFM. Compared with NoFM, ContFM increased soil temperature and moisture by 18.60% and 58.31%, respectively, suppressed aerobic oxidative metabolism, reduced cumulative CO2 emissions by 52.66%, and increased CH4 emissions by 1.44-fold through enhanced methanogenesis-related potential, especially acetoclastic methanogenesis. In nitrogen cycling, ContFM enhanced dissimilatory nitrate reduction potential, favored NH4+ retention, and strengthened terminal N2O reduction potential, thereby reducing NO3− content by 65.70% and N2O emissions by 95.37%. Consequently, ContFM lowered GWP by 62.40%. However, delayed establishment of O2-limited conditions in IntFM may have caused a mismatch between upstream N2O-producing processes and terminal N2O reduction, resulting in only a 7.01% reduction in N2O emissions and a 20.10% reduction in GWP relative to NoFM. All treatments achieved high inactivation of F. oxysporum, while ContFM accelerated early-stage pathogen suppression. These findings suggest that ContFM can optimize GHG emission patterns and support cleaner biosolarization.

title: Trends and coupling coordination of agricultural carbon effects and food security in the Yellow River Basin, China
abstract: Agricultural systems are significant contributors to carbon emissions while also possessing substantial carbon sequestration potential. Understanding how agricultural carbon effects interact with food security is vital for reconciling China's ‘dual-carbon’ ambitions with sustainable food supply. However, quantitative assessment of their coupling relationship remains underexplored, particularly in major grain-producing regions like the Yellow River Basin (YRB). Here, we propose an integrated evaluation framework that combines Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Sets (IT2FS) to capture multi-uncertainties, and Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD) with Relative Development Degree (RDD) to diagnose the relationship between agricultural carbon effects and food security. Applying this framework to nine provinces across the YRB from 2003 to 2021, the results revealed considerable interprovincial variation in both subsystems. Agricultural carbon sequestration outweighed emissions by approximately fivefold; meanwhile, food security remained generally stable yet vulnerable to quality and ecological constraints. Four distinct coupling trajectories were further identified: Good Coordination – Synchronous Development (Inner Mongolia), Intermediate Coordination – Synchronous Development (Ningxia, Gansu, Sichuan, Shanxi, Shaanxi), Intermediate Coordination – Carbon Effects Lagging (Henan, Shandong), and Low Coordination – Food Security Lagging (Qinghai), associated with variations in resource endowment, economic development and policy orientation. Our findings support tailored regional policies for synergistic advancement of low-carbon agriculture and food security in the YRB.

title: Hybrid energy system based on co-firing municipal sludge coupled with power generation: energy balance, carbon emissions, and thermo-economic analysis
abstract: This study investigated a hybrid energy system for the co-firing coupling power generation of municipal multi-source organic solid waste sludge. Under the condition of a sludge treatment capacity of 300 t/d, project experimental study on coupled power generation by co-firing sludge with moisture contents of 40, 60, and 80% was conducted. Based on the on-site analytical data, an energy balance model for the sludge integrated treatment system and coal-fired boiler system was established, and the energy consumption of the hybrid energy system was calculated. Five types of unit loads 300, 360, 450, 480, and 540 MW were selected for a comprehensive comparative analysis in terms of thermal economy, carbon emissions, exhaust emissions, and profitability. The results demonstrate that, the maximum fluctuation range of the energy consumption loss was 41.49%, the maximum fluctuation range of the heat consumption of power generation was 7.32%, with a variation of 564.30 kJ/kW·h, and the maximum fluctuation range of the net standard coal consumption rate was 7.58%, with a variation of 22.80 g/kW·h. The maximum fluctuation range of carbon emissions resulting from electricity consumption was 17.93%, and the maximum fluctuation range of carbon emissions resulting from energy consumption was 70.21%. This study can provide a reference for the energy conservation and carbon reduction optimization design of municipal multi-source organic solid waste co-firing coupled with a power generation hybrid energy system.

title: Optimizing dual sourcing and transportation strategies for sustainable flower supply chains: A stochastic model with application to Sian flowers
abstract: The global floriculture industry faces critical sustainability challenges with air freight generating 3.5 kg CO2 per dozen roses—8-10 times higher than ocean alternatives. This research develops a novel dual-sourcing optimization framework that strategically allocates flower shipments between air and ocean transportation while balancing carbon footprint reduction with product quality preservation. Using stochastic mixed-integer programming, we model demand uncertainty, product deterioration, and environmental costs. Applied to Sian Flowers—a Kenyan exporter—our model demonstrates how strategic modal allocation can reduce emissions by 43.3% while increasing costs by only 2.4% through optimal 58% air freight allocation. Sensitivity analyses reveal carbon taxation thresholds at $45/ton CO2-eq trigger significant modal shifts. The study contributes to sustainable perishable supply chain literature by quantifying tradeoffs between environmental impact and operational feasibility, providing actionable insights for floriculture managers implementing resilient decarbonization strategies.

title: Redox-active Fe2O3 as a catalyst for humic substance synthesis in composting: Linking iron biogeochemistry with carbon stabilization
abstract: Humification is a key process affecting compost maturity and carbon stabilization, but the mechanisms by which iron oxide regulates humic substance (HS) formation in different composting substrates remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the process-level responses through which Fe2O3 influences HS formation and carbon stabilization in two contrasting composting systems, fruit-vegetable waste (FW) and chicken manure (CM). Composting experiments were conducted with Fe2O3 additions of 0.5% and 1%, and changes in physicochemical properties, humic precursors, iron speciation, microbial community composition, and carbon transformation were systematically analyzed. The results showed that Fe2O3 significantly enhanced organic matter (OM) degradation and HS accumulation, with final HS contents increasing by 9.8% in FW1% and 9.3% in CM1% compared with their respective controls. Fe2O3 addition was also associated with increased Fe3+/Fe2+ transformation, higher Fep levels, shifts in microbial community succession, and enhanced conversion of labile organics into more stable humified fractions. Overall, the responses to Fe2O3 were substrate-dependent, with FW and CM showing different patterns of precursor turnover, microbial succession, and iron-related transformation. These findings suggest that Fe2O3 may contribute to compost humification through coupled iron transformation, microbial regulation, and carbon stabilization, providing process-level insight into the role of iron oxides in organic waste valorization.

title: A graph-based C-BOM framework integrating multi-view xBOM data for efficient product carbon footprint assessment
abstract: Efficient Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) assessment is critical for manufacturing enterprises to enhance core competitiveness and meet regulatory requirements. The Bill of Materials (BOM) contains comprehensive enterprise data covering the entire product life cycle, serving as a key foundation for PCF assessment. However, traditional BOM frameworks suffer from data silos and a lack of carbon-related attributes, thus failing to support reliable PCF assessment and cross-system data integration. In this research, a Carbon-Bill of Materials (C-BOM) framework was proposed to integrate multi-view data for precise carbon source management. In this work, the carbon-related information across life-cycle stages was systematically organized by establishing a mapping model that links carbon flows with enterprise business activities. To tackle multi-source heterogeneous data issues, a unified C-BOM data model was constructed using a graph-based transformation algorithm, converting disparate data into a consistent, carbon-enriched representation. A case study on a telecommunications die-cast enclosure with 23 C-BOM items was conducted to validate the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the C-BOM framework effectively resolves data heterogeneity and enables accurate carbon accounting. This approach provides manufacturing enterprises with a scalable solution for optimizing product life-cycle low-carbon management and achieving regulatory compliance.

title: A multi-scale adaptive graph convolution-based carbon price prediction model
abstract: Carbon price prediction is crucial for improving carbon market efficiency and supporting climate policy implementation. To address the limitations of existing models in capturing multiscale temporal dependencies and inter-variable relationships, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Adaptive Graph Convolution Network (CETPNet). Integrating Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), adaptive graph learning, temporal-frequency dual-domain graph convolution, and interactive convolution, CETPNet effectively captures periodic features, cross-scale nonlinear dependencies, and the fusion of local and global information. Experiments were conducted on daily carbon price data (2015–2024) from three representative Chinese carbon pilot markets (Guangdong, Hubei, and Shanghai). The results indicate that: (1) CETPNet outperforms mainstream models (DLinear, Transformer, Autoformer, MAGNN, and MSGNet), reducing MAE by 15.6% and RMSE by 13.3% compared with the optimal baseline MSGNet; (2) ablation studies confirm that adaptive graph convolution plays a critical role, and its removal increases MAE and RMSE by 106.6% and 89.4%, respectively; (3) scale-specific adjacency learning overcomes the limitations of shared adjacency matrices in modeling scale-specific dependencies. Overall, CETPNet exhibits strong multi-scale learning and generalization capabilities, providing technical support for carbon price discovery.

title: Collaborative optimization of thermal safety and interphase stability of sodium-ion batteries based on ethoxy (pentafluoro) cyclotriphosphazene additive
abstract: The conventional electrolytes are highly flammable and it is a key factor leading to the thermal runaway of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Ethoxy (pentafluoro) cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN) is recognized as a good electrolyte additive for SIBs. In this study, the evolution of electrochemical performance and safety performance are systematically revealed by controlling the concentration of PFPN. The results show that the addition of 5 vol% PFPN can not only achieve an ideal flame retardancy but also maintain a good electrochemical performance. Na‖NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) coin cells using the electrolyte with 5 vol% PFPN shows good electrochemical compatibility and low interface impedance. When the addition of PFPN reached 7 vol%, the fire risk was further reduced, but the reversible capacity of the cells decreased rapidly. Quantitative thermal-safety evaluation of electrolyte, electrolyte/electrode mixture and full cell by PFPN addition is carried out. Key parameters obtained from the cone calorimeter test indicate that 5 vol% PFPN can effectively delay the ignition time, reduce the peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (HRR) of electrolyte. Meanwhile, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) tests reveal that PFPN can effectively suppress the thermal decomposition of electrolyte, the mixture of electrolyte with NFM at 0% SOC, the mixture of electrolyte with Na metal anode, and the full cell at 0% SOC, but its inhibition effect is limited for the mixture of electrolyte with NFM at 100% SOC and the full cell system at 100% SOC due to the violent exothermic reaction between the electrolyte and highly desodiated NFM with high oxidizing reactivity.

title: Resource-toxicity tradeoffs for cleaner production of battery-grade lithium carbonate via attention-enhanced LCA
abstract: Traditional life cycle assessment (LCA) fails to capture the critical tradeoffs between strategic resource dissipation and solid waste-specific toxicological risks in battery-grade lithium carbonate (BGLC) production, causing incomplete and biased cleaner production decision-making in the lithium battery industry. This study proposes a novel attention mechanism-enhanced LCA framework, integrating emerging indicators for lithium depletion potential (Li-DPEM) and thallium/beryllium toxic hazard potentials (Tl-THPE, Be-THPE). Multiple BGLC production pathways (lepidolite-based S1, spodumene-based S2, waste LiFePO4 recycling S3) were systematically analyzed to reveal insights obscured by traditional LCA. Traditional LCA results show that S1 presents the highest burden in traditional impact categories (e.g., GWP100, and HTPnc). In contrast, the proposed innovative framework realizes a significant restructuring of the environmental impact profiles for primary ore-based pathways. The environmental impact gap between S1 and S2 is substantially narrowed from over 400 times under the traditional framework to 64.68%, which is mainly attributed to the massive lithium loss in spodumene smelting slag (Li-DPEM: 0.255 kg LCE). Meanwhile, S1 exhibits markedly higher specific toxic risks (Tl-THPE: 0.00314 kg 1,4-DCB-eq; Be-THPE: 0.08 kg 1,4-DCB-eq), which are rarely captured by traditional LCA. The comprehensive evaluation guided by the attention mechanism conclusively identifies S3 as the most sustainable cleaner production pathway, with the overall impact index reduced by 25.5% (S1) and 14.4% (S2), respectively. This framework reveals the multiple advantages of waste LiFePO4 recycling in reducing fossil fuel dependence, avoiding secondary release of highly toxic elements, and mitigating ecological impacts from primary ore mining, strongly supporting the development of circular economy in the battery industry. This study not only provides a methodological advance for more adaptive and accurate LCA to address emerging environmental challenges, but also offers quantitative scientific support for cleaner production process optimization and circular economy strategy formulation in the lithium battery industry.

title: The robot revolution's green footprint: A threshold analysis of industrial robots and carbon emissions
abstract: As primary instruments of intelligent automation, industrial robots sit at the intersection of digitalization and decarbonization. Their environmental implications, however, are not straightforward, especially when total carbon emissions rather than emission intensity are considered. To examine this issue, this study uses a country-industry panel covering 33 countries and 15 harmonized industry groups. The linear specifications use the full 2000-2020 sample, while the non-linear analysis relies on a strongly balanced 2000-2018 panel to meet the requirements of the dynamic threshold model. The results show that industrial robot adoption is associated with lower carbon intensity, and this association remains stable across endogeneity treatments and sensitivity checks. For total emissions, the estimated relationship is non-linear: robot density identifies an empirical inflection point of approximately 2.149 robots per 1000 workers. Above this level, the marginal association between robot adoption and total emissions becomes more favorable, suggesting that the technique effect strengthens only after automation reaches sufficient intensity. The channel results further indicate that robots are linked to lower emission intensity through changes in factor allocation and production efficiency. By identifying where and when robot adoption is more likely to support decarbonization, the study offers a more cautious empirical basis for aligning intelligent manufacturing with climate policy.

title: The spatial impact of pixel scale PM2.5 driven by policy dissemination. New evidence from a super urban agglomeration
abstract: Accurately quantifying the effectiveness of air pollution control policies is critical for the regional mitigation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5). However, most existing assessments are confined to the urban scale, thereby overlooking the fine-grained spatial impacts of policy implementation. This study integrated the 1 km-resolution PM2.5 dataset from the Multiple Air Pollutants (MuAP) with PM2.5 control policies across the Greater Bay Area (GBA) to quantitatively analyze the nonlinear relationship between the two at the 1 km pixel scale. We processed and counted the number of PM2.5 control policies, and quantitatively scored the quality of each policy based on Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Deepseek. We use the quartile segmentation method applied to population data to reasonably distinguish the entire GBA and main urban region for multidimensional difference analysis. At the urban scale, through the K-means clustering and Pearson correlation analysis, it was found that the PM2.5 concentration difference (time lag scenario) was significantly positively correlated with the quantity and quality of policies (best scenario R = 0.691, p < 0.01). At the pixel scale, the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model was utilized to construct a robust multi-factor nonlinear relationship (0.86 ≤ R2 ≤ 0.88) effectively fitted between PM2.5 and the quantity and quality of PM2.5 control policies. Further, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework was used to analyze the nonlinear spatial heterogeneity between multi-dimensional factors and the quantity and quality of PM2.5 control policies. Crucially, our findings also clarified that PM2.5 concentration changes between cities can be affected and propagated through the diffusion and dissemination of policies across different cities. This research provides new analytical paths and key insights for promoting environmental policy assessment, air quality evolution modeling, and health risk assessment.

title: Resilience formation mechanism and policy simulation of drone industrial innovation ecosystems: A system dynamics approach
abstract: The rapid development of the low-altitude economy is significantly propelled by the drone industry, a key pillar of its sustainable high-quality growth. However, the industry faces multiple external risks, including technology blockades and restrictions, talent shortages and brain drain, and declining public acceptance, which lead to its systemic vulnerabilities. Therefore, achieving strategic sustainable development goals through policy measures represents a critical challenge. Adopting a system dynamics approach, this study constructs a model of the industrial innovation ecosystem, incorporating enterprises, universities, research institutions, government bodies, investors, and the public. The model integrates four dimensions of resilience—diversity, evolvability, mobility, and buffering, to simulate the resilience under external shocks of varying intensities and recovery strategies. Findings indicate: (1) Resilience formation involves highly complex system coupling and dynamic feedback; (2) Different types and intensities of shocks have distinct effects on resilience. Technology blockades and restrictions are the most disruptive, particularly in scenarios involving abrupt or multiple shocks; (3) While single policy tools offer targeted benefits in specific contexts, they are insufficient for fully restoring system resilience; (4) Combined policy tools perform significantly better than single measures, demonstrating a synergistic structure led by supply-side initiatives, supported by demand-side measures, and facilitated by environmental-side coordination. This approach substantially improves the system's resilience to multiple shocks. This study not only enriches the theory of innovation ecosystem resilience but also offers a theoretical and methodological foundation for governments to formulate differentiated policies, optimize resource allocation, and build a highly resilient drone innovation ecosystem.

title: Facilitating group consensus for offshore oil and gas decommissioning options: An improved similarity-based model
abstract: The decommissioning of offshore oil and gas (O&G) infrastructure is a complex process that requires balancing diverse priorities of decision-makers (DMs) across various criteria. While multi-criteria group decision-making (MCGDM) methods have been used for evaluating decommissioning options, it is challenging to determine the final option when DMs hesitate among several evaluation values. This study proposes an improved similarity-based model to facilitate this decision-making process. It integrates hesitant fuzzy numbers (HFNs) to capture DMs hesitation during evaluation. This model employs objective weighting mechanisms, using the Louvain community algorithm for DMs weights and linear programming technique for the multidimensional analysis of preference (LINMAP) method for criteria weights. A comprehensive evaluation framework is constructed to thoroughly assess decommissioning options. The model is validated through a real-world case, as results match the actual decommissioning decision. The research findings highlight the model's strengths in modeling DMs hesitation, reducing subjective bias, and balancing conflicting decommissioning criteria. The primary contributions are: (1) an improved similarity-based model framework for MCGDM problems; (2) integration of HFNs in offshore O&G decommissioning projects; (3) objective weights of DMs and criteria using the Louvain community algorithm and LINMAP method; and (4) a systematic criteria system designed for offshore O&G decommissioning requirements.

title: Rapid nickel extraction from saprolitic laterite based on synergistic effects between mechanochemical activation and nitric acid
abstract: The shift to clean energy is driving a surging demand for the extraction of battery metals like nickel and cobalt from laterite ores. Atmospheric acid leaching offers mild operating conditions and straightforward process control; however, its practical application often suffers from long leaching durations and limited extraction. This study optimized the nitric acid atmospheric leaching of saprolitic laterite using the response surface methodology. The optimized conditions were 228 g L−1 HNO3, 96 °C, 100 min, and a liquid-to-solid ratio of 5.9:1 mL g−1, under which Ni and Mg extractions reached 94.82% and 94.05%, respectively. Four mechanochemical activation pretreatments on leaching performance were subsequently evaluated, with HNO3-assisted ball milling demonstrating the greatest enhancement. During ball milling, mechanochemical activation transformed the serpentine structure into a more reactive amorphous phase, while H3O+ and NO3− altered serpentine surface properties and reactivity, contributing to the disruption of inert plane, reduced particle size, and improved wettability. The reaction mechanism was further explored by first-principles calculation and molecular dynamics simulation. The synergistic effects between mechanochemical activation and HNO3 significantly reduced the required leaching conditions, shortened the leaching duration from 100 min to 30 min, increased Ni extraction to 98.2%, and improved slurry filterability. This work develops a facile and effective method for enhanced Ni extraction from saprolitic laterite, paving the way for greener and more efficient processing of laterites and other silicate minerals.

title: Biogas production from Co-digestion of chicken litter, swine manure, and whey: A comparative study of batch and semi-continuous regimes
abstract: This study investigates the anaerobic co-digestion of agro-industrial residues, specifically chicken litter, swine manure, and whey, as a sustainable approach for managing waste and generating renewable energy. The improper disposal of agricultural by-products can lead to soil and water contamination, along with increased greenhouse gas emissions.
