Anaerobic digestion represents an effective alternative by converting organic residues into biogas and nutrient-rich biofertilizers, thereby contributing to both environmental and economic sustainability. The research compares co-digestion performance under batch and semi-continuous operating conditions, emphasizing the role of solid–liquid fraction separation. Batch experiments showed that co-digestion improves biogas production relative to mono-digestion, and that separating the solid fraction further enhances gas yield. Kinetic modeling (Modified Gompertz, Cone, and BPK) confirmed this synergy, showing enhanced hydrolysis efficiency and higher maximum methane production rates in the co-digestion mixtures. A 20 L pilot-scale semi-continuous reactor was operated through two distinct cycles to evaluate process performance under different Organic Loading Rates. During the first cycle (150 days), with swine manure as the main substrate, the highest biogas production was achieved at an OLR of 1.00 kgVS·m−3·d−1, resulting in volumetric and specific methane productions of 3.58 LN·gVS−1·d−1 and 2.47 LN·gVS−1·d−1, respectively. In the second cycle (140 days), where chicken litter and whey were used as feedstock, the maximum biogas yield occurred at an OLR of 1.50 kgVS·m−3·d−1, producing 2.70 LN·gVS−1·d−1 of biogas and 1.88 LN·gVS−1·d−1 of methane. Overall, the results offer practical insights for developing anaerobic digestion systems at larger scales, promoting efficient waste utilization and the advancement of sustainable bioenergy technologies.

title: High-pressure de-sublimation for enhanced cryogenic CO2 capture in LNG production from natural gas with high CO2 content
abstract: The growing exploitation of natural gas with high CO2 content poses significant challenges to the liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry. In particular, the conventional amine-based purification process incurs substantial energy consumption for CO2 removal, which escalates non-linearly with the CO2 concentration in feed gas. This high energy consumption severely undermines the process's economic viability and environmental footprint, necessitating the development of more efficient CO2 capture technologies. Cryogenic techniques have potential advantages over chemical absorption for this aspect, but the existing low-pressure de-sublimation process significantly increases the energy demand of liquefaction. To address this issue, this study innovatively proposes cryogenic CO2 capture by supercritical pressure de-sublimation, and the core innovation is pressure-synchronous operation of the capture and liquefaction units. This design achieves dual energy-saving advantages: it significantly enhances cooling heat transfer efficiency and, crucially, eliminates the latent heat consumption for subsequent methane liquefaction. System simulations demonstrate that this approach reduces the specific energy consumption for LNG production to 0.9183 kWh/kg LNG, achieving a 15.4% reduction compared to a benchmark low-pressure de-sublimation system of equivalent configuration. This enhancement contributes to an increase of 7.3 percentage points in the overall exergy efficiency of the system. Due to the reduction in power consumption, the power consumption of the refrigeration cycles and purchase cost of the compressors are significantly reduced, resulting in a cost reduction from 113.5 to 98.8 $/t LNG. Compared with established technologies such as chemical absorption and membrane separation reported in the literature, the specific energy consumption is reduced by 16.0% to 55.6%. The proposed high-pressure de-sublimation process shows considerable promise for advanced CO2 capture, thereby enabling a pathway to cleaner LNG production.

title: Bridging the biophysical gap of Water-Energy-Carbon nexus in agricultural systems: A unified emergy-based framework for evaluating regenerative and demand-side interventions
abstract: The transition to sustainable agriculture requires navigating the complex trade-offs within the Water-Energy-Carbon nexus, especially as decentralized renewable energy reshapes the temporal and spatial dynamics of resource availability. However, current assessments often face the incommensurability challenge, where environmental costs (user-side) and ecological contributions (donor-side) are evaluated in isolated metrics, ignoring the potential of agricultural infrastructure to act as a functional buffer for the energy transition. This paper proposes a unified emergy-based framework to bridge this gap, moving beyond a conventional burden-oriented nexus evaluation toward an biosphere-work-oriented valuation logic. By introducing a phasic assessment approach, we capture the temporal dynamics of agricultural metabolism, redefining irrigation not merely as a resource sink but as a “virtual energy storage” component capable of synchronizing demand with renewable power profiles. Emergy, introduced by the ecologist H.T. Odum, is a measure of the biosphere's work in support of resource generation over time and spatial scales. Beyond standard accounting, we define two novel emergy-based indicators: the System-Wide Net Carbon Emergy Balance (USNCEB) to evaluate the shift from carbon load to ecological regulation service, and the Renewable Resource Substitution Emergy Efficiency (ƞRRSEE) to quantify the multiplier effect of the technological nexus. We applied this framework to a comparative case study of an integrated solar-wind-drip irrigation system versus conventional fossil-based farming across diverse intensive agricultural scenarios (China and Argentina). Results reveal a fundamental metabolic shift: the integrated system increases the renewable emergy share to ∼55%-70% and drastically reduces the Environmental Loading Ratio. The USNCEB shifts from a negative ecological debt to a positive value, confirming that the system functions as a net climate regulator rather than a passive emitter. Furthermore, an ƞRRSEE > 1.0 demonstrates a positive synergy, where the renewable infrastructure investment unlocks biophysical savings (fossil fuel and water) that exceed its own embodied cost. Our findings suggest that by aligning agronomic flexibility with precision resource management, agricultural systems can achieve a triple win of water productivity, decarbonization, and grid resilience. The study establishes emergy synthesis as a vital tool for revealing the donor-side value of low-carbon technologies, advocating for policy shifts from linear input subsidies to integrated payments for ecological regulation services.

title: Thermomechanically-beneficiated waste concrete fines as binder in 3D-printing concrete formulation
abstract: Excessive reliance on high cement content to achieve printability in 3D-printed concrete (3DPC) increases its carbon footprint. This study evaluates the potential of thermomechanically-beneficiated waste concrete fines (WCF) as an extender to maximise the binder substitution. A series of 3DPC mixes were prepared by replacing limestone calcined clay (LC2) with uncarbonated (UWCF) and carbonated (CWCF) waste concrete fines at 30%, 50%, and 100% levels, while ordinary portland cement (OPC) was replaced at a 30% level. Rheological characterisation, including the determination of the static and dynamic yield stresses, plastic viscosity, thixotropy and structuration rates, was conducted. Printability was assessed by extrusion pressure, layer deformation and surface defect spacing during the fabrication of 1 m-high hollow cylinders. Carbonated WCF (CWCF) improved rheological performance by reducing water demand, plastic viscosity, and yield stresses, leading to lower extrusion pressure and enhanced printability. Mixes incorporating 30% CWCF in OPC or LC2 systems outperformed reference mix (RefMix), achieving smoother extrusion (defect spacing >15 cm), stable buildability, and minimal deformation (<7%) at reduced extrusion pressure (112.5 kPa). In contrast, uncarbonated WCF (UWCF) increased viscosity and extrusion resistance (up to 235.8 kPa), resulting in poor printability at higher replacement levels. Under the investigated conditions, CWCF replacement levels of 30–50% provided a balanced performance in terms of printability and compressive strength. From a sustainability perspective, CWCF incorporation reduced binder-level carbon emissions. Specifically, a 30% CWCF replacement level achieved up to a 36% reduction in carbon footprint relative to RefMix through a combined effect of CO2 sequestration and partial replacement of conventional binders.

title: Energy efficiency-oriented R&D effectiveness in türkiye: A fourier-based analysis of renewable energy use, energy prices, energy imports, and foreign direct investment
abstract: This study examines the determinants of energy efficiency–related R&D effectiveness (RDEFF) in Türkiye over the period 1990–2022. The analysis investigates the associations between energy prices, energy imports, renewable energy use, and foreign direct investment within an output-oriented framework that measures R&D effectiveness based on energy-saving outcomes per unit of R&D input. Fourier-based econometric methods are employed to account for potential structural breaks in the long-run relationships. The results indicate distinct short- and long-run patterns. Energy prices are positively associated with RDEFF in both the short and long run. Energy imports are consistently negatively associated with RDEFF across all specifications. Renewable energy use shows no statistically significant short-run relationship, while it is positively associated with RDEFF in the long run. Similarly, foreign direct investment is statistically insignificant in the short run but shows a positive long-run association. Overall, the findings suggest that RDEFF is related to macroeconomic conditions such as price signals, external energy dependence, and investment flows within a multi-factor long-run framework. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing between short- and long-run relationships in an aggregate time-series context with structural breaks.

title: Associations between urban 5D morphology and thermal environments: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and socioeconomic interaction across Chinese prefecture-level cities
abstract: While optimizing the multidimensional built environment is increasingly advocated to address urban heat islands (UHI), current research predominantly relies on static, dimensionally fragmented evaluations at narrow spatial scales. Crucially, comprehensive evidence regarding how morphological associations dynamically evolve across heterogeneous baseline climates, socio-economic contexts, and distinct urbanization phases remain underexplored. Addressing these multidimensional gaps, we construct a decadal panel dataset (2011–2020) evaluating UHII across 325 Chinese prefecture-level cities by applying the unified 5D framework. Using explainable machine learning, we systematically decode morphological elements' nonlinear associations and their interactive patterns with overarching socio-environmental covariates. Results demonstrate these morphological associations are profoundly context-dependent, revealing the limitations of one-size-fits-all planning assumptions. First, background climate significantly contextualizes spatial thermal patterns; Notably, high-density development transitions from exhibiting a strong escalating thermal trajectory in arid regions to manifesting relatively lower thermal associations within specific density thresholds in wet zones. Second, morphological patterns exhibit strict stage dependency. As cities evolve from rapid physical expansion to refined stock optimization, structural layouts like polycentricity correlate with lower thermal loads, whereas background densification increasingly aligns with a weakened association between fragmented green spaces and relatively lower thermal predictions. Furthermore, socioeconomic contexts systematically define these boundaries: economic affluence emerges as a statistical condition correlating with compact development's environmental potential, while hyper-urbanization corresponds to weakened macro-ecological buffering and indicates that extreme spatial connectivity correlates with elevated thermal risks. Ultimately, drawing from a comprehensive suite of findings, this study advances framework integration and scale innovation, providing context-resolved evidence that supports a shift from universal targets toward localized, stage-calibrated, and socioeconomically aligned precision planning.

title: Thermophilic/hyperthermophilic stage as component of temperature-phased anaerobic digestion or pretreatment of mesophilic digestion to enhance bio-methanation of oily food waste?
abstract: Anaerobic digestion of oily food waste is subject to inhibition of long chain fatty acids, key intermediates of lipid degradation. Given enhanced mass transfer during pre-digestion at elevated temperatures, thermophilic/hyperthermophilic stages in two configurations were evaluated: as integrated components of temperature-phased anaerobic digestion (TPAD) and as pretreatment units for mesophilic digestion (MD). When integrated into TPAD, these stages improved process stability and effluent quality but did not elevate methane yields relative to single-stage MD. Used as pretreatment, they effectively alleviated high-loading inhibition, driving substantial increase in methane yield by approximately 30.0%. Pretreatment contributed to high-quality biogas with a methane content of approximately 75.0%, enabling the total system to achieve a net profit increase of 10.0-20.0%. Thermophilic pretreatment was optimal for moderate-lipid substrate. Hyperthermophilic pretreatment showed superior lipid conversion capacity and mesophilic archaea preservation for high-lipid feedstock. Hyperthermophilic pre-digestion was more competitive in maintaining archaea survival under high-lipid loading. Future work should focus on enhancing hyperthermophilic lipid tolerance and hybrid stage integration.

title: Spatiotemporal degradation of coastal ecosystem services in mainland China: A land-sea integrated assessment
abstract: The coastal zone is a critical land-sea interface essential for ecological security and regional sustainable development. Existing ecosystem service assessments often fail to integrate terrestrial and marine subsystems and may overlook gradual hidden ecological degradation, resulting in fragmented understanding of coastal ecosystem dynamics. To address this gap, we constructed a Land-Sea Integrated Assessment framework to quantitatively evaluate the ecosystem services of Mainland China's Coastal Zone (CCZ) from 2000 to 2020, and introduced the Magnitude of Change in the Ecosystem Service Index (MC-ESI) to quantify the relative change in ESI and identify hidden ecological degradation hotspots. The results showed that: (1) the ESI of the CCZ remained relatively stable and exhibited a “first decrease then increase” trend during 2000–2020, while 55.97% of the CCZ experienced declining ESI values and the area proportion of Good and Excellent ecosystem-service grades continuously decreased, revealing widespread hidden ecological degradation under long-term anthropogenic disturbance; (2) spatially, ecosystem services exhibited pronounced patterns of “South strong–North weak” and “north improvement versus south degradation”, with the average terrestrial ESI decreasing continuously by approximately 2% (2.50 to 2.45), whereas marine ESI rebounded by approximately 6% from 1.51 in 2010 to 1.60 in 2020, highlighting the important buffering role of marine ecosystems; (3) terrestrial ecosystem-service degradation was primarily driven by anthropogenic factors such as land-use changes and nighttime lights, whereas marine ecosystem stability depended mainly on nonlinear synergistic interactions among oceanographic factors including temperature, salinity, and distance to the coastline. This study highlights the importance of integrated land-sea ecosystem assessment for revealing hidden ecological degradation and understanding spatially heterogeneous coastal ecosystem dynamics. The proposed framework provides a scientific basis for adaptive coastal governance and spatially differentiated land–sea coordinated conservation under increasing urbanization and climate change pressures.

title: Using interpretable machine learning method to predict children's fluoride exposure health risks based on routine water quality data: An empirical study in the Huaihe River Basin, China
abstract: Fluoride exposure in surface water is a persistent public health concern worldwide. Current approaches still face challenges in continuous assessment and timely warning of fluoride-related health risks. To address this limitation, this study used the Huaihe River Basin in China as a case study. Monthly water quality data from 377 monitoring stations collected between January 2021 and September 2025 were employed to develop an exposure-oriented assessment framework. The framework predicted children's fluoride health risks using routinely monitored physicochemical water quality parameters. The study first systematically analyzed the spatiotemporal distribution of fluoride in the basin. Health risk values were evaluated for adult males, adult females, and children. Four machine learning models were constructed and compared for predictive performance. These models included Light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), multilayer perceptron, decision tree, and extreme learning machine. The optimal model was combined with the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method to identify key influencing factors. Results indicated that fluoride concentrations exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity, fluoride concentrations ranged from 0.003 to 2.26 mg/L. Health risks follow the order of children (13.75%) > adult females (0.24%) > adult males (0.05%). The LightGBM model achieved the highest predictive performance, with an overall accuracy of 90.7%, outperforming the other models. SHAP analysis identified five-day biochemical oxygen demand, total nitrogen, ammonia nitrogen as key indicators influencing the prediction of fluoride health risks in children. This study demonstrates that reliable prediction of children's fluoride health risks can be achieved using routine monitoring data. The framework provides a feasible tool for early screening and preventive interventions for regional fluoride exposure.

title: Novel dual-cone hydrocyclone for efficient recovery of micron-sized catalyst: Turbulence suppression and separation enhancement
abstract: Micrometer-sized catalyst particles are essential in numerous green chemical processes, yet their efficient recovery from wastewater remains a major challenge for resource conservation and environmental protection. Discharge of these particles causes significant economic loss and poses serious risks to aquatic ecosystems. Conventional single-cone hydrocyclones suffer from flow field instability and high turbulence intensity, severely limiting their ability to recover fine catalyst particles. This study introduces a novel dual-cone micro-hydrocyclone that optimizes internal flow field distribution through strategic cone section modification, thereby suppressing turbulence and enhancing separation efficiency. A comprehensive investigation combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, particle image velocimetry (PIV), and experimental validation was conducted across four hydrocyclone configurations. The CFD and PIV results showed excellent agreement, confirming that the dual-cone structure effectively reduces turbulence intensity in the main separation zone, increases tangential velocity, and stabilizes axial velocity profiles. These flow-field improvements lead to more stable particle trajectories, weaker fine-particle escape, and enhanced underflow enrichment. Under the tested optimal condition, the Type II hydrocyclone achieved a TS-1 catalyst recovery efficiency of 90.4%, reduced the overflow solids concentration to below the industrial requirement, and improved the concentration performance of the underflow. The proposed dual-cone hydrocyclone provides a chemical-free, compact, and energy-efficient strategy for recovering high-value micron-sized catalysts from industrial wastewater. This work offers mechanistic guidance for hydrocyclone structural design and supports cleaner catalyst recycling in sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Moisture-regulated pad dyeing of cotton fabrics: mechanistic insights into water migration and energy-efficient fixation
abstract: Reducing water and energy consumption in cotton dyeing is essential for cleaner textile production. In reactive dyeing of cotton fabrics, improving dye fixation while reducing water, salt, and energy consumption remains an important challenge for cleaner production. In this study, a moisture-regulated pad dyeing strategy was investigated. A rapid and non-destructive method for measuring fabric moisture content was established and combined with time-domain nuclear magnetic resonance (TD-NMR) to characterize internal moisture migration during pre-drying. The results showed that during pre-drying, water migration and moisture loss were accompanied by substantial removal of free water and gradual contraction of the internal pores within cotton fibers, while the remaining moisture mainly existed as loosely and strongly bound water within the fibers. On this basis, the effects of fixation temperature, humidity, and time were systematically investigated to identify the matching rule between pre-drying moisture content and fixation temperature and humidity conditions. Under practical fixation conditions, complete removal of free water did not further improve dye fixation. Instead, dye fixation was mainly governed by the matching between residual moisture content and fixation temperature and humidity conditions. By appropriately matching pre-drying moisture levels with fixation environments, dye fixation exceeding 90% were achieved. Compared with conventional pad-steam dyeing, the optimized moisture-regulated fixation process reduced electric energy consumption and steam usage by up to 53.57% and 42.73%, respectively. This study provides mechanistic insight into moisture-regulated dye fixation and offers a practical optimization strategy for cleaner cotton dyeing.

title: Collaborative modeling and multi-objective optimization of integrated energy systems with diverse energy storage and flexible hydrogen regulation
abstract: Driven by the “Dual Carbon” strategy and the transformation of energy systems, integrated energy systems (IESs) have become a key pathway for improving energy efficiency and enabling multi-energy synergy. To address strong multi-energy coupling, complex operation, and high-dimensional optimization, this study develops a deeply integrated IES architecture incorporating diverse energy production, conversion, and storage technologies. A laddered carbon trading mechanism is introduced to internalize emission costs, while a flexible hydrogen-blended gas strategy and a two-stage power-to-gas model enhance system flexibility and resilience. In addition, Monte Carlo simulation is employed to characterize the stochastic behavior of electric and hydrogen vehicles. To solve the resulting multi-objective optimization problem, a feedback-driven bi-level collaborative optimization framework is proposed, along with a novel multi-objective k-means optimizer (MOKO) integrating shift-based density estimation, fitness allocation, and enhanced archive strategies. The model is solved using Gurobi in combination with MOKO. Results demonstrate that coordinated multi-energy storage significantly improves system performance. Compared with benchmark system 1, the proposed method reduces economic cost by 25.89%, improves energy efficiency by 4.32%, and decreases pollutant emissions by 96.28%. Compared with benchmark system 2, it achieves a 5.36% performance improvement and a 99.09% enhancement in environmental indicators. Furthermore, after obtaining the optimal solutions and conducting benchmark comparisons, a post-analysis is performed, including multi-parameter sensitivity analysis and multi-scenario Monte Carlo-based load uncertainty analysis, to further evaluate system robustness under parameter variations and stochastic load conditions. The proposed framework provides an effective and scalable solution for low-carbon, flexible, and efficient IESs operation.

title: Beyond performance-cost trade-off: Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC) incorporating ultra-high-volume coal gangue wastes
abstract: Coal gangue (CG) is a bulk solid waste with an urgent need for high-value utilization. To promote its sustainable upcycling, this study successfully developed Engineered/Strain-hardening Geopolymer Composites (EGC/SHGC) with an ultra-high tensile ductility of 8.4% using 100% coal gangue aggregates (CGA) and 60% calcined coal gangue (CCG) precursors under a low fiber dosage of 1.2%. Results showed that replacing fine silica sand with CGA increased tensile ductility by 17.9%, and the increment of CCG/fly ash replacement ratio from 0% to 60% further raised the value by 27.3%. From X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetric analysis, Brunauer-Emmett-Teller, microhardness, and X-ray computed tomography test results, the role of CGA as “additional flaws” was demonstrated, thereby lowering cracking strength while enhancing tensile ductility of EGC. Meanwhile, with increasing CCG contents, although the reaction degree of precursors increased, the microhardness of gel regions decreased whereas the average paste microhardness almost remained unchanged, resulting in enhanced strain-hardening potential while maintaining the tensile strength of EGC. The proposed ultra-high-volume CG waste substitution strategy achieved a synergy between cost reduction and tensile performance enhancement in EGC, offering a promising pathway for the application of CG-based EGC in sustainable and resilient infrastructure.

title: Integrated bioprocessing of garlic peel waste: Dual valorization through prodigiosin production using Serratia marcescens NITDPER1 and sustainable nanocarbon dots synthesis
abstract: Agricultural peels are the ecological burden that is of immense environmental concern in today's world. One of such wastes, produced in tons, is the outer skin of garlic (Allium sativum), which remains dumped, only leading to landfill issues and soil contamination. Looking into the lignocellulosic content of these peels, the objective of the present study was to utilize it as a bacterial growth matrix for producing prodigiosin through solid state fermentation (SSF) using ligninolytic Serratia marcescens NITDPER1 and subsequently converting it into a cellulose-rich mass to generate carbon dots (CDs). At the lab scale, the highest prodigiosin yield was 60.35 ± 2.3 mg/g at 36 h, with a maximum production of 55.22 ± 3.1 mg/g at 48 h in scale-up. Analysis of garlic peels (GPs) after pigment extraction unleashed 32.7% relative lignin degradation and 26.3% cellulose enrichment compared to the initial content, respectively. Analysis of GPs after SSF, through FESEM, FT-IR, and XRD, confirmed the structural changes in the substrate due to bacterial action. The cellulose-rich fraction after pigment recovery was successfully converted into high-value CDs, which revealed a broad peak at 340 nm in the UV-Vis scan, excitation-emission peaks at 380 nm and 470 nm, respectively, in the fluorescence spectra, particle size of 2.5 nm, and characteristic peaks in FT-IR, revealing successful production. The produced CDs were found to be non-toxic in haemolytic assay and immobilization studies on Daphnia magna. This study showed efficient prodigiosin production using GPs along with ligninolysis, turning it into cellulose-rich biomass for further valorization into biocompatible CDs.

title: Compatibility assessment and comprehensive evaluation model for co-production of natural gas hydrate and shallow gas
abstract: Natural gas hydrate is regarded as a strategic unconventional energy resource with enormous global reserves. Co-production of gas hydrate and shallow gas represents a promising approach for advancing the industrial development of gas hydrate resources. However, significant differences in reservoir properties between hydrate-bearing sediments and shallow gas reservoirs cause mutual interference during production, affecting energy recovery performance. The quantitative impact of these differences on co-production remains poorly understood, presenting challenges in evaluating compatibility. In this study, a numerical simulation model for hydrate–shallow gas co-production was developed to systematically examine the effects of reservoir properties on production performance. A compatibility evaluation method was further proposed to assess co-production feasibility under different reservoir conditions. The results indicated that production performance increased with the flow capacity and reserves of the shallow gas layer, as well as the permeability, thickness, and porosity of the hydrate-bearing layer, while exhibiting a parabolic relationship with hydrate saturation. A compatibility index integrating productivity contribution and recovery factor was introduced to quantify compatibility windows of key reservoir parameters. The permeability ratio (ppe) and thickness ratio (pth) exhibited logarithmic growth, with co-production windows defined by ppe > 1.07 and pth > 3.68. In contrast, the saturation ratio (psa) and porosity ratio (ppo) showed parabolic and exponential relationships, with ranges of 2.13 < psa < 5.50 and ppo > 4.09. A comprehensive compatibility evaluation model was developed and validated using a large-scale co-production experimental system, providing a practical tool for evaluating co-production compatibility and contributing to the efficient development of unconventional gas energy resources.

title: Uncovering the interaction between surface water heavy metal pollution and industry-induced pressures in Chinese cities
abstract: Heavy metals in surface waters are major pollutants that pose substantial threats to aquatic ecosystems and public health, with industrial activities representing a primary source. However, the industry-source contribution to heavy metal contamination in surface waters remains insufficiently characterized. This study focuses on five priority heavy metal(loid)s, including arsenic, mercury, cadmium, chromium, and lead, developing an integrated assessment framework to disentangle the relationships between aggregated surface water heavy metal pollution levels and industry-driven pollution pressure. A case study was conducted using data from 336 Chinese cities during 2020–2023. Over the study period, the composite pollution level and industry-driven pollution pressure of heavy metals in surface waters generally declined. Nonetheless, their relationships were complex and spatially heterogeneous, exhibiting a hyperbolic relationship between overall intensity and interaction patterns. To further explore the driving mechanisms, we conducted a machine learning analysis incorporating the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework. The results indicate that industrial sectors such as non-ferrous metal processing, chemical manufacturing, ferrous metal processing, leather tanning, and metal products manufacturing play prominent roles in explaining the heavy metal pollution levels in surface water. Non-industrial pollution sources, hydrological conditions, and inter-city spatial relationships also showed high importance among the model features.

title: Integrative design process for structural optimization: A life cycle assessment-driven approach for sustainable office building design
abstract: This study explores the integration of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) within the sustainable construction of office buildings, focusing on a case study in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with relevance to national sustainability strategies. Using a cradle-to-grave LCA framework for structural components, environmental impacts associated with material production, construction, use, and end-of-life phases were evaluated, while operational energy (B6) was assumed to be identical across all design alternatives and therefore excluded from the comparative LCA model to isolate the environmental impacts of structural system optimization. The functional unit was defined as the provision of 10,400 m2 of gross floor area of an office building over a 60-year service life, and environmental impacts were assessed using the CML life cycle impact assessment method. The baseline design, featuring a conventional reinforced concrete structural system, was optimized through multiple iterations, including the adoption of functionally equivalent and optimized steel structural systems, the use of high-strength steel, and the incorporation of supplementary cementitious materials such as fly ash. The results show that transitioning from reinforced concrete to the optimized steel-based solution reduced Global Warming Potential (GWP) by approximately 26%, alongside notable reductions in Acidification Potential (AP), Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), and non-renewable energy consumption. Prefabrication of steel components contributed to reduced construction-phase waste, while material-efficient structural design and recycled steel content further enhanced environmental performance. The integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM) tools with LCA methodologies proved instrumental in enabling iterative design optimizations and informed decision-making. This research demonstrates the value of integrating LCA in the early design process to achieve meaningful environmental improvements. By addressing key impact categories, such as GWP, AP, and Eutrophication Potential (EP), the study demonstrates how iterative optimization and material innovations can significantly lower a building's environmental footprint. The sensitivity analysis further shows the substantial environmental benefits of optimizing steel usage and increasing recycled content. Adjustments in steel quantities by ±10% and variations in recycled content from 0% to 70% revealed significant fluctuations in GWP, with the highest reductions observed in designs utilizing high-recycled-content steel. These findings offer a replicable LCA-driven design workflow for evaluating and optimizing structural systems in sustainable construction, while acknowledging that quantitative outcomes are case and context specific. The outcomes contribute to advancing sustainable urban development and support global efforts to mitigate climate change through environmentally responsible construction.

title: Manure and sewage dominate nitrate sources in runoff from key headwaters area in China
abstract: Effective riverine nitrogen pollution control necessitates the accurate quantification of nitrate (NO3−) sources. In this study, water quality monitoring, ion analysis, and environmental isotope tracers (δ2H-H2O, δ18O-H2O, δ15N-NO3-, δ18O-NO3-) were coupled with the Bayesian mixing model (MixSIAR) to apportion riverine NO3− contributions from four potential sources in the Dan River Basin, which is the headwater region of China's South-to-North Water Diversion Project. The results revealed that nitrate concentrations fluctuated between 1.20 and 5.51 mg/L, with significant seasonal variation (P < 0.05). Isotopic values ranged from 0.70‰ to 13.53‰ for δ15N-NO3- (mean = 6.70‰) and from −5.02 to 3.25‰ for δ18O-NO3- (mean = −0.40‰). Isotopic data demonstrated that during the wet and dry seasons, NO3− was primarily derived from the conservative mixture of multiple sources, with limited influence from biological removal processes. MixSIAR analysis revealed manure and sewage (M&S) as the primary nitrate source, accounting for 67.6% of the nitrate in the dry season and 46.1% in the wet season. Meanwhile, chemical fertilizer (CF) accounted for 16.1% and 34.8% of the nitrate in the dry and wet season, respectively. Atmospheric precipitation (AP) contributed the least (0.8% in dry season, 1.1% in wet season). Uncertainty and sensitivity analyses revealed relatively high uncertainties for M&S, CF, and soil organic nitrogen (SON) (uncertainty index (UI90) = 0.299–0.534), with the δ15N isotopic signature of M&S exerting the strongest influence on source apportionment results. Overall, the study provides critical insights to help local authorities develop evidence-based pollution control and sustainable water resource strategies for the region.

title: Hybrid fiber-reinforced shield muck-slag-based engineered geopolymer composites: multiscale thermomechanical behavior and sustainability assessment
abstract: Engineered geopolymer composite (EGC) is a sustainable fiber-reinforced cementitious composite, with an excellent cracking-control ability and superior tensile strain capacity. However, the insufficient supply of conventional geopolymer materials and the low melting point of commonly used fibers (i.e. polyvinyl alcohol and polyethylene fibers), restrict the wide engineering application of EGC in high-temperature environments. In this study, a novel hybrid fiber-reinforced shield muck-slag-based engineered geopolymer composite (SS-EGC) was proposed, a series of tests were performed to explore the influence of hybrid fibers on the multiscale thermomechanical behavior of SS-EGC. Results indicate that the synergistic enhancement mechanisms of hybrid fibers for SS-EGC at elevated temperatures can be ascribed to the release of vapor-driven pore pressure through channels left by melted PE fibers and the post-thermal residual strength of refractory fibers. SS-EGC (P1S1) containing 1 vol% PE fibers and 1 vol% steel fibers maintains the highest integrated residual strength index (IRSI) values across the entire temperature range. Meanwhile, SS-EGC (P1S1) exhibits the best heat resistance at 800 °C, its compressive, flexural, and tensile strengths increase by 34.4 %, 28.3 %, and 140.0 %, respectively, compared to the SS-EGC(P2) with 2 vol% PE fibers. In addition, the carbon emission, embodied energy, and cost of SS-EGCs decreases by 19.6 %∼25.0 %, 15.2 %∼27.1 %, and 8.9 %∼21.1 % compared to the M45-ECC.

title: Optimizing CO2 absorption and desorption in water-based nanofluids: Predictive modeling and analysis of multifactor interactions
abstract: Nanofluids have emerged as a promising medium for efficient carbon capture, with water serving as an ideal base fluid due to its sustainability and low cost. However, the performance of water-based nanofluids is governed by multiple operational and material factors, making systematic optimization challenging. Additionally, the interactions between these factors and their influence on carbon dioxide (CO2) absorption and desorption remain inadequately explored, despite being critical for practical system design. This study systematically evaluates and optimizes the CO2 absorption and desorption performance of deionized water (DIW) enhanced by Fe3O4, SiO2, TiO2, and ZnO nanoparticles in a bubble flask. Experiments were conducted following a Box-Behnken Design (BBD), considering nanoparticle concentration, inlet gas flow rate, inlet orifice diameter, and nanoparticle type. Response surface methodology (RSM) was used to develop predictive models and analyze factor interactions. Results demonstrated that interactions among factors significantly influence CO2 absorption and desorption. After optimization, the maximum CO2 absorption amount increased by 54.47%, 42.46%, 35.42%, and 180.89% for Fe3O4-, SiO2-, TiO2-, and ZnO-DIW nanofluids, respectively, compared to pure DIW. Meanwhile, the CO2 desorption efficiency was enhanced by up to 29.42%. The significant enhancement in capture performance, together with nanoparticle recyclability and the low-temperature regeneration capability of water, indicates that this optimization approach not only improves process efficiency but also provides a feasible route to reduce material consumption and regeneration energy. These findings underscore the potential of simple oxide nanofluids to advance environmentally sustainable carbon capture systems, offering guidance for process optimization and scale-up.

title: Completing the puzzle of aged microplastics towards microalgae at environmental concentration: effects of polymer type, size, aging method, and aging duration
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) could substantially impair microalgal growth. However, existing experiences were mostly based on pristine MPs under non-environmental concentrations. Fewer studies considered aged MPs, yet polymer type, aging method, and aging duration were never simultaneously concerned, regardless of MPs concentration. This study firstly investigated the effects of 1000 μg/L 1∼100 μm pristine polyamide (PA), polyethylene (PE), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) on Chlorella sorokiniana, with 10 μm MP displaying minimum impact among all polymers. Afterwards, 10 μm MP were aged via multiple methods (UV, heat, biofilm coating) and durations (30 d, 60 d), and aged PVC displayed most variation both morphologically and infrared spectroscopically. Microalgal impairment by aged MPs comparing with pristine MPs ranked PVC > PA > PE, while 30-d bio-aged MPs enhanced microalgal growth among all polymers. Influence of aging method was UV > heat > biofilm for PVC and PA, with microalgal growth inhibition being respectively up to 19% and 13% comparing with pristine MPs. Influence of aging duration was more observable for PVC, while 60-d UV-aged PA particularly displayed severe photosystem II damage (by 34%). Microalgal growth properties among various PE exposure displayed insignificant differences except for intracellular biochemical composition under 60-d aged PE. Influenced by MPs morphology and microalgal stratified extracellular biochemical profiles, aged and pristine PA as well as PVC displayed limited differences in nutrients removal, while 60-d UV- and bio-aged PE significantly enhanced nutrients removal. This study innovatively unveiled that, impact of environmental concentration aged MPs towards microalgae was most determined by polymer type, then aging method, and least aging duration.

title: Multi-source carbon emission monitoring and certification for carbon-neutral industrial parks
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-source carbon emission monitoring and certification framework for carbon-neutral industrial parks that addresses critical limitations in existing assessment approaches. To overcome boundary elasticity, temporal resolution constraints, and monitoring accuracy challenges that plague current certification standards, we develop a spatially explicit diffusion model based on modified three-dimensional Brownian motion processes governed by Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution principles, incorporating meteorological drift coefficients and establishing probabilistic relationships between emission sources and monitoring points through noncentral chi-squared distributions. The framework deploys a network of cylindrical monitoring zones with real-time carbon concentration measurements, coupled with inverse modeling techniques that simultaneously estimate individual source emission rates through constrained optimization of linear equation systems relating observed concentration differences to predicted molecular arrival patterns. We introduce Daily Carbon Emissions (DCE) as an operational metric enabling continuous rather than annual assessment, incorporating both absolute emission thresholds and carbon density indicators normalized by industrial output value. Implementation of this scheme demonstrates its capability to identify emission rates across multiple sources and quantify total daily emissions, enabling systematic comparison against proposed certification criteria. The integrated approach transforms discrete monitoring observations into continuous emission estimates while providing a comprehensive solution to boundary inconsistency, temporal coarseness, and verification accuracy limitations that currently undermine credible carbon-neutral park certification. This framework enables continuous verification for carbon-neutral park operation, as demonstrated for a combustion based or electricity dominated industrial park under the studied monitoring layout and meteorological conditions.

title: Intergenerational inequality and its mitigation scheme of carbon pricing policy under China's dual carbon goals
abstract: As China advances toward its dual-carbon goals, carbon pricing is recognized as a core policy instrument. However, the intergenerational distribution of its welfare impacts and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear, potentially leading to intergenerational inequity. This study constructs a framework to evaluate the intergenerational effects, including a CGE model that disaggregates the household and labor sectors by age group and a Theil index to quantify inequity. By simulating different carbon pricing policies over the period 2021-2060, we find that intergenerational factors are the primary source of inequality in welfare losses, accounting for more than 90% of the total. Carbon pricing drives intergenerational inequality through both age effects and period effects, with the former indicating greater losses for younger households and the latter indicating heavier burdens on future households. Further, we design an inequality mitigation scheme based on carbon revenue recycling, combining intratemporal redistribution and intertemporal allocation. The simulation using the NDRC scenario demonstrates the effectiveness of our scheme, showing a 49.06% reduction in intergenerational inequality. The findings provide policy insights to alleviate unequal social impacts of carbon reduction and facilitate a just transition.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell systems accelerate decarbonization of urban buildings in China
abstract: Through an active transition to clean energy, China's power sector has achieved substantial emissions reductions. However, owing to regional disparities in geography and energy structure, carbon emissions from the building sector remain high. This study proposes a strategy for the large-scale deployment of distributed solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) systems to accelerate decarbonization in urban buildings. High-carbon energy sources are progressively replaced by natural-gas-fueled SOFC CCHP systems, while enabling their coexistence with low- and zero-carbon energy. A novel provincial planning model focusing on long-term economic feasibility is developed to optimize installed capacity for every deployment period, as well as efficiency and emission upgrade pathway in the subsequent operating period. Comparative analysis with the business-as-usual scenario shows that the deployment schemes in different provinces exhibit distinct regional characteristics. This transitional strategy reduces carbon emissions in the urban building sector across 31 provinces by 25.5%-53.6%. Although the strategy yields a total net benefit of approximately $73.46 billion, it is not suitable for all provinces. Pilot projects should be prioritized in provinces with both high economic returns and significant mitigation potential, such as Xinjiang, Hubei, Chongqing, Sichuan, and Gansu. This work provides an economically viable pathway to accelerate decarbonization in the building sector, supporting China's ambitious carbon neutrality goals.

title: Chemical-free lithium separation from high-salinity brines using model-informed and machine learning-optimized multi-column zwitterionic chromatography
abstract: Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technologies often struggle to produce high-purity lithium salts from high-salinity brines, as current approaches require chemical-based elution, regeneration, and precipitation steps, resulting in significant environmental footprints. A novel salt fractionation approach using carboxybetaine resin, known as zwitterionic chromatography (ZIC), has demonstrated that lithium ions can be separated from divalent cations under high-salinity conditions using only water as eluent, with no regeneration required. To enable continuous and scalable deployment of this approach, we developed a chemical-free Multi-column Zwitterionic Chromatography (MZC) process and its theoretical and process models. To predict and optimize this nontraditional separation system, we introduced a novel anti-Langmuir isotherm, and the isotherm parameters were estimated through a machine learning-driven optimization based on artificial neural network ensembles with numerical feasibility assessment. Using machine learning-driven optimization, the MZC process achieved 98.0% lithium recovery, 99.5 % Li/(Li + Mg + Ca) purity, a 31.3% productivity increase, and a 33% reduction in water use compared to batch operation. The proposed MZC process enables lithium separation at $0.6–1.2 kg−1 Li, with costs dominated by resin manufacturing, while offering lower separation costs and carbon footprint compared with conventional carbonation. Overall, these findings position the MZC process as an effective polishing step within scalable and sustainable lithium production pipelines.

title: Organic amendment-induced enzyme activation regulates microbial nutrient limitation and soil multifunctionality under arsenic stress
abstract: Arsenic (As) pollution severely impairs soil ecological functions, disrupts microbial nutrient cycling and declines soil multifunctionality. Although organic materials aid soil remediation, exogenous organic carbon (Exogenous-OC) alleviates arsenic-induced soil functional degradation remains poorly understood. This 120-day microcosm experiment explored how Exogenous-OC structural complexity regulates soil ecological functions under As stress. Multiple indicators including nutrient availability (DOC, available N and P), activities of C-, N-, and P-acquiring enzymes, microbial biomass (MBC, MBN, MBP), microbial carbon and nitrogen use efficiency (CUE, NUE), and basal respiration. After 120 days, the addition of Exogenous-OC increased the soil multifunctionality index by 3.0–43.8%. In contrast, As addition reduced the index by 7.6–22.3% in oxalate and amylum treatments but increased it by 3.5–18.0% in the glucose and xylan treatments, depending on the OC source. Early soil multifunctionality was mainly governed by MBC, basal respiration and ammonium content, whereas β-1,4-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity, total enzyme activity index (TEI) and organic matter decomposition dominated in the later stage. Moreover, elevated As levels increased microbial carbon limitation after 120 days. However, this effect was mitigated by Exogenous-OC addition, particularly when the carbon had greater structural complexity, as revealed by ecoenzymatic stoichiometry. Notably, glucose, xylan, and carboxymethylcellulose shifted the effect of As on TEI from inhibition to stimulation. This study demonstrates that OC structural complexity strongly modulates microbial nutrient limitation and soil multifunctionality under As stress. Glucose, xylan and carboxymethylcellulose are promising amendments for targeted remediation, offering theoretical support and practical guidance for the ecological restoration of arsenic-contaminated soils.

title: Fine allocation of agricultural water resources at “Region-Grid” coupled-scale based on water rights management
abstract: Confronted with accelerating global water scarcity and intensifying pressures on food security, the pursuit of precise and resource-efficient agricultural water allocation has become a critical condition for sustainable development. This study integrates geographic information techniques supported by remote sensing, multi-objective game theory and a bilevel optimization framework to build a county scale and grid scale agricultural water rights allocation model that operates through a dynamic optimize and verify loop. The model introduces an iterative feedback mechanism that links macro scale and micro scale processes, thereby overcoming the limitations of single scale water rights trading and enabling precise allocation together with dynamic cross scale coordination of agricultural water resources. Applied to the black soil region of Northeast China, the model substantially improves allocation performance during 2005 to 2022 by eliminating excess allocation at the grid scale. It achieves water savings of 23.82%-38.06% of total available water resources, corresponding to 8.55 × 109 to 1.78 × 1010 m3, and increases the number of supply and demand balanced grids by 1.014 × 105 to 2.074 × 105. The analysis further identifies pronounced spatial differences in regional water rights trading. The Sanjiang Plain and the central and western agricultural core zones in Northeast China function as major receiving areas, whereas the humid southeastern zone and the northwestern ecological zone act as primary supplying regions. This configuration produces a new allocation pattern centered on Heilongjiang and eastern Inner Mongolia, where post trade water availability increases by approximately 2.83 × 109 and 1.83 × 109 m3, respectively. The scale coupling approach developed in this study provides a new pathway to resolve structural imbalances in agricultural water resource distribution.

title: Circular economy-oriented catalysis: Waste PET plastics-derived Co-N5 single-atom catalysts for sustainable pollutants removal via non-radical electron transfer
abstract: The growing environmental burden of plastic waste and antibiotic contamination demands scalable solutions. Accordingly, this study valorizes waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into asymmetric Co-N5 single-atom catalysts (Co-SA/NPC) through a multi-step protocol: molten salt carbonization, Zn/Co bimetallic coordination, and N-doped pyrolysis. The resulting catalyst features atomically dispersed Co sites within a hierarchically porous carbon matrix, demonstrating exceptional peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation capability. Specifically, the system achieves 83.2% tetracycline (TC) removal within 20 min with a kobs of 0.096 min−1, while maintaining over 80% efficiency across a broad pH range of 3 to 11 and under high ionic strength conditions, thus establishing a laboratory foundation for future practical water treatment applications. Mechanistic investigation via DFT calculations reveals that the asymmetric Co-N5 configuration induces a 1.34 eV downshift in the d-band center. This electronic modulation optimizes electron transfer kinetics and elongates the O-O bond in PMS. Consistent with this, experimental analyses (electron paramagnetic resonance, electrochemistry) confirm a dominant non-radical electron transfer pathway. This mechanism confers tolerance to radical scavengers and enables selective oxidation of electron-rich contaminants. Furthermore, to demonstrate practical utility, a fabricated Co-SA/NPC/PVDF composite membrane module achieved stable contaminant removal (>72 h continuous operation) when tested in diverse real water matrices. Beyond performance, techno-economic analysis based on a laboratory-scale levelized cost model shows that the total levelized production cost of the as-prepared Co-SA/NPC catalyst is approximately 40,222 $/kg, with electricity consumption identified as the primary cost contributor for catalyst production (accounting for 86.43% of the total cost), a cost structure consistent with the industry benchmark of similar persulfate-based advanced oxidation processes. Concurrently, the toxicity assessment indicates >80% detoxification of TC degradation intermediates, with negligible mutagenicity and bioaccumulation risks identified. Collectively, this work integrates valorization of plastic waste and atomic-scale catalytic engineering, thereby providing an industrially viable blueprint for sustainable environmental remediation under a waste-treats-waste paradigm.

title: Decoding the effect of SO2 on CO2 capture: A combined Ab initio molecular dynamics and spectroscopic approach
abstract: SO2 co-absorption can impair amine-based CO2 capture, but its molecular impact on CO2–amine reaction pathways remain unclear. Here, AIMD-metadynamics, in situ Raman spectroscopy, quantitative 13C NMR, and dynamic desorption measurements were combined to clarify how SO2 perturbs aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA) chemistry. The free-energy surfaces show that SO2 increases the barrier for proton transfer from the zwitterionic intermediate to carbamate, while lowering the reverse carbamate-to-zwitterion barrier, indicating inhibited carbamate formation and reduced carbamate stability. AIMD trajectories further reveal enhanced amine protonation and weakened MEA–CO2 association under SO2 loading. These predictions are validated experimentally: Raman and 13C NMR spectra show decreased MEACOO− signals and increased MEAH+/HCO3− contributions during CO2/SO2 co-absorption. Dynamic desorption tests further demonstrate earlier CO2 release but a lower total desorbed amount after SO2 loading. These results identify SO2-induced proton-transfer inhibition, carbamate destabilization, and amine protonation as key mechanisms governing the loss of CO2 capture–regeneration performance.

title: Sustainable growth capacity and growth alignment: The roles of ESG performance and cost stickiness
abstract: This study examines how environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and cost stickiness are associated with firms’ sustainable growth rate (SGR) by distinguishing between growth capacity and growth alignment. Using an unbalanced panel of non-financial firms listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand from 2014 to 2024, the analysis employs firm fixed-effects models with weighted least squares and autocorrelation adjustments to address heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and dynamic growth behavior. The results show that cost stickiness is positively and significantly associated with SGR across all specifications (β = 0.0028, p < 0.001), suggesting that retaining organizational resources may strengthen long-term growth capacity and resilience. However, cost stickiness is also positively and significantly associated with GAP (β = 0.0469, p < 0.001), indicating that rigid cost structures may reduce operational flexibility and increase growth misalignment. In contrast, ESG performance is negatively and significantly associated with SGR (β = −0.0002, p < 0.001) and does not exhibit a consistent relationship with GAP, suggesting that ESG engagement reallocates resources toward long-term sustainability objectives, particularly environmental investment and compliance commitments rather than aggressive short-term expansion. Economically, a one-standard-deviation increase in cost stickiness is associated with approximately a 0.26 percentage-point increase in SGR, whereas a one-standard-deviation increase in ESG performance corresponds to an approximate 0.28 percentage-point reduction in SGR, relative to a mean SGR of 6.8%. The ESG pillar decomposition further reveals that the environmental dimension primarily drives the negative ESG–SGR relationship, while the social dimension is negatively associated with GAP, suggesting improved growth alignment. Thus, cost retention appears to strengthen sustainable growth capacity while increasing growth misalignment, whereas ESG engagement is associated with more disciplined growth without materially increasing misalignment. These findings contribute to the sustainable growth literature by integrating the resource-based view and stakeholder theory within a dual-dimensional framework of growth capacity and growth alignment. The study highlights that sustainable growth should be evaluated not only in terms of growth magnitude, but also in terms of how closely realized growth aligns with internally sustainable capacity. The findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal, and future research may further explore these relationships using causal identification strategies and cross-country evidence.

title: Exploring necessary and sufficient values in driving consumers’ willingness to pay premiums and purchase intentions for green food
abstract: Amidst myriad sustainable challenges associated with food consumption, green food is gaining prominence. Despite the growing importance, the green food market is at its nascent stage. Understanding consumption value perceptions to effectively stimulate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intention for green food has become ubiquitous in consumer research. Using the well-established theoretical lens-the theory of consumption value, the present study aims to get a comprehensive understanding of multidimensional consumption values impacting WTP and green food choice behaviour. Unlike the existing research, predominantly focused on sufficient value, the study applies a dual-methodological approach that integrates both sufficiency (should have) and necessity (must-have) perspectives. Data were collected from individuals aged 18 and above living in India (n = 340). Structural equation modelling (SEM) was applied to identify the values influencing WTP and purchase intention for green food. By incorporating necessary condition analysis (NCA), the study identifies the necessary values indispensable to achieving the outcome related to WTP and green food purchase intention. Results indicate that all of the proposed consumption values - functional, social, epistemic, health and environmental-significantly influence consumers' WTP from both “sufficiency” and “necessary” perspectives, whereas these value perceptions, except environmental value, are either ‘sufficient’ or ‘necessary' for the choice outcome related to green food purchase intention. The most critical influencing factor is environmental value, as it shows consistent influence on WTP and PI from both perspectives, sufficiency and necessity. Enhancement of environmental values significantly enhances WTP and, thereby, PI for green food. This study adds new depths to the existing understandings of the value propositions of green food to effectively stimulate the value-based positioning of green food products in the Indian context.

title: Labor and education factors' empirical enlightenment on environmental-economic decoupling: Evidence from China
abstract: Labor, as the foundation of economic activities, influences low-carbon economy through factor inputs. China's educational system is undergoing a transition from quantitative expansion to qualitative improvement, shaped by the interplay between policy regulation and social demand. This paper delves into the roles played by labor and education factors in the decoupling of economic growth from CO2 emissions in China from 2000 to 2023. Results show that: (1) The decoupling process of China can be specifically divided into four phases comprising five decoupling statuses: weak decoupling (WD), expansive coupling (EC), weak decoupling (WD), strong decoupling (SD) and weak decoupling (WD). (2) Labor productivity (DLD), educational density (DPK) and educational scale (DK) constitute the primary determinants of decoupling. This underscores a nonlinear relationship where human capital initially exacerbates CO2 emissions during industrialization, yet subsequently fosters cleaner growth through the expansion of skill-intensive sectors. (3) The impact of demographic dividend (DDD) on decoupling has remained at a low level, indicating that quality rather than quantity serves as the high-quality input driving low-carbon economic development. It is imperative to integrate the enhancement of educational quality and workforce capacity building into the core strategy of national low-carbon development. Specifically, optimize the allocation of educational resources and shift fiscal investment from a broad-based approach to a targeted investment model; reduce institutional transaction costs and promote the spatially optimal allocation of highly skilled talents; and drive the digital and intelligent transformation to unleash the ‘multiplier effect’ generated by the synergy between digital technologies and high-quality human capital.

title: Tracking the carbon footprint of the iron and steel industry along the supply chain: From the urban agglomeration level
abstract: The cross-city carbon footprint (CF) transmission and structural evolution of ISI at the urban agglomeration scale are firstly quantified from both production- and consumption-driven perspectives. Using an environmental extended multi-regional input-output (EE-MRIO) model and structural path analysis (SPA), the CF spatial evolution and the supply-chain transmission of ISI at the urban agglomeration level were first traced. From 2012 to 2017, the total CF increased by 29%, accompanied by structural shift from dispersed multi-point pattern to a core-periphery configuration dominated by key production cities such as Anshan, Benxi and Yingkou, indicating the central role in interregional CF transfer. Upstream CF were primarily driven by energy-intensive sectors, especially electricity and heat supply, coking, and coal mining, reflecting a transition from local resource dependence to cross-regional energy-system dependence. Notably in 2017, external energy inputs from the HCM induced about 12.4 MtCO2 to CF growth. Downstream demand expanded from intraregional construction and manufacturing to major regions such as the YRD and BTH. From 2018 to 2023, the driving factors and evolutionary simulation show the improvements in energy intensity and structure partly offset CF, but industrial expansion and final demand remains the dominant driver of CF growth. Without structural adjustment, demand growth will continuously reinforce CF along existing supply chain paths. These results reveal a CF structural mechanism of ISI, provide differentiated implications for urban agglomerations: traditional industrial regions should prioritize reducing upstream energy and material dependence, emerging industrial regions should focus on restructuring and technological upgrading, while consumption-oriented regions should address embodied CF through demand-side measures.

title: Artificial intelligence model-based high-accuracy estimation of global PM2.5 concentrations using gap-filled aerosol optical depth
abstract: Fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter smaller than 2.5 μm (PM2.5) exerts significant impacts on public health and the environment, yet high-precision estimation of global PM2.5 concentrations remains challenging. Aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieved from satellite observations is commonly employed for PM2.5 estimation; however, missing AOD data can lead to substantial biases, thereby necessitating effective gap-filling approaches. In this study, we proposed a two-stage modeling framework to achieve high-precision PM2.5 estimation by filling AOD gaps. During model selection, twelve artificial intelligence (AI) models were compared using ten-fold cross-validation, integrating hourly multi-platform ground-based PM2.5 observations, meteorological variables, and population density data to estimate monthly global PM2.5 concentrations from 2019 to 2021. The results indicated that the Random Forest (RF) model outperformed other models in both AOD gap-filling and PM2.5 estimation, with cross-validation R2 values of 0.835 and 0.851, respectively. The proposed model achieved 100% AOD gap-filling while maintaining high accuracy, with an R2 of 0.721 against AERONET validation. The global PM2.5 estimations exhibited high accuracy, with monthly validation R2 values ranging from 0.75 to 0.90, and spatial-scale validation R2 values between 0.75 and 0.85. From 2019 to 2021, global PM2.5 concentrations showed an overall declining trend, albeit with pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity: PM2.5 in highly urbanized regions was predominantly driven by anthropogenic activities, whereas that in less urbanized regions was largely influenced by natural factors. Among all influencing factors, AOD has the greatest impact on PM2.5, whereas PD has the least impact. The proposed framework provides important insights into the formation mechanisms of PM2.5 and offers substantial value for improving the quality of global PM2.5 datasets.

title: High-performance and recyclable HKUST-1-derived CuxO/Steel electrode for electrocatalytic dechlorination of trichloroacetic acid
abstract: Haloacetic acids (HAAs) are the second most prevalent disinfection by-products (DBPs) in drinking water and significantly contribute to the overall DBPs carcinogenic risk owing to their persistence and established carcinogenic mechanisms. This study focuses on the development of high-efficiency HKUST-1-derived CuxO/Steel(St) composite electrodes for the electrolytic dechlorination of trichloroacetic acid (TCAA), showcasing a novel approach for mitigating such contaminants. The low-temperature carbonization of HKUST-1 yielded CuxO-derived carbon materials, which were used to modify three low-cost electrodes (stainless St, Fe, and Cu), resulting in a novel CuxO/St composite electrode. This electrode exhibited a superior TCAA reduction efficiency due to its optimal material characteristics and electrode configuration. Electrocatalytic performance studies revealed positive correlations between TCAA removal rates and current density/electrode loading, and a negative correlation with solution pH. The CuxO/St-based composite electrode demonstrates efficient dechlorination of TCAA while maintaining high stability over five consecutive cycles. Quenching experiments identified the key active species, atomic H∗ and Cu ions, which facilitated a dual dechlorination pathway through both direct electron transfer and H∗-mediated indirect reduction. The developed HKUST-1-derived CuxO/St composite electrodes provide a recyclable electrocatalytic solution for the end-of-pipe treatment of DBPs in drinking water.

title: Local climatic effects and their spatiotemporal dynamics in subtropical stable forests
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying climate change and anthropogenic activities, forests serve as crucial regulators of local climate. However, their stability and thermal environmental effects face increasing perturbation. Elucidating local forest climatic effects and stability is essential for informing regional forest management and enhancing ecosystem services. Using multi-source remote sensing data, this study systematically investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of stable forests in subtropical China from 2001 to 2023. Furthermore, it quantifies the evolution of their local land surface temperature (LST) regulation across annual mean, seasonal, and diurnal dimensions. The study found the following: 1) Landscape dynamics. Compared to 2000–2010, the bidirectional conversion between forest and cropland increased approximately seven-fold during 2010–2023. The areal proportion of stable forests decreased from 98% to 89%, exhibiting characteristics of fragmentation. 2) Local LST regulation effects. Annually, stable forest coverage was positively correlated with local LST, particularly during the daytime. However, this warming effect attenuated over time. Seasonally, the correlation between stable forest cover and local LST displayed distinct patterns: a predominantly negative association in spring; a persistently positive but attenuated relationship in summer; diurnally divergent responses in autumn; and a synergistic correlation during both day and night in winter. 3) Patch size thresholds. Large patches (>20 km2) exhibited superior thermal regulatory capacity and spatiotemporal stability, offering significant cooling benefits particularly in winter. Conversely, small patches (<10 km2) were susceptible to interference from the surrounding environment, resulting in greater thermal fluctuation. 4) Local LST regulation effects of continuous stable forests. Distinct seasonal differences were observed, primarily characterized by warming during the growing season and cooling during the dormant period.

title: WSF-Bench: A regime-aware benchmarking framework for sustainable monitoring of wood-related production and trade systems
abstract: Short-horizon forecasting is increasingly important for cleaner-production and resilience-oriented monitoring in forest-based value chains, where production capacity, trade flows, and procurement decisions can change rapidly under structural disruption. However, existing forecasting studies in wood-related sectors are mostly application-specific and rarely test whether model rankings remain stable across production and trade tasks, official-data coverage constraints, and pre-shock, shock, and post-shock regimes. This study develops WSF-Bench, a regime-aware benchmarking framework for monthly monitoring of wood-related production and trade systems in Europe. The framework uses Eurostat short-term industrial production indices for wood products and furniture manufacturing, Comext wooden-furniture export and import data, and annual forestry-related anchors to evaluate one-step-ahead forecasts for 12 production countries and 8 trade countries over 2005–2024. Rather than imposing a single artificial country panel, WSF-Bench constructs task-specific balanced panels and compares Seasonal Naïve, ETS, pooled LightGBM, and a focused recurrent challenger under common chronological split rules. Forecast accuracy is evaluated primarily with MASE and interpreted together with execution validity, so that fallback predictions are not treated as equivalent to valid pooled LightGBM runs. The results show a clear production–trade asymmetry. In production, pooled LightGBM provides large gains in stable pre-pandemic windows, but this advantage weakens under later regimes, where ETS remains competitive and some nominal LightGBM wins depend on fallback handling. In trade, pooled LightGBM achieves the lowest error for both exports and imports across all regime windows, and this ranking is not overturned by the recurrent challenger. These findings indicate that, under structural change, the preferred monitoring architecture depends on which segment of the wood value chain is being monitored: strong classical models remain indispensable for production monitoring, whereas pooled LightGBM provides more consistent and execution-valid support for trade monitoring.

title: A novel three-stage modification method for enhancing the performance of rubber concrete: Shear-embedding of nanoparticles, heat treatment, and gel-based surface reconstruction of waste rubber particles
abstract: Utilizing waste rubber particles (WRP) to produce rubber concrete serves as an effective approach for solid waste recycling and enhancing concrete functionality. This material not only consumes a large amount of waste rubber but also imparts excellent toughness, acid and alkali resistance, and shock-absorption properties to concrete, demonstrating significant potential for specialized engineering applications such as hydraulic and military construction. However, the low density, low elastic modulus, surface impurities, and hydrophobicity of WRP lead to particle flotation, stress concentration, and weak interfacial bonding, causing the strength of rubber concrete to drop significantly. Although numerous studies have attempted to address these issues, existing methods often lack systematicity and fail to provide comprehensive and synergistic solutions targeting the multiple causes of mechanical performance degradation in rubber concrete. This paper proposes a novel and systematic three-stage pretreatment method for WRP, which reconstructs the surface structure of WRP. In the first stage, nano-silica is embedded into the internal structure of WRP via supercritical CO2-assisted shearing. The second stage involves high-temperature stirring pretreatment to achieve surface cleaning of WRP. In the third stage, tetraethyl orthosilicate at varying concentrations is used as a precursor to in-situ grow nano-silica on the surface of WRP. The results demonstrate that after the three-stage pretreatment, the density of WRP increases by up to 9.38%, the elastic modulus improves by up to 29.16%, and the water contact angle decreases by a maximum of 25.38%, while the particle flotation during concrete preparation is significantly mitigated. The nano-silica-coated WRP can participate in cement hydration, strengthening the interfacial transition zone. Compared with rubber concrete prepared using untreated WRP, the modified material exhibits significantly enhanced mechanical properties, which first improve and then stabilize with increasing tetraethyl orthosilicate concentration. When WRP pretreated with 8 wt% tetraethyl orthosilicate (relative to WRP mass) is used, the resulting rubber concrete shows a 65.1% increase in 28-day cubic compressive strength and a 75.9% improvement in tensile strength.

title: Recycling of vanadium-extraction tailings by controllable aluminothermic reduction process
abstract: Vanadium-extraction tailings (VET) are solid waste residues generated during the vanadium extraction. In the present study, a controllable aluminothermic reduction strategy was developed to upcycle VET into value-added products via two selectable routes. Specifically, route 1 represents the selective reduction of Fe followed by alkaline purification to obtain Ti-rich slag, whereas route 2 represents the deep reduction of both Fe and Ti to produce FeTi alloy. The feasibility of reducing the Fe- and Ti-bearing components in VET under high-temperature conditions, as well as the reaction priority, was evaluated through thermodynamic analysis. Reduction experiments at different temperatures were carried out, and the reaction mechanism of the aluminothermic reduction process of VET was examined. The optimum process conditions for the selective reduction route and the deep reduction route of VET were studied. The results showed that, at 950 °C for 60 min under Ar protection, tuning the Al ratio enabled selective or deep reduction of VET. In route 1, a Ti-rich slag with 63.27% TiO2 was obtained, with Fe and Ti recoveries of 83.78% and 96.58%, respectively. In route 2, supplementing TiO2 to raise the feed TiO2 content to 60.85% produced a FeTi40B alloy containing 40.9% Ti, with Fe and Ti recoveries of 81.31% and 51.56%, respectively. The lower Ti recovery in route 2 was attributed to thermodynamic constraints and micro-encapsulation within an Al2O3-based matrix. This method provides a tunable and cleaner route for the value-added utilization of VET.

title: Assessment of cost and environmental impacts of single point incremental forming and deep drawing for a range of production volumes
abstract: Sheet metal forming is crucial for producing lightweight, durable components. Single-point incremental forming (SPIF) presents an alternative to deep drawing (DD), but its use remains limited due to insufficient analysis of its pre- and post-forming stages. This study compares the cost of goods sold (COGS) and environmental impacts of SPIF and DD for an asymmetric battery cell casing at various production volumes. It utilizes the manufacturing process design (MPD) and life cycle assessment (LCA) methods to assess all stages needed to produce a part. SPIF shows higher costs and impacts at 1000 parts/year due to longer forming times. Global warming potential (GWP) is similar at 1000–2000 parts/year, after which the impacts of SPIF outweigh those of DD.
