abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide with solar-driven solid oxide electrolysis cell is promising for achieving superior current density and efficiency. In this work, a novel integrated solar-driven autothermal solid oxide electrolysis cell reactor was invented, which comprised a solid oxide electrolysis cell for carbon dioxide electrolysis and a combustion chamber for heating. An autothermal solid oxide electrolysis cell reactor model and a system model were developed and validated with experiments. The energy flows of the entire solar system for endothermal, thermoneutral and exothermal operation modes were visually studied. The preferentially thermoneutral mode exhibited a 2% higher solar-to-carbon monoxide efficiency than the other two modes. Additionally, effects of the temperature, voltage, and ohmic heat recovery effectiveness on the efficiency were investigated parametrically. The results showed that a sufficient heat recovery and an optimal combination of temperature and voltage could significantly improve energy efficiency. With a techno-economic analysis, the total levelized cost for the system was more sensitive to the solid oxide electrolysis cell price than the electricity price, i.e., a 20% reduction in solid oxide electrolysis cell price can reduce the total levelized cost by 13.3%. Having performed a multi-objective optimization on both the efficiency and the cost, an optimal solar-to-carbon monoxide efficiency of 23.7% (assuming a PV efficiency of 32.6%) and cost of 414 $/ton carbon monoxide were achieved. This work presents a unique, efficient, and economically feasible strategy for solar-driven CO2 electroreduction, offering a practical pathway for green carbon monoxide production and supporting global sustainable energy and decarbonization goals.

title: Predicting potential water storage and installed capacity of global riverine barriers
abstract: Artificial riverine barriers associated with water storage and/or hydropower generation provide essential human services while also causing ecological impacts, yet their attribute records remain incomplete worldwide. This data gap limits large-scale assessments of water resources, hydropower development, and riverine ecosystem management. Here, we developed an automated machine learning (AutoML) framework to estimate water storage and installed capacity using georeferenced barrier records, environmental predictors, and a self-compiled global database. Within the repeated H2O AutoML workflow, the stacked ensemble model (SEM) achieved the lowest testing root mean square error (RMSE) and stable performance, with global full-dataset R2 values of 0.84 for water storage and 0.87 for installed capacity. Hydrological predictors, especially upstream watershed area, showed the strongest predictive contributions, followed by geographic and climatic variables. We applied the optimal models to fill missing attribute records in the Lancang-Mekong Basin and validated predictions within the empirically supported prediction window. Sliding-window diagnostics revealed a regression-to-the-mean pattern, with overestimation for the smallest barriers and underestimation for the largest barriers. Thus, the generated estimates are most appropriate for regional-to-global attribute gap filling within the empirically supported prediction range, particularly where direct engineering records are unavailable. Improving predictions for very small and very large barriers will require additional records and engineering, operational, and socioeconomic predictors. Overall, the proposed framework and datasets provide a reproducible basis for large-scale barrier-attribute estimation, preliminary water-resource assessment, infrastructure screening, and sustainable river management.

title: Land transfers, efficiency improves? The land–labor–capital synergy behind grain eco-efficiency gains in China
abstract: Farmland transfer plays a critical role in shaping Grain Production Eco-Efficiency (GPEE). This study evaluates the GPEE across 30 subnational regions from 2009 to 2022 using the Window EBM super-efficiency data envelopment analysis model, incorporating multiple desirable outputs (economic, ecological, and social values) and undesirable outputs such as carbon emissions and grey water footprint. The spatiotemporal evolution patterns and cross-regional disparities in GPEE are analyzed based on these measurements. Employing a benchmark two-way fixed effects model, with spatial and instrumental variable robustness checks, we further investigate the heterogeneous impacts of farmland transfer dimensions on GPEE. Specifically, farmland transfer is examined from three dimensions: Land, referring to land-use-right reallocation intensity; Labor, referring to operator type and organizational restructuring; and Capital, referring to transfer rents and related cost pressures. Several key findings emerge: First, GPEE improved during the study period and cross-regional disparities gradually narrowed, although substantial improvement potential remains in lagging regions. Second, both higher land-use-right reallocation intensity and a higher share of farmland flowing to non-household operators significantly enhance GPEE, with these positive effects being more pronounced in non-main grain-producing areas. Third, transfer rent does not exert an independently positive effect; instead, its contribution to GPEE becomes significant only in the joint configuration of Land, Labor, and Capital, as indicated by the positive three-way interaction term. Collectively, these findings underscore that the eco-efficiency gains from farmland transfer hinge not merely on isolated mechanisms, but on the coordinated configuration of land, labor, and capital elements. This study offers new insights into optimizing farmland transfer strategies for sustainable agricultural development.

title: Design-integrated circularity assessment in early architectural design: Development and application of RhinoCircular
abstract: The transition toward a circular economy in the built environment requires design tools that allow designers to evaluate material circularity in all project stages, where key decisions about material systems and construction strategies are made. However, most existing circularity assessment methods are applied only after design development, limiting their ability to influence architectural decision-making. This paper contributes a design-integrated methodology that enables circularity evaluation at the level of material systems during early architectural design. RhinoCircular (RC) is a computational tool developed for the Rhino3D/Grasshopper environment that integrates circularity indicator calculations directly into architectural workflows. The method links geometric building models with material datasets and user-defined parameters to calculate Circularity Indicators (CI) and visualize material pathways. The framework adapts the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI) methodology for design-stage applications while providing compatibility with current standards. The approach is demonstrated through a case study of the Urban Mining and Recycling (UMAR) Unit in Dübendorf, Switzerland. Results illustrate how design decisions regarding material selection, reuse strategies, and design for disassembly influence building-level circularity performance. By embedding circularity assessment directly into design workflows, RC supports data-informed design decisions and contributes to the operationalization of circular economy principles in architectural practice.

title: Leveraging tourism for rural clean energy transition: Evidence from tourism market participation in Ghana
abstract: This study examines the association between tourism market participation and clean energy consumption among rural households in Ghana, investigating the mediating roles of Internet use and environmental attitudes. Against the backdrop of Ghana's Energy Transition and Investment Plan, which targets net-zero energy-related emissions by 2060 through low-carbon deployment across power, cooking, transport, industry, and oil and gas, this research investigates how tourism can support this national strategy. Using data from a household survey and an Endogenous Treatment Regression (ETR) model to address selection bias, we find that tourism market participation has a significant positive effect on household expenditure for both clean cooking and lighting energy. Mediation analyses reveal that tourism market participation increases Internet use and strengthens pro-environmental attitudes, which, in turn, increases clean energy consumption, confirming complementary information/transaction and normative channels. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the effect is stronger for female, higher-income, and healthier households, though the specific energy priorities (cooking vs. lighting) differ by health status. Robustness tests by IV-Tobit yield similar conclusions. Policywise, coupling tourism development with digital inclusion, environmental-behavior programs, and targeted finance can amplify clean energy consumption and advance SDG 7 in rural settings.

title: Electrokinetic continuous separation of cationic dyes using an anion-exchangeable multiscale porous channel system
abstract: Dyes in wastewater pose serious environmental and health risks, particularly cationic dyes due to their high cellular uptake and toxicity. Although electrokinetic filtration offers a continuous alternative to conventional treatments, its application to cationic contaminants is limited by the lack of commercially adaptable anion-permselective materials capable of repelling positively charged species and by confinement to low-throughput, chip-scale systems. Here, we report a scalable nanoelectrokinetic platform based on ion concentration polarization for continuous cationic dye removal. By integrating custom nanoporous anion-exchange materials with a microscale porous sponge, we create a hierarchically confined structure that ensures high permeability while sustaining a stable ion depletion region. The system achieves up to 99% removal at fluxes exceeding 400 L m−2 h−1, maintains performance over 10 regeneration cycles without observable fouling, and operates stably for over 15 h under hourly backwashing. These results establish a scalable and antifouling electrokinetic strategy for durable cationic dye wastewater treatment.

title: Dynamic payment for ecosystem services standard: Improving the minimum-data approach using ecosystem service flows and threshold effects
abstract: Dynamic standard setting for payment for ecosystem services (PES) is a first-order priority for improving the precision of program design and the sustainability of on-the-ground implementation. This study designs a dynamic PES standard calculation method based on the minimum-data approach (MD), which extends MD logic by redefining the incremental ecosystem service (ES) quantity using ecosystem service flows (ESF), so standards reflect the pathways through which ES are generated, transmitted, and received. It then introduces ES threshold effects to operationalize a diagnosable marginal-return boundary that links ecosystem states and disturbances to the timing, intensity, and adjustment of payments and to instrument choice. Theoretically, a dynamic standard functions as both a compensation schedule and a measure of responsibility, linking net-flow-based identification of payers and recipients with effectiveness diagnosis when marginal returns to cash decline. The proposed framework supports more transparent cross-regional payer and recipient identification, more defensible payment updating, and a clearer basis for shifting from cash-dominant transfers to diversified governance instruments when incentives weaken.

title: Lake-to-pixel algal bloom early warning for Chinese lakes with satellite observations
abstract: Climate change has intensified algal bloom proliferation in Chinese lakes, jeopardizing both water security and ecosystem stability. While various algal bloom early warning models exist, they lack scalable frameworks that integrate regional monitoring with fine-scale risk assessment capabilities. Here, we developed a lake-to-pixel hierarchical framework for algal bloom early warning across 20 major Chinese lakes (>100 km2), coupling with satellite observations. This framework includes a two-stage weighting process that integrates correlation-based feature selection with neural network to quantify lake-specific environmental influences. We systematically evaluated different variable combinations. The model incorporating trophic state information with five core meteorological parameters (Model 4) achieved optimal performance. At a 10% zero-ratio setting, this model reached mean precision of 0.74 and F1 score of 0.73. Lake-specific implementations achieved an accuracy above 0.65 for 80% of study lakes. This performance exceeded combined regional approaches. Correlation-based feature selection results revealed temperature as a primary trigger for bloom formation. Air temperature and lake water surface temperature were selected as predictors for all 20 lakes during model development. Shallow lakes showed higher sensitivity to temperature forcing than deeper systems. Spatial risk assessment across three representative lakes revealed substantial heterogeneity in bloom risk distribution. Coefficient of variation ranged from 0.29 to 0.59. Global Moran's I values spanned 0.45 to 0.85, indicating distinct spatial clustering patterns. Overall, these findings illustrate that effective bloom prediction requires lake-specific driver characterization rather than uniform regional models. The lake-to-pixel framework addresses this requirement by integrating lake-specific driver characterization with pixel-scale risk assessment, enabling targeted management across diverse lake systems.

title: Data-Driven Co-management: synergizing soil quality and crop productivity for sustainable agriculture
abstract: Widely implemented management systems often entail critical trade-offs between maintaining soil quality and achieving high yields, whereas integrating diverse management approaches offers transformative potential. However, how to integrate multiple technologies to balance these dual goals under regional variable climate-soil regimes remains a challenge largely unaddressed due to fragmented data and the lack of scalable methodological frameworks. Herein, we developed a data-driven model framework that generated spatially explicit (1 km × 1 km) best-integrated management practices (SBMPs) by coupling soil and climate factors to improve soil quality and crop productivity. Taking the Yunnan–Guizhou region of southwest China as an example, we found through a soil quality index (SQI) assessment based on 13 soil properties that the average SQI was 0.40 (ranging from 0.20 to 0.49), with 67.58% of cultivated land classified as low-to-medium-yielding croplands (Grades IV and V), primarily constrained by high bulk density, low soil organic matter content, and suboptimal pH. We then evaluated 1024 management combinations using a machine learning model to identify optimal SBMPs that maximize the synergistic improvement of SQI and yield. Optimized SBMPs increased SQI by 9.73% on average (0.21–26.33%) and crop yield by 38.28% (19.96–61.72%) relative to conventional practices. Time-series models demonstrate that SBMPs exert a long-term influence on the synergistic improvement potential of both SQI and crop yield, characterized by an initial rapid increase followed by sustained cumulative effects, and project that by 2040, the average SQI will rise from 0.40 to 0.61, with total grain production reaching 51.38 million tons. These findings highlight the significant co-benefits of SBMPs compared with traditional agricultural practices and provide a scalable pathway for improving SQI and crop productivity.

title: Uncovering the synergistic effects of digital–intelligent transformation and industrial structure upgrading on eco-efficiency:Evidence from 284 Chinese cities
abstract: Under the global low-carbon transition, cities are pivotal sources of energy consumption and pollution emissions, making the coordinated advancement of digital–intelligent transformation and industrial structure upgrading an increasingly urgent pathway for cleaner production to improve urban eco-efficiency, yet its synergistic effects and underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Using panel data for 284 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2023, we assess urban eco-efficiency with the super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model that considering multi-factor inputs, desirable socioeconomic outputs, and undesirable carbon- and pollution-related emissions. The coordination between digital–intelligent transformation and industrial structure upgrading, together with its spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear driving mechanisms, is examined using a modified coupling coordination framework and an interpretable machine-learning approach. The results show that digital–intelligent transformation improved rapidly, while industrial structure upgrading exhibited greater volatility, leading to a steady increase in coordination at the national level, with the mean coordination degree rising from 0.13 in 2011 to 0.22 in 2023 and 25 cities entering coordinated-development stages. Spatially, the coordination network evolved from a sparse coastal-core structure toward a more polycentric and clustered pattern, indicating enhanced cross-regional diffusion and the emergence of inland hubs. Human-capital-related factors, particularly universities, advanced industrial labor, and green total factor productivity, play dominant and complementary roles, with pronounced nonlinear threshold effects. The findings suggest that coordinated digital–intelligent and industrial structure upgrading provides an effective and scalable pathway to enhance urban eco-efficiency, support cleaner production, and reduce spatial disparities in the low-carbon transition.

title: A multi-source traceability and assessment framework for comprehensive environmental impacts in national parks: A case of Wuyishan National Park
abstract: Multi-dimensional environmental impact assessment and governance in national parks are critical pathways for improving ecological environmental quality and maintaining ecosystem stability. This study innovatively constructs the national parks' multi-dimensional environmental impact assessment (NPMEIA) framework by integrating multi-source data and modeling methodologies, aiming to analyze differences in the intensity, typology, and gradient of environmental impacts, along with their internal interaction mechanisms. The results indicate that environmental impacts in national parks are closely associated with tourism activities, production activities, and topographic elevation. A transition from discrete natural disturbances to clustered socio-economic interferences occurs as elevation decreases. The hierarchical and seasonal characteristics of tourist activities' impacts, the multi-type and gradient features of tourism enterprises' impacts, and the settlement and core–periphery effects of community settlements' impacts, exhibit a spatially nested and superimposed pattern, collectively shaping spatial polarization and infrastructure lock-in effects of environmental impacts. Overall, moderate environmental impacts dominate, with tourism activity as the primary pressure source. This study has established a multi-dimensional environmental impact assessment framework applicable to tourist-oriented national parks. It expands the study on the environmental impact of national parks to the analysis of the formation mechanism of environmental impacts driven by multiple stakeholders' behaviors, forming a chain analysis paradigm of “impact source identification—mechanism quantification—spatial trade-off assessment”. This provides a new analytical perspective and decision support for the spatial governance and environmental management of tourist-oriented national parks in developing countries.

title: How does carbon emissions trading affect renewable electricity consumption? City-level evidence and mechanisms from China
abstract: Carbon emissions trading (CET) is widely regarded as a key market-based policy, the intention of which is to reduce carbon emissions and guide the transition toward low-carbon energy systems. However, the extent to which CET affects renewable electricity consumption, and through which mechanisms, remains insufficiently explored. This study employs city-level panel data from 2005 to 2022 to analyse the impact of China's CET policy on renewable electricity consumption (REC); the underlying mechanisms and heterogeneous effects are also examined. The results reveal that China's CET policy significantly increases REC, with an average increase of 0.205 million tons of standard coal equivalent (approximately 43% of the sample mean). A further mechanism analysis indicates that the CET policy facilitates REC by stimulating renewable energy-related technological innovation and reallocating capital through tighter financing constraints for high-carbon firms and more favourable financing conditions for renewable energy firms. China's CET also raises energy costs, while adjusting the pattern of interprovincial renewable electricity flows. The effects of China's CET policy vary across regional conditions. Specifically, there are larger impacts in contexts characterized by lower carbon emission intensity, higher marketization levels, stronger local government capacity, the deployment of ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission infrastructure, relatively scarce renewable energy endowments and more active carbon markets. Further disaggregation by renewable electricity type shows that hydropower contributes most in absolute terms to the aggregate increase in REC. Meanwhile, solar power exhibits a larger percentage increase when normalized by its average consumption. In light of these findings, this study puts forward context-specific policy implications to promote renewable energy adoption.

title: Digital-twin driven thermo-mechanical coupled modeling for temperature-prediction in reheating furnaces
abstract: Accurate furnace-roof temperature prediction is critical for energy-efficient reheating-furnace operation, refractory safety assessment, and cleaner production. However, nonlinear radiation–conduction–convection coupling, multilayer refractory interfaces, heterogeneous boundary conditions, and real-time inference requirements remain difficult to reconcile using conventional numerical or purely data-driven models. This study proposes a multidimensional digital-twin framework for thermo-mechanical coupled modelling of a 2250 walking-beam reheating furnace. The framework couples geometric, thermal, and stress surrogate models with an application-specific Generalized Physics-Informed Neural Network (G-PINN). G-PINN integrates finite-element shape-function-based derivative evaluation, nodal degree-of-freedom assignment for prescribed Dirichlet boundaries, and Gaussian-quadrature-based energy-functional loss within a unified furnace-roof modelling pipeline. Under synchronized quasi-steady validation, the fixed trained model independently maps each time-indexed boundary-condition vector to its corresponding temperature field without online retraining. In Heating Zone II, G-PINN achieves an MAE of 2.3–3.2 °C and an R2 of 0.920–0.942, reducing RMSE by approximately 40–50% relative to the steady-state FEM reference. The full framework obtains a mean MAE of 2.75 °C, satisfies prescribed Dirichlet boundaries exactly, and completes end-to-end temperature prediction, gradient evaluation, stress computation, and von Mises post-processing within 8.2 ms. FEM-referenced stress assessment indicates that operational stresses remain below 13 MPa in structurally active regions, while first-order heat-loss sensitivity analysis suggests a 0.64–2.18% uncertainty-bounded potential reduction in redundant heat loss. These results support real-time quasi-steady furnace-roof temperature prediction, stress assessment, and cleaner-operation decision support, while transient thermal inertia remains outside the present validation scope.

title: Designing carbon allowance allocation for blast furnace decarbonization in China: Impacts on retirement and low-carbon transition
abstract: The steel industry is one of the critical sectors for global emissions mitigation. In recent years, China has established the China Carbon Emission Trade Exchange (CCETE). Under its current operating rules, the incentive effect for promoting emission reduction in the steel sector still has room for improvement. In this study, the CCETE was optimized, and a facility-level blast furnace carbon emission database was established. Different carbon allowance allocation schemes and profit thresholds were then defined to simulate CO2 mitigation effects through 2050. The results show that the current scheme allocates a total of approximately 29.2 Gt of carbon allowances. Compliance costs induced by allowance surpluses or deficits range from −11 to 9 CNY/tHM. The optimized schemes reduce total allowances by 1.8-2.7 Gt. Carbon reductions driven by the phase-out of high-emission blast furnaces under the optimized schemes are estimated at 0.7-9.8 Gt. Blast furnace-intensive regions contribute 47%-49% of the total mitigation. Different allocation schemes are projected to eliminate 313-868 Mt of high-emission capacity. They also accelerate low-carbon retrofitting of high-emission blast furnaces. The mitigation effect of low-carbon technologies is influenced by the allowance allocation scheme, with total reductions ranging from 0.3 to 12.4 Gt. These findings can support the design of carbon allowance allocation schemes for China's steel industry and other sectors, thereby facilitating deep decarbonization across society.

title: Spatial grid constraints, financing risk, and social-cost-adjusted generation costs in Vietnam's power transition
abstract: This study estimates private and social-cost-adjusted levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) for Vietnam's power-generation technologies under grid constraints and financing risk. Project-finance and operating inputs from 112 commissioned utility-scale projects during 2019–2024 are combined with a four-zone representation of the national grid. Uncertainty is propagated through copula-based Monte Carlo simulation that preserves correlated shocks in CAPEX, real WACC, and capacity factors. The estimates apply to the commissioned operating cohort and should not be read as population averages for the full licensed pipeline. National median private LCOE is 60.8 USD/MWh for solar PV and 79.6 USD/MWh for onshore wind under design utilization, while South-zone curtailment raises the corresponding solar and wind estimates to 76.9 and 134.4 USD/MWh, respectively. A supplementary fixed-effects IV-GMM check provides predictive elasticities for scenario analysis, not structural causal estimates. Social-cost-adjusted LCOE is computed by adding monetized lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions under alternative social-cost-of-carbon scenarios. At SCC ≥75 USD/tCO2e, coal and LNG lose their private-cost advantage relative to renewables in the social-cost ranking. The results suggest that financial de-risking, targeted grid and flexibility investment, and carbon pricing should be evaluated jointly because their effects depend on the same financing, utilization, and emissions margins.

title: Cross-scale environmental drivers jointly shape waterbird diversity in coastal aquaculture ponds
abstract: As natural wetlands continue to decline, aquaculture ponds have been proposed as potential supplementary habitats for waterbirds, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the combined effects of landscape configuration and local conditions. Previous studies have mainly focused on single spatial scales, with limited exploration of the relative importance and interactions of cross-scale factors. To bridge the gap between mechanistic understanding and conservation practice, this study applied a Joint Species Distribution Model to investigate how landscape- and local-scale environmental conditions jointly shape waterbird diversity in aquaculture ponds. Among the 1474 surveyed aquaculture ponds, 43.01% were used by waterbirds. Waterbird abundance and species richness peaked during the migration season. Most ponds (84.51%) supported low waterbird species richness, with no more than two species recorded per pond. Vegetated pond dikes and greater distances from marsh wetlands were key factors associated with higher waterbird diversity, while local-scale variables showed greater explanatory power than landscape-scale variables. In addition, the threatened Saunders's Gull (Larus saundersi) showed a clear preference for seawater ponds, highlighting the importance of specific pond types for species of conservation concern. These findings demonstrate that biodiversity-friendly pond management can enhance the conservation value of artificial wetlands while supporting the sustainable development of coastal aquaculture systems.

title: Moderate climate targets promote more resilient Food-Water-Emission nexus
abstract: Achieving climate targets may reshape interactions within the Food–Water–Emission (FWE) nexus. However, it remains unclear how different climate mitigation pathways influence coordination and stability within the FWE nexus. To address this gap, this study develops a FWE nexus framework evaluating how mitigation policies reshape the FWE nexus from both synergistic interaction and structural resilience perspectives. Agricultural systems in 14 major food production regions are simulated under three climate mitigation scenarios by using the Global Change Assessment Model (GCAM). Spearman correlation analysis quantifies synergies and trade-offs among key sub-indicators, while nexus resilience is assessed by examining the stability of these interactions under climate policy constraints. The results reveal that: 1) climate mitigation impacts are highly regional and uneven; 2) climate policies effectively alleviate water stress and foster synergies in FWE nexus, but non-CO2 emissions continue to exhibit trade-offs with food and water systems, underscoring conflict between food production and climate mitigation; 3) nexus resilience shows strong regional divergence, with some regions maintaining more stable and synergistic coordination under stringent mitigation, while others exhibit declining resilience or deteriorating coordination; 4) moderate climate target like well-below 2°C, promotes more balanced improvements in nexus coordination while maintaining nexus resilience under climate change. Compared with previous studies, this study quantifies how climate mitigation reshapes FWE subsystem interactions and nexus resilience at the global scale, highlighting that moderate mitigation coupled with differentiated policy strategies is crucial for achieving sustainable global agriculture.

title: Designing of an IoT-based sustainable intelligent logistics in healthcare
abstract: Pharmaceutical logistics is responsible for delivering vital medical supplies and medicines from warehouses to pharmacies or healthcare institutions across geographically diverse regions. This study aims to create an efficient route planning, delivery schedule, and optimal charging policy based on Internet of Things (IoT) technologies for the electric vehicle (EV) fleet in the last-mile delivery of the pharmaceutical industry. Therefore, the last-mile sustainable logistics problem is mathematically formulated as a mixed integer programming (MIP). The problem aims to deliver multiple medicines to various geographically scattered locations within the desired time windows with a minimum delay by considering their characteristics and urgencies. Hence, we first employ a spherical fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (SF-AHP) method to obtain the weights and calculate the urgency of medicines. We then develop a heuristic solution approach, namely an adaptive general variable neighborhood search (AGVNS) with several successful integrated mechanisms to solve newly generated problem instances. The comparison of green and conventional diesel fleets, as well as their cost and environmental impacts, are also examined through scenario analyses. Extensive computational results show that the proposed hybrid heuristic approach performs quite well on newly generated instances. Furthermore, the results provide insight into the charging technology usage of the EV fleet and indicate that it has advantages over the conventional fleet in terms of cost and environmental impact when using the presented IoT-based fuzzy weighted optimization framework.

title: Revealing gradient differences and nonlinear characteristics of extreme dry-hot events on ecosystem carbon sinks in urban agglomerations
abstract: Extreme dry-hot events (EDHE), as a typical compound extreme climate event, are profoundly reshaping the patterns of ecosystem carbon sinks (ESC). However, existing studies predominantly focus on single spatial scales, lacking a systematic understanding of the differentiated and nonlinear characteristics of urban-rural gradient ESC of urban clusters. Therefore, this study examines China's five major urban agglomerations, uses net ecosystem productivity (NEP) to characterize ESC and treats urban, urban-rural fringe, and rural areas as gradient units. By integrating multisource remote sensing data, meteorological and hydrological records, and XGBoost with geographically weighted machine learning models, we systematically analyse the spatiotemporal patterns, nonlinear characteristics, and multiscale heterogeneity of EDHE impacts on ESC from 2001 to 2023. The results show that: firstly, the annual average net ecosystem productivity (NEP) in rural areas fluctuated from 178.92 g C/m2 in 2001 to 275.66 g C/m2 in 2023. The annual average NEP in the urban-rural ringe was 146.27 g C/m2. The minimum NEP in urban areas was −61.92 g C/m2. EDHE generally presents a trend of increasing frequency, increasing intensity, and expanding influence range, and the regional differences are significant. Among them, the annual average value of EDHE fluctuates, with average duration (AD) ranging from 1.24 to 2.73 days, duration days (ND) ranging from 2.29 to 10.36 days, and average severity (AS) ranging from 0.96 to 1.09. Secondly, the estimated effect of AD on rural ESC was 1.55 times that of urban and 1.35 times that of urban-rural fringe. The estimated effect of ND on urban-rural fringe and rural was about 1.67 times that of urban. Thirdly, the critical thresholds of EDHE were significantly different on the urban-rural gradient, among which AD and ND showed "urban-rural fringe > urban > rural," and the average severity (AS) showed the characteristics of increasing with the urban-rural gradient. Fourthly, at multiple response scales, EDHE generally presents a single-threshold response law of "promoting first and then suppressing". Among them, the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration is the most sensitive, the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei urban agglomeration responds significantly to the AS, and the Yangtze River Basin shows strong ecological resilience. At the city scale, the response spatial heterogeneity of urban in mid-latitudes is prominent. This study provides a scientific basis for formulating differentiated climate adaptation and land-space governance strategies under the constraints of carbon neutrality goals.

title: From intelligence to sustainability: AI's role in green innovation in Chinese manufacturing
abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping manufacturing firms, yet its impact on corporate green innovation (GI) remains contested. Drawing on the neo-Schumpeterian framework, this study conceptualizes the AI-GI relationship as evolving from installation to deployment phases. Using a panel of 2602 Chinese listed manufacturing firms from 2010 to 2023, this study examines the impact of AI adoption on corporate green innovation within a two-way fixed-effects framework. The results reveal a U-shaped relationship: AI adoption initially suppresses but subsequently promotes firms' green innovation. Mechanism analyses further confirm that absorptive capacity and human capital serve as two key transmission channels. Media attention, as an external governance mechanism, shifts the inflection point leftward and accelerates firms' transition from inhibition to promotion. The U-shaped relationship is stronger among firms in eastern and western regions, firms operating in less competitive industries, and high-technology firms. These findings help reconcile conflicting evidence on AI's green innovation effects and advance the neo-Schumpeterian understanding of how general-purpose technologies shape firms' long-term sustainability trajectories.

title: A novel process for the treatment of low-grade laterite with the aim to a higher yield of valuable metals
abstract: Nickel sulfate is a key raw material for producing the precursors used in the lithium-ion battery cathodes, and it is primarily sourced from lateritic ores. However, conventional laterite processing routes, including high-temperature smelting and high-pressure acid leaching (HPAL), remain costly and operationally demanding, particularly for low-grade saprolitic resources. In this study, a low-temperature carbothermic reduction pretreatment was introduced before oxygen-pressure acid leaching to modify the mineral phases of saprolite-type laterite. The characterization showed that reduction roasting disrupted the silicate framework and generated a more reactive intermediate. Subsequent oxygen-pressure acid leaching enabled selective dissolution of Ni and Co, while Fe was retained in the residue as hematite. Under the optimized conditions, Ni and Co leaching efficiencies reached 97.2% and 95.4%, respectively, with the Fe leaching efficiency limited to 1.8%. This route improves metal leaching rate while lowering acid demand and leaching temperature. A preliminary technoeconomic analysis also suggested a modest relative economic advantage over HPAL.

title: Three-stage temperature-ramping stirred-tank bioleaching enhances copper recovery from chalcopyrite by mitigating surface passivation
abstract: Bioleaching of chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) is often limited by slow dissolution kinetics and the formation of surface passivation layers, which restrict the efficient utilization of low-grade copper sulfide resources. In this study, a three-stage continuous temperature-ramping stirred-tank bioleaching system was developed to enhance copper recovery by coupling temperature-gradient regulation with spatially separated reaction stages. The system consisted of a 35 ± 2°C stage for microbial establishment and mineral-surface activation, a 45 ± 2°C stage for Fe2+/Fe3+ cycling and intermediate-phase transformation, and a 55 ± 2°C stage for thermally enhanced ferric/acid deep leaching. Single-tank stirred bioleaching at constant temperatures of 35 ± 2°C, 45 ± 2°C, and 55 ± 2°C was conducted as the control. The copper leaching efficiencies in the single-tank systems at 35 ± 2°C, 45 ± 2°C, and 55 ± 2°C were 41 ± 0.2%, 46 ± 0.2%, and 54 ± 0.2%, respectively, whereas the three-stage temperature-ramping system achieved a maximum copper leaching efficiency of 86 ± 0.1% within 6 days. This corresponds to a 32 percentage-point improvement compared with the single-tank 55 ± 2°C system. The stage-specific pH/ORP evolution and copper dissolution behavior indicated that the staged system promoted a sequential leaching pathway from initial surface activation to intermediate-phase transformation and finally to deep copper dissolution. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses further showed that the staged process reduced the localized accumulation of passivation products, including elemental sulfur, Cu5FeS4 (bornite), and jarosite, thereby maintaining the reactivity of the chalcopyrite surface. These results demonstrate that continuous temperature-ramping stirred-tank bioleaching can improve chalcopyrite dissolution by integrating microbial activation, iron cycling, and thermally enhanced ferric/acid leaching in sequential reactors. This strategy provides a promising route for improving the biohydrometallurgical recovery of copper from refractory sulfide concentrates and offers a useful basis for further process optimization and scale-up.

title: Fast infrared co-pyrolysis of biomass and typical medical waste for clean fuel production: Insights into heating rate effects, dechlorination, and PSO-ANN modeling
abstract: This study investigates the synergetic mechanisms of infrared-assisted co-pyrolysis of corn stover (CS) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) for high-quality fuel production. An infrared heating reactor was employed to optimize product distribution through Particle Swarm Optimization-Artificial Neural Network (PSO-ANN) modeling. The maximum oil yield of 36.24% was achieved at 700 °C, yielding a bio-oil enriched with aromatic hydrocarbons and gasoline-range fractions. Mechanistic analysis reveals that HCl released from PVC dehydrochlorination interacts with alkali metals in CS ash, generating metal chlorides. Supported by existing literature, these chlorides can act as Lewis acid sites to catalyze biomass deoxygenation and aromatization. Furthermore, XPS characterization confirms a dramatic shift in chlorine speciation, with inorganic chlorine in the char increasing from 1% to 64%, effectively mitigating the formation of toxic organochlorine precursors. These findings demonstrate that infrared co-pyrolysis facilitates tunable chlorine migration and enhanced oil quality, providing a sustainable strategy for integrated lignocellulosic and plastic waste valorization.

title: Rhamnolipid@Ag bio-nanofluids for enhanced oil recovery: Multiscale experimental and molecular mechanism elucidation
abstract: With the increasing global energy demand and the progressive depletion of conventional oil reservoirs, enhanced oil recovery (EOR) has become an important strategy for sustainable petroleum development. Compared with conventional chemical flooding systems, green bio-nanofluids have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent interfacial regulation capability, environmental compatibility, and stability. In this study, a rhamnolipid-stabilized silver bio-nanofluid (RLa@Ag BNFs) was successfully synthesized using Pseudomonas aeruginosa fermentation products through a green biosynthetic strategy. The interfacial regulation behavior and EOR mechanisms of the bio-nanofluid were systematically investigated through experiments, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and quantum chemical calculations. The results demonstrated that RLa@Ag BNFs exhibited excellent dispersion stability under high salinity, elevated temperature, and wide pH conditions, while significantly reducing oil–water interfacial tension, altering rock wettability, and enhancing crude oil emulsification and dispersion. The spontaneous imbibition recovery reached up to 44%, while the final recovery in core flooding experiments reached 64.7–66.3%, which was significantly higher than those of the individual RLa and Ag NPs systems, indicating excellent residual oil mobilization capability. MD simulations revealed that RLa molecules preferentially adsorb and directionally arrange at the oil–water interface, whereas Ag nanoparticles contribute to stabilizing the interfacial adsorption layer and enhancing interfacial assembly behavior. Interaction energy analysis and quantum chemical calculations further demonstrated that van der Waals interactions, amphiphilic interfacial adsorption, and structural disjoining pressure collectively promoted oil-film detachment and residual oil migration, thereby revealing the intrinsic molecular mechanisms underlying the enhanced oil displacement performance of the RLa@Ag bio-nanofluid. This study developed a green bio-nanofluid system with high oil displacement efficiency, excellent environmental compatibility, and favorable stability. The findings provide new theoretical insights and technical support for the application of biosurfactant–metal nanomaterials in chemical EOR, and also offer valuable references for green and low-carbon petroleum development.

title: Trace volatile sulfur compounds in biogases from sanitary landfill site: emission level, toxicity, and mitigation measure
abstract: Trace volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs) accumulated under high-density polyethylene (HDPE) films in closed landfills pose severe risks to both environmental and human health. A sanitary landfill in northern China was investigated to elucidate the occurrence characteristics and health risks of VSCs. A clear spatial distribution and a distinct seasonal pattern were observed, with VSC concentrations significantly higher in summer than in autumn, driven by temperature and humidity. Hydrogen sulfide (H2S), methyl mercaptan (MeSH) and dimethyl disulfide (DMDS) were identified as the dominant VSCs, with concentrations ranging from 0 to 35.40 mg/m3. Comprehensive toxicological assessments, including cell viability, inflammatory responses, and transcriptomic profiling, revealed that DMDS exhibited pronounced cytotoxicity. Long-term exposure to DMDS may lead to chronic respiratory inflammation, accompanied by an elevated risk of cancer. The constructed upflow biofilter stably and efficiently removed VSCs, achieving H2S removal rates of up to 82.76%, MeSH removal nearing 100%, and an average removal rate of over 70% for the refractory DMDS. After treatment with the biofilter, the cytotoxicity and inflammation-related risks induced by DMDS were reduced. Microbial community analysis showed that Bacillus, Paenibacillus, Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter were the core functional genera involved in VSC degradation. This study elucidates the emission characteristics and toxicity risks of trace VSCs in closed landfills. Furthermore, the developed upflow biofilter technology presents an engineerable and scalable technical solution for controlling VSCs pollution beneath HDPE films.

title: Thermodynamic, environmental, and economic analysis of a solar-driven dimethyl ether production system integrating biomass staged-gasification and vanadium chloride cycle
abstract: To reduce fossil fuel dependence and promote clean energy, this study develops a novel dimethyl ether (DME) production system integrating solar-driven biomass staged-gasification with the vanadium-chlorine cycle, further incorporating the reverse water gas shift, DME synthesis, and an organic Rankine cycle. The staged-gasification effectively removes tar and enhances syngas quality, while the vanadium-chlorine cycle supplies additional hydrogen to optimize the H2/CO ratio for DME synthesis. System performance is evaluated through energy, exergy, economic, and environmental analyses, and a comparison with reference systems. The sensitivity analysis of key operating parameters is performed. The results show that the energy efficiency of the system is 59.20%. The DME yield reaches 678.05 kg/t-bio, exceeding that of conventional gasification-based DME synthesis systems. The exergy efficiency is 63.47%. Economic analysis shows a net present value of 8.18 M$, a dynamic payback period of 6.31 years, and a levelized cost of 0.78 $/kg for DME. Environmentally, the internal CO2 recycling strategy substantially reduces direct emissions. Sensitivity analysis identifies the recommended operating parameters. The DME price has a strong effect on the economic viability of the system. This study offers a novel pathway for biomass-DME production.

title: Development of a distributive Canadian energy-water-carbon nexus system planning model for accomplishing net-zero carbon emissions by 2050
abstract: Energy, water, and carbon are tightly interconnected, and balancing these linkages is critical for Canada's low-carbon transition and sustainable development. A major challenge lies in capturing the socio-economic and environmental (SEE) impacts of green alternatives while addressing regional disparities, interregional interactions, and uncertainties within the energy-water-carbon nexus system. Accordingly, this study develops a Canadian Energy-Water-Carbon Nexus (CEWCN) planning model to support strategic decision-making for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. Built on a mixed-integer interval chance-constrained programming framework, the model addresses multidimensional uncertainties and regional heterogeneity under multi-risk conditions. Scenario analysis and Sustainable Development Goals assessments are further integrated to examine how climate policies, technological innovation, socio-economic development, and interregional cooperation affect system sustainability. Results indicate that by 2050, renewable energy will supply over 90% of Canada's electricity, primarily from hydropower, wind, and solar. Natural gas with carbon capture and storage (CCS) and small modular reactors are expected to replace conventional natural gas and nuclear. Water consumption will remain highest in Quebec, British Columbia, and Ontario due to hydropower, biomass, and nuclear generation, though total withdrawals will decline by [16–20]% compared to 2030. National emissions are expected to fall sharply, reaching net-zero by 2050 through large-scale renewable deployment and negative emission technologies such as bioenergy with CCS. Moreover, regional carbon cooperation can redistribute abatement efforts, easing mitigation burdens in high-emission provinces and lowering system costs. Overall, the findings offer strategic insights for shaping resilient, low-carbon transition pathways and managing multidimensional risks in the CEWCN system.

title: Conservation practices reverse soil degradation in subtropical intensive agriculture: From policy measures to farmers’ behavioral decision-making
abstract: Amid growing concerns over food security, addressing soil degradation caused by excessive intensification is imperative for sustainable agriculture and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. The primary challenges in current research include the lack of effective interdisciplinary data support and limited research on the integration of agricultural technology development and application with farmers' behavioral decision-making mechanisms. It is precisely this gap that has impeded the accurate identification of target groups for technology promotion and undermined farmers' willingness to respond to policy measures. To address this, this study aims to effectively uncover the mechanisms underlying farmers' adoption of prevention and control technologies, and evaluate the impact of policy-driven prevention and control behaviors on the actual degree of soil degradation, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for the design and implementation of relevant policies in intensive agriculture. This study innovatively employed one-to-one matched soil experimental data and questionnaire data, and utilized partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to empirically analyze the constructed comprehensive analysis framework. This framework encompasses policy measures, farmers' behavioral decisions, and soil indicators such as soil pH and organic carbon. The results indicate that the adoption of technologies such as soil testing and formula fertilization is the key factor in reversing degradation. Farmers' technology adoption behavior mainly depends on the benefits of adopting technology, external constraints, and their perceived difficulty of adoption. Prevention and control policies affect soil degradation by influencing farmers’ attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. The combination of different policy measures has a synergistic effect, mitigating the limitations of single-measure approaches. These findings highlight the critical need to provide farmers with customized training and precise guidance tailored to the actual severity of soil degradation. Furthermore, establishing a targeted subsidy system for degradation control, alongside promoting farmland transfer and enhancing public awareness, is imperative, particularly for smallholder farmers in developing countries.

title: Climate velocity outpaces static building-code assumptions in China
abstract: Climate velocity is rapidly shifting bioclimatic zones, creating a mismatch between evolving exposures and static, location-based building codes. Codes anchored in outdated meteorological baselines and infrequent revisions risk undermining building-energy performance, envelope-design suitability, and climate-zone relevance, particularly in regions undergoing rapid climatic transition. High-resolution climate records (2006–2023) combined with commercial-building envelope-load diagnostics were used to track spatial and seasonal realignment of thermal loads. Subtropical conditions advanced northward by up to ∼7° latitude (∼700 km), moving warm-temperate cities toward subtropical regimes and reshaping seasonal risk profiles. In warm-temperate zones, winter heating burdens declined, while temperate and sub-temperate regions experienced intensified summer cooling and latent loads, signaling a broader transition from winter-dominant to multi-season stress. These heterogeneous patterns reveal potential mismatch hotspots where rapid climatic shifts may place increasing pressure on existing climate classifications, design assumptions, and envelope-performance requirements. The findings provide diagnostic evidence to inform dynamic climate zoning, routine reassessment of climatic design parameters, and prioritization of envelope-performance reviews in regions undergoing rapid climate reclassification. This China-wide analysis supports more timely and spatially targeted adaptation planning, while further work is needed to translate these diagnostics into operational code benchmarks, multi-archetype building simulations, and retrofit decision frameworks.

title: Fabrication and forming mechanism of polychlorotrifluoroethylene membranes with tunable pore architectures for efficient oil-water separation
abstract: The efficient purification and recycling of oily waste rely heavily on membrane separation technology, where fluoropolymer-based membranes hold particular promise. This study demonstrated a sacrificial template strategy to fabricate polychlorotrifluoroethylene (PCTFE) membranes with tunable pore architectures. This approach leveraged a solvent-assisted process to incorporate a fluoroelastomer (FR) template, forming PCTFE/FR sintered films. By controlling FR content, sintered films with co-continuous morphology can be obtained, which subsequently enabled the formation of penetrating pore structure. A key finding was the linear correlation between sintering time and phase size, which provides precision in pore structure control, complemented by the use of smaller PCTFE particles for refining the phase morphology. The optimized membranes integrated strong hydrophobicity/oleophilicity, robust mechanical properties, excellent creep resistance, and efficient oil/water separation performance. They delivered high separation fluxes (15351 L/(m2 h) for oil/water mixtures; 7649 L/(m2 h) for emulsions) with superior efficiency (>99%) and oil purity (>99.95 wt%). Moreover, they retained excellent performance after 15 operational cycles or 7-day immersion in various corrosive media (including DMF, DMAc, 1M H2SO4, 1M NaOH and concentrated HNO3), with no significant performances degradation observed. These findings underscore the great potential of the developed membranes for treating and recycling oily wastes, even under harsh environmental conditions.

title: Recirculating aquaculture can reconcile food supply and afforestation in Great Britain
abstract: The afforestation planned in the UK as part of the pathway towards carbon neutrality by 2050 will reduce food availability. The impact, as we show, would be larger on livestock-based animal protein production. We quantify both this overlooked side-effect and its attenuation through domestic production of animal protein using high-productivity recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). We assessed both supply and demand for king prawns with detailed data from Great Britain (GB). RAS-based supply was simulated, at 5 km level, with positive mathematical programming and agricultural censuses, financial and labour wages data. Demand was estimated with demand-system econometrics from supermarket purchase and imports data. The two sides of the British farm-gate king prawn market were integrated into a partial equilibrium model. Results revealed that the economic viability of RAS was sufficient to offset nearly 80% of the protein loss induced by afforestation on well under 1% of the land area converted into woodland. Capital grants subsidising the initial investment in RAS further attenuated the drop in food and expanded avoided GHG emissions, proportionally to the grant's value. Notwithstanding, a moderate grant value, covering the investment in one RAS facility, was the most cost-effective option.

title: Household economic capacity and renewable energy capacity: Cross-country dynamic evidence from the United States, China, and Germany
abstract: Households play an increasingly important role in the global energy transition, yet the effect of household-level economic capacity on renewable energy (RE) consumption remains underexplored. This study examines the dynamic impact of household economic capacity (HIPC) on renewable energy use in the United States, China, and Germany from 2013 to 2022—three economies representing market-oriented, state-led, and policy-driven transition models. Using two-way fixed effects, Mean Group (MG), Dynamic Mean Group (DMG), Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CMG), and panel ARDL methods, the analysis accounts for cross-sectional dependence, heterogeneity, and persistence in energy consumption. The results confirm a stable long-run cointegrating relationship between HIPC and renewable energy consumption. Long-run elasticities indicate that a 1% increase in household economic capacity leads to roughly a 1.6% rise in renewable energy use, underscoring the central role of household purchasing power in energy adoption. In contrast, short-run effects are weak and statistically insignificant due to strong persistence in renewable energy consumption (lag coefficient ≈ 0.90). Overall, the findings show that household economic strength is a key driver of renewable energy uptake, and effective policy must prioritize long-term affordability, targeted incentives, and structural support for household-level adoption.

title: Novel hydrometallurgy separation and recovery of silicon/silver from waste crystalline silicon solar cells
abstract: The recycling of waste crystalline silicon solar cells presents a dual challenge: recovering high-value metal silver with high efficiency while also recovering high-purity silicon. This study introduces an innovative selective etching approach to achieve preferential etching of metal gates and silicon substrates at sintering points. Leveraging the characteristics of screen printing and sintering—high defect density and variations in silicon nitride coverage at sintering points—the initial stage employs silicate accumulation combined with mask etching to remove the silicon dioxide film, exposing fresh silicon surfaces and enabling a continuous self-catalyzing cycle for silicon-silver separation. Subsequent metal-catalyzed chemical etching (MCCE) enables precise etching at the sintering junctions, achieving solid-state separation of silver grids from silicon substrates without apparent damage. The catalytic corrosion method yields superior results compared to the initial thermal alkali stripping process. The overall silver recovery ratio is doubled, while the total weight loss of the silicon cell is only half of that in the previous method, simultaneously ensuring the recovery of high-purity silicon. Through response surface methodology (RSM) optimization and combined etching processes, the final silver grid can be almost completely stripped, with a minimum silver recovery efficiency of 93% in the optimal process range, silicon purity reaching 99.99%. The silicon substrate maintaining structural integrity and can be used as raw material for purification into high-purity silicon. Overall, this method highlights the potential for sustainable, low-damage silicon-silver separation, promoting the development of a circular economy in renewable energy technologies.

title: Thermodynamic-kinetic integrated analysis of heat exchanger scaling and control techniques: A case study from a potash processing plant in northwest China
abstract: The inaccurate prediction of scale formation in heat exchangers, particularly under conditions of saline-alkaline water, has been relatively overlooked. This study systematically investigates both severe scaling and technique for effective control in heat exchangers at a potash processing plant in northwest China using two types of complex water supplies: Mixi surface water (MX) and Hongliu groundwater (HL). By integrating classical nucleation theory with PHREEQC (a geochemical modeling software) simulations, a comprehensive thermodynamic–kinetic analytical framework was developed to explore the effects of supersaturation state on precipitation and surface deposition. The feasibility of non-chemical scaling mitigation strategies for MX and HL was further evaluated. The findings indicate that CaCO3 scaling is jointly governed by supersaturation evolution and kinetic constraints. Although MX and HL have similar saturation indices (SI) and initial nucleation rates under the same conditions, pronounced differences in the final precipitation and surface deposition amounts were observed due to variations in the ionic composition. Grey relational analysis (GRA) further revealed that HCO3− has a stronger impact than Ca2+ on both precipitation and deposition in real saline-alkaline water. This underscores the critical roles of carbonate species derived from bicarbonate in controlling post-nucleation crystal growth and deposition behavior. Based on these findings, an ultrasonic descaling strategy was proposed. Under representative operating conditions (80 °C, pH = 8.5), ultrasonic treatment reduced wall deposition by approximately 70 %. During 73 days of industrial operation, the retrofitted heat exchanger maintained an inlet-outlet temperature difference (ΔT) above 50 °C for approximately 57 % of the operating time, more than twice the 26 % observed for the non-retrofitted unit. Overall, this study provides both a theoretical framework and a practical solution for mitigating mineral scaling in heat exchangers operating with saline-alkaline industrial waters.

title: Synergistic SF6 abatement and desalination brine valorization for valuable resource recovery: Techno-economic and environmental assessment
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) is a potent greenhouse gas with a long atmospheric lifetime, necessitating effective treatment despite substitution efforts. While thermal incineration is widely utilized, most systems overlook by-product recovery. Desalination brine discharge presents environmental challenges but offers potential as a chemical resource. In this study, four process configurations for treating 250 kg h−1 of SF6 were designed, simulated, and evaluated from economic and environmental perspectives. The baseline configuration (Case 1) based on single-stage scrubbing resulted in the highest levelized cost of SF6 destruction (LCOD) of 13.95 $ kg−1. In contrast, multistage systems (Cases 2–4) enabled selective capture and by-product recovery. Case 2 significantly reduced the LCOD to 3.25 $ kg−1 SF6 but remained dependent on purchased neutralizers. Cases 3 and 4 utilized desalination brine-derived reagents. While sensitive to fluctuations in by-product revenues, electricity costs, and taxation, they achieved negative LCOD values (−2.32 and −4.01 $ kg−1 SF6). Heat-exchange network (HEN) integration in Case 4 improved performance, reducing heating and cooling demands by 56.15% and 63.74%, respectively. Life cycle assessments showed that all configurations achieved >99.8% reductions in global warming potential relative to direct SF6 emissions (26,241.7 kg CO2 eq kg−1 SF6). With a 35% share of renewable energy, the HEN-optimized system achieved net-negative emissions while maintaining economic viability. These results demonstrate the benefits of integrated waste management for simultaneous emission reduction and economic gain, supporting the development of coupled SF6–brine treatment systems.

title: A multi-task learning model integrating physical property databases and multidimensional descriptors for predicting thermophysical properties of type III and V deep eutectic solvents and assisting screening
abstract: Organic solvents are widely recognized as environmental hazards due to their high pollution potential. In contrast, deep eutectic solvents (DESs), particularly Type III and V DESs, are promising green alternatives. Their structural tunability enables numerous possible combinations, which makes identifying DESs that meet industrial requirements challenging and necessitates systematic screening. In practice, industrial performance depends on multiple interrelated physical properties rather than a single parameter. Accordingly, we constructed a DES property database containing 10,537 data points for melting point, viscosity, density, and surface tension. Using this database and multidimensional descriptors, we developed a multi-task learning (MTL) model to predict these properties simultaneously. The model achieved high predictive accuracy, with R2 values of 0.980 for melting point, 0.971 for viscosity, 0.993 for density, and 0.963 for surface tension. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis quantified feature–property relationships, improving model interpretability and supporting DES molecular design. The MTL model was further applied to screen DESs based on composite physical properties and identify promising solvent combinations. Overall, the model enables accurate property prediction and efficient screening of DESs for industrial applications.

title: Evaluation of the carbon intensity of biomethane under Brazil's National Biofuel Policy (RenovaBio): impacts of system boundary variations
abstract: Biomethane from organic waste is a strategic option for decarbonizing energy systems and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions. However, system-boundary definition strongly affects carbon-intensity accounting and economic incentives under Brazil's National Biofuel Policy (RenovaBio). This study compares four emission-allocation approaches for biomethane certification, considering different boundaries and avoided-emission assumptions. The results showed that carbon intensity varied strongly according to the boundary approach adopted. Scenario 1 produced the highest impacts, especially for swine manure systems and MSW landfills, with average carbon intensities of 114.45 ± 90.57 and 597.22 ± 52.01 g CO2eq MJ−1, respectively, mainly due to fugitive methane emissions. Scenario 2 resulted in more stable environmental-efficiency scores, with an average NEEA of 74.46 g CO2eq MJ−1, by assigning waste-treatment burdens to the waste-generating activity. In contrast, Scenarios 3 and 3.1 substantially increased the mitigation potential of anaerobic-digestion routes, with NEEA values ranging from 256.77 to 893.39 g CO2eq MJ−1 under avoided-emission accounting. For landfill biomethane, Scenario 3 remained unfavorable, with an average carbon intensity of 404.12 ± 192.23 g CO2eq MJ−1, whereas Scenario 3.1 improved performance to 2.10 ± 51.84 g CO2eq MJ−1 and a positive average NEEA of 84.60 ± 51.84 g CO2eq MJ−1. Overall, Scenario 2 emerges as the most balanced short-term approach for the current RenovaCalc framework, offering regulatory predictability while correctly attributing environmental responsibility to the waste-generating activity. In the longer term, Scenario 3.1 represents a promising methodological improvement, provided that robust rules for baseline definition, monitoring, verification, additionality, double-counting prevention, leakage control, and market stability are established. Aligning RenovaCalc with international carbon-intensity-based fuel policies could strengthen the competitiveness of biomethane in Brazil and support its integration into national decarbonization strategies.

title: Social acceptance of solar fuels in Germany: Evidence from a national survey on artificial photosynthesis-derived isobutanol
abstract: Innovative energy carriers, such as solar fuels, are essential for decarbonizing hard-to-abate mobility sectors and industrial processes. Social acceptance is pivotal for the implementation and scaling of solar fuels, influencing policy feasibility and market uptake. However, empirical evidence remains scarce. Conducting an online survey (N = 830), we assess acceptance levels and perceptions in Germany of a hybrid artificial photosynthesis pathway that produces solar isobutanol. Attitudes are moderately favorable, with moderate sociopolitical support and market acceptance, while community acceptance is neutral. Support for solar fuels is highest in freight transport, followed by public transport and aviation, while acceptance is lowest for private car use and industrial solvent applications. Perceived risks are associated with uncertainties for consumers, production, local implementation, and poor sustainability performance. Perceived benefits include fossil fuel substitution, sustainability, local implementation potential, consumer convenience, and consumer sustainability feelings. While the perceived benefit of fossil fuel substitution, interest in solar fuels and their perceived relevance are the main drivers of sociopolitical and market acceptance, community acceptance is limited by risks relating to production and local implementation, among other factors. Acceptance of genetically modified bacteria for fuel production emerges as a key predictor of acceptance across all dimensions. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the acceptance of solar fuel and emphasize the importance of multidimensional acceptance modeling. Based on this understanding of acceptance levels, drivers and barriers, socially accepted pathways in the production, deployment and roll-out of solar fuels can be identified and effective communication strategies developed.

title: Development of a multi-criteria indicator for product life cycle decision-making
abstract: Maximizing product value and resource efficiency has been widely regarded as a key objective throughout the product life cycle, supported by improved product designs, informed manufacturing decisions, and regenerative approaches. Despite the importance of effectively evaluating how well these objectives are achieved, there remains a lack of indicators that comprehensively characterize multi-dimensional performance at the level of individual product life cycle stages. To address this gap, this study develops a novel indicator, the Life Cycle Performance Indicator (LCPI). This indicator combines multiple dimensions (economic efficiency, pollutant release level, and workforce stability) into a single integrated measure using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to evaluate performance at each life cycle stage. The proposed indicator is applied in a case study of a diesel engine remanufactured into an LNG engine at the end of a use cycle to identify underperforming life cycle stages and support targeted improvement efforts. Scenario-based analysis under the evaluated data variation scenarios indicates that the LCPI could potentially be improved by up to 60%, demonstrating substantial opportunities for enhancing life cycle performance. This study provides decision-makers with insights to identify underperforming life cycle stages, prioritize improvement efforts, and understand trade-offs among multiple performance dimensions.

title: Timber carbon stocks in China's forest production-consumption nexus: Interregional redistribution and implications for sustainable forest resources
abstract: As China advances its national agenda for carbon neutrality and ecological civilization, understanding how timber use affects forest carbon sinks across regions is increasingly important for forest policy and governance. Using data from 31 provincial-level administrative regions from 2002 to 2020, this study constructs a timber carbon stock satellite matrix and applies a multi-regional input-output model to quantify the interregional redistribution of timber carbon stocks within China. It constructs a Forestry Carbon Sink Pressure Index to identify whether the consumption of timber-related carbon is compatible with provincial sink capacity. The results show that interprovincial timber carbon stocks expanded markedly over time and underwent a clear north-to-south reconfiguration shaped by forestry policies and industrial restructuring. Central and eastern provinces increasingly became major inflow regions. The FCSPI shows that the Bohai Rim and most of the central and eastern provinces face pressure as demand exceeds local sink capacity, while the southwestern and northeastern regions act as net ecological suppliers. This study links the constraints on forest ecosystem goods and services with the interregional trade flow of timber, provides suggestions for a reasonable coordination of timber use and carbon-sink management in China, and addresses China's climate and forestry strategy.

title: Recycling neutralization sludge into hydrotalcite for source control of acid mine drainage: From waste to value-added passivation material
abstract: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) from sulfide oxidation in mining waste rocks poses long-term environmental threats. The traditional chemical neutralization treatment method consumes a large amount of reagents and produces alkaline sludge. In this study, two hydrotalcite-like materials, Layered Double Hydroxides (LDHs) and modified LDHs (AS-LDHs), were synthesized utilizing sludge from the AMD neutralization process. They were applied to in-situ control of mining waste rocks to achieve source reduction of AMD. Results showed that acid-extractable and reducible metal fractions (Cd, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn) in waste rocks were the main pollution sources. With 1% addition and uniform mixing, LDHs exhibited optimal performance. After 28 days of reaction, the barrier rates of LDHs for Cd, Cu, Fe, Mn, and Zn reached 73.08%, 62.77%, 64.59%, 85.56%, and 58.48%, respectively, and the dominant mechanism was the adsorption of LDHs. LDHs also achieved 50% acidity barrier efficiency, enhancing the self-neutralization of carbonate minerals in waste rocks. Quantitative analysis attributed acidity removal to LDHs (46.5%), MgCO3 (43.5%), and CaCO3 (10.0%), raising waste rock pH 4.5 to 6.88 and classifying it as general industrial solid waste. This study demonstrates a sustainable “waste-treats-waste” closed-loop strategy, providing a cost-effective paradigm for at-source AMD control and solid waste resource utilization.

title: A process-informed framework for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for PPCPs by integrating machine learning and vadose-zone transport modeling
abstract: Conventional approaches for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) often simplify subsurface transport and neglect attenuation in the vadose zone, which can lead to overly conservative screening outcomes. To support more realistic and proportionate groundwater protection, this study developed a process-informed framework that integrates machine learning with HYDRUS-based vadose zone transport modeling. A global dataset covering 24 PPCPs and 584 soil and sediment samples was first used to predict the solid–liquid partition coefficient (Kd), and the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model showed the best performance. The results indicated that molecular properties and soil organic carbon were the major controls on partitioning. Vadose zone attenuation factors (AF) were then quantified by coupling HYDRUS simulations with machine learning, and the best performing model achieved an R2 of 0.90. Depth, KOC, and precipitation were identified as the dominant controls on attenuation, accounting for 76% of the total contribution. By integrating Kd, AF, and groundwater dilution factor (DF), groundwater-protective soil thresholds were derived for trimethoprim, nalidixic acid, and niflumic acid, with HC5 values of 0.06, 0.80, and 41.12 mg kg−1, respectively. Compared with conventional EPA-style calculations, explicitly accounting for vadose-zone attenuation materially changed the threshold estimates. These findings demonstrate that explicit representation of vadose-zone processes improves the realism of soil screening and supports science-based site management and groundwater risk control for emerging contaminants.

title: Enhancing early-stage hardening of autoclaved aerated concrete with high-dosage pisha sandstone through composite alkali activation and kinetic modeling
abstract: To mitigate the shortage of siliceous raw materials in autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC), this study explores the potential of replacing quartz sand with locally available, low-grade pisha sandstone (PS). Due to its high montmorillonite content, PS tends to absorb water and expand, significantly delaying the hardening of AAC green bodies. However, previous studies have mainly focused on the hydration behavior or low-replacement utilization of PS, while the hardening mechanism and process optimization of high-dosage PS-AAC systems remain poorly understood. To address this challenge, a composite alkali-activation approach using NaOH and Na2SiO3 is adopted. This method aims to sequentially activate reactive phases in both PS and fly ash (FA), thereby facilitating the co-development of mixed gel and expediting early-stage structural hardening. Under optimal composite activation conditions (1 wt% NaOH + 1 wt% Na2SiO3, 40 °C pouring temperature, and 60 °C pre-curing temperature), the PS content reaches 90-100 wt%, with t500 controlled between 1.9 h and 3.2 h, with no structural collapse observed. After autoclaving, the resulting AAC blocks exhibit compressive strength >3.9 MPa and dry density <541 kg m−3, meeting GB/T 11968-2020 A3.5/B05 grade requirements. Additionally, A mathematical hardening kinetic model is developed to predict the time required to achieve cutting hardness (t500). The model demonstrates high fitting accuracy (R2 = 0.95, MAE = 0.18 h, RMSE = 0.22 h) and can guide industrial process optimization. These findings demonstrate that mechanism-guided composite activation, combined with predictive modelling, enables industrially feasible, high-dosage PS utilization in AAC production.

title: Research on quality–energy–emission collaborative optimization framework for CO2-enhanced basic oxygen furnace steelmaking process
abstract: Complex interdependent relationships exist among smelting quality, energy consumption, and pollutant emissions in basic oxygen furnace steelmaking, making traditional processes unable to achieve multi-objective optimization.
