abstract: Against the background of the global low-carbon energy transition, long-distance power delivery from large-scale wind and photovoltaic bases to remote load centers has become an important pathway for improving renewable energy utilization. However, hydro–wind–solar–pumped storage complementary systems for ultra-high-voltage direct current power delivery still face two key challenges. The first is the difficulty of formulating stable transmission profiles. The second is the mismatch between generation-side capacity and grid-side transmission capacity. To address these challenges, this study develops a source–grid coordinated optimization framework with transmission corridor capacity treated as a rigid engineering constraint. Photovoltaic installed capacity and transmission corridor capacity are defined as the core decision variables. A multi-timescale dual-layer dispatch model is incorporated into the proposed framework. The CRITIC–GLDS multicriteria decision-making method is further integrated to identify the economically optimal scheme within the technical feasibility domain. A clean energy base in the upper reaches of the Yellow River, comprising 2320 MW of hydropower capacity and 4200 MW of pumped storage capacity, is selected as the case study. The results show that stable transmission profiles can be generated under a 95% export plan fulfillment rate constraint. The economically optimal matching relationship between transmission corridor capacity and photovoltaic installed capacity is approximately 1:2.5. The preferred configuration is identified as 18 GW photovoltaic capacity and 8 GW transmission corridor capacity. Under this configuration, the levelized cost of electricity is 256.62 RMB/MWh, the transmission corridor utilization rate is 61.78%, and the renewable energy utilization rate is 91.11%. This study provides decision support for the long-distance transmission of large-scale renewable energy bases and source–grid coordinated planning.

title: Coal to carbon quantum dots via Fenton’s reagent
abstract: Industrial scale-up of top-down synthesized carbon quantum dots (CQDs) is currently bottlenecked by the environmental hazards of harsh acidic oxidizers and a total lack of predictive process and techno-economic frameworks. This work addressis this gap by presenting a novel and environmentally friendly process for converting Wyoming Powder River Basin coal into carbon quantum dots (CQDs) by leveraging naturally occurring iron to drive an in situ Fenton reaction. XPS and FTIR characterization confirmed the formation of highly functionalized CQDs, validating the molecular models used in our kinetic analysis. A two-step sequential mechanism was developed and validated using a global basin-hopping optimization algorithm. Operating at an optimized 8-hour/90 °C regime, the process maximizes CQD yield (43%) while ensuring high photoluminescent quality. Process modeling and techno-economic analysis were performed on a potential coal-to-CQD process at pilot, intermediate, and industrial-scale production rates to establish the first commercial viability benchmarks for this green technology. It was found that pilot and intermediate-scale facilities could be built with limited capital investment. CQDs produced in these plants could be sold at prices lower than CQDs currently available commercially. Capital and operating costs at the industrial scale are significantly higher than those at the intermediate scale, but the staged deployment scheme presented here minimizes investment risk while allowing CQDs to move from niche uses as laboratory reagents into bulk commodity applications. Ultimately, these findings establish a scalable blueprint for repurposing fossil fuel resources into sustainable, high-value carbon materials.

title: Smart municipal waste management with source segregation and recovery optimization
abstract: This study develops an integrated optimization framework for designing a source-segregated municipal solid waste management network. A mixed-integer linear programming model is proposed to determine the optimal configuration of collection stations, assignment of waste generation points, installation of smart monitoring systems, and allocation of waste flows to treatment and recycling facilities within a multi-echelon municipal logistics network. The model minimizes total system cost while satisfying capacity, budget, and recycling constraints. A numerical experiment based on a representative case study of Tabuk city, Saudi Arabia, is conducted to demonstrate the applicability of the model. The results show that the optimal network opens three collection stations and allocates waste efficiently across treatment facilities, achieving a diversion rate of approximately 72% from landfill. The comparative and sensitivity analyses indicate that integrating source segregation with monitoring-enabled operational coordination, optimized infrastructure utilization, and resource recovery can significantly improve economic performance while reducing landfill dependency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that segregation participation, recycling revenue, and disposal cost are key drivers of system performance. Increased participation in source segregation leads to higher recovery rates and improved economic outcomes, while higher recycling revenues and disposal costs promote waste diversion from landfill. The findings highlight the importance of coordinated planning, economic incentives, operational coordination, and public participation in developing sustainable waste management systems. The proposed framework provides a practical decision-support tool for municipalities seeking to transition toward circular economy practices and improve resource efficiency in urban waste management.

title: Linking anisotropic chloride transport to annualised carbon intensity: A durability-informed sustainability assessment of 3D-printed UHPC
abstract: Chloride-induced corrosion significantly shortens the service life of reinforced concrete infrastructure and increases life-cycle carbon emissions through repeated maintenance interventions. In 3D-printed ultra-high-performance concrete (3DP-UHPC), build-induced anisotropy alters chloride transport behaviour, yet its long-term durability and sustainability implications remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a durability-informed comparative framework that links anisotropic chloride transport to maintenance-normalised carbon implications in 3DP-UHPC. Long-term immersion experiments were conducted to obtain depth-resolved chloride profiles for different build orientations. A time-dependent diffusion model incorporating surface chloride accumulation kinetics was used to identify orientation-dependent transport parameters, which were subsequently translated into corrosion-initiation-based service life and a parameterised carbon amplification formulation over a 50-year design horizon. Results show that corrosion initiation under a 20 mm cover condition is governed primarily by surface accumulation kinetics rather than instantaneous diffusion intensity. A stable durability hierarchy (3D-Z > MC ≈ 3D-Y > 3D-X) persists under realistic variations in corrosion threshold and cover depth. Within the adopted comparative framework, and using 3D-X as the reference condition, orientation optimisation yields up to a 38% relative reduction in the parameterised annualised carbon-intensity indicator without altering material composition or structural geometry. The findings indicate that build orientation can function as a non-material sustainability lever by regulating durability-controlled maintenance demand in chloride-exposed infrastructure.

title: Selective suppression of key hazardous asphalt VOCs by MIL-101: From risk screening to mechanistic insights
abstract: As a fundamental component of the global transportation network, asphalt pavements inevitably release complex volatile organic compounds (VOCs) throughout their entire life cycle, posing persistent threat to ecosystems and human health while hindering cleaner production in sector. Owing to the extreme compositional complexity of asphalt VOC emissions, existing studies have largely focused on total emission control, often overlooking the dominant contribution of a small number of highly toxic components to overall risk. To address this limitation, this study proposes a risk-oriented selective suppression strategy. A multidimensional evaluation framework was established to identify key hazardous components, prioritizing isoprene, p-xylene, dimethyl disulfide, and methyl vinyl ketone as primary control targets. Subsequently, a low-emission asphalt material was developed using the high-surface-area metal–organic framework MIL-101 as a modifier to enable targeted adsorption of these characteristic pollutants. Multiscale molecular simulations reveal that the abundant unsaturated metal sites and unique pore environment of MIL-101 generate deep free-energy wells and pronounced diffusion barriers, endowing the material with higher adsorption affinity and stronger intracrystalline retention for selective capture of the target pollutants. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) experiments further validate the simulation predictions, demonstrating that MIL-101 significantly reduces emissions of the risk-dominant pollutants, Overall, this work integrates risk-oriented screening with mechanism-guided material design, providing an effective pathway for cleaner production of low-emission asphalt materials and the development of more sustainable transportation infrastructure.

title: Entrepreneurial leadership and resource management efficiency as necessary conditions for SME sustainability: A moderated mediation analysis of digital readiness and financial inclusion
abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are central to employment and value creation, yet pressures from sustainability transition expose endemic financing frictions and uneven digital readiness (DR), particularly in emerging markets. This study examines how SME capabilities viz.: entrepreneurial leadership (EL) and resource management efficiency (RME) associate with triple-bottom-line (TBL) sustainability across economic (ECOS), environmental (ENVS), and social (SOCS) pillars, whether firm-level financial inclusion (FI) statistically mediates capability-to-TBL associations, and whether DR conditions these associations. Using survey data from 429 Malaysian SMEs, we apply a sequential analytics design: Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modelling to test direct, mediated, and interaction effects; followed by Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) and Importance-Performance Map Analysis in the bid to identify bottlenecks and practical priorities. Results show that EL is positively associated with ECOS, ENVS, and SOCS; whereas RME is strongly positively associated with ECOS and ENVS but is not significant for SOCS. FI is TBL pillar-asymmetric: it bolsters ENVS and SOCS but exhibits a negative effect on ECOS, and the mediated effects through FI mirror the pattern. DR significantly strengthens the FI to TBL pathways, yet conditional indirect effects indicate that high DR can neutralise FI's economic drag without reliably improving ECOS. NCA sharpens the conclusion: high ECOS is unattainable without RME, while high ENVS and SOCS require EL-RME-FI jointly; DR is not a robust necessity condition. Practically, SMEs should tighten efficiency routines first, mobilise leadership for adoption, channel finance through verified upgrading milestones and invest in DR only where it improves monitoring, traceability and compliance.

title: Lignin-based aqueous epoxy emulsified asphalt: Preparation, performance characterization, and sustainable applications
abstract: Under the macro-background of the global carbon neutrality strategy driving the transition of transportation infrastructure construction materials toward “bio-based green production,” the frequent occurrence of distresses such as potholes during pavement maintenance poses extreme challenges to the overall performance of repair materials. In this context, the use of aqueous epoxy emulsified asphalt is regarded as an effective maintenance solution. However, its large-scale application still faces practical challenges, particularly regarding the carbon footprint associated with petroleum dependence and the fluctuating economic costs of synthetic raw materials. As a renewable resource with abundant reserves and excellent affinity with asphalt, lignin provides a strategic opportunity to break this deadlock. This study developed a “green preparation method for lignin-based aqueous epoxy emulsified asphalt.” Lignin-based aqueous epoxy resin was synthesized through simple chemical grafting of lignin with glycerol triglycidyl ether (GTE). Furthermore, the thermodynamic spontaneity and chemical bonding process of the grafting reaction were demonstrated at the molecular level using electrostatic potential (ESP) calculations and FTIR spectroscopy. Performance evaluations indicate that the construction of a three-dimensional cross-linking network within the system, when the lignin-based aqueous epoxy content reaches 12 wt%, is the physical essence behind the enhancement of macro-performance. Moreover, rheological and interfacial thermodynamic analyses confirmed that this network significantly reinforces the high-temperature rheological properties and adhesion performance of the system. At the mixture level, performance tests including high-temperature rutting, low-temperature bending, and moisture stability confirmed that the proposed material maintains robust high-temperature stability while balancing low-temperature crack resistance and resistance to hydrothermal damage. Furthermore, a simplified life cycle assessment (LCA) indicates that the incorporation of lignin-based aqueous epoxy provides a potential reduction of approximately 10% in global warming potential compared to conventional bisphenol A-based systems. This research not only achieves the transformation of industrial byproducts into green pavement toughening agents but also provides a scientific basis and technical pathway for the development of high-performance, cost-effective, and eco-friendly road maintenance materials.

title: Multiphase flow and hydrate plugging during liquid CO2 injection into water-saturated sediments: Experimental and CFD insights for geological CO2 storage
abstract: Reliable CO2 injection into geological formations is essential for large-scale carbon storage, yet hydrate formation during injection can significantly impair injectivity and flow stability. This study investigated the multiphase flow behavior of liquid CO2 injected into water-saturated sediments using a combination of laboratory experiments and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Liquid CO2 injection experiments were conducted in a horizontal one-dimensional reactor designed to simulate water-saturated sediment. Under hydrate-stable conditions at 274.15 K and 4.0 MPa, CO2 hydrate formation caused severe flow restriction and eventual plugging within the reactor, whereas stable CO2 transport was maintained at 286.15 K without persistent plugging. The addition of monoethylene glycol as a thermodynamic hydrate inhibitor mitigated hydrate formation; however, its apparent inhibition performance deviated from closed-system expectations. CO2 discharge resumed after approximately 4 h at 4.6 mol% MEG, whereas the pressure increased to approximately 10 MPa after about 8 h at 8.8 mol% MEG, owing to dynamic water/inhibitor redistribution during liquid CO2 injection. CFD simulations complemented the experiments by resolving internal phase distributions and multiphase transport processes that cannot be directly observed experimentally. The simulations revealed the formation of an inlet-side dry-out region, hydrate accumulation in the mid-section, and preferential flow pathways that control CO2 migration and injectivity. These results provide mechanistic insight into hydrate-induced flow restriction during liquid CO2 injection and highlight important considerations for hydrate mitigation in geological CO2 storage systems.

title: RSM–ANN-driven process engineering for greener polyphenol extraction from kodo millet husk and their translational efficacy against acute lung inflammation in both in vitro and in vivo models
abstract: This study establishes the first systematic translation of kodo millet husk into a biologically validated functional resource via extraction of polyphenol-rich fractions with demonstrated anti-inflammatory efficacy. A data-driven framework integrating simplex-lattice solvent optimization, response surface methodology–artificial neural network (RSM–ANN) hybrid modeling, and kinetic–thermodynamic analysis was employed to enhance extraction efficiency and functional performance, followed by validation in cellular systems and a preclinical acute respiratory distress syndrome model. Under optimized conditions, the extract yielded 35.41 μmol FAE g−1 total phenolics, 3.05 μmol QE g−1 flavonoids, and 98.34% ABTS inhibition, corresponding to ∼66% and ∼9% improvements, respectively. ANN exhibited superior capability in resolving nonlinear process interactions. Kinetic and thermodynamic assessments indicated a diffusion-controlled, endothermic, and entropy-driven process with low activation energy (11.57 kJ mol−1) and negative ΔG°, confirming spontaneity. HPLC-DAD-ESI-MS/MS profiling identified fifteen phenolics, dominated by hydroxycinnamic acids. Preclinical evaluation demonstrated significant attenuation of LPS-induced inflammation, including reduced cytokine levels, modulation of macrophage response, and preservation of lung architecture, with efficacy comparable to dexamethasone. Overall, this study provides a mechanistically grounded and scalable framework for the translational valorization of kodo millet husk.

title: A policy-driven and climate-adjusted Weibull framework for forecasting end-of-life photovoltaic module waste in Korea
abstract: This study quantitatively predicts the future generation of end-of-life (EoL) photovoltaic (PV) module waste in South Korea and assesses uncertainty associated with key lifetime and modeling assumptions. Separate lifetime models were developed for commercial and self-consumption PV systems using a Weibull-based framework that incorporates the contractual structures of national PV support policies and empirical evidence from module disposal cases. For commercial systems, distinct Weibull distributions were applied to installation cohorts according to policy-specific contract termination periods under the Feed-in Tariff (FIT) and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) schemes. For self-consumption systems, an Acceleration Failure Time (AFT)-Weibull model was employed, integrating region-specific climatic risk factors—temperature, precipitation, humidity, particulate matter (PM), and ozone concentration—as determinants of lifetime degradation. Annual waste generation is projected to increase sharply, peaking around 2040, with cumulative EoL PV waste estimated to reach approximately 1.7-1.9 million tons by 2050. Regional analysis reveals higher waste generation in Jeonnam, Jeonbuk, Gyeongbuk, and Chungnam provinces, primarily driven by installed capacity rather than accelerated degradation. Sensitivity analyses, including variations in climate acceleration factors and reuse rates, indicate that uncertainty mainly affects the magnitude of waste generation whereas the overall temporal pattern remains robust. These findings provide a quantitative foundation for developing PV recycling policies and planning resource recovery infrastructure in Korea.

title: Self-driven antibiotic dehalogenation via novel decoupled aluminium-carbon system: Performance, mechanism, and biodegradability assessment
abstract: The residual presence of halogenated antibiotics in aquatic environments poses threats due to the stability of carbon-halogen (C-X) bonds. Herein, we propose a self-driven purification technology comprising zero-valent aluminium (ZVAl) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) for the efficient dehalogenation of florfenicol (FLO). The physical separation of the ZVAl anode and CNTs cathode into distinct chambers facilitates the direct replacement of spent anodes and permits the facile recovery and reuse of CNTs. The ZVAl//CNTs system achieved high removal efficiency of FLO (>81.4%) over a wide pH range (3–11) and showed strong resilience to various water matrix components (NO3−, SO42−, and humic acid); other halogenated compounds such as chloramphenicol and thiamphenicol could also be effectively degraded by this system. Mechanistic investigations revealed that dehalogenation proceeds predominantly via proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathways. Integrated experimental and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed that C-Cl bonds are cleaved prior to the C-F bond during FLO reduction. The ZVAl//CNTs process successfully diminished the antibacterial activity and phytotoxicity of FLO, and improved the biodegradability of effluents (BOD5/COD increased from 0.08 to 0.29). This study establishes a sustainable paradigm for dehalogenating refractory halogenated pollutants, emphasizing a strategy that fosters the circulation of carbon materials.

title: Bayesian material flow analysis and life cycle assessment reveal decarbonisation and land use trade-off in England's cement and concrete sector
abstract: Concrete is essential for modern infrastructure, but its production has significant environmental costs, including carbon emissions and land use. Comprehensive material life cycle data for cement and concrete are currently lacking, hindering assessment of its life cycle environmental impacts and strategies for mitigative action including policy decisions. This study applies Bayesian Material Flow Analysis (BaMFA) for the quantitative material flow analysis of the 2019 cement and concrete life cycle in England. Integrating the BaMFA results – estimates of material flows and stocks – into Life Cycle Assessment enables more complete assessment of the material system's potential life cycle impacts. This study has two aims. First, to establish the first quantitative material life cycle for cement and concrete in England; second, to demonstrate the potential of BaMFA in strategic material assessment. The modelled system has a global warming potential of 17.0MtCO2-eq, 2.6% of the reported 2019 UK total. Including land use (239km2a crop-eq, 0.1% of England's land area) highlights difficulties of achieving improvements concurrently across them. Priority actions for decarbonisation alongside land use reduction is clinker substitution in cement manufacturing and reduced coal use in steelmaking. Greater attention should also be paid to reducing impacts related to transport, which contributes 1.34 Mt CO2-eq and 54.5% of land use in the system, especially where interventions affect logistics and infrastructure needs. Data availability is a persistent barrier to informed policy and decision-making, including decarbonisation for net-zero, and system optimisation through modelling. BaMFA can help to estimate incomplete or absent data in any complex material systems.

title: From predictive accuracy to prescriptive value: A data-driven framework for sustainable multi-period electric vehicle battery recycling networks
abstract: With the accelerated expansion of global electric vehicles, the recycling of end-of-life electric vehicle batteries (EVB) is crucial to achieving a circular economy. In this study, a data-driven multi-period EVB recycling network design problem is investigated from a fourth-party logistics (4PL) perspective. The contributions involve two main aspects. First, an advanced data-driven optimization framework is proposed, wherein forecasting methods are evaluated based on the quality of the resulting decisions, thereby establishing a closed-loop linkage between prediction and optimization. Second, the 4PL concept is integrated into EVB recycling network design by jointly optimizing site selection and transportation link selection, facilitating the effective coordination of multiple third-party logistics providers, whereby network flexibility and operational efficiency are enhanced. To solve this problem, a two-stage stochastic multi-period network design model is formulated, and subsequently reformulated as a mixed-integer linear programming model using sample average approximation. To ensure computational scalability, a scenario decomposition and relaxation-based heuristic algorithm is developed, which integrates Latin hypercube sampling, Lagrangian relaxation, and the progressive hedging algorithm. Finally, numerical experiments using realistic profiles are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that the Transformer-based design achieves the lowest decision regret, with only 0.03% regret relative to the actual-demand benchmark. Compared with the GRU-based design, which performs strongly at the forecasting layer but yields 1.28% decision regret, the Transformer-based design reduces regret by approximately 97.3% and lowers the realized cost by about USD 0.62 million. These findings indicate that evaluating forecasting methods through downstream optimization outcomes can help mitigate the suboptimality caused by relying on statistical accuracy alone. Furthermore, the extended low-carbon analysis shows that carbon regulations significantly reshape the EVB recycling network. A moderate carbon tax (0.08–0.10 USD/kg) increases green 3PL adoption from 46.22% to over 53% while reducing variable emissions per EVB by approximately 1.4%, while RCR decreases only from 75.39% to 74.23%. In contrast, stringent carbon caps reduce variable emissions per EVB by about 4.4% but substantially decrease the recovery rate from 75.39% to 58.93%, highlighting a critical trade-off between decarbonization and circularity.

title: Carbon continuum across Eastern Himalayan forests: Elevational shifts in productivity, storage and turnover
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) that enhance carbon (C) sequestration while maintaining ecosystem resilience are central to climate-change mitigation and sustainable land management. Forests of the Eastern Himalaya, spanning steep elevational gradients, offer a unique opportunity to examine how productivity, carbon storage, and turnover together sustain these outcomes. This study quantified biomass, net primary productivity (NPP), vegetation and soil organic carbon (SOC) pools across tropical (TRF), subtropical (STRF), and temperate (TMF) forests in Mizoram, Northeast India, using intensive field-based measurements of trees, shrubs, herbs, litter, fine roots, and soils. Carbon dynamics varied significantly with elevation. The STRF exhibited the highest total biomass (286.70 Mg ha−1), vegetation C (134.75 Mg C ha−1), SOC pools (104.3 Mg C ha−1), and C sequestration rate (10.81 Mg C ha−1 yr−1), reflecting an optimal balance between productivity and carbon residence time. In contrast, TRF showed rapid C turnover with lower standing stocks (107.00 Mg C ha−1) but high fluxes, while TMF functioned as a long-term C reservoir with moderate biomass (254.10 Mg ha−1) and slow decomposition kinetics. Distinct litter and fine-root dynamics revealed complementary C cycling strategies along the elevational gradient. Collectively, these forests constitute a functional C continuum in which tropical systems act as high-exchange zones, subtropical forests as efficient C sinks, and temperate forests as stable long-term C stores. Conserving this elevational mosaic represents a robust nature-based sustainability solution that simultaneously supports climate mitigation, ecosystem resilience, and regional C balance in the Eastern Himalayan forests.

title: Synergistic enhancement of low-carbon cement-based materials and CO2 sequestration via graded carbonization and composite design of rice husk ash
abstract: To achieve solid waste recycling and carbon emission reduction in the cement industry, this study proposes a graded carbonation and functional compounding strategy that utilizes rice husk ash (RHA) as CO2-sequestration functional carrier capable of active CO2 sequestration and structural regulation. The progressively refined RHA samples (S1, S2, S3) were subjected to activation-carbonation treatment and graded compounding (Scheme A, B, C) and subsequently incorporated into an alkaline composite cementitious system at contents of 4%–20%. CO2 adsorption tests combined with the Avrami model were employed to quantitatively evaluate the CO2 capture capacity, while FTIR confirmed the coupling of physical adsorption and chemical carbonation processes. MIP, TG-DTG and SEM-EDS were used to systematically characterize the influence of the compounding schemes on the workability and mechanical performance of the system. The results demonstrate that progressive refinement from S1 to S3 transforms the pore structure of RHA from a macropore-dominated system to one enriched in micropores and mesopores, with the specific surface area increasing from 21.49 to 104.19 m2/g. FTIR and CO2 adsorption experiments confirm the concurrent enhancement of physical adsorption and chemical carbonation, with the maximum CO2 adsorption capacity increasing from 3.21 to 16.21 cm3/g. RHA-S3 exhibits a higher density of high-energy adsorption sites and enhanced adsorption kinetics. The RHA20-C group achieved the highest compressive strength of 51.11 MPa. TG-DTG analysis indicates that appropriate gradation enhances the pozzolanic reaction, promotes CH consumption, and facilitates the formation of stable carbonate phases. Pre-carbonation with CO2 further refined the pore structure and reduced the total pore volume, thereby increasing the proportion of harmless pores from 30%–34% to 34%–40%. Graded compounding counteracted structural degradation induced by macropores. The proposed system reduced carbon emissions by up to 11.16% and achieved a carbon sequestration capacity of 39.48 g CO2/kg. These findings provide a feasible pathway for the high-value utilization of solid waste and the development of low-carbon alkaline cementitious materials with integrated carbon sequestration functionality.

title: Integrated nitrogen fertilizer management strategies for sustainable subtropical vegetable production: A multi-objective approach
abstract: Optimizing nitrogen (N) management is key to high-yield, high-quality, and environmentally sustainable vegetable production. However, the long-term sustainability of integrated N management strategies considering agronomic performance, environmental impacts, and economic outcomes remains insufficiently evaluated, particularly in subtropical vegetable systems. This study combined two consecutive four-year field experiments with a multi-objective sustainability assessment framework integrating life cycle assessment (LCA) to systematically evaluate representative N management strategies in subtropical open-field pepper production. Experiment 1 assessed five N application rates, and Experiment 2, using the optimized rate, evaluated four N sources: conventional urea (CU), organic–inorganic fertilizer (OIF), stabilized fertilizer with nitrification inhibitor (NI), and controlled-release urea (CRU). In Experiment 1, the conventional N practice (FNP) with the highest N rate was the least sustainable, characterized by low N use efficiency, high environmental burdens, high social costs (including ecosystem and human health damages), and poor fruit quality. In contrast, the optimized N strategy (OPT) reduced N input while maintaining yields, improving N use efficiency and fruit quality, and decreasing environmental burdens by 43–59% and social costs by 46%. Experiment 2 further demonstrated that, compared with CU, the OIF, NI, and CRU further enhanced sustainability. Notably, NI and CRU enhanced pepper yield by 9–11%, N use efficiency by 9–17%, and improved fruit quality traits. These treatments also reduced environmental burdens by 14–52% and social costs by 31–40%, and increased net ecosystem economic benefits by 8–16%. Overall, integrating optimized N application rates with enhanced-efficiency fertilizers offers a promising strategy to achieve high yield, better quality, lower environmental burdens, and greater economic benefits in subtropical vegetable production. This study provides long-term field evidence and a comprehensive assessment framework for identifying sustainable N management strategies and supporting region-specific fertilizer management decisions.

title: Dynamic emission evolution and synergistic effect of heavy metals and primary air pollutants in China's iron and steel industry
abstract: At present, most reductions in heavy metals (HMs) emissions in the iron and steel industry (ISI) are attributable to synergistic decreases resulting from the implementation of dust removal, desulfurization, and denitrification facilities. However, the correlation between HMs and primary air pollutants (PAPs) emissions remains understudied. In this study, we systematically investigated the spatiotemporal evolutionary dynamics of HMs and PAPs emissions, as well as their synergistic effects, using an established long-time-series HMs and PAPs emission inventory based on a facility-level point source activity database. The results showed that HMs and PAPs emissions from the ISI in China were estimated at 1445.8 t and 1327.1 kt in 2023, respectively. Basic oxygen furnace and electric arc furnace processes were identified as the primary sources of HMs emissions. The Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region and the Yangtze River Delta were identified as the main areas with high levels of HMs and PAPs emissions. Spring and summer were also identified as the primary seasons associated with elevated HMs and PAPs emissions. From 2013 to 2023, emission reductions of HMs ranged from 21.2% to 81.1%, while reductions of PAPs ranged from 37.0% to 87.0%. Among the PAPs, NOx exhibited the greatest synergistic reduction potential with HMs, whereas PM demonstrated the strongest synergistic effects with HMs. End-of-pipe treatment levels (65.9%–85.7%) and energy intensity (13.5%–33.4%) were identified as the primary drivers of synergistic emission reductions. These findings provide data support for the formulation of targeted policies aimed at achieving synergistic emission reductions of HMs and PAPs in the ISI.

title: Predicting corporate environmental violations in China: Evidence from machine learning based on the Fraud Triangle Theory
abstract: Existing studies on corporate environmental violations mainly examine determinants from separate perspectives, lacking an integrated framework to explain their complex behavioral drivers. To address this limitation, this study integrates the Fraud Triangle Theory (FTT) with interpretable machine learning to develop a theory-driven framework for predicting and explaining corporate environmental violations using Chinese A-share listed companies. The results show that LightGBM model achieves the best predictive performance, and SHAP analysis reveals nonlinear effects, suggesting that environmental violations are driven by complex behavioral processes rather than simple linear relationships. Among the three FTT dimensions, pressure exhibits the greatest importance than opportunity and rationalization, indicating that external institutional and economic pressures dominate environmental violation risks. Further analysis reveals that the FTT-based risk structure is context-dependent. By integrating behavioral theory with interpretable machine learning, this study provides a theory-driven and interpretable framework for understanding the complex drivers of environmental violations, offering new insights into their underlying behavioral mechanisms.

title: Beyond a hydrological conduit: Highly reactive interfaces partition the capillary zone into a compartmentalized nitrogen bioreactor
abstract: The agricultural capillary zone (CZ) serves as a critical barrier preventing surface-derived pollutants, particularly nitrate, from reaching groundwater. To elucidate the vertical variation of microbial communities, nitrogen transformation functions, and their environmental drivers within this zone, we delineated a typical agricultural profile into three distinct functional microhabitats separated by highly reactive physical boundaries: the upper soil (US), the unsaturated capillary zone (CZunsat), and the saturated capillary zone (CZsat). By integrating intensive physicochemical profiling, 16S rRNA sequencing, metagenomic sequencing, and metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), we mapped the spatial succession of the nitrogen cycle. Results showed that water-saturation gradients were associated with distinct physicochemical conditions and microbial functional profiles across the CZ. At Interface 1, nitrate depletion coincided with a local increase in water saturation, Bacillota enrichment, denitrification-related marker genes, and nirS-encoding candidate denitrifiers, suggesting a possible spatial association between facultative anaerobes and denitrification potential. Further down in the relatively stable CZunsat, ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA)-related marker genes were consistent with localized nitrification potential. As 100% water saturation was reached at Interface 2, nitrification-related markers declined, whereas nrfAH and gudB persisted, suggesting a shift in ammonium-cycling potential. Finally, within the CZsat, Methylomirabilota and MAG43 carrying nxrAB-like genes were associated with functional potential related to anaerobic oxidation of methane coupled to denitrification (AOM-D), which may be relevant to deep nitrogen-flux buffering. Our findings provide new mechanistic insights into nitrogen migration and transformation within the CZ, highlighting its vital role in groundwater protection.

title: Decoding China's low-carbon resilience: A discrete numerical integration approach to spatiotemporal dynamics and influencing factors
abstract: Under the dual pressures of global climate change and economic transformation, balancing economic development with ecological protection has become a critical global challenge. Low-carbon resilience (LCR), as a core indicator for measuring a country's ability to maintain sustainable development during low-carbon transitions, provides a perspective for evaluating the efficacy of China's coordinated economic-ecological development. This study develops an LCR evaluation model that integrates total factor carbon productivity with numerical discrete integration and applies it to 30 Chinese provinces from 2004 to 2024. Additionally, kernel density estimation, the gravity center migration model, the Moran's I index, the Dagum Gini coefficient, and the Geodetector model are employed to explore the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and influencing factors of the LCR. The results show that China's LCR followed an N-shaped (rise–decline–rise) evolution between 2004 and 2024. Eastern China consistently maintains the highest LCR, whereas Western China remains the lowest; the Central and Northeastern regions occupy intermediate positions. The center of gravity for the LCR is concentrated in central-eastern China and undergoes a two-stage shift: first moving northwestward and then turning northeastward. Overall, regional disparities in the LCR initially narrowed and then widened again, with interregional differences and the spatial overlapping of high- and low-LCR provinces identified as the primary contributors. Technological progress, foreign trade activity, and energy efficiency are core influencing factors of LCR, whereas the economic development level, environmental regulation intensity, and green credit level serve as potential influencing factors. This study provides an analytical framework for assessing LCR and offers insights for low-carbon governance.

title: Machine learning advances volatile fatty acids production in anaerobic sludge fermentation: linking substrate traits to operation parameters
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation of waste activated sludge (WAS) to produce volatile fatty acids (VFAs) provides a promising pathway for sludge resource recovery. However, findings across different studies remain highly inconsistent due to the wide divergence in experimental conditions, making it difficult to derive generalizable patterns for VFAs production and product-spectrum regulation. To address this challenge, comprehensive datasets for untreated sludge (U-WAS) and pretreated sludge (P-WAS) were constructed, and an integrated machine learning framework was developed to predict VFAs production and identify key factors associated with product-spectrum regulation across different fermentation systems. The models achieved satisfactory predictive performance for total VFAs production, with R2 values of 0.82 and 0.90 for U-WAS and P-WAS, respectively, and moderate predictive accuracy for individual VFAs components (R2 = 0.65–0.79). Model interpretability analysis further revealed that the key factors associated with VFAs production differed markedly between the two systems. In the U-WAS system, fermentation pH was identified as the most influential predictor, and alkaline conditions were associated with higher VFAs production and acetate enrichment. In contrast, in the P-WAS system, the model infers that altering the composition of substrates (soluble proteins and carbohydrates) is the preferred strategy for regulating VFAs composition. Batch experiments using both model and real substrates further supported the model-derived substrate-composition trends, showing that lower protein/carbohydrate ratios favored acetate and butyrate accumulation, whereas higher ratios were associated with increased propionate and valerate proportions. In addition, several microbial genera potentially associated with VFAs production were identified. Overall, this study provides a data-driven framework for predicting and regulating VFAs production from sludge fermentation and offers practical guidance for selecting pretreatment strategies and co-fermentation substrates toward targeted VFAs production.

title: Optimized design of the bulge structure for alkaline electrolyzers based on response surface methodology
abstract: This paper aims to reduce energy consumption in alkaline electrolytic cell systems by conducting a parametric optimization study on the regular protrusion structures on the cathode surface. The protrusion height, width, and spacing gradient were selected as key geometric variables. Numerical simulations were performed based on electrode kinetics and gas-liquid two-phase transport models. By combining central composite design with response surface methods, quantitative relationships were established between the average cathode current density and the overall cell overpotential on one hand, and the structural parameters on the other. The results indicate that the protrusion height has the most significant and negative correlation with both responses; the optimized protrusion structure reduces gas accumulation near the electrode and improves mass transfer conditions. Under conditions of a bump height of 1.3 mm, a width of 2.6 mm, and a spacing gradient of 1.28 mm, as well as for a set of configurations with intermediate parameters, the average local reaction current density at the interface was reduced by 6.33% and 5.28%, respectively, compared to the structure without bumps, while the overall overpotential was reduced by 0.553% and 0.470%, respectively. A comparison of the polarization curves further verified that the optimized configuration exhibits a lower cell voltage at the same current density.

title: Assessing energy poverty alleviation, energy security enhancement, and decent work and economic growth in China under SDGs 7 and 8: A meta parallel two-stage dynamic SBM-DEA analysis
abstract: Energy poverty alleviation and energy security enhancement are two important dimensions of SDG 7 and are closely associated with the realization of decent work and economic growth (SDG 8). This study applies a meta parallel two-stage dynamic undesirable slacks-based measure (SBM) data envelopment analysis (DEA) model to evaluate the relative efficiency of 30 Chinese provinces from 2015 to 2021. Energy poverty alleviation and energy security enhancement are modeled as two parallel sub-stages under SDG 7, while SDG 8 is evaluated as the second stage. The results show clear regional heterogeneity across three stages. The western region records the highest average efficiency, followed by the central and eastern regions. The TGR results further indicate that the western regional frontier remains closer to the meta-frontier, whereas the eastern region maintains a persistent technology gap. The average efficiencies of the western, central, and eastern regions are 0.956, 0.911, and 0.862 for energy poverty alleviation; 0.927, 0.911, and 0.795 for energy security enhancement; and 0.946, 0.890, and 0.786 for SDG 8 efficiency, respectively. Slack-based results show that inefficiency is mainly related to clean energy substitution, energy use efficiency, supply diversification, environmental pressure, and the conversion of fiscal and energy inputs into employment related outputs. These findings support differentiated energy-governance strategies across regions and provinces.

title: Upcycling waste plastic into carbon nanotubes-basalt fiber hybrids: synthesis, mechanism, and asphalt pavement application
abstract: Transforming waste plastics into valuable resources and utilizing them to enhance asphalt performance have emerged as key research focuses in the field of sustainable materials. To address the poor dispersion and weak interfacial bonding of basalt fiber (BF) in asphalt, carbon nanotubes-basalt fiber (CNTs-BF) hybrids were synthesized via in-situ growth of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) on BF surfaces through catalytic cracking of waste plastic. The growth parameters were systematically optimized by varying the pyrolysis temperature, holding time, carbon source type (e.g., waste polyethylene (PE), polypropylene, and polystyrene), and catalyst type (cobalt or nickel). The synergistic effect of CNTs-BF hybrids on asphalt performance was investigated. The results showed that uniform CNTs growth on BF was achieved under optimized conditions using waste PE as the carbon source, cobalt as the catalyst, a pyrolysis temperature of 900 °C, and a holding time of 6 h; the asphalt composite with 3 wt% CNTs-BF hybrids exhibited optimal properties: high-temperature stability, low-temperature cracking resistance, and enhanced multiple stress creep recovery performance. Specifically, at 46 °C, the rutting factor and creep recovery rates at 0.1 and 3.2 kPa increased by 229.9%, 78.2%, and 34.6%, respectively; at −18 °C, the creep stiffness decreased by 35.1%, while the creep rate increased by 18.7%. In addition, CNTs-BF hybrids changed the microscopic surface morphology of the asphalt and substantially enhanced its dielectric properties. At a CNTs-BF content of 10 wt%, the total shielding effectiveness reached 12.26 dB, indicating effective electromagnetic wave attenuation. This work provides a promising strategy for the high-value utilization of waste plastics and the development of multifunctional asphalt composites for smart pavement applications.

title: Collaborative production scheduling of energy-differentiated components in three-echelon sustainable supply chain under time-of-use tariffs
abstract: Equipment manufacturing enterprises face a critical trade-off between energy efficiency, cost control, and on-time delivery under time-of-use (TOU) electricity tariffs, especially when components are sourced through multi-echelon supply chains. In the considered three-echelon sustainable supply chain, production operations at the first and second echelons jointly determine the lead time of components and dominate energy consumption and delivery delay risks. To address this challenge, this study focuses on the integrated production scheduling of first-echelon and second-echelon suppliers, capturing the key trade-offs among energy-related costs and tardiness penalty. We develop a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that minimizes the total system cost, comprising production energy costs at both supplier echelons, inter-echelon storage energy costs for components, and delay penalty cost. Given the NP-hard nature of the problem, we propose a supply chain total operating cost-based adaptive large neighborhood search (STOALNS) algorithm tailored to coordinate two-echelon suppliers' production operations and balance heterogeneous energy costs. Numerical experiments show that the proposed STOALNS outperforms the three advanced algorithms in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency. Sensitivity analyses verified the robustness of our model and algorithm under varying TOU tariff structures, part energy consumption differences, and supply chain scales. Our results highlight the necessity of integrating two-echelon suppliers’ production coordination and energy heterogeneity into scheduling decisions. We provide an extensible framework for cost-effective and energy-efficient operations in three-echelon supply chains under TOU tariffs, directly supporting manufacturing enterprises in their pursuit of low-carbon and sustainable development.

title: Research on multi-cycle recyclable straw heating supply chain design based on intelligent algorithms
abstract: Straw heating is very important for straw energy utilization. However, the current straw heating supply chain model rarely considers the recyclable of straw ash and further fertilizer returning to the field, and it is mostly a single-cycle supply model, and it lacks the consideration of ecological value in the site selection process, which is not conducive to the sustainable development of the heating system. In this paper, the intelligent algorithm is used to take Suiping County as a case, set each month as a decision cycle, identify the patches through GIS technology to determine the amount of straw in each cooperative, and build a “farmland-cooperatives-briquetting base-boiler plant-ash processing center-large-scale agricultural users-farmland” considering the ecological value. A multi-cycle recyclable heating model. Research findings indicate: (1) In terms of site selection, supply chain costs are optimized when three briquetting bases (K8, K13, K12) and two ash processing centers (L2, L3) are located. (2) Regarding supply, transportation routes and supply volumes between nodes during each week were determined. (3) In the sensitivity analysis, the impact of the utilization efficiency of straw energy, the storage process, the transportation process, as well as the recovery efficiency of ash and slag on the supply chain is analyzed. The research results can provide reference value for the design of the straw heating supply chain at the county level, and have profound significance for the sustainable development of the supply chain.

title: Instrumental and normative rationality as dual drivers of sustainable consumption intentions: A study of usage and payment intentions for drone last-mile delivery
abstract: Drone delivery is regarded as a potential low-carbon consumption model to replace traditional high-carbon last-mile logistics. However, existing research has mostly focused on technical feasibility or single-dimensional user acceptance, lacking a systematic integration of the dual pathways of instrumental rationality and normative rationality and overlooking the driving mechanisms of payment intention. To address this gap, this research integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) theory to construct a dual-pathway integrated model. Based on 646 valid questionnaires, structural equation modeling is conducted to reveal the psychological mechanisms underlying users’ adoption of this low-carbon alternative model. The results show that both TAM and VBN pathways significantly influence behavioral intentions, with perceived usefulness exerting the strongest effect. However, environmental awareness enhances only perceived usefulness and has no significant effect on perceived ease of use, while the corresponding mediation pathways are not supported. Additionally, personal innovativeness positively moderates only the relationship between environmental awareness and perceived usefulness. Finally, all pathways have weaker effects on payment intention than on usage intention. The research recommends that enterprises prioritize improving interface ease of use and leverage highly innovative users to disseminate green value, while policy-makers should strengthen public education to promote sustainable consumption behaviors. This research validates the explanatory power of the TAM-VBN model for sustainable consumption intentions in the context of service-oriented green technology, reveals the boundary condition that environmental awareness does not affect perceived ease of use, and distinguishes the differentiated driving mechanisms of usage intention and payment intention.

title: Circular valorization of waste polyester fabric/hemp stalk into fire-safe structural composites
abstract: Upcycling of textile and agricultural waste into structural materials offers a promising pathway towards sustainability, yet the inherent flammability of organic feedstocks remains a formidable obstacle to their deployment in safety-critical applications. Here, we demonstrate a circular valorization strategy that transforms waste polyester fabrics and hemp stalks into rigid and fire-safe composite panels engineered via a binary intumescent flame-retardant system comprising piperazine pyrophosphate and melamine polyphosphate. Thermogravimetric and char residue analyses indicate a staged intumescent action in the waste polyester fabrics/hemp stalks matrix, in which piperazine pyrophosphate promotes early dehydration and carbon skeleton formation, while melamine polyphosphate releases non-combustible gases at elevated temperatures to support char expansion. The resulting phosphorus-nitrogen hybrid structures form a dense, continuous, and thermally insulating barrier that effectively suppresses heat and mass transfer during combustion. Consequently, the optimized composites achieve a limiting oxygen index of 28.3% and a UL-94 V-0 rating, accompanied by a 50.7% reduction in peak heat release rate. Crucially, the composite balances stringent fire safety requirements with structural rigidity, effectively navigating the trade-off between flame retardancy and mechanical properties caused by interfacial heterogeneity. These findings establish a material-design strategy that integrates the complementary functions of mixed agro-textile wastes with PAPP/MPP-assisted intumescent protection, providing a basis for their conversion into value-added, fire-safe rigid panels.

title: Incorporating fairness into mixture design and material procurement for ultra-high-performance concrete
abstract: Traditional concrete design practices focus on material properties and economic parameters, often overlooking social parameters which are however important for real practices. This paper introduces fairness as a social parameter and presents a design approach to enable simultaneous consideration of technical, social, economic, and environmental parameters in concrete design. Machine learning models are trained to predict the compressive strength of ultra-high-performance concrete, and multi-objective optimization is performed to discover optimal design solutions in a large design space involving various raw materials provided by different suppliers. The approach has been applied to a case study based in New Jersey. Concrete mixture design and supplier-level procurement information are considered. The results show that strategic consideration of fairness has the potential to increase the compressive strength of concrete by 7% and reduce material cost by 28%, while the conflict between different parameters may increase carbon emission when carbon emission has a low priority. This research offers a new path to designing concrete with high compressive strength (>120 MPa) and reduced cost while improving fairness and facilitating waste valorization.

title: Spatiotemporal variations of near-surface CO2 concentrations in China and their multiple drivers: Modeling pathways towards the “dual carbon” goals
abstract: The transition from static emission inventories to dynamic atmospheric concentration assessments is crucial for evaluating and optimizing pathways toward China's “dual carbon” goals. This study develops a modeling framework using the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF-Chem), driven by a comprehensively coupled multi-source carbon emission inventory, to quantitatively decouple the impacts of anthropogenic, meteorological, and natural drivers on near-surface carbon dioxide (CO2) concentrations across China. Based on the historical baseline simulations, our results reveal a pronounced “southeastern high and northwestern low” spatial pattern of CO2 concentrations, with major urban agglomerations emerging as primary hotspots. Scenario projections for 2030 reveal distinct regional divergences: CO2 concentrations in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) and Pearl River Delta (PRD) continue to rise, primarily driven by expanding emissions from the “Industrial Boilers” (e.g., an increase of 1.06 × 108 Mg in the YRD) and “Mobile Sources” sectors, whereas regions like Shanxi exhibit a downward trend due to aggressive early structural transitions in the “Power” sector (−20.4%). By 2060, a universal deep decarbonization driven predominantly by extensive emission reductions in the “Power” and “Industrial Boilers” sectors translates to an 85.31% overall emission reduction across major urban agglomerations, yielding a decrease in CO2 concentrations by 6.51 ppmv (1.55%). Furthermore, meteorological drivers exert dual controls: boundary layer and wind speed variations drive local accumulation by affecting atmospheric dispersion, whereas temperatures indirectly modulate concentrations via biosphere-atmosphere feedbacks. Notably, terrestrial biogenic fluxes alter localized concentrations by up to 8.93%, highlighting the importance of natural sink preservation. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of regional numerical modeling for multi-factor decoupling, providing a reliable scientific foundation for implementing sector-specific dynamic emission controls and cleaner production policies.

title: Novel hydrovoltaic electricity generator based on electrospun recycled PET nanofibrous membranes
abstract: Hydrovoltaic energy harvesting, which converts natural water evaporation into useful electricity, has emerged as a promising technology for sustainable power generation. However, most existing devices rely on pristine or specially synthesized materials, limiting their environmental benefits and sustainability. In this study, we report a waste-derived hydrovoltaic electricity generator using nanofibrous membranes fabricated from electrospun recycled polyethylene terephthalate (r-PET). To overcome the intrinsic hydrophobicity of r-PET, the nanofibrous membranes were modified via carbon black (CB) coating, which effectively enhanced surface wettability and capillary-driven water transport, while simultaneously improving porosity and mechanical robustness. A single recycled-PET nanofibrous hydrovoltaic electricity generator (r-PHEG, 20.0 × 40.0 × 0.7 mm3) produced an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of ∼206 mV and a short-circuit current (ISC) of ∼127 μA upon LiCl activation, and maintained a continuous output of ∼155 mV and ∼91 μA for over 24 h. Scaling experiments demonstrated nearly linear voltage enhancement in series configurations (up to ∼ 1.07 V) and significant current amplification in parallel assemblies (∼587 μA). In addition, comparative analysis with previously reported waste-derived hydrovoltaic systems revealed that r-PHEG exhibits higher or comparable performance despite its low-cost and sustainable origins. Overall, this work demonstrates a sustainability-oriented route for converting post-consumer PET waste into an electrospun nanofibrous scaffold for evaporation-driven hydrovoltaic electricity generation. By combining waste-plastic upcycling, CB-assisted wettability modification, capillary water transport, and modular device integration, the proposed r-PHEG platform highlights the potential of recycled polymer feedstocks for low-cost and eco-friendly energy-harvesting applications.

title: Resilience archetypes across 106 arid and semi-arid cities as a framework for SDG 11 policy
abstract: Arid and semi-arid cities face compounding pressures from water scarcity, extreme heat, and rapid urbanization, yet whether resilience is primarily determined by climatic aridity or by socioeconomic and institutional capacity remains largely untested at the global scale. This study applies principal component analysis (PCA) and k-means clustering to a 15-indicator dataset comprising 106 arid and semi-arid cities to derive resilience archetypes and examine the relative influence of climatic and socioeconomic factors. Four archetypes were identified and validated using complementary internal and external validation metrics: a high-resilience Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) archetype, a Western diversified archetype, a mid-to-low-resilience Middle East and North Africa/South Asia (MENA/SA) archetype, and a low-resilience Sub-Saharan Africa archetype. Aridity class explained less than 6% of the variance in resilience outcomes, demonstrating that resilience archetypes transcend climatic boundaries and are primarily shaped by institutional capacity and economic development. The GCC archetype exhibits a wealth-buffered resilience paradox, whereby exceptionally high SDG 11 performance coexists with the highest per-capita CO2 emissions (18.9 t/capita) and the lowest renewable energy share (3.9%). This finding highlights a limitation of current SDG 11 assessment frameworks, which reward infrastructure performance without accounting for carbon intensity. The proposed archetype classification provides a transferable framework for differentiated SDG 11 monitoring and targeted urban climate adaptation strategies, enabling policy interventions that reflect the distinct structural constraints of different dryland city types.

title: Decarbonization of brownfield coal-based ironmaking via hydrogen enrichment and carbon capture: A techno-economic case study of the 2.0 Mtpy FINEX process
abstract: This study evaluates hydrogen enrichment and carbon capture options for a 2.0Mtpy brownfield FINEX smelting reduction plant operating at POSCO’s Pohang Steelworks, using a validated Pyomo-based process simulation model. A linear reduction kinetics model for the fluidized bed reactor was derived from thermogravimetric data and validated against an Arrhenius-based nonlinear formulation, with agreement within 3%. Three hydrogen enrichment pathways were analysed under a CO2 taxation framework—external syngas supply via steam methane reforming (SMR), external grey hydrogen supply via SMR, and internal CO-shift reactor integration within the off-gas recycling loop—together with cryogenic CO2 liquefaction as a capture option. CO-shift integration showed the best overall performance, lowering both CO2 emissions and production cost across all tax scenarios by raising the hydrogen content of the reducing gas and enhancing CO2 separation in the pressure swing adsorption unit. Grey hydrogen addition achieved the greatest coal saving but raised production cost owing to natural gas use. Cryogenic CO2 liquefaction reduced emissions linearly with capture capacity; under a constant-specific-energy assumption its break-even CO2 tax was essentially independent of scale.

title: Exploring nonlinear effects of driving behavior on vehicular emissions based on vehicle following trajectories
abstract: Vehicle emissions are sensitive to transient driving dynamics, yet the contribution of car-following heterogeneity to emission variability remains insufficiently quantified. This study develops a trajectory-based analytical framework that integrates a Newell Car-Following model, localized MOVES emission estimation, and Generalized Additive Models to examine nonlinear relationships between car-following behavior and emission factors. High-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle trajectories from urban expressways in Nanjing, China, were used to identify 222 valid leading–following vehicle pairs. Car-following heterogeneity was quantified using a cumulative trajectory-deviation indicator, which measures deviations from a Newell-based benchmark trajectory. A localized MOVES model was applied to estimate CO, HC, NOx, PM10, and CO2 emission factors for light-duty gasoline passenger cars. GAM models were developed separately for the five pollutants, explaining 54.5%–73.5% of the deviance. Across all pollutants, the trajectory-deviation indicator was positively and significantly associated with emission factors; a one-unit increase in this indicator corresponded to a 3.7%–7.6% increase in the expected emission factor. The smooth terms further indicated nonlinear emission responses to speed variability and acceleration dynamics. Speed variability exhibited broadly similar nonlinear associations with emission factors across the five pollutants, whereas the response patterns of deceleration-related variables differed by pollutant and value range. These findings indicate that car-following instability is associated with increased emission factors and provide empirical support for emission-oriented traffic control, eco-driving assistance, and trajectory-smoothing strategies.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions and mitigation strategies for two greenfield crude-to-chemicals pathways in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Crude-to-chemicals (CtC) pathways enable the direct conversion of crude oil into petrochemical products, offering increased flexibility in response to shifting demand from fuels to chemicals. This study compares the cradle-to-gate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensities of ethylene and propylene production for two integrated refinery-petrochemical systems configured for high petrochemical yields - a hydrocracker-based and a fluid catalytic cracker (FCC)-based steam cracking configuration. GHG emissions are reported as GWP100 per kilogram of ethylene and propylene, and benchmarked against conventional production using life cycle assessment (LCA). Mitigation scenarios are considered to assess the potential of additional reduction measures for the CtC configurations, including carbon capture and storage, electrification, solar hydrogen, and hydrogen-fueled burners. Results show emissions between 1.8 and 2.0 kg CO2-eq kg−1 for ethylene and 1.6 to 2.0 kg CO2-eq kg−1 for propylene, consistent with benchmark values for conventional fossil-based production. The FCC-based system exhibits slightly lower impacts, and all mitigation options contribute to further reductions, resulting in 1.0 kg CO2-eq kg−1 for ethylene in both configurations and 0.8 to 1.0 kg CO2-eq kg−1 for propylene. These findings illustrate integrated process optimization and targeted mitigation strategies as priority levers to reduce climate impacts across current petrochemical supply chains.

title: Integrating interpretable multimodal machine learning and Pareto optimization for energy-efficient removal of diverse PPCPs in plasma water treatment
abstract: Plasma-based advanced oxidation processes show great potential for the removal of pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) from wastewater, yet the simultaneous optimization of removal efficiency and energy consumption remains challenging due to complex multi-factor interactions. Most existing machine learning (ML) models rely on single-modal data, which limits both interpretability and reliability in process optimization. This study developed a novel multimodal machine learning (MML) framework that integrates experimental parameters, ultraviolet spectral data, and molecular descriptors to accurately predict the plasma removal efficiency of six structurally varied PPCPs. The predictive performance was evaluated through three complementary validation strategies. In a per-compound modeling approach, a separate model was trained and tested for each PPCP individually, yielding individual R2 values that averaged 0.8216 across the six target compounds, with ibuprofen reaching the highest R2 of 0.9293. Global five-fold cross-validation using all samples yielded a mean R2 of 0.9040. Leave-one-compound cross-validation, in which each compound was left out in turn as an unseen target, yielded an overall R2 of 0.8685 but showed compound-dependent performance, with norfloxacin exhibiting the lowest predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.5670). These results support preliminary within-domain transferability across the six target PPCPs. Further interpretability analysis indicated that the MML model can identify key influencing factors and quantify the contribution of each data modality. Crucially, by integrating Pareto optimality theory, a dual-objective optimization system was established to target maximum removal efficiency together with minimum energy consumption. This data-driven strategy derives the optimal conditions that inherently align with cleaner production principles. The optimized plasma process achieved higher removal efficiencies (93.76–99.07 %) for all target PPCPs while lowering energy consumption to 20.57–53.97 kWh·m−3, with generally lower energy consumption than previously reported plasma-based PPCP removal processes. Based upon the integration of interpretability with multi-objective optimization, this study presents a practical framework that balances PPCPs removal efficiency with energy savings in intrinsically greener plasma water treatment. This strategy enhances the operational sustainability and controllability of the plasma process, paving the way for smarter data-driven wastewater treatment solutions.

title: Preference-guided land-use optimization and trade-off coordination under different development goals from a township zoning perspective: A case study of rural Qiqihar, China
abstract: Land-use optimisation is critical for achieving sustainable rural development. However, existing studies often insufficiently address township-level differences in development priorities. Taking rural Qiqihar, China, as a case study, a differentiated land-use optimisation framework was developed in this study by integrating NSGA-II (Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II), RF (Random forest), and IntPLUS (Interaction network-based patch-generating land use simulation) to optimise the land-use quantity and spatial pattern under township-specific planning priorities. The framework was applied to analyse land-use change during 2005–2020, identify differentiated driving factors, and simulate optimised land-use patterns for 2035 in Economically-Focused, Agriculture-Focused, and Ecology-Focused Townships. Results showed that cropland remained the dominant land-use type in rural Qiqihar, whereas grassland was the main source of land conversion and supported the expansion of impervious surfaces, forest, and water. The driving-factor associations of land expansion showed clear heterogeneity among township types, with NDVI (Normalized difference vegetation index), elevation, and accessibility-related factors exerting differentiated influences. Compared with the natural development scenario, the optimised scenario better aligned with township functional orientations by prioritising the dominant development objective while maintaining coordination among economic development, ecological protection, and cropland conservation. In Economically-Focused Townships, economic value increased by 17.67%, indicating improved development efficiency under spatial optimisation. In Ecology-Focused Townships, the ESV (Ecosystem service value) increased by 2.64%, whereas the economic value decreased only slightly by 0.74%. In Agriculture-Focused Townships, cropland changed from a 1.24% decrease to a 1.04% increase, and impervious-surface expansion was reduced from 25.93% to 10.62%. Overall, the results demonstrate that township-level differentiated regulation can improve the scientific basis and policy relevance of rural land-use optimisation, providing support for sustainable land-use management and rural revitalisation.

title: From co-extraction to decoupled separation: Structural thermodynamics governing the dual recovery of germanium(IV) and chloride in an amine extraction system
abstract: Efficient recovery of germanium (Ge(IV)) and reduction of the chloride (Cl−) load from complex hydrometallurgical systems are key for securing the supply of critical metals and advancing cleaner production. This study developed an anti-emulsification R3NH+–KL-2 synergistic extraction system for the co-extraction of Ge(IV) and Cl− from acidic zinc leachate and their subsequent selective separation. An ANN–GA model was established to elucidate the nonlinear coupled effects of process parameters and identify suitable extraction conditions. McCabe–Thiele analysis showed that three counter-current extraction stages reduced the Ge(IV) and Cl− concentrations in the raffinate to 0.024 mg/L and 219.50 mg/L, respectively. Recycling results confirmed the excellent reusability of the organic phase, with extraction efficiencies for Ge(IV) and Cl− retained of 97.24% and 97.13% after five cycles. Given these results, an integrated multistage extraction, scrubbing, stripping, and hydrolytic precipitation process was achieved for the selective separation of Ge/Cl−. SEM-EDS and XPS analyses confirmed the selective conversion of Ge(IV) into a solid Ge product, while Cl− was concentrated into a Cl−-rich aqueous stream for subsequent purification and salt recovery. Slope analysis, apparent thermodynamic, FT−IR, Raman, HRMS, and DFT calculations revealed that Ge(IV) extraction was governed through multi-point electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bond-mediated stabilization, and polarization-enhanced interactions between R3NH+ and [Ge(IV)–Tar]2–. Cl− extraction correlated with localized ion-pair association. This study provided a laboratory-scale basis for Ge(IV) recovery, chloride resource utilization, waste minimization, and the development of cleaner hydrometallurgical processes.

title: Sustainable one-bath dyeing of nylon 66/cotton fabric via metal-ion complexation: mechanism, performance, and environmental assessment
abstract: The conventional two-bath dyeing process for nylon 66/cotton fabrics is characterized by lengthy procedures, high energy and water consumption, and significant wastewater generation. To address these challenges, this study proposes a sustainable and efficient one-bath dyeing strategy based on metal-ion complexation modification. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were first employed to systematically investigate the effects of blend ratio, metal ion type, copper ion (Cu2+) concentration, and temperature on the hydrogen-bond network within the nylon 66/cotton system. The modification mechanism and subsequent acid dye adsorption were further elucidated through molecular electrostatic potential (ESP) and binding energy analyses. Guided by these simulations, Cu2+ was selected to modify the fabric via complexation, and the modification efficacy was characterized by zeta potential, FTIR, XRD, XPS and SEM. The one-bath dyeing process with acid dyes was systematically optimized, and its dyeing performance, energy consumption, cost, and carbon emissions were benchmarked against the conventional two-bath method. Simulation results reveal that, owing to its d9 electron configuration and Jahn-Teller effect, Cu2+ coordinates with functional groups on the fiber molecules, reconstructing the hydrogen-bond network and significantly enhancing (making more negative) the binding energy between fibers and acid dyes. Experimentally, Cu2+ modification shifted the fiber surface zeta potential from negative to positive (up to +12.12 mV). Under optimized one-bath conditions (1% dye, pH 3, 90°C, 50 min), the dyed fabric achieved a color depth (K/S) of 3.42, color fastness ratings of 4-5, excellent levelness (DE = 0.57, RUI = 0.12), and an approximately 23.07% reduction in total dyeing cost. ICP-MS analysis showed that the residual copper content on the finished fabric (24.4 mg/kg) is below the OEKO-TEX® limit, and the copper in the spent bath can be efficiently recovered by precipitation. This work demonstrates that the Cu2+ complexation enabled one-bath acid dyeing not only ensures high dyeing quality but also significantly reduces energy consumption and environmental impact, offering a promising green manufacturing route for multi-component textiles.

title: Semantic knowledge structure and evolutionary pathways of carbon neutrality research: Implications for cleaner production and sustainability transitions
abstract: Carbon-neutrality research has expanded rapidly across climate governance, energy-system transformation, and low-carbon technology innovation, but its semantic organization and relevance to cleaner production remain insufficiently clarified. Using 13,453 Web of Science articles explicitly indexed by the term "carbon neutrality", this study combines abstract-level semantic representation with hierarchical clustering to identify the knowledge structure, temporal evolution, and national differentiation of carbon-neutrality research. The results reveal a dual-track structure composed of carbon-neutral transition pathways and carbon mitigation technologies, further divided into emission accounting, energy transition, catalytic conversion, and CCUS engineering. The field evolved from early problem identification and accounting-boundary construction toward system-pathway organization and technology-oriented implementation deepening. National patterns show differentiated research configurations rather than homogeneous global diffusion. China exhibits a comprehensive structure centered on emission accounting, the United States and the United Kingdom show stronger framework-organization features, and Japan and South Korea are more closely linked with energy security, CCUS, and engineering deployment. For cleaner production, the four topics correspond to complementary functions: measurement and responsibility allocation, energy-system redesign, hard-to-abate industrial mitigation, and CO2 utilization/process innovation. Expanded-term and fractional country-counting sensitivity checks indicate that the main two-track interpretation and national thematic patterns are broadly robust, while also confirming that the findings should be interpreted as term-specific evidence from the carbon-neutrality discourse rather than as a complete map of all net-zero and decarbonization research.

title: Cleaner catalytic recycling of retired wind turbine blades via ethanol-assisted hydrogenolysis and waste-plastic co-valorization
abstract: Retired wind turbine blades (RWTBs) are becoming a challenging composite-waste stream because their highly crosslinked thermoset matrix limits efficient material recovery.
