These findings advance theoretical understanding by integrating Lewis's dual economy theory and the Environmental Kuznets Curve into a unified spatial framework, offering actionable insights for aligning digital policy design with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially in balancing growth with green transformation at the local level.

title: Zero-residue valorization of chrysotile asbestos tailings via oxygen-free NaOH roasting: Stepwise recovery of SiO2 and MgO with chromium stabilization
abstract: Chrysotile asbestos tailings contain abundant silicon and magnesium resources. Existing extraction processes mainly focus on the efficient recovery of silicon and magnesium, yet they often cause the oxidation of Cr(III) to Cr(VI) and the co-dissolution of metal impurities, reducing product purity and producing secondary residues. Herein, this study developed a stepwise clean separation process via oxygen-free NaOH roasting-water leaching. Under an oxygen-free atmosphere, the oxidation of Cr(III) to highly toxic Cr(VI) is effectively suppressed during alkali roasting. Meanwhile, silicate minerals react with NaOH to form soluble sodium silicates (Na4SiO4 and Na2MgSiO4) and insoluble periclase. During water leaching, sodium silicates dissolve while Cr(III) and Fe(III) species reprecipitate as hydroxides under strong alkaline conditions, enabling selective silicon extraction. Under optimized conditions (750 °C, 60 min, Na2O/SiO2 molar ratio of 2.25, liquid-to-solid ratio of 8 mL/g), the SiO2 leaching efficiency reaches 93.59% with an ultra-high filtrate purity of 99.96%, while the leaching efficiencies of Cr and Fe are 4.74% and 0.09%, respectively. The magnesium-rich residue is subsequently subjected to selective acid leaching, achieving 85.55% Mg2+ recovery with 98.96% purity, and leaving an iron-rich residue suitable for ironmaking feedstock. These results demonstrate that atmosphere control can suppress Cr(III) oxidation while maintaining efficient silicate activation, thereby integrating Cr stabilization with the stepwise selective recovery of SiO2 and MgO. This work provides a new route for the full-component and zero-residue valorization of chrysotile asbestos tailings.

title: Optimization of filter bag structure for metal dust removal system based on multi-physical field simulation of high-temperature flue gas
abstract: High-temperature flue gas from aluminum smelting carries ultrafine metal dust featuring high chemical reactivity and explosion risk, which imposes critical challenges to the efficient and safe operation of pulse-jet baghouse systems. This study develops a gas-solid two-phase multi-physics coupled model incorporating high-temperature corrections for non-spherical particle dynamics and full-mode heat-mass transfer. The independent and coupled effects of pipeline velocity, dust concentration, and flue gas temperature on comprehensive performance are systematically investigated via computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The global optimal operating condition is identified using entropy weight-grey relational analysis (EW-GRA). Furthermore, a hybrid multi-objective optimization framework integrating orthogonal test, response surface methodology (RSM), and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) with an elite retention strategy is developed for filter bag structural parameter optimization. Results show the influence ranking: flue gas temperature > dust concentration > pipeline velocity. The globally optimal operating condition is determined as a pipeline flow velocity of 24 m/s, dust concentration of 500 mg/m3, and flue gas temperature of 523 K, while the optimal filter bag configuration is length 1405 mm, diameter 580 mm, and thickness 3.5 mm. Post-optimization, dust removal efficiency reaches 99.02% (＋1.22%), system pressure loss drops to 1228 Pa (−12.41%), and velocity standard deviation and bag temperature difference decrease by 91.54% and 81.89%, respectively. This work provides theoretical support and quantitative technical guidelines for the design and operational optimization of high-temperature dust removal systems in the aluminum smelting industry.

title: Beyond compliance: How sustainability assurance achieves value creation under resource scarcity
abstract: Sustainability assurance serves as a critical measure to alleviate resource and environmental constraints. However, how it facilitates value creation remains underexplored. Compared to the extensive literature on financial auditing, scholarly work dedicated to sustainability assurance is notably sparse. Using a sample of A-share listed companies from 2014 to 2025, this paper examines how sustainability assurance achieves value creation under resource scarcity. The results show that: (1) Sustainability assurance plays a significant role in promoting corporate value creation and serves as a vital tool for resource allocation. (2) Investor confidence partially mediates the relationship between sustainability assurance and corporate value creation, and financing constraints positively moderate this relationship. (3) Further analysis finds that if sustainability assurance entities are certified public accounting (CPA) firms, or sustainability assurance and financial statement auditing are conducted by the same entity, the effect of sustainability assurance on corporate value creation is more pronounced, and sustainability assurance plays a more significant role in promoting corporate value creation among high-risk enterprises. This paper offers policy insights and empirical support for enhancing sustainability assurance, boosting investor confidence, alleviating financing constraints, and achieving corporate value creation.

title: Forecasting Sustainable Development Goals scores through the vulnerability–resilience framework: A global income group analysis
abstract: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for integrated, forward-looking analysis that goes beyond retrospective monitoring to examine the structural conditions shaping future trajectories. This study proposes a framework that combines vulnerability-resilience diagnostics with time-series forecasting and scenario-based simulation to analyze SDG Index dynamics across four World Bank income groups from 2000 to 2024 and project trajectories to 2030. Composite Vulnerability and Resilience Indices are constructed from 98 normalized SDG sub-indicators, with the Resilience Index decomposed into hard (physical and infrastructure capacity) and soft (institutional, social, and innovation capacity) sub-dimensions. Both indices show strong correlations with the overall SDG Index (−0.961 and +0.994, respectively) with robustness confirmed across five alternative weighting methods. Forecast performance is evaluated using rolling-origin walk-forward cross-validation. ARIMAX is retained as the primary structural model, while Holt and Linear Regression-Holt smoothing serve as complementary trend benchmarks. Under the ARIMAX business-as-usual baseline, projected 2030 scores range from approximately 78.4 for high-income to 49.4 for low-income countries, with Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests confirming that all income-group distributions remain statistically distinct throughout the projection period. Elasticity analysis shows that the vulnerability-resilience framework accounts for more than 99 percent of within-group SDG variation. Scenario-based sensitivity analysis shows that vulnerability reduction yields the largest modeled SDG gains across all income groups, with marginal SDG gains of approximately 0.22 points per 1% reduction for upper-middle-income countries and 0.15 points per 1% reduction for lower-middle-income countries. For low-income countries, positive gains from both vulnerability reduction and resilience improvement support a dual-intervention approach. These findings support differentiated, income-group-specific policy recommendations grounded directly in the empirical results.

title: International trade redistributes global nitrous oxide emissions and responsibility patterns
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance, yet existing assessments remain dominated by production-based accounting (PBA), obscuring the role of consumption in global supply chains and potentially masking emission outsourcing and apparent mitigation. Therefore, we develop a long-term consumption-based assessment of global N2O emissions from 1995 to 2020 that jointly tracks trade-embodied emission flows, production–consumption responsibility asymmetries, decoupling patterns, and their underlying structural drivers. This integrated framework enables us to examine how changing global supply chains reshape the spatial distribution of N2O emissions, mitigation responsibility, and the balance between efficiency improvements and consumption-driven emission growth. N2O emissions increased by 25.8%, while trade-embodied emissions grew faster, reaching 36.9% of total emissions in 2020. Embodied N2O flows exhibited a dual restructuring: the traditional South-to-North responsibility asymmetry persisted, while South-South transfers expanded rapidly and became increasingly concentrated around major emerging-economy corridors, particularly the Brazil–China linkage. Divergences between PBA and CBA indicate a growing spatial separation between where emissions are generated and where the associated consumption occurs. Meanwhile, reductions in emission intensity failed to offset demand growth. These findings call for a shift in N2O governance from territorial emission control toward global consumption responsibility, linking nitrogen mitigation to trade justice and environmental equity.

title: TINeXt-G: A dual encoding ConvNeXt-powered time-to-image representation framework for electricity load forecasting
abstract: Electricity load forecasting plays a pivotal role in maintaining the reliability and economic efficiency of power grids, enabling operators to plan generation schedules, optimize transmission and manage demand fluctuations. Traditional methods, including statistical (e.g., ARIMA) and machine learning (e.g., random forests) techniques, have long been employed for such predictions, but many struggle to capture the nonlinear and multi-seasonal complexity of modern electricity consumption patterns. These methods often rely on simplified assumptions or overlook critical temporal correlations, resulting in suboptimal handling of abrupt load variations and intricate seasonality. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel spatial–temporal forecasting framework that encodes raw consumption data into high-resolution images, leveraging both Gramian Angular Field (GAF) and line-plot transformations to better preserve diverse aspects of the time-series structure. A modern ConvNeXt backbone then processes these encoded images, extracting hierarchical “spatial-like” features that reflect the data’s underlying intricacies. To account for temporal dependencies and align with real-world rolling or iterative forecast scenarios, the extracted embeddings are merged with a bidirectional GRU (BiGRU) architecture capable of capturing both short- and long-range fluctuations. Experimental evaluation is performed on a large-scale dataset with significant daily and seasonal variations. The dataset is rigorously split into training, validation and testing subsets to ensure reliability of findings. Results indicate that the proposed image-encoded deep learning pipeline not only offers stable and accurate load forecasting (with average RMSE: 1.010 and MAE: 0.395) but also demonstrates improved adaptability over conventional single-branch or purely time-series-based methods. By enhancing the predictive capacity of electricity load forecasting, the approach contributes to more reliable power system operation, supports cleaner energy transitions, and facilitates informed decision-making for sustainable energy management.

title: Spillover effects of green infrastructure on the supply–demand utility of flood regulation services: A telecoupling perspective
abstract: Flood regulation services (FRS) are directional ecosystem services, for which green infrastructure (GI) provides a key biophysical foundation. However, current FRS research remains largely confined to local scales, overlooking remote upstream–downstream influences. This study constructed a novel indicator system integrating quantitative supply–demand indicators with Supply–Demand Utility (SDU). Furthermore, the Spatial Durbin Model was employed to quantify the spillover effects of GI on downstream SDU. Results indicated that Total Demand, Actual Supply, and Unsatisfied Demand accurately captured quantitative supply–demand relationships under realistic hydrological processes. SDU integrated both the physical supply–demand deficit (Unsatisfied Demand) and flood impact severity (Flood Hazard Intensity). Specifically, differences in Unsatisfied Demand among the representative flood events reflected the combined effects of flood magnitude and duration, whereas Flood Hazard Intensity generally increased with flood magnitude. Notably, the spillover effects of several GI composition variables reversed in direction across the representative events of different flood magnitudes. During the minor flood, evergreen forests and water bodies significantly reduced downstream flood hazards, whereas wetlands and grasslands exhibited opposing effects. During the major flood, evergreen forests, deciduous forests, and water bodies exhibited positive spillover effects, whereas wetlands and grasslands exhibited negative spillover effects in the baseline model. Furthermore, greater GI patch intermixing was robustly associated with reduced downstream flood hazard during the minor flood, whereas greater GI patch diversity consistently increased downstream flood hazard across model specifications during the major flood. Drawing on telecoupling theory, this study bridges the water balance principle with supply–demand indicators, providing a scientific basis for trans-regional adaptive flood management.

title: How does digital industry agglomeration affect the environmental efficiency of power systems in China
abstract: Existing research has largely overlooked the impact of fixed-sum outputs in power system efficiency assessment, whereas studies on digital industry agglomeration (DIA) have focused almost exclusively on geographical agglomeration and have neglected the role of virtual agglomeration. To address these gaps, this study develops a novel two-stage fixed-sum output DEA model, decomposes DIA into digital industrial geographical agglomeration (DIGA) and digital industrial virtual agglomeration (DIVA). The results suggest the following: (1) The total environmental efficiency of power system (PSEE) and the environmental efficiency of electricity generation (EGEE) exhibit a downward trend, while the environmental efficiency of T&D (TDEE) is on a slight upward trend. (2) DIGA significantly improves PSEE and TDEE. DIVA significantly enhances PSEE, EGEE and TDEE. (3) The effects of DIGA and DIVA on PSEE exhibit significant regional heterogeneity. These results offer valuable insights for policymakers to devise differentiated strategies for leveraging DIA to enhance PSEE.

title: Renewable energy integration and grid stability: Heterogeneous effects of virtual power plants across Chinese provinces
abstract: In the context of global efforts to address climate change and promote energy transition, China's renewable energy industry has been thriving. However, the intermittent nature of renewable energy poses challenges to the stable operation of the power system. Virtual power plants (VPP) have emerged as an innovative power management model, but there are differences among provinces in China across many aspects, and their applications exhibit heterogeneity. This paper focuses on ensuring the integration of renewable energy and the stability of the power grid. It constructs a differential game model with thermal power plants, green power plants, and source network consortium (composed of a VPP and the power grid) as the game players, and elaborates on the characteristics and operating mechanisms of the four types of power-related entities. Differential data simulations are conducted based on the actual conditions of 31 provinces in China. The study found that without VPP participation, the average renewable energy integration rate was 9.38%, and the grid stability index was 0.4923. With power type VPP participation, the integration rate increased to 52.77%, but the stability index decreased to −0.0401. The integration rates of load type and energy type VPP were 20.84% and 19.99%, respectively, with their stability index remaining at 0.4064 and 0.4046. A total of 29 provinces completed the model matching, among which 14 provinces selected the power type, 9 selected the load type, and 6 selected the energy type.

title: Do green innovation and advertising intensity enhance financial performance? Firm-level evidence from the global chemical sector
abstract: The transition toward a low-carbon economy has intensified scrutiny on the environmental strategies of carbon-intensive sectors, such as the chemical industry. This paper examines the impact of green innovation on corporate financial performance (CFP), as empirical testing of the NRBV remains limited in such sectors, as well as the moderating role of advertising intensity in this relationship. In this study, advertising intensity refers to a firm's overall advertising expenditure relative to sales, which may include environmental and sustainability-related communication activities used to enhance stakeholder awareness, corporate legitimacy, and the market visibility of green initiatives. Using an unbalanced panel of 105 publicly listed chemical companies from 2015 to 2023, this study examines two dimensions of green innovation, namely, environmental performance-based innovation (EnvPS) and invention-based innovation (IS), and analyses their effects on return on equity (ROE), return on assets (ROA), and return on sales (ROS). The results of the panel regression indicate that the effect of green innovation on CFP is not significant in the short term, indicating a lack of market awareness of sustainability activities and slow returns on innovation. However, advertising intensity introduces a dual interacting role: it amplifies the financial gains associated with EnvPS, while concurrently weakening the profitability effects of IS due to increased short-term cost burdens. This study offers novel empirical evidence on how advertising intensity differentially conditions the relationship between innovation and performance in the global chemical industry, demonstrating that visibility, rather than innovation alone, is critical for converting sustainability investments into financial value.

title: Detailed breakdown of companies carbon footprints per origin of emissions using distributed input output analysis
abstract: A new approach based on input–output (IO) analysis has emerged recently to estimate the carbon footprints of companies and their products from cradle to gate, using a distributed iterative framework with all companies interacting to solve the high dimensionality IO linear system. Earlier papers have proposed to compute the footprint of a company as a single value, or to decompose it into three components accumulating separately primary and secondary Scope 1/2/3 data. This paper shows the distributed framework can be generalized to decompose the footprint of a given company into the additive contributions of all other companies of its upstream value chain, or into the aggregated contributions of any predefined partitioning of them. In practice, the distributed framework can be applied to predefined coarse-grain decompositions into countries and economic sectors taking part in the company's value chain. The single value footprint or the Scope1/2/3 accumulation footprints proposed in previous papers are two special cases of the general framework. In addition, we derive from the fine-grain decomposition at company level a loopback probing scheme to estimate the double counting inherent in the footprint of any company, or more interestingly, of any group of companies. We illustrate the model on macroeconomic data for 44 sectors and two regions (Europe and Rest of World), using the Inter-Country Input–Output database from the OECD. Future research will need to evaluate the framework on representative field data. Finally, we discuss the merits and limitations of the distributed framework compared to a centralized framework based on digital billing.

title: Experimental study on co-combustion and co-pyrolysis characteristics of end-of-life wind turbine blade (WTB) and coal
abstract: A concentrated wave of wind turbine blades (WTB) decommissioning is anticipated globally over the next few years. However, there remains a lack of systematic understanding regarding the thermochemical conversion and co-processing of end-of-life WTB composite waste. Although a series of laboratory-scale research has been conducted, the thermochemical behavior and interaction mechanisms of WTB-derived composite materials during co-processing with coal remain insufficiently understood. Most existing research focuses on a single composite material or model compound, while little attention has been paid to the thermal conversion mechanism of actual end-of-life WTB-derived composite materials and their coupled conversion with coal. In the current research, the thermal weight loss behavior and product evolution patterns of end-of-life WTB-derived materials, coal, and their blended samples during pyrolysis and combustion were investigated. A series of characterization techniques was employed, and a comprehensive comparative analysis of the combustion and pyrolysis process was conducted. The product distribution patterns and kinetic characteristics of the WTB-coal blend samples during thermochemical conversion were revealed. The findings show that there is significant synergistic cracking and oxidation between coal and WTB. The reaction behaviour of the WTB samples is jointly governed by epoxy resin matrix cracking, aromatic structure reconstruction, and high-temperature oxidation of residual char. After coal addition, the reaction mechanism shifts from a complex, multi-step chain-scission process to one dominated by volatile release and surface reactions. In addition, quantitative measurements from settling-furnace combustion experiments showed that the addition of 10 wt% WTB-1 reduced NOx concentrations by approximately 7.2∼17.2% at 1000–1300 °C, with an average reduction of approximately 11.6%, while NO concentrations decreased by approximately 7.1∼17.3%.These findings provide experimental evidence and mechanistic insights into the coupled thermochemical conversion of end-of-life WTB-derived materials and coal, and provide a scientific basis for further evaluation of WTB/coal co-processing.

title: Intensifying wheat production increases bread yield with a minor increase in global warming potential: A life cycle assessment of Kansas wheat
abstract: There is a growing pressure to increase food production while reducing the negative environmental impact of farming. Here, we assessed management options to increase wheat and bread production and minimize negative environmental outcomes. Based on a survey of 656 commercial winter wheat fields, we identified four management levels that represented low, average, high, and top-yielding fields, and replicated these across 23 field experiments in Kansas, the largest wheat producer in the United States (US). Yield, residue, grain protein concentration, bread yield, and environmental outcomes were compared across the four management levels, including global warming potential (GWP) and energy balance quantified using seed-to-grain and seed-to-bread life cycle assessments (LCA). Grain yield and protein concentration increased with improved agronomic management, increasing bread yield. While energy use and GWP per unit area increased with management intensification, yield increases partially offset GWP and energy use per unit of grain and per unit of bread. Nitrogen and diesel were the primary drivers of GWP and energy input during the grain production phase, which accounted for 9-18% of the total bread footprint owing to larger contributions from transportation, milling, and baking. Uncertainties associated with nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from N fertilization resulted in 6-17% variation in GWP estimates. Refining the current management of US wheat systems can help achieve the dual goal of increasing high-quality wheat production while minimizing environmental impact per unit of grain or bread.

title: Conservation leakage: Do nature reserves intensify land use in their surroundings?
abstract: As a core spatial vehicle for ecological conservation, the establishment of nature reserves (NRs) exerts profound influences on surrounding land use patterns. However, existing literature pays insufficient attention to the directionality, causal identification, and underlying mechanisms of such spillover effects. Drawing on data from Chinese nature reserves and multi-period land use datasets, this study employs a combination of counterfactual comparative analysis and double machine learning methods to identify the causal effects of NR's establishment. Furthermore, XGBoost and SHAP analyses are adopted to disentangle the contribution, threshold effects, and interactive mechanisms of driving factors. The results indicate that: (1) NR's establishment generates a stable positive ecological containment effect on surrounding land use, significantly reducing the proportion of pressure-type land categories by 11.78% on average. This finding confirms that ecological regulation by NR does not merely displace ecological degradation to neighboring areas, but delivers tangible ecological burden reduction; (2) The bidirectional spillover effects of NR exhibit a clear distance-based regulatory threshold, with 15 km identified as the attenuation boundary, providing quantitative support for differentiated, tiered spatial governance; (3) The dynamic evolution of spillover effects is a nonlinear process jointly driven by natural background conditions and socioeconomic factors. Annual mean temperature, slope, population density, and annual mean precipitation each contribute over 13% to the observed effects, among which population density emerges as the key controllable factor. This study extends the theoretical framework of NR's spatial externalities from the perspectives of spatial heterogeneity, causal identification, and multi-factor interactive driving mechanisms, offering scientific evidence and practical pathways for promoting differentiated land use governance and regional ecological security.

title: Identifying and analyzing technological ideas in hydrogen fuel cells using topic models and large language models
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells are a crucial clean energy technology. This study provides a comprehensive identification and analysis of the technological ideas within the hydrogen fuel cell domain, systematically tracing their full life-cycle from origination and evolution to application. Here, technological ideas are defined as creative problems and solutions generated through human or human–machine collaboration during research and development processes. Using global patent data collected from 1978 to 2025, this study identifies 111 fine-grained technological ideas in the hydrogen fuel cell domain based on Latent Dirichlet Allocation and further synthesizes them into 19 coarse-grained clusters with the aid of GPT-5. The findings reveal that the original technological ideas in hydrogen fuel cells emerged through three stages, demonstrating an evolutionary path from foundational materials toward system integration and end-use applications. Based on a proposed multidimensional dynamic measurement framework for emerging technological ideas, hydrogen fuel cell technological idea clusters exhibit four S-curve patterns, and the following recent emerging directions are identified: membrane electrode assembly and polymer membranes, secondary battery materials, energy conversion and storage systems, vehicles, and wireless communication and information transmission. Furthermore, 12 strongly associated technological idea combinations are uncovered using the Apriori algorithm, and idea mining conducted with large language models suggests that future innovation will increasingly emphasize systematic, cross-scale integrated design paradigms. Integrating scientometric methods with large language models, this study expands the boundaries of idea mining, offering a micro perspective for research on technological idea development in hydrogen fuel cells and inspiring future innovation.

title: Interpretable machine learning insights into the impact of environmental regulation on low-carbon transition: Evidence from the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Environmental regulation (ER) has become an important instrument for achieving environmental goals and advancing the low-carbon transition (LCT). However, existing studies still suffer from several limitations, including incomplete indicator systems, difficulties in capturing the nonlinear relationship and multifactor interaction effects between ER and LCT, and a lack of empirical analyses at the watershed scale. Consequently, the mechanism through which ER affects LCT warrants further in-depth exploration. To address these gaps, this study employs panel data from 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt from 2010 to 2023 to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics of ER and LCT and applies the XGBoost-SHAP model to identify the impact of ER on LCT. The results show that: (1) the spatial patterns of both ER and LCT present high values in the east and low values in the west, with high-value areas gradually agglomerating toward core regions, such as the Yangtze River Delta; (2) ER contributes 20.87% to LCT and exhibits a significant threshold effect, with its positive impact increasing markedly when ER exceeds 0.338; (3) synergistic effects between ER and factors such as urban transportation and financial development significantly enhance LCT. This study constructed a multidimensional evaluation system for ER and LCT and, for the first time, revealed the nonlinear threshold mechanism and multifactor synergy rules of ER affecting LCT at the watershed scale of the Yangtze River Economic Belt. This provides new empirical evidence for understanding their interaction mechanism and offers implications for optimizing the LCT pathways in this region.

title: Integrating diffusion and penetration functions: A novel balanced multi-component rejuvenator for sustainable asphalt recycling
abstract: Conventional rejuvenators face a bottleneck where interfacial penetration and deep diffusion are mutually restrictive. To address this challenge and promote sustainable asphalt recycling, a novel ester-bridged composite rejuvenator (RA-N) was designed and prepared based on a multiphase functional complementarity concept. To quantify migration differences among RA-N and commercial (RA-C), penetrative (RA-P), and diffusive (RA-D) rejuvenators in long-term aged asphalt (LT-A), a multidimensional research framework was established. This integrates layered viscosity tests, fluorescence microscopy (FM), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, COMSOL Multiphysics simulations, and performance recovery tests. Results show that RA-N overcomes typical surface retention and local aggregation defects, achieving uniform penetration and diffusion in LT-A. FTIR confirms that the rejuvenation is predominantly driven by physical blending. Combining macroscopic experiments and FTIR characterization, a physical restoration mechanism is proposed, utilizing the coordinated effects of aromatic ring disaggregation, aliphatic chain lubrication, and ester group compatibilization to disperse the dense agglomerated network. Simulations reveal a critical 25-min threshold at 130 °C for RA-N to overcome interfacial resistance and achieve deep diffusion, offering a qualitative reference for actual field operations. Furthermore, RA-N successfully recovers the viscoelastic properties of LT-A, restoring penetration (72.3 (0.1 mm)), softening point (44.2 °C), and 10 °C ductility (70.2 cm) to a near-virgin, slightly softer state. This study establishes that balancing interfacial penetration and deep diffusion is the core design principle for efficient composite rejuvenators, providing targeted material support for optimizing on-site hot recycling techniques and advancing cleaner production in large-scale RAP applications.

title: Steel slag-assisted valorization of wet weathered granite washing sludge for lightweight ceramsite production: Mechanism and sustainability assessment
abstract: Lightweight ceramsite was prepared by co-utilizing wet weathered granite washing sludge (WGWS) and steel slag (SS), thereby opening a sustainable pathway for industrial solid waste. The physical properties of ceramsite were optimized by adjusting the composition of WGWS, SS dosage, and sintering parameters. The optimal performance is obtained when the SS dosage is 17.5 % after holding at 1230 °C for 20 min. The apparent density is 492.97 kg/m3, the bulk density is 268.92 kg/m3, and the compressive strength is 1.51 MPa. The XRD Rietveld refinement results of WGWS demonstrate that higher feldspar and clay mineral content is more conducive to expansion performance. Chemical and structural analyses, combined with the FactSage thermodynamic model, indicate that CaO and iron oxide in SS alter the aluminosilicate network in WGWS, leading to its depolymerization and promoting melt formation. The resulting liquid phase reduced melt viscosity, which facilitated the encapsulation of gases generated during high-temperature reactions and consequently promoted pore development and porous ceramsite formation. During cooling, Ca- and Fe-containing substances drive phase reconstruction, forming stable calcium aluminosilicates and complex Fe-containing mineral phases. This Ca-Fe-mediated evolution contributes to mechanical performance and may enhance heavy metal immobilization, reducing leachability and shifting ecological risk from high to low after sintering, although Hg volatilization may also contribute to the reduced Hg leaching. Life cycle results further demonstrate that carbon emissions and production costs are reduced, indicating the method is environmentally sustainable.

title: From policy-related proxy indicators to scenario space optimization: Carbon-neutrality-oriented emission reduction pathways for the building sector in Shaanxi Province, China
abstract: With China's carbon-peaking target being progressively advanced, identifying key emission drivers and feasible reduction pathways in the building sector is essential for supporting the transition toward carbon neutrality. To address the limitations of conventional driver analysis and limited predefined scenarios, this study develops an integrated framework combining implementation-oriented policy-related proxy indicators, Ridge–STIRPAT estimation, feasible scenario-space construction, sensitivity analysis, and stage-wise interval-constrained optimization. Taking Shaanxi Province as a case study, the results show that building-sector carbon emissions increased from 25.83 MtCO2 in 2001 to 318.09 MtCO2 in 2022, with an average annual growth rate of 13.73%. Material production and transportation were the dominant sources, accounting for up to 76.19% of total emissions. Although carbon emission intensity declined from 9.23 to 2.39 tCO2/104 CNY, stable decoupling from economic growth was not achieved. Steel consumption was the dominant sensitivity factor, contributing 60.23% of the Shapley effect, followed by GDP, building electricity consumption, clean-heating proportion, and the electricity emission factor at 8.08%, 5.58%, 5.02%, and 3.02%, respectively. Under the constrained future scenario, median emissions rise to 338.74 MtCO2 in 2030 and then decline to 164.54 MtCO2 in 2060, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 48%–51% from 2022. Material-efficiency, power-decarbonization, building-operational-efficiency, and construction-stock-transition pathways achieve similar long-term outcomes. Under the Expanded stress-test scenario, the 2060 median falls to 85.59 MtCO2, while the screened high-implementation-potential pathways reach 102.03 MtCO2, representing a 67.92% reduction and retaining 92.93% of the original stress-test reduction. These findings highlight coordinated material-demand control, power-system decarbonization, building-energy-efficiency improvement, and construction-stock transition as the core of differentiated low-emission pathways.

title: Innovative valorization of low molecular weight lignin/SBS composite modifier for sustainable pavement construction: Antioxidant and rheological evolution during long-term aging
abstract: Lignin, a bio-renewable antioxidant resource derived from the pulp and paper industries, remains underutilized in pavement construction. For successful lignin valorization towards value-added asphalt modifiers, this study employed ethyl acetate to directly fractionate the low molecular weight (LMW) fraction from parent lignin, which was then introduced into the SBS system by hot-melt extrusion. LMW lignin fractions, lignin/SBS composite modifiers, and modified asphalt binders were studied by analytical chemistry, thermochemical, morphological, and rheology. The results indicated that the LMW fractions of lignin exhibited higher antioxidant activity, with the composite modifiers showing longer oxidation induction times and lower oxidation rates. Concurrently, SEM and FTIR confirmed the homogeneous dispersion of lignin within the SBS matrix and indicated that the hot-melt extrusion was primarily a physical process. Additionally, a comprehensive comparison based on the rheological indexes and their respective aging indexes demonstrated that, compared to parent lignin, LMW lignin enhanced high-temperature deformation resistance and low-temperature relaxation performance, but adversely affected fatigue performance. During long-term aging, although LMW lignin retards the aging of SBS modified asphalt, aging indexes under multivariate rheological performance encounter information redundancy issues, making it difficult to comprehensively characterize the aging degree of binders. Hence, principal component analysis (PCA) was conducted to capture the overall rheological evolution of the modified binders during thermo-oxidative aging. The established comprehensive aging index (AComprehensive) indicated a lower aging degree of LMW lignin/SBS modified binders, providing critical insights for the development of sustainable asphalt pavements.

title: Comfort or climate? Consumer trade-offs between sustainable aviation fuel and flight amenities
abstract: Decarbonizing aviation is essential to achieving global climate targets, yet sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production and use remain far below U.S. and international goals. While technical and policy barriers are well documented, less is known about consumer preferences for SAF-powered flights and the trade-offs travelers are willing to make. To address this gap, we conducted a nationally representative choice-based conjoint survey in which respondents selected between two hypothetical flight options varying in fuel type (SAF vs. conventional jet fuel), airline, price, seat type, legroom, and baggage allowance. Switching a flight from conventional fuel to SAF increases the probability of selection by approximately seven percentage points, an effect comparable to popular comfort features such as extra legroom or free checked baggage. Estimated willingness to pay for SAF-powered flights is about $17. Preferences vary substantially by scientific knowledge, climate attitudes, and political affiliation. The effect of SAF on flight choice exceeds 10 percentage points among respondents with high scientific knowledge or strong climate action preferences, while among Republicans and climate skeptics the effect is small and statistically insignificant. Perceived SAF safety also strongly moderates the effect of SAF on choice. These findings highlight that consumer demand for SAF is real but conditional, suggesting that targeted communication, transparent certification, and pricing incentives could complement supply-side policies to accelerate SAF adoption.

title: Proactive early-warning of effluent through OUR process feedback: An innovative intelligent prediction framework for wastewater treatment as a substitute for end-point monitoring
abstract: The implementation of intelligent regulations in wastewater treatment requires timely and reliable data. The existing end-point feedback control technique employed in most wastewater treatment systems is hindered by inadequate timeliness due to its intrinsic latency, while process feedback can markedly diminish this lag. The Oxygen Uptake Rate (OUR) is a robust process indicator for characterizing activated sludge physiological status and metabolic activity in wastewater treatment. Therefore, investigating the information about the wastewater treatment process contained in OUR becomes crucial for obtaining such data. This study focuses on the key process parameter of OUR, systematically elucidating its intrinsic mechanisms in response to temperature, sludge concentration (MLSS), and substrate concentration. The results indicate that the maximum OUR follows an exponential relationship with temperature and exhibits a significant linear correlation with Mixed Liquor Suspended Solids (MLSS). The real-time OUR of Ammonia-Oxidizing Bacteria (AOB) in response to NH3-N conforms to the Monod kinetic model. Then, based on the above understanding of the mechanism, a novel K-value method (KPR) for effluent NH3-N compliance assessment was introduced. Furthermore, a Random Forest (RF) algorithm was developed to predict effluent NH3-N based on OUR. This model achieved excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9532). The result was interpreted by variable importance measures and microbial community. Subsequently, a combined KPR-RF strategy was formulated for compliance determination, achieving a precision for compliance prediction of 100% and a precision for exceedance prediction of 100%. This study introduces an innovative theoretical framework and technical tools for executing “process feedback-based intelligent regulation” in wastewater treatment.

title: Hydrodynamic characteristics of tensile floating island-type offshore floating photovoltaic array
abstract: In this study, an array composed of eight tensile floating island-type offshore floating photovoltaic (FPV) platforms was investigated. Wave-tank model tests were conducted to examine its hydrodynamic characteristics under different irregular wave conditions. Taking the prototype installed capacity of 2 MW as an example, a 1:40 scale model was tested in a wave tank using wave data from the Bohai Sea. The motion responses of pitch, roll, and surge acceleration were analyzed in both time and frequency domains. The results show that: (1) The motion response of the wave ward-side floating structures is the largest, whereas the central structures exhibit minimal motion due to array constraints and shielding effects. (2) The FPVs array exhibits significant phase differences between units, indicating complex nonlinear interactions. (3) The response is more sensitive to wave height than to spectral peak period, and long-period waves (6–7 s) induce the largest motion. (4) Frequency-domain analysis indicates that wave ward-side structures receive the highest energy input, central structures are the most stable, and leeward-side structures experience strong responses with high-frequency components. (5) Under conditions of wave heights greater than 0.075 m and spectral peak periods above 0.949 s, surge acceleration of some floating structures exceeds 0.5 g, suggesting the need to limit array operation to ensure safety. These findings provide valuable guidance for the design, optimization, and safe operation of tensile floating island-type offshore FPV arrays.

title: Microplastics release from recycled plastic modified asphalt: Detection, characterization, and environmental implications
abstract: Recycled Plastic-Modified Asphalt (RPMA) has gained increasing attention in pavement engineering for its dual potential to reduce plastic waste and enhance pavement performance. Despite this growing interest, previous research and practical applications have focused mainly on engineering performance, with limited attention to the potential release of microplastics during pavement service life. This unresolved issue is environmentally important because released particles may enter surrounding soil, water, and air. Therefore, this study aimed to explore experimental methodologies to evaluate microplastic release from RPMA mixtures and their individual components under simulated environmental and traffic loading conditions. Using Laser Direct Infrared Imaging (LDIR), a vibrational spectroscopy technique that combines the surface sensitivity of attenuated total reflectance (ATR) with high-throughput, spatially resolved detection, spectra resembling low-density polyethylene (LDPE) were identified in asphalt binder and asphalt mixtures. This suggests that the inherent asphalt components may complicate microplastic source attribution, particularly after stress and environmental exposure. To quantify the release potential of RPMA, an apparent normalized particle area (NPA) index was proposed. Results showed that RPMA mixtures maintained greater structural integrity than unmodified mixtures under the tested laboratory conditions. Based on all particles tentatively identified as LDPE-like by LDIR, RPMA exhibited an apparent NPA that was 56.5% lower than that of the unmodified asphalt after combined high-temperature and moisture-conditioning. Although based on limited experiments, these preliminary findings highlight both the potential environmental trade-offs and the benefits of RPMA, demonstrate the utility of ATR-LDIR in differentiating polymeric sources, and underscore the need for standardized methods to assess microplastic releases from infrastructural pavement materials.

title: Tolerance and bioaccumulation mechanisms of the microalgae Scenedesmus obliquus to beryllium ions: Insights from physiological and transcriptomic responses
abstract: Beryllium (Be) is a widely utilized industrial metal with favorable physicochemical properties but poses severe chronic toxicity to aquatic organisms and humans, mandating safe and efficient removal from aqueous solutions. Current algal biosorption research remains limited for Be2+ separation and underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, the green microalgae Scenedesmus obliquus was exposed to varying concentrations of BeSO4 (0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, and 20.0 mg/L), and its growth, photosynthesis, oxidative stress response, Be2+ removal performance, and transcriptomic responses were investigated. Short-term exposure to BeSO4 had negligible effects on microalgal cell growth, chlorophyll a content and antioxidant system, whereas high dose (20.0 mg/L) or prolonged exposure (4 days) significantly inhibited these processes. The total bioaccumulation amount of beryllium increased continuously with elevating BeSO4 concentrations, ranging from 0.002 mg to 3.53 mg. Although the beryllium removal efficiency was relatively lower under 1 mg/L BeSO4 treatment (40.02%), it exhibited a steady increase with rising BeSO4 concentration and ultimately reached 88.14% at 20.0 mg/L BeSO4 on day 1. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that most genes associated with photosynthesis (44 transcripts), antioxidant system (33), stress response (60), nitrogen metabolism (46), endocytosis (38), and ion binding and transport (86) were upregulated, contributing to the high tolerance and total bioaccumulation of S. obliquus to beryllium ions. These findings revealed physiological and molecular mechanisms of beryllium tolerance and bioaccumulation in S. obliquus, providing a scientific foundation for the treatment of beryllium-containing wastewater and aquatic bioremediation.

title: Research on vehicle-to-grid flexibility potential to the grid in China based on the coupled transportation-power model
abstract: With the increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energies, power systems face growing demand for flexibility resources. The rapid expansion of electric vehicles (EVs) provides a large pool of distributed flexibility capacities. However, their flexibility potential for the power grid, interactions with storage and transmission, and performance under different policy constraints remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a coupled transportation-power system modeling framework to assess system flexibility potential of EVs. The impacts of uncontrolled charging (UC), smart charging (V1G), vehicle-to-grid (V2G), and sensitivity scenarios on system operation are analyzed based on the data from 31 Chinese provinces. The modeling results show that V2G reduces national load variance by 48.02% and intraday peak-valley differences by 51.46%. Importantly, this study identifies a temporal reorientation of system value, whereby V2G increasingly contributes to seasonal system balancing. Under high renewable penetration, summer discharge remains negligible, while winter discharge accounts for 49.22% of the annual total to compensate for the misalignment between renewable output and demand. At the provincial level, V2G value is driven by resource-load alignment rather than fleet scale. Guangdong has the largest EV fleet but contributes little discharge. V2G also changes infrastructure needs, reducing national new transmission capacity from 416.32 GW under UC to 362.33 GW under V2G, while selected renewable electricity transmission corridors remain important. It further changes the operating rhythm of conventional storage, indicating that EV flexibility interacts with conventional storage rather than simply replacing it. These findings suggest that future V2G planning should be region-specific and coordinated with storage deployment, transmission expansion, and compensation mechanisms for seasonal availability.

title: Development and testing of a high-temperature superconducting cable for high-power electric vehicle charging stations
abstract: Conventional high-power charging cables for electric vehicles (EVs) charging stations face challenges including limited power capacity and excessive weight. High-temperature superconducting (HTS) cables offer a promising solution for high-power EV with compact structure, zero direct current (DC) loss and high current density. In this study, a flexibilie HTS cable suitable for DC charging stations is designed, manufactured and tested it integrates terminations that can be connected to the EV battery, and liquid nitrogen ports for liquid nitrogen circulation. A platform was established to measure the temperature and strain of the charging cable during operation. The effect of bending deformation on critical current was investigated. Experimental results demonstrate that the charging cable cools from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperature within 300 s, the critical current is 605 A without bending, and decseases at 350 A when the bending angle layers reaches 65° with a temperature variation within 0.2 K.

title: Sustainable utilization of steel slag in asphalt pavement: Three-dimensional deformation characterization and environmental performance assessment
abstract: Steel slag (SS) has been widely investigated as an alternative aggregate for sustainable asphalt pavement. However, comprehensive characterization of deformation evolution and quantitative evaluation of structural stability remain challenging for steel slag asphalt mixture (SSAM). This study investigates the high-temperature deformation behavior and environmental performance of asphalt mixtures incorporating four types of SS at different replacement levels. The chemical composition and surface characteristics of SS aggregates were characterized, while wheel tracking tests and three-dimensional laser scanning were conducted to capture the deformation evolution under high-temperature loading. The results indicate that SS exhibits significantly different chemical and morphological characteristics from basalt aggregate, with higher alkalinity and rougher surface textures. Increasing SS content effectively improves rutting resistance, and the maximum dynamic stability reaches 12,987 cycles/mm. Based on the three-dimensional deformation field, the settlement-heave ratio Vr and volumetric deformation stability index VDSI were proposed to quantitatively describe deformation redistribution and stability characteristics. The established nonlinear model using these indicators achieved an R2 value of 0.908, indicating that the proposed indicators effectively characterize variations in the comprehensive deformation response. Furthermore, carbon emissions assessment and leaching tests demonstrate that SS utilization can reduce carbon emissions while maintaining environmental safety. This study provides a three-dimensional evaluation approach for understanding deformation characteristics and promoting the sustainable application of SSAM.

title: Towards sustainable oil storage: Multi-scale inhibition mechanism of green ionic liquids on the spontaneous combustion of sulfur corrosion products
abstract: Sulfur corrosion products in oil tanks are prone to oxidation and heat accumulation at ambient temperatures, risking fires and explosions. Thus, effective inhibitors are urgently needed for tank safety, yet the synergistic inhibition mechanisms of novel inhibitors across multiple scales remain underexplored. Herein, four imidazolium-based ionic liquids—[EMIM][OAc], [BMIM][OAc], [EMIM]Cl, and [BMIM]Cl—were selected to systematically investigate their inhibition of low-temperature oxidation from microscopic, mesoscopic, and macroscopic perspectives. Results show that at micro/mesoscopic scales, ionic liquids coordinately adsorb onto active iron sites on particle surfaces, passivating active crystal planes and reducing pore size. This process increases resistance to oxygen mass transfer and interfacial charge transfer while simultaneously decreasing the binding energy between oxygen and the crystal planes. Macroscopically, ionic liquids alter the reaction pathways, causing exothermic peaks of oxidation to shift toward higher temperatures, reducing peak heat flow, and elevating the apparent activation energy. The inhibition efficiencies follow: [BMIM][OAc] > [EMIM][OAc] > [BMIM]Cl > [EMIM]Cl, with [BMIM][OAc] exhibiting optimal performance (50.12%) due to synergistic anion coordination and cation steric hindrance. This study elucidates the cross-scale inhibition mechanism and demonstrates a preventative green strategy for mitigating spontaneous combustion risks. By replacing conventional toxic passivation agents with low-toxicity ionic liquids, this approach avoids secondary pollution and embodies cleaner production and inherently safer design for the petroleum storage industry.

title: Comparative mechanistic kinetic models for predicting anaerobic co-digestion outcomes across different total solid concentrations of cow manure and corn stover
abstract: Cow manure and corn stover pellets are co-digested in mesophilic conditions to assess the influence of total solid (TS) content on the digestion performance and process parameters. The 10.0% TS treatment exhibited the highest cumulative methane yield. When the TS content exceeded 12.5%, a decline in methane yield was observed with noticeable drop in pH and alkalinity, which suppressed methanogenic activity and consequently reduced methane production. Additional insights were gained through kinetic modeling of the collected data. Three kinetic models, modified Gompertz, first-order kinetic, and Chen-Hashimoto, were regressed to the data and their respective performances were evaluated. The modified Gompertz model exhibited the most optimal performance across all the treatments, though additional investigation through global sensitivity analysis revealed significant instability in the model output when regressing samples exhibiting inhibition.

title: Fish-cage removal as a source-control strategy: Phytoplankton community reorganization and stability enhancement in coastal aquaculture
abstract: Intensive fish-cage mariculture contributes to coastal eutrophication and restricted hydrodynamics, elevating the risk of harmful algal blooms (HABs). While aquaculture facility removal is a recognized cleaner production strategy for source control, its impacts on phytoplankton community processes remain unclear. Eukaryotic phytoplankton dynamics were assessed during a three-year fixed-station survey in Daya Bay, South China Sea. The assessment integrated water chemistry with 18S rRNA gene metabarcoding across the pre-removal, transitional, and post-removal phases. Following removal, nutrient concentrations declined significantly, yet spatial heterogeneity remained stable. Community change was driven primarily by species replacement, leading to a stronger distance-decay relationship and reduced taxa sharing among stations, indicating increased spatial patchiness. Concurrently, null and neutral models indicated increased stochasticity in community assembly. Effective immigration and phytoplankton cell density declined at the same time. These changes suggest a smaller effective community size and a stronger role for ecological drift in assembly. Co-occurrence networks evolved towards a less centralized, more complex, and stable architecture, suggesting enhanced community resistance and resilience. Furthermore, indicator taxa showed a successional shift from eutrophic, HAB-associated genera (e.g., Phaeocystis, Scrippsiella) to small-sized chlorophytes (e.g., Pycnococcus, Ostreococcus). This shift signaled reduced eutrophication risk. These findings indicate greater phytoplankton community stability and a functional shift consistent with ecological recovery after source control through fish-cage removal. These findings demonstrate the ecological benefits of source control through fish-cage removal. Cage removal enhances phytoplankton community stability and promotes a functional shift toward ecological recovery. The integrated analytical framework and eDNA-based indicators provide a reproducible approach for assessing the long-term effectiveness of cleaner production interventions in coastal ecosystems.

title: Ecological risk of antibiotic resistance genes in biofilms from the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project: insights from distribution patterns, driving factors, and mobility potential
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) have been recognized as emerging environmental pollutants, and aquatic biofilms serve as potential reservoirs for their enrichment and dissemination. The Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project (SNWDP-MR) is a key artificial water diversion system in China; however, the influence of biofilms on antibiotic resistance pollution risks remains unclear. In this study, metagenomic approaches were used to investigate the distribution, drivers, and mobility potential of ARGs in biofilms. A total of 22 ARG types were detected across the biofilm samples, with multidrug resistance genes being dominant. ARG composition varied significantly among seasons (p < 0.01), whereas spatial differences along the canal were relatively weak. Core ARGs were closely associated with microbial community structure, especially potential host taxa such as Sphingomonas, Novosphingobium, and Flavobacterium. ARG distribution was jointly shaped by environmental selection, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and microbial communities, with soluble reactive phosphorus, flow velocity, and electrical conductivity identified as key factors. Only a limited subset of core ARGs were frequently co-localized with MGEs such as transposases and insertion sequences. Among these, MacB and TaeA were most strongly associated with transposition-related elements and multiple MGE categories, suggesting potential horizontal transfer. ARG ecological risks were higher in summer and autumn, but the overall risk was slightly lower than levels previously reported for drinking water systems. This study clarifies the occurrence patterns and potential dissemination characteristics of ARGs in biofilms of the SNWDP-MR, providing a scientific basis for resistance pollution control, drinking water safety, and ecological risk management.

title: Gains and pains: Economic, social, and environmental impacts of China's designation of historical and Cultural Cities
abstract: Taking the Designation of Historical and Cultural Cities (DHCC) policy as a quasi-natural experiment, this study applies the Sun-Abraham event-study estimator to systematically examine the economic, social, and environmental effects of the policy. First, the DHCC policy significantly promotes urban economic growth and improves public service provision, but it also increases the intensity of sulfur dioxide emissions. This indicates a trade-off in which economic and social benefits improve while environmental pressure simultaneously intensifies. Second, the DHCC policy promotes urban economic growth through industrial agglomeration and expands public service provision by expanding local fiscal revenues. However, the expansion of economic activities and firm agglomeration also increases both production-based and consumption-based pollution sources. In addition, tourism development occupies urban green space and weakens the capacity of vegetation to purify pollutants. Third, the effects of the DHCC policy exhibit heterogeneity across four dimensions. Cities characterized by historical relics and traditional style achieve a better balance between development and environmental protection, whereas cities with ethnic cultural characteristics face the most pronounced pollution problems. Cities characterized by scenic and cultural attractions do not experience significant environmental deterioration. In regions with stronger local government competition, the DHCC policy generates stronger economic growth effects but entails higher environmental costs, while regions with weaker competition place greater emphasis on public service provision. The economic growth effect of the DHCC policy is significant across eastern, central, and western China, but decreases progressively from east to west. Improvements in public service provision are concentrated in eastern China, whereas pollution pressure is mainly concentrated in central China. For medium-sized cities, the economic growth effect of the DHCC policy is the strongest, while significant improvements in public services are observed only in large cities.

title: Road to sustainable development: How does green finance affect cultivated land green and low-carbon use efficiency?
abstract: Growing evidence indicates that conventional cultivated land use practices aimed at maximizing grain production have resulted in land degradation, declining productivity, and increasing environmental pressures. Improving cultivated land green and low-carbon use efficiency (CLGUE) is therefore critical for achieving a balance between food security and ecological sustainability. Based on panel data from 202 prefecture-level cities in China during 2011 to 2023, this study employs a difference-in-differences (DID) model to empirically examine the impact of green finance (GF) on CLGUE. The main findings are as follows: (1) CLGUE in China demonstrates an overall upward trend, rising by 39.34% during the study period. High-efficiency areas are concentrated in northeast China and central–western transitional zones, while low-efficiency clusters are predominantly distributed in eastern coastal regions. (2) GF significantly promotes CLGUE, increasing it by 0.0494 on average. The finding remains valid under a set of robustness tests. (3) GF generates significant positive spatial spillover effects on CLGUE, with the spatial spillover range extending approximately 450 km (4) Mechanism analysis reveals that agricultural infrastructure construction (AIC), agricultural green enterprises (AGE), and digital inclusive finance (DIF) may serve as potential mechanisms through which GF enhances CLGUE. (5) The positive impact of GF exhibits significant heterogeneity. Specifically, the positive effects are stronger in resource-based cities, non-major grain-producing areas, regions with higher agricultural insurance coverage, and areas located east of the Hu Line. These findings provide valuable insights for policymakers seeking to optimize green finance policies and accelerate the green and low-carbon transformation of cultivated land use.

title: The bright prospect of China's photovoltaic under the double carbon goal: A potential assessment based on the life cycle of photovoltaic power plants
abstract: China's proposed "double carbon" strategy (achieving peak carbon, then net zero) offers an unprecedented opportunity for the development of solar photovoltaic (PV). Assessing land suitability and development potential is essential for scaling up PV infrastructure. However, the possible impacts of climate change and land conversion over the long-life cycle of PV systems have not been sufficiently explored. Here, this study develops a spatiotemporal assessment framework that integrates subjective Multi-Criteria Decision Making with the objective Geographic Detector to evaluate the land suitability and development potential of centralized photovoltaic (CPV) systems in China under both current condition and future scenarios of climate change and land conversion. This study spans the 30-year PV life cycle, overcoming the static siting limitations. Results indicate that in 2020, approximately 2,486,158 km2 (26.26%) of China's land was suitable for CPV development. The technical potential was 57 times that year's national electricity, offering a CO2 mitigation potential of 247.66 Gt. Future prospects are even more promising, with the potential projected to reach 1.5 times the 2020 level. The most suitable regions for CPV development are western Inner Mongolia and the northeastern and southwestern parts of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. In areas with low CPV potential, composite PV projects tailored to local conditions could be implemented. Our results confirm that CPV holds significant potential for decarbonizing China's power system by 2050 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2060. Internationally, this methodology offers a replicable framework for spatially explicit renewable energy planning under global change scenarios.

title: An integrated manufacturing-process optimization method for tubular heat exchangers considering carbon emissions
abstract: Manufacturing activities are a major contributor to global carbon emissions, making the decarbonization of production processes essential for meeting international climate targets. However, process-parameter optimization in real-world manufacturing faces two challenges. First, the relationship between process parameters and carbon emissions is complex, which limits the ability of conventional methods to quantify emission-reduction potential. Second, existing methods rarely integrate industrial constraints systematically, making their solutions difficult to implement. This study proposes a Demand-Manufacturing-Parameter-Carbon (DMPC) optimization framework to support process-level low-carbon decision-making under constrained conditions. First, the manufacturing process is decomposed into carbon-related units, and a physics-based parameter-emission model quantifies the effects of manufacturing decisions on carbon emissions. Global sensitivity analysis then identifies emission-dominant parameters, characterizes parameter-emission relationships, and informs the subsequent optimization. Finally, a penalty-based fuzzy logic controller algorithm performs dynamic multi-objective optimization under industrial constraints to identify feasible parameter schemes. In a case study of industrial tubular heat-exchanger manufacturing, the optimized scheme reduced total carbon emissions by 10.14%, processing time by 12.87%, and energy costs by 3.88% relative to the empirical baseline. These results support the effectiveness and modeled feasibility of the DMPC framework and indicate the potential value of systematic parameter optimization for process-level emissions reduction.

title: A conceptual framework for uncertainty-informed system boundary expansion in life cycle assessment
abstract: Life cycle assessment (LCA) is the most comprehensive framework for evaluating the environmental impacts of products and services, yet defining system boundaries remains a subjective exercise and can lead to unknown truncation error and complications in comparing across studies. Here, we introduce an uncertainty-informed, iterative boundary-expansion algorithm that quantitatively guides boundary expansion by answering which processes in the foreground system should be included and expanded to upstream detail and which may be aggregated or omitted. The proposed algorithm starts with the foreground system and identifies hotspot processes by comparing predefined thresholds to a process's mean and upper-tail contribution share, computed from Monte Carlo results that propagate uncertainty in both a process's input amount and emission intensity. We developed a stochastic simulation framework and created synthetic production system trees to examine the behavior of the proposed algorithm under controlled conditions. Our results show that the cut-off threshold is the dominant factor in determining final model complexity, while uncertainty-driven expansion is most beneficial in low-data-quality scenarios. Foreground impact concentration could shape the distribution of effort required for system boundary expansion, suggesting that conventional LCA practices focused on primary supply chains may systematically miss significant impacts in diffuse systems. Applying the proposed approach could potentially enhance the documentation of system expansion and improve uncertainty analysis within LCA, ultimately increasing reproducibility and transparency in environmental assessments.

title: Impact of pre-decarbonization on biogas-to-hydrogen performance: A combined catalysis and simulation approach for economic analysis
abstract: Pre-decarbonization, as a conventional step in the steam reforming process for hydrogen production from biogas, lacks comparative studies on its impact on the steam reforming (SMR) and water-gas shift (WGS) processes, as well as on the overall process economics. In this study, the feasibility and economic advantages of omitting pre-decarbonization were investigated through catalyst performance evaluation and full-process simulation. Biogas conversion experiments were conducted using various SMR and WGS catalysts under feeds with pure CH4 and different CO2/CH4 ratios. The results reveal that the CO2 content has a negligible effect on CH4 conversion in the SMR stage (over 98% for all catalysts at 700 °C), and the final hydrogen yield decreases by only 3-5% as the CO2/CH4 ratios increase. Two process routes (A: “Pre-decarbonization + SMR and WGS + H2 purification”; B: “SMR and WGS + H2 purification”), were established using Aspen Plus, and an economic assessment was performed for 500-1500 m3/h biogas feeding. The results indicate that the process without pre-decarbonization achieves a lower levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) across all capacities (2.00 USD/kg H2 at 1500 m3/h). The cost difference is mainly attributed to the equipment cost of the pre-decarbonization unit (accounting for 33.7%-36.6% of total capital expenditure) and its high steam consumption. This study demonstrates that a biogas-to-hydrogen process without pre-decarbonization offers potential economic advantages, providing a research foundation for simplifying process design.

title: Fueling the future of ethanol: An IETB-based multi-criteria analysis in leading producer countries and regions
abstract: This study evaluates the readiness of ethanol programmes in five leading producer countries and regions (i.e., Brazil, the United States, the European Union (EU), India, and China) by integrating a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework. It combines coded qualitative and quantitative indicators into a transparent 0–10 scoring scheme based on IETB (institutional, economic, technological and behavioural) dimensions. Equal weights across the four dimensions serve as a normative baseline, and composite performance rankings and scores are computed with the TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) method. AHP-style weighting scenarios were applied to individual dimensions to assess robustness, and the composite TOPSIS scores were compared with external benchmarks such as ethanol production volumes. Results showed that India and China are in the emerging stage, the EU is in an intermediate position, but Brazil and the United States remain consistent leaders. Used as a quantitative diagnostic tool, this framework has enabled the identification of country-specific priorities, bottlenecks, and strengths for ethanol and decarbonisation policies in transport fuels.

title: Water footprint and sustainability assessment of sustainable aviation fuel production from castor oil, soybean, switchgrass, and corn stover in the Tongliao region
abstract: Decarbonizing aviation through sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) requires pathways that are both resource-efficient and regionally adaptable, particularly in water-limited areas. This study evaluates the life cycle sustainability of SAF produced from four biomass feedstocks—castor, soybean, corn stover, and switchgrass—through Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids, Fischer-Tropsch, and Alcohol-to-Jet pathways in the semi-arid Tongliao region of Northeast China. Life cycle assessment quantified water footprint (WF), carbon footprint, and soil carbon sequestration, and an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)-based surrogate model was developed using castor as a case study to estimate crop-specific WFs within the observed climatic domain. Castor- and switchgrass-based SAF exhibited the lowest life cycle WFs (0.1571 and 0.1195 m3/MJ). Accounting for induced land use change and soil carbon sequestration, switchgrass-based fuel achieved net-negative emissions, whereas castor-based fuel reduced emissions by 88.12% compared with fossil jet fuel. Multi-criteria decision analysis integrating environmental, technical, economic, and social dimensions identified the castor-based pathway as the optimal SAF option, followed by corn stover-based and switchgrass-based pathways. These findings highlight the role of non-food, drought-tolerant feedstocks and AI-assisted modeling in guiding feedstock selection, process optimization, and policy formulation for SAF development in water-stressed regions.

title: Rose petal biochar induces oxygen vacancies in Bi2MoO6 for efficient photocatalytic Cr(VI) reduction and degradation of hydrochloride tetracycline
abstract: Photocatalysis plays a vital role in aquatic environmental remediation, and the development of high-performance photocatalysts is essential for overcoming current technological limitations. In this study, S-scheme waste rose biochar (MC)/Bi2MoO6 heterostructures with abundant oxygen vacancies (OVs) were fabricated with the assistance of waste rose petal biomass. The incorporation of MC influences the nucleation process of Bi2MoO6 (BMO) and promotes the formation of OVs on the surface of Bi2MoO6. Acting as electron traps and active sites, OVs and the conductive MC synergistically boost the photocatalytic performance of Bi2MoO6. Under simulated sunlight irradiation, the MC-2 sample (mass ratio of MC to Bi2MoO6 is 2%) exhibits the highest photocatalytic activity. The reduction rate of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) over MC-2 is 12.4 times higher than that on the reference Bi2MoO6, while the degradation rate of hydrochloric tetracycline (HTC) is improved by a factor of 1.79. This study provides a promising strategy for the rational utilization of waste resources to develop high-performance Bi2MoO6-based catalysts for the remediation of aquatic ecological environments.

title: CO2 mineralization-assisted stabilization of loess with fly ash, MgO and Ca(OH)2: Static and dynamic performance, multiscale pore evolution, and carbon balance
abstract: Carbonation-based loess stabilization has mainly focused on static strength, leaving the links among CO2 mineralization, dynamic properties, microstructure, and carbon balance unclear. This study developed a fly ash-MgO-Ca(OH)2 ternary system and integrated static and dynamic tests with X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP), and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). MgO-rich mixtures showed rapid early strengthening, with the maximum dynamic shear modulus increasing by 142.0-195.7% after 12 h, whereas Ca(OH)2-rich mixtures developed more gradually. XRD, XRF, and SEM–EDS confirmed carbonate formation, particle coating, and contact cementation. For P25F6M4A0, MIP porosity decreased from 27.90% to 19.44% at 12 h but rebounded to 25.00% at 24 h; micro-CT connected porosity similarly changed from 5.68% to 1.06% and then 3.54%. The empirical interpolation model achieved R2 = 0.8863 on the internally held-out P20 dataset. Apparent carbonation efficiencies reached 73.2-91.5%, 75.0-86.1%, and 79.2% for F6M4A0, F6M2A2, and F6M0A4, respectively. In the preliminary binder-level carbon balance, the mineralized CO2 offset 60.3-69.5% of the estimated binder-production emissions. These results provide a composition-specific basis for balancing mechanical performance and net binder-level carbon emissions in stabilized loess.

title: Upcycling titanium gypsum into pH-gated calcium peroxide hydrogel beads for integrated water remediation with phosphorus-reuse potential
abstract: Cleaner remediation of eutrophic waters requires technologies that simultaneously improve chemical-use efficiency and create value from industrial by-products. Here, titanium gypsum (TiG), a calcium-rich industrial by-product, was upcycled into CaO2 nanoparticles (CaO2 NPs) and encapsulated in a sodium alginate/carboxymethyl chitosan/gelatin matrix to fabricate CaO2 hydrogel beads (CaO2 HBs) enabling pH-responsive swelling-controlled release. The biopolymer network served as a structural gate: protonation-driven contraction under acidic or near-neutral conditions restricted water access to CaO2, whereas alkaline deprotonation induced swelling and promoted CaO2 hydrolysis. This pH-responsive swelling-controlled response increased H2O2 accumulation under alkaline conditions while moderating alkaline shock, thereby reducing premature CaO2 consumption under non-target conditions.
