To address these limitations, this study introduces a novel pyridinecarboxamide-based (PA14) extraction system, featuring an elongated alkyl side chain that substantially enhances the oil solubility of extracted metal complexes and effectively eliminates emulsification. A continuous countercurrent extraction system comprising six extraction, six scrubbing, and seven stripping stages was developed and operated for over 480 h using real industrial leach liquor from spent NCM523 cathode materials. The system achieved over 99% recovery for both Ni and Co, yielding a strip liquor with 79 g/L Ni and 32 g/L Co, which, after di-(2-ethylhexyl) phosphoric acid (D2EHPA) purification, met battery-grade impurity specifications. Systematic parameter evaluation revealed that Fe(III) is co-extracted and migrates to the product stream, necessitating upstream removal or side-stream bleeding; feed acidity must be controlled below 0.1 mol/L to prevent protonation-induced emulsification; and elevated temperatures improve phase disengagement but reduce extraction efficiency, effects that are readily compensated by multistage configuration. Notably, the PA14 extractant demonstrated exceptional long-term stability over 800 h of continuous operation, with no detectable degradation, loss of extraction capacity, or metal poisoning. This work provides a complete, practical, and sustainable engineering solution for the clean recovery of valuable metals from spent NCM batteries, overcoming the bottlenecks of both extractability and process stability that have hindered prior chloride-based approaches.

title: CO2-triggered instantaneous weathering upcycles industrial solid wastes into safe land reclamation substrate
abstract: Pedogenic functionalization represents a promising strategy for the large-scale ecological reutilization of industrial solid wastes. However, the transformation of basic metallurgical slags into functional soil-like substrate is severely constrained by the sluggish kinetics of natural weathering. In this study, an accelerated aqueous CO2 weathering approach was developed to achieve the rapid structural reconstruction of basic steel slag (SS). Comprehensive multi-scale characterizations revealed a Dissolution-Repolymerization-Precipitation mechanism, in which CO2-induced cleavage of Ca-O-Si bonds promoted and then the formation of a hierarchical core-shell structure composed of neo-formed carbonates and a mesoporous silica-gel network. Consequently, the pH of SS decreased dramatically from 12.3 to 7.93, accompanied by the formation of a favorable toward a soil-like substrate. Moreover, the reconstructed mineral matrix enhanced ecological safety through the physical encapsulation and chemical immobilization of trace heavy metals. This study provides an efficient and scalable waste-to-Technosol pathway that integrates industrial solid waste valorisation, carbon capture, and ecological landscape restoration.

title: Dual-carbon goal oriented optimization of sustainable land use based on ST-GTNet model
abstract: Accurate estimation of carbon emissions is crucial for supporting China's strategic Dual-Carbon goals, which aim to reach a carbon peak by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). However, conventional estimation methods (land use coefficient-based and energy consumption-based approaches) significantly underestimate the potential of land use optimization in contributing to carbon neutrality. To address these limitations, a Land Use Carbon Emission Accounting and Spatial Pattern Assessment System (LUC-SPAS) framework is proposed. Firstly, the Spatio-Temporal GRU-Transformer Network (ST-GTNet) model was established, which couples historical carbon emission data and employs deep learning techniques within the neural network to establish a quantitative relationship between the land use pattern index and carbon emissions. Secondly, the Patch-based land use Simulation (PLUS) model projected land use from 2030 to 2060 under three scenarios: the Business-as-Usual Scenario (BAUS), the Crop Land Guarantee Scenario (CLGS), and the Sustainable Low-Carbon Development Scenario (LCDS). Finally, based on the trained ST-GTNet model and predicted land use pattern, future carbon emissions under three scenarios were predicted. Specifically, the ST-GTNet model achieves high accuracy (R2 = 0.89) in carbon-emission forecasting by harmonizing the temporal memory of GRU and the global spatial attention of Transformer. The study found that, under LCDS, through ecological restoration and compact urban growth, a 9.2% reduction in regional carbon emissions by 2060 compared with BAUS is achieved. The Shanghai-Nanjing-Hangzhou corridor is identified as a key decarbonization hotspot. This study presents a replicable GeoAI framework for predicting carbon emissions in urban agglomerations. The ST-GTNet model establishes a new paradigm for spatio-temporal GeoAI, bridging mechanistic knowledge and data-driven learning.

title: Toward a sustainable green campus: Short-term co-composting of cafeteria food waste and cow manure with an algae bio-scrubber
abstract: To promote a sustainable green campus, this study surveyed the composition of food waste and developed a predictive model at Kasetsart University. Subsequently, an aerobic co-composting experiment using food waste and cow manure was performed, alongside an assessment of CO2 utilization for algae cultivation using compost exhaust gas. Briefly, this study aimed to integrate food waste composting and CO2 exhaust mitigation via algae cultivation. Carbohydrates were identified as the dominant food waste component, exceeding 65%, and the prediction model accurately reproduced the dominant carbohydrate fraction, with lower accuracy for trace components. Composting was conducted at 45–60 °C to achieve thermophilic conditions. A correlation between cow manure proportion and pH was observed; compost with 30% manure had a pH of 6.17, whereas that with 10% manure had a pH of 4.82. Nutrient analysis showed that compost from 30% manure contained 1.48% phosphorus and 2.13% potassium, whereas compost with 10% manure had the highest nitrogen content (2.85%) and electrical conductivity (9.75 dS/m). Compost exhaust gas contained 0.05–0.128% CO2 by volume, while closed-loop microalgae bioreactors reached 0.18–0.20% CO2 due to gas recirculation that supported microalgal growth, indicating the potential use of compost exhaust gas for bio-scrubber-based algae cultivation. Exploratory metabarcoding of one pooled sample from the 30% treatment detected diverse bacterial and fungal taxa and generated predicted ecological guild annotations. These findings provide an initial microbial community profile that can guide future replicated studies of microbial dynamics and compost-associated functions. Overall, co-composting food waste with cow manure was effective at producing nutrient-rich compost, while the emitted CO2 supported algal growth and reduced CO2 emissions compared with conventional landfilling.

title: Mitigating seed sedimentation for sustainable sulfur hexafluoride hydrate formation using cyclopentane hydrate seeds
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) is a highly potent greenhouse gas with a long atmospheric lifetime, necessitating efficient and low-energy capture strategies. Hydrate-based SF6 capture has emerged as a promising alternative due to its low operating cost and high uptake capacity compared with conventional technologies. This study investigates a static hydrate-based SF6 capture process employing cyclopentane (CP) hydrate seeds and evaluates the synergistic effects of CP seeds and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) under varying driving force (DF) conditions. Visual observations revealed an unfavorable seed-drowning phenomenon under 5 K DF, where SF6 hydrate accumulation on CP seeds induced early sedimentation. Increasing CP seed concentration suppressed sedimentation by reducing the overall density and increasing the seed stability. Higher DF promoted vertical growth and wall adhesion, mitigating sedimentation even at low seed loadings. The optimized condition (0.0556 mol% CP seed and 500 ppm SDS, 10 K DF) achieved high SF6 uptake (51.009 mmol SF6/mol H2O) and rapid formation (t90 = 0.492 h) without retardation. Compared with agitated or porous media systems, the CP seed process achieved comparable uptake while exhibiting significantly lower energy demand and improved volumetric efficiency. These findings demonstrate the application of CP seeds to static SF6 hydrate formation while providing mechanistic design criteria for clean and feasible SF6 capture.

title: Integrating Supply Chain Life Cycle Decisions: Empirical model validation for a large-scale case
abstract: Companies are under growing pressure to improve the sustainability of their supply chains, yet quantifying and optimizing life cycle impacts remains challenging in practice. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) provides a standardized methodology for evaluating environmental impacts, but its integration with supply chain optimization has been limited in scope and scale. The Supply Chain Life Cycle Optimization (SCLCO) framework (Hülagü et al., 2025) addresses this gap by embedding LCA within a matrix-based optimization model that jointly considers environmental and economic objectives across the supply chain, for a small-scale and single-objective illustrative example. This paper presents the first large-scale, multi-objective empirical application of SCLCO, applied to a semi-finished aluminum rolled products manufacturer with 2294 customer orders and 51 alloy groups. The case study extends the generic SCLCO model (Hülagü et al., 2025) with case-specific formulations for a real-life industrial setting. It demonstrates the model’s capability to handle multifunctional processes by avoiding allocation (which the earlier mono-functional example could not evaluate) and integrates real-life company data with LCA databases within a unified data structure, tackling the heterogeneity and incompleteness issues inherent to industrial data. This matrix-based data structure proves effective for systematic data collection and cross-disciplinary communication between LCA and supply chain teams, making data gaps immediately visible. Moreover, computational experiments validate that the SCLCO model delivers actionable, data-driven sustainability insights for complex supply chains. Analysis of the Pareto-optimal solutions reveals a relationship between carbon footprint and cost that is governed by sourcing and energy decisions. Finally, sensitivity analyses confirm that the resulting supply chain configurations are robust to energy data variability and demonstrate that optimizing for different environmental indicators yields distinctly different optimal supply chain designs.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and drivers of agricultural ammonia emissions in China (1990–2020)
abstract: Agricultural ammonia (NH3) is an important precursor for the formation of atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in China. However, the long-term evolution and driving mechanisms of its emissions remain poorly understood, particularly at fine spatial scales. Based on the bottom-up emission factor approach, this study developed a county-level agricultural NH3 emission inventory of China for 1990–2020. The logarithmic mean Divisia index (LMDI) method was applied to quantitatively decompose the drivers of changes in agricultural NH3 emissions. From 1990 to 2020, total emissions rose from 6.15 Tg to 8.69 Tg. NH3 emissions from livestock production increased from 3.08 Tg to 4.90 Tg and gradually became the dominant emission source. Meanwhile, NH3 emissions from fertilizer application increased from 3.07 Tg to 3.79 Tg. Spatially, NH3 emission hotspots were concentrated in major agricultural regions, including the North China Plain, the Northeast China Plain, and the Sichuan Basin, with relatively high emissions also observed along basin margins in Northwest China. Driving factor decomposition results indicated that agricultural structural adjustments, technological and management improvements, and emission control policies exerted significant mitigating effects on agricultural NH3 emissions during different periods. For livestock production, promoting the development of intensive production systems is important. Regarding fertilizer application, sustained efforts are required to optimize fertilization practices. These findings provide scientific support for further exploiting the substantial potential for NH3 emission reduction in China.

title: Recovering bioactive components from waste sludge reinforces microbial interactions for resilient anaerobic wastewater treatment
abstract: Anaerobic treatment is an energy-efficient technology for industrial wastewater management, yet its practical application is often constrained by poor stability under inhibitory perturbations. Here, we recovered bioactive components from waste sludge to develop a bioregulatory material for enhancing the resilience of anaerobic reactor. Bioactive signaling molecules and biopolymers recovered from sludge were integrated with sludge-derived biochar to construct a bioregulatory scaffold (BioReg-SC) capable of slow signal release and efficient electron transfer. In a continuous up-flow anaerobic reactor operated for 185 days under repeated Congo red shocks, the BioReg-SC system maintained stable performance and rapidly restored chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal to 85.7% within 5 days, while sustaining methane production. The sustained release of signaling molecules, enabled by the biopolymer matrix, stimulated extracellular polymeric substances secretion and microbial aggregation, facilitating the formation of compact and stable sludge granules within 80 days. Meanwhile, the conductive carbon framework facilitated direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET), promoting the enrichment of electrogen (Geobacter) and DIET-capable methanogens (Methanothrix, Methanosarcina). Collectively, these functions established a coupled bioregulation-electron transfer mechanism that stabilizes microbial metabolism under long-term inhibitory stress. This work demonstrates a circular strategy recovering bioactive components from waste sludge to create functional bioregulators, providing a sustainable approach for resilient anaerobic wastewater treatment.

title: Consumers' intentions to return PET bottles in a hybrid waste management system: evidence from Vietnam
abstract: Despite the expansion of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) to reduce plastic waste in emerging economies, consumers’ return intentions in the hybrid formal–informal waste management systems remain insufficiently understood. This study extends the theory of planned behavior (TPB) by incorporating environmental concern, economic incentives, convenience of return, and perceptions of informal recycling to explain PET bottles return intentions. A dual-channel survey (online and face-to-face) was conducted in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, yielding 325 valid responses from January to March 2026. Employing covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM), several key findings emerge. Perceived behavioral control is the strongest predictor of return intention (β = 0.307, p < 0.001), followed by subjective norms (β = 0.219, p = 0.002) and attitude (β = 0.141, p = 0.033). Perceptions of informal recycling positively influence return intention (β = 0.129, p = 0.040). Rather than acting as a competitive barrier, positive perceptions of the informal sector serve as a complementary enabler that supports formal return intentions. These findings highlight the need for EPR policies to coordinate stakeholders across the entire value chain. It is essential to prioritize infrastructural accessibility and incorporate informal scrap dealers into official reverse logistics chains to achieve sustainable circularity.

title: Synergy or crowding-out? How the superposition of mitigation and adaptation policies shapes firm green innovation in China
abstract: Climate governance increasingly requires the simultaneous pursuit of mitigation and adaptation. However, whether their policy superposition promotes or constrains firm green innovation remains unclear. Drawing on Policy Mix Theory, this study applies a Double Machine Learning framework to analyze 11,012 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed firms (2005–2023), exploiting the overlapping implementation of the Low-Carbon City Pilot and the Climate-Resilient City Pilot. We find that the superposition of the two pilots generates policy synergy and significantly enhances firm green innovation (β = 0.259, p < 0.01), with a stronger response for invention patents (β = 0.319, p < 0.01) than for utility models. Mechanism analysis reveals that this dual-pilot superposition heightens managerial climate-risk attention (β = 0.099, p < 0.01) and increases government environmental subsidies (β = 1.300, p < 0.05). The synergy effect is concentrated among state-owned enterprises and financially unconstrained firms, is stronger in non-super-large cities and eastern regions, and is activated primarily when mitigation pressure is high but adaptation pressure is low. These heterogeneous responses across ownership types and regional conditions further suggest that the realization of such cross-objective policy synergies depends on firms’ absorptive capacity and the local institutional environment, factors largely overlooked in current policy-mix designs.

title: Thermodynamic analysis of biogas reforming for hydrogen production: A comparative investigation
abstract: Organic solid waste (OSW) can be valorized through anaerobic digestion, producing biogas as a renewable energy carrier while enabling efficient resource recovery. As biogas is primarily composed of CH4 and CO2, its conversion into hydrogen offers a promising pathway for both renewable energy production and greenhouse gas utilization. However, multiple thermochemical conversion routes have been proposed, and their relative advantages in terms of hydrogen production performance, carbon utilization, and energy consumption remain unclear. In this regard, three thermochemical pathways, namely methane decomposition (MD), dry reforming of methane (DRM), and combined steam and dry reforming of methane (CSDRM), are systematically evaluated using Aspen Plus to identify the most suitable process for hydrogen production from OSW−derived biogas. CSDRM represents the best comprehensive performance among the investigated pathways. In this process, the simultaneous steam and dry reforming reactions synergistically enhance methane conversion. The hydrogen concentration and hydrogen utilization efficiency achieve 57.9 vol % and 94.3 %, respectively, accompanied by the highest syngas yield of 127.9 kmol h−1. The hydrogen production rate of CSDRM increases by 34.9 % and 35.5 % compared with MD and DRM, respectively.

title: Tensor product fusion of LIBS and acoustic emission signals for waste identification in recycling
abstract: Accurate identification of recyclable waste is essential for efficient material recovery. However, existing spectroscopic studies have not fully addressed the combined challenges of integrating hierarchical identification requirements, representing subtle spectral differences, and effectively exploiting cross-modal complementarity. To address these gaps, this study develops a two-stage classification framework for recyclable waste, integrating laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and plasma acoustic emission signals (PAES). For coarse classification, a Difference–Summation Gramian Angular Field (DSGAF) encoding method transforms one-dimensional LIBS spectra into two-dimensional representations to enhance spectral discriminability. For fine subclassification, LIBS-derived elemental-composition information is combined with complementary physical-response information carried by PAES. Mutual information (MI) and Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) are used for feature selection, and a LIBS–PAES Tensor Product Enhancement (LPTE) method is introduced to explicitly exploit cross-modal interactions. The DSGAF-based 2DCNN increased the independent-test accuracy from 91.11% to 98.48% for classifying recyclable waste into paper–wood, glass, plastic, metal, and textile categories. For fine subclassification of plastic, metal, and textile waste, the MI_LPTE model achieved accuracies above 99% and outperformed unimodal and conventional fusion models. These results demonstrate the potential of hierarchical LIBS–PAES sensing for recyclable-waste sorting and material recovery.

title: Distributionally robust capacity co-planning for transportation-power nexus with mixed traffic considering autonomous vehicles
abstract: Carbon neutrality targets worldwide drive the integration of electric transportation and renewable energy sources (RES), increasing the spatiotemporal interdependencies between transportation networks and power distribution networks. Meanwhile, cross-system multi-source uncertainties in traffic charging loads and RES generation create challenges for capacity planning and low-carbon economic operation of renewable-based transportation-power nexus (TPN). This work proposes a hierarchical cross-disciplinary capacity co-planning framework for TPN. The planning layer optimizes the sizing of TPN infrastructures to balance economic performance, carbon reduction goals, and operational resilience. The operational layer describes coordinated cross-network scheduling. Traffic flow is formulated as a mixed user equilibrium-system optimal (UE-SO) model with asymmetric elastic travel demand, which captures behavioral differences between conventional human-driven vehicles and autonomous electric vehicles. The complementarity constraints of the UE-SO equilibrium are transformed into equivalent variational inequalities and solved via a projection-contraction algorithm. To characterize uncertainties in travel demand and RES output, an empirical ambiguity set constrained jointly by 1-norm and infinity-norm distances is constructed and integrated into a data-driven two-stage distributionally robust optimization model. A tailored column-and-constraint generation algorithm is adopted for the resulting min–max–min problem. In addition, a fast adaptive alternating direction method of multipliers is developed to support distributed coordination with reduced information between the transportation and power networks. Numerical case studies demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model and algorithm to larger test systems, and identify several coordination mechanisms supporting carbon reduction and renewable energy integration.

title: Unveiling driving factors of carbon emissions in the iron and steel industry from the perspective of energy-material-economy nexus
abstract: Controlling carbon emissions from the iron and steel industry (ISI) involves a multidimensional network interlaced by energy systems, material flows, and economic demand. However, these three perspectives are rarely well integrated to present a comprehensive understanding of the overall generation mechanism of ISI's carbon emission and the multidimensional driving factors in previous studies. To address this issue, this study developed an integrated carbon emission calculation framework based on the energy-material-economy nexus by combining production-side Material-Energy-Carbon Flow Analysis (MECFA) and a consumption-side Input-Output (IO) method, and applied it to China's ISI (CISI). Within the framework, we established the formula for Carbon emissions from Iron and Steel industry based on the Energy-Material-Economy nexus (CISEME) to explicitly represent the mathematical linkages among material production, energy consumption, and economic demand, thereby enabling the simultaneous decomposition and consistent comparison of driving factors across these three systems. Based on the CISEME formula, the carbon emissions from CISI were measured and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) method was applied to reveal the comparable impacts of various driving factors on carbon emissions from 2007 to 2022. The results show that, the coke-intensive blast furnace (BF) process accounted for over 60% of carbon emissions, while final demand was the dominant driver of emission growth over 68% during the study period, together highlighting the importance of coordinating supply- and demand-side measures for carbon mitigation. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in diagnosing structural emission drivers and providing insights into coordinated supply- and demand-side mitigation strategies for the low-carbon transition of the ISI.

title: Leveraging blockchain for sustainable agro-food Systems: A hierarchical analysis of critical implementation
abstract: A framework for identifying and analyzing the Blockchain Enablers (BEs) necessary for sustainability in Agro-Food Supply Chains (AFSCs) is developed in this work. The methodology integrates Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) with the fuzzy MICMAC technique, classifying a set of 22 specific enablers according to their driving and dependent powers. Results from the analysis identify foundational enablers, including traceability and transparency, as structurally central to the enabler system underlying core AFSC challenges related to perishability, environmental impact, and food safety. The primary contributions are twofold: a context-specific classification of BEs for AFSCs, and a structural model mapping their interdependencies to inform strategic prioritization. The findings offer supply chain practitioners a structured basis for deploying blockchain technology to enhance sustainability performance.

title: Achieving urban green transformation in China: Pathways based on multidimensional urban characteristics
abstract: Advancing urban green transformation (UGT) is a central strategy for addressing climate and environmental degradation, yet its progression is shaped by multidimensional urban characteristics. Existing studies on UGT evaluation often overlook interdependencies among indicators and predominantly adopt single-causality perspectives when examining relationships with selected urban characteristics (e.g., digital economy, urbanization rate). To fill these gaps, this work constructs a theoretical framework for UGT evaluation based on the Pressure–State–Response theory from the perspective of the synergy among carbon reduction, pollution control, greening, and economic growth, and proposes an integrated multicriteria decision-making and modified coupling coordination degree model evaluation approach. Furthermore, multiple AI methods are combined to examine the non-linear relationships and interaction effects between UGT and multidimensional urban characteristics, and to identify systematic pathways for advancing UGT. The findings indicate that: (1) the average UGT level increased from 0.665 in 2010 to 0.716 in 2024, with a structural transition from primary to moderate synergy stages and persistent spatial clustering that shifted from Northeast China toward developed coastal regions; (2) among 27 initially selected urban characteristics, 14 key features are identified through a LASSO–Boruta procedure for model development; (3) the CatBoost model outperforms benchmark models in predictive accuracy and in capturing complex relationships; (4) SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals that all 14 features exhibit threshold-dependent non-linear relationships with UGT, accompanied by significant synergistic or antagonistic interaction effects; and (5) based on Interpretative Structural Modeling and Bayesian Network framework, two dominant pathways for advancing UGT are identified—namely, a digitalization- and AI-oriented pathway and a high-quality financial development pathway—based on which targeted policy implications are proposed.

title: Topographic constraints and economic centrality jointly condition building material stock distribution: high-resolution evidence from the Sichuan-Chongqing region
abstract: As lowland developable land diminishes, urban expansion increasingly encroaches on hillsides and rugged terrain, yet the physical constraints of topography on the accumulation of building material stocks (MS) remain insufficiently quantified. Using the Sichuan-Chongqing Region as a case, we constructed a 30-m resolution building MS inventory and applied XGBoost with Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attribution to examine the nonlinear relationships between building MS, terrain, and economic centrality. Our results reveal that gentle slopes, which account for 61% of urban land, accommodate 68.4% of building MS, thereby demonstrating a strong low-gradient preference. In plain-dominated Chengdu, building MS density exceeds 1.0 Mt/km2 across gentle gradients, whereas in hilly Chongqing, building MS are concentrated on scarce valley floors, and stock density decreases by approximately 75% as slope increases. In Chongqing, non-residential stocks occurred on gentler terrain than residential stocks, with average deposition slopes of 6.9° and 7.7°, respectively. Among structural types, reinforced-concrete stocks occurred on gentler terrain than brick-concrete and brick-wood stocks, with corresponding average slopes of 6.9°, 8.4°, and 9.9°. Machine learning attribution reveals that economic centrality exerts a stronger influence near Chongqing's urban core, whereas the contribution of slope increases toward the periphery, reflecting a spatial transition from continuous urban development to fragmented, valley-based accumulation of building MS.

title: Optimal strategy selection for green logistics and decarbonization for sustainable household plastic waste logistics networks
abstract: Household plastic waste management is increasingly recognized as a critical challenge for green logistics, decarbonization, and circular urban waste systems. This study develops an application-oriented intuitionistic fuzzy decision-support framework for selecting sustainable household plastic waste logistics strategies. It provides an application-oriented decision-support structure for evaluating conflicting criteria and uncertain expert judgments. The proposed framework combines Intuitionistic Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (IF-SWARA) and Intuitionistic Fuzzy Compromise Ranking of Alternatives from Distance to Ideal Solution (IF-CRADIS). The criteria are determined through a detailed literature review and an expert panel comprising academicians and engineers who have researched similar subjects. IF-SWARA is used to determine the relative importance of 16 criteria grouped into environmental, operational, economic, and social dimensions, while IF-CRADIS ranks 5 practical strategy alternatives. The results show that the environmental criterion emerged as the most influential factor, with a weight of 0.269. The operational criterion is determined to be the second most vital criterion for this, with a weight of 0.263. Collection rate and capture efficiency, greenhouse gas emission reduction potential, and landfill diversion and residual waste reduction are identified as the most important sub-criteria. The municipality-producer-recycler collaboration platform is selected as the best strategy, followed by the deposit-refund and buy-back system. Robustness was examined through alternative expert-weighting schemes, leave-one-expert-out tests, fuzzy-model checks, Monte Carlo weight perturbations, criterion-dependency tests, and cross-method comparison. S5 remained first in all major tests, and IF-TOPSIS, IF-VIKOR, and IF-MARCOS reproduced the same ranking. The findings provide a stable decision-support basis for low-carbon and circular household plastic waste logistics planning.

title: Rising food production and persistent inequality over global border areas: A conflict between growth and distribution
abstract: Political borders divide governance, yet food systems and environmental risks transcend them, creating distinct borderland food security vulnerabilities. Rapid population growth may further intensify local production-demand mismatches, which have not yet been deeply understood. Here, we integrated geographic data and an interpretable machine learning model (XGBoost-SHAP) with the SSP-RCP framework to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the spatio-temporal dynamics, driving factors, and future projections of food security in global border areas. Between 2000 and 2020, total crop production in border areas increased by over 68%, reaching 4.79 × 108 t in 2020, with per capita crop production rising from 0.29 to 0.35 t, still below the global average (0.38 t). The population-weighted Gini coefficient of local crop production in border areas increased from 0.41 to 0.51, signifying a marked increase in inequality. Elevation and population each contributed over 12% to boosting crop production, whereas geopolitical conflicts showed strongly negative model contributions. Under the sustainability pathway with low radiative forcing (SSP126) and the fossil-fueled development pathway with high radiative forcing (SSP585), the share of border populations facing local production shortfalls approaches zero by 2100. By contrast, under the regional-rivalry pathway (SSP370), population growth exceeds production, leaving more than half of the border population in areas where local production cannot meet estimated demand. This study highlights the urgent necessity for targeted policies to address food distribution imbalances and enhance sustainable development in border regions.

title: NMR insights of pore oil mobilization and redistribution by CO2 flooding under varied pressures and injection rates
abstract: In this work, CO2 flooding experiments were conducted under different pore pressures and injection rates to investigate pore oil mobilization and residual oil redistribution using low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Three displacement patterns were observed under different pore pressures during the vertical downward CO2 flooding process: completely stable displacement, partially stable displacement, and unstable displacement. As the injection rate increases, the fingering behavior is further enhanced, which is associated with enhanced viscous forces and reduced flow stability. For pores of different scales, residual oil in large pores is reduced due to dynamic flushing, whereas oil mobilization in medium and small pores depends more strongly on the mass transfer time. High-rate injection shortens the CO2-oil mass transfer time and promotes channeling and bypassing, thereby increasing residual oil after displacement. A comparison of residual oil distribution characteristics under different conditions reveals pronounced pore-size selectivity. Therefore, injection-production parameters should be optimized by balancing the displacement driving force and CO2-oil mass transfer time. This study provides guidance for improving oil recovery and optimizing injection parameters.

title: Genetic algorithm-driven optimization and scaling-up of a thin-layer fountain photobioreactor for efficient, cost-effective and sustainable Spirulina sp. production
abstract: Microalgae represent a promising solution for carbon sequestration and sustainable products of biochemicals. However, large-scale microalgae application is still constrained by high production costs. The thin-layer fountain photobioreactors (TLF-PBRs) have demonstrated enhanced productivity and low costs, but their designs remain limited to small scale (<2 m2) and intensive volumetric mixing energy consumption (6272 W m−3). Herein, this study addressed this bottleneck through a genetic algorithm optimized fountain pump layouts in a 12.0 m diameter cylindrical TLF-PBR (113 m2), designed to maximize spray coverage while reducing energy consumption. The optimal layout, including five 100 W peripheral pumps and one 75 W central pump, achieved an effective spray coverage ratio of 92.81% at a volumetric mixing energy consumption of 152.2 ± 0.3 W m−3, which was 40-fold lower than lab-scale versions. Outdoor cultivation of Spirulina sp. yielded a maximum areal productivity of 16.83 ± 0.51 g m−2·day−1, representing improvements of 28.2% and 42.3% over the thin-layer cascade system (TLCS) and open pond, respectively. Based on techno-economic analysis, the biomass production cost at a 20-ha production scale was estimated at $2.27 per kg, which is lower than that of the open pond ($3.27 per kg) and the TLCS ($2.52 per kg). Although the outdoor cultivation data were collected over a limited short-term period and the techno-economic projections rely on model-based scale-up assumptions requiring further validation through extended pilot trials and commercial-scale operation, this work successfully scales up the TLF-PBR beyond 100 m2, demonstrating its strong potential as a high-efficiency, cost-effective and sustainable platform.

title: How the Pollutant Discharge Permit system drives firms’ green transformation: evidence from supply chains
abstract: Amid China's “dual carbon” targets, transforming supply chains toward more sustainable and environmentally efficient operations has become a central concern in environmental governance. Drawing on matched firm-level data covering Chinese listed companies and their major trading partners over the 2012–2023 period, this study leverages the rollout of the Pollutant Discharge Permit (PDP) policy as an exogenous policy shock to identify its transmission effects along supply chains. The empirical results indicate that regulatory constraints imposed on downstream customers are positively associated with greener practices among their upstream suppliers, suggesting that environmental policies may generate potential spillover effects through supply chain linkages. These findings remain robust to alternative measures of green transformation and to additional checks addressing potential concerns related to sample structure and other robustness tests. Further analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity across firm characteristics, geographical proximity, and bargaining power. Specifically, the spillover effect is more pronounced among large-scale or heavily polluting supplier firms, between geographically closer upstream-downstream pairs, and when customers hold stronger bargaining power than their suppliers. Mechanism analysis suggests that customers' environmental regulations affect their suppliers' green transformation primarily through two channels: investment-related knowledge spillovers and environmental awareness spillovers. These findings uncover the transmission mechanisms of environmental regulation within production networks, providing novel empirical support for the formulation of more effective policy frameworks, thereby fostering coordinated emission reduction across supply chains.

title: Diffusion dynamics of smartphone trade-in strategies under government intervention: A complex network evolutionary game approach incorporating prospect theory
abstract: The rapid expansion of the smartphone industry and the surge in e-waste highlight the need for effective Trade-in (TI) programs. To examine the diffusion of TI strategies among smartphone enterprises, this study develops a complex network evolutionary game model that integrates government intervention, enterprise pricing, consumer demand, and network topology. The baseline model is further extended by incorporating prospect theory to capture bounded rationality, comparing four canonical network structures, conducting external benchmarking with aggregate public evidence, and performing joint parameter sensitivity analyses. Regulatory intervention generally promotes TI diffusion, although a conditional diffusion ceiling may persist under certain parameter settings, suggesting that stricter enforcement alone may not ensure full market saturation. Government subsidies and enterprise social reputation further facilitate early-stage diffusion, but their marginal effects gradually weaken. Meanwhile, a larger share of green consumers and a broader network scale support TI adoption, although their effects remain bounded, whereas pricing strategies create a competitive trade-off between TI and Non-Trade-in (NTI) adopters. The prospect theory extension shows that loss aversion emerges as an influential behavioral factor, whereas psychological discounting weakens the effect of abstract social reputation. Comparisons across four canonical network topologies indicate that long-run adoption remains broadly stable, while external benchmarking and joint sensitivity analyses further support the plausibility and robustness of the main findings. Overall, large-scale TI adoption may benefit from coordinated regulatory enforcement, adaptive subsidies, and behavior-oriented signals. This study provides model-dependent implications for improving smartphone recycling systems and resource-efficient industrial development.

title: Identifying user engagement conditions for scaling returnable food packaging in Türkiye: A product–service system design perspective
abstract: Returnable systems, a business-operated form of reusable packaging, are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to disposables. However, in Türkiye, their adoption remains limited, particularly in the rapidly expanding food-delivery sector where widely implemented solutions are still absent. This study investigates the conditions shaping user engagement with returnable packaging in the Turkish context from a product–service system (PSS) design perspective. A mixed-methods approach was employed: semi-structured interviews identified key engagement factors which enable or hinder participation, followed by a survey using pairwise comparisons to evaluate their relative importance using representative examples. The findings show that material health (28.8%) and hygiene (26.3%) emerge as the most critical criteria for acceptance. System reliability (14.9%) plays a mediating role by shaping trust in both safety and environmental claims. Environmental impact (11.3%) functions primarily as a motivating factor for participation, while experiential qualities, including system usability and understandability, and packaging functionality and appearance (18.6% combined), shape system interaction and reinforce desirability. Overall, this study identifies context-specific conditions shaping early-stage user engagement with returnable packaging by interpreting how empirically identified factors relate to one another within everyday practices. The study also provides design and policy implications for scalable returnable packaging services by identifying priorities for developing PSSs. These priorities highlight the need for trustworthy return systems that ensure hygienic practices, health-safe packaging materials, and credible environmental benefits, while also emphasizing the design of product–service experiences that are convenient and meaningful for users.

title: Systematic evaluation and optimization of seawater mineral carbonation pathways for net-negative emissions and valorization of carbonate products
abstract: Seawater mineral carbonation (SMC) offers a pathway to couple CO2 removal with stable carbonate formation, yet its scalability is constrained by system-level trade-offs: alkali-source routes incur high upstream burdens, while electrochemical pathways eliminate reagents at the expense of electricity and capital intensity. Here, we evaluate eight SMC pathways using a unified framework integrating life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA). We show that alkali-based and bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED)-driven routes are limited by distinct bottlenecks. To address this, we propose various integrated configurations, including INT2 that decouples alkalinity generation from ion recovery by producing Na2CO3 via BMED and using it to precipitate Ca2+/Mg2+ from seawater. INT2 delivers the lowest energy demand among electricity-driven options and requires ∼63% renewable electricity to achieve net-zero emissions. Techno-economic-environmental results further highlight the critical role of product valorization, particularly MgCO3·3H2O and CaCO3, in offsetting costs, with INT2 exhibiting the most robust overall performance. These findings underscore that the viability of SMC hinges on system-level integration.

title: Comparison of NIR and Raman spectroscopy for determining used cooking oil properties using chemometric methods
abstract: This study compares the performance of near-infrared (NIR) and Raman spectroscopy in the quantitative analysis of used cooking oil (UCO), focusing on critical parameters such as acid value, density, and kinematic viscosity. Monitoring these properties ensures that the feedstock meets the necessary specifications for optimal biofuel production, contributing to the sustainability and performance of the final product. NIR and Raman spectroscopy offers significant advantages by enabling rapid, real-time and non-destructive measurements of several properties at once. Partial least squares (PLS) was employed, enabling the correlation between reference results and spectral information obtained by NIR and Raman spectroscopy. NIR spectroscopy demonstrated superior performance compared to Raman spectroscopy in analyzing UCO properties. Results revealed the better performance of NIR spectroscopy for the measurement of acid value (R2P = 0.99, RMSEP = 0.087 mg KOH g⁻¹, RPD = 8.12), and kinematic viscosity at 40 °C (R2P = 0.97, RMSEP = 0.325 mm²/s, and RPD = 5.20). Raman spectroscopy was pointed out as the most suitable for the determination of density at 15 °C (R2P = 0.97, RMSEP = 0.167 kg m⁻³, RPD = 4.20). However, both techniques presented excellent results and are suitable for the accurate determination of UCO propreties.

title: Extraction of soil nutrient information from visible and near-infrared signals using deep learning models
abstract: This study aims to combine the deep learning algorithm and the visible and near-infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy technology to build a soil nutrient information extraction model. A deep learning framework based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is proposed to establish optimal calibration model for the analysis of the full range of Vis-NIR spectral data. Moreover, an influence function is designed to select the informative wavelength variables, which is an important goal in engineering application of spectroscopy for reducing the model dimensionality and enhancing model robustness. Experiment was performed for the prediction of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) contents of soil. The modeling results showed that the proposed model could improve the modeling efficiency of soil nutrient information extraction, and also obtained higher accuracy in the modeling and predictive procedures than the conventional model. This will provide effective response to the challenges in engineering applications, to promote the Vis-NIR spectroscopy technology be applied for fast detection, and to obtain robust models with high precisions in soil nutrient information extraction process.

title: Decoding brain tumor patterns in MRI images: Unleashing optimized insights with Progressive Wasserstein generative adversarial network
abstract: Brain tumor (BT) detection and segmentation are of vital importance for accurate diagnosis, but are still difficult because of intricate brain anatomy, non-spherical tumor shapes, and low contrast of MRI images. Conventional manual methods are time-consuming and invasive with observer variability, whereas traditional machine learning (ML) approaches based on handcrafted features tend to miss subtle patterns of tumor areas. Even the deep learning (DL) models like CNNs, despite their effectiveness, have limitations such as high computation expenses, poor generalization to heterogeneous data, and complexity in delineating tumor boundaries accurately, which are subtle. These drawbacks are sought to be overcome by this manuscript, suggesting an innovative technique for automatic BT detection in MRI samples. Initially, the normalized gamma corrected contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (NG-CCLAHE) is introduced for enhancing the MRI image quality. Then, the Faster 2D-Otsu Thresholding technique is introduced for segmenting the tumor regions from the MRI samples. Followed by this, the synchroextracting Transform (SET) technique is employed to extract features, which are then optimized with an Improved Ladybug Beetle Optimization Algorithm (ILBOA). The improved features are fed into the PWGAN, allowing for more accurate and effective tumor detection. Experimental assessment using the Br35H Brain Tumor Detection 2020 dataset reflects high-level performance with 98.6 % accuracy, 92 % DSC, 95 % PDR, 23 % classification error, 37.8s computation time, and an F1-score of 98.59 %. These aspects identify the proposed approach's efficiency and competency in brain tumor patterns from MRI images.

title: Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy and improved parallel factor framework-clustering analysis for oil spill type identification and concentration quantification
abstract: Oil spills hidden below the sea surface and in a suspended state are known as submerged oil. Determining the source of an oil spill and evaluating the amount of oil spilled can provide a basis for the effective development of oil spill emergency response strategies and policies. Because of this, this paper proposes an oil spill species identification and concentration quantification analytical method based on the combination of time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy (TRFS) and improved parallel factor framework-clustering analysis (IPFFCA). The IPFFCA model first decomposes the oil TRFS data to extract the loading matrix and reconstructs the landscape maps corresponding to each component based on the loading matrix. Subsequently, the non-negative least squares algorithm was employed to fit the component landscape maps to the unfolded actual spectra, thereby estimating the score matrix of the samples. Building upon this, the score matrix was used as input to develop oil species identification and concentration quantification models via particle swarm optimization support vector machine (PSO-SVM) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), respectively. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed analytical method, six typical submerged oil samples were experimentally prepared, and their TRFS data were collected and analyzed. The experimental results show that the analytical method proposed in this paper achieves 92 % accuracy in the oil species identification task, the average coefficient of determination of the concentration prediction in the validation set of the six types of samples reaches 0.95, and the root mean square error is 0.08, indicating strong predictive performance.

title: Enhancing IoT anomaly detection with the Dwarf Mongoose-Chaos optimized deep belief framework
abstract: Anomaly detection is essential for identifying deviations from normal patterns in data, enabling the detection of security breaches or system faults, particularly in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. However, traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods often struggle with the dynamic and complex nature of IoT environments, where attack patterns are non-linear, continuously evolving, and context-dependent. These models typically require large labeled datasets and retraining to adapt to new threats, which limits their responsiveness and scalability. Additionally, their high computational demands make real-time deployment on resource-constrained IoT devices challenging. Furthermore, many ML/DL models exhibit poor generalization, performing well in controlled scenarios but failing to maintain accuracy across diverse, real-world IoT settings with varying devices, protocols, and data distributions. To address these issues, this work proposes the Dwarf Mongoose-Chaos Optimized Deep Belief (DCODB) Framework, which combines advanced preprocessing, feature selection (FS), and classification techniques. Initial preprocessing involves Min-Max Normalization and One-Hot Encoding to scale numerical features and transform categorical data for effective model input. FS is optimized by the novel Dwarf Mongoose-Chaos Fusion Optimization (DMCFO), which is a swarm intelligence algorithm that leverages chaotic maps to improve the effectiveness of the Dwarf Mongoose Optimization Algorithm (DMO), reducing dimensionality and improving classification accuracy. The refined features are then classified using a Deep Belief Network (DBN), which processes hierarchical feature representations to differentiate between normal and anomalous behaviors in the NSL-KDD dataset. The proposed framework has been thoroughly assessed using diverse metrics, demonstrating its effectiveness in anomaly detection by achieving above 99 % Balanced Accuracy, along with exceptional Precision, Recall, F1 Score, Specificity, and the AUC-ROC curve. These high-performance metrics affirm the model's capability to deliver reliable and scalable anomaly detection in IoT environments, strengthening overall security.

title: A reliable deep neural network using the radial basis for the spreading virus in computers with kill signals
abstract:
Purpose
The purpose of this work is to provide a reliable neural network process for the spreading virus in computers with kill signals. The mathematical model shows susceptible, exposed, infected individuals to form the virus inactive, and kill signals classes.
Method
A structure of deep neural network (DNN) is designed by using two different hidden layers having radial basis activation functions in both layers, optimization through the Bayesian regularization, twenty and thirty numbers of neurons in primary and secondary hidden layers for the spreading virus in computers with kill signals. The stochastic DNN framework is presented to solve the spreading virus in computers with kill signals by selecting the data for training as 70 %, and 15 %, 15 % for both validation and testing.
Results
The accuracy of the scheme is observed through the overlapping of the solutions along with negligible absolute error for solving the model. The consistency of the solver is observed through the process of error histogram, regression, and state transition.
Novelty
The proposed DNN structure having radial basis activation function has never been applied for the spreading virus in computers with kill signals.

title: Impact of converting graphs into spanning trees on node and graph classification in Graph Neural Network
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of graph reduction to their spanning trees on Graph Neural Network (GNN) performance in node and graph classification across six GNN architectures. The proposed approach leverages spanning trees for graph sparsification while preserving critical structural information, achieving performance comparable to or better than full-graph models. A theoretical connection is established between edge sampling via determinantal point processes (DPPs) and the transfer-current matrix, showing minimum spanning trees effectively approximate DPP-selected subgraphs. Four edge-weighting schemes are analyzed such that their sparsification trade-offs are revealed. The method consistently reduces memory usage and computation while maintaining accuracy. Findings indicate that spanning tree pruning offers a scalable, theoretically grounded strategy for efficient GNN training without compromising classification accuracy. Experiments on node classification benchmarks (Cora, Citeseer, PubMed, PPI) and graph classification biological and chemical datasets (AIDS, MUTAG, PROTEINS, NCI1, IMDB-BINARY) demonstrate excellent graph classification results, notably 98.27% accuracy on AIDS, with reduced computational overhead.

title: A combination of gas detection system and adaptive deep learning network (GFC-Net) to identify different production batches of beer
abstract: Even for products of the same brand, the quality of beer may vary across different production batches. Strict quality testing is essential to ensure product consistency, safety, and consumer satisfaction. In this work, an e-nose system, combined with the proposed deep learning algorithm, achieves the qualitative identification of beers from different production batches. First, the e-nose system is applied to acquire the gas information of beers from different production batches. Then, to comprehensively extract features characterizing the gas information, a fusion computational module that integrates local and global features from convolution and self-attention mechanism is proposed, called the Gas Features Calculation Module (GFCM). Finally, a Gas Features Classification Network (GFC-Net) is designed to enable the adaptive identification of beers from different production batches. Through structural optimization, ablation experiments, and comparison with state-of-the-art gas classification methods, GFC-Net achieves an accuracy of 98.50 %, a precision of 98.70 %, and a recall of 98.58 %. The integration of gas information that characterizes the overall chemical quality, along with GFC-Net, enables the qualitative identification of beers from different batches, providing an effective approach for quality monitoring.

title: Machine learning and evolutionary computation on e-nose datasets: A preliminary approach to ergot alkaloid detection in wheat
abstract: To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first time that an approach based on the use of machine learning (ML) algorithms combined with genetic programming (GP) was used to process small-sample-size e-nose data. The approach was proposed to classify the volatile compound information of wheat samples based on the contamination of ergot alkaloids, a class of emerging mycotoxins which pose a severe threat to food safety and consumer health. Unlike previous studies that applied convolutional neural networks to full e-nose response profiles, our approach focused on a small set of features extracted from the steady-state region of each response curve. Despite the low dimensionality, using GP to generate optimal features significantly improved the classification performance of several ML models. Different classifiers, including Decision Tree, Linear Discriminant Analysis, the Mahalanobis Distance Classifier, an artificial neural network-based method and ensemble methods were assessed and applied to a dataset of 21 wheat samples. These samples were classified according to their compliance with the EU maximum limit of 150 μg/kg for ergot alkaloids in wheat. The combined application of GP-based feature transformations, specifically using M3GP, and ML classifiers resulted in significant improvements in accuracy, F1 score, precision and recall compared to models trained on untransformed features. These findings highlight the unexplored potential of GP as a powerful tool for feature construction in sensor-based classification tasks for food safety signal processing.

title: Nondestructive detection of total flavonoids content in daylily using Vis-NIR and NIR hyperspectral imaging: data fusion combined with SHAP for model interpretability
abstract: Flavonoids, vital bioactive compounds in daylily (a nutritionally and medicinally valuable food), have antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antidepressant properties, which boost its nutritional value, health benefits, and quality. Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) for detecting trace flavonoids usually uses single systems, failing to leverage multispectral complementarity and restricting detection performance. This study integrates a data fusion strategy with two HSI techniques (visible–near-infrared (Vis-NIR) and near-infrared (NIR)) for the non-destructive detection of total flavonoids content (TFC) in daylily. The investigation employed partial least squares regression (PLSR) and least squares support vector machine (LS-SVM) for spectral data. Additionally, data-level and feature-level fusion strategies are implemented for data fusion modeling, while the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) methodology is used to comprehensively evaluate spectral feature contribution rates. The findings demonstrate that modeling based on the fusion strategy of LS-SVM yields substantially superior results compared to single-system approaches. Notably, the Mid-level fusion model incorporating competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) and LS-SVM demonstrates optimal performance. The determination coefficient (R2P), root mean square prediction error (RMSEP) and residual prediction deviation (RPD) of the prediction set were 0.9332, 0.0186 and 3.3560, respectively. This study confirms the feasibility of HSI technology in non-destructively detecting flavonoids in daylily. Furthermore, the collaborative optimization of multi-spectral HSI systems through a data fusion strategy effectively enhances the accuracy of non-destructive flavonoids detection. This study presents innovative technical approaches for non-destructive trace substance detection and agricultural product quality and safety monitoring, thereby providing essential technical support for developing intelligent agricultural product quality and safety monitoring systems.

title: Environment aging analysis of animal bloodstains with ATR-FTIR and CNN
abstract: Bloodstain analysis is a critical component of forensic science, particularly for determining the time of deposition and understanding the effects of environmental conditions on evidence. This study presents an innovative bloodstains environment aging model, which integrates attenuated total reflection fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) with a convolutional neural network (CNN) optimized using the black-winged kite algorithm. Bloodstains from common sources (pig, cow, and chicken) were analyzed under varying environmental conditions, including temperature fluctuations (0 °C, 40 °C, 100 °C) and simulated sunlight exposure, across multiple aging periods (1, 2, 4, 8 days). Spectral data obtained through ATR-FTIR scanning served as the input for the optimized CNN, enabling precise differentiation and classification of bloodstains based on aging and environmental factors. The model achieved high predictive accuracy, with 97.86 % for pig blood, 95.47 % for cow blood, and 97.15 % for chicken blood under 0 °C conditions, demonstrating its robustness and reliability in forensic applications. Additionally, this research highlights the potential for integrating spectroscopic data with advanced deep learning techniques to enhance forensic methodologies. By improving accuracy, accessibility, and cost-effectiveness, this work represents a significant advancement in bloodstain analysis and forensic science.

title: Advanced hyperparameter optimization for lung cancer detection using DenseBeetle network
abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, underscoring the urgent need for accurate and early detection to improve patient outcomes. However, current detection systems often struggle with issues like elevated false-positive rates and insufficient feature extraction. These challenges largely stem from the visual resemblance between nodules and nearby tissues, as well as the inability of conventional models to effectively capture the complex features of pulmonary nodules. This research presents a deep learning-based approach for identifying lung nodules in CT images. The framework incorporates advanced preprocessing steps such as Gaussian filtering and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization to enhance image sharpness and overall visual quality. A Residual Pyramid Attention-Enhanced DenseNet201, integrated with SE and CBAM modules, is used for effective feature extraction, while a sigmoid function supports binary classification. Hyperparameter tuning is performed using a novel optimizer based on Latin Hypercube Sampling and Mean Differential Variation. Evaluated on LUNA16 dataset with 888 CT scans, the model reached 98.7 % accuracy, 99.2 % sensitivity, and a 95.38 % F1-score on the test set. The framework significantly reduces false positives and demonstrates strong generalization for clinical lung cancer identification.

title: Feature extraction using differential amplification singular value decomposition in Vis–NIR spectroscopy: Application to cigarette brand identification
abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of cigarette brands is crucial for combating counterfeiting and protecting tax revenue. Vis–NIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning is a promising identification method. Nevertheless, redundant information abounds in high-dimensional spectral data, which affects classification accuracy. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel feature extraction method ― Differential amplification singular value decomposition (DA-SVD). This method optimizes the feature projection direction by amplifying both the individual differences among samples and the overall differences between classes, thereby achieving effective dimensionality reduction of spectral data. By applying DA-SVD, the classification accuracy of KNN, SVM, and RF models on the test set significantly increased from 36 %, 34 %, and 30 % (based on the original data) to 98 % for all models, with precision, sensitivity, and F1 score reaching 97.86 %, 98.14 %, and 97.86 %, respectively, and all outperforming conventional feature extraction methods such as LDA, SVD, and PCA. The experimental results further demonstrated that DA-SVD could achieve satisfactory classification performance without additional preprocessing steps (outlier detection and spectral denoising). In addition, the 10-fold cross-validation results confirmed the stability of the DA-SVD method, and validation on public datasets further demonstrated its generalization ability and applicability. Overall, DA-SVD provides an efficient and robust feature extraction strategy that, when combined with machine learning, enables reliable cigarette brand identification and has broad potential for other spectroscopic applications.

title: Decentralized federated learning enables privacy-preserving NIR spectroscopy calibration: A proof-of-concept study
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is a key analytical tool across industries, providing fast, non-destructive measurements. However, traditional centralized models face key challenges regarding data privacy, instrument heterogeneity, and limited inter-institutional collaboration. We present a decentralized federated learning (DFL) system for NIR spectroscopy that enables institutions to collaboratively train accurate models without sharing raw data. The proposed system combines standardized spectral preprocessing with lightweight communication protocols to achieve modeling efficiency and data confidentiality. Extensive experiments were conducted on augmented Corn and Gasoline datasets using PLSR, SVR, and 1D-CNN models. In our simulations, we modeled a network of 30 clients communicating via a ring topology and applied FedProx regularization (μ = 0.1). The proposed DFL system produces predictions within 5–8 % of centralized results, while its architecture inherently offers improved scalability, fault tolerance, and privacy protection. The combination of FedProx and model personalization preserves training stability under non-IID data conditions, recovering 20 % of lost accuracy. In cross-instrument scenarios, the DFL approach outperforms both local-only and standard centralized FL models, reducing prediction errors by up to 52 % and showing strong generalization to new devices. While DFL requires more training rounds, system efficiency analysis shows its total communication cost is 25 % lower than centralized FL. Our research indicates DFL as a promising and practical approach for NIR spectroscopy, offering privacy, scalability, and generalizability for real-world, multi-party deployments with heterogeneous devices. However, performance can decline under extreme data heterogeneity, highlighting the need for further enhancements in model personalization.

title: Marginal region-integrated regressive conditional variational autoencoder-generative adversarial network: A soft sensing enhancement method
abstract: In industrial processes, due to limitations of actual industrial production, many industrial data are difficult to obtain directly, which limits sample size and leads to uneven data distribution, ultimately affecting the fitting performance of soft sensing models. To address this challenge, we propose a marginal Isolation Mega Trend Diffusion with Regressor Conditional Variational Autoencoder-Generative Adversarial Network (IRCVGAN). designed to improve model accuracy by expanding the sample size. Specifically, the proposed method first applies the isolation forest algorithm to detect sparse marginal regions in the dataset, followed by Mega Trend Diffusion (MTD) to broaden the range of input data by generating virtual samples, thus increasing dataset diversity. Next, an improved regressive conditional Variational Autoencoder-Generative Adversarial Network (RCVAEGAN) is developed to perform fine-grained selection on the virtual samples generated by MTD. Furthermore, the mapping between input variables and production quality indicators is embedded in RCVAEGAN, enhancing the representativeness of the samples and improving the model’s fitting accuracy, the effectiveness of our proposed method is validated through function fitting tests and real-world industrial data from a purified terephthalic acid (PTA) solvent system.

title: Boosting pneumonia diagnosis with machine learning and spectroscopic data fusion techniques
abstract: Photonic techniques combined with chemometrics offer promising opportunities for next-generation medical in vitro diagnostics. In this work, we evaluate the ability of vibrational spectroscopy to distinguish viral respiratory infections that have progressed to pneumonia. Pneumonia remains a major global health burden and is currently the eighth leading cause of death worldwide. Reliable and differentiated diagnoses are still challenging, as existing methods are time-consuming and require specialized laboratories and expertise. We present a rapid, machine-learning–based in vitro approach for classifying influenza A and seasonal flu and for discriminating between these pathogenic strains. To enhance diagnostic performance, we employ data fusion of complementary Raman and Fourier-transform infrared absorption spectra acquired from microliter-scale droplets of human blood plasma. By integrating spectral information from both modalities, the models capture a broader range of physiological changes and more comprehensively reflect the biochemical profile of the samples, leading to more robust classification. Using generalized linear models, we achieve accuracies of up to 95% in distinguishing healthy controls from influenza A– and seasonal flu–infected samples. The results further highlight specific scenarios in which data fusion yields measurable improvements in predictive power.

title: Advancing molecular property prediction for environmental fate using graph neural networks: A comparative analysis
abstract: In cheminformatics, predicting molecular properties is crucial for enhancing material research, toxicity assessment and drug discovery. This research investigates the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for predicting molecular properties by examining three different architectures: Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN), Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) and Graphormer. We show that GNNs that include structural and geometric information perform noticeably better than conventional descriptor-based machine learning models using benchmark datasets like as QM9, ZINC, and OGB-MolHIV. This study further plays a pivotal role in understanding the environmental fate and transport of chemical compounds by find partition coefficients like Octanol-Water Partition Coefficient (Kow), Air-Water Partition Coefficient (Kaw) and Soil-Water Partition Coefficient (K_d). Graphormer achieves the best performance on log Kow (MAE = 0.18) and MolHIV classification (ROC-AUC = 0.807). EGNN with its E(n)-equivariant updates and 3D coordinate integration achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) on geometry-sensitive properties like log Kaw (0.25) and log K_d (0.22). The significance of architectural alignment with molecular property traits is underscored by these findings.

title: SigmaCCS2: Collision cross section prediction using molecular topological and geometric information with graph neural network
abstract: Collision cross section (CCS) values are crucial for compound characterization in ion mobility spectrometry (IMS), yet their experimental determination is often resource-intensive. To overcome this, we introduce SigmaCCS2, a graph neural network (GNN)-based method that predicts CCS values by integrating both molecular topological and geometric information. By representing molecules as dual graphs, where molecular graphs encode topological structures and line graphs encode molecular geometries, SigmaCCS2 captures comprehensive structural features for accurate predictions. This approach achieves highly competitive and robust predictive performance, generally superior or comparable to state-of-the-art methods on external test sets. SigmaCCS2 demonstrates robust versatility across different instruments and molecular superclasses. Furthermore, a user-friendly web server is provided, enhancing accessibility for researchers. This advancement in CCS prediction enhances compound identification in various fields, including metabolomics, lipidomics, and drug discovery, by improving CCS coverage in databases.

title: High precision classification method for black tea: Deep learning combined with two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy
abstract: Tea is a widely popular beverage across the globe. However, its medicinal content and value vary from one species to another. As a result, consumers need a quick and efficient method to distinguish between species. This paper introduces a method for species classification using two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2DCOS) images combined with deep learning (DL) models. Initially, 345 thin-section samples of five different black teas were prepared, and their near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) data were obtained. From this preprocessed one-dimensional NIRS data, 8280 2DCOS contour images and contour fill images were generated. MobileNet model with various bottleneck residual blocks was constructed, and trained using these 2DCOS images as samples, achieving a classification accuracy of 100 %. The model testing results indicated that the optimal NIRS data preprocessing method and 2DCOS image format are Standard Normal Variate transformation (SNV) and contour fill image. Furthermore, the classification results of one-dimensional NIRS data, 2DOCS matrix data, and 2DCOS image data were compared, showing that the 2DCOS images provide higher classification accuracy. Finally, comparative experiments were conducted between the MobileNet model and other deep learning models, demonstrating that the MobileNet model has the advantages of fewer parameters, lower computational load, high accuracy, and fast convergence speed. Therefore, combining 2DCOS images with the MobileNet model for black tea classification is effective. This paper offers a promising approach for the identification of black tea species, with extensive potential applications in species classification.

title: Recent developments in evolutionary computation for generative adversarial networks: A comprehensive survey
abstract: In recent years, evolutionary generative adversarial networks (EGANs) have been proposed as a emerging research area that merges the well-known original concept of generative adversarial networks (GAN) for generating realistic data and evolutionary computation (EC) techniques to optimize solutions by inspiration from nature. In this review paper, we delve into the synergetic relationship between EC and GAN with an emphasis on EGANs — an emerging direction that has the potential to spark a multitude of practical applications. To this end, we first introduce the key concepts of GANs and EC respectively in detail to illustrate their synergism for modeling novel data efficiently while keeping consistency with reality. Then we describe how EC techniques have been incorporated into these architectures to improve both performance and diversity. This paper presents a thorough analysis of the EGANs in various domains. In this perspective, EGANs have been proven to be very effective in various real-world problems like data scarcity as well as mode collapse and training instability. We also consider the limitations of EGANs and suggest methods for addressing them. For the future, we present new research directions for EGANs and suggest that it could potentially transform artificial intelligence (AI) as well as push forward cutting-edge applications in personalized content generation, virtual reality (VR) experiences, and medical diagnosis. In conclusion, it will provide a solid foundation for EGANs. It represents a promising trajectory for AI space due to a combination of two powerful paradigms, GAN and EC. It aims to handle the challenges which will result in enabling the new world in data synthesis and optimization.

title: Modeling and statistical analysis of cancer drugs using M-polynomial indices for their characteristics
abstract: This study computes M-polynomial indices for Doxorubicin and Mitoxantrone, two widely used anthracycline and anthracenedione anticancer drugs, respectively. Doxorubicin, a potent topoisomerase II inhibitor, is commonly employed in treating various cancers, including breast, ovarian, and leukemia. Mitoxantrone, with its unique DNA-intercalating properties, is effective against acute myeloid leukemia, breast cancer, and non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. We produced M-polynomial indices by partitioning graph edges depending on degree and adjacency matrix. A Python algorithm is written using an adjacency matrix to efficiently compute the indices, reducing calculation time from days to minutes and eliminating human error. Simple linear regression models in SPSS software are used to create QSPR and predict the physical attributes of cancer medicines. Our findings show that M-polynomial indices accurately predict physical attributes, providing important insights into the structural requirements for maximum anticancer action. In addition, we proposed models for each physical attribute. This study aids in the development of new cancer therapies and the prediction of physical features for uncharacterized medications.

title: A classification model for early detection of breast cancer by Raman spectroscopy based on categorical embedding transformer
abstract: At present, Raman spectroscopy combined with deep learning has been widely used in the field of disease screening. Transformer is an important architecture for deep learning and has excelled in several areas with technologies such as its self-attention mechanism. However, as an architecture originally designed for the field of natural language processing, Transformer has disadvantages such as high computational complexity and easy overfitting in small data sets when processing spectral data.
