Repeated stratified random-split evaluation over 100 physical-sample-level partitions yielded OA = 0.9549 ± 0.0203 and macro-F1 = 0.9531 ± 0.0214, indicating favourable but still partition-dependent internal stability under the current laboratory dataset. Sensitivity analysis of the predefined grade-interval formulation showed that adjacent-grade discrimination was more challenging than the original four-interval task, but the proposed strategy retained useful performance in neighbouring-grade settings. These results suggest that process-mineralogy-contextualized VNIR–SWIR chemometric modelling provides a feasible laboratory route for rapid grade-interval screening of powdered molybdenite flotation products under controlled measurement conditions. Further validation under independent flotation batches, moisture variation, particle-size variation, packing-state changes, and instrument-transfer conditions is required before at-line or cross-plant application.

title: Raman-based taxonomic identification of animal body fluids via a spectra-aware wavelet-nonlinear collaborative network
abstract: Animal blood and semen represent pivotal biological evidence, encapsulating essential biochemical and genetic profiles of a species. While Raman spectroscopy holds immense potential for the non-destructive identification of trace body fluids, the intrinsic Raman signals are frequently confounded by intense autofluorescence backgrounds. Moreover, subtle inter-species spectral variances are often obscured under long-tailed distributions, rendering it challenging for conventional deep learning models to simultaneously optimize classification accuracy and maintain a lightweight architecture. To overcome these hurdles, we propose S-WNACNet, a lightweight collaborative network for multi-species Raman spectral classification, structured around a “distribution stabilization – fine-grained feature decoupling – global background adaptation” framework. Our core innovations include: (1) Spectra-aware Dynamic Root Mean Square Normalization (S-DRMSNorm), which employs a residual bidirectional gating mechanism to adaptively enhance features while preserving the zero-anchored sparse topology of Raman signals; (2) Wavelet Non-Linear Convolution (WT-NLConv), utilizing a lightweight nonlinear residual branch to resolve complex biochemical overlapping peaks in the frequency domain ; and (3) Wavelet-Adaptive Instance Normalization Convolution (WT-AdaINConv) for dynamic background drift calibration. Experimental results demonstrate that S-WNACNet achieves Top-1 accuracies of 98.49% and 98.60% on reflective and transmissive Raman datasets covering over 40 species, respectively. With only 0.46M parameters and millisecond-level inference latency, the model exhibits robust cross-dataset applicability across multiple public datasets, providing a fast and portable solution for field-based species identification and grassroots law enforcement.

title: Rapid prediction of chemical constituent levels in Gastrodia elata at different steaming degrees using hyperspectral analysis and machine learning
abstract: Gastrodia elata (G. elata) is recognized as a plant with both medicinal and edible values, and its modern processing is predominantly performed through steaming; therefore, precise control of the steaming procedure is required to ensure consistency and controllability in clinical application. In this study, Hyperspectral (HSI) data of G. elata subjected to different steaming degrees were acquired over the spectral range of 350–2500 nm. Partial least-squares regression (PLSR) was employed as the modeling framework, in combination with multiple spectral preprocessing and feature-wavelength selection methods, to achieve quantitative prediction of the contents of major active ingredients including gastrodin (GAS), p-hydroxybenzyl alcohol (HBA), parishin E (PE), parishin C (PC), and parishin A (PA). The optimal modeling strategies for the six target compounds were GAS-SNV+1d, HBA-SG + ICO, PE-SG + CARS, PB-1d + ICO, PC-SNV+1d + VISSA, and PA-1d + VISSA. The RPD values of all models were greater than 2.5, indicating good predictive ability and stability. In summary, this study has provided a viable methodological approach for rapid and precise quality monitoring and process standardization in traditional Chinese medicine manufacturing.

title: Knowledge distillation for near-infrared quantification of ternary starch mixtures
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is widely used for multi-component quantitative analysis of food powders, but resolving subtle compositional differences in mixtures with similar chemical structure and highly overlapping spectral responses remains challenging for conventional regression models. Focusing on a ternary system of sweet potato (A), cassava (B) and potato (C) starch, this study proposes a multi-output feature distillation model based on a residual multilayer perceptron (MLP). Three teacher networks are trained on the AB, AC and BC binary subsets, and their bottleneck-layer features are used as supervision to guide a ternary student network in jointly predicting the mass fractions of components A, B and C. Experiments were performed on self-collected binary and ternary NIR datasets covering the spectral range of 1000–1600 nm. By transferring compositional relationships learned from binary subsystems into intermediate-layer constraints, the proposed framework improves the quantitative analysis of ternary starch mixtures. Among the conventional models, support vector regression (SVR) achieved the best performance, with an average coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.7607. The multi-output MLP increased the average R2 to 0.9020, while the incorporation of binary teacher features through knowledge distillation further improved the performance of MLP-distill. On the ternary test set, MLP-distill achieved the highest average R2 of 0.9362 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0472.

title: Quantification of disperse dye concentrations through stacking ensemble learning of fused multiband spectral features
abstract: Due to the low solubility of disperse dyes at room temperature, the aqueous system forms a polydisperse suspension, limiting concentration detection accuracy as single-band features provide insufficient information and models fail to concurrently capture linear and nonlinear spectral characteristics. This study proposes multidimensional spectral data acquisition via a hemispherical sample cell to extract band-specific features and employs ensemble learning for feature complementarity and multi-model fusion. For 81 ternary disperse dye samples, data in the 610–800 nm band exhibited saturation, prompting a split-band spatial feature extraction approach. In the non-saturated band (420–600 nm), gradient-based selection reduced dimensionality to 1/56. In the saturated band (610–800 nm), multiscale Otsu thresholding and elliptic Fourier descriptors were applied to extract spot contour morphological features. Given the inadequacy of single-band features and significant dimensionality disparities, a Stacking ensemble model was developed. It utilizes dual channels processing non-saturated and saturated features separately, with PLS, SVM, and XGBoost as base learners. Their outputs form a meta-feature matrix input to a ridge regression meta-learner, integrating full-band information and addressing linear-nonlinear relationships. Results demonstrate Stacking outperforms single models, with test set R2 improvements of 0.40%–0.92%, achieving R2 values of 0.9539, 0.9231 and 0.9899 for Disperse Orange S-4RL, Disperse Rubine S-5BL, and Disperse Navy Blue HGL, respectively.

title: High-precision prediction of bloodstain aging time based on near-infrared spectroscopy and a dual attention mechanism
abstract: Accurate estimation of bloodstain aging duration is a critical challenge in forensic biology, as it underpins event timeline reconstruction and behavioral interpretation at crime scenes. Existing spectroscopic methods face limitations including biochemically unguided spectral selection, insufficient model interpretability, and limited environmental robustness. To address these issues, this study proposes a one-dimensional convolutional network, termed BloodAttention-CNN, which integrates channel and spatial attention mechanisms for aging classification of porcine bloodstains using 900–1800 cm−1 near-infrared spectra. After applying a standardized preprocessing pipeline, we compared the proposed network with conventional machine learning models. BloodAttention-CNN achieved 92.35% accuracy on the test set, substantially outperforming all competing methods. Attention visualization revealed that the model consistently prioritized regions near 1120–1130 cm−1, 1650 cm−1, and 1720 cm−1—peaks closely corresponding to hemoglobin oxidation and protein unfolding during stain maturation. Systematic perturbation experiments further confirmed that perturbing these high-attention regions caused up to a 35.29% accuracy drop, whereas perturbation of the negative control region caused only a 5.88% drop, providing perturbation-based evidence that these regions influence model decisions and are associated with biochemically relevant spectral features. Cross-species and cross-temperature validation further demonstrated robust generalization (82.35–90.12% accuracy). This framework offers a rapid, non-destructive, and forensically accountable strategy for bloodstain deposition time estimation, establishing a traceable link between spectral inputs, deep learning decisions, and underlying molecular mechanisms.

title: Chemometric and machine-learning strategies for calibration transfer and uncertainty quantification in portable optical analytical systems
abstract: Spectral and imaging data generated by portable optical analytical instruments are being increasingly subjected to chemometric and machine-learning analysis. Instrument variability, illumination conditions, and use on various instruments often degrade predictive performance and thus limit the transferability and the quantitative robustness of models. In this review, the methods for calibration transfer and domain adaptation with widely used modern chemometrics techniques, direct standardization (DS), piecewise direct standardization (PDS), orthogonal signal correction (OSC), canonical correlation analysis (CCA) as well as emerging deep-learning transfer approaches such as low-rank adaptation and adversarial domain alignment are scrutinized. The performance of various linear and nonlinear regression methods, e.g., partial least squares regression (PLS-R), support vector regression (SVR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and multimodal late-fusion frameworks, are evaluated in multiple aspects by data requirements, robustness, interpretability, and cross-instrument generalizability. Special attention is given to uncertainty-aware modeling including but not limited to bootstrap prediction interval, Bayesian variance estimation, and integrated uncertainty budget following guidelines from metrology. A comprehensive protocol is developed, which integrates stepwise protocols for data acquisition, normalization against references, transfer-learning calibration, drift detection, and uncertainty propagation to perform independent quantitative analyses. By promoting the development of methods yielding transferable, uncertainty-calibrated models rather than the best single-instrument model, the framework allows development of intelligent laboratory systems with the capability of making traceable, decision-grade predictions across different sensing modalities.

title: An industrial process soft sensor model based on dual-dependency matrix fused graph attention temporal convolution network
abstract: To address the poor prediction accuracy caused by insufficient synergy between dynamic and stable features and the inconsistent modeling of spatiotemporal dependencies in industrial process quality prediction, this paper proposes a soft sensor model based on Dual-Dependency Matrix Fused Graph Attention Temporal Convolution Network (DDMF-GATCN). First, a dual dependency learning mechanism is designed. By employing a dynamic dependency learner to capture short-term dependencies and integrating a stable dependency variational autoencoder to learn long-term topological structures, the model is infused with dual path prior knowledge. Second, a Dependency-Enhanced Graph Attention Network (DEGAT) is constructed, which dynamically reconstruct adjacency relationships using the fused dependency matrix to enhance the model's ability to capture nonlinear spatial dependencies among variables. Finally, a Dependency-Aware Temporal Convolutional Network (DATCN) is constructed, which integrates dependency information into the normalization process of temporal convolutions in a multi-scale manner, significantly enhancing the efficiency of dynamic feature extraction. Experiments conducted on two typical industrial processes—penicillin fermentation and debutanizer tower—demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing mainstream soft sensor models in terms of prediction accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability.

title: Two-stage wavelength selection strategy of laser induced fluorescence spectroscopy of power transformer oil by SiPLS combined with CPO
abstract: Transformers are critical components in power systems, requiring accurate operational status assessment and fault identification for effective maintenance. This study proposes a novel two-stage method integrating laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) spectroscopy with synergy interval partial least squares (SiPLS) and crested porcupine optimizer (CPO) algorithms for transformer oil analysis. Various transformer oil samples were analyzed using an LIF acquisition system to obtain fluorescence spectra. Initial spectral processing with SiPLS revealed optimal performance when dividing spectra into 27 sub-intervals, with sub-intervals 5, 6, 8, and 9 showing minimal RMSECV (0.9599) and containing 304 wavelength positions. Subsequent CPO optimization further refined the selection to 126 characteristic wavelengths, yielding minimal classification error. These optimized wavelengths, which correspond to specific fluorophores (e.g., anthracene and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons) and reflect oil aging and fault-induced chemical changes, were used to construct fluorescence spectrum identification models with conventional classifiers. The SiPLS-CPO method demonstrated statistically significant superiority over competitive adaptive weighted sampling (CARS) and principal component analysis (PCA) in spectral feature selection, as confirmed by paired t-tests (p < 0.05). The experimental results confirm the method's effectiveness in screening characteristic wavelengths for transformer oil analysis, providing a practical and physically interpretable approach for transformer fault diagnosis.

title: Multimodal data fusion and multi-objective optimized CatBoost models for origin traceability and active compound prediction of Salvia miltiorrhiza
abstract: The quality of traditional Chinese medicines is strongly influenced by geographical origin; however, existing methods for origin traceability and quality evaluation still struggle to balance analytical efficiency, operational convenience, and information completeness. In this study, 120 samples of Salvia miltiorrhiza (SM) were collected from five representative production regions in China. Computer vision (CV) was used to extract appearance features, including color, texture, and contour characteristics, while high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was employed to determine the contents of active components. By integrating machine learning with multivariate statistical analysis, origin classification models were developed using single-modality data as well as data-level, feature-level, and decision-level fusion strategies, followed by prediction of chemical component contents based on CV features. Results from 50 repeated stratified random splits showed that the Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) model under the decision-level fusion strategy achieved an accuracy of 99.17% ± 1.29% for origin identification, demonstrating strong classification performance and stability. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis under the feature-level fusion strategy indicated that appearance traits and chemical constituents made synergistic contributions to origin discrimination. The CatBoost model was further optimized using five multi-objective optimization algorithms, which improved the overall predictive performance for active component contents, with NSGA-II exhibiting a comparatively balanced overall advantage. The multimodal data fusion and multi-objective optimization framework developed in this study provides a new technical pathway for the origin traceability and quality evaluation of SM and offers a methodological reference for the intelligent analysis of multisource information in Chinese medicinal materials.

title: Hybrid modeling of penicillin fermentation via temporal-constrained multi-modal identification and multi-agent optimization
abstract: Accurate prediction of penicillin concentration relies on the precise identification of multi-modal characteristics in the fermentation process. However, existing methods often neglect these characteristics, leading to insufficient model stability and prediction accuracy, which severely compromises engineering practicality. To address this issue, this paper proposes an integrated modeling strategy based on Temporal-Constrained Dynamic Bilateral Support Vector Data Description (TDBSVDD), Kernel Slow Feature Analysis-Gaussian Mixture Model (KSFA-GMM), Weighted Support Vector Regression (W-SVR), and Multi-Agent Critic Particle Swarm Optimization (MAC-PSO). First, to tackle the problem of discontinuous identification in transition phases, a temporal smoothing regularization term and a dynamic sphere center mechanism are introduced to construct the TDBSVDD model, enabling accurate partitioning of normal, abnormal, and transition modes. Second, considering the relatively abundant data in normal mode, KSFA-GMM is employed to extract slow-varying features and establish a probabilistic prediction model. For the abnormal mode characterized by small samples and high noise, a W-SVR model based on mutual information feature selection and local density weighting is developed. Meanwhile, to optimize the hyperparameters of the models, a hierarchical parameter optimization method using MAC-PSO is designed. Experimental results on a penicillin fermentation dataset demonstrate that the proposed modeling strategy effectively identifies normal and abnormal modes and significantly outperforms traditional methods in prediction accuracy and stability.

title: Implementation of accurate identification of different processing degree Paofupian and prediction of key component content based on multimodal data fusion and machine learning strategies
abstract: The degree of processing of the Paofupian (PFP) directly determines their clinical safety and effectiveness, but currently, there is a lack of relevant research, and actual production relies solely on subjective judgment based on experience, lacking objective standards and quality control measures. This study employs computer vision and Fourier Transform Near-Infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy for rapid, non-destructive, and accurate evaluation of the processing degrees of Paofupian. Machine learning techniques, including Optimizable Tree, Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear SVM), Cosine K-Nearest Neighbors (Cosine KNN), and Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), were used to develop models for qualitative identification and quantitative prediction of PFP. Initial results show poor classification accuracy using only RGB or GLCM features. However, fusing these features with the original near-infrared spectra improved accuracy significantly, achieving 77.5% for Optimizable Tree and Linear SVM, and 60.0% for Cosine KNN. Despite this, the models remained below high precision standards. After preprocessing the original spectral data with Multivariate Scatter Correction, classification accuracy surged to 100% for Optimizable Tree and Linear SVM, and to 90.0% for Cosine KNN, demonstrating the efficacy of spectral preprocessing combined with machine learning. Furthermore, characteristic wavelengths were selected using algorithms such as Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS), leading to a PLSR model for predicting the five alkaloid components in PFP. The five alkaloid models exhibited different levels of predictive performance. The mesaconitine model showed strong predictive performance, with an R2p of 0.93555 and an RPDp of 4.0237. The models for benzoylmesaconitine, benzoylaconine, benzoylhypaconine, and hypaconitine yielded RPDp values between 2.6560 and 2.9208, indicating potential for rapid screening or approximate quantification. Further validation using additional independent batches is required before these models can be applied as alternatives to conventional reference analysis.

title: A novel key process indicator prediction strategy with trend-guided dual-path collaborative compensation LSTM for complex industrial processes
abstract: Accurate soft sensing of product quality for non-stationary industrial processes remains a challenging task due to the dynamic operating conditions, variable coupling, and transient disturbances. Therefore, a novel key process indicator prediction strategy with trend-guided dual-path collaborative compensation LSTM (TDCC-LSTM) for complex industrial processes in this paper. Firstly, the trend of variable changes is characterized using first-order differences, second-order differences, and standard deviations. A hierarchical perception mechanism is introduced, and a recursive trend-aware gate is added to LSTM to update the production information state. Moreover, considering the continuity and temporal dependence of process industry processes, an autoregressive mechanism is introduced on the basis of trend-aware LSTM. Besides, according to the confidence level and the trend change, a dynamic weight selection method is developed to adaptively fuse the prediction results of trend-aware LSTM and autoregressive trend-aware LSTM. The verifications on three real industrial cases indicate that the TDCC-LSTM model is significantly superior to the compared model in terms of trajectory fitting accuracy, amplitude stability and prediction error, which provides an effective way to achieve reliable and robust key process indicator prediction in complex industrial environments.

title: Successive monitoring task oriented layerwise feature distillation dictionary learning with applications to multimodal industrial processes
abstract: Complex industrial processes in general successively generate new operating modes in response to changes of production plans and product specifications, which poses challenges to multimodal industrial process monitoring. The existing traditional multimode process monitoring approaches tend to store the entire data from all potential modes to update the model when new modes arrive, which is time-consuming and cost-prohibitive. This paper proposes a multimode monitoring approach named layerwise feature distillation dictionary learning (LFDDL) to monitor industrial processes with an infinite stream of operating modes, achieving long-term monitoring applications. The LFDDL explicitly learns commonalities across different modes, which allows the trained model to learn the successive modes with limited storage and computational costs. Moreover, layerwise feature distillation is developed to distill individualities of the previous mode into the new mode to alleviate the catastrophic forgetting issue. Additionally, a deep unique dictionary is constructed to extract the multilevel characteristics of data, such that deeper insights can be provided into multimodal processes. Based on these distinct modeling strategies, the proposed approach is capable of monitoring various modes in a successive manner and facilitated to long-term monitoring applications. The effectiveness of the LFDDL is verified through case studies on the benchmark Tennessee Eastman process and a real-world fluid catalytic cracking process.

title: Sensitivity of joint-parameter geometry to spectral overlap and dynamic-range imbalance in 99Tc qNMR of pertechnetate
abstract: Quantitative NMR uncertainty is commonly interpreted using marginal standard errors and assumed to improve monotonically with increased signal averaging or refined fitting workflows. In spectra characterized by partial overlap and large dynamic-range disparities, however, marginal precision can misrepresent how independently fitted parameters are constrained. Using 99TcO4− isotopologues as an internally controlled system, we show that strongly overlapped minor resonances develop elongated joint distributions under full-spectrum fitting, but normalized anisotropy does not exhibit a universal monotonic dependence on spectral overlap. Independent perturbation of fitting condition and noise magnitude tests how covariance geometry responds to participation of dominant resonances and changes in stochastic variance. Relative standard deviation of the area generally remained greater among the more strongly overlapped peaks, although its absolute magnitude depended on the participation of higher-amplitude resonances in the shared regression objective. Restricting higher-amplitude resonances generally reduced normalized anisotropy while increasing joint extent and relative standard deviation of the area, but also changed the across-peak ordering of anisotropy. Increasing signal averaging contracted joint extent while producing a fitting-condition-specific anisotropy ordering. These results demonstrate that marginal relative uncertainty and joint covariance geometry report distinct properties of the regression. Relative standard deviation of the area uncertainty retains a broadly consistent overlap ordering, whereas the magnitude and rank ordering of normalized anisotropy depend on fitting condition and signal averaging. Accordingly, interpretation of trace-component quantification in high–dynamic-range quantitative NMR applications is strengthened by inspection of joint-parameter covariance in addition to marginal precision metrics.

title: LiteGov: A reproducible protocol for post-generation molecular filtering and ranking
abstract: Generative molecular models produce candidate libraries containing structures with poor descriptor profiles or structural alerts that can be removed before docking or expert review. We test whether this early selection can be implemented as a reproducible filtering and ranking protocol. LiteGov applies medicinal-chemistry and structural-alert filters and ranks retained molecules using the quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) and synthetic accessibility (SA), with fixed 0.8/0.2 weights. Across evaluations, mean QED increases from 0.665 to 0.887, mean SA decreases from 2.818 to 2.198, and pan-assay interference compound (PAINS) alerts decrease from 4.6% to 0%. In an exact ablation of 10,678 unique structures, LiteGov attains Spearman correlation 0.911, Top-100 overlap 0.620, and normalized discounted cumulative gain 0.977 against an author-specified property-priority reference; relative to QED-only ranking, Top-100 SA decreases by 0.232 with a QED difference of −0.003. Generator-held-out calibration selects weights of 0.64–0.68 and raises mean property-reference Spearman correlation from 0.900 to 0.917. AiZynthFinder route-solution rates increase from 0.58 to 1.00 for GenMol and from 0.64 to 0.80 for MoLeR. Complementary structure-aware audits report Spearman correlation 0.067 and Top-100 overlap 0.028 with an AutoDock Vina–GNINA affinity consensus, alongside a ChEMBL activity-label area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.369. These evidence layers establish LiteGov as a descriptor-based triage and computational route-feasibility protocol for preparing candidate libraries for target-aware screening.

title: Transfer learning with time-series feature extraction for key variables robust prediction in penicillin fermentation under limited data
abstract: To enhance the prediction accuracy of key variables in penicillin fermentation under small-sample constraints, this paper presents a transfer learning framework utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with L2-distance to Starting Point (L2-SP) regularization. A deep temporal feature extractor is pre-trained on source-domain data to capture general fermentation dynamics and long-range dependencies. The learned representations are subsequently transferred to the target domain as a parameter initialization, enabling knowledge reuse under data-scarce conditions. A dedicated regularization strategy is introduced during fine-tuning to constrain the deviation of model parameters from their initial pre-trained values, thereby preserving transferable knowledge while preventing overfitting on limited target samples. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework generally outperforms training from scratch and conventional transfer learning in moderate-to-high sparsity regimes, while exhibiting decisive advantages over feature-alignment baselines such as CORAL. These findings validate the effectiveness of the proposed method and clarify its conditional applicability across varying data sparsity levels.

title: FewTox: Resource-efficient molecular toxicity prediction via multi-source frozen representations and multi-task learning
abstract: Accurate molecular toxicity prediction is essential for chemical safety assessment. Chemical language models (CLMs) offer powerful molecular representations, but their GPU-intensive fine-tuning limits accessibility. We present FewTox, a resource-efficient, CPU-trainable framework that combines frozen multi-source CLM features with multi-task learning for 12-endpoint toxicity prediction on Tox21. Under strict inductive evaluation, a compact MLP built on concatenated PubChem and ZINC ChemBERTa embeddings achieves a mean scaffold AUROC of 0.702. This performance approaches a fully fine-tuned ChemBERTa baseline (0.733) at approximately 160× lower training cost. ECFP-Random Forest remains a strong baseline (AUROC 0.728), demonstrating the effectiveness of explicit substructure fingerprints under scaffold splitting. FewTox complements fingerprint-based models by integrating ECFP substructures with continuous CLM representations; this hybrid reaches an AUROC of 0.725. The multi-task neural head also supports post-hoc temperature scaling, which improves NLL and Brier score without changing discrimination. On the two-endpoint ClinTox benchmark, FewTox achieves a scaffold AUROC of 0.979. These results establish a practical accuracy–efficiency profile for frozen molecular representations in resource-constrained toxicity modeling.

title: Time-aligned predictive learning for soft sensing of irregularly sampled industrial time series
abstract: Accurate modeling of temporal dependencies is crucial for industrial soft sensing of time series, where deep learning approaches have achieved remarkable progress. However, time series collected from real industrial processes are often irregularly sampled due to practical factors such as sensor malfunctions, communication interruptions, and data corruption. The irregularly sampled time series poses significant challenges for most deep learning models, including recurrent neural networks and Transformers, as traditional dynamic soft sensing methods cannot directly handle heterogeneous sampling intervals. Addressing this issue, this article proposes a time-aligned predictive learning (TAPL) framework that explicitly models sampling time intervals to effectively capture temporal dependencies among irregularly sampled sequences. TAPL consists of two core modules, including a Fourier position embedding-based time-aware attention and a positional time-aligned recurrent network. The former integrates sampling time information into attention score computation and assigns adaptive weights to modulate temporal correlations, while the latter incorporates time intervals into recurrent updates, adjusting the influence of past observations on current states. Experiments on real-world industrial datasets verify the efficacy and superiority of the proposed approach.

title: X-ray-free guidewire tracking via arterial pressure sensing in a benchtop vascular model based on a hybrid graph neural network
abstract: The reliance on X-ray fluoroscopy for real-time guidewire visualization presents a major clinical challenge due to cumulative radiation exposure for patients and medical personnel. To address this issue, we developed a radiation-free guidewire positioning framework based on a novel hybrid model that integrates a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) with a Random Forest (RF) classifier, enabling accurate vessel localization using only intravascular pressure data. The GCN captures topological relationships within the vascular network, while the RF classifier leverages graph-derived representations for robust classification. To mitigate the limitations of a relatively small clinical dataset, a comprehensive data augmentation strategy incorporating Gaussian noise injection, feature scaling, Mixup, and feature permutation was employed. The proposed GCN+RF model was extensively evaluated against a diverse set of benchmark methods, including traditional machine learning, ensemble-learning, feature-engineering, and deep-learning approaches. Experimental results demonstrated superior performance, achieving an Accuracy of 0.7667 ± 0.0990, F1 Weighted score of 0.7668 ± 0.1095, AUC of 0.9243 ± 0.0547, Precision of 0.7689 ± 0.0178, and Recall of 0.7667 ± 0.0404. The proposed approach outperformed most competing methods, including RF (0.7564 ± 0.0483 accuracy), Bagging (0.7513 ± 0.0500 accuracy), and LightGBM (0.7410 ± 0.0531 accuracy), while substantially surpassing the standalone GCN model (0.6261 ± 0.0518 accuracy). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of pressure-based guidewire localization in a controlled benchtop vascular phantom and highlight the potential of graph-enhanced machine learning for radiation-free endovascular navigation. Further validation in animal studies and clinical settings is required before clinical translation.

title: An interpretable knowledge-enhanced soft sensor framework for basic oxygen furnace endpoint prediction via LLM-driven feature engineering and SHAP-based threshold analysis
abstract: Basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steelmaking is a high-temperature chemical reaction process where endpoint carbon content and temperature are critical variables determining molten steel quality. Traditional data-driven models rely on manual feature engineering and iterative hyperparameter tuning, with predictions difficult to translate into actionable guidelines. This paper proposes an interpretable soft sensor framework integrating large language model (LLM)-based knowledge feature engineering, Tabular Prior-data Fitted Networks (TabPFN), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based threshold analysis. The framework generates physicochemical knowledge-enhanced features via multiple LLMs, combines correlation screening with recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV) to select the optimal feature subset, applies TabPFN for rapid endpoint prediction, and extracts sensitive intervals and operational thresholds via SHAP dependence fitting. Using 814 heats from a 220-ton BOF, the model achieved test-set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.5318 and 0.8315, hit rates (HR) of 79.75% (±0.01%) and 92.64% (±10 °C), and training times of 0.3805 s and 0.3944 s for carbon content and temperature, respectively. Against state-of-the-art models, R2 increased by 5.75% and 1.66%, HR by 3.06 and 1.23 percentage points, and training speeds by factors of 402 and 453, respectively. SHAP analysis identified a high-sensitivity interval of [1682, 1792] kg for light-fired dolomite on carbon content, and an efficient temperature regulation region within 700 kg of ore consumption. Over 52 industrial heats, HR reached 94.23% and 100% for carbon content and temperature. These results demonstrate that the framework enables rapid BOF endpoint prediction and operational threshold extraction, providing a quantitative basis for endpoint control.

title: Hybrid kernel deep orthogonal subspace analysis-based anomaly detection for key performance indicators
abstract: In modern industrial processes, the accurate detection of key performance indicators (KPIs) is often challenged by high system nonlinearity compounded by incipient anomaly characteristics. To address this issue, a hybrid kernel deep orthogonal subspace analysis algorithm is proposed in this paper. First, a hybrid kernel combining Gaussian and polynomial kernels is utilized to project the original nonlinear process data onto a high-dimensional feature space. This projection enhances linear separability, while the Gaussian component preserves local neighborhood similarities and the polynomial component captures global high-order feature interactions. Within this feature space, a kernel correlation matrix (KCM) is constructed to characterize the associative properties of the relevant information between process inputs and KPIs. A deep singular value decomposition scheme is then applied to this KCM to hierarchically decompose the KPI-related information into multiple kernel subspaces. Hierarchical decomposition further enables the construction of a multi-order subspace structure, which significantly enhances sensitivity to incipient anomalies that are easily obscured by noise in first-order projections. Furthermore, complexity is assessed via floating-point operations, serving to illustrate the feasibility for both the training and detection phases. Finally, experiments on the penicillin fermentation process and thermal power plant process are carried out. The practical applicability of the proposed method is verified, and superior performance over state-of-the-art techniques is demonstrated.

title: Scale analysis method coupled with a salp swarm algorithm to study the heat transfer rate of liquid metal nanofluids
abstract:
Background
The problem of natural convection heat transfer of nanofluids subjected to an external magnetic field has been extensively studied in recent years because of its various applications in different fields of engineering. Most of these studies have focused on conventional nanofluids obtained by dispersing nanoparticles in ordinary liquids such as water, however, few studies have focused on liquid metal nanofluids. Compared to traditional base fluids, liquid metals exhibit a much higher thermal and electrical conductivities, which significantly alters the effect of adding nanoparticles on the heat transfer rate.
Novelty and methodology
In this paper, we propose to study the heat transfer rate of molten gallium with suspended nanoparticles in a cubic cavity laterally heated and subjected to an external magnetic field. First, for pure molten gallium, the scale analysis method is used to obtain a general correlation of the heat transfer rate which depends on several adjustable parameters. Then, based on the already published experimental data, the salp swarm algorithm is used to identify these parameters. The obtained correlation is then developed for nanofluids whose base fluid is molten gallium. The effect of the addition of Cu or Al2O3 nanoparticles on the heat transfer rate is studied.
Significant results
For pure molten gallium, the results show that the maximum error between the predicted and experimental data is less than 3%, which demonstrates that the scale analysis method coupled with an optimization algorithm represents a promising approach to obtain precise correlations. For nanofluids, the results show that the improvement of the heat transfer rate by the addition of Cu nanoparticles is generally better than that of Al2O3, but it strongly depends on Hartmann and Rayleigh numbers. Also, for weak Hartmann numbers, Al2O3 nanoparticles are useless because the heat transfer rate decreases.

title: CLKAN-DBPred: Leveraging pre-trained protein language models with convolutional layer Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for predicting DNA-binding proteins
abstract:
DNA-binding protein prediction helps to understand the fundamental process of life activities. Existing computational methods targeting large-scale DBPs are cost-effective and fast compared to conventional biochemical experiments. However, many earlier in-silico techniques rely on shallow or handcrafted descriptors that may not fully capture contextual sequence information. Recent pre-trained biological language models (BLMs) improve sequence representation by learning rich contextual characteristics from proteins.
Methods
In this study, we develop CLKAN-DBPred, an integrated framework for predicting binding activity of DBPs using a fine-tuned approach that integrates DistilProtBert, Prot-T5, and ESM2 embeddings, the RFE-F7-1195 representation, and a convolutional KAN classifier. Training used hard-label cross-entropy together with a KL-divergence term computed against smoothed targets (epsilon = 0.10; kl_weight = 1.5). Additional component-wise loss ablations, KAN pathway and spline-parameter sensitivity analyses, pure machine-learning baselines, and paired statistical tests were conducted.
Results
CLKAN-DBPred achieved 85.04 Acc, 0.7009 MCC, 0.8489 F1, and 0.9075 AUC in the reported fivefold CV evaluation and 81.76 Acc, 0.6352 MCC, 0.8163 F1, and 0.8905 AUC on PDB296. It obtained the highest AUC and MCC among the compared DBP predictors. The added analyses localized most of the KAN contribution to the spline pathway and showed limited sensitivity to the tested loss and spline settings. Against a direct XGBoost baseline on RFE-F7-1195, CLKAN-DBPred achieved stronger mean CV performance; paired independent-test differences in Acc, MCC, F1, and AUC were not significant. These results support CLKAN-DBPred as a competitive sequence-based framework for DBP prediction. All data and models are available at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18023779.

title: A comparative evaluation of deep learning and traditional clustering methods for automated point-of-care urinalysis
abstract: Accurate interpretation of urine test strips is vital for point-of-care (POC) diagnostics; however, manual readings are constrained by subjectivity, inter-observer variability, and inconsistent environmental conditions. This study presents a systematic comparison of three segmentation paradigms, K-means clustering, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN), and the Segment Anything Model (SAM), for automated identification and delineation of reagent pads on ACON MISSION 10-parameter urine test strips. A dedicated portable imaging system was developed using a Raspberry Pi 4 with controlled LED-based illumination inside a fully enclosed 3D-printed chamber. Analytically prepared synthetic urine solutions (S1–S4) spanning clinically relevant concentration ranges for seven analytes, including glucose (500–2000mg/dL), protein (50–200mg/dL), and occult blood (0.75–3.0mg/dL), were used to generate a dataset of 120 images across five test conditions. All experiments were performed with five replicates per condition and five image captures per strip to assess reproducibility. From aggregate confusion-matrix analysis, SAM achieved 99.34% pixel-wise accuracy (± 0.15%), 94.34% precision, 87.71% recall, and an F1-score of 0.909, compared to K-means (96.57% accuracy, 52.69% precision, F1 = 0.622) and DBSCAN (94.56% accuracy, 38.46% precision, F1 = 0.513). The mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 83.32% (± 0.54%) further confirms SAM’s superior ability to delineate reagent pad boundaries with high fidelity. Statistical analysis revealed that SAM maintained a coefficient of variation below 0.5% across all concentration levels, demonstrating robust invariance to chromatic shifts. While this proof-of-concept utilizes synthetic samples under controlled conditions, the results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying transformer-based segmentation on low-cost embedded hardware for objective, automated urinalysis.

title: Bayesian-inspired fusion-based deep orthogonal decomposition strategy for quality-oriented fault detection
abstract: In modern industrial processes, quality-oriented fault detection is significantly challenged by the presence of multiple quality indicators, complex variable interactions, and the coexistence of quality-related and quality-unrelated variations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Bayesian-inspired Fusion-based Deep Orthogonal Decomposition (BF-DOD) strategy. First, a Bayesian-inspired mutual information fusion mechanism is developed to integrate the relevance scores across multiple quality indicators. This enables an effective partition of the original process variable space into distinct quality-related and quality-unrelated subspaces. Subsequently, a deep orthogonal decomposition framework is applied to hierarchically extract latent features from both partitioned spaces. Specifically, the quality-related subspace undergoes singular value decomposition based on cross-covariance structures to capture both dominant and subtle quality-sensitive variations. Concurrently, the quality-unrelated subspace is modeled using a deep residual principal component analysis strategy to recursively extract residual dynamics. During online monitoring, a unified Bayesian-inspired evidence-fusion mechanism heuristically combines the multi-layer monitoring indicators through Bayes-type normalization, thereby enhancing fault sensitivity, interpretability, and robustness. Finally, extensive case studies involving a numerical example, a three-phase flow process, and the Tennessee Eastman process, along with an ablation study, demonstrate that the proposed BF-DOD method exhibits competitive advantages. It successfully improves the detection of quality-related faults while effectively suppressing false alarms triggered by quality-unrelated disturbances.

title: Machine learning-driven analysis of Raman spectra for high-throughput characterization of functionalized graphene oxide composites
abstract: A combination of electrochemical exfoliation of graphite and machine learning was employed for the design of functionalized graphene oxide. From the Raman spectra of 31 samples modified with phenolic and amine compounds, the band area ratios SD/SG, SD′/SG, SD′′/SG, SD′/SD were calculated. The ensemble algorithms CatBoost and AdaBoost were applied to regression and classification tasks. CatBoost delivered the best overall performance: R2 = 0.97 ± 0.03 for defectiveness prediction and classification accuracy of 0.99 ± 0.01 (phenols 91%, amines 89%). The effectiveness depends on the nature of the modifier: AdaBoost predicts oxidation parameters more accurately for phenols (MAE = 0.19 ± 0.03), whereas CatBoost better predicts defectiveness for nitro compounds and heterocyclic amines (MAE = 0.14 ± 0.06). SHAP analysis confirmed the leading role of spectral descriptors, with the degree of oxidation dominating defectiveness prediction (mean |SHAP| = 0.63). Fundamental limitations were revealed for the amorphous phase descriptor, showing negative R2 under leave-one-group-out cross-validation (CatBoost: −0.12, AdaBoost: −0.48). The approach is promising for high-throughput analysis and the rational design of carbon composites.

title: Dual-branch spectral prediction network based on pearson feature marking
abstract: Aiming at the three core problems prevalent in deep learning models for near-infrared spectroscopic quantitative analysis, namely insufficient ability to distinguish the importance of wavelengths features, difficulty in collaborative extraction of global-local spectral information, and high redundancy of network structures, this paper proposes a Pearson feature marking-based dual-branch spectral prediction network (Mark-GLNet). This method first quantifies the correlation between each wavelengths feature and the prediction target via the Pearson correlation coefficient, screens key sensitive wavelengths, and effectively suppresses spectral redundant information; furthermore, a dual-branch parallel architecture consisting of Global Dependency Modeling (GDM) and Local Feature Mining (LFM) is constructed, in which the GDM module captures the long-range dependencies of spectral sequences through the multi-head self-attention mechanism, the LFM module extracts local fine-grained features of adjacent spectral wavelengths using multi-scale convolution, and collaborative optimization of global semantics and local details is finally realized through feature fusion. Systematic experiments on four public near-infrared spectral datasets from the pharmaceutical, agricultural and food fields demonstrate that Mark-GLNet exhibits excellent performance in both prediction accuracy and model robustness, and its dual-branch structure can effectively balance the global dependency characteristics and local feature details of spectral sequences. Ablation experiments further verify the independent effectiveness and synergistic enhancement effect of the GDM and LFM modules. The proposed network has a concise structure, favorable scalability and engineering practical value while maintaining high performance, providing a reliable deep learning solution for the quantitative analysis of high-dimensional complex spectral data.

title: Temporal representation enhanced latent predictive modeling for multivariate process monitoring
abstract: Fault detection in multivariate dynamic processes remains challenging because of strong variable correlations, temporal dependencies, and limited abnormal labels. Conventional statistical monitoring may be insufficient for weak dynamic deviations, while deep learning models do not always exploit compact latent representations or explicit temporal information. To address these issues, this study proposes a latent predictive monitoring framework that combines principal component analysis (PCA), learnable temporal encoding, and gated recurrent unit (GRU)-based multi-step prediction. Process measurements are projected into a compact PCA score space, augmented with explicit temporal representations, and monitored through prediction residuals between observed and predicted latent trajectories. The proposed framework is evaluated on the Benchmark Simulation Model No. 1 and further validated using industrial papermaking process data. On the BSM1 benchmark, the method achieved an average fault detection rate of 88.02 ± 2.73% with an average false alarm rate of 1.62 ± 0.15%, outperforming classical statistical methods and several deep learning baselines, particularly in slowly evolving and weakly distinguishable fault scenarios. The industrial case further demonstrated the transferability of the framework while revealing section-dependent false alarm behavior. These results indicate that integrating latent space projection with explicit temporal representation can improve the separability of prediction residuals in multivariate dynamic monitoring tasks.

title: Spatiotemporal learning with dynamic coordination for simultaneous classification and concentration regression of ozone and coexisting pollutant gases via MOS sensor arrays
abstract: Accurate monitoring of ground-level ozone and coexisting air pollutants remains challenging for low-cost metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensor arrays because their cross-sensitive responses are jointly governed by inter-sensor spatial correlations, gas-surface temporal dynamics, and task conflicts between gas identification and concentration regression. Here, we propose Spatiotemporal feature Decoupling with Dynamic task Coordination for Multi-Task Learning (STDC-MTL), an uncertainty-coordinated learning framework for simultaneous gas classification and concentration regression using MOS sensor-array signals. STDC-MTL explicitly integrates a hybrid spatiotemporal encoder for array-temporal correlation modeling, a dual-branch local-global feature learning module that separately captures neighborhood temporal variations and long-range response dependencies, and a Bayesian uncertainty-driven coordination mechanism for adaptive task balancing. Experimental results on a custom dataset of ozone, acetone, NO, NO2, and NH3 show that STDC-MTL achieves 100% classification accuracy and a concentration regression R2 of 0.998. More importantly, it reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) by 42.6% compared with the state-of-the-art Gaussian-TCN baseline, with an average normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) of 0.0138 and only 0.37 million parameters. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves quantitative prediction under cross-sensitive MOS responses while maintaining a lightweight architecture, providing an effective algorithmic strategy for intelligent air-pollutant sensing.

title: Testing for dilution effects in group testing
abstract: Group testing is widely used to improve screening efficiency in populations with low prevalence, but pooling may reduce assay sensitivity through dilution. Existing statistical work often incorporates this effect as a modeling assumption or design constraint, while the question of whether a dilution effect is present in a specific testing procedure is less often treated as a formal inferential problem. This paper develops a hypothesis testing framework for assessing dilution effects under a binary measurement error model. Dilution is represented by an increase in the group-specific false negative rate as pool size increases, with specificity assumed to remain stable across pool sizes. We derive closed-form estimators and one-sided test statistics for both unknown- and known-prevalence settings, using normal and Poisson approximations together with null-bootstrap critical-value calibration. Simulation studies show that the proposed procedures control type I error reasonably well and gain power as the dilution effect becomes stronger, although detection is more difficult under very low prevalence. Applications to infectious disease screening settings and SARS-CoV-2 pooled NAAT data illustrate how the framework can quantify evidence for reduced sensitivity under pooling.

title: Tail-aware Vis–NIR calibration of soil traits: Partial and sparse-group-lasso quantile regression versus PLS on the LUCAS library
abstract: This paper applies quantile-based statistical methodologies to visible and near-infrared (Vis–NIR) spectral data. Vis–NIR spectroscopy is the standard tool for rapid, non-destructive estimation of soil and agricultural traits, a task for which partial least squares (PLS) regression has been the gold standard for years. PLS, however, targets the conditional mean: it returns a single central value that is silent about the spread and tails of the conditional distribution. Its wavelength-level interpretations are also dense and tied to that mean. Yet when soil traits are skewed and heteroscedastic, predictive uncertainty varies sharply from sample to sample, so a description of the full conditional distribution — and a calibrated prediction interval — is more informative than a point estimate. We reframe spectral calibration as a high dimensional, multivariate quantile regression problem, benchmarking two methodologies against PLS on the LUCAS topsoil Vis–NIR library: fast partial quantile regression (FPQR) for prediction, and adaptive sparse group lasso quantile regression (ASGL-QR) for prediction and band selection. Across 100 Monte Carlo train–test partitions, both quantile methodologies matched PLS performance at the median. They additionally estimated the 10th and 90th percentiles, forming calibrated 80% prediction intervals with empirical coverage close to nominal. ASGL-QR band selection was stable across repetitions and revealed that the informative spectral region shifts toward the tail for right-skewed traits. These results show that quantile calibration delivers the full conditional distribution and a per-sample uncertainty statement at no cost to central accuracy.

title: Stationary-based self-supervised contrastive learning for soft measurement of free Calcium Oxide
abstract: Free Calcium Oxide (f-CaO) content in cement clinker is a pivotal quality indicator for cement production, and accurate detection of this content is considered the core of intelligent control for cement calcination processes. However, the scarcity of labeled f-CaO samples limits the performance of traditional soft measurement models. More critically, the stationary of the cement production process exerts a dominant impact on clinker f-CaO content, where non-stationary dynamic fluctuations in the cement production process directly affect the variation of f-CaO content. Nevertheless, existing self-supervised contrastive learning methods developed for industrial soft measurement are rarely tailored to the non-stationary of cement production processes, leading to learned features that deviate from actual production state characteristics and fail to cope with complex dynamic process variations. To address these problems, a stationary-based Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning (SSCL) method for f-CaO soft measurement is proposed. Stationary labels and scores are constructed via a dynamically adjustable sliding window and the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test. A multi-channel attention and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) feature extraction module is designed to capture variable coupling and long-range temporal dependencies, and a stationary weighted contrastive loss function is developed to guide the learning of robust stationary features. Experimental results obtained from real industrial cement production data verify that the proposed SSCL model achieves optimal prediction performance. The proposed model is demonstrated to outperform comparative models, and prediction accuracy and generalization ability are significantly improved under limited labeled data conditions.

title: Leakage-safe benchmarking of conventional chemometric and deep learning models for food NIR spectroscopy regression
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is widely used in food systems for rapid, non-destructive estimation of compositional and quality attributes. Although machine-learning and deep-learning models are increasingly reported for spectral regression, practical model selection is often hindered by heterogeneous validation setups and the risk of information leakage during preprocessing and tuning. In this study, we provide a leakage-safe benchmark across nine food-related regression tasks spanning different sample sizes and spectral dimensionalities. Conventional chemometric and regression baselines (partial least squares regression, ridge regression, and support vector regression) are compared with lightweight deep-learning baselines (a shallow artificial neural network and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network) under a unified leakage-safe evaluation framework combining nested cross-validation with acomplementary fixed held-out test-set assessment, fold-wise preprocessing, and repeated training for stochastic models. Performance is summarized primarily using prediction error (RMSE in nested cross-validation and RMSEP on the held-out test set), while the coefficient of determination is retained as a secondary descriptive measure, complemented by cross-validation and fixed held-out-test learning-curve analyses together with model-complexity analysis. Across both validation analyses, ridge regression achieved the largest number of numerical task-level wins, while partial least squares regression and support vector regression remained competitive across multiple tasks. Paired randomization tests following van der Voet further showed that some small numerical differences between models were not statistically distinguishable. Artificial neural network and one-dimensional convolutional neural network baselines did not provide a reliable generalization advantage and showed greater variability in some data-limited settings. From a food-measurement perspective, these findings indicate that well-validated conventional models remain a strong default for routine NIR calibration workflows and non-destructive quality assessment. Deep learning appears most justified when calibration settings provide larger datasets, stronger experimental control, or spectroscopy-specific inductive bias that can translate added model complexity into practical measurement gains. Overall, this study serves as a controlled benchmark and reference for model selection under realistic food-spectroscopy data regimes.

title: Diffusion regulated particle filtering via Bayesian transfer learning for nonlinear state estimation
abstract: Particle filtering is effective for nonlinear Bayesian state estimation, but uncertain model dynamics may bias particle propagation and degrade posterior approximation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a diffusion regulated particle filter via Bayesian transfer learning for nonlinear state estimation under model uncertainty. Different from existing robust particle filters that only exploit target domain information, the proposed method incorporates predictive knowledge from a related source domain and adaptively regulates its contribution according to target measurements. The source predictive distribution is represented by weighted particles and transformed into a kernelized transferable density. A positive tuning factor is introduced to regulate the diffusion degree of this transferred particle density, thereby extending the covariance scaling mechanism from Gaussian transfer estimation to nonparametric particle based Bayesian filtering. The tuning factor is inferred online from target measurements under a variational Bayesian criterion, so that source knowledge is strengthened when it is consistent with the target data and weakened when negative transfer may occur. Compared with conventional robust particle filters, the proposed approach provides an adaptive mechanism for balancing source predictive knowledge and target measurements, thereby improving posterior approximation accuracy without requiring an exact target dynamic model. The resulting estimator preserves the essential transfer mechanism of covariance regulated Gaussian prediction while removing the linearity and Gaussian restrictions. Theoretical analysis is provided to establish boundedness of the transfer corrected importance weights and convergence of the empirical posterior approximation. Simulation studies on nonlinear target tracking and a nonlinear torsion system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method under uncertain dynamics and measurement models.

title: State-of-the-art review of graph neural networks for chemical process fault detection and diagnosis: Applications and implementation guidelines
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) offer a novel and effective approach for fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) in highly interconnected chemical process systems. By explicitly modeling relational and structural dependencies among process variables and units, GNNs provide a powerful alternative to conventional deep learning methods, which often overlook the intrinsic connectivity of chemical plants. This review presents a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art GNN-based FDD frameworks and their applications in chemical process industries. We first introduce the fundamental principles and architectures of GNNs, including graph convolutional networks, recurrent GNNs, graph autoencoders, spatiotemporal GNNs, graph attention networks, semi-supervised GNNs, and multi-scale GNNs, emphasizing their ability to capture fault propagation pathways and inter-unit interactions. Recent studies are surveyed, highlighting the superior performance of GNNs in fault detection and localization. Key advantages, including relational learning, early fault identification, and message-passing mechanisms for local and global behavior, are discussed. Practical implementation guidelines are provided, including graph-based process representation, graph representation learning, model training strategies, and online deployment. Industrial case studies, particularly distillation columns, demonstrate how graph-structured modeling enhances fault detection, localization, and interpretability. Finally, current limitations such as limited industrial adoption, interpretability challenges, and a lack of standardized implementation practices are outlined, and future research directions are proposed to develop robust, scalable, and explainable GNN-based FDD frameworks for Industry 4.0 chemical plants.

title: Inversion soil organic matter using transformer based on partitioned attention mechanism with ZY1-02D hyperspectral
abstract: This study focuses on the highland red soil area in Dongchuan District, Kunming City, Yunnan Province. Using ZY1-02D satellite hyperspectral imagery as the data source, a total of 266 soil samples were collected, and the dataset was divided into a training set and a testing set in a 7:3 ratio. To address the issues of high noise and complexity in remote sensing data, we jointly applied direct standardization (DS) and piecewise direct standardization (PDS) for spectral correction. Furthermore, we combined standard normal variate (SNV), Savitzky-Golay (SG) smoothing, and first derivative (FD) preprocessing, along with competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) for feature band selection. On this basis, we proposed a partition-based deep learning model, SpecPAT-Net, for soil organic matter (SOM) content inversion. The model employs a lightweight CNN-Transformer hybrid architecture, incorporating a partition attention mechanism and a partition-weighted loss function to focus on critical spectral regions. The results demonstrate that the SpecPAT-Net model achieves optimal predictive performance on the test set: R2 = 0.5263, RMSE = 12.2293 g/kg, RPD = 1.4529, and RPIQ = 1.8644. Compared to the unimproved Transformer baseline model, R2 is improved by 0.2434, RMSE is reduced by 2.8176, and RPD and RPIQ are increased by 0.2720 and 0.3491, respectively. Furthermore, SHAP analysis was employed to interpret the 10 sensitive bands associated with SOM, and the proposed inversion model was used to predict the spatial distribution of SOM in the study area. The inversion results reveal that SOM in the study area exhibits a patchy distribution pattern, with higher contents in mid-to-high elevation gentle slope zones and lower contents in river valleys and agricultural reclamation areas. This spatial pattern is closely related to vegetation cover, topographic slope, and climatic conditions. This study provides a new framework for large-scale remote sensing inversion of SOM in mountainous red soils of the Yunnan Plateau. Codes are available at https://github.com/Liu641aaa/SpecPAT-Net.

title: Instrument-shift-informed source-domain augmentation for calibration transfer in near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Differences in instrumental response can degrade a calibration model when it is transferred to another instrument. We propose instrument-shift-informed source-domain augmentation (ISSA), which uses a limited number of paired spectra to adapt a source calibration model without target-domain reference values during transfer-set construction, parameter selection, or model fitting. Source-space PCA-KS preselects M candidates for paired measurement, and unlabeled screening retains K representative inter-instrument differences. Scaled convex perturbations generated from these differences augment the source spectra used to train a partial least squares regression model. ISSA was evaluated on the Corn, Tablet, and Wheat datasets across 10 transfer directions and six budgets (K=5–30; M=7–38). It reduced validation RMSE relative to direct application of the source model in all 60 direction–budget combinations, with a mean reduction of 73.3%. Thus, ISSA improved cross-instrument prediction under the pointwise-aligned, limited-pair conditions studied here without correcting target spectra at prediction time.

title: BRing Harmony to oscillatory systems: A Hue–SSWT approach for descriptor extraction from non-stationary chromogenic oscillations
abstract: Oscillatory chemical reactions often exhibit time-dependent period variations, limiting the usefulness of conventional scalar period descriptors for non-stationary signals. Here, we combine Hue-based digital imaging with the synchrosqueezed wavelet transform (SSWT) to extract operational descriptors from chromogenic oscillations, including frequency-drift turning points, harmonic-transition behavior, and symmetry-related temporal indices. Surrogate-signal analysis demonstrated recovery of predefined structural features under controlled waveform conditions. Applied to the Briggs–Rauscher reaction, the method revealed that starch and Mn(II) affect different aspects of oscillatory dynamics, including persistence, frequency drift, harmonic organization, and waveform symmetry. Replicate-level analysis further showed that these descriptors exhibit distinct condition-dependent response patterns, providing complementary information. The Hue–SSWT workflow therefore provides a methodological proof of concept for compact and interpretable characterization of non-stationary chromogenic oscillations.

title: An adaptive multimodal fusion framework based on hyperspectral imaging for geographical origin authentication of botanical products: A case study of Forsythiae Fructus
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) simultaneously provides spectral and spatial information, thus offering a promising tool for geographical origin authentication of botanical products. However, the respective contributions and complementarity of various modalities remain inadequately understood, making it difficult to effectively integrate their complementary information. This study aimed to evaluate the respective contributions of spectral and image modalities to the geographical origin authentication of Forsythiae Fructus (a traditional Chinese medicine) and develop an adaptive fusion strategy for integrating these complementary modalities. Samples were collected from four major production regions in China, and their HSI data were acquired. A transfer learning-based Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) was employed to automatically extract regions of interest (ROIs) from individual fruits. Single-modality models based on spectral, shallow-image (textural), and deep-image features, together with early fusion models and an adaptive spectral–deep-image mid-level fusion model, were systematically established and compared. Among the single-modality models, the spectral modality achieved the best classification performance. However, the image modalities captured discriminative characteristics different from those of the spectral modality, thereby providing complementary information for multimodal fusion. The early fusion model combining spectral and shallow-image features achieved an accuracy of 0.9093, whereas the proposed adaptive spectral–deep-image fusion model achieved the highest accuracy of 0.9402. Ablation experiments further demonstrated that the adaptive mechanism enhanced fusion effectiveness and improved the ability of the model to capture inter-sample differences. These findings clarify the complementary contributions of different HSI modalities and establish an adaptive framework for geographical origin authentication of botanical products.

title: Rapid profiling of relative chemical distribution patterns of major constituents in whole green Amazonian Robusta beans by near-infrared spectral resolution
abstract: To address the limited chemical data on Amazonian Robusta, this proof-of-concept study evaluated the relative distribution patterns of trigonelline, caffeine, carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and organic acids in green coffee beans from Rondônia produced by indigenous farmers, Acre, and Amazonas. Analyses were conducted directly on whole beans using near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy, providing a rapid and minimally invasive approach, while analytical standards of coffee constituents were similarly analyzed and incorporated into the resolution process as chemically oriented initial estimates. Principal component analysis revealed substantial overlap among the coffee samples, supporting the subsequent application of multivariate curve resolution–alternating least squares (MCR-ALS) to obtain more interpretable chemical information. MCR-ALS resolved spectral profiles associated with the target constituents and revealed distinct relative chemical distribution patterns among coffee samples, mainly for chlorogenic acids, caffeic acid, sucrose, casein, and lipids. These results provide preliminary comparisons of compositional trends that may be associated with origin-related chemical patterns among Amazonian regional coffees, as well as correlations between relative concentration profiles and overall sensory quality. The use of chemically oriented initial estimates enabled the resolution and interpretation of complex coffee spectra as multiple relative chemical profiles directly from whole coffee beans.

title: Transfer calibrated mode probability learning for multiple model state estimation in dynamic process monitoring
abstract: This paper studies multiple model state estimation for dynamic processes operating under switching regimes, model mismatch, and uncertain mode transitions. Such situations frequently arise in process monitoring, soft sensing, and laboratory dynamic systems, where different operating modes may coexist and the available model set is often imperfect. Classical interacting multiple model (IMM) estimators update mode probabilities only through likelihood-based Bayesian recursion. When the transition matrix is misspecified or the local process models are inaccurate, the resulting mode posterior may remain diffuse or assign excessive probability to an incorrect operating mode, leading to degraded state estimation performance. To address this problem, a transfer-calibrated mode probability learning scheme is proposed. The conventional IMM mode posterior is treated as a baseline and is corrected by a transferable compatibility prior constructed from innovation statistics, fused-state consistency, and transition information. The calibrated mode probabilities are obtained in a closed form through probability reweighting, while the per-mode Kalman filters and the original multiple-model structure remain unchanged. A KL-based calibration strength is further introduced to control the deviation from the IMM baseline and reduce the risk of negative transfer. Probabilistic analysis shows that, under moderate compatibility assumptions, the calibrated posterior increases the concentration of probability on the true operating mode. Simulation studies on a switching dynamic process, a one-degree-of-freedom laboratory torsion system, and a multimode continuous stirred-tank reactor demonstrate that the proposed method improves state estimation and mode identification under model mismatch, with more reliable mode probability learning than the conventional IMM.

title: Overcoming intra-root heterogeneity in astragali radix through multi-segment LIBS spectral fusion for improved mineral element quantification
abstract: Intra-root heterogeneity poses a major challenge for the quality control of Astragalus membranaceus (Astragali Radix). Conventional assessment typically relies on a single representative segment, which overlooks the inherent structural variations and fails to capture the holistic profile of the entire organ. In this study, we demonstrate that the heterogeneity is predominantly radial, between phloem and xylem, rather than longitudinal. Each root was divided into four key segments (upper/lower × phloem/xylem) and analyzed by laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS). Principal component analysis combined with Mahalanobis distance (PCA-MD) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) revealed strong spectral differences between phloem and xylem, which were validated by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) elemental analysis. To overcome tissue-specific bias, low-level and mid-level data fusion strategies were developed. A supervised fusion strategy combining variable importance in projection (VIP) and competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) was used to select key features from each tissue before concatenation. The fused spectra, correlated with a mass-weighted average of the whole-root elemental content, demonstrated significantly superior predictive performance for K and Ca (PLSR: R2 = 0.841 and 0.846, respectively) compared to any single segment. K and Ca serve as demonstration targets for methodological validation rather than comprehensive markers of medicinal efficacy, thereby facilitating robust model development. Our findings offer a more information-rich approach for spectroscopic quantification of mineral elements in spatially heterogeneous medicinal roots, and in future work this strategy could be extended to bioactive compounds such as saponins, flavonoids and polysaccharides.

title: Leakage-aware window-based chemometric monitoring for event-level anomaly detection in batch distillation
abstract: Batch distillation processes exhibit dynamic and phase-dependent behavior, making anomaly detection a challenging task in multivariate process monitoring. This study proposes a leakage-aware window-based chemometric learning framework for event-level anomaly detection using sensor and actuator time series. The framework transforms multivariate process trajectories into temporal windows described by local statistical descriptors, compares several supervised classifiers, and evaluates predictive performance using stratified grouped cross-validation by experiment. This validation strategy keeps all windows from the same experiment within the same fold, reducing information leakage and allowing model performance to be assessed on unseen experiments. The final analytical dataset contained 11,413 windows, 217 predictor variables, and 119 experiments. Tree-based ensemble models achieved the strongest window-level performance. Extra Trees obtained the highest F1-score, 0.655 ± 0.047, while Random Forest achieved a comparable F1-score, 0.653 ± 0.037, with ROC-AUC 0.862 ± 0.022 and average precision 0.719 ± 0.083. At the experiment level, Random Forest provided the best operational trade-off, detecting 75 out of 81 anomalous experiments while producing false alarms in 15 out of 38 normal experiments. Threshold-based and temporal persistence-based alert rules were analyzed to study the balance between sensitivity and false alarm reduction. Permutation importance showed that temperature-related variables, pressure-related variables, and actuator signals contributed to anomaly detection, with range and standard deviation emerging as the most informative window descriptors.
