Under the reference structural scenario, assuming afforestation of 70% of the site area, locally plausible forest types compensated 37.3–39.6% of the initial carbon debt at Site 1 after 100 years, while a theoretical evergreen broad-leaved forest upper bound reached 60.2%. The corresponding compensation at Site 2 was 11.9–20.0%, and none of the simulated forest types fully repaid the project carbon debt within 100 years. The projected compensation was strongly influenced by land availability and assumptions governing forest productivity-heterotrophic respiration coupling, whereas afforestation-establishment emissions had only a minor effect. Afforestation can therefore provide partial, long-term compensation for remediation-stage carbon debt but cannot substitute for direct emission reductions during remediation. Integrating remediation-stage environmental assessment with post-remediation carbon accounting provides a life cycle-oriented basis for coordinating lower-carbon remediation with ecological redevelopment of industrial brownfields.

title: Regional cleaner production through carbon unlocking strategies assessment: lessons from major industrial hubs
abstract: Most studies on carbon efficiency and carbon unlocking have generally focused on aggregate performance or single-stage production processes, providing limited evidence on how carbon unlocking constraints arise from the interdependent production and environmental treatment stages and how these constraints evolve over time under heterogeneous conditions. To address this gap, this study constructs a two-stage dynamic network slacks-based measure (SBM) model based on a meta-frontier framework, dividing the carbon unlocking process into the production stage and the treatment stage, and conducts dynamic measurement and decomposition analysis for 29 provinces in China from 2011 to 2022. The results show that, under the meta-frontier, provincial carbon unlocking efficiency is generally lower than that under group-frontier, indicating significant regional technology gaps. Efficiency in the treatment stage is generally higher than in the production stage, with the latter constituting the main bottleneck to overall efficiency improvement. Further grouping analysis based on different development characteristics reveals systematic differences in the sources of carbon unlocking constraints and improvement paths across region types. High development and technology frontier regions need to focus more on treatment investment efficiency and abatement cost control, whereas regions with medium-to-low development levels, high carbon dependence, or technology catch-up characteristics face carbon unlocking bottlenecks mainly in the production stage, particularly in energy use patterns and carbon emission efficiency. By moving beyond aggregate or static assessments of carbon unlocking efficiency, this study provide a novel perspective on regional carbon unlocking efficiency, identify transferable unlocking pathways under different development conditions, and offer policy-relevant insights for countries with diverse economic structures and development stages seeking to advance carbon unlocking.

title: A four-party evolutionary game analysis of port emission reduction under constraint-based carbon regulation and cargo owner preferences
abstract: This study develops a four-party evolutionary game model involving government, port, shipping enterprise, and cargo owner to examine port emission reduction under constraint-based carbon regulation and cargo owner green preferences. The objective is to clarify how regulatory constraints and demand-side green preferences interact to influence enterprise emission-reduction behavior and the stability of coordinated port decarbonization. Constraint-based policy instruments are represented through policy-specific penalty functions, while a market response function links the evolving cargo-owner green preference to the market share benefits and losses of both the port and shipping enterprise. The results show that a minimum regulatory threshold is necessary for the coordinated emission-reduction equilibrium to become stable. When enforcement intensity is below this threshold, demand-side green preferences alone cannot drive system-wide convergence. Cargo owner green preferences can complement regulatory penalties within bounded parameter ranges by increasing the market returns of proactive emission reduction and the market losses of passive behavior. The system also shows a staged convergence pattern in which government regulation first affects enterprise emission-reduction behavior, and cargo owner green preferences become effective only after low-carbon service supply becomes sufficiently credible. These findings suggest that coordinated port emission reduction is more likely to be supported by credible regulatory enforcement combined with market cultivation than by relying on either regulatory pressure or market preferences alone.

title: Closed-loop recovery of Pt from acidic wastewater using thiazole-functionalized polyethyleneimine: self-separation and electrochemical polymer regeneration
abstract: Platinum (Pt) accumulates in industrial wastewaters from electronics manufacturing and hydrometallurgical processes, causing both resource waste and potential ecological risks. Current recovery methods using polyelectrolytes are generally limited by poor selectivity and their reliance on ultrafiltration or immobilization. This work proposes a closed-loop process for Pt recovery based on a cooperative coordination self-separation strategy using a thiazole-functionalized polyethyleneimine (PEI), which bears S/N donor sites and spontaneously forms micrometer-sized aggregates upon coordination with Pt(IV). Compared with PEI-assisted ultrafiltration, this strategy exhibits substantially improved selectivity and greatly simplified separation. Leveraging this property, Pt(IV) can be directly separated by microfiltration without immobilization or ultrafiltration, achieving a maximum uptake capacity of 696.7 mg/g and adsorption equilibrium within seconds (<10 s), with a removal of >97% under strongly acidic, chloride-rich, multi-metal, and ligand-containing conditions. Importantly, this metal-bridging self-separation behavior is selective: aggregation is induced only by metal ions that are both soft acids and possess sufficient coordination connectivity, such as Pd(II), Au(III), and Hg(II). In contrast, hard acids, borderline ions, and low-connectivity Ag(I) do not induce bridging. The Pt-loaded polymer phase can be converted to PtO2 by calcination or electrochemically reduced to metallic platinum with simultaneous polymer regeneration, enabling both metal recovery and material reuse, with >94% removal after four cycles, thus establishing a closed-loop recovery process. This “coordination recognition-bridging aggregation-self-separation” strategy provides a generalizable molecular design principle for the selective recovery of critical metals.

title: MICP versus MIPP for Cd immobilization: kinetics, products, leaching stability and conversion feasibility
abstract: Microbially induced carbonate/phosphate precipitation (MICP/MIPP) are prevalent techniques for heavy metal (HM) remediation. However, systematic comparative studies on their functional strains, mineralization efficiency, precipitate stability, and integrated application potential are still scarce. Here, the MICP-functional strain Sporosarcina sp. DF-C31 and MIPP-functional strain Burkholderia orbicola PSB4 were employed to investigate their cadmium (Cd2+) mineralization performance. The MICP system achieved 98.98% Cd2+ removal efficiency within 36 h and generated stable calcite precipitate within 72 h, while MIPP immobilized 98.39% of Cd2+ within 168 h and yielded highly crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) within 120 h. The MICP precipitates consisted of a Ca1-xCdxCO3 solid solution, and the MIPP precipitates were composed of Ca10-xCdx(PO4)6(OH)2. Multiple characterization techniques collectively demonstrated that Cd immobilization proceeded via Ca-site substitution and lattice incorporation in both systems. Specifically, MIPP adopted a pathway of surface adsorption followed by lattice migration, while MICP operates via coprecipitation-mediated entrapment. In two-month acid leaching tests, Cd2+ release from MICP precipitates increased significantly under aggressive low-pH conditions. For MICP precipitates, Cd2+ release rates reached 23.86% and 1.70% at pH 2 and pH 4, respectively. In contrast, MIPP precipitates showed only a moderate increase to 10.18% and 0.55%. The sequential MICP-to-MIPP phase conversion process was further evaluated. At an initial Cd concentration of 50 mg/L, HAP formation was negligible at 30 °C and only partial (35.98% conversion) at 50 °C. The corresponding Cd removal efficiencies remained unchanged and increased by 1.1%, respectively. Overall, this integrated strategy provides a condition-dependent remediation approach, where the stability enhancement is critically dependent on the extent of HAP conversion.

title: Improving efficiency in renewable energy systems: A generalized exponential entropy and combinative distance-based assessment for evaluating photovoltaic thermal modules
abstract: The combination of photovoltaic thermal (PVT) modules into contemporary renewable energy sources (RESs) provides a favourable result for improving energy competence and sustainability perspectives. PVT modules generate electricity and heat with sunlight as their energy source. The utilization of multiple criteria decision analysis (MCDA) approaches over diverse factors is significant in evaluating the performance and competence of PVT modules in RESs. Though performance for PVT modules is estimated by diverse attributes including cost, energy generation, durability, and environmental aspects, measuring these indicators remains inspiring to the assessment. This paper discusses a decision-making framework that recognizes commercially presented PVT modules and creates main performance attributes for evaluation. In this line, first, we develop an exponential entropy of order α to determine the weight of indicators. Second, we discuss a combinative distance-based assessment (CODAS) model for assessing PVT modules. The CODAS approach determines the attractiveness of options based on distances from a negative ideal solution using Euclidean and Manhattan distances to enhance prioritization performance. Subsequently, existing MCDA approaches are implemented to prioritize the PVT modules. This study delivers a methodical framework for PVT module assessment. The outcomes highlight the performance of the developed framework in refining the choice of PVT modules and their potential adaptability to further implications.

title: Anabaena azotica alleviates vanadium toxicity and promotes extracellular polymer-associated vanadium sequestration in hydroponically grown Zea mays L
abstract: Vanadium (V) contamination of agricultural systems threatens crop productivity and food safety, while sustainable bio-based remediation strategies remain insufficiently developed. This study investigated whether inoculation with Anabaena azotica (A. azotica) alleviates vanadium (V) toxicity in hydroponically grown maize (Zea mays L.) and examined the potential role of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) associated with the plant–cyanobacterium system in V immobilization. Exposure to 200 μM V severely reduced shoot (66.7%) and root (64.7%) biomass, total root length (95.2%), and photosynthetic efficiency (Fv/Fm, 56.9%), while increasing lipid peroxidation (malondialdehyde, +229%). A. azotica (20 mg L−1) inoculation reduced leaf and root V accumulation by 45.9% and 26.7%, respectively, and recovered biomass (20-28%), root growth (26%), and photosynthetic parameters (47-52%). Oxidative stress was alleviated, as indicated by a 60–65% reduction in MDA levels, accompanied by coordinated changes in antioxidant enzyme (SOD, CAT, APX, POD, GST, and GPX) activities. FTIR, SEM, and ICP–OES characterization of the recovered EPS suggested that hydroxyl-, carboxylate-, and sulfate-associated functional groups may contribute to extracellular V immobilization and reduced V bioavailability. Although extracellular material was substantially higher in V + A than in V alone, the use of living A. azotica means that the observed effects are attributed to combined cyanobacterial–plant-derived extracellular materials, rather than A. azotica-derived polymers alone. Under the hydroponic conditions, A. azotica showed potential as a bioinoculant for reducing V accumulation and alleviating V-induced physiological stress in maize, thereby enhancing plant resilience and supporting its potential as a sustainable strategy for crop production in V-contaminated agroecosystems.

title: Industry-specific sustainability priorities in new product development: Evidence from automotive and chemical industries
abstract: Sustainable new product development requires firms to evaluate product-development options by considering financial, market, product environmental, process environmental and social criteria together. However, the sustainability priorities guiding such decisions may differ across industries because product characteristics, production processes, regulatory exposure and end-of-life conditions are not the same. This study examines how cleaner production-related sustainability priorities shape product-development option prioritization in the automotive and chemical industries. Data were collected from certified industrial R&D professionals and product-development decision makers in Türkiye. A fuzzy multi-criteria decision-support procedure was used to derive sector-specific criterion weights, evaluate real product-development options and aggregate method-specific rankings. The results reveal distinct priority structures. In the automotive application, financial criteria received the highest priority, followed by product environmental and process environmental criteria. In the chemical application, process environmental and product environmental criteria dominated the priority structure, reflecting stronger emphasis on material, recyclability, waste, water, energy and production-related environmental concerns. At the option level, the electric high-passenger-capacity urban bus ranked first in the automotive case, while the 100% recyclable metallocene polyolefin-based packaging film ranked first in the chemical case. These leading options remained stable across sensitivity scenarios. The study contributes to cleaner production-oriented decision making by showing how sector-specific sustainability priorities are translated into product-development option prioritization. The findings should be interpreted as expert-based decision-support results from selected automotive and chemical R&D contexts rather than as direct measurements of product sustainability performance.

title: Longevity index for small electrical and electronic appliances: Qualitative assessment of reliability and durability
abstract: The growing concern over electronic waste and the need to extend product lifespans have highlighted longevity as a key aspect of sustainable product design. This research presents a longevity index as a practical tool for manufacturers and stakeholders to assess, communicate and improve the longevity of small electrical and electronic equipment (sEEE). The main novelty of the study lies in the integration of reliability and durability into a single operational index specifically developed for sEEE, combining technical, repairability, maintenance and warranty-related indicators through a transparent scoring and weighting system. The proposed methodology combines qualitative and quantitative elements to evaluate product longevity in a structured and comparable manner. The index was developed for application to different products within the sEEE category and implemented through an Excel-based tool that guides data collection and automatically calculates the final score. A controlled case-study application involving two products from the same category and three evaluators was conducted to examine the practical application of the method, its ability to differentiate between comparable products and inter-evaluator variability. A sensitivity analysis was also performed to assess the stability of the product scores and ranking under variations in the factor weights. As a decision-support tool, the longevity index contributes to circular economy objectives by providing structured information to support sustainable product choices.

title: Sustainable closed-loop recovery of lithium and cryolite from spent aluminum electrolyte: An alkaline leaching process
abstract: To address the challenge of synergistically extracting lithium and fluorine elements from spent aluminum electrolyte (SAE), this study proposes an integrated resource recovery process of "alkaline leaching — selective lithium adsorption — carbonation for cryolite synthesis — crystallization mother liquor recycling". Following efficient leaching of valuable elements from SAE using sodium hydroxide solution, lithium was first selectively separated through a titanium-based adsorbent. The adsorbent exhibited excellent cycling stability. After six adsorption–desorption cycles, the recycled desorption solution was enriched to 18.04 g/L Li, enabling single-step precipitation of crude Li2CO3 with a purity of 94.59 %. The Li transfer efficiency through the adsorption–desorption stage was estimated to be 75.63 %. Subsequently, fluorine and aluminum were recovered from the residual solution through CO2 carbonation to synthesize cryolite. Under optimized conditions of a synthesis temperature of 70 °C and endpoint pH 10, the cryolite quality met the national standard CH-0 grade. The "causticization–calcination" process was implemented to enable leaching solution recycling. After ten cycles of leaching solution reuse, the leaching efficiency remained above 78.1 %, while cryolite yield stabilized above 94.54 %. Economic analysis indicated the potential economic feasibility of the proposed process. Overall, the proposed route provides an integrated approach for the high-value utilization of SAE.

title: Contextual analysis of Black Soldier Fly farming as a sustainable organic waste treatment system in Bangladesh: Comparative case studies
abstract: Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming has emerged globally as a promising approach to transform organic waste into high-value protein and soil-enhancing frass. However, its novelty faces context-dependent constraints that limit sustainability and broader diffusion, often leading to discontinuation or stagnation. This study aims to explain how interconnected contextual factors affected the implementation and operational processes of BSF farming in practice, thereby hindering its sustainability as an organic waste treatment system. This study selected 10 cases for a comparative case study, comprising discontinued, stagnant, and operational statuses, from six climatic subregions of Bangladesh, established in urban, rural, and peri-urban locations. This study employed multiple qualitative methods for data collection, including participant observation and semi-structured interviews. Following an inductive approach and thematic content analysis, this study identified several limiting and supportive factors across social, economic, environmental, institutional, knowledge, spatial, and temporal aspects that are intertwined with the persistence of BSF farming in the context. Overall, adaptive operations were more frequent, but greater economic uncertainty was evident in cases that discontinued or stagnated. This study found that operational farms demonstrate “multinetwork resilience” to overcome most limiting factors with supportive ones, as evidenced by flexible spatial strategies, experiential knowledge competence, temporal adjustments, and institutional engagement, whereas discontinued farms were overwhelmed. Stagnating farms represented a “persistent niche,” achieving internal viability through partial adaptation but lacking the viable networks and institutional engagement needed to scale production. This study claims that the sustainability of BSF farming emerges from iterative learning and context-specific adjustments. Wider diffusion will require context-sensitive models that appreciate locally led knowledge advancements, incorporate socio-technical and spatio-temporal competencies, accommodate cumulative economic processes and affordability, and are legitimized through multi-level collaborations.

title: Trajectories of carbon storage and productivity dynamics during post-fire forest recovery in severely burned areas of Daxing'an Mountains
abstract: The forest recovery cycle in heavily burned areas is protracted, and carbon sink-oriented restoration strategies remain unclear. This study examines severely burned sites in the Daxing'an Mountains. Planted Larix gmelinii forests (3300 and 4400 trees hm−2) were compared with naturally regenerated Betula platyphylla forests. The standard tree method was used to examine temporal patterns of forest carbon stock (FCS) and stand productivity (SP). Thinning was actually implemented in birch stands and simulated in high-density larch plantations. RDA and path analysis identified primary drivers. Results showed that plantation FCS remained significantly higher than natural forest FCS 35 years post-fire, with the highest value (30.99 t hm−2) in the 3300 trees hm−2 plantation. SP exhibited an initial increase followed by decline. Specifically, natural forest SP peaked earlier and decreased, whereas plantation SP continued increasing for 20 years post-fire before declining. Plantation SP remained higher than natural regeneration for over 20 years post-fire. Thinning increased SP within 5 years, but the effect weakened after 10 years. FCS increased by 105.54% in birch and 60.02% in high-density larch within 10 years after thinning. RDA and path analysis indicated stand density as the primary driver of FCS and SP, and growing-season temperature as the key climatic factor. These results demonstrate that plantations enhance carbon sequestration more than natural regeneration over the medium to long term. Meanwhile, thinning effects exhibited distinct temporal sensitivity. Subsequent management should employ intermittent density regulation to sustainably promote forest recovery.

title: Enhanced-robustness HTO control strategy for safety in alkaline electrolyzer operation
abstract: Alkaline water electrolysis systems are widely used to integrate renewable energy fluctuations and hydrogen production. Due to the high dynamics and intermittency of wind and solar energy, achieving stable and safe dynamic control in such systems remains a challenge. This paper proposes a robustness-enhanced hydrogen to oxygen (HTO) concentration control strategy to improve system safety and operational flexibility. Unlike previous studies employing optimal operation curve tracking controllers, this work proposes a feedforward-feedback composite structure integrated with the Active Disturbance Rejection Control algorithm to enhance control robustness under uncertain conditions through real-time disturbance estimation and compensation. To address the inherent lag in HTO response, an inertial compensation component is incorporated into the Extended State Observer to improve dynamic response speed. Additionally, a Pareto-based pressure feedforward module is developed to balance HTO concentration and electrolysis efficiency and determine a compromise pressure schedule. Validation under five typical dynamic conditions, including load, pressure, and temperature fluctuations, demonstrates that the proposed method reduces HTO control errors by 15% to 80% compared to the optimal operation curve tracking controller, significantly lowering the probability of threshold violations. Monte Carlo simulation-based probabilistic robustness analysis further indicates a 0.8% reduction in the variation range of electrolysis efficiency. Furthermore, measured data confirm that the proposed method achieves renewable energy utilization efficiencies of 96.9% (wind) and 89.6% (photovoltaic) while ensuring fast and disturbance-resistant HTO responses. These results highlight the robustness and efficiency of the proposed method. This study contributes to enhancing the safety margins of green hydrogen production systems and ensuring the secure operation of renewable energy integration.

title: Assessing the impact of realistic fracture network structures on aquifer thermal energy storage efficiency: A comparative analysis of weathered, diagenetic, tectonic, and hydraulic fractures
abstract: Aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) in fractured aquifers is a promising way to mitigate seasonal imbalances between energy supply and demand. However, most existing studies have relied on simplified fracture representations, and the impacts of realistic fracture patterns on ATES performance remain insufficiently quantified. In this study, we numerically investigated ATES performance under three natural fracture patterns of weathered, diagenetic, and tectonic fractures—along with one artificial fracture pattern of hydraulic fractures. Hydraulic fractures with a radial pattern exhibit the highest and most stable heat recovery efficiency (0.92 ± 0.01). Under natural conditions, tectonic fractures with directional patterns lead to a higher heat recovery efficiency (0.75 ± 0.09) compared to weathered/diagenetic fractures with grid patterns (0.67 ± 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirm that enhancing hydraulic connectivity and advection between the injection and extraction wells in fractured aquifers, such as by increasing fracture density and permeability ratio between fractures and rock matrix, can improve thermal performance. The findings clarify that an aquifer with tectonic fractures is more suitable for ATES construction than one with weathered and diagenetic fractures; furthermore, creating hydraulic fractures through reservoir stimulation can further improve ATES efficiency. Quantifying the impact of realistic fracture patterns on ATES performance provides a new reference for selecting optimal fractured aquifer to construct ATES.

title: Multi-dimensional interactive industrial carbon-neutrality pathways for megacities under economic, policy, and technological constraints: Insights from coupled models of Long-Term Energy Alternatives Planning, System Dynamics and Technology Readiness Level
abstract: The challenge of industrial decarbonization in megacities lies in the gap between carbon-neutrality targets and implementable pathways constrained by multi-dimensional interactive factors from technology maturity, policy timing, and the carbon intensity of energy supply. To address this challenge, a novel loosely coupled model using Long-term Energy Alternatives Planning-System, Dynamics-Technology and Readiness Level (LEAP-TRL-SD) model was developed to design implementable industrial carbon-neutrality pathways by integrating economic growth, policy feedback, and maturity-constrained technology deployment, achieving an accuracy of 95.6%. The LEAP model was employed to simulate industry restructuring–driven changes in energy demand and energy carriers, SD was applied to represent dynamic interactions among economic development, policy intervention, and technological progress, and TRL was used to constrain technology deployment timing. Application to Beijing indicated that the optimal scenario reduced carbon emissions from a peak of 161.8 million tons (Mt) to 7.3 Mt. Approximately 81.7% of this reduction was derived from renewable energy-based electricity (83.4%), heat (13%), and hydrogen (3.6%). Sensitivity analysis further identified GDP growth rate as the dominant driver, with a ±10% change leading to an 11.01% deviation in energy demand. This was followed by renewable energy substitution ratio (±6.2–6.6%), process optimization technologies (±3.1%), and policy intensity (±0.32%). By 2050, Beijing's carbon neutrality pathway sustains a 2.8-fold economic growth while reducing emissions to 7.3 Mt, with high-tech service sectors expanding to 50% of industry and average technological decarbonization efficiency rising by 28.5%. The LEAP–TRL–SD model provided a quantitative and practical tool for designing phased, implementable industrial decarbonization strategies under multi-dimensional interactive real-world economic, technological, and policy constraints.

title: Synergistic CO2 capture and NO enrichment by gas separation membranes: Molecular simulation and process analysis
abstract: The enrichment of NO from flue gas provides an important opportunity to enhance wastewater denitrification by the Anaerobic Ammonium Oxidation (Anammox) process, but membrane materials capable of simultaneous CO2 capture and NO enrichment remain underexplored. This study integrates experimental permeation tests with molecular simulations to evaluate various polymeric materials. Among them, the polyvinylamine (PVAm) membrane demonstrated superior performance, characterized by balanced transport properties. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that gas transport in PVAm is primarily driven by a solubility-selective mechanism, with its high-density amino groups providing potent reversible adsorption sites for polar CO2 and NO. Furthermore, its high chain mobility compensates for its low free volume fraction, ensuring a moderate diffusion rate. These insights effectively account for the balance between permeability and selectivity observed in the experiments. Under conceptual process evaluation, CO2 and NO permeability coefficients for PVAm reach 175.67 and 142.53 Barrer, with CO2/N2 and NO/O2 selectivities reaching 46.69 and 5.36. Based on these pure-gas transport parameters, a double-stage conceptual membrane process was projected for future mixed-gas validation. The system effectively concentrated CO2 from 15 vol% to 98.58 vol% and NO from 0.1 vol% to 0.43 vol%, while reducing O2 to 0.75 vol% to mitigate oxygen interference. These results establish a balanced strategy for synergistic carbon capture and Anammox-based wastewater treatment.

title: Diffusion mechanism of pro-environmental behaviors in social networks: Experimental approach
abstract: The diffusion of pro-environmental behaviors in society is crucial because we need to gain time and mitigate social damages due to environmental burdens, considering that solutions based on technological innovations are uncertain. In this article, we aim to elucidate the diffusion mechanism of human pro-environmental behaviors in social networks, identify the factors that promote pro-environmental behavior, and discuss implications for remedies. We conducted laboratory experiments involving university students as subjects. They participated in a public goods game in which they could control the risk of climate change disasters by their contributions within social networks. We examine the effects of an online communication opportunity and an autonomous agent (a bot) that conducts pro-environmental behavior. Generalized linear regression models, generalized linear mixed-effects models, and multinomial logit models are applied to the data of subjects' behaviors. We detect each subject's dominant learning pattern based on estimated parameters for DeGroot, best-practice, and free-riding learning. We obtain three main results. First, communication opportunities seem to positively promote and diffuse pro-environmental behavior, while receiving specific messages urging you to increase your contribution decreases individual contributions. Second, introducing a bot implementing best practices increases the contributions of subjects directly linked to the bot. Third, individual decisions to adjust pro-environmental behavior are determined by a combination of three learning patterns: DeGroot, best-practice, and free-riding learning. The number of those who dominantly use the best-practice learning pattern is much smaller than that of those who dominantly use the free-riding learning pattern.

title: Resilience of copper-cobalt supply chains for the energy transition: A dynamic cascading failure analysis
abstract: Enhancing the resilience of critical mineral supply chains is essential for mitigating risks arising from export disruptions and upstream supply concentration. This study develops a multilayer trade network framework to assess the resilience of global copper and cobalt supply chains under export-reduction shocks. Chile and Peru are selected as copper shock sources, while the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the United States are considered for cobalt. Results show that Peru-origin copper shocks cause disruption-phase impacts comparable to Chile but greater recovery-stage losses, revealing a “smaller-exporter, larger-impact” pattern. DRC-origin cobalt shocks produce greater disruption and recovery losses than U.S.-origin shocks, highlighting vulnerability associated with upstream concentration. Increasing export-reduction ratio reduces resilience, whereas greater risk-resistance capacity mitigates these effects but requires stronger buffering when dominant upstream suppliers are disrupted. Node-level analysis further reveals that apparently stable aggregate resilience can conceal substantial vulnerabilities across countries and supply-chain layers. These findings support differentiated resilience governance based on shock-source position, supply concentration, and layer-specific vulnerability.

title: Influence of food residue contamination on recyclability performance of polyethylene flexible packaging within store drop-off recycling systems
abstract: Flexible plastic packaging is a major source of waste and nuisance litter around the world. Mechanical recycling is an attractive and most widely used, end-of-life option to create a plastic circular economy; however, the impact of residual food contamination on its mechanical recyclability remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the impact of food residue contamination on the recyclability of polyethylene-based food-contact films intended for store drop-off recycling following the Association of Plastic Recyclers (APR) critical guidance protocol. Films from depacked food items (e.g., cheese, snacks, frozen meats, and powdered sugar) were compared to identical clean control films. A 50/50 blend of food-contaminated polyethylene films and control films simulated a worst-case scenario for recycling conditions without a wet wash. Both types were processed into flakes, pelletized, and blown into new films. Residual food content on the package surface ranged from 0.07 to 0.45 mg cm−2 (0.48–6.66 wt.%). Among the tested products, only the sliced cheese blend met APR's melt pressure requirement and all other APR requirements for food-contaminated films. The results indicate food-contaminated polyethylene films require effective cleaning methods, or frequent screen pack changes, to reduce melt pressure and preserve material quality during recycling. These findings demonstrate that food residue represents a critical barrier to achieving circularity in polyethylene film systems under dry mechanical recycling conditions and highlight the need for improved contamination mitigation strategies to maintain recycled material quality in store drop-off streams.

title: Optimizing organic nitrogen substitution for environmental and economic performance in Chinese solar-greenhouse vegetable production: Evidence from a 13-year field experiment and carbon pricing analysis
abstract: Intensive greenhouse vegetable production relies heavily on synthetic nitrogen (N) fertilizers and contributes substantial greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions, yet evidence that organic-N substitution can reduce those emissions while remaining profitable comes mostly from short-term trials. Here, a 13-year randomized tomato–cucumber rotation experiment in a Chinese solar greenhouse was combined with a cradle-to-farm-gate life-cycle assessment and a 30-year techno-economic analysis to compare five fertilization strategies; robustness was tested with a one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis, a 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and simulations at Chinese, U.S., and European carbon-price levels. In the balanced treatment, replacing 50% of synthetic N with N from pig manure and maize straw simultaneously achieved the lowest product carbon footprint, 1870 kg CO2-eq per tonne of fresh vegetables, 17.3% below the conventional over-fertilization baseline. Annual revenue reached approximately US$102,800 per hectare, and the 30-year net present value was positive. In contrast, direct composting and return of crop vines raised total emissions by 4.7% on a per-hectare basis relative to the conventional baseline. Fertilization management dominated environmental differences across scenarios, whereas labor cost constituted the major source of economic uncertainty, whereas carbon pricing increased emission-reduction revenue without altering the strategy ranking. These results provide long-term field evidence that appropriately designed organic-N substitution can align climate mitigation with farm economics in intensive protected-vegetable systems, and they caution against treating organic inputs as inherently low-carbon without a full life-cycle evaluation.

title: Integrating ecosystem services and avian biodiversity for the construction of ecological security patterns: A case study of the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration
abstract: Traditional methods for constructing ecological security patterns (ESPs) primarily focus on ecosystem services or landscape structural connectivity. They rarely characterize ecological processes from the perspective of target species' habitat requirements, resulting in ecological networks that inadequately respond to biological migration, dispersal, and habitat maintenance functions. As critical indicator taxa for ecological environmental changes, birds possess habitat suitability and migration-dispersal processes that effectively reflect urban ecological quality and ecosystem service functions. Taking the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration as a case study, this research integrated ecosystem service assessments and species habitat suitability simulations to identify ecological sources. Furthermore, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) machine learning algorithms were introduced to optimize the ecological resistance surface, facilitating the construction of an ESP that accommodates avian habitat requirements. The results demonstrated the following: (1) Integrating ecosystem services and species habitat suitability simulations identified a total of 136 ecological sources. These sources covered an area of 21,788.05 km2, exhibiting a spatial pattern characterized by “peripheral agglomeration and central sparsity.” (2) The XGBoost model demonstrated high reliability in optimizing the ecological resistance surface, achieving scores of 0.970 and 0.964 for the training and testing sets, respectively. The resistance values displayed a spatial differentiation of “high in the center and low in the periphery.” (3) Based on circuit theory, 135 ecological corridors with a total length of 758.87 km were extracted. Ecological pinch points were primarily concentrated in critical corridor areas, such as northern Kunming City and central Qujing City, whereas ecological barrier points were relatively dispersed. Building upon these findings, this study constructed an ESP featuring “one core, two belts, and multiple zones.” This framework further enhanced the structural integrity and ecological process connectivity of the regional ecological network, aiming to provide a scientific basis for biodiversity conservation and territorial spatial ecological optimization in urban agglomerations.

title: Policy instruments reshaping production profitability: NPV optimization under carbon policy scenarios for an offshore oilfield in the South China Sea
abstract: As carbon regulation expands across China’s industrial sectors, offshore oil and gas operations must incorporate carbon constraints into production decisions to support low-carbon and cleaner production. However, conventional net present value (NPV) optimization often relies on static carbon estimates, with insufficient consideration of changes in emissions and carbon costs induced by production reallocation. This study develops a carbon-accounting and decision-support workflow that couples reservoir numerical simulation with surface equipment modeling. For each production strategy, the workflow evaluates production performance, equipment energy consumption, and carbon emissions, which are then incorporated into an NPV model that accounts for carbon policy instruments. A random-forest sensitivity analysis identifies oil price and production allocation as the two leading factors affecting NPV variability, with normalized importance scores of 48.0% and 24.2%, respectively. Optimization across 32 carbon policy scenarios shows that combining multiple incentive-based policies does not necessarily improve NPV and may reduce it by up to 13.35%. In contrast, a phased policy pathway sustains NPV growth while reducing CO2 emission intensity by 11.1%. Beyond this specific case study, the framework is generalizable to other offshore fields through recalibration. The proposed workflow supports carbon-constrained production planning by linking reservoir performance, surface-equipment energy consumption, carbon accounting, and economic optimization. These findings provide practical decision support for offshore oilfield operators and policy implications for designing coordinated carbon-market instruments.

title: Rotational grazing modulates the soil–plant–animal carbon cycling pump in an alpine ranch on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
abstract: Alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP) store substantial carbon, yet how grazing management regulates carbon transfer across the soil–plant–animal continuum remains poorly resolved. Based on a 5-year (2010–2014) experiment, we compared continuous grazing (CG) and rotational grazing (RG) at two intensities (8 and 16 sheep ha−1) and quantified carbon transfer across plant, livestock, soil, and ecosystem subsystems. At 8 sheep ha−1, RG increased gross primary production by 24.6%, plant to soil carbon by 37.2%, and livestock product carbon by 20.8%, while reducing livestock emissions by 12.0% relative to CG. These benefits were larger at lower intensity. The higher intensity suppressed productivity and respiratory fluxes but elevated emissions. Variation partitioning analysis showed that grazing intensity × climate interactions explained most variation in carbon fixation and respiration fluxes, whereas grazing system × intensity interactions governed trophic carbon transfers. Structural equation modelling revealed that grazing system exerted an indirect positive effect on ecosystem carbon transfer through improved soil physicochemical properties, grazing intensity an indirect negative effect via reduced aboveground biomass, and climate a direct negative effect. Against a dominant climatic forcing, rotational grazing at 8 sheep ha−1 acts as a secondary but actionable modulator of the carbon cycling pump, providing a low-cost strategy to partially buffer climatic pressure while sustaining livestock production on the QXP.

title: Attributing streamflow extremes under compound scenarios via hybrid of explainable AI and hydrological modeling: Implications for sustainable watershed management
abstract: Accurate projection and attribution of streamflow extremes under compound climate and climate and land-use scenarios are critical for sustainable watershed management, yet conventional assessments predominantly evaluate isolated factors and overlook dynamic anthropogenic regulations. This study develops an integrated scenario-based hybrid attribution analysis of streamflow extremes (abbreviated as SHASE) framework for (i) tackling non-linear boundary inflows and reservoir dispatches via a mass-conserving explainable AI (GBR-SHAP) topology; (ii) capturing the regulatory streamflow reshaping by extracting extreme quantiles (Q10, Q50, Q90) from empirical Flow Duration Curves (FDCs); (iii) quantifying the individual and interactive effects of climate and land-use on different subbasins using analysis of variance (ANOVA). The SHASE framework is applied to the “Ji"-shaped region of the Yellow River Basin. Key findings indicate: (1) GBR-SHAP feature sensitivities reveal empirical response patterns that align with known catchment moisture memory (dominated by 12-month rolling precipitation); (2) FDC analyses reveal an asymmetric flow-reshaping effect along the regulated channel, where reservoir operations truncate wet-season high flows (Q10) while supplementing dry-season low flows (Q90); (3) while climate change acts as the dominant macro-scale driver across more than 75% of the watershed (contributing over 76% of streamflow variance on average), urban surface hardening triggered high flow in 12.5% of the subbasins, while the interaction between climate and land use dominated the low-flow deficits in 20.0% of the subbasins during dry-season. The findings suggest that achieving sustainable watershed management requires a shift from isolated climate assessment to integrated climate-land-water coordination that addresses the local extreme-flow drivers in strictly regulated watersheds.

title: Selecting climate mitigation indicators for tracking municipal climate targets and goals
abstract: Over half of the global population lives in urban areas, a number expected to reach nearly 70% by 2050. Urbanized areas are responsible for 70% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and 75% of energy consumption. In response, local governments are setting GHG emissions reduction targets and developing climate action plans. The extent of implementation and effectiveness of these plans remains uncertain, as standardized measurement frameworks are scarce. This study catalogued indicator sets to explore climate mitigation indicators for measuring local performance. A document analysis was conducted to identify climate-related indicators currently used by 21 Canadian municipalities already engaged in formal climate action and reporting. The study categorized the indicators using the logic model framework and predefined local GHG emissions activity sectors. An indicator evaluation matrix was used as part of an expert scoring procedure to propose a parsimonious list of climate mitigation indicators derived from existing practice. Results from this study show an uneven distribution across the logic model, with only one impact indicator identified that is currently in use by two municipalities. Input and activity indicators were also scarce, and none of these types were included in the final list. Categorizing the indicators by activity sector revealed nature-based solutions as an emerging area of climate mitigation in municipalities. The examination of climate-related indicators yielded 19 indicators across various GHG emissions activity sectors, including buildings, energy, transportation, and waste. These indicators complement GHG emissions inventories and aim to contribute to practices that track progress towards climate targets and goals.

title: Towards plastics circularity in Mexico: A systematic assessment of barriers, policy gaps, and operational strategies
abstract: Plastics circularity has emerged as a major challenge for middle-income economies, where growing consumption, fragmented infrastructure, and uneven governance often reproduce linear material flows. Mexico provides a particularly relevant case because it combines growing circular-economy ambitions with persistently low national circularity. This study presents a PRISMA-informed systematic literature review and system-level assessment of plastics circularity in Mexico, integrating academic literature, policy documents, and industry reports to examine structural barriers, policy gaps, transferability of international practices, and operational bottlenecks across the plastics value chain. Findings indicate that plastics circularity is constrained not by the absence of policy instruments but by multidimensional fragmentation across governance, infrastructure, markets, and information systems. Circularity outcomes are highly uneven, with PET, HDPE, and selected polymers benefiting from established recovery pathways while many other plastic streams remain predominantly linear, a condition described here as two-speed circularity. Additional constraints include weak domestic markets for recycled materials, territorial disparities in infrastructure, inconsistent reporting systems, and limited integration of informal recovery activities. The study identifies priority pathways involving regulatory harmonization, strengthened producer responsibility, infrastructure expansion, waste-picker integration, and improved monitoring systems. Mexico's experience offers insights for other middle-income economies seeking to accelerate plastics circularity under fragmented institutional conditions.

title: A probabilistic Gaussian mixture model framework for groundwater contamination risk classification in central China's industrial parks
abstract: In heavily industrialized regions, groundwater contamination often presents complex and heterogeneous risk characteristics that cannot be fully captured by conventional threshold-based assessments. To address this issue, a multidimensional probabilistic framework based on a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) was developed by integrating contamination intensity (NIPI), human health risk (HI and TCR), and receptor sensitivity (TSS). The framework was applied to 15 industrial parks in central China based on 27 hydrochemical parameters. Results indicate widespread contamination across the investigated industrial parks, with NIPI values ranging from 1.71 to 24.05 and 11 of the 15 parks exceeding 3.0. Health-risk and receptor sensitivity indicators further showed heterogeneous risk characteristics among parks. The GMM-based classification identified three structurally distinct risk regimes: an extreme high-risk group (P15), a mechanism-differentiated high-risk group (P7 and P11), and a weakly coupled group characterized by limited multivariate risk amplification. Posterior probabilities further identified transitional risk states between regimes. Overall, the proposed framework demonstrates that groundwater risk is better represented as a multidimensional risk configuration rather than a single deterministic value, providing a probabilistic basis for mechanism-oriented classification and differentiated management.

title: Calcined layered double hydroxides assisted carbonation curing of cement mortar: mineral carbonation enhancement and potential carbonate capture behavior
abstract: Calcined layered double hydroxides (CLDHs) possess excellent CO32− adsorption capacities. Incorporating CLDHs into cement-based materials in combination with carbonation curing is expected to further enhance CO2 mineral sequestration efficiency and improve material performance. In this study, the effects of different CLDHs content on cement mortar under normal curing and carbonation curing were studied by means of mechanical tests, pore structure analysis, SEM, XRD/QXRD, TG/DTG, adsorption test, and molecular simulation. Among the investigated dosages and carbonation curing conditions, 2% CLDHs produced the best overall performance, increasing compressive and flexural strengths by 12.56% and 34.03%, respectively, while refining the pore structure and promoting carbonate formation. In contrast, excessive CLDHs (4–8%) caused particle agglomeration, interfacial defects, and increased unfavorable pore regions, which disrupted the continuity and uniform distribution of hydration and carbonation products and thereby weakened the beneficial effect of carbonation curing. XRD and TG/DTG results further indicated increased carbonate-related formation/mass loss at an appropriate CLDHs dosage. In the simulated concrete pore solution (SCPs), CLDHs exhibited potential affinity for CO32− and reconstructed into carbonate-intercalated LDHs through the memory effect. DFT calculations show that CO32− can be stably accommodated in the interlayer region of LDHs through electrostatic attraction, multiple hydrogen bonds, and interlayer confinement, with higher binding stability than that of the LDHs–OH system. These findings demonstrate that CLDHs can not only improve the pore structure and mechanical properties of carbonation-cured cement mortar, but also enhance CO2 mineral sequestration, providing experimental evidence and mechanistic insights for the application of CLDHs in low-carbon cement-based materials and CO2 mineral carbonation curing systems.

title: Translating policy signals into corporate carbon information disclosure: Evidence from China's low-carbon city pilot program
abstract: Clarifying the effects and transmission mechanisms of subnational low-carbon policies on corporate carbon information disclosure (CID) is essential to advancing climate governance research. Using a staggered-adoption difference-in-differences design and 2009–2022 panel data on listed firms in eight high-energy-consumption industries, this study estimates the effect of China's Low-Carbon City Pilot (LCCP) program on CID. It assesses media risk translation and policy complementarity. The LCCP increases CID, with generally larger estimates at longer post-treatment horizons. Full-sample evidence is consistent with transition-risk translation, whereas physical-risk translation receives conditional support only in coastal cities. The complementarities of the LCCP with media dissemination, public concern, and local low-carbon policy intensity vary with regional digitalization. Between-group differences are significant for public concern, marginally significant for media dissemination, and not statistically significant for local policy intensity. Further analysis finds that policy-linked CID is associated with more green invention patent applications and higher citation-based quality of green invention patents, but not with additional operational decarbonization beyond the direct LCCP effect. These findings refine explanations of subnational climate policy transmission by situating policy-induced CID within media and multilevel governance processes while distinguishing disclosure responses from immediate operational decarbonization.

title: Narratives of sustainable transition: A semiotic and statistical text mining analysis of European permaculture as a transformative niche within the CAP regime
abstract: Agricultural sustainability transitions depend not only on technological and institutional innovation but also on communication between grassroots initiatives and policy frameworks. This study examines how European permaculture, conceptualised as a transformative radical niche, constructs its discourse and relates to the European Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). We analyse 496 English-language blog posts published between 2018 and mid-2025 by European permaculture organisations and practitioners using text mining, sentiment analysis, and semiotic interpretation. Permaculture discourse is coherent and affectively rich, centring on regeneration, community, biodiversity, and ecological care, with trust, joy, and anticipation emerging as the predominant emotions. Although it partially converges with CAP discourse around ecological practices and sustainability goals, deeper misalignments emerge in narrative logics, value systems, and interpretations of agricultural transformation. These findings indicate that communicative and narrative disconnects may constrain niche empowerment alongside institutional and structural barriers. Building on these findings, the study proposes an exploratory bridge vocabulary intended to facilitate communication between grassroots initiatives and policy actors, although its practical effectiveness remains to be empirically tested. By integrating computational text analysis and semiotic interpretation, the study advances methodological approaches to analysing discursive alignment in niche–regime interactions.

title: Design and multi-dimensional evaluation of bio-fermentation equipment for the circular economy in agriculture
abstract: The transition toward a circular economy in agro-industrial systems requires energy-efficient and sustainable technologies for organic waste processing. This study evaluates high-density polyethylene (HDPE) as an alternative to structural steel (St3/S235JR) for drum-type biofermenter construction. Three drum scales (L = 3, 6, and 12 m) were analyzed using multiphysics modeling (Ansys Workbench, 2023 R2), dynamic heat–mass transfer simulation (MATLAB), full-scale prototype testing, and techno-economic assessment based on life cycle costing and discounted cash flow analysis. Results demonstrate that HDPE construction reduces structural mass by 59–70% (from 8945 kg to 3670 kg for the large drum, steady-state heat losses by up to 6.6 times, and drive power requirements by 47–51% (from 30.4 kW to 16 kW for the large drum), while maximum deformations (0.42 mm) remain within GOST/ISO permissible limits. A cradle-to-gate LCA indicated a significant reduction in GWP by up to 66.6% for smaller drums. Economic viability was achieved exclusively for large-scale installations (12 m drum): the HDPE configuration showed 7.3% lower capital expenditures, 11.3% reduced operating costs, a discounted payback period of 1.5 years, net present value of USD 57.5 k, and internal rate of return of 79%. Small and medium configurations exhibited negative NPV under current market conditions, highlighting critical economies of scale. The HDPE biofermenter reached a stable thermophilic regime (63.4 °C) within 48 h with a temperature uniformity coefficient of variation below 7%, outperforming traditional windrow composting. These findings confirm that polymer-based biofermenters are technically feasible and economically attractive for industrial-scale organic waste valorization. The integrated Ansys–MATLAB modeling framework provides a scalable digital twin tool for equipment optimization in circular bioeconomy applications.

title: Bridging consumer acceptance evidence and stakeholder priorities in upcycled food markets: A literature-informed Delphi study
abstract: Upcycled food can reduce food waste and improve resource efficiency by converting food side streams into marketable products, yet its adoption remains constrained by limited consumer acceptance. Here, we ask whether stakeholder priorities align with the behavioral determinants that consumer research has identified. A PRISMA-guided review extracted hypotheses concerning attitudes, purchase intention, willingness to buy, and willingness to pay. The importance and practical usefulness of these hypotheses was then evaluated in a two-round modified Delphi study with nine experts; eight participated in Round 2. Consumers were not directly surveyed. Comparing the two streams of evidence, we find an alignment gap in implementation: stakeholders prioritized environmental concern, education, and sustainability-oriented communication, while consumer studies more consistently emphasized proximal personal value and risk-reducing signals, including food safety, health and nutritional benefits, product quality, credible labeling, certification, and price. Environmental concern may create receptiveness, but it does not appear to translate into purchase when personal value, trust, and uncertainty remain unresolved. These findings support testable, expert-informed propositions for explanatory labeling, third-party certification, benefit-oriented communication, segmented pricing, and targeted education. Better alignment between stakeholder interventions and consumer acceptance mechanisms can strengthen the commercial viability of food side-stream valorization, support circular food market formation, and contribute to waste reduction, resource efficiency, and cleaner production.

title: The green push: How does China's carbon-emissions trading drive corporate green transformation?
abstract: China's carbon-emissions trading (CET) scheme is a key market-based instrument for achieving carbon neutrality, yet its impact on corporate green transition remains hard to assess. This study develops a multidimensional Corporate Green Transformation Index (CGTI) using Word2Vec and textual analysis of annual reports from firms listed on China's A-share market. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design over 2008-2024, we find that CET coverage raises the CGTI by about 0.017, or 7% of its sample mean, consistent with the Porter Hypothesis. We further find mediating effects through upgraded human capital and increased research-and-development investment, which account for about 6.5% and 2.7% of the total effect, respectively. The estimated effect is 0.0231 for non-state-owned firms against 0.0124 for state-owned firms, and 0.0285 and 0.0304 for firms in central and western China against 0.0151 for those in the east. The response is also stronger among medium-sized firms, firms with poorer disclosure quality, and firms facing intense competition, whereas polluting industries show no significant pooled response. These results indicate that even a modest carbon price can steer firms toward broader green transformation, and that complementing the national carbon market with support for skills and innovation would strengthen its effect.

title: Administrative challenges and efficiency in integrating education for sustainable development in Jordanian universities: A mixed-methods analysis
abstract: Universities are increasingly expected to translate Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) commitments into institutional practice, yet the administrative conditions shaping this process remain underexamined in Middle Eastern higher education. This study examines administrative challenges and efficiency in integrating ESD within Jordanian universities. Using an exploratory sequential mixed methods design, the study conducted 22 semi-structured interviews with deans, heads of departments, lecturers, and students, followed by a survey of 113 academic staff. The qualitative phase identified four major challenges: curriculum integration, educational practices, resources and support, and stakeholder engagement. The quantitative phase showed that existing administrative practices address ESD challenges only moderately overall (M = 3.47). Operational Procedures recorded the highest level of practice (M = 3.68), indicating relative progress in visible sustainability-related operations, while Faculty Members recorded the lowest level (M = 3.24), highlighting weaknesses in staff development and pedagogical readiness. The findings show uneven ESD integration, with operational progress ahead of curriculum reform, research support, faculty capacity, stakeholder participation, and governance coordination. The study argues that administrative efficiency is the institutional capacity to connect sustainability-related decisions, resources, people, and learning processes across the university.

title: Engine exhaust waste heat recovery and utilization: synergistic optimization of Cu-based ternary catalysts for hydrogen-rich fuel production from green methanol cracking
abstract: Valorizing engine-exhaust waste heat through conversion into reusable chemical energy can improve energy utilization and reduce thermal-energy losses. Green-methanol cracking offers a potential route for such waste-heat recovery while producing hydrogen-rich fuel. This study develops a data-driven framework for selecting Cu-based ternary catalysts for hydrogen-rich fuel production by green-methanol cracking using engine-exhaust waste heat. Sixteen Cu–Zn–X and Cu–Ni–X catalysts were evaluated at 220–340 °C and three methanol feed rates, and their composition–operation–performance relationships were examined through multi-criteria decision analysis, interpretable machine learning, and robustness testing. Catalyst preference depended strongly on the evaluation objective. In the application-oriented TOPSIS analysis, Cu3Ni1Mn1/Al2O3 delivered the strongest cross-condition performance, ranking first under 13 of 21 operating conditions. By contrast, Cu3Zn1Co1/Al2O3 provided the best balance in the Pareto-based evaluation and machine-learning-assisted recommendation. At 0.7 mL min−1 and 340 °C, Cu3Zn1Co1/Al2O3 achieved 94.3% methanol conversion and an apparent H2-yield index of 64.0%. Interpretable models identified temperature and feed rate as the principal determinants of conversion and product distribution, while promoter composition controlled catalyst-specific responses. XRD, H2-TPR, XPS, physisorption, and microscopy analyses associated the balanced performance of Cu3Zn1Co1/Al2O3 with dispersed Cu–Co–Zn interfacial structures, favorable reducibility, and hierarchical morphology. The proposed workflow provides an experimentally grounded approach to catalyst screening and operating-condition selection for waste-heat-driven methanol cracking.

title: Navigating the green gap: Environmental justice and the challenge of inclusive sustainability education in Chinese universities
abstract: The pursuit of sustainability in higher education has gained global momentum, yet universities increasingly prioritize quantifiable outcomes over the social and equity dimensions of sustainability. Despite widespread institutional commitments to both sustainability and diversity, the intersection between these agendas remains underexplored, particularly regarding how underrepresented students experience campus sustainability education. This study addresses this gap by investigating inequities in student participation, benefit, and influence within campus sustainability initiatives in Chinese higher education. Informed by environmental justice theory, it explores how underrepresented students navigate sustainability education amid China's top-down "Ecological Civilization" and "green campus" policies. Through semi-structured interviews with 24 students, three core tensions emerge: performative inclusion versus meaningful partnership; hidden economic, temporal, and cultural costs of participation; and epistemic dissonance between technocratic sustainability narratives and students' community based environmental knowledge. The findings reveal a "green gap" that manifests as a tripartite justice crisis: procedural, distributive, and recognitional. Beyond critique, the study presents student envisioned pathways toward equitable transformation, including co-governance structures, barrier free program design, and integration of pluralistic knowledge systems into sustainability curricula. This research offers a student centered, empirically grounded roadmap for embedding equity into campus sustainability practice, challenging universities to move beyond tokenism and reposition underrepresented students as co authors of just institutional change.

title: Breaking the cycle: Corruption, innovation, and sustainability in emerging economies
abstract: Increasingly high expectations for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) sustainability have become an important issue for companies operating in an unpredictable institutional context. This problem is especially critical for post-Soviet countries that have not yet been able to strengthen their institutions due to corruption. However, the role of corruption in the innovation-sustainability relationship remains underexplored. Although, according to the "sand-the-wheel" approach, corruption negatively affects business performance through inefficiency and uncertainty, the "grease-the-wheel" approach suggests that this negative impact may be reversed if corruption helps business activities in an inefficient bureaucratic environment. Based on the Institutional Theory, the Agency Theory, the Transaction Cost Economics, and the Resource-Based View, this study explores the effect of a weak institutional environment on firm performance, the impact of corruption on the worsening of the principal-agent problem, informal payments made to decrease transaction costs, and firm innovation capacity that helps to become sustainable. For this purpose, firm-level data from the World Bank Enterprise Survey of 2023-2024 were obtained, and a stratified random sampling method was used with a particular regression estimation technique. It was found that corruption had a statistically significant negative influence on firms' sustainability efforts, supporting the "sand-the-wheel" concept. However, corruption also had a positive influence on firms' innovation capacity - thus, a "grease-the-wheel" effect can be assumed in the post-Soviet context, characterized by an inefficient bureaucratic system and a weak institutional environment. Innovation, in turn, positively influences firms' sustainability efforts.

title: Repair or recycle? Changing financial performance of circular economy strategies among South Korean social enterprises, 2012–2025
abstract: Circular economy frameworks rank strategies by how much product value they retain, yet whether that ranking holds financially for the social enterprises expected to carry the transition is unknown. This article examines the financial performance of circular strategies disclosed by South Korean social enterprises from 2012 to 2025. Classifying every disclosure on its own year's text yields 880 strategy records from 377 enterprises across repair and reuse, sharing and product-service systems, recycling, and collection. About one reporting enterprise in ten discloses substantive circular activity, mostly repair and reuse, organised as building repair in construction, recycling in the waste sector and equipment access in services. The difference in operating margins between repair and recycling enterprises is largest in the disclosures covering fiscal years 2022–2024 and negligible in the preceding period, and it emerged as recyclers recovered from deep losses and repair margins stayed weak. Holding sales, age, industry and year constant, repair's operating margin is 10.6 percentage points below recycling's over the whole period, and sharing and collection do not separate from recycling. The results hold under alternative classifications, although the evidence that the gap changed between periods is then weaker. Subsidised employment, wages and social reinvestment do not explain the gap, the net-margin gap is smaller, and growth does not differ between the families. The circularity hierarchy is therefore neither a financial ranking nor a stable one. Evaluation and support should follow strategy families across periods, and explaining the different recoveries requires evidence on prices, costs and contracts.

title: Decoding carbon footprint patterns in biopharmaceutical supply chains: Standardized inventory and quantitative structural attribution analysis
abstract: Biopharmaceutical supply chains are important targets for healthcare decarbonization, but aggregate carbon footprints do not show whether mitigation should focus on one stage or a coordinated portfolio. This study develops a standardized cradle-to-gate inventory and a structure–pattern–label framework for Acarbose Chewable Tablets, Bailing Capsules, and Polymyxin B. Using one kilogram of finished product as the functional unit, the analysis combines lifecycle accounting, concentration and dispersion indicators, uncertainty analysis, exploratory machine learning, and emission-reduction scenarios. The reported total footprints are 3.01, 2.85, and 2.17 kg of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilogram, respectively. Dominant stages account for 46.3–54.2% of each footprint. Entropy values of 1.524, 1.763, and 1.786 bits distinguish the more concentrated acarbose profile from the two more dispersed profiles. The exploratory model reports a coefficient of determination of 0.91, and automatic labels agree with expert consensus for 17 of 20 products. Combined scenarios report reductions of 24–32%; stage-based accounting distinguishes overlapping savings from operational complementarity. These results support product-specific mitigation screening, while the small, partly parameterized dataset and incomplete product-family validation limit generalization. The framework links emission structures to manufacturing and supply-chain priorities; clinical comparisons require equivalent treatment-based functional units and downstream lifecycle information.

title: Novel proteins for sustainable food systems: Techno-economic feasibility and consumer acceptance in selected EU respondents
abstract: This study integrates techno-economic and consumer-oriented perspectives to assess the feasibility of algae- and insect-based proteins as sustainable food options. Using exploratory evidence from respondents in Belgium, Germany, and Poland, it combines secondary Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) benchmarks from modular production studies with three demand-side modules: the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) (n = 55), the Food Neophobia Scale and Food Technology Neophobia Scale (FNS/FTNS) (n = 529), and the Price Sensitivity Meter (PSM) (n = 30). AHP results show that Healthiness is the most important criterion (55.6%), followed by Sensory Attractiveness (27.4%) and Availability (17.0%); within Healthiness, Safety is the dominant sub-criterion. TEA/LCA indicators suggest favorable environmental performance for both systems, with emissions of 2.77 and 3.48 kg CO2-eq/kg for insect- and algae-based production, respectively, although algae production is more capital-intensive. FNS/FTNS results indicate mainly neutral attitudes, with non-negligible shares of neophobic respondents (13.4% in FNS; 15.1% in FTNS). PSM estimates acceptable price ranges of EUR 3.66–5.85/kg for insect-based foods and EUR 4.79–6.91/kg for algae-based foods. The findings suggest that adoption of novel proteins depends not only on environmental and economic performance, but also on perceived safety, sensory expectations, neophobia, and price acceptability. The study offers an exploratory framework for linking supply-side feasibility with demand-side readiness in sustainable protein transitions.

title: Beyond barriers: A multi-level capability perspective on circular economy adoption by social entrepreneurs in small island contexts
abstract: This study moves beyond the conventional focus on barriers and enablers to examine how multilevel capabilities shape circular economy (CE) adoption among social entrepreneurs in resource-constrained small-island contexts. This study handles the limited comprehension of how individuals, organizations, and institutions develop and mobilize capabilities to facilitate circular business transformation. Adopting a qualitative, inductive approach, this study draws on in-depth interviews with 16 social entrepreneurs in Bali and Labuan Bajo, Indonesia, and employs thematic analysis to develop a multi-level capability framework. The findings reveal that CE adoption is driven not by isolated factors but by the configuration of interdependent capabilities, where organizational elements such as strategic commitment, innovation, and resource reconfiguration are reinforced by societal engagement, institutional support, and entrepreneurs’ environmental orientation. These interactions form a community-embedded and context-sensitive capability system that enables circular business models and sustainable performance. The study further demonstrates that fostering CE adoption requires integrated capability-building ecosystems, including policy incentives, community collaboration, and targeted capacity development. By shifting the focus from static drivers to dynamic processes, this study advances a multi-level capability perspective and extends dynamic capabilities and stakeholder theory in small island economies.

title: Assessing the circular transition progress across Pakistan's textile supply chain: Empirical evidence from the field
abstract: Textile manufacturing constitutes one of the most resource-intensive industries, which faces growing pressure to shift from traditional, linear production to a circular economy (CE). Although extensive literature exists on circular business models (CBM), most studies focus on Global North country contexts, leaving a limited understanding of how firms in emerging economies implement circular practices across supply chains. The study addresses this gap and applies a novel circularity evaluation framework that integrates the Resource-Based View and the Socio-technical Transition Theory. The framework examines patterns in circular practice adoption and differences in circularity performance. Using a qualitative multiple-case study of 26 large textile firms, the research collected primary data through key informant interviews and field observations. The analysis combines thematic analysis, pattern matching, and multi-value Qualitative Comparative Analysis (mvQCA) and descriptive statistics to map R-strategies across supply chain stages and cluster firms by circular performance. Findings reveal a strong emphasis on internal operations and end-of-life solutions, characterized by lower-value strategies, e.g., recycling and recovery. Consequently, the industry exhibits uncoordinated patterns of circular practices that only partially close material loops, driven primarily by customer demand, transnational governance, and competitive pressures. Export-oriented firms show stronger performance, revealing industry polarisation. Overall, systemic CE implementation remains absent across the fragmented supply chain, constrained by limited strategic knowledge, and the lack of a national regulatory roadmap. The study's findings further hint to a need for stronger policy and management engagement towards green procurement, industrial symbiosis, reverse logistics, closer cooperation with international buyers, and inclusive national policies.

title: From past trends to future costs: The influence of economic parameter selection on building life cycle costs in Belgium
abstract: While upfront investment costs remain a key decision parameter in building design due to budget constraints, life cycle costs have become increasingly important for evaluating financial feasibility due to rising energy, material, and maintenance costs. Estimating life cycle costs requires assumptions on price evolution and discount rates, which are particularly uncertain given the long service life of a building. Accurately estimating life cycle costs therefore requires reliable economic parameters. This study analyses the historical evolution of key economic parameters in the Belgian context. A long-term dataset is constructed and analysed across multiple observation periods. Derived rates are used to assess how variations in parameter values influence the life cycle cost of a case study building. The results show that parameter values vary significantly depending on the selected observation period. Energy and material cost growth rates exhibit the highest variability, while labour costs show a more stable trend. The discount rate is identified as one of the most influential parameters, with low values leading to higher life cycle costs. The findings highlight the importance of transparent and context-specific parameter selection.
