Based on the analysis, a 50-year observation period is proposed as a reference to estimate LCC parameter values, supplemented by a sensitivity analysis using shorter periods to assess the influence of alternative economic conditions. For Belgium, this corresponds to a recommended real annual discount rate of 4,20% and real material, labour, and energy growth rates of 0,74%, 0,50% and 2,00% respectively.

title: Electro-regulated microbial interface drive sulfur cycling for enhancing anaerobic reduction of nitro-compounds: insights into electron distribution and metabolic response
abstract: In sulfate-containing anaerobic systems, electron competition between nitroaromatic compound reduction and sulfate reduction severely limits pollutant removal efficiency. In this study, an electro-assisted anaerobic system was constructed to elucidate electro-regulated electron distribution driving sulfur cycling for enhanced nitrobenzene reduction (NB). The results demonstrated that NB removal efficiency highly increased to approximately 99%, along with enhanced sulfate reduction at cathode potentials ≤ −700 mV. At the cathode, conductive pili and electroactive proteins facilitated electron uptake, while propionate metabolism supported NADH-related reducing processes, thereby promoting NB and sulfate reduction. At the anode, sulfide was oxidized (S2−→S0→SO42−), providing electrons that facilitated NB reduction. Elemental sulfur (S0), as a key intermediate in the oxidation pathway, functions as an electron relay to establish a dynamic electron transfer bridge between anodic and cathodic bio-interfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed favorable interfacial configurations between sulfur and heme proteins, suggesting its potential involvement in extracellular electron transfer. Electro-regulation was associated with sulfur redox transformation and changes in electron utilization, while the responses of sulfur-transforming microorganisms and NB degraders suggested a potential shift from electron competition toward more cooperative electron utilization under electro-regulated conditions. This study proposes the mechanism underlying electro-regulated enhancement of anaerobic nitroaromatic compound transformation from the perspective of electron distribution coupled with sulfur cycling, providing a novel strategy for the efficient treatment of wastewater co-contaminated with sulfate and nitro-compounds.

title: A dual-calcium regulation strategy for variable-temperature adaptive red mud-based binders: Hydration optimization, resource efficiency and sustainability assessment
abstract: With the increasing demand for industrial solid waste valorization, the development of cementitious materials that adaptability to harsh service conditions has become an important direction for sustainable construction materials, CaO-CaO2 composite synergistic regulation system was developed in this study. LT-DSC, FTIR, TG-DTG, and MIP were employed to characterize the hydration and microstructural evolution. In addition, multi-objective optimization was conducted using the NSGA-II coupled with the TOPSIS. The effects of CaO-CaO2 dosages on mechanical properties, variable-temperature thermal behavior, hydration product formation, and pore structure evolution were systematically investigated, and conduct economic feasibility and resource efficiency evaluation. The results demonstrated that the dual-calcium system enhanced the adaptability of the material to variable-temperature curing. When CaO–CaO2 completely replaced the alkaline activator, the strength retention ratio reached 72.07%. The incorporation of CaO2 reduced the freezing temperature of the paste and decreased the amount of freezable water, resulting in reductions of 8.67% and 31.78% in the freezing temperature and melting enthalpy at the final setting stage, respectively. CaO(4%)-CaO2(2.5%), CaO(7%)-CaO2(2.5%), CaO(8.2%)-CaO2(3.5%) were identified as optimal formulations for cost efficiency, variable-temperature mechanical performance, and multi-objective balance, respectively. This study elucidates the synergistic regulation mechanism of the CaO–CaO2 composite system on the variable-temperature hydration behavior of strong-alkali-free red mud-based cementitious materials and provides a theoretical basis for the resource utilization of industrial solid wastes in cold regions.

title: Enhancing robustness and reliability of underwater RGB-based water quality retrieval under inland cross-water and cross-seasonal conditions
abstract: To address cross-domain generalization challenges and depth-related optical variations in water quality retrieval, this study proposes FMC-ConvNeXt, a five-module framework for underwater RGB imagery. Built on ConvNeXt, it combines spectral-attenuation attention with data-driven components to improve adaptability under cross-water and cross-seasonal shifts. Datasets covering different inland water types and seasons were constructed in Handan, China, and evaluated using complementary image-level and sampling-point-isolated protocols. Evaluation covered overall performance, module contributions and configuration dependence, cross-domain adaptation, unseen-sampling-point generalization, uncertainty reliability, and robustness to simulated optical perturbations and reservoir depth variations. Under image-level supervision, FMC-ConvNeXt achieved R2 values of 0.9334 and 0.9561 for turbidity and suspended solids, respectively, in the Summer Target Domain. Fine-tuning with 20% target samples reduced RMSE to 2.082 and 0.858 NTU. Under moderate to severe spectral distortion, RMSE and MAE in the Winter Target Domain remained at 0.3757 and 0.2424 NTU. Uncertainty calibration reduced regression ECE in the Summer Target Domain from 0.1561 to 0.0728, with uncertainty significantly associated with absolute error. Reservoir evaluation yielded R2 = 0.6387, while image luminance and texture responses decreased with depth. Ablation results showed configuration dependent rather than linearly additive module contributions. Under sampling-point isolation, turbidity R2 values were 0.8208, 0.5047, and 0.3550 in the Source Domain, Summer Target Domain, and Winter Target Domain, respectively. Overall, FMC-ConvNeXt improved Turb and SS retrieval and retained predictive capability under controlled perturbations and field conditions, supporting ROV assisted high frequency screening, repeated inspection, confirmatory sampling, pollution anomaly identification, and cleaner-production-related water management.

title: An efficient conditional diffusion model for meteorological data super-resolution based on stochastic differential equations over Eastern China
abstract: Global weather forecasts provide essential support for socioeconomic activities, but their applications remain constrained by coarse spatial resolution and systematic, regime-dependent biases, particularly over meteorologically heterogeneous regions. This study develops a conditional diffusion model based on stochastic differential equations, which integrates intensity-boundary structural learning with adaptive refinement via dynamic convolution and channel attention to produce high-resolution meteorological fields across multiple forecast products. Evaluations over Eastern China against ERA5-Land show that the super-resolution forecasts achieve strong agreement with the reference, with temperature and wind fields at a 12 h lead time reaching R2 values of up to about 0.90 and 0.87, respectively, and precipitation event skill reaching stable equitable error in probability space (SEEPS) values as low as approximately 0.05, consistently outperforming interpolation-based and deterministic learning methods. Compared with representative baseline models, the proposed framework demonstrates more robust performance across variables and forecast settings, with improved preservation of coherent spatial distributions, localized gradients, and extreme-value features. Using the super-resolution weather forecasts, we further demonstrate an application to gridded daily maximum 8 h ozone prediction. Compared with ozone predictions driven by the low-resolution meteorological fields, the use of super-resolved meteorological fields yields systematic improvements in predictive performance, with R2 increased by 4.6–5.8%. For the evaluated forecast products and meteorological variables over Eastern China, these results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for regional-scale forecast refinement and downstream air-quality prediction.

title: Sustainable development performance shortfalls and corporate ESG greenwashing
abstract: Amidst the rising strategic importance of ESG disclosure and concerns about greenwashing, a key unresolved question is under what performance conditions firms become more prone to such behavior. This study investigates the relationship between corporate sustainable development performance shortfalls and ESG greenwashing by developing and testing a contingency framework. Methodologically, we develop ESG-BERTopic, a deep learning framework for constructing a text-based measure of corporate ESG greenwashing based on the relative emphasis on future-oriented commitments in corporate reports. Analyzing a panel of Chinese A-share listed firms (2008–2024), we find that sustainable development performance shortfalls are associated with higher levels of corporate ESG greenwashing. This association is stronger in firms with more slack resources and weaker in firms with higher institutional ownership. Further analysis based on rating-based ESG greenwashing also shows a positive association with performance shortfalls. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that this association is statistically significant only among non-high-tech firms in heavily polluting industries. By linking shortfalls against an integrated sustainability aspiration to corporate ESG greenwashing, the study extends research on performance feedback and clarifies the moderating roles of slack resources and institutional ownership. The findings inform the review of ESG commitments by linking disclosure assessment to firms’ performance context, the implementation basis of proposed initiatives, and evidence of subsequent progress.

title: Optimizing rural sewage management systems: A spatial configuration typology approach with multivariate factor analysis
abstract: A scientific and applicable evaluation system for rural domestic sewage is a key prerequisite for efficient treatment. However, the selection of rural sewage treatment process still mainly refers to the urban sewage treatment process and relies on human judgment, lacking the multi-dimensional objective decision-making basis matching the spatial characteristics of the village. This study provides a rural domestic sewage treatment model and process decision-making system integrating village objective spatial pattern analysis and expert experience evaluation. Through the verification and analysis of 233 natural villages in Dengkou County, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, it is found that the residential density of villages in this county is mainly decentralized (43.25%), and the terrain type is mainly flat dam (85.85%). The treatment model is dominated by centralized (61.05%) and resource utilization (23.23%), which is consistent with the regional characteristics of the Yellow River Basin and the high degree of agricultural intensification. Combined with the decision tree and AHP-TOPSIS model, this study proposes the optimal sewage treatment process for different emission standards, and its comprehensiveness and applicability are better than the existing local processes. Partial least squares regression analysis was used to evaluate the influencing factors of treatment mode selection, and the results showed that population size (0.92) and gross domestic product (0.76) had a significant positive impact on the choice of treatment mode. By coupling objective spatial pattern analysis with expert experience evaluation, this study provides a replicable decision-making framework for rural sewage treatment technology screening while offering methodological support for relevant policy formulation.

title: Ranking green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) framework: Empirical evidence from Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry
abstract: The petrochemical industry faces increasing pressure to decarbonize due to its high energy intensity, carbon emissions, and environmental footprint. This study evaluates and ranks green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework to identify the highest-ranked mechanisms for supporting the sustainable transition of Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry. A two-stage multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework integrating the Analytic Network Process (ANP) and fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was employed to assess six alternatives comprising four green finance instruments and two finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms against three ESG dimensions and fifteen industry-specific sub-criteria. The results show that the Environmental dimension carries the highest priority, followed by Governance and Social, highlighting the importance of measurable environmental outcomes supported by robust governance structures. Among the evaluated alternatives, green tax policies ranked first, followed by green credit mechanisms and investor risk mitigation instruments. The findings suggest that progressive environmental taxation, preferential green lending, and blended-finance mechanisms are better positioned to support industrial decarbonization while limiting abrupt cost pressures during the transition. Furthermore, the effectiveness of green bonds and emission trading systems depends on transparent governance, regulatory compliance, and credible sustainability reporting frameworks. This study provides policy insights for aligning industrial finance with Saudi Vision 2030, the Saudi Green Initiative, and the Kingdom's 2060 net-zero target, while offering a practical decision-support framework for prioritizing sustainable finance in energy-intensive industries.

title: Local fiscal science and technology expenditure, air quality, and house prices: Evidence from Chinese metropolitan areas
abstract: Local fiscal science and technology (S&T) expenditure is an underexamined form of urban fiscal effort. Whether it is associated with cleaner air and whether environmental improvement is reflected in housing values remain unclear, particularly across metropolitan hierarchies. We analyse panel data for 151 prefecture-level cities across 27 nationally designated Chinese metropolitan areas over 2008–2020. Treating local government expenditure on science and technology as a fiscal input, we estimate two-way fixed-effects models that control for industrial composition and socioeconomic covariates. We also conduct exploratory subgroup analyses of core and non-core cities and use 1000 bootstrap replications to assess the indirect association operating through PM2.5. Fiscal S&T expenditure is negatively associated with PM2.5 in the full sample and both city groups. Its total association with housing prices is positive in the full sample and non-core cities but not significant in core cities. Bootstrap confidence intervals for the indirect association include zero in the full sample (estimate: 0.0024) and core cities. The indirect association was positive and supported by bootstrap results in the non-core-city sample (0.0034; 95% confidence interval: 0.0002–0.0071), equivalent to a 10% increase in S&T expenditure being associated with approximately 0.03% higher housing prices via PM2.5. This study provides city-level evidence on the associations among government expenditure on science and technology, air quality, and housing prices.

title: How farm size reshapes straw management structure? Evidence from household surveys in five Chinese provinces
abstract: Expanding farm size is often regarded as a key driver of the green and low-carbon transition in agriculture. However, unlike green technologies such as substituting chemical fertilizers and pesticides, crop straw management is a matter of allocating post-harvest byproducts across multiple pathways, and the direction in which farm-size expansion affects this process remains unclear. Based on 3675 household-crop-year observations from Jiangsu, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jilin, and Hebei provinces in China in 2018 and 2022, this study classifies straw management into four pathways: disposal, returning-to-field, household self-use, and selling. Using a Seemingly Unrelated Regression model, this study estimates the effects of crop-level farm size on crop straw management. The results indicate that farm size is not associated with the disposal share although the burning component alone rises with farm size; it is associated with higher returning-to-field and selling shares and a lower household self-use share. A decomposition into absolute quantities shows that all four pathways expand with farm size. The compositional movement therefore reflects differences in how fast each pathway grows and in how likely larger farms are to use it, rather than a physical transfer of straw between them. The returning-to-field response is concentrated in Sichuan and among rapeseed and soybean growers. The scale association also varies across terrain, household income, and educational attainment. The study suggests that farm size is an important prerequisite, but not a sufficient condition, for resource-oriented straw utilization. Only when mechanized services and collection, storage, and transportation systems are in place can scale advantages be translated into cleaner utilization pathways.

title: Hydrothermal water–CO2 co-processing of immature kerogen: operating-window optimization, light-hydrocarbon selectivity and molecular pathways
abstract: Hot pressurized water can convert immature oil shale into light liquid hydrocarbons, but under severe conditions, the liquids are cracked into gas or condensed into heavy residue. This study shows that adding CO2 to the hydrothermal conversion of immature kerogen, the insoluble organic matter of oil shale, shifts the products from permanent gases toward liquid oil, and it identifies the operating conditions under which this occurs. Hydrothermal experiments on Type I kerogen-bearing shale from the Chang 7 Member, Ordos Basin, were combined with a statistically designed response surface and with reactive molecular dynamics simulations of a kerogen model built from spectroscopic data. A light-component enrichment index, which combines the number of detected liquid compounds with their light fraction, reached a broad plateau near 400–410 °C and was largely insensitive to the initial CO2 pressure, whereas CO2 strongly suppressed the formation of hydrogen, carbon monoxide and methane. At the validated condition, adding CO2 raised the oil yield by about 40% relative to water alone. The simulations show water acting as a recyclable hydrogen-transfer medium that stabilizes cracked fragments, nitrogen released mainly via ring cleavage to form hydrogen cyanide, and sulfur retained in organic structures. These results define a practical window for steering immature kerogen toward light liquid products while limiting over-gasification.

title: Active suppression of wind-induced coal particle migration via flow optimization and fluid-structure interaction using gondola fairings
abstract: Coal particle migration induced by aerodynamic effects causes safety and environmental hazard during railway transportation. Apart from the existing particle isolation strategies from airflow, the optimization of flow driving forces could theoretically suppress particle migration. Guided by fluid-structure interaction, this study proposes semi-enclosed aerodynamic fairings above gondola carriages to intercept and redirect incoming airflow, thereby achieving flow optimization along coal accumulation surfaces. Discrete Phase Model with Computational Fluid Dynamics coupling simulations (DPM-CFD coupling) and streamline analyses in ANSYS-Fluent were adopted to compare the suppression effects of various fairing configurations, and the aerodynamic load effect and operation energy consumption were evaluated with the optimal fairing design during open-line and tunnel operations. Relevant results show that, despite the non-uniform and unsteady distribution along the coal accumulation surfaces, the fairings substantially weakened the horizontal airflow speed. The upward-closed fairing reduced the sweeping effect during the particle start-up process and established a more favorable flow direction and spatial relationship between vortices and structures. Under standard double-track tunnel operation conditions with train speed of 80 km/h, the fairing application achieved net mass reduction of 64.81% for one carriage during tunnel entry, and 42.81% migrated mass reduction under reality condition could be realized. The fairings increased the overall frontal area and, by enclosing and shielding the coal accumulation surface, reduced the sweep velocity over it. The flow optimization was realized by the enhanced fluid-structure interaction, which will also induce extra aerodynamic load on structures and drag energy consumption.

title: Nanoscale surface on internal runner of thin-walled micro-grooved channel produced by a novel combined jet polishing process using three developed devices
abstract: Adhered powder and spherical particles usually appear on the internal runners of parts produced by additive manufacturing. These defects must be removed to prevent them from detaching and entering moving components. Nevertheless, conventional polishing methods cannot effectively remove these defects when the groove size is less than 0.5 mm. To overcome this challenge, a novel approach was developed to achieve a nanoscale surface on the internal runners of thin-walled micro-grooved channel using three developed devices. Micro-grooves with a minimum size of 0.22 mm are located in a channel with a thickness of 0.7 mm fabricated by a custom metallic three-dimensional printer. Air abrasive jet polishing (AAJP) was carried out using silicon carbide (SiC) abrasives by a custom-made polisher. After AAJP using a traditional circular nozzle, surface roughness Ra values were 36.99, 1.79, and 5.46 μm on the side, top, and bottom surfaces of a groove, respectively. Ra increased by 39% on the side surface after AAJP compared to the pristine surface of the laser powder bed fusion, and this phenomenon is firstly discovered. To address this, a novel multi-lobed nozzle was designed. AAJP and ultrasonic-assisted immersed jet polishing (UAIJP) were conducted using the new lobed nozzle on two self-made polishers. The novel UAIJP slurry consisted of SiC and ceria hybrid abrasives, hydrogen peroxide, and sodium bicarbonate. The Ra values were 15.83, 0.79, 3.16 μm and 0.86, 0.07, 0.26 μm on the side, top, and bottom surfaces after AAJP and UAIJP, respectively. After AAJP, Ra values were reduced by 57%, 56%, and 42% on the side, top, and bottom surfaces, respectively, compared to the circular nozzle; after UAIJP, the reductions reached 99%, 96%, and 98%, respectively. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) calculations reveal that surface defects are preferentially removed by abrasive particles. The structure of the lobed nozzle suppresses the central straight-through airflow, causing radial turbulent disturbances and reducing the radial ineffective collision rate of abrasives from 50.96% for the conventional circular nozzle to 41.84%. Meanwhile, the modulation effect of the flow field in the lobed nozzle forces more abrasives to enter the micro-grooves, increasing the radial collision frequency rate of abrasives on the side surface from 45.65% to 51.82%. The lobed nozzle broadens the collision angle of abrasives from near 0° for the circular nozzle to 60°, promoting more abrasives to impact defects at an optimal impact angle of 18.43°, calculated from the Finnie erosion model. Our findings provide new outcomes to fabricate nanoscale surface on the internal runner of thin-walled micro-grooved channel of Ti6Al4V via AAJP and UAIJP using a multi-lobed nozzle by three developed setups.

title: Oil–dependent control of methane hydrate kinetics and slurry rheology by a kinetic hydrate inhibitor in oil–water systems
abstract: Gas hydrate blockage remains a major flow-assurance challenge in gas condensate pipelines, where the coexistence of condensate oil and water creates non-emulsified or weakly dispersed oil–water environments that affect hydrate formation and slurry flow behavior. Although kinetic hydrate inhibitors (KHIs) are widely used to delay hydrate nucleation, their influence on post-nucleation hydrate aggregation and slurry rheology in non-emulsified condensate oil–water systems remains insufficiently understood. In this study, methane hydrate formation kinetics and slurry rheological behavior were investigated in systems containing the tested KHI and model condensate oil (n-hexane) at different oil volume fractions. The results show that, at 20 vol% n-hexane, the tested KHI significantly prolongs the early warning period for hydrate nucleation, whereas at 80 vol% n-hexane, it extends the low-risk growth period, with no transition to the high-risk agglomeration stage observed within the 720 min post-nucleation observation window. In this high-oil system, a relatively high water conversion rate is accompanied by low final slurry viscosity. Rheological measurements further reveal that the resulting hydrate slurry exhibits shear-thinning behavior, yield stress, thixotropy, and a transition from elasticity-dominated to viscosity-dominated behavior. The yield stress increases with shut-in duration and depends strongly on shear history, indicating potential restart risk. These results demonstrate that the dominant role of the tested KHI shifts from nucleation delay under low-oil conditions to post-nucleation aggregation control and slurry flowability maintenance under high-oil conditions. This study provides experimental evidence for evaluating KHI performance from a coupled kinetic–rheological perspective in non-emulsified condensate oil–water systems.

title: Simultaneous dark fermentation and microbial fuel cell for co-production of hydrogen and electricity from typical garden waste using two co-culture systems
abstract: Dark fermentation (DF) faces inherent drawbacks of low hydrogen yield and soluble microbial product accumulation. To address these limitations, the single-stage dark fermentation and microbial fuel cell (sDFMFC) system was constructed to evaluate its performance for lignocellulose treatment and co-production of hydrogen and electricity using four typical fallen leaves (poplar, ginkgo, oak, and pine) as substrates under continuous flow (HRT = 8 h). Two model co-culture systems (fermentative bacterium + electroactive bacterium) were employed in the experiment: Escherichia coli + Shewanella oneidensis and Enterobacter aerogenes + Shewanella oneidensis. The results showed that the E. aerogenes + S. oneidensis system exhibited superior hydrogen production (43.04 mL-H2/g-removedCOD) and total energy recovery efficiency (19.64%), but lower power density (91.13 mW/m3). In contrast, the E. coli + S. oneidensis system achieved higher power density (180.5 mW/m3) and higher COD removal (42.5%), but lower hydrogen yield. Notably, hydrogen accounted for more than 99.9% of the total energy recovery; electricity was negligible. Furthermore, substrate fermentability was the key factor governing overall performance. Poplar leaves showed the best performance for combined hydrogen and electricity production, while pine needles performed the poorest due to high lignin content and the presence of inhibitors. This study confirms the feasibility of continuous-flow sDFMFC for treating garden waste and reveals the metabolic pathway differences between two co-culture systems, providing a reference for cascaded valorization of lignocellulosic waste.

title: Carbon-associated nitrite partitioning between DNRA and denitrification in relation to N2O emissions during thermophilic composting
abstract: Despite growing recognition that thermophilic composting is a major hotspot for nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, the metabolic mechanisms governing N2O production during the thermophilic phase remain poorly understood. This knowledge gap hampers mechanistic interpretation of thermophilic N2O emission pulses and constrains the development of targeted strategies for greenhouse gas mitigation. By integrating additive-based regulation with process monitoring, metagenomic analysis, kinetic analysis and path modeling, this study revealed how intensified carbon turnover regulates the partitioning of NO2−-N between dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) and denitrification during thermophilic composting. Kinetic fitting showed a closer association of nitrite than nitrate with N2O formation. Under thermophilic conditions, intensive organic matter degradation and oxygen consumption may increase electron-donor availability, a pattern consistent with greater DNRA-related functional potential relative to N2O-producing denitrification in NO2−-N utilization. Consistent with this interpretation, the Bacillus subtilis-inoculated treatment and biochar-amended treatment showed higher DNRA-related NO2−-N reduction potential and lower N2O -producing denitrification potential, accompanied by cumulative N2O emission reductions of 84.15% and 76.35%, respectively, relative to the control. These findings suggest that carbon-driven competition between DNRA and denitrification may be an important mechanism associated with N2O mitigation during thermophilic composting.

title: Bio-fiber envelopes for digital twin-enabled thermal management: Decoupling cold-chain from high-global warming potential insulations
abstract: Global cold-chain logistics relies heavily on energy-intensive and hard-to-recycle materials that offer excellent thermal insulation, but are often made using highly polluting materials and are vulnerable to punctures. Here, we developed mycelium-bound bio-fiber envelopes (BFEs) obtained by growing Ganoderma lucidum mycelium on discarded lignocellulosic cardboard, rice husk, and oats. The hyphal fiber network bonds the waste substrates into a mechanically robust (yield strength = 0.72 MPa), thermally insulating (thermal conductivity = 0.05 W/m.K), hydrophobic (contact angle = 121.4°), fire-resistant, and fully biodegradable composite in tropical ambient outdoor climate. The BFE delivers thermal insulation comparable to foams, while achieving 6× lower carbon emissions and 4.2× lower energy demand than other cold-chain materials. To overcome the issue of performance uncertainty, a digital twin framework is integrated for real-time monitoring. Combining bio-based materials with digital tracking can reduce risks and make them reliable for demanding applications such as cold-chain logistics. Unlike prior mycelium composites, which are typically characterized in isolation from real-time performance monitoring, this work couples a living bio-based insulation material with a physics-based digital twin, turning biological variability into a bounded and monitored quantity and offering a practical route to qualify bio-based materials for regulated cold-chain logistics. This study is limited to prototype-scale envelopes and to a digital twin validated on a bounded set of payloads, geometries, and ambient profiles, and wider qualification is the subject of ongoing work.

title: The rationality gap and information bridging:Explaining farmers’ abandonment of sustainable agricultural practices
abstract: The rice-green manure rotation system (RGRS) shows great potential in producing nutrient-enhanced rice and improving paddy field ecosystem. To clarify the behavioral mechanism of farmers' sustainable adoption of RGRS, this study systematically examined the tripartite rationality framework and its role in shaping sustainable behavior using a sample of 934 farmers, while revealing the moderating effect of digital information access. The main findings include: first, only 11.2% of farmers maintained continuous adoption throughout the observation window, while 27.1% never adopted RGRS and 61.7% adopted it only on a sporadic basis; second, farmers give priority to maximizing economic benefits while pursuing the satisfaction brought by ecological rationality; Third, although the current explanatory power of health rationality for sustainable behavior is weak, its role is expected to be significantly enhanced in the long term; fourth, economic rationality and the ecological rationality are mutually exclusive, healthy rationality strengthens ecological rationality while suppressing economic rationality; fifth, digital information access can stimulate sustainable behavior by alleviating the contradictions among the triple rationality and strengthening coordination. Under the assumption that newly expanded areas share similar agroecological and institutional conditions with existing cultivation zones, the potential diffusion area could increase by approximately 49% relative to the current base. This expansion would generate substantial economic, ecological and health benefits. These insights hold particular significance for policymakers seeking to enhance the scalability of RGRS through targeted information interventions that strategically align farmers’ rational motivations with sustainable agricultural objectives.

title: Preparation of MSCF via MPAM: A thermally stable modified material for the ecological backfilling of mine waste rock
abstract: In this study, a bentonite–polymer composite modifier (MPAM) was synthesized from sodium bentonite (NaB), cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTMAB), acrylamide (AM), and polyacrylamide (PAM). PAM in the original SCF formulation was subsequently replaced with MPAM to produce the modified backfill material MSCF. The compressive strength, water retention, and thermal stability of SCF and MSCF were compared. Thermal analysis, cone calorimetry, CT, and COMSOL simulation were then used to examine how MSCF regulates pore structure and forms an interlayer composite network. The results indicate that, under identical conditions, MSCF consistently exhibits higher strength; simultaneously, MSCF demonstrates superior water retention capacity and thermal stability. As the MSCF content increases, the heat release, smoke generation and CO2 emission of the coal gangue composite system are all significantly suppressed, internal pore connectivity is reduced, and the tendency for long-term heat accumulation is weakened. The improvement in the comprehensive performance of MSCF is primarily attributed to the uniform dispersion and stable incorporation of MPAM-modified bentonite layers within the polymer network, resulting in a denser interlayer composite network structure. MSCF achieves synergistic optimisation of the mechanical performance and thermal safety of backfill materials, while showing low raw-material cost potential; however, its laboratory-scale material-plus-energy cost remains higher than that of SCF, indicating that further process optimisation and scale-up are required to realise its economic advantage. MSCF shows potential for the safe backfilling and resource utilisation of coal gangue.

title: Waste lignin-derived carbon nanotube fibers: Isotope tracing mechanisms and structural optimization
abstract: Biomass-derived carbon, particularly from waste streams such as lignin, offers a sustainable feedstock for carbon nanotube (CNT) synthesis. However, the complex pyrolysis pathways obscure its influence on CNT growth mechanisms. Here, lignin-based CNTs were investigated using isotope labeling and tailored catalysts in a floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition (FCCVD) system to elucidate high-temperature transformation processes and regional growth characteristics. Catalyst composition critically modulated CNT structure and properties: iron catalysts achieved the highest yield (116 mg h−1), while Fe-Co-Ni ternary catalysts produced highly graphitized CNTs (IG/ID = 7) with elevated electrical conductivity (8.5 × 104 S m−1). Isotopic analysis confirmed that lignin contributed 83% of the carbon, with methanol accounting for 17%. Life cycle assessment further demonstrated a lower global warming potential than ethanol-derived CNTs, underscoring the sustainability and circular-economy relevance of lignin as a carbon source. These findings provide mechanistic insight and practical guidance for the controllable synthesis of high-performance biomass-derived CNTs.

title: Experimental study on the degradation of inorganic nitrogen via biochar loaded with magnetic particles nZVI-LDH in the Erhai plateau lake, SW China
abstract: In plateau lake watersheds, the simultaneous removal of surplus NH4+ and NO3− is critical for mitigating soil nutrient surplus and aquatic eutrophication. Accordingly, this study synthesized a composite material, nZVI-LDH@Biochar (nZVI-LDH-BC), to facilitate the deep adsorption and redox degradation of NH4+ and NO3−. Specifically, removal rates reached 89.93% for NH4+ and 99.24% for NO3− under optimal conditions, with N2-N proportions of 90.18 wt% and 94.36 wt% in the degradation products, respectively. Moreover, the material achieved near-complete removal of both NH4+ and NO3− when applied to natural water from the Erhai Lake watershed. The recyclability of nZVI-LDH-BC is enhanced by its magnetic properties. It maintained 87.44% (NH4+) and 92.79% (NO3−) of its original removal capacity after 5 successive cycles. Batch degradation experiments, density functional theory calculations, intercalated ion concentration measurements, and scavenging experiments elucidated the degradation mechanisms of NH4+ and NO3−. ·OH and ·O2− consistently dominated the redox pathways for both NH4+ and NO3−, contributing 35.96%/23.69% directly to NH4+ removal and 11.02%/7.44% indirectly to NO3− removal. This study provides a fresh perspective on the development of materials for water pollution control.

title: Mixing and sequencing matter: How policy instruments shape rural human settlements improvement under the “Motivation–Capacity–Trigger” governance framework
abstract: Governments worldwide have adopted diverse policy instruments to improve rural human settlements (RHS), yet how these instruments interact, combine, and should be prioritized remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Fogg Behavior Model (FBM), this study develops an integrated framework encompassing motivation-enhancing, capacity-building, and trigger-based policy instruments. Using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces during 2005–2023, we combine NCA, fsQCA, and Geodetector approaches to examine the effectiveness of RHS policy instruments. The results show sustained improvements in both RHS performance and policy instrument intensity, accompanied by clear spatial stratified heterogeneity (SSH). Several instruments exhibit degree-based necessity under NCA, but no single policy instrument is universally indispensable across cases and performance levels. Consistently, fsQCA identifies no single condition as necessary in kind. Instead, nine antecedent conditions jointly generate seven effective pathways, which can be grouped into four configuration types, highlighting the prominent roles of economic incentives, social demonstration, technical–human support, infrastructure construction, and evaluation feedback. Policy implementation priorities vary across configurations, indicating that additional policy effort should be tailored to the existing policy mix rather than follow a uniform sequence. Spatially, eastern–central and western China exhibit distinct configurational pathways and implementation priorities, demonstrating that SSH extends from RHS outcomes to the policy mechanisms through which high performance is achieved. Overall, RHS improvement depends less on any universally indispensable instrument than on the context-specific combination, complementarity, and prioritization of policy instruments.

title: Evaluating fiber harvesting modules as subsurface stormwater retrofits: Hydrologic, life-cycle environmental, economic, and decision-analytic evidence from contrasting urban contexts
abstract: Urban stormwater retrofits face a growing mismatch between hydrological demand and available surface space. The fiber harvesting module (FHM), a buried mineral-fiber system designed to create subsurface storage–release capacity, has been deployed at scale and incorporated into technical standards in China, yet systematic evidence remains limited. This study assessed FHM as a standalone retrofit and as a hybrid component with bioretention cells (BC) or green roofs across two contrasting catchments in Tianjin, China. Six configurations were compared under 15 design storms using SWMM, life cycle assessment, life cycle costing, marginal cost analysis and stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis. FHM-based systems reduced runoff by up to 93.2% and maintained greater stability as storm severity increased. FHM also achieved the lowest life-cycle environmental burden, with aggregated impacts 89–90% lower than conventional drainage, and consistently produced the lowest external cost. BC-FHM hybrid further outperformed standalone BC in runoff control, life-cycle environmental impact and cost. Decision analysis revealed that FHM and BC-FHM competed under different stakeholder priorities in the factory catchment, whereas FHM remained robustly preferred in the park catchment. These findings suggest that subsurface modular regulation can expand the stormwater retrofit design space, shifting selection from facility-based comparison toward context-specific combinations of surface ecology, subsurface capacity, and life-cycle efficiency.

title: Supply chain digital innovation and the clean energy transition: Evidence from urban China
abstract: The clean energy transition (CET) depends on technological substitution and on the capacity to coordinate information and resources. This study evaluates whether exposure to China's 2018 Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Policy (SCIAPP) is associated with changes in urban CET. We use a balanced panel of 279 prefecture-level cities observed from 2008 to 2021 and a difference-in-differences design with city and year fixed effects and city-clustered standard errors. In the controlled specification, SCIAPP exposure is associated with a 0.032-log-point increase in the CET index (95% CI: 0.008–0.056), equivalent to approximately 3.27%. Adding province-specific linear trends yields a smaller estimate of 0.024 (95% CI: 0.007–0.042). Mechanism-proxy regressions are consistent with greater ESG-oriented fund allocation and forecasting performance as well as a lower energy-loss rate. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect is more significant in cities outside the Yangtze River Economic Belt and in areas with higher levels of market segmentation. Key limitations concern external validity beyond Chinese prefecture-level cities. Policy design should strengthen ESG-oriented green-finance allocation, forecasting and information capabilities, and operational-loss monitoring, while tailoring implementation to local market conditions and institutional capacity.

title: From exploitation-driven accumulation to mutualistic coordination: Evolutionary transitions of urban metabolic networks in 20 representative cities based on a process-structure-function framework
abstract: Rapid urbanization has imposed unprecedented resource and environmental pressures on Chinese cities. To identify keystone sectors in urban metabolism and reveal how sector-system interactions evolve with increasing material flows, we constructed an eight-sector urban material metabolic network for 20 representative Chinese cities by integrating material flow analysis with ecological network analysis. Ecological relationships, the Mixed-trophic impact (MTI) index, and ecological benefit were quantified within a process-structure-function framework and linked to total material flow. The results show that exploitation/control relationships dominated in all cities, typically accounting for 50-65% of interactions. The proportions of mutualistic relationships ranged from 14% to 33% and exceeded 25% in certain years in half of the cities. Mining was the keystone sector in all cities except Shenzhen, where energy conversion dominated, accounting for more than 35% of the total MTI. The MTI share of mining remained above 22% throughout the study period and reached 89%. Manufacturing generated the lowest ecological benefit across all city types except Shenzhen, and its ecological benefit declined in 75% of the cities. In leading-development cities, waste treatment produced the highest ecological benefit, generally exceeding 1.0, whereas mining produced the highest ecological benefit at other development stages. As metabolic scale increased, systems shifted from dominance by exploitation/control relationships toward stronger competition and ultimately to dominance by mutualistic relationships. The MTI share of mining rose from 40-60% to 80-90%, while total ecological benefit declined and stabilized at 5.3-5.9. These findings reveal an “accumulation-efficiency-coordination” trajectory and provide measurable indicators for identifying sustainable development pathways, cross-stage benchmarking, and improving resource efficiency across different urban types.

title: Joint decision-making for contract duration and benefit sharing in energy performance contract: A China-based shared-savings building retrofit case
abstract: Energy Performance Contract (EPC) is a pivotal market mechanism for building energy efficiency retrofits. However, challenges persist in coordinating contract duration and benefit allocation between building owners and energy service companies (ESCOs), weakening investment incentives and contractual adaptability. This study develops an integrated decision-making framework coupling contract duration determination with benefit allocation design. The framework applies a fuzzy real options model to define a flexible contract-duration domain under technological, policy, and investment uncertainty. A Stackelberg game is used to simulate the realistic leader-follower bargaining, while a modified Shapley value model refines benefit allocation by incorporating risk bearing, capital input, task complexity, and cooperation level. Application to a China-based shared-savings EPC retrofit case yielded an 8-year contract and a 71.2% ESCO benefit share, compared with the observed 7.5 years and 60.0%, respectively. A 20% increase in initial investment raised the optimized ESCO share to 81.9%, whereas a separate 20% reduction in annual energy-saving benefits raised it to 88.9%; both changes extended the duration to 10 years. The ESCO share remained within 71.0-71.3% across variations in the Stackelberg-Shapley combination weight, but ranged from 64.30% to 72.84% under alternative contribution-factor weighting structures. These results indicate that less favorable project economics require adjustments to both contractual terms under the case assumptions, while allocation outcomes depend more on contribution-weighting priorities than on the combination weight within the tested settings. Although case-specific, these findings provide a quantitative basis for coordinating investment recovery and benefit allocation, informing EPC contract design to balance between cooperation efficiency and benefit equity in building energy efficiency improvements and cleaner production.

title: Carbon emission efficiency of China's manufacturing industry and choice of precise carbon reduction paths——Analysis perspective based on the potential cost framework
abstract: Targeted decarbonization in manufacturing requires more than identifying efficiency losses; it also requires assessing each energy source's technical abatement potential, marginal abatement cost, and implementation priority. Using a balanced panel of 29 manufacturing subsectors in China from 2010 to 2024, this study estimates carbon emission efficiency with slacks-based measure directional distance function (SBM-DDF) models under meta-frontier and group-frontier technologies. It then uses undesirable-output slacks to quantify the abatement potential for coal, oil, and natural gas and combines these estimates with marginal abatement costs derived from parametric linear programming to construct a potential-Boston matrix. The results show that the manufacturing sector's meta-frontier efficiency increased from 0.520 to 0.641, although substantial room for improvement remains. For the medium- and high-emission groups, group-frontier efficiency was markedly higher than meta-frontier efficiency, indicating the need for both within-group catch-up and technological upgrading toward the meta-frontier. The high-emission group had the greatest abatement potential and the lowest average marginal abatement cost, whereas abating emissions associated with natural gas was generally more costly than abating those associated with coal or oil. The potential-Boston matrix classifies the 29 subsectors into four decarbonization pathways: phased advancement (13), comprehensive advancement (2), steady maintenance (12), and priority-focused mitigation (2). The proposed framework uses the meta-frontier to define long-term targets and group frontiers to set near-term catch-up benchmarks, translating efficiency, potential, and cost estimates into industry-energy priorities. Technology retrofits, fuel substitution, carbon pricing, transition finance, and regulatory measures can then be tailored to limit output losses while prioritizing high-potential, low-cost abatement opportunities.

title: A physics-guided grey-box residual framework for cleaner production and energy-efficiency optimization in aluminum electrolysis
abstract: Aluminum electrolysis production is a typical high-energy-consuming continuous industrial process, and its energy consumption prediction and optimization are of great significance to industrial energy systems. To address the issues of existing data-driven models being unable to characterize the complex coupled effects within electrolytic cells, lacking sufficient analysis of spatial topological heterogeneity, and failing to provide reliable decision support, this paper proposes an integrated learning framework that combines physics-guided prediction, calibrated uncertainty assessment, and constraint-screened counterfactual optimization. A physics-enhanced feature set integrating temporal, spatial, thermal, and electrical information was constructed, and XGBoost was used as the baseline predictor. To improve predictive accuracy while retaining physical interpretability, a two-stage residual framework based on a calibrated first-order Faraday-law energy anchor was introduced. The anchor was combined with a topology-aware residual learner to capture higher-order process deviations. The 86-feature physics-guided XGBoost baseline achieved a test-set R2 of 0.821, and the enhanced Faraday-topology residual model improved this value to 0.865 with RMSE reduced to 77.9 kWh/t. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was used to identify the main influencing factors. A risk-aware prediction module and a constraint-screened counterfactual recommendation strategy were further developed for high-energy-consumption conditions. Under joint operating-feasibility, local-trust-region, and abnormal-sample-screening constraints, the optimization strategy yielded an average expected energy-saving potential of 63.0 kWh/t for 159 high-energy-consumption samples. These results suggest that physics-guided feature construction, structured residual learning, and uncertainty-informed constraint screening can improve prediction accuracy, interpretability, and decision support for aluminum electrolysis.

title: Rare earth elements as emerging tracers for sustainable urban water management: Insights from weekly monitoring of a typical river in Beijing
abstract: Urban rivers are critical components of sustainable water management in megacities, yet strong temporal variability complicates the identification of pollution sources and anthropogenic impacts. This study employed weekly monitoring in a densely populated urban river in Beijing over an entire hydrological year to investigate the temporal dynamics, sources, and anthropogenic signatures of dissolved rare earth elements (REEs). Total REE concentrations ranged from 34.96 to 350.24 ng/L. Although several concentration peaks occurred during the monitoring period, no systematic wet season versus dry season differences were observed. The river consistently exhibited medium REE enrichment, while positive Gd anomalies (δGd: 7.28 ∼ 248.43) persisted throughout the monitoring period. Anthropogenic Gd accounted for more than 98% of dissolved Gd, and δGd was positively correlated with Cl−, indicating a persistent wastewater-related contribution and similar transport pathways. In contrast, La, Sm, and Eu anomalies showed greater temporal variability, suggesting additional and less persistent urban inputs. Temporal variations in dissolved REEs were primarily controlled by reclaimed water inputs rather than by precipitation driven dilution or natural weathering processes. Overall, the weekly year-round observations captured both the persistence of anthropogenic Gd and the temporal variability of other anthropogenic REE signatures, providing improved constraints on wastewater inputs in reclaimed water fed urban rivers.

title: Machine learning-driven intelligent optimization of layered double hydroxides-peroxymonosulfate system for antibiotic degradation: Interactive effect analysis and precise prediction
abstract: Traditional single-factor analysis based on the control variable method requires extensive experimental data to explore interactions among multiple parameters, which substantially increases experimental complexity in nonlinear catalytic systems. Herein, a closed-loop framework integrating data integration, machine learning modeling, and experimental validation was proposed to rapidly and accurately predict optimal operational parameters for the elimination of recalcitrant pollutants in water. By collecting and preprocessing literature-derived and experimental data on antibiotic degradation in layered double hydroxides–peroxymonosulfate (LDH-PMS) systems, a multi-dimensional database was constructed for the first time and evaluated using six representative machine learning models. Feature importance analysis, partial dependence plots, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interaction analysis identified reaction time, LDH dosage, and PMS dosage as the dominant driving factors, while revealing their threshold behaviors and nonlinear interactions. Model reliability was demonstrated by the strong agreement between predicted and experimental results (R2 > 0.900). Notably, experiments conducted under model-guided conditions achieved significantly higher median removal efficiencies (93-98%) than those obtained without model guidance (73-94%). This study provides a data-driven framework for rational experimental design and highlights the potential of machine learning-assisted strategies for optimizing advanced oxidation processes in environmental remediation.

title: Spatio-temporal evolution and driving mechanism of the level of coordinated transitional development between fossil fuel energy and clean energy in Chinese Cities: Insights from geospatial explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: Against the background of global warming, the coordinated transitional development between fossil fuel energy (FFE) and clean energy (CE) has become a core issue in China's energy transition. Most existing studies have analyzed energy transition at the national or provincial scale from a single dimension, overlooking city-level spatial heterogeneity and the need for an integrated FFE-CE perspective. Taking 291 Chinese cities as research objects, this study applies the coupling coordination degree (CCD) model to measure the level of coordinated transitional development during 2011–2021 and constructs a geospatial explainable artificial intelligence (GeoXAI) framework integrating XGBoost and the GeoShapley algorithm to analyze the spatially heterogeneous contributions of predictor variables to CCD predictions at national, regional, and city levels. The results show that: (1) CCD increased across all 291 cities during 2011–2021, with significant spatiotemporal differentiation. (2) CCD exhibited significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Global Moran's I > 0.6, Z > 2.58, p < 0.001), with High-High clusters concentrated in the eastern coastal region and Low-Low clusters emerging at the central-western border. (3) The XGBoost model achieved high prediction performance (test-set R2 = 0.9481, MAE = 0.0142, RMSE = 0.0206), and nuclear power plant accessibility (NPPA) was the most important factor at all scales, contributing 37.33% of total GeoShapley importance nationally and up to 42.79% in the Eastern Region. (4) Factor interactions were markedly stronger in the Western Region than those at other scales, with the NPPA-Temperature interaction reaching 8.62 × 10−4. The findings of this study not only provide scientific guidance for the formulation of multi-scale energy coordinated transition policies, but also promote the implementation of the “Dual Carbon” goals in China.

title: How can composite policy potential energy drive county green innovation? A quasi-natural experiment of fiscal decentralization-performance evaluation synergy
abstract: Green innovation is crucial for reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, but its success relies on effectively motivating local governments to guide and support green innovation activities, addressing the dual externalities involved. This study constructs a compound quasi-natural experiment by combining China's “Province-Managing-County” fiscal reform with the 2013 performance evaluation reform. Using an unbalanced panel of Chinese counties from 2000 to 2019 and a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) approach, we examine the impact of this institutional complementarity on county-level green innovation. The results show that the institutional complementarity significantly promotes green innovation. These findings remain robust under placebo tests and PSM-DID estimations. Mechanism analyses show that institutional complementarity promotes green innovation by reshaping local government behavior through increasing local governments' environmental attention, expanding public investment, and intensifying promotion-based competition among officials. Moreover, the effects are more pronounced in counties with higher environmental assessment pressure, tighter financing constraints, and greater fiscal pressure. To maximize the impact of institutional complementarity, fiscal, assessment, and related policy tools should be integrated into a complementary and reinforcing framework.

title: Cooling effects of urban blue-green spaces across China's climate zones: A dual-perspective and multi-factor analysis
abstract: Quantifying the cooling effects of urban blue-green spaces (UBGS) and identifying their driving factors are essential for optimizing blue-green infrastructure and mitigating urban thermal stress. This study investigated 950 UBGS samples across 30 major Chinese cities representing five distinct climate zones (BWk, BSk, Dwa, Cfa, and Cwa). Using remote sensing, GIS analysis, and Boosted Regression Tree (BRT) modeling, we quantified six cooling indicators, including cooling temperature (CT), distance (CD), area (CA), efficiency (CE), intensity (CI), and gradient (CG) from both maximum-value and cumulative-value perspectives. The primary findings are as follows: (1) Cooling effects exhibited pronounced climatic differentiation. The BWk zone showed superior performance in CT, CD, CI, and CG, while the BSk zone showed moderate performance, the Dwa zone exhibited balanced and favorable performance with the largest CA, the Cwa zone exhibited generally weak cooling performance, and Cfa demonstrated the highest CE. (2) Four distinct cooling typologies were identified: High-Intensity Cooling (large area, complex morphology), Marginal Cooling (high impervious coverage), Optimal Synergistic (strong aggregation, complex water geometry), and Extensive Radiation (high fragmentation). (3) Scale and composition characteristics showed the highest relative importance for CT, CD, CA, and CE, whereas landscape patterns ranked first in CI and CG, highlighting a functional differentiation in thermal regulation. Patch area (AREA) and green-space patch density (PD_GR) emerged as universal high-importance factors, frequently exhibiting non-linear threshold effects (e.g., CT enhancement when patch area is within the 0–300 ha range). Based on these insights, differentiated climate-adaptive planning strategies are proposed. These findings provide a robust scientific basis for cross-climatic urban thermal management and the enhancement of human settlement quality.

title: Eco-fiscal sustainability of plain afforestation: From ecological value creation to value realization
abstract: Afforestation projects can enhance ecosystem services (ESs) but may leave persistent fiscal commitments for land leasing and forest maintenance after project construction. Existing ES and Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) assessments have largely focused on ecological value creation, with limited attention to whether and under what conditions this value can be converted into funding for long-term operation. This study develops an eco-fiscal sustainability framework integrating spatial restructuring, GEP accounting, life-cycle cost analysis, future projection, ecological value realization (EVR), and uncertainty analysis, using the Plain Afforestation Project in Xiji Town, Beijing, as a case study. From 2010 to 2023, afforestation transformed the landscape from cropland dominance to a forest–cropland mosaic, while GEP increased by 26.6% to CNY 839.5 million and regulating services accounted for 92.02% of total GEP. Assuming no further afforestation, total GEP is projected to increase to CNY 916.2–939.8 million by 2080, mainly through forest development within the afforestation area, whereas annual fiscal costs generally decline as construction expenditure ends and maintenance requirements decrease. However, cumulative cost coverage depends strongly on EVR: under the 2030 baseline activation scenario, and given the specified cost pathway and GEP uncertainty, the 10% and 20% EVR scenarios do not achieve cumulative cost coverage by 2080, whereas all 3000 simulations under the 30% scenario reach non-negative cumulative net cash flow before 2080. These findings show that eco-fiscal sustainability depends not only on ecological value creation but, more critically, on the capacity to convert realizable ecological value into stable funding, providing a framework for the long-term management of post-construction peri-urban plain afforestation.

title: Cleaner production of ceramic fracturing proppants from bauxite tailings and oil-based drilling cuttings: process optimization, resource substitution and hazardous-element risk reduction
abstract: Cleaner production of oilfield and alumina-industry residues requires routes that convert hazardous and bulk solid wastes into functional products while reducing subsequent environmental risk. Here, oil-based drilling cuttings (OBDC) and bauxite tailings (BT) were co-sintered as solid-waste-derived aluminosilicate precursors for ceramic fracturing proppants. The study integrates raw-material complementarity, process optimization, proppant performance, pH-dependent leaching and hazardous-element fraction transformation to evaluate whether the proposed route can deliver both product utility and environmental-risk reduction. Single-factor experiments showed that sintering temperature, sintering time and OBDC dosage jointly controlled liquid-phase formation, quartz consumption, transient cordierite formation/dissolution and mullite crystallization. A processing window centered on 1280 °C, 60 min and 20 wt% OBDC produced a mullite-rich interlocking ceramic framework; response surface analysis and validation further supported an optimized condition of approximately 1339.42 °C, 53 min and 19 wt% OBDC for preparing the final ceramic proppant. Validation produced CP with an 8.6% breakage ratio at 52 MPa, a bulk density of 1.30 g cm−3 and 4.0% acid solubility; the breakage and acid-solubility values satisfy the respective 9% and 7% limits in SY/T 5108-2014. Environmental assessment identified Na, As, Mn, Ni and Sb as target risk elements. Sintering sharply reduced OPTI values under standard and pH-dependent leaching scenarios, while BCR/RAC results showed strong stabilization of Mn, Sb and Na and more element-specific behavior for As and Ni. XRD, FTIR, SEM–EDS/mapping and XPS evidence linked this risk reduction to mullite/aluminosilicate skeleton formation, glass-phase encapsulation, Fe/Al/Ca−associated binding, Na redistribution in the glassy network and densification-induced diffusion limitation. The work establishes a cleaner-production route that couples complete waste-derived mineral substitution with standard-compliant proppant performance and multi-element risk reduction.

title: Carry-over release of microplastics and additives from PBAT mulch film residues affects soil-maize-microbiota system
abstract: Although biodegradable mulch films (BDMs) are promoted as sustainable alternatives to polyethylene films, their degradation may generate microplastics (MPs) and release chemical additives. In this study, commercial poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate)-based BDM (PBAT-BDM) residues were evaluated as a polymer additive system in a two-year carry-over greenhouse maize experiment. PBAT-BDM fragments were incorporated into soil at 0%, 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1% (w/w), and maize was grown for two consecutive cycles (P1 and P2) in the same continuously irrigated, residue-amended soil. During degradation, PBAT-BDMs developed progressive surface cracking, increased hydrophilicity, decreased C/O ratios, and generated more PBAT-derived MPs. Ultraviolet absorbers (e.g., UV-234 and UV-360) and organophosphate esters (e.g., AO168=O and TNPP) were also released and showed compound-specific dissipation and organ-dependent accumulation in maize. Increasing PBAT-BDM amendment levels altered soil physicochemical properties, reduced chlorophyll content, and increased antioxidant enzyme activities, particularly in P2, indicating carry-over physiological stress after prolonged exposure. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed shifts in the microbial community composition, including changes in the relative abundances of Pseudomonadota, Bacteroidota, Bacillota, and Actinomycetota. Structural equation modeling suggested that additive uptake disrupted antioxidant defense and contributed to maize biomass reduction. These findings indicate that commercial PBAT-BDM residues should be assessed as integrated sources of MPs and additives, rather than as biodegradable polymer matrices alone. They provide a scientific basis for managing the combined pollution risks of biodegradable plastics and their additives in agricultural environments.

title: Prolonged (80-day) exposure to waste drilling fluids alters the structure and trophic networks of marine plankton communities in a microcosm study
abstract: The ecological risks associated with the direct discharge of waste drilling fluids (WDFs) into the ocean must be systematically assessed. Through an 80-day microcosm experiment, we assessed main pollution characteristics and seawater quality after introducing WDF water extracts at three concentrations and examined the prolonged dynamic effects of continuous exposure on natural plankton communities. WDF input altered key water quality parameters, increased Cr and As, and caused Cr and Hg in the HIGH group to exceed GB 3097-1997 Class I seawater standards. Chlorophyll a (Chl a) and dissolved oxygen (DO) levels and the pH decreased, whereas turbidity increased. WDF input also changed phytoplankton and zooplankton species compositions, increased spatial differentiation within communities, and generated dose-dependent effects. Phytoplankton responded more quickly than zooplankton, and toxicity verification experiments confirmed that phytoplankton were more sensitive. RDA indicated that Cr and Hg were the primary variables that explained changes in the community structure of phytoplankton and zooplankton, respectively. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed decreases in the total network and subnetwork topologies and the connectivity and abundance of key taxonomic groups, suggesting general network degradation. Based on the random forest model and Spearman's correlation analyses, cross-trophic interactions dominated the total network responses, followed by the phytoplankton subnetwork. These results indicate that the central mechanism underlying WDF ecological risk is weakening planktonic interactions via direct interspecies interference and impaired phytoplankton supply. These findings provide a systematic foundation and theoretical support for establishing an ecological risk assessment system for WDFs and promoting their eco-friendly use and emission management.

title: Sustainable recovery of silver wires from crystalline silicon solar cells
abstract: Silver is a valuable metal in end-of-life crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules, yet recycling mainly relies on acid leaching, which converts metallic Ag into Ag+ and generates acidic wastewater. Although molten salt Ag-recovery methods avoid acid use, they cannot effectively control Si-substrate corrosion loss, and the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here, NaOH-KOH molten salt etching of Al-BSF solar cells was investigated to elucidate the mechanisms of Ag wires recovery and Si-substrate loss. The molten salt etched the SiNx passivation layer and weakened Ag/SiNx interfacial adhesion, allowing Ag wires to detach without ionic dissolution. Thermodynamic calculations showed that Si3N4 and exposed Si reacted with NaOH-KOH molten salt to form Na2SiO3 and K2SiO3. Experimental results showed that the Si-substrate loss ratio was only 2.62 % at 230 °C for 100 s. At 230 °C for 150 s, Ag recovery reached 94.34 %, and the SiNx passivation layer was effectively removed, maximum Ag recovery was 97.11 %. Regarding the mechanism of Si-substrate loss, the exposed Si substrate undergoes alkaline molten salt etching after SiNx removal, during which OH− promotes conversion of Si into soluble Na/K silicates, causing localized Si-substrate loss and pitting. These findings clarify the mechanisms of acid-free, low-loss precious-metal recovery from crystalline silicon photovoltaic materials.

title: Defect-mediated electric-field coupling enables low-threshold methane hydrate dissociation toward cleaner gas recovery
abstract: Methane hydrate is an important unconventional natural gas resource, but its dissociation is commonly constrained by slow kinetics and inefficient heat delivery during conventional thermal stimulation. Electric fields provide a potential route for reducing the dependence on intensive thermal input, yet the molecular mechanism by which field energy couples with intrinsic hydrate defects remains unclear. Here, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate methane hydrate dissociation under direct-current, terahertz sinusoidal, and terahertz bidirectional pulsed electric fields in the presence of water and methane vacancies. Water vacancies were found to dominate hydrate destabilization by disrupting the hydrogen-bond network and forming structural vulnerability gradients, whereas methane vacancies mainly perturbed the guest sublattice. Terahertz pulsed fields induced the fastest cage collapse, whereas weak direct-current fields produced the largest relative defect-induced gain within the sampled parameter space, indicating that field mode and framework integrity jointly govern hydrate dissociation. Monte Carlo-calibrated targeting analysis confirmed preferential field activation near water-vacancy sites, while a dual-index percolation model linked critical dissociation boundaries to hydrogen-bond and cage-network connectivity losses. These findings reveal vacancy-mediated electric-field coupling as a molecular mechanism for low-threshold methane hydrate dissociation and provide molecular-level insight for developing less thermally intensive hydrate dissociation strategies.

title: Impact of slurry additives on nitrogen emissions, grass agronomy and soil microbial communities following slurry landspreading
abstract: This study assessed the effects of specific slurry additives on nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, grass herbage yield and N uptake and soil microbial communities. The experimental work was conducted on two soil types: i) a moderately to poorly drained fine loam and ii) an imperfectly drained clay loam over two growing seasons. Cattle slurry was applied in three split applications at both sites simulating trailing shoe application method and the treatments were control (no treatment), unamended slurry, slurry + sulphuric acid, slurry + biochar, slurry + gypsum and urea + urease inhibitor N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) (NBPT-urea). Nitrous oxide was measured during the growing period using the static chambers and dry matter yield was measured at every harvest. Ammonia (NH3) was also quantified at one of the sites, therefore NH3 responses are site-specific. Ammonia was measured within the first week of slurry application using dynamic chambers coupled with a photoacoustic gas analyser. Soil samples were collected after the end of the experiment for microbial analysis at both sites. The acidified slurry increased grass yield by more than one tonne ha−1, increased plant N recovery by 21 to 24 kg N ha−1, suggesting improved nitrogen conservation may have contributed to these agronomic benefits, and increased fungal abundance however, it also increased N2O on one occasion. The other slurry amendments did not have significant effect on N2O. The cumulative N2O emissions from the moderately drained soil were significantly lower than the imperfectly drained soil. None of the amendments significantly reduced NH3 emissions in the moderately to poorly drained soil, while biochar increased NH3 during a single application timing.

title: Dietary transitions for urban water sustainability in arid regions: A planetary health case study from Ürümqi, China
abstract: We develop an integrated domestic water-conservation framework combining dynamic water pricing with healthy-diet interventions to jointly manage physical and virtual water use. (Virtual water refers to the total interregional flow, through trade, of water consumed in the production of traded products.) Relative to the baseline diet, healthy, vegetarian and meat-based diets reduced annual per-capita food water footprints (The water footprint quantifies the total water use associated with consumption by an individual, region or country.) by 166.11, 208.42 and 167.97 m3, respectively, and industrial water footprints by 14.95, 22.05 and 15.17 m3 through supply-chain linkages, while direct domestic water use remained largely unchanged. Dynamic water pricing reduced annual per-capita shower water use by 10.58–15.88 m3 and total domestic water use by 42.32–83.58 m3. Acceptance differed between interventions: 41.67% supported water-price regulation, mainly influenced by consumption habits, whereas 53.57% accepted dietary adjustment, with willingness more strongly associated with ethnicity and income. After accounting for acceptance rates, the three dietary scenarios reduced city-wide annual food water footprints by 370, 464 and 374 million m3 and industrial water footprints by 33, 49 and 34 million m3, respectively. Dynamic water pricing reduced annual urban water use by 73–145 million m3, including 18–27 million m3 of shower water. Water pricing therefore primarily affects direct domestic use, whereas dietary adjustment propagates upstream through supply chains, generating broader water-footprint effects. This framework advances domestic water conservation towards coordinated social–ecological governance of physical and virtual water, offering a transferable pathway for water-scarce cities.

title: A high-performance integrated PV water-electricity cogeneration device via enhanced steam circulation and dropwise condensation
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) water-electricity cogeneration offers a compelling pathway to simultaneously address water scarcity and rising energy demand. However, current systems are typically constrained by inefficient steam transport and suboptimal condensation heat transfer, limiting overall performance. Here, we present an integrated PV water-electricity cogeneration (IPVWC) device that overcomes these limitations through a rationally designed dual-enhancement strategy: a dedicated steam circulation module coupled with an amphiphilic hybrid copper condenser that enables rapid steam transport and efficient dropwise condensation. Comprehensive COMSOL Multiphysics simulations were performed to elucidate the entire transport chain from capillary wick evaporation to steam flow dynamics and condensation and to guide the optimization of device architecture. Concurrently, a theoretical framework describing droplet nucleation, growth, and departure on the condenser surface was established to inform surface design. At an illumination of 1 kW/m2, the optimized IPVWC device achieves a significant PV temperature reduction of 24.61°C while maintaining a continuous water production rate of 0.58 L/m2·h with the hybrid copper condenser, a chamber thickness of 5 mm and a nominal fan outlet velocity of 0.5 m/s. This work provides a viable design paradigm for next-generation integrated water-energy systems with strong potential for sustainable desalination applications.

title: Efficient separation and recovery of tellurium, germanium, and gallium from crystallized waste chalcogenide glass by sustainable vacuum distillation strategy
abstract: Tellurium (Te), germanium (Ge), and gallium (Ga) are critical strategic metals. They are widely used in photovoltaic devices, infrared optical systems, semiconductors, and advanced defense technologies. Waste chalcogenide glass represents an important secondary resource for these valuable elements. However, its clean and efficient recycling remains challenging due to the complex occurrence states of Te, Ge, and Ga and the limitations of conventional recovery processes. In this study, a two-stage vacuum distillation strategy was proposed for the selective separation and recovery of Te, Ge, and Ga from crystallized waste chalcogenide glass. The feasibility of the process was first evaluated based on saturated vapor pressure, maximum evaporation speed, separation coefficient and evaporation characteristics analyses.
