Two process routes were then designed and experimentally validated: high-temperature followed by low-temperature vacuum distillation (HTLT vacuum distillation), and low-temperature followed by high-temperature vacuum distillation (LTHT vacuum distillation). The results indicated that the HTLT vacuum distillation process yielded three products: the tellurium product contained 98.53 % Te, the germanium product contained 57.61 % Ge, and the gallium product contained 44.81 % Ga. The LTHT vacuum distillation process yielded three products: the tellurium product contained 95.69 % Te, the germanium product contained 34.73 % Ge, and the gallium product contained 27.31 % Ga. The proposed process features a short flowsheet, high adaptability to different raw material compositions, and environmental compatibility. This work provides a clean technical route for the separation and recovery of strategic metals from crystallized waste chalcogenide glass.

title: Can cropland yield and production resilience be reconciled? Evidence from a symbiotic framework in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain, China
abstract: Unraveling the complex interplay between yield and resilience is crucial for sustainable cropland development and food security. However, existing resilience assessments have largely relied on subjective indicator-based approaches and have paid limited attention to the dynamic interactions between yield and resilience. Therefore, this study quantified the spatiotemporal evolution of cropland production resilience in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain (HHHP) from a recovery dynamics perspective and developed a symbiotic framework to characterize its interaction with yield. Subsequently, the Lotka-Volterra and multiscale geographically and temporally weighted regression models were employed to characterize symbiotic states and their influencing factors. Results indicate that cropland production resilience in the HHHP exhibited a spatial pattern of increases in the central region but declines in the northern and southern regions, with approximately 47% of cities showing resilience growth. The yield-resilience symbiosis shifted from a competition-dominated to an antagonism-dominated regime, accompanied by a directional transition from resilience-favoring to yield-favoring pathways and an increasing prevalence of high-gain states. In contrast, mutualism remained scarce and was more susceptible to degradation. The impacts of individual driving factors on this symbiosis exhibited significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Agricultural inputs and technological progress showed predominantly positive influences, while climatic influences were relatively localized, whereas socioeconomic and cropland utilization factors exhibited bidirectional influences. Notably, in the absence of targeted interventions, the yield-resilience symbiosis still faces long-term risks of lock-in in competition and antagonism. These findings provide new insights into reconciling cropland yield and production resilience, supporting sustainable agricultural management.

title: Techno-economic analysis of a sequential bioprocessing facility for sustainable dairy feed production
abstract: An alternative feed supply from upcycling of food wastes in agri-food system would make dairy farms more independent from feed price oscillation. A techno-economic analysis of the sustainable dairy feed production facility via sequential fermentation of crop residue and fresh fruit/vegetable (FFV) discards was conducted. The facility has a 10-year lifetime with an annual capacity of producing 82,787 metric tons (MT) of fermented feed for dairy cattle from 18,081 MT of wheat straw, 43,396 MT of FFV discards, and 12,151 MT of alfalfa hay. The facility was profitable when sale price of the fermented feed was $90 MT−1 (the minimum selling price was $83.2 MT−1), FFV tipping fee was $67 MT−1, at an annual inflation rate of 2.0%. This condition created annual net cash flow of $1,687,450 (year 1) to $656,262 (year 10), a payback period of 3.96 years, and annualized return on investment (ROI) of 10.6%. At 5% discount rate, the net present value (NPV) of the investment was $3,436,129 with an internal rate of return (IRR) of 18% and discounted payback period of 4.63 years. Sensitivity analysis showed that the sale price of the fermented feed was the greatest determinant of the facility's profitability followed by FFV landfill tipping fee, cost of alfalfa hay. Cost of wheat straw, equipment and labor force had relatively less impact on profitability of the facility. Process capacity analysis suggested that the facility needs to be operated at least 20% of its full capacity to be profitable. This study theoretically demonstrated the economic feasibility of a proposed sequential bioprocessing facility as a method of producing sustainable dairy feed in the agricultural industry.

title: Decoding the ecological–economic transition in Beijing city through culturomics and co-expression networks: from trade-off to synergy
abstract: The synergistic advancement of economic development and ecological quality in a city is central to sustainable development. While the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis posits an initial trade-off followed by a turning point toward synergy, high-resolution quantitative evidence identifying these inflection points and their potential underlying dynamics in specific city contexts remains scarce. In this exploratory study, we investigated the relationship between ecological and economic activities of Beijing (2005–2024) by applying culturomics and word co-expression network (WCN) analysis to longitudinal textual data from the Beijing Daily. The results indicated that negative ecological words (NEs) and environmental pollution indicators in Beijing followed an inverted U-shaped EKC, with a potential peak occurring around 2015 at a per capita gross domestic product (GDP) of approximately 16,666 USD. Media discourse exhibited a fundamental structural transition, shifting from non-ecologically friendly economic activities toward ecologically friendly terms, with ecological activities gaining a systemic advantage (Revealed comparative advantage [RCA] > 1) by 2018. The synergy-to-tradeoff ratio of the ecological-economic co-expression network increased to 1.20, coinciding with a 63% increase in non-negative ecological terms and a 40% decrease in negative terms within the core lexicon, as well as reductions in pollutant levels. City sustainability was characterized by a dynamic balance, in which overall synergistic transformation was punctuated by transient periods of synchronized decline in both ecology and economy, reflecting the system's “adaptive sustainability”. Ultimately, this study provides a replicable, data-driven framework for diagnosing city sustainability transitions and highlights the pivotal role of policy intervention in restructuring the trajectory of city development.

title: Carbon intensity–cost trajectories and policy implications for sustainable aviation fuels under electricity and hydrogen transitions
abstract: Existing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) assessments show that pathway carbon intensity and production cost vary across technologies, feedstocks, regions, and background energy systems. Yet static pathway rankings reveal little about how these differences translate into policy outcomes as electricity and hydrogen systems evolve. We use a scenario-consistent prospective life-cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis framework to trace how region- and scenario-specific electricity and hydrogen trajectories alter pathway carbon intensity and production cost. A carbon-intensity-based policy-mapping layer then translates these trajectories into compliance windows, credit balances, and break-even credit prices relative to the used-cooking-oil reference pathway. The analysis covers seven pathways, four regions, four transition scenarios, and 2025–2050, while forward-projecting only electricity- and hydrogen-related emission factors and prices to isolate this background-energy channel. Power-to-liquid with direct air capture shows the largest carbon-intensity and cost response, whereas the Fischer–Tropsch pathways remain comparatively stable. Under the assumed central carbon-intensity benchmark trajectory, only 17.9% of pathway–region–scenario cases remain compliant in 2050. At a fixed credit price of 200 USD/t CO2, power-to-liquid with direct air capture has positive median 2050 credit balances in EU-15, the USA, and Japan but a deficit in China. Break-even credit prices vary substantially across regions and years, indicating different incentives required for cost parity. These results show that regional energy-system changes propagate through pathway-specific environmental and economic responses and interact with policy parameters to shape modeled SAF compliance and incentive outcomes that cannot be inferred from static pathway rankings alone.

title: Methodological framework for planning and evaluating circular economy projects in socio-environmental vulnerable territories
abstract: The transition to a circular economy requires context-sensitive projects that integrate resource circularity with socioenvironmental inclusion, particularly in vulnerable territories where infrastructure and institutional support are uneven. However, practical and reproducible frameworks that guide both the planning and evaluation of community-based circular economy projects across their life cycle remain limited. This study proposes a structured methodological framework aligned with cleaner production principles that integrates participatory planning with a multidimensional impact assessment. The framework operationalizes 24 indicators grouped into six analytical dimensions and uses an explicit 1-5 scoring rubric supported by traceable evidence sources. Because the 6D/24I framework is conceived as a formative, multidimensional evaluation architecture rather than a reflective measurement scale, classical psychometric validation techniques, such as internal consistency coefficients or factor analysis, are not conceptually appropriate. The indicators do not represent interchangeable manifestations of a single latent construct; instead, each captures a substantively distinct dimension of project performance. In formative models, low inter-item correlation does not indicate measurement weakness, but dimensional independence. The framework is therefore designed as a structured multi-criteria diagnostic system rather than a latent-variable measurement instrument. Robustness is assessed through evidence traceability, explicit scoring rubrics, triangulation of qualitative and quantitative sources, and sensitivity analysis of weighting schemes. The framework was applied to four socioenvironmental projects in Brazil that reuse glass waste in distinct intervention modes: sustainable materials development, ecojewelry production, eco-brick manufacturing in quilombola communities, and socioenvironmental entrepreneurship in basic education schools. An additional ex post application to an externally developed project (Acelera Rio Doce), assessed by evaluators who were not involved in either the author team or the project, was used to examine the framework's operational usability beyond the author-led cases; this application is interpreted as an external methodological illustration rather than formal validation of inter-rater or cross-context reproducibility. Cross-case application revealed differentiated performance profiles across dimensions and highlighted boundary conditions for implementation, including institutional arrangements, infrastructure availability, and the maturity of local governance networks. The study contributes a transparent and evidence-traceable assessment architecture for practitioners and researchers, providing a structured basis for criterion-referenced diagnosis and offering design principles that are potentially transferable to comparable Global South contexts when enabling conditions are considered.

title: Sustainable artificial stone production using recycled glass waste and determining aesthetic performance
abstract: Waste generation and waste management have become critical components of environmental sustainability and successful waste management is crucial for protecting human health, conserving natural resources. The increasing generation of glass waste has created an urgent need for sustainable recycling strategies and alternative utilization methods. In this study, artificial stone composites were produced using soda-lime glass waste with different particle sizes and unsaturated polyester resin. The waste glass was first crushed and milled, and then sieved to obtain different particle size fractions. Based on the average particle size, the glass particles were classified into three groups: fine (150 μm), medium (300 μm), and coarse (600 μm). The aim of the research was to evaluate the effects of particle size on the physical, mechanical, and surface properties of artificial stones and to investigate their resistance to environmental aging conditions, including freeze–thaw, thermal shock, and salt crystallisation cycles. For this purpose, weight, porosity, water absorption, colour, and gloss were measured before and after the ageing cycles, and the changes between the two measurements were evaluated. The results indicate that particle size distribution plays a critical role in determining the microstructure and durability of artificial stones. Samples containing mixed and medium particle sizes exhibited improved particle packing and lower porosity due to better resin penetration. In contrast, coarse particle samples showed higher porosity and weaker interfacial bonding. Among the aging mechanisms, thermal shock produced the most significant deterioration, generating internal stresses at the resin–particle interface and resulting in higher weight losses. Freeze–thaw and salt crystallisation cycles mainly caused surface degradation, particularly in terms of gloss reduction. Interestingly, thermal shock led to an apparent increase in gloss in some samples due to resin redistribution and surface smoothing, although this did not correspond to improved structural integrity. The outputs of the result demonstrated that glass waste can be effectively reused in artificial stone production.

title: When is it valuable to be green? Impact of green practices on firm resilience
abstract: Against the global green transition, green practices have become imperative for manufacturing firms, yet their divergent impacts on firm resilience remain underexplained. Existing sustainable operations management literature overemphasizes green practice effectiveness but neglects the heterogeneity of practice types (substantive vs. symbolic) and the strategic value of adoption timing, lacking a contingent framework to interpret their boundary conditions. Using 2012-2023 data from Chinese listed manufacturers and the Awareness-Motivation-Capability (AMC) framework, this study explores how substantive (Sub) and symbolic (Sym) green practice adoption timing affect firm resilience. We find that Sub exhibit a first-mover advantage: earlier adoption of substantive practices is positively associated with firm resilience. Managerial myopia weakens the advantage, while customer concentration strengthens it. In contrast, Sym do not exhibit a clear first-mover advantage individually; however, their association with firm resilience becomes positive conditionally, at higher levels of managerial myopia or asymmetric cost management. The results provide clear guidance for firms to select green practices and optimize adoption timing, and help green initiatives effectively improve resilience against market fluctuations.

title: Upcycling spent coffee grounds into deprotonated carboxyl-rich dissolved organic matter for functional gypsum-based thick coatings
abstract: Enhancing the mechanical strength of composites with agricultural waste has long been a bottleneck in advancing environmental sustainability. This study successfully introduces a circular economy strategy by incorporating spent coffee ground-derived dissolved organic matter (SDOM) into gypsum-based thick coatings, where interfacial complexation and retarding effects are proposed to govern the molecular structural development. The objective of this study is to convert spent coffee grounds (SCGs) into dissolved organic matter with high water solubility (>90%), enriched with deprotonated carboxyl functional groups through solid-to-solute (STS) technology. The resulting SDOM is incorporated into commercial gypsum matrices. FTIR and mechanical evaluations suggest that the deprotonated carboxyl groups in SDOM undergo coordinate complexation and hydrogen bonding with the calcium ions and hydroxyl groups of the gypsum components. This chemical interaction is expected to exert a regulatory retarding effect that promotes uniform dispersion, mitigates stress concentration, and facilitates a more complete matrix hydration. Consequently, the composite yields high-strength thick coatings with robust complexed carbonyl (C=O) coordination structures. Taguchi orthogonal design and analysis of variance (ANOVA) identified the SDOM solution concentration as the most influential factor affecting mechanical strength. Under optimal conditions, the maximum bending strength of SDOM-incorporated thick coatings reached 30.11 MPa, representing a 1.65-fold increase compared with pure gypsum (control). Moreover, SCG-derived SDOM enriched with hydrophilic deprotonated carboxyl functional groups facilitates uniform dispersion in water-based gypsum, enabling the composite thick coatings to exhibit superior surface thermal barrier capability and storability. The findings provide a transformative demonstration for the green building and waste-upcycling industries, contributing to the realization of environmental sustainability goals.

title: Unlocking the carbon reduction potential of building integrated photovoltaics beyond rooftops in an urban core considering inter building shading
abstract: Building integrated photovoltaics have substantial potential for large scale deployment in existing urban areas under climate change mitigation. However, conventional assessments often neglect inter building shading and differences among façades. This may overestimate solar resources and carbon emission reduction potential. This study develops a three-dimensional assessment framework for the urban core of Fuzhou. The framework integrates solar radiation modelling, dynamic technical and economic evaluation, and future operational carbon emission reduction. The results show that the mean shading ratio of urban building surfaces was 28.04%, and technically useable solar energy reached 3.56 × 1010 kWh. This resource could generate 5.69 × 109 kWh of annual alternating current electricity, covering about 10.11% of Fuzhou's citywide annual electricity consumption and avoiding about 3.60 × 106 tCO2 of operational carbon emissions. The technical and economic evaluation further identified rooftop deployment as the most robust option, with west façades more favorable than south façades. Long term scenario analysis also showed that technology improvement produced greater carbon reduction gains than expansion of installable area. By 2060, under the fast pathways, technology improvement and urban expansion increased the annual carbon emission reduction potential to 8.77 × 106 and 5.69 × 106 tCO2, respectively. These results show that photovoltaic deployment on building surfaces beyond rooftops offers considerable carbon emission reduction potential and can be incorporated into future urban planning to support climate change mitigation.

title: How does corporate ESG shape urban economic resilience?
abstract: Enhancing urban economic resilience is critical amid global uncertainty. Using panel data from 260 Chinese cities over 2009–2021, we construct an Urban Corporate Aggregated ESG (UESG) index by aggregating firm-level ESG ratings using firm-size weights. We examine the association between UESG and urban economic resilience and explore potential mediating channels. The results show that higher UESG is significantly associated with greater urban economic resilience. Mediation estimates are consistent with partial mediation involving external openness, green total factor productivity, and industrial structure, with estimated mediation proportions of 8.74%, 6.89%, and 11.74%, respectively. Subgroup analyses identify statistically significant positive associations in eastern regions, tier-2 cities, and non-resource-based cities. These findings link aggregate corporate ESG performance to urban economic resilience and inform discussions of urban sustainability policies suited to local conditions.

title: Sustainable production of ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage particles from molten steel slag
abstract: Steel slag (SS), a high-volume byproduct (150 kg/ton steel) with severe disposal burdens, poses critical environmental challenges. To transform this waste into value, we propose the novel TERSEG protocol–a sustainable valorization route that, for the first time, simultaneously enables ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage (TES) particle production from molten SS via centrifugal granulation and recovers its >1400 °C waste heat. By modifying molten SS with blast furnace slag (BFS) to drastically reduce its viscosity by ∼90% (to 0.23 Pa s at 1500 °C), we overcome prior barriers to granulation. The engineered particles (1-3 mm) exhibit exceptional thermal stability (<1% mass loss over 10 cycles at 400-1000 °C), good sphericity (axis ratio of 1.5), and low porosity (<4%), making them ideal TES materials. This approach recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional materials. The TES particle production scalability is demonstrated via an empirical correlation validated across broad operational conditions. This approach pioneers a sustainable valorization route that simultaneously recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional TES materials. This work provides a circular economy strategy for the steel industry, diverting slag from landfills, reducing industrial CO2 footprint, and advancing net-zero goals.

title: Life cycle assessment of heat pipe grinding wheels for cleaner machining of aerospace superalloys
abstract: Global carbon-neutral commitments are compelling aerospace manufacturers to reconcile high-performance machining with environmental sustainability. Grinding nickel-based superalloys conventionally demands flood cooling to prevent thermal damage, creating substantial carbon footprints from energy-intensive coolant systems and hazardous waste treatment. This study introduces a heat-pipe grinding wheel (HPGW) combined with minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) as a tool-enabled cleaner grinding route. Orthogonal experiments were conducted to compare the thermal performance of the HPGW and conventional grinding wheel (CGW), followed by a stage-wise life cycle assessment covering wheel manufacturing and one-pass grinding. At vs 55 m/s, vw 120 mm/min, ap 0.2 mm, the CGW-MQL route causes workpiece burn at 696 °C, while the HPGW-MQL limits it to 494 °C without burn. This result establishes the feasibility of replacing the CGW–flood route with the HPGW–MQL route. In the manufacturing stage, the HPGW reduces steel use by 52.3%, lowering the fossil global warming potential (GWP) from 40.0 to 27.7 kg CO2-eq, despite higher electricity. In the grinding stage, the fossil GWP for CGW-flood route decreases from 0.184 to 0.0434 kg CO2-eq per pass for HPGW-MQL, corresponding to a 76.4% reduction, compared the CGW-flood cooling route. This route eliminates waste treatment requirements and achieves consistent improvements across acidification, toxicity, and resource scarcity indicators. Tool-structure-enabled process-route substitution offers a feasible pathway to prevent grinding burn in difficult-to-machine materials while reducing grinding-stage environmental burdens, enabling machining decisions to be evaluated more comprehensively from a system-level environmental perspective.

title: Temperature–humidity operating windows for mitigating degradation and enhancing passive shutdown recovery of a PEMFC stack under long-term WHVC operation using in situ water balance analysis
abstract: This study experimentally investigated the effects of operating temperature and inlet relative humidity (RH) on initial electrochemical performance, irreversible voltage degradation, internal water balance, and passive shutdown recovery of a three-cell proton exchange membrane fuel cell stack under the World Harmonized Vehicle Cycle (WHVC). Nine temperature–humidity conditions (50–70 °C and 50–90% RH) were evaluated using three 50-h WHVC blocks per case, each followed by a 15-h passive shutdown, corresponding to 150 h of WHVC operation and 195 h per case. The highest initial performance was achieved at 60 °C/90% RH, whereas the lowest voltage degradation rate and highest mean shutdown recovery rate were obtained at 50 °C/90% RH. At 1.1 A/cm2, the voltage degradation rate ranged from 143.4 μV/h at 50 °C/90% RH to 1318.2 μV/h at 70 °C/50% RH. In situ water-balance analysis showed higher calculated water accumulation and lower outlet vapor flow rates at 50 °C/90% RH, whereas 70 °C/50% RH exhibited limited calculated water accumulation and high outlet vapor flow rates. The relationship between mean total water accumulation fraction and irreversible voltage degradation became stronger under load, with R2 increasing from 0.503 at 0.5 A/cm2 to 0.828 at 0.8 A/cm2. The mean shutdown recovery rate was 67.61% at 50 °C/90% RH and 18.13% at 70 °C/50% RH. Within the tested matrix, lower-temperature, high-RH conditions provided a more suitable operating window for limiting irreversible degradation and maintaining voltage recovery under WHVC operation.

title: Synergistic reinforcement and heavy metal stabilization of lithium slag-feldspar powder composites via microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation
abstract: The continued accumulation of lithium slag (LS) and low-activity feldspar powder (FP) causes high disposal costs and persistent heavy metals (HMs) leaching hazards. Large-scale synergistic treatment methods for these wastes are still critically lacking. This study utilized microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) for the synergistic solidification of the LS-FP micro-graded system. The micro-graded skeleton was constructed through particle micro-grinding and subsequent size classification. Response surface methodology (RSM) optimized the process parameters, and the mechanical responses and HMs stabilization mechanisms were systematically investigated. Maximum CaCO3 precipitation of 15.3% was obtained at 1.25 mol/L and 12 grouting cycles, while the RSM-optimized parameters (80% LS, 0.76 mol/L, and 10 grouting cycles) produced a UCS of 0.84 MPa and a peak shear strength exceeding the untreated control by 60.57% (348.6 kPa). The lateral ultimate strain exhibited a 45.4% decrease, pointing to a distinct improvement in deformation and spalling resistance. Multi-scale microstructural characterizations indicate that CaCO3 precipitates provide physical entrapment through pore filling and co-precipitation, the micro-gradation and interlocking of LS–FP particles form a load-bearing framework, and the C-(A)-S-H gel network generated by the pozzolanic reaction of reactive aluminosilicate phases provides particle cementation and interlayer adsorption. The interplay of these three components creates the physicochemical basis for mechanical reinforcement and HMs stabilization. Leaching inhibition rates of 18.5% and 44.1% were recorded for Be(II) and Tl(I), respectively. Overall, the proposed approach offers a sustainable avenue for the synergistic recycling of LS and FP, subject to further field-scale validation.

title: Self-assembled biofilm consortia resist volatile fatty acid inhibition: Mechanisms underlying robust anaerobic digestion at high organic loading rates
abstract: High organic loading rate (OLR) often induce volatile fatty acids (VFAs) inhibition, destabilizing anaerobic digestion. To address this, an anaerobic fixed-bed biofilm reactor was operated under a stepwise increased OLR from 0.9 to 16.3 kg COD/m3/d. Results demonstrated that elevated VFAs stress triggered protein-driven self-assembly, fostering a robust biofilm consortium dominated by Methanothrix. A distinct niche partition emerged: suspended flocs, enriched with fermentative bacteria (e.g., Escherichia-Shigella), acted as a microbial seed bank for rapid substrate hydrolysis, while the biofilm, hosting specialized syntrophs like Anaerotignum, ensured stable methanogenesis. Functional gene profiling revealed the enrichment of norank_Geobacteraceae and c-di-GMP signaling pathways, suggesting potential direct interspecies electron transfer and enhanced structural integrity. Despite effluent VFAs peaks of 2000 mg COD/L, the system maintained a COD removal efficiency of 73%. This resilience was attributed to the functional redundancy between flocs and biofilm, which mitigated hydraulic washout and metabolic imbalances. This study elucidates the mechanistic underpinnings of microbial self-assembly into biofilms conferring robust resistance to VFAs inhibition, providing a viable technological paradigm for full-scale high-rate anaerobic digestion of concentrated wastewaters.

title: Proteus mirabilis reshapes the gut microenvironment and enhances protein degradation and nitrogen conversion in Hermetia illucens larvae via enzyme-mediated ammonia accumulation
abstract: Black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) can efficiently convert high-nitrogen organic wastes such as food waste and livestock manure, and their gut symbiotic microbiota serve as the core regulator of protein degradation and nitrogen cycling. A urease-producing Proteus mirabilis strain was isolated from BSFL. In vitro assays confirmed its extracellular urease, serine protease, and phenylalanine deaminase activities, which enable ammonia production through both urea hydrolysis and amino acid deamination. In vitro co-culture assays revealed that this strain inhibits the dominant gut bacterium Klebsiella through a dual mechanism: ammonia accumulation elevates the microenvironmental pH and exerts ammonia induced cytotoxicity. Klebsiella metabolically produces acids, which can alter the microenvironment, induce protein flocculation and precipitation, and impede substrate hydrolysis. In contrast, ammonia production by Proteus mirabilis neutralizes acidity and alleviates this protein precipitation bottleneck. In vivo inoculation combined with metagenomic analysis confirmed that colonization by Proteus mirabilis reshaped the gut microbial community structure, reduced Klebsiella abundance, and enhanced the activity of metabolic pathways associated with protein degradation. Thus, Proteus mirabilis suppresses Klebsiella populations through its multiple ammonia-producing functions, modulates local gut microenvironment pH, improves protein digestion capacity in BSFL fed with high-protein organic waste, and enhances organic nitrogen conversion efficiency. These findings provide theoretical support for the application of functional microorganisms to enhance insect-mediated bioconversion of organic solid waste.

title: Acetate-rich short-chain fatty acid production from waste activated sludge via in situ sulfate-mediated anaerobic fermentation
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation of waste activated sludge (WAS) is a promising route for recovering short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), but its performance is often constrained by limited substrate accessibility, unfavorable electron partitioning, and methanogenic SCFA consumption. This study investigated direct Na2SO4 supplementation as an in situ fermentation-stage strategy for enhancing acetate-rich SCFA production. At the preferred dosage of 4500 mg Na2SO4/L, peak SCFA production increased from 211.7 to 298.8 mg COD/g VSS, while acetate selectivity increased from 64% to >90%. Sulfate supplementation promoted EPS restructuring and soluble organic matter release, as indicated by EPS redistribution, a zeta-potential shift toward neutrality, and elevated SCOD and NH4+-N release. In parallel, sulfate transformation was supported by dose-dependent sulfide accumulation and supplementary sulfur-speciation evidence showing sulfate depletion, minor sulfite accumulation, and HS−-dominated dissolved sulfide under the final alkaline conditions. Gas-phase measurements further indicated a lower estimated reactor-level H2 partial pressure and suppressed CH4 production under sulfate supplementation, providing an experimentally constrained basis for interpreting sulfate-associated electron dissipation and reduced methanogenic consumption. Metagenomic and enzyme analyses revealed enrichment of sulfate-reducing populations (Desulfovibrio, Desulfomicrobium) and sulfate-reduction genes (dsrA/B, +3.2-fold; aprB, +2.08-fold), enhanced SCFA-forming functions, and reduced methanogenesis-related functional potential (mcrA gene abundance reduced to 52.2% of the control). These shifts suggest that direct sulfate addition enhances acetate-rich SCFA accumulation through coupled improvement of substrate accessibility, sulfate-associated electron partitioning, and attenuation of methanogenesis-related SCFA consumption. This work provides a fermentation-stage sulfur-regulation strategy for producing acetate-rich internal carbon sources from WAS.

title: Solvothermal carbonization of waste activated sludge using deep eutectic solvents: A solvent-directed route to tunable biochar properties
abstract: The disposal of waste activated sludge (WAS) poses a persistent environmental challenge. While hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) enables sludge valorization without pre-drying, the resulting hydrochar often exhibits low carbon content, high nitrogen levels and inferior fuel properties. This study aimed to determine whether the acidity/basicity and composition of preformed DES-based media could redirect the carbonization pathways of WAS compared with conventional aqueous HTC. Unlike previous DES-assisted HTC systems, in which low-dose DESs are added to water-dominated media, the preformed DES-based media replaced the conventional bulk aqueous medium. Acidic DES showed characteristics consistent with enhanced dehydration, decarboxylation, and condensation characteristics, producing a biochar with substantially higher carbon content (21.97% vs. 9.60% for HTC), low H/C (1.57) and O/C (0.41) atomic ratios, relatively enhanced aromatic character, reduced hydrophilicity, and higher thermal stability (dominant combustion peak at 445.1 °C). In contrast, alkaline DES was associated with enhanced hydrolysis and solubilization, yielding a carbon-depleted, highly hydrophilic residue. Neutral DES exhibits intermediate behavior, producing an oxygen-enriched surface. Overall, DES chemistry produced distinct transformation pathways and tunable biochar properties relative to conventional HTC, providing insights into solvent-mediated regulation of sludge-derived carbon materials.

title: Green conversion of wild plant biomass into agricultural biostimulants: Fermentation dynamics and microbial associations
abstract: Despite growing interest in Agricultural Jiaosu (AJ) as a sustainable biostimulant, the use of wild plant feedstocks remains underexplored, and the underlying fermentation dynamics are poorly understood. Here, we employed Humulus scandens (HS) and Portulaca oleracea (PO) to produce AJ through a 90-day natural fermentation, systematically analyzing the multi-scale dynamics of physicochemical parameters, metabolites, microbial communities, and functions. Both AJs exhibited typical fermentation features (rapid pH decline to 3.6–3.7, organic matter degradation 40.8%–68.8%, organic acids accumulation >5 g/L and mineral release with phosphorus activation >8-fold). However, from day 15 onward, the two systems diverged along distinct temporal trajectories: HS-AJ progressively enriched amino acids and salicylic acid (903.14 μg/L), while PO-AJ accumulated high levels of oxalic acid (1846.6 mg/L) and citric acid, accompanied by a sharp drop in soluble calcium. Correspondingly, microbial communities shifted from Proteobacteria to Firmicutes (shift of ∼60%) with different assembly drivers, methionine and auxin in HS-AJ versus organic acids in PO-AJ. Functional predictions and PLSR analysis further revealed that phosphorus, salicylic acid, and lactic acid were positively associated with seedling growth rate, whereas oxalic acid and electrical conductivity correlated with seedling robustness. These divergent metabolic and microbial trajectories culminated in distinct agronomic outcomes: optimal dilutions were 100-fold for HS-AJ and 400-fold for PO-AJ, enhancing seedling vigor index by 42.3% and 17.6%, respectively, achieved comparable effects to the nutrient solution. Together, this study elucidates the cascade from feedstock chemistry to microbial function and agronomic performance (feedstock-microbe-metabolite-effect), providing a quantitative basis for the rational design of plant-derived biostimulants.

title: Three-dimensional heterogeneity andpersistence of petroleum contaminants in a deep vadose zone
abstract: Petroleum contamination in deep vadose zones at legacy pipeline leaks is often hidden, develops over decades, and can create delayed groundwater risk. However, its three-dimensional (3D) architecture, environmental associations, and long-term trajectories remain poorly quantified. Here, we investigated a representative legacy refined-oil pipeline leak site where a leakage incident occurred in 2009. We collected 374 vadose-zone soil samples across depth and combined pollution indices with 3D geostatistical interpolation to delineate the spatial patterns of benzene, ethylbenzene, and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH). All three contaminants exhibited pronounced 3D heterogeneity, including a persistent enrichment zone at 60-75 m and laterally localized hotspots. Machine-learning analysis revealed pollutant-specific associations: benzene with moisture and soil properties, ethylbenzene with spatial position and soil properties, and TPH with spatial position and hydraulic and pore-structure variables. Feature importance reflects relative predictive contributions rather than causal controls, supported by the good performance of the representative models. HYDRUS simulations, initiated from the sampling date, indicated that benzene remains highly mobile, with its maximum concentration reaching 10.795 mg/kg after 10 years, exceeding the screening value (4 mg/kg). Although concentrations decline over 18-30 years, benzene continues migrating downward toward the underlying aquifer. Collectively, our findings show that the deep vadose zone functions as an active regulatory compartment characterized by long-term retention and delayed release, rather than a passive barrier. This study provides quantitative evidence to support groundwater risk assessment, depth-targeted monitoring, and long-term management of legacy petroleum-contaminated sites.

title: An integrative design framework for campus souvenirs: Fostering product attachment and sustainable use
abstract: Campus souvenirs carry emotional and cultural value, yet many fail to support sustained, meaningful use. This study developed the positive experience-driven design (PEDD) framework as an integrative approach to campus souvenir design, exploring how product attachment may be directed toward continued and meaningful use rather than passive retention. Using qualitative user research, we identified users' experiential motivations and psychological needs, translated these insights into design opportunities through structured tools, and evaluated the resulting concepts through prototype-based feedback. The findings provide preliminary qualitative evidence that the framework may support concept generation and refinement, while participatory and meaningful experiences were associated with product attachment, and participants reported intentions for continued engagement with the product. By clarifying how experience-driven design may shape product attachment toward sustainable usage, this study contributes an integrative perspective to research on product attachment and subjective well-being and provides practical guidance for campus souvenir design.

title: Predictive energy management for hybrid amphibious vehicles integrating operating condition recognition and condition-matched speed prediction
abstract: The substantial differences between land and water operating conditions, abrupt power-demand variations, and multi-objective optimization conflicts pose significant challenges to real-time energy management for hybrid amphibious vehicles. This study proposes a coordinated predictive energy management strategy integrating online operating-condition recognition and speed prediction to improve power response, fuel economy, and battery safety. A switchable hybrid powertrain operates in series mode on land and parallel mode on water. Representative operating conditions are identified offline using kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) and K-means++ clustering, and the resulting labels are used to train a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for online recognition. A dual-path condition-dependent adaptation mechanism is established: discrete condition labels select the corresponding condition-matched variational mode decomposition–radial basis function (VMD-RBF) speed predictors, while continuous distances to cluster centers adaptively adjust the power-response and fuel-economy weights of the predictive equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS). Real-vehicle tests show that the proposed strategy reduces the mean 0–100 km/h acceleration time on land by 14.9% compared with the conventional predictive strategy, avoids the engine-overload shutdown observed in six of ten rule-based tests, and reduces the mean 0–60 km/h acceleration time on water by 9.2% compared with the rule-based strategy. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for coordinated energy management across amphibious operating domains.

title: 3D spherical Fe-Mn-N co-doped porous carbon catalyst for peroxymonosulfate activation toward 2,4,6 trichlorophenol degradation: Performance and singlet-oxygen-dominated mechanism
abstract: Powdered metal-carbon catalysts for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation suffer from difficult solid-liquid separation, poor hydraulic stability, and severe metal leaching, restricting their continuous-flow wastewater treatment applications. Herein, a millimeter-scale 3D spherical Fe-Mn-N co-doped porous carbon catalyst (DCN4@FS0.3-SA) was fabricated via a low-cost, eco-friendly route using delignified balsa sawdust, steel blast furnace ferromanganese sludge (FS), melamine, and sodium alginate. Delignification pretreatment optimized the biomass pore framework, while FS supplied Fe/Mn bimetallic active species, and melamine enabled uniform nitrogen doping. The optimal catalyst possessed a well-developed hierarchical micro-mesoporous network, uniformly dispersed Fe-Mn oxide/nitride nanoparticles, high graphitization, and abundant surface defects. Under optimal conditions, the DCN4@FS0.3-SA/PMS system achieved 99.5% removal efficiency and 62.4% mineralization of 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (TCP) within 50 min with the kobs of 0.098 min−1. Batch and continuous-flow filtration tests verified its favorable hydraulic adaptability and recyclability, with thermal regeneration effectively restoring deactivated activity. Results revealed 1O2 as the dominant reactive species, accompanied by SO4•−, HO•, and O2•− via synergistic Fe-Mn redox cycling and N-doped carbon-mediated electron transfer. Three parallel TCP degradation pathways were proposed based on mass spectrometry intermediates, and toxicity evaluation confirmed that complete ring-opening mineralization drastically reduced aquatic ecological risks. This work provides a sustainable strategy for co-valorizing biomass and metallurgical solid wastes to develop separable spherical catalysts for refractory halogenated phenolic wastewater remediation.

title: Hydrogen-enhanced pulverized coal combustion under ultra-low load for deep peak regulation: A stability-constrained techno-economic assessment
abstract: The transition toward carbon neutrality is transforming coal-fired power plants from baseload suppliers into flexible resources for deep peak regulation. However, ultra-low-load operation of pulverized-coal boilers remains constrained by flame instability, degraded heat-transfer performance, and costly auxiliary stabilization. This study proposes a hydrogen-enhanced pulverized-coal combustion pathway and develops a techno-economic and environmental framework informed by combustion-stability boundaries for a 600 MWe supercritical unit. The framework integrates on-site alkaline water electrolysis using surplus zero- or negative-price renewable electricity, combustion-limit analysis, boiler heat-transfer modeling, full-chain economics, and carbon pricing. A key novel effort of the present study lies in embedding quantifiable combustion-stability boundaries into the techno-economic model, allowing hydrogen demand and minimum load to be evaluated under safety, performance, and economic constraints. Results show that hydrogen addition lowers coal ignition temperature and ignition energy, extending the calculated combustion stable boundary from 30% of full load to 5% of full load; the 5% load case represents a theoretical boundary close to, or already at, practical safety limits and subject to plant-specific constraints. Moderate hydrogen co-firing improves furnace temperature uniformity and heat flux distribution, maintaining boiler efficiency at about 85% at the condition of 10% of full load. The Performance Index (PI)-Economic Index (EI) evaluation identifies 20% – 30% load as the practical range, with the case of 20% of full load showing the best overall PI-EI performance. With an annual financial internal rate of return of 8%, the investment payback period is approximately 11 years. Assuming about 42 TWh, equivalent to 60% of estimated 2024 curtailed wind and solar electricity in China, is fed to on-site electrolyzers, the resulting hydrogen could support about 81% of the considered coal-fired capacity at 20% load, reducing annual CO2 emissions by 8.76 MtCO2 and standard coal consumption by 3.35 Mtce.

title: Examining associations of urban green-space greenness and net primary productivity with water quality using interpretable machine learning
abstract: Urban green spaces (UGSs) are widely used to support urban water-quality improvement, and vegetation cover in many cities is becoming greener. Existing the UGS-water-quality studies have mainly focused on landscape composition and configuration, whereas the associations of the UGS greenness and net primary productivity (NPP) with water quality remain insufficiently evaluated. We analysed monitoring records of chemical oxygen demand (COD), total phosphorus (TP), ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N), and dissolved oxygen (DO) at 44 sites in the Xi'an City during wet and dry seasons and combined these observations with multi-source remote-sensing and socioeconomic data. Redundancy analysis (RDA), Geodetector, and XGBoost-PSO-SHAP-LOWESS were integrated to compare linear, spatially stratified, and nonlinear predictive associations across spatial supports and to identify approximate turning regions. The results revealed that: (1) across the monitoring network, NH3-N concentrations ranged from 0.118 to 1.802 mg/L; higher urban concentrations were spatially consistent with potential anthropogenic inputs, while water-quality indicators differed between wet and dry seasons; (2) The XGBoost-SHAP provided feature-level nonlinear interpretation complementary to RDA and Geodetector; (3) The UGS greenness and NPP were associated with water-quality variation, but meteorological and socioeconomic variables were often equally or more influential, and the direction of association differed among indicators; and (4) The SHAP-LOWESS curves indicated approximate turning regions for selected greenness and NPP indicators rather than precise causal thresholds. These findings support season- and context-specific UGS planning while emphasizing the exploratory nature of the inferred associations.

title: Temporal feature augmentation for transient fuel consumption prediction of heavy-duty trucks: Toward sustainable road freight and cleaner operations
abstract: Transient operations substantially increase fuel consumption in heavy-duty trucks, while conventional static models fail to capture these short-term dynamics. Existing data-driven models either treat the engine-vehicle system as memoryless or rely on black-box sequence models that sacrifice interpretability. This study introduces a physics-informed, model-agnostic Temporal Feature Augmentation (TFA) framework that encodes unobserved internal states, such as turbocharger spool state, manifold filling, and thermal inertia, into compact and interpretable derivative-based proxy features computed causally from standard onboard measurements without additional hardware. TFA enriches the feature space by incorporating instantaneous temporal derivatives of measurable engine and air-path states, including the excess air coefficient λ, intake pressure, and pre-turbine pressure and temperature, which serve as compact proxies for unobserved transient dynamics. Validated on standardized CHTC-TT (1800 s) and extensive real-world cycles (5350 s) using five algorithms (RF, XGBoost, SVM, RNN, LSTM), TFA consistently enhances prediction accuracy and cross-cycle robustness: the best model achieves R2 = 0.996 and reduces RMSE by 23.4% relative to static-feature baselines. Feature-importance analysis confirms that temporal-derivative features effectively proxy load transients. The proposed framework supports eco-driving assistance, fleet fuel monitoring, and data-driven quantification of fuel-saving opportunities, contributing to low-carbon, cleaner production operations in commercial road freight.

title: Hofstede cultural dimensions and sustainable development goals disclosure: Evidence from Europe
abstract: This study examines whether national culture is associated with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) disclosure among 1650 firms in 21 EU countries over 2019–2024 (9900 firm-year observations). SDG disclosure is measured as a provider-coded indicator of disclosure breadth: the share of the 17 SDGs that Refinitiv/LSEG codes as addressed in firms' reporting, while culture is captured using Hofstede's six dimensions. Pooled OLS with year and industry fixed effects is complemented by firm- and country-clustered inference, wild-cluster-bootstrap tests and multiple robustness analyses. Indulgence shows the most consistent positive association with SDG disclosure and is the only dimension that remains significant under country-clustered inference after a Holm adjustment for testing six dimensions, although not under the wild-cluster bootstrap. Masculinity is negatively associated and uncertainty avoidance positively associated under firm- and country-clustered inference, but neither survives the wild-cluster bootstrap. Power distance, individualism and long-term orientation show weaker, specification-sensitive associations. Disclosure is also highly persistent over time. The evidence is therefore suggestive rather than robust, and is consistent with persistent cultural heterogeneity in SDG disclosure under increasingly common European reporting pressures. The findings also show the importance of matching statistical inference to the country level at which cultural variables vary and caution against treating disclosure breadth as equivalent to sustainability performance.

title: An interpretable decision-making model for identifying socio-environmental transition intervals in rural wastewater management pathway planning
abstract: In rural wastewater management, inappropriate pathway selection can lock settlements into over-engineered centralized facilities or underperforming decentralized systems, generating avoidable capital waste, inefficient resource use, and long-term operation burdens. This study develops an interpretable transition-interval identification framework to support cleaner production-oriented rural wastewater pathway planning. Using village-level data from 353 settlements in Guangdong Province, China, the framework combines class balancing, Random Forest classification, SHAP response mapping, rule extraction, administratively grouped cross-validation and spatial autocorrelation analysis to translate nonlinear model behavior into transparent screening rules between decentralized resource-recovery and centralized engineering pathways. Within Guangdong, five-fold administratively grouped cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.766 ± 0.146. Direct application of the frozen Guangdong model to 8595 Shandong villages yielded an AUC of 0.525, whereas Shandong-local redevelopment under nested administratively grouped cross-validation produced a mean fold-specific AUC of 0.585 ± 0.144 for the best-performing candidate model. Two prominent empirical transition intervals were identified: a permanent population of 1000–1600 residents, representing the principal scale-related transition interval, and an NH3-N pollution intensity of 3.1-3.2 kg·person−1·yr−1, representing the primary pollution-related refinement. Settlement compactness and topographic slope showed additional context-dependent associations with model-predicted pathway preference. Spatial autocorrelation analysis revealed pronounced geographic clustering of observed pathway choices (Moran's I = 0.885), with centralized engineering pathways clustering in high-density coastal plains and decentralized resource-recovery pathways prevailing in mountainous settlements. The resulting boundary system provides county-level planners with a data-derivable screening tool based on routinely available village indicators, helping reduce infrastructure-context mismatch and improve resource-efficient wastewater investment before detailed project-level design.

title: Reconfiguring urban mining: Orchestrating multi-actor E-waste supply chains for circular value recovery through an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling framework
abstract: The accelerating generation of e-waste in developing economies presents both an environmental challenge and an opportunity for circular value recovery through urban mining, yet fragmented coordination among heterogeneous formal and informal actors limits the realization of this potential. This study addresses the gap between causal diagnosis and dynamic simulation by proposing an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) framework for reconfiguring multi-actor e-waste supply chains toward enhanced circular value recovery. The framework was operationalized through ten expert panelists who validated fifteen coordination factors. DEMATEL identified causal structures and systemic influence, BWM established strategic priorities, and ABM translated these findings into agent-level behavioral rules and environmental conditions across six orchestration scenarios. The DEMATEL analysis revealed regulatory and institutional factors as primary causal drivers, with regulatory enforcement exerting the strongest systemic influence. The BWM analysis confirmed regulatory enforcement as the most strategically important factor. The ABM simulation demonstrated that combined orchestration achieved a 134.81% improvement in recovered material and a 100% collection rate, while economic incentives provided the best overall multi-metric performance. The constant recovery rate across all scenarios confirmed that improvements were driven by increased formal participation and collection throughput rather than technological efficiency, underscoring systemic coordination failures as the primary barrier to circular value recovery. The priority-causal matrix identified regulatory factors and formal-informal integration as priority intervention points offering both high causal influence and strategic importance. These findings are conditional on expert-elicited parameters and should be interpreted as exploratory simulation evidence rather than externally validated prediction. This study provides a methodological foundation for bridging causal diagnosis, strategic prioritization, and dynamic simulation in circular supply chain research, offering practical guidance for policymakers and practitioners seeking to unlock the value of the urban mine in developing economy contexts.

title: Extended oxygenation control of endogenous contaminants induced by load fluctuations in bio-trickling filters treating decentralized sewage
abstract: Load fluctuations are a primary factor disrupting biofilm integrity and microbial growth in bio-trickling filters treating decentralized rural sewage. This disruption can trigger the migration of loosely attached biomass into the treated effluent, thereby impairing treatment performance. To overcome this limitation, this study explored the formation of endogenous contaminants induced by load fluctuations and proposed an extended oxygenation (EO) strategy to regulate microbial biomass transformation. The incorporation of an EO layer enabled stable removal efficiencies of 92.7% for organic matter and 82.1% for total nitrogen (TN), with the EO layer contributing 13.2% to TN removal. In the EO layer, the biofilm extracellular polymeric substances contained a higher abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups, enabling them to intercept endogenous biomass migrating with the water flow. By utilizing the intercepted biomass, denitrifying bacteria, represented by Dechloromonas and Zoogloea, were enriched within the EO layer. Metagenomic analysis revealed that the abundance of functional genes related to reactive oxygen species synthesis and quorum sensing in microorganisms within the EO layer increased significantly. These genes regulated substance transport as well as polysaccharide and lipid metabolism, thereby compensating for the suppression of metabolic activity during substrate deprivation. The EO strategy enables microorganisms to intercept and transform endogenous contaminants into energy and material sources, thereby, ensuring their survival and pollutant removal functions under substrate deprivation and oxidative stress. This study provides valuable insights into enhancing the efficiency and stability of biofilter processes under load fluctuations.

title: Utilization of carbonyl-modified carbon nanotubes for selective removal of perfluorinated sulfonates from surface water
abstract: The simultaneous treatment addressing large-scale, low-concentration PFAS in natural waters is still a challenge due to the persistence of perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) compared to perfluorocarboxylic acid (PFCA). This study presents a breakthrough treatment for PFAS wastewater based on carbonyl multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) for selective PFSA capture. The developed MWCNTs near-completely removed perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and its substitute 6:2 chlorinated polyfluorinated ether sulfonate (F53-B) from 50 mL of surface water within 5 min from six mixed PFAS solutions with different chain lengths and functional groups, with maximum adsorption capacities of 407.3 mg g−1 and 611.9 mg g−1, respectively. The material characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that this outstanding performance arises from three synergistic mechanisms: a specific interaction between carbonyl groups and C-F bonds, enhanced electrostatic attraction, and π-π stacking interactions. These interactions enable preferential PFSA even in complex matrices containing humic acid and competing anions. The material maintains excellent stability, with complete F53-B removal sustained over five of adsorption cycles. Notably, the F53-B eluted from MWCNTs was near-completely defluorinated in UV254/sulfite system, effectively mitigating secondary pollution risks. This study provides a new approach to address the key challenges of PFSA and PFCA pollution in natural water, providing reference for the rapid separation of PFSA and the subsequent harmless treatment of residual PFCA, which protect water ecology and water resources security.

title: Continuous score-based optimization of pressure sensor placement for burst detection in water distribution networks
abstract: Pipe bursts in water distribution networks (WDNs) can cause substantial water loss and service disruption, making reliable pressure monitoring essential. However, existing event-driven methods for optimal pressure sensor placement (OSP) commonly rely on a single predefined detection threshold to distinguish burst-induced pressure residuals from background noise. This can lead to unstable optimization outcomes, multiple equivalent layouts, and degraded performance under varying noise conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a continuous score-based placement optimization (CSPO) method. Compared with commonly used threshold-based binary placement optimization (TBPO), CSPO uses a sigmoid function to map pressure residuals to continuous scores and optimizes the continuous detection score (CDS). This preserves hydraulic response magnitudes and provides a more discriminative objective for sensor placement. Results from the Hanoi and C-Town networks show that CSPO produces more stable and consistent layouts than TBPO while requiring fewer simulated burst events. It also reduces solution multiplicity and yields a single Pareto-optimal layout for each sensor count, providing a clearer basis for deployment decisions. Under cross-evaluation across multiple background noise conditions, CSPO maintains robust performance, with the mean relative performance index generally above 0.98 and the coefficient of variation below 0.02. Further results from L-Town, with pressure data and an expert-guided reference layout, show that CSPO provides a more balanced layout than the TBPO variants across threshold-based detection standards. Overall, CSPO provides a robust and practical method for pressure sensor placement, supporting the design of reliable and effective monitoring systems in WDNs.

title: Synergistic Pt single atoms and nanoparticles boost atomic-hydrogen spillover at Cu2O interface for highly selective nitrate-to-ammonia electroreduction
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3RR) to ammonia (NH3) holds promise for wastewater remediation and sustainable NH3 production. However, its efficiency is often curtailed by competing hydrogen evolution (HER) and insufficient active hydrogen (*H) supply on Cu-based catalysts. We designed an electrocatalyst (PtCSA/Cu2O/NF) that features coexisting clustered platinum nanoparticles (PtC) and platinum single atoms (PtSA) anchored on Cu2O/NF to overcome these limitations via a synergistic hydrogen-spillover network. Under the potential of −0.39 V vs. RHE, this catalyst achieves complete nitrate (NO3−) removal (100%) and high ammonia (NH4+) selectivity (98.7%). In-situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support a plausible three-stage PtC/PtSA-assisted hydrogen spillover mechanism: PtC facilitates H2O dissociation to generate *H; coexisting PtSA may regulate *H adsorption and lower the barrier for hydrogen transfer; and Cu sites consume *H to promote NO3− reduction, accelerate the Cu(I)/Cu(0) redox cycle, and suppress hydrogen evolution. Furthermore, a 100% nitrogen recovery as ammonium sulfate has been achieved from nitrate-contaminated water in an integrated flow-through device. This work establishes an energy-efficient strategy for simultaneous nitrate remediation, resource recovery as green ammonia, and restoration of the disrupted anthropogenic nitrogen cycle in wastewater treatment.

title: Sustainable electro-osmotic dewatering and stabilization of Cu- or Zn-contaminated dredged sludge with sodium alginate and calcium chloride
abstract: High-water-content dredged sludge contaminated with heavy metals is difficult to reuse because dewatering, mechanical upgrading and contaminant control must be considered together. This study evaluated sodium alginate (SA)- and SA/CaCl2-assisted electro-osmosis as a laboratory-scale process for the dewatering, strengthening and stabilization of Cu- or Zn-contaminated sludge. Eight treatment conditions, each represented by one electro-osmotic model test, were evaluated through electrical response, drainage, water content, bearing capacity, leaching behavior and microstructure. Because the C and Z series differed simultaneously in contaminant species, initial concentration and potential gradient, additive effects were interpreted primarily from comparisons within each series. In Z2 (1.0% SA), the five-zone mean water content decreased from 45.00% to 22.47% after 36 h, i.e., by 22.53 percentage points (50.07% relative reduction), and the mean bearing capacity was 11.5 times that of Z0; its quasi-steady energy coefficient was 0.169 W h/mL. CaCl2 increased early current but did not produce a proportional increase in drainage, particularly in Z3. SEM showed particle aggregation and surface deposits, but their bonding states and phase compositions were not identified. Leaching tests indicated that metal retention was conditional and pH-sensitive. Overall, SA-assisted electro-osmosis showed potential for simultaneously improving dewatering and mechanical performance of heavy-metal-contaminated dredged sludge, while the effects of CaCl2 depended on the treatment condition. The results also suggest that additive dosage and delivery strategy should be further optimized with consideration of energy consumption, metal retention and collected-water management.

title: Upcycling agricultural biomass waste into sustainable carbon dots with dual-color emission for optical security applications
abstract: Upcycling agricultural biomass waste into value-added functional materials represents a promising pathway toward sustainable development. Herein, carbon quantum dots (CQDs) were fabricated from xylan that a major hemicellulose component of agricultural residues with via hydrothermal carbonization, followed by surface functional modification with histidine and tea polyphenols. The obtained X-CQDs, NX-CQDs, NX/His-CQDs, and NX/TP-CQDs exhibited well-dispersed nanoscale morphologies with average sizes of 6.44-10.13 nm. Structural analyses confirmed disordered carbon domains with abundant oxygen- and nitrogen-containing surface groups. Photoluminescence was strongly temperature-dependent, and 180 °C was identified as the optimal hydrothermal temperature for achieving enhanced fluorescence emission. Compared with native xylan-derived CQDs, those derived from Nano-xylan showed enhanced UV-vis absorption, stronger fluorescence, and prolonged lifetime, indicating that precursor nanostructuring promoted more stable emissive centers. Fluorescence quantum yields reached 3.92%, 8.35%, 11.76%, and 9.18% for X-CQDs, NX-CQDs, NX/His-CQDs, and NX/TP-CQDs, respectively. Histidine modification enhanced blue emission, while tea polyphenol-assisted surface regulation induced red-shifted green emission. The CQD-based waterborne inks enabled invisible QR-code printing, handwriting encryption, and multi-substrate anti-counterfeiting under UV irradiation, offering a sustainable strategy for converting agricultural biomass into fluorescent security materials.

title: Estimating the economic and environmental impacts of critical infrastructure failure in the global natural gas industry: A case study of Nord Stream pipeline
abstract: Geopolitical tension is becoming an increasingly significant risk that threatens the safe operation of critical energy infrastructure. However, existing studies pay little attention to how infrastructure failures spill over into global gas supply chains, causing economic, environmental, and distributional effects. Drawing on granular infrastructure data, this study builds a large-scale linear optimization model to quantify the economic and environmental implications of the Nord Stream pipeline failure. First, we simulate how the global natural gas supply chain reconfigured across production, liquefaction, trade, regasification, and consumption. Then, we estimate the economic spillovers and life-cycle climate impacts resulting from this reconfiguration and its components. Finally, we compare the estimated economic impact of Nord Stream pipeline failure with other key infrastructure disruptions. Our major findings are: (1) By reshaping the supply chain, the Nord Stream failure increases the theoretical lowest global costs by 2.80 billion dollars, primarily through production misallocations. Europe bears only 20.7%, highlighting massive spillovers. (2) The Nord Stream failure results in winners and losers, with Norway benefiting most economically. (3) Economic impacts vary drastically across key infrastructures, ranging from $0.02 billion (Pyeongtaek regasification) to $25.8 billion (Groningen field). (4) Environmentally, the disruption reduces the global carbon footprint by 28.31 million tons CO2 eq, because the shift to more expensive but cleaner gas.

title: A sector-national-global cross-scale assessment for China's building carbon gap and its cascading effects on global decarbonization
abstract: China's first National Natural Disaster Risk Census discloses a total building stock of 128 billion square meters, providing a nationwide benchmark for building-stock assessment. This study developed a cross-scale analytical framework to assess the implications of this stock benchmark update for China's building sector, national carbon neutrality, and global decarbonization. The framework follows a three-stage logic—demand reconfiguration, carbon budget gap identification, and impact quantification—and is operationalized through the Building Carbon Demands Integration Model (BCDIM), which couples building stock turnover, LCA-based emission accounting, and socio-technical transition pathways to quantify embodied and operational carbon demands for urban/rural residential and public buildings. Under equity-based allocation of global 2°C/1.5°C carbon budgets, the post-disclosure carbon-budget gaps are 2.47 times (2°C) and 1.50 times (1.5°C) the pre-disclosure estimates, reflecting the combined influence of stock revision and broader building coverage. Closing the gap now requires faster decarbonization and annual mitigation efforts 3.88 times (2°C) and 1.76 times (1.5°C) the pre-disclosure estimates. The study also reveals that the additional national and global mitigation requirements estimated after disclosure are greater in the earlier period. These findings redefine China's building sector as a linchpin in both national and global mitigation, and demonstrate that empirically grounded stock data are essential for aligning sectoral decarbonization pathways with global temperature targets.

title: Exploring the potential and limits of non-profit-maximising business models in transformative change: Insights from Italian fashion small and medium enterprises
abstract: Transformative change in production and consumption systems is required to address intertwined socio-ecological crises. While businesses are key actors in this process, the relationship between organisational transformation and broader change remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how non-profit-maximising business models seek to contribute to transformative change and the constraints they face by analysing three Italian small and medium fashion enterprises. Drawing on sufficiency- and degrowth-oriented scholarship, we develop an extended business model canvas that conceptualises business models as potential boundary-spanning interfaces and uses selected business model dimensions to trace connections between organisational practices, value chain interactions, and broader structural conditions. Our findings show that firms implement a range of sustainability-oriented organisational changes, including durable and circular product strategies, reduced production volumes, territorially embedded supply chains, and initiatives promoting sufficient consumption and fair labour practices. These changes are accompanied by relational dynamics with consumers, suppliers, and networks, through which firms seek to influence production and consumption patterns and cultural norms beyond their organisational boundaries. However, these contributions remain partial and contingent. Bottom-up, market-based strategies face structural limitations, including constrained market power, rebound effects, and limited engagement with policy and collective actors. As a result, whether firm-level transformations contribute to broader socio-economic outcomes remains uncertain. Business-led initiatives may play a role in transformative change but are unlikely to be sufficient in isolation. We suggest that broader policy interventions and collective action to phase out unsustainable practices and define market limits are critical to address the structural drivers of socio-ecological unsustainability.

title: Cryogenic boil-off sustainable inventory system for liquid hydrogen under insulation investment and uncertainty
abstract: Liquid hydrogen (LH2) is a central energy carrier for hard to abate sectors, but its cryogenic supply chain suffers an unavoidable evaporative loss known as boil-off (BOG) that existing operations research and hydrogen engineering literatures both treat as an exogenous efficiency loss rather than an economic decision. This paper closes that gap by reconceptualizing boil-off as endogenous, investment dependent deterioration within a sustainable economic order quantity framework whose total cost per unit time objective couples a convexly insulation-reducible boil-off rate, carbon taxed liquefaction and reliquefaction emissions, and freshness sensitive demand. Joint convexity in cycle length and insulation investment is established, first-order optimality conditions are derived, and the calibrated boil-off function is validated against published LH2 storage benchmarks spanning the industry regime of 0.1–0.5% per day. Three extensions strengthen the analysis, which are a stochastic model with random demand and heat ingress that endogenizes safety stock, a differential evolution metaheuristic, validated across 30 seeds, that confirms global optimality, and a Sobol variance-based sensitivity analysis. For a calibrated mid-sized depot, jointly optimising insulation cuts total cost by ∼1.1%, nearly halves annual boil-off losses (49%), and lowers emissions. Under uncertainty the depot rationally shortens cycles and carries a safety buffer at a value of the stochastic solution of ∼31% of expected cost, while demand scale and unit liquefaction cost jointly explain ∼97% of cost variance. The framework transfers deteriorating-inventory theory to the green hydrogen economy, giving managers a defensible basis for coordinating cryogenic storage, replenishment, and decarbonization decisions.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and production–emission decoupling of the carbon footprints of China's staple crops
abstract: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions during staple-crop production while ensuring food supply requires effective production–emission decoupling and mitigation strategies. We quantified the selected cradle-to-farm gate carbon footprints of rice, wheat, and maize in China from 2006 to 2021 using a source-specific GHG inventory. We further evaluated production–emission decoupling and probabilistically ranked competing mitigation pathways using Tapio decoupling, Monte Carlo, and sensitivity analyses. Grain production and GHG emissions increased by 43.89% and 15.84%, respectively, indicating weak decoupling (Tapio elasticity = 0.36). Production increased by 10.53% while emissions reduced by 0.45% during 2015–2021, indicating strong absolute decoupling. Yield-scaled carbon footprints decreased for all three crops, although the area-scaled carbon footprint of wheat increased by 16.09%. For rice, methane (CH4) emissions were predominant during the cultivation stage, whereas nitrogen-based emissions dominated wheat and maize. Under the baseline M0 specification, fertilizer-production decarbonization had the highest dominance probability for wheat (60.84%) and maize (60.58%), whereas cultivation-stage CH4 mitigation ranked highest for rice (78.55%). These rankings were stable across alternative Monte Carlo distributions, dependence structures, and year-specific source shares; however, under the upper nitrous oxide emission-factor inventory, nitrogen-use efficiency improvement became the highest-ranked pathway for wheat and maize. Thus, crop-specific mitigation rankings were robust to alternative Monte Carlo specifications but remained sensitive to influential inventory assumptions, particularly for wheat and maize.

title: Aspects of sustainable plant and project management in the Polish tanning industry
abstract: The article aims to characterize the Polish tanning industry in terms of the integration of sustainable development and Sustainable Development Goals into plant management and project management. Information obtained from 20 Polish tanneries that participated in the survey research was analyzed. The majority of them (n = 17, i.e. 85%) declared that they take into account the principles of sustainable development in their plant management and operations, while just under half of the companies (n = 8, i.e. 40%) declare that their strategic goals are consistent with at least one and up to 16 SDGs. Five of the 20 plants (25%) also declared project-based activities, usually involving the implementation of production and technology projects. Among the five plants implementing projects, four declared that they take SDGs into account in project planning. In addition, the same four tanneries declared that they follow the principle of the sustainable development triad during project implementation, that their projects are designed to achieve sustainable results, and that sustainable and lasting outcomes are pursued at project closure. The study provides exploratory evidence on the incorporation of sustainable development principles into plant and project management in Polish tanneries and may offer useful insights for companies with a similar business profile.

title: Village and farm ponds differ in contaminant retention and mobility: Implications for sustainable management of rural agricultural landscapes
abstract: Pond systems are small but functionally important components of rural agricultural landscapes, where they intercept wastewater and runoff, and influence local environmental quality. However, village ponds (VPs) and farm ponds (FPs) may differ substantially in their contaminant inputs, retention behavior, and management needs. To address this gap, we conducted a cross-regional survey spanning 15 provinces and one municipality in China, focusing on the densely populated region southeast of the Hu Huanyong Line, which contains more than 93% of China's population. Paired water and sediment samples were analyzed to quantify representative emerging contaminants (ECs) at the molecular level.
