This paper investigates the joint planning of type-specific container capacities at a depot and the dynamic allocation of available containers to incoming leasing requests. For a fixed capacity vector, the operational problem is formulated as an infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision process (MDP), and several properties are established to characterize state-dependent acceptance, rejection, and substitution thresholds. A Bayesian optimization and dynamic programming (BO+DP) approach is then developed to determine the capacity vector, supported by queueing-based screening and coarse-to-fine value iteration. Numerical experiments show that the optimal thresholds vary with container availability, customer segment, and directional substitution factors. The screening rule removes about 93.5% of candidate capacity combinations and reduces average computation time from 393.8 s to 47.7 s. The capacity-planning results show that faster container returns can reduce the required capacity even when leasing demand is higher. Under fixed capacities, two-way asymmetric substitution increases expected discounted profit by 7.38% on average relative to one-way substitution and by 9.12% relative to no substitution. Across eight scenarios, BO+DP improves the MDP-based expected discounted profit by 41.78% on average relative to the two-stage stochastic programming benchmark. The results indicate that capacity size should account for both leasing demand and container return rates, while the capacity mix and allocation rules should reflect directional substitution revenues and the effective rejection penalties used to represent implicit service commitments.

title: Integrated metro train timetable and rolling stock rescheduling with passenger rerouting under multi-location disturbances
abstract: The expanding scale of infrastructure and rising passenger demand in metro systems increase the frequency of stochastic disturbances, significantly impacting metro train operations. This is particularly evident in multi-location disturbances (MLD), often occurring during extreme weather events, equipment failures, and unexpected passenger demand. Compared to the single-location disturbance scenario, the decision-making process for train rescheduling in the MLD scenario is inherently more complex, posing challenges in mitigating passenger congestion at stations and ensuring the feasibility of rolling stock circulation, including rolling stock turn-back and deadheading operations. To enhance the quality of rescheduling decisions under the MLD scenario within limited computational times, this study investigates a range of comprehensive rescheduling strategies, including holding, retiming, train cancellation, short-turning, skip-stopping, and rolling stock reassignment. Recognizing the necessity for passenger rerouting due to the application of short-turning and skip-stopping strategies, we develop a mixed integer linear programming model for metro train timetable and rolling stock rescheduling, aiming to minimize the weighted sum of four objectives: deviations with the planned train timetable, the number of backup rolling stocks used, additional average passenger travel times, and passenger gathering risks. We introduce various auxiliary variables to capture the coupling relationship between the application of rescheduling strategies while employing a discretization mechanism to facilitate the linearization of passenger rerouting constraints. To effectively address the problem and improve the quality of the train rescheduling solution, we develop a novel hybrid simulation-optimization (HSO) algorithm based on the rescheduling strategies mentioned above. Finally, real-life case studies from Chongqing Rail Transit Line 5 demonstrate that the proposed algorithm delivers superior rescheduling solutions efficiently, with an average improvement in the objective value of 47.59% over the two-stage method, 20.83% over a standard local search algorithm, and 9.57% over the HSO algorithm without implementing the tabu search mechanism.

title: An online approach for integrated railway schedule replanning and passenger reassignment with unknown passenger reactions under hub disruptions
abstract: Major railway disruptions, such as city-wide disasters, in hub areas often persist for a long time and affect multiple routes simultaneously. Original railway schedules, including line plans, timetables, and rolling stock dispatching, become invalid and require strategic replanning to maintain serviceability. Under such conditions, original trains may be delayed or canceled, resulting in passengers stranded in overcrowded stations or abandoning trips and leaving independently. An effective replanned railway schedule should minimize not only passengers’ delay but also the number of passengers abandoning their trips and the risk of overcrowding during the disruption period. However, passengers’ independent reactions make the effective passenger demand that practically complies with the replanned railway schedule unknown beforehand. Therefore, this paper proposes an online approach that dynamically and integrally optimizes railway schedule replanning and passenger reassignment by referring to the real-time passenger demand remaining at stations. This study designs a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning framework that operates without requiring deterministic forecasts of future passenger demand. A real-world disaster case in Chinese railway network demonstrates the advantage of our approach in offline computational efficiency by benchmarking against single-level deep reinforcement learning, polynomial surrogate models, rule-based strategies and rolling horizon approaches. The online application is validated across diverse disruption scenarios. This result shows that our approaches have strong potential to mirror the dispatcher’s role for real-time disruption management.

title: Statistical modeling of metro passenger flow dynamics under large-scale events
abstract: Accurate probabilistic forecasting of metro passenger flow under large-scale events is fundamental for proactive urban transit management. However, this task is challenging due to the small sample size of historical data and the complex event-driven travel behaviors. Most current approaches are deterministic and thus unable to quantify forecast uncertainty. Moreover, existing probabilistic models generally fail to capture the underlying causal relationship between pre-event arrivals and post-event departures, limiting their ability to model the generative process of metro flow dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Bayesian model designed to forecast event-induced passenger flows one week in advance. Our framework decomposes passenger flow into routine baselines and event-induced deviations, and models the deviations using a Gamma mixture distribution. Crucially, we formalize an arrival-driven departure causal relationship, where post-event boarding flows are explicitly conditioned on pre-event alighting flows and external event attributes (e.g., ticket sales and schedules). By leveraging a hierarchical prior architecture, the model effectively pools information across diverse event instances to ensure robust parameter estimation. Empirical experiments on the Beijing metro system demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian model achieves accurate forecasting. In addition, the model offers superior interpretability and robust uncertainty quantification, providing transit agencies with insightful information for transit operation optimization and crowd management.

title: Equilibrium analysis of certification programmes for energy-saving products: Specification-based vs. contribution-based
abstract: External certifications are credible signals of product qualities, enhancing consumers’ valuation of energy-saving products. We study two certification programmes: specification-based certification, which requires products to meet a threshold energy efficiency level, and contribution-based certification, which requires firms to share a portion of profit with stakeholders. We demonstrate the theoretical equivalence of contribution-based certification to a price regulation scheme, where the price cap decreases with energy consumption. This finding provides a clear prospect for implementation using existing regulatory tools. Both programmes reduce energy use as requirements become stricter. We identify a key trade-off that represents the significance of our research: under equal firm profit, specification-based certification leads to lower energy consumption, while contribution-based certification yields greater sales, higher consumer surplus, and improved social welfare. We further examine three extensions: (1) switching the contribution baseline from profit to revenue lowers firm profit, (2) specification-based certification can mitigate rebound effects whereas contribution-based certification may not, and (3) both improve system-wide energy efficiency, though the efficiency is not monotonic in certification stringency.

title: Improving lithium extraction from claystone: Maximizing efficiency and sustainability with integrated beneficiation and sulfuric acid leaching
abstract: Sedimentary claystones in Nevada are a new type of resource for lithium. However, the large presence of carbonate gangue minerals impose a significant processing challenge because these carbonates not only increase sulfuric acid consumption during leaching but also lead to the generation of carbon dioxide. Therefore, understanding the potential of carbonate removal and its subsequent impact on downstream leaching constitutes a significant knowledge gap meriting further investigations. In this study, a smectite claystone was beneficiated using an enhanced gravity separation technique to remove its carbonate content, and subsequently leached using sulfuric acid. Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to study the effects of acid concentration, leaching temperature and time, and solid-liquid ratio on the lithium extraction from the beneficiated claystone. The results showed that the optimum beneficiation was able to reject most of the calcite, with 86 % of calcium removed while recovering 91 % of the lithium. Leaching of the beneficiated claystone yielded a high lithium recovery of 89.18 % at conditions of 1.31 M acid concentration, temperature of 80 °C, time of 1.93 h, and 26 % solid-liquid. Furthermore, incorporating the beneficiation stage reduces the acid consumption from 106 g/g lithium to 23 g/g lithium, and the emission of carbon dioxide from 4.26E-01 kg CO2eq/g lithium to 1.51E-01 kg CO2eq/g lithium. The findings show the significance of prior beneficiation in enhancing leaching efficiency and mitigating environmental impacts, thereby providing understandings to address the previously identified knowledge gap.

title: Multi-objective optimization of crop distribution in arid agriculture: From water-carbon-food nexus perspective
abstract: Crop planting is high consumer of water and energy resources and a major contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions (GHG). Expanding demand for food increases dependence on these resources, which in turn leads to water scarcity and increased GHG emissions. To address these challenges, optimization models were developed based on resource nexus. This study incorporates water and carbon footprints into an optimization framework for agricultural planting structures in arid regions, integrating Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) with Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), aiming to achieve optimal water conservation, greenhouse gas emission reduction, and improved grain production. The findings reveal that variations in agricultural inputs and management practices result in a higher carbon footprint per unit of production for cotton than for maize and wheat by 38.8 % and 56.4 %, respectively. The agricultural water footprint in arid regions is predominantly composed of blue water, with spatial heterogeneity driven by regional climatic differences. Carbon emission intensity, agricultural economic development levels, and water resource utilization efficiency were identified as the major drivers of the increase in water and carbon footprints in Xinjiang over the past 20 years. By reallocating sown areas of major crops to establish an optimal planting configuration, reducing arid agricultural carbon emissions by 11.4 % and curbing blue water usage by 12.6 %. The results provide a scientific basis and feasible solutions for achieving efficient resource use and environmental protection in arid farming systems while ensuring food security.

title: Vehicular VOC speciation dynamics under China's progressive emission standards: Mechanistic drivers from real-time monitoring
abstract: Vehicle emissions are a key source of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in Chinese cities, requiring urgent cuts to combat ozone and secondary organic aerosol pollution. VOC emissions from vehicle exhaust are influenced by multiple factors, with driving conditions being one of the most critical one. In this study, two online instruments—a proton transfer reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry (PTR-ToF-MS) and an ion-molecular reaction mass spectrometry (IMR-MS)—were employed in parallel to monitor second-scale VOC components emissions from vehicles with varying emission standards and fuel types under different driving conditions. Results revealed a 98.3 % reduction in total VOC emissions of gasoline vehicles (GVs) from China I to VI standards, compared to 87.8 % for diesel vehicles (DVs) from China III to V standards. GVs across emission standards concentrated high emission-rate zones under high-acceleration conditions (>0.5 m/s2), while DVs primarily triggered emission peaks at higher speeds (>7 m/s). Vehicle specific power, a comprehensive indicator reflecting engine load, revealed distinct compositional differences with higher proportions of alkanes and aromatics from GVs and greater fractions of alkenes and oxygenated VOCs from DVs. This indicates that the dynamic emission profiles are influenced by fuel type and the interplay between engine load conditions and combustion completeness across driving conditions. The results in this study elucidate the underlying mechanistic drivers of VOC component emissions under different driving conditions and shed light on directions for further mitigation of VOC emissions from vehicle exhaust.

title: Cleaner production of net-negative emissions via integrated Biogas–LNG multigeneration system: 5E analysis, LCA, and artificial intelligence-driven optimization
abstract: The study introduces a novel multigeneration system powered by sorghum-fermented biogas and enhanced with LNG cold recovery, a gas turbine, an organic Rankine cycle (ORC), and a thermally integrated carbon capture unit. The system is designed to simultaneously generate electricity, heating, cooling, and captured CO2 while achieving net-negative emissions. Integrated multigeneration systems are crucial for meeting global energy demands and environmental concerns, but conventional configurations frequently suffer from limited fuel flexibility, high CO2 emissions, and inefficient energy integration. In order to assess system performance, a thorough 5E (energy, exergy, economic, environmental, and emergy) analyses and a life cycle assessment (LCA) were conducted. Parametric studies revealed the effects of turbine inlet temperature, ORC pressure, LNG pressure, and LNG rate. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural network precisely predicted important metrics (R2 = 0.999), and multi-objective optimization (SPEA-II) was used to balance cost, efficiency, and sustainability. In order to achieve −386 kg/h net CO2 emissions, the system produced 5240 kW of net power, 52.19 % energy efficiency, 40.59 % exergy efficiency, and 65.81 % CO2 removal. Economic analysis showed a net present value of 14.19 M$, levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.29 $/kWh, and payback period of 5.91 years. A total product unit cost of 23.11 $/GJ, exergy efficiency of 43.8 %, and LCOE as low as 0.228 $/kWh were obtained from optimization scenarios. For carbon reduction and sustainable energy production, this system provides a scalable solution.

title: Photocatalytic fuel cell based on highly conductive pathways for norfloxacin removal in mariculture wastewater and simultaneous electricity generation
abstract: Antibiotic contamination in mariculture wastewater urgently requires effective remediation. Seawater's natural conductivity facilitates photocatalytic fuel cell (PFC) deployment for meeting this challenge. In this study, the ZnSe/ZnO/Ti core-shell nanorod array photoanode was successfully prepared, which was assembled with carbon cloth (CC) cathode to build the PFC system for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation and simultaneous electricity generation in mariculture wastewater. Experimental results demonstrated that the introduction of the ZnSe shell effectively enhanced the light harvesting capability and formed interfacial electric field at the heterojunction interface, promoting charge transfer performance. The ohmic resistance was the limiting factor for PFC performance enhancement. The Ti plate effectively reduced ohmic resistance, enhanced ion migration rates, and maximized the efficiency of interfacial reactions. The heterojunction, nanorod array, and Ti current collector formed high-conductivity pathways for the rapid directional transport of both charge carriers and electrolyte ions, reducing the resistance of the PFC and significantly enhancing its performance. The PFC system exhibited superior degradation performance with 94.42 % removal of NOR in 120 min. The simultaneous electric energy output of ZnSe/ZnO/Ti-15 was 2.46 mW/cm2, which was 2.48 and 2.2 times higher than those of the ZnO/Ti and ZnSe/ZnO/FTO systems, respectively. Moreover, the abundant Cl− in mariculture wastewater acted as supporting electrolyte while also generating Cl•, ClO• radicals, thereby further facilitating degradation. This study provided new insights for the performance improvement of PFC and the resource utilization treatment of marine aquaculture wastewater.

title: Development of green low-carbon denitrogenation process for EAF- reaction behavior and industrial performance of Ar-CH4 injection via hollow electrode
abstract: Reducing nitrogen content in electric arc furnace molten steel is crucial for enhancing product quality and advancing green manufacturing. This study proposed a low-carbon denitrogenation method, in which hydrogen plasma was generated by injecting an Ar-CH4 mixed gas through a hollow electrode to promote nitrogen removal via the 3H + [N] = NH3 reaction. Thermodynamic calculations using Factsage 8.1 software confirmed the reaction's feasibility at standard steelmaking temperatures. Systematic laboratory experiments demonstrated over 90 % nitrogen removal from molten steel, with efficiency increasing as the CH4 proportion increased. At a 60 % CH4 ratio, nitrogen content was successfully decreased from 180.19 ppm to 28.39 ppm within 600 s. Real-time flue gas analysis revealed a correlated increase in NH3 concentration, thereby validating the reaction mechanism. Industrial trials in a 115 t Quantum EAF further verified the process's effectiveness: operating at a total gas flow rate of 5000 Nl/min and 60 % CH4 ratio reduced nitrogen content from 58.5 ppm to 47.8 ppm while decreasing smelting costs by 0.737 RMB/t and reducing CO2 emissions by 3.49 kg/t. This technology provides a practical and cost-effective solution for low-carbon steelmaking, supporting the development goals of “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality.”

title: Research on water-energy-carbon consumption and emission situation and nexus in iron and steel industry
abstract: The iron and steel industry's (ISI) intensive consumption of energy and water, coupled with its high emissions, exacerbates resource scarcity and environmental degradation. Consequently, exploring the water-energy-carbon nexus (WECN) is crucial for the sustainable development of the industrial sector. This study develops a framework for the WECN in the ISI, uses balance degree (BD) to assess ISI' consumption and emissions, explores the interrelationships between water-energy, energy-water, energy-carbon and water-carbon, and constructs a synergistic development index (SDI) to evaluate the sector's synergistic situation. The results indicate that the case enterprise consumed 134.9 m3 of water and 561.4 kgce of energy per ton of crude steel, while generating approximately 1.7 tCO2. The BD analysis indicates high energy consumption in ironmaking (IM) and cold-rolling (CR), excessive water use in hot-rolling (HR) and CR, high carbon emissions in coking (CO) and sintering (SI), and severe imbalance between resource consumption and emissions in steelmaking (SM). IM and SM are at a low level of synergy and have high potential for energy conservation and emission reduction. This research provides an important foundation for policy-making and achieving sustainable development in the ISI.

title: Evaluation of floating photovoltaic deployment potential and associated environmental benefits on China's lakes and reservoirs
abstract: Floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems represent a promising pathway for expanding renewable electricity generation in China without competing for limited land resources. Drawing on the China-LERL dataset, this study evaluates 3051 lakes and 2194 reservoirs larger than 0.1 km2 under 5 %–30 % surface coverage scenarios, including a 15 % cooling gain. The results indicated that lakes contribute approximately 70 % of national FPV potential, with western provinces such as Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, and Qinghai each exceeding 100,000 GWh of electricity generation, saving over 1200 hm3 of water and avoiding 734 Mt of CO2 emissions. Reservoirs, accounting for roughly 30 % of the total, provide more balanced geographic distribution and strengthen energy security in the east. A dual strategy combining lake-based deployment in arid regions with reservoir-based expansion in populated areas can enhance renewable generation, conserve water, and reduce emissions, supporting China's sustainable energy transition.

title: Resilience assessment and optimization of ecological networks under multi-scenario disturbances: A 40-year analysis in Northwest China’s agro-pastoral transition zone
abstract: Accelerating climate change and intensifying human activities are reshaping the resilience of ecological networks, especially in arid and semi-arid agro-pastoral transition zones where ecosystems remain highly disturbance-sensitive. Long-term resilience dynamics in northwestern China’s agro-pastoral ecotone (1985–2023) were analyzed by constructing ecological networks using an integrated “importance-sensitivity-connectivity” framework combined with self-organizing map neural networks and circuit theory. Five disturbance scenarios were applied to assess temporal resilience trajectories and identify effective optimization strategies. Three key findings emerged. First, resilience exhibited a distinct U-shaped evolution across three phases: initial stability (1985–2000), mid-term fluctuation (2000–2015), and restabilization (2015–2023), closely mirroring major policy transitions. Second, resilience responses were disturbance-specific, indicating differentiated adaptive capacities. Networks remained robust under random attacks but vulnerable to targeted disturbances, while resistance to overgrazing improved most substantially under long-term grazing management. Third, optimization strategies exhibited scenario-dependent thresholds with paradoxical effects: source expansion enhanced sensitivity-based resilience by 14.68% but reduced overgrazing resilience by 10.25%; corridor optimization peaked at 0.1–0.2 addition ratios before triggering negative returns. These results support a spatial–temporal-functional framework to guide disturbance-specific strategies across management zones, clarifying mechanisms shaping resilience evolution in arid ecosystems and providing a transferable basis for precision ecological engineering and resilience-oriented land management globally.

title: Dynamic suitability site selection and policy pathway for decommissioned photovoltaic recycling in China: Integrating spherical fuzzy sets and dynamic computable general equilibrium model
abstract: Driven by global energy transition and Sustainable Development Goals, photovoltaic (PV) capacity has expanded rapidly. However, this growth has simultaneously created formidable challenges in managing decommissioned PV recycling. This study constructs a latitude-longitude level spatiotemporal database of China's decommissioned PV by 2040 using a geographic information system. Thereby clarifies the spatiotemporal distribution of decommissioned PV to establish a research foundation for subsequent studies. Improved integrated multi-machine learning models predict key indicators to enhance assessment precision. Based on this, it dynamically evaluates recycling site suitability across four phases from 2028 to 2040. An integrated model supports this evaluation: Spherical Fuzzy Set (SFS) handles uncertainty; Analytic hierarchy process and Criteria importance through intercriteria correlation determine subjective and objective weights, fused via game theory combination weight method; SFS-Multi-attribute based analytic compromise quantifies suitability. A dynamic computable general equilibrium model assesses the impacts of Research and Development (R&D) subsidy policies from 2020 to 2050 for the decommissioned PV industry on energy structure, carbon emissions, and economic growth. Results reveal that decommissioned PV exhibits a west-to-east shift, with northwest regions dominated by large-scale centralized PV and east regions by distributed PV. Suitability is shaped by transportation and economy beyond decommissioned volume. The score difference between the points in the dynamic assessment and those in the static assessment is 1.4 %. R&D subsidies demonstrate diminishing marginal returns when increased beyond 20 % of baseline levels, with optimal effectiveness at moderate levels. This study contributes to advancing the sustainable production and management of decommissioned PV on a global scale.

title: Environmental impacts and benefits of vertical greenery systems in humid subtropical climate: A comprehensive life cycle perspective
abstract: In a context where the urgency for sustainability and renewable energy is undeniable, adopting vertical vegetation systems in urban buildings has emerged as a promising strategy for mitigating environmental impacts. However, despite the apparent benefits, continuous innovation is still needed to optimize these green solutions. In this drive for progress, this study investigates the efficiency of using recyclable materials in constructing green walls, analyzing the sustainability of this system through a life cycle analysis. Three rooms with similar characteristics and solar orientation were selected for analysis, differing only in the shading system: living wall (plants in recycled pots made of liquid packaging board), green façade (metal structure trellises), and control room (no vegetation). The shading potential of each system was assessed by measuring environmental variables, including indoor and outdoor air temperature, indoor and outdoor surface temperature, globe temperature, and indoor relative humidity. The results indicated that the vertical vegetation systems could effectively reduce the buildings' temperature. In summer, the living wall recorded a reduction of up to 9.2 °C and the green façade, a difference of up to 6.5 °C compared to the control room, demonstrating the effectiveness of these systems. Vertical vegetation systems, especially living walls with recycled materials, have effectively reduced energy and resources, mitigating environmental impacts in several categories. The natural shading provided by these systems has contributed significantly to energy savings and improved air quality by absorbing CO2 and other pollutants, thus promoting a more sustainable future. By examining the feasibility and performance of these recycled materials, the study contributes to developing more eco-friendly alternatives for creating vertical vegetation in urban areas. This approach benefits the urban environment and promotes more responsible and resource-conscious practices, aligning with modern cities' sustainability and resilience goals.

title: Towards cleaner production of methyl glycolate: Techno-economic-environmental optimization via hybrid physics-machine learning modeling
abstract: The transition to sustainable chemical manufacturing requires a balance among technical feasibility, economic viability, and environmental impact. This challenge is particularly evident in the dimethyl oxalate to methyl glycolate (DTMG) process, a promising route for producing a key monomer of biodegradable polymers. To address these, this study develops a hybrid physics-machine learning framework for multi-objective optimization (HyMeO) of the DTMG process. It seamlessly integrates the strengths of process simulation, automated machine learning, and natural heuristic algorithms. A high-fidelity dataset of 1058 operational scenarios is generated via rigorous process simulation. Eight machine learning models are developed and automatically optimized, with the deep neural network model demonstrating the best performance (R2 > 0.96). The Shapley additive explains and partial dependency analyses are conducted to unveil the internal prediction mechanism of this model, which reveal that the distillate-to-feed ratio of the MG refining column and the hydrogen flowrate are the most influential factors governing the trade-offs between economic and environmental objectives. The preferred model coupled with the genetic algorithm to maximize exergy efficiency while minimizing production cost and CO2 emission of the DTMG process. The optimal solution achieves an 8.82 % increase in exergy efficiency, an 8.91 % cost reduction, and a 0.31 % decrease in CO2 emissions. Therefore, the proposed HyMeO framework can effectively reconcile the trade-offs among economic, technical, and environmental objectives in the DTMG process, providing a generalizable methodology for the sustainable intensification of chemical processes.

title: Interfacial behavior and mechanistic insights into CGAs-mediated remediation of crude oil-contaminated sludge
abstract: Oily sludge, laden with hazardous constituents, poses a significant risk to both human health and ecological integrity. Colloidal Gas Aphrons (CGAs) were prepared and optimized using a binary surfactant system composed of sodium dodecyl benzene sulfonate (SDBS) and rhamnolipid (RL). Findings revealed that the RL/SDBS composite system markedly augmented the stability of CGAs. Maximal synergistic interaction emerged under an equal proportion between components, resulting in minimized surface and interfacial tension and achieving an oil removal efficiency of 95.1 %. The corresponding CGAs displayed a mean particle diameter of 66.03 μm, approximately a 50 % reduction relative to monocomponent systems. The interfacial area increased by 115 %, corresponding to an approximate 9 % improvement in oil removal efficiency. With a mean particle size, the collision likelihood between CGAs and oily sludge was quantified at 29.73 %. CGAs facilitate the effective detachment and migration of crude oil from the solid matrix of oily sludge via van der Waals interactions. The detached oil compounds tended to accumulate on the surface of CGAs. Following the adsorption of crude oil, CGAs exhibited intensified fluorescence within the liquid film, and their thickness expanded from 14.38 μm to 23.24 μm, signifying that CGAs enabled the solubilization of crude oil driven by hydrophobic interactions. This research established a practical foundation for the efficient oil removal application of CGAs in the remediation of oil-contaminated sludge, while offering theoretical insights into the interfacial behavior within complex multiphase systems.

title: GenX triggers concentration-dependent photosynthetic inhibition and defense strategy shifts in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) seedlings
abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), a widely used alternative to perfluorooctanoic acid, has been increasingly detected in agricultural soils. However, its phytotoxic mechanisms at environmentally relevant concentrations remain poorly understood. In this study, the phytotoxicity of GenX at environmentally realistic concentrations (0.1–100 ng g−1) in wheat seedlings was systematically investigated using physiological and multi-omics (proteomic and metabolomic) analyses. GenX exposure led to insufficient activation of superoxide dismutase, resulting in persistent superoxide anion accumulation and specific oxidative stress that ultimately impaired photosynthetic efficiency and osmoregulatory capacity. In response, an antioxidant defense network involving peroxidase, glutathione, and proline was activated. Multi-omics analyses revealed that GenX-induced remodeling of amino acid metabolism enhanced reactive oxygen species scavenging and nitrogen homeostasis. Molecular evidence indicated that GenX caused concentration-dependent cellular damage and stress responses. As exposure levels increased, damage to the photosynthetic system progressed from functional impairment to structural disruption: at 0.1 ng g−1, GenX primarily reduced light-harvesting efficiency by suppressing chlorophyll biosynthesis and destabilizing photosystem II, whereas higher levels caused structural damage to the photosynthetic apparatus and inhibited electron transport, thereby hindering carbon fixation. Defense mechanisms also shifted from protein translation to epigenetic regulation with increasing GenX concentration. This study provides the first comprehensive elucidation of the toxicity pathway of GenX in wheat at environmentally relevant concentrations, offering crucial mechanistic insights for ecological risk assessment and advancing understanding of the phytotoxicity of emerging substitute pollutants.

title: Engineering phytic acid-modified Zr-based 2D MOF nanoflowers for selective detection and efficient removal of uranium ions
abstract: Uranium contamination has caused a serious threat to the environment and human health due to its chemical toxicity and radiological hazards. Developing materials for sensitive detection and efficient removal of U(VI) is essential for the advancement of nuclear energy. Herein, ZrCl4 and 1,3,5-tri(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene (H3BTB)/2′-amino-5'-(4-carboxyphenyl)-[1,1':3′,1″-terphenyl]-4,4″-dicarboxylic acid (H3BTB-NH2) were used to prepare Zr-BTB (ZB) and Zr-BTB-NH2 (ZBN). Subsequently, post-synthetic modification with phytic acid (PA) was performed to obtain PA-modified ZB and ZBN, denoted Zr-BTB-PA (ZBP) and Zr-BTB-NH2-PA (ZBNP), respectively, for the selective detection and removal of U(VI). Compared with ZB and ZBN, the adsorption capacity of ZBP and ZBNP for U(VI) was significantly increased, and the theoretical maximum adsorption capacity of ZBNP for U(VI) was 254.45 mg/g. More importantly, ZBNP demonstrated outstanding adsorption selectivity for U(VI) in simulated seawater. The distribution coefficient (Kd) reached 3.65 × 104 mL/g, which is attributed to the synergistic interactions between the amino/phosphate groups in ZBNP and U(VI). Furthermore, the ZBNP exhibited a well-calibrated linear relationship between fluorescence intensity and U(VI) concentrations, and the correlation coefficient reached 0.989. Moreover, ZBNP exhibited selective fluorescence responses to U(VI) in the presence of competing metal ions. This study presents a novel dual-functional material that possesses significant potential for real-time monitoring and removal of U(VI).

title: From bamboo biomass to geopolymer binders: Valorizing SiO2 and K2O-rich residual ashes for the low-carbon construction
abstract: Global cement production is projected to exceed (4.6–5.0) × 1012 kg yr−1 by 2050, reinforcing the urgency of developing clinker-free binders to reduce the construction sector's ∼40 % share of CO2 emissions. This study presents a novel valorization pathway for Dendrocalamus asper bamboo residues, leaves, and inner/outer culm sawdusts, as dual-function sources of reactive SiO2 and K2O for alkali-activated (geopolymer) binders. After optimized calcination at 630 °C, the ashes were characterized by PSD, XRF, XRD, TG–DSC/DTA, SEM–EDS, FTIR, and solid-state NMR. Leaves ash showed a unimodal PSD (∼80 μm), high amorphous SiO2 (76.9 wt %), and strong calcium uptake, confirming its high pozzolanic reactivity. Culm ashes were bimodal (10–700 μm), crystalline-rich, and enriched in K2O (up to 40.3 wt %) and P2O5 (14.5 wt %), suggesting complementary alkaline and fluxing functions. In the fresh state, bamboo-ash-based geopolymer pastes exhibited moderate workability (flow = 215 mm, viscosity ≈ 28 cP) and cohesive behavior favorable for precast applications, while the reference mix (pyrogenic-silica activator) showed lower viscosity and higher spread (240 mm). Upon curing, the bamboo-leaves-ash geopolymer achieved 16.7 MPa compressive strength, forming aluminosilicate networks structurally comparable to those synthesized with commercial waterglass, as evidenced by 29Si/27Al MAS-NMR, the first direct spectroscopic validation of bamboo-ash-derived activators. This proof of concept demonstrates that bamboo residues can supply both reactive silica and alkalis for geopolymerization, advancing circular, region-specific strategies for low-carbon construction.

title: Forward osmosis to concentrate coconut water and impact of ultrafiltration Pre-treatment: Insights into membrane fouling
abstract: Coconut water is a widely consumed healthy beverage due to its nutritional benefits, and demand for packaged products is steadily increasing. Traditional concentration methods, particularly thermal processes, can compromise quality and are energy-intensive. Forward osmosis (FO) offers a promising nonthermal alternative with lower energy requirements and reduced transportation costs. This study investigates FO-based concentration of coconut water, focusing on fouling behavior and performance under ultrafiltration pre-treatment (UFPT) and constant osmotic pressure (COP) operation to increase the volumetric concentration factor (VCF). The results show that UFPT enhanced water flux by up to 50 % at 1 M NaCl and 25–30 % at 4 M NaCl compared to untreated feed, while the VCF increased by 50 % with UFPT. COP operation helps maintain a higher water flux for longer durations, enabling a higher VCF than the conventional FO mode. Thermal and fouling analyses identified critical VCF points where gel layer formation caused a sharp decline in flux. These findings offer new insights into optimizing FO-based juice concentration, providing a sustainable, and energy-efficient approach that enhances product quality and advances nonthermal beverage processing.

title: Cobalt encapsulated doping via framework solvation of MIL-88A for anchoring peroxymonosulfate to generate surface-bound radicals
abstract: Stable binding and activation of peroxy species in Fenton-like reactions are the central challenge. Herein, the solvation properties of MIL-88 A were exploited for surface cobalt doping, applying in peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation for sulfamethazine removal. Initially, the electrostatic attraction-driven binding of PMS activated by cobalt sites consistently generates surface-bound SO4•− and O2•−. This surface catalysis as well as the identification of reactive oxygen species was effectively determined by correlation analysis. Besides, the spectroscopic and probe experiments demonstrate synergistic interactions between cobalt and inert iron in the original node, enriching the catalytic pathway and reactive species generation. Compared with one-pot introduction, the solvation doping method makes the modified MIL-88 A surface more catalytically active and effectively reduces the cost of preparing membrane filtration reactor. In addition, competitive experimental studies monitored the effect of surface microenvironment on PMS catalysis. This work provides new insights into the activation behavior of PMS at bimetallic sites, while promoting the application of MOFs in Fenton-like systems for cost-saving and efficiency enhancement.

title: New strategies for synergistic inhibition of mild steel corrosion by dual-functionalized chitosan: Film formation and Fe2+ adsorption
abstract: Steel corrosion is a critical issue impacting the durability and sustainability of concrete structures. To address this challenge, eco-friendly chitosan derivative inhibitors, ferulic acid modified chitosan (CTS-FA) and ferulic acid and cysteine modified chitosan (CTS-FA-Cys), were designed and synthesized using a dual-functionalization strategy to enhance both spontaneous surface film formation and Fe2+ adsorption for effective corrosion inhibition. Based on experiments and theoretical calculations, their corrosion inhibition performance and mechanisms were systematically evaluated. Electrochemical measurements demonstrated that both CTS-FA and CTS-FA-Cys significantly improved the corrosion resistance of steel in simulated concrete pore solution containing 3.5 % NaCl (SCPS-NaCl, pH ≈ 12.5), especially for CTS-FA-Cys, achieving a maximum inhibition efficiency of 95.97 % at 500 mg/L. During immersion for 168–1176 h, the inhibition efficiency of CTS-FA-Cys remained at 83.63–92.35 %, demonstrating superior durability and stability compared to unmodified chitosan (91.28–92.65 % within 12–168 h). Theoretical calculations revealed that both inhibitors formed an adsorption film on the Fe (110) surface by donating electrons to the empty d-orbitals of Fe and forming covalent bonds. Adsorption experiments revealed that both inhibitors effectively adsorbed Fe2+, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 60.12 mg/g (CTS-FA-Cys), and their adsorption behaviors followed the pseudo-second-order (PSO) kinetics and Langmuir isothermal adsorption model. This study aims to provide novel strategies for prolonging the durability of reinforced concrete through innovative design and synthesis of inhibitors with a dual inhibition mechanism.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity of environmental sustainability in China: A strong sustainability assessment integrating planetary boundaries and environmental footprints
abstract: Human activities are causing escalating environmental crises, making sustainable development a paramount global challenge. This research introduces a comprehensive and integrated framework to assess the environmental sustainability of China's provinces over time and across regions. By adapting the global ‘Planetary Boundaries'(PBs) concept to create local, science-based targets, we measured each province's consumption-based footprint for four key elements: carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and water (W). Specifically, environmental footprints quantify consumption-based anthropogenic pressures, whereas the downscaled PBs thresholds define the safe biophysical limits. We then evaluated these footprints against the safe environmental limits. Our findings from 2007 to 2017 reveal that China's national carbon, phosphorus, and water footprints grew, while the nitrogen footprint showed a decline. Spatially, we found stark regional disparities, with northern provinces bearing much heavier environmental loads. The assessment shows that most provinces have breached the safe limits for C, N, and P, creating a distinct “high-north, low-south” pressure pattern. The risk of water unsustainability was particularly acute in northwestern provinces. Crucially, no province managed to stay within the safe thresholds for all four elements simultaneously. To address these challenges, we classified provinces into high-, medium-, and low-risk zones and formulated tailored policy recommendations. This study provides vital data-driven support for China's sustainability goals and offers a scalable analytical framework for other nations facing similar regional environmental challenges.

title: Systematic inter-plant carbon integration through emission-optimal design of robust carbon dioxide reuse networks
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) reuse networks can play a crucial role in reducing CO2 emission by connecting CO2 supplies with demands. In this paper, an optimization-based approach to the synthesis of emission-optimal CO2 networks is proposed. The novelty lies in accounting for process uncertainties through a robust optimization approach such that the network is guaranteed to remain feasible under concentration and flow disturbances. This is achieved by considering a flexible (or robust) design framework in a superstructure optimization algorithm. The optimization objective is fresh CO2 minimization subject to supply concentration uncertainties and constraints such as CO2 purity thresholds and a desired emission reduction for the supplies, according for environmental regulations. Also, a two-tier optimization framework is proposed to minimize unused CO2 emission to the atmosphere along with the fresh CO2 minimization. This allows for detecting multiple design solutions that can possibly minimize both fresh CO2 consumption and total CO2 emission, thereby further reducing the overall environmental impact. Case studies demonstrate that optimal networks yield significant reduction in the fresh CO2 consumption (over 80%) and CO2 emission, with certain cases achieving even zero source emission. Moreover, the emission-optimal design guarantees the network feasibility over the entire uncertainty range. It is shown that in a real operation involving disturbances, this benefit may come at even a lower fresh CO2 usage than a network designed without uncertainty considerations. This work highlights the potential for carbon reuse networks in advancing sustainability and environmental friendliness of industrial parks.

title: Chronic C-S-Fe defense dominance over nutrient removal in nanoplastics-exposed constructed wetlands: persistent feoA as the core biomarker
abstract: Constructed wetlands (CWs) face intensifying threats from nanoplastics (NPs). While existing evidence confirmed NPs impaired pollutant removal by disrupting microbial metabolism, critical knowledge gaps persist regarding how acute metabolic disturbances escalate into sustained functional impairment through self-sustaining cycles, and what strategies can effectively detect and disrupt such cycles. This study bridged this critical gap by examining how NPs reprogrammed interconnected biogeochemical networks during stress phases. Initially, microbial communities in CWs efficiently coupled C-N-P metabolism within a robust network, achieving high removal efficiencies of 92.23 % for total nitrogen (TN) and 90.13 % for total phosphorus (TP). However, prolonged NPs exposure (>90 days of operation) triggered a decisive metabolic shift toward a prioritized C-S-Fe defense module, with feoA identified as the top biomarker confirming Fe-centered defense via random forest. This redirected carbon flux into S-dependent glutathione biosynthesis and Fe-mediated antioxidant pathways while simultaneously suppressing N/P cycling investment. Consequently, microbial networks fragmented, sharply reducing TN (55.48 %) and TP (49.01 %) removal efficiencies. While partial C-N-P reintegration occurred during stabilization >150 days of operation), restoring TN removal efficiency to 73.53 %, the persistent topological dominance of the C-S-Fe defense module signals a chronic, defensive resource allocation strategy. Critically, the sustained primacy of feoA established its potential as a definitive biosensor for ecosystem dysfunction. Future development of cost-efficient assays targeting this biomarker could enable early detection of metabolic compromise and trigger tiered interventions, shifting environmental management from reactive pollution control to proactive functional governance to prevent chronic degradation.

title: Green sustainability of chelating agents used in cadmium-contaminated soil washing remediation: experimental validation and life cycle assessment
abstract: Despite the prevalence of soil washing as a soil remediation technique, there is a lack of comprehensive guidance on the selection of washing agents in the context of green and sustainable remediation. Therefore, the three most used chelating agents, including ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), glutamic acid N, N-diacetic acid (GLDA), and citric acid (CA), were evaluated in terms of cadmium (Cd) removal efficiencies, impacts on the soil environment, and life cycle assessment (LCA). The findings demonstrated that whereas CA had a lower removal efficiency of 48.4 %, GLDA could reach a similar removal efficiency of up to 68.8 % as EDTA. Compared with the control group (deionized water washing), the three chelating agents can significantly increase soil nutrients. Following EDTA washing, available nitrogen (AN), available phosphorus (AP), and available potassium (AK) increased by 10–15 %, 36–83 %, and 42–54 %, respectively. The application of GLDA resulted in an increase of 18 % in AN, 13–77 % in AP, and 36–83 % in AK. After CA washing, AN, AP, and AK increased by 3 %–15 %, 13–37 %, and 36–129 %. However, EDTA had the strongest inhibitory effect on urease, which was 56.8 %–69.3 %. The activity of sucrase was all enhanced by all three chelating agents, with an increase of 0.8–1.2 times. After 90 days of natural soil restoration, the soil properties tend to stabilize, where the enzyme activity of the GLDA-washed soil recovered to be closer to the initial value. The results of soil planting showed that all the remediated soil had a positive effect on the germination rate of cabbage. Notably, GLDA washing promoted root length more significantly, increasing it by 9.56 %–10.22 %. Based on LCA, the environmental impact of the production process of the three chelating agents and the environmental impact of the final washing process were CA > EDTA > GLDA. In summary, GLDA is a more suitable green chelating agent for this soil. This study will provide reference and comprehensive evaluation methods for selecting suitable chelators for future chemical remediation while balancing the effectiveness and green sustainability of soil remediation methods.

title: Multi-criteria optimization of methanol-based energy systems in ports using PMPEF-TOPSIS: A path to sustainable and efficient operations
abstract: Ports are strategic, energy-intensive nodes in global logistics, and decarbonization pressures are driving the need for low-carbon, infrastructure-compatible solutions. Methanol offers a technically practical pathway due to its liquid form, established handling compatibility, and lower emission potential relative to conventional fuels. This study presents the first structured comparative evaluation of methanol-based port power systems across thermochemical, electrochemical, and hydrogen-carrier routes. A new multi-criteria decision-making model, the Port Methanol Power System Evaluation Framework–TOPSIS (PMPEF-TOPSIS), is developed to assess feasibility across technical, economic, environmental, and regulatory dimensions. The TOPSIS results indicate substantial differentiation in criterion influence. Technological Innovation (1.000) and Environmental Impact (0.941) exhibit the highest proximity to the ideal solution, followed by Cost Efficiency (0.735), demonstrating that technology advancement and emissions performance remain the primary leverage points for methanol system feasibility. Performance in Dynamic Scenarios (0.000) and Economic Feasibility (0.382) ranked lowest, highlighting current limitations in operational robustness and macro-economic resilience. Electrochemical conversion ranked first among the alternatives (0.73), indicating the strongest overall suitability for port deployment. This framework offers a robust basis for strategic prioritisation and investment sequencing in port energy transition planning.

title: Water–energy–food nexus in a multi-product biomass supply chain
abstract: Brazil faces persistent undernutrition and increasing resource pressures across its agricultural, food, and bioenergy sectors. Existing Water–Energy–Food nexus models rarely integrate nutritional security as a primary optimization objective, which limits their relevance for sustainable development policy. This study addresses this gap by optimizing the Brazilian agri-food and bioenergy supply chain through a multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear programming model that simultaneously incorporates social (food security), environmental, and economic objectives. The formulation explicitly links food distribution to nutritional density, redirecting flows toward states with the highest vulnerability. As a result, undernutrition decreases sharply, reaching near-zero values in the most effective scenarios. For example, Maranhão declines from 2.59 % to 0.0014 % and Pará from 2.16 % to 0.0011 %, with reductions exceeding 90 % in several northern and northeastern regions. Economically, the most efficient configurations achieve annual net profits of up to USD 13.89 million per year. Simultaneously, the valorization of agro-industrial residues for biofuel production reduces dependence on fossil fuels and strengthens the circular bioeconomy. By incorporating indicators of water use, energy consumption, CO2 emissions, and economic value generation, the model demonstrates that it is possible to satisfy a significant share of food and energy demand without overexploiting natural resources. Overall, this research provides an integrated decision-support framework for policymakers and planners to balance nutritional equity, energy transition, and environmental resilience, advancing the Water–Energy–Food nexus toward actionable sustainability solutions.

title: Rational design of Pt-Ti electrodes for accelerated ammonia removal and metabolic steering towards N2 mitigation by Oceanimonas sp. in microbial electrochemical systems
abstract: Efficient and sustainable removal of ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N) from wastewaters is crucial due to its toxicity and environmental implications. While biological methods show promise, their effectiveness can be hindered in challenging conditions, often resulting in the unwanted nitrous oxide (N2O). This study focuses on enhancing NH3-N removal efficiency through the application of microbial electrochemical technologies (METs) using Oceanimonas sp., a halophiolic bacterium sourced from saline-alkaline soil. By applying optimal electrical stimulation at 0.6 V with a platinum (Pt) electrode, we achieved an NH3-N removal efficiency of 78.18 %, significantly surpassing control treatments. Transcriptomic analyses indicated that this improvement was linked to the upregulation of key genes (glnA, gltB, gltD) involved in ammonia assimilation. However, the Pt stimulation also led to partial denitrification, resulting in the generation of the greenhouse gas N2O. To optimize the nitrogen conversion pathway while minimizing byproducts, we developed a novel tandem electrode strategy. This approach consists of a "Pt first" stage to maximize initial NH3-N remove, followed by a "Ti optimization" stage. This functional transition is supported by the upregulation of upstream denitrification genes (napA/B, nirK, norB) and resulted in a dramatic reduction of N2O emissions by over 78.56 % compared to the Pt-only treatment, suggesting enhanced beneficial electron supply from the electrode. This research provides critical mechanistic insights into electrochemically stimulated ammonia metabolism and demonstrates the Pt-Ti tandem strategy as an approach for achieving high removal rates with sophisticated metabolic control to minimize byproducts.

title: Heat mitigation effects of urban parks and gardens on surrounding areas in hot, arid environments: A case study of Shiraz
abstract: Urban green spaces represent a highly effective strategy for mitigating elevated air temperatures and reducing the intensity of the urban heat island (UHI) effect. Existing research on the cooling effects of urban parks and gardens has been relatively limited, often relying on two-dimensional analyses and remote sensing methodologies. This study aims to address this gap by utilizing local weather station data, conducting three-dimensional analyses, and employing Envi-met simulations to investigate the role of urban parks and gardens in alleviating urban heat. The primary objective of this research is to examine the thermal conditions of urban green spaces and their contributions to mitigating the magnitude of the UHI within urban canyons surrounding these green spaces in Shiraz, Iran. The methods used in this study include field measurement, and simulation using ENVI-met. The simulation results demonstrated that the urban green space geometry in Shiraz had a cooling effect of about 5 °C. The cooling impact was extended to the surrounding areas (up to 140 m away). It was also found that the percentage of pavement was directly related to the increase of air temperature in surrounding urban canyons. Additionally, studying the orientation of urban canyons around the examined urban green spaces demonstrated that better thermal conditions are achieved by moving further west, ultimately reducing the intensity of UHI. Furthermore, examination of the thermal conditions of the study sites indicated that the average value of Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) in Shiraz in summer lays within the range of extreme heat stress (47.8 °C).

title: Sustainable ethylene production: A life cycle perspective on oil, coal, and natural gas derived industrial pathways in China
abstract: Under stringent Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction (ECER) policies, a comprehensive evaluation of the environmental and economic performance of ethylene production technologies has become an imperative. This study assessed five predominant industrial ethylene production pathways, including three petroleum-based (OTE), one coal-based (CMTE), and one natural gas-based (NETE), using integrated life cycle assessment (LCA), life cycle cost (LCC) analysis, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions accounting. Results indicated that the NETE route exhibited the lowest environmental impact, representing only 21.4 % of that associated with CMTE. Coal-derived methanol constituted the primary environmental burden in CMTE, significantly affecting primary energy consumption, CO2 emissions, industrial water use, and VOC releases. GHG analysis revealed that CMTE had the highest emissions, reaching 8298.58 kg CO2 eq per ton of ethylene, allocated almost equally between ethylene (45.3 %) and propylene (44.2 %). The three OTE routes followed in GHG emissions, with ethylene responsible for 32–37 % of CO2 eq. In contrast, NETE exhibited substantially lower emissions at only 1374.52 kg CO2 eq, with 77.4 % assigned to ethylene. Economically, NETE achieved the lowest total cost (internal and external costs), approximately 55.8 % lower than OTE routes. The analysis further revealed distinct regional disparities in ethylene production and GHG emissions across China, with high emissions in the central region attributable to CMTE dominance and elevated emissions along the eastern coast resulting from the prevalence of OTE routes. This spatially explicit assessment provided a foundation for developing region decarbonization strategies for the ethylene industry.

title: Enhancing rockfall barrier performance using waste used car tyres: A step towards sustainable civil engineering
abstract: Rockfall events pose a significant threat to infrastructure in hilly regions, necessitating robust and cost-effective mitigation strategies. This study initially evaluates the performance of traditional energy-absorbing material EPS-11 foam in enhancing the impact resistance of reinforced concrete rockfall barriers. A finite element model of a double-anchored rockfall barrier subjected to a high-velocity impact (25 m/s) from 1 m, diameter spherical rock was developed using Abaqus/Explicit. To explore sustainable alternatives, used car tyres were then investigated as hyperelastic energy-absorbing layers. The tyres were modelled using the Arruda-Boyce hyperelastic model. Three different configurations were examined: unprotected barrier (control), single tyre layer, and double staggered tyre layers. An additional energy absorption analysis showed that the double-layer staggered configuration exhibited higher internal energy dissipation (EVDDEN), indicating its superior ability to redirect and absorb impact energy through the tyre layers. Simulation results revealed that tyre layers significantly outperformed EPS foam in reducing peak deformation and vertical settlement. Compared to the unprotected case, single and double tyre layers reduced peak deformation by 16.08 % and 51.16 %, and vertical settlement by 10.90 % and 48.79 %, respectively. Further, supplementary impact velocity simulations (15–30 m/s) confirmed that the double-layer system maintained its effectiveness under increasing velocities, with peak performance observed at 25 m/s. Crack propagation and energy transfer to the structure were also notably mitigated with tyre protection. These findings highlight the potential of recycled tyres as a low-cost, sustainable, and highly effective alternative for improving rockfall protection systems.

title: Electrokinetic dual-cathode permeable reactive barrier system: Efficient Cr(VI) removal and Cr(III)/Fe(III) resource recovery from contaminated soil
abstract: Conventional electrokinetic (EK) remediation of Cr(VI)-contaminated soil faces considerable challenges, including extreme pH gradients, inadequate total chromium (TCr) removal efficiency, challenges in Cr(III) recovery, and the risk of causing secondary pollution. Here, this study proposes a novel electrokinetic dual-cathode permeable reactive barrier (PRB) system integrated with membrane separation. The following key advancements have been made: the dual-cathode design in combination with an AEM is effective in blocking Cr(III) back-migration. The removal rates of Cr(VI) and TCr were 98.17 % and 93.8 %, respectively. Dynamic electrolyte circulation maintained the soil pH (5.33–7.87) in a near-neutral state, thereby effectively suppressing the focusing effect. The optimized PRB filler ratio (zero-valent iron to sand = 1:5) reduced material costs. This configuration enabled the targeted enrichment and recovery of Cr(III) and Fe(III) in secondary cathode chamber (Cathode 2), with recovery rates of 33.97 % and 10.67 %, respectively. This technology provides an environmentally benign solution for efficient remediation and resource recovery from Cr(VI)-contaminated soils.

title: Identification of drought-flood abrupt alternation thresholds triggering vegetation loss
abstract: Frequent drought-flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) events significantly threaten vegetation carbon sequestration and ecosystem stability. Previous studies have primarily focused on the impacts of individual extreme events, with limited attention to the complex effects of DFAA sequences on vegetation. In this study, we identified DFAA events using the short-cycle drought-flood abrupt alternation index (SDFAI), and estimated vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) via the Carnegie–Ames–Stanford Approach (CASA) model. Furthermore, we developed a copula-based conditional probability framework to determine the DFAA intensity thresholds that trigger vegetation loss and to quantify the drought-to-flood (DTF) and flood-to-drought (FTD) thresholds in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River Basin (MLRYRB). The results reveal that: (1) DTF and FTD events occur 22–26 times on average, with moderate intensity being most prevalent. Hotspots include western Hunan, southern Anhui, and southern Jiangsu. (2) Vegetation growth is relatively good, with NPP increasing at 2.82 gC·m−2·a−1. High NPP values cluster in southern Shaanxi and northwestern Hubei, while lower values appear in central Hubei, southern Jiangsu, and southern Anhui. (3) Vegetation NPP exhibits similar response patterns to DTF and FTD events, with the likelihood of vegetation loss increasing as the intensity of DFAA increases. NPP is highly sensitive to DFAA events, with the threshold intensities for DTF and FTD that trigger vegetation loss being relatively low, respectively ranging from 1 to 1.8 and −2.1 to 1, with area proportions reaching 73.75 % and 80.35 %, respectively. Vegetation in southern Anhui, northern Hubei, and southern Shaanxi resists DTF events more effectively, whereas central-northern Hunan and western Jiangxi vegetation shows higher FTD resistance. Among driving factors, vapor pressure deficit (VPD) most significantly influences DFAA-related vegetation loss thresholds. This study advances understanding of vegetation responses to DFAA events in the MLRYRB and supports strategies for maintaining regional vegetation health and enhancing carbon sequestration capacity.

title: Improving the performance of green office buildings in mainland China through facility management under the "dual carbon" goals
abstract: This study examines how facility management (FM), influenced by national policy and technological advancements, can enhance the carbon reduction capacity (CRC) of green office buildings in mainland China. Addressing a significant research gap, it examines the operational phase of green buildings, often neglected in traditional design-focused evaluations. A novel theoretical framework, Integrated Technology Acceptance and Policy Change Theory (I-TAM-PCT), is introduced to analyze the institutional and technological drivers of FM effectiveness. A hybrid analytical method, Entropy-TOPSIS–Machine Learning (ET-ML), is applied to 203 survey responses and nine expert interviews. A composite index, the Integrated Carbon Reduction Performance Index (ICRPI), was developed using 16 dimensions from policy and technology indicators. Among eight evaluated algorithms, Gradient Boosting achieved the highest accuracy (0.89), with SHAP analysis indicating that policy incentives, responsiveness, and Digital Twin-based FM (DTFM) features, especially real-time consumption monitoring and predictive optimization, are the most significant factors in enhancing CRC. Notably, buildings implementing DTFM showed an average CRC improvement of 18.4 % compared to non-adopters. By integrating a multi-level policy–technology framework with a reliable computational model, this study advances both theoretical understanding and practical approaches for carbon-neutral building operations. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers and practitioners in China and other developing economies pursuing low-carbon growth through intelligent FM.

title: Microenvironments outweigh mobility in PM2.5 exposure inequality: A case study of Beijing commuters
abstract: PM2.5 exposure poses significant public health risks by contributing to respiratory and cardiovascular diseases. Traditional static PM2.5 exposure assessments, which focus on residential or workplace locations, overlook human mobility and microenvironmental variations, leading to biased estimates. To address this, we developed the Microenvironment-bAsed Dynamic Exposure (MADE) framework to assess PM2.5 exposures for Beijing commuters. Using mobile phone signaling data and fuzzy mathematics, we simulated spatiotemporal behaviors across residential, occupational, commuting, and other microenvironments. The MADE framework integrates geographic PM2.5 variations and indoor-outdoor concentration differences, achieving precise, large-scale exposure estimates. The mean PM2.5 exposure estimated by the MADE framework (40.82 μg/m3) is 6.9 % lower than that estimated by the static model (43.86 μg/m3). The PM2.5 exposure concentrations present a geographic pattern of being higher in the south and lower in the north, which is consistent with the static model but with smaller values. The reductions in exposure concentrations for individuals living in southern areas with high PM2.5 concentrations are slightly greater than for those living in northern areas with low PM2.5 concentrations. Differences in indoor-outdoor concentrations are the primary drivers of disparities, challenging the notion that geographic variations in PM2.5 concentrations dominate exposure inequality. Commuting, owing to its limited time proportion, contributes minimally to overall exposure. These findings correct overestimations in static models and highlight the need to incorporate indoor environmental complexity and diverse population activities for accurate exposure assessments. By addressing these factors, the MADE framework advances environmental justice and informs equitable public health policies.

title: Dual-atom-site photocatalysts enhanced CO2 reduction coupled with benzylamine oxidation
abstract: Solar-driven artificial photosynthesis via CO2 reduction represents a promising method for generating renewable feedstock in a sustainable manner. However, CO2 activation is very demanding and the separation of undesired O2 as by-product is challenging. Promoting the oxidation of organic substances by consuming photo-generated holes can effectively prevent O2 production, improving energy conversion, product selectivity and separation. In this study, we report a photosensitizer-functionalized (tris(2,2′-bipyridyl)ruthenium, PS) dual-atom-site [Ru(C10N2H4)2Cl2]H4[Ru2Cl2(CH3COO)4]·H2O (PS-Ru2) photocatalyst that promotes the conversion of CO2 to CO with the photooxidation of benzylamine to liquid benzylidenebenzylamine, enabling facile separation without additional photosensitizers or sacrificial agents in a single redox cycle. This is the first reported dual-atom-site photocatalytic system to promote an artificial photosynthetic CO2 reduction coupled with benzylamine oxidation, delivering high activity, selectivity and separability. Modification of the photosensitizer resulted in an eleven-fold increase in yield, representing a significant advancement in catalytic CO2 photoreduction. The findings of this study establish a novel dual-atom-site catalyst design strategy that facilitates dual-functional artificial photosynthesis, enabling by-product reuse with improved performance.

title: Coordinating net-zero: Organizational learning as a meta-capability in carbon-intensive Indian firms
abstract: Despite rising net-zero commitments, many carbon-intensive firms struggle to translate ambition into change in everyday work. This study examines how organizational learning operates as a coordination meta-capability linking strategic net-zero intent to operational transformation. Using Gioia-style grounded theorizing, we analyse 25 semi-structured, multi-level interviews from five large Indian firms in the energy, oil and gas, steel, cement, and automotive sectors. We inductively identify four micro-foundations and six cross-cutting learning routines that together constitute organizational learning as a coordination system. We then introduced capability fluency and proposed a Distribution–Reflexivity–Integration (D-R-I) rubric to operationalize the quality of this system. The rubric assesses how widely routines are deployed, whether periodic reviews trigger within-cycle changes, and how tightly micro-foundations are linked. Two firms in our sample exhibit high capability fluency, two moderate, and one low. Variation in net-zero learning stems less from the presence of routines than from their D–R–I quality and the strength of coupling mechanisms. We further translate the Dynamic Capabilities View into a measurable, auditable architecture, offering a simple D–R–I rubric, count-based indicators, and a learning maturity roadmap that provides managers and policymakers with concrete diagnostics and low-cost design options for integrating net-zero into day-to-day decisions in emerging economies.

title: Green manure incorporation as a solution to synergistically improve crop yields and soil organic carbon sequestration
abstract: Planting and incorporating green manure has been widely used worldwide due to the benefits of improving soil quality and crop yields. However, a comprehensive assessment of the effects of planting and incorporating green manures on soil properties and crop production is still lacking. Here we conducted a meta-analysis to determine the effects of green manure planting and incorporation on soil nitrate-N leaching, soil water, soil properties, SOC sequestration, and crop yield in wheat, maize, rice, and tobacco. Results showed that planting and incorporating green manure reduced soil nitrate-N leaching during its growing season by 44 %, and reduced the soil water storage in the 0–200 cm soil layers before sowing and at harvest of the following crop by 11 % and 5 %, respectively. Incorporating green manure increased soil total nitrogen, soil available phosphorus, soil available potassium, and SOC sequestration rate by 13 %, 8 %, 8 %, and 64 % in the 0–20 cm soil layer, respectively. As a result, green manure incorporation increased the mean yield of the following season by 12 %, with maize yields significantly higher than those of rice and tobacco. Over the past six decades, the area harvested for green manure has increased substantially worldwide, playing an important role in sustainable crop production. Scientific management of green manure will therefore be a key strategy to achieve a win-win situation for both food security and environmental protection.

title: The digital divide and hog industry: The impact of digital technology levels on the sustainability of the hog industry in China
abstract: The hog industry is vital for food security and global protein supply, yet it faces challenges in achieving sustainability due to environmental issues and inefficiencies in production processes. The rapid growth of the digital economy provides new opportunities for transforming traditional industries, including the hog sector, by enhancing efficiency, optimizing resource use, and reducing environmental impacts. This study aims to explore the relationship between digital technology and the sustainable development of the hog industry, this study employing the Entropy Weight and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method to construct two comprehensive indices: the Digital Technology Level (DTL) index and the Sustainable Hog Industry (SHI) index. Using a two-way fixed effects model, this study analyzes the impact of DTL on SHI and identifies key findings. From 2012 to 2021, DTL in China showed a continuous upward trend, increasing from 0.091 to 0.176 nationally, while SHI rose slowly from 0.269 to 0.295. However, significant regional disparities remain, with developed eastern regions such as Tianjin and Beijing achieving both high DTL and SHI, while central and western regions lag behind. DTL is found to be a key driver of SHI, with a significantly positive correlation across all models. However, the digital divide weakens the positive effects of digital technology in underdeveloped areas, hindering sustainable development. To address these challenges, this study proposes narrowing the digital divide, enhancing digital technology applicability in different regions, and fostering regional collaboration. These findings provide valuable insights for promoting the sustainable transformation of the hog industry through digital technologies.

title: Seaweeds as a nature-based solution to mitigate nutrient and carbon emissions from shrimp farming (Penaeus vannamei) under current and future climate conditions
abstract: Economically important agarophyte seaweeds have proven to be excellent biofilters for mitigating excess nutrients from shrimp farming. However, the effects of warming on their bioremediation capacity have been little explored, which is concerning given the current context of climate change. Thus, this study evaluated the performance of the agarophytes Gracilaria caudata and Gracilaria birdiae as biofilters for mitigating excess nutrients and carbon produced by shrimp cultivation (Penaeus vannamei) in an outdoor integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) experiment using two recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS): one at ambient temperature (ambient-RAS) and the other under elevated temperature (warmed-RAS). Shrimp in the ambient-RAS exhibited relative growth rates (RGRs) ranging from 0.25 % to 3.24 % day−1, with final weights increasing from 11.6 g to 18.4 g. In the warmed-RAS, RGRs ranged from 0.31 % to 1.97 % day−1, with final weights increasing from 11.4 g to 16.2 g. No significant differences in shrimp productivity were observed between treatments. In seaweed cultivation of the ambient-RAS, NO3− concentrations decreased by 7–39 %, NH4+ by 4–33 %, and PO43− by 1–18 %. In the warmed-RAS, reductions were 8–31 % for NO3−, 5–21.5 % for NH4+, and 1–17 % for PO43−. Warming did not significantly affect biofiltration efficiency. Seaweeds cultivated in RAS exhibited increasing content of nitrogen, phosphorus, and phycobiliproteins over time, confirming nutrient uptake. CO2 concentrations in seaweed cultivation were reduced by 38 % under ambient conditions and by 27 % under elevated temperature. In the IMTA experiment, seaweeds stored from 8 to 12.4 g C m−2 in their dry biomass. Gracilaria caudata exhibited better performance under elevated temperature compared to G. birdiae. Our findings support the feasibility of implementing IMTA in shrimp farms as a sustainable strategy for cleaner shrimp production. In addition to environmental benefits, seaweed cultivation in IMTA can generate social and economic gains through the production of agar, organic fertilizers, natural pigments, and carbon credits.

title: Industry heterogeneity of environmental, social, and governance performance, impact mechanisms and trend forecasts - Evidence from big data and machine learning analysis
abstract: This paper aims to delve into the industry-specific heterogeneity of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance among Chinese listed companies by employing a comprehensive research design that integrates descriptive statistics with analysis of variance (ANOVA), time series modeling, correlation analysis, cluster analysis. Through an in-depth examination of 188,006 ESG score records from Chinese listed companies spanning from 2009 to the first quarter of 2024, the study reveals that financial services and insurance sectors generally exhibit higher ESG scores, whereas traditional manufacturing industries lag in ESG performance, facing more significant environmental and social challenges. ANOVA results indicate highly significant differences across industries in terms of E, S, G, and composite ESG scores. Time trend forecasting based on Prophet model time series analysis suggests that ESG scores for Chinese listed companies will continue to rise over the next few years but with fluctuations, providing crucial forward-looking decision support for enterprises and policymakers. Correlation analysis reveals generally weak interconnections among the E, S, and G dimensions, with the strongest (though modest) association observed between environmental and social scores, suggesting limited cross-dimensional spillover effects.
