New methods are needed to assess WEFE nexus comprehensively. Cooperative game theory emphasizes collaboration, which aligns with the characteristics of resource flows in WEFE nexus. Assessing WEFE cooperative efficiency and identifying key drivers is crucial for optimizing resource allocation and improving efficiency. This study employs a cooperative game-based SBM model (CG-SBM model) grounded in game theory to assess both original and cooperative efficiency within China's WEFE nexus and applies the Tobit model to analyze efficiency drivers. Results reveal that: (i) from 2005 to 2023, WEFE nexus efficiencies in China increased, with ecosystem efficiency growing fastest at 23 % annually. Efficiency varies spatially, with higher levels in the southern regions and lower levels in northern regions; (ii) ecological efficiency was the primary driver of WEFE nexus improvements, with the potential for improvement ranking highest in ecological systems, followed by energy, food, and water systems; (iii) driving factors vary by system and region and differ before and after cooperation. Regionally, both internal and external factors significantly influence efficiency. However, at the system level, efficiency is more strongly influenced by internal factors. Therefore, focusing on internal factors, particularly water utilization structure and industrial structure optimization, is essential for improving both system and regional efficiency.

title: Explaining policy implementation gap by policy network analysis: Evidence from China's energy renovation project quality failures
abstract: As climate change becomes a global concern, policymakers and practitioners are paying increasing attention to low carbon development in urban building zones. Among various measures, energy-saving renovations of existing residential buildings have become among the most vital developments for reducing carbon emissions in China. However, Quality failures—such as improper installation of steel nails or missing rivetsdefined as completed work that does not comply with prescribed technical standards—occur frequently during construction processes. These quality failures, representing a gap in policy implementation for residential building energy renovations, have received relatively little academic attention. This research seeks to address this gap by applying policy-network analysis to two case studies of renovation projects in Inner Mongolia in China, examining how actor interdependencies and adoption of policy instruments contribute to quality failures. The findings indicate that market-based policy instruments incur significant administrative costs, thereby impeding the maintenance of project quality. Additionally, mandatory policy instruments frequently lead to goal displacement at various governmental levels, further compromising the quality of energy renovation projects. Conversely, involving residents as a voluntary policy instrument can alleviate financial pressures on local governments while enhancing oversight of renovation quality. Nonetheless, this approach may impose financial burdens on economically disadvantaged groups. Based on these results, it is recommended that the government adopt a nuanced combination of policy instruments to minimize quality failures and realise the energy-efficiency potential of residential renovation initiatives.

title: Limited synergy of existing emission controls for carbon and air pollutants in the Chinese refining industry
abstract: China's oil refining industry accounts for about a quarter of the country's energy consumption, accompanied by significant emissions of air pollutants and carbon dioxide (CO2). How to build a phased and collaborative optimization technology path for China's refining industry based on the penetration rate of emission reduction technologies is a key challenge that has not yet been addressed in existing research. This study initially used data from field investigations to develop emission inventories for air pollutants and CO2 for the Chinese refining industry in 2022 and innovatively incorporated information on emission reduction technology penetration rates to conduct the corresponding assessment. Results showed emissions of SO2 (2.0 Mt), NOx (12.3 Mt), VOCs (25.32 Mt), PM (0.009 Mt), and CO2 (404.6 Mt). The average emission factors for NOx (0.2 kg/t), VOCs (0.4 kg/t), and CO2 (0.6 t/t) were much higher than for SO2 and PM, suggesting priority should be given to reducing the former. The mapped roadmaps for coordinated pollution and carbon mitigation in the Chinese refining industry across different periods indicated that not all technologies can address both the carbon and air pollutant emission reduction goals, which delayed their effectiveness in supporting the dual mitigation targets. Scenario analysis found that ignoring the energy consumption of reduction equipment could achieve an 84.4 % average pollutant reduction by 2060, but considering it lowered the rate to 21.8 %. Mitigation pathways must consider both reduction potential and secondary emissions from energy use, including carbon sequestration technologies.

title: Electro-sustainable aviation fuel via reverse water-gas-shift based Fischer–Tropsch synthesis: Decarbonization pathways and economic prospects
abstract: Electro-sustainable aviation fuel based on the reverse water-gas shift and Fischer-Tropsch synthesis processes is currently garnering significant attention due to its low CO2 emissions and its ability to utilize syngas derived from diverse feedstocks. With the increasing emphasis on achieving net-zero emissions in the transportation sector and the utilization of CO2 sources, optimizing which CO2/H2 sources to integrate with the aviation fuel production process has become crucial. This study analyzed potential combinations of various industrial CO2 and green H2 sources from both economic and environmental perspectives. A well-to-wake boundary was employed, including the penalty of the CO2 capture process for CO2 supply and the economic issues of green H2, from primary feedstocks to the end use of jet fuel. Importantly, the process electrification index was defined to represent the degree of “process electrification” for each combination of the aviation fuel production process. The higher the electrification index, the greater the reduction in CO2 emissions, but the tendency for economic competitiveness to decrease. Furthermore, the future position of electro-sustainable aviation fuel production technology was predicted by applying the learning-by-doing analysis of renewable H2 production and the CO2 capture process. This study highlights the potential of electro-sustainable aviation fuel production technology combined with direct CO2 utilization as an alternative to existing sustainable aviation fuel production and provides a powerful tool for exploring future development strategies.

title: Catalytic hydrothermal liquefaction of Enteromorpha prolifera for bio-oil upgrading through in-situ hydrogenation
abstract: Biomass energy is increasingly recognized as a promising substitute. Algae can be transformed into high-quality biofuels (rich in 5-methylfurfural) through the process of hydrothermal liquefaction. In this study, the lumped reaction kinetics approach is employed to investigate the reaction mechanism of hydrothermal liquefaction. The results indicate that during the initial stage of HTL, Enteromorpha prolifera (EP) is predominantly converted into water phase substances with activation energy value (E) of 15.0 kJ/mol which subsequently undergo further transformation into bio-oil (E = 87.2 kJ/mol). To further enhance the quality of bio-oil, two distinct approaches are applied for in-situ hydrogenation: (1) employing various types and volume fractions of alcohol-water solutions (methanol or ethanol) as hydrogen donors, and (2) utilizing polypropylene (PP, medical plastic waste mainly consists of substances) as a hydrogen source for in-situ hydrogenation. The effects of different mass ratios (1:3, 1:2, 1:1, 2:1 and 3:1) of EP and PP on in-situ hydrogenation performance are revealed. When an alcohol-water solution is used for in-situ hydrogenation, the maximum 5-methylfurfural content reaches 50.2 % using a 40 % ethanol-water solution higher than that with 40 % methanol (46.4 %). Besides, the 5-methylfurfural content is 48.1 % at a mass ratio of 1:1 between PP and EP, in which PP is employed as the hydrogen source. The highest content of 5-methylfurfural reaches 52.5 % used 5 wt% Ni/HT-1.0. The response surface analysis results indicate that the loading amount of Ni has the greatest impact on the content of 5-methylfurfural. The research of this study can provide solutions to the increasingly severe energy problems and environmental issues caused by medical plastic waste and EP, thereby providing a scientific basis for its energy utilization.

title: Methane emissions from global shallow lakes: Patterns, key drivers, and mitigation strategies
abstract: Shallow lakes are predominantly located in human activity hotspots and typically exhibit various nutrient pollution levels and climate sensitivity. These changing environmental conditions often drive complex and variable biogeochemical processes of methane (CH4) production and emission in lakes, leading to significant uncertainties in global estimation. This study systematically analyzed the CH4 emission patterns and driving factors from global shallow lakes (water depth ≤6 m) and quantified the mitigation potential achievable. Results demonstrated an average CH4 emission flux of 3.41 ± 2.08 mg m−2 h−1 from collected shallow lakes, with a global total emission estimated at 29.66 Tg yr−1. Of which, ebullition was identified as the predominant pathway (56 %) and exhibited a greater temperature dependence than diffusion. In comparison, smaller (<1 km2), shallower (<2 m), low-latitude (<30°), and higher eutrophic status (eutrophication index >61.29) lakes exhibited significantly higher CH4 fluxes (p < 0.01). Concentrations of total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) in lakes and local air temperature were the key factors governing CH4 fluxes. A global 10 %–50 % synergetic reduction in TN and TP is projected to reduce CH4 fluxes and emissions by 11 %–38 % and 12 %–44 %, respectively. Controlling TN is more effective than TP at reducing CH4 flux, particularly in low-latitude, smaller, shallower hypereutrophic and eutrophic lakes. This research further advances understanding of the CH4 emission patterns in global shallow lakes and provides potential sustainable management strategies within the context of accelerating environmental change.

title: Towards Industry 5.0: An integrated readiness assessment of EU-27 Member States
abstract: The contemporary global economy, driven by technological progress, is entering a new stage of transformation referred to as the Industry 5.0. This concept, building on the foundations of Industry 4.0, emphasizes a more sustainable, inclusive and resilient model of economic development. However, despite numerous conceptual discussions in the literature, no integrated empirical assessment of countries' readiness for Industry 5.0 has been conducted to date. Moreover, no comprehensive study covering the scope presented in this work has previously been carried out. This study fills this gap by presenting the first data-driven assessment of the readiness of the EU-27 countries to implement the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Its foundation is a novel, two-stage research methodology combining multiple multi-criteria decision-making methods, three independent indicator weighting techniques and the Laplace criterion. This multidimensional approach significantly enhances the robustness of the results and reduces methodological bias. Based on 27 indicators representing four dimensions: digital transformation, human-centricity, sustainability and innovation and systemic resilience, the Industry 5.0 Readiness Index was constructed. This is an entirely new measurement tool with no equivalent in the existing literature. The results reveal substantial disparities in the readiness levels of the EU-27 countries to implement Industry 5.0. Sweden, the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany and Ireland demonstrate the highest readiness, while Poland, Greece, Bulgaria and Romania face significant structural barriers. These findings confirm that readiness for Industry 5.0 depends not only on technological progress but also on social and environmental factors. The proposed methodology provides a unique, flexible and adaptable tool that supports decision-making processes and the development of evidence-based policies within the European Union.

title: Incorporating ecosystem quality and stability into protected area planning on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau: Towards integrated conservation targets
abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are widely regarded as an effective strategy for conserving biodiversity and natural ecosystems. As conservation objectives expand to include multiple ecosystem services, climate adaptation capacity, and landscape aesthetics, it is increasingly necessary to incorporate integrated ecological indicators—such as ecosystem quality (Qeco) and ecosystem stability (Seco)—into PAs planning, which not only provides a more comprehensive assessment of ecological status but also enhances the innovation and applicability of conservation prioritization. This study conducts a representativeness analysis of existing PAs on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP) with respect to biodiversity (Bio) and climate refugia (CR), and advances conservation planning by incorporating two comprehensive indicators—Qeco and Seco. The results indicate: (1) Existing protected areas on the QTP show significant conservation gaps across the four major targets (Bio, CR, Qeco, and Seco) and their components, with complex interrelationships among these factors. (2) Optimized PAs identified through the inclusive conservation framework are mainly concentrated in the eastern and southern QTP, covering 27.81 % of the region and meeting at least three out of the four conservation targets. (3) Compared to current 33 % PA coverage, these optimized PAs improve conservation efficiency by more than 36.84 % for different conservation targets. The findings provide valuable insights for the optimization and efficiency enhancement of the PAs network, thereby contributing to the ecological security of the QTP. Moreover, this framework can be applied to other regions to support the implementation of the post-2030 Global Biodiversity Framework.

title: Algal bloom control through machine learning guided inverse design of pre-oxidation-coagulation
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) threaten drinking water safety and ecosystem stability. Pre-oxidation–coagulation is an effective control method, but its operational optimization remains challenging due to nonlinear parameter interactions and limited systematic datasets. A machine learning–based inverse design framework was developed to optimize pre-oxidation–coagulation processes for algal removal. Literature data (n = 328) were supplemented with 471 newly conducted orthogonal experiments, yielding a balanced dataset (n = 799) covering nine oxidants, three coagulants, and pre-oxidation times from 5 to 60 min. A stacked ensemble model, employing CatBoost as the meta-learner over four base algorithms, was trained and interpreted using SHAP analysis. The model was coupled with sequential quadratic programming (SQP) for inverse parameter optimization, with target removal efficiency of 90 %. The ensemble model achieved an average test R2 = 0.783, with substantial gains for challenging oxidants such as K2FeO4 (+34.01 %). SHAP analysis ranked parameter importance as coagulant dose > oxidant dose > pre-oxidation time > oxidant type, revealing saturation of pre-oxidation effects within 5–20 min. Inverse design reduced experimental workload by over 98 % (384–6 validation runs) while maintaining ±8.34 % accuracy. Experimental validation (6 triplicate runs) confirmed both predictive reliability and process efficiency. Balanced datasets are critical for capturing oxidation-specific dynamics. The proposed framework offers a cost-effective, data-driven solution for rapid, precise HAB control, bridging laboratory studies with full-scale water treatment operations.

title: Process development and multi-criteria optimization of industrial large-scale integrated carbon capture and sulphur recovery process: A step towards cleaner energy and waste valorization
abstract: Computational advancements and the usage of emerging evolutionary algorithms have seen an increased engagement in engineering and its domains. This study uses the NSGA-II algorithm to optimize a large-scale integrated carbon capture (CC) and sulphur recovery unit (SRU) for an industrial plant, using real-world gas sweetening plant data. Five objective functions, eleven decision variables, along with imposed constraints, are used to perform bi-, tri-, and four-objective optimization. In case 1 (maximization of sulphur mass flow and minimization of acidification potential (AP)), regenerator feed pressure converges to the upper limit of 280 kPa. The sulphur mass flow values start increasing from 267.89 kg/h to 452.1 kg/h, and acidification potential values increase from 20.94 mPETEU2004 to 434.85 mPETEU2004. For case 2 (minimization of AP and global warming potential (GWP)), the AP values increase from 21.93 mPETEU2004 to 63.26 mPETEU2004, and GWP values decrease from 168715.2 mPETW2004 to 168178.7 mPETW2004. For case 3 (maximization of sulphur mass flow, minimization of AP and net energy consumption), at a steady feed molar flow rate of 350 kgmole/h the sulphur mass flow increases from 142 to 250 kg/h. TOPSIS, NFM, and MOORA methods of Pareto ranking are used to determine the best and worst optimal solutions. The economic specific study is reported for the best and worst optimal solutions, including total capital cost, total operating cost, and utility cost. This study sheds light on achieving a cleaner energy approach for the industrial decarbonization sector. Sustainable sulphur recovery is integrated with a decarbonization process to achieve waste valorization.

title: Towards cleaner solid fuels: Co-pelletization of ethylene vinyl acetate from decommissioned photovoltaic modules with pine sawdust & comprehensive performance evaluation
abstract: To promote the transition to renewable resources and address waste pollution, in this study, waste ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) generated during the recycling process of decommissioned photovoltaic modules was co-pelletized with pine sawdust at mass ratios of 0:10, 2:8, 3.5:6.5, and 5:5 to prepare hybrid fuel pellets, and a comprehensive evaluation was conducted from multiple dimensions. The results showed that: compared with pure sawdust pellets, the calorific value of the hybrid pellets increased by 21.88 %–57.06 %, both their mechanical durability and impact resistance increased to over 99.5 %, and their hygroscopicity decreased by a maximum of 72.87 %. The addition of EVA at a low proportion could effectively reduce the burnout temperature of the pellets, and the variation in ignition temperature was no more than 5 °C. EVA significantly reduced the emissions of CO2, NOx, and sulfides. The ash of the pellets with a 2:8 ratio was classified as Type C, which exhibited the lowest risks of deposition and corrosion. The addition of EVA lowered the total cost of the pellets, among them, the total cost of the pellets with a ratio of 5:5 was reduced by 31.76 %. Multi-criteria decision analysis indicates that the 2:8 mixing ratio is suitable for scenarios with strict requirements for combustion characteristics and ash-related risks, while the 5:5 ratio achieves the optimal balance in other aspects. This study provides technical support for the high-value utilization of waste EVA and the development of clean solid fuels, contributing to the low-carbon transition of energy.

title: Waste not, emit not: How circular economy strategies shape climate and growth outcomes in G-20 nations?
abstract: This study examines how circular economy (CRE) practices and green logistics (GRLS) shape carbon emissions and economic growth in G-20 economies using annual data from 1990 to 2023. Drawing on OECD waste and recycling indicators and World Development Indicators, we estimate long- and short-run effects with a PMG-ARDL framework, complemented by FMOLS and VECM for robustness and dynamics. The results show that recycling-oriented circularity particularly packaging waste delivers substantial long-run emission reductions: a 1 % increase in packaging-waste circularity lowers CO2 emissions by up to 0.71 %. ICT-based green logistics further reduces emissions in the long run while supporting economic growth, although short-run adoption phases can temporarily raise emissions due to infrastructure upgrades. We note that ICT serves as an enabling proxy for logistics digitalization rather than a direct measure of freight emissions, and results should be interpreted accordingly. Overall, the findings highlight the complementary roles of circularity and logistics modernization in achieving decarbonization without sacrificing growth. This study contributes novel evidence by leveraging a 34-year G-20 panel to jointly quantify CRE and GRLS impacts on both CO2 emissions and GDP, offering policy-relevant insights for long-run sustainable transitions.

title: Recycling waste polypropylene in asphalt binders: A sustainable MPP-OMMT composite for enhanced compatibility, rheological performance, and aging resistance
abstract: The recycling of waste polypropylene (Waste PP) in asphalt binders provides notable environmental benefits but faces challenges due to poor compatibility and phase separation. To overcome these drawbacks, maleic anhydride grafted polypropylene (MPP) was used to improve interfacial adhesion through chemical grafting, while organic montmorillonite (OMMT) was incorporated to further enhance compatibility and anti-aging performance via its layered silicate structure and barrier effect. The physical, rheological, and aging behaviors of the modified asphalts were comprehensively evaluated. Compared with base asphalt, MPP increased the softening point by 45.2 % and enhanced high-temperature deformation resistance, but reduced ductility due to limited flexibility of the polymer phase. The addition of 6 % OMMT effectively mitigated this drawback, improving ductility by 128.6 % and reducing stiffness at −12 °C by 71.3 %. The fatigue life of the MPP–6 % OMMT composite increased by 370 % relative to base asphalt, demonstrating superior fatigue resistance and structural durability. In terms of anti-aging performance, the MPP–OMMT composite significantly suppressed oxidative degradation. After short-term aging, the carbonyl index (CI) and sulfoxide index (SI) decreased by 85.8 % and 90.0 %, respectively, compared with base asphalt, confirming the strong antioxidative effect of OMMT. This improvement is attributed to the dual mechanism of chemical grafting and physical shielding, where MPP strengthens molecular bonding while OMMT forms a dense silicate barrier that restricts oxygen diffusion and retards oxidation. In addition, the MPP–OMMT composite markedly enhanced storage stability, reducing the softening point difference and ΔT index, and effectively suppressing phase segregation during thermal storage. Overall, the synergistic modification of MPP and OMMT effectively resolved the incompatibility and oxidation issues of Waste PP-modified asphalt. This strategy provides a sustainable and high-performance pathway for recycling polymer waste into durable asphalt binders with balanced thermal stability, flexibility, and long-term durability.

title: Projected increases in environmental resources due to population growth and wealth-driven dietary changes. Data, uncertainties, and prospects
abstract: Food production causes over 30 % of global environmental emissions and resource use. This paper provides a realist estimation of how population growth and dietary change increase the global Food Resources Requirement (FRR) through 2060. The FRR-Model links GDP-driven caloric and meat uptake with population growth, using wheat equivalents (wheatEQs) as a composite proxy for environmental resource demand. Latent Class Analysis identifies five country clusters reflecting differing meat dependence and meat affinity. Two main groups emerge: OECD+ (81 % of current population) with diet-driven demand growth, and with population-driven pressure on future food resources. Results indicate a magnitude up to 40 % global increase in Food Resources Requirement (FRR) by 2060. Two opposing trends emerge: in OECD + countries, GDP growth of 128 % raises food-related resource use by 17 % without population growth, whereas in Africa+, minimal GDP and diet change coincide with a 162 % population surge—raising Africa's share to 40 % of the global total. Country clusters differ by meat affinity—the GDP-driven rise in meat consumption—and meat dependence, where meat remains an unsubstitutable staple food. Mitigating FRR growth demands policies that integrate these cultural and biophysical realities while acknowledging epistemological limits of forecasting. The discussion outlines cleaner, context-specific, and lower-resource food system pathways.

title: Enhanced phosphorus release and sludge reduction via a novel worm reactor: Process optimization and mechanisms
abstract: Addressing the dual challenges of excess sludge disposal and phosphorus (P) resource scarcity, this study developed a novel worm reactor (WR) integrating mechanical agitation and continuous weak aeration to achieve simultaneous sludge reduction and enhanced P release. The unique reactor design minimized worm loss while creating heterogeneous microenvironments conducive to P solubilization. By leveraging worm predation, the impacts of dissolved oxygen (DO), initial sludge concentration (ISC), and sludge retention time (SRT) on process efficiency were systematically investigated. Optimal conditions-DO 1.0 mg L−1, ISC 7000 mg L−1, and SRT 1.7 d-were identified via response surface methodology (RSM), achieving a sludge reduction rate of 732 mg L−1 d−1 and supernatant P release of 54.2 mg L−1. Significantly higher pollutant release (COD, NH4+-N, TN, TP) was observed in the WR compared to a control reactor, confirming that worm predation enhances P release. Mechanistic analysis revealed synergistic P migration pathways: biological fragmentation disrupted extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) and cells, while microbial metabolism facilitated organic P mineralization. This work provides an efficient strategy for simultaneous sludge minimization and P resource reclamation, advancing sustainable wastewater management.

title: Sustainable utilization of red mud and coal gasification fine slag for iron recovery and cementitious material preparation
abstract: The massive accumulation of red mud (RM), a byproduct rich in aluminum and iron, and coal gasification fine slag (CGFS), a waste rich in silicon and carbon, presents a critical environmental problem. This study proposes an integrated two-stage process that synergistically valorizes these wastes by exploiting their unique chemical attributes. First, the residual carbon in CGFS was used as an in-situ reductant to recover iron from RM via co-reduction roasting followed by dry low-intensity magnetic separation, yielding a magnetic concentrate with a total iron (TFe) grade of 56.03% and a recovery rate (ε) of 17.28%. Thermodynamic, phase and microstructural analyses confirmed the targeted reduction of ferric minerals to magnetite without over-reduction. Second, iron separation tailings, rich in activated Al-Si phases, were directly repurposed as precursors for RM-CGFS-based alkali-activated cementitious materials (RCAM). Using water glass activation supplemented with blast furnace slag (BFS) and mechanical activation, RCAM achieved a 28-day compressive strength of 37.95 MPa. Microstructural analysis confirmed its strength derived from a dense gel matrix of calcium (sodium) aluminosilicate hydrate (C/N-A-S-H) phases. The RCAM met and surpassed the requirements for commercial Portland-slag cement, exhibiting higher early-age strength and a sulfate corrosion resistance coefficient of 0.9959. This integrated waste-to-resource pathway offers a feasible solution for the simultaneous management of two major industrial solid wastes and supports more resource-efficient construction.

title: Upcycled diatomite and red mud as bitumen modifiers and multi–functional fillers for durable, eco–efficient asphalt pavements: A critical review
abstract: Despite significant research on diatomite and red mud as individual asphalt modifiers, a comprehensive review evaluating their synergistic potential as multifunctional fillers for sustainable pavements, integrating technical performance, waste valorisation, and circular economy principles, remains lacking. This gap hinders a full understanding of how these materials can optimize pavement performance and promote sustainability. Therefore, this review examines the physicochemical properties, preparation methods, and environmental benefits of diatomite and red mud in alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Diatomite enhances pavement durability and aids in removing over 90 % of suspended solids from stormwater, supporting SDGs 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). Red mud, a by-product of bauxite processing, improves rheological properties by reducing non-recoverable creep compliance by up to 70 %, contributing to SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), though its high alkalinity requires leaching management. Life-cycle assessments show 5–15 % reductions in CO2 emissions and lower reliance on virgin materials, advancing SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). Trade-offs include diatomite-induced low-temperature brittleness and red mud's reduced moisture resistance. Based on these insights, this review identifies future research priorities in hybrid filler design, long-term validation, and contaminant mitigation, proposing a circular economy framework for cleaner, eco-efficient road infrastructure.

title: Unveiling mechanisms governing heavy metal leaching from solid waste-vitrified glasses for cleaner resource recovery
abstract: Upcycling solid wastes into glass products offers a high-value pathway for waste minimization and resource conservation. However, the environmental risk of these products remains insufficiently understood, primarily due to the limited mechanistic knowledge of heavy metal leaching under beneficial use scenarios. Herein, using municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (FA)-vitrified glasses as a representative system, the dominant mechanisms and controlling parameters of heavy metal leaching were unveiled by integrating systematic glass characterization, geochemical speciation modeling, and kinetic rate laws. The normalized releases of heavy metals were comparable to those of major constituents (e.g., Na and Ca), highlighting the necessity of assessing their release risks. Heavy metal leaching was strongly pH-dependent but relatively insensitive to temperature, governed i) by ion exchange under acidic conditions, ii) by secondary phase precipitation (hydroxides and silicates) at pH 8–11, and iii) by congruent dissolution at pH > 11. High content of alkalis and alkaline earths from FA (i.e., Ca, Mg, and Na) depolymerized the glass network, accelerating ion exchange and reducing overall leaching durability. Consequently, glass alteration transformed from initial rate to residual rate stage at pH < 9 within a short time (<2 days). The mechanisms identified and models developed in this study lay a solid foundation for designing more durable waste-vitrified products and for supporting their safer and cleaner reuse in resource recovery.

title: Quantifying the climate mitigation potential of China's South-to-North Water Transfer Megaproject
abstract: Water transfer megaprojects (WTMPs) adapt arid regions to climate-driven water scarcity by diverting freshwater, potentially enhancing carbon sequestration through aquatic ecosystems restoration. However, their potential to mitigate climate change has not yet been explored. Here we propose a WTMP-based climate mitigation framework that integrates the long-lived mega water infrastructures with food, water, and energy sectors. The applications of our framework to China's South-to-North Water Transfer Project (SNWTP) demonstrate that WTMPs can help mitigate climate change through enhancing food security and promoting energy transition. Our framework highlights three key findings: (1) the median annual net primary production (NPP) sum of irrigated crops across the pan-North China Plain increased by 4.39 % between 2015 and 2021 (84.79 million tons) relative to 2007–2014 (81.22 million tons); (2) the enhancement of crop NPP boosts the production of crop residue-based biochars (approximately 75 million tons annually) that can avoid ∼187 million tons of CO2 emissions annually after the SNWTP's operation; (3) SNWTP within a lifespan of at least 50 years can help promote the deployment of canal-based solar photovoltaic (PV) units with an installed capacity of approximately 80 GW, which could contribute to a 6.58 % increase for China's renewable energy and avoid 1495.23 million tons of CO2 emissions. Our research highlights the importance of exploring more untapped benefits of long-lived mega water infrastructures for climate mitigation when most of the existing low-carbon and negative emission technologies are still far from sufficiently deployed.

title: Carbon emission reduction of bike-sharing around the COVID-19 pandemic based on fine-grained recognition of riding activities
abstract: Bike-sharing systems (BSS) is a sustainable and low-carbon travel option. While many studies have evaluated their environmental benefits, most assessments assume that all bike trips equally contribute to carbon emission reduction, overlooking differences in trip purposes. In particular, leisure riding, which does not substitute motorized transport, can lead to overestimations of bike-sharing's carbon reduction. This limitation becomes even more critical under large-scale disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, which significantly reshaped urban mobility patterns. To address this gap, this study proposes a refined framework that distinguishes emission-reduction riding (ER-riding) from leisure riding and develops a hybrid method combining the threshold approach and nested logit model to more accurately estimate BSS carbon emission reduction. With the proposed methodology framework, we perform a comparative spatiotemporal analysis to investigate the impact of the COVID-19 on carbon emission reduction and its recovery before, during, and after the COVID-19 in New York, Washington, and Chicago. Results show that the pandemic significantly disrupted the carbon emission reduction of bike-sharing, with recovery patterns varying across cities. New York demonstrated the strongest resilience, with its emission reduction levels in 2021 surpassing those of the pre-pandemic period in 2019.This resilience may be attributed to the expansion of its BSS infrastructure, as well as a higher proportion of private transport replacement compared to public transport. These findings highlight that Washington and Chicago could enhance their bike-sharing carbon benefits by learning from New York's system. Overall, this study enhances the understanding of bike-sharing's environmental role in multimodal transport and highlights the need for resilient systems to sustain carbon emission reductions under external shocks.

title: Prospective life cycle assessment of the Spanish electricity mix (2023–2050): Interrelation between climate change, water footprint, and costs
abstract: In response to the climate emergency, the European Union (EU) launched the “Fit for 55” package in 2023, aiming to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by 55 % in 2030 and achieve climate neutrality in 2050, including targets like increasing the share of renewable energy to 42.5 %. This study evaluates the environmental and economic performance of Spain's primary electricity generation technologies in the context of the EU's 2030 climate objectives and the national energy strategy. Using life cycle assessment (LCA), it quantifies the global warming potential (GWP), water scarcity impacts, and costs associated with wind, hydropower, solar thermal, photovoltaic, coal, combined cycle and nuclear power. Results indicate that coal and combined cycle technologies present the highest GWP and costs. As it could be anticipated, hydropower exhibits the highest water footprint. Wind energy shows the most favourable balance across the three categories, followed by solar technologies. The prospective analysis of the 2030 and 2050 scenarios shows that the planned transition would progressively reduce the electricity mix's fossil GWP by over 50 % and its water footprint by approximately 25 % by 2050 compared to 2023 levels. These findings support Spain's current energy transition path, though they suggest reconsideration of the planned nuclear phase-out given its relative performance in the triangle of the three assessed categories. Further LCA studies focusing on water scarcity are recommended to broaden the existing literature and therefore strengthen decision-making.

title: Zero-valent metal enhanced BN/TiO2 photodegrades PFOA via regulating the Mott-Schottky Junction
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pose significant risks to both ecosystems and human health, necessitating the development of effective remediation techniques for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in aquatic environments. We engineered Mott-Schottky heterojunctions by depositing Pt0 onto BN/TiO2, which promotes electron transfer from TiO2 to Pt, facilitates spatial separation of charge carriers, and substantially inhibits recombination processes. The incorporation of Pt modification extends the photoresponse range spectrum from 400 to 600 nm, narrows the bandgap from 3.0 to 2.8 eV, and markedly improves PFOA degradation under UVC (3 times higher degradation rate, 1.6 times higher defluorination rate) and UVA (1.6 times higher degradation rate, 2.8 times higher defluorination rate). Through comprehensive systematic material characterization and energy band analyses, the role of the Schottky junction was elucidated, thereby providing a strategic framework for rationalizing materials aimed at efficient aqueous PFOA remediation. This work not only advances the fundamental understanding of Mott-Schottky junctions in PFAS remediation but also provides valuable insights for the rational design of efficient photocatalysts toward PFAS degradation.

title: Biochar addition reduces soil greenhouse gas fluxes in terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Biochar addition is gradually recognized as a nature-based solution for mitigating greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes from soils. However, its overall climatic benefits remain unclear due to the high heterogeneity and complexity of ecosystem types, biochar properties, and experimental conditions. We provide a comprehensive global meta-analysis that integrates 13,523 paired observations from 59 studies to evaluate the overall effect of biochar addition on soil carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O) fluxes in terrestrial ecosystems. Our results reveal that biochar addition notably promoted soil CO2 and CH4 fluxes by 2.2 % and 12.4 %, respectively, but reduced N2O fluxes by 17.9 %, culminating in a net reduction of 3.3 % in the combined 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) derived from soil greenhouse gas fluxes. The stable mitigation effect on N2O fluxes was mainly attributed to improved soil aeration, increased pH, adsorption of inorganic nitrogen, and the suppression of nitrification and denitrification processes. Interestingly, the positive effect of biochar addition on soil CO2 fluxes was primarily observed in the pot and incubation experiments, whereas a negative effect was noted in the field. This difference was mainly caused by the duration of the experiment. The former is usually short-term, during which CO2 fluxes are enhanced, but the latter has a relatively longer period, with the efflux effect gradually decreasing. Soil CH4 fluxes increased in forests in response to biochar addition, which contributed to the formation of an anaerobic environment and a supply of substrate for methanogens from the increase in soil moisture and organic carbon. Our results suggest that biochar with high-temperature pyrolysis, high carbon content, and fine particles exhibits greater mitigation capacity in warm and humid environments. This work emphasizes the notable potential of biochar in improving soil physicochemical properties and reducing GHG fluxes, offering a helpful reference for clean and sustainable production.

title: Integrating system dynamics and machine learning to establish the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus of aquavoltaics
abstract: Traditional aquaculture faces growing challenges from climate change, including rising water temperatures, reduced water availability, and declining yields. This study explores aquavoltaic systems—integrating aquaculture with solar panels—as a sustainable, climate-resilient solution. We used clam farming at the Mariculture Research Center Taihsi Station in Yunlin County, Taiwan, as a case study. Within the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus framework, we applied system dynamics (SD) modeling enhanced by a hybrid machine learning approach. By combining the genetic algorithm (GA) and the backpropagation neural network (BPNN), we improved the accuracy and reliability of SD models, simulating real-world conditions using in-situ monitoring datasets to promote sustainability, resource use efficiency, and policy coherence in aquaculture. Results show that 40 % solar panel shading reduced water temperatures by 2.5 °C, improved water use efficiency by 30 %, and generated renewable energy to offset emissions. Although clam yields declined by 27 %, solar power compensated for production losses, creating an economically viable system. Further optimization identified 45 % shading as ideal, preserving 70 % of yields while maximizing energy output. This study offers valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders, showcasing aquavoltaics as a scalable framework for balancing food production, renewable energy generation, and climate adaptation—advancing sustainable aquaculture in Taiwan and beyond.

title: Nighttime lights-based downscaling for high-resolution electricity mapping: Insights into consumption, efficiency and footprint for sustainable energy management
abstract: Electricity consumption is a key indicator of urbanization and sustainability, yet its fine-scale spatiotemporal patterns remain insufficiently explored. Nighttime lights are a widely recognized remote sensing proxy for human activities. They offer great potential to downscale and map electricity consumption at high resolution. This study develops a grid-based downscaling model that integrates nighttime lights with socioeconomic data to generate annual 1 km resolution maps of electricity consumption in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA). The model demonstrates high accuracy and robustness across two decades. Results indicate that electricity consumption increased more than fivefold, evolving from a single-core to a multi-core pattern in GBA from 2000 to 2020. Linkages among Guangzhou, Foshan, Shenzhen, and Dongguan strengthened, with Foshan and Dongguan driving westward expansion. Efficiency improved overall, diffusing from the eastern to the western bank, while inter-city gaps narrowed. This pattern reflects spillover driven by industrial upgrading in eastern cities through industrial linkage extension, factor mobility, and regional collaborative innovation. The footprint expanded from the Guangzhou-Shenzhen core to Zhongshan and Huizhou, shaped by population and industrial migration. These findings reveal pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity in electricity consumption-efficiency-footprint, and highlight the uneven dynamics of energy demand across an urban agglomeration. By providing a comprehensive grid-level assessment of electricity consumption and its implications, this research advances the use of nighttime lights for urban energy mapping and offers transferable insights for sustainable electricity planning in other rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: Effects of clean energy equipment manufacturing industry's growth on carbon emission in China: An analysis based on emission-offsetting effect
abstract: The rapid development of China's clean energy equipment manufacturing industry (CEEMI) exerts a dual impact on carbon emission: generating emission at the production while achieving emission abatement at the consumption through substitution of traditional energy sources. Based on provincial panel data from China spanning 2011 to 2023, this article specified a simplified STIRPAT (Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence and Technology) model. By isolating the elasticity coefficients of production and usage, this article quantitatively measured the net “offsetting effect” of clean energy equipment, incorporating mechanism variables such as Global Value Chain (GVC) participation, GVC position, and technological progress. The findings reveal: (1) An increase of one unit in output from China's CEEMI offsets 30.72 % of carbon emission. (2) The effectiveness of this “offsetting effect” depends on regional industrial development levels, product technology maturity, and the co-located cluster of production and consumption. Growth in the CEEMI significantly inhibits carbon emission in eastern regions, whereas western regions, despite their resource endowment advantages, exhibit no significant emission-offsetting effect. (3) Enhanced GVC participation and technological progress drive carbon emission reduction. (4) A decline in GVC position indicates that the industry currently faces a “low-end lock-in” dilemma, yet this does not significantly affect the “offsetting effect”, as domestic technological progress plays a more significant role. This study provides a policy foundation for giving full play to the promotion role of CEEMI in China's carbon emission reduction.

title: Role of energy consumption, gross capital formation, and urbanization in determining economic growth in Spain: Evidence from non-parametric methods
abstract: This study explores the relationship between urbanization, energy consumption, and gross capital formation, while accounting for the roles of foreign direct investment (FDI) on economic growth using annual time-frequency data from 1970 to 2024 in Spain. This study leverages time-frequency domain by capturing short- and long-time dynamics, such as the Wavelet Coherent analysis and Wavelet Granger Causality (WGC). The results show urbanization has a direct causal impact on foreign direct investment, which aligns with the urbanization-induced FDI growth. Similarly, economic growth also exhibits causation on capital formation, as proposed by GCF, reflecting Spain's reliance on energy use to sustain investment. The Wavelet Granger Causality approach revealed that another vital channel is the causality from energy consumption (EC) to gross capital formation (GCF), reflecting Spain's heavy reliance on energy use to sustain investment during periods of industrial expansion, particularly the construction boom of the 1990s and early 2000s, when energy-intensive sectors played a central role in driving capital accumulation. The results call for a shift from Spain's historical reliance on energy-intensive, construction-driven, and externally financed growth toward a model centered on renewable energy adoption, energy-efficient investment, sustainable urban transformation, and enhanced domestic investment capacity.

title: Speciation of N, P, K nutrient elements and heavy metals in sewage sludge char produced from a pilot-scale thermal carbonization device and its utilization in soil amendment
abstract: Municipal sewage sludge is featured by both pollution risks and resource attributes. However, existing collaborative disposal technologies suffer from several inevitable defects including heavy metal residues, pollutants control, and limited nutrients utilization. Nevertheless, thermal carbonization technology offers several advantages for resource recovery and utilization by converting sewage sludge into high value-added biochar. To clarify its potential of sewage sludge char (SSC) utilization in soil amendment, this work aimed to comparatively analyze the speciation of N, P, K nutrients and heavy metals in dried sewage sludge (DSS), and SSC produced from a pilot-scale thermal carbonization device. The results showed that the total nutrient element in SSC was increased to 10.02 % (as the form of N + P2O5+K2O), in comparison with DSS. Specifically, total N element in SSC accounted for 3.68 %, and its speciation shifted towards more stable pyridine/pyrrole-N. Total P element increased to 4.11 %, primarily existing as the form of biologically-available inorganic-P. Total K element was slightly decreased to 0.58 % but the relative proportion of available-K content was increased. Moreover, pilot-scale thermal carbonization process also showed a satisfactory fixation effect on heavy metal elements, and it promoted the transformation into oxidizable and residual form with a lower leaching risk level. Critically, with SSC improving soil structure and nutrient content (e.g., N, P, K, and organic matter), maize pot experiments further confirmed its promoting effect on plant growth, including accelerated germination, increased plant height and root/stem biomass. This pilot-scale thermal carbonization method provided a cleaner utilization paradigm for municipal sewage sludge valorization.

title: Long-term scenarios for climate adaptation of cotton crops in China, considering multidimensional biophysical and socio-economic scenario analysis
abstract: Climate change is fundamentally reshaping agricultural land suitability, with profound implications for water use, carbon emissions, and crop productivity. Understanding the long-term drivers of climate on the planting suitability of arable land and exploring multi-sectoral coordinated response solutions for the climate-agriculture-society system are essential for mitigating and adapting to climate change. This study develops a multidimensional framework to assess climate adaptation scenarios for cotton−one of the world's most important cash crops−in China from 1960 to 2100. Integrating species distribution modeling with socio-economic scenario analysis, we identify three key findings: (1) Historical cotton's highly suitable areas has shifted northward (+166 km) and to higher elevations (+47 m average) due to changing climate-soil-topography interactions; (2) While climatic suitability determines land potential, actual planting decisions are still mainly driven by economic returns, coordinating to local production management level; (3) Sustainable adaptation requires balancing biophysical suitability with production efficiency and circular economy practices. This study emphasizes not only the climate impact on agricultural land use changes but also reveals the synergistic mechanisms between climatic suitability, socio-economic, and production factors, that inform targeted land-use planning. Based on these findings, we recommend that future agricultural policies prioritize climate-smart land-use zoning, support adaptive infrastructure development in emerging suitable regions, and provide economic incentives to guide planting structure optimization under climate change scenarios. These insights play a crucial role in optimizing climate-smart farming structures, promoting agricultural adaptation and mitigation of climate change, and realize the sustainable and cleaner production under climate change.

title: Internet use and public acceptance of nuclear energy: Evidence from China
abstract: As nuclear power projects remain controversial in many countries worldwide, it is crucial to understand the determinants of public acceptance of nuclear energy. This study attempts to explore the relationship between Internet use and an individual's willingness to accept (WTA) compensation for the construction of nuclear power plants. Based on data from the Chinese General Social Survey, instrumental variable estimates reveal a significant and negative correlation between Internet use and WTA. Further analyses show that Internet use improves individuals' knowledge of nuclear energy and reduces their safety-related risk perception, thus leading to a lower WTA. Meanwhile, Internet use increases individuals' environmental-related risk perception, which is negatively correlated with WTA. These findings provide several implications for policymakers designing nuclear policy in the digital age.

title: Improving the multi-temporal dissolved oxygen estimation using statistically enhanced remote sensing proxies in data-scarce, optically complex inland water
abstract: Monitoring optically inactive water quality (WQ) parameters, such as dissolved oxygen (DO), through remote sensing presents a significant challenge due to their lack of spectral signatures. Traditional in-situ methods provide only point measurements with limited spatial coverage. This study introduces a novel remote sensing framework for spatially continuous, multi-temporal dissolved oxygen (DO) estimation in inland water bodies. The framework is demonstrated on the river Ganga in Varanasi, India. The approach leverages satellite-derived normalised Water Surface Temperature (n-WST) and Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) as key proxies. Symbolic Regression (SR) was selected for its modelling efficacy with limited datasets and ability to generate interpretable mathematical relationships. The SR model achieved Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 17.44 % on the test dataset of February 5, 2025, and MAPE of 18.12 % when applied to satellite data of November 26, 2025, demonstrating robust multi-temporal generalization. Trained on the dataset of November 26, 2025, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Regressor (SVR) exhibited MAPE (%) values of 21.26 and 26.43 respectively on the test dataset. Satellite based seasonal analysis revealed DO variability from 6.32 ppm during summer to 9.06 ppm in winter. The framework emphasized the importance of thermodynamic control through inverse DO-temperature relationships over positively correlated association between DO and chlorophyll-a while capturing spatial-temporal heterogeneity. By coupling interpretable machine learning with remote sensing proxies, the framework addresses data scarcity and lack of spectral signature of certain WQ parameters, offering a scalable and effective framework for monitoring WQ parameters using satellite data.

title: Interfacial engineering of amyloid nanocomposites for eco-friendly and high-efficacy herbicide delivery
abstract: To address the critical issue of pesticide loss (up to ∼60 % of applied pesticides) caused by splash, rebound, and rain-induced runoff, which contaminates groundwater and poses risks to human health and the environment, this study presents a novel interfacial engineering strategy to enhance herbicide droplet deposition and adhesion on (super)hydrophobic leaf surfaces. This strategy utilizes the interfacial assembly of amyloid-like protein/laponite (PTB/LAP) nanocomposites to create stable oil-in-water (O/W) nanoemulsions with strong foliar affinity. Specifically, bovine serum albumin (BSA) is first adsorbed onto laponite (LAP) surfaces via hydrogen bonding; subsequent introduction of tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) reduces BSA's disulfide bonds, triggering in situ amyloid-like aggregation of surface-bound BSA (PTB) to form PTB/LAP nanocomposites. These nanocomposites significantly enhance interfacial activity, reducing aqueous surface tension to ∼36 mN/m, and form elastic-dominated interfacial networks with excellent mechanical strength. The resulting PTB/LAP nanoemulsion remains stable (mean droplet size ∼250 nm, polydispersity index <0.2) for over 180 days. It exhibits rapid, nanosecond-scale anchoring on leaf cuticles, yielding a 3.6-times higher retention rate than BSA/LAP emulsions under simulated heavy rainfall (150 mm per day). At an equal dosage of 2,4-D isooctyl ester, the nanoemulsion achieves 96.9 % efficacy against shepherd's purse, 2.2 times higher than conventional emulsifiable concentrates (ECs), which only achieve ∼43.5 % efficacy. Furthermore, the PTB/LAP nanoemulsion demonstrates exceptional biocompatibility, with 100 % survival of non-target land snails after 120 h and no significant cytotoxicity or genotoxicity in CHL cell assays. This work provides an eco-friendly, scalable platform for improving pesticide efficiency, reducing environmental contamination, and advancing sustainable agriculture.

title: Comparative assessment of manual and UAV-based deep learning approaches for beach litter
abstract: Since the 1980s, marine litter has increasingly accumulated on global coastlines. Traditional monitoring methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and face significant challenges in consistently detecting small or partially buried litter, which has driven the need for intelligent, data-driven approaches. This study proposes an optimized UAV-deep learning framework to address these challenges. We selected two typical coastal regions in Guangdong Province, China: Donghai Island (Zhanjiang) and Daya Bay (Huizhou). At these sites, a high-resolution dataset consisting of 6300 UAV images through aerial photography and manual annotation. An enhanced YOLOv8 model with Gold-YOLO-inspired feature extraction and fusion was developed and trained on this dataset. The optimized model achieved 96.50 % precision, 87.00 % recall, 91.50 % F1-score, and 89.80 % mAP@0.5, markedly outperforming baseline YOLO variants and traditional manual methods in both accuracy and efficiency. Field validation at 12 sampling sites showed that the system improves operational efficiency by 75 %, completing surveys in hours instead of days. Environmental assessment using the Clean Coast Index (CCI), Plastic Abundance Index (PAI), and Hazardous Litter Index (HLI) revealed that plastics account for 85 % of all detected litter. The proposed UAV-deep learning framework enables rapid, accurate, and cost-efficient large-scale beach litter monitoring, providing coastal managers with a practical tool for data-driven environmental management and pollution control. It paves the way for integration with automated cleanup systems and long-term ecological risk assessment, contributing to global marine plastic pollution mitigation.

title: Synergistic pyrolysis of concentrated seawater and agricultural waste for phosphorus recovery and release from wastewater: A multi-fold resource utilization strategy
abstract: Addressing the dual challenges of waste disposal and the phosphorus resource crisis, the development of cost-effective and sustainable adsorbents for phosphorus recovery through the utilization of concentrated seawater and agricultural waste is of great significance. Herein, an effective strategy was presented for synthesizing Ca/Mg biochar composites by integrating concentrated seawater and agricultural waste through a co-precipitation and low temperature carbonization (400 °C), aimed at phosphorus recovery and release. The introduction of 3.0 mol/L KOH during preparation increased the specific surface area, optimized the pore structure, and promoted the co-precipitation of Ca/Mg from concentrated seawater into the biomass framework, providing more active sites. Characterization results confirmed the mesoporous structure and the presence of surface-loaded metal species in all three Ca/Mg-modified biochar composites. The adsorption of phosphorus by the Ca/Mg biochar composites produced from three types of agricultural waste was well-described by the pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir isotherm models, recording a maximum adsorption capacity of 138.192 mg/g. This suggested that the biochar preparation strategy possessed considerable universality, yielding biochar with consistent physicochemical properties and phosphorus adsorption performance. The characterization and analysis further reveal that the primary adsorption mechanisms include electrostatic attraction, chemical precipitation, and ligand exchange. Significantly, excessive Ca/Mg in individual biochar composites group (CBC-K) inhibited Mung beans germination and growth, whereas phosphorus-saturated Ca/Mg biochar composites group (P-CBC-K) still promoted crops growth due to the formation of calcium- and magnesium-containing phosphorus compounds, resulting in a 2.64-fold increase in fresh biomass compared to CBC-K group. This study enables the simultaneous phosphorus removal and recovery, along with the harmless treatment of concentrated seawater and agricultural waste, thus achieving a multi-fold resource utilization.

title: Multiple enhanced PMF framework addressing ambient processing and factor allocation for VOC source apportionment
abstract: Volatile organic compound (VOC) pollution control is a key driver of the sustainable improvement in air quality. As one of the most commonly used approaches for linking emissions with ambient pollution, Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) model exhibits limitations due to its neglect of ambient processing and reliance on subjective factor allocation. This study developed multiple enhanced PMF framework. By incorporating corrections for photochemical losses and secondary formations, the Initial Number PMF (IN-PMF) addressed gaps between the observed and initial concentrations. On this basis, the Initial Number and Dispersion Normalized PMF (IN-DN-PMF) was developed to exclude atmospheric dilution. Triaxial characteristic species ratios screened from extensive emission tests were raised to constrain all models, enabling precise apportionment of highly collinear mobile sources. Taking a typical corridor city in China as a case study, the IN-PMF model traced contributions of active species across sources and corrected underestimation of emission intensities. The IN-DN-PMF model provided a spatial distribution of local VOC emissions more closely aligned with actual source locations, while reducing the influence of wind-direction relative to sources. Improvements were most pronounced for gasoline vehicles due to the high emissions of active substances and strong mobility. The traditional PMF underestimated the contribution of gasoline vehicles during pollution episodes by 28.58 % due to photochemical reactions, and by 44.70 % when both photochemistry and dilution were considered. These biases indicate that the traditional model could weaken the importance of vehicle emissions, underscoring the value of the enhanced PMF approach for reliable pollution governance and policy formulations.

title: Staged pyrolysis of corn cob to improve the production of glycolaldehyde, acetic acid, and acetol
abstract: During high-temperature fast pyrolysis, cellulose and hemicellulose undergo simultaneous pyrolysis with partially overlap decomposition temperature ranges, resulting in the concurrent release of abundant molecular fragments/intermediates. The coexistence of these active intermediates readily induces side reactions like polymerization, which inhibits the formation of small molecules (e.g., glycolaldehyde and acetol). Pre-releasing the products of either component is a viable strategy to alleviate this overlap inhibition effect. Given that hemicellulose has a lower decomposition temperature than cellulose, staged pyrolysis is implemented by leveraging this temperature difference. The staged pyrolysis was divided into two sateges, first at 290, 320, or 350 °C to release hemicellulosic derivatives, and then at 600 °C. The results indicated that higher first-stage temperature significantly reduced the inhibition effect, enhancing the production of small molecules (C1-C5), including hydrogen storage molecules. However, extending the first-stage residence time detrimentally decreased the hydrogen storage molecules production, excluding acetic acid. Conversely, a longer second-stage residence time improved the yield of both small molecules and hydrogen storage compounds. Ultimately, staged pyrolysis yielded the highest amount of small molecules (C1-C5) and hydrogen storage molecules when firstly pyrolysis of corn cob at 350 °C with 0.5 min, and subsequently at 600 °C for 0.5 min (350-0.5 + 600-0.5). Direct pyrolysis of cellulose-corn cob blends to test the effectiveness of attenuating the overlap inhibition effect. This discovery has implications for optimizing pyrolysis efficiency and designing reactors for future applications.

title: Quantifying transport contributions and diagnosing ozone formation sensitivity: An integrated approach using machine learning with high-resolution gridded data and backward trajectories
abstract: Regional transport of air pollutants poses a serious challenge to tropospheric ozone (O3) pollution control. Although recent study has combined machine learning and backward trajectories to quantify the contribution of transport, the accuracy of these models has been limited due to the use of average transport times. Therefore, this study integrates high-resolution pollutant concentration data with machine learning and backward trajectories (XGBoost-Traj-Grid), significantly improving the model's simulation performance. The Mangdang Mountain, located at a high-altitude background site on the southeast coast of China, exhibits daily minimum values as high as 80.00 μg⋅m−3, and the difference between daily maximum and minimum values of only 9.14 μg⋅m−3. The XGBoost-Traj-Grid model identified the top five features with the largest contribution to O3 at this site as nitrogen dioxide (NO2), fine particulate matter, coarse particulate matter, relative humidity, and O3 concentration corresponding to a backward trajectory of −3 h. The positive relationship between NO2 and O3 shown in the dependence plot, together with the high HCHO/NO2 ratios observed in OMI satellite data, provides strong evidence that O3 production at this site is NOx-limited. The transport has a predominant role in Mangdang Mountain, with the contribution of transport increasing from 46 % to 56.5 % after meteorological normalization., The contribution of direct O3 transport has always been the largest among the various transport components, with 34.9 % and 32.4 % respectively before and after the meteorological impact. This study indicates that the control of O3 at high-altitude background sites requires joint prevention and control measures. The XGBoost-Traj-Grid model can not only quantify regional transport contributions but also identify O3 formation sensitivity, providing a basis for ozone management.

title: Pilot-scale ultrasonic agglomeration of flue gas particulates for reduced energy consumption during industrial gas cleaning
abstract: Waste-to-energy (WTE) is a widely adopted and effective approach for waste reduction and energy recovery. However, flue gas generated during WTE processes must be treated prior to discharge, and the removal of high concentrations of ultrafine particles at elevated temperatures remains an energy-intensive challenge. Acoustic agglomeration (AA), particularly when implemented using ultrasonic waves, offers a promising method to reduce energy consumption by promoting the coagulation of fine particles into larger aggregates that can be more readily captured with lower energy input. To date, most studies on AA have been confined to laboratory-scale systems or low-temperature conditions, with limited validation at the pilot or industrial scale. In this study, AA was successfully applied in a pilot-scale particle removal system at an operational WTE facility. Particle removal efficiency, bag filter pressure drop and energy consumption were systematically quantified to evaluate performance. The results demonstrate substantial energy savings of up to 36.8 % in the purge system, along with a modest 1.3 % reduction in draft fan energy consumption. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents one of the first applications of AA in a full-scale operational WTE facility, providing valuable insights into the feasibility of AA for industrial deployment and guiding future research and optimization efforts.

title: Global synthesis of agricultural practices on crop yield, soil organic carbon and greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Low-carbon agricultural practice is crucial for reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and enhancing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, without compromising crop yield. However, consensus on which practices were certain to deliver positive outcomes remains limited. Synthesizing global meta-analysis evidence (covering 81 first-order meta-studies and 275 paired observations), this study identified different agricultural practices effects of crop yield, SOC content and GHG emission caused through secondary use of meta-analysis data on the topics. Results showed that crop rotation, film mulch, new crop variety and various fertilizer management strategies significantly increased crop yield (up to 62 %); crop rotation, conservation tillage, deep tillage, biochar addition, organic fertilizer addition, cover crop, straw management significantly increased SOC content (up to 34.30 %); the CH4 emission were effectively reduced by new crop variety, deep fertilization, enhanced-efficiency fertilizer and non-flooding irrigation, while N2O emission declined with reduced nitrogen fertilizer and herbicide application. Among all practices evaluated, rice-animal co-culture emerged as one of the most consistently beneficial strategies in paddy field, increasing crop yield by 2.48 %, enhancing SOC by 10.03 %, and reducing CH4 emissions by −36.30 %. Biochar was the most beneficial strategies in unspecified land use pattern that could increase crop yield and SOC (12.79 %, 32.71 %), decrease GHG emission (−8.68 % to −6.22 %). By quantifying weighted effect sizes for paddy, upland, and mixed cropland systems, this synthesis offered a clear evidence base for designing low-carbon farming systems.

title: Air-source high-temperature heat pump systems for zero-carbon parks: Performance and application
abstract: In the pursuit of global carbon neutrality, zero-carbon industrial parks urgently require efficient and low-emission technologies for high-temperature heat supply. This study investigates an air-source high-temperature heat pump (ASHTHP) system by establishing a cascade cycle model and validating its performance through both laboratory tests and field operation in a pharmaceutical park. Results indicate that system efficiency rises with ambient temperature: under a 125 °C supply condition, the coefficient of performance (COP) increased from 1.35 at −20 °C to approximately 1.85 at 35 °C. In contrast, raising the supply temperature led to a decline in efficiency. The deviation between simulations and experiments was within 5 %, confirming the accuracy of the model. Field operation further demonstrated stable delivery of 115 °C steam with an average COP of 2.1, meeting the continuous high-temperature demand of pharmaceutical production. Economic and environmental analyses highlighted the advantages of ASHTHP over conventional boilers. Compared with coal-fired boilers, CO2 emissions were reduced by 35 %. Under conventional electricity supply, annual operating costs were 10 % lower than gas-fired boilers and more than 30 % lower than electric boilers. When coupled with renewable electricity, costs further decreased by 38 %, while near-zero emissions were achieved. Overall, the ASHTHP system combines high efficiency with strong decarbonization potential for high-temperature applications in zero-carbon parks, demonstrating both engineering feasibility and significant potential for large-scale deployment. These results provide a practical pathway toward the development of zero-carbon industrial parks.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and enhancement potential of global water retention: Insights from a water balance-geographical detector framework
abstract: Water retention is one of the essential ecosystem service functions, playing a critical role in maintaining regional ecological security and the sustainable development of water resources. This study, based on the principle of water balance and employing the optimal parameters-based geographical detector, revealed the spatiotemporal patterns of global water retention from 1991 to 2019, identified the main driving factors, and proposed a method for assessing water retention potential. The results indicate that tropical regions represent the core zones of global water retention, whereas arid and semi-arid areas exhibit pronounced declining trends in water retention. Autumn and winter represent the peak periods of retention, while spring and summer correspond to risk periods. Precipitation is the primary factor influencing the spatial variability of water retention, and it exhibits a significant nonlinear-enhance interaction with evapotranspiration, jointly shaping the spatial pattern of water retention. Globally, the potential for increasing water retention is predominantly at medium to high levels, with most regions having room for enhancement, and South America showing the greatest potential. This study provides a critical theoretical foundation and data support for the scientific enhancement of water retention in the future and offers valuable reference for the formulation of sustainable water resource management and ecological conservation policies.

title: Attribution analysis of spatial differentiation in green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency based on geographical detector and random forest models: A case study of the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Green and low-carbon transition and development represents a global issue encompassing economic, social and environmental dimensions. To objectively assess the efficiency of this transition, this study establishes an evaluation index system from input-output perspectives of economy, resources and society, focusing on 108 prefecture-level cities along the Yangtze River Economic Belt. Through trend surface analysis and spatial autocorrelation methods, we investigate the spatio-temporal characteristics of green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency during 2011–2022. The geographical detector method integrated with random forest model is employed to identify driving factors. The main result are as follows: (1) Distinct spatial disparities in transition efficiency across the economic belt, with an overall upward trend despite suboptimal efficiency levels. Regional clusters demonstrate intensified agglomeration patterns, exhibiting a “high-east-west, low-central” spatial configuration. (2) Spatial positive correlations show increasing trends, with local spatial clusters predominantly manifesting as high-high or low-low agglomerations. (3) Dynamic variations in factor explanatory power across study years, with enhanced combined effects through factor interactions. Notably, the top three determinants, industrial development level, urban development level, and social consumption level exhibit nonlinear relationships with transition efficiency, while the nature of these relationships varies. This research provides empirical evidence for understanding regional transition mechanisms and offers decision-making support for formulating differentiated green development strategies.

title: Advancing polyhydroxybutyrate-co-polyhydroxyvalerate (PHBV) production from coconut coir pith waste: An intensified and targeted approach for sustainable bioconversion through enzymatic hydrolysis
abstract: The extensive use and indiscriminate disposal of petroleum-derived, non-biodegradable plastics have created an urgent global environmental and health crisis. Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV), a microbial co-biopolymer, represents a promising alternative due to its favorable mechanical and thermal properties. However, its large-scale production is hindered by higher costs than those of conventional plastics. This study establishes an integrated and cost-effective strategy for PHBV production from low-cost coconut coir pith (CCP) hydrolysate using Brevibacillus invocatus MTCC 9039. Sequential alkaline H2O2 pretreatment of CCP resulted in a 67.94% lignin reduction and a 58.46% increase in cellulose content. An intensified fed-batch enzymatic hydrolysis of cellulose-enriched CCP at 15% (w/w) solid loading (5% + 4% + 3% + 2% + 1%) under an intermediate enzyme addition condition, supported by RSM-based pre-optimization, ultrasonication-enhanced enzyme–substrate interaction, and ultrafiltration-based enzyme recycling, yielded 99.74 g/L reducing sugars with a 66.49% conversion efficiency. Utilizing the diluted form of CCP hydrolysate at 30 g/L glucose in combination with 50% (v/v) mineral salt medium, achieved a 66.36% PHB accumulation yield. A fed-batch fermentation strategy with optimized sodium propionate supplementation at 0.2% (w/v) and stepwise CCP hydrolysate feeding at 30 g/L glucose at 72, 96, and 120 h yielded maximum biomass and PHBV titers of 17.76 g/L and 13.6 g/L, respectively. FTIR and NMR analyses confirmed the structural identity of the biopolymer. Overall, this work demonstrates a robust, low-cost, and scalable bioprocess utilizing lignocellulosic waste for efficient PHBV production, advancing the development of sustainable bioplastics.

title: Selective separation of bismuth from high-acid copper electrolytes: design of highly stable antimony-based adsorbent and investigation of strong adsorption mechanisms
abstract: Bismuth (Bi) in high-acid copper electrolytes (HACEs) substantially impairs copper electrolytic refining and cathode copper quality while being a critical strategic metal. Selective separation of Bi from HACEs enables electrolyte purification and Bi resource recovery. Although antimony (Sb)-based purifiers have shown promise as green HACE purification materials, they suffer from high self-dissolution losses, poor selectivity for Bi, and complex synthesis processes. In this study, a highly stable amorphous mesoporous Sb2O5 adsorbent (specific surface area: 109.6 m2/g) was synthesized via a facile one-step water bath method. The adsorbent exhibited exceptional resistance to interference from Cu, As, and H2SO4, thereby enabling effective and selective Bi separation. Under optimal conditions, the adsorbent selectively removed 91.79% of Bi from industrial HACEs to 0.05 g/L— thereby fully meeting the electrolyte purification requirements—with a dissolution loss of only 0.33%. Thermodynamic and kinetic analyses revealed that the adsorption process followed the Langmuir isotherm and a pseudo-second-order kinetic model, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 88.50 mg/g.
