Mechanistic investigations revealed a multistage chemisorption process: electrostatic attraction caused Bi3+/BiO+ to aggregate on the surface of the adsorbent, coordination with the Sb-OH active sites on secondary particles on the adsorbent surface, and finally, localized crystal rearrangement for stable Bi fixation. The Bi-loaded adsorbent achieved Bi separation and recovery through chloride desorption and simultaneously enabled adsorbent regeneration, maintaining a Bi removal rate of more than 80% over five purification cycles. This study provides a promising strategy for the HACE purification and Bi resource recovery.

title: Optimal capacity configuration of the wind-solar-hydrogen multi-energy system for green data computing centers: An integrated AI forecasting and improved multi-objective optimization approach
abstract: The explosive growth of artificial intelligence and cloud computing has triggered an unprecedented global demand for computing power, pushing the energy consumption and carbon footprint of Data Computing Centers (DCCs) to critical levels. Clean energy supply systems are crucial for supporting their sustainable development. This study innovatively integrates concentrated solar power (CSP) and hydrogen storage into the multi-energy system for DCCs, constructing a deep-coupled wind-solar-hydrogen multi-energy complementary system (MCES) tailored to the load coupling characteristics of DCCs. An integrated KOA-ITransformer-BiLSTM model is developed to predict wind-solar output, and Latin hypercube sampling combined with scenario reduction is adopted to characterize and mitigate system uncertainty. A multi-objective optimization model is further established to minimize economic expenditure and carbon emissions while enhancing energy utilization. The study improves the NSGA-III algorithm by adding an NDX-SBX crossover operator to achieve a better solution set. Finally, the optimal capacity configuration is chosen using a multi-attribute decision-making approach. Findings indicate that the optimized wind-solar-hydrogen system demonstrates strong economic and environmental performance for a DCC in Hami, Xinjiang. The optimal configuration achieves 100% energy utilization efficiency, with an annual cost of 7.65 million CNY and annual carbon emissions of 678.25 tons. Compared with the unoptimized scheme, carbon emissions are reduced by over 15%, and both energy efficiency and economic performance are improved. The findings offer practical guidance for advancing low-carbon energy transitions and sustainable development in DCCs and other high-demand campuses.

title: A practical way to reduce slag entrainment during ladle teeming: Regular cleaning of ladle outlet adherents
abstract: In the final stage of ladle teeming, slag entrainment caused by drain sinks degrades molten steel cleanliness and reduces metal yield. Actual ladle outlets often experience clogging and protrusion formation. A water model of a 300-ton ladle was established to study the effect of outlet structure on the critical drainage height for slag entrainment, with varied outlet configurations.​ The results indicated that, for a constant outlet taper, the critical drainage height increased by 27.0% from 21.6 to 27.43 mm as the upper diameter of the discharge cone decreased from 50 to 30 mm; for a fixed lower diameter, it rose slightly by 2.56% from 27.43 to 28.13 mm as the upper diameter was reduced from 30 to 18 mm​ A modified theoretical model, distinguishing between the upper diameter of the discharge cone and the outlet diameter of the nozzle, was developed to explain this trend, which contradicted traditional theoretical models. Furthermore, in the water model, the critical drainage height rose significantly by 86.9% from 28.13 to 52.57 mm as the protrusion height increased from 0 to 30 mm​ Industrial application confirmed that ladle outlet clogging led to a significant increase in residual molten steel, while systematic cleaning of the ladle outlet effectively reduced this residual molten steel. Therefore, it was recommended to regularly clean adherents from the ladle outlet and maintain the integrity of the outlet structure. This practice would help improve metal yield and molten steel cleanliness, thereby advancing cleaner production in steelmaking processes.

title: Decoupled greening and vegetation resilience in the arid Tarim River mainstream and its driving mechanisms
abstract: Vegetation resilience reflects the capacity of ecosystems to withstand and recover from disturbances. However, current research on greenness trends has predominantly focused on changes in vegetation cover or biomass, with limited attention to resilience dynamics and their underlying drivers. Using the arid Tarim River mainstream as a case study, this study quantified vegetation resilience based on the first-order autoregressive coefficient (AR(1)) derived from kNDVI time series during 2000–2020, and identified the environmental drivers of greening and resilience change using random forest models. Results show that the region exhibited significant (p < 0.05) overall greening, yet 51.1% of the area showed a significant (p < 0.05) decline in resilience, and 45.2% of greening areas simultaneously experienced resilience loss, most prominently in the upper and middle reaches. Attribution analysis indicated that greening was dominated by increased surface soil moisture, whereas resilience loss was primarily driven by deep groundwater depletion, with thresholds favorable for greening and resilience maintenance identified as soil moisture trend >0.0005 m3 m−3 yr−1 and groundwater storage anomaly trend > −7.3151 mm yr−1, respectively. Ecological water conveyance improved resilience within the core zones of the lower reaches, but the benefits were spatially constrained, motivating a shift from linear conveyance to spatially distributed delivery with resilience-based zoning and rotational scheduling. Overall, greening does not necessarily imply enhanced resilience, underscoring the value of integrating resilience metrics into future arid ecosystem management.

title: Sustainable hydrogen production from biogas under operational variability: Feed forecasting with a rolling horizon scheduling strategy
abstract: Hydrogen production from biogas is strongly affected by upstream feedstock variability and market fluctuations, creating challenges for efficient and sustainable production planning. This study proposes a digital scheduling framework for hydrogen production via combined steam and CO2 reforming (CSCR), integrating feed forecasting, surrogate modeling, and rolling horizon optimization to enable adaptive operation and support future operational planning under variable conditions. First, detailed process simulations of the integrated CSCR system were conducted to generate technical, economic, and environmental performance data over a wide range of operating conditions. A deep neural network–based surrogate model was then developed to represent the nonlinear behavior of the process with low computational cost. Forecasts of feed biogas CH4 concentration were generated using a gated recurrent unit (GRU) model over a seven-day horizon. Rolling horizon (RH) optimization was employed in a multi-step scheduling scheme to determine optimal daily operating parameters within predefined bounds, aiming to meet hydrogen demand while adapting to predicted feed variability and market fluctuations. The results showed that the GRU model provided accurate forecasts (R2 = 0.9411), enabling advanced estimation of feed biogas composition. Informed by these forecasts, the RH approach allowed flexible adjustment of the CSCR operating parameters, leading to increased hydrogen production, reductions in net CO2-equivalent emissions of up to 1470 kgCO2/day, and improvements in cumulative profit of up to 47% compared with fixed scheduling over the seven-day horizon. Overall, the proposed scheduling approach effectively coordinates production with feedstock and operational fluctuations, enhancing adaptability and supporting sustainable hydrogen production planning.

title: Digital transformation and sustainable industrialization: the role of dynamic digital capabilities and continuous auditing as digital governance
abstract: This study examines the role of digital transformation in promoting sustainable industrialization in resource-limited manufacturing and the functioning of continuous auditing within this framework. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and digital governance, we develop a model of three digital dynamic capabilities (sensing, capturing, and transforming) that drive digital transformation. We also look at how these capabilities, along with continuous auditing, affect sustainable industrialization in Jordanian industrial companies. We use PLS-SEM to analyze survey data from 580 managers across 69 companies. The findings indicate that digital sensing (β = 0.46) and digital transformation capability (β = 0.36) have the most potent effects on digital transformation (R2 = 0.66). In contrast, digital capture (β = 0.09) has a more negligible yet notable effect. Digital transformation significantly enhances sustainable industrialization (β = 0.71, R2 = 0.78), with continuous auditing exerting a notable direct effect (β = 0.58). In contrast, the interaction between digital transformation and continuous auditing is not statistically significant (β = −0.27, p > 0.30), suggesting that, in this context, continuous auditing primarily serves as an independent governance layer rather than a moderating factor. The research situates the outcomes of sustainable industrialization within an information-governance framework. It helps managers and policymakers determine how to integrate digital investments, continuous auditing, and industrial sustainability under resource and regulatory constraints.

title: Cycle efficiency and economic analysis of the Ca-looping thermochemical Carnot battery for coal-fired power plants
abstract: Against the backdrop of the global energy transition, the increasing share of renewable energy poses greater demands on grid flexibility. This paper proposes three Ca-looping thermochemical Carnot battery models for the flexibility retrofit of supercritical coal-fired power plants, enabling dedicated electrical storage, combined thermal and electrical storage, and stable discharge of either electric or thermal energy. Based on the HEATSEP framework and an improved pinch analysis incorporating exergy information, a multi-objective genetic algorithm was developed to evaluate the thermodynamic and economic performance of Carnot batteries operating with different gas working fluids. Results indicate that in pure electrical storage and discharge scenarios, the argon cycle performs best overall, achieving an electrical cycle efficiency of 0.44 and a dynamic payback period of 10.54 years. This model can directly absorb renewable electricity. When solely considering power plant retrofit, the combined thermal and electrical storage model using air as the working fluid proves more competitive. Its efficiency-sensitive (electrical discharge) and investment-sensitive (thermal discharge) configurations achieve cycle efficiencies of 0.44 and 0.37, with dynamic payback periods of 9.0 and 8.1 years, respectively. The Carnot battery can also be extended to integrated solar photovoltaic and photothermal power stations, and demonstrates potential advantages for integrating renewable electricity, which can be intuitively compared with existing commercial energy storage solutions.

title: Exploring urban human mobility patterns and the effects of air pollution and weather conditions from a dockless bike-sharing lens
abstract: Air quality, weather and other environmental conditions affect people's daily lives. Air conditions have improved in many areas due to strict air pollution control measures. However, severe ozone pollution still occurs in some cities due to high temperatures and atmospheric chemical changes. And there is limited evidence on the impact of ozone pollution on urban human behaviour. This study analysed the effects of ozone pollution on urban human mobility and daily activities from the lens of bike-sharing. Firstly, we explored urban human mobility patterns based on spatial and temporal statistics (RQ1). The results confirmed the important role of bike-sharing in bridging the ‘last mile’ to the subway system. Then, based on panel regressions, we analysed the effects of weather, and air pollution on human mobility and daily activities, which were conducted at both city-level (RQ2) and community-level (RQ3). The results indicate that apart from the influence of weather conditions and commuting needs, severe ozone pollution has an inhibitory effect on urban human mobility and daily activities. Depending on the activity types, for every 10 μg/m3 increase in ozone pollution concentration, the number of bike-sharing trips decreased by between 9 (95% CI: 4, 14) and 81 (95% CI: 41, 121) trips. In addition, we find that particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5) is positively associated with human mobility when pollution levels are not severe, which is different from the conventional understanding that PM2.5 can inhibit human activities. Although ozone pollution is difficult for urban residents to perceive directly, early warnings from the air monitoring department will serve as a guide. These findings provide evidence of the impact of ozone pollution on urban human behaviour and can provide references for healthy travel.

title: Enhanced decoupling of multiple elements in coastal reclaimed soils following intensive agricultural use in eastern China
abstract: Understanding the biogeochemical coupling of multiple soil elements is essential to evaluating soil health and ecosystem stability. However, the effects of long-term coastal wetland reclamation on soil elemental enrichment and geochemical interactions remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate the evolution of multi-element behavior in soils across a chronosequence (0, 10, 30, 65, and 90 years) of coastal reclamation. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of 31 elements (including As, Al, B, Br, Ca, Cd, Cl, Co, Cr, Cu, F, Fe, Hg, I, K, Mg, Mn, Mo, N, Na, Ni,C, P, Pb, Rb, S, Sb, Si, Sn, Sr, Zn) in the soils, focusing on exploring the evolution of element enrichment, dispersion, correlation, and multi-element coupling (MEC) along the reclamation gradient during an increase in reclamation duration. The results revealed that several elements were significantly enriched after reclamation, whereas others remained below background levels. Fertilization, irrigation, and intensive cultivation significantly alter the soil geochemical processes and elemental interactions. With the extension of the reclamation duration, the concentrations of organic carbon (SOC), N, P, Zn, Cu, Cd, Hg, F, and Cl increased, whereas those of S, Na, Mg, Ca, Cr, Mn, Sr, Br, As, and Mo decreased, highlighting the regulatory role of agricultural activities in shaping elemental distribution. Temporal declines in the number of positive correlations, mean correlation coefficients, and MEC values suggest progressive weakening of element coupling under human influence. Major elements maintained higher correlation strengths and coupling degrees than minor elements, indicating greater resistance to anthropogenic disturbances. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) revealed that while MEC is primarily regulated by stable natural factors such as soil texture, human activities also serve as key drivers of elemental decoupling because of their continuous and cumulative impacts on soil element interactions. This study provides novel insights into the long-term alteration of geochemical interactions in reclaimed soils and emphasizes the need for sustainable management strategies to preserve soil multifunctionality in coastal reclamation regions.

title: Valorization of waste polyolefins to butene, unsaturated fatty alcohols, and branched alkenes using CO2 and plasma catalyst
abstract: Butene, branched alkenes, and short-chain unsaturated fatty alcohols are among the chemicals that have a wide range of industrial applications in the production of fuels, chemicals, and polymers. In this work, we produced these valuable commodity chemicals from waste plastics using a single-step plasma-catalytic process at atmospheric pressure CO2. The study shows that combining non-thermal plasma and zeolite could convert polyolefins at a temperature of 200 °C within 15 min, producing liquids rich in C5 and C6 branched alkenes and C6-C8 unsaturated fatty alcohols. Additionally, gaseous products include a high yield of butene. Comparative studies indicate that combining CO2 plasma with zeolite synergistically increases reaction rates and alters product compositions. Product selectivity was strongly dependent on reaction conditions, including plasma power, gas flow rates, reactor temperature, and catalyst loading. This process was applicable to common polyolefins and post-consumer polyethylene, indicating that the plasma-catalytic approach has promising potential to valorize waste plastics and greenhouse gas CO2 into versatile chemicals.

title: Optimal scheduling of mixed conventional and modular autonomous bus fleets for sustainable urban transit
abstract: Modular autonomous vehicles (MAVs) are considered a promising solution to mitigating the mismatch between travel demand and service capacity in public transit systems. However, integrating them into existing fleets of conventional human-driven buses (CHBs) introduces a complex scheduling problem that remains unsolved under real-world operational constraints. This study develops a novel optimization framework for mixed fleets comprising CHBs and MAVs on a single route, jointly optimizing bus departure times, vehicle type assignments, and MAV configurations to minimize total cost. The mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model explicitly incorporates vehicle resource limitations, redeployment requirements, and MAV penetration thresholds that reflect regulatory and societal acceptance. Through exact linearization, the MINLP is transformed into a tractable mixed-integer linear programming formulation and solved to global optimality. Numerical results show that the optimal mixed-fleet schedule significantly outperforms CHB-only operations, achieving a total cost reduction of 57.7%. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses quantify the effects of critical factors on optimal results. The findings reveal that: (i) marginal returns to additional modules diminish beyond an optimal threshold, enabling precise inventory planning; (ii) optimal fleet composition depends critically on demand, with MAVs most cost-effective at moderate levels and CHBs preferable under high demand; and (iii) even under a conservative 10% MAV penetration threshold, the mixed fleet outperforms CHB-only operations. These insights confirm the efficacy of the proposed model as a strategic tool for transit agencies in making informed decisions on fleet composition and service design across diverse operational contexts.

title: From imbalance to regulation: Simulating the dynamics and future scenarios of ecosystem service supply-demand in Wuhan using a PLUS-ARIMA-LSTM model
abstract: The intensifying pace of urbanization has rendered the imbalance between ecosystem service supply and demand (ESSD) a pivotal bottleneck for sustainable urban development. Using Wuhan, a rapidly growing megacity in central China, as a case study, this research addresses the pressing challenges of ecological space compression and rising ES demand. An integrated modeling framework was developed by coupling the PLUS land-use change model with a hybrid ARIMA-LSTM predictor. Model validation through 3-fold time series cross validation and dynamic multi-step rolling window validation confirmed its robustness and reliability for long-term projections. This validated framework was applied to systematically analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of ESSD in Wuhan from 2011 to 2023 and to project its future trajectories for 2035 under three contrasting scenarios: Natural Development (NDS), Economic Priority (EPS), and Ecological Conservation (ECS). The results reveal a consistent decline of 11.26% in total ecosystem service value during 2011-2023, driven primarily by the conversion of water bodies and cropland into built-up areas. Spatially, a persistent core-periphery mismatch was identified, with urban cores trapped in a “low supply-high demand” deficit and suburban zones functioning as “high supply-low demand” surplus areas. Scenario projections to 2035 indicate divergent pathways. The EPS would intensify this imbalance, triggering the highest demand growth (+27.21%) and the greatest ecological loss. In contrast, the ECS effectively moderates demand escalation (+12.87%) and best preserves ES supply, highlighting the significant leverage of land-use regulation. This study demonstrates that while urban expansion structurally drives ESSD imbalances, strategic policy interventions can meaningfully reshape their trajectory. The proposed integrated modeling framework offers a replicable tool for simulating ESSD dynamics and assessing policy efficacy. The findings provide a critical scientific foundation for guiding spatial planning and instituting cross-regional ecological compensation mechanisms, with direct implications for sustainable governance in rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: The role of social influence in shaping consumer preferences for plant-based meat
abstract: The increase in global meat consumption has increased the attention devoted to efforts to mitigate the environmental, health, and animal welfare consequences of the livestock industry. With advances in technology, plant-based meat is considered a promising solution with which to reduce the negative impacts of farm-raised meat production. However, consumers often exhibit negative attitudes toward plant-based meat. Social influence plays a key role in shaping consumer behavior, as individuals frequently adapt their actions based on the behavior of others. In this study, we explore whether various forms of social influence, namely word-of-mouth, electronic word-of-mouth, social norms, and neighborhood effects, affect consumer preferences regarding plant-based meat. Based on a labeled hypothetical discrete choice experiment with 1500 Chinese respondents, our results reveal that word-of-mouth and neighborhood effects significantly increase consumer preference for plant-based meat. In contrast, electronic word-of-mouth and social norms show no significant impact. A latent class model identified two consumer clusters: an adopter segment (81%), which is characterized by higher education, incomes, and neighborhood influence and exhibits positive preferences for both farm-raised and plant-based meat, and a smaller reluctant segment (19%), which shows no strong preferences for plant-based meat and is more likely to be married and price sensitive. These findings suggest that targeted, neighborhood-anchored interventions and word-of-mouth campaigns can help accelerate the diffusion of plant-based meat.

title: Interfacial electron-rich centers in MoOx/fine slag derived from mining waste enable durable Li-O2 batteries with enhanced kinetics
abstract: Escalating coal gasification slag generation from the expanding coal chemical industry has intensified environmental and waste-management concerns. Converting coal gasification fine slag into functional energy materials offers a promising pathway for sustainable resource recovery from mining-related solid residues. Here, a heterostructured MoOx/fine slag electrocatalyst is prepared through a scalable pre-activation and hydrothermal growth route. Unlike most waste-derived or biomass-carbon cathodes that mainly serve as conductive hosts, this work leverages the slag-derived mineral–carbon matrix to construct a MoOx–slag heterointerface that drives charge redistribution and creates electronically activated interfacial sites referred to as interfacial electron-rich centers. These sites, associated with reduced Mo species, oxygen-vacancy-related defects, and oxygen-containing surface groups, accelerate oxygen redox kinetics and promote more reversible Li2O2 formation and decomposition. Under capacity-limited galvanostatic cycling, lithium–oxygen batteries using the MoOx/fine slag cathode deliver a low voltage polarization of 0.66 V at 500 mA g−1 and maintain stable operation for 246 cycles at a fixed capacity of 1000 mAh g−1. Compared with pristine MoO2, the polarization is reduced from 1.04 V to 0.66 V and the cycling duration is extended from about 200 h to over 1200 h, demonstrating markedly improved reversibility and durability. Ex situ characterization combined with density functional theory analysis indicates that the heterointerface modulates intermediate adsorption and steers Li2O2 reaction pathways. This study provides a waste-to-value strategy and mechanistic guidance for designing durable heterostructured cathode catalysts for advanced metal–air batteries.

title: Enhanced chalcopyrite bioleaching performance through CO2-driven process intensification
abstract: Chalcopyrite, a major copper-bearing mineral, exhibits limited industrial bioleaching efficiency due to slow oxidation and surface passivation. To explore process intensification, this study evaluated the effect of 5% (v/v) CO2 to supplementation on chalcopyrite bioleaching performance. Under carbon-free conditions, elevated CO2 promoted microbial biomass accumulation and carbon assimilation, accompanied by accelerated Fe2+ oxidation and more dynamic interfacial redox activity. Compared with air controls, CO2 enrichment shortened the bioleaching cycle by two days, increased cell density by 41.6% ± 3.75%, and improved Cu2+ extraction efficiency by 31.7% ± 4.58%. SEM-EDS, XRD, electrochemical measurements, and XPS analyses confirmed increased mineral dissolution, biomass accumulation, faster charge transfer, and a lower relative accumulation of passivating surface species under CO2-enriched conditions. These results suggest that moderate CO2 supplementation can serve as a functional process-enhancing factor in chalcopyrite bioleaching and provide process-level insight into CO2-coupled biohydrometallurgical systems.

title: Evaluating the role of onboard carbon capture and storage system in remedial unit balancing under the IMO net-zero framework: Insights from GFI and 4E analysis
abstract: With the introduction of the International Maritime Organization net-zero Framework, the methodology for calculating remedial units based on GFI (GHG Fuel Intensity) has been implemented. This study investigates the contribution of OCCS (onboard carbon capture and storage) system to different fuel remedial units. The OCCS system is developed with EEDI (Energy Efficiency Design Index) phase III requirement as the baseline for operation. The study examines the extent to which the OCCS system improved fuel GFIattained values and compares changes in remedial units required by ships before and after equipping OCCS. 4E (energy, exergy, economic and environmental) analyses are conducted on the system, focusing on comparing changes in the system's PBP (payback period) before and after implementing the GFI framework. The results indicate the optimized average values for diesel, LNG (Liquefied Natural Gas), methanol, LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas), and ethane fuels are 15.65%, 12.05%, 13.15%, 16.71%, and 16.91% under the EEDI phase III requirement. Furthermore, at the same CO2 captured amount (800 kg/h), LNG with OCCS profits for six consecutive years (2028-2033) and reduces the average PBP by 1.40 years. Its average remedial unit is only 21.47 × 104 $, while the average revenue reaches 133.36 × 104 $. Meanwhile, the system achieved the highest energy efficiency (27.04%) and primary energy saving (5.85 MW) when using LNG cold energy. Additionally, it is important to set the liquid-to-gas ratio to approximately 1.0-1.2 to avoid the negative effects of absorption reaction saturation. In summary, the OCCS system plays a positive role in achieving the net-zero framework.

title: Stable methane storage via hydrate-based composite coating systems
abstract: Although solid natural gas (SNG) represents a promising approach for large-scale natural gas storage, its further development is limited by the thermodynamic instability of gas hydrates under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. To overcome this challenge, this study proposes a composite storage system in which sII-type CP/CH4 hydrates encapsulate sI-type CH4 hydrates, aiming to enhance the thermal stability of the hydrate system under atmospheric pressure. A systematic investigation was conducted to evaluate the effects of various kinetic hydrate promoters (KHPs), storage temperature, the water consumption ratio during sII-type CP/CH4 and sI-type CH4 hydrate formation (defined as the Rc value), and the storage density of sI-type CH4 hydrate on the thermodynamic stability of the composite system. Experimental results demonstrate that hydrate decomposition behavior varies depending on the type of KHPs employed. The system exhibits good stability at temperatures above the ice point; however, decomposition gradually increases with rising storage temperature. At 285.15 K, the composite system achieves a low hydrate decomposition rate of only 10.35 % over 14 days, with a comprehensive gas storage capacity of 125.28 v/v. The Rc value significantly influences system stability: higher Rc values enhance stability but lead to a reduction in overall gas storage capacity. Furthermore, under fixed Rc value conditions, increased storage density of sI-type CH4 hydrate correlates with decreased stability. These findings provide a robust theoretical foundation and practical technical guidance for advancing efficient and stable SNG storage technologies.

title: Single-atom calcium catalysts with C-N-Ca coordination improve the efficiency of preparing olefins from plastics
abstract: Catalytic pyrolysis of waste plastics to high-value olefins offers a sustainable route to address pressing global white pollution and realize plastic resource recycling, yet it faces a long-standing core dilemma limiting industrial application: low-cost calcium-based catalysts suffer from critical activity and stability defects under high-temperature conditions, while high-performance single-atom catalysts rely heavily on expensive noble or transition metals with poor industrial scalability. Notably, alkaline-earth metal single-atom catalysts remain largely underexplored for this high-temperature plastic pyrolysis application, with no mature catalytic system reported to date. Herein, we designed and fabricated a calcium single-atom catalyst with a well-defined carbon-nitrogen-calcium coordination structure through a facile synthetic strategy, to address these technical bottlenecks and enable efficient polypropylene pyrolysis for targeted olefin production. Calcium atoms are atomically dispersed and stably anchored on nitrogen-doped carbon supports via C-N bonds, fully overcoming the sintering-induced deactivation and active site loss of traditional calcium oxide-based catalysts. This catalyst exhibits an outstanding pyrolysis oil yield of 96.19 wt% with 73.82 wt% olefin selectivity; it also markedly reduces reaction activation energy, promotes selective β-scission of polymer chains, suppresses undesired byproduct formation, and retains atomic-level dispersion even after multiple cyclic reactions. This work provides a low-cost, high-efficiency catalyst for waste plastic upcycling, and lays a critical theoretical foundation for the rational design of alkaline-earth metal single-atom catalysts for high-temperature pyrolysis systems.

title: Environmental and economic assessments of novel polyurethane prepolymer modified porous asphalt: A case study in Hong Kong
abstract: Porous asphalt (PA) has gained increasing attention in pavement engineering due to its benefits in stormwater management and traffic noise reduction. However, its open-graded structure generally results in lower durability and a shorter service life compared to dense-graded asphalt mixtures. Recent research show that modification with polyurethane prepolymer (PUP) can effectively improve the durability and longevity of PA. Despite these technical advantages, quantitative assessments of its environmental and economic impacts are lacking. To address this research gap, this study investigates PUP-modified PA (PU-PA) as a sustainable alternative to conventional styrene-butadiene-styrene-modified PA (SBS-PA) using a life cycle perspective. Initial production and construction costs, along with associated greenhouse gas emissions, were quantified and comparatively analyzed for both materials. A life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost assessment (LCCA) were then conducted to evaluate the environmental and economic performance of PU-PA. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis was performed to identify critical factors influencing its economic feasibility. Results indicate that, despite slightly increased initial costs and emissions, PU-PA offers significant life cycle economic and environmental benefits due to its enhanced mechanical properties and extended service life. Sensitivity analysis identified three critical factors affecting the economic viability of PU-PA: service life, PUP content, and PUP cost. The findings of this study support the feasibility of adopting PU-PA as an innovative and sustainable paving material over conventional modified porous asphalt.

title: Anthropogenic activities drive variability in Dissolved Organic Matter composition and characteristics among and within reservoirs
abstract: Reservoirs are critical water sources for drinking and agricultural supply, with their dissolved organic matter (DOM) strongly influenced by anthropogenic intensity. This study examined the impact of anthropogenic activities on the composition and characteristics of DOM in reservoirs from the same region, employing three-dimensional excitation-emission matrix spectroscopy (3D-EEM), Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), and microbiome analysis. The results suggest that anthropogenic activities may significantly influence the composition and characteristics of surface DOM in reservoirs. In the reservoir, DOM under lower anthropogenic intensity was dominated by microbial metabolites (Peak T) and characterized by nonoxygen-heteroatom free (CHO) and nitrogen-containing (CHON) compounds, reflecting a primarily endogenous origin. In contrast, the reservoir DOM under higher anthropogenic intensity was enriched in anthropogenic humic acids (Peak C1), with chlorine-containing (CHOCl) and phosphorus-containing (CHOP) compounds as signature components, indicating combined anthropogenic and endogenous inputs. Relative to drinking water source reservoirs, DOM in the agricultural irrigation reservoir that experienced greater anthropogenic activity was more humified and exhibited a higher abundance of sulfur-containing (CHOS) compounds. Furthermore, the transformation and characteristics of DOM at different depths in reservoirs may be jointly influenced by photochemical degradation and microbial metabolism, while the impacts of anthropogenic activities are attenuated. The study suggests that the differential impacts of anthropogenic activities on reservoir DOM, support improved management of drinking water sources.

title: How to account for the unaccounted? An analysis of governance barriers to consumption-based carbon accounting in European cities
abstract: Cities across the world are committed to carbon neutrality, playing an essential role in reducing global greenhouse gas emissions (GHG). However, the impact, effectiveness, and credibility of emission reduction depends on the methodology used to measure and track carbon emissions. Whilst production-based carbon accounting (PBCA) is the most common approach, consumption-based carbon accounting (CBCA) produces a more comprehensive overview of GHG emissions through accounting for emissions produced via the consumption of goods and services. These emissions, which are produced beyond the city boundary, are observed within academic literature as a key source of urban carbon emissions, resulting in their reduction as being of significance within urban decarbonisation efforts. However, CBCA is a more complex process than PBCA, and is seldom implemented at the urban level. This paper aims to fill a gap in the literature and inform urban carbon accounting practice by providing a critical overview of the governance barriers and challenges facing cities when adopting CBCA. Through 17 in-depth semi-structured interviews conducted with practitioners across European cities, findings reveal that data-related challenges, political uncertainty, lack of jurisdiction, and difficulties to influence individual consumption patterns are interlinked barriers which influence further integration of CBCA practices. Key barrier relationships and feedback loops, which collectively constrain the transition towards CBCA, are also presented, along with potential approaches towards reducing the impact of the identified barriers, with this paper arguing for greater inter-city collaboration as a means of supporting wider adoptions of CBCA.

title: Seasonal estrogenic exposure in reclaimed-water systems: Microbial community associations, functional pathway responses, and cellular tolerance signatures
abstract:
Background
Residual estrogenic compounds in reclaimed-water-associated systems may pose endocrine-related ecological risks, but their links with microbial community responses and cellular tolerance signatures remain unclear.
Methods
Secondary effluents from three wastewater treatment plants in Jilin City, Northeast China, were collected during dry, normal-flow, and wet periods. Five estrogenic compounds (E1, E2, E3, EE2, and BPA) were quantified by LC-MS/MS and evaluated using risk quotients. Microbial responses were examined using 16S/18S rRNA profiling, estrogen–taxon correlation analysis, metatranscriptomic pathway mapping, molecular docking, TEM, LiP-MS, and DESI-MSI.
Results
Estrogenic compounds showed hydrological-period-dependent variation, with generally higher concentrations during the dry period. Concentrations ranged from ND–10.25 ng/L for E2, 3.59–186.97 ng/L for E1, 4.18–230.37 ng/L for E3, 2.08–34.04 ng/L for EE2, and 5.38–61.97 ng/L for BPA. Risk assessment indicated potential ecological risk for steroidal estrogens, especially EE2, while BPA showed borderline risk. Bacterial associations were more evident during dry and normal-flow periods, whereas eukaryotic associations were stronger during the wet period. Metatranscriptomics indicated steroid-transformation-related responses involving redox transformation, hydroxylation, methylation, glucuronidation, and sulfation. TEM, LiP-MS, and DESI-MSI further indicated ultrastructural remodeling, protein-level perturbation, and redistribution of amphiphilic or lipid-like ions under estrogen exposure.
Conclusions
Seasonal estrogenic exposure in reclaimed-water-associated secondary effluents was linked to microbial community co-variation, steroid-transformation-related functional shifts, proteostasis-associated remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and lipid/interface-associated redistribution, providing multi-level indicators for monitoring and safer reclaimed-water reuse.

title: A digital-enabled circular recovery system for post-consumer inhalers: Linking material recovery, behaviour, and carbon reduction
abstract: The widespread use of inhalers for chronic respiratory diseases generates a growing stream of complex post-consumer medical waste, with limited material recovery and significant environmental impacts. However, existing approaches remain fragmented and fail to integrate user behaviour, reverse logistics, and environmental performance into a unified circular system. This study presents a pilot-scale real-world implementation framework for a digitally supported circular recovery system that links consumption behaviour with material recovery processes in a real-world setting. A total of 1173 inhaler devices were collected through a digitally supported traceability system functioning as an operational coordination mechanism for reverse logistics, enabling the quantification of material flows and recyclability across different device types under pilot-scale operational conditions. The results show that 47.50 kg of recyclable materials were recovered, with device-level recyclability ranging from 18.29% to 90.53%, highlighting the critical influence of product design on material recovery efficiency. A life cycle assessment (LCA) using an avoided burden approach provided a pilot-scale estimate of 103.52 kg CO2e (carbon dioxide equivalent) reduction. While the absolute reduction at pilot scale was modest, illustrative scenario-based extrapolation suggests potential cumulative environmental benefits under broader implementation scenarios, although logistics-adjusted estimates would be lower and require further validation. The system integrates digital traceability functions intended to support recovery coordination and reduce operational uncertainty associated with dispersed post-consumer waste streams. This study provides an exploratory implementation framework for decentralised post-consumer inhaler recovery within a clinical setting. The findings suggest that integration of design-for-disassembly (DfD), extended producer responsibility (EPR), and digital traceability infrastructures may facilitate future circular healthcare transitions and net-zero initiatives.

title: Climate impacts and sustainable implications of large-scale desert solar farms across regions
abstract: The unsustainability of fossil fuel-based energy sources has made large-scale renewable energy deployment an urgent policy priority, with desert solar farms increasingly promoted as a low-carbon solution. However, whether large-scale desert solar farms alter climate systems and affect long-term sustainability remains unclear. Using a slab-ocean global climate model with photovoltaic-induced energy-balance changes, we assess distinct climate effects of large-scale desert solar farms across regions. We find that although local warming is modest, solar farms generate hemispheric heating asymmetries that reorganize atmospheric circulation and redistribute precipitation across monsoon and dryland regions. The magnitude of these impacts depends strongly on location, with installations in North Africa exerting disproportionately large remote effects. Consequently, climate-vulnerable regions such as the Sahel, South Asia, and Brazil experience contrasting precipitation responses. These findings, derived from thermodynamic climate simulations, demonstrate that large-scale desert solar farms are not climate-neutral and highlight the need to integrate climate teleconnections into renewable energy planning for sustainable development.

title: Global shipping pollutant emissions from 1970 to 2022: spatiotemporal changes and exposures
abstract: Global shipping plays a crucial role in international trade but has significant environmental and social implications due to pollutant emissions. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of shipping-related pollutant emissions from 1970 to 2022 and examines population exposure disparities between the Global North and South. Using EDGAR v8.1 dataset, this research quantifies emissions of eight major pollutants (SO2, NOX, PM2.5, BC, CO, NMVOC, NH3, OC) and their exposure in coastal cities worldwide. The study employs multi-scale statistical analyses, including correlation assessments and trend decomposition, to identify long-term patterns and inequalities in pollution exposure. The findings reveal that shipping-related emissions have increased substantially over the past five decades, particularly in the Global South. Between 1970 and 2022, NOX emissions in the South surged by 270.87 t/yr, while the North exhibited a net reduction of −19.61 t/yr. Similarly, SO2 emissions in the South increased by 178.39 t/yr, whereas the North saw a decrease of −23.40 t/yr. Strong correlations exist between pollutant exposure and GDP, with a correlation coefficient of 0.79 (p = 0) for NOX,suggesting that higher-income coastal cities bear disproportionate pollution burdens. Additionally, shipping carbon emissions exhibit a robust association with population exposure, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.462 to 0.846, further highlighting the environmental risks borne by densely populated regions. This study underscores the urgent need for equitable environmental governance and targeted emission reduction policies to address pollution disparities, particularly in the Global South.

title: Energy- and oxidant-efficient VUV/H2O2 polishing via surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning
abstract: Vacuum ultraviolet/hydrogen peroxide (VUV/H2O2) advanced oxidation is a promising polishing strategy for low-total-organic-carbon (TOC) high-purity water systems. However, its practical operation is constrained by coupled trade-offs among TOC removal, residual H2O2, and energy demand, often leading to inefficient energy use and excessive oxidant consumption. This study developed a surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework for energy- and oxidant-efficient single-pass VUV/H2O2 polishing under low-TOC conditions, using methanol as a neutral low-molecular-weight model organic. A high-fidelity COMSOL multiphysics model was used to generate simulation data, and a deep neural network (DNN) surrogate replaced direct simulations, reducing evaluation time from minutes-scale COMSOL calculations to second-scale prediction and enabling scalable policy learning. Among the evaluated RL algorithms, Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) achieved the best performance under a multi-objective formulation integrating TOC removal, residual H2O2, electrical energy per order (EEO), and apparent reaction kinetic performance. The optimized policy identified operating regimes characterized by low energy consumption (EEO ≤ 2.5 kWh m−3 order−1), sufficient hydraulic throughput (>79 mL min−1), and high TOC removal (>71.8 %). Experimental validation confirmed the applicability of the optimized policy, with RL predictions agreeing with measurements within 1.5–3.4 % for TOC removal. Compared with an empirical baseline under identical influent conditions, the optimized operation increased TOC removal by 18.0 percentage points, from 58.3 % to 76.3 %, while reducing EEO by 55.8 %, from 4.39 to 1.94 kWh m−3 order−1. These results demonstrate that integrating physics-based modeling, surrogate learning, and RL can support energy-efficient and residual-oxidant-aware operation of VUV/H2O2 polishing, providing a scalable pathway toward resource-efficient water treatment.

title: Comprehensive 12E assessment of hybrid nano-PCM and metal-mesh PVT-integrated hexagonal solar still for sustainable desalination
abstract: Growing global demand for renewable energy and freshwater resources integrated, long-term solutions, especially in water-constrained and off-grid areas. This work describes a novel hybrid solar system that combines a photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) unit with a hexagonal solar still (HSS), with the goal of addressing both energy and water scarcity through improved thermal energy recovery and storage that rarely explored in previous studies. A key innovation lies in the development of a hybrid nano-phase change material (HNPCM), composed of paraffin wax, graphene, Al2O3 nanoparticles, and radial metal mesh, which significantly improves thermal conductivity and latent heat storage. Six HSS configurations were developed and experimentally evaluated using combinations of sensible and latent heat storage materials such as granite, black sand, and metal sponge. The system was comprehensively assessed under a 12E framework covering energy, exergy, economic, environmental, and sustainability metrics. Results showed that the optimized PVT module (Panel 4) achieved a peak overall energy efficiency of 92.05% (combined electrical and thermal heat extraction). Furthermore, the integrated HSS system achieved a 60.22% higher freshwater yield, while the modified PV panel demonstrated a 24.09% relative improvement in electrical efficiency over the conventional system. Energy payback time was reduced to 0.266 years, and CO2 emissions mitigation reaching 1042.5 kg/year. The study demonstrates a scalable, multifunctional design suitable for decentralized applications, aligning with circular economy principles. This work contributes to the advancement of low-carbon, resource-efficient solar technologies for cleaner production in developing and climate-vulnerable regions.

title: Carbon footprints of RFID labels in mass production
abstract: This study presents the first comparative carbon footprint assessment of four industrially manufactured UHF RFID label technologies under an identical design framework, addressing a critical knowledge gap in understanding the environmental impacts of emerging RFID manufacturing processes. While RFID labels have become essential for supply chain traceability, inventory management, and digital product identification, limited studies have quantified and compared the carbon footprints of different antenna fabrication technologies using primary industrial production data. In this work, cradle-to-gate carbon footprints were evaluated for four commercially relevant RFID label types manufactured using etching, printing, laser die-cutting, and embroidery processes. The assessment was based on detailed manufacturing inventories collected from industrial production lines, including material consumption, energy use, and process-specific inputs. The results demonstrate that RFID labels fabricated using laser die-cut antennas exhibited the lowest carbon footprint, indicating the environmental benefits of simplified manufacturing routes and reduced material waste. In contrast, labels produced using embroidery technology showed the highest carbon footprint under current manufacturing conditions, primarily due to the high environmental burden associated with silver-coated conductive yarns. However, embroidery-based RFID labels also displayed the greatest long-term potential for carbon reduction because of their simplified process chain, eliminating several conventional manufacturing steps. Across all technologies, antenna conductor material was identified as the dominant contributor to overall greenhouse gas emissions, with aluminium based conductors exhibiting substantially lower carbon footprints than silver-based alternatives. These findings provide new insights into the environmental performance of RFID technologies and offer practical guidance for developing more sustainable label solutions aligned with global net-zero goals.

title: Reducing the carbon footprint of asphalt production through crude oil selection guided by refining history
abstract: Asphalt production is a carbon-intensive industrial process, yet refineries lack predictive tools to link crude oil characteristics to final binder performance. This knowledge gap forces conservative, energy-intensive over-distillation, unnecessarily increasing the carbon footprint of pavement materials. Here we explore whether machine learning can decode the crude-to-binder structural evolution to enable a cleaner production pathway. Tracking two crude oils through laboratory-scale refining (crude oil, atmospheric residue, vacuum residue, asphalt binder), we combine multi-scale characterization with Random Forest analysis to identify which molecular features govern pavement performance. We identify preliminary evidence for a temperature-dependent switching mechanism: high-temperature performance is associated with peak molecular weight (Mp) and methylene-to-methyl ratio (ICH2/CH3), while fatigue resistance shows links to asphaltene content and sulfur content. These findings translate into three strategies for reducing carbon emissions: (i) pre-refining selection of crude oils with favorable molecular profiles, avoiding over-distillation of marginal crudes; (ii) targeted process control to engineer these molecular features, replacing empirical trial-and-error; and (iii) climate-tailored binder design to eliminate over-processing. Unsupervised clustering indicates that crude oil molecular fingerprints reflect final binder performance, suggesting the feasibility of crude selection. This work offers a knowledge-driven perspective that replaces energy-intensive over-processing with predictive design, contributing to low-carbon asphalt production and sustainable infrastructure.

title: In situ Zn-substituted CuFe2O4 for enhanced peroxymonosulfate activation and antibiotic degradation in real wastewater
abstract: The persistence of antibiotic residues poses a severe threat to ecosystems and human health. While sulfate radical-based advanced oxidation processes (SR-AOPs) are effective for tetracycline degradation, their engineering application faces three major bottlenecks: low persulfate utilization efficiency, challenging solid-liquid separation of powdered catalysts, and metal ion leaching leading to secondary pollution. This work reports a synergistic strategy that integrates atomic-scale Zn2+ doping with macroscopic immobilization to simultaneously overcome these limitations in a CuFe2O4 platform. Theoretical and experimental analyses revealed that Zn2+, with its d10 configuration, preferentially occupies the tetrahedral sites in CuFe2O4. This doping inhibits Jahn-Teller distortion, reduces Cu ion leaching to 0.8 mg/L, and optimizes the electronic structure, significantly increasing the Cu+/Cu2+ ratio. Consequently, the rate constant for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation and tetracycline degradation reached 0.1329 min−1, which is 3 times as higher as that of the undoped sample. The optimal catalyst (Zn0.2CFO) maintained high activity across a broad pH range (3–11) and under high ionic strength. Critically, the powder separation bottleneck was overcome through sodium alginate-Ca2+ dynamic crosslinking, transforming the nano-powder into millimeter-sized granules that preserve active site accessibility. In fixed-bed reactors treating real aquaculture wastewater, the granular catalyst achieves >99.99% tetracycline removal with zero powder loss and no secondary pollution. This work demonstrates a synergistic atomic-level doping regulation and macroscopic-level structure immobilization strategy, providing a novel pathway for designing advanced oxidation catalysts with high activity, stability, and engineering practicality.

title: Bioelectrochemical enhancement for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons degradation in saline wastewater
abstract: The biological treatment and biogas recovery of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in high-salinity wastewater from coal chemical industries are often severely inhibited by salt stress, resulting in low efficiency and a lack of energy recovery. This study proposes that weak current intervention in anaerobic digestion offers an effective method for treating high-salinity PAH wastewater. Anaerobic degradation was conducted on salinity (up to 5%) wastewater containing naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene. Weak current intervention (0.8 V) significantly enhanced PAHs degradation efficiency, with the total organic carbon removal rate increasing by up to 2.5 times, a peak degradation efficiency of 1307.8 mg/(L∙d), and removal rates of naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene reaching 99.3%, 98.9%, and 94.0% in 4 days, respectively. When applied to coal chemical wastewater treatment, the chemical oxygen demand removal rate was increased to approximately threefold, with removal rates of naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene at 79.38%, 79.44%, and 81.39% in 4 days, respectively. Notably, methane and hydrogen were collected at volumes of 73.23 ± 0.50 mL and 5.94 ± 0.23 mL per cycle, respectively, corresponding to an energy recovery rate of 109.6% of the input electrical energy, excluding the energy from organic matter in wastewater. Moreover, weak current intervention enhanced microbial activity, adenosine triphosphate activity, and microbial diversity, while promoting the enrichment of salt-tolerant, halophilic, and methanogenic microorganisms. Distinct microbial community shifts were observed under weak current-assisted conditions, indicating enhanced biological adaptation to salinity stress and improved anaerobic treatment performance. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of applying weak current-assisted anaerobic digestion to real coal chemical wastewater and highlight its potential for simultaneous pollutant removal and energy recovery in high-salinity industrial wastewater treatment.

title: Cleaner transportation through energy-oriented vehicle routing under disrupted arcs
abstract: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) represents a challenging optimization task with direct implications for energy consumption, emissions, and sustainable transportation. In this study, we extend classical VRP formulations to account for the effects of arc disruptions, such as road closures, congestion, or infrastructure failures, on energy efficiency and service reliability. We investigated three models: the single-depot capacitated VRP, the single-depot VRP with time windows, and the VRP with simultaneous pickup and delivery, all of which were reformulated to account for disruption probabilities and arc availability. A normalized energy-impact measure, reflecting the environmental implications of routing decisions (including potential CO2 emissions), is embedded into the objective function. A Genetic Algorithm is developed to solve these models efficiently, and numerical experiments, supported by sensitivity analyses, highlight the trade-offs between resilience, energy use, and service quality. The results demonstrate that the proposed energy-oriented, disruption-aware models yield more realistic, environmentally responsible, and cleaner routing strategies than conventional VRPs. This work underscores the potential of integrating energy and disruption considerations into vehicle routing to promote sustainability in logistics and support cleaner production practices.

title: Magnetic response associated enhancement of magneto-Fenton degradation of p-Nitrophenol over amorphous FeSiB
abstract: P-Nitrophenol (p-NP) is a refractory organic pollutant that can be removed by Fenton oxidation. However, the efficiency of conventional Fenton oxidation is often limited by sluggish Fe redox cycling. Herein, an amorphous Fe93.7Si3.1B3.2 alloy (FeSiB) was employed to construct a magnetic field assisted Fenton system for efficient p-NP degradation. Under a static magnetic field of 130 mT, FeSiB achieved 95.0% p-NP removal within 15 min, with a reaction rate constant 5.6 times that under non-magnetic conditions. Comparative experiments using weakly magnetic FeCrMo and annealed FeSiB indicate that the magnetic response of FeSiB is closely associated with its magneto-Fenton enhancement, although the activity is not governed solely by bulk magnetization. Mössbauer spectroscopy reveals Fe-centered local environments with pronounced magnetic hyperfine interactions and metallic character, which may facilitate Fe redox cycling during H2O2 activation. Combined XPS, Fe-leaching, filtration, radical-quenching, fluorescence, and open-circuit potential results suggest that the enhancement arises from coupled FeSiB surface-mediated H2O2 activation, improved Fe2+ availability, dissolved Fe-assisted redox cycling, and magnetic field affected interfacial behavior. TOC and LC-MS analyses further show partial mineralization through hydroxylation, oxidative denitration, oxidation, and ring-opening reactions. This work provides guidance for designing intrinsically magnetic amorphous catalysts for wastewater treatment.

title: Mechanistic insights into coupled Fe–S–N cycling in constructed wetlands: potential contributions of cable bacteria and their community associations
abstract: Cable bacteria exhibit remarkable electron-transfer capabilities and are commonly enriched in sulfur (S)-rich environments, where they actively interact with diverse microorganisms. However, the potential link between cable bacteria-mediated S cycling and nitrogen (N) metabolism in constructed wetlands (CWs) remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, four sets of CWs with different Fe and S conditions were developed under near-natural conditions to investigate the underlying microbial mechanisms. The findings showed that cable bacteria functioned as key modular hubs within the microbial network, linking abiotic FeS2-mediated electron-transfer processes with biogeochemical S cycling. By employing long-distance electron transfer (LDET) and extracellular electron transfer (EET), cable bacteria enhanced the quinone pool capacity of N-removing bacteria. They promoted direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) within S-autotrophic denitrification (SAD) pathways and among associated microbial populations. This electron-transfer mechanism contributed to the coupled Fe–S–N cycle, resulting in a 30.89% increase in nitrogen removal efficiency compared with CWs-CK. Overall, this study provides novel insights into the synergistic interactions among S, Fe, and microbial communities, offering a mechanistic basis for optimizing SAD-based processes in CWs.

title: Is ESG always profitable? Sustainability transition and dimension-level evidence from an emerging market banking system
abstract: Banks play a central role in financing sustainability transitions by allocating credit to firms engaged in green investment, climate-risk adaptation, and cleaner production activities. Yet empirical evidence on whether ESG engagement improves bank profitability remains mixed, partly because ESG is often measured through composite indices that combine heterogeneous environmental, social, and governance dimensions. This study examines whether ESG measurement design shapes the observed ESG–profitability relationship in a regulated emerging market banking system. Using panel data from BIST-listed banking institutions in Türkiye with available Refinitiv ESG data over the 2016–2023 period, the study estimates fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors to compare composite and dimension-specific ESG specifications. ESG variables are lagged to partially reduce simultaneity concerns, while the estimates are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects. The results show that the composite ESG score is not statistically associated with bank profitability, measured by return on assets (ROA). When ESG is decomposed into its individual pillars, only the social dimension exhibits a negative and statistically significant short-term association, whereas the environmental and governance dimensions remain insignificant. This pattern suggests that composite ESG scores may obscure dimension-specific financial dynamics, although limited statistical power, unequal pillar variation, measurement error, and finite-sample instability remain plausible alternative explanations. The study provides context-specific evidence that ESG measurement design matters for sustainable banking and cleaner production financing. For regulators, bank boards, and ESG reporting units, the findings are consistent with the practical value of pillar-level ESG assessment. Whether the environmental pillar translates into green credit allocation, transition finance, and long-term cleaner production investment remains a direction for future research rather than a finding directly established by this analysis.

title: Evolution path of anti-involution in photovoltaic enterprises driven by digital twin technology
abstract: In the context of the global energy transition and the “dual carbon” goals, China's photovoltaic industry is trapped in an involutionary dilemma characterized by overcapacity, homogenized competition, price wars, declining profits, and low operational efficiency. Traditional decision-making methods are inadequate for supporting dynamic and quantitative anti-involution governance. To address these challenges and optimize strategic decision-making, this paper introduces digital twin technology into the decision management of the photovoltaic industry. Based on data from 98 listed photovoltaic companies between 2020 and 2024, this study processes the indicators, calculates a comprehensive price, and constructs a baseline real-time information matrix. Three proactive anti-involution strategies are designed: price increases, Research and Development (R&D) investment, and combined strategy, along with a passive non-intervention option. A 300-day dynamic simulation matrix iteration mechanism is established, and a profit and loss evaluation model is constructed to quantify the decision effects. The research results show that while a pure price increase can improve short-term profits, it lacks sustainability. Independent R&D investment can enhance product differentiation but increases financial pressure. Within the proposed simulation framework, the combined strategy achieves the highest comprehensive profit and loss value among all tested alternatives, suggesting that the simultaneous pursuit of value-recovery pricing and R&D intensification offers a structurally superior path for balancing short-term profit recovery with long-term technological upgrade needs, subject to the model's calibration assumptions and the absence of strategic competitor retaliation. This study extends the application of digital twin technology to the field of industrial strategic decision-making and constructs a quantitative anti-involution framework, providing a reference for companies to escape low-price competition, optimize resource allocation, and achieve high-quality development.

title: Urban organisms’ metabolic laws and policy effects: A weight-physique perspective
abstract: Rapid urbanization has given rise to severe resource consumption and environmental pollution, which can be conceptualized as urban material and pollutant metabolism issues. Drawing parallels between cities and natural organisms, this study treats cities as “urban organisms” and explores how urban weight (population, GDP, built-up area) and physique (industrial structure-based functional types) shape urban metabolism, aiming to enhance the sustainability of urban material metabolism. Using 20 typical Chinese megacities as cases, we analyzed metabolic patterns from 2000 to 2020 and projected future trajectories (2025–2035) under policy intervention and no-policy scenarios. The results reveal that urban weight and metabolic scale exhibit a negative allometric growth pattern (coefficient = 0.76), analogous to natural organisms. Metabolic characteristics vary significantly across urban physique types, with material consumption structure and metabolic network functionality being most notably differentiated. Policy interventions are projected to reduce urban metabolic scale by approximately 20%, improve the metabolic network functionality of over 50% of cities, and refine the allometric growth coefficient to 0.75, bringing it closer to Kleiber's Law. This study provides a metabolic perspective on sustainable urban transitions, underscoring the necessity of tailoring governance strategies to specific urban physiques to mitigate metabolic pressures from expansion, providing evidence-based insights for sustainable urban policy-making.

title: Unveiling the role of soil in urban vegetation greenness: City-scale evidence from field sampling across green spaces in Shanghai
abstract: Urban green spaces (UGSs) provide essential ecological functions in highly urbanized landscapes, yet city-scale associations between soil conditions and vegetation greenness remain insufficiently understood due to limited field-based evidence. This study investigated Shanghai, China, by integrating long-term Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) time-series data from 2000 to 2020 with field soil sampling from 183 UGS sites, covering 18 edaphic properties. Together with vegetation baseline, human activity, and climate covariates, we assessed the relative and spatially heterogeneous associations of soil conditions with vegetation greenness dynamics (VGD) and current vegetation greenness (VG). Shanghai's UGSs showed substantially stronger greening than the broader urban background, with a mean VGD of 0.074 decade−1 compared with 0.017 decade−1 citywide, and 87.98% of sampled sites exhibited positive greening trends. Park green spaces maintained higher VG and stronger VGD than roadside green spaces, while VGD and VG were significantly but only moderately associated, indicating that they represent distinct dimensions of UGS performance. Attribution analysis showed that vegetation baseline and soil properties were the dominant contributors to VGD, explaining 17% and 11% of the variance, respectively. For VG, soil emerged as the leading determinant, independently explaining 15% of spatial variation, with associations distributed across multiple edaphic dimensions rather than controlled by a single soil property. Spatial modeling further revealed scale-dependent soil associations: soil–VGD associations were strongest in intermediate and outer urban zones, whereas soil–VG associations were more outward-oriented and more frequently negative. These findings provide city-scale empirical evidence that soil conditions are associated with urban greenness patterns in spatially heterogeneous ways, highlighting the need for soil-sensitive UGS assessment and management across urban gradients.

title: Mechanistic insights into lidocaine degradation in UV/H2O2 and Fenton systems: A computational investigation of pathways, kinetics, and toxicity evolution
abstract: Lidocaine (LDC), a widely used local anesthetic, is incompletely removed during wastewater treatment and may persist in aquatic environments. In this study, density functional theory (DFT), transition state theory (TST), kinetic modeling, QSAR-based toxicity prediction, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were integrated to investigate the transformation of LDC initiated by reactive species, its degradation performance in advanced oxidation processes, and the associated risk evolution. Among ·OH, HO2·, 1O2, and O3, ·OH exhibited the highest reactivity toward LDC, with a calculated second order rate constant of 9.39 × 109 M−1 s−1 at 298 K. Kinetic simulations showed that both UV/H2O2 and Fenton oxidation performed more effectively under acidic conditions but exhibited distinct treatment characteristics. Under the selected operating conditions, Fenton oxidation provided faster initial removal, whereas UV/H2O2 achieved more sustained and extensive removal during prolonged treatment. Reaction network analysis proposed 14 plausible intermediates and transformation products formed through hydroxylation, hydrogen abstraction, demethylation, and amide bond cleavage. Transformation was not predicted to necessarily result in detoxification, as several products showed increased aquatic toxicity or bioconcentration potential. Notably, MD simulations indicated that the transformation product 2,6-dimethylphenol exhibited stronger membrane affinity than LDC and caused greater expansion and thinning of the lipid bilayer. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the transformation of pharmaceutical contaminants by reactive species and support process optimization, environmental risk assessment, and cleaner treatment process design.

title: Structure-guided tuning of the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio enables low-temperature fiberization of red mud slags
abstract: Producing high-quality inorganic fibers from red mud is an effective route for its high-value utilization; however, the high-alumina, high-alkali nature of red mud gives rise to melts with limited fluidity and a strong crystallization tendency, thereby impairing fiberization performance. To enable the production of high-quality fibers from red-mud-derived slag, this study combines thermodynamic calculations, crystallization-kinetics analysis, and structural characterization by Raman spectroscopy, MAS NMR, and XPS to elucidate how the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio governs the minimum suitable fiber-forming conditions and melt structure; these findings are further validated by centrifugal fiberization experiments. The results show that increasing the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio from 0.8 to 2.8 markedly improves melt fluidity, lowering the flow temperature by 92 °C. During melting, the coexisting mineral phases evolve from Al-rich refractory phases to Ca-Mg silicate phases, substantially narrowing the temperature interval between the deformation and flow points. During cooling, the primary crystalline phase precipitating from the melt is nepheline (NaAlSiO4). With increasing SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio, the crystallization driving force (Ran) decreases by 0.177%/K, whereas the crystallization activation energy (Ec) increases by 141.1 kJ/mol, indicating a substantially reduced crystallization propensity. Moreover, the crystallization process is surface-crystallization-dominated (n = 0.9-2.3). The minimum suitable fiber-forming temperature decreases by approximately 200 °C as the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio increases, and the controlling factor shifts from crystallization-limited to fluidity-limited behavior at SiO2/Al2O3 = 1.8. Structural analysis at the minimum suitable fiber-forming temperature shows that increasing the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio raises the fractions of Q3+Q4 units and bridging oxygen, increases the proportion of [AlO5]7- species, and enhances network polymerization. Meanwhile, the tendency toward local ordering weakens, leading to a gradual improvement in the glass-forming ability of the red-mud-derived melt. Centrifugal fiberization experiments demonstrate that increasing the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio reduces the average fiber diameter by approximately 41% and the slag-shot content by 5.7 percentage points. At SiO2/Al2O3 = 1.8, the fiber properties meet the relevant national standards, supporting the synergistic improvement in fiber performance arising from the optimized melt structure and enhanced amorphous-forming ability at this composition. Collectively, these results demonstrate that tuning the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio to synergistically regulate network polymerization, Al coordination, and the local Si-O-Al configuration enhances the glass-forming ability of red-mud-derived melts, thereby providing a mechanistic basis for compositional redesign and process optimization toward high-quality inorganic fibers.

title: Manufacture or recycle? Strategies for green products in a closed-loop supply chain
abstract: This study develops a two-period model for a closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) focused on manufacturing and recycling green products supported by government subsidies. The manufacturer produces green products in the first period and, in the second period, may supplement new production by recycling used products collected from the market. We find that the structure of optimal decisions of agents in centralized and decentralized settings is driven by the savings from recycling. The study highlights the inefficiencies in the decentralized supply chain under the wholesale price contract and proposes a two-part tariff contract to achieve coordination. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of retailer competition on the CLSC performance and we find that under competition, manufacturers produce new products in the second period irrespective of the savings from recycling. In contrast, the manufacturer in the monopolistic retailer setting refrains from manufacturing new products for higher levels of savings from recycling.

title: Driving green ethical behaviour: the sequential effects of transformational leadership, ethical climate and co-worker ethical behaviour
abstract: This study examines how owner-managers’ transformational leadership influences employee green ethical behaviour through ethical climate and co-worker ethical behaviour. Data were collected from 388 owner-managers and employees of manufacturing SMEs in Ghana. The results show that transformational leadership positively influences employee green ethical behaviour. Although ethical climate does not significantly moderate the relationship between transformational leadership and green ethical behaviour, it mediates this relationship. The findings also reveal a sequential mediation effect, where transformational leadership enhances ethical climate, which promotes co-worker ethical behaviour and, in turn, improves employee green ethical behaviour. The study highlights that green ethical behaviour is driven not only by leadership directly, but also through the combined influence of organizational norms and peer behaviour.

title: The impact of green finance on the synergy between pollution control and carbon reduction: Exploring the moderating role of institutional environment and spatial spillover effects
abstract: Promoting the synergy between pollution control and carbon reduction (PCCR synergy) is now a key strategy in climate-change governance. By channeling capital toward clean industries, green finance (GF) plays a key role in promoting economic growth alongside environmental improvement. Using data from 282 Chinese cities during 2007-2023, this paper examines the direct impact of GF on PCCR synergy, as well as the mechanisms and spatial spillovers involved. We demonstrate that GF substantially enhances PCCR synergy. The mechanism analysis shows that GF promotes PCCR synergy mainly by strengthening green technology innovation, promoting energy transition, and advancing industrial upgrading. In addition, regional integration strengthens this positive impact by reducing administrative barriers, whereas climate policy uncertainty weakens the effectiveness of GF by increasing investment hesitation. The heterogeneity results suggest that GF promotes PCCR synergy more strongly in resource-based cities than in non-resource-based cities. Further analysis shows that this promoting effect is most pronounced in growing and mature resource-based cities. Furthermore, we reveal a beggar-thy-neighbor phenomenon. Although GF improves local synergy, it generates negative spatial spillovers for neighboring areas through resource siphoning and pollution transfer. These findings deepen the understanding of GF-induced environmental synergy and offer policy guidance for differentiated governance and the promotion of environmental equity across regions.

title: Enhancing sustainable oil palm management through plantation age mapping and yield estimation
abstract: Improving oil palm production without further land expansion requires spatially explicit identification of both yield potential and renewal pressure. Here, we combine remote-sensing-based plantation age mapping with biophysical suitability and management adjustments to estimate oil palm yield across Malaysia. In 2020, 28.1% of stands were 9–14 years old and 26.0% were 15–24 years old, indicating mounting renewal pressure in the coming decade. Consistent with this pattern, 32.2% of cultivated area was classified as high-yield, whereas 13.8% was identified as requiring replanting.
