Predicted state-level production agreed well with official statistics for 2018–2022 (R2 > 0.73; error < 1.6 Mt) and reproduced the main production cores in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak. These findings show that integrating age structure, site suitability, and management constraints can identify where productivity can be sustained and where delayed renewal may threaten future supply. Its outputs are intended to support regional screening, replanting prioritization, and more efficient resource allocation; application elsewhere requires region-specific recalibration and independent local validation.

title: Doped NiFe2O4 spinel oxygen carriers for enhanced H2 production in photo-assisted chemical looping reforming with water splitting under mild conditions
abstract: Photo-assisted chemical looping reforming coupled with water splitting (PA-CLR-WS) provides a promising route for H2 production under relatively mild conditions, but its performance strongly depends on the ability of oxygen carriers (OCs) to balance redox activity, structural stability, and photo-response behavior. In this study, NiFe2O4 spinel was selected as the matrix, and a series of Co- and Cu-doped AxNi1−xFe2O4 OCs (A = Co or Cu; x = 0.10, 0.25, and 0.50) were prepared to clarify the dopant-dependent regulation of NiFe2O4 in PA-CLR-WS. The results show that the introduction of Co and Cu affects NiFe2O4 through different pathways. Low-level Co doping helps maintain the spinel structure and improves photo-generated charge separation and transport, thereby promoting H2 production during the steam reaction. In contrast, Cu doping enhances low-temperature reducibility but excessive Cu incorporation leads to stronger carrier recombination and particle agglomeration, which limits the effective utilization of photo-generated carriers and weakens the overall H2 production performance. Among the tested OCs, Co0.10Ni0.90Fe2O4 exhibited the best overall performance at 600°C under light irradiation, achieving an H2 yield of 9.5 mmol g−1 OCs with a purity of ≥98%. During 20 cycles, it maintained high H2 purity, with H2 yield fluctuating within 8.0-9.5 mmol g−1 OCs. These findings demonstrate that moderate Co introduction is more effective than Cu introduction for optimizing NiFe2O4 in the present PA-CLR-WS system and provide guidance for the compositional design of spinel OCs for low-temperature chemical looping hydrogen production.

title: Digital transformation and the diffusion of social sustainability practices in supply chains: Evidence from buyer–supplier dyads
abstract: Digital transformation (DT) has been widely acknowledged for its potential to promote social sustainability practice (SSP). As the world's primary manufacturing center, China has witnessed rapid adoption of DT; nevertheless, lingering social sustainability issues have exposed a significant gap in research on how such transformation drives the diffusion of SSP along supply chains. To address this research gap, this study employs fixed effects regression and difference-in-differences analysis using panel data from 2750 Chinese manufacturing firms and 186 buyer–supplier dyads from 2011 to 2021. Grounded in the knowledge diffusion perspective, the study identifies that DT exerts a positive effect on the SSP of both focal firms and their suppliers, while supplier SSP mediates the link between buyer DT and buyer SSP. Furthermore, high buyer power attenuates the reverse diffusion pathway of SSP from suppliers to buyer firms. These findings are further validated by difference-in-differences estimation. By framing DT as an enabler of SSP-related knowledge transfer and power asymmetry as a barrier to reverse knowledge flows from suppliers to buyers, this study deepens theoretical understanding and offers practical implications for industry practitioners.

title: A data mining-enhanced machine learning model considering breakpoint events for daily carbon dioxide emissions forecasting
abstract: Accurate prediction of carbon dioxide emissions is crucial for formulating emission reduction strategies in various sectors. However, major events such as the pandemic and policies can alter the underlying driving mechanisms of carbon dioxide emissions, leading to breakpoints that reduce prediction accuracy. Therefore, a data mining-enhanced machine learning model considering breakpoint events was proposed for daily carbon dioxide emission forecasting. This model integrated breakpoint detection with segment clustering to identify segments with similar underlying driving mechanisms, thereby effectively filtering out anomalous fluctuations and mitigating the adverse impacts of structural shifts caused by shocks from major events. Furthermore, an adaptive prediction framework based on complexity classification was constructed to accurately predict carbon dioxide emissions in sectors with different features. Six carbon dioxide emission sectors in China were employed to validate the effectiveness of the model. Results indicated that the proposed model achieved high prediction accuracy, with the average mean absolute percentage error of only 0.42%. Comparative analysis showed that the integration of breakpoint detection with segment clustering and the adaptive prediction framework improved the forecast accuracy by 43.75% and 60.48%, respectively. Therefore, the proposed model can serve as an effective predictive tool to support carbon reduction efforts across sectors.

title: BCT adoption for organic product deter counterfeiting: Tripartite evolutionary game with government involvement
abstract: Counterfeiting has triggered a series of food safety issues. Organic firms and governments face dilemmas in deciding whether to adopt blockchain technology (BCT) and enforce strict supervision, respectively. Based on this context, we construct a tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, conventional firms, and organic firms. We analyze key factors influencing individual stability and examine the impact of organic product attractiveness on system equilibrium. The findings indicate that: (1) When organic products have high (scenario H) or extremely high (scenario E) attractiveness, the government should adopt a lenient supervision approach combined with high-level fines to maintain market order. (2) The adoption of blockchain by organic firms is most stable under conditions of extremely high organic product attractiveness (scenario E). (3) The counterfeiting strategies of conventional firms have limited applicability. Such behaviors are more likely to occur in markets markets with low organic product attractiveness (scenario L) or low-level fines. This study extends the organic agricultural supply chain literature beyond traditional operational decisions by revealing the dynamic evolutionary mechanism underlying technology adoption, counterfeit deterrence, and government regulation. Furthermore, it identifies organic product attractiveness as a novel contingency factor that reshapes the evolutionary stability of supply chain stakeholders, thereby advancing the theoretical understanding of blockchain-enabled market governance. Practically, the findings provide guidance for organic firms’ blockchain adoption decisions and government anti-counterfeiting policies.

title: Modeling sustainable development in resource-based regions: New evidence from an improved multivariate grey model
abstract: As global climate change intensifies, reducing carbon emissions has become a critical global issue. As a pivotal energy-producing province in China, Shanxi Province has high carbon emissions and therefore faces significant challenges in meeting the national “Dual Carbon” goals. To address the inherent limitations of first-order accumulation in the traditional grey model, which struggles to handle the volatility of raw data sequences effectively, this study proposes a variable-order weighted multivariate grey model integrated with grey relational analysis. This model is employed to analyze the dynamic evolutionary characteristics of carbon emissions in Shanxi Province and to simulate emission trends under various scenarios. Grey relational analysis was employed to identify key factors influencing carbon emissions, including coal consumption, thermal power installed capacity, and the value added by the secondary industry. The results indicate that by 2030, carbon emissions in Shanxi Province under the business-as-usual scenario will continue to rise to 691.13 Mt, whereas emissions will be 597.70 Mt under the low-carbon sustainable development scenario and 812.58 Mt under the fossil energy-driven scenario. Notably, Shanxi Province is projected to achieve its carbon peak target before 2030 under the low-carbon sustainable development scenario. Furthermore, the robustness of the proposed model was verified by constructing a validation framework that incorporates the three dimensions of sample input, model parameter structure, and data statistical error interference to assess the model's accuracy. Based on the research findings, relevant recommendations are provided to reduce carbon emissions in Shanxi Province.

title: Assessing the impact of green certificate market transformation on China's carbon market under a multi-market coupling framework
abstract: China's 2023 revision of its green-certificate policy marks a new phase for tradable green certificates (TGCs), but its implications for national carbon emission trading (CET) remain unclear. The reform turns TGCs into an accounting basis for renewable-electricity environmental attributes, whereas current CET compliance remains centered on direct emissions. We construct a system dynamics model coupling China's TGC, power, and CET markets to examine how this accounting reform could affect carbon-market outcomes as policy boundaries expand. A mechanism-separated scenario ladder distinguishes TGC issuance expansion, tiered industrial CET expansion, indirect-emission accounting under compensating free allocation, and bundled green-power deduction. Monthly simulations over a January 2022 to January 2035 horizon, with 2022 used for base-year initialization and the post-reform policy transition evaluated from January 2023 onward, show that TGC issuance expansion alone has limited direct carbon-market effects: the 2035 carbon price rises by 5.24% while allowance demand remains broadly stable. Scarcity is reshaped mainly by CET design: the two industrial-expansion steps raise the carbon price by 7.85% and 3.53%, and adding electricity-related indirect emissions increases gross allowance demand by 22.29% and the carbon price by 10.41%. Once this boundary is active, bundled green-power deduction credits 56.94 million MWh/month by 2035, equal to 15.33% of covered purchased electricity, reducing electricity-related allowance demand by 6.06%, total allowance demand by 1.63%, and the carbon price by 6.07%. The reform therefore functions first as renewable-attribute accounting infrastructure; its carbon-market role emerges only when explicit, double-counting-safe linkage rules convert those attributes into bounded compliance flexibility.

title: Pyrolysis temperature controls long-term stability of heavy metals in sludge-derived biochar after soil application and oxidative aging
abstract: We evaluated how pyrolysis temperature and post-application aging jointly control heavy-metal speciation and ecological risk in sewage sludge-derived biochars. Metal-enriched sludge was pyrolyzed at 300, 500, 700, and 900 °C, mixed with soil, and aerobically incubated for 300 days; metal partitioning was quantified using a modified BCR (European Community Bureau of Reference) sequential extraction. To evaluate the resistance of metal stabilization to accelerated oxidative aging, pristine materials were pretreated with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2; 1% or 5%, w/v) before 30-day soil incubation. A temperature-dependent transition in metal stabilization occurred between 500 and 700 °C, with metal partitioning shifting from oxidizable fractions (F4) to mineral-dominated residual fractions (F5) at ≥700 °C. During pyrolysis, Hg was almost completely volatilized at 300 °C, and Cd decreased markedly at ≥700 °C, indicating volatility-driven reduction in solid-phase risk. In contrast, Pb, Cr, Cu, Zn, Ni, and As were largely retained and exhibited element-specific redistribution during soil incubation. Pb, Cr, Cu, and Zn showed progressive enrichment in F5, whereas Ni stabilization was mainly established during pyrolysis. Arsenic remained comparatively sensitive to oxidative alteration, displaying measurable redistribution during aging. The fraction-based modified ecological risk index values were lowest for ≥700 °C biochars and remained low after aging, indicating that high-temperature pyrolysis enhances long-term stability but requires emission control for volatilized metals.

title: Determining time- and region- specific electricity carbon emission factors with dynamic spatial zoning
abstract: Constructing a high-resolution electricity carbon emission factor (ECEF) accounting model is the foundation for the low-carbon transition of new-type power systems. Existing research on zoning methods for carbon emission factor accounting remains insufficient, and green Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) face the risk of distorted green electricity rights accounting when transmission channels are congested. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Time- and Region- Specific ECEF accounting model that decouples the physical base-map from the market floating-layer. First, based on multidimensional features such as grid impedance and generation-load characteristics, spatial spectral clustering is performed to reconstruct the physical responsibility base-map, thereby forming Carbon Isomorphic Zones (CIZs). Second, by incorporating PPA data, the market contract floating-layer is constructed to delineate Virtual Trading Synergy Zones (VTSZs). Furthermore, a dynamic reachability verification model based on modeled AC power-flow results is introduced to adjust contracted green-electricity attributes under channel-congestion conditions, and the deficit load is returned to its corresponding base-map region for accounting. The case study analysis demonstrates that the proposed model successfully aggregates nodes with high carbon similarity into the same zone and quantifies the spatial reachability range of green electricity environmental attributes. This provides a novel approach for refined electricity-carbon synergy and a more balanced allocation of carbon responsibilities.

title: Investigating the relationship between physical climate risk and green bonds: Disaggregated level evidence from the United States by novel quantile-based methods
abstract: Climate-related issues have increasingly attracted the attention of policymakers and governments due to their severe environmental, economic, and social consequences. Among these issues, physical climate risk (PCR), including extreme temperature, rainfall, and drought events, have posed substantial challenges to environmental sustainability and economic resilience. In this context, green finance instruments, particularly green bond (GB), have emerged as strategic tools for mitigating the adverse impacts of climate-related risks and supporting sustainable development. Accordingly, this study investigates the relationship between disaggregated-level PCR indicators and GBs in the USA using monthly data from 2014/8 to 2023/12. To capture heterogeneous and tail-dependent dynamics that conventional methods may overlook, the study employs novel quantile-based methods. The empirical findings reveal that: (i) GBs exert a consistently negative impact on the extreme high-temperature index across all quantiles; (ii) GBs have mixed (positive and negative) impacts on the extreme rainfall index, extreme drought index, and climate physical risk index across quantiles; (iii) causal relationships generally run from GBs to PCR subtypes across quantiles, except at several specific quantiles; (iv) the impacts of GBs on aggregated and disaggregated level PCR measures differ mainly at lower quantiles, whereas similar patterns emerge across remaining quantiles; (v) the results remain mostly robust in case of employing alternative GB indicators and econometric model as well as considering income as controlling macroeconomic factor. Providing disaggregated-level evidence and applying novel quantile-based methods, this study contributes to the climate finance literature through offering deeper insights into the heterogeneous role of GBs in managing PCRs. The findings provide policy options for the USA policymakers, regulators, and investors seeking to strengthen sustainable finance strategies and enhance climate resilience.

title: An integrated chemical looping cycle for green ammonia and syngas co-production driven by staged oxidation of oxygen carrier: Process simulation and thermodynamic evaluation
abstract: Green ammonia and syngas are pivotal intermediates for decarbonizing the chemical and energy sectors. However, the H2 generation and air separation for N2 are always energy-extensive. Driven by the concept of staged oxidation of oxygen carrier using H2O and air, a cleaner green ammonia and syngas co-production system is proposed, where the high-purity H2 and N2 are prepared in biomass chemical looping hydrogen generation without any external air separation unit while they are used in chemical looping ammonia synthesis, which contributes to the economic. Using carbon-neutral rice husk as feedstock, a comprehensive thermodynamic model for this system was developed to investigate the effects of key operating parameters on syngas quality, hydrogen yield, and ammonia output. The results demonstrate that at a gasification temperature of 725 °C and an αOC/C of 0.5, a high-quality syngas with a hydrogen concentration of 47.7% is achieved while the highest gasification efficiency of 91.4% occurs at 900 °C. The hydrogen production in the hydrogen reactor reaches a plateau of 19.99 kmol/h at an αOC/C of 0.9 and a reactor temperature of 500 °C. The staged air reactor enables the generation of high-purity N2 for nitrogen carrier regeneration. For ammonia synthesis, the suitable conditions are identified at 30 bar and 200 °C with an αNC/C of 0.10, yielding 5.38 kmol/h of NH3 with complete conversion of the nitrogen carrier. The proposed dual chemical looping cycle thermodynamically demonstrates a viable pathway for the flexible co-production of syngas and green ammonia, with a material flow analysis confirming the efficient utilization of biomass and internal hydrogen streams.

title: Average photon energy based solar spectrum reconstruction for building-oriented TMY databases
abstract: With the transition of solar energy utilization toward a spectrum-regulation paradigm, solar spectral irradiance distribution (SID) has become increasingly important for building energy and photovoltaic (PV) applications. However, conventional typical meteorological year (TMY) databases generally lack spectral information, limiting their use in advanced energy analyses. To address this challenge, this study proposes a decoupled shape-intensity data-driven framework for high-fidelity solar spectrum reconstruction and TMY database enhancement featuring three core innovations. First, a shape-intensity decoupling mechanism is proposed, in which average photon energy (APE) characterizes spectral morphology while global horizontal irradiance (GHI) independently determines spectral intensity, enabling high-resolution spectral reconstruction from low-dimensional meteorological inputs. Second, an APE-GHI dual-variable spectral representation paradigm is established, providing a lightweight and data-driven alternative to conventional radiative transfer models. Third, this study pioneers the quantitative spectral enhancement and diagnostic analysis of mainstream TMY databases, revealing systematic spectral discrepancies among different data sources and climatic regions. The Random Forest model (RF) achieves an R2 of 0.949 with an RMSE of 0.009 eV for APE prediction while the reconstructed spectra exhibit an average error of 0.0177 W·m−2·nm−1 under diverse atmospheric conditions. Furthermore, the proposed multi-input prediction strategy maintains an R2 above 0.866 even without irradiance input, demonstrating adequate adaptability in data-scarce scenarios. This study provides a low-cost and scalable framework for enriching building-oriented TMY databases with dynamic spectral information, supporting advanced photovoltaic evaluation and spectrally responsive energy analyses.

title: Developing a phased implementation strategy for greenhouse gas mitigation in Korea's cement industry with the MESSAGEix model
abstract: The cement industry is difficult to decarbonize because fuel-combustion emissions and process emissions from limestone calcination occur simultaneously. This study develops a Korea-specific MESSAGEix-based bottom-up optimization model that integrates energy and material flows in the cement production system. Scenario analysis is conducted to distinguish reductions in total greenhouse gas emissions from reductions in clinker-specific emission intensity and to quantify the phase-specific roles and deployment timing of product and material substitution, process technology substitution, and CO2 capture and storage (CCS) through 2050. The results indicate that expanding blended cement and increasing supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) content in Portland cement can provide immediate mitigation and cost-saving potential by reducing clinker demand. Advanced kiln and raw mill technologies become increasingly important for lowering clinker-specific emission intensity in the medium term. In the long term, low-temperature calcination and CCS are required to manage residual process emissions under a 2050 carbon-neutrality constraint. These findings suggest that Korea's cement sector decarbonization requires a sequential portfolio strategy combining near-term reduction in clinker demand, mid-term process innovation, and long-term residual-emission management.

title: Interfacial electron redistribution stabilizes Cu-centered redox cycling for efficient Fenton-like catalysis
abstract: Efficient degradation of organic pollutants via Fenton-like catalysis remains a challenge due to the instability of the redox cycle under prolonged operation. Herein, we construct an interface-engineered FeCu layered double hydroxide/g-C3N4 heterostructure (FeCu-LDH/g-C3N4) to establish an internal electron-supply pathway for stabilizing Cu-centered redox cycling. Spectroscopic analyses, together with DFT calculations, support interface-induced electron redistribution, which favors electron depletion in the g-C3N4 framework and preferential electron enrichment at Cu sites, promoting partial Cu2+ reduction to Cu+, while Fe3+ remains largely stable as a structural and electronic modulator. Benefiting from this site-selective electronic regulation, FeCu-LDH/g-C3N4 exhibits markedly accelerated H2O2 activation and achieves near-complete Rhodamine B degradation within 20 min, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant 4.6 times that of pristine FeCu-LDH. Active-site substitution confirms Cu as the primary redox center, while ROS quenching and electron paramagnetic resonance analyses identify 1O2 as the dominant oxidative species, accompanied by •OH and O2•-. The catalyst further shows robust recyclability, broad pH adaptability, and strong tolerance to humic substances and common ions. This work demonstrates a Cu-site-selective interfacial electron-regulation strategy for designing stable and efficient Fenton-like catalysts.

title: Annual energy use and economic performance of rice-based cropping systems: A three-year field study in Southwest China
abstract: Rice-based cropping systems are central to food security in Southwest China, yet integrated energy–economic assessments across diverse rotations remain scarce, particularly for rice-green manure and rice-vegetable systems. A three-year field experiment (2022–2025) was conducted in a typical rice-growing region of Southwest China to compare four upland–paddy rotations, namely wheat-rice (RW), rapeseed-rice (RR), green vegetables-rice (RG), and Vicia villosa var.-rice (RV), against a fallow–rice (RF) control, using an integrated energy input–output and cost–benefit framework. Results showed that RG recorded the highest annual energy input (51,754 MJ ha−1), dominated by nitrogen fertilizer, while RV had the lowest (31,345 MJ ha−1) without chemical fertilizer, corresponding to 84% and 12% increases over RF. Energy use efficiency (EUE) diverged even more markedly: RV achieved the highest annual EUE (25.37), with a dry-season EUE of 130.75, whereas RG had the lowest (8.14) despite the highest grain-equivalent yield (22,547 kg ha−1). Economic assessment revealed a clear efficiency–profitability trade-off. RG generated the highest net returns (5924 USD ha−1, benefit–cost ratio 1.11); RR and RW were intermediate (0.82 and 0.64); and RV yielded the lowest (1274 USD ha−1), as green manure provides no direct commodity income. The systems were thus classified into three patterns: high input, high output and low efficiency (RG); balanced (RW and RR); and low input, high efficiency and low return (RV). These findings provide quantitative evidence for region-specific strategies. RG with enhanced nutrient management is recommended for peri-urban areas, RR and RW for major grain-producing regions, and RV with ecological compensation for ecologically sensitive zones, thereby supporting the green transformation of rice-based agriculture.

title: Towards cleaner rare earth metal production: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of direct Nd2O3 pyroelectroreduction in low-temperature chloride-based molten salt
abstract: Industrial neodymium metal production is currently dominated by high-temperature fluoride-based molten salt electrolysis, a process plagued by high energy demand, aggressive corrosion, fluoride waste generation, and significant greenhouse gas emissions. This work evaluates a cleaner alternative using a chloride electrolyte, in which Neodymium metal (Nd) is produced in a LiCl-KCl eutectic at 450°C. The analyzed route incorporates Neodymium (III) oxide (Nd2O3) pellets, a novel approach that enables stable electroreduction, reduces material losses, enhances current efficiency, and simplifies solid handling compared to conventional dissolved feedstocks. We compare this method against the established LiF-NdF3 process operating near 1000°C. Capital and operating expenditures were evaluated using validated cost-scaling correlations, an electrowinning-specific CapEx model, and experimentally supported process assumptions, with a novel density-based correction factor introduced to reconcile discrepancies and improve prediction accuracy. Our results demonstrate that the chloride-based pellet process operates with substantially lower energy input, reduced anode consumption, and lower CapEx and OpEx across all evaluated production scales.

title: Interface interaction between yeast and β-glucan drives soil aggregate stabilization: molecular mechanisms and bioremediation functions
abstract: Soil aggregates formed during microbial-mediated soil remediation contribute critically to consolidating soil particles, enhancing soil stability, and improving soil permeability. However, the molecular-scale interaction mechanisms among microorganisms, their extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), and soil minerals during aggregate formation remain unclear. This study systematically elucidates the molecular mechanism underlying soil aggregate formation in a model yeast-EPS (β-glucan)-mineral system specifically designed to address soil structure degradation in the Loess Plateau. By integrating multi-scale experimental approaches with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate that β-glucan mediates stable adhesion between yeast cells and soil-driven SiO2 particles primarily through van der Waals forces, thereby facilitating the assembly of a three-dimensional “microorganism–EPS–mineral” composite architecture. The co-application of yeast and β-glucan increased the proportion of macroaggregates (>0.25 mm) to 22.58%, compared to only 2.49% in the unamended control. Notably, owing to yeast's intrinsic dormancy response under environmental stress, the aggregates exhibited remarkable resilience against aging and repeated freeze-thaw cycles. This bioengineered system significantly improved soil functions. Total organic carbon (TOC) content increased from 2.57 g/kg to 20.90 g/kg, while total dissolved solids (TDS) remained stably below 2.5 g/kg through yeast metabolic regulation. Furthermore, the soil erodibility factor and fractal dimension analysis confirmed that the β-glucan/yeast/loess aggregate significantly enhanced soil structural integrity and markedly reduced erosion susceptibility. Our findings underscore the promise of biologically driven remediation strategies for restoring degraded soils in the Loess Plateau and provide mechanistic insights that may inform future studies on complex interfacial interactions among microorganisms, organic polymers, and mineral surfaces.

title: Fewer children, higher carbon intensity? Exploring household carbon emission intensity in low-fertility contexts
abstract: Low fertility and global warming have become pressing global concerns. However, systematic research on how low fertility and regional disparities affect household carbon emission intensity remains limited. To address this gap, we adopt a micro level household structure perspective and utilize CFPS panel data for 2014-2022 to analyze the temporal dynamics of household carbon emission intensity across China's eight major economic zones. On this basis, a bidirectional fixed-effects model, along with mediation and moderation analyses, is employed to explore the impact of low fertility on household carbon emission intensity and to further identify its transmission channels. Results show that, in terms of temporal trends, low fertility and household carbon emission intensity display a synchronous relationship, with notable stage-specific and regional differences. In terms of empirical results, low fertility raises household carbon emission intensity, with the effect being especially pronounced in regions with very low-fertility. The results further indicate that scale effects and neighborhood effects are key channels influencing the relationship between the two, while environmental awareness and internet use play moderating roles. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that families without intergenerational care, households with a first-born girl, developmental consumption and those in the Northeast and Northern coastal regions all exert an amplifying effect on household carbon emission intensity. Therefore, it is essential to align the consumption patterns of low-fertility households with national and regional carbon emissions, offering valuable policy insights for the integrated optimization of population and low-carbon strategies.

title: Machine learning prediction and analysis for LFL of C0-C2 combustible gases and blends under wide operating conditions
abstract: The safe deployment of low- and zero-carbon fuels requires reliable prediction of lower flammability limits (LFLs) over broad temperature, pressure, and composition ranges. This need is increasingly important for hydrogen, ammonia, alcohols, ethers, and C0-C2 combustible-gas blends used in storage, transport, and energy-conversion systems. However, conventional LFL prediction methods tend to be inaccurate for gases with a reference Lewis-number factor below unity (Leref < 1), particularly hydrogen and hydrogen-rich mixtures. They are also difficult to apply efficiently to multi-component blends under variable operating conditions because direct extinction-limit calculations require repeated flame simulations and boundary tracking. A C0–C2 reaction mechanism with 110 species and 682 reactions was developed. In addition, an enhanced counterflow premixed flame model was introduced, incorporating flame stretch, radiative heat loss, and an Leref-based stability correction, which significantly reduced prediction errors for combustible gases with Leref < 1. Sensitivity analysis and symbolic regression over 250–500 K and 0.05–2 MPa show that increasing temperature consistently lowers LFL, whereas pressure effects are nonlinear and gas dependent. To reduce the computational burden of blend prediction, eight machine learning algorithms were benchmarked, and the optimal model was coupled with the Le Chatelier's principle as a rapid surrogate for multi-component LFL estimation. Validation against 793 experimental data points confirms that the proposed framework can accurately predict multi-component LFLs while greatly reducing the need for direct flame simulations. The trained model provides predictions within seconds, offering a practical tool for large-scale parametric screening, safety-boundary assessment and cleaner utilization of low-carbon combustible-gas blends in storage, transport, and energy-conversion applications.

title: Resilience and reconfiguration: A CPD-STERGM analysis of structural breaks in the BRI LIB trade network
abstract: Amid the global energy transition, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are a key commodity underpinning clean energy and electrified transport. The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), centered on intergovernmental dialogue and coordinated infrastructure, fundamentally reshapes how trade ties form among participating countries. Understanding this network's resilience requires identifying structural breaks in the mechanisms governing trade tie formation and dissolution. This study identifies the timing of these breaks in the BRI LIB trade network from 2017 to 2022 to examine how geographic, institutional, and technological factors drive trade tie dynamics across distinct evolutionary phases. Using trade data from 56 BRI countries, this study integrates Change Point Detection with the Separable Temporal Exponential Random Graph Model (CPD-STERGM) to estimate phase-specific mechanisms of tie formation and dissolution. Four breakpoints are detected at October 2017, January 2019, January 2020, and April 2022. The network evolved through five phases, exhibiting a pronounced “core-transit-periphery” stratification. Driving mechanisms shifted from “hard” factors like geographic proximity to “soft” factors including common language and bilateral investment treaties. Consequently, this study proposes a differentiated supply chain governance framework encompassing emergency response mechanisms, logistics hub upgrading, and institutional coordination via the mutual recognition of standards and investment protection. This offers actionable policy insights to enhance LIB supply chain resilience within the BRI.

title: Green efficiency under heterogeneous technologies: Evidence from Indian manufacturing industry
abstract: The manufacturing industry is central to India's economic growth, but it also accounts for substantial energy use and CO2 emissions. An understanding of green efficiency under heterogeneous technologies is crucial for designing differentiated industrial decarbonisation strategies. This study evaluates the green efficiency of 21 manufacturing industries in India from 2010 to 11 to 2022-23 using an input-oriented window data envelopment analysis model within a metafrontier framework. Labour, capital, and energy are used as inputs, gross sales are used as the desirable output, and CO2 emissions are treated as the undesirable output. A non-linear path in green efficiency is observed, indicating a broad transitional adjustment process accompanied by technical inefficiencies. Significant industry heterogeneity is observed, with technology-intensive industries remaining closest to the frontier, while labour- and capital-intensive industries exhibit persistent inefficiencies and technology gaps. Policy recommendations are proposed to facilitate cluster-specific strategies for improving green efficiency.

title: Modified lignosulfonate-assisted in situ synthesis of Co3Mo3N/CoMo2S4 heterojunction electrocatalyst with strong interfacial interactions for efficient overall water splitting
abstract: The high cost of precious metals has driven the pursuit of efficient and stable non-precious metal electrocatalysts, which remains a central challenge for electrocatalytic water splitting. Herein, aminated sodium lignosulfonate served as a biomacromolecular skeleton for the construction of a novel bifunctional electrocatalyst, CoMo@NSLA, via a hydrothermal-pyrolysis approach. This approach enabled the in situ formation of Co3Mo3N particles and CoMo2S4 nanosheets on the derived carbon matrix. CoMo@NSLA showed high HER and OER efficiency in alkaline media, with overpotentials as low as 102 and 251 mV at 10 mA cm−2. The assembled CoMo@NSLA-based electrolyzer exhibited a low operating voltage of 1.61 V at 10 mA cm−2 and maintained 94 % performance over 30 h, demonstrating excellent durability. As confirmed by experimental and theoretical analyses, the superior performance originated from its porous architecture, high surface area, as well as strong interfacial interaction within the Co3Mo3N/CoMo2S4 heterojunction. Specifically, interfacial charge transfer induced electronic reconfiguration that activated Mo sites and optimized the d-band center. This synergistically regulated the adsorption/desorption of reaction intermediates, thereby enhancing the kinetics of HER and OER. This work achieves the high-value utilization of lignosulfonate and paves a new route toward high-performance electrocatalysts based on biomass-carbon-supported bimetallic nitride/sulfide composites.

title: Regulating interface charge separation to unlock photocatalytic non-radical pathways: Construction of BiOCl/COF S-scheme heterojunction for efficient antibiotic remediation
abstract: The inefficiency of charge separation and the unselective nature of radical-based pathways severely limit the practical application of photocatalysis for water purification. Herein, a BiOCl/COF (BOC/COF) S-scheme heterojunction was successfully constructed via ultrasonic assistance. Remarkably, the optimized S-scheme heterojunction significantly enhanced photo-generated carrier separation efficiency, which effectively promoted ROS generation and improved the removal rate of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) (degradation rate: 91.6%). The research has found that non-radical pathways collectively accounted for 89.11% of the degradation activity, endowing the system with high selectivity. It is worth noting that the BC-20 membrane can efficiently eliminate TC in a continuous-flow wastewater treatment system. Furthermore, BC-20 can degrade TC in an enlarged reactor under natural sunlight irradiation. The three possible degradation pathways were analyzed through Fukui function and LC-MS. The toxicity of the TC solution after being treated with the BOC/COF S-scheme was evaluated using mung beans as a crop model. Through (in-situ) characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the S-scheme charge transfer mechanism and interfacial electric field (IEF) driving efficient 1O2 production were systematically elucidated. These findings not only deciphered the interface engineering-mediated non-radical generation mechanism in BOC/COF S-scheme photocatalysis but also advanced its practical application in aquatic environmental remediation.

title: Investigating the regulatory effects of surfactants to design high-performance and eco-friendly soybean oil-based emulsions for the manufacturing industry
abstract: To address the critical challenges associated with vegetable oil-based emulsions in the ultra-precision machining of TC4 titanium alloy-namely, insufficient stability, limited lubrication performance, and environmental compatibility concerns-the regulatory regulation mechanism of surfactant charge characteristics and molecular configuration on the multiscale properties of emulsions was systematically investigated. The results revealed that the anionic surfactant (SDBS) significantly enhanced interfacial mass transfer and oil droplet replenishment through the formation of a low-viscosity, small-droplet-size emulsion system, thereby inducing a stable mixed lubrication film at the friction interface. In addition, its strong adsorption behavior, in conjunction with ultrasonic cavitation effects, promoted the in-situ generation of a dense TiO2 passivation layer on the TC4 surface. This dual composite structure, consisting of an adsorption layer and a passivation film, endowed the system with remarkable corrosion resistance. Regarding machining performance, the SDBS emulsion facilitated efficient swarf removal and suppressed interfacial adhesion by virtue of its superior wetting and spreading capability and high oil film load-bearing capacity, while also minimizing the wear and blunting of diamond abrasives. Compared with the T80 and CTAC systems, the SDBS system reduced tool wear rates by 35.12% and 31.05%, respectively, and increased material removal rates by 25.14% and 20.11%. Furthermore, this system exhibited satisfactory antibacterial activity and low biotoxicity, demonstrating notable eco-friendly characteristics. Collectively, these findings provide a systematic theoretical and experimental foundation for the design of plant oil-based emulsions tailored for green and high-efficiency manufacturing processes.

title: Sustainable salt recovery from DMF-containing industrial brines through integrated nanofiltration and space-confined catalytic ozonation
abstract: Industrial waste brines containing trace refractory organics remain difficult to purify and reuse, limiting sustainable salt recovery. In this study, an integrated process combining nanofiltration (NF) and ceramic-membrane-enabled space-confined catalytic ozonation was developed for the treatment of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF)-containing industrial brines. NF achieved 96.27% SO42− rejection with minimal chloride loss, while the subsequent catalytic ozonation step, optimized at an initial pH of 12.41, an O3 flow rate of 384 mL min−1, and a catalyst dosage of 14.25 g, reached 96.7% TOC removal. Radical quenching experiments indicated that hydroxyl radicals played a dominant role in the confined oxidation process. For real industrial brine, although the TOC of NF permeate fluctuated between 130 and 195 mg L−1, the catalytic ozonation step consistently reduced the final TOC to 3–10 mg L−1, meeting the organic-content requirement for downstream chlor-alkali use. Electrolysis tests further showed that the refined brine supported stable cell operation under the tested conditions. These results demonstrate that the integrated NF and space-confined catalytic ozonation process is effective for sulfate control, deep organic removal, and subsequent brine reuse, providing a feasible route for sustainable salt recovery from DMF-containing industrial brines.

title: Structural vulnerability and operational adaptation: Insights from ecological network analysis of China's chromium supply chain security
abstract: The key mineral chromium is a core feedstock for stainless steel production and irreplaceable in modern industry. China is the world's largest importer and consumer of chromium, with a 99% import dependence on chromite. Global chromium market fluctuations can have a strong impact on China's domestic supply chain. Currently, rising geopolitical tensions and U.S.-China trade frictions have further amplified supply chain security risks, making it critical to evaluate China's chromium supply chain security. Therefore, this research applies ecological network analysis (ENA) to assess the structural and operational dynamics of China's chromium supply chain from 2000 to 2023 to provide policy-relevant evidence for maintaining supply stability and strengthening supply chain security. The research results show that: (1) Structurally, China's chromium supply chain exhibits high sensitivity to policy shifts in core chromium-associated countries. The ENA system of China's chromium supply chain is dominated by competitive inter-compartment relationships, with persistently weakening indirect effects, low complexity, and limited internal connectivity, driving rising systemic vulnerability. (2) Operationally, the expansion of China's chromium supply chain has contributed to an enhancement in its overall stability. Over time, there has been an improvement and stabilization in the alignment between resource availability and the system's capacity. (3) Scenario analysis shows that supply and demand contractions alter inter-compartment competitive dynamics and reduce system synergy, and that balancing supply and demand does not always yield positive system outcomes. Based on these findings, this paper proposes policy recommendations including: implementing precise and balanced supply, elevating the strategic status of secondary chromium, promoting collaborative governance across the industrial chain, and advancing follow-up research on the chromium supply chain.

title: Coupling effect of stress and dry-wet cycles on self-healing performance of geopolymer cutoff wall backfills incorporating microcapsules
abstract: Cutoff walls are widely used to prevent lateral migration of contaminated groundwater in geoenvironmental applications. The change in hydraulic conductivity (kw) due to dry-wet cycles (DWC) has been recognized as a long-term performance concern for cutoff walls. Most existing laboratory methods are unable to maintain stress effects during continuous DWC processes, which limits accurately assessing kw of cutoff wall backfills. This work developed an experimental apparatus to reproduce the coupling effect of stress and DWC on the microcapsule self-healing cutoff wall backfill (MSHCWB). Supplementary crack closure observations under unstressed condition were also conducted. The microstructural characteristics were measured by X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Computed Tomography (CT). MSHCWB exhibited promising self-healing capability, achieving over 50% crack width reduction and up to 236.71% improvement in crack closure rate after 28 days of healing. Under the axial stress of 150 kPa, the kw of MSHCWB containing 8% microcapsules remained below 1 × 10−9 m/s after ten DWC. The microcapsule structure, whether single-walled or double-walled, had little effect on the kw under higher axial stress. The axial stress reduced the pore space and decreased the seepage path to enhance impermeability, while higher stress level also positively contributed to microcapsule rupture and the self-healing process. The empirical function of kw with respect to the cycle number and axial stress was further proposed. The axial stress substantially influences the variation magnitude of kw during the DWC, which requires consideration in cutoff wall design.

title: Synergistic water regulation and byproduct confinement in non-woven fabric-encapsulated Al@MgH2 for controlled hydrogen generation via parallel and sequential reactor designs
abstract: Active Al-based composite hydrolysis for hydrogen production holds broad application prospects in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, key challenges such as controllability of hydrogen production, byproduct recovery, and hydrogen purity still need to be addressed. This study tackles these issues by designing a non-woven fabric-encapsulated hydrogen production unit and two hydrolysis reactors. This unit consists of a non-woven fabric envelope and an internal Al@30 % MgH2 block. The regular pore structure of the non-woven fabric regulates water mass transfer and confines byproducts. This leads to effective control of hydrogen production, enhanced solution utilization, and one-step byproduct recovery. The parallel and sequential hydrogen production reactors were designed according to the hydrolysis characteristics of the encapsulated unit. The flow paths of the reaction solution were controlled accordingly. Under low solution flow rate conditions, the parallel reactor achieved a stable hydrogen generation rate (sHGR) of 1.36 mL s−1 over 3573 s. The measured total hydrogen generation was 4579 mL. In contrast, the sequential reactor maintained a sHGR of 0.84 mL s−1 over 5177 s. The measured total hydrogen generation was 4448 mL. Purity tests confirmed that the hydrogen purity exceeded 99.2 %. This study combines physical encapsulation, solution injection strategy, and reactor design. This integrated approach overcomes the explosive reaction of active powders, achieves tunable hydrolysis kinetics, and provides a practical pathway from laboratory to application.

title: The impact of international technology investment on carbon emissions: Global evidence
abstract: Despite international technology investment emerging as a key feature of the globalizing world, its impact on global carbon emissions has yet to attract attention. Using a compiled dataset of international technology investment deals, this study examines the spatiotemporal patterns of international technology investment and the corresponding carbon-emission-reduction performance from 1998 to 2023. Our findings demonstrate that an increase in international technology investment transactions contributes to reductions in carbon emissions globally, in both the home and host countries. However, in a subsample analysis, we found that the carbon-emission-reduction performance of international technology investment is closely related to the level of national development. Although transactions in advanced economies have achieved greater reductions in carbon emissions, those in non-advanced economies have not yet optimized their carbon emissions, since the emission-increasing scale effect of production expansion outweighs and dominates the energy-saving technique effect in non-advanced economies. Further research shows that technology investments from advanced economies into non-advanced economies weaken host countries’ emission-reduction performance. In contrast, transactions from non-advanced to advanced economies enhance the host countries' abatement results but weaken mitigation efforts in their home countries. This result tentatively suggests that advanced economies hold a relatively advantageous position in cross-border carbon governance associated with technology investment. Based on the analyses in this paper, we emphasize the need for advanced economies to assume greater responsibility in global environmental governance, while suggesting that non-advanced economies consider adopting environmental taxation frameworks.

title: Coastal bird migration exposure as a spatial constraint for wind energy and airports in eastern China
abstract: Bird migration creates collision risks for wind farms and airports, yet many regions lack radar and bird strike data for infrastructure planning. Using eBird checklist data, distance to coast, and weekly reanalysis climate variables, we developed a screening level assessment of migration exposure for eastern China's lowlands, a key segment of the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. Migration intensity was aggregated to 25 km grid cells and weekly periods for spring and autumn 2021–2025. Distance to coast (0–300 km) captured a weak but temporally consistent decline in exposure inland, with negative slopes across all ten migration seasons. At the 25 km weekly resolution used here, the selected weekly climate metrics explained little of the week-to-week variation in the eBird based migration exposure index. We summarized this coastal gradient into simple high- (0–100 km), medium- (100–200 km), and low-exposure (200–300 km) belts for screening-level mapping, providing a transparent migration-exposure map for planners. This distance-based zonation does not provide operational forecasts or calibrated collision-risk estimates but offers a practical, within region screening framework for identifying relative exposure patterns where high-resolution migration and strike datasets are unavailable. By steering new projects away from the highest-exposure coastal belts where feasible, the approach supports cleaner production by helping avoid costly ecological conflicts, retrofits, and operational constraints.

title: Computer-aided ionic liquid design integrated with process parallel computing for enhanced C4 hydrocarbon separation
abstract: The molecular solvent-based extractive distillation used for the separation of 1,3-butadiene from C4 hydrocarbons continues to be challenging due to the presence of multiple azeotropes and close-boiling mixtures. Ionic liquids (ILs) are regarded as promising alternatives, but due to the time-consuming nature of process optimization, only a limited number of IL processes can be evaluated, so ILs with outstanding thermodynamic abilities may still underperform in practical applications. To address this contradiction, this work proposes a novel method integrating computer-aided ILs design with process parallel optimization. It solves a multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear programming model using a sequential strategy, first maximizing the separation selectivity to identify 10 preferred IL structures, and then rapidly minimizing their process costs. The optimization time based on rigorous process models is significantly reduced from 11.32 h in serial mode to 3.83 h in parallel mode. The [MMIM][TFA] exhibits the best process performance, reducing the total annual cost by 44.34% compared to the conventional NMP-water process. Notably, the ranking of thermodynamic selectivity ([HMIM][TFA] ranks highest) is inconsistent with the ranking of the process costs, highlighting that solely pursuing thermodynamic abilities may lead to suboptimal designs at the process level. Furthermore, quantum chemical calculations reveal that the superior separation performance of [MMIM][TFA] for binary C4 mixtures is mainly governed by the combined effect of its stronger electrostatic interactions and dispersion interactions, compared with NMP. This method framework provides an integrated solution for the green separation, spanning from the molecular to the process scale.

title: Robust deployment optimization of flue gas enhanced oil recovery systems under oilfield production uncertainty
abstract: Effective deployment of flue gas enhanced oil recovery (EOR) systems requires coordinated decisions under changing techno-economic conditions and uncertain oilfield production. This study develops an integrated framework for optimizing the deployment of flue gas EOR systems by combining flue gas composition characterization, dynamic forecasting of techno-economic parameters, and two-stage robust optimization. A column-and-constraint generation (CCG) algorithm is employed to solve the model. The results indicate that (1) the proposed model coordinates facility and capacity planning with flue gas allocation, producing deployment plans that remain feasible under worst-case realizations of oilfield production; (2) the CCG algorithm achieves faster convergence and greater computational efficiency than Benders decomposition (BD) while retaining a verifiable optimality guarantee, demonstrating its suitability for larger deployment problems; and (3) compared with conventional CO2-EOR, flue gas EOR reduces the total system cost by approximately 48.3%, while its compression-related cost is 59.0% lower than the capture-related cost of the benchmark system. These findings provide a quantitative and methodological basis for the robust and economically efficient deployment of flue gas EOR systems under uncertain operating conditions.

title: Additive-free microwave co-pyrolysis of polyethylene and sewage sludge for cleaner waste valorization and energy recovery
abstract: This study evaluated the additive-free microwave co-pyrolysis of commercial polyethylene packaging bag waste (PEB) and municipal sewage sludge (SS), without externally added microwave absorbers or commercial catalysts. In this study, conventional pyrolysis (CP) and microwave pyrolysis (MWP) of PEB and PEB + SS were systematically compared at 400-800 °C in terms of product distribution, gas and liquid composition, char functional groups, and energy extraction. For PEB, MWP resulted in a markedly different apparent low-temperature conversion behavior compared with CP. At 400 °C, the liquid-tar yield reached 71.3% under MWP, whereas CP retained 92.6% solid residue. After SS addition, MWP-PEB + SS showed a more pronounced redistribution of products than CP-PEB + SS. The observed increase in liquid yield and the changes in gas composition suggest that the polar organic matter, retained water, and inorganic constituents in SS may contribute to microwave-assisted conversion and product regulation, thereby facilitating PEB-SS conversion. At 800 °C, MWP-PEB + SS achieved a liquid tar yield of 60.3% with an HHV of 21.95 MJ/kg. Meanwhile, the gas composition shifted from hydrocarbon-rich products toward H2/CO-enriched gas, which was consistent with possible reforming-related pathways. Energy extraction analysis further demonstrated that MWP-PEB + SS at 800 °C was the most favorable microwave co-pyrolysis condition, achieving a product energy recovery efficiency of 64.02%, with liquid tar serving as the dominant energy carrier. Overall, this study indicates that SS may reduce the dependence on external microwave absorbers and commercial catalysts by providing intrinsic microwave-responsive and reaction-regulating components. This additive-free strategy may simplify solid-residue management and provide a cleaner-production-oriented route for converting mixed solid wastes into energy-dense liquid products and H2/CO-enriched gas.

title: A Bayesian Network-based non-deterministic optimization model for planning climate-resilient and low-carbon power systems: A case study of Nova Scotia, Canada
abstract: Extreme events such as hurricanes pose challenges to clean power system planning. Existing studies rarely jointly manage the interactive relationships among uncertain climate, socioeconomic, and environmental risks. To address this gap, this study develops a Bayesian Network-based non-deterministic optimization model that integrates multidimensional risk management with system optimization to support long-term climate-resilient and low-carbon power system planning. The model enables robust decision-making under multiple risks while balancing trade-offs among system resilience, economic costs, and emission mitigation. A case study of Nova Scotia, Canada (2026–2045) demonstrates its applicability in hurricane-prone regions. To evaluate hurricane impacts on system reliability, a system performance loss index (SPL) is developed. Results show that high-intensity hurricanes could increase SPL to 10.69–22.70%, causing 25,847.54–54,891.40 GWh of unavailable supply and C$ 208.22–776.78 million in economic losses. SPL may also rise five-fold to 17.81–37.81% with increased hurricane frequencies. Low-fragility natural gas generation will supply ∼30% of electricity, with its capacity losses roughly one-third of wind generation. Energy storage-based planning would strengthen system resilience and reduce additional emissions of ∼3.42 Mt but comes with high electricity costs, reaching 0.21–6.87 C$/kWh and increasing by 20–50% under high hurricane frequency. In comparison, diversified generation and grid hardening strategies would maintain stable costs within 0.064–0.081 C$/kWh. Therefore, transitioning to a diversified mix of natural gas and renewables with underground lines, supported by cost-feasible storage measures, would offer a balanced climate-resilient strategy. This study provides quantitative insights into climate adaptation-mitigation linkages and identifies cost-effective management plans.

title: Human preference and vegetation features enhance soil carbon sequestration in urban green spaces: implications from soil oxidizable carbon fractionation
abstract: Urban areas drive >70% of global energy CO2 emissions, positioning urban green spaces as critical yet underoptimized nature-based climate solutions. However, coupled effects of human preferences (a proxy for management probability and public use patterns) and multi-layer vegetation on soil organic carbon (SOC) stability remain poorly understood, hindering evidence-based low-carbon urban management. We surveyed 370 subtropical urban forest plots to disentangle drivers of four soil oxidizable carbon fractions: very labile, labile, less labile, and non-labile, covering human preference metrics, vegetation traits, soil nutrients, aggregation and water-holding capacity (total 63 parameters). Redundancy analysis, variation partitioning and partial least squares structural equation modeling revealed: (1) Tall, large-diameter, and low density trees combined with sparse-short herb layers significantly elevated less & non-labile fractions and improved the soil carbon stability, a vegetation structure strongly aligned with high-human-preference areas subject to intensive management near roads; (2) Soil total nitrogen (explaining 28.9% of SOC fraction variation) and glomalin-related soil protein were the dominant direct regulators of carbon accrual, while soil aggregate stability and water-holding capacity acted as core mediators linking vegetation/human factors to SOC dynamics; (3) Human preference mainly exerted indirect effects on SOC and its fractions via regulating soil nutrient availability, physical structure and water-holding capacities. We propose a preference-stratified management framework, and recommend "tall open-canopy trees + sparse herb" configuration at high human preferred regions reconciling recreational demands with long-term carbon sequestration. Our findings highlights that integrating appropriate vegetation and human preferences can enhance soil carbon sequestration—a nature-based pathway toward low-carbon urban transition.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and drivers of vegetation greenness and resilience in China's open-pit coal mines over the past four decades
abstract: Open-pit mining and reclamation directly reshape land surfaces, making vegetation a sensitive remote sensing indicator of ecological dynamics in mining areas. However, most existing assessments focus on vegetation greenness, even though greening does not necessarily imply enhanced resilience. In mining areas, non-stationarity and signal mixing hinder large-scale, long-term assessment of vegetation resilience. Here, we combined VegDecouple with critical slowing down theory to extract vegetation disturbance signals and quantify vegetation resilience. Using Landsat-derived annual maximum NDVI data from 1987 to 2025, we extracted the steady-state NDVI component, NDVIss, to represent vegetation greenness and investigated the spatiotemporal patterns of vegetation greenness and resilience across 329 open-pit coal mines in China, identified their trajectory types, and evaluated the effects of climatic and anthropogenic drivers using mixed-effects models. The results showed that (1) vegetation greenness exhibited a three-stage trajectory, with slow growth during 1987–2005, degradation during 2006–2016, and recovery after 2017, and was generally higher in northeastern China and lower in central China; (2) vegetation resilience fluctuated during 1993–2007, declined during 2007–2014, and increased after 2014, without a clear macrogeographic gradient; (3) four greenness–resilience trajectory types were identified, among which greening with resilience enhancement was dominant nationally and most concentrated in the Shendong coal base; and (4) mixed-effects models revealed divergent driver responses. NDVIss was mainly associated with the long-term climate background, particularly mean precipitation, and with recovery age, whereas vegetation resilience was primarily associated with annual temperature anomaly, mean precipitation, and annual net solar radiation anomaly. Sensitivity analyses using alternative water indicators further suggested that NDVIss was more closely related to persistent water availability and soil moisture in the upper 0–7 cm layer, whereas vegetation resilience was more sensitive to water deficits captured by SPEI over 3 and 6 months than to total annual precipitation. This study advances the understanding of long-term vegetation greenness and resilience dynamics in China's open-pit coal mines and provides a remote sensing perspective for assessing ecological change in mining areas.

title: Acid mine drainage as a lixiviant for rare earth element recovery from ion-adsorption clay mine tailings: leaching behavior, mechanistic interpretation, and machine-learning-assisted analysis
abstract: This study evaluates a mine-internal waste-to-waste strategy in which raw acid mine drainage (AMD) generated at an ion-adsorption rare earth mine is reused as an on-site lixiviant to recover residual rare earth elements (REEs), including yttrium (Y) and scandium (Sc), from associated mine tailings. One-factor-at-a-time screening identified favorable laboratory conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio [S/L] = 1:50, 50 °C, 135 rpm, and 3 h), under which the reported calculations gave REE extraction efficiencies of approximately 70-92%. Solution and surface analyses documented REE release and iron enrichment of the leached residue, while XGBoost-SHAP provided internally evaluated predictive associations that require external validation. The findings support laboratory-scale technical feasibility for integrated management of two mine-derived waste streams, rather than establishing AMD itself as an unconventional REE resource or demonstrating a net environmental or economic benefit. The analytical scope focused on REEs and did not provide a complete mass balance for coexisting Fe, Al, Mn, Pb, As, Th, and U. Scale-up therefore requires assessment of seasonal AMD variability, acid-neutralization demand, downstream REE separation, treatment of the co-contaminated pregnant leach solution, and the long-term stability and leachability of the Fe-rich residue.

title: Climate change, ecosystem service value loss, and adaptive policy evaluation: Evidence from Chinese cities
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens regional ecosystem service value (ESV), while mismatches between ecological pressures and adaptive policy capacity may constrain sustainable development. This study combines climate-grid data, land-cover-derived ESV accounts, and panel data for 281 Chinese prefecture-level cities (2000–2020) to estimate associations between long-term climate normals and ESV. We then analyze 21,930 ecological policy documents using the Qwen2.5 large language model to characterize policy scope, depth, and speed, and use a two-dimensional framework to describe policy–ecology coordination. Results show that higher temperature normals are associated with lower ESV, with larger estimated losses in warmer regions, whereas higher precipitation normals are associated with higher ESV. The cumulative ESV loss associated with observed long-term climate changes exceeds 30 billion yuan; hydrological regulation accounts for the largest estimated loss (7.47 billion yuan). Policy–ecology coordination displays an east–central–west gradient, but the policy scores are text-based indicators and the coordination analysis is descriptive rather than causal. Effective adaptation therefore requires policy design to be aligned with local ecological conditions and implementation capacity.

title: Photovoltaic-induced heterogeneity drives plant–soil feedback divergence and microhabitat differentiation in a typical steppe
abstract: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) power stations is profoundly altering grassland ecosystems, yet the mechanisms that link plant community responses to belowground ecological processes remain unclear. Here, three microhabitats in a typical steppe PV station located in Inner Mongolia: under-panel, between-panel, and control microhabitats were investigated. The results showed that PV-induced microhabitat heterogeneity reshaped plant-derived inputs to the soil and microbial activity, thereby generating different aboveground and belowground feedbacks that reinforced the heterogeneity. The under-panel community exhibited low diversity but high aboveground biomass dominated by a few species (e.g., Carex lanceolata), whereas between-panel plots maintained higher plant diversity with moderate biomass. These differences affected the belowground ecological processes. Under the panels, greater litter accumulation but reduced rhizosphere carbon inputs were accompanied by lower soil organic carbon and total nitrogen, higher NO3−-N, a higher microbial biomass C to N ratio, and enrichment of RB41, exhibiting a more conservative microbial strategy. In contrast, between-panel plots were characterized by higher peroxidase activity and NH4+-N, together with enrichment of Humicola and Hygrocybe and greater predicted potential for organic matter transformation and nutrient mineralization. Together, these findings show that PV-induced heterogeneity creates functional trade-offs among productivity, biodiversity maintenance, and belowground nutrient processes within a single power station. Therefore, increases in vegetation biomass or cover alone should not be interpreted as evidence of ecological improvement, because they may coincide with biodiversity loss and altered soil C–N cycling. PV development should balance energy production with biodiversity conservation and long-term ecosystem functioning.

title: Subcritical extraction enhances the milk thistle value chain by improving economic and nutritional-functional performance with limited environmental trade-offs
abstract: The industrial production of Silybum marianum has expanded rapidly in recent years. However, its conventional processing chain, mainly based on mechanical pressing followed by silymarin extraction, still faces challenges in resource utilization and value enhancement. In this study, three oil extraction pathways, including solvent extraction (SE), mechanical pressing (PE), and subcritical butane extraction (SBE), were evaluated by integrating life-cycle environmental assessment, economic analysis, and nutritional-functional evaluation. PE exhibited the lowest environmental impacts among the three pathways, whereas SBE achieved higher economic value and nutritional-functional performance under the baseline weighting scheme due to its higher oil recovery and favorable product characteristics. Compared with PE, the transition to SBE increased the full-chain carbon footprint by approximately 12.7%, while increasing economic value by about 76.6% under realistic commercialization conditions. Under the expanded refined-oil commercialization scenario, SBE showed an approximately 86.8% higher modeled economic value than PE. These results indicate that SBE can improve the value generation potential of the milk thistle processing chain while maintaining an acceptable environmental burden. This study provides insights into the selection of extraction technologies for sustainable and high-value utilization of milk thistle resources.

title: Multi-objective optimization for sizing of residential hybrid renewable systems with battery storage: Balancing economic, environmental, and energy autonomy perspectives
abstract: The expansion of residential prosumer systems has increased the need for sustainable sizing models that incorporate local generation and storage. This study proposes a multi-objective model for the optimal sizing of residential hybrid renewable energy systems, evaluated from economic, environmental, and energy autonomy perspectives. The approach combines Response Surface Methodology and Normal Boundary Intersection to model and optimize three objective functions: Net Present Value, equivalent CO2 emissions, and Self-sufficiency. A post-Pareto selection method is used to identify an optimal solution from each Pareto front. A case study is developed across the nine capitals of the Brazilian Northeast region, considering the current regulatory changes to the net-metering system established by Law 14,300/2022. This study advances the literature by explicitly integrating economic, environmental (accounting for life-cycle emissions of renewable technologies), and energy self-sufficiency objectives in the optimal sizing of residential photovoltaic/wind/battery systems under a real regulatory transition. The main results indicate that, despite the regulatory change, investments remain viable, particularly when based on photovoltaic energy. The selected solutions achieved self-sufficiency levels of 54.7% to 68.1% and life-cycle emissions of 6894 to 8655 kgCO2eq. The results also indicate the benefit of small-scale wind energy over increasing battery bank capacity, as it enables greater self-sufficiency with a lower environmental impact. Despite this, the use of wind energy remains limited to regions with favorable wind regimes; however, these areas still represent a considerable portion of a country with continental dimensions such as Brazil. Formulating public policies and incentives tailored to each region's specificities can ensure greater integration of distributed generation without negatively affecting energy distributors or consumers who do not use this technology, thereby providing a more sustainable model in the long term.

title: Synergetic high selectively Uranium(VI) adsorption via molecularly engineered tetradentate Schiff base functionalized chitosan/carboxymethyl cellulose bio-composite: From molecular design to life cycle assessment
abstract: The extraction of uranium has been an important solution for resolving the radioactive contamination in water resources and the nuclear fuel shortage. Developing effective eco-friendly bio-adsorbents is urgently needed. A composite biomaterial was designed by combining chitosan (CS) and carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) (CS/CMC), which is further functionalized by a novel unsymmetrical O-phenylenediamine tetradentate Schiff base ligand (LOph) (3-bromo-2-((E)-((2-(((E)-2-chloro-6-hydroxybenzylidene)amino)phenyl)-imino)-methyl)phenol) (CS/CMC-LOph). CS/CMC-LOph composite showed a strong binding affinity to U(VI) and was able to adsorb 782.4 mg/g of uranyl ions at pH 5, 318 K, and 300 ppm. From an environmental perspective (1 ppm), the CS/CMC-LOph achieved significant adsorption, with a removal rate of 99.6% and a uranium residual concentration of 3.1 ppb after 24 h, which is below the WHO standards (15 ppb). In simulated real seawater, the material removes 98.7% of uranium with a Kd of 378663.3 mL/g. The thermodynamic study confirms that the process is endothermic and spontaneous. DFT calculations demonstrate a binding energy of −54.75 kcal/mol for U(VI) with the LOph, which is significantly stronger than those of chitosan and CMC. The CS/CMC-LOph demonstrated good recyclability with a removal capacity of 81.6% after six cycles. An LCA study has been conducted to assess the environmental impact of manufacturing 1 kg of CS/CMC-LOph. The minimum total cost of reusability and use of sustainable technologies proved to be effective in water treatment, uranium separation, and recovery.

title: Bioconversion of nuisance macroalgal biomass into fish production: Implications for low-input and circular aquaculture
abstract: Excess macroalgal blooms represent a persistent waste-management challenge in coastal aquaculture systems. Therefore, developing low-input, resource-efficient strategies that prevent waste accumulation while recovering value from nuisance biomass is a key objective of cleaner production. Here, we evaluate trophic bioconversion as a resource-recovery pathway by testing whether an herbivorous fish can convert nuisance macroalgal biomass (Ulva prolifera) into marketable seafood while mitigating water-quality risks associated with algal decomposition. Juvenile orange-spotted spinefoot (Siganus guttatus) was used as a model species to assess the feasibility and functional consequences of macroalgal-based feeding. The fish were fed either formulated feed or U. prolifera in a 90-day controlled experiment, complemented by a 98-day field-based assessment of macroalgal dynamics and water quality. Growth performance, digestive morphology and enzyme activities, antioxidant responses, tissue-specific nutrient composition, and ecosystem-level responses were evaluated. Compared with formulated feed, macroalgal feeding supported high survival and sustained growth, although at lower rates, indicating that U. prolifera can meet basic nutritional requirements under low-input conditions. This dietary regime induced pronounced digestive adaptation, including intestinal expansion and a redistribution of enzyme activities, with elevated amylase activity reflecting adaptation to a carbohydrate-rich, low-lipid diet. At the physiological level, macroalgal feeding enhanced primary antioxidant defenses without a parallel increase in downstream detoxification pathways, indicating a selective and efficient stress-response strategy. At the product level, macroalgal-derived nutrients were preferentially allocated to edible muscle rather than nonedible tissues, resulting in a high-protein, low-fat profile and enrichment of nutritionally valuable ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids. At the system level, active grazing by S. guttatus accelerated macroalgal removal and altered nutrient dynamics, reducing the risk of secondary nutrient release during algal decomposition. This study provides empirical evidence for a low-input trophic bioconversion pathway that transforms nuisance macroalgal biomass from an environmental liability into a productive aquaculture resource, thereby enhancing resource-use efficiency and supporting cleaner and more circular aquaculture systems.

title: Gamification and sustainable mobility: Determinants of green travel app adoption
abstract: While sustainable transport is increasingly called for in urban environments to address congestion and pollution, the uptake of environmentally friendly modes of transport is still low because of implementation challenges and low incentives. Gamified green travel applications address this gap by integrating points, badges, challenges, and rewards into travel planning. In this study, the authors integrate the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and examine the intention of the passengers to use such apps. The study uses a survey data collected from urban residents to examine relationships between perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, enjoyment, incentives, and adoption intention, using structural equation modelling. The results indicate that perceived usefulness and ease of use improve attitudes and enjoyment and incentives improve perceptions. Gamification indirectly benefits adoption through usefulness and enjoyment, and social norms and behavioral control play a pivotal role in explaining adoption, which is in line with the integrated TAM–TPB framework.

title: Sustainable production of bio-methanol via integrated CO2-Assisted catalytic pyrolysis process: A comprehensive energy, economic, and environmental analysis
abstract: Bio-methanol is emerging as a practical low-carbon fuel for the decarbonization of the international shipping sector.
