abstract: The widespread occurrence of phenol in industrial and natural water systems presents a significant environmental and public health challenge, driving the demand for monitoring technologies that are not only sensitive but also sustainable and deployable outside laboratory settings. Herein, a green synthesis strategy is introduced for producing copper oxide nanostructures with controlled morphology using Citrus limon extract as a biogenic reducing and structure-directing agent. By regulating the reaction pH, the growth of CuO was steered from disordered aggregates toward uniform, high-aspect-ratio nanorod structures, demonstrating a level of morphological control rarely achieved through phyto-mediated routes. The resulting phyto-mediated CuO nanorods (PM-CuONRs) were immobilised onto indium tin oxide electrodes and employed as the active interface in a miniaturised electrochemical sensor for phenol detection. Phenol was quantified indirectly through its adsorption-induced inhibition of ferri/ferrocyanide redox kinetics, providing a robust fouling-based sensing mechanism. The sensor delivered consistent responses across buffered solutions and real water matrices, including tap and river water, achieving limits of detection of 0.069 μg/L, 0.137 μg/L, and 0.801 μg/L, respectively. These detection limits are statistically estimated from blank and low-concentration replicate measurements and lie below the lowest experimentally tested standard (0.5 μg/L). Decreased sensitivity in natural waters was linked to matrix-induced surface crowding and competitive adsorption rather than degradation of the sensing interface. The platform further exhibited strong resistance to interference from common inorganic ions and organic compounds, alongside stable performance over extended storage. This study demonstrates how phyto-mediated nanostructure engineering can be directly translated into functional, low-cost sensing devices. The compatibility of the sensor with simple, 3D-printed microfluidic flow cells highlights its potential for portable and field-deployable water monitoring. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable pathway from green nanomaterial synthesis to practical environmental diagnostics.

title: Revealing the hidden heavy metal pollution in secondary aluminum dross: From environmental risk assessment to tailored removal strategy
abstract: Most previous studies on secondary aluminum dross (SAD) have addressed the removal or stabilization of N, F, and Cl, whereas the toxicity and mitigation of heavy metals have received limited attention. Here, the leaching behavior and environmental risks of heavy metals in SAD are systematically evaluated using multiple leaching protocols, revealing substantial metal mobilization under acidic conditions. Given the coexistence of heavy metals, reactive aluminum phases, and halide salts in SAD, an integrated and composition-specific solution is required. Accordingly, a tailored MgCl2·6H2O-assisted chlorination roasting strategy was developed to mitigate the heavy metal leaching risk through a dual-track mechanism of high-temperature evaporation and solid-phase stabilization. This process simultaneously stabilizes reactive aluminum phases, removes halide salts, enables chlorination-volatilization of most heavy metals, and immobilizes residual metals, ensuring compliance with stringent environmental safety criteria. On this basis, a segregation-chlorination-volatilization mechanism was proposed to elucidate the migration behavior of heavy metals. Furthermore, the flexural strength of ceramics sintered using treated powder increased by 31.9%, exhibiting enhanced resource utilization potential. Overall, this work fills a critical gap in the environmental risk assessment of SAD and provides a targeted strategy for coupling detoxification with resource recovery, supporting safer and more sustainable aluminum recycling.

title: Pt/Pd coatings on nickel foam working electrodes for simultaneous biohydrogen production and wastewater treatment in microbial electrolysis cells
abstract: Electrodes play a key role in microbial electrolysis cell (MEC), and the material composition, geometries, physicochemical properties, and surface morphologies of the electrodes directly determine energy conversion efficiency, energy consumption, hydrogen production, microbial stability, and wastewater treatment performance. In this study, a two-chambered MEC, cheese whey wastewater (CW), nickel foam (NiF) as the working electrode were used. A comprehensive set of electrochemical and surface characterization techniques was conducted, including linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), Tafel, field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), together with wastewater quality parameter and biohydrogen production rate measurements. To improve catalytic behavior, NiF were modified with Pt/Pd using electroplating and hydrothermal coating methods. Among all configurations, the hydrothermally Pt coated electrode (NiF-Pt-H) demonstrated the highest overall performance. NiF-Pt-H provided up to 124% higher electrical conductivity, nearly 99% reduction in charge transfer and diffusion resistance, up to 43% faster hydrogen production, 4212% increase in Cdl and electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), corrosion resistance improved by 135%, almost complete removal of major wastewater contaminants (COD, NH4+) approximately 99%. Surface characterization results confirmed a uniform distribution of noble metal species throughout the porous structure, which explains the observed improvements in electrochemical stability, catalytic activity, and mass transport behavior. These findings show that NiF working electrodes are a highly effective strategy for achieving simultaneous high efficiency biohydrogen production and advanced wastewater treatment in MEC. The proposed electrode architecture offers strong potential for scalable and sustainable waste to energy conversion technologies.

title: Assessing the benefits of material circularity in the textile sector: the case of MCashmere® fibres
abstract: The textile sector is widely recognized for the significant environmental impacts of its resource-intensive and polluting value chains. Cashmere fibres are a particularly critical case, as their production depends strongly on biodiversity and ecosystem services. Extensive grazing by cashmere goats in fragile regions such as Mongolia contributes to soil desertification, habitat degradation and declining species richness. Circular economy strategies that reduce reliance on land and virgin resources therefore represent a promising pathway to mitigate these pressures. Life cycle assessment (LCA) is a key method for evaluating potential benefits and impacts of such strategies; yet detailed and region-specific LCA data for cashmere fibre production and recycling remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by providing disaggregated, reproducible, process-based life cycle inventories for both virgin and recycled (MCashmere®) cashmere fibres, based on literature and primary industrial data. An attributional cradle-to-gate LCA is applied to provide the potential environmental impact profile of both the virgin and the recycled cashmere fiber production, and to analyse potential benefits of circular economy strategies in the textile sector using the circular footprint formula (CFF). The findings show that a circular system including recycled cashmere fibres consistently exhibit lower impacts across environmental indicators than a linear system using virgin fibres. The magnitude of the benefits depends on the methodological choice. Specifically, the potential impacts of recycled cashmere fibres production compared to the production of virgin cashmere fibres spans from 2 to 3 times by applying the CFF (representing a mature circular system), to more than 670 times, a theoretical maximal benefit obtained in a cut-off system where the recycled fibre's value chain excludes the upstream burden of virgin fibre production. Impact reductions are mainly driven by market related parameters, such as the substitution of virgin fibres with recycled ones (parameter A, determined by the elasticity between demand and supply of fibres) and by increased recycled content (parameter R1). In contrast, virgin cashmere production remains highly impactful due to extensive land use, water consumption, infrastructures and GHG direct emissions generating from animal digestion and manure. Despite methodological limitations of the CFF, the results robustly indicate that recycled cashmere aligns with circular economy principles by reducing dependence on virgin resource extraction.

title: Ensemble learning-based ecological speed optimization approach for plug-in hybrid electric vehicles with integrated energy consumption and battery aging
abstract: Both energy consumption and battery lifespan of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) are significantly affected by driving speed. However, precise optimization of ecological velocity remains challenging due to the absence of established relationships that reflect the influence of driving state on both energy consumption and battery aging. To address this issue, this study proposes a velocity optimization strategy that simultaneously considers powertrain characteristics and battery aging, aiming to jointly enhance fuel economy and battery lifespan. A stacking ensemble-based integrated operating cost model is developed to capture the mapping relationships among vehicle driving state, energy consumption, and battery degradation. This model evaluates the integrated operating cost during ecological velocity optimization, which incorporates both the cost of energy consumption and battery aging. Furthermore, an iterative dynamic programming approach is employed in conjunction with the ensemble learning model to optimize the ecological velocity trajectory by integrating Bellman's optimality principle with the data-driven cost model. The simulation results demonstrate that incorporating powertrain characteristics and battery aging into the PHEV ecological velocity planning facilitates superior speed trajectories, enhanced fuel economy and prolonged battery lifespan under various driving conditions.

title: Light-enhanced synchronous capture of uranium and iodine using Ag-doped amidoxime-functionalized carbon nanotube composites
abstract: The safe and sustainable development of nuclear energy urgently demands advanced materials capable of simultaneously capturing uranium(VI) and iodide from complex aqueous systems. Nevertheless, conventional adsorbents often struggle to synchronously sequester cationic uranyl ions and anionic iodide ions owing to mismatched active sites and inadequate charge-selective affinity. In this study, amidoxime-functionalized carbon nanotubes loaded with Ag nanoparticles (CNT-AO-Ag) were prepared using an in situ silver-ammonia reduction strategy. SEM-EDS, XRD, XPS, and BET analyses were used to characterize the material structure and surface properties. The composite integrates amidoxime functional groups and Ag nanoparticles on a CNT framework, providing complementary functionalities for U(VI) capture and iodide immobilization. The adsorption kinetics of both U(VI) and iodide were well described by the pseudo-second-order model, while both Langmuir and Freundlich models provided good fits to the equilibrium data. Notably, visible-light irradiation enhanced U(VI) removal, achieving a removal efficiency of 91.4% within 3 h, compared with 89.2% after 12 h in the dark. Based on the observed light-enhanced adsorption behavior, a possible mechanism is proposed in which the photoinduced charge carriers generated by silver nanoparticles may facilitate electron transfer between uranyl species and amidoxime coordination sites, thereby accelerating U(VI) adsorption. The coexistence of U(IV) and U(VI) after adsorption suggests that partial reduction of U(VI) may occur on the material surface. After five consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles, the composite retains good reusability. In the presence of the investigated competing metal ions, the U(VI) removal efficiency remained at 91.23%, whereas the removal efficiencies of the competing ions were below 10%, indicating preferential U(VI) uptake under the tested conditions. These findings demonstrate the potential of CNT-AO-Ag for the simultaneous capture of U(VI) and iodide under laboratory-simulated aqueous conditions. Further validation using realistic radioactive wastewater matrices is required before practical application can be established.

title: From fit to sustainability: How person–environment alignment shapes circular work practices
abstract: Organizations increasingly rely on employee-level capabilities to advance circular economy (CE) transitions, particularly in contexts marked by sustainability demands and evolving institutional expectations. Although prior research has acknowledged the relevance of individual motivation, competence, and organizational support for sustainable behavior, the integrated mechanisms through which person–environment alignment drives CE adoption and operational performance remain insufficiently examined. Addressing this gap and emerging organizational challenge, this study develops an original model grounded in person–environment (PE) fit theory and tests it using structural equation modeling with 1724 employees from a Brazilian agro-industrial company. The findings show that individual motivation and technical competence significantly reinforce value congruence, thereby strengthening perceptions of organizational support. Social influence emerges as the strongest driver of circular behavior, while sustainability-oriented goals amplify the effect of perceived support on CE adoption. Once embedded in routine work, circular practices substantially improve sustainable operational performance. The study offers a cohesive explanation of how psychological alignment, social norms, and organizational conditions jointly enable circular transitions. Theoretically, it extends PE fit theory to the CE domain by identifying value congruence and social influence as essential antecedents of circular behavior. Practically, it provides actionable guidance for designing work environments that align individual dispositions, social climates, and organizational priorities to accelerate CE implementation.

title: Development and optimization of rapid synthesized Ni-Fe electrodes for the OER in an alkaline electrolysis cell
abstract: The development of highly efficient and easily scalable electrodes is crucial for advancing alkaline water electrolysis. In this study, a corrosion-based synthesis method was employed to fabricate nickel-iron (Ni-Fe) electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This approach offers a rapid alternative with minimal precursor consumption compared to conventional techniques. The synergistic interaction between Ni and Fe species was leveraged to enhance catalytic activity. Through systematic optimization of precursor concentrations, reaction time, and temperature, the Fe-NaP/2 electrode was obtained using 1.050 g of ferric nitrate (Fe(NO3)3) and 0.050 g of sodium phosphate (Na3PO4), with a contact time of 2 min at 23 °C. The resulting material demonstrated excellent electrocatalytic performance, with an overpotential of 275 mV at a current density of 100 mA cm−2. Additionally, it exhibited low Tafel slopes, indicating high intrinsic activity. The improved performance is primarily attributed to the formation of Ni and Fe (oxy)hydroxide phases and a rough, amorphous surface morphology that promotes efficient charge transfer by increasing the number of active sites. These findings confirm that corrosion engineering can be an effective strategy for producing high-efficiency OER electrodes using minimal resources for hydrogen production.

title: Catalytic upcycling of waste polypropylene into light aromatics over bimetallic Ga-Zr modified hollow ZSM-5 under CO2 atmosphere
abstract: The high-value conversion of waste polyolefins is crucial for mitigating environmental pollution and recovering hydrocarbon resources. Herein, a Ga-Zr bimetallic-modified hollow hierarchical ZSM-5 catalyst (5Ga-Zr/ZSM-5-H) was developed for the catalytic pyrolysis of polypropylene (PP) to light monocyclic aromatics under a CO2 atmosphere. At 550 °C, the catalyst achieved relative aromatic and BTX (benzene, toluene, and xylenes) contents of 83.93% and 77.17%, respectively, corresponding to estimated feed-based yields of 55.30 wt% and 50.85 wt%. The apparent activation energy was reduced by 138.76 kJ mol−1. Comprehensive characterization, in situ FTIR, and DFT calculations revealed that the hollow hierarchical structure alleviates mass-transfer limitations, whereas the Ga–Zr synergy enhances C–H activation and dehydrogenation. Activated CO2 acts as a hydrogen acceptor and suppresses coke formation, promoting selective aromatization and catalyst stability.

title: Techno-economic assessment of lithium recovery from spent batteries by nanofiltration: trade-offs between recovery, purity and cost
abstract: The surging global demand for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) underscores the urgent need to secure sustainable lithium supply chains for the transition to a green economy. Over the past few years, hydrometallurgical routes have been widely explored to treat spent LIBs, valorise their components, and recover critical raw materials. However, achieving battery-grade metal purity requires advanced separation and purification technologies. Nanofiltration (NF) is emerging as a promising alternative due to its ability to discriminate between single-charge (Li+) and multi-charge (e.g., Co2+, Al3+) metals. Nevertheless, NF performance depends heavily on solution composition; specifically, the choices of leaching acid and neutralising alkali directly impact lithium recovery and purity. This study utilizes the Solution-Electro-Diffusion-Film model to assess the technical and economic viability of NF under different operational scenarios, comparing HCl and H2SO4 for leaching, alongside NaOH and Mg(OH)2(s) for neutralisation. The transport model was first calibrated using lab-scale experimental data, and subsequent predictive simulations evaluated single-pass and two-pass configurations under varying operating pressures and permeate recovery rates. The results reveal a distinct techno-economic trade-off: while chloride-based systems minimise operational costs, they yield lower-quality products. Conversely, sulphate-based systems incur higher costs and slightly lower Li+ recoveries but provide superior permeate quality, thereby significantly reducing the need for expensive downstream refining steps and offering a clearer path toward circular battery recycling.

title: Prospective assessment of emerging circular economy technologies: A case study for sewage sludge-to-biofuel via hydrothermal liquefaction
abstract: This study evaluates the prospective techno-economic and environmental performance of four hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL)-based technological pathways for converting sewage sludge into biofuels at facilities co-located with wastewater treatment plants. Two sewage sludge carbon-accounting cases based on IPCC guidelines are considered: a 100 wt% biogenic carbon case and a case containing 7 wt% fossil carbon in the sewage sludge stream. Four technological configurations differing in their energy sources for HTL and biocrude upgrading are considered. Technology 1 relies on natural gas for process energy and hydrogen production, while Technology 2 utilizes onsite biomethane. Technology 3 combines natural gas-based HTL with electricity-driven hydrogen production, whereas Technology 4 integrates biomethane-based HTL with electricity-driven hydrogen production. Their performance is assessed under three prospective background climate scenarios: REMIND-SSP2-Base (3.5 °C), Pkbudg1150 (below 2 °C), and Pkbudg500 (below 1.5 °C), for 2030, 2040, and 2050. An integrated techno-economic and environmental objective function (OF), applied within a technological superstructure, is used to evaluate and rank 36 scenarios for each carbon-accounting case. Results consistently identify Technology 4 as the optimal configuration across all scenarios. For a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) plant in 2025, maximum credits reach 697 € t−1 DSS for 100 wt% biogenic sludge and 510 € t−1 DSS for fossil-containing sludge under Pkbudg500. For an nth-of-a-kind (NOAK) plant in 2050, sensitivity analysis considering 10%, 50%, and 100% utilization of European sludge availability yields credits of 969–1008 € t−1 DSS and 732–776 € t−1 DSS, respectively. These findings highlight the potential of biomethane-integrated HTL with electricity-driven upgrading for economically and environmentally sustainable sewage sludge valorization within a circular economy framework.

title: Designing circular business models under rebound risk: Firm-level tensions and tendency statements
abstract: Circular business models (CBMs) may fail to deliver expected environmental gains when lower effective prices stimulate additional demand or secondary products do not sufficiently displace primary alternatives, causing circular production to add to primary production – a phenomenon known as circular economy rebound (CER). Drawing on paradox theory, this study combines focused integrative reviews of CBM and CER literature with a constructivist case study of an Italian textile company, involving 19 interviews with four organizational informants and 19 customer interviews, to investigate how firm-level CBM design choices relate to exposure to the market-level CER mechanisms of price effects and insufficient substitutability. The analysis identifies three non-mutually exclusive CBM design paradoxes associated with these CER mechanisms: Profitability vs Displacement, Short-term orientation vs Long-term orientation, and Product lifecycle extension vs Waste supply continuity. Building on these paradoxes and different combinations of case evidence, prior literature, and theoretical inference, the study develops thirteen context-sensitive tendency statements concerning potential links between CBM design choices and exposure to CER mechanisms. These statements underpin exploratory insights for future development and empirical assessment of firm responses. By linking CBM design tensions with CER mechanisms, the findings suggest treating displacement as a CBM design criterion alongside economic viability.

title: Polydopamine-derived carbon modified FeS2 electrodes for selective electrochemical Cu2+ capture from acidic electroplating wastewater
abstract: Selective capture of Cu2+ from acidic electroplating effluents remains challenging because of strong competition from protons and coexisting metal ions for binding sites. Here we designed a Prussian blue-derived FeS2 electrode encapsulated with a polydopamine-derived carbon interphase (FeS2@PDA-C) that couples electrically driven ion enrichment with sulfur-mediated Faradaic immobilization. The PDA-derived carbon interphase enhances electronic conductivity and electrolyte accessibility while preserving accessible sulfide sites for Cu–S interactions. FeS2@PDA‐C delivers a Cu2+ electrosorption capacity of 568.0 mg g−1 at 1.0 V. A distribution coefficient of up to 1.6 × 104 mL g−1 was achieved in the presence of competing ions, along with 88.6% Cu2+ removal from real electroplating wastewater. Mechanistic analyses reveal that Cu2+ uptake proceeds via electric double-layer adsorption, Cu–N interfacial coordination, and Cu–S complexation, followed by reduction of Cu2+ to Cu + to yield Cu2S. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further show that the PDA-derived N-doping strengthens Cu adsorption by promoting interfacial charge transfer and enhancing Cu–substrate interactions. This work demonstrates an interphase-engineering strategy that exploits strong Cu–S affinity for selective Cu2+ removal from real acidic electroplating wastewater.

title: Influence of fuel cell heat dissipation on the performance of a hydrogen-driven CO2 heat pump with PCM
abstract: To date, very few investigations have specifically addressed the influence of hydrogen fuel cell (HNFC) heat dissipation on energy flow pathways in an HNFC-driven CO2 heat pump (CMP) with a PCM tank (PK). Therefore, this study assessed the effects of natural convection heat transfer coefficient, natural convection heat transfer area, and forced convection heat transfer area on system performance. A simulation platform was established by coupling experimentally validated models of the HNFC, CMP, and PK. Results demonstrated that increasing the natural convection heat transfer coefficient from 5 W/(m2·K) to 25 W/(m2·K) caused a decline in hydrogen-to-electricity factor from 11.246 kWh/kg to 10.8744 kWh/kg (−3.3%) and a decrease in hydrogen-to-heat factor from 32.8165 kWh/kg to 32.1992 kWh/kg (−1.88%). When the natural convection heat transfer area was enlarged from 142 cm2 to 369.2 cm2, hydrogen-to-electricity factor decreased from 10.8744 kWh/kg to 10.4024 kWh/kg (−4.34%), and hydrogen-to-heat factor decreased from 32.1992 kWh/kg to 31.4996 kWh/kg (−2.17%). As the forced convection heat transfer area was increased from 23 cm2 to 59.8 cm2, hydrogen-to-electricity factor fell from 10.8744 kWh/kg to 8.8204 kWh/kg (−18.89%), and hydrogen-to-heat factor decreased from 32.1992 kWh/kg to 28.5092 kWh/kg (−11.46%). Thus, this study provided guidance for investigations into effects of HNFC thermal dissipation on performance of PCM-integrated CMP systems.

title: Enrichment trajectories associated with inoculation morphology and depth-resolved functional potential in polyurethane sponge-based anammox reactors
abstract: Carrier-assisted biomass retention can ease anammox start-up constraints associated with slow growth and biomass washout. However, the influence of initial inoculum structure on biofilm establishment and subsequent community depth distributions remains unclear. Two synchronously operated 3-L slow-moving bed biofilm reactors containing polyurethane (PU) sponges were inoculated with intact granules (R-G) or sludge fragments (R-S) from the same anammox reactor. Both reached a nitrogen removal rate of 0.40 g N/(L·d) within 16 d and maintained stable nitrogen conversion over 105 d. Between days 21 and 42, EPS protein and polysaccharide contents increased in both reactors, coinciding with the transition from discrete retained particles to integrated biofilms. By day 105, attached biomass reached 4.71 and 4.37 g VSS/L-reactor in R-G and R-S, respectively, revealing faster early accumulation in R-S but greater late-stage accumulation in R-G. Candidatus Brocadia and anammox-associated genes occurred throughout the 10-mm carrier depth, with core-weighted profiles in R-G and surface- or transition-weighted profiles in R-S. Under prescribed connected-pore architecture and matched substrate demand, the model estimated weighted-mean core accessibility above 83% for both NH4+-N and NO2−-N. By linking early cell-surface interactions to mature community profiles and nitrogen-cycling genes, these findings reveal how initial inoculum structure governs enrichment trajectories.

title: Assessing the temporal bioaccumulation of pharmaceuticals in lettuce grown in soil: A comparative evaluation of conventional, time-weighted, and kinetic modeling approaches
abstract: Concentration factors are widely used as key indicators to evaluate the bioaccumulation capacity of pharmaceuticals in crops grown in soils. However, their temporal reliability remains uncertain, particularly under dynamic exposure conditions. To address this issue, we conducted greenhouse experiments with lettuce (Lactuca sativa) seedlings exposed to 14 pharmaceuticals representing various ionic forms (neutral, cationic, and anionic), and harvested at 14, 28, 35, and 45 days. We found that conventional soil pore water (SPW)-based concentration factor frequently yielded missing values at later harvest stages due to undetectable concentrations in SPW, indicating the temporal instability of conventional concentration factors. To overcome this limitation, we introduced time-weighted concentration factors, which remained quantifiable across all harvest stages and exhibited a high Kendall coefficient of concordance (W > 0.86), indicating strong temporal consistency. These factors successfully captured cumulative exposure and provided more robust and reliable estimates of bioaccumulation capacity for studied pharmaceuticals. Additionally, a multi-compartment kinetic model was applied to derive compound-specific bioaccumulation rates, offering a dynamic perspective on uptake behavior. For compounds primarily taken up via passive transport, such as carbamazepine, caffeine, sulfamethoxazole, and lincomycin, the estimated bioaccumulation rates showed a linear correlation with their log D values (R2 = 0.90). This study highlights the importance of incorporating temporal dynamics into plant uptake assessments, as it can significantly improve the reliability and comparability of bioaccumulation evaluations across variable exposure durations.

title: Novel hydrothermal conversion of multisource solid wastes: Sustainable cementitious materials and potentially toxic elements immobilization
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (IFA) contains high content of CaO but limited amounts of SiO2 and Al2O3, necessitating the addition of supplementary aluminosilicate sources for its potential resource utilization in construction materials. Direct application of IFA in cementitious systems is critically limited by high levels of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) and soluble chlorides. This study innovatively applied hydrothermal (HT) curing to convert hazardous IFA into sustainable cementitious materials by adding both reactive coal fly ash (CFA) and inert kaolin as aluminosilicate sources. Compared to conventional air curing (20–90 °C), HT curing at 200 °C enhanced the compressive strength of IFA-CFA composites by 145–318% and that of IFA-kaolin composites by 300–373%. Mineralogical analyses revealed that tobermorite crystallized in IFA-CFA composites (CF50), contributing to higher Cr immobilization efficiency, but tobermorite exhibited thermal instability and led to pore coarsening above 225 °C. In contrast, IFA-kaolin composites (KF50) promoted the formation of a heat-resistant calcium aluminosilicate hydrate (C-A-S-H). This stable, highly polymerized microstructure maintained superior mechanical properties and effective encapsulation of PTEs such as Cu, Zn, Cd at elevated HT temperatures. Chloride removal reached 80.4%–82.7% at 225 °C, primarily through dissolution and steam-driven transport of dissolved chlorides. This work demonstrates that HT curing strategy is broadly applicable for IFA detoxification and resource recovery, effective with diverse aluminosilicate sources ranging from reactive to inert. The performance distinctions between the IFA-CFA and IFA-kaolin systems provide a scientific basis for designing HT-cured composites with tailored properties for specific engineering and environmental goals.

title: Microplastic distribution in relation to hydrological seasonality in the triple confluence of major upper Yangtze tributaries: insights from wet and dry seasons
abstract: River confluences are critical nodes for microplastics (MPs) accumulation. However, how MPs behave under varying hydrological scenarios in large river confluence zone remains poorly understood. This study systematically investigated the occurrence, flux, and driving factors of MPs in the confluence zone of the Min-Dadu-Qingyi River (upper Yangtze River basin). Surface water samples were collected during the wet and dry season, MPs were identified using micro-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and multivariate statistical analyses were applied to elucidate the coupled relationships between MPs characteristics and environmental factors. The results showed that MPs abundances ranged from 2.62 n/L to 25.40 n/L, with an average value of 8.77 n/L. Polyethylene (PE, 30.10%), low-density polyethylene (LDPE, 16.26%), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET, 14.32%) were the dominant polymers, with fragments overwhelmingly prevailing (82.53%). MPs abundance was significantly higher in the wet season than in the dry season, while the estimated MPs fluxes were also higher, with the maximum flux in the Min River reaching 1.18 × 108 n/s during the wet season. The risk assessment indicates that the pollution load index remains at a mild pollution level, but the polymer hazard index indicates a pollution class III (moderate risk) in the catchment area. Multivariate analysis revealed that in such regulated river systems, intense seasonal hydrological disturbances overwhelm local spatial heterogeneity, making the hydrological contrast between the wet and dry sampling campaigns the dominant factor shaping microplastic dynamics in this study. This study provides inferential evidence for seasonally modulated source-sink dynamics of MPs in river confluences based on the river surface water observations, and underscores the necessity of prioritizing seasonal hydrological dynamics in sampling design and pollution management strategies.

title: Economic–carbon optimization of macroalgae aquaculture under blue carbon objectives
abstract: As blue carbon strategies continue to advance, we developed a multi-objective optimization model for macroalgae aquaculture that maximizes net economic returns and minimizes carbon sequestration opportunity cost under historical cultivation and production constraints. The ε-constraint method was used to generate the Pareto frontier, from which a representative solution was selected using the minimum-distance-to-ideal-point criterion. We then compared this solution with observed cultivation patterns from 2020 to 2024 and examined its robustness through sensitivity analyses. The results revealed a clear nonlinear trade-off between the economic and carbon objectives. From the carbon-optimal to the economic-optimal solution, net economic returns increased by 22.9%, alongside increases of 35.0% in carbon sequestration opportunity cost and 11.7% in cultivation area. The representative solution captured 87.78% of the potential economic gain while incurring only 27.0% of the increase in carbon sequestration opportunity cost across the Pareto range. Relative to the average performance of the observed cultivation patterns from 2020 to 2024, it increased net economic returns by 8.88% and reduced carbon sequestration opportunity cost by 8.92%, mainly through structural reallocation rather than expansion of total cultivation area. The optimized allocation was relatively robust to alternative cost-allocation methods and changes in the effective carbon sequestration coefficient, although interannual parameter variation affected absolute objective values, particularly net economic returns. This study provides a quantitative basis for balancing economic returns and carbon sequestration in macroalgae aquaculture.

title: Decision-support model for prioritizing components for future circular economy investigation
abstract: Complex industrial products are often difficult to analyze for circular economy opportunities because relevant components may be hidden within multilevel Bill of Materials structures. This paper proposes a decision-support framework to support the identification and prioritization of product elements by combining environmental impact, supply risk, and cost. The framework is implemented as an interactive prototype and applied to an industrial case study from GE HealthCare involving an anonymized complex medical device. The tool enables users to navigate the product structure, select a decision scope, identify hotspots across several indicators, analyze lowest-level components, and build a Focus List of candidates for further investigation. A multicriteria decision-support module ranks candidate components using normalized weighted scoring, while complementary sensitivity analyses examine the influence of criterion weights, normalization procedure, and MCDA aggregation method on the resulting prioritization. The case study shows that the proposed approach improves visibility within complex product structures and supports the identification of components that may deserve further investigation for future circular economy or product-improvement actions. The framework does not replace expert judgement, but provides a transparent and traceable basis for prioritizing candidate components under environmental, supply-risk, and economic considerations.

title: Predicting international trade-link formation and dissolution for midstream copper products: Directed dynamic graph learning with multilayer industrial-chain information
abstract: Growing copper demand during the low-carbon transition highlights the need to monitor trade partnerships. However, the predictive value of information across the copper industrial chain remains insufficiently assessed. This study predicts directed trade-link formation and dissolution and evaluates the added value of multilayer information. Using annual bilateral trade data for 195 countries and territories during 2000–2023, we construct a directed multilayer network with a midstream target covering all subcategories under Harmonized System (HS) heading 7403 (unwrought refined copper and copper alloys). Upstream copper ores and concentrates and selected downstream copper products provide auxiliary trade information. ST-CopperNet, a directed dynamic graph learning framework, integrates direction-sensitive spatial encoding, cross-layer attention, and temporal encoding to rank country pairs for next-year link changes within complete task-specific candidate sets. Network connectivity increased alongside persistent partner turnover. In the 2020–2023 rolling information-configuration comparison, adding upstream, downstream, and chain-position information increased average precision (AP) from 0.151 to 0.238 for formation and from 0.497 to 0.599 for dissolution relative to the M configuration. Precision among the top 100 candidates (P@100) increased from 0.309 to 0.435 and from 0.610 to 0.756, respectively, and all improvements were significant in paired tests. Higher trade-value thresholds reduced AP and P@100, and uniform 1:5 negative sampling performed best among the compared strategies. Multilayer information thus provides an effective complement to midstream trade-link prediction. The framework supports potential-partner screening and existing-link monitoring and, with production and environmental data, can inform sustainable copper sourcing assessments.

title: More circular redistribution, less sustainable? Shortage-relief saturation and coordination-conditioned rebound under pharmaceutical waste-shortage-transport-carbon trade-offs
abstract: Pharmaceutical systems face a cleaner production paradox: useable and near-expiry medicines may be discarded while healthcare providers experience essential-drug shortages. Circular redistribution can reduce both pressures, but its redistribution-related sustainability value may change when matching, delay, transport carbon, trust, and self-protective inventory holding are considered jointly. Here, “circularity” is operationalized specifically as the normalized activation intensity of a pharmaceutical redistribution policy, not as economy-wide circularity or the physical share of medicines transferred. This study develops a data-informed system dynamics model of a stylized regional hospital-pharmacy redistribution network. External empirical and literature evidence anchor observable scales and relationship directions, while unobserved behavioral and operational quantities are reference-parameterized and uncertainty-tested. The model links pharmaceutical waste, shortage backlog, marginal redistribution transport carbon, trust, hoarding, and an integrated sustainability performance index over 52 weeks. Scenario analysis, coordination-preserved and capacity-mismatch circularity sweeps, mechanism ablation, alternative weighting and outcome indices, one-way and multivariate tests, and probabilistic Latin hypercube analyses were used. The direct shortage-relief channel reaches a model-implied saturation onset at approximately CI = 0.60; this onset is neither an empirically estimated threshold nor an SPI optimum. High redistribution activation remains sustainability-enhancing when baseline coordination is preserved (0.8822), and the best configuration in the 16-run high-activation factorial design reaches 0.8862, whereas the capacity-mismatch case falls to 0.7909. The study contributes an integrated dynamic explanation of how waste, shortage, coordination, transport, and behavior jointly condition pharmaceutical redistribution performance.

title: Interpretable machine learning links algal-bacterial symbiosis to wastewater C/N/P removal
abstract: Discharge of organic- and nutrient-rich wastewater can exacerbate eutrophication. Algal-bacterial systems can enhance pollutant removal and biomass recovery, yet cross-study links between bacterial communities and C, N, and P removal remain unclear. This study integrated literature-derived 16S rRNA data with nutrient-removal performance from algal-bacterial and bacteria-only systems and found that algal-bacterial systems generally showed higher C, N, and P removal efficiencies. Most bacterial genera were shared between the two systems, while PCoA based on CLR transformation and Aitchison distance revealed modest but statistically significant community differentiation, suggesting shifts in the relative abundances of shared taxa and a possible association between microalgal presence and bacterial community restructuring. CLR-transformed genus-level abundances were subsequently used to predict C, N, and P removal efficiencies, and eight supervised learning algorithms were compared using repeated 10-fold cross-validation. GLMNet performed best across all three tasks, being the only model with R2 > 0.7 for C removal and achieving R2 = 0.8247 and 0.7693 for N and P removal, respectively. Integrating LIME interpretation, Spearman correlation analysis, and between-system abundance comparisons identified key genera that were enriched in algal-bacterial systems and positively associated with the corresponding nutrient-removal efficiencies. Functional inference using PICRUSt2 and CNPS.cycle indicated that these key genera showed distinct predicted C-, N-, and P-metabolic profiles, including greater predicted potential for carbon transformation involving aerobic respiration, CO oxidation, and fermentation; ammonium-centered nitrogen metabolism involving organic-N mineralization, DNRA, ammonium uptake, and assimilation; and PhoR/PhoB-related phosphate-limitation responses. By integrating cross-study prediction, model interpretation, statistical prioritization, and functional inference within a unified framework, this study provides candidate taxa and functional traits for subsequent experimental validation and process optimization.

title: Financial dynamics of circular construction in the United States
abstract: The construction industry is one of the most resource-intensive industries in the world and accounts for the largest portion of raw material use in the United States. A shift from the traditional linear construction to a circular one is needed to minimize the demand for raw materials. However, industry decision-makers are often dissuaded from incorporating circular materials, as studies have shown economic factors tend to outweigh environmental factors. While research has been conducted on the barriers hindering the adoption of a circular economy (CE) model in construction, few papers focus solely on economic factors. There is a missing analysis of economic factors from a socio-technical system perspective in developed countries with systemic low CE weight. To fill this gap, this study aims to identify cost factors preventing the adoption of circular construction within the U.S. through a socio-technical system and provide a framework to overcome these barriers. Using a System Dynamics (SD) perspective informed by literature, policy analysis, and stakeholder interviews, this study identifies how cost barriers emerge from interactions among design decisions, stakeholder incentives, material recovery processes, and life-cycle economic considerations. Results show that circular construction implementation is constrained by reinforcing feedback mechanisms linking upfront costs, life-cycle costs, deconstruction activities, salvaged material markets, and stakeholder decision-making. The analysis further demonstrates how alternative circular construction strategies generate different cost trajectories over the project life cycle. Based on these findings, this study proposes a framework to support industry practitioners and policymakers in prioritizing interventions that improve the economic feasibility of circular construction. This study contributes a dynamic understanding of circular construction implementation costs, reveals the feedback structures that drive cost-related adoption barriers, and provides a decision-support perspective for evaluating circular construction strategies across the asset life cycle.

title: Coordination mechanisms for closed-loop supply chains under carbon tax policy
abstract: Centralization in a carbon-taxed closed-loop supply chain can increase recycling and social welfare without reducing total emissions. At a common tax rate, emissions rise when demand expansion outweighs the reduction in emissions per unit, showing that recycling gains alone do not guarantee an environmental benefit. In the illustrative parameterization (not an industry estimate), comparing each decision mode at its own optimal tax rate yields a 25-percentage-point recycling gap and a realized decentralized-to-centralized welfare ratio of approximately 0.80. We establish these results in a three-tier Stackelberg model with a vertically integrated firm as the centralized benchmark. We also derive the participation and government budget conditions under which a combined revenue-sharing and recycling-subsidy contract reproduces the centralized decisions; it is win-win for supply-chain members when both participation constraints hold, and its subsidy is covered by modeled carbon-tax revenue in the benchmark.

title: The impact of transport on CO2 emissions along the construction flat glass supply chain in Europe
abstract: An integrated geospatial modelling tool was developed to estimate and map annual CO2 emissions from road freight transport across the European construction flat glass supply chain. One reference scenario and five truck payload-capacity mitigation scenarios are assessed across eight hypothetical supply chain circuits. The study considers transport connections among raw material extraction, glass manufacturing, transformation, final production, retail, construction, and end-of-life management facilities. Due to the absence of company-level origin-destination data, the eight hypothetical road freight supply chain circuits were constructed using georeferenced facility data and shortest-path routing. Depending on the circuit, the resulting transport networks comprise between 2230 and 9790 nodes. These circuits are intended for exploratory comparison and should not be interpreted as observed or fully representative logistics networks. In the reference scenario, estimated emissions range from 30 to 241 kt CO2/yr across circuits. Germany, Poland, Italy, France, and Spain together account for approximately 80% of the estimated emissions within the analysed circuits. Monte Carlo simulations are used to assess uncertainty in selected transport and operational parameters, including fuel-consumption, transported quantities, empty-return rates, country-specific emission factors, and silica-sand allocation assumptions, and to evaluate their effects on estimated CO2 emissions across circuits and scenarios. The results provide a scenario-based assessment of road-freight emissions and demonstrate the importance of explicitly accounting for uncertainty in vehicle-capacity and operational assumptions in logistics-emission modelling.

title: Evaluating material handling systems for sustainable open-pit mining across production scales and sustainability priorities: An integrated FCM-ER framework
abstract: The transition toward sustainable material handling systems (MHSs) in open-pit mining requires decision-support approaches capable of addressing multiple sustainability criteria, causal interdependencies, and uncertainty in expert judgments. This study proposes an integrated Fuzzy Cognitive Map-Evidential Reasoning (FCM-ER) framework to evaluate five alternative MHSs: diesel trucks (DT), diesel-electric trucks (DET), battery-electric trucks (BET), hydrogen-electric trucks (HET), and in-pit crushing and conveying (IPCC). Unlike previous studies that compare a limited number of haulage alternatives using independent criteria, this study simultaneously evaluates five conventional and emerging MHSs using 27 sub-criteria spanning economic, environmental, social, and technical-operational dimensions. The framework captures causal interactions among sustainability criteria through FCM, incorporates uncertainty arising from incomplete and imprecise expert judgments using ER, and examines how production scale influences technology selection. FCM was used to derive criteria weights, while ER aggregated uncertain performance assessments into expected utility scores on a 0-100 scale. The framework was applied to large-scale and small-scale open-pit mining cases. For the large-scale case, IPCC achieved the highest utility score (57.20), closely followed by BET (56.81), indicating that capital-intensive low-emission technologies become increasingly attractive when costs are distributed over long mine lives. HET, DET, and DT ranked third to fifth, respectively. In contrast, DET ranked first in the small-scale case (54.39), followed by DT (50.03) and BET (49.64), highlighting the importance of lower capital requirements and shorter payback periods. Preference-based sensitivity analysis demonstrated that technology selection depends on both mine characteristics and stakeholder priorities. The proposed FCM-ER framework provides a transparent and flexible decision-support tool for sustainable haulage planning under uncertainty.

title: Ecosystem service consequences of global agricultural trade across 186 countries: A four-dimensional Kaya-LMDI decomposition
abstract: Global agricultural trade affects ecosystem service (ES) supply through land-use change, yet the contribution shares of the driving factors lack systematic quantification. We introduce the Kaya-LMDI decomposition, established in the energy and carbon-emission fields, into the analysis of trade's ES effects, decomposing the 2000–2020 change in four-dimensional ES supply (carbon sequestration, CS; water yield, WY; soil conservation, SC; food production, FP) across 186 countries into four factors—economic scale, trade dependence, land expansion and ecological intensity. We find that (1) the land effect is the largest negative factor in all four ES dimensions (−143.4% to −212.8%), an accounting contribution rather than direct ecological degradation, while the scale and trade effects are consistently positive; (2) the intensity effect diverges in direction and is the key to the divergence in net ES change, with food production rising and water yield falling, and after 2010 the factor contributions generally contract while water yield and soil conservation reverse; (3) the land effect in the Global South is 1.2–1.5 times that in the North, bearing a disproportionate share of the land effect associated with agricultural land expansion; (4) 73.7%–84.4% of countries achieve decoupling between trade growth and ES change, predominantly weak, with negative decoupling in food production concentrated in the South. The trade-embedded Kaya-LMDI framework quantifies the trade contribution independently, can be extended to indicators such as virtual factor flows, and provides a quantitative basis for region-specific environmental governance and cleaner-production decisions in agricultural trade.

title: Factors influencing consumers’ behavioral intentions toward plastic-free nursery production in the U.S.: An application of the health belief model
abstract: Plastic materials have dominated horticultural production, especially within the nursery and greenhouse sectors, since the 1980s. Microplastics pose significant environmental and human health concerns due to their potential impact on aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, water quality, and human health. While existing studies have examined plastic use in horticultural production from the perspectives of scientific communities and industry experts, less attention has been given to the consumer perspective. Based on the Health Belief Model (HBM), this study examines psychological variables and demographic characteristics associated with consumers' willingness to pay for nursery products produced with plastic-free practices and their support for plastic-free nursery production practices. A total of 1235 survey responses were descriptively analyzed, and then a hierarchical multiple linear regression model was used to identify significant variables influencing consumers’ behavioral intentions. Regression results indicated that perceived severity, benefits, self-efficacy, health motivation, and environmental self-identity positively predicted both behavioral intentions. Perceived susceptibility positively predicted consumer support, whereas perceived barriers negatively predicted support. Neither perceived susceptibility nor perceived barriers significantly predicted willingness to pay in Model 2. Age negatively predicted both behavioral intentions. HBM constructs explained a substantial proportion of the variance in both behavioral intentions, and incorporating health motivation, environmental self-identity, and demographic characteristics further enhanced the models' explanatory power. These findings suggest that communication strategies promoting plastic-free nursery production should emphasize perceived benefits, health motivation, environmental self-identity, and perceived self-efficacy to encourage consumer support and willingness to pay.

title: Global forest quality assessment using satellite observations and ecological potential references
abstract: Global forest assessments commonly emphasize forest extent, biomass, and productivity, but these indicators alone cannot adequately characterize the multidimensional nature of forest quality. Here, we developed an ecological-potential-constrained State–Stability–Pressure (SSP) framework to assess global forest quality at 500 m resolution using satellite observations. Ecological-potential references were established within biome-by-forest-origin groups. The framework integrates three dimensions: State, representing the realization of canopy height, aboveground biomass, and net primary productivity (NPP) relative to ecological potential; Stability, characterizing short-term interannual NPP variability; and a positively oriented Low-pressure score (LP), representing mapped external pressures from human modification, recent forest loss, and fire disturbance. These dimensions were combined multiplicatively into a Forest Quality Index (FQI). The global mean FQI was 0.514, with low, medium, and high-FQI categories accounting for 21.7%, 35.8%, and 42.5% of the analyzed forest area, respectively. State was the dominant relative limiting dimension in 89.3% of forest pixels. Productivity realization exceeded structural stock realization in 70.7% of forest pixels, revealing widespread stock–productivity asymmetry. External comparisons with GEDI-derived foliage height diversity and plant area index showed positive associations with FQI (Spearman's ρ = 0.62 and 0.61, respectively), providing complementary evidence of structural consistency. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the principal FQI patterns were robust to changes in ecological-potential references, model parameters, and NPP observation windows. The resulting framework provides a spatially explicit and decomposable assessment of potential-relative forest condition, supporting broad-scale forest comparison and the identification of dominant limiting dimensions without equating FQI with comprehensive ecological integrity or biodiversity status.

title: Multi-indicator parameter adaptive method with parallel subpopulation information exchange for heat exchanger network optimization
abstract: Heat exchanger network (HEN) synthesis is crucial for reducing energy consumption and capital investment in process systems. The random walk algorithm with compulsive evolution (RWCE) shows promise for solving combinatorial optimization problems. However, when applied to HENs, its greedy nature and the absence of information exchange among individuals often result in decreased population diversity, insufficient search capability, and premature convergence. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-indicator parameter adaptive method with parallel subpopulation information exchange (MPM-SIE). First, multiple guidance indicators are employed to enable control parameters to adaptively respond to the requirements of different evolutionary stages, ensuring sufficient competition among variables and facilitating the identification of promising structures. Second, a parallel computing framework is introduced, in which threads are divided into exploration and exploitation groups. The exploration group learns from local optima, while the exploitation group learns from the global optimum. A balance between exploration and exploitation is achieved through information exchange between the two subpopulations. Specifically, the decline rate of the optimal total annual cost and the variation rate of the unit number are adopted as guidance indicators to regulate the step size, the probability of rejecting good solutions, and the probability of accepting inferior solutions. Population diversity, measured by the Jaccard similarity coefficient, serves as a global evaluation indicator. An individual interchange perturbation strategy is also introduced to help escape local traps. The proposed method is validated on four benchmark cases. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses premature convergence and enhances global search capability, confirming its effectiveness.

title: Synergistic intensification of fluorine conversion and migration by high-shear reaction and diatomite in wet-process phosphoric acid production
abstract: Fluorine associated with phosphate rock (PR) readily migrates among gas, liquid, and solid phases during wet-process phosphoric acid (WPA) production, leading to fugitive emissions and fluorine retention in phosphogypsum (PG), which pose environmental risks and resource losses. Herein, a source-control strategy integrating high-shear reactor (HSR) intensification with diatomite (DE)-induced fluorine conversion was developed to achieve in-situ conversion of free HF into stable liquid-phase H2SiF6. Mechanistic elucidation revealed that H2SiF6 exhibits markedly superior liquid-phase retention than HF, owing to its enhanced thermodynamic stability and increased steric hindrance, which collectively impede its volatilization. In contrast, F− ions generated from HF dissociation tend to be incorporated into the gypsum lattice, thereby limiting fluorine recovery. Accordingly, DE was employed as an external active silicon source to drive the in-situ conversion of HF into H2SiF6, while HSR intensification was applied to enhance liquid-solid mass transfer and accelerate the reaction kinetics. The intensified process achieved a total fluorine leaching efficiency of 97%, with 94% of the initial fluorine leached into the liquid phase in the form of H2SiF6, while gaseous fluorine release was substantially suppressed. Notably, the liquid-phase fluorine proportion was increased by approximately 20% relative to the conventional process. These results confirm that the dynamic interfacial renewal and intensified surface reactions induced by high-shear mixing collectively steer fluoride migration pathways toward H2SiF6 formation, rather than gypsum incorporation or gaseous release. The resulting clean gypsum contained ≥98 wt% CaSO4·2H2O and ≤0.02 wt% F. This study not only provides a mechanistic foundation for fluorine migration control during WPA, but also offers a practical, scalable reference for cleaner production and efficient fluorine resource recovery in the phosphate industry.

title: How digital technology innovation affects agricultural economic resilience – New evidence from double machine learning
abstract: Amid rising global uncertainty, strengthening agricultural economic resilience (AER) is critical to national food security and sustainable development. Digital technology innovation (DTI), a key factor underlying current industrial transformation, is reshaping agricultural production, operational models, and resource allocation. However, systematic empirical evidence on whether and how DTI enhances AER remains limited. This study uses a 2010–2023 prefecture-level dataset covering 278 cities in China and employs double machine learning (DML) to examine the effect, mechanisms, and heterogeneity of DTI on AER. The findings show that DTI significantly improves AER, with a stronger impact on Recovery and Re-orientation. It enhances AER through the supportive base of the agricultural industrial chain and the organizational base for agricultural industry digitalization. The beneficial impact of DTI is greater in higher marketized areas, lower urban–rural disparity, and major grain-producing functions. Regarding climate risk, DTI significantly improves AER and its four dimensions under lower climate risk, while under higher climate risk, its effect is mainly reflected in Renewal. Regarding digital infrastructure, the marginal effect of DTI is stronger in non-pilot areas of the “Broadband China” initiative, while in pilot areas, it only has a significant positive effect on Renewal. Quantile DML results further show that the effect of DTI increases as the level of AER rises. The spatial effect indicates that local DTI may attract resources from neighboring cities to converge in the innovation-advantaged areas, thereby exerting a negative spatial spillover effect on neighboring cities. By examining the economic effects of DTI in agriculture from a resilience perspective, this study extends the analytical framework of agricultural economy research beyond the external digital environment and provides empirical evidence and policy implications for improving AER.

title: Low-carbon targeted pretreatment of steel slag using recyclable materials for enhanced volume stability: Multi-objective optimization based on RSM-BO-GA
abstract: Free calcium oxide (f-CaO) is a major cause of steel slag volume instability, while applying uniform aging conditions to different particle-size fractions can lead to inefficient reagent use. This study developed a particle-size-targeted pretreatment using recyclable ethylene glycol and oxalic acid, and optimized the process through an RSM-BO-GA framework. RSM established response models and feasible regions, after which Bayesian optimization (BO) and genetic algorithm (GA) searches refined candidate solutions, enhanced exploration of the response space, and verified convergence consistency and solution stability. Accordingly, the optimized conditions for 3–5, 5–10, and 10–15 mm steel slag were 3.64% oxalic acid for 13.58 h, 3.43% for 14.63 h, and 3.30% for 15.23 h, respectively. Compared with RSM alone, RSM-BO-GA reduced oxalic acid dosage by 9.92%–16.98%, treatment duration by 3.40%–17.62%, and predicted residual f-CaO by 8.1%–13.1%. Experimentally, the semi-quantitative f-CaO contents decreased from approximately 7.0%, 6.5%, and 6.6% to approximately 1.3%, not distinguishable by XRD, and 1.5%, respectively, corresponding to decreases of about 81% and 77% for the measurable 3–5 and 10–15 mm fractions. Moreover, the expansion ratios decreased from 4.88% to 4.56% for untreated slag to 0.98%–0.66% after targeted treatment. Meanwhile, the treatment promoted the formation of CaC2O4-rich aging layer and reduced the release of several potentially harmful elements. The ethylene-glycol-based solution achieved approximately 98% recovery and stable performance over 10 reuse cycles. Furthermore, treatment-stage carbon emissions were 16.36–17.08 kg CO2 e/t, lower than hot-water and steam aging.

title: Techno-economic study of a distributed renewable energy system for a French paper mill
abstract: This paper evaluates a distributed renewable energy system for a paper mill located in Rouen, France, with the objective of achieving net-zero emissions by eliminating the paper machine's reliance on natural gas and grid electricity. To this end, a renewable energy system utilizing hydrogen as the primary fuel carrier to meet the mill's thermal power demand of 5.26 MW and electrical power demand of 12.45 MW was designed. Three scenarios were considered: wind power, solar power, and a hybrid system combining both. This analysis reveals that, while wind power yields a lower nominal Levelized Cost of Energy, a mixed scenario emerged as the most cost-effective option to satisfy continuous baseload requirement. The study demonstrated that a mixed scenario consisting of 12 wind turbines and 43,924 solar panels emerged as the most cost-effective option. Consequently, the economic footprint of this renewable energy system proves viable. However, reductions in hydrogen subsystem costs and offshore operating expenses (OPEX) could further lower the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) as the maturity of the technology advances. The cost avoided of 23,513.66 €/tCO2 represents a steep initial mitigation cost for industrial-scale decarbonisation projects, though it could be further improved with broader adoption and technological advancements. These findings highlight the technical and economic progress required to make such deep-decarbonisation projects increasingly competitive.

title: Salting-out directed porous lignin-based IPN gels for fluorescent detection and adsorptive removal of Co2+ and Hg2+ ions
abstract: Traditionally, the underutilization of biomass resources and heavy metal contamination in water have become pressing environmental challenges, driving the urgent need for sustainable multifunctional materials. Herein, we report a lignin-based interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) gel, fabricated via hydrogen-bond-driven topological interlocking between p(DMAPS-co-JS)-HDDA and AL-g-PEGE, thereby enabling the selective detection and adsorptive removal of Co2+ and Hg2+. The salting-out effect of SO42− (1.5 M) was used to modulate polymer chain aggregation and pore-size distribution, thereby enhancing mass transfer. Quantitative adsorption studies showed that the adsorption capacity of Co2+ increased from 88.7 mg/g to 104.7 mg/g. The adsorption behavior conforms to the Langmuir monolayer chemical adsorption model. Crucially, the gel retains more than 90% of its adsorption performance in complex real-world water matrices, demonstrating exceptional environmental robustness. Additionally, the gel exhibited selective fluorescence enhancement toward Co2+ and Hg2+, enabling sensitive and discriminative detection, while lignin components and quaternary ammonium groups endowed the material with antibacterial activity. This work integrates three functions: fluorescence detection, antibacterial activity, and efficient adsorption, which provides a new idea for the design of lignin-based high-value environmental functional materials.

title: A multifunctional double-layer hydrogel for simultaneous alkalinity indication and soil remediation in alkali-stressed environments
abstract: Saline-alkali soils in arid regions pose major challenges to agriculture due to poor water management and high salt content. Hydrogels have shown promise in improving soil moisture and reducing salt damage, but most lack multifunctionality and cannot simultaneously monitor soil conditions while delivering nutrients. This study solves this gap by developing a novel temperature-responsive, pH-indicative, and phosphorus-loaded double-layer hydrogel MC-g-PAA/P(VPES-co-AM) and MC-g-PAA/DAP/P(VPES-co-AM)) via template polymerization for integrated soil amelioration and qualitative visual indication of alkalinity. The hydrogel consists of a lower water-absorbing layer (MC-g-PAA) and an upper color-changing layer (P(VPES-co-AM)), exhibiting excellent swelling capacity (1956 g g−1), reversible thermo-responsiveness with a lower critical solution temperature (LCST) about 40°C, and distinct pH-dependent chromism. Structural characterization confirmed MC participation in graft polymerization and porous morphology conducive to water retention and controlled nutrient release. In saline-alkali soil, the hydrogel significantly reduced Na+ migration, lowered pH and electrical conductivity, and enhanced maize germination and seedling growth, particularly when loaded with diammonium phosphate (DAP), Available phosphorus increased through sustained release. The multifunctional design integrates salt inhibition, moisture regulation, visual pH indication, and nutrient supply, offering a promising “indication-remediation-fertilization” strategy for sustainable saline-alkali land restoration. This work provides a scalable approach for eco-functional polymeric materials in agricultural.

title: Oxygen vacancy-induced selectivity switching in Mn2V2O7/BiVO4 heterojunction photocatalysts for photocatalytic water splitting
abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting represents a vital technology for efficient solar-to-hydrogen conversion, yet remains bottlenecked by incomplete understanding of oxygen evolution half-reaction mechanisms, which seriously impairs precise construction of high-performance photocatalysts. This study systematically reveals the intrinsic correlations between intermediate adsorption characteristics and water oxidation reaction pathways through modulating the electronic structure of oxygen sites and oxygen vacancy on Mn2V2O7/BiVO4 (MBO) heterojunctions, while simultaneously optimizing photocatalytic hydrogen production efficiency. In situ Raman spectroscopy reveals enhanced O-O stretching vibrations in oxygen-vacancy-containing MBO (MBOv) samples with prolonged illumination time, facilitating the four-electron pathway for water oxidation to O2. Conversely, pristine MBO exhibits diminished O-O bond strength with amplified O-H stretching signatures favoring two-electron H2O2 formation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that oxygen vacancies stabilize *OOH intermediates through local electronic reconfiguration, accelerating four-electron oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics, whereas lattice oxygen facilitates *HOOH intermediate formation to enhance selectivity for two-electron H2O2 pathway. Remarkably, optimized MBOv-3 achieves near-theoretical H2:O2 stoichiometry (≈2:1) with peak oxygen evolution rate reaching 3622 μmol h−1 g−1 and hydrogen evolution rate reaching 7344 μmol h−1 g−1. The pristine MBO exhibits excellent H2O2 production performance, with a maximum yield of 1569 μmol h−1 g−1. These findings establish new paradigms for reaction pathway engineering in photocatalytic systems and provide design blueprints for dual-functional photocatalyst development.

title: Janus WSSe/Ti3C2 2D/2D heterojunction: A high-efficiency piezocatalyst for anaerobic tetracycline degradation and hydrogen evolution
abstract: The coexistence of water antibiotic pollution and energy shortage has become a severe global challenge. Piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical vibration energy into chemical reactions, provides a promising strategy for wastewater remediation and clean hydrogen production. Traditional centrosymmetric two-dimensional tungsten dichalcogenides suffer from weak piezoelectric polarization and severe charge recombination, restricting their piezocatalytic activity. Herein, Janus WSSe with asymmetric crystal structure was rationally hybridized with highly conductive Ti3C2 MXene to fabricate a series of 2D/2D heterojunction piezocatalysts. Benefiting from the broken central symmetry of Janus WSSe and tight interfacial coupling between WSSe and Ti3C2, the optimized WSSe/Ti3C2 (5:1) composite exhibited superior piezocatalytic performance. Under anaerobic ultrasonic conditions, it achieved 93.7% degradation efficiency of tetracycline within 4 h and a high hydrogen evolution rate of 1.232 mmol g−1 h−1 simultaneously. Contrastly, the hydrogen evolution rate reached 1.744 mmol g−1 h−1 in 10 vol% methanol solution, which was 3.07 times that of pure WSSe. Electron spin resonance and radical trapping tests confirmed that piezo-generated electrons acted as the major active species, and no reactive oxygen species were produced in the oxygen-free environment. Electrochemical, photoluminescence and piezocurrent measurements demonstrated that Ti3C2 significantly accelerated interfacial charge transfer and suppressed carrier recombination. Furthermore, the anaerobic reductive degradation pathway of tetracycline was proposed based on the identification of intermediates, which differed greatly from aerobic oxidation pathways. This work not only fills the research gap of Janus WSSe in piezocatalysis, but also offers a novel design strategy for high-efficiency bifunctional piezocatalysts toward practical water treatment and energy recovery.

title: Sewage sludge phosphorus recovery delivers climatic gains yet brings environmental and economic trade-offs: Insights from a carbon-emergy-economy-based integrated TOPSIS framework
abstract: Climatic, environmental, and economic interactions governing sewage sludge management remain poorly understood, which hinders evidence-based optimization of sludge treatment strategies. This study developed a harmonized pathway-level assessment framework integrating carbon footprint accounting, emergy analysis, and economic evaluation, coupled with a Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) multi-criteria model to rank the comprehensive performance of alternative treatment schemes. Three scenarios sharing a thermal hydrolysis–anaerobic digestion (TH-AD) front-end were evaluated for a large centralized sludge treatment facility in Beijing, China: Sc1 (TH-AD + deep dewatering + sanitary landfilling), Sc2 (TH-AD + struvite recovery + deep dewatering + sanitary landfilling), and Sc3 (TH-AD + deep dewatering + drying–incineration + thermochemical phosphorus recovery from ash + inert residue landfilling). Under full phosphorus substitution (α3 = 1.00), Sc3 achieved the lowest carbon footprint intensity (−3.30 kg CO2-eq t−1 DS) and highest baseline environmental sustainability (1.58), whereas Sc2 showed the best economic performance (NEBR = 0.36). Sc3 maintained a net-negative carbon footprint only at α3 > 0.985, but retained its TOPSIS advantage until α3 declined to approximately 0.794. The emergy ranking was robust to DALY-factor uncertainty but sensitive to combustion-air accounting. Under equal weights, Sc3 ranked first (Ci = 0.63) in terms of comprehensive performance, underscoring that pathway preference is conditional on agronomic effectiveness, accounting boundaries, and economic priorities.

title: Advancing cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment in aviation: application of an integrated methodology to turboprop propulsion systems
abstract: Despite the well-recognized environmental relevance of the aviation sector, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) studies remain limited, largely due to the scarcity and confidentiality of Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) data. Within the Clean Aviation AMBER project, which is developing a hydrogen fuel-cell hybrid-electric demonstrator for regional aircraft, this study addresses the conventional 2020 state-of-the-art turboprop used as the project baseline. In this context, this study applies an integrated inventory framework to the aviation sector, combining top-down (module-level) mapping with bottom-up (component-level) refinement. The approach builds on the long-standing experience gained in the automotive sector and combines screening and iterative LCI practices with expert review and explicit data-quality assessment. Its application enables the construction of a transparent and progressively updatable inventory under conditions of data scarcity and industrial confidentiality and allows the resulting model to be used to identify the main material and module hotspots and the priorities for subsequent inventory refinement. The applied case study is a 2020 state-of-the-art turboprop propulsion system in the 1500–2500 kW power class, relevant for regional aircraft applications. The propulsion system is decomposed into major modules (namely the gas turbine engine and the propeller system), sub-modules, and components, with material compositions mapped at different levels of granularity. The system boundary includes raw-material extraction and upstream production of the metals, alloys and CFRP constituents represented in the inventory, while component-specific manufacturing operations, use, maintenance and end-of-life are excluded. The resulting inventory is implemented in an LCA model to derive indicative environmental impacts using the Environmental Footprint method. The baseline climate-change impact is approximately 9.4 t CO2 eq. per propulsion system. Sensitivity analyses show that this result is influenced by assumptions on primary-magnesium production and carbon-fibre production, with the contribution of the propeller system ranging from approximately 23% to 46.5% across the CFRP production scenarios. These results illustrate the applicability of the framework and identify the materials and assumptions that should receive priority in subsequent inventory refinement. Overall, the primary outcome of the study is the development of a transparent, expert-reviewed and progressively updateable inventory structure rather than definitive impact values. The work demonstrates that LCA modelling in aviation can be effectively initiated at an early stage of data maturity and provides a foundation for progressively refining environmental assessments as more detailed industrial data become available.

title: Assessing microplastic fibre emission potential in Europe's textile waste trade
abstract: The rapid expansion of fast fashion has intensified microplastic fibre (MPF) pollution from textile waste. This study investigates long-term trends (2004-2024) in European Union (EU) textile-waste trade and evaluates the associated MPF emission potential using a novel indicator, the Textile Trade Microplastic Intensity (TTMI). To examine microplastic emission risks embedded in the used-textile trade, literature-derived emission factors were applied to estimate country-level transboundary flows of textile waste and their associated MPF release potential.
