Results show that although textile waste constitutes only a marginally increasing share of total waste trade (slope < 0.001), export flows exhibit a pronounced shift toward synthetic-rich compositions. The ratio of synthetic-to-natural fibres increased by 663 percent, from 2.53 to a peak of 19.30, suggesting an increasing externalization of synthetic-textile waste through international trade. Trade-share disparities across the EU (0.38-45.87%) reveal the development of specialized textile-waste redistribution hubs, especially in Eastern Europe. However, synthetic-textile waste is expanding across both high and low trade share countries. MPF emission potential increased over time for both imports and exports (slope = 0.04-31.60), with export-related values consistently higher (5.86-702.81 mg·capita−1·yr−1). Fixed-effects regression analysis identifies domestic consumption levels, trade openness, and carbon-intensive production systems as key drivers of TTMI variation. These effects are particularly strong in high trade-share countries, where the textile industry plays a dominant economic role (β = 8.73, p < 0.01). The findings highlight the uneven distribution of MPF risks across EU textile waste trade networks. These results underscore the need for life-cycle-based policy interventions and strengthened extended producer responsibility frameworks that address microplastic emissions across international textile value chains.

title: A decomposition-based hybrid neural network for 24 h ahead sewer water-depth forecasting and operational risk identification
abstract: Real-time sewer water-depth prediction is essential for identifying surcharge risks and improving drainage system operation. However, sewer monitoring data are highly nonlinear and affected by rainfall, infiltration, and operational disturbances. This study developed a hybrid CEEMDAN-DBO-LSTM (CDL) framework for hourly water-depth forecasting and degree-of-fill-based risk warning. The framework was evaluated using 92,614 processed records from 142 monitoring points in a smart sewer system in Baiyun District, Guangzhou, China. Complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) was used to extract multiscale temporal features, while dung beetle optimizer (DBO) optimized long short-term memory (LSTM) parameters. Results showed that the CDL model achieved R2 values of 0.860–0.918 for 6–24 h forecasting horizons and reduced prediction errors by about 15%–17% compared with LSTM. The predicted water depths were further converted into operational warning states, achieving overall accuracies of 92.0%–95.6%. Field replay validation using four representative nodes further demonstrated the performance of the forecast-to-warning workflow, with R2 = 0.872 and a three-state warning accuracy of 85.1%. The proposed framework provides an effective data-driven approach for real-time sewer risk identification and supports intelligent drainage system management.

title: Biochar recycling for sustainable remanufacturing of polymer composites
abstract: Although biochar reinforced composites show better environmentally friendly, excellent performance, and broad application prospects, the challenge of the difficulty in effectively separating and recycling retired biochar reinforced composites urgently needs to be addressed. This study proposes a recycling strategy based on pyrolysis recovery and remanufacturing. This study proposes a recycling strategy based on pyrolysis recovery and remanufacturing. Biochar reinforced composites were first prepared by melt blending and hot pressing using biochar and high-density polyethylene (HDPE). The composites were then pyrolyzed at 1000°C for 2 h under an N2 atmosphere at a flow rate of 200 mL/min, and the recovered biochar (RB), with a recovery yield of 32.5%, was used to prepare RB reinforced composites by the same method. One recycling cycle was examined. The results showed that RB was essentially the same as biochar in terms of structural properties and the stable interface bonding of RB reinforced composites was also achieved by the mechanical interlocking structure. Compared with BHC30, RBHC30 retained 107.1% of the flexural strength, 103.0% of the flexural modulus, 105.8% of the elongation at break, 99.7% of the tensile strength, and 100.9% of the tensile modulus, while the impact toughness was retained at 91.0%. Moreover, RB reinforced composites also exhibited similar excellent mechanical properties due to the interfacial structure that enabled effective stress transmission, better thermal properties due to the good nucleation effect of RB, and remarkable electromagnetic shielding performance due to the continuous conductive network of RB. The SET values of BHC70 and RBHC70 were 52.47 and 50.54 dB, respectively. These results confirm the feasibility of the recycling strategy based on pyrolysis recovery and remanufacturing and provide a feasible technical path for the high-value recycling of biochar-reinforced composites.

title: Bridging theory and practice for circular urban food systems: An expert-informed conceptual framework and sustainability assessment
abstract: Urbanization is reshaping how, where, and which foods are being demanded, produced, distributed, and consumed around the world while also intensifying multidimensional sustainability challenges in the global food system. Increasing circularity in urban food systems is emerging as a promising solution to these economic, environmental, and social challenges, yet its conceptualization remains fragmented, constraining the development of coherent strategies, policies, and evaluation methods. Drawing on a constructivist epistemology and qualitative data from 12 expert interviews across academia and practice, this paper develops a transdisciplinary heuristic comprising of three interrelated components: (i) an empirically grounded definition of a circular urban food system (CUFS); (ii) a provisional systems map visualizing interactions among actors, activities, drivers, feedback loops, and trade-offs; and (iii) a multi-layered, context-sensitive sustainability assessment capable of generating both goal-level dashboard outputs and a composite performance index. The first two components form the conceptual framework that clarifies what CUFS are and how they operate while the third component translates this new understanding into a structured yet adaptable assessment approach for measuring and monitoring progress toward sustainable development. Together, they equip city governments, researchers, and practitioners with a common language and practical toolkit for measuring CUFS performance and guiding evidence-based policy across diverse urban contexts.

title: Joule heating–driven rapid in situ growth of carbon nanotubes with low energy consumption
abstract: In situ growth of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) on carbon fiber (CF) surfaces is an effective strategy to enhance the performance of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP). Joule heating-driven growth, with its low energy consumption and high efficiency, is expected to replace chemical vapor deposition. However, related studies are extremely limited. This study systematically investigates the effects of electric current, catalyst concentration, energization time, and electrochemical anodic oxidation (EAO) pretreatment on CNT growth. The results demonstrate that current and time have greater influence than catalyst concentration, with the optimal parameters determined as 4.5 A(679 °C)/0.02 mol/L/30 s. Insufficient parameters lead to a shortage of catalytic sites and active carbon sources, while excessive parameters cause catalyst agglomeration and excessive amorphous carbon deposition, ultimately resulting in deactivation. CNT growth exhibits a clear energy threshold: temperature (determined by current) governs the reduction state of the catalyst and thereby influences growth. 564 °C (3.5 A) is identified as the onset temperature for CNT growth. EAO can improve the activity and roughness of CF surfaces, thereby regulating catalyst anchoring and distribution. The sample with EAO pretreatment achieved the best CNT forest and CNT-CF properties. CNT-CF directly determines CFRP performance. The electrical resistivity, single-filament tensile strength, and contact angle of the CNT-CF were improved by 89%, 19.4%, and 29.9%, respectively. These enhancements originate from current-induced lattice strengthening of fibers and the additional conductive pathways, cross-linking with graphite microcrystals, and capillary action provided by CNT network.

title: A water-food-carbon nexus framework informs region-specific optimal strategies for agricultural sustainability in China
abstract: Reconciling food production with water security and carbon mitigation remains a major challenge for sustainable agriculture. Yet how water–food–carbon (WFC) interactions evolve across space and time, and which factors are associated with variations in their synergy, remain poorly understood. Here, we combine exploratory spatiotemporal analysis with interpretable machine learning to examine WFC synergy across 365 prefecture-level cities in China from 2000 to 2022. We quantify WFC synergy using a bivariate index integrating water productivity and carbon productivity, and characterize spatial persistence and nonlinear driver–response associations. WFC synergy increased by 24.3% overall but remained strongly spatially clustered, with persistent local trajectories. Improvements were concentrated in major northern agricultural regions, whereas some cities in southern and southwestern China experienced declines. Irrigation intensity showed the strongest negative association with synergy, whereas grain yield, per capita grain availability, and grain supply–demand balance were generally positively associated with synergy. Agricultural inputs exhibited comparatively weaker associations overall but were increasingly associated with lower synergy at high levels, indicating diminishing returns and nonlinear environmental costs. Climatic and ecological conditions further modified these relationships, with higher temperature and potential evapotranspiration generally associated with lower synergy, whereas vegetation cover showed positive associations. These findings suggest that improving agricultural WFC sustainability requires greater emphasis on irrigation and production efficiency rather than continued expansion of resource inputs. Regionally differentiated strategies that decouple food production from additional resource use and GHG emissions are therefore critical for advancing low-carbon and resource-efficient agricultural transitions.

title: Multidimensional impact assessment of household energy transition pathways on the economy, environment, health and society
abstract: In the context of China's "dual carbon" strategy, the residential sector has emerged as a critical domain of national final energy consumption. The prevailing household energy structure, predominantly reliant on carbon-intensive solid fuels, continued to intensify greenhouse gas and PM2.5 emissions, while simultaneously exacerbating health inequalities across social groups through differentiated pollution exposure pathways and heterogeneous health risk mechanisms. Drawing on longitudinal data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) spanning 2012-2022, this study developed a comprehensive analytical framework for household energy transition (HET) integrating economic, environmental, health, and social dimensions. Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to identify the net causal effects of HET, complemented by heterogeneity analysis to reveal disparities across social groups. Machine learning algorithms were employed to construct a predictive model and identify key predictors of HET. Four scenario pathways grounded in the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) framework were developed to simulate PM2.5 concentration reductions, health improvements, monetized health benefits, and health inequality effects under alternative HET pathways. This study provided robust empirical evidence for the comprehensive evaluation of divergent HET pathways, and offered actionable policy implications for advancing the HET and fostering high-quality development in China under the "dual carbon" targets.

title: “Tailored Solutions”: The enhancement path of heavily polluting enterprises’ green technology innovation ——A qualitative comparative analysis based on fs-QCA
abstract: Green technology innovation (GTI) serves as a vital engine for advancing economic green transformation and achieving the “dual carbon” goals. Based on the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) theory, this study selects 102 heavily polluting enterprises (HPEs) listed on China's Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share markets as research samples. Centering on the activation of corporate agency, it adopts the fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fs-QCA) method to explore the “joint effects” of multiple antecedent conditions on GTI in HPEs. The findings indicate that: (1) GTI in HPEs arises from the complex interplay of multiple factors, and no single factor constitutes a necessary condition for either high or non-high GTI; (2) Two distinct configuration paths can facilitate the enhancement of GTI in HPEs, which are summarized as the “market-social synergy” ability-motivation co-creation path and the “government-driven” motivation stimulation path. Among them, the “government-driven” motivation stimulation path represents the prevalent path to boost GTI for China's HPEs; (3) Further analysis identifies diverse linkages between government and market forces. The organic integration of “market dominance with government guidance” proves to be the most efficient mode, which jointly enables HPEs to achieve high GTI; (4) The analysis of deviant configurations reveals that when applying the established AMO theory originating from human resource research to organizational behavioral studies, signaling serves as a necessary precondition. That is, beyond sufficient ability, motivation and opportunity, firms' GTI behaviors demand signal guidance from the government or society. This study remedies the limitations of existing research that neglects corporate agency and broadens the research horizon of configuration studies on firm-level GTI. Meanwhile, it identifies the critical prerequisite for the application of AMO theory at the organizational level. The findings offer valuable implications for GTI practices of HPEs and help regulators formulate targeted policies to promote GTI in HPEs by stimulating corporate agency at the source.

title: UV-aged polyethylene film microplastics intensify phytotoxicity under cadmium co-exposure in sweet potato: Integrated soil biochemical disruption and metabolomic responses
abstract: Microplastics are emerging contaminants that interact with co-occurring heavy metals in soil, with potential implications for crop productivity. However, the role of microplastic aging in modulating metal phytotoxicity and underlying metabolomic responses remains poorly understood. In this study, a 60-day pot experiment was conducted to investigate the combined effects of pristine and UV-aged polyethylene microplastics (PEMPs) and cadmium (Cd) on soil biochemical processes, plant physiology, and metabolomic responses in sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas L.). Results showed that co-exposure to Cd and PEMPs, suppressed soil enzyme activities (amylase, urease and phosphatase by up to 28%, 24%, and 21%, respectively), altered soil C, N and P-related biochemical properties and nutrient distributions. These soil disturbances were associated with inhibited plant growth, decreased chlorophyll content and enhanced oxidative damage and antioxidant responses, as indicated by elevated MDA, SOD and GSH levels. Metabolomic analysis revealed substantial reprogramming of primary and secondary metabolism, including alterations in amino acids, fatty acids, and carbohydrate metabolism, as well as disruption of the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, suggesting perturbation of central carbon metabolism and stress adaptation both in roots and shoots. Shoot Cd concentration did not differ significantly among Cd-containing treatments, while aged PEMP-Cd produced stronger growth inhibition, oxidative responses, and metabolic perturbations, reflecting largely additive effects of aged PEMPs and Cd on plant growth. This reveals that the agro-ecological risk of weathered plastic residues is not driven by heavy metal accumulation alone, but is associated with coordinated disruption of soil enzymatic functioning, nutrient balance, oxidative homeostasis and plant metabolism. Overall, this study suggests that UV aging of PEMPs may intensify phytotoxicity under Cd co-exposure through coordinated changes in soil biochemical properties, plant physiology and metabolic dysregulation, providing insights into the interactions between aged PEMPs and Cd in agroecosystems. These findings emphasize the urgent need to adopt cleaner agricultural practices, enforce post-harvest film recovery, and transition toward non-toxic biodegradable mulching alternatives.

title: Paying attention to sustainability: The role of attentional fit in mitigating firms’ environmental exposure
abstract: Firms are increasingly under pressure to integrate environmental issues into their strategy. Because environmental risks vary by organisational context, understanding how firms manage their specific environmental exposure is critical to improving their financial and environmental outcomes. We use the Attention-Based View of the firm (ABV) to introduce the concept of “attentional fit”, the alignment between internally prioritised issues and externally defined environmental exposure. In doing so, we shift the focus from the quantity of attention to its quality, emphasising issue relevance—an understudied dimension in both exposure and ABV research—to explain how attentional fit shapes firm performance. Empirically, we operationalise attentional fit by proposing a novel textual analysis measure that identifies gaps in attention which we apply to 11,000+ 10-K Risk Factor Disclosures from approximately 2200 companies, spanning the five-year period from 2014 to 2018. Our results show that exposure to environmental issues is negatively associated with both financial and environmental performance and that attentional fit moderates this relationship. We contribute to theory by demonstrating how the quality of managerial attention may enhance the strategic management of environmental exposure. Practically, our findings can help managers address material risks and opportunities, give investors a benchmark to hold firms accountable for attention gaps, and enhance the effectiveness of regulations and disclosure standards.

title: Translating ecological mechanisms into action: Leveraging niche complementarity and selection effects for subtropical forest management
abstract: Subtropical forests are vital for global biodiversity and carbon sequestration, and understanding how structural diversity influences biomass accumulation is essential. However, the mechanisms remain unclear across forest types. This study investigated how structural diversity, mediated by forest type and environmental conditions, drives biomass stocks across three characteristic subtropical forests: coniferous forests (CFs), broadleaved forests (BFs), and mixed coniferous–broadleaved forests (MFs). We evaluated biomass stocks of 90 plots by measuring aboveground, belowground, and total biomass and analyzed the roles of structural diversity and environmental factors, including soil properties, climate, and topography, in shaping biomass patterns. Although aboveground biomass showed no significant differences, belowground biomass was significantly higher in BFs (49.82 t ha−1) compared to CFs (27.09 t ha−1) and MFs (24.52 t ha−1), with a significantly lower above-to-belowground biomass ratio (BFs = 3.01, CFs = 6.36, MFs = 5.19). Structural diversity positively influenced biomass stocks, consistent with the niche complementarity effect. In contrast, the combination of high belowground biomass and low structural diversity in BFs suggested a concurrent selection effect. Environmental factors primarily indirectly affected biomass stocks by modifying structural diversity, although soil properties also exerted a substantial direct effect. These findings underscore that structural diversity plays a crucial role in influencing biomass stocks of subtropical forests and highlight the value of maintaining the structural diversity of forest stands, particularly those rich in broad-leaved species, to enhance biomass stocks. Forest managers can apply these insights by designing multi-layered afforestation technical plans while utilizing selective harvesting to sustain horizontal and vertical canopy diversity.

title: Attributional and consequential life cycle assessment of end-of-life options for flexible pipelines from oil well decommissioning
abstract: Decommissioning oil wells in Brazil will generate large quantities of subsea pipelines that require end-of-life (EoL) management. This study evaluated four EoL options for flexible pipelines using attributional and consequential life cycle assessment (LCA) with system expansion: (1) landfill disposal; (2) steel recycling combined with mechanical recycling of high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polyamide (PA), and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF); (3) steel recycling combined with energy recovery from HDPE and PA and mechanical recycling of PVDF; and (4) pipeline reuse. Substitution rates of 100% for recycled polymers and 24% for steel scrap were adopted, and their effects were evaluated through sensitivity analyses. For reuse, the difference between well and pipeline service lives resulted in a Reuse Efficiency Factor (REF) of 37.5%, which was used to calculate the credit for avoided new pipeline manufacturing. Attributional LCA identified landfill disposal as the lowest-impact option, whereas, under the adopted substitution and reuse assumptions, consequential LCA produced the opposite ranking, with reuse showing the lowest impacts, generally followed by mechanical recycling, energy recovery, and landfill disposal. Relative to landfill disposal, reuse avoided approximately 5140 kg CO2-eq per t of pipeline for global warming potential (GWP), corresponding to an estimated upper bound of 1.34 billion kg CO2-eq from the decommissioning of 261,368.60 t of flexible pipelines in Brazil over the next decade, assuming that all pipelines still within their service lives are available for reuse. These findings show that the modeling perspective can reverse the environmental ranking of EoL options and that reusing remaining pipeline service life can reduce demand for new pipelines.

title: Climate-resilient and ecologically screened production opportunities for black pepper and long pepper in Asia under future climate change
abstract: Climate-driven redistribution of tropical cash crops can create adaptation opportunities while simultaneously increasing pressure on ecologically sensitive land. To support preventive cleaner-production planning, we developed a staged framework linking Asia-wide climatic suitability projections for black pepper (Piper nigrum) and long pepper (Piper longum) with independent cultivation-site correspondence and ecological safeguards in China. We combined Asia-wide GLM–RF models, spatial-block validation, PCA-env niche analysis, three CMIP6 GCMs across SSP126/245/585, uncertainty diagnostics, and China-based cultivation and ESI/HQ evidence. Spatial-block CV yielded AUC/TSS values of 0.876/0.719 for P. nigrum and 0.784/0.606 for P. longum, respectively. Both were lower than random-CV estimates, indicating that random partitioning inflated apparent predictive performance. Corrected niche overlap was Schoener's D = 0.572 and Warren's I = 0.757; 97.0% of the current black-pepper binary envelope overlapped long pepper. Under SSP585–2090, multi-GCM median suitable area increased from 2.53 to 6.72 × 106 km2 and from 12.27 to 24.42 × 106 km2, respectively. Differences across GCMs, thresholds and algorithms, together with climatic extrapolation, identified model-dependent gains requiring targeted verification rather than certain cultivable land. To add present-day, decision-relevant evidence, we assessed independent Chinese cultivation-site correspondence and applied ecological safeguards. All 46 surveyed black-pepper sites yielded finite raster scores; 14 corresponded to the current climatic envelope (30.4%; Wilson 95% CI: 19.1%–44.8%). With ESI≥0.92 and avoidance of relatively high/high habitat-quality areas, only 7313 and 115,982 km2 (7.37% and 9.13% of Chinese climatic bases) remained as lower-conflict candidates. This staged framework connects climatic opportunities, observed correspondence and ecological-conflict prevention to guide further field and agronomic assessment.

title: Binder-specific influence of natural and recycled fine aggregate particle size on the sustainability performance of mortars
abstract: Previous studies have largely assessed recycled fine aggregate mortars using isolated performance indicators, leaving their binder-specific mechanical, durability, environmental, and economic trade-offs insufficiently understood. This study develops an integrated framework for selecting binder-specific fine aggregate particle sizes by balancing mechanical, durability, environmental, and economic performance. Natural fine aggregate (NFA) and recycled fine aggregate (RFA) particle size fractions ranging from 0.25 to 2.0 mm were investigated in geopolymer and cement mortars. Mechanical performance was evaluated through compressive strength, while durability was assessed using strength retention and mass change response under 5% NaCl and 5% HCl exposure for up to 84 days. Environmental impacts were quantified through a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment, and economic performance was evaluated using material and variable processing costs. The normalized mechanical, durability, environmental, and cost indicators were integrated into a sustainability index (SI). Cement mortars achieved substantially higher compressive strength, reaching 73.23 MPa at 28 days, whereas geopolymer mortars generally maintained higher strength retention under NaCl and HCl exposure. Under the adopted multi-criteria framework, geopolymer mixtures received more favorable environmental and cost scores than OPC mixtures, although NaOH production remained a major environmental hotspot. G-RFA0.25 achieved the highest durability performance, potentially reflecting the filler effect and surface reactivity of fine RFA in the alkaline matrix. Conversely, G-RFA2.0 achieved the highest SI of 0.708, supported by its high durability score (0.925) and superior environmental (0.859) and cost (1.000) scores, partly due to its lower processing-energy demand. Therefore, G-RFA2.0 represented the highest-ranked alternative under the investigated conditions and equal-weight assessment framework.

title: Environmental sustainability begins at the top: The combined role of CEO attention and power
abstract: Firms aiming to implement environmental projects require strong leadership from their chief executive officers (CEOs) to drive through changes in environmental strategies and, hence, performance. This study follows Ocasio's (1997) attention-based view and the CEO power literature to theorize and empirically test the proposition that superior corporate environmental performance requires that the CEO has a strong environmental orientation and the power and authority to overcome resistance from competing interests within and outside the firm. This power may take the form of CEO control power (based on share ownership) and CEO persuasive power (based on tenure). We empirically disentangle these complex relationships in Japan, a country with a distinctive corporate governance system and a distinctive cultural context. Using a longitudinal dataset of 159 firms (328 CEOs) across 18 industries from 2012 to 2020, our empirical findings provide full support for all hypotheses within our integrative research framework. Our study contributes to the literature on environmental management by empirically verifying the significance of aligning CEO environmental orientation with different CEO power bases in tackling complex environmental problems.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on incentives and misalignments in prospective sustainable ship recycling: The Finnish maritime cluster
abstract: Ship recycling can recover substantial material and component value from end-of-life vessels, but responsible dismantling also requires strict environmental, safety, and waste management standards. These requirements may improve sustainability performance while increasing the costs and risks borne by the actors responsible for end-of-life decisions. Previous research has identified major economic, environmental, regulatory, technological, and organizational barriers to sustainable ship recycling, as well as stakeholder conflicts and incentive problems. However, limited empirical attention has been given to how value and burdens are perceived to be distributed across actors, where these distributions become misaligned, and how respondents associate possible responses with such misalignments in prospective high-standard recycling systems. This study examines these issues in the context of the prospective development of domestic sustainable ship recycling in Finland, drawing on 50 open-ended questionnaire responses from maritime actors and experts. The responses were analyzed through thematic analysis. The analysis indicates that respondents perceived potential value across material recovery, business opportunities, environmental and social outcomes, and knowledge development, whereas key costs, risks, and responsibilities were located at specific decision and investment points. Four recurring forms of perceived misalignment were identified: end-of-life decision misalignment, standards-cost misalignment, lifecycle misalignment, and flow-investment misalignment. The analysis links respondents' proposed responses to these four interpretive categories, although their feasibility and effectiveness were not tested. The study offers a differentiated, context-specific framework for understanding stakeholder perspectives on the prospective viability of high-standard ship recycling in Finland and provides implications for the future development of sustainable ship-recycling capacity in Finland and comparable maritime settings.

title: Patterns and factors associated with residential vacancy in the Chinese megacity of Chongqing: implications for embodied carbon emissions
abstract: Amid China's rapid urbanization, residential vacancy has become a prominent issue, yet systematic evaluations of its upfront embodied carbon emissions (ECEs) remain limited. This study focuses on the main urban area of Chongqing, integrating nighttime light (NTL) imagery, web-scraped real estate data and census records to estimate the vacancy rate. Subsequently, a life-cycle assessment (LCA) was employed to quantify ECEs across materialization, transportation, and construction stages at the district and sub-district scales. Results showed that 20.44 Mt of ECEs were locked in vacant housing, with materialization, construction, and transportation accounting for 84%, 13%, and 3%, respectively. High-emission hotspots were concentrated in the northern peripheral areas. Buildings completed in 2010–2020 accounted for 46.37% of the locked embodied carbon, while post-2020 vacant housing also constituted a notable component of the current underutilized embodied-carbon stock. In the predictive importance analysis, geographic location ranked first among the included housing attributes, followed by building age and housing price. These findings underscore the importance of improving public amenities and living conditions in high-vacancy communities, regulating new housing supply, and reusing existing housing stock to improve housing stock utilization, enhance embodied-carbon utilization efficiency, and avoid further idle carbon lock-in.

title: Renewable generation shares are not enough: Threshold conditions for cleaner electricity in OECD countries
abstract: Adding renewable generation does not uniformly produce cleaner electricity because its carbon-reduction performance depends on the energy system into which it is introduced. This study examines when wind and solar generation shares are associated with lower electricity carbon intensity across 36 OECD economies during 2010–2023 (2010–2022 for specifications that include energy intensity, which is unavailable for 2023). The nominal panel contains 504 country-year observations; the main estimation sample contains 465. Two-way fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors estimate average within-country associations, and Hansen panel-threshold models identify changes across energy-intensity and fossil-generation regimes. In the average model, a one-percentage-point increase in wind or solar generation share is associated with reductions of 5.67 and 5.37 gCO2/kWh, respectively (associations, not causal effects; see Section 3.2). The threshold results qualify these averages. Solar's negative association weakens markedly above an energy-intensity threshold of 1.638 tonnes of oil equivalent per thousand 2015 USD (bootstrap p = 0.083 with 1000 replications), becoming statistically indistinguishable from zero in the upper regime. Both the wind and solar associations weaken as fossil generation rises. However, the pattern differs: the negative wind association disappears entirely above a fossil-share threshold of 84.8%, whereas the negative solar association merely shrinks in magnitude (from −18.7 to −3.9 gCO2/kWh) above a much lower fossil-share threshold of 10.14% (95% CI: [5.7%, 13.1%], p < 0.001). Renewable generation shares and cleaner production are therefore not equivalent. Effective electricity decarbonization requires that renewable deployment be coordinated with energy-efficiency improvements, fossil-generation retirement, grid reinforcement, storage, demand flexibility, and market arrangements that enable renewable output to displace thermal generation.

title: Light/dark-cycle-mediated microbial selection and metabolic differentiation reshape pollutant removal pathways in microalgal–bacterial granular sludge
abstract: Light/dark cycle (LDC) is a key operational parameter regulating light energy input and algal–bacterial interactions in microalgal–bacterial granular sludge (MBGS) systems. However, how different LDCs affect nitrogen and phosphorus removal performance and the associated removal pathways in MBGS remains unclear. In this study, three LDCs (12 h/12 h, 4 h/4 h, and 2 h/2 h) were applied under the same total light energy input to systematically investigate pollutant removal and transformation characteristics, microbial community composition shifts, and metabolic potential in MBGS systems. The potential mechanisms underlying the differentiation of nitrogen and phosphorus removal pathways under different LDCs were further elucidated. The results showed that high removal efficiencies of COD, NH4+-N, and PO43--P were maintained when the LDC was shortened to 4 h/4 h and 2 h/2 h. Meanwhile, TN removal efficiencies increased from 72.6 ± 6.06% and 72.16 ± 6.58% to 84.1 ± 11.94% and 88.03 ± 8.73%, respectively. Despite comparable TN removal efficiencies between the two shortened LDCs (p > 0.05), the TN removal pathways differed markedly. Under the 4 h/4 h LDC, higher abundances of glycogen-accumulating organisms/denitrifying glycogen-accumulating organisms, together with greater intracellular carbon storage and denitrification potential, were associated with a higher contribution of bacterial simultaneous nitrification and endogenous denitrification (SNED). In contrast, the 2 h/2 h LDC exhibited higher microalgal photosynthetic activity and nitrogen assimilation potential, along with higher abundances of functional microorganisms associated with polyphosphate-accumulating organisms/denitrifying polyphosphate-accumulating organisms, resulting in TN removal jointly mediated by microalgal assimilation and bacterial SNED. Although PO43--P removal efficiency did not differ significantly among different LDCs, LDC altered the relative contributions of enhanced biological phosphorus removal, microalgal assimilation, and bacterial assimilation to phosphorus removal. Overall, the LDC influenced nitrogen and phosphorus removal pathways and their relative contributions in MBGS systems by modulating microalgal photosynthetic pigment accumulation and physiological status, functional microbial differentiation, and key metabolic processes. These findings provide a theoretical basis for optimizing light-time allocation to achieve efficient nitrogen and phosphorus removal in MBGS systems.

title: Evaluating the equity of environmental sustainability and economic growth kinetic energy conversion based on planetary boundaries
abstract: Environmental sustainability (ES) is increasingly pressured by multiple planetary boundaries, yet its relationship with economic growth kinetic energy conversion (EGKEC) and the associated spatial equity implications remain insufficiently understood. Based on panel data from 30 Chinese provinces over the period 1990 to 2020, we develop a “Boundary Constraints-Kinetic Energy Conversion-Equity Evaluation” framework to measure ES and EGKEC and analyze their spatial matching and interaction mechanisms. The results reveal a clear spatial mismatch between ES and EGKEC, with most provinces falling into Quadrant III. Their interaction shows factor-specific heterogeneity, with phosphorus exhibiting the strongest bidirectional relationship. Spatial inequity also varies across environmental factors. Intra-regional inequity is highest in North China and lowest in Northeast China, whereas inter-regional inequity is most pronounced between North/East China and West China. The sources of inequity differ by factor. Carbon inequity is shaped by both intra-regional and inter-regional differences, while inequities in other factors are mainly driven by inter-regional differences. Moreover, the effects of ES and EGKEC on inequity vary across factors, with carbon and phosphorus showing the most significant effects. These findings clarify the spatial misalignment between ecological constraints and economic transformation, and provide a scientific basis for designing differentiated policies that balance planetary boundary safety with regional equity.

title: Leveraging metabolites from straw degradation to engineer microbial communities for enhanced soybean nitrogen fixation capacity
abstract: Straw decomposition byproducts are known to enrich nitrogen-fixing microbial communities, the molecular mechanisms governing their assembly and functional enhancement remain elusive. To address this, we established a continuous enrichment strategy targeting nitrogen-fixing bacteria during straw decomposition and combined it with multi-omics analysis and microbial community assembly theory to investigate the straw-decomposing nitrogen-fixing bacteria (SDNFB). Results revealed significant accumulation of organic acids (OA) and lipids (LL) during enrichment, both positively correlated with nitrogen-fixing community structure (P < 0.05). Straw decomposition intensified homogeneous selection, driving the targeted enrichment of key diazotrophs like Pseudomonas and Comamonas. Structural equation modeling confirmed that OA and LL accumulation, mediated by this assembly mechanism, boosted expression of the nitrite reductase gene (nrfA) by 85.08% compared to the initial consortium before enrichment. Metabolomic analyses further showed that lipid and amino acid metabolism pathways act synergistically to maintain redox homeostasis and optimize nitrogen allocation, underpinning enhanced nitrogen fixation. When formulated as a bioinoculant, the SDNFB consortium improved soybean growth: increasing biomass, nutrient uptake, and antioxidant capacity while mitigating oxidative stress. This work elucidates how straw-derived metabolites shape functionally efficient microbial consortia through deterministic assembly, offering a science-based foundation for next-generation biofertilizers that enhance nitrogen use efficiency and reduce environmental burdens in sustainable agriculture.

title: Crisis as catalyst: Board composition and ESG controversies in crisis conditions
abstract: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) controversies are discrete, incident-based events with reputational and financial consequences that aggregate ESG scores overlook. We examine whether board gender diversity, board tenure and board-specific skills are associated with firms’ exposure to such controversies, and whether these associations differ between stable and crisis periods. Using a balanced panel of 386 S&P 500 firms for 2017–2022 and the LSEG (formerly Refinitiv) ESG Controversies Score, where higher values mean fewer controversies, we interact each board attribute with a post-COVID indicator in two-way fixed-effects models and test the post-COVID associations directly. The within-firm association between board gender diversity and the controversy score becomes significantly more positive after 2020, with no sign of change in earlier years. The shift is robust to sample trimming, alternative samples, control sets and inference procedures, but weakens when board characteristics are lagged. The post-COVID association itself is positive but not statistically distinguishable from zero. Board tenure and board-specific skills show no significant association in either period and no robust change, and dynamic panel estimates are too weakly identified to be informative. The evidence is associational: the relation between gender diversity and controversy exposure changed when stakeholder scrutiny intensified, consistent with a crisis-contingent resource dependence account, but more diverse boards cannot be shown to have reduced controversies, and changes in media attention, disclosure and economic conditions may have contributed. For large listed firms under intensive ESG scrutiny, board evidence from stable periods may not carry over to crises.

title: Beyond Slices: a Narrative-Driven, Multi-User, Multi-Modal Virtual Reality System for Medical Imaging Presentation.
abstract: Patient education in pediatric oncology is particularly challenging when radiologists and surgeons rely on conventional 2D diagnostic imaging to explain tumors to patients and their families. Standard MRI and CT scans present anatomy as grayscale image slices, making it difficult for non-experts to understand the tumor's three-dimensional structure and its spatial relationship to surrounding tissues. In addition, caregivers frequently ask “why and how did this happen?”, requiring explanations that go beyond visualizing anatomical abnormalities. This work proposes a narrativedriven, multi-user extended reality (XR) approach that presents 3D anatomical reconstructions derived from 2D imaging data. The system emphasizes a shared-viewpoint design to support collaborative understanding and introduces a set of custom 3D user interface (UI) techniques, including opacity adjustment, linked 2D-3D representations, zoom-based animated disease progression, and hapticenhanced virtual touch, to help clinicians contextualize anatomical and causal relationships when addressing caregivers' questions.

title: More Than Speed: User Agency and Social Comfort in Speech-Based Interaction for Multiscale Medical AR Applications.
abstract: In augmented reality (AR), voice-based input offers a hands-free approach to interacting with 3D content across multiple domains, including medical training and surgical rehearsal environments. While existing 3D user interface research has explored voice-based interaction techniques, these have primarily focused on simple manipulation tasks using predefined commands. We present a natural speech- based technique for target-directed viewpoint control that enables users to navigate across different levels of scale in 3D multiscale data. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study, we found that users tended to favor AI-assisted navigation for its autonomy, lack of social pressure, and sense of control through overall preference differences were not statistically significant. Notably, qualitative findings indicated that most users did not perceive AI-related response delays as more disruptive than those with human assistance. Our findings suggest that natural speech interfaces in AR may yield strong user acceptance, potentially driven more by psychological benefits-such as user agency and social com-fort-than by absolute speed alone. These exploratory insights warrant further investigation in future research.

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Application with 3D Audio-Visual Scene Reconstruction from Single 360° RGB-D.
abstract: We propose a virtual reality (VR) system that enables users to experience an immersive 3D environment with full 360° surroundings and spatial sound in real time from a single 2D 360 RGB-D input. The system includes a 3D semantic scene completion and material recognition pipelines, and a Unity3D-based VR application for audio rendering with material geometry within the scene. Demo access is available at:https://github.com/MonaIA1/Repo360

title: Physiological Response to Phantom Touch in VR: Investigation of the Impact on Electrodermal Activity and Heart Rate.
abstract: Phantom Touch in VR - a phenomenon which originated in the Metaverse which allows users to experience social touch in VR without any stimuli or haptic devices. Previous research has primarily relied on participants’ subjective responses to determine whether they feel Phantom Touch. However, objective physiological response to the phenomenon is scarce. This work presents findings on electrodermal activity and heart rate during Phantom Touch in VR development experiments, alongside subjective response to confirm the physiological results. The findings reveal measurable physiological changes associated with Phantom Touch, indicating heightened arousal in response to the newly developed sensations.

title: FeMLA: A QoE-Driven Federated Multi-Link Aggregation Framework for Multi-User Social XR Over Dense Wi-Fi Networks.
abstract: Extended reality (XR) technologies are rapidly advancing and becoming an integral part of our day-to-day life. XR technologies enable immersive multi-user applications such as virtual reality, collaborative augmented reality (AR), and shared virtual environments. Such multi-user XR (MuXR) applications place strict demands on local wireless networks, like dense Wi-Fi environments where latency, fairness, and stability directly impact user experience. In this paper, we propose a federated multi-link aggregation (FeMLA) framework for dense multi-link (ML-AP) Wi-Fi networks, designed to optimize quality of experience (QoE) for MuXR traffic under multi-link (multi-band) spectrum configurations. FeMLA exchanges lightweight local learning metrics among interfering neighbors and constructs a max-min global learning reward to explicitly optimize worst-user QoE. We evaluate our proposed framework with varying network densities (interference conditions) and XR traffic loads, using throughput, delay, and worst-user performance as key metrics. Simulation results show that in dense deployments with up to 16 ML-APs, FeMLA reduces mean XR delay to 28 ms, achieving an 86-93% latency reduction compared to fixed, random, and standalone reinforcement learning baselines, while improving mean QoE to 0.85. Moreover, FeMLA elevates the median worst-user QoE from near-zero or moderate levels to 0.81, demonstrating strong fairness and stability under severe interference. These results highlight federated, QoE-driven coordination as a scalable and effective approach for supporting next-generation multi-user Social XR over dense Wi-Fi networks.

title: Can You See It? Evaluating Color Visibility in Simulated Outdoor Environments.
abstract: Evaluating color visibility in outdoor augmented reality (AR) is challenging due to the visual complexity and variability of realworld environments. Outdoor scenes feature diverse textures and lighting conditions, limiting the applicability of visibility evaluation methods developed for simple or static backgrounds. This work introduces a methodology for evaluating AR cue color visibility in an outdoor environment by sampling visibility across realistic scenes and identifying design considerations for evaluating color visibility under dynamic, visually complex conditions.

title: Moving Towards Visibility Evaluation in Augmented Reality Using Simulated Environments and Continuous Psychophysics.
abstract: Assessing the visibility of augmented reality (AR) cues in outdoor environments is challenging due to complex background structure, motion, and lighting variability. Simulating AR cues within virtual reality (VR) enables controlled manipulation and measurement of these factors while preserving immersive viewing conditions. This work presents a perception-driven methodology for evaluating AR cue visibility that combines simulated AR cues in VR, high-resolution stereoscopic 360° video, and continuous psychophysics. Using this methodology, tracking-based performance data provide a continuous behavioral measure of visibility in complex scenes. Multiple analysis approaches are examined to support interpretation of tracking-based measures of perceptual performance in visually complex scenes. Together, this work illustrates progress toward a more ecologically valid and objective framework for studying AR cue visibility in outdoor settings.

title: Light-Field Modulation for View-Dependent Material Appearance in Spatial Augmented Reality.
abstract: This paper proposes a spatial augmented reality approach for perceptual material appearance manipulation based on environmental light-field modulation. Unlike conventional projection-based SAR, the proposed method modulates existing environmental illumination by directionally attenuating incident light rays using a lightfield modulator (LFM), enabling appearance manipulation even under strong ambient lighting conditions. The LFM consists of lens arrays and an LCD panel, allowing direction-dependent attenuation of environmental illumination. By designing aperture patterns based on a target bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF), the system modulates the incident light-field such that the reflected illumination distribution on the target surface perceptually corresponds to the desired material appearance without dynamic projection mapping or per-pixel geometric calibration. Experimental results qualitatively demonstrate controllable reproduction of various illumination characteristics, including parallel, converging, diverging, and diffuse lighting, as well as viewdependent material appearance effects such as specular highlights and color gradation changes. While the current implementation focuses on validating the feasibility of the proposed concept, limitations remain in optical calibration accuracy, angular coverage, and adaptation to directional environmental illumination. Addressing these issues constitutes important directions for future work.

title: Reducing Loneliness in Older Adults with AI and VR: A Caregiver-Informed Study on Design and Implementation of Virtual Environments and Conversational Agents.
abstract: Loneliness is a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline in older adults. Virtual reality (VR) and embodied conversational agents (ECAs) are promising tools for promoting social connection in this population, but defined design standards are lacking. We conducted a cross-sectional study with 53 caregivers using a 49-item online questionnaire, following CHERRIES and STROBE guidelines, to define design requirements for loneliness-reducing VR and ECA environments. Caregivers preferred naturalistic, familiar environments (gardens, parks, home), natural soundscapes, personalized autobiographical objects, and static or guided locomotion with visual and audio landmarks. The ideal ECA was realistic, genderneutral, empathetic, with natural voice dialogue and high personalization. The perceived impact on loneliness was moderate, with expected daily or weekly use. Based on these results, we developed a prototype virtual environment and ECA. Despite limitations from selection bias and online administration, this study provides stakeholder-based guidelines for subsequent validation with older adults.

title: Virtual Tours with Accessibility Annotations: A Prototype for Campus Accessibility Assessment for Mobility-Disabled Students.
abstract: Mobility-disabled students often face barriers when visiting campus. Consequently, they rely on detailed planning to meet their individual needs. The planning process depends on accessibility information, especially of building interiors. This project examines the potential of a virtual tour featuring 360-degree images with accessibility annotations. A proof-of-concept prototype was developed based on requirements gathered through a focus group. The resulting prototype enables users to virtually explore the building to judge accessibility. Our initial findings suggest that combining 360-degree imagery with textual information could enable more accurate accessibility judgments tailored to individual needs than existing information sources.

title: Investigating Eye-Body Coupling and Gaze Adaptation in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Gaze plays a central role in guiding human movement, yet most VR locomotion systems still treat gaze and motion as separate signals. Our research examines how these modalities interact during natural and redirected walking, and how this coupling changes under altered visual-motor contingencies. We first showed that integrating binocular gaze with sparse VR tracking enhances fullbody pose estimation. Building on this foundation, we now analyze high-frequency gaze behaviour during both short- and longterm exposure to redirected walking (RDW) to investigate whether gaze strategies adapt over time. The overall goal of our research is to characterize how gaze-locomotion coupling reorganizes under RDW and to determine whether gaze remains informative for understanding walking direction throughout adaptation. This paper summarizes our completed and ongoing work and outlines key questions for discussion during the Doctoral Consortium.

title: Exploring Robotic Armrest for Supporting Mid-Air Interactions in Room-Scale VR.
abstract: We explore a robotic armrest system that provides physical support for mid-air interactions to reduce arm fatigue in room-scale VR. The system dynamically adjusts the armrest's position, orientation, and height to center support around the user's arm while preserving input freedom and interaction consistently. We developed a prototype using actuators and a customized robotic station. A user study with a virtual handwriting task compared the robotic armrest to conventional mid-air interaction. Results show that the robotic armrest significantly reduces subjective physical workload while maintaining comparable input accuracy.

title: Illusion of Weight: The Impact of Virtual Dumbbell Size and Vibration on Isometric Exercise in VR.
abstract: We investigated whether multisensory feedback affects motor control by measuring limb steadiness during an isometric dumbbell exercise in a virtual environment, manipulating virtual dumbbell size (normal vs. large) and tactile feedback (with vs. without vibration). Conditions were counterbalanced per participant. We recorded hand position changes, physiological responses, and subjective feedback from 27 participants aged 18-30. Results showed the largest vertical hand displacement with tactile feedback and significant effects of both dumbbell size and tactile stimuli on physiological responses. These findings suggest that multisensory VR influences limb steadiness, though effect sizes were small and interaction effects indicate further study is needed.

title: Virtual-Reality and Behavioural Studies: A Useful Tool for Testing Passenger Wayfinding in Railway Station.
abstract: This study presents a virtual-reality-based assessment of three alternative wayfinding systems in a medium-size French regional railway station. Using a high-fidelity VR replica of the station, 20 participants completed three navigation scenarios under three signage configurations: suspended signage, a continuous colored ground line, and a control configuration. Eye-tracking, dwell-time metrics, and subjective data were collected. Results show that both suspended signage and the colored line significantly improved navigation efficiency and structured gaze patterns. Findings seem to support deploying a hybrid system combining overhead and ground guidance in comparable stations.

title: Navigating Borders and Identities: Aligning Governance and Immersive Design for Public Sector Engagement in the Metaverse.
abstract: As public entities enter the metaverse, their efforts to meet public service obligations and uphold ethical values lead to governance challenges that directly affect immersive design. Metaverse characteristics of anonymity, interoperability, borderlessness and immersivity create tensions that need to be addressed. Drawing on interviews and document analysis across three metaverse initiatives, this study identifies key governance concerns around jurisdictional boundaries, regulatory alignment, and identity management. These insights inform an emerging framework for ethically aligned and compliant public sector engagement in the metaverse.

title: Examining Behavioral Resurgence in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Behavioral resurgence, the reappearance of a previously extinguished behavior, poses challenges in applied settings. Traditional human operant studies often rely on in-vivo procedures, but emerging technologies such as virtual reality (VR) offer immersive environments that may alter motivating operations and contextual control. This study compared resurgence patterns in VR and invivo contexts using a three-phase procedure: Baseline, Differential Reinforcement of Alternative Behavior (DRA), and Extinction. Thirty undergraduate participants completed two sessions, one in VR and one in-vivo, involving arbitrary responses (placing virtual or physical ping-pong balls into baskets) under identical contingencies. Results indicated that resurgence occurred in both contexts, with no statistically significant differences in target responding across phases. However, VR sessions demonstrated slightly higher extinction rates and unique interaction patterns, suggesting VR can replicate operant contingencies while offering opportunities for enhanced experimental control and gamification. These findings support VR as a viable modality for studying complex behavioral processes and highlight future directions for leveraging immersive technology in behavioral research.

title: Systematic QoE Assessment of Multi-User VR: Task Taxonomy, Performance, and Delay Sensitivity.
abstract: This paper proposes new cooperative tasks for subjective research in Virtual Reality (VR) and examines the hypothesis that perceived Quality of Experience (QoE) is affected differently by network conditions across various categories of cooperative tasks in VR. We conducted a study analyzing the impact of different network delays on multiple categories of collaborative tasks. The motivation for this research was the need to develop standardized tasks that can effectively evaluate user collaboration in immersive systems. These tasks should be easy to replicate, engaging, and should encourage active communication. The tasks were designed to provide precise control over task dynamics, allowing to isolate key aspects of collaboration. User performance was also evaluated. Our results indicate that different task categories exhibit varying levels of sensitivity to network delay. This research provides new insights into communication in immersive systems and contributes to the refinement of ITU-T Recommendations P.1301, P.1305, P.920, and G.1035.

title: VR Games Based on Circumplex Model of Group Tasks for QoE Measurements and Beyond.
abstract: This research demo presents a system for studying collaboration in Virtual Reality. The system was developed in Unity and provides a multi-user VR simulator with a set of collaborative tasks categorized according to McGrath's circumplex model of group tasks. The platform is fully configurable, allowing researchers to adapt tasks and parameters to their own studies on VR cooperation. The system integrates in-VR subjective assessment, enabling users to rate Quality of Experience without removing the headset. In addition, it automatically collects performance data to support quantitative analysis. In this demo, participants collaborate in dyads while our system varies the network delay using the Clumsy tool. The demo presents a novel approach to studying subjective QoE in networked VR cooperation.

title: Voice-Based Access Control in Virtual Reality Using Natural Conversational Speaker Verification.
abstract: Voice-based biometric authentication offers a natural and handsfree alternative for access control in immersive Virtual Reality (VR) environments. We present a VR-based access control demo in which a non-player character (NPC) acts as a virtual gatekeeper, authenticating users through conversational speaker verification. Instead of explicit enrollment procedures or predefined passphrases, the system leverages a short, natural greeting exchange to perform speaker verification and, when necessary, seamless enrollment. The demo illustrates how voice biometrics can be integrated into VR in a user-friendly manner, preserving immersion while enabling secure and personalized access control.

title: A Lightweight Audio-Driven Blendshape Prediction Pipeline for Agent's Facial Animation in XR.
abstract: Real-time, expressive facial animation is essential for social presence in Extended Reality (XR) and autonomous virtual agents, yet existing solutions typically trade emotional fidelity for efficiency. We present a speech-driven 3D facial animation framework for standalone XR deployment. We utilize acoustic representations coupled with a Bidirectional LSTM and Multi-Head Attention architecture to map continuous audio streams to high-fidelity facial blendshapes. Trained on the emotional MEAD dataset, the model demonstrates strong generalization with a test MSE of 0.0088, particularly in high-intensity emotions. We further validate the pipeline by deploying it into Unity for future interactive virtual agents.

title: Rethinking Long-Term Educational Engagement with Virtual Reality.
abstract: Virtual Reality is emerging as a transformative educational technology owing to its immersive and interactive capabilities. However, much of this potential has been studied in short-term exposures ignoring how VR functions over extended periods in educational settings. To understand this, we ran a semester-long VR deployment within an undergraduate course on prototyping interactive systems followed by 25 semi-structured interviews. Based on our findings, we outline best practices and key considerations, offering design pathways for sustained integration of VR in learning ecosystems.

title: ResXR: An Open-Source Toolkit for Standardized XR Behavioral Research.
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) offers unique opportunities for behavioral and psychological research by combining experimental control with ecological validity. However, widespread adoption for research is hindered by high technical barriers and the absence of standardized data formats. To address this gap, we present ResXR, an end-to-end open-source software project for conducting behavioral XR experiments. ResXR provides a Unity-based experiment template for multimodal data capture (head, hand, eye, and face tracking from Meta's Quest Pro head mounted display) alongside a Python processing pipeline that automates the creation of a standardized data structure, validation, preprocessing, and quality reporting, inspired by established neuroimaging data formats and tools like fMRIPrep. By lowering entry barriers and promoting reproducibility, ResXR positions standalone headsets as accessible “human research mobile laboratories” for rigorous XR research.11https://youtu.be/tK_10BTGtuY

title: Distributed Flânerie: Electronic Orbits of Memory as a Spatial Soft Montage.
abstract: Return to the North: Virtual Archaeology of Electronic Orbits is a 6DoF XR interactive narrative set in post-industrial railway cities in northern China. It examines how rail connectivity reshaped everyday visual culture amid long-term extraction and depletion. We assemble public media footage, personal archives, printed atlases, handheld LiDAR scans, and photogrammetric captures into a traversable layered space using SfM/MVS and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for real-time rendering. A provenance-preserving strategy keeps differences in era, resolution, and context perceptible as volumetric fault lines, ghosting, captions, and seams-forming what we call a Digital Volumetric Layering aesthetic. Through embodied drift beyond prescribed paths, viewers infer relations among fragments, tracing how economic geography and memory politics surface in the seams of reconstruction.

title: Advanced Haptic Directional Awareness in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Haptic feedback can augment human spatial awareness in virtual reality (VR) by conveying information without overloading visual or auditory channels. This paper investigates vibrotactile directional feedback as a form of sensory augmentation for navigation in immersive environments. We present a VR system using a wearable vibrotactile vest that provides head-referenced, real-time directional cues with minimal tracking requirements. A user study (N=42) evaluated the system across three navigation tasks with limited or no visual guidance. Participants reliably located targets and avoided hazards using haptic feedback alone, independent of prior experience. Subjective results indicate high confidence and usability without significant cognitive interference. Eye-tracking analysis further revealed correlations between saccadic behavior, task performance, and subjective experience, suggesting opportunities for adaptive haptic feedback. These results demonstrate that vibrotactile directional feedback is an effective approach to spatial human augmentation in VR, supporting navigation and awareness when visual cues are unreliable or unavailable.

title: Dart Throwing in Virtual Reality with Aim Assistance.
abstract: Throwing tasks in virtual reality (VR) are often challenging due to limitations in depth perception, force control, and the absence of familiar physical feedback. Aim assistance may help alleviate some of these challenges, potentially allowing users to perform throwing actions more accurately and consistently. This demo presents the application of aim assistance in a VR dart-throwing task. The demonstrated system incorporates a subtle, trajectory-based aim assistance method that operates at the moment of release. Rather than visibly guiding the trajectory, our approach gently adjusts the dart's initial flight direction to partially compensate for throwing errors. During the demo, attendees can directly experience and compare dart throwing with and without aim assistance, allowing them to observe the differences in accuracy, control, and the overall interaction experience firsthand.

title: Architecture Education and Immersive Learning in Schools: A Scoping Review and Curriculum Exemplar.
abstract:
As the nature of work evolves, with future jobs that may not yet exist, education must adapt to prepare students for these shifts through the development of transferable, 
21
st 
 Century Skills (21CS) such as Creativity, Communication, Collaboration and Critical Thinking (4Cs). Emerging technology, including immersive learning technologies (ILTs) such as augmented, mixed and virtual reality, are increasingly integrated into education, offering significant learning affordances. ILT has historically been used in the field of architecture education and professional practice to enhance spatial reasoning and design processes with innovation in this discipline continuing. Despite architecture's interdisciplinary nature and its potential as a platform for Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Maths (STEAM) education, it is typically not included in secondary education curricula. This scoping review canvases the integration of architecture education into school curricula as a vehicle for immersive learning which can present unique opportunities to foster development of the 4Cs to equip students with the skills required for future employment. A secondary school curriculum exemplar is provided to illustrate the potential.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of a Bimanual Tangible Simulator for Microsurgical Clipping.
abstract: Virtual rehearsal systems have emerged as a crucial tool in micro-surgery, yet current approaches predominantly emphasize the evaluation of system validity while overlooking the operator's skill assessment. To tackle the above issue, this study first develops a space-aware bimanual tangible interface for high-fidelity microsurgical clipping simulation of intracranial aneurysms. After that, we evaluate the validity of this interface through user studies with six neurosurgeons and seven residents. Building upon this interface, we design an objective and quantitative assessment scale. Through consultations with neurosurgeons, we employ 15 construct validity metrics to analyze the operation accuracy and kinematic dexterity. These metrics are systematically consolidated into five standardized scoring criteria to evaluate users’ skills. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our prototype and exhibit promising potential to be applied in real neurosurgical rehearsal.

title: Exploring the Effects of a Clinical VR Rehabilitation System Post-Knee Surgery: A 14-Week Autoethnographic Study.
abstract: In recent years, virtual reality (VR) interventions have become a staple in physical therapy and rehabilitation research. In this study, we present an autoethnographic account of the REAL y-Series immersive rehabilitation system, a sensor-based VR experience specifically developed for clinical settings. Over 14 weeks, the first author examines the effects of using the y -Series as a complement to standard physical therapy after knee surgery. Through the integration of inertial measurement units (IMUs), the y-Series provides motion capture data to supplement the user's understanding of their physical progress and helps to promote autonomy and competence, which is also reflected in increased motivation and compliance to rehabilitation protocols. Our exploration suggests that this system has adaptable utility for various recovery contexts. We also highlight gamified design choices that complement the system's clinical utility and recommend further research to evaluate this approach.

title: Immersive Mediality and the Field of Digital Heritage.
abstract: Digital heritage emerged as a recognised field nearly two decades after the early development of immersive technologies. Paradoxically, its earliest practical applications were already deeply rooted in immersive media at a time when virtual reality was entering its 'second wave' of application areas, amidst second-generation technologies grouped into three domains: 3D documentation, 3D representation, and 3D dissemination. These developments enable immersive media to expand into new application domains, which in turn contribute to the understanding of the medium's structures and properties. Over the past two decades, advances in theory, technology, and scientific methods have progressively consolidated the field, shifting the emphasis toward the substance, accuracy, and long-term value of heritage through immersive media. How far, how deeply, and how well have immersive technologies penetrated digital heritage practice? This keynote paper critically examines the intersection of cultural heritage and immersive media, combining computational analysis with field-based experience to evaluate the field's development, current limitations, and future prospects, and providing a roadmap for designers and developers.

title: Perceptually Optimized Chromatic Power Saving in XR Using Binocular Asymmetry.
abstract: High-resolution Extended Reality (XR) rendering imposes energy demands. While perceptually driven power optimization methods exploit properties of the human visual system, they assume symmetric visual sensitivity across both eyes. We investigate whether inter-ocular asymmetry in chromatic sensitivity can be leveraged for power reduction. Using 4-Alternative Forced Choice (4AFC) measurements and Radial Basis Function Neural Network modeling (RBFNN), we derived per-eye discrimination maps. These maps were discretized and validated on video content using 2-Alternative Forced Choice evaluation. Results show that the nondominant eye tolerates stronger chromatic reduction without degrading binocular quality, enabling up to 24% power savings.

title: Spherical Harmonics Coefficient Prediction for Gaussian Splat Coding.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-quality free-viewpoint rendering but suffers from large data sizes due to its high-dimensional attributes, particularly spherical harmonics (SH) coefficients. In MPEG Gaussian Splat Coding (GSC), both the video-based TMCV framework and fast-track VPCC extensions are under developed; however, explicit tools that effectively exploit the structural correlation among SH coefficients remain limited. This paper proposes a prediction-based residual coding method that compresses prediction residuals as 2D attribute maps using HEVC by exploiting the correlation among SH coefficients within each color channel. The proposed method is implemented in both the Test Model Candidate Video (TMCV) and the V-PCC reference software (TMC2), and its performance is evaluated under the GSC common test conditions (CTC). For forward-facing sequences, the proposed method achieves average BD-rate reductions of 16.6% and 3.5% (in terms of RGBPSNR) compared to the TMCV and V-PCC anchors, respectively. In contrast, average BD-rate increases are observed for object-centric sequences, motivating future work on adaptive application of the proposed SH coefficient prediction method depending on sequence characteristics.

title: Two of Us: Bridging Asymmetric Perspectives.
abstract: Two of Us is an immersive collaborative work that investigates how self-understanding is shaped through cooperation with others under an asymmetric information structure. Through complementary roles that provide access to different viewpoints and information, participants' task performance depends on communication and mutual interpretation, transforming collaboration into a mirror for selfawareness and reflection. By leveraging presence and embodied agency in XR, the system is designed to externalize users' past psychological habits under real-time constraints and to simulate relational changes based on the interaction data that emerge in this process. This work presents XR as not merely a simulation medium, but as a reflective framework for analyzing how past, present, and future are interconnected and reconfigured in human collaboration.

title: Cultural Heritage Exploration Through LLM-Enabled Question Answering and Quiz Interaction in Mobile Augmented Reality.
abstract: This study presents an LLM-based augmented reality (AR) system designed to enhance cultural heritage exploration through natural language question answering (QA) and quiz-based interactions. A structured knowledge base guides the LLM to provide context-aware explanations in response to user queries, while generated quiz items transform cultural heritage data into interactive learning content within an AR environment. The system supports in-situ and map-based exploration, enabling users to review and learn from questions generated by others, fostering collective knowledge building. This design demonstrates the potential of combining LLM-driven interaction with AR to enrich interpretation, support learning, and promote cultural heritage experiences.

title: Teleportation Destination Previews Support Memory Retention During Virtual Navigation.
abstract:
Teleportation is one of the most widely used locomotion techniques in virtual reality (VR) because it is efficient, minimizes motion sickness, and enables large-scale spatial traversal with minimal effort. However, research on the Doorway Effect shows that spatial transitions can impair memory of information encountered just before the transition. Event Segmentation Theory (EST) explains this by proposing that salient changes disrupt a person’s working memory representation, causing recently encoded information to be replaced and reducing its availability for retrieval. By extension, the design of spatial transitions in VR may influence whether memory is disrupted or preserved, which could be a consideration in applied contexts such as education and training. One way to mitigate such impairment is to provide predictive cues about the upcoming change to reduce disruption. In VR, this can be implemented through teleportation previews, which give users a glimpse of the destination before arrival. In this experiment, we adapted the Doorway Effect paradigm to examine how two teleportation design factors — preview availability and environmental change — affect memory. Using a within-subjects 2 × 2 design (N = 27), participants studied a set of 3D objects, then teleported either within the same environment or into a different one, with or without a preview of the destination. After each transition, they completed a visual recognition task. Results showed two key findings: (1) without previews, recognition declined when teleporting into a different environment compared to remaining in the same one, and (2) when transitioning between different environments, providing a preview improved recognition relative to no preview. Together, these results indicate that both the distinctiveness of environments and the availability of previews shape memory during VR transitions. We discuss how these findings align with EST, highlight the cognitive consequences of teleportation design, an...
Show More

title: AI-Enhanced Multisensory Navigation for Visually Impaired Users in Virtual Environments.
abstract: VR applications often exclude individuals with visual impairments, creating a significant accessibility gap. We present a real-time assistive framework integrating Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) to interpret complex visual scenes. The system generates context-aware audio descriptions combined with haptic collision feedback, translating visual data into perceptible patterns. A user study with blind (N=3) and low-vision (N=2) participants was conducted in simulated clinic and classroom environments. Findings show that AI-driven assistance significantly enhanced spatial awareness, independence, and task performance. Qualitative results confirmed reduced cognitive load and heightened presence, providing a robust, VLLM-powered path for designing inclusive immersive systems.
