A comparative study showed that while basic models provide predictable feedback, the physics simulation method offers real-time internal tissue behavior and complex force feedback. This approach significantly enhances the user experience and is essential for effective training in high-realism VR fields, particularly in medical environments.

title: Systems-Theoretic Integration of VR and AI for Human Digital Twin.
abstract: This article aims to establish a rigorous mathematical foundation for the human Digital Twin (DT) within Cyber-Human-Physical Systems (CHPS) paradigm, by integrating multimodal data streams and artificial intelligence (AI), as well as Virtual Reality (VR) as a functional interface to facilitate real-time data assimilation and user control refinement. This work formulates DT through structural homomorphism with its real-world counterpart (PT) and demonstrates that immersive interactions enable the optimization of control inputs on the DT and thus maintain dynamic coherence. By mapping the twin structure across George Klir's epistemological hierarchy, particularly focusing on the data-level (Level 2) and behavior-level (Level 3), this framework ensures digital representations remain high-fidelity surrogates for physical counterparts. The utility of this framework is validated through two case studies of medical robotic navigation and bedside patient care, illustrating how VR-mediated control transforms static simulations into dynamic, informed decision-making tools.

title: Effects of Dynamic Field-of-View and Background Opacity Modulation on Cybersickness Reduction in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Users of virtual reality (VR) systems often experience cybersickness during navigation within VR environments due to vi-sual-vestibular conflicts. For mitigating cybersickness, field-of-view (FoV) reduction has been widely studied. However, peripheral real-world view (PRV) remains relatively underexplored. We first conducted a pilot study to identify users’ perceptual thresholds and preferred minimum values for FoV, soft-edged cutouts, and PRV. Based on these results, we derive perceptual threshold-aware design parameters for combining FoV and PRV modulation in VR navigation.

title: Structured Gaussian Mapping for Memory-Efficient Immersive XR.
abstract: High-fidelity and scalable 3D scene representations are critical for immersive VR and XR systems under strict latency and memory constraints. Although recent studies demonstrate real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting on head-mounted displays, uncontrolled Gaussian growth during RGB-D mapping remains a key scalability bottleneck. We propose Structured Gaussian Mapping, a KD-tree guided allocation framework that limits Gaussian growth at the mapping stage for sequential RGB-D SLAM. By partitioning image space and allocating compact Gaussian sets only in perceptually relevant regions, our approach replaces pixel-wise densification. Experiments show up to $\mathbf{8 2} \boldsymbol{\%}$ fewer Gaussians with improves PSNR, enabling memory-efficient and scalable XR-ready Gaussian mapping.

title: Multi-Sensor Monitoring for Cultural Heritage Preservation: Overcoming Single-Modality Limits with RGB-IR Sensor Fusion.
abstract: Cultural heritage inspection often relies on RGB images and single-sensor 3D capture, which limits subsurface defect evidence and long-term condition tracking. A multi-sensor digital-twin pipeline is presented for non-contact diagnosis and time-series archiving. The pipeline synchronizes RGB and infrared thermography, fuses multi-view multispectral observations with RGB-IR Gaussian Splatting to build an as-is 3D restoration model, and stores repeated scans for longitudinal comparison. An AR interface overlays the multispectral digital twin on the physical artifact for interactive defect exploration and reporting. Experiments across three crack phases validate crack detectability and reconstruction quality (RGB PSNR 32.12 dB; IR 36.03 dB).

title: Capturing the Temporal Dynamics of Awe in VR: Using Retrospective Continuous Self-Report Method.
abstract: Research on awe in VR has largely relied on post-hoc self-reports (e.g., Awe-S), limiting insight into its temporal dynamics. This study introduces a Retrospective Continuous Self-report (RCS) method to assess how awe experiences change over time and how people share similar cues that elicit awe. Results showed that awe peaks clustered around specific environmental cues with shared phenomenological features across participants. These moments also involved longer behavioral dwell times, indicating that the RCS effectively captures the temporal unfolding of awe. Overall, the RCS provides a useful complementary tool for studying the dynamic aspects of awe beyond traditional post-hoc surveys.

title: Demonstrating Controller-Free Mixed Reality X-Ray Machine Training.
abstract: We demonstrate a controller-free, Mixed Reality training system that enables hands-on X-ray machine operation through natural hand interaction. The system addresses key limitations of conventional medical device training, including restricted physical access, high equipment costs, and radiation exposure risks. By leveraging optical hand tracking on a standalone head-mounted display, users can interact with a virtual X-ray machine using gestures that closely resemble real-world operation. A central component of the demo is a Virtual Tablet interface, which provides video-based operational guidance and allows users to seamlessly select and execute training scenarios for different patient postures. All interactions—including device manipulation and user interface navigation—are performed entirely through hand tracking, enabling immediate, walk-up use without controllers or calibration overhead. The system is designed specifically for live demo settings, allowing first-time users to experience realistic medical device operation within minutes. Informal user feedback from nursing students and clinical professionals indicates high engagement, strong perceived realism, and clear potential for scalable deployment in medical education and clinical training environments.

title: In-Situ Progressive Evaluation of VR Immersion: A Comparison Between Voice and Controller-Based Questionnaires Validated with EEG.
abstract: In-situ VR surveys offer ecological validity compared to poststimulus questionnaires. However, surveying during the ongoing task can cause interruption and bias measured variables. Thus, insitu data collection is designed to be simple and quick - typically relying on controller-based Likert-scale responses to short 2D pop-up questions. This pilot study proposes using voice communication instead, validating its effectiveness in maintaining gradual immersion without disrupting user experience. Results indicate voice interaction enabled a more stable, stress-free immersive state compared to the controller-based method.

title: SoundSphere: Multimodal Captioning for Equitable and Collaborative VR Offices.
abstract: We present SoundSphere, a multimodal captioning system designed to support equitable and collaborative work within Virtual Reality (VR) offices. While VR enables immersive professional collaboration, existing captioning solutions often lack non-verbal context and conversation history, resulting in structural communication barriers for users with hearing impairments during fast-paced meetings. SoundSphere addresses these challenges through a hybrid architecture that integrates on-device processing with cloud-based intelligence. The system employs YAMNet for real-time environmental sound classification (e.g., alarms) and orchestrates Whisper and Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide accurate transcription, real-time translation, and context-aware meeting summarization. By integrating verbal and non-verbal cues, SoundSphere aims to promote more equitable participation in collaborative VR workspaces. A preliminary system validation with XR domain experts indicates that SoundSphere's hybrid architecture is technically viable and effective in reducing cognitive load during complex discussions. Rather than framing captioning as a supplementary assistive feature, our work positions it as an infrastructural component of inclusive and ethically grounded VR collaboration. Through a heuristic evaluation of verbal and non-verbal cue integration, this study establishes a validated technical foundation as a preparatory step toward future deployment in inclusive virtual offices.

title: Implicit and Explicit Visual Framing Effects on Illusory Relative Weight Perception in Virtual Reality.
abstract: In virtual reality, weight perception can be framed through visual cues only, yet effects of different types of visual framings has not been fully explored. We experimentally investigate the individual/interactive effects of implicit (by visual surface) and explicit framing (overt depiction of deformation) and when combined in a congruent or possibly conflicting way. Preliminary results demonstrated that explicit framing dominated the implicit. Correct selection rates peaked when framings aligned congruently. These findings characterize how explicit and implicit visual framings can bias illusory relative weight judgments in VR and provide insights into how to apply them in conjunction with pseudo-haptic techniques.

title: SafeMask-VR: Real-Time Explicit Content Masking for Secure Social Interaction.
abstract: User-Generated Content (UGC) plays a crucial role in social VR platforms, but it also exposes users to sexually explicit content, which poses serious threats to their safety. This paper introduces a novel system, referred to as SafeMask-VR, that automatically detects and filters sexually explicit content from users' views in near real-time. We developed SafeMask-VR by collecting real sexually explicit images from VRChat and using them to train a detection model with YOLOv5. Our results show that the trained model achieves an F1 score of 0.70. Furthermore, we implemented a Unity-based prototype that demonstrates SafeMask-VR can detect and mask sexually explicit images within 8 milliseconds.

title: Is Meshing Always Necessary? The Limited Impact of Rendering Fidelity on VR Spatial Perception.
abstract: While textured meshes are widely used in virtual reality, their computational cost raises questions about their perceptual benefit. We conducted an experiment (N=15) utilizing a real-world baseline to normalize individual spatial biases. Results demonstrated comparable global spatial accuracy between representations (p=0.921), confirming the non-inferiority of point clouds. However, local judgments revealed a significant overestimation bias in meshes (+9.69 {\%}), consistent with the effects of high visual density, whereas point clouds remained unbiased. Overall, these findings suggest that higher visual fidelity does not inherently improve spatial judgment, highlighting point clouds as an efficient alternative for immersive environments.

title: Situately: Embodied Conversational Agent with LLM-Powered Nonverbal Behavior and Object Interaction.
abstract: Embodied conversational agents possess virtual bodies in virtual environments, yet often lack socially and spatially plausible bodily behavior during interaction. We present a real-time, concurrent framework for embodied conversational agents that controls and coordinates nonverbal behavior and spatially grounded actions beyond verbal interaction alone. Built on large language models and ongoing conversational context, our system enables multimodal control by generating structured outputs for avatar-level nonverbal expression and object interaction. These structured outputs are directly mapped to real-time avatar animations, allowing users to perceive the agent's nonverbal expressions and object interactions in a shared space. We demonstrate our approach through an interactive virtual environment demo, showing how it supports richer embodied interaction and increases perceived animacy.

title: EfficientPBD: View-Frustum Culling for Real-Time Deformable Simulation in XR.
abstract: Recent advances in mixed reality systems enable the reconstruction of real-world environments as dense scene meshes, allowing physical interaction between virtual objects and the surrounding space. However, direct collision handling between deformable objects and such meshes remains computationally expensive and can lead to unstable behavior in real-time XR applications. We propose EfficientPBD, a collision filtering framework that integrates view-frustum culling with budget-based triangle selection for real-time deformable simulation. By restricting collision processing to a selected subset of surface triangles in a GPU-based Position-Based Dynamics loop, EfficientPBD achieves up to a 74.2 % improvement in frame rates for complex models.

title: No Dwarves for the Bear: An MR-Based Immersive Artwork Reinterpreting Modern Polish History.
abstract: “No Dwarves for the Bear” is a Mixed Reality (MR)-based immersive artwork that conveys the universal message of the value of freedom, inspired by motifs from modern Polish history, particularly the 1980s martial law period. This work is an artistic attempt, designed to allow the viewers to experience a virtual narrative superimposed on physical reality. The work adopts a childlike aesthetic, creating the impression of paper-made characters. Leveraging the Unity engine and the color passthrough feature of the Meta Quest 3s, the work establishes an interactive experience with virtual objects in a real-world environment. By utilizing these tools, this project is intended to go beyond simple message delivery, providing an artistic experience where the audience can personally discover and interpret the message within the work.

title: Null-Space Interaction: Enabling Reaching Task During Typing via Shoulder Movements.
abstract: In workspaces, users often engage in manual tasks such as typing, where their hands are physically anchored to a device. Existing interaction paradigms typically require those users to lift their hands for mid-air gestures to interact with distant virtual objects, causing context switching costs and physical fatigue. However, the human upper limb possesses kinematic redundancy, meaning the proximal joint can move independently within the kinematic null space even while the end-effector remains fixed. Leveraging this biomechanical characteristic, we propose an interaction interface that utilizes shoulder movements to control a virtual arm for reaching tasks, while keeping the hand on the primary task. Our system maps the subtle protraction and elevation of the shoulder to the virtual hand's position using a linear amplification gain, allowing users to reach objects without disengaging from their primary manual task. To validate the feasibility of this approach, we designed a dual-task user study comparing unimanual typing performance (primary task) with and without the concurrent shoulder-based reaching task (secondary task). We analyze key metrics including typing speed, reaching time, and trajectory of virtual hand. This work explores the potential of utilizing the body's unused degrees of freedom to expand interaction capabilities, aiming to achieve seamless parallel processing of manual and spatial tasks.

title: Reducing Cybersickness for 2D VR Spectators Using a Gaze-Based Stabilized Third-Person View.
abstract: While motion sickness in VR has been widely studied for HMD (head-mounted display) wearers, the experience of external spectators watching VR content on 2D monitors has received relatively little attention. This paper proposes a gaze-based stabilized thirdperson view that adjusts the spectator camera according to the HMD gaze behavior of the HMD wearer. Through a repeated measures experiment using the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire (SSQ), we show that the proposed view reduces cybersickness experienced by spectators watching VR content on 2D monitors, compared to conventional first-person and third-person spectator views.

title: Characterizing Gingival Electrical Stimulation Toward Intraoral Texture Display.
abstract: Food texture perception during mastication involves kinesthetic and somatosensory feedback. However, the somatosensory contributions of intraoral tissues remain poorly characterized as haptic channels. As a preliminary study toward dynamic texture rendering, we conducted psychophysical profiling of electrotactile stimuli at six frequencies (2-500 ~\text{Hz}) and three electrode locations. Results suggest that the spatial distributions largely overlapped across electrode locations, whereas perceptual qualities were modulated by stimulation frequency. Stimuli between 10-500 ~\text{Hz} tended to be perceived as vibrotactile sensations, while carbonation-like sensations showed a marginal tendency toward higher ratings around 80 Hz.

title: A Study of the Onsite H-BIM Prototyping of Korean Traditional Wooden Architecture.
abstract: Historic Building Information Modeling (H-BIM) offers clear benefits for the digital preservation of architectural heritage. In Korea, many traditional wooden buildings still lack H-BIM data due to the complexity and labor required for component-level modeling. In this paper, we propose an onsite mobile system for H-BIM prototyping with 3D scan of architectural components, virtual assembly and direct input of preservation information. It enables rapid generation of component-based H-BIM data in the field. It is expected to be a way to provide 3D preservation management capabilities for heritage buildings without H-BIM data.

title: Methods for Safely Co-Designing Embodied Mental Health VR Interventions with Youth.
abstract: Emotion regulation is a vital skill for youth, yet traditional therapeutic models often overlook the somatic nature of emotional experiences. VR offers a promising solution through immersive embodiment. We suggest designing effective interventions requires involving youth as experts in their lived experiences. This paper presents preliminary methodological insights from a 7-day co-design workshop with 20 drama students (ages 15-18). We reflect on how to cultivate safety, scaffold reflection on sensitive topics, and support embodied ideation for VR-based emotion regulation tools. By integrating drama techniques (e.g., tableau, role-play, and perspectivetaking), our workshop demonstrates how embodied co-design captures “tacit knowledge” that verbal or written methods may miss. Findings highlight the importance of established trust, the role of community champions, and the efficacy of drama as a precursor to and vessel for VR design. Ultimately, this approach empowers youth to externalize internal states, providing insights for developing future embodied mental health VR interventions.

title: User Perspectives on the Role of LLM-Based AI Agents in Social VR.
abstract: As Large Language Model (LLM)-based AI agents emerge in social Virtual Reality (VR), understanding the roles they might play is critical. We conducted interviews in VRChat with experienced users and developers $(\mathrm{N}=6)$ and, using thematic analysis, identified five primary roles: information sharing, personal companionship, moderation, content generation, and self-development and learning. While participants recognized the potential for increased accessibility and support, they expressed concerns regarding overmoderation, the replacement of human creativity, and the psychological impact of AI co-dependency. These preliminary findings highlight the need to balance AI utility with the preservation of authentic human connection in social VR.

title: StoryBaker: Generative Memoryscapes from Personal Narratives in XR.
abstract: We introduce StoryBaker, a generative system for constructing memoryscapes, spatialized representations of personal narratives. StoryBaker enables everyday, non-technical users to externalize lived experiences as XR memoryscapes by translating narrative and emotional elements into spatial layouts, objects, sound, and interaction. Leveraging multimodal generative models and affective design frameworks, the system maps emotional and narrative cues onto spatial structures that support reflection and exploration. Through a preliminary pilot study, we probe how users engage with the generated memoryscapes of their own and others', highlighting opportunities and challenges in emotional fidelity, symbolic interaction, and perspective-taking. We discuss the implications of using XR as a medium for memory representation and outline future directions for generative approaches to spatial memory in immersive systems.

title: Beyond Audio: Visual Cues to Complement Football Commentary for Fans with Visual Impairments.
abstract: People with visual impairments face unique challenges while attending sports events. Likewise, the stadium atmosphere presents obstacles for using auxiliary interfaces on common media devices. In this work, we present a proof-of-concept AR-based VR application that uses visual cues to highlight key elements of football soccer matches. Following an exploratory approach, we conducted interviews and a qualitative co-design user study with football fans with visual impairments to gather their needs and preferences for such cues. Our findings indicate that AR visual cues can enhance the football spectating experience for fans with visual impairments.

title: Timing Matters: Step-Synchronized Mastoid Vibration Improves Turning Detectability in Redirected Walking.
abstract: Redirected walking is limited by sensitivity to unintended turning. Mastoid vibration reduces detectability, but constant stimulation increases discomfort. We examined if step-synchronized vibration improves tolerance without extra discomfort. Participants performed tasks under baseline, constant, and step-synchronized conditions. Step-synchronized vibration increased detection thresholds by 50% over baseline with similar discomfort. Constant vibration showed comparable benefits but higher discomfort. Neither condition affected presence or simulator sickness. These results suggest that step-synchronized vibration shows potential to expand redirected walking while preserving user comfort.

title: Library: A Large-Scale Outdoor Gaussian Splat Reconstruction Dataset.
abstract: Large-scale outdoor scenes captured by drones exhibit wide spatial extent and diverse viewpoint distributions, making training view density an important factor in view synthesis. While recent Gaussian Splatting-based methods have demonstrated efficient real-time rendering, their behavior under varying numbers of training views in real-world, building-scale scenes remains insufficiently explored. This work introduces a large-scale drone-captured dataset of a university library and its surrounding area, which has been adopted as a representative large-scale outdoor sequence in the MPEG GSC common test conditions (CTC) to support standardized evaluation of Gaussian Splatting-based reconstruction in outdoor environments. The dataset was captured along circular flight trajectories at multiple altitudes and distances, providing systematic coverage of near-range and far-range viewpoints. Using a fixed set of evaluation views, the results show that faithful large-scale scene coverage can be achieved with as few as approximately 200 training images, despite the wide spatial extent of the outdoor environment.

title: Improving Visual Fidelity of Gaze-Dependent Color Image Presentation Using High-Speed Projection.
abstract: Large displays and projectors have been widely used in public spaces to present information to multiple viewers simultaneously. While such approaches enable efficient information sharing, they cannot personalize content for individual viewers, and existing solutions using HMDs or camera-based tracking are impractical in public settings due to device scalability and privacy concerns. As an alternative, methods based on high-speed projection have been proposed, in which images become visible only when motion occurs in the viewer's gaze or observation target. In this paper, we propose a colorization method for gaze-dependent image presentation using a high-speed projector that was not achieved by previous approaches, and investigate how variations in the proposed method's parameters affect the fidelity of the presented images.

title: Hands vs. Controllers with and without Haptics in VR Object Sorting: Performance, Cognitive Load, and Sense of Agency.
abstract: Designing natural and efficient ways to interact in virtual reality (VR) often comes down to two key choices: whether users rely on hand tracking or physical controllers, and whether haptic feedback should be included. To better understand these trade-offs, we compared four interaction modes on the Meta Quest 3: bare hands, hands with palm-mounted haptics, controllers, and controllers with vibrotactile feedback. In a within-subjects study (\mathrm{N}=15), participants completed an object-sorting task where cubes and spheres had to be organized into straight lines across a virtual table. We measured completion times and collected ratings of workload (NASATLX), sense of agency, and qualitative impressions through survey Questionnaires. Results showed that controllers generally enabled faster sorting than hands, with mean times of 24-28 seconds versus 29-37 seconds. Vibrotactile feedback were appreciated as confirmation of grasp and release. However, hand-mounted actuators were sometimes described as intense or slightly delayed, which corresponded to slower performance. Overall, controllers provided speed advantages, while hand-based haptics highlighted the importance of feedback intensity and latency to avoid added workload. These findings help clarify the strengths and limitations of commodity VR input methods and suggest design directions for ergonomic, latency-aware haptic systems that enhance immersion without compromising efficiency.

title: A Neuroergonomic Comparison of Immersive Virtual Reality and Desktop-Based Neurofeedback During Human-Drone Interaction.
abstract: Sustained attention and efficient workload regulation are vital for human–drone interaction in industrial, defense, and safety-critical contexts. While EEG-based neurofeedback enhances attentional control, most studies use desktop paradigms, limiting understanding of immersive modulation of neural regulation. This study compared EEG-based neurofeedback in immersive virtual reality (VR-NF ; n=15) and desktop environments (Desktop-NF ; n=15) during a controlled drone task. Both groups completed five sessions with identical feedback from a composite Focus Index. EEG spectral power (delta, theta, alpha, beta) and subjective workload (NASA-TLX) were measured pre- and post-training. VR-NF elicited reduced alpha, theta, and delta power with enhanced beta activity, reflecting heightened attention and efficient workload regulation. These neural effects persisted, indicating modality-specific adaptation. Workload decreased in both groups, but VR-NF showed greater temporal demand reduction and higher mental engagement. Results identify immersion as a key modulator of neural regulation and inform neuroergonomic XR system design.

title: Avatar Diversity in Social VR: From the Perspectives of Compatible Outfit Concentration and Customization Range.
abstract:
In Social VR, avatars and outfits are 3D models through which users present embodied representations and update self-expression across changing contexts and relationships. The practical viability of an avatar is therefore shaped not only by the availability of avatar types but also by how easily users can continue updating their appearance after selection through outfits and related resources. In UGC-oriented ecosystems such as VRChat, many transactions for avatars and outfits occur via external marketplaces, and outfit listings commonly specify which avatar(s) they are compatible with because compatibility is not universal across rigs and settings. This market structure makes the number of outfit listings explicitly marked as compatible with an avatar an observable proxy for postselection customization resources. In this preliminary analysis, we focus on BOOTH, a major marketplace in the VRChat ecosystem, and analyze a single-time-point snapshot dataset as of December 6, 2025, restricting measurement to avatars with at least five compatible outfit listings. We characterize the distribution of compatible outfit counts at two levels: the avatar level and the creator level after normalizing creator names and aggregating counts by creator. The results reveal a pronounced long-tail structure and a two-stage pattern of concentration: compatible outfit counts cluster around a limited set of avatars with many compatible listings, and the skew becomes more pronounced when aggregated at the creator level, indicating that a relatively small number of creators account for a large share of compatible outfits. Because the data capture one point in time, we do not infer causal direction; instead, we present mechanism hypotheses consistent with the observed patterns. On the supply side of avatar-compatible outfit creation, avatar-specific compatibility work can create incentives to concentrate effort on avatars that are more likely to be widely used. On the demand side, as users b...

title: Evaluation of Ambient Text Privacy Risk via Outward-Facing Cameras on XR HMDs.
abstract: Outward-facing RGB cameras integrated into XR head-mounted displays (HMDs) are increasingly used to support video passthrough and camera-sharing in multi-user and social XR environments. While such functionalities enable new forms of collaboration and remote assistance, they also pose privacy risks regarding ambient information captured by HMD cameras. In particular, ambient text may contain privacy-sensitive or confidential content. This paper investigates the ambient text privacy risks via HMD cameras by experimentally evaluating text recognition accuracy on images captured using a commercial XR HMD, Meta Quest 3. In our experiment, using printed text captured under controlled conditions, we apply optical character recognition (OCR) and evaluate recognition performance using the Character Error Rate (CER). Our findings highlight the need to consider ambient text privacy risks when designing and deploying camera-sharing functionalities in XR systems.

title: Neural Activity Analysis of Athletes in Baseball Batting Using Virtual Reality and EEG.
abstract: This study proposes a measurement system for neural processes in baseball batting using virtual reality (VR). Investigating neural processes of baseball batting in real-world environments is challenging due to physical constraints. To address this, we integrated a baseball VR environment with electroencephalography (EEG) recording to track brain activity in a setting that mimics actual game conditions. We conducted a pitch-type recognition task to compare neural responses between experienced and non-experienced groups. Our results revealed that experienced players exhibited significantly more pronounced positive amplitudes, demonstrating that expertise-related differences in perceptual-cognitive processes are quantifiable in immersive settings. These findings suggest that EEG metrics in VR environments can serve as effective objective indicators for evaluating a batter's expertise and perceptual-cognitive abilities.

title: User Experience and Performance During Immersive Avatar Customization.
abstract: In this work, we present a methodology that treats avatar customization as a measurable cognitive-perceptual task and report results from a pilot study examining how presenting the same customization interface across different mediums affects user experience and performance. Participants completed an avatar target matching task on either a tablet or a VR headset. Interaction metrics, subjective workload and usability measures, and similarity ratings were analyzed. While subjective measures did not differ substantially, preliminary results showed VR users tended to perform fewer actions and take longer between actions. We discuss implications for future studies investigating immersive customization interface design.

title: HapticServant - Delivering Haptic Products in a Virtual Reality Supermarket.
abstract: This paper presents HapticServant, an encountered-type haptic system that utilizes a robotic arm to deliver passive props on demand, enhancing the shopping experience within a Virtual Reality (VR) supermarket simulation. The system comprises several 3D-printed components, including a modular palette mechanism that enables the presentation of tangible objects with various shapes and sizes. This enables users to physically grasp, rotate, and inspect items in a way that supports multisensory perception. In a user study $(N=32)$, a shopping task was evaluated across three different conditions: “Visual-Only Interaction” (without tangible props), “Single-Haptic Interaction” (one generic prop), and “Multi-Haptic Interaction” (three product-specific props). The evaluation focused on how different levels of robotic prop delivery affect presence, interaction quality, and task behavior. With props, participants described their experience as an improvement in terms of realism and engagement. The use of multiple, product-specific props maximized haptic fidelity for object handling, whereas a single generic prop may be sufficient when the task is focused on traversing the supermarket. HapticServant illustrates how simple and low-cost robotic encountered-type haptics can be leveraged for focused grocery item interactions, and can serve as a promising framework for similar VR applications beyond the supermarket context.

title: Towards EMG-Driven Pseudo-Haptic Feedback for VR Surgical Training.
abstract: Haptic feedback is prevalent in virtual reality applications, but replicating effort-dependent sensations required for surgical incision practice remains difficult without dedicated force-feedback devices. This work explores whether surface electromyography (EMG) can drive an effort-adaptive pseudo-haptic alternative for VR-based incision training. Our system streams forearm EMG to estimate users' muscular effort in real time and adaptively modulates visual, audio, and vibrotactile cues when effort deviates from a predefined target range, fostering force awareness and self-correction without physically grounded haptics. We implemented the system on a VR platform and conducted an exploratory within-subject study comparing three feedback conditions: visual-only feedback, a non-adaptive pseudo-force baseline, and EMG-adaptive pseudo-force feedback. Initial results suggest that EMG-adaptive feedback improves perceived force awareness and self-correction tendencies without a disproportionate increase in perceived workload. Although limited in scale, these findings indicate the potential of EMG-driven pseudo-haptics as a lightweight approach for early-stage surgical skill training and motivate larger-scale evaluations.

title: Influence of Animal-Agent Appearance on Pro-Environmental Behavior and Targeted Attention in Young Adults.
abstract: Immersive technologies offer significant potential for communicating environmental issues, often employing virtual agents to guide users and structure interaction. In conservation-oriented applications, animal agents, particularly flagship species, are assumed to foster empathy and prosocial engagement. We report a between-subjects VR study in which young adults interacted with an educational application about Caribbean manatees, accompanied by either a realistic animal agent, a cartoon-style agent, or no agent. Targeted attention and short-term behavioral responses were assessed using trivia performance and voluntary donation behavior. Results show that visual appearance alone did not affect donation behavior or trivia performance under brief exposure. However, agent presence, independent of style, improved perceived perspicuity and efficiency. These findings suggest that in short educational XR sessions, animal agents primarily support cognitive structuring rather than persuasion, with implications for XR design and the interpretation of null results.

title: A Multi-Resolution Pipeline for High-Fidelity Coastal Terrain Reconstruction for XR From Heterogeneous Geospatial Data.
abstract: The reconstruction of digital heritage environments increasingly demands the coherent integration of heterogeneous spatial data as a foundation for visually immersive XR applications. However, existing terrain-generation pipelines are typically not designed to support the levels of geometric detail, continuity, and scale consistency required for high-fidelity first-person exploration in real-time XR. This paper presents a reproducible processing pipeline for constructing a physically and perceptually coherent coastal virtual environment from heterogeneous geospatial datasets of varying resolution and origin. The pipeline integrates high-resolution aerial point clouds, lower-resolution satellitebased elevation data, and global bathymetric data into a continuous, multi-resolution terrain suitable for real-time XR applications, such as high detail and resolution for first-person exploration. We describe data cleanup, multi-resolution fusion, procedural enhancement of underwater terrain, terrain texturing, vegetation generation, and background simplification. The resulting virtual coastal environment serves as a multimodal-ready spatial substrate that can support synchronized visual, acoustic, and physical simulations. We demonstrate the pipeline through a case study of a critical segment of the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica and discuss its implications for multisensory digital heritage reconstruction and environmental communication.

title: A Voxel-Based Grid Coordinate for Virtual Object Positioning in Outdoor Mobile Augmented Reality.
abstract: Humans perceive and describe space using relative expressions, while computers use absolute coordinates. This difference creates a gap in spatial communication, especially in outdoor environments where objects with complex surfaces serve as references. To address this, we present a voxel-based surface grid coordinate system for outdoor mobile augmented reality. This approach voxelizes reference object models obtained from a 3D map and defines grids on them. Each surface grid maps to geographic coordinates and provides a surface-based index for placement. Quantitative outdoor experiments and a pilot user study show how surface grids and visual cues support spatial perception at different levels.

title: Group-Wise PCA of SH Coefficients for 3DGS Compression.
abstract: MPEG is currently standardizing Gaussian Splat Coding (GSC) as a compression standard for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models. In this process, a video-based compression framework, referred to as Test Model Candidate Video (TMCV), is used to efficiently compress Gaussian attributes, including spherical harmonics (SH) coefficients. This paper proposes a group-wise Principal Component Analysis (PCA) apporache to improve the compression efficiency of SH coefficients within the TMCV framework. The proposed method groups SH coefficients based on their correlation characteristics and applies PCA individually to each group, thereby enabling more effective exploitation of the structural correlation properties inherent in SH coefficients. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperfoms the TMCV anchor in terms of compression efficiency, achieving BD-rate reductions of $19.0 {\%}, 19.5 {\%}$, and 17.4% for RGB-PSNR, YUV-PSNR, and YUV-SSIM, respectively.

title: Audio-Visual Augmented Reality: Enhancing Visual Art Experiences Through Sonification and Visualization.
abstract: The ways of art appreciation can be extended through augmented reality technologies. In the current study, augmented audio and augmented visual features enabled viewers to appreciate artworks in greater depth with a novel understanding. Twenty-four participants appreciated each artwork under four different conditions (with/without audio augmentation and with/without visual augmentation). Art appreciation time and interview data were collected. The results indicated that augmented visual elements led to significantly higher engagement time. Thematic analysis revealed that both augmented audio and augmented visual elements structurally aligned with the artworks, guiding viewers in how to explore and appreciate the paintings. These findings demonstrate that AR technologies can facilitate deeper, more structured engagement with artworks, while also supporting viewer-specific cognitive strategies for art appreciation.

title: How do we Look Around? A Survey of Viewport Control Techniques in 360° Video Players.
abstract: Looking around is fundamental to VR experiences, yet head rotation alone can be limiting due to comfort, posture, and accessibility constraints. Although numerous alternative viewport control techniques have been proposed in academia, it remains unclear which are actually implemented in consumer-facing systems. We present a systematic survey of viewport control techniques in 28 VR 360° video players available on major platforms. We identified and classified implemented techniques, revealing that only half of surveyed players supported alternatives to 1: 1 head rotation by default, and all such alternatives were controller-based. Among these, Controller Drag is the most common, whereas Controller Snap—prominent in academia—appears less frequently in practice, highlighting the gap between research and real-world deployment while raising concerns about the limited diversity of techniques in current consumer-facing systems. Our findings provide an overview of current industry practice and inform the design of future viewport control techniques.

title: Project Deep Dive: Investigating Audio-Visual Cue Design for Stress-Response Training in Underwater VR Environments.
abstract: Project Deep Dive is a virtual reality (VR) training prototype designed to investigate how audio-visual stimuli evoke stress responses in underwater environments. As a pre-exposure training tool for occupations requiring underwater operations, the system delivers auditory and visual cues within a deep-sea wreck scenario to help trainees identify personal fear thresholds and practice emotional regulation. The experience tasks users with investigating a sunken military cargo plane while being exposed to fearrelevant audio-visual stimuli. A pilot study with 12 participants explored how different auditory and visual cues affected self-reported fear and physiological measures. Preliminary findings suggest that spatial audio-particularly sounds implying unseen threats-may be more effective than post-processing visual effects in inducing immersion and discomfort, with 75% of users rating audio cues as more impactful. We discuss implications for designing VR training environments where auditory realism may enhance stressmanagement skill development for real-world contexts.

title: Continuous and Interpretable Empathic Behaviors for Embodied Intelligent Virtual Agents.
abstract: We present an embodied intelligent virtual agent (IVA) for empathic human-agent communication in immersive extended reality (XR). The agent supports low-latency streaming conversation using a commercial artificial intelligence (AI) service and synchronizes speech with viseme-driven lip sync and facial dynamics. During communication, the agent's empathy state and nonverbal behaviors are computed from user interaction data, including gaze, facial expressions, gestures, and vocal features. The empathy state integrates understanding-oriented and affect-oriented components, enabling the agent to express empathic behavior through eye contact, nodding, mimicry, body proximity, and facial expression in a continuous and interpretable manner. Our demonstration highlights the potential of grounding empathic IVA behavior in empirical observations of externally expressed empathy in dyadic XR communications.

title: Social VR Administrator: A Context-Aware Model Agent Design for Harassment Prevention in Social VR.
abstract: As Social VR platforms continue to expand, ensuring user safety against interpersonal harassment has become an increasingly critical challenge. Existing mitigation approaches—largely dependent on human moderation or invasive biometric sensing—suffer from limited scalability, privacy concerns, and insufficient contextual understanding. In this paper, we present Social VR Administrator (SVRA), a context-aware intelligent agent framework designed to provide cost-effective, transparent, and automated moderation in social VR environments. SVRA employs a novel modular architecture comprising three key components: A Context Analyzer that interprets behavioral norms by incorporating environmental settings and social relationships; a Dynamic Model Selector that adaptively balances detection accuracy and computational efficiency by escalating analysis from lightweight screening models to advanced Vision Language Models (VLMs); and an Action Module that executes graduated interventions ranging from warnings to blocking. Experimental results demonstrate that SVRA effectively balances detection accuracy with resource consumption, enabling a robust, privacy-preserving harassment prevention.

title: Facilitating Discussions in Immersive Virtual Meetings with Virtual Agents.
abstract: This research investigates using virtual agents for facilitating collaboration in immersive virtual meetings. We especially focus on how proactive engagement of virtual agents can improve user experience in discussions held in immersive virtual meetings. We developed an immersive virtual meeting system with a virtual agent that proactively provides feedback on discussions based on the agenda, meeting time left, and talk time of each participants. Findings from a user study comparing passive and proactive virtual agent behaviours suggest proactive behaviours can help facilitating an immersive virtual meeting yet could be distracting, needing further investigation to provide more nuanced and relevant intervention.

title: Optical Flow Modulation: Counteracting Physical and Apparent Motion to Regulate Motion Impression.
abstract: We propose a visual cueing method termed luminance mixing, inspired by apparent motion, which induces motion impression through temporal luminance modulation across images captured from multiple static viewpoints, without geometric displacement. We examined whether luminance mixing produces optical-flow-like signals and whether such signals, when opposing those from physical motion, regulate perceived motion impression. Optical-flow was evaluated via participants’ subjective self-motion impression reports. Results showed that luminance mixing reliably elicited motion impression between static images and attenuated motion impression induced by physical motion, demonstrating control over motion impression.

title: TamagotchU!
abstract: TamagotchU is an emotionally intelligent organism in an immersive XR ecosystem that fosters human dialogue. Running on low-energy edge devices, it critiques large-scale ecological costs through decentralized companionship. Portable tamapagers capture real-time facial and voice emotions, collectively evolving digital pufferfish inspired by Yangtze River indicators. The work proposes eco-sentient systems emphasizing modest computation, collective care, and symbiotic futures over extractive spectacle.

title: Educational Effects on Virtual Reality Based Exhibitions of Elementary School Students' Artworks.
abstract: Recently, virtual reality(VR) technologies have been widely applied in education fields by providing immersive experience. In particular, teachers at the remote sites can deliver realistic and interactive three-dimensional contents to a large number of students. In this paper, we present a VR museum system for elementary school students to visualize and interact with their self-created drawings. The proposed system is a desktop-based metaverse platform that enables virtual interaction. Our system was deployed in several elementary schools, and a survey study was conducted with participating students. Qualitative analysis indicated high levels of interest in avatar-based interactions within the virtual exhibition environment. The results further suggest that the proposed system can enhance educational effectiveness.

title: Real-Time Superquadric Representation of Cuboids and Cylinders Using Instant Surface Normal Map for Dynamic Object Integration in AR.
abstract: We present a real-time AR system that enables interaction with physical cuboid- and cylinder-shaped objects by representing them as compact superquadrics. Our approach uses Instant Surface Normal (ISN) maps-color images encoding per-pixel geometry-to detect and segment objects based on shape rather than appearance. Superquadric parameters are extracted sequentially, allowing efficient and updatable 3D modeling in real time. Experimental results show accurate detection, consistent segmentation, and reconstruction quality comparable to existing methods, while achieving over 5 \times faster inference. This system allows physical objects to be seamlessly integrated as interactive elements in dynamic AR environments.

title: Dual-Map Spatial Augmentation for Collaborative VR Crisis Management.
abstract: Geospatial data visualization in crisis management is traditionally confined to 2D displays, which limits users’ ability to intuitively grasp complex topographical data related to disaster progression. This research explores the concept of spatial augmentation by introducing a dual-map interface within a collaborative virtual reality (VR) environment designed to support joint analysis, communication, and skill development. The system synchronizes a vertical 2D wall map for high-level coordination with a horizontal table map for tactical 3D terrain analysis, allowing multiple users to share spatial understanding and coordinate decisions in real time. We conducted a user study (N = 18) using data from a real-world wildfire scenario to evaluate how spatial orientation influences user preference and accuracy across the two mapping visualizations and interaction modalities. Our analysis reveals a statistically significant performance advantage for the table interface in spatial measurement accuracy, despite a steeper initial learning curve. Additionally, we identify a correlation between participant height and interface preference, with shorter users showing some reluctance toward the fixed-height table interface. These findings suggest complementary benefits for both interfaces and indicate that collaborative VR-based spatial augmentation tools can enhance communication and teamwork in augmented environments, but must account for user ergonomics to be effective.

title: Symmetrical Reality-Based Large-Scale Simulation of Embodied Agents for the Evolutionary Virtual World.
abstract: Autonomous robots face significant challenges in dynamic, unstructured, and socially complex outdoor environments. A key limitation is the lack of frameworks for evaluating perception, navigation, and cognition under realistic social dynamics. Leveraging the Symmetrical Reality (SR) paradigm, we present a large-scale SR-based simulation framework for embodied intelligence in dynamic social settings. It integrates a hierarchical human behavior model that combines Vision-Language Models for high-level decision-making with model-based low-level motion planning, enabling avatars to respond intelligently to robot behaviors. The framework further supports VR-enabled human-in-the-loop interaction, allowing users to act as virtual robots or humans for bidirectional interaction and rich data collection.

title: I Like the Way you Talk: Exploring Speech Influence on Social Priming Conversation Between Virtual Humans.
abstract: Social priming in virtual reality (VR) refers to utilizing an intentional conversation exposure to shape users’ perceptions of a virtual human (VH), including social presence, affective attraction, etc. In this paper, we aim to investigate the effect of speech on social priming in VR. Specifically, we explore three factors of audibility, intelligibility, and information content by executing a within-subjects experiment. Our experiment reveal that intelligibility and information content positively affect social priming in VR. With experiment results, we provide a practical guidelines for social priming and virtual speech design.

title: Aftermath : AI-Human Asymmetry in VR Interaction.
abstract: An asymmetric VR experience interrogating the unequal dynamics of control between human and AI systems, revealing the quiet hierarchies embedded in our interactions with technology. Aftermath foregrounds the asymmetrical power dynamics between human ingenuity and AI omniscience, probing whether artificial systems can truly understand, replicate, or ultimately surpass human creativity. Game mechanics are designed to simulate AI's control over human agency in subtle yet powerful ways. The asymmetry between the VR player (AI) and the PC player (human) mirrors the real-world dynamic where AI operates from an unseen, omnipresent perspective, shaping human choices without direct intervention. The VR player can manipulate the environment in real-time, controlling how the PC player perceives and interacts with space. The PC player, in contrast, must navigate this dynamic world, always reliant on AI's assistance. Through this unequal relationship, Aftermath invites players to confront the evolving balance between human agency and artificial influence.

title: Embodied Learning of Fractions in Virtual Reality.
abstract: This study explores how embodied interaction in virtual reality (VR) supports fraction estimation. In a between-subjects design, 68 participants completed a fraction estimation task either by physically walking along a virtual number line (embodied condition) or by indicating fractions on a tablet-based number line while seated (non-embodied condition). Fraction estimation accuracy, task completion time, and cognitive-affective measures were recorded. Participants in the embodied condition demonstrated higher estimation accuracy and reported a stronger sense of presence than those in the non-embodied condition. In addition, prior mathematical ability was a strong predictor of estimation accuracy, and the effect of embodiment was moderated by intrinsic motivation.

title: Free-View XR Tours Using 3D Gaussian Splatting with an Avatar Guide.
abstract: XR tours are often built from manual 3D authoring, 3D scanning, photogrammetry, or fixed-view 360° video, which can be timeconsuming to produce or limit free exploration. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offers photoreal free view rendering from captured imagery, yet its use in end-to-end XR touring experiences, especially with lightweight in-scene guidance remains underexplored. We present an XR tour system for free-view exploration of 3DGS scenes in XR that combines controller-based 6-DoF navigation with an avatar guide that delivers proximity triggered text-to-speech narration. We demonstrate the system in a public setting and report observations from a case study with $>50$ participants.

title: Emotion-Aware Bargaining System for Negotiation Training Based on Symmetrical Reality.
abstract: Negotiation is a key skill in everyday consumption and workplace communication. However, most existing negotiation training tools rely on text based interfaces and rule driven scripts, providing limited situational context and insufficient support for practicing complex negotiation processes. To explore more context aware training approaches, we develop a Unity based virtual night market negotiation platform. The system consists of three core modules. A user preference modeling module estimates pricing preferences and concession tendencies from user inputs, historical bidding records, and interaction level cues, including linguistic style features and facial expression related visual indicators derived from image processing. An environmental factor modeling module represents predefined scene level variables such as noise level, crowd density, lighting conditions, visual distractions, and time constraints as contextual factors relevant to negotiation. A strategy selection and language generation module integrates user related and environment related factors within a unified framework to produce dynamic vendor pricing and context appropriate verbal responses. Dialogue generation in the system is supported by a large language model to simulate diverse negotiation styles for training purposes.

title: When and What to Speak: An Autonomous Embodied Chat Agent in Symmetrical Reality.
abstract: Most LLM dialog agents respond only when prompted. We study an autonomous inserter for multi-party talk that decides whether and when to join. Insertion is modeled along three dimensions: speaker persona, scene context, and topic. Using a Qwen-7B backbone, we train persona-, scene-, and topic-aware regression heads to predict a continuous willingness score, plus a classifier over three intervention styles. Deployed in a Unity multi-party simulation, the agent monitors dialogue and inserts itself accordingly. Three-stage evaluations on transcripts, dyadic chats, and group discussions compare model and human insertion judgments. This provides an measure of how human-like its timing can be.

title: Virtual Human in Symmetrical Reality: A Mobile System for Human-AI Coexistence.
abstract: The advancement of artificial intelligence has intensified the challenge of creating intelligent virtual human capable of sustaining long-term companionship. This paper presents a general framework for a virtual companion system based on augmented reality (AR), which prioritizes four key dimensions: situational coherence, immersive interactivity, conversational naturalness, and continuity of presence. We instantiate this framework in a functional AR prototype for handheld mobile devices and develop a comparable nonAR system for a controlled comparison. Through comprehensive user studies, we evaluate the system's effectiveness across the proposed dimensions. Our findings offer important insights and a valuable reference for the future development of companion virtual human.

title: Realizing the Potential of Pervasive Augmented Reality as a Tool to Support Newcomers on-Boarding and Remote Factory Visits.
abstract: Industry 5.0 combines advanced technologies to enhance the role of the human operator. It focuses on creating more collaborative, human-centric workplaces where people and machines work together seamlessly. Pervasive Augmented Reality (AR) strongly supports these goals by extending traditional AR into continuous spatial experiences. It can adapt to the human's context and position, remaining responsive across different environments. However, the potential scope is much broader, with many other scenarios that could benefit from its adaptive/context-aware characteristics. This work discusses the applicability of Pervasive AR for training of newcomers on the shop floor displaying additional layers of information, guiding their activities in a step-by-step manner. Also, enabling remote individuals to conduct virtual visits to factories, having access to the visual feed of on-site individuals, being able to see the same (shared) digital content. These reflections arise from a Human-Centered Design in collaboration with industrial-partners, ensuring insights are grounded in real-world practice.

title: Exploring the Synergy of Combining eXtended Reality and a Robotic Arm for Supporting Scenarios of Remote Collaboration.
abstract: The growing interest in remote collaboration arises from different factors, most notably the rapid advancements in digital technologies, making it increasingly feasible to work from any location. These innovations open new possibilities for global cooperation and productivity. However, several challenges hinder seamless collaboration. Among these are the inherent limitations faced by remote participants in interacting directly with on-site physical objects. Additionally, their perspective remains significantly constrained, often limited to the viewpoints and visual inputs shared by on-site members. Addressing these is essential to unlock the full potential of remote collaboration. This paper explores a robotic arm within an eXtended Reality (XR) environment to transform collaboration practices. The architecture and main features are described, including streaming the task context, on-site and remote manipulation of the robotic arm, and the capacity to display safety zones, among others. Finally, a reflection on applicability is discussed and future directions are drawn.

title: Preliminary Exploration of Sonification for Spatial Augmentation of Ball-Approach Dynamics and Timing in Tennis.
abstract: Open-skill sports require training methods that address perceptual–cognitive functions that influence action timing, in addition to movement technique. Sonification can support action timing by mapping continuous task dynamics to sound without visual overlays. We present a preliminary design exploration of sonification for real-time ball-position feedback in tennis. We implement an end-to-end system that estimates ball position using event-based vision and renders distance dynamics as continuous audio. We examine a 2×2 design space that crosses representation style (explicit tone vs. implicit wind) with frequency range (low: one octave vs. high: two octaves), reflecting a trade-off between change legibility and attentional demand. Pilot observations suggest that highly interpretable sonification can facilitate users’ motor timing perception, whereas implicit designs may support attentional stability.

title: The Interface as a Markov Blanket: Reframing VR Interaction via the Free Energy Principle.
abstract: This paper argues that VR is a natural “testbed” and “design medium” for the Free Energy Principle and active inference: it can (i) systematically manipulate sensorimotor contingencies, precision weightings, and crossmodal conflicts that shape presence, embodiment, and cybersickness; and (ii) expose interpretable control knobs for interface design in terms of variational and expected free energy. Building on recent VR-FEP perspectives and an active-inference reinterpretation of interaction, we propose a practical mapping from VR components to a Markov-blanket interface, derive design implications for presence and embodied interaction, and outline a measurement-driven agenda for estimating individual sensory characteristics and optimizing VR feedback. The resulting framework reframes usability as the joint reduction of prediction error and complexity and reframes exploration-exploitation in VR as balancing epistemic and pragmatic value.

title: Spatial Guidance in Asynchronous Collaboration: The Impact of Embodied Mixed Reality Instructions on Task Accuracy.
abstract: Asynchronous collaboration requires instructions that remain interpretable without immediate feedback, yet conventional guidance is often separated from the workspace and may induce errors. A between-subjects study $(\mathrm{N}=43)$ compared embodied, spatially registered Mixed Reality guidance ($M R$ Guide) with smartphone video (Video Guide) in an asynchronous commissioning procedure. Higher task accuracy was observed for $M R$ Guide during the initial phase in an unfamiliar workspace, whereas differences diminished later. These findings motivate spatially registered messages and novelty-adaptive guidance strategies in asynchronous collaboration. Future work should quantify attention and examine its relationship with accuracy.

title: I Like to Move It, Move It - Non-Intrusive Full Body Tracking for Caves.
abstract: This paper examined full body tracking (FBT) for a CAVE system and proposes a non-intrusive FBT approach. Through FBT the user's entire body is tracked for interactions with the immersive experiences. Within the field of VR, the interest in gesture or FBT input has grown but the majority of research focuses on HMD applications. This paper aims to overcome that research gap. The non-intrusive FBT system is based on 3D Human Pose Estimation (HPE) with a single RGB sensor to minimize setup and financial hurdles usually accompanying FBT. The non-intrusive concept aims to enhance user experience through the lack of external trackers or devices the user is usually required to wear for FBT as well as place the tracking sensor behind the user. A proof-ofconcept was created and a user study performed (\mathrm{N}=42) to evaluate the concept by directly comparing non-intrusive FBT with a standard input device. Our results highlight the potential of nonintrusive FBT for immersive experiences in addition to challenges HPEs currently face for real-time FBT.

title: An Immersive Technical Document - Applying Game Design Techniques to Immersive Visualization Laboratories.
abstract: Immersive visualization laboratories (IVL) offer a wide range of immersive hardware, software and expertise, e.g. virtual reality (VR) to extended reality (XR). Each IVL offers a unique hardware and software infrastructure depending on their focus and use-cases. Not only are these laboratories highly specialized, so is the development process for XR applications. One common use case for IVLs is the collaboration with a domain scientists, each with their own data formats and requirements with regard to output hardware. Based on development processes often employed in the gaming industry, we examine the concept of game design documents (GDD) and developed an immersive technical document (ITD) to optimize immersive application development process. The ITD can mitigate scope creep and help communication between IVL experts and external partners. We have used our ITD in practical courses and general projects and examine advantages and challenges of the document.

title: This Is Not a Classroom: Theorizing Affordances for Learning.
abstract: Virtual Reality provides many opportunities to move beyond the bounds of physical classrooms in the pursuit of designing effective learning environments. A key design consideration of VR learning environments are the potential perceived affordances that might influence learning outcomes. However, design may influence different types of learning in diverse ways. This position paper outlines the importance of affordances, presents the case of perceived environmental fidelity and proposes a set of additional affordances that designers, educators, and researchers should consider.

title: Powering Clinical Communication Training with an LLM-Powered Virtual Reality Simulation.
abstract: Clinical communication is essential for health professions (HP) students, yet simulation labs and prior VR systems often rely on rigid scripts that fail to capture the unpredictability of real patient encounters. We present VAPS, a Virtual AI Patient Simulator that integrates embodied conversational agents (ECAs) with large language models (LLMs) to support dynamic, voice-based interactions. We conducted a mixed-method evaluation with 40 HP students from five disciplines, examining usability, sense of agency, emotional engagement, and perceived realism. Results show that VAPS was usable, reduced nervousness, and was perceived as immersive and emotionally authentic. Students viewed VAPS as a supplement rather than a replacement for simulation labs and envisioned future extensions including diverse patient cases and interprofessional training. Our findings suggest that VR simulation should evolve from looking real toward fostering experiences that feel real, with conversational AI playing a central role in enabling more adaptive and authentic learning.

title: Calm but Alert: Neurofeedback Enhances Stability in Virtual Reality Landslide Driving.
abstract: Mountain driving with landslides is hazardous. Warning systems are typically based on external cues, but we understand less about the addition of light internal-state feedback with substantial warnings. We examined whether real-time neurofeedback (NF) can help individuals remain regulated in a virtual reality (VR) landslide driving task with warning poles. In a between-subjects design, 47 participants were randomly assigned to either an NF group, which received a Focus-Index panel from four EEG channels, or a control group without NF. The dependent variables were speed, path deviation, and number of collisions. Physiological variables were EEG-derived focus and heart rate variability (HRV). After outlier removal, there were no statistically significant differences in the behavioral data. However, NF increased the Focus Index, reflecting improved attentional engagement, and HRV indicated greater autonomous regulation. These results suggest that simple EEGbased NF can contribute to hazard warnings by improving drivers' calm and alertness during safety-critical driving.

title: 4D Minimally Invasive Surgery Scene Reconstruction and Simulation Using Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting.
abstract: Reconstructing deformable tissues from endoscopic videos is essential for surgical simulation, training, and automation. We present a 4D endoscopic reconstruction framework based on deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), featuring an integrated pipeline for 3DGS-to-closed-mesh conversion and tetrahedralization for solver-based physics simulation. We further demonstrate the practical utility of reconstructed tissues across multiple simulation engines, highlighting the pipeline's potential for interactive surgical education and high-fidelity, data-driven Extended Reality (XR) simulation systems.

title: Doubled Pedagogical Agents in an Immersive Virtual Environment.
abstract: To enhance the effectiveness of remote lectures and asynchronous education, researchers have investigated how the design of virtual pedagogical agents influences learning. While prior research has primarily focused on the effects of agent appearance, this study examined the impact of the number of agents within an immersive virtual environment on memory and agent perception. We hypothesized that presenting information from two pedagogical agents would improve performance on memory tasks compared with a single agent, but would also elicit uncanniness due to their identical appearance, known as the clone devaluation effect. We conducted a preliminary study, and results from eight participants suggested that the order of conditions might reverse effects on recall accuracy in the within-participants design. These findings indicate that the experimental design should be carefully reconsidered, for example, by including a practice trial to familiarize participants with the memory task and virtual environment.

title: Perceptually Calibrated Foveated Chroma Attenuation for Gaze-Contingent VR Displays.
abstract:
We introduce a foveated chroma attenuation strategy for gazecontingent virtual reality (VR) displays. Conventional stereo rendering maintains uniform color fidelity across the visual field, disregarding its perceptual non-uniformity at increasing retinal eccentricities. To exploit this perceptual asymmetry, we propose an adaptive chroma modulation technique that preserves full chroma at the fovea and progressively attenuates saturation toward the visual periphery. This strategy is evaluated in real-time rendering with diverse virtual scenes. Through perceptual calibration experiments, we found the color degradation weights 
[0.70,0.85]
 for the blueyellow and [0.35,0.55] for the red-green channel. Within these bounds, theoretical analyses indicate a potential chroma bandwidth reduction of 
31−37%
.

title: Edge- and Eccentricity-Guided Foveated Path Tracing with Adaptive Russian Roulette.
abstract:
Path tracing is widely regarded for its ability to produce physically accurate photorealistic imagery. However, high computational cost and slow convergence limit its real-time applications, particularly in interactive or immersive environments. Therefore, we present a dynamic foveated path tracing approach that exploits the non-uniform sensitivity of human vision to accelerate the rendering performance. Our method combines (i) an eccentricity-dependent sampling allocation derived from a cortical magnification model, (ii) edgeaware importance modulation that increases sampling near highcontrast structures, and (iii) foveated Russian roulette termination that shortens expected path length toward the periphery while maintaining unbiasedness via throughput compensation. We evaluate six complex scenes under uniform (4 SPP) and foveated (max 4 SPP) sampling budgets at 
4K
 resolution. The foveation improves the performance up to 
2.77×
 with OIDN denoiser and scores similar or higher in FovVideoVDP's just- objectionable-difference (JOD) scores. These results indicate a favorable quality-efficiency tradeoff for real-time path tracing under perceptual constraints.

title: An LLM-Driven Pipeline for Synthetic Surveillance Video Dataset Generation in Virtual Environments.
abstract: Collecting real-world surveillance data for rare and security-critical behaviors is challenging due to ethical, legal, and practical constraints. In this work, we present a behavior-driven simulation pipeline for generating controllable surveillance scenarios in virtual environments. Built on Unreal Engine and MetaHuman actors, the proposed system combines graph-based spatial constraints with an LLM-driven semantic behavior planner to generate executable human behavior sequences. Unlike recent text-to-video generation approaches that primarily focus on pixel-level realism, our framework emphasizes structured behavior execution, reproducibility, and explicit control over agent roles, routes, and interactions. Scenarios generated by the proposed framework are rendered from multiple fixed, CCTV-like viewpoints and paired with structured annotations. The proposed framework enables the generation of synthetic surveillance data with structured annotations, including temporally segmented actions and object interactions, through roleconditioned human behavior simulation under explicit spatial and semantic constraints.

title: Emotional and Energy Variations in University Personnel. A VR Intervention.
abstract: This work expands the knowledge about Virtual Reality (VR) based therapeutic interventions for mental health issues, with a new pilot study directed to university personnel. We use VR applications to promote emotional well-being in university environments, analyzing their influence on emotional management and the energetic state of participants. Our methodology was co-designed with psychologists of our Occupational Health and Safety Department as an alternative for treatment for all personnel. Results show a positive impact on participants’ energy levels and mood states, and the need for different approaches for different mood states.

title: AeroScale: A Resizable Drone-Based POV Display for Mobile and Shared Augmented Reality.
abstract: Drone-based displays leverage their physical mobility and inherent sharability to ground digital content in the physical world, creating a form of shared augmented reality accessible without individual headsets. However, their potential is fundamentally constrained by a fixed form factor, which enforces a trade-off between mobility (navigational agility) and sharability (display visibility). To this end, this paper presents AeroScale, which features a retractable persistence-of-vision mechanism capable of actively varying its display diameter in flight. This design addresses the trade-off between mobility and sharability, allowing the AR display to prioritize mobility in confined environments or maximize sharability for public conditions.

title: Comparing Fingerprint to Haptics-Based Authentication Methods in XR Devices.
abstract: Secure and seamless authentication in extended reality (XR) environments remains a significant yet understudied challenge. Traditional passwords are cumbersome with 3D controllers and novel methods are needed. We present a formative comparative evaluation of fingerprint to a haptics-based authentication methods for XR. Fingerprint authentication was implemented using an ESP-based capacitive sensor, while the haptics-based authentication was achieved through the replication of a Morse code-style vibration pattern displayed to the user. While fingerprint biometrics offer a fast login option, the haptics-based method does not require preregistration, can be used as a one-time passcode, and does not require custom hardware.

title: How we Learn in Extended Reality: A Systematic Look at Learning Frameworks in XR Education.
abstract: A large body of literature has demonstrated significant potential of extended reality (XR) technologies for improving learning outcomes and educational experiences across a wide range of disciplines. Numerous literature reviews summarize these contributions. In this paper, we present a review of 224 literature reviews that were conducted to analyze and understand the research that has been conducted in this topic area. We summarize how learning theories have been leveraged in these works, and correlate how they align with the Cognitive Affective Model of Immersive Learning (CAMIL) XR learning framework. The goal is to reinforce the efficacy of CAMIL with existing research and evaluate patterns in the corpus.

title: Electroencephalographic Assessment of Comfort in Urban Environments Using Virtual Reality.
abstract: Rapid urbanization affects well-being and stress, motivating research in “neurourbanism”. However, many studies rely on 2D representations of urban environments, which lack realism. We combined VR with 64-channel electroencephalography to assess comfort in urban environments. Green visibility induced reduced heart rate, suggesting relaxation. Building height induced increased betaband activity, suggesting cognitive engagement. Building coverage most strongly affected the perceived restorativeness scale, suggesting subjective restoration. This multi-indicator approach enabled us to pinpoint specific urban elements linked to different aspects of comfort, demonstrating that VR combined with diverse physiological and subjective measures can effectively identify comfort-related factors.

title: Bug in My Software.
abstract: Bug in My Software (BIMS) is a real-time simulation paired with handmade textile installation that reimagines artificial intelligence along the biological, cultural, and industrial history of silk production. The project is centered on the silkmoth (Bombyx mori), one of the earliest lifeforms redesigned by human intervention. In BIMS, Silkmoth DNA, reproductive cycle, and labor role become the blueprint for a real-time synthetic ecosystem populated by evolving digital agents. Situating AI within the history of textile labor, biological engineering, and industrial automation, BIMS reframes machine intelligence as collective, biological, and materially entangled.

title: Demographic Influences on Balance-Based Locomotion in Virtual Reality.
abstract: This study investigates how demographic factors influence movement behavior in virtual reality (VR) during balance-based locomotion (BBL). Twenty-eight participants navigated a virtual track using isometric and elastic balance boards across virtual, physical, and conditional orientation modes.
