Mixed-design analyses revealed significant interaction effects involving gender, body weight, height, and prior board-sport experience, indicating that these characteristics modulated responses to orientation strategy and balance feedback. Anthropometric factors (i.e., weight and height) primarily altered efficiency- and stability-related outcomes across orientation modes, consistent with differences in effective mechanical coupling and balance regulation demands. Prior board-sport experience modulated sensitivity to feedback and orientation constraints but did not uniformly improve traversal accuracy or movement efficiency. Together, these findings suggest that BBL behavior emerges from the interaction of user characteristics and control configuration, motivating adaptive calibration and inclusive interface design.

title: Simulating the Future: The Role of Multimodal Virtual Reality in Futuristic Technologies' User Testing and Training.
abstract: Immersive multimodal Virtual Reality (VR) simulations can effectively bring futuristic technologies to life, providing users with a meaningful insight into how the product will operate and feel, as well as support training for technologies that are still in development. This study investigates the effectiveness of VR experiences in shifting users’ thinking from abstract to concrete, using flying cars as an illustrative example. The preliminary data suggest that multimodal VR facilitates a transition from abstract to more concrete thinking, albeit potentially with adverse effects on individual risk perception. Areas of future research include largersample studies that will enable diversity in initial attitudes towards given technology, as well as diversity in personality characteristics.

title: HA-VTON: Prompt-Guided Human Avatar Generation with Virtual Try-ON Result from Single Human and Garment Images.
abstract: 3D human avatar generation has been a hot topic of the 3D research community for many years, particularly in the VR domain. One of its downstream tasks, Virtual Try-On (VTON) is a transformative technology commonly applied in e-commerce and fashion design. Recent 3D VTON works relied on 3DGS human models as input and achieved promising results. However, capturing a 3DGS human input is generally costly compared to an image input. To address this limitation, we propose a Prompt-guided Human Avatar Generation with Virtual Try-On Result (HA-VTON) framework. Given a human image, a garment image and an outpainting prompt, it can generate a 3D human avatar with virtual try-on result. Additionally, we introduce an outpainting module which is designed for completing body information in the human image for reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework is effective in generating 3D human avatars when compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

title: Directional Guidance Device Using Skin Shear Deformation on the Nasal Bridge.
abstract: Haptic feedback on the nose has gained attention as a method for presenting information that does not interfere with the visual or auditory senses, particularly in the context of navigation. Among these approaches, methods utilizing eyeglass nose pads are promising as they impose minimal additional burden on the user. However, existing methods mainly rely on vibration stimuli, which face challenges such as sensory adaptation, discomfort during continuous use, and reduced discriminability due to the propagation of vibrations. To address these issues, we propose a directional guidance method that induces skin shear deformation using rotating motors embedded in the nose pads to provide clearer directional cues. We developed a prototype and conducted an experiment to identify eight types of stimulus patterns. The results showed an overall accuracy of 72.8%. In particular, the directional recognition accuracy (classifying into Left, Right, or Both) reached an extremely high rate of 96.9%. On the other hand, response time analysis suggested that cognitive load increased under complex conditions where both motors were active. Subjective evaluations highlighted that while the clarity of the stimuli was appreciated, the shifting of glasses caused by shear deformation posed a challenge for wearability. This study demonstrates the high discriminability of skin shear stimulation on the nasal region, but optimization of parameters balancing comfort and accuracy is necessary for practical application.

title: Eliciting Care in VR: A Multi-Modal Pseudo-Haptic Approach to Virtual Object Fragility.
abstract: Conveying nuanced physical properties like fragility in Virtual Reality (VR) without specialized haptic hardware is a significant challenge [7]. This paper evaluates a multi-modal pseudo-haptic system that layers auditory feedback, a diegetic UI, and a procedural visual shader. Through a study (N=31), we demonstrate that calibrated visual and auditory feedback can enable nuanced perceptual judgments and foster cautious behaviors equivalent to handling real-world delicate materials. Our findings suggest that layered feedback effectively induces a sense of “care” and psychological tension, enriching interaction plausibility in consumer VR.

title: Hands-On Fragility: A Multi-Modal Pseudo-Haptic System for Delicate Interaction in VR.
abstract:
This research demo presents a multi-modal pseudo-haptic system designed to simulate object fragility in Virtual Reality (VR) using bare-hand interaction. While consumer VR lacks granular haptic feedback, our system employs a procedural cracking shader, stressdependent audio, and a diegetic UI to elicit a sense of “care” in users. A user study 
(N=31)
 confirms that these software-driven cues allow users to distinguish between fragility levels and significantly alter their motor behavior. This demonstration allows participants to experience this psychological tension firsthand, providing a novel framework for handling delicate virtual artifacts without specialized hardware.

title: ElectroEncephaloGraphy Verification of Speed Adaptation in Time-Distortion Ski Training System.
abstract: Speed adaptation is a perceptual effect in which continuous exposure to fast motion causes subsequently viewed motion to appear slower. Although previous works show that skill training with time distortion in VR is effective, the statistical evidence underlying how they work remains limited. In the gradual speed-increase condition, non-beginner participants reported significantly lower subjective speed. EEG results from consistent responders showed significant changes in parietal Alpha (Pz) and posterior temporal Theta (P8) bands. These findings confirm that the VR time distortion system induces measurable speed adaptation, accompanied by corresponding changes in parietal and posterior temporal neural activity.

title: VR Builds Lasting Empathy & Compassion: Observation Edges Embodiment in Adolescents.
abstract:
We tested whether VR perspective-taking enhances empathy and compassion in adolescents, comparing first-person embodiment and third-person observation. In a randomized trial (N=703, ages 13-18, Kenya and Nigeria), participants experienced VR scenarios depicting ethnic discrimination in Embody (first-person), Observe (third-person), or Control conditions. Both VR conditions produced medium-to-large effects on empathy and compassion among low-baseline participants (d=0.45–0.80), with effects persisting at four-week follow-up. Observe outperformed Embody: in the full sample, Observe significantly increased empathy and compassion relative to Control at post-intervention (d=0.21) and followup (d=0.30). Path models revealed a suppression effect explaining Embody's underperformance: Embody increased social presence (d=0.24), which predicted higher compassion, but simultaneously exerted a direct negative effect on compassion 
(
c
′
=−3.84,p=.016)
, partially cancelling the benefit. For emotionally intense content, third-person observation may cultivate empathy and compassion more effectively than first-person embodiment in adolescents.

title: The Bathroom as a VR Space: How Visual-Tactile Congruence Shapes Presence and Naturalness During Bathing.
abstract: Japanese bathrooms hold the potential to become novel VR spaces. However, bathrooms remain unexplored as VR spaces, and almost no research has been conducted. To explore this potential, we created a multisensory system for use in a real bathroom and conducted the first exploratory user study on VR experiences during full-body immersion in hot water. Our results demonstrated that visual-tactile congruence significantly impacted user perception (presence and naturalness). These findings highlight the critical role of visual-tactile congruence in modulating the bathing experience and suggest that the bathroom holds potential as a novel space for VR applications.

title: Sonic Sensemaking: Augmenting Narrative Integration of Invisible Intellectual Processes.
abstract: The purpose of this study is to facilitate sensemaking-the integration of subjective experiences into a “self-narrative”-by using fragmented environmental sounds to reclaim moments often lost to efficiency-driven values. In modern intellectual labor, daily value is often dominated by objective results, causing invisible cognitive processes and subtle social interactions to be forgotten as “worthless” due to a lack of tangible output. While AI-driven lifelogs attempt to verbalize experiences, they often impose fixed meanings and hinder reflection on information that is difficult to process as language. We propose a method to induce a process where users actively retrieve memories and reconstruct meaning by intentionally providing ambiguous auditory fragments with lowered information resolution. We developed a system that presents 30-second environmental sound fragments via web-based interfaces and propose a 3-day auto-ethnography to investigate how these interactions evolve over time. By analyzing the retrieval frequency of non-task memories and their impact on subjective value, we aim to clarify the process of constructing self-narratives independent of productivity metrics. The success criteria include the rediscovery of subjective meaning in previously discarded time and the qualitative enrichment of daily journaling.

title: Viewpoint Suggestion of Feature-Rich Photos Using Smartphone Photogrammetry and Keypoint Detection.
abstract: We propose a smartphone-based system that automatically suggests the suitable camera position and angle to a target object when we try to take a feature-rich photo of it. The system first captures a 3D mesh of the object using photogrammetry and virtually takes photos of the mesh from different positions and angles. Then, the system extracts and compares the keypoints of each virtual shot and outputs the one with the largest number of keypoints. We describe the system and demonstrate its effectiveness through examples.

title: Estimating Mental Effort in Virtual Reality Using Multimodal Biosignals.
abstract: We present a pilot study about estimating mental effort in Virtual Reality (VR) using multimodal physiological signals. A dual N-back task was implemented in VR to induce graded levels of mental effort, assessed using a subjective mental effort questionnaire (SMEQ) and physiological signals (EEG, ECG, and EDA). These signals were used for real-time estimation of mental effort. To examine general applicability, we conducted a preliminary evaluation in an interactive VR shopping environment. Our findings highlight both the feasibility of mental effort estimation in VR and the challenges of evaluating real-time inference in interactive VR contexts.

title: Reconstructing 360-Degree Memories in Virtual Reality with Generative Artificial Intelligence.
abstract: Reminiscence is the activity of recalling and revisiting a memory. Past research highlights that reminiscence in older adults can promote healthy aging, improve psychological well-being, and could foster inter-generational communication. Virtual reality offers benefits to reminiscence as it allows users to reenact the past in embodied, immersive, and multi-sensory ways. A key challenge in VR reminiscence is the recreation of past scenes that are relevant and familiar to each user. Thus, this research seeks to evaluate and implement GenAI to prototype 360-degree scenes based on inputs that are relevant to each user. In particular, we examine the implementation 1) text-to-image and 2) panorama outpainting generation methods for 360-degree scenes. This study aims to bring personalization and control to the recreation of memories in VR. Moreover, this work strives to support the democratization of content creation in VR for users with various degrees of technical expertise.

title: Low-Cost VR Teleoperation of a 5-Dof Robotic Arm with a Synchronized Digital Twin and Ultrasonic Safety Loop.
abstract: High-fidelity virtual-reality (VR) teleoperation systems remain costly and technically demanding, limiting adoption in education, healthcare and small-scale robotics industrial space. This paper presents a reproducible, low-cost VR teleoperation framework for a 5-degree-of-freedom (5-DOF) robotic arm integrating Unity-based immersive control, a synchronized digital twin, and an ultrasonic safety feedback loop. The system links a Meta Quest 3 headset and Unity interface to an Arduino microcontroller through a cloud MQTT broker (HiveMQ) for real-time bidirectional communication. An HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor continuously monitors proximity and triggers both visual cues in VR and autonomous safety responses on the physical arm. We detail the system architecture, Unity-MQTT-Arduino data pipeline, and preliminary latency observations. The results indicate that affordable VR teleoperation with digital-twin synchronization and closed-loop safety can be achieved using off-the-shelf components, providing a practical baseline for educational, research, and industrial field-training applications.

title: Beyond Frame: A Remediation Authoring Tool for Transforming 2D Artworks into VR Experiences.
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI has expanded the possibilities for VR content creation, yet the remediation of 2D paintings into immersive 3D experiences remains a fragmented and technically demanding process. Creators often struggle with disjointed AI tools that produce randomized, uncontrollable results. This paper introduces a unified “2D-to-VR” authoring framework designed to lower technical barriers while creating a “Human-in-the-loop” workflow. We present a prototype system that automates the analysis and spatialization of 2D art into 2D, 2.5D, and 3D VR modes, and we demonstrate its efficacy through a pilot implementation using Claude Monet's Water Lilies.

title: Study on the Impact of Detector Replacement on Accuracy and Coding Efficiency in Video Coding for Machines.
abstract: Recently, the video compression industry has increasingly focused on developing compression approaches tailored to machine vision applications. Enhancing detection accuracy is essential to preserve critical information. We show that replacing the legacy ROIgeneration detector in the MPEG Video Coding for Machines reference software (VCM-RS) with a state-of-the-art detection model delivers better preservation of object information and improved reliability compared with the existing baseline. In the current implementation of the MPEG VCM-RS, the ROI module uses older detectors that often miss small or occluded objects. The study measures end-to-end impact on the random access scenario. Average detection accuracy increases from 47.84 to 51.16 mAP and for certain sequences, coding efficiency also improves. This paper highlights the need for broader testing of recent detection models within VCM-RS.

title: Design and Implementation of a Virtual Reality-Based Electronic Voting System.
abstract: 2D web/mobile voting collects ballots efficiently but provides little sense of shared procedure in formal meetings. We present a VR prototype for shareholder-style voting in a shared virtual conference room. Avatars review agenda boards and cast a single-choice ballot via in-world buttons, while an operator console configures minimum participation and approval rules and queries the final tally. A Delightex client and a lightweight server record one vote per authenticated account. Informal demos suggest clearer procedural staging than a web ballot, while scalability and election-grade security remain future work.

title: Multi-User Mixed Reality Control of a Multi-Arm Robotic System.
abstract: This work presents a mixed reality (MR) user interface integrated with a Digital Twin (DT) for collaborative control of a multi-arm robotic system in laboratory environments. The DT maintains a synchronized virtual representation of the robots and task scene, enabling multiple operators to interact in a shared MR workspace. Using HMDs and motion tracking, users intuitively select and control robot arms through natural hand motions. A preliminary user study with a collaborative manipulation task demonstrates reduced task completion time and lower subjective workload compared to a conventional leader-follower interface, highlighting the system's potential for intuitive multi-user robot teleoperation.

title: Learnability of Embodied Control Interfaces for Real-World 3D Navigation.
abstract: We investigated how users learn to cope with delays in embodied interfaces during navigation in three dimensions (3D), and whether haptic sensory anticipation of movement direction enhances navigation performance. To this end, we utilized Levitas, an embodied interface that enables both physical and virtual displacement within an Immersive Virtual Environment (IVE). In this interface, two wearable sensors control a mechanical motion base that suspends a user, allowing them to “fly” at their own will. A wristband with haptic feedback was implemented to reduce the perceived delay in movement during 3D navigation. We explored the benefits of haptic feedback anticipation and the effect of adaptation after four sessions of use. Practice improved participants' completion times in the embodied interfaces. Learning patterns were similar regardless of whether haptic feedback was included. Additionally, participants exhibited anticipatory body movements even during Joystickbased navigation, underscoring the potential for combining both interaction types.

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Simulator with Real-Time AI-Based Evaluation for Improving Surgical Team Performance.
abstract: Surgical Safety Checklist (SSC) consisting of Timeout and Debrief performed at appropriate time in the operating room (OR) has shown to be a critical and effective tool to reduce errors and improve patient safety. Simulation-based training of OR team members is critical for performing SSC but remains challenging using traditional methods. We have developed a VR simulator that utilizes the Operating Room Black Box (R) (ORBB) recordings, Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and Large Language Models (LLM) to simulate and evaluate realistic scenarios. Virtual Humanoid Avatars representing surgical team members, allowed trainees to interact with and learn from scenarios derived directly from ORBB Recordings. Trainees' speech transcribed using Whisper AI were analyzed in real-time using LLM fined tuned with SSC assessment rubrics. We compared zero-shot LLM-based evaluations against ORBB grades using accuracy and F1-score. For Timeout, GPT-OSS 20B achieved 0.88 accuracy / 0.91 F1, and Gemma 3-27B 0.87 / 0.90. For Debrief, both models achieved 0.90 accuracy, with GPT-OSS slightly higher (0.92 F1) than Gemma (0.91 F 1). The results show that the VR simulator for training in SSC with automated assessment model using LLM is highly realistic, reliable and can be used for improving operating room team performance.

title: Using AI Entities in Extended Reality to Reinvestigate Cold Cases.
abstract: Cold case investigations face difficulties because original crime scenes and witnesses are no longer accessible. Our early-stage concept explores the feasibility of reconstructing crime scenes in an extended reality environment, alongside AI-driven Non-Player Characters embodying the personas of former investigators and potential perpetrators. Our proof-of-concept prototype allows users to revisit crime scenes and speak to relevant parties, enabling them to iteratively refine hypotheses and reasoning strategies. We derive preliminary insights into how this system can support the formation of plausible leads and the integration of spatial evidence with narrative reasoning, contributing lessons learned toward future XR-AI investigative tools.

title: Mixed Reality for Group-Based, Integrated Instruction of Anatomy, Pathology, and Physical Examination.
abstract: Anatomy is fundamental to medical education and clinical practice. Traditional instruction involves 2D atlases, dissections, and plastic models. Translating 2D images into a 3D spatial map is difficult. Dissections suffer from the cost of cadavers, formalin exposure, and emotional distress. Plastic models lack sufficient details and anatomical variation. Mixed reality (MR) addresses these issues by offering a rich, 3D environment where students can affordably and safely explore a virtual body. Anatomy instruction is typically delivered in small groups to promote active learning and knowledge sharing. Using MR for group study simplifies the body tracking burden because participants meet face-to-face, allowing both verbal and nonverbal communication while enabling them to safely move through the space. Medical curricula have integrated anatomy with clinical sciences to highlight its relevance. In clinical practice, students must link anatomy with pathology and diagnostic methods. We present a novel MR system that facilitates group-based, integrated instruction of anatomy, pathology, and physical examination. Feedback shows the system boosts learning, yet performance and learning curve need improvement.

title: Use of Exoskeleton Chair for Supporting Posture Change in VR Experience.
abstract: This study investigates the impact of a posture-supportive device on user experience in virtual reality (VR), focusing on fatigue, cybersickness, overall experience, and task performance. Using an adjustable exoskeleton chair, participants engaged in a custombuilt VR game that required posture transitions between sitting and standing while completing interactive tasks. While the Normal Chair (N) condition resulted in the highest task performance, participants in the Without Chair (W) condition reported a more positive game experience. Physiological signals, including heart rate and electrodermal activity, indicated that the posture-supportive exoskeleton (E) condition resulted in reduced fatigue compared to the without-chair (W) condition.

title: Exploring and Evaluating Multimodal Interaction Techniques for Reducing Fatigue in Long-Duration VR.
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) enables immersive experiences, but longduration use can challenge user comfort when relying on conventional controller-based interaction. We investigate how multimodal interaction techniques influence comfort and performance in extended VR use. We conducted a one-hour between-subjects study with 45 participants comparing three input techniques: controllers, head-gaze with touch input, and head-gaze with voice commands. Our results provide initial evidence that multimodal techniques can reduce sustained physical effort while maintaining effective interaction. These findings offer early design insights for creating more ergonomic and sustainable interaction techniques for long-duration VR experiences.

title: Event-Based Network Resource Management in Azure Digital Twins for Multi-User XR Systems.
abstract: Traditional network resource management methods primarily rely on network key performance indicators to allocate resources, often neglecting user experience and interaction quality. However, in immersive XR applications, real-time user interaction and quality of experience (QoE) significantly impact resource requirements. Therefore, we propose an event-based adaptive multi-user XR network resource management system that considers both real-time network conditions and user interaction information. The Azure Digital Twins (ADT) platform creates twins for both users and the network, enabling real-time data updates. The system also employs event-based Azure Functions to generate priority signals and write the generated priority decisions back to the ADT model. This ADT architecture is modular and scalable, reflecting the state of the multi-user XR environment in near real-time, thereby enabling user-aware priority decisions for future network resource management. Experimental results show an average control-loop reaction time of 1-2 seconds under a simple decision logic. This outlines the technical requirements for event-based network resource management in MU-XR scenarios and demonstrates, through a small-scale implementation on Microsoft Azure, how such a mechanism can be realized in practice.

title: Surgical Instrument Trainer: Design and Evaluation of a Mixed Reality System for the Training of Operating Theatre Assistants.
abstract: Surgical education requires the combination of declarative knowledge with spatial, procedural, and sensorimotor skills, yet most training materials rely predominantly on two-dimensional media and passive instruction. This paper presents a mixed reality (MR) training system that enables learners to physically manipulate real surgical instruments while receiving spatially registered, context-aware digital guidance. The system is designed to support embodied learning and to improve the transition between training and clinical practice. In a controlled study $(\mathrm{N}= 42)$, MR-based training was compared to conventional text- and image-based instruction. Results show that MR significantly improved recall of spatially embedded instrument knowledge, such as component names, while no overall advantage was observed for purely symbolic information. Both groups reported comparable gains in perceived learning success. User experience measures indicate high engagement, immersion, and minimal discomfort in the MR condition. These findings suggest that MR is particularly effective for learning tasks involving spatial relations and interaction, and may serve as a complementary modality to existing instructional approaches in early-stage surgical training.

title: Objective Estimation of Cybersickness Using Spatially Resolved Visual Motion Metrics.
abstract: Cybersickness remains a key barrier to the widespread adoption of immersive virtual reality (VR), yet objective prediction of cybersickness from VR content remains challenging. Visual motion, or optic flow, is a primary driver of cybersickness, and its effects depend not only on motion intensity but also on structural properties, coherence, and spatial distribution within the visual field. In this work, we develop an interpretable, content-driven framework for estimating cybersickness from naturalistic VR visual data. We compute dense optical flow and derive motion descriptors capturing intensity, translational and rotational structure (via divergence and curl), and spatial coherence. By segmenting the visual field into central and far-peripheral regions, we account for known differences in motion sensitivity across eccentricity. To address multicollinearity among motion features, we project them into orthogonal principal components, yielding stable predictors aligned with perceptually meaningful motion dimensions. We analysed visual data from a dataset collected from a previous cybersickness study. The results show that general motion intensity strongly predicts cybersickness in the far periphery but only modestly in central vision. Motion coherence and structural variability increase cybersicknessrelated discomfort predominantly in peripheral regions, whereas structured variability in central vision can be stabilizing. These results demonstrate that optic-flow-based components provide spatially resolved, objective indicators of cybersickness, offering a practical foundation for predicting cybersickness.

title: Challenges and Initial Ideas for Scaled Natural Jumping in Large Immersive Environments.
abstract: Navigating expansive immersive virtual environments remains a fundamental challenge in Virtual Reality, necessitating locomotion metaphors that balance efficiency with physical presence. Natural jumping has emerged as a promising solution to bridge the gap between the intuitiveness of natural walking and the efficiency of teleportation. However, recent studies have shown that significant challenges remain in physical fatigue, simulator sickness, and spatial awareness. In this position paper, we analyze the current state of natural jumping research, identify critical design limitations, and propose a multi-stage research agenda. By conducting systematic reviews, controlled user studies, and functional case studies, we aim to contribute evidence-based guidelines that establish scaled natural jumping as a safe, effective, and intuitive locomotion hybrid for the future of VR navigation.

title: Towards Multimodal User State-Aware Adaptive Guidance in MR.
abstract: Most mixed reality (MR) guidance systems rely on static instructions, overlooking user behavioral and cognitive variability. We present a multimodal adaptive guidance framework that combines LLM-generated task graphs with semantic step tracking driven by multimodal interaction events. The system also continuously logs gaze, hand, and head signals to support future temporal user state modeling. In an example MR guidance task, the system achieves robust step tracking with real-time responsiveness (\approx 60 \text{ms} action-to-classification latency). Together, these results demonstrate reliable task progress monitoring and establish a foundation for user state-aware adaptive MR guidance.

title: Advancing Perceptual Training in Arts Education Through Immersive Extended Reality Systems.
abstract: The accessibility of affordable virtual reality (VR) headsets with passthrough capabilities offers new opportunities in arts education. This paper introduces a VR-based perceptual training system for arts, designed using Unity and featuring a customizable 3D grid overlay in passthrough mode on a Meta Quest 3. A pilot study with 14 participants showed improved drawing accuracy and spatial understanding, as self reported by the participants, with high confidence levels (M=8.1) and low motion sickness (M=3.1). We detail our pedagogical principles, study results, and suggest future evaluation studies.

title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: A Conceptual Framework for Personalizing XR Navigation Based on Individual Capacity and Context.
abstract: Our research introduces a conceptual framework for personalizing navigation interfaces in Extended Reality (XR) environments. We challenge the one-size-fits-all paradigm that dominates current XR navigation design, addressing the significant individual differences in spatial cognition that impact navigation performance. Our framework synthesizes evidence from multiple studies showing that users form distinct groups with different preferences and performance patterns when using navigation techniques. We demonstrate how the interaction between individual characteristics and application domains creates unique requirements that drive interface adaptation. Our framework identifies key components for effective personalization: (1) Incorporation of user Characteristics to incorporate individual capacity; (2) consideration of varied application domains; and (3) implementation of personalized and adaptive navigation interfaces in XR. This framework aims to transform XR navigation design from a one-size-fits-all approach to personalized solutions that are context-dependent to accommodate the full spectrum of individual human needs and capacities, ultimately creating more inclusive and optimal XR experiences.

title: CAVE Challenges and Use Cases: A Case Study of the X-SITE CAVE.
abstract: The X-SITE CAVE is a custom, high-resolution visualization platform that has a history spanning more than 17 years. In this paper we summarize the key challenges and considerations we faced over the past years and discuss advantages and disadvantages of design choices. Ongoing development efforts focus on accelerating the provision of new content and improving maintainability, while simultaneously lowering costs and staffing needs. Third-party open-source software is central to these efforts and is complemented by in-house developments, e.g., for customized calibration tools and system control software as well as an adapter to the Godot game engine. We also report successful use cases that highlight the benefits of large-scale VR environments in several application domains.

title: Acceptance of Simulated Body-Proximate Technologies in XR: A Transhumanist Perspective.
abstract: Current hardware developments exhibit a trend towards bodyproximate technologies, moving beyond handheld devices to smart glasses, rings, and possibly bio-integrated sensors. As technology transitions from external tools into the user's immediate personal space and biological boundaries, the requirements for adoption shift; users should be able to trust the device, and feel a sense of ownership, perceiving it as an integral part of themselves, at the same time. By simulating body-proximate technology in Extended Reality (XR), we aim to understand how the degree of invasiveness influences technology acceptance and the psychological construct of embodiment. We propose a study design featuring three distinct scenarios representing an incremental scale of invasiveness, ranging from external wearables to structural body modifications. In this paper, we present the results of an explorative pre-study $(N=37)$ that evaluates user perceptions and the validity of these chosen scenarios. We discuss these preliminary findings and outline the methodological framework for a planned main study designed to investigate the interplay between invasiveness, embodiment, and user acceptance.

title: Virtual Reality-Based Digital Shadow of Quadruped Locomotive System.
abstract: Quadruped robots over years have gained significant application due to their advance terrain adaptability and tenet stability compared to wheeled platforms, nonetheless, the locomotion remains one of the most challenging problems in legged robotics over multi-joint coordination, operating in unpredictable environments, and dynamic stability constraints. We propose a low cost open-source quadruped designed to track the head orientation of an operator wearing a virtual reality (VR) headset, while also utilizing joystick commands for locomotion control with the integration of digital shadow to achieve stable locomotion by synchronized digital models of the physical entity for teleoperation applications.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Virtual Reality Training System for Dental Education.
abstract: Immersive virtual reality is increasingly being adopted in medical education as a scalable and safe approach to procedural training. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an immersive VR training system for conservative dental procedures, specifically aimed at supporting procedural learning in the early stages through real-time guidance. The system replicates a realistic dental office and integrates anatomically accurate 3D models, interactive tools, and a voice tutor that provides immediate and contextualized feedback during task performance. A pilot study involving 16 dental students with theoretical knowledge but no previous practical experience was conducted to evaluate the system's usability, perceived workload, and training effectiveness. Objective performance metrics were collected, including completion time and number of errors, along with subjective measures such as the System Usability Scale, NASA-TLX, and Simulator Sickness Questionnaire. The results indicate a progressive reduction in procedural errors and completion time, high perceived usability, low cognitive workload, and minimal simulation sickness. These results suggest that immersive VR environments enriched with real-time voice feedback can effectively support procedural learning in conservative dentistry. Although the system is intended as a complement rather than a substitute for clinical training, it offers a scalable and accessible solution for preclinical education.

title: Evaluation of a State-Aware Conversational AI Agent for Immersive Anatomy Education.
abstract: The dynamic 3D morphology and temporal complexity of embryonic heart development make it difficult to comprehend. We introduce Reinheart, a conversational AI tutor for anatomy education that is state-aware and integrated into a mixed reality learning environment. The AI tutor uses OpenAI services to provide voicebased tutoring in real-time with interactive 3D visualization. Using a mixed-method analysis, ten anatomy experts assessed pedagogical performance, usability, and trust. The results indicated high ease-of-use and positive social presence, while qualitative feedback revealed limited uncertainty in communication and instability in challenge tasks. Experts supported the tutor's potential for conceptual reinforcement and guided exploration. To improve contextual reasoning and instructional reliability in MR anatomy learning, future work should extend this framework with domain-specific, uncertainty-aware AI.

title: User-Centric Active Learning Through Immersive Visualization.
abstract: Understanding data structure is critical for effective human involvement in machine learning, particularly in user-centric active learning, where annotation decisions by humans shape model behaviour. Learned embedding spaces capture this structure, but are typically explored through 2D interfaces. Virtual Reality (VR) offers an opportunity to present these embeddings immersively, supporting richer perception and interaction. We present a VR-based system for user-centric active learning that enables users to explore and annotate samples directly within an immersive embedding space. The system visualizes a continuously updating 3D embedding space derived from an audio classifier and augments it with common active learning cues, including uncertainty, density, diversity, and class coverage through visual encoding. User annotations trigger iterative retraining, allowing the model and visualization to co-evolve in response to human input.

title: Exploring Augmented Reality Visualizations for Communicating Robot Intent in Robotic Ultrasound.
abstract: Working safely in close proximity to robots, such as during robotassisted medical procedures, requires communication of robot intent. We investigated how augmented reality (AR) visualizations can convey robot poses, trajectories, and motion progress by comparing several designs in a laboratory study with six participants. Results showed that arrow-based visualizations are preferred for representing robot poses and trajectories. Explicit progress displays were perceived as clearer and safer, but trajectory-based cues were preferred overall due to reduced distraction. Overall, visualizations that conveyed essential information while minimizing occlusion were rated most valuable. This work contributes an initial perspective towards structuring the AR design space for humanrobot interaction with a robotic arm, illustrated through the example of robotic ultrasound.

title: Combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Augmented Reality for Automatic Assembly Instructions.
abstract: Studies have shown that Augmented Reality (AR) is an effective tool for improving workers' efficiency in manual assembly and maintenance processes. However, creating high-quality AR instructions remains a significant challenge due to the high development costs, complex assembly procedures, and the continuously evolving nature of instructional materials. To address these challenges, we propose using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to automatically generate AR assembly instructions from PDF-based manuals and present them in a tablet-based assembly assistant application. This approach leverages the content generation capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and the adaptability of RAG to produce rich AR instructions that include text, images, animations, and 3D models without requiring labor-intensive manual intervention or technical expertise. The system was evaluated by 20 experts from Siemens, each performing a complete assembly of an Industrial Automation System (IAS). The generated AR instructions consistently outperformed PDF-based manuals in both the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) and System Usability Score (SUS) while reducing task completion time and error rates of workers in a real-world assembly scenario. This demonstrates that the AR assembly instructions generated by our RAG pipeline significantly improve workers' efficiency, highlighting the potential of a combined approach for scalable AR guidance across industrial domains.

title: Being a Giraffe: Embodied Locomotion Interfaces for Understanding Non-Human Morphology in VR.
abstract: Can physical embodiment of an animal's body in Virtual Reality (VR) support presence and empathy toward radically different beings? We present Being a Giraffe, a VR system that employs custom leg controllers and sustained forward leaning to examine how productive defamiliarization shapes embodied animal experiences. Through two-phase exploratory testing, we found that novel physical constraints triggered curiosity and perspective shift, while informational content and atmospheric audio were necessary to maintain presence. We identify preliminary design considerations for balancing physical defamiliarization with multimodal immersion in crossspecies embodiment.

title: Exploring Review Delivery Contexts in VR Shopping: A Study Design.
abstract: As VR shopping environments increasingly support social presence and embodied interaction, consumer reviews may serve not only as sources of information but also as socially situated cues. This study explores review delivery in VR shopping from a socially embedded perspective and proposes an experimental design to examine how delivery context and message characteristics may influence user judgment and conformity. By framing review delivery context as a novel design dimension in VR shopping environments, this work is expected to offer implications for marketing, VR commerce, and research on persuasion mediated by virtual agents.

title: Interactive Engineering Training Framework in Mixed Reality Environments.
abstract: Maintenance and assembly training within the engineering aerospace and automotive industries involves several complex procedures that must be executed in the right order, correctly, safely and efficiently. Traditional training involves hands-on manipulation and it is conducted via physical demonstrations, assistance or self-practise. It can also involve more than one trainer/trainee, incorporating the element of collaboration, requiring physical presence. Currently, engineering training has been extended with the combination of audiovisual, interactive Computer-Based Training and Virtual/Augmented Reality, bringing many benefits, which address several of the limitations of the traditional methods, making training more cost-effective and efficient. The recent wider adoption of Mixed Reality technology provides further opportunities for a transition to Mixed Reality engineering training platforms, which will be able to bridge the gap with the traditional methods. This paper presents current related work, its limitations and a proposed framework for developing an innovative and practical Mixed Reality collaborative engineering training environment.

title: EcoQuest - an Open World Sustainability Game.
abstract: EcoQuest is an immersive virtual reality experience designed to teach players the impact of environmental decision making through interactive gameplay. Set on a fragile island ecosystem, players harvest resources and manage an inventory while their actions dynamically alter environmental health and endgame outcomes. Unlike traditional survival games, EcoQuest ties player behavior to persistent ecological change: deforestation reduces ground cover, wildlife disappears, and the island becomes barren if resources are mismanaged. EcoQuest demonstrates how VR can promote environmental awareness by combining embodied interaction with realtime ecological feedback.

title: DNA-MESS: Dynamic Narrative Adjustment via Multi-Modal Emotion Sensing & Simulation.
abstract: We present DNA-MESS, a closed-loop adaptive VR system that dynamically adjusts narrative and sensory feedback based on users' physiological and behavioral states. A custom hybrid headset integrating PPG sensing, bone-conduction audio, and haptics enables real-time affect-responsive interaction. Signals are processed in Unity and mapped to generative AI-driven adaptations of audio, haptics, and environmental parameters. Unlike existing systems that rely on behavioral inputs or single modalities, DNA-MESS demonstrates a unified multi-modal sensing-feedback pipeline. The system is showcased through an interactive VR horror demo, illustrating the design space of emotionally adaptive virtual environments.

title: Adaptive Worlds, Active Users: Physiology-Driven Adaptation During Active Interaction in Virtual Environments.
abstract: We present a physiology-driven adaptive virtual environment that supports stress regulation during active interaction. The system integrates real-time heart rate sensing with a closed-loop adaptation pipeline to dynamically modulate environmental audio and lighting while users freely navigate and interact within an immersive virtual garden. Unlike many biofeedback-based VR experiences that emphasize passive viewing, this work demonstrates continuous physiological adaptation alongside object-based interaction, including drawing, object manipulation, and exploration. The adaptation logic operates in parallel with user activity, enabling uninterrupted engagement while maintaining responsive environmental modulation. This demo focuses on system design and technical validation, establishing a foundation for future studies on adaptive, interactive virtual environments for stress regulation.

title: Resonant: A Web-Based Extended Reality Platform for Heartbeat Sharing via Headset Ballistocardiography and Mobile Remote Photoplethysmography.
abstract: This paper presents Resonant, a work-in-progress Web-based Extended Reality platform designed to capture and share cardiac signals through haptics using virtual reality headsets and mobile phones. The system integrates headset-based ballistocardiography, mobile remote photoplethysmography, and commercial heart rate monitors for validation and comparison. This system enables heart rate monitoring without the need for an external heart rate device, as well as provides haptic feedback. Resonant is motivated by the goal of enabling physiological signal sharing without requiring specialized sensing devices to support novel XR experiences that can enable better social connections. This paper describes the system design, sensing approaches, and a workflow for synchronizing heartbeat-driven haptic feedback with narrative media. The intended psychophysiological effects remain to be evaluated in future studies.

title: Autostereoscopic Transparent Display for High-Fidelity 3D Imaging without Resolution Loss.
abstract: We propose a transparent display system capable of presenting high resolution autostereoscopic 3D images that naturally blend into the real-world environment. Conventional methods struggle to achieve lifelike aerial 3D representations due to resolution degradation and the conspicuous physical presence of the display hardware itself. Our proposed method combines a directional display, which presents high-resolution autostereoscopic images, with a transparent reflector to create the visual sensation of a physical 3D object floating in mid-air.

title: Presentation of Impact Sensations by a Floor-Mounted Turntable.
abstract: Previous studies on impact sensation presentation have primarily focused on delivering impulses to the hands using wearable or handheld devices. On the other hand, impact reaction forces propagate through the entire body, ultimately acting between the feet and the ground. Leveraging this physical property, we hypothesize that presenting reaction forces to the feet can enhance impact sensation. This study investigates a method using a floor-mounted turntable. As the user stands on the device, it rotates impulsively during a striking motion to present a reaction force, thereby enhancing the realism of the impact experience.

title: Heritage Soundscape and Experiential Sense-of-Place Design in Virtual Reality Towards Heritage Interpretation.
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) is a powerful tool for heritage interpretation, yet the role of heritage soundscapes remains undervalued compared to visual heritage components. This paper argues for repositioning soundscapes as “interpretive infrastructures” that construct a sense of place in VR. Focusing on Magoksa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Korea, the study outlines a preliminary design approach: identifying heritage sound elements, articulating their relationships with site components, and translating these into VR design strategies. This direction aims to enhance contextual heritage reconstruction, providing a holistic and immersive user experience in virtual heritage.

title: Efficient RAW Patch Segmentation via Iterative AABB Merging for V-PCC Based Gaussian Splat Coding.
abstract: The MPEG Gaussian Splat Coding (GSC) standard adopts the Video-based Point Cloud Compression (V-PCC) framework to compress 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) data. The current V-PCC encoder uses a “fixed-grid patch segmentation” (typically 1024 units), which causes inefficient boundary splitting and oversegmentation in sparse point clouds. This results in excessive metadata overhead and suboptimal atlas image packing. To address this, we propose an Iterative AABB RAW Patch Merging algorithm that decouples the grid alignment resolution from the maximum patch size. By iteratively adjusting the RawShift parameter to shift the AABB origin to finer intervals (e.g., 512, 256, 128, 64 units), our method merges fragmented patches while maintaining V-PCC syntax compatibility. Experimental results across all 16 GSC CTC sequences demonstrate that applying alignment resolutions ranging from 9-bit to 6-bit achieves average patch count reductions between 8.96 % and 17.53 %. The 6-bit resolutions yield the best coding efficiency, with an average BD-rate gain of -0.5 \% in RGB-PSNR and -0.2% in YUV-SSIM for forward facing sequences.

title: Improving User Experience in VR-Based Gamma Entrainment During Cognitive Tasks via Edge-Only Flickering: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Gamma-frequency entrainment is a potential therapeutic approach for Alzheimer's disease. This study developed a method integrating gamma entrainment into a VR-based cognitive task while preserving user experience. A pilot study with eight participants evaluated user experience after completing four Rivermead Behavioral Memory Test-III (RBMT-III) subtests under different flickering conditions. Results showed that the Edge-Only flickering condition, closely resembling the no-flicker condition, yielded better user experience. EEG analyses confirmed higher gamma entrainment in this condition. These findings suggest that Edge-Only flickering effectively induces gamma entrainment while maintaining user experience.

title: Preliminary Exploration of the Effects of Ceiling Height and Spatial Sharing Methods on Cognitive Load in Collaborative Virtual Reality.
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) environments increasingly support shared spaces in which multiple users interact across physically separate locations. While prior studies have explored usability in shared environments, the impact of spatial design factors on users’ cognitive load remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how ceiling height and spatial sharing methods influence cognitive load during interactions in VR shared spaces. We conducted a controlled user study examining combinations of three ceiling height conditions (low, high, and open) and two spatial sharing methods (portal and overlay). The results indicate that ceiling height significantly affects overall cognitive load, with high- and open-ceiling conditions yielding lower load compared to low-ceiling condition. Additionally, overlay-based spatial sharing resulted in reduced temporal demand, task effort, and frustration relative to portal-based sharing. Based on these findings, this paper suggests spatial design guidelines for VR shared spaces that minimize cognitive load and enhance cognitive efficiency in multiplayer VR environments.

title: A Unified Framework for Spatially-Aware Embodied Agents in XR.
abstract: For embodied AI agents to function effectively in XR environments, they must understand space, navigate within it, and converse and act in contextually appropriate ways. This work presents an XR agent system that integrates these capabilities. The proposed system constructs a virtual environment on top of the user's physical space, enabling the agent to converse with users in natural language and perform appropriate actions while maintaining awareness of spatial context. Through a unified loop where dialogue and motion share the same spatial state, consistency between the agent's utterances and actions is maintained. This work explores how spatially grounded embodied agents can perform natural interaction within personalized XR environments.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Distractions and Spatial Constraints in Public XR.
abstract: As extended reality technologies expand into public sectors such as museums and education, existing usability frameworks fail to capture the complexities of dynamic public environments. This study investigates the impact of auditory distractions, visual distractions, and spatial constraints in public XR. A within-subject study was conducted using an augmented reality application simulating public settings with varying levels of sensory stimuli. The findings reveal a complex duality of environmental factors. While auditory distractions increased Focused Attention, and visual distractions enhanced Involvement, both factors simultaneously contributed to increase Mental Demand. Results indicate that larger spatial layouts amplified the effect of sensory distractions. This led to significantly higher Mental Demand in complex settings, likely due to the expanded visual search area and navigation effort. The highest user Involvement was observed in large environments with combined sensory distractions, suggesting that additional environmental stimuli may actually foster engagement rather than disrupting it.

title: KAUST Visualization Core Lab: Going Beyond Immersive Visualization in the Laboratory.
abstract: This article gives an overview of the KAUST Visualization Core Lab (KVL) and discusses recent success stories highlighting different ways of going beyond traditional immersive visualization constrained within laboratory settings. With its shift towards few largescale systems and more HMD systems, KVL uses frameworks to easily port applications between CAVEs and HMDs to maximize their benefits. KVL adapted to provide AI expertise to users, often finding unique research opportunities in immersive visualization projects that are rich in image data. KVL continuously innovates in immersive storytelling, and works with domain scientists to create research communications experiences that can engage and benefit the wider community. While some of the lessons presented here are not necessarily groundbreaking, the goal is to share how KVL continuously learns, adapts, and innovates to remain relevant in an ever-changing research landscape, in hopes of inspiring other labs.

title: Giving a Humanoid Robot a Face - 3D Avatar Generation for Remote Hospital Visits via Telepresence.
abstract: Telepresence robots offer a promising solution to mitigate the challenges of physical absence in healthcare settings, particularly by enabling remote interaction between patients, caregivers, and relatives. This work focuses on enhancing Robody, a humanoid robot, by integrating personalized, photorealistic 3D avatars, thereby increasing the sense of embodiment and reducing the feelings of eeriness that previously arose from the use of 2D avatars. The robot is controlled using a VR headset and corresponding controllers, while a camera captures the user's face and determines the blendshape parameters used for avatar animation. This research explores the automatic generation of photorealistic 3D avatars from monocular smartphone recordings, making it accessible to nonexpert users. A mobile application was developed to guide users through the recording process. Three state-of-the-art avatar generation pipelines, GaussianAvatars, INSTA, and IMavatar, were evaluated in terms of quality, robustness, generation time, and long-term viability. Based on technical evaluation and empirical observations, GaussianAvatars emerged as the most suitable approach for the Robody platform, producing the qualitatively best avatars. A pilot study was conducted in a German neurorehabilitation clinic, involving nursing staff, patients, and their relatives, to assess the impact of Robody with personalized 3D avatars in the intended environment. Results suggested that while the system was easy to use and enjoyable, perceived usefulness and willingness to adopt the system in a hospital indicate areas for improvement. Nonetheless, the inclusion of 3D avatars enhanced emotional engagement, demonstrating strong potential for telepresence robots in future healthcare environments.

title: LiveShowVR: A Tool to Navigate Through Controlled Environments for Immersive Presentations.
abstract: Through the practical application of the subject “Exploring Costa Rica's biodiversity through its national currency” and taking inspiration from special effects consoles found in theaters, the LiveShowVR tool allows the reimagination of traditional slides as immersive scenes. The presenter has subtly integrated controls at their disposal, with specific functionalities and previously set special effects for each scene. It ranges from basic needs such as note reviewing, microphone use, and audience management, to complete control over the visuo-haptic effects of their environment.

title: VR Zen Garden: Designing a Virtual Environment for Stress Relief.
abstract: We propose VR Zen Garden, a virtual reality (VR) application designed to support stress relief and meditation through interactive spatial soundscapes. The system enables users to create personalized auditory environments by combining two key interactions: Object Placement, which spatializes sound-emitting objects, and Sand Pattern Raking, which modulates sound properties through visual patterns. These inputs are processed by the Sound Spatializer and the Metaphoric Sound Mixer, allowing users to intuitively shape immersive 3D soundscapes in real time. VR Zen Garden offers an engaging and embodied approach to mindfulness, highlighting the potential of sound-driven design in immersive wellness applications.

Abstract:
This work demonstrates GenAssist, a system for generating interactive Extended Reality (XR) programs from natural language prompts. Given plain-text descriptions, our system utilizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to fetch relevant documentation and example code, enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to synthesize and execute XR programs in real time. To ensure outputs align with user specifications, GenAssist incorporates a closed-loop feedback mechanism that uses virtual cameras to inspect the scene and iteratively refine the code, mimicking the manual development cycle of compiling and testing. Beyond static object placement, the system generates functional scripts that animate objects and enable complex user interactions. Our demo showcases the live generation of interactive XR content, allowing users to use voice or text prompts to iteratively build, view, and interact with 3D programs through a headset.

title: A Scalable and Cost-Effective Multi-View Capture System for Photorealistic Dynamic Human Reconstruction.
abstract: Photorealistic human representation is a key factor for embodiment and presence in Virtual and Social Virtual Reality. While recent approaches such as 3D Gaussian Splatting enable high-quality reconstructions, dynamic human capture remains challenging due to the need for synchronized multi-view data. Existing capture systems are often costly and inaccessible, limiting reproducibility and dataset availability. We present a low-cost, reproducible multi-view capture rig consisting of 68 synchronized Raspberry Pi cameras arranged for full 360° coverage. The system enables reliable acquisition of dynamic human data suitable for 3D Gaussian Splatting and VR applications.

title: Toward Interpretable Cognitive Screening in Epilepsy: Eye Tracking in a VR Trail Making Test.
abstract: Cognitive screening is a routine component of epilepsy care. Established pen-and-paper instruments such as the Trail Making Test (TMT) primarily yield summary outcomes (e.g., completion time) that provide limited insight into visual search and executive-control processes affected by epilepsy-related brain network dysfunction. We present an eye-tracked Virtual Reality TMT (VR-TMT) as a controlled research instrument that enables process-level interpretable measurements. The system synchronizes continuous eye-movement streams with timestamped task events (task start/stop and node selections) and logs gaze-to-Area of Interest (AOI) intersections. To reduce VR-specific confounds that can compromise cognitive interpretation, we specify concrete design guidelines for 3D stimulus geometry and the VR+eye-tracking setup (e.g., viewing distance, field-of-view placement, target size). In a feasibility pilot ($\mathrm{n}=8$) usability ratings were favorable and cybersickness was low. Building on this foundation, we outline an analysis framework that derives contextualized gaze features and evaluates their added value in explaining established cognitive screening outcomes in epilepsy cohorts.

title: The Impact of AI Agent Personality in Virtual Debates.
abstract: Recent advances in large language models have enabled Embodied Conversational Agents (ECAs) to function as social actors capable of rich, multimodal interaction. In this work, we investigate how adapting an agent's personality to the user influences social connection and persuasion in debate contexts. We conducted a user study comparing three personality conditions in VR debate interactions: Similar (matching traits), Neutral, and Inverse (opposing traits). Our results showed that similar personality consistently enhances social presence and social connection, highlighting the importance of personality-adaptive ECAs in social interactions.

title: Exploring Proprioception and Spatial Awareness During Auditory and Visual Feet Guidance in Bouldering.
abstract: Besides strength and visual planning, bouldering heavily depends on continuous bodily sensing and spatial judgment. Through a qualitative user experiment, we explore proprioception and spatial awareness during indoor bouldering using augmented reality for feet guidance. We compare a novel spatial sonification guidance method-mapping tempo to horizontal distance, and pitch to vertical direction-to a laser-based visual baseline. Results showed that audio tended to prompt greater attentional focus on foot movements and exploratory decision-making, while visual cues aligned closer with climbers' perceptual expectations, easing posture planning and lowering workload, while making proprioception more implicit. Overall, we highlight how auditory guidance can alter focus and orientation in bouldering, offering insights into the role of multimodal interfaces in shaping embodied sport experiences.

title: Abacus, a Virtual Environment for Learning Spatial Programming.
abstract: Abacus is a virtual learning environment that combines the benefits of visual programming languages with the embodied advantages of virtual environments. As the number of applications involving 3D programming increases, immersive learning environments may help novice programmers achieve higher levels of understanding and performance.

title: AmplifiedTeacup: Trajectory Design in the VR Teacup Experience Using HMD and Electric Wheelchair.
abstract: Wheeled motion platforms (MPs) like small electric cars or electric wheelchairs have been combined with VR visuals via HeadMounted Displays (HMDs) to create immersive experiences. However, space constraints and safety issues make it difficult to map virtual trajectories and speeds directly to physical movements. In this study, we investigate trajectories for a VR ride system combining HMDs and electric wheelchairs, focusing on the classic teacup amusement park ride. We evaluated multiple wheelchair trajectories under the same VR teacup visuals by systematically varying translational and rotational motion. Our findings suggest that wheelchair trajectories incorporating rotational speeds from the VR visuals have the potential to maintain user experience consistency, even with reduced translational speeds. This approach allows the wheelchair to rotate around a fixed point, which could be safer and less costly to operate, while still providing an immersive VR teacup experience.

title: Multimodal Integration of Visual Masking and Phantom Sensation for 3D Object Interaction in Hand Projection.
abstract: Projected hand-arm extension technology (ExtendedHand) enables users to interact with remote objects beyond their physical reach, but faces challenges such as visual discrepancy from 2D projection on 3D objects and a lack of haptic feedback, which inhibit bodily perception. This study proposes a multimodal presentation method that integrates dynamic visual masking for depth-aware spatial perception and position-dependent vibration using Phantom Sensation (PhS). Our user study revealed modality-specific effects: visual factors primarily contribute to the sense of agency and penetration sensation, while vibration independently enhances tactile realism. In particular, the physically unnatural penetration effect serves as a symbolic feedback mechanism that maintains operational continuity, leading to a significantly higher sense of agency compared to the non-penetration condition. In conclusion, the combination of the penetration effect and position-dependent vibration provides an optimal configuration for achieving a heightened penetration sensation and practical usability without compromising the bodily experience of the projected hand.

title: Experiencing Weight Illusion in AR Extended Displays: A Portable Community Demo.
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) design parameters, such as spatial layout and visual delay, are typically optimized for system performance, yet they can also influence human perception. Prior research has shown that visual manipulation alone can alter perceived weight through pseudo-haptic effects, even in the absence of physical feedback. In particular, the perceived weight of AR extended displays (AREDs) has been reported to vary depending on their spatial arrangement relative to a handheld device and the visual delay applied to them. In this demonstration, we present an interactive AR system that enables participants to directly experience how these design parameters affect perceived weight. By transforming a laboratorylevel experimental setup into a demonstration-oriented system, participants can freely adjust the layout and visual delay of AREDs in real time and experience corresponding changes in weight perception. This demonstration highlights how subtle system-level design choices in AREDs can shape perceptual experiences and provides an accessible platform for exploring pseudo-weight illusions beyond controlled experimental settings.

title: VR-Based Visualization of Walking Fatigue in Simulated Environment of Variable PM2.5 and PM10 Particulate Concentration.
abstract: Urbanization and environmental pollution significantly impact human health. This impact is often imperceptible due to its long-term nature. However, virtual environments can simulate the effects of various phenomena on the human body, including poor air quality. We propose a solution that considers the reduced speed of human movement in a VR environment. It adjusts the player's movement speed according to the level of urbanization in the environment, as determined by the dispersion of PM2.5 and PM10 pollution.

title: Analyzing User Behaviors in Metaverse Brand Events that Drive Real-World Store Visit Intentions.
abstract: As metaverse platforms evolve into social and commercial spaces, companies increasingly host virtual events to enhance brand awareness and customer engagement. However, how participation in such events translates into real-world outcomes-specifically, increased intention to visit physical stores-remains underexplored. We analyzed behavioral logs and survey responses from 814 participants at “Metaverse AEON,” a month-long commercial event on the Cluster platform. Six behavioral metrics were compared between users who reported increased store visit intention and those who reported no change. Results suggest that active engagement-game play, photography, emote use, and revisits-was significantly associated with increased visit intention, while dwell time alone showed inconsistent effects. Moreover, these association patterns varied by user segment: Virtual YouTuber fans showed positive associations across multiple metrics, whereas non-fans responded mainly to general-audience content. These findings suggest that engagement quality may play a key role in the transfer from virtual events to real-world behavioral intentions, offering design implications for metaverse brand experiences.

title: ChronoShore: Diegetic Exploration of Short- and Long-Term Environmental Time in a Virtual Coastal Ecosystem.
abstract: We present an extended version of ChronoShore, an immersive virtual reality (VR) environment for interacting with environmental time at multiple temporal scales. The virtual environment is based on a multi-resolution reconstruction of a real segment of the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica, generated from heterogeneous geospatial datasets including aerial point clouds, satellite-based elevation data, and global bathymetry. Unlike conventional timeline-based controls, ChronoShore enables users to explore and manipulate time through diegetic environmental cues, or zeitgebers, embedded directly in the virtual world. In addition to short-term time control via celestial bodies such as the sun and moon, the new version introduces long-term temporal interaction through vegetation, particularly trees, allowing users to traverse years or decades within the simulation. The environment features an enhanced weather model with realistic seasonal dynamics, including rain patterns and cloud morphologies that evolve over the course of the day in response to atmospheric conditions. ChronoShore serves as a research and application platform for studying time perception in VR, immersive storytelling of geological and environmental processes, and relaxation-oriented experiences. The platform is available to other researchers upon request.

title: CoPianist: Co-Playing with a Virtual Pianist in an Interactive VR System for Piano Practice.
abstract: Professional piano practice often lacks immediate and expressive feedback when conducted without an instructor or collaborative partner. This pilot study explores how immersive and generative technologies can enhance advanced piano training through CoPianist, a virtual reality system integrating generative AI for MIDI-based guidance and virtual hand simulation. The system combines adaptive MIDI performance generation with synchronized virtual hand movements, allowing learners to observe and co-perform with a virtual pianist on a simulated piano. Using hand tracking and realtime MIDI analysis, CoPianist delivers feedback on note accuracy, tempo stability, and technical execution.

title: Grayscale Gradation Representation for Direction-Dependent Visualization using High-Speed Projection.
abstract: Projection-based information display offers the advantage of presenting information to multiple users simultaneously using a single device. However, because all users inevitably view the same projected content, it is difficult to provide personalized information tailored to individual users. To overcome this limitation, prior work has introduced high-speed projection techniques that display different images depending on the observer's gaze movement direction. These methods require neither tracking devices nor user-specific hardware; instead, the perceived content changes solely through the observer's own gaze motion. Nevertheless, the presentable images have been restricted to binary images. In this study, we extend this paradigm by enabling grayscale representation, and we propose a method for achieving richer visual presentation for directiondependent visualization.

title: Cezve: A Virtual Turkish Coffee Pot Interaction Technique for 3D Target Selection in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Interaction techniques in virtual reality (VR) are typically designed either for peripersonal space, where direct hand-based manipulation is effective, or for distal space, where indirect techniques such as ray casting are commonly used. However, the space in near distant field remains underexplored. We introduce CEZVE, a virtual toolmediated interaction technique designed to support embodied interaction in near distant space by extending the user's effective reach without ray-based abstraction or mode switching. CEZVE preserves continuous proprioceptive control by treating the tool as a natural extension of the arm. We evaluate Cezve in a user study comparing it with raycasting and virtual hand for object selection tasks performed beyond immediate reach. Results show that CEZVE enables more accurate and efficient interaction, reduces perceived cognitive workload, and is preferred by users over conventional interaction techniques. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly addressing intermediate interaction space and demonstrate the benefits of reach-extension techniques for VR.

title: Investigating Adaptive Hand Visibilities for Accurate 3D User Interactions in Augmented Reality.
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) tasks that require fine motor control often rely on visual hand representations, yet fully visible hands can introduce occlusion and reduce accuracy. In this work, we investigate adaptive hand visualization techniques that dynamically adjust hand visibility based on the current interaction phase to improve accuracy in AR. We designed an AR-based pedicle screw placement task, in which users insert virtual screws into a physical spine model. To evaluate how hand visualization affects task performance, we conducted a user study with 15 participants who performed the task under five hand visualization conditions: Opaque, Transparent, Invisible, Speed-based and Position-based visibility. Our results show that adaptive visualization techniques significantly improve screw placement accuracy compared to the commonly used opaque hand representation. These findings demonstrate the benefits of dynamically adapting hand visibility can support accuracy-critical interactions.

title: Being Together Without Interaction: Ambient Connection and Collectivity in a Multiplayer XR Rave Experience.
abstract: This paper examines how extended reality (XR) can enable social presence and collective engagement without explicit interaction. Using In Pursuit of Repetitive Beats (IPORB), a multisensory VR experience recreating Coventry's 1989 rave scene as a case study, we combine audience evaluation data (n=586) with design analysis to explore inclusion, accessibility, and emotional dynamics. IPORB achieved high scores for immersion, cultural value, and emotional intensity, suggesting that co-presence and synchronised narrative experiences may contribute to meaningful social connection even in the absence of verbal or task-based collaboration. Inclusive design features, such as low-barrier interaction, adaptable participation modes, and culturally situated representation, aim to broadened access to diverse audiences, including those new to XR. Findings highlight the role of shared emotional experience and embodied awareness in shaping socially cohesive XR environments and call for integrating broad evaluative frameworks with targeted social XR measures in future research.

title: ColdMap: Compaction-Aware Cost-Benefit Zone Cleaning for ZNS-Based Key-Value Stores.
abstract: LSM-tree–based key-value stores are widely deployed on Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs to exploit their sequential write semantics. However, despite extensive research on data placement and compaction in LSM–ZNS systems, the problem of victim zone selection during zone cleaning (ZC) has been largely overlooked. Existing designs either rely on greedy heuristics or implicitly assume that victim selection is trivial, which results in unnecessary valid-data copying and avoidable I/O blocking during ZC. This paper presents ColdMap, the first ZC framework that explicitly targets accurate victim zone selection in LSM–ZNS file systems. The key insight behind ColdMap is that zone coldness is not governed by history-based modification metrics, but by the future evolution of the LSM-tree driven by compaction. To capture this behavior, ColdMap (i) predicts zone coldness by proactively simulating future compactions and estimating file invalidation timing, and (ii) applies a cost–benefit ZC algorithm tailored to ZNS file systems. We implement ColdMap in RocksDB and ZenFS and evaluate it on real ZNS SSDs under diverse workloads. Experimental results show that ColdMap reduces ZC overhead by up to 49% compared to state-of-the-art victim selection schemes, resulting in an average 15.7% improvement in overall throughput.

title: COMETS: Cost-effective Multi-node Efficient Training System with Memory Pooling and Sharing.
abstract: Rapid growth of large language models (LLMs) presents major challenges for distributed multi-node training, due to insufficient inter-node bandwidth and lack of scalability in memory expansion. To address both challenges, we propose COMETS, a cost-effective multi-node efficient training system with memory pooling and sharing. By enabling scalable GPU memory expansion and introducing an alternative inter-node data path, COMETS reduces reliance on NIC-based inter-node networking and supports efficient training across diverse cluster environments. We also propose a heterogeneous-aware training strategy to identify optimal training configurations. Experiments show that COMETS improves training throughput by up to 2.11 × over ZeRO-Infinity across eight hardware setups, and boosts performance-per-dollar by 1.98 × and 1.37 × on homogeneous and heterogeneous clusters, respectively.
